First off, I am not an audiophile. This is a review from a simple person who wanted music at work.

I am a Rural Carrier for the United Stated Postal Service. I deliver mail in an LLV truck and these vehicles are basically mobile tin cans. Every panel rattles, making for quite an unpleasant environment, audio wise. I tried playing music directly off my phone, but alas my speakerphone is only so loud and is constantly drowned out by the LLV.

So, I researched Bluetooth speakers and, based on the reviews and popularity, recently purchased two:
-[[ASIN:B016XTADG2 Anker SoundCore Bluetooth Speaker with 24-Hour Playtime, 66-Foot Bluetooth Range & Built-in Mic, Dual-Driver Portable Wireless Speaker with Low Harmonic Distortion and Superior Sound - Black]]
-[[ASIN:B01LZV6TYQ OontZ Angle 3 PLUS Splashproof Bluetooth Speaker - Designed & Engineered by Cambridge SoundWorks for Richer Bass, HD Sound, and 30-Hour Playtime, 10W+ Power, Water Resistant, Portable Wireless Speaker]]

The Anker SoundCore is being returned while I am keeping the OontZ Angle 3 Plus and here is why.

I tested both speakers in my home at first. My very first impression, out of the box:
OontZ Angle 3 Plus - was nice to touch and just felt solid and very well built.
Anker SoundCore - just felt like a simple lightweight brick. It really didn't give the impression of longevity or durability.

The set-up guides were quite different from each other.
OontZ Angle 3 Plus - Extremely easy to read, follow and understand (remember, I am not a music nut lol. This was my first time ever using a Bluetooth speaker and was in completely uncharted territory.) It was all in English, and only English and the diagrams were detailed and made the entire set-up process seamless and carefree.
Anker SoundCore - This guide was very hard to follow. It is printed in darn near every language, in tiny print and the diagrams were quite small as well. I ultimately did get the speaker paired with my phone and figured out what buttons did what, but it took nearly 15 minutes to do so.

Bluetooth Pairing
With both speakers and my phone lined up on a table (well within the proximity specified in each set-up guide), both speakers paired, however:
OontZ Angle 3 Plus - MUCH faster in pairing (mere seconds!).
Anker SoundCore - took nearly two minutes to complete the pairing process.

Pause/Play Button
Since I dismount to deliver packages to a customer's door routinely on my route, I really need to have a simply way to pause my music. I really like how both speakers offer this function on directly on the units, saving me from having to handle my phone.
OontZ Angle 3 Plus - I barely press the Play/Pause button and the speaker immediately reacts. There is NO hesitation.
Anker SoundCore - I press the Play/Pause button and there is a delay of about 5 seconds.. just long enough to make me think I didn't press hard enough and reach to do it again only for the speaker to finally react.

Volume/Overall Playback Quality
OontZ Angle 3 Plus - Wow. Just wow. It is truly unbelievable to hear such full sound, and bass(!), coming from such a small unit. I found myself perfectly pleased with the output without ever reaching max volume on the speaker itself. So I am looking forward to how well it will work in my LLV during my first road test. As for now, I am thoroughly impressed!
Anker SoundCore - I maxed out the volume on my phone and the speaker and was just not impressed. If I could guess, I'd say the max output this speaker achieved was only about 25% more than my speakerphone alone (while the OontZ Angle 3 Plus blew it out of the water with close to double, if not more, output than my speakerphone alone).
I also noted some kind of distortion or interference type background sound with the Anker SoundCore at mid volume and above.

Speakerphone/Mic
I was able to answer an incoming phone call on both units as described in each set-up guide. The quality of in-call sound on each speaker differed:
OontZ Angle 3 Plus - My husband's (the caller) voice was crisp and clear, as if he was sitting talking right next to me. There was no distortion or feedback out of the speaker. Husband reported nothing but a clear voice on his phone.
Anker SoundCore - Husband's voice was clear, but echoed horribly. No matter what volume level I used. There was no distortion (I was expecting this given the distortion with the music playback) bu the continuous echoing is a major issue for me. Husband reported a slight "faded" type of echo on his phone.

Road Test (in my LLV)
OontZ Angle 3 Plus - The sound is amazing in the truck! Thinking I would need it, I maxed the volume on both the speaker and my phone then pressed play on my music. Well, I certainly don't need max volume. I reduced the volume on both the speaker and my phone and found a very happy medium output. This speaker performs perfectly in the loud, rattling setting of a USPS LLV.. even while bouncing down rural dirt two tracks and washboard gravel roads. I am extremely pleased with this tiny speaker.
Anker Soundcore - Even with maxed volume settings, I could not get this speaker to perform anywhere near as well as the OontZ Angle 3 Plus. It had volume and was loud enough to hear over the vehicle's own noise, however the distortion/interference mentioned earlier was still present and in the truck during the road test it had what I would describe as an echoing effect on the music, specifically the singers' voices. It just wasn't clear. (I hope that makes sense.)

Battery Life/Listen While Charging
OontZ Angle 3 Plus - So far, the battery life is impressive. After receiving it, I charged it overnight (as recommended). I then had it connected to my phone for about an hour of home testing. Turned it off and I next used it at work on a Saturday.. had it powered on and connected to my phone and actively playing music for about 5.5 hours. I then used it again on Monday (much longer and busier days in the USPS, FYI).. had it on, connected and active continuously for nearly 9 hours. I have yet to see the low battery light come on. I plan to see just how many days of work I can get out of a single charge.
Anker Soundcore - I have no information for this section on this speaker since I am returning it.

Exterior/Cleaning
At first, I had the OontZ Angle 3 Plus setting on the dashboard of the LLV. This didn't last more than two stops. Despite having the four rubber "feet", the speaker still slid around causing more of a distraction than I would like. I ended up setting it on top of my personal bag, in a bin by my feet with the speaker facing up. This move really helped my piece of mind, knowing it will not go anywhere. This speaker has a soft rubber exterior. It is quite nice and feels luxurious, however... this exterior attracts all dust particles within 50 feet! USPS LLVs are *not* known for being the cleanest and even though I moved the speaker from the dust-ridden dashboard to a bin, it was still slathered with dust and dirt by the end of my route. I figured it was a fair trade, sacrificing the appearance for the gain of having decent music. But.. I got home and went to clean it. I will tell you, my expectations of this working were very low. I didn't think the dust would come off that supple rubber. But with a wet paper towel and a few slow wipes, it did. So, it can be cleaned up!

Case
I did purchase the case for this speaker ([[ASIN:B01NBDY6VP [Official] OontZ Angle 3 Plus Bluetooth Portable Speaker Carry Case, Neoprene with Aluminum Carabiner, reinforced zipper, by Cambridge SoundWorks [NOT FOR OontZ Angle 3]]]). I was mainly wanting a safe way to transport and store the speaker, but after reading the other reviews I was hoping I would be able to keep it clean in the case and still enjoy my music on my route. I received the case and used it yesterday. The case is extremely nice and I appreciate the interior mesh pocket. I have no need for it now, but I'm sure it will come in handy if I ever take this speaker on vacation and need to take the charging cables along. As for playback while in the case? Yeah, it was terribly muffled. It didn't work for me as it apparently has for others. Yet, the case itself is exactly what I was wanting for taking it to and from work. It is not as thickly padded as I would have expected, however it does protect the speaker.

Overall, for my specific purpose and intended use for a Bluetooth speaker, the Anker SoundCore simply won't cut it. However, it is still a nice speaker and will perhaps fit your needs perfectly. After all, most people don't drive LLVs and have the same high demands that go along with that. For me, the OontZ Angle 3 Plus is what I'll be bopping down the road to, mailbox to mailbox.

Happy hunting! Hope this review helps you out!

I purchased this protector due to the overwhelming positive reports from other verified buyers. I do not like my cell phone's screen being unprotected and now with my first Kindle I feel the same way. The HDX screen is gorgeous and I want a way to keep it as such. This screen protector seemed the answer to my predicament.

This protector is, indeed, extremely simple to 'install'. It takes more time to remove it from its packaging and throw the trash away afterwards than it does to apply the protector itself. Simply line up the cutouts on the protector film with the camera and flash at the top and center of your Kindle and you are done. I found it helpful to guide the film into place by kind of rolling the sides down, guiding them to ensure proper placement. Then just apply a little pressure (basically, run your hand around the edges) to activate the adhesive.

Only the outer black margin of the protector has adhesive to stick it to the border and outer edges of your Kindle, thus leaving the clear center which covers your Kindle's screen loose, or non-sticky. This manufacturing and design approach has both pros and one con I have noticed so far.

Pros:

It allows for lightning fast and super easy installation.

Because of the solid black border, you can accidentally touch the sticky side while installing and lining it up without any fingerprints showing through as with a normal screen protector. This was a bonus to me as these things are always so difficult to install without this happening.

The clear center portion that covers the screen is completely 100% bubble free.

Due to some micro hairs/fibers being on the screen despite having wiped it down prior to installing the protector, I learned that I could remove the protector (lifted up one corner and peeled it halfway back to do a quick swipe with the MF cloth again) and it would re-adhere to the Kindle's surface just as well as it did the first time.

The company claims that, if it should lose its stickiness, the protector can be rinsed/washed and used again. I have yet to need to go this far so I cannot comment on the credit-worthiness of this claim, however from my experiences so far, I can see the possibility of this claim holding up.

I have not noticed any blurring or the rainbow affect the company mentions on its packaging. The screen is crystal clear and appears to not even have a screen protector on it.

Con:

Since the clear center portion does not adhere to the screen, it is allowed to float just above the screen thus reducing the screen sensitivity and requiring more force from either your fingertip or your stylus.

After using my Kindle for a few hours after installation of this screen protector, I have come to the above conclusions. As bad as the con is for me and my preferences, I will leave it on for a few days to give myself a little more time and to see if anything changes. This screen protector ranks very high on my list of desirable protectors (I even searched to see if they make a version for my Droid cell phone) so I am really hoping that the sensitivity issue works itself out soon.

***The first part of this review is for the Red option***

I needed more than just a simple case for my Kindle as it pulls double duty serving as my tablet and my planner. I also needed something that would provide it with supreme protection as it accompanies me to and from work every day.

I purchased this case/portfolio in the red color in hopes that it would make it stand out at work. Many of my co-workers have Kindles as well and I didn't want mine to accidentally get picked up. The red is nice, but way too much for me. I have been considering exchanging it for the black and the following issues are what sent me over the edge and led to my returning the red case.

This case/portfolio worked nicely for my needs. However, I removed two stars for two reasons.
#1 The case stunk to high heaven. It was so bad that I thought a stink bug had gotten into my house. Though the "scent" did lessen over a few weeks, it was still very present after five weeks.
#2 The description claims that this case has the ability to put the Kindle to sleep when you close it up. Not true. After my battery died over night, I realized that the sleep/wake feature was not working in my case. I had to physically turn my Kindle off before closing the case (may not seem like much of a hassle, but it quickly becomes a time consuming annoyance).

There was one benefit to this case though. It is the first case I have had for my Kindle that does not have any issues with using the Camera App while still encased in the removable inner sleeve. This was a very nice feature, however not nice enough to get me to keep it.

**This is the review of the Black option**

So, I just returned the red case and opted to give the black version a shot. It arrived this evening and wow, what a difference!

It doesn't stink at all and the sleep/wake feature is functioning properly! I do, however, now have the ghastly on-screen message of needing to slide my Kindle up in its case to take a picture. But this does not bother me very much as I have not used my Kindle for taking pictures more than a handful of times in the month that I have owned it.

All in all, it is a nice, professional case/portfolio that offers the features for my Kindle that I was needing. It also has a fair amount of pockets inside, though do not expect to be able to store much bulk as you will run into two problems..
#1 If you add too many things to the pockets, you run the risk of the pockets bulging and possibly damaging your Kindle's screen.
#2 Also, if you add too much to the pockets, you will possibly not be able to close the case. And if you manage to close it, you may run the risk of stretching the zipper and ultimately damaging the case.

Personally, I keep a small stack (about 10) of my business cards, five gift certificates and a little cash in the pockets and the zippers still flow smoothly with no issues and nothing from the pocket side comes in contact with my screen. Overall, I would recommend this case, as long as you are willing to take a risk on getting one that has the features you are wanting/needing as it seems to be a completely random toss-up as to which case has which features.

On a side note, the included stylus/pen is a great idea, but it isn't executed very well here. The plastic tip leaves a lot to be desired - it takes more force than I care to apply to my screen for the Kindle to register the stylus' contact on the screen. I did some research and purchased [[ASIN:B00E0GV9IC The Friendly Swede Bundle of 6 Micro-Knit Hybrid Fiber Tip Universal Capacitive Stylus Pens 4.5" for Smart Phone Touch Pad + 6 x 15'' Elastic Tether Lanyards + Cleaning Cloth in Retail Packaging]]. These stylus' are VERY nice in appearance and easy to use without requiring much force on the screen at all.

I've had WD drives for decades, and the only issues I ever had were with WD Green and Black drives. Red, Red Plus, and Red Pro work where they're intended to work, as they're intended to work. So do WD Blue. Before buying a WD drive, learn what each color is intended for. The Black drives I've had fail were due to insufficient cooling. Blue are to be used in a PC with one or two drives that sees daily use. That's daily, not 24/365. Not in an array. Each level of Red drive is intended for arrays of different numbers of drives. They are not quiet desktop drives. You really want them somewhere other than next to where you sit.

More importantly than all that, carefully check prices in several places. Don't pay the absurd prices that some people want after buying their stock at retail price. They'll go back down. WD will make more.

This is the third tablet I've used my Verizon SIM card in. The first was a tablet I bought through Verizon. The second was a TabActive2, and now I'm using the same SIM card in this TabActive3. This does not apply to the WiFi-only version. Don't confuse the two.

I pulled the SIM card out of the TabActive2, inserted it in the TabActive3, restarted the device as requested, and a few minutes later the line was active on the new device. I ignored Verizon's emailed instructions, because they don't appear to apply to swapping a current SIM card into a new device. I even restored a Google backup from the 2 to the 3 and saved a lot of time installing apps.

So, why this tablet? It's rugged. It's Samsung. I really like having an 8" tablet. It works with Verizon.

Why 4G/LTE? It's not 5G. I drive a truck through at least 5 states on a regular basis, and in some areas the signal constantly switches between 4G and 5G and the data connection is interrupted. When I can't access online banking, credit cards, and apps relating to business with my 5G phone, I often can with a 4G tablet. I have unlimited data on a second plan for only $10/mth, since I already have a smartphone plan. No hotspot/WiFi needed.

Why upgrade? My TabActive2 only had 16GB of internal storage. The TabActive3 I bought has 128GB. The TabActive3 has DEX. The TabActive2 didn't. I didn't manage to hurt the 2, and the 3 is physically very similar. The 3 has a faster CPU, and a faster GPU.

From the beginning, everything about the TabActive2 as a usable tablet simply wasn't enough. It wasn't fast enough. It didn't have enough storage. But it was rugged. It still is. This is the first time I've upgraded when the old tablet still worked as well as it did when I bought it. It appears that the TabActive3 is just as rugged.

Cons:

I'm pretty picky about how good speakers perform. I'm not a hard nose audiophile, but I know good speakers when I hear them. I have used the same song for decades to truly test the quality of the bass. That song is Alan Parson's "The Raven" and the bass test is the very last note in the song. Most speaker systems cannot handle this deep bass guitar note at any volume. This set did. So as far as the bass, this speaker set passed the toughest test I could throw at it.

The high end was strong and clean, the midrange was the only level I saw a little lacking. This was playing music of the classic rock genre. I play my music pretty exclusively through Windows Media Player which offers a built-in equalizer. Just a little adjusting on the equalizer and I had all levels well balanced, sound was very good.

Some reviewers had mentioned hearing a hum or the like from the right speaker (the one which contains the power and volume controls). When I first hooked everything up out of the box I heard it too. It was noticeable and given time I could see it becoming irritating. I know what causes this hum and how to fix the problem. The problem is caused by poor shielding on the speaker wiring. I added 3 ft. extensions that were double shielded and lo and behold...no more hum, dead silence. I have since put 10 ft. double shielded extensions on both speakers and they are working flawlessly with zero degradation in performance. If you check the answered questions you will find the exact extensions you need. Be careful, not any VGA extension will work for the right speaker! Keep the original speaker wires away from any power cords or power sources and you should get the same result in the end.

I haven't had these speakers for very long so I can't comment on longevity yet. If they unexpectedly have problems I will definitely update this review. But in my honest opinion they seem like a good deal for the money.

I had an iPod 2GB Nano and wanted to get something with larger capacity. I did some research and finally bought the Walkman. I was around for the very first Sony Walkman casette tape player, so the idea of getting a Sony MP3 player was appealing.
After using it for over a month, I find it a great little device. The battery life is amazing. I charged it over two weeks ago and have used it on multiple three hour car rides. I also had it hooked up to a speaker in my office and left it on for several hours and it stil has battery life.
It took me some time to get used to the navigation, but now I am fine with the difference between the Walkman and the iPod. The sound quality is good and although the volume could be better, it is acceptable for my use.
The major problem I have with the unit is the software. Sony included one of those mini disc's which loaded a couple of software programs on my computer. The main program is one which allows you to drag and drop files from your computer to the player; however, it doesn't work. I dragged a few tunes to see how it worked and then started dragging all the music. The software kept accepting the tunes, but after it "loaded" for about 2 hours, I discovered it had only loaded the first set of tunes. The rest, and the two hour wait, was for nothing. The software also has a "delete" function, which also doesn't work. It tells you that it delets items from the player, but they are still there.
So, I junked that software and decided to use the Windows Media Player. This is ok, except that the Media Player has a very odd way to create playlists. There are some round about ways to create the play list and I have finaly learned how to do it, but it took way too long compared to iTunes. The other odd thing is that when you create a play list it has to be from tunes on your computer, not on the device. Then when you sync the device to load the playlist, it may or may not put duplicate versions of the music on the device. Sometimes it finds the songs on the device and sometimes it does not. So, I ended up with multiple copies of some songs. The device software is also pathetic. It doesn't allow you to create playlists on the device, and as others have noted, there is no way to delete items from the device without using the software.
I finally just had the computer recognize the device as an external drive and was able to load songs and delete them with no probme.
Despite the isues, I still like the device better than my Nano. For one thing it has an FM receiver, which works great. Now that I have come to terms with the crappy software, it works great. So, if you are looking for an alternative to the iPod, this is a good option. Just stay away from the software provided by Sony and you will be fine.

I have trouble with the OEM silicone tips keeping a good seal. If I do something wild and crazy (like turning my head /sarcasm) the seal breaks and noise cancellation is diminished. They fit more snugly and hold a seal better than Apple’s silicone tips, so that’s a plus. However, they aren’t as comfortable for long listening sessions. I’d also suggest being very careful when removing them as well - the Apple tips are surprisingly resilient (seemingly indestructible, despite the impression that the silicone is easily tearable. I bought these to use with Brain.fm. I would have preferred wireless but Bluetooth enabled models don’t seem to be able to run all night (8 hours) on a charge. These are actually better than I expected in a couple ways - first, they sound surprisingly good for the price. The bass response is acceptable and the sound is well balanced across the audible spectrum. Second, the cable is a very flexible and durable mesh fabric. It doesn’t kink and tangle as easily as plastic and is reinforced at the plug end. The headband is a light fleece type material - it tends to be warm, but that would be a plus outdoors in cold weather. The transducers are relatively easy to reposition by sticking your finger into the slots made for that purpose. That’s really my only complaint - there’s nothing to really keep them firmly positioned. They tend to shift around easily when putting on or removing the headband. (This tugs on the cable where it enters the back of the headband.) It might be helpful to put a couple of stitches on either side of them to hold them in place. Initially, the headband was a little tight on me but I was able to stretch it out a bit for better comfort - still snug enough to stay in position, but not enough to be uncomfortable.

Everybody has an opinion and they're all different. I finally settled on a pair of MDR-EX51LP buds for my iPod. The buds that come with the iPod are poor sounding and uncomfortable, no matter how trendy it may be to have a white wires dangling from your ears. I tried several different types and brands and settled on these. They have a more balanced sound than the other headphones in the sub $50 bracket that I tested - good bass, clean highs and mids. Do they compare with premium studio cans? No, but neither do the price tag, size or weight. They block office noise at a reasonable SPL and allow me to concentrate on my work without distraction. I can still hear some outside sound if I keep the music volume low enough - as has been mentioned before, that can be a good thing. They're very comfortable - I wear them for hours at a time on a daily basis. I don't get the uneven cord length, but it really isn't a big deal. Headphones are like operating systems - there is no such thing as one size fits all. Get the ones that work for you (and your audio device!) and don't start a holy war with someone who prefers something different.

3.5 STARS. I rounded up because it is more good then bad:
Bought as a Christmas gift for the boyfriend. We are long distance and we FaceTime a lot. Well, actually, I FaceTime with the underside of his kitchen cabinets, the blanket on his bed, the ceilings in all his rooms, or the top of his nightstand. He talks away, oblivious until I say something. It's funny mostly but sometimes in a relationship you need all the connection you can get, even if it's their face on your device while they smile or laugh or talk you through a bad moment. So, I got him this for Christmas so that he could hands-free me and I could still see his pretty face. He finally put it together and started using it the other day... with an asterisk. *THE INCLUDED SCREW/BOLT IS GARBAGE. It was machined badly. Really badly. So it only screws maybe halfway into the arm/neck or whatever it is called, which sits in the weighted base. Thankfully he really doesn't need the screw/bolt because the arm/neck (like a metal dowel, I suppose, that inserts into the base maybe half an inch. The screw/bolt is inserted from under the base and - if it fits correctly) recesses into the base when it's tightened. As this one had threads that weren't smooth about halfway down on the screw/bolt, it left the screw/bolt jutted out. The base won't sit on the nightstand or other flat surface with this issue unless he just doesn't use the screw/bolt. I'd post a photo for clarification but the stand isn't available and getting him to send photos isn't always something I remember when we do talk.

The screw/bolt is I'm sure metric and it does use an Allen wrench (included) to screw in; the threading is very tight, so finding a true replacement screw/bolt is probably gonna require going to a specialty nuts/bolts/hardware store. That's annoying enough to take off 1.5 stars for me.

These are really, really high quality earbuds, especially for the price. The sound quality is actually pretty amazing. I had a middling-quality pair of those "Inked" earbuds attached to my laptop at work. The sound quality was always disappointing, but I had sort of assumed that it was probably due to the laptop sound card, etc. Then today I attached my new Sony Fontopias and wow...what a difference! Yes, they have bass boost, but not so much that it overwhelms the music.

These headphones are also surprisingly comfortable. They aren't the typical in-ear shape that gets jammed all the way into your ear, but there's a little more to them than the default "sort of hang in the outer part of your ear" that you get with the default iPod earbuds, for example. I like the hybrid, in-between quality and they fit me pretty well. They're not noise-cancelling, but the sound is so good that I really don't notice other office sounds (not even my disgusting cubicle neighbor who eats cookies like the Cookie Monster and sounds completely disgusting - now you know why I need to listen to music at work!). I'm so happy with the sound quality and comfort of these headphones, I'm willing to give then four stars in spite of one very major drawback:

THE CORD IS RIDICULOUSLY SHORT.

I have NEVER seen such a short cord on any pair of headphones, earbuds, headset, etc. that I have owned. I measured the cord from the jack to the point where the "Y" that goes to each individual bud starts, and it is barely 2 feet. TWO FEET! People, that is SHORT. So I'm going to go to Radio Shack at lunch today and buy an extension cord/adapter. So unless you're going to sit right next to the source you are connecting the headphones to, whether it's a computer or MP3 player or stereo, you'll need to add the cost of an extension cable to the price. Trust me - it's way too short as sold, like it wouldn't even stretch from my iPod in a backpack to my ears if I was walking around.

Otherwise, awesome headphones.

I like listening to music when I spend time in my backyard. I used to rely on my alexa for this purpose, but more often than not, the volume and clarity were not that good. A portable Bluetooth speaker was the answer and I found just what I needed with this Bluetooth, from Tpone.

What you get with this Bluetooth is a portable, chargeable speaker with that offers up to 18 hours of playback on a single charge. Getting it fully charged will take time, but after that, it’s a matter of pairing it with the Bluetooth on your phone. In about two minutes, it will be ready for use.

The sound quality you get with this Bluetooth speaker is quite good. I like the bass, and for my needs, the volume is sufficient. It’s not powerful enough to blast you away, but for what I need, the volume level works. I use it mostly when I sit on my back patio and/or jump in the pool. I don’t need extreme volume, so this works. There is a plus and minus button on the unit that at first seem like volume controls, but they are not. If you push these, the music will either advance forward or backward to the next song on the list. The volume is controlled by your phone or whatever device you have paired.

There are different colored lights on this speaker that react to the music, adding to the visuals. Again, for my needs, I really don’t care about the lights. But I can see how this could certainly add to the coolness factor for some people. The added colors and the way they react to the intensity of the music is a nice addition. Oh, and I like that I can use this to charge my phone. If a phone is paired, it could drain the phone’s power quickly while you play music. You can easily counter this by plugging your phone directly into the unit, helping to keep your phone charged.

Having the means to listen to music is an ongoing need for me. Whether I am listening to music in my backyard or taking a trip to a nearby beach, I need to be able to play my tunes and the easiest way is to use a portable Bluetooth speaker. This Bluetooth from Tpone delivers on most all counts. The easy pairing, the bass, and the overall sound quality make this an easy winner and an excellent Bluetooth choice.

I have several flat screen televisions in my household. With the improved technology, it’s usually simple enough to access the controls and bring most anything from the internet onto the big screen. But for those times when I need to connect a laptop or something else to the flat screen, an HDMI cable is needed and a very good choice for the task is this HDMI from Talk Works.

Six feet in length, this cable is designed for relatively short distance connections. Both ends of this HDMI are the same, so it doesn’t matter which end you use on which device. What matter is that you connect to the correct in/out plug, based on which one is the receiving end.

Once connected, this HDMI connects electronics with precision and clarity. It features a gold plated design that helps keep it from wearing out and apparently improves the connection, or so it seems. I don’t have any issues with it. If you want to improve the life even longer, be sure to save the plastic caps and place them back on the ends of the cord after use.

Connecting electronics is often necessary. This HDMI from Talk Works performs its intended task, with a snug connection that won’t come loose and a good deal of clarity from one device to another. It’s an excellent means to keep your electronics connected.

A mouse is a must for most people. Unless you use a laptop or some other computer that already has a built- in mouse, you need a way to navigate and if you want to eliminate messy cords, a good option is this wireless mouse from BreSii store.

I’ve used other wireless mouses, but this one is better. It’s wireless by way of Bluetooth, which makes connection about as simple as it can be. You just plug it into the usb on the laptop or desktop pc and your ready to use. The mouse fits comfortably in your hands and is easy to use and control. There are no lights on this mouse or sounds made, but it does what you need it to do.

On the subject of sound, this brings me to what I consider this device’s greatest attribute: It’s quiet! You can’t hear the clicking sound, like you can with most others. This is great for those who get irritated listening to someone in another room, constantly clicking away on their mouse. With the silence of the clicks, there is no distraction. This is something I wish more manufacturers offered.

A computer mouse is a must- have item. If you want a better mouse that functions intuitively and keeps quiet while you work, then this wireless mouse from BreSii is the tool for you. It hooks up to most any computer or laptop and will navigate your way without cords or sounds.

Navigating on a pc screen requires a mouse of some sort. They have come a long way over the years, with more features and more comfort. One that is great for those who like to add a little color to their navigation is this wireless mouse from PEIOUS.

Shaped for your hands, this mouse is comfortable to hold and click. It’s easy enough to use and you can’t feel any strain on your hands, so it earns good marks there. But the feature that is most appealing is the lights. You can change the lights to different modes and even shut them off completely, if you prefer. I like that the lights are soft- you notice them, but they are not so bright that they distract from what you are doing.

The bluetooth works okay on this mouse and one of the more unusual features is that you have to plug it in to charge. With most others I have used, you need to supply batteries, but this one charges by plugging it into a usb outlet. It’s nice not to have to buy batteries, but it also means you need to have a usb nearby for charging purposes. I consider this feature a plus, as I hate having to search for batteries when the need arises.

To conserve power with this mouse, there is a switch to shut it off. Plus, it will automatically shut off, to preserve power, if there is no movement for several minutes. This is good because, with regular use, you will need to recharge this more than you realize and saving power makes a difference.

Computers need a means for navigation and that requires a mouse of one type or another. You could go for the boring, ordinary mouse with buttons to click and nothing more, or you could have a little fun and get this wireless mouse from PEIOUS. I vote for the latter. It might only be a mouse, but the lights and the elimination of batteries make this a standout mouse and one I recommend.

If you use electronics and like to create videos, you need a good, reliable and preferably small camcorder for the job. A good option for this level of need is this 2.7K Video Camera Camcorder from Ordro.

Compact in size, this camera weighs only about half a pound and it comes complete with a pair of batteries plus a remote control. There are no other accessories in the package, but it has what you need to get plugged in and start recording.

This camcorder is easy enough to use and it does offer 2.7k resolution and 48 megapixels, which means good picture quality overall. I agree there are better cameras that create better, crisper video picture quality but this is quite good for the price point. There are no issues with sound at all, it is quite good. I have noticed just small concerns with the picture and that is why I recommend a more deluxe camera if that is what you feel you need.

For my household, this camcorder gets most of its workout for you tube, and we find it quite useful for that purpose. It’s also good for social media video- taking. It gets the job done and everything certainly looks good for our level of needs. It’s tough to beat this camcorder for the price and it thus earns an easy recommendation from me.

My sound system on my work pc isn’t the best. Internal speakers are often not the best quality- you need an external speaker set if you want the enjoy better overall sound. This need convinced me to add Creative Pebble 2.0 USB-Powered Desktop Speakers to my office.

These speakers are round and are angled at approximately 45 degrees. This is good, because it aims the sound more directly at you, when you’re sitting at a desk. The sound quality is generally good, especially for this price range. There is a volume control on one of the speakers, which controls both. If you feel you can’t get the desired volume, don’t forget to check your existing volume, on your pc. The control on these speakers works with your built- in speakers volume control.

I really like the bass delivered by these speakers. When you consider how small these speakers are, it is not something you would expect. Oh, and speaking of the size, they are small enough to fit into tight quarters. They are less then five inches wide, so you should have no problem finding a place on your desktop to sit them.

These speakers come in either white or black, to fit your décor. I picked black because it matches best with my color scheme. II like what I have and, again, for the price point it would be difficult to find a set of speakers any better than Creative Pebble 2.0 USB Powered Desktop Speakers. They are easily worth the small investment.

With the current emphasis on streaming, there is less and less need to have a physical machine like a Blu-ray player in your home. But however small it may be, the need for this type of electronic hasn’t gone away and since I needed to upgrade mine, I went ahead and got this Sony Blu-ray Player.

This Sony Blu-ray player is ready to use straight from the box and even includes an HDMI so you don’t need to go out and buy one. There is an ethernet and digital coax connection also. The included remote control completes the hardware package.

Testing this unit with 4D Blu- ray disks shows that it lives up to its advanced claims. The picture and sound are both quite good and it can be used with regular DVD also. The colors are vivid- much more so than when played on ordinary electronic devices. If you would rather stream, you can do that as well. We are hooked on Netflix in my household, so it was nice to discover that this unit is ready for Netflix streaming.

This Sony Blu-ray player is compact in size and fits in most any space. It’s certainly a well- engineered electronic device and it’s great for anyone who wants to enhance the improve on their television screen. I can’t really find anything to criticize, so it earns an easy 5 stars from me.

Modern- day monitors are a vast improvement over the bulky monitors of the past. Today, monitors are thin and flat, making them easy to fit into small spaces. However, monitors are often too low to the surface and require leaning down to look at them. A riser stand solves the problem and a good choice for the purpose is the Husky Mounts Monitor Riser Black Steel Laptop Stand.

Unpackaging these monitor stands reveals that a small amount of assembly is needed. But small is the word, as it takes no tools and almost no effort to screw the four legs into place. The black color makes this stand neutral and makes it match most any office space or décor.

What I like best about this stand is the adjustable legs. You can twist the knobs on the bottom of each leg to elevate the stands a little more. The stand can be adjusted from 2.5 to 3.25 inches in height and, if you’re like me, you will probably want to maximize the height, for the greatest level of viewing comfort.

Flat screen monitors are great, but they often need a little boost in height and Husky Mounts Monitor Riser Black Steel Laptop Stand gets the job done. They are strong enough to hold a small flat screen television, too. I purchased a pair and I like the results so far. It’s a sturdy stand that helps take the strain out of monitor viewing.

More often than not, computer monitor screens are a little too low. They are too close to the table or desk on which they stand, and they require that you lean down to view. A simple elevation makes things much better and an excellent choice for the purpose is Husky Mounts Monitor Riser Bamboo Laptop Stand.

I got this pair of stands for my workplace monitors. I have two monitors and I selected this product first for the color. I like the natural wood and I knew it would help add some much-needed contrast to my workspace, which is comprised of black, white, and dark brown. If you like, you could apply stain and change the color to the shade of your choosing.

Taken from the box, all you need to do is screw the four legs into place and you’re ready to go. An added bonus with this stand is that the legs are adjustable- you can loosen and turn the knobs on the bottom and make the stand slightly taller. The brushed stainless steel legs look cool and the stands even have a wide slot on top, perfect for placing an iPad or something similar.

There is a small amount of space underneath these stands, so you can store other office items, thereby conserving desktop space. They are sturdy and can easily support my two large monitors. All things considered, Husky Mounts Monitor Riser Bamboo Laptop Stand is a winner in my book and I’m glad to have a pair of these stands in my workplace office.

Most of the places I have lived have been reasonably safe, so I have never felt any pressing need to add a camera security system to my home. I already have an alarm system, which is useful, but no camera system. I decided that it would be good to be able to see people at the main entrances to my home/property and this convinced me to add the Arlo Ultra - 4K UHD Wire-Free Security 2 Camera System to my house.

Setting this security system up is simple enough. You have to mount the included 2 cameras and it doesn’t take much time to complete this step. I placed one of them by my front door and the other one just outside my garage, facing the driveway. The gated entrance to my backyard is right there, and I usually leave my car in the driveway and not the garage, so this seemed like a good place.

There are many things to like about this security camera system, like the wide angle of view that is good for seeing from my backyard gate to the end of my driveway. You can even speak back and forth with someone at your front door and this can prove useful when you want to avoid talking directly, face to face, with solicitors.

With the image quality, although it isn’t as sharp as I expected, it seems sufficient to me. I haven’t experienced any intruders thus far- knock on wood- so I haven’t necessarily needed to get crystal clear details. One limitation I have is that I haven’t owned a camera security system before. This is a first for me, so I don’t have any point of comparison. Still, the picture quality seems good. And I like the notification system. Any motion detection is set up to record, so you can see what is going on and you know quickly.

The app itself is user- friendly enough but one thing to keep in mind is that the Arlo Smart Servive and cloud recording are free for only the first year. After that, you have to pay for a subscription. I will wait to see if the system is worth my while, then decide whether to subscribe. A year of free usage time should be sufficient to make the call.

Security is important and the Arlo Ultra - 4K UHD Wire-Free Security 2 Camera System is a good way to keep safe. Two cameras are definitely better than one because I am able to secure the two areas of my property where an unwanted individual is most likely to show up. I find the app and picture quality good and the system as a whole has enough positive points to recommend.

I’m never been a huge fan of headphones. I recognize their value and necessity when you want to listen to something but no one around you does. The reason I don’t like headphones is the bulkiness and wires but Soundcore Anker Liberty Air True Wireless Earphones with Charging Case have eliminated these issues.

These earphones come in a small case and they are extremely lightweight. You simply remove them from the package, connect via Bluetooth, insert in the ears, and start listening to your favorite tunes. There are no wires so you can move around as you please and because they are so small, you don’t have the bulkiness. Many people, unless they take a close look at you, will not even know that you are using earphones.

Of course, what matters most with something like this is the sound quality and these earphones score above average marks for sound. The bass is especially good and I like that I can pause, skip music, take calls, etc with a simple push of the touchpads. And to charge, you just place them back into the case. They claim to last up to 20 hours on a charge, but I haven’t come even close to using them for that much time, so I cannot verify the claim.

Soundcore Amker Liberty True Wireless Earphones do not provide any way to control the volume using touch controls, so this is one issue I have with them. But other than that, these are very good earphones and certainly worth a try

Electronics have become a regular part of life. There is really no sense in resisting- electronics are here to stay and most would agree, even if they have slight reservations, that electronics have improved our lives overall. These electronic devices need to be continuously recharged and an excellent tool for the job is this Kasa Smart Wifi Power Strip.

This power strip is intended to charge lots of electronics at once. It has six standard outlets and three USB outlets. That means you can charge up to nine devices at once, making this a very useful and popular item to take with you at your next conference. You will find that people around you will ask to plug themselves in and you will have no trouble obliging. It has surge protection, too, so that your electronics stay safe.

What sets this power strip apart, however, is its high tech personality. It can be controlled remotely using the Kasa app and you can see exactly how much power each item is using, then shut off individual outlets if you like, all from the app! And if you have Google Assistant, Alexa, or Microsoft Cortana, you can use voice commands to control the outlets. That means being able to turn on and off, say, a light that is plugged into the strip with a simple utterance. It’s a geek’s power strip dream come true. I plan to use it on my holiday lights when the season comes around- it will be much easier then climbing behind the tree to manually turn the lights on and off.

Kasa Smart Wifi Power Strip is a heavy- duty power strip that seems like it was made to last. The plug on the strip does require a three prong outlet to plug it in, so make sure you can accommodate before you buy. It has all of the things you would want in an app controlled, voice activated power strip and it receives my highest recommendation.

As much as we travel in my household, we need an assortment of luggage, backpacks, and other user- friendly containers. We have several different pieces and that’s great because it means there is always an appropriate bag for the trip at hand. But one area my household lacks a little is with smaller bags and that is what convinced me to add the Solo Gramercy Rolling Case Laptop Bag to my collection.

First and probably foremost, this bag is made to hold a laptop computer and it has a separate compartment for it. I like that the laptop compartment is quickly accessible because it means that, if you take this to an airport, you can quickly remove the laptop, as you are required to do. But this is much more than a place to store your laptop computer. It is also good for carrying books, brochures, and other paper items, with large and small compartments to keep everything organized.

I sometimes take very short trips that don’t require much clothing or grooming items and I was concerned at first that this bag wasn’t designed correctly to hold such items. But in fact, it is, provided that you don’t have much. As a man, I normally don’t need to take much with me anyway and I have found that I can fit what I need for a day’s change in clothing, plus my personal grooming items, plus my laptop, all within the confines of this bag. It won’t hold much more than that, so don’t think of using this as your sole piece of luggage for a multi- day trip. There isn’t sufficient storage space in that instance, but you can get away with using it for a one or two day trip.

To help maneuver, this laptop bag has four spinner- style wheels and a telescopic handle. This makes it ideal to drag along when you’re at an airport, but I should also point out that this bag is useful even if you have no need or limited need to use it during air travel. It’s also very useful when you need to carry your laptop and school or business books and documents from place to place. It’s better than a traditional briefcase because it has more ways to organize your items.

We like and need an assortment of bags in my household because we never know where we will travel next and what we will need. The Solo Gramercy Rolling Case Laptop Bag is a useful storage bag for airport or other uses and it has made an excellent addition to our collection thus far, as it has come in handy for both travel and business uses.

Computers are an important part of life. I know, I know- we need to get away from electronics and try to return to the days when more personal interactions were the norm. But regardless of how you feel about the proliferation of electronics in everyday living, there is no denying that most of us need them to one degree or another. We are writers/bloggers in my home and need good machines to carry us through the day. And the Acer Aspire Touch Desktop is one excellent machine for everyday use.

Let’s start with the physical attributes. This Acer computer features a very large flat screen with excellent clarity, making it ideal for watching videos, television shows, etc. The keyboard and mouse are wireless, so there is no issue over wires getting tangled as you work. Best of all, the CPU is part of the monitor. There is no separate tower or other computing unit, and that means this computer is space efficient. All you need is a place wide enough to handle the width of the monitor. The keyboard is certainly different from the one I was using previously and it took some adjusting to get used to. But this is the case with any new keyboard and you know what?- the adjustment period for this keyboard was less than a day. In almost no time at all, my wife and I took to the change and had no further issues.

As for the set up, well, it doesn’t get much better than this. I can remember when it would take several hours and much frustration to set up a new computer. But with Acer Aspire, the set up was complete and the computer was ready to use in less than 10 minutes after removing it from the box! We actually scheduled some time in our day, thinking it was going to require a fair amount of time to complete everything. It was so fast I started to worry that I did something wrong. But that wasn’t the case- everything is pretty much ready to go, straight from the package.

Because of our writing and blogging, we often need to have multiple windows open at any given time. This was an issue with my wife’s laptop and it would often slow her computer to a crawl. With this Acer computer, there is no such problem. She can have ten separate windows open, along with Microsoft Word and Excel, and the speed is still as good as ever. Again, this is a definite plus, as computer speed is a top concern for us and many other computer users.

I always try to find something that needs improvement when I write a product review but with the Acer Aspire, I can think of only one thing, and it relates to the Office Suite. They give you Office Suite for a free trial but once the trial is up, you will have to purchase it yourself. Acer could easily make this improvement and while this type of criticism has really nothing to do with the functionality of the product itself, it is about the only issue I can find. Everything else about this computer is well above average.

Computers are essential to my household. We need our computers for writing, for the classes I teach, and other uses. With the Acer Aspire Touch Desktop, we have found a cutting- edge computing machine that fits our needs perfectly and has everything we desire. It’s an excellent computer that would look really good on your desktop and I recommend it when it comes time for your next pc upgrade.

Looking for a quality laptop at a fair price? Then one you might want to consider is the Dell Inspiron 7000 Series. This laptop computer offers the latest in technological improvements for an all- around user- friendly experience.

I have owned many Dell products over the years and have generally had good success with them. This Dell laptop impresses from the start, first with its attractive, modern design. It looks and feels the way a top- of- the- line computer should look and feel, with a lightweight composition and sleek appearance. Second, this Dell product is extremely easy to set up. A person needs no computer skill whatsoever to prepare this laptop for use. You just answer a few simple questions, link and e-mail account if you like, set up a user name, etc., and presto- you are logged in and ready to connect your wifi for home usage.

As for its usefulness, this Dell computer scores well in most areas. One of my kids likes to use it and she was immediately impressed by the fact that the hinges allow the screen to be folded backward, flush with the base, for a tablet- like arrangement. She likes to use the computer to play games, so she liked this capability. The images are very clear, too, better than those I have on my previous laptop, which was an HP model a couple of years old.

One of the key features of this laptop is its touchscreen capabilities. I must admit, I was a little skeptical about this feature for a few reasons. First, I was concerned that it wouldn’t work the way it should and second, I didn’t know if I would take to the new technology. I normally adapt to change quickly, but touching a computer screen when I could easily use the built in mouse control? I just wasn’t sure this would work for me. But now that I have used it, I like the touch screen feature. I use it more than expected and have now abandoned the use of the mouse, in most circumstances. The only slight issue I have had is with the tendency of the touch screen to not always react immediately. Sometimes, it requires a second touch for the command to accept. Other than that, it seems to work well.

Dell Inspiron 7000 Series has a 13 inch screen which is just slightly smaller than that of my previous laptop. The speed of this laptop is better, however, and it quickly moves from one web site to the next without much trouble. It’s a very good laptop for the price and it’s one I recommend.

Corsair 1100 Gaming Headset is a very nice headset with many good reasons to consider it for purchase. It is manufactured by a company known for its quality headsets and this latest model is every bit as good as many from Corsair's past.

Taking a close look at this headset, the first positive aspect is the appearance. It is very modern, slick, and cool- the type that most anyone would not mind wearing, just because it looks so good. The comfort level is very good too, with just the right amount of cushioning and lightweight design.

Most important to many is the sound quality and what you get with this Corsair headset is excellent. The sound is crisp, clear, and among the best I have ever used. No matter what type of sound is flowing through the wires, it enters your ears sounding the way it should, without any fuzziness or interference. Even when you try different sounds, music, etc., it still sounds excellent.

Most products have at least one potential flaw but with this Corsair headset, I am hard- pressed to find any thing wrong or anything I would change. Okay, it would be nice if it was priced a little lower, but with quality like this- both in comfort and in the sound- a few extra dollars is certainly money well invested.

Logitech Trackball Marble Mouse is one of the better computer accessories I have used and it offers a noticeable improvement compared to traditional computer mice. Its unique shape makes it much more comfortable and a no- sliding- necessary design eliminates the need to drag your mouse across a flat surface to move the computer pointer on your screen. To move the pointer, all you do is move the large, red marble trackball. There is less strain on the fingers and wrist, making for a more comfortable experience.

Besides the added comfort, another advantage of the Logitech Trackball Marble Mouse is that it requires less space than a traditional mouse. Because this mouse is stationary and doesn't need to be dragged across a desk or other surface, it can fit into many small spaces. You don't need to make room to drag it, so it can be placed in tight quarters. This is great for those who work in offices with limited desk space.

The Logitech Trackball Marble Mouse offers four buttons to use for clicking. The large tabs on each side of the mouse are used for the usual right and left click functions and then there are two smaller tabs right above each of the larger tabs that are used for various functions. These two small tabs can be programmed to perform several things, and many will likely program them to scroll since this Logitech mouse doesn't have a scroll wheel. But the tabs can be programmed for other things, too. Since I don't necessarily need to scroll, my small tabs have been programmed as browser back and forward buttons. This makes life a little easier because I no longer need to move my mouse to the top of my screen and click the forward and backward arrows in the upper left corner. I just click my small left tab to go back and my small right tab to go forward.

The Logitech Trackball Marble Mouse is a marked improvement compared to the standard mouse, but I admit that it does take some getting used to. Having used a traditional mouse for most of my computer- using years, I had grown accustomed to sliding my mouse across the desk surface. Thus, when I started to use the Logitech Trackball Marble Mouse, I kept sliding it around on my desk also, even though I knew this mouse didn't need to be dragged. It took some time to break this habit. It also took time to get used to the sensitivity of the trackball. The slightest movement sends your pointer flying and when I first started to use this mouse, I would continually underestimate the precision of the Logitech Trackball Marble Mouse. My movements of the trackball were far too extreme. The pointer would soar across my computer screen, even though I would swear I wasn't moving the trackball very much. It is a very sensitive device that almost seems too loose at first because it moves so freely and with such little effort.

Compared to a traditional mouse, the Logitech Trackball Marble Mouse has many great things to offer and it is a mouse I am happy I took the time to try. It is superior to the traditional model in most areas, reducing pain and strain and offering greater accuracy and an easy grip. It does take time to get used to, but it is worth it in the long run and even those who initially resist the change will be happy, in due time, that they made the switch to Logitech.

Hewlett Packard Photosmart M407 is a nice little digital camera that is small enough to fit inside your pants pocket. This camera is one of the best buys around among cameras with greater than 4 megepixels and while there are better cameras on the market, this is a very nice one for the money.

My favorite qualities of this camera are its size, its ease of use, and its sharp resolution. Pictures can be taken in VGA (lowest quality) or in 2 MP or 4MP resolution. These higher resolutions are going to eat up more memory but they produce sharp, clear photos. For everyday picture taking, I have found the VGA to be just fine, but for someone who is more experienced as a photographer, the 4 MP setting is needed to produce the sharpest images. The ones you get with this camera at that resolution level are very good, but you need to keep in mind that the memory (without buying a memory card) is capable of storing only about 10 images at this level. Lower the quality to VGA, and you can store about 160 images.

Some of the disadvantages of this camera include its video capabilities and the placement of certain buttons and controls. The video is offered with an MPEG format and it produces images at 30 frames per second. Its quality isn't very good and I recommend it only to people who really need/want to take a video and have no other alternative. I don't like the placement of the video and picture shutters on the top of the camera either. The picture button is larger than the video shutter, like it should be since it is used more frequently. But the picture shutter is placed to the left of the video shutter on the top of the camera. The picture shutter is used more and it should be on the right side because, to most people, your instinct is to press the button furthest to the right. I cannot count the number of times I have accidentally pressed the video button by mistake.

This camera comes with batteries, two USB cables, a strap, a user manual, and HP image software. This software is nice because it helps new photographers organize pictures and upload them into a pc. The other additions are expected with a digital camera but they help aid in the usability of this electronic device.

Overall, HP Photosmart is a good digital camera for the money and it is one of the few that offers more than 4 megapixels at such a low price. It was the first digital camera I ever purchased and I haven't regretted making the buying decision.

I have 3 of these units in the house, each in a different room. The first one is about 3 years old and working just fine.  Installation is very simple and value for convenience is great.  They are in strategic locations with a light plugged in on the top plug and two usb cords in the bottom.  One for the apple orchard and the other for all the other items (Alexa, android or Kindle).  Which ever room I find myself in and in need of a quick charging of equipment it is ready and waiting.  The one in the family room is the newest and is located by my favorite sitting spot so a quick charge of something I forgot to do earlier can go on while I still use it.  This has really worked out for my phone and Kindle.  I did not buy the units at the same time but after each time I found a "good" spot for one more. Although this review may seem to be "a little late", I do think that my experience with the earlier model of this Sony is appropriate. I bought a KDS-60A2000 in January of 2007 so I've had it for a few months over a year. As most of you will recognize, my unit is a 60" SXRT from the previous model year.

Like many of you, I did a lot of Internet research before settling on the Sony - it was very highly rated by a number of sites. The final straw was live viewing many sets side-by-side on the same program from the same source - it was a no-brainer - the Sony had at least as good a picture as any Plasma in the store and the price couldn't be beat.

I use Verizon's FIOS fiber optic service and have the unit hooked up through my home theater audio. The picture - indeed the HD experience - is simply awesome - especially live sports - like ice hockey.

I did "tune" the picture using the DVE (Digital Video Essentials) HD optimization DVD and it remains the sharpest, most accurate picture that I have personally seen (including the high-bucks plasma sets). I've had absolutely no problems of any kind and there have been no regrets on purchasing this set.

Another tidbit: I also purchased a Logitech Harmony 880 remote control and am able to control the Sony, the Verizon HD receiver, a Yamaha home theater receiver and a Sony upscaling DVD with a single click. It's programmed via the Logitech Internet site (using a USB connection) and can handle about any peripheral you might have. I've got a bowlful of unused remotes now. It's a little pricey at $150 but it has contributed to my HD enjoyment by simplifying the mechanics.

Like so many others with multiple remotes, I view this unit as a very attractive alternative to a sixpack of remotes. A single button turns on (in sequence) my Sony HDTV, Yamaha receiver, and FIOS DVR/receiver. Or, alternatively, the Sony, receiver, and Sony DVD - depending on the selection. It even switches the input on the receiver appropriately. A single button turns off whatever units are "on". And one of the best features is the ability to re-program the remote via the Logitech website if/when something is upgraded or replaced.

The only downside is that (obviously) a "universal" remote can't select EVERY option that may be available with the manufacturer's OEM unit. But those options tend to be little used ones. Another peeve is that sometimes I must shake the unit to get the display to light up. Otherwise, I don't see how most folks can get along without one. I really like mine.

UPDATE (4/3/2013) I don't know if anyone will be interested due to the original date of this review, BUT just to show the utility of this remote, I thought I'd post this update. I recently replaced the previously mentioned Yamaha receiver with a new Denon unit and the Sony DVD was replaced by a Sony Blu-ray AND I added a Roku streaming box. I went to the Logitech site and created new profiles using the new equipment and now I control all of the new units just as well as it had controlled the original units. So, the point is - the remote can grow with your system when you change or add new equipment. Pretty great, huh?

I am very excited with this keyboard and that's very unusual for me. I usually get excited with food and travel. Not typing!

Like almost everything about this. I have to Alexa's in the apartment and having a similar "companion" in the car is perfect!

I only wish I could name it differently (my oldest is Alexa and the youngest in Echo). The App doesn't allow to change the name or what to call it like it does for the other in-home Alexas.

I have an older Audi and the audio is via cable. But the actual integration is via bluetooth with the phone. My phone can also connect to the car-phone via bluetooth and this unit is clever enough to know when to let the phone part connect directly to the car and when to switch to Aux audio.

I am very happy with my dotty! Plugged right into my home network and became the boss of the house! Voice recognition is great and I think it's making the older siblling Alexa a bit jealous. Alexa got reassgined from my bedroom to the living room.

The sound is really booming for such a little cutie! Love the fact that it connects to my bluetooth speaker so nicely!

This is just great stuff! My old sony stdr3300es doesn't have streaming but all my music is now from streaming. So this was a perfect marriage between old and new.

Connects really quick with my Samsung S7 and Amazon Echo Dot. I had to admonish my S7 not to connect automatically with it every time I had the two close by. Same with my Echo. After a few stern commands, these pairs are behaving.

Set up was no issue at all. The sound is crisp and clear, although my Amp warbles a bit if I switch it to this device and I haven't connected the source via Bluetooth yet. Not sure if this "warble" is present in the signal after connecting though. My ears aren't that awesome to pick up something like that.

Yet.

Maybe when I have bionic ears, it might pick up the "warble". 😏🤔😊

I have a few recent newer devices and my old Sony DE3300ES's HDMI connections are not all working (or the sound signals are jumbled enough for the DVI output not to work). So these connectors allows me to get the video out through component YPbPR and the LDCM audio so that the surround works. I am really pleased with these. Construction is great and small enough to be tucked behind the amp. Powered via USB (comes with the charger) so I was able to easily hook them up to my multi USB charger and saving the provided ones for some other use in the future.

Just fantastic! I have the first generation Kindle also which had the voice thing so it could read the book to me. But I barely used it. This new version doesn't have audio capability. But it's light and easy to operate. This is the base model, so it can only connect via wi-fi.

Blown away by the quality of this bag. Comes with a TSA lock for the main lens/camera compartment. There's a plastic frame to keep other gear or clumsy bystanders from crushing the bag along with camera equipment. The back and straps are padded and vented with about 1/4" clearance. Overall build quality is way above its pricing. I expect this bag to safely transport my gear no less than 5 years.
Easy to set up work well nice sound, and cool stereo split. Better sound and comfort than grandsons 200$ bud type

I’ll use my own words thank you! I wanted the 1080 to be crisp, and it is. It doesn’t WiFi with the rest of my gear but it does Bluetooth sound. It’s HDMI for picture. Like all projectors it’ll wash out if there’s too much light. I haven’t tried USB input.

You have to wire it to the back-up lights, and you have to wire it to full time 12v. The instructions are badly translated. It only comes with 2-40’ cables, so you have to store what you don’t use. The display is only bright enough if the screen is aimed right at the viewer. None of this is clear in the directions.
Interestingly the infrareds come on with the camera, even in daylight red cars light up.
The hardware is adequate for the price.
The video quality is good. Nice screen size. The remote does not work right away when I press buttons. I have to press them more than once. Also, the sound while the DVD spinning is a bit loud.
I was actually very surprised at the quality of sound this produces for something so small and inexpensive. I use it regularly, and I love it. It's a rugged little speaker that will get the job done.

THESE SPESKERS ARE OK.  THEY SOUND OK.  THE ONLY THING I DON'T LIKE ABOUT THEM IS THAT THE VOLUME CONTROL ARE PUSH BUTTON RATHER THAN DIAL BUTTON. AND YOU HAVE TO HOLD THE SPEAKER IN ORDER TO ADJUST THE VOLUME.  THEY WERE EASY TO CONNECT.  JUST PLUG IN THE USB CABLE.

I had been looking for earbuds that wouldn't continually fall out of my ears and started researching here on Amazon and was immediately drawn to these "earhook" headphones.  I was a little worried that they might be uncomfortable because I have very sensitive ears but I was pleasantly surprised by how comfortable these are.  I would have thought that after wearing them for a while, they would start to feel heavy wrapped around my ears but they don't!  I just love the fact that I can wear them on my walks and while running around town and not have to worry about my earbuds falling out every few minutes.  The sound quality is very good and it blocks out other noises because they fit (and stay) in your ears so well. I couldn't wait to get this! I had the PS-100 for several years and loved it, wore it out! So I stuck with the brand. I loved the idea of an amplifier and control so I could change the volume without having to reach for the radio. And I love the slim design of the speaker. My only complaint would be it doesn't have as much bass as the PS-100. But it's well worth it's weight in gold for us night music lovers!
1st time using and so far I like them very much. They don't hurt my ears and the sound is just like I like it.
so easy to use and sounds great in small office room…The only thing missing however is that it came without mentioned cover.

I purchased a pair last week and got a defective pair. However, I got a new pair in Copper Red and these are highly recommended for the gym or if you enjoy a quality Bluetooth earbud. The Equalizer settings work very well and so does the application Jabra offers in the App Store. I listen to a wide variety of music from modern rap, old hip hop, 80s-90s death metal, classical, and EDM. The equalizer really does make a difference and you can make any genre sound well. I’ve tried many brands at the gym and so far the “65T Elite Active” really are elite compared to others.
Works good. I just don’t like the hissing noise it makes but it’s me being SUPER picky. It can charge 2 phones and play music from a phone.

My wife bought this for me, from amazon, Christmas 2015. I have to say I love them. Other reviewers have said they lack bass, this might be true if you have hearing issues. The bass boost is right on. No it does not thump like car ghetto bass, nor is it suppose too. Buy some cheap Dr's if that is what your looking for. The clarity is beautiful when listening to music, TV shows and movies. Crisp, Clear, and Detailed. I can now watch movies, TV etc. without bothering my sleeping beauty (big bonus)! I opted for the RS165s because my TVs have different sound modes and they come through the headphones. Will be purchasing the Digital ones whenever our forever home is done being built to use in the living room area and keep these for the bedroom.

It's just plain spectacular how good the Kindle Voyage is.

I'm kind of a gadget junkie. Whenever a new Kindle reader comes out, I pass on the old one and buy the new. So I'm coming from a place that has used everything from the old Kindle Keyboard through to this, my newest Kindle, the Kindle Voyage 3G.

First, screen quality. I knew it had 300 v. 221 PPI I had on my PW2, but until I saw it, couldn't believe how much of a difference it made. Now, the PW2 screen is great, but this beats it soundly. For regular reading, I don't see any reason to switch from a PW2 to a Voyage, but I'd imagine that with illustrations and such, it would make a really big difference. I can actually read at one size smaller font than I could on the PW2.

The light: Nice light, no weird shadings. My device is smoothly lit from bottom to top.

Size/Weight: It's smaller, definitely (not the screen though). Couldn't really see any difference in weight between this and the PW2, but honestly, what's an ounce either way, especially once you start sticking covers on it? It's not something I particularly care about.

Storage/Memory: I wish it were a bit bigger. Not that I have any desire to have 2,000 on my Kindle at any given time, but once you get into using about half the memory, these devices always slow down and get ornery.

Wishes/Dreams for the next e-reader: That they'd include text to voice. I doubt this will happen, but I wish it would.

I'm giving these 5 stars, but honestly, I wouldn't have had I not watched MJ Leonard's video review.  At first use, they're barely a 2, but once you break them in (Leonard's instructions on how to do so were awesome and simple) and figure out how to get them to fit properly, they are outstanding.  Great natural sound, decent noise reduction and very comfortable.  I don't even feel them.

I have typically bought and loved Dell Inspiron desktop computers for use with school and business purposes and have been very satisfied over the years.

When we were told that we needed Windows 10, I tried to download it to my old Inspiron but was not successful because my Dell equipment was really too old for a successful install; I really love the Inspiron and Windows 7.

In February 2020, I bought a new desktop and had a really stressful experience. There was something wrong with the configuration, and the tech support people could not get the computer to perform properly. After many hours online with tech support, the situation started to seem hopeless. The pandemic began to become worrisome both here and in India (tech support), and I returned the desktop for a fully refund.

Last week I started again trying to find a desktop with Windows 10. I didn't want to spend a small fortune for a computer that I use primarily for shopping, email, browsing, and, rarely, online banking transactions. I found this Acer after reading good reviews. Since my current desktop is an I3 and has basically the same specs, I chose this computer rather than the I5.

One of my siblings told me that Acer has a long history of excellent quality and that I would be pleased. He was right! This desktop is great.

PROS:
Comes with Windows 10 pre-installed. Plug it in. It's ready to go.
Norton Security is pre-loaded with a 30-day trial period.
The computer is extremely user friendly. I had no struggles with glitches with any of the programs.

CONS:
There really are no cons except that the "feel" of the plastic components is not as hefty as some of the desktops that I have used in the past (other companies). The plastic casing of the tower, the keyboard, and the mouse are beautifully designed but not quite as heavy as prior desktops that I have owned. That isn't necessarily a "con," and I like the keyboard, mouse, and computer case. Very attractively designed.

MY RATING:
5 STARS
