If you are on the fence, take my advice and go for it. This is a good value, and a decent case--especially for this price. I did, and I have no regrets.

Note: you will have to remove the case to access the battery/SD card compartment and the ports, as is the norm with all cases of this type for this camera (I was unable to find one that did not require this).

---

UPDATE: After several months of hard use, this case has held up remarkably well. No evidence of wear. I get compliments on it, as well. Note: Do not attach the camera to a tripod with the bottom of the case on. The knob on the case is threaded to allow you to do this, but getting it off the tripod mount afterwards is a nightmare. Just take it out of the case--trust me.

So , a while back (<1 yr) I did a whole bunch of research for a friend who needed a new laptop. Everything I read pointed to Asus, so we went that route. Everything worked out just fine, so when it came time for me to upgrade, I followed suit. I got this box, with a slightly faster processor and a 500GB HDD for $299 on sale elsewhere two weeks ago. Happy with it thus far. The keyboard layout is a little unusual, and definitely takes some getting used to. Battery life is excellent, and even at the dimmest setting, the screen is totally fine indoors. I wish it had another USB port, and the lack of Bluetooth seems silly (I miss it though). Built-in cameras is not great, but for Skype, its just fine. Love how quiet this thing is. Yet to feel any heat from it. Happy camper.

---
UPDATE: After using this for a while now, I can safely say it is a great laptop except for one, glaring fault: the keyboard is terrible. Worst layout I have ever had on a laptop. Makes me want to replace the laptop. If only this was not a problem... *sigh*

This is ridiculous. Never before have I ever gotten so much joy from an electronic gadget (and I'm a gadget NUT). After renting from Netflix for YEARS, I finally got a Roku box for Xmakkah from my girlfriend, who shall henceforth be worshiped as a god. I LOVE it (and yes, her too!). I have only two complaints, neither of which has anything to do with the Roku box itself, but rather the service I receive from Netflix.

1) Netflix desperately needs to step up the selection of available streaming content. The vast majority of the 20K titles currently available are old, unloved, and largely undesirable. Sure there is some decent content, but nowhere near enough of it. A good example of this is TV: I can Watch Dexter, LOST, and Heroes, but not Survivor, X-Files, or The Sopranos. I can watch the Old Battlestar Galactica, but not the new one. I can watch Masters of Horror, but not The Twilight Zone. You get the idea.

2) Video quality degrades when other devices are used that eat up bandwidth. I use my broadband cable connection for everything except my microwave oven. Seriously: telephony (Vonage), Internet access, online backup, and Roku. If I am watching something on the Roku box and I answer the phone, the resolution on the screen drops dramatically and the audio quality on the call is terrible. You get the picture (pun intended)...

Oh, and I have one more issue, although this is not really an issue--more of a request: Roku needs to greatly expand the channel store!!! YES PLEASE!!

Setup was a breeze and I was watching a movie in less then 10 minutes (and 9 of those minutes were the Roku box connecting to Roku itself and registering/updating firmware). :o)

Get one of these.
Trust me.
Best thing I got for Christmas by a mile.

This is exactly what I needed to tame the mess of USB cables surrounding my PC. What I like best about it is the fact that it is WEIGHTED. This means is does not slide around all over the place on your desk like other (lightweight) hubs do. It's small (about the size of 1/2 a large Florida orange or a small grapefruit) and it offers all the features I wanted: weight, lots of ports (7) and LED port-in-use indicators for each port. the top-mounted port is nice too; great for plugging in and removing things frequently such as flash drives. This is one of the best PC gadgets I have bought in some time. Oh--and the free light that comes with it is a neato bonus. Highly recommended.

Love my new Sony Earbuds! They hooked up to my bluetooth so easy! Easy to charge! You can go into the App and change the touch sensors to your specifications. Sound quality is great and I love the noise canceling feature! The only downside for me is I must have a little ear canal because I can't find an ear cover that's small enough so they don't fall out!!

Because I teach college and often work privately with my students, I needed a way to attach 2 sets of headphones to one PC. This USB unit splits the audio into two headphones and does it well. I ordered this unit as well as the regular headphone jack splitter (also from this company) for those instances where the regular splitter doesn't work because of a particular computer's issues.

Very pleased and highly recommended !

This wireless keyboard/mouse combination is excellent. The wireless connectivity has always been highly responsive. When the keyboard or mouse goes to sleep, the first keypress or mouse gesture wakes the unit up, with nothing lost. The wake up is super fast and responsive and accurate.
I have never used the slot on the keyboard as phone holder but I do use it hold a pen.
I like the separate screen lock key because it eliminates the need for the 2 key Win + L to accomplish the same thing.
This keyboard comes with preprogrammed function keys which default to the manufacturers settings (audio volume increase/decrease/mute etc.) To use the functions keys for normal windows operations, simply hold the fn key and press any function key to accomplish this.

IMPORTANT: I have NOT had any of the problems posted in the review section!
I go through keyboards and mouses like tissues. On average, they last a few months and then deteriorate. Often times, because I have a tendency to drop the mouse a lot, they break pretty fast. The mouse included with this keyboard has held up well. As with most other mouses, when they are dropped, the batteries come flying out. To avoid this, I have placed a small piece of tape over the battery cover and case being careful not to cover the mouse's optical component. This solves the problem
I would highly recommend this product.

I have had the Topping D10s DAC for about 3 weeks. It has proven to be a high quality DAC .
This is my current configuration:
PC -> DAC via usb
DAC -> headphone amp or AV receiver via RCA cable, or to second DAC via Digital COAX or Optical Toslink

The resulting audio is far superior using this DAC, compared with plugging my PC audio out directly into either my headphone amplifier or AV amplifier.
When using a DAC, the audio is much cleaner and there seems to be better channel separation. The DAC does not enhance the audio signal at all. There is no high, mid, or low end over amplification. The audio out is the same as the audio in, and that's the way it should be.

I have used other DACs and the Topping D10s is a good as the others

I highly recommend this product.

It's "almost" (see my edit below) impossible to find a negative review of the Audio-Technica ATH-M50x Closed Back Headphones. And I have to agree. Probably the best headphones I've ever owned. They've been available now for 10 or so years. You can't get this high end quality audio anywhere else for this price point. I got an excellent deal. The headphone purchase also included 3 high quality extra items for just about the same price as the headphones alone. My package included an extra cable, a solid hard plastic carrying case, and a FiiO A1 headphone amplifier.
The headphones live up to all the positive reviews, and the extras included made for a very good total price.
I would definitely recommend this product.
Updated 2/4/2021, 4 months later.
I still love these headphones. I have to laugh when I occasionally check the customer reviews and find that most of the criticisms are based on how these headphones were purposely engineered. Let me be more specific. Some of the negative comments include:
-others around you can hear what you're listening to. Oh well. Too bad. They should probably put on their own noise cancelling headphones. Which brings me to my next point:
-they're not noise cancelling. Yup, that's right. When I did my search for headphones, I specifically did NOT want noise cancelling OR Bluetooth. Much prefer putting the money saved when not buying these options and putting it toward better cans.
-there is no microphone on the cables. Correct again. These headphones were not necessarily intended for those who want a set of cans primarily to support their cell phone addiction.
-they must be used with the company's proprietary cables to attach to the headphones. I'll take that and love it. Why? Because they twist and lock into the bottom of the can. How many times, with other headphones, have I moved too far, or stood up or whatever, and the cord would be ripped out of the cans!!
-too much bass, not enough base. Midrange too pronounced, or not enough. And they go on and on and on.
-the "best" (tongue in cheek) criticism stated that none of the included cables, nor the included adapters fit his computer. I don't know what kind of a computer this person has, but, if Bill Cosby appears in TV commercials for your computer, headphones should not be your #1 focus right now
-and finally, and I quote, "I needed to add an EQ to make them sound like I wanted them to". Precisely! These cans were designed and manufactured specifically for those who are looking for an accurate, unadulterated representation of the original recording. The way the musicians and the recording engineers intended it to sound. If one doesn't find that acceptable, and that's fine, include an EQ somewhere in the mix. As a matter of fact, I have more than my share of sound shaping hardware and software all over my system in order to tailor the music to my liking.
You need to like the sound quality reproduced through headphones and speaker systems alike. And this is very subjective. One person's likes are another person's hates, especially when it comes from those who love to sound like they "might" know what they are talking about.. I bought and returned a number of headphones because I didn't care for how they sounded. I kept these.
I do agree with one common complaint. The earpads do get uncomfortable after a while. I checked for aftermarket replacements, but many included their own negative reviews that they changed the sound quality from the originals. That's the last thing I want.

This cable is far superior to any other of its kind that I have purchased in the past.  It is well constructed, super heavy duty, well shielded against noise.  Does exactly what I need at a very low price!

Sending a VGA signal from a Windows 7 PC to a 55" LG Smart TV. I was very surprised by the excellent quality of the VGA signal displayed on the TV. It is for my older computer and for what I use it for, it works in every way. The audio is equally good.
Highly recommended.

(added 1/08/2021) My second order for this item was to connect my newer Windows 10 PC (only 1 HDMI out, 1 VGA out) to my new 55" TCL 55s535 QLED Smart TV. I want to be able to connect two displays to the computer to extend the video signal, but HDMI will not split the video. HDMI will only duplicate the same video. Next best thing is to use the VGA which will split the video output, and connect to the QLED with this cable adapter.
Until I get a get my next PC with more than one UHD video output, this will do fine.

This works excellently for my application, provides additional volume as needed, metal case is crush proof, unit is small with a big clip so it's easy to attach to clothing...highly recommended!
These headphones were perfect for school use. Durable, beautiful colors, excellent volume control, and perfect for any school aged child.

Typically I stick to higher end gaming keyboards. Mechanical and optical switches are generally my go to. I had never used a keyboard from this brand before so when I was given the chance to grab one, I figured I would see how it stacks up.

So far I'm fairly impressed. I've used some tournament edition keyboards with the smaller form factor from other brands so I knew what I was getting into when it came to the size of the keyboard. All in all, sizing is fine. They key placement and distance between keys works fine. I do run into issues at times where my fingers get lost on the right side of the keyboard. Getting used to that will come in time though. The key response is quick. They are mechanical switches but they do manage to deaden the sound a bit which is nice. The RGB features are basic at best. You have a few settings you can select from and all of it is done directly on the keyboard itself. It has your normal basic modes. It illuminates well though and you can increase/decrease the brightness. The build quality is nice. For being a 75% keyboard, it has some weight to it. I like the fact the keys are labeled for both Mac and PC. I primarily use it on my PC though. The place where it seems to shine is in the connectivity department. I can connect it by bluetooth to numerous devices or I can have it wired. I generally run wired to my main PC and if I need to use it on my MacBook or other devices, I just unplug it from the PC and connect by BT to the other device. It works out nicely.

From a gaming standpoint (which I do a lot of), I'm not certain that I like it as much yet. Emphasis on the "yet". I know it takes some time to become accustomed to a new keyboard. The response and feel. I'm going to continue gaming on it for a while to see if I become more adapted to it. It just feels different than what I'm used to. It most likely has to do with the key spacing more so than anything else.

This is definitely a nice keyboard and I recommend it. I will most likely continue to use it as my daily keyboard for a while longer to see how it holds up over time.

These earbuds are great for their price, however I don't know that they deserve so many accolades that they're receiving through reviews here or on other sites.  There is nothing spectacular about them.  Sound quality is average.  Nothing like you'd find in much higher end (and higher priced) IEMs.  Comfort can be subjective.  What is comfortable to one person may not be comfortable to the next.  I personally prefer foam inserts but with that being said, these are relatively comfortable.  If you're looking for a cheap pair of earbuds, these will fit the bill.  If you're looking for something with higher end sound quality, you may want to move on.

This product came in handy for a few reasons.  I typically use it to output audio from my phone to the line-in on a computer.  I also use it to output audio from my phone to a car stereo.  In both cases the cord works flawlessly.  The audio quality is what I would expect and I've yet to have an issue with the cord.  So far so good and if you're looking for an adapter of this style, this one will fit the bill just fine.
fantastic radio card reader bluetooth all in one loud little box
Didn’t know how great the quality would be, but even 3 years later it sounds amazing!

I bought a projector to show movies outside against the side of my house. The projector has a good picture but is lacking in the sound department. I've tried several speakers and finally found this one. It's loud enough to her speech from 40-50 ft away over top the night time insects and street noise. Even better I don't have to run a power cord for it.

With not being able to go out as much lately I wanted to find a fun way for our family to have movie nights. I had been thinking about a projector and saw this one go on sale low enough I figured I'd take a gamble. It has worked great for movie nights in our backyard. I've hooked a dvd player up to it, but most times we just plug in the chromecast and use our phones. We did have to get some unexpected extras to get the full enjoyment out of this: a 150in projector screen (the project goes up to 200), speakers (because the built-in one just isn't loud enough for outside), and a tripod.
Great little speaker. Price is good and quality is too. Sounds surprisingly good.

These really cancel out the noise quite well. I had a set of similar earbuds but one found it’s demise in the toilet (not a good day).
I tried to find the old pair since I liked them but no luck. These popped up as an item that was similar. I liked that the charging dock shows the battery power as my wife has a set from a different seller that doesn’t show this and it’s quite frustrating to gauge battery life.

The standard ear plugs that came with the device worked for me but there are a couple more size options.

The sound is great and since they snug right in your ear it’s easy to keep them in and not falling out. I don’t notice any static and have actually found they are louder than my other pair (I’ve had to adjust the volume down on my walks from my previous pair).

Great set. They are a little hard to get out of the case but that’s the same issue all of these earbuds have since there’s not a tiny handle piece to grab hold of (just a rounded top of the earbud).
Great and highly recommend!

I wanted a dual set because we have two backseat drivers that need distraction. Well, maybe they just need a better driver but in any case I needed a DVD player set. I decided on these based on the reviews and am thoroughly impressed.

There is a built in battery which has served us well given I didn’t realize that at first and while driving the DVD player stopped. I thought it was broke and then realized it had just not been plugged in properly. After reading through I was pleasantly surprised by this feature.

My kids like the ease of access and to be able to use the remote. I really like the lack of skipping that occurs while driving as a previously set we had would skip and then restart the disc. No issues in that regard here.

The audio is great though we have the kids wear headphones as usually we have a few different sounds happening (radio, wifes phone, older sons phone, and DVD player would just add to that). I did listen to it at first as I didn’t want to have the headphones given it’ll only be a few years before he wears them all the time (teen years are fun).

If there were a downside to these, it is something that happens to all DVD players in that when cold, the laser reader has to warm before it can read the disc. That happens with all players though so it’s more of a tip than anything.

Highly recommend

I want to kick this review off with a key point, as the title states, the center button on the front of the speaker is the power button. I didn’t read the directions to see if this was mentioned, I just charged it and struggled to power it on when it was charged.

Outside of that the sound quality and overall volume on this is great. When it first powered on, the automated voice had me concerned as it doesn’t sound clean, but it seems to be just how it was recorded.

I turned on a song and naturally had to crank up the volume to see what it could do. I was pleasantly surprised and it didn’t have issues with quality (sometimes speakers get louder in volume and it sounds like someone just singing closer and closer to a microphone).

This does include a short Aux cord (2 ft) and the charging cable (but no plug). The charging cable is USB C that goes into the speaker (but still plugs into a standard usb plug).

I am very pleased here!

I am really enjoying the sound quality from these as I needed to switch from a corded headset to something wireless. This is Bluetooth but the Bluetooth chip works well and doesn’t seem to have issue where it disconnects from my laptop and connects to my phone (I’ve had this with a few speakers).

The mic works great as I do user testing and the sound quality is important for good feedback as a tester.

I was pleasantly surprised to find out that the chip isn’t needed unless Bluetooth isn’t available on the device. There was no issue with connectivity either as my laptop recognizes the USB Bluetooth chip and automatically paired with the headset. A plus for me since my laptop tends to lag.

The headset has a good/decent look to it. The earpieces are squishy and comfortable. The headset adjusts easily. The plastic seems to be of decent quality so putting them on and taking off repeatedly should not be an issue. Very pleased overall.

I bought this adapter because the other one I have always caused static and I’d have to turn my stereo up quite a bit to get the volume at a decent level.
I have had far less issues with static when this is plugged in while listening to the radio (weaker channels are always going to be an issue either way).
I am also able to turn the volume up about 25% less than with the other (knob was at 22 with other adapter and this one works well on 16 or 17).
Thoroughly pleased with this one and I got it because we are slowly moving toward the USB c style charging cables (as newer items seem to also be doing the same).

We picked up this camera because we were getting a new puppy and needed to keep an eye on him during the day.

The clarity is pretty solid overall given the cost and can be seen in the photo above (which includes our little pup).

The camera can take snapshots which I am not able to save to my phone (or haven’t quite figured out how to save to my iPhone but they do save in the app).

I don’t really need this for motion detection but have tested that feature out as a just in case measure if we used in the future. The sensitivity can be adjusted but overall a very nice feature.

The camera does have a micro sd slot that would allow storage of footage (like movements) but we use the live footage as our means of checking the feed.

The connection to the device was fairly smooth but we did have to refresh our router when completing the process. It could’ve been a bandwidth issue given we have more Smart items than ever.

The app is fairly user friendly and my wife and I can both view the live feed at the same time. The feed itself is about .5 -1 second slow which we haven’t found as a problem.

The audio in/out is also quite clear which was fantastic. We try not to talk to our pup too much but it definitely was a nice feature for the first 2-3 days of him being in the crate (and being able to hear him as well as talk to him if he got frustrated).

Highly recommend this one!

This is actually my second headset of this type because I let my son use the last one and he decided to stretch it until it broke.
I really like that it has a clean sound quality as I do usertesting and that requires clear sound quality. They are also very comfortable and I enjoy they go on the ear versus in the ear which tends to irritate my ears.
The cable is also of solid quality which seems like it plays a role in producing clear audio.
Great buy!

You NEED braided if you want these types of cords to last. I bought two standard style white cords and they were flimsy and ended up melting. These have worked exceptionally well and the long cord has been really nice as 3' is just slightly too short and pulls my headphones down. 6' is the way to go.
The sound quality is as expected. The audio plug that goes into your headphones is a little large but still ended up fitting in my headphones but I had to push a little bit. No loss of sound and I am incredibly pleased!

The microphone easily attached to my camera. I did like that there was a replacement camera mount included (the red piece) as I’ve heard of people breaking those for similar looking mics. This one DID come attached to the red mount so there were no issues and I have a spare. The red piece is fairly flexible which has both pros and cons as the mic can move a little and not stress this piece, but the con being the mic can move.

As far as the mic audio, there was a good improvement when about 3 feet away and a major improvement when up closer. The audio is cleaner than the on mic camera which makes this a nice minor cost improvement.

There are different cables which allow you to attach the camera to a standard audio port or a TRRS port like on some iPhones.

The mic does not need batteries so there are no issues with needing the check the batteries before each use. This does seem to have a downside somewhat in that the mic doesn’t really have a power boost which would come from the batteries.

The mic comes with a pop filter screen as well as a wind screen filter which are nice additions for recording audio in any condition.

The mic can be sensitive with some light wind so if there is a breeze do not forget the wind screen filter.

I would definitely recommend this as a low cost alternative to the similar Rode mic.

Unfortunately this item was far better than expected. I know that sounds odd but the item was well made, with a solid cord length. The cord itself was of thick material/casing which helps add durability.

I was pleasantly surprised by this item.

“Some assembly required”. Keep reading.

The disk wasn’t formatted properly to be used right away. Luckily I work with someone who is tech savvy and could get it formatted properly. The disk also needed a name, not in the sense that I have to name my devices but since it wasn’t recognized by my computer as a registered device, I had to give it a name which was interesting.

It does work but will require some tech knowledge to get it to actually store files. I would not deem this as a ready to go item.

This mic came in a nice package that was foam packed so it had a very professional look.
The mic is solid plastic so it does seem like it would be easy to break (this review could be edited later should an incident occur).
The mic quality is much more improved over the mic on my EOS M (video difference is shown in my yt video, LiftingDad).
The +10db gain is a nice addition to the mic and really helps with improving the overall sound volume.
The shotgun aspect of the mic is decent but not the best from what I've truly seen from shotgun mic's (i.e. The sound picked up best is directly in front of the mic and dissipates from the sides to the back of the mic). It still pick up sounds fairly well from the sides and back. This is NOT ideal when shooting an interview or similar which is the common method for these mic's.
It does come at a nice price point and is a great piece for those on a budget (like myself).

This is one solid unit which is great. The arms are their own pieces, but the mount is one solid structure. I have noticed some mounts are needed to be bolted together which isn't as structurally sound.

The only thing to be cautious of is to tighten the screws that allow it to tilt. Otherwise, you'll be in for a surprise when you attach the arms to the tv and set it on the mount.

I took a chance on this fan. Thought it was a bit much for a hand held fan but it was well worth the price. The fan is well designed. It folds down into a smaller size for carrying. It opens up to hold in hand. There's even a stand that the fan can go in and be propped up. I have it facing my computer sometimes to cool it down. There are three speeds. The highest speed is strong! It operates quietly and has a rechargeable battery that runs long and quickly recharges. So far I have used it at home, work, out in the hot sun and given it to a friend that was having a hot flash!

I am amazed at how good this is. I use it mostly for music and now I get the beautiful sound "everywhere" when paired with Alexa Echo bluetooth. The surround sound is exquisite .  This is the best gift to myself ever.
Love everything about it. The sound for music is extremely clear. It makes phone calls without lifting a finger. I have a smart plug attached to my BOSE stereo system. Makes my life easier.

I purchased the 25" model of the same bag from this brand in August 2021 and it has held up admirably. No tears; the zipper is solid and the outer material is tough.

My primary use is to use the bag for some drum hardware. I have a dedicated hardware bag for stands, etc., but for individual parts like floor tom legs, shell-mounted cymbal arms, and bass drum tom mounts I prefer this bag and found that the 25" model was larger than I normally need. The only bass drum tom mount that I use that will NOT fit in this bag is the Gretsch GS1THSL single tom mount that comes with modern Catalina and Renown kits. Obviously the double mount will also not fit. However, my other mounts do and this bag is the perfect way to transport drum kit-specific hardware and leave my general hardware bag separate.

My first one has lasted nearly a year and is still going strong. I expect many more years of use from that bag and see no reason why I won't have the same experience with this one.

I subtracted a star because this battery does not last as long as an OEM one when you are not on external power. However, I am always plugged into external power when working, so I use it as a safeguard to give me time to shut down my laptop when we have a power outage. Those are sadly frequent where I live in central FL. For the price and the fact that it supports my ancient Thinkpad model I consider it a bargain. If you are looking for a replacement battery that will allow you to work untethered from external power you probably should invest in a genuine OEM battery from Lenovo. If you use it the way that I do, though, this is an ideal solution.

I am not going to cover every feature in detail since other reviews have some an excellent job of that. My points of comparison are a Galaxy Tab S6 Lite 10.4-inch Android Tablet 128GB that I purchased in June 2021, and my first large format Galaxy, the Samsung Galaxy Tab Pro SM-T9000ZWAXAR 12.2-Inch Tablet that I purchased in June 2015.

This one is a major performance improvement over the most recent (June 2021) Galaxy, and better in all respects than the much older 12.2 Galaxy I purchased in June 2015.

I was totally pleased with the Tab S6, but missed the larger screen of the Tab Pro 12.2. This screen is significantly more vivid than the 12.2 Tab Pro, and the 256gb memory in this one pretty much assures that the performance is significantly better than either the 32GB Tab Pro or the 128GB Tab S6. But that is expected.

What I truly love about this tablet over the older large format one is the body is sturdy and not prone to bending. That is why my Tab Pro ultimately failed: the body was so thin that it flexed and at some point it started acting crazy. It would have cost more to repair it than to purchase the Tab S6. Prior to purchasing this one I made sure that that issue had been resolved. Yes, it's not as light, but it more than makes up for it in sheer speed, superior display, and even sound quality.

If you want or need a large format tablet that is reasonably priced and provides excellent battery life and performance this is worth considering.

I ordered this and had to return it simply because of my own stupidity: I did not carefully read the product description. This is specifically for newer laptops and other devices that do not have VGA out, but have HDMI out. It is designed to allow you to connect your device to a legacy monitor or TV that has VGA in, It will NOT work in the other direction. For what it does and its intended market this is an inexpensive way to continue using a legacy, VGA equipped monitor or TV with newer devices that are HDMI only.

This device connects to the VGA port and from there connects to a monitor or TV HDMI port, It WILL NOT work in the other direction, and it requires a source of 5V 1A power (any standard phone charger will work.)

It comes with a USB charging cable and a 3.5mm cable for transmitting sound. Apparently it will not send sound interlaced with the HDMI signal through the HDMI cable (that you will need to supply.) For me this is not an issue because I am using it on a legacy laptop to send video only to a legacy TV, which I am using as extended video under Windows 7. Yes, it's using some ancient gear. But that is why I rated it five stars.

Limitations: even if your TV or monitor is capable of higher resolutions this is not going to provide more than 720p from an old laptop or PC to an old monitor or TV. I know the specs say that this will go higher, but I could not get it there. Yet, going straight VGA from my T400 to my Sanyo TV it went into higher resolution as an extended screen. I am OK with the limitation because I am only using the TV as a second screen with MS Office,

On an old Windows 7 system it's truly plug and play. I had it up and running without the scant instructions in mere minutes. For me it is a perfect solution.

I finally upgraded my circa 2018 Galaxy Tab A to this. The Tab A and this one represent lower tier Galaxy tablets, meaning that they were not the flagship models. This one does everything I want. That said, my needs are relatively simple: mostly web browsing, and streaming movies from Netflix and Prime. Things that I absolutely love:

- the old Tab A had 16GB and this has 128, a major increase in storage.
- screen quality is amazing. Streaming videos is noticeably better from a visual standpoint.
- in the same price range as the old Tab A, so when I upgraded I felt as though I was getting a much better tablet for about the same price as I paid for the old one in 2018.

While the battery life on this new tablet is much better, it longer than I thought it would to charge it. And, yes, I am using the included fast charger and cable. When I was transferring my data and apps from the old tablet the power consumption of WiFi, CPU and whatnot resulted in the charging rate crawling to a snail pace. It was as though it was consuming power at close to the same rate as it was being charged. In normal use, the charging is faster, but still not as fast as I guessed it would be using a fast charger. Not a real issue, but I thought I would mention it to set expectations.

As for the S-Pen, I am not currently using it. I am using an old fashion stylus in lieu of fingers to navigate (old habits die hard), and have not found a use for the S-Pen that requires its power and capabilities. It is certainly more than just a stylus, and is designed to integrate with some specific apps. I did watch a Youtube video explaining and demonstrating it, and it is impressive. But that is for a later time when I feel like experimenting and exploring.

Overall I love this tablet and am not only pleased with its features and capabilities, but am very happy with its modest price tag.

I purchased this to replace a GLS Audio 20-Feet Ethercon CAT 6 cable that would not transmit phantom power because GLS stupidly cut one end of the shield for "ground lift".  I was attempting to use that cable to connect a pair of LyxPro 4 Channel 3 Pin Multi Network XLR Cable Breakout boxes. Since I needed phantom power I went searching and came across this cable. I was dubious since the price was so low (and half the price of the GLS cable), but the reviews were good so I took a chance. This is the perfect solution and a cost-effective one at that. Nicely made too.

I stupidly broke my main tripod my accidentally placing a heavy crate on it. I wanted something sturdy and took a chance on this. It turned out to be even better than my more expensive tripod that it replaced, and the extra quick release plate is an added bonus. It allows me to quickly swap between my Canon and the also included cell phone mount for when my wife takes quick videos of my band's performances.

Initially I thought the bottom leg extensions were a bit flimsy, but while they have flex they are rock solid. The flex allows them and the movable feet to provide a stable platform on uneven ground.

The only thing that I don't care for is the center post that uses a crank to lift and retract. My gear is not that heavy, so a tension knob or ring would have worked better for me, but if you are using this for precision positioning (which I am not) you may find that feature to be to your advantage.

The bag that comes with it is more than adequate for my needs, but is pretty basic. If you venture into harsh environments you may want to order a more robust bag.

I purchased this as a drum kit hardware bag for a Tama Club Jam (small size) drum kit. It easily accommodates the center tom holder, the bass drum mounted cymbal holder, a Tama classic straight cymbal stand and a Tama HP30 bass drum pedal. I was also able to fit the floor tom legs. I could have managed the Tama classic hi-hat stand and classic snare drum stand, but that was pushing it and I was afraid that those last two components would have damaged the zipper. I am using a separate, small Tama hardware bag for those, plus a throne base and small stick bag.

The padding is superior to the Tama hardware bag, and the overall construction, including zipper is as good if not better. This bag actually holds more than the Tama one that was designed for drum hardware, and is about half the cost.

I also own a nice camera tripod that this case would easily protect and I will probably order another case for that. However, this case is a lot larger than the tripod, and I so rarely transport it, that the value proposition is nowhere as good as for my current use as a drum hardware bag. I am totally pleased with this bag!

Not too many years ago purchasing charging cables was hit-or-miss. No name brands like this one were usually shoddy and would not work will some phone brands. That has changed, so these days I shop strictly for price and have never been disappointed. I purchased these based solely on price and long length and am not disappointed. As an aside, I purchased this pack to power a device that required 5v via a micro USB cable. These cables do the job and are sturdy. For me it was a safe purchase.

The company for which I work sent me this to upgrade my Levono T400. I was running out of space on the mechanical, 250GB SATA internal drive. Not to mention that the drive was starting to make alarming noises.

When this drive arrived I used a SATA to USB cable to connect it to one of my T400 USB ports, downloaded the free app that was recommended in instructions that came with the SSD drive, and cloned my mechanical internal drive to the new one. That process took about four hours since the old drive was getting very full.

While that was going on I went on Youtube and found a video that showed how to remove the original internal drive from the laptop. I was expecting a nightmare, but lucked out because the Lenovo T400's internal drive takes less than five minutes to swap out. Obviously your experience is going to be different depending on the computer that you are swapping the internal drive. If you are using this as an external, then you don't need the app, nor do you need to swap out anything. Just get a SATA to USB cable, connect it, format the new drive and you are done.

Some reviews complained about this drive being slow compared to other SSD drives. I cannot comment on that. I will say that compared to a mechanical drive this one is blazing fast. And since there are no moving parts, very quiet.

A few final notes: raw capacity of my drive was a little over 953GB, but formatted capacity is 887GB. Also, my install was on a computer running Windows 7 Professional and there were no issues.

I needed to extend a 15 foot HDMI cable from an HDMI switch box to an HDMI port on a smart TV. The switch box is carrying video from a camera, as well as a signal from a ChromeCast.

While the above application is relatively simple and just about any HDMI cable will handle my requirements, this cable's cost point and the fact that each end mated perfectly with the target connectors made it an ideal solution for my needs.

It has worked flawlessly since I received it and I expect a long service life.

I purchased this to mount an independent light source (a RALENO Led Video Light) but also tested it with my Canon T7i camera. The Led video light is light and is no real test. The camera is heavier, yet this small ball head held it steady at any angle with no need to overtighten.

The threads (male and female) mated perfectly with my tripods, camera and other adapters.

In my opinion this is a precision-machined ball head that is heavy-duty and reliable. I have yet to find any flaws or other issues with it after a month of frequent use.

No issues whatsoever with this battery in my Canon 800D (T7i.) There are a few things that I don't like. First, the battery life per charge is about 75% of my genuine Canon batteries. for someone on a budget these are an alternative to Canon batteries if you are willing to compromise.

Another issue is the charger is flimsy and not as travel-worthy as I would like. But you can use it in a vehicle or powered by an external battery pack. Just make sure that you have adequate protection for the charger if you are planning to use it in the field. Also, note that only one battery can be charged at a time.

Overall, I knew the main limitations when I purchased this set, so am pleased (especially by the fact that my camera accepts them!) If you are a casual photographer who wants some spares without spending a fortune these are a good deal. If you want the same performance as original Canon batteries, you will be better off getting those.

I purchased both a 15 and a 25 foot cable to run from a splitter box to two monitors. The video and audio were perfect, especially since the splitter input was fed by a 10 HDMI cable (a different brand), making the total length for the longest run approximately 35 feet.

Be aware that these cables are stiff and not easy to work with right out of the box. Since my use was to have them permanently attached to the splitter and monitors there were no issues. On the other hand, if you are planning to run one of these from an adapter connected to a DSLR, I would recommend checking out lighter duty cables.

Overall, I am more than pleased with both the construction and the price. For my specific use they work perfectly and are a solid value.

I ordered a three pack because I wanted one for my music room, living room and one for my girlfriend. Set up was super simple for the basics - connecting to a bluetooth speaker, your calendar (I use google's calendar), and a music source. For the latter I use Pandora and that, too, was simple.

The subtracted star is because while I own a few thousand dollars worth of MP3 albums that I purchased from Amazon, I cannot access them. Apparently you can only stream music from Amazon's cloud if you have Prime, and even then I am not sure that you can access any of your own music that resides in their cloud. To me that is a fail, and an indication that the business and requirements analysts who assisted in the development of this device do not fully understand customer requirements at a very basic level. Another nit is the iHeart Radio music source that is plain confusing to use.

Some other areas where this would be a LOT more useful is to have the ability to set up more than one route for traffic (currently I can only identify a single route, home-to-work or back, whereas I am frequently traveling from one place to the other and traffic conditions for those trips would be very helpful. The same for the calendar: you can get all events for a single day, but not for a week, or weekend so you still have to fire up a calendar app on your phone, tablet or computer if you want to get a sense of how busy you will be over a period longer than a day.

Still, for fifty bucks each - plus the discount for purchasing a three pack - this is a decent device that has proven to be surprisingly useful in my home. My girlfriend instantly took to hers too. In the week or so that I have been using it I find that I am growing increasingly dependent on mine for streaming music from Pandora, looking up quick information while I am reading or watching a documentary, and letting me know what is on my calendar for a specific day.

I have one of mine connected via bluetooth to a [[ASIN:B019PGACR0 LD Systems MAUI 5 Channel PA System]], and my girlfriend has hers connected to a [[ASIN:B00W8O6MJO Creative Sound Blaster Roar 2 Portable NFC Bluetooth Speaker]], both of which greatly out perform the larger Echo. However I also use my other Dot with just its integrated speaker and it is more than adequate, even for streaming music since I have it on an end table.

Overall, for the current fifty bucks this is a bargain (warts notwithstanding), and while I purchased mine more out of curiosity all three have proven to be useful and practical.

I received these as a free review sample. I also own various other high-end cable brands and this is the equal of most of them (I do have a few that are world class, but they are also a lot more expensive.) In that respect I consider these to be a great value.

My main use is to connect this cable to dual RCA tape out on my mixing board using an adapter. I then run the angled end into an AUX in on a small speaker array that I sometimes use as a monitor. Note that I have not used this for studio applications, so cannot comment on how noise-free this cable truly in. For live performances, though, it's solid and as noise-free as I need.

While testing this out I discovered that either end will fit the AUX jack on my Note 4 phone, even while it's encased in an [[ASIN:B00NF4SXSO OtterBox Samsung Galaxy Note 4 Case Defender Series]] if you own and use a Defender series case you already know that many cables will not work with it.

Overall, the construction is first rate, and for live applications (or plugging phones into a device protected by a Defender series case), this cable is a bargain and is super reliable.

I received this as a free review sample. The reason why I docked it a star is the active tablet window needs improvement (and that could have been one of the stand-out features if properly designed.) Here is the problem: it's the perfect size for an iPad Air 2, but could not accommodate my Tab 2 10.1 inch tablet. It did hold my Samsung Tab Pro 8.4 (even in an Otterbox Defender case). The vinyl window wrinkles and also reduces sensitivity when you interact with your tablet.

If the active tablet window is unimportant to you, then the rest of this backpack is a winner. Pairing my phone to the bluetooth speakers was as simple as flipping a switch and scanning for it on my phone's settings. And the speakers are loud with better than expected sound quality. I was pleased with that - some thought went into the speakers.

The padding is more than ample for protecting electronics, and there are sufficient pockets for the geekiest geek. What I like, though, is the storage areas are not overly complex. I own a Booq bag that is a storage dream come true, but almost requires a photographic memory to remember were all of the pockets are. This one is designed much simpler, but still efficient and effective.

Construction (except for the active tablet window) is first rate. The tablet window is marred by a difficult zipper, whereas all of the other zippers on this bag are sturdier and smooth. The outer fabric seems tough (I have not had it long enough to make any claims beyond that), and all of the seams are reinforced, straight and tight.

It's very comfortable and can be adjusted to evenly distribute the weight of a fully loaded pack. Considering that the bag itself is somewhat heavy this is a major plus for me.

I do want to note one thing about the backup battery: it is rated at (and stores) the full 4000mAh. However, like all batteries using this one's technology it's only 70% efficient, so expect about 2800mAh of usable capacity. That is not a flaw in this bag, but a reality that I wanted to point out so your expectations are properly set.

Overall, this is a well made bag with some innovative features (battery back-up and bluetooth speakers). If the active tablet window is not an important feature it's definitely worth considering. This one will be replacing my Booq because the storage is there without the complexity.

I received this as a free review sample. I actually had a need for one of these because I wanted to run an audio signal out of my Yamaha receiver to an older analog reel-to-reel recorder. The receiver had a toslink out, and the recorder had RCA in. This box was the perfect DAC.

My signals were noise free, but understand that I was not running the analog cable more than a meter. So in that respect I did not have an adequate test of noise characteristics for longer cable runs. Moreover, I did not really use the volume feature. I set it mid way and used controls on the recorder for volume level. However, for my needs this worked perfectly.

The instructions are a little weak, but anyone who knows what a DAC is should be able to connect and use this without them. The power supply is a standard 5V DC at 1 Amp with a center positive connector. I ran it for an extended length of time and it did not overheat (I have learned from experience to test power supplies because of occasional failures and issues.)

Overall, this is a reasonably priced DAC that I found to be easy to use. The performance was what I had hoped, so am pleased with it.

I received this as a free review sample. I subtracted a star because in small quarters the fan can get irritating, and also the picture area is a little skewed. The latter is not enough to ruin a video, but combined with the fan noise I felt that this falls into the four star category. To be fair, this is about on par with other portable projectors in this price range and sharing the general form factor.

On the plus side, this is an inexpensive way to get a large screen TV (assuming that your wall is the screen), that does a credible job of projecting movies, TV and presentations. I tested it using a Chromecast and streaming video from YouTube to my phone, then casting from my phone to the Chromecast dongle connected to one of the HDMI ports in the rear. No issues and it was actually a treat. I also tested it with an old Roku in an HDMI port streaming a movie from Netflix. To be sure, neither experience compares to my HD TV screen and surround sound system, but this does not come close to the price tags of those. Bang for the buck this is excellent if you are in a budget.

Frankly, I did not test the other ports, but do want to point out that the 'SD' card port is really USB A that will take a flash drive or an SD card using an adapter. Actually, I think that is a plus as well because flash drives are cheap and a 32GB one can hold a respectable amount of movies, home videos or presentations.

Sound quality is not spectacular, but is definitely adequate. Overall, this is as good as any projector among the four that I have either owned or tested, and is better than some. It would easily be a five star projector if it had a quieter fan. If you can live with that you will probably love it.

I received these as a free review sample. They are one of three different models of Spider phone that I have tested, and these are the loudest and deepest from a low frequency perspective (to my ears) among the three.

Like another reviewer, I noticed that the right and left channels are inverted, but that is not a problem for me. The sound quality is very good across the high, medium and low frequency bands. These are compressed at the high end, with a definite bias in the mid and low frequency ranges. The mids are very realistic, while the low end is a bit on the processed side if you are listening to acoustic jazz, or similar styles of music. For modern music they are perfect. Factor that into your purchase decision.

I do need to mention that these can get a little on the loud side, especially if you are listening from a device that automatically attenuates SPL levels on phones and you opt to override that setting. For example, my Note 4 phone will attenuate direct AUX connections, but I can override that and listen full volume. These phones can actually damage hearing if you do that and listen at max for prolonged periods of time. For me the attenuated setting is still plenty loud.

Overall sound quality and level is perfect for modern music, especially genres that are bass and drum centric. For acoustic music (jazz, Americana, older country and the such), these are a little too processed. For those styles I recommend that you consider the [[ASIN:B01BY0262O Spider USA SPEB112-BK Jade Series Metal Earbuds]].

I received these as a free review sample. Note: these are NOT bluetooth. They are wired ear buds that should fit any device with a 3.5mm output jack.

My rating is based on both sound quality and price. The list on these are in the twenty buck range, but the sound quality, in a blindfold test, would fool you into thinking that these are a tier above other buds in this price range.

The mid range and lower end of the frequency spectrum seem to be emphasized, with highs a bit compressed. These are perfect for casual (and even some critical) listening. An audiophile would probably not like the bias and compression, but most other folks will appreciate it. I mentioned the 'lower' end of the frequency spectrum. At the lowest end it is deep, but not thumping (although it will reproduce 20Hz, which you can feel if not hear.) For anyone listening to acoustic or lightly amplified music, and especially music that uses a big chunk of the audio frequency spectrum (for consumer phones), these are surprisingly good.

There is a disparity between the product description's claim that there have flat, tangle-free cable and the actual cable, which is tangle-free, but round. I want to point that out because one of the things I check when reviewing is any differences between product specs and claims, and what you actually receive.

Basically, these are priced at the upper end of entry level phones, but are good enough to pass for high end intermediate level phones.

I purchased one of these from a different source to power a 12V portable fridge that was designed to operate from a lighter socket. This converter puts out a full five Amps, which is 60 Watts (5 Amps x 12 volts.)

In addition, this will easily charge tablets and phones if you use a multi-port USB vehicle charger with it. In fact, any 12V DC device like an air pump, etc., that is designed to operate from a vehicle lighter socket is fair game as long as it does not require more than 5 Amps or is rated at 60 Watts or less (and to be on the safe side I would probably lower that to 50 Watts.)

This runs fairly cool as long as you are not operating it at the edge of its capacity or for sustained periods, and mine has never gotten so hot that it alarmed me.

If you are a musician who deals with pedals and pedal boards, or has other gear that uses DC power within the range of this power supply, this can be a life saver. Since I own pedal boards that use both 9V DC (Boss and a few other guitar effects pedals), and 12V DC (TC Helicon), this is a spare that sits in my gig bag in case I misplace or damage one of the wall warts that powers those pedals.

Also, because this can put out up to 1.2 Amps, it can power three of my TC Helicon pedals off of a power cable chain. I usually employ a TC Helicon power supply for that, but since I use this one as a spare, it is always ready if needed. I have tested it with the pedals and verified that it will power all of the ones I use simultaneously.

If you do get this and find that the adapters that come with it are not the sizes you need, you may want to consider this add on set by another brand: [[ASIN:B00CMMO6AE Generic Universal 28 DC Power 5.5x2.1mm Jack to 28 Plug Power Adapter for Notebook]]. For my needs, though, this is all I require and I am very pleased with it.

I purchased this cable based on my very positive experience with some other cables that I ordered from this brand ([[ASIN:B003L18XKE Monoprice 104749 1.5-Feet Premier Series XLR Male to XLR Female 16AWG Cable]].)

Like the XLR cables, this one is slightly different in size that what is described. Overall length is 18.5 inches and the cable that is approximately 17 7/8 inches when measured from the housing of the connectors. For me that is not a real issue, but what may be an issue of you are planning to use these with pedals mounted on a pedal board, the length from the strain reliefs to the top of the connector housings is 2 inches. Also, the TRS end's tip to the top of the housing is 2.25 inches, with 5/8" of the housing protruding when the TRS end is fully inserted. Those numbers should help you to determine if this will work in your particular pedal board.

The cable is noise free in my application, which is interconnecting a [[ASIN:B00HMQ1G9O TC Helicon VoiceTone Correct XT Vocal Effects Processor]] to a [[ASIN:B00HMQ1SHO TC Helicon VoiceTone H1 Vocal Effects Processor]]. I did notice that the housing ends are split, two piece design that are held together by the strain reliefs. Also, at the end of the strain relief, the bend radius of the 16AWG cable is very tight, which was a pleasant surprise.

Bottom line: the only potential issue I see with this cable the it may not work well on a pedal board with tightly spaced pedals. In all other respects it has proven to be mechanically and electrically sound, and I intend to order more.

I received this as a free review sample. M.Erb's extremely detailed and helpful video review of May 14, 2016 covers this in a great deal of depth. I'll add my thoughts and reasons why I also rated this five solid stars.

First, I have tested and used at least a dozen dashcams, many of which were excellent in their own right. However, the shortfall in each was the screen and a complicated array of controls. With this one your screen is your smartphone or tablet, and your controls are those that are provided with the app you need to download (for free) to control the camera and settings. There is a separate remote control, which is really just a clicker that does one thing: triggers a short video and a snapshot.

Another thing I personally love is the mounting kit. This one, properly used, will run your power cable in an unobtrisive manner (well, as unobtrusive as possible), and the cable is sufficiently long to run the cable from close to my rear view mirror to my dashboard lighter socket in my 2016 Outlander. Other dashcams either forced you to put up with dangling cable or - in one case - have the power and video feed cables professionally installed. Plus this uses a standard USB cable with USB A on one end and micro USB on the other. Some dashcams require a proprietary cable with a barrel connector that makes it difficult to replace if necessary.

Video quality is not award winning (indeed, the camera lens is a fisheye), but is still more than sufficient to capture accidents and even scenic drives. You can also use this for other than a dashcam. I discovered that will fit in a standard microphone clip that fits a Shure SM58 (i.e., a very common size.)

You can use up to a 64GB micro SD card, which will store almost eleven hours of video. Most dashcams are limited to 32GB. The instruction manual is adequate, but not comprehensive, and it also does not cover the software and its capabilities. I hope the company rectifies that, which will make this dashcam even more user friendly, especially for novices. However, most folks do not want to wade through a manual anyway, and the one that comes with this will get you going.

Bottom line: as far as dashcams go, this one is probably the easiest one to use that I have come across. My FAVORITE feature is simplicity that allows my phone or tablet to be the screen and controls.

I received this as a free review sample. The reason why I subtracted a star is the cables (both the one from the charger to the control module, and the 3.5mm connection) are hardwired. This means that if either cable becomes damaged it can cost more to repair than to replace, unless you have the skills to repair them. Had the charger been configured with a micro USB port and the control module with a 3.5mm port for separate cables that can be easily purchased just about anywhere (including pharmacies and supermarkets these days), a damaged cable would be an easy swap and the value and utility of this solution been a lot more.

Operationally, this kit functions as promised. The mic will pass through commands if your phone has voice recognition, and the overall quality of sound is more a function of your vehicle's stereo system than this unit. Since my vehicle is already bluetooth-enabled I used a small, powered speaker with a 3.5mm input to test this. Since the cable, as mentioned, is fixed I had to still perform the test in my vehicle. The sound quality was overall good, and making and receiving test calls were easy and the connections clear enough to be heard without 'can you hear me now?'

Surprisingly the extra USB port in the charger was relatively fast, and proved to be as good as any high-speed (but non QC) charger on both my Note 4 and a friend's iPhone 5S. In fact, that is why I only subtracted one star because while the cable issue does detract, the charging capability of the extra port is better than I expected.

Bottom line: this is an OK hand's free solution for older vehicles that have an AUX port, but no bluetooth (and you NEED an AUX port to make this work.) Since the control module is hardwired into a lighter-style charger you cannot use this with a home stereo that does not have bluetooth, but does have 3.5mm input. There are similar solutions that use basically the same design, but replaceable cables that do allow this, so this one is restricted to vehicle-only use. If that is all you need, this one does perform as claimed.

I received one of these as a free review sample. Up front, the reason I subtracted a star is the set-up using the libratone app is maddening (to say the least.) On the other hand the sound quality is simply the best I have come across for a wireless speaker. That means I have to eat some recent words along the lines of there is no bluetooth speaker that is truly audiophile quality. This speaker disproves that.

Out of the box this quickly pairs and connects to bluetooth devices. I tested mine with a Note 4 phone and it took literally seconds to have it up and running. I was so blown away by the fact that this speaker reproduces music in a neutral manner by default that I was ready to sit down and give it a glowing review. Then I downloaded and installed the app.

The app is the Achilles heel. It had trouble finding the speaker, and the scant instructions were not very helpful either. Some how, some way it finally found the speaker, then was totally confusing when it came to setting up my personal profile (speaker location, bias and other features.) It also presented me with radio stations that were accessible via WiFi, and after connecting to my router I was able to access those. However, I am not personally interested in those offerings so did not explore them too deeply.

Basically, the app is good for linking multiple speakers, and some basic controls. Since I still cannot get the profiles set correctly I cannot speak about those. I will say that out of the box, without the libratone app and just connecting from my phone via bluetooth this speaker is spectacular. That is why I gave it the four stars that I did.

Bottom line: if you are looking for [possibly] the best bluetooth speaker on the market (and, yes, that includes Bose), this is it. If you want a speaker that can do everything this one is supposed to do, including fine tuning it for your room and musical tastes, you may be disappointed or frustrated. With a more intuitive app and more detailed instructions this would easily be a solid five star product that would keep Bose engineers and marketing up late at night. Until that happens, though, it's merely a superior bluetooth speaker that has crossed over into audiophile country.

I received this as a free review sample. Since there are ample specs and two very detailed reviews before this one I am going to stick to some observations and why I rated it so highly. First, though, if you are looking for a portable projector for a road warrior who needs to travel light this is NOT it. It's light enough, but bulky. As a home or office projector, though, this one has a lot going for it.

The main reason why I rated this so highly is it works in rooms with some ambient light. I tested it in normal lighting conditions in my living room with typical morning light with open drapes and sunlight behind partially closed blinds. I could read a newspaper in that light, so was surprised and pleased that the picture quality of a video I was displaying through it was adequate. What I mean is I could see all of the details in the video, but, of course it would have been sharper and more vivid in lower light or even a dark room. I also own a high end business projector that would not display any discernible picture in the same lighting conditions.

What I did not care for is the fact that I needed to included remote controller to access all of the features. Since this is a home and office projector I can live with that. On the other hand, unlike another reviewer's experience that this did not default back to the last input setting, mine did. Consistently.

Another reason why I rated this so highly is the array of inputs - you have two HDMI ports, two USB, a VGA and AV connectors (the latter employ RCA jacks). I tested this from an old Lenovo T61 laptop via its VGA connector as well as using a Samsung Tab Pro 8.4 using an [[ASIN:B00K76A732 Addao® 5 in 1 Multifunction MHL Micro USB MHL To HDMI HDTV Adapter Connection Kit]].

Bottom line: this is an inexpensive way to get a wide screen TV for streaming movies from the web. It's also perfect as a fixed projected in corporate settings. It comes with all of the cables you need, a terse - but useful - user guide and a lens cover.

I received this cable with a keyboard bundle similar to [[ASIN:B014G8W338 Casio Privia PX-360 Digital Piano - Black TMS CABLE Bundle]]. While I have not used it with the keyboard, I have used it for other connections. It has proven to be reliable and noise-free in a number of roles and environments.

The outer sheath is actually pretty beefy, but does not hamper the flexibility of the cable. The strain reliefs did give me pause because I was initially unsure if they would allow for a decent bend radius, but after literally dozens of times of using this cable as a patch or primary connection cable between amplifiers and bluetooth receivers, and other connections it has not failed. It has proven to be so reliable that it's now in my gig bag and I am planning to purchase a few spares for my home studio and other uses.

Bottom line: I go through a lot of cables. Some because they are cheaply made and fail (unlike this one), and others because I either misplace them or need more than one. For minijack cables I have settled on this brand and model for patch and short connection cables.

I received this as a free review sample. Note that this only accepts HDMI as an input and converts that signal composite RCA out. It cannot go in the opposite direction (connecting composite RCA devices to HDMI).

For me this is a great way to add an additional HDMI port to a monitor I own that has a single HDMI and a single set of AV composite ports. I can also use this on an older TV that has HDMI and a dual set of AV composite ports. I did test this using a Blu-Ray player on the HDMI and to the TV and it worked beautifully as long as you do not set your video resolution to be higher than 1080p for Blu-Ray, but will support ancient 640x480 all the way up to 1920x1080.It also supports 480i or 480p up to the 1080p I mentioned above. Of course, if you are using this to add HDMI to older display devices you are probably going to be limited in resolution anyway.

Then converter itself is small, hassle-free and does not require any external power. For expanding to an additional HDMI port on a TV or monitor with a spare set of AV composite ports, or connecting HDMI devices to legacy equipment that only has AV composite input this is an inexpensive solution.

I purchased these based on the shorter [[ASIN:B00FC4Z842 Hosa HSS-010X2 Pro Dual Cable]] set that came bundled with a keyboard that I purchased.

The construction is excellent in all respects. As a point of comparison to Monster, I also own a set of [[ASIN:B001UAM2ZU Monster StudioLink Interconnects - 2 Meters - 1/4-Inch to 1/4-Inch]], which are much more expensive inch for inch, and these are their equal in both construction and noise-free performance. I've used these to connect the L and R outputs to a mixer, and I also have used them as L and R out to a pair of small powered speakers from my Soundcraft Ui12 Digital Mixer with Wi-Fi Router and they worked equally well in that role.

They are siamesed together, but ou can easily separate them if you need two separate cables to run to separate speakers (if you use them in that way.) Or you can leave them as are to keep your cable runs cleaner. If you do decide to keep them as are I highly recommend that you tape the places where the pairs split because they are very easy to peel back and separate.

Basically, if you want a high quality set of interconnect cables for stereo that take 1/4 inch connections these are well worth considering.

These came bundled with a keyboard I purchased from a different source ([[ASIN:B0130VVOOG Casio PX360BK Key Digital Piano]]. I have not only used this cable pair to connect the L and R outputs to a mixer, but I also have used them as L and R out to a pair of small powered speakers from my [[ASIN:B00UBJ6ZM2 Soundcraft Ui12 Digital Mixer with Wi-Fi Router]] and they worked well in that role too.

The construction is excellent in all respects. They are siamesed together, but ou can easily separate them if you need two separate cables to run to separate speakers (if you use them in that way.) Or you can leave them as are to keep your cable runs cleaner. If you do decide to keep them as are I highly recommend that you tape the places where the pairs split because they are very easy to peel back and separate.

A final factor is price and quality. I also own a set of [[ASIN:B001UAM2ZU Monster StudioLink Interconnects - 2 Meters - 1/4-Inch to 1/4-Inch]], which are much more expensive (and shorter), and these are their equal in both construction and noise-free performance.

I received this as a free review sample. It it intended to be used with the [[ASIN:B018JVE7PU 001 | bitplay SNAP! PRO iPhone Case for iPhone 6/6S]], and like that kit, this is a professional quality lens. However, this will work with any camera or adapter that has 13mm threads.

Before you purchase you need to know that this lens has a polarizer than can be rotated to reduce reflections and/or enhance color. The caveat it this lens will NOT work properly if you have your camera's flash active.

The lens itself is high grade optical glass with no distortions that I could detect. If you are accustomed to pro quality optical gear you will appreciate this lens. On the other hand, if you are a point-and-shoot type who is content with clip on lenses or the basic video capabilities of your iPhone this is probably overkill. I am not trying to discourage anyone from purchasing this, but I do want to point out that this is a lens for pros or serious hobbyists, and, moreover, will require either the aforementioned kit or an adapter for the 13mm threads for either an iPhone or a camera that has that lens mounting size.

Bottom line: this is constructed with the same quality as lenses used with my vintage Nikon SLR (although different form factor) and intended for high-end users. I did some test shots and it has zero distortion and can be adjusted to control some reflections and color saturation. If you are serious about photography this one merits serious consideration.

I purchased this to compare to another case that I own - the [[ASIN:B00V6I7NBE TOUGH Cardioid Condenser Microphone Hard Case with Dense Foam for Audio-Technica AT2020 / AT2020USB / ATR2500-USB / AT2035 Studio and USB Microphones]]. I am using that case to house a [[ASIN:B00DYD77WY Samson Concert 88 Handheld 16-Channel True Diversity UHF Wireless System]], and it was a tight fit. This one will hold my second Concert 88 system, and it does so with a lot more room and flexibility.

This case is significantly better than the Tough case. For one thing the diced foam is easy to remove. I had to use a box cutter on the foam in the other case because it was not completely cut through. For another, the three bottom layers of foam (described in the product description) make it more convenient to work with, as well as the extra depth and overall inside dimensions of this case. Bear in mind that this and the case to which I am comparing it are the same price.

I do wish there were more dividers included, and also that the long dividers would go across the entire width. However, for my purposes what came with this case is more than sufficient.

One final point of comparison - I believe that in the long run the Tough box will outlast this one because of design and materials. That one is all plastic, while this one is a combination of materials that over time are going to break if roughly handled. That said, I prefer this case and will probably order a few more for some other microphones that I own.

I received this as a free review sample. I am not using it for drones, but to house a [[ASIN:B00378GEAM BEHRINGER EUROLIVE B205D]] along with some mics, DI boxes, a tablet and miscellaneous cables.

From a protection perspective I truly trust this backpack. It's well padded and the convex form factor combine to provide excellent protection for the electronics I carry. I do want to point out that if you use it as a carrying case instead of as a backpack the tablet compartment is not as protected. On the other hand, using it as a backpack will protect any tablet, even ones without their own covers and cases. Plus that particular compartment is more than large enough to accommodate my [[ASIN:B00HWMPTI2 Samsung Galaxy Tab Pro 12.2]].

The complexity comes in with the myriad of clasps, pockets and system of dividers. It actually takes a good hour to become thoroughly familiar with the pockets and other features. The dividers are versatile enough to be reconfigured to accommodate smaller (or larger) items. I am not using all of the dividers since I am storing a fairly large speaker, but the dividers from the set that I am using allow me to separate and organize the peripherals and cables that I mentioned above. One nice thing about the dividers is that they, too, are heavily padded and well constructed.

Overall construction is excellent. The zippers are smooth and come with convenient pull tabs. The material is water resistant and will take a lot of abuse. Also, the straps are nicely padded and are not going to fray or wear out even if you are rough with this backpack.

Bottom line: this is perfect protection for more than drones. For the equipment I am using it for this is a little on the expensive side. However, since I am using the gear in live performances I feel that the assurance that the equipment will be operational when I need it to be. That makes the value proposition more sane for the way I am using it.

I purchased mine on an impulse, not totally convinced that it was any better than the fabric type pop filters I use. How wrong I was. For evidence of that see Thomas G. Umstattd Jr.'s very helpful November 18, 2013 video review for a compelling demonstration of this pop guard.

Currently I am using this on both a MXL 550 and a MXL V67G mic (I am swapping the guard back and forth until I can purchase another one.) What I love is this fits directly over the two mics I cited. More importantly, there is no clumsy gooseneck and clamp, and even more importantly I can clean this one without destroying it.

As shown in the video I cited, this is as effective as the fabric pop guards. I will say that they will NOT make a good windscreen outdoors (I tested that and they pick up a lot of noise.) For indoors, though, they completely control pops and plosives.

One final reason why I love this: my fabric pop filters are prone to moving from their position if I accidentally bump into a mic stand. It seems that I am forever fine adjusting them, whereas this fits right over the mic and does not budge.

I received this as a free review sample. Volume is surprisingly loud for such a tiny speaker. I was able to clearly hear music I was streaming from nearly seven meters away. Most small, personal speakers are good for up to three meters, so it's ahead of most speakers in its class regarding sound volume.

Sound quality is equally impressive. I happened to have [[ASIN:B00ZJ5QXDO The Complete Concert By The Sea]] queued up on my phone when I went to test the speaker and the quality was superb. Every note in the high, medium and low frequency bands was crystal clean, even with the volume cranked to max. I tested a few other tracks from other albums to listen to the sound across all frequency bands with no problems.

The claimed play time is up to twelve hours. I got eight with the volume turned to maximum, and ten with it half way. If you keep the volume level at a quarter it will provide the full twelve hours. That is not an issue if you are listening to this close in like on a night stand or desk. At a quarter it's plenty loud. It does have an auto shut-off feature that turns it off if you are not playing music through it for fifteen minutes.

One final note: this comes up in bluetooth mode as soon as it's powered on. That means that even a novice can pair and connect to it by following the simple instruction sheet.

I received this as a free review sample seven months ago and have finally used it to solve a very real problem. Specifically, connecting my Blu-Ray player to a [[ASIN:B00RPJOQQ8 ViewSonic VA2465smh 24-Inch SuperClear MVA LED Monitor]] and still getting decent sound. The monitor has a gorgeous display, but the speakers integrated into it are, well, lame.

Using this I was able to send the video from the Blu-Ray player to the monitor, but split out the audio and send it to a [[ASIN:B00K6QKWWY Turcom TS-404 2.1 Channel Stereo HDTV Home Theater Surround Sound Soundbar]]. I used the RCA out on this box to the RCA in on the sound bar, and now have the best of both worlds.

There are other ways that I could have accomplished this. The value of this particular box is that it made it much easier and with a minimum of wires. It's also fairly straightforward to use.

I received this as a free review sample eleven months ago and am only now getting around to using it. When you need one of these, you NEED one. I wanted to connect my [[ASIN:B00M933WUQ Keedox MXIII Amlogic Android 4.4.2 M82 S802 Quad Core Smart 4K TV Box]] to a monitor I have.

The monitor's HDMI ports were fully populated, but the VGA port was open. The MXIII did not have a VGA out, but did have HDMI. This adapter did the trick - it was truly plug and play.

A great feature (in my opinion) is the ability to split video and audio. I ran the 3.5mm audio jack to a better speaker than the one integrated into my monitor. I did use a third party cable that I deemed better than the three foot one that ships with this dongle.

Bottom line: this is a great product. Not everyone will need it, but if you have the same situation as the one I described this is an effective solution.
