I purchased this to mount a [[ASIN:B00RPJOQQ8 ViewSonic VA2465smh 24-Inch SuperClear MVA LED Monitor]] to a speaker stand (a very light weight [[ASIN:B006H0DY3C Adam Hall SPS023S Speaker Stand]].

Frankly this mount is far sturdier than the stand on which I mounted it, and is so well constructed and heavy that it's overkill for the monitor. My monitor weighs less than eleven pounds and I am pretty sure this mount could easily support a monitor twice that weight.

Note that you can rotate your monitor 360 degrees, going from landscape to portrait, and every angle in between. However, you cannot tilt the viewing angle. I am not sure why not since the gimbal upon which the VESA mounting plate looks as though it should allow it, but it doesn't,

The clamp that mounts to the pole has a thick, anti-marring insert that will protect poles. It's also one of the reasons why this mount is so heavy - the construction is very heavy duty. All of the tools you need are provided to mount this to a pole and adjust it. The four bolts that come with it are a bit on the short side, although they worked with my monitor (and you need to provide a screwdriver for those.)

I am thoroughly pleased with this mount, especially since I almost purchased an [[ASIN:B001TMCVDW Audio2000'S AST420Y Portable Flat Panel TV/Monitor Stand with Foldable Tripod Legs]], but took a chance on this at the last minute. That decision saved me a lot of money and accomplished exactly what I wanted.

I received these as a free review sample eight months ago. Since there are a lot of detailed reviews I will focus on my experience with these and also compare them to other sports phones.

First, these are good quality for twenty buck phones. But do be aware that sports phones are designed for comfort more than sound quality. Not that these are marginal - they have a typical bias towards the mid range, with compressed highs and adequate bass. They are not going to win acclaim from audiophiles, but do reproduce music that is clear and perfect for background listening.

Another thing I like is comfort. I can wear these for a few hours at a time without even noticing them. For sports phones that is a major plus. These allow in a little ambient noise for safety, but it does not appreciably affect the quality of music. Volume is somewhat limited. If you like music super loud these are not going to make you happy. On the other hand, high volume defeats the purpose of sports phones since you need to be aware of ambient noise and your surroundings. I cannot emphasize strongly enough that these are NOT general purpose phones.

Finally, the specs claim about four hours of music play time. That is true with the volume at about a third. If you crank the volume to max you can cut that time in half.

I received these as a free review sample. I want to point out that these are hard-wired only. They use a 3.5mm connector and ARE NOT bluetooth. If you want phones for critical listening and transcribing music (or listening to a raw feed before mixdown) these are perfect. Bluetooth always entails some loss of sound quality, but these, and other direct connect phones, do not.

They are neutral enough to pass for high end in-ear monitors (IEMs), but there is a little bias on the low end. As long as you take that into account you can mentally compensate when listening to raw feeds.

One of the things that I found impressive is I could not detect any bias towards the mid range frequencies, nor do the high end frequencies sound compressed. For me this means that I can listen to acoustic jazz and hear the music as originally recorded. This is especially important for a lot of mid 1950s recordings before engineers started playing games with the mix. For these phones I sampled tracks from [[ASIN:B00CJYWUM6 At the Showboat / See What I Mean? / Settlin' In]] and [[ASIN:B000QQV5FM Dorothy Donegan Live]], and listened to the entire two hours and forty-eight minutes of Erroll Garner's [[ASIN:B00ZJ5QXDO The Complete Concert By The Sea]]. That test proved that these phones are absolutely superb for folks for love music.

While this is claimed to be for Android, I tested it on an iPad Air 2 and a ThinkPad T61 - it worked beautifully on both. In fact, on the ThinkPad I was playing from CD instead of an MP3 file and the sound quality was better than a direct connect from my Note 4 phone.

A few notes about the physical characteristics and features: I tested out the control block using my Note 4 phone and found it to be less than intuitive. I prefer controlling functions using those integrated in my Note 4 (including EQ.) I love the tangle free cord, and the comfort of the phones though. Everything about the construction and sound are of the highest quality.

Bottom line: if you are fanatical about sound quality these phones are ones that I highly recommend. I own other IEMs that cost twice as much that are close to these. Granted the expensive ones have completely neutral low frequency response, but if you are not mixing down these are as good in the overall scheme of things.

I received this as a free review sample nearly a year ago and have been using it at least twenty times a month. I use it for carrying microphones, adapters and miscellaneous electronics I use when performing as a musician. For protection this is ideal, and the inside and outside zippered pouches make this even more versatile.

It does an excellent job of protecting the delicate microphones and adapters that I store in it. I am not using the dividers as vertical separators the way they were designed. Instead, I lay them on top of the mics, and then store the cables on top. That arrangement is perfect, and the bag and insert are relatively light and sturdy.

Close to a year of constant use is testimony to just how sturdy this bag is, especially considering the times it have been accidentally stepped upon. Since the canvas part is so sturdy I am guessing that the insert will probably last even longer. One of the reasons is the overall construction, though lightweight, is of the highest quality. I am betting that if this were used for its intended purpose of protecting a DLSR or other photo equipment it would do as great a job as it does protecting my mics and other items.

I purchased this sight unseen, and solely to give my eyes a break from the much smaller laptop monitor I had been using. Since others have gone into the technical details (which are also amply described on this page), I'll stick to what I love about it and how I am now using it.

The main thing was price. At less than a hundred fifty bucks I took a chance. Hooking it up was super simple: a power cord, a VGA connection to my laptop (using the included cable), and screwing in the VESA adapter from my [[ASIN:B005C2914C Mount-It! MI-705, 3-Way Adjustable Tilting Desk Mount Bracket]] took literally ten minutes. This comes with a pedestal base that is more than adequate, but I wanted the mount I mentioned to free up desk real estate as well as to make this monitor a grab-and-go solution for a second use, which I'll get into below.

If there is one thing that I do not care for, it's the cramped area for connecting cables. The cable adapters for VGA, HDMI and power are inserted vertically, and the VGA and HDMI connections are closer together than necessary. Since I am connecting and disconnecting cables often this is a peeve, but if you plan to install it and leave it in one spot it's not even an issue.

The speakers are not the loudest when you are running sound via the HDMI port, but are more than adequate when you directly connect to the audio in port. This monitor comes with a 3.5mm cable for that purpose.

For my laptop (an aging ThinkPad) it is literally plug and play. I have finally migrated from XP to Windows 7 and this monitor's model was immediately recognized.

My second use is to press this into service as a large sheet music display. I am mirroring the screen using an [[ASIN:B00ZWOU5R2 EZcast 5GHz Wireless HDMI Streaming Media Player]] to display [[ASIN:B00WLIDHA4 MobileSheetsPro Music Reader]] mirrored from a tablet screen. Since this monitor weighs less than ten pounds it is fairly easy to set up at a gig. As a side note, if you do intend to use this on a gig or as a karaoke display this is an excellent mount: [[ASIN:B001TMCVDW Audio2000'S AST420Y Portable Flat Panel TV/Monitor Stand with Foldable Tripod Legs]].

Do note that the HDMI port will not power devices. For the EZcast dongle I have to use either a battery backup or a small wall wart (the same kind I charge my phone and tablet with), but that is not an issue either. I figured that for the price some corners had to be cut.

Although this is designed to be a desktop monitor I do wish there was a remote option for it. When I am using it to extend my laptop display it's perfect. For the screen mirroring use I mentioned a remote would be helpful.

The bottom line is I am thoroughly pleased with this monitor and may, in fact, purchase a second one so I am not swapping my laptop monitor out to take on gigs.

I received this as a free review sample. This is NOT a bluetooth device. These phones are strictly for 3.5mm stereo connections. That means that this will work with a wider variety of devices.

The sound quality to my ears is why I awarded it five stars. There is definitely a crossover built into these phones because I could hear the separation of low and high frequencies, with a prominent bass in one ear. Also, there does not seem to be any compression at the high end of the frequency spectrum, which gives these phones a more natural sound. I listen to mainly acoustic jazz (piano jazz trios, vocalists, and similar), so I appreciate the realistic sound these phones provide.

There are a few areas that I would love to see improved: the cable is long and would be nicer if it were flat, tangle-proof. Also, the controls are a little too high up on the cable in my opinion. I can easily reach them, but when testing them I could not see the buttons. Of course, those are not show stoppers - just my own preferences. And regarding the controls, I already am familiar with their placement from use and memory, so that is really a non issue.

The phones are comfortable. They ship with small, medium and large tips and I used the ones that were already installed. The fit was perfect. These also ship with an extra set of premium, noise blocking tips. I have not tried them since the regular tips are more than adequate for me.

Other nice features are the zippered, hard case, velcro cable wrap and shirt clip. To be sure, they are value-added items, but the real value is the sound quality and these phones have that without a doubt.

Bottom line: if you want hard wired phones that allow you to listen critically to music (or transcribe it), this is a surprisingly inexpensive solution. I have used everything from high end studio in-ear monitors and premium phones, and these come close at a much more affordable price. I am not saying that these are as good as the expensive phones, but am saying that bang for your buck these are hard to beat and will surprise most audiophiles.

I received this as a free review sample five months ago and have been using it for around four months. This is a rear view monitor only - not a dashcam - and it works far better than one of the combination rear monitors/dashcams that I have also used.

Since there are a large number of reviews that cover this in detail I am going to keep mine brief. Here is the single thing I do not like about it: the terrible documentation. On the other hand you can have this professionally installed for not a lot of money, which is the route that I took. If you are a do-it-yourselfer installing it right is less than an hour job (according to the tech who installed mine).

What I love is the clear visual behind me. The camera works in dark and low light, and the display has sufficient clarity and resolution to easily see what is behind you and estimate distances. If you were to purchase this as an option on a vehicle I shudder to think of the cost, but for less than one hundred fifty bucks professionally installed this is a bargain. And if you do install it yourself you can knock a C-note off that cost.

If you parallel park frequently this is a perfect way to make that easier. For rural driving this may not be a needed accessory, but for city use it's a convenience (and a safety feature as well.) Do note the information in the product specs too because they are clear about what this will and will not work with.

I received this as a free review sample and have been using it often for the past eleven months.

My main use is to house some microphones, adapters and miscellaneous electronics I use when performing as a musician. For that use this is ideal. Plus the inside and outside zippered pouches make this even more versatile.

The does an excellent job of protecting the delicate microphones and adapters that I store in it. I am not using the dividers as vertical separators the way they were designed. I lay them on top of the mics, and then store the cables on top. That arrangement is perfect, and the bag and insert are relatively light and sturdy.

Eleven months of use are testimony to just how truly gig worthy this bag is for what I use it. Based on this the insert will probably last a long time, and the overall construction, though lightweight, will probably last if this is used for its intended purpose of protecting a DLSR or other photo equipment.

I'll keep my review brief because there are a number of excellent ones that go into the features and benefits. I am approaching this as someone who owned a Roku 2 and was on the fence about moving up.

Here are the features I personally like: integrated YouTube access. When I got the Roku 2 a few years ago that was only possible with a third party service and forced me to also purchase a Chromecast to conveniently access YouTube. So for me, this feature alone justified the upgrade because that particular channel is important to me.

Another improvement - for me - is you can now select Paypal in lieu of a credit card. I do not use credit cards, and had to purchase a prepaid one to install the earlier model. You cannot get through the install process without some payment method. There are no hidden charges, but the payment method is required to be on file in case you may want to pay for a premium service. If you have Paypal and do not want to (or cannot) give a credit card number, you can still proceed with the installation process.

Installation, like the earlier model, is a breeze. I had mine up and running in practically five minutes.

As for the voice feature - I honestly never bothered with it so cannot say one way or the other if it's good or bad. Check other reviews for that. I will say that the upgrade was worth it to me. If you are still on a Roku 2 and are happy with it in all respects this is not going to be a bargain. If you want expanded features and channels and faster response this is a good choice.

If you are new to Roku and are considering cutting the cable this is worthwhile - I am using Netflix at less than ten bucks per month and am getting all the entertainment I want from just that. It's certainly a bargain for me compared to local cable services, which I deem to be way overpriced. This may be the first step in 'cutting the cable' if Netflix, Prime Movies or other inexpensive services have offering that satisfy your needs.

I received this as a free review sample. I immediately plugged it into one of the USB 2.0 ports on my ThinkPad T61 running Windows XP and was up and running. No drivers, no fuss.

Since I do not have any laptops with USB 3.0 I could not test that speed, but a directory containing 19.4GB transferred via my USB 2.0 port in a little over twenty minutes. Blazing fast? Not by USB 3.0 standards, but darn quick form the ancient laptop (which may have actually slowed the process down.)

The real reason why I rated this so highly is the cost. I recall purchasing a 64GB SD card a year ago that was vastly more expensive (at the time) than this half terabyte drive. Of course the SD card was miniscule, but this drive will fit in a shirt pocket. For me this is a convenient way to not only back up my two laptops, but also my phone and two tablets. Those are backed up via a hard connection to my laptop because they require FAT32 while this drive out of the box is NTFS. I would have reformatted it, but it worked so well with my laptop that I left it as is.

If you are planning to use this with an Apple IOS or Android device only, you will need to reformat it via those operating systems.

This comes with a cable that is USB A on the end that connects to your laptop or OTG connector, and USB 3.0 for the end that attaches to the drive itself. The 3.0 end is a little tight in tolerance, but once it's perfectly aligned it slips in and holds firmly.

Bottom line: this is inexpensive mass storage that is great for backing up files and documents, storing large media such as movies and music, or transporting files to and from work.

In 2011 I purchased a [[ASIN:B000WJB1AW Tripp Lite TLM825SA Safety Surge Protector 120V 8 Outlet Metal 25ft Cord OSHA]], which is still going strong. A few months age I purchased another and recently purchased a pair of these. That alone should tell you how satisfied I am with the brand.

This is a heavy duty protector, both physically and electrically. I live in Central Florida, which is notorious for power problems, so not using well designed protection is inviting disaster, which can be very costly considering my investment in the gear this is protecting. The main reason why I own so many is I am a musician who owns amps, a PA and keyboard and the power in many venues is marginal at best. This is inexpensive protection and I have witnessed other musicians' gear getting fried in the same venues in which I play, so I know these surge suppressors work.

My combined experience with both of these models has resulted in zero problems. This is a professional-grade piece of gear and it designed to protect your equipment and to last if properly cared for and used properly. I do want to note that one rule of thumb I use is to not overload protected power strips. If you do you will be defeating the protection that this one affords. Please bear that in mind and read the specs while making a purchase decision. If the devices that you want to plug this into exceed the rated specs on this product page this is not the outlet for you.

I received this as a free review sample. As advertised the protection is excellent. The construction is as well, and you actually can turn it inside out to change the color scheme.

Here is the 'but': this case literally fits the Sound Blaster Roar 2 like a glove (and it is only for the Roar 2 model.) The stretching and pulling required is a bit onerous. I thought it would be a learning curve issue, but each time I use this bag it is as difficult as the last time. Difficult, but not impossible. On the other hand, had this been designed for an easier fit I am not sure the same level of protection would be there.

Also note that this is strictly for transporting the Roar 2. Once it is inserted in this case you cannot access controls. I kind of like that because I do carry my Roar 2 around and appreciate the fact that this will keep it from getting dinged.

One final thing: the top cover does not completely close. There is a gap and there is no zipper. That is why you can turn this inside out.

Bottom line: this provides excellent protection and is well made. On the other hand, there are challenges as I noted above and you will need to weight those into a purchase decision. I do use mine a lot and have a love/hate relationship with it.

I received this as a free review sample. As a music stand light it's functional, but not ideal. As a night light or even a clip on to a book for night time reading when your partner of sleeping this is truly useful.

Be aware that it's small and even at max illumination with all LEDs active it is not glaring. That is a good feature, but the tradeoff is as a music stand light you may have to keep adjusting the goosenecks to get optimum illumination.

The goosenecks are a little on the thin side, which is another reason I think this is best suited to clamping directly on a book or headboard (if you can find a spot that the clamp can grip). On a music stand turning pages too briskly can change the position of the LEDs; not a problem when reading a book, but not the distraction you want when playing an instrument.

Bottom line: if you are looking for a light for your music stand carefully comparison shop. If you are looking for a portable and effective reading light you will love this one.

I received this as a free review sample. I'll spare you a regurgitation of the product specs or paraphrasing the previous two reviews, but will focus on what sets this one apart from the pack.

The biggest surprise I had was volume. This is a relatively small speaker and most bluetooth speakers in this one's size and price range are designed as personal speakers that are meant to be nearby on a desk, night stand or counter top. I can clearly hear this one two rooms away indoors and even outdoors in areas with high ambient noise this can cut through and project sound.

Sound quality is neutral, and I mean that in a good way. While there is some bias towards the mid range frequencies it does not 'color' the sound of music being streamed to it. To be honest, this is not going to crank out heavy bass, so if you listen to bass-centric music you may be disappointed. On the other hand, the highs and lows are practically seamless, with a slight emphasis towards the mid range, so if you listen to jazz, blues or some forms of rock and Americana this speaker will probably please you.

One review discussed bluetooth range issues so I specifically tested that. Even two rooms away, which normally causes drops in quality, I was able to get crystal clear streaming with no drops in the music quality streamed from a Samsung Note 3. The distance is approximately twenty feet, but definitely not line of sight, so I am happy with that aspect.

While the product specs claim six hours of music, you can realistically expect somewhere between four and four and a half hours if you have the volume cranked. If you drop it to about a quarter - perfect for near listening up to two or three meters - you will get the claimed play time.

I purchased this to support a [[ASIN:B00ND1KHY2 Mackie Mix Series Mix12FX -Watt 12-Channel Mixer]], which it easily does. What impressed me the most is the construction. I had been using a music stand with the tray perpendicular to the ground and it worked, but was not nearly as stable as this stand. Moreover, I looked at a few other brands, but most were cheaply made.

Here are a few things that set this one apart: first, the clamping mechanisms are quick release type and not the cheesy knobs that every other stand I tried employs. Second, if you are considering this for a truly heavy device like a projector the pins for the support pole guarantee that it will be supported. Frankly, the pins are probably never going to be needed because the main release mechanisms hold firmly.

Dimensions are:
Tray: 15 9/16 x 10 7/8 inches with lips along the widths top and bottom.
Stand: adjusts from 23 to 53 inches - this is ideal if you are a keyboardist or drummer who wants to control your instrument and mics via a mixer because the height range is perfect for most scenarios.
Footprint: 25 inches between tripod feet points.

This also comes with a sticky silicone pad that measures 12 x 7 5/78 inches to hold a mixer or laptop firmly in place. My Mackie mixer did not budge when it was placed on the pad and the table tilted 30 degrees.

Finally, I purchased a [[ASIN:B000XZYXTG Hamilton Carrying Bag for KB50 & KB990 Series Stands]] that easily holds and protects this stand. I recommend it if you do opt for this model.

I purchased this specifically to connect a condenser mic to my Samsung Tab 3 10.1. I needed two other devices to make it work - an XLR M to F cable and a phantom power source (for the latter I am using an [[ASIN:B00KAPGLQC InnoGear® 1- Channel 48V Phantom Power Supply]] and the combination works like a charm.

The cable itself is not especially heavy gauge, but the connectors and strain reliefs are high quality. I live the precise fit of both the 3.5mm and XLR connectors, and the strain reliefs are such that the critical areas on both ends will not be subjected to bends that will fray or harm the inner conductors.

Of course, the main point for me is this works with my tablet, and it not only does for it, but also for my Note 3 phone. I use my tablet as a video camera for recording musical performances and until I added a condenser mic (an MXL 551R) the sound quality was poor. Since using the mic - made possible in part by this cable - the sound quality has dramatically improved.

Basically, I carefully checked out a number of similar cables and this is the one that had the best reviews and specs. I paid more for it, but feel that I also received commensurate value because of the construction and overall solid performance.

I received this as a free review sample and it was sorely needed because the internal fan in my ThinkPad T61 finally died. Note: if you are looking at this as a cure know that many laptops report a fan failure then shut down. In the case of mine, I found that I could press the On/Off button briefly when that happened and it would power back up and boot Windows.

This fan array moves a lot of air, promoting excellent heat transfer. So far it has worked well and I have had no premature shutdowns (although I still have to go through the On/Off button sequence every time I power the ThinkPad up.)

Do be aware that this fan array will interfere with other USB peripherals if you power it directly from your laptop, and especially if you add even more peripherals to the ports integrated into this unit. That is because the power draw form USB ports may exceed the capacity of the laptop, especially if you are running it off an unpowered USB hub. I had that problem when I tried running this, a mouse and a speaker from my laptop. I moved this one to a powered hub and the problem was immediately resolved.

Also, this raises a laptop 1 3/8 inches higher at its lowest setting. For me it took a day to become accustomed to the raised typing height, but since it solved a genuine problem the tradeoff was worth it. Just know that you will need to adjust to that and it may slow down your productivity for a day or two.

If your laptop has a fully functioning internal fan this array will augment that and keep your laptop cool even in unairconditioned spaces on a hot day. That will definitely prolong the life of the internal electronics and the hard drive.

When I purchased my Note 3 from Verizon I also purchased a 64GB Samsung card that has served me well for nearly eighteen months. I decided to purchase another 64GB card to back up the one in my phone and I took a chance with this one. It has yet to let me down.

Since my files are nearly static on my phone (the only major charges are new music and photos), after I synched my Samsung's card to this one I swapped this one into the Note 3 as my primary card. I figured that any issues with streaming music, shooting video clips and photos would show up fairly quickly with constant use. That is why I am pleased. I honestly cannot discern any difference in either performance or reliability with this card.

I am so pleased that I am going to purchase another to back up my laptop. At present the price of these cards have dropped dramatically since I paid Verizon nearly ninety bucks for my Samsung card. I am sure that brand has also dropped in price, but this one is so solid and reliable that I am going to stick with it - at least for the time being. The bottom line is if you own a phone or tablet that will recognize 64GB this is an inexpensive way to upgrade an older 16 or 32 GB card.

I received this as a review sample and even though I am experienced with setting up and configuring networks, this was so easy that I honestly believe anyone can set it up with the scant instructions.

My initial set up was to connect it to my DSL modem just to check it out. Although the instructions are terse, you do need to read them regardless of level of experience. For one thing, it requires you to completely power off your broadband modem. For another, it takes a bit to boot up no matter how you intend to use it. Connecting to broadband was a snap.

What I really wanted was a range extender and this was as simple to configure for that as it was to configure for broadband. In that mode, when you first power it on and boot up it takes over a minute and you may be tempted to think it's broken. Don't. Once it is powered up, like the broadband set up (DSL or cable), the wizard makes it simple to discover your wireless router, connect to it and extend the range of your network. My wireless router turns in a weak -70dB from my master bedroom (measured with [[ASIN:B004EBZX6W Wi-Fi Analyzer]]) and once I installed this in the same room the signal dramatically improved to a strong -40dB. In the same room with my master wireless router this comes in at -47dB while the master router measures in at -56dB. That indicates that the signal of this router is exceptionally strong.

There are options for adding sensors for home control. I did not test that set of features because I did not receive sensors, but it is functionality that makes this router/extender a great choice if you do want to pursue home control too. There are IOS and Android apps that can be used in conjunction with the sensor features. Again, I did not explore those and probably will not since I am not interested in them. As a router alone I love this, and especially the overall signal strength and ease of setting up and configuring.

I received the four port model as a review sample. Note that this is a quick way to expand or multiply USB ports on a PC or laptop, but you cannot plug external hard drives into it along with other devices because you will quickly max out the USB power limit. I use mine for my mouse, a camera synching cable and a 32GB thumb drive. That leaves me a spare port for synching (but not charging) my phone or tablet.

For my purposes this hub is perfect. It gives me the expansion for the low power peripherals I use, and it is handier to plug those into this hub than to fumble around with ports on the back and sides of my laptop.

As for full speed, I cannot test this because my old laptop only supports USB 2.0. The speeds that I get from that, though, are on par with what I get if I were to directly connect my phone or tablet (or thumb drive) to the laptop's integrated USB ports. I will leave it to others to discuss USB 3.0 performance.

This is truly plug and play on my Win XP and Win 7 laptops, and I tested it on my Note 3 phone with an OTG adapter and it worked in that configuration too (I connected a keyboard and mouse for that test.)

Bottom line: if you are planning to plug in hard drives and other high power drawing devices you will need a hub with an external power supply. For mice, synching and other low power peripherals this is both convenient and well made, and is at the least the equal of every other USB hub I own or have tested.

I received my headband as a review sample. I want to note that I did not experience any drops in streaming as noted by other reviewers when using this with my Samsung Note 3 phone, but did have some issues with my Samsung Tab 3 10.1. The latter has some bluetooth problems that are well known, so I am attributing my issues with Tab 3 flaws and not this headband. I briefly tested this with an HTC One Remix with no problems either.

This headband is unique in that it was designed with real, strenuous sports in mind - or at least activities that make you work up a sweat. As such I tested my streaming as noted above with my source devices (phones and tablets) at least twenty feet away. That simulates where you would place those devices during a game of tennis.

It does seem impervious to sweat, although I would not call it sweat-proof. If you use it heavily and frequently you'll need to clean it at least weekly - see some of the top rated video reviews on this page for instructions for that because it is a bit tricky disassembling it the first time.

Also note that it's a snug fit on my head, which is size 6 7/8. I am guessing that if you wear a men's hat size above 7 1/4 it will be too snug. Take that into account.

Sound quality is excellent in my opinion. For the past nine months or so (at the time of this review) all brands or phones seem to have taken a major leap in that respect and these are no exception. The high frequency response of the phones is clear at max volume and the bass is deep (but not thumping). The mid range seems to be the sweet spot, and is rich and full. The volume itself is not super loud, and it is not noise-isolating. It does keep out most ambient noise though, and while these are not perfect for critical listening they are excellent for casual listening during sports and other strenuous activities.

If you want phones that stay in place regardless of that you are doing, and also demand respectable sound quality these merit consideration. I have not researched the market, but these are the only headband phones I have come across among the dozens I have tested to date.

I received this as a review sample and have been using it for a little less than a week. At the time of this review this tablet is shipping with Android 4.4.4. Before I dive into what I like and why I rated it so highly I want to set expectations.

This DOES NOT come with bluetooth, and the screen and cameras are not especially spectacular. The screen is readable (easily so) and has nice, vivid colors. However compared to even my Note 3 phone it falls short. As the cameras, for some reason tablet makers seem to skimp on those as though they are an afterthought.

Since there is no bluetooth you are stuck with the internal speaker or using phones. The internal speaker is not what I would call optimum for listening to music, but the included phones are surprisingly decent. I also connected one of my bluetooth speakers that accepts 3.5mm input and the sound was excellent, so while this does not have bluetooth, you can still stream music to it.

Another thing it does not have is bloatware that every other tablet (and phone) seems to be plagued with. That is one of the reasons why I rated this so highly. But the real reason why I gave this tablet five stars is price. At the time of this review it is selling for sixty bucks, which is not a bad deal for an entry level tablet - especially if you want to browse the web, stream music or wile away the day on facebook.

It is a complete package that includes a stylus, soft bag, charger and cable, and OTG adapter. The latter allows you to connect USB peripherals to the micro USB charging port. I tested it with a keyboard, then a mouse and it recognized both. The USB charging port is another thing I like - it;s a micro USB type, which is a major improvement over some entry level tablets that I have tested that use a non-standard barrel connector.

You can add a 32GB SD card using a TF adapter. I tested it with an old SanDisk Ultra 32GB MicroSDHC Class 10 UHS Memory Card that was immediately recognized. The application manager allows you to move some apps to the SD card, so as you add your favorites some will be eligible for running off an external card (depending on the app, of course.) Browsing the web, using Google's location feature and maps, and Youtube all performed with no lag or issues. In fact I would put the performance head-to-head against my Verizon Ellipsis 7 4G LTE Tablet, Black 7-Inch 8GB tablet. Do note, though, that if you have all services turned on and are constantly using this tablet you are going to get about 2.5 to 3 hours of use time if you are not connected to a charger. For some folks that may be a deal breaker, so take that into account.

Basically this is a stripped down, but very functional tablet for folks on a budget. If you can live without bluetooth and will be using it near a power source it's a decent tool (or toy, depending on your outlook) at an affordable price, It is a perfect first tablet for someone who also has an Android phone, and is definitely useful for folks addicted to the web.

I use this to occasionally connect two [[ASIN:B0002E38EE Monster Keyboard - 12' Instrument Cable - Straight to Straight 1/4" plugs]] together when twelve feet is not sufficiently long. For that cable brand and model this connector works like a charm.

A few things I like are the fact that this does not introduce extraneous noise into the signal path, and the cables I cited snap firmly into the female ends and hold firmly. I am not doubting other reviews that claim they need tape to hold cables in, but that comes down to the cable itself. For the higher end Monster cables this is not an issue for me.

Since I only occasionally need to use this connector I cannot speak to the overall longevity. Time will tell on that and if it prematurely fails I will update my rating and review to reflect that. Thus far, however, this has performed as a five star product for me and has allowed me to avoid buying a longer instrument cable.

I purchased this to transform a [[ASIN:B0002E38EE Monster Keyboard Cable - Straight to Straight 1/4" plugs]] to right angle at one end. The female connection mated perfectly with the Monster cable. Note that that cable is relatively high end with beefy plugs, so I did not expect problems with this adapter and have not experienced any.

Since my instrument is a keyboard there is practically zero movement or opportunities for the connections to jiggle. In addition to no issues or complaints about the female end, I am as happy with the male plug, which has firmly mated with a few amps and a PA.

If there is any issue, it's the fact that this adapter adds a lot of bulk to the end into which you plug a cable. On my keyboard it does protrude, especially with the cable I cited above. But the sound quality is noise free with my arrangement, and as I said, the connections at each end are firm and solid.

It may just come down to the quality of cable that you intend to use with this adapter. For the Monster model I am using this is a perfect way to change one straight end to angled.

I received this as a review sample. I had low expectations regarding the sound quality, but was pleasantly surprised. In particular, the mid range response is rich and full, with a decent high end that does not break up, and a low end that turned out to be unexpectedly boomy. Not in your face boomy, but not anemic either.

Also, this paired and connected easily to my Note 3 phone. I did not make test calls with it so cannot credibly discuss that feature. I also only wear it occasionally and normally for an hour or two in the evening or morning if I am outside, so cannot validate the battery life claims. Even if those are in the ballpark (and I suspect they are) then their specs are excellent for any speaker in this price range.

Finally, the cap keeps my head and ears warm in thirty and forty degree weather, which we actually have in central and north Florida Granted it is not many days out of the year, but when we do have sub thirty degree weather a cap such as this is greatly appreciated, and is a key feature in my opinion.

Regarding the speakers protruding as claimed by another reviewer, that is true to a point. But they do not look horrible (or not to me anyway). My high rating is based on the sound quality, ease of pairing and play time, and the fact that they keep my ears warm.

I purchased the [[ASIN:B000WJB1AW Tripp Lite TLM825SA with 25ft Cord]] four years ago and my experience with that one convinced me to purchase this one when I needed a second set of outlets. The only difference between the two is this one has a twelve foot cord where the other one had a 25 foot one.

Since I have only owned this one for two months I cannot make sweeping statements. I live in Central Florida, which is notorious for power problems, so not using well designed protection is inviting disaster, which can be very costly considering my investment in the gear this is protecting.

I will say that this one seems to have the same high quality as the older one. Plus I have already used this in locales with marginal power and it has protected my music amplifiers and keyboards. Note that one rule of thumb I use is to not overload protected power strips. If you do you will be defeating the protection that this one affords. Please bear that in mind and read the specs while making a purchase decision. If the devices that you want to plug this into exceed the rated specs on this product page this is not the outlet for you.

My combined experience with both of these models has resulted in zero problems. This is a professional-grade piece of gear and it designed to protect your equipment and to last if properly cared for and used properly.

Note: there is a [[ASIN:B00QEY99DU Newer version] of this earpiece that I have also reviewed. Like that one I received this as a review sample. This one is still impressive for the following reasons: foremost is price. Even at full list this is an ideal way to use your phone legally in locales that enforce hands free laws (and the number is growing.)

It's also comfortable, which is surprising to me because I hate in-ear buds. In this case, the array f provided ear pieces in various sides ensures a good fit regardless of your age or size. Ironically the medium fit me perfectly.

Sound quality for music is not spectacular, but more than adequate for casual listening. I made and received calls and the clarity of those on both ends were also adequate. Not spectacular, but not terrible. When you consider that this is less than twenty bucks at the time of this review then in that context you are getting more than you are paying for in that department.

This may not be the best single ear headset on the market, but it's by far among the best in its price range - and since it is so inexpensive and does what it should do I am rating it five stars.

Since there are some incredibly detailed and helpful reviews already I will focus on where these phones are best suited. I received mine as a review sample and have been using them for nearly a week to make sure I thoroughly test them.

For me these are best for critical listening, and especially raw mixes if you do recording. Of course they are not limited to that. The fact that these phones are fairly neutral across the entire frequency spectrum makes them ideal for listening to unmixed recordings, as well as music that you are studying or transcribing. The reproduction is so balanced that listening to albums with these compared to other phones - including some other Brainwavz models - is like night and day.

If you are listening to music that is heavily biased towards bass and drums these may not be the best phones for you. If you listen to acoustic music these are near perfect because you can easily hear every note. I tested it on a few jazz albums that I own as well as a broadcast of two friends from a local station that had been recorded directly from the sound board and it was wonderful to hear what was actually recorded versus what a biased pair of phones normally reproduce.

A few notes about comfort: these are light, do a great job of isolating ambient noise without totally eliminating it, and are easy to wear. I am not an IEM (in ear monitor) type of person, but these presented no problems even when I wore them for three to four hours straight. A big plus is this set comes with different sized foam ear pieces and a nice case (the [[ASIN:B00HPPL1M4 Brainwavz Hard Earphone Case]]).

While these phones may not be for everybody, they are perfect for those of us who spend a lot of time critically listening to music and/or transcribing it. If you fall into that category you will probably love them.

I will not regurgitate the product specs since they are not only complete, but have been validated by more than a few previous reviews. I'll stick to some key observations about the review sample that I received and why I think this light deserves five stars.

The main reason why I love this light is price and performance. I own a few other music stand lights and they either perform on par with this one, but are priced twenty-five percent (or more higher), or they are not as well made.

Features are also more than I expected for a twenty buck light. For one thing you can easily get seven hours of continuous use on a single charge. I did a rundown test on mine and it remained illuminated for a little over seven hours before it started dimming, That was with both LEDS in each head switched on. I ended the test when it started appreciably dimming, but even at seven hours this is more than adequate since I actually do use this as a music stand light and the longest performances are less than three hours.

Another feature that I love is the LED indicator in the USB A end of the charging cable. It will be red until the light fully charges, then it will turn green.

Note: there are two things that I do not care for: (1) the charging end is a barrel connector instead of a micro USB connector, so if you lose of damage the included cable you are going to have difficulty replacing it, and (2) the barrel connector does not completely seat into the charging port. It charges, but I would be hesitant of using this light in a studio where you wanted to suppress all electrical interference. I am not sure there is any from this light, but the fact that a conducting connector is partially exposed gives me pause.

Bottom line: for stage performances this light is better and brighter than most other two-LED models and illuminates sufficiently to read music or lyrics. It holds firm when clamped to my music stand, and the flexible arms allow me to position the lamp heads for optimum reading while staying put.

Before proceeding I want to state that unlike some other reviews the sample that I received had no strong odor, There was a slight one from the synthetic material from which it is made, but nothing lingering or particularly obnoxious (to me anyway.)

What I love about this insert is it's truly padded to the point that you can entrust delicate gear to it. Another feature that I like is the bottom and the top open and can be sealed with the velcro strips incorporated into the insert. In fact, do not lose sight of the fact that this is an insert that is designed to go into another case. I am using mine to store a wireless microphone, received and power supply. I store those in this insert and this insert in an [[ASIN:B000HZGFMA Arriba Cases Ac-140 Padded Gear Transport Bag]]. The Arriba case offers very little protection, so this insert is important to me.

The material is water resistant, but the case itself is not because of the way the top and bottom flaps close. Again, this is designed as an insert and not a carrying case, so I am not complaining about that.

Overall, this is a wonderful way to protect delicate equipment that is carried in unpadded (or lightly padded) bags. It has dividers for camera lenses that can be arranged to accommodate other kinds of equipment, or removed for larger gear. I am so impressed with it that I am considering ordering another for my second wireless microphone set up.

The review sample that I received had a sturdy elastic band that did not break on me. I do not doubt the earlier reviewer who claimed that theirs did, but my experience was different.

When I claimed in the title that this is a clever design I am comparing this one to other headrest mounted tablet holders. I have tested literally dozens of other models and all required that either you remove your tablet from any case you may be using, or you endure less than optimum grips of the mount will accommodate a case. This one is a case plus headrest mount.

There are some trade-offs in this one's design. First, you can only mount your tablet in landscape mode. Since that is the mode I always use this is perfect for me. If you need a mount that will accommodate portrait mode, or you need to switch between the two, this is NOT the mount for you.

Some physical details that I do like include the heavily padded case when you are using outside of vehicle back seats. While the holder into which you insert your iPad is not the hard plastic, snap in design that affords optimum protection, it does dampen and absorb some shock. The covers are thick and provide a great deal of protection. In fact, that feature is better than ninety-five percent of every case I have ever tried. The organizer is handy, and all of the cutouts and accesses are perfectly aligned to an iPad's camera and various buttons and ports.

If you need a case that will function as both a case and headrest mount this one is worth considering - as long as you understand the limitations that I have cited.

It may be a bit pricey, but is definitely at home in a conference room and does make an impression. However, the key is the protection it provides and the folio's flexibility in accommodating right- or left-handed folks.

You can change the orientation of the sketch pad and tablet by simply turning the folio upside down, reinserting the sketch pad from that direction, and doing the same with the tablet holder, which is held in place by a magnet. In addition, this offers two different viewing angles as well as a typing angle when the folio is configured as a stand. See my customer-supplied images for details.

I love the absolute protection that this folio/tablet holder provides. The holder into which the iPad snaps in is tough and shock resistant, and the folio itself is equally so. This comes with a screen protector to add yet another layer of protection. Of course, with the paper sketch pad covering the face of the iPad when this is closed gives maximum protection to the screen should you accidentally drop it.

While the functionality and protective features are outstanding, this folio has looks too. If you like understated elegance this has it. Or it does in my opinion. I love the feel of the exterior, which is akin to a fine suede, but is truly tough.

The pad itself can be replaced with 6x9 inch refills. The actual size of the one that ships with the case is slightly undersized, but I did test a standard 6x9 and it fit.

The product specs and RatherLiveInKeyWest's excellent November 23, 2014 review cover all of the highlights of this box. I'll confine my review to a few details that I love about this and why this one is yet another milestone in the evolution of these boxes.

First I'll share my opinion about the lack of bluetooth. Frankly I do not feel that it's needed since this box is designed to integrate with a TV and usually that means a home audio system as well. If bluetooth is truly important to you there are two USB ports on this box, so you can purchase a blutetooth dongle and add that capability.

One of the features that I love is you can not only control this with the remote that comes with it, but also wired or wireless keyboards and mice, and a Miracast-enabled phone. The instructions cover all of these options, including the Miracast one. I do recommend using a keyboard and mouse for the initial set up because the remote is tedious. The instructions are terse, but sufficient to get this box up and running. If you own an Android phone or tablet you will have an easier time than if you are more in the Windows or IOS camp. But even then it's not a steep learning curve.

Like the control options you have an array of connetions options as well. They are covered in the product specs so I am not going to repeat them here. Suffice to say, this box is flexible and will connect to legacy TVs as well as the latest and greatest.

Another feature I like is this will recognize SD cards up to 64GB, which provides more than ample space for media files. Plus this box is both stable and blazing fast compared to the previous generation.

Bottom line: the boxes I have used in the past were better suited for geeks who loved tinkering. This one is a major step towards a friendly addition to your home entertainment system that an average, quasi-technical consumer can effectively use. It is also a key building block to seamless integration of home computing and entertainment system. For all of the above reasons I rated it five stars.

J. Chambers' November 4, 2014 review provides the complete specs that are missing from the product description at the time of this review as well as a helpful video. I will not repeat his information and encourage you to read it.

Like him I received my station as a review sample. What I like about this versus other surge protector solutions is this one actually has features that protects against electrical surges and spikes and provides the specs to back them up. That may sound like a no-brainer, but I have reviewed 'surge protectors' in the past that were really power strips with no real protection.

What I especially like is the small, convenient footprint. That, plus the three outlets (one what is spaced to accommodate wall warts), and the convenience of two USB charging ports. I will say that the charging ports are slow. On my Galaxy Note 3 phone using a high speed wall charger I get a 1% per 2.5 minutes charging rate. It's over 5.5 minutes with this station, but for overnight charging is not an issue for me. Do factor that into your purchase decision, though. Another thing to take into account is the slide out holder for phones is 7/16 inches fully extended and may not accommodate most phones unless you remove them from any protective case. I charge my phone flat on my desk top, so it's not an issue for me, but if you want to take complete advantage of this station's features you should measure your phone's thickness in its case.

Bottom line: I am totally pleased with this station despite some of the noted limitations. The convenience to me outweighs the compromises, which I cited to ensure that you are armed with enough information to make a purchase decision.

As 'cool' as the cloth covered outer jacket is, this retro look on this cable has a real purpose. Most cables use PVC for the jacket and the dielectric properties will cause some signal distortion when they go through their store/discharge cycle. Granted, the amount of charge a PVC jacket will store and eventually discharge is minute and also will not affect charging. However, many of us use our cables to sync to laptops and other devices and with the cloth jacket this effect is so minimized as to be nominal.

There are other reasons why I awarded the review sample I received five stars. At the top of the list is this cable not only supports charging my Note 3, but also is flawless when it comes to synching it. Not all cables I own will synch (sounds incredible, but unfortunately true), This one will and my guess why it's done so without errors so far is the gold plated connector that do aid in conductivity. Another reason for the five stars is the heavy duty housing for the connectors and how they manage to be both thin enough to be unobtrusive and substantial enough to assure a long service life. There are even strain reliefs on each end of the cable to minimize wear that can eventually cause diminished transmission at the weak points in any USB cable.

Finally, the ends mate perfectly with every device with which I've tried them. I have only tested the micro USB end on my Note 3, but have tested the USB A end on my laptop, various chargers and battery backups and the fits on all are precise.

I received one of these as a review sample. I am not going to regurgitate the product specs, but will comment on some of them as they pertain to my own experience.

First, the sound is very good. Not excellent, but close. I have a few albums with which I test speakers and this one was clear across the frequency spectrum when I tested it with Miles Davis' [[ASIN:B00IS4187Y Kind Of Blue]]. That album exercises the high, mid and low ranges of speakers and this one passed. The bass was a little on the weak side, but still deep. The highs and mids were as good as any bluetooth speaker in this one's class that I have tested.

The volume in a shower is a little anemic. I an still hear music over it, but when the nozzle is at full blast it comes close to drowning out the sound. On the topic of shower - I had no problem securely affixing the suction cup to my tiled wall, even when the cup overlapped tile seams and grout.

If you have the speaker cranked do not expect more than 3.5 hours of use time. The ten hours provided in the specs is a figure that assumes you will be playing this at thirty percent volume. Outside of a shower this is sufficiently loud at that setting as a close in speaker, but for showers or other high noise environments I am betting you will have it cranked to max.

Overall, this is a nice speaker, especially for the thirty-some buck price that is listed at the time of this review. It stacks up well against other speakers in this price range.

I am not going to refute the other reviewers who had more success than I with this antenna. For one thing my house is located a good twenty-five miles from the nearest station (I am in west Volusia County, Florida and the nearest station is in Winter Park). I have had issues with other antennas, so am inclined to believe my problem has more to do with the local market and transmitters, as well as my home. The latter is because my house is framed in cinder block, which will attenuate an already weak signal.

Assembly was easy and connecting to my TV easier still. I was able to get ghosted signals of a few stations but were unable to dial them in by repositioning the antenna or the fine tuning knob. I tested my TV reception without this antenna and got rasterized static, so the fact that it pulled in anything speaks highly of the design.

Instructions are on the back of the box and easy to follow. I recommend that you do a web search for TV reception problems and signal strength in your area before making a purchase. Obviously this antenna works because there are customer reviews from verified purchasers who are happy with it. I received mine as a review sample and blame location and the other circumstances that I described.

I received this hub as a review sample and just had to test it on a [[ASIN:B00KCG95M6 Keedox® M8 TV Box With Remote Control]]. It was immediately recognized and worked perfectly. I also use it to extend my USB ports in my [[ASIN:B00C7SK2J2 Micro USB OTG Host Cable to USB 2.0]] with the same results. That one was connected to a Samsung Tab 3 10.1, then a Galaxy Note 3. All of those tests was using the hub unpowered.

For connecting high power devices like external hard drives and DVD ROMs, I powered this hub using a [[ASIN:B00MRGKPH8 Sabrent 5V 4A 100V-240V to DC Power Adapter]]. I only tested a single external hard drive and a DVD player with this test and then only using the USB 2.0 speed since it was connected to a ThinkPad T61 running Windows XP. The arrangement worked and I was able to get expected USB 2.0 performance - not blazing, but not molasses slow either. The only USB 3.0 device I currently own is my Note 3 phone and I could not adequately test this hub using that.

I do love the looks of the hub, but the important thing for me is I was able to use it on some legacy devices as well as three Android devices with no problems whatsoever. I also like the fact that you can transform it into a powered hub with an optional power supply, or just use it out of the box for low power devices. Just be aware that if you opt to use it as a powered hub using the Sabrent power supply make sure that the devices that you intend to plug into it do not exceed 4 Amps total. Some of the larger external hard drives can easily eat into the power budget. Also note that of you attempt to use this as a charger (which you can do standalone with the optional power supply) you are only going to get 1 Amp per port and no over charging protection. I recommend not using it for that unless you are in a pinch.

Bottom like: this is a versatile hub that has worked with every device I tested, and it looks good as well.

Like most of the other reviewers I received this as a review sample along with a [[ASIN:B00N38TQJC Sabrent Premium 4 Port Aluminum USB 3.0 Hub]]. This will actually work with just about any of Sabrent's hubs as well as most other 5 volt (DC) devices on the market that require up to 4 Amps of current.

The barrel connector comes with an adapter to a larger size barrel connector to cover Sabrent hubs. I have checked every source I could find to get the barrel connector specs, but none are to be found. This is frustrating to say the least because this is truly a multi-purpose power supply that can be used on non-Sabrent products. Since it is not claimed to be universal I am giving it five stars because it works perfectly with the hub with which I tested it.

One feature that I particularly like is the fact that the cable is heavy duty with good strain reliefs on both ends. This is not your typical, flimsy power supply cable. Another thing I like is this runs cool even with constant use. I am using it to power a hub with a disk drive and both the hub and this power supply are running cool even after a twenty-four hour period.

This is capable of providing up to four Amps, but will only 'push' what the device requires. What that means is if you are powering four devices that draw .6 Amps each this supply will only push 2.4 Amps, so there is no worry about overloading. On the other hand if you are attempting to power a hum that requires over 4 Amps this is not the proper power supply and will not work.

If you own a Sabrent powered hub this is a safe choice, Do make sure you know the total current draw of the devices into the hub and make sure that the total does not exceed four Amps.

There are two things that I immediately noticed when I tested the review sample that I received: (1) the controls are on the bottom of the speaker, and (2) it's louder than other speakers in its size and price range.

As for the placement of the controls, it isn't an issue for me because I usually control the volume level and track skipping from my phone. Regarding the volume it's capable of putting out, it's more than just a personal speaker. I can stream music to the speaker in my kitchen and hear it clearly in my living and dining rooms. That's pretty loud.

The heart and soul of a speaker is the sound quality and this one is very good in that category too. It has good frequency response across the high, mid and low bands, but emphasizes the mids, then the highs and finally the low end in that order. While the bass is surprisingly prominent for such a tiny speaker it is not the dominant frequency band. The mids and highs are very clear and you can hear nuances in music in those frequency bands better than the bass.

One final thing that I love is the ease of pairing and connecting. As soon as you power it up and scan for it from your phone or other device it shows up in the list of available devices. A simple touch of the device name on your screen and it pairs and connects. If you want to use the aux port (the 3.5mm one for headphones) all you need to do is press the button on the speaker that has a bluetooth and phone logo for three seconds and it switched to aux port mode.

I test a lot of speakers and this is one of the better ones I've come across. Not only does it perform, but I like the styling, which counts for something. It's an easy five stars the way I rate, which factors price, ease of use, performance and sound quality. This one has it all.

The review sample that I received is priced in the intermediate range of phones, yet this one sounds as good as some I own that were in the hundred fifty dollar price range.

What impressed me the most is the reproduction of frequency bands. These phones sound as though they are biased towards the higher frequencies, although the mid and low ranges are full and rich. No matter what volume the highs are clear and articulated, and the mids are also very clear and full. The bass is more than respectable and come in at the standard 20Hz. The upper end is at 22KHz, which accounts for the superb high end response. The response curve is fairly smooth and linear across the spectrum, so you can easily use these for transcribing music or critical listening.

I love the comfortable, gel buds that ship with this set. It comes with small, medium and large buds that will accommodate just about any ear size. I have no problem wearing these for four plus hours at a time (and I normally dislike ear buds). Another reason why I awarded these five stars is the tangle free, flat cable. It's not only a joy to use, but noise free.

The product description claims that these will attenuate ambient noise. It does, but not greatly so - or in my case anyway. I normally insert buds lightly into my ears, so that may account for my experience with them.

One final note: I did not test the microphone function. I was so taken with the sound quality that I lost interest in that feature. I will say that if sound quality is important you will probably love these. I am still pondering how phones of this quality can sell for less than fifty bucks, but I am not going to look a gift horse in the mouth.

Kimberly R. Norton's helpful August 3, 2014 review thoroughly covers most aspects of this card. Actually, after spending a lot of time with the review sample that I received, this is a solution more than a mere card.

First, a caveat. This card requires a reboot of a Windows XP system before it's recognized as a removable disk drive. In a real medical emergency this could be an issue. Granted, XP is obsolete, but Murphy's Law would probably go into effect if you were in a time-critical situation. Plus, this is strictly a Windows based solution.

Now for the reasons why I love this. Foremost is the app itself. It leads you through the creation of medical information that is needed if you were being treated while unconscious or unresponsive. The text files can be read by any system, as well as uploaded to your phone. I have labeled my data card to note that the information is also on my smart phone - just in case the card fails for some reason. The heart of this solution is the app that created the medical data and the files that it produces.

The card itself is clever in that an 8GB flash drive is contained in the form factor of a credit card. The USB 2.0 plug slides out of a protected channel that does not appreciably add to the thickness of the card, so it will easily fit in a wallet.

In addition to the medical data this solution provides a scanner guard that you can use to sandwich your credit cards between that and the Medic ID Guard card. What this part does is guard against RFID identity theft, which is a very real problem. It does not take much to thwart thieves - wrapping credit cards in aluminum foil will do the trick - but this solution is much cleaner and is actually a side benefit. Prior to getting this solution I had been using [[ASIN:B00GC4RTKC RFID Blocking Secure Sleeve]]s. This solution, however, is a lot more convenient.

Bottom line: there are some things that I do not like about this solution, but the benefits greatly outweigh them. As I mentioned, the app alone is worth the cost of this solution because it allowed me to create complete medical data in a structured way. I could have never done that on my own without additional hours of research to discover what information is actually relevant.

There are a few things that set the review sample I received apart from most other bluetooth speakers. At the top of the list is sound pressure level because this is the loudest bluetooth speaker I have ever tested. Literally, this can compete with waves on a beach, which can get pretty loud when the tide is changing. I tested it from three rooms away from my writing desk and it could easily be heard. In that respect it could provide background music for a flash mob, which is way beyond the power of most other speakers, which are designed for personal listening on a desk or night stand.

The sound quality is also a cut above. While I have tested speakers that are better, this one is still on the short list of my favorites. The speakers are large and powerful, and they do a remarkable job of handling the high, mid and low frequency bands. As advertized the bass is pretty intense compared to ninety percent of the bluetooth speakers I have owned or tested (about fifty!)

In addition to volume and sound, this is ruggedized. I mentioned that it could compete with wave noise at the beach. It can also withstand moist and sandy environments and being banged around. It's not waterproof, but is designed to resist it.

While the product description and specs are complete I do want to highlight a few features that I personally love. First is ease of connecting this to my phone. When you turn it on it immediately beacons its presence (and announces it in a human voice.) Do a scan from your device for other bluetooth devices and this pops up immediately. A simple touch pairs and connects it. If you have an NFC-enabled phone like my Galaxy Note 3 it's even simpler. Just touch the device to the NFC logo on the speaker and you'll get a message on your screen asking if you want to connect to the speaker.

Finally, time and distance claims are accurate. This actually will play longer than most speakers. The claim is twelve hours. I had it on and playing for ten and it probably would have lasted another two hours. So say at least ten hours to set expectations. It also claims to work from 25 meters, which is significantly more than the normal 10 for bluetooth. I tested mine at about 18 meters and it did not falter - the music streamed with no breakup or dropouts.

Basically, if you want to play your music loud and still get decent sound this is the speaker for you. It has a lot of features that I did not mention (but are listed in the product description), but the defining one is sound pressure level.

The qualification I mentioned in the title is as long as this is used as a close, personal speaker the superior bass frequency response is there. Since M. Erb thoroughly covered most of the characteristics in his excellent July 24, 2014 review I am going to focus on the sound quality and a few observations.

As stated, this speaker provides high quality sound in the lower frequency spectrum as long as it's within one to three feet. Even at twenty feet the sound is excellent, but the effect of the bass diminishes. The woofer is in the bottom part of the casing and do emphasize that part of the frequency spectrum.

Although this is marketed as a 'bass machine' the high and mid range response is actually better than the bass (to my ears anyway), and the overall sound quality makes this one of the best personal speakers that I have tested. In fact, while I normally use Miles Davis' [[ASIN:B00IS4187Y Kind Of Blue]] to test speakers because it does exercise the full spectrum, for this one I used two other albums. First was Scott Lafaro's [[ASIN:B007CSETZU The Complete Live At The Village Vanguard 1961]] because Scott LaFaro's bass is prominent. That is how I arrived at my assessment of the bass response that I described above. I also tested this with a Chico Hamilton Trio album titled [[ASIN:B0089PCUT2 Jazz Essentials]] that contained a fuller range of instruments, including cello and flute. The reproduction of frequencies across the full spectrum was so spectacular that I had to give this speaker five stars.

For features and characteristics read (and watch) M. Erb's review. If you are picky about sound quality, as far as I am concerned this should be on your short list of personal speakers. It will not fill a room with sound, but you'll be able to hear every nuance if you have it near by.

Normally when I receive a review sample I can do a thorough evaluation and write a review within two days. This one took longer. The reason is that it took me a while to hear the differences in this model versus the [[ASIN:B00G4UQ6U8 Brainwavz S1 In Ear Headphones]], which also impressed me (and I also own).

After going through a pile of albums to try to understand what the product description meant by smoother bass I finally found an album that allowed me to hear it: [[ASIN:B00492ANTS Portrait In Jazz]]. When Scott LaFaro's bass came in on Autumn Leaves I started switching back and forth between this and the S1, and also hauled out some studio reference monitors. These phones are capable of going down in the 18Hz range for the low end, which is lower than most in ear monitors and phones that are usually in the 20Hz range at the low end. I am not sure my ears can discretely detect the differences between 18 and 20, but I was able to detect nuances that the lower end provided.

These also go up a little higher than more phones, which are usually in the 20 KHz range, Again, I am not sure I can truly hear sounds at 24KHz, but there is a discernible difference. I tested that end of the frequency spectrum with a few Ahmad Jamal albums since he tended towards the right side of his pianos.

One other thing that took me some getting accustomed to was the over-the-ear way of wearing these. I am use to in-ear or the old fashioned over-the-hear phones and I had to play around with these before I figured out how to place them in my ears perfectly. If you are use to over-the-ear you will probably not experience the learning curve that I did.

A few other features that I have come to expect from this brand are here: extra tips of different sizes, a hard case ([[ASIN:B00HPPL1M4 Brainwavz Hard Earphone Case]]) and a 1/4" adapter. I love the flat, tangle-free cable that is tougher than it feels. And it has an adjuster like a chin strap on a cowboy hat that aids in keeping these firmly in place with the over-the-ear way of wearing them.

This is definitely a five star set of phones (according to my way of grading, anyway), and one that I will not hesitate to recommend to fellow musicians. We tend to spend a great deal of time listening to music and these do an excellent job of reproducing it. My advice, though, is to take your time when you first get them because their true power is not immediately apparent. When you do start hearing the difference you will understand why I rated them so highly.

I received these phones as a review sample and wanted to test the claim that they are studio quality. In point of fact they are very close. What I mean by studio quality is they are neutral sounding - there is no bias towards any particular frequency band. These are fairly even on the highs, mids and lows.

Of course, if you are listening to modern music that emphasizes low frequency response with a lot of bass you may want to check out other phones that do a better job. I will say that while the frequencies are naturally divided, the separation is excellent so I am certain these phones have a crossover.

Since there are ample specs in the product description (and two video reviews at the time of this one) I will spare you a recitation of that information. I tested these using a few key albums, and also plugged the 1/4 inch connector directly into my Roland RD-300NX keyboard to hear that instrument's natural responses. Both tests confirmed that these are studio quality. However, audiophiles who want unbiased sound will also love them. I played some of my favorite test albums like Miles Davis' Kind of Blue, Ahmad Jamal's Live at the Pershing and some 20-bit mastered CDs. In all cases the frequency response in each band was perfect and the ability to hear nuances (including the natural reverb on Kind of Blue) was a treat. More importantly I heard the albums the way the engineers wanted me to hear them.

To be sure I do have other phones that are at this level of quality, but most are in a much higher price range. I did not expect to be impressed with I accepted a review sample, but not that I've had time to put these through their paces I am impressed. They are now in my practice room/music studio and there they will remain. Definitely recommended.

I received this pack as a review sample and quickly came to the conclusion that these are excellent for noise-free applications. The most critical test was when I used this cable to connect a pair of [[ASIN:B006MA9XXM Brainwavz HM5 Studio Monitor Headphones]] to my stereo. The sound was as neutral and noise free as when I used the high grade cable that came with the phones, so the claim of double shielding hold weight. I would not hesitate to recommend these to audiophiles or sound engineers.

In addition to the listening test I thoroughly inspected the physical characteristics. That revealed attention to detail like what appears to be copper cladding or gold plating on the tip, ring and sleeve portions of the connector. The barrel housing is also well constructed and is probably stainless steel. The strain reliefs on the ends are also well done and should protect the ends from internal breakdown even if you frequently handle the cable. The cable itself will stretch to a full twelve feet, but at rest is a little over a foot and a half.

What I did not test is the claim that this will fit most phones through their case. That's because the cases that I have on hand will accommodate regular cables. There is a chamfer on the barrel that houses the connector and it looks as though it will fit some of the more finicky iPhone 5 cases, but I cannot guarantee that it will for all cases.

These are top quality cables that should last a long time if properly handled and stored. If I do experience a premature failure I'll update this review to reflect that.

Note: at the time of this review this cable set is described as '3.5mm Male To 3 RCA Cable' when it's really a 3-RCA male to 3-RCA male for composite signals. My HDTV has legacy composite jacks to connect older DVD players and I am using the review sample that I received for that purpose.

I replaced it with a premium grade cable by Monster, which cost me significantly more than this one is priced at, and there is no discernible difference in video and audio quality.

The outer shield is slightly different in appearance form the standard 6 cut ones that most RCA connectors employ, but the fit of this set is as precise as others that I have used, and the integrated strain reliefs are some of the beefiest I have ever seen on any brand of RCA composite cable.

Among the reasons why I awarded this five stars is value (relatively low price with high quality construction). This set sports construction features that are not usually found in sub ten dollar cable sets (the price range at the time of this review). For example, the connectors are gold plated, and the copper wire is oxygen free. The overall cable is both flexible, but heavy duty and is not likely to fail if properly used.

My advice is if you are shopping for composite cable, consider this one before investing a lot more in a 'premium; brand that does not really outperform this one.
