Then I'll only need 5-10 minutes each week to add the relevant music to a collection for quick access.

I also use the Kindle not so much for reading, but for listening. I love the text-to-speech feature. I use it for casual reading as well as my Cisco tech books. Funky digital voice and some unusual phrasing and pronunciation, but you can't beat having it read to you while your hands and eyes are otherwise engaged in other things such as driving or crocheting :D

I have used the web feature while camping. Nothing great, but you can check email, news, Facebook and other text or mobile supported sites. I've also used it when traveling to get directions or check Yelp while on the go. Since I don't have a smart phone this is actually a huge plus! One thing to keep in mind is that image intensive sites may crash the Kindle (due to lack of memory) and you will have to reload it to clear the issue.

The music player is lacking, but for an e-reader, I guess that's expected. You can load music and it will play in the order you loaded it. You can pause and skip, but that's about it. No actual controls or playlist features.

One major feature that is currently lacking is hands free page turning. Since there is no USB driver or bluetooth support, I don't foresee this ever being available, but it is definitely something to keep in mind. I also play flute and am unable to use the Kindle to display my flute music unless it is a single page.

So, for my needs, it's great. However, if you're looking for more media support or better web access, you should look elsewhere.

This is an Asus Eee Slate EP 121-1A010 update; we've changed the rating from "Like it" to "Love it" and we're adding a couple more to the office. I chose it for a gastroenterologist friend who needed it for her medical practice. Now that patient records need to be digitized, she uses this tablet to keep track of all her business's management needs, which include patient vitals, records, and billing. In the doctor's own words:

"I log into Athena, which is our electronic medical record and practice management, and then all the info regarding a patient gets put in. So, the girls will use the tablet to populate BP, pulse, etc, past medical history, chief complaint, etc. Some of it is clicking onto specific fields and it will auto-populate with a touch. I think the ASUS Eee Slate is the perfect size screen by the way. I really like that one. The Acer (an alternate tablet which we tested) is good but, screen is small so it's difficult to maneuver over fields."

The doctor had been advised to get a Windows tablet and the ASUS fits the bill. She tried it and an Acer tablet so that she and her staff could get the feel of two different products. The Acer is considerably less expensive, has less memory, and lacks a few features that the Asus has. We had hoped to get tablets with the anticipated Windows 8 that MS announced around March 2011, but by August 8th, the anticipated release date was 2012. Failure to comply with new federal laws for digitized medical records means incurring penalties, so she wanted to have everything by September, hence these two touch tablets seemed to be the best choice as of August 2011. After nearly three months of use, it became clear that the Acer couldn't meet her needs, but the ASUS has been wonderful. The doctor and her staff can download medical templates and macros directly from her provider, Athena Health, onto a main computer or the tablet.

While her medical staff handles the initial patient consultations, the info can be transfered to or from a tablet into the office's mainframe computer, athenahealth.com, and to the doctor's own tablet via e-file or e-mail. They no longer need to transcribe handwritten information into the office's computer; it can now be done on the spot, saving time. The tablets can also be used to read Kindle books.

The ASUS has the added advantage of a wireless Bluetooth keyboard and a digital pen, which I believe can be an asset for anything that requires a signature, e.g. a prescription or an MS Office Word business letter. It also interfaces well with a wireless printer, but it does have USB ports. The ASUS also comes with a mediocre MS Office program that can be upgraded for a better version.

My initial favorites were the Apple iPad2 or a Toshiba tablet. However, neither of them comes with a Windows operating system (OS). Toshiba uses Google's Android (aka Droid) and Apple uses its own system. While you can change Toshiba's OS to a Windows OS, I wouldn't recommend it if you're not technically savvy.

Two issues for my particular hardware, the Satellite and a OCZ Agility. First there is a small bracket in my laptop that secures the optical housing to the machine with one screw underneath the memory bay. There are two screws from the laptop of adequate length to reach the original equipment optical housing though this bracket. These screws cannot reach down to the thread portion located deeper inside this caddy. Although I have probably hundreds of screws, none were both long enough and thin enough to get through the holes in the Satellite's hold down bracket to the caddy. I ended up using electrical tape to secure the bracket to the caddy. I think it will be fine.

Second, the Agility did not appear in the bios or in windows when laptop was booted. After much messing around with other drives in the caddy I finally realized that the Agility was not shoving up tight enough to the connectors. I had to push it from behind with a thick screwdriver. Success. A Vertex was not a problem nor was the mechanical drive. Just the Agility. I believe it is just a problem with this drive, probably connector board a little off but not noticeable when regular SATA and power cables are applied to it.

Last is I guess a non-issue from function but not from form. The bezel or lack thereof. Yes, it will look a little funny without a bezel. I had quite the time removing the Satellite's bezel from the optical drive but did manage it in the end. And I can still pop the optical in when needed (like when I was troubleshooting) and run it without its bezel in a pinch. YMMV

Overall OK certainly for the price. They might want to look into how deep those threads are where a hold down bracket is applied. My mfr screws certainly were not long enough. Would be nice if they could supply two in addition to the HD screws they already do. And the lack of even some sort of generic-ish bezel were the only reasons for the one star off.

First and foremost, this is a monopod, and should not be expected to perform the duties of a tripod. The two are not on the same playing field, especially if said field is not level, and the monopod's job is simply to hold the fort when a tripod can't go into battle.

Pros:
1. This monopod comes with its own little stand, and is perfectly capable of standing on its own three feet.
2. It can easily support a DSLR with a medium telephoto lens.
3. Set up is simple, requiring only unscrewing the bottom section, opening the legs and screwing the base back on securely.
4. Extends over six feet tall with two adjustable sections
5. Perfect for concert and theatre events in low or changing light, when a tripod either isn't allowed or is impractical.
6. Great for weddings and museum visits
7. You can sit with the monopod braced against your chair and your feet anchoring the legs for extra stability. (I also use a cable release)
8. Padded grip
9. Handy against attacks by stray animals in the wild.

Cons:
1. At the shortest it's still more than two feet long, and doesn't fit well in the external tripod section of smaller camera bags.
2. It's very heavy for all-day trekking around theme parks, museums, big city tours and the like.
3. No carrying case (but has a strap to fasten it on to stuff)
4. Little legs make a lot of noise when concealed (but see below)
5. A bit tricky on uneven ground if you want to use the legs

Things you can fix:
1. Needs a Quick Release head (albeit adding extra weight and cost)
2. Rattling feet can be muffled with a rubber band

Overall, I'm happy with this monopod, except perhaps for the length and weight. It does a great job when you're rushing around in crowded places where tripods fear to tread.

Amanda Richards, June 19, 2013

Pros:

1. Easy to set up - no tools required. Just attach the stainless steel/aluminum mount to the tripod socket at the bottom of the camera and tighten the thumbscrew. (And recheck ever so often that it's tightened)

2. Fits a lot more comfortably than a regular neck strap. All DSLRs should come with this type of strap. No neck burn or awkward carrying positions.

3. Can be tightened against the body by pulling on the pivot ring and camera (in opposite directions) for when you need to go hands free across some difficult terrain (or when your hands are otherwise occupied)

4. Can be worn on either shoulder or even behind your back as needed.

5. There's a locking mechanism to hold the strap in place when you're not shooting.

6. Strap adjusts itself and extends when you raise the camera to take a shot (when the locking mechanism is disengaged of course)

7. This strap is built for a man, (the women's strap has a small curve for the zaftig photographer) but it's still comfortable (and strong enough) regardless.

Cons:

1. Dangling an expensive camera and even more expensive lens
upside down,
from ONE screw,
in ONE spot,
on the bottom of the camera,
is a bit nerve-wracking. (But regular straps can malfunction also)

2. Strap could have been improved with a bit more padding.

3. Strap takes up quite a bit of space in a camera bag (but you can't have everything) For smaller bags you can detach the strap and reattach when needed in a couple of seconds.

4. Obviously you have to detach the strap when you want to use a tripod

5. No fault of the strap, but the models in the video on the product page need some instruction on how to hold a DSLR properly (LOL)

Overall, this has solved a big problem for me, as this is a much more comfortable way to carry around a heavy camera and lens for hours at a time.

Amanda Richards, January 8, 2013

I would not use this drive as a portable device as mentioned in the product description. The product is described as a Desktop external drive, and in my opinion it is too bulky to carry around in addition to a power supply cord, since it uses external power. There are smaller external drives, albeit with less storage capacity, that are better designed for portability.

Users should note that even though it might be plugged into a power outlet, it only powers up when it is connected to a computer. Once disconnected, or if the computer is shut down, the drive powers off.

Amanda Richards, November 10, 2012

What looks like a flash, acts like a flash, but is much more than your average flash?

This gadget provides a painless backup solution for businesspersons and students who can't survive without their trusty laptop/netbook/notebook and the information therein. Even for users unfamiliar with backup software, the Echo software included on the drive is a snap to use. Once the backup drive is inserted into a USB port on your computer, it will take you through some simple steps to configure the backup. You can choose the easy predefined Automatic plan or you can choose the more advanced Custom backup plan. There is a Quick Start Guide, also included on the drive, which provides a brief explanation of the options that are available.

When configuring your Custom backup profile, you can specify which file types you want backed-up. You can select ALL files, or there are some basic ones such as text, spreadsheet, presentation, music, videos, photos et al that you can select. There is also an OTHER category where you can define other file types that may be important to you, for example, zip, rar, pdf, etc. In addition, you select which folder(s) you want backed-up, set filters if required, and set the number of versions of files to keep, a useful option if you accidentally delete or modify a file. There is also the option to select an Automatic backup which activates every time you plug in your flash drive, and Live which continuously backs up your modified files to the flash drive without your intervention.

Restoring files is just a matter of clicking on the Restore menu button, selecting the files and/or folders you want restored and setting the location where to restore the files, then hit RESTORE. Alternatively, if when creating your profile, you had decided not to password protect it and encrypt it, the files can be accessed quite easily from directly on the root of the backup drive in the My Backup folder.

To backup another computer, you would have to install the software on that computer and set up another backup profile.

This version of the Lexar Echo has only 16GB of storage capacity, and is really too small to back up more than one home computer with music and video files; it can barely back up one computer, much less two or more. On the other hand, it would certainly be good for business people on the road since they will generally be using smaller files and the backup is a no-brainer.

While it has a good feel to it and the retractable connector saves losing caps, it is a bit on the `chunky' side and competes for space with other USB devices. It can also get damaged if you're not careful when moving the laptop around and it gets hit during the process, as it sticks out quite a bit.

I did not check for backup/restore speeds nor did I follow up on the 2GB of free online backup space which was offered in the setup. It appears this is no longer available at DMAILER, the backup software manufacturer; but instead I was guided to check YuuWaa online backup services.

Extremely handy for business or school use, and especially for people who have senior moments and accidentally delete or write over important files on a regular basis.

You can zoom in and out by pressing the + and - signs on top of and below the red button. The microphone will pick up and record whatever's going on at the time.

5. Playback is a one button operation.

6. Deleting your mistakes is a one button operation.

7. You can scroll through your videos by using the arrow keys to the left and right of the red button.

8. Getting it on your computer is the easiest part. With the red button facing you, pull down on the latch on the left side, and - surprise!!! Out pops a USB arm which you then connect to your computer. Once you're linked up, the Flip Video software will show you the way home. (It takes a while to pop up) Choose the option to view your videos, and agree to the terms and conditions, and then the "Muvee Video Mixing Software" begins loading. This is a one time installation. From there you can easily play, name, edit and share your videos.

9. You can also capture still shots from your videos, but you can't use these when making your movies with the software provided.

10. There is an option for making a movie, where you can arrange your edited videos, choose from a selection of six movie styles and music, or even add your own music. Choose your style, click on the "Make Mix" button, and the computer does the rest. If you're happy with the results, you can save the file.

11. The camera comes with a wrist strap, a velvet drawstring case, and also the necessary cables to connect it to your television for a bigger view. There's also a place to connect a tripod.

12. There is a "Help" feature included with the software.

Cons:
1. Being a simple "point and shoot" camera, the resolution isn't fantastic, but quite good enough for action shots. Forget detail close-ups such as words and logos - zooming in and out will just get you various degrees of blurry.

2. You'll need to be careful with background noise, as the microphone will pick up the sound of your fan or your stomach growling.

3. The video editing capability is limited to the length of the video you want to save, and the order you want to save it. There are no options for titles, fade ins or outs or any bells and whistles. If you're filming yourself giving a speech, you'll pretty much have to get it right in one complete take.

4. As with all videos, if your hands shake, you'll need to get a tripod, or you may make a lot of people seasick.

5. If you have big fingers, you may have some problems with the red button. Once your finger covers the area around the button, you'll have trouble starting and stopping the video. If you can't get it to work, you may have to use just a fingernail, because if you press anywhere other than dead center of the red button it won't start or stop.

Overall, this is a very good camcorder if used for the purpose for which it is intended. It isn't going to make you the next Stanley Kubrick, but it's a good start.

Amanda Richards, October 9, 2007

This Targus notebook case is a great way to carry around all your stuff and still look cool, professional and ready for action.

The other stuff:
1. If you have a 17" laptop, there's not enough space in the padded section to hold your power cord, but there are so many other compartments and pockets that this shouldn't pose a major problem - other than remembering where you put it. (There's plenty of space for a bottle of Ginkgo Biloba)

The one important thing to note when buying electronic equipment is that once you pop, you can't stop. Every time you think that you have the perfect system, something else comes along that you absolutely HAVE to have, which leads to something else, and so on ad infinitum.

Having bought new surround sound speakers, we needed a new DVD player, and then, naturally, a new receiver. The weight of this system is a big plus, being less than half the weight of our old one, but the new one's not as aesthetically pleasing with those shiny silver buttons.

Leaning over the shoulder of my resident techie, I can now advise as follows:

1. You cannot connect a turntable to this receiver; there are no phono inputs. Not good for those of us who still have LPs.

2. It's DVD-Audio ready for the audiophiles among us.

3. Setup is relatively easy, controlled by two buttons only: a multi control button and the input selector button. This can be irritating if you need to adjust the tone after you have finished setting up, since there are no separate bass and treble buttons, and you have to go through the setup menu again. You can however adjust the level of the surround speakers and subwoofer from the remote.

4. No onscreen display available

5. No switched AC outlets to allow you to plug in other components.

6. In addition to the receiver, the universal remote can be used to control a TV, tape, DVD player/recorder, VCR, CD player and the radio. This reduces the number of remotes you need around you. It has a weird shape that takes some getting used to, and I still use my separate remotes - guess old habits die hard.

7. Input jacks on the front make connecting camcorders, video games, etc. quite easy.

8. When listening to music or looking at a movie, there are SFC (Sound field control) modes which you can choose to enhance the sound environment. For music there are six modes (live, pop/rock, jazz, etc.), and for movies another six (action, drama, sports, etc.) However, to the untrained ear, like mine, I cannot detect a significant difference if any of these modes are selected.

Overall, the sound from this receiver is quite good, very clean, though it doesn't seem as powerful as my old receiver (a Technics SADX930). This could be due to differences in the calibration of the volume control, but since I rarely play it at very high volumes this is a non-issue. The centre channel seems a bit weak compared to the other channels, but with so many sound options to choose from and customize, it is very possible that I may have missed something and need to tweak it some more.

A very nice receiver for the price and features.

Amanda Richards, December 14, 2004

Love Love this. It is so tiny but holds so much music. I can't wait to try an audio book to see how that goes.
Good value for money. Volume slowly decreases over time. Battery life is great though.

We're working on a cabin project with a partner out in the desert and music is a must. This speaker is very useful for us. It fits in my purse and a tiny corner of a work bench when in use.

It has paired with and connected immediately with my Pixel 7Pro, a Pixel 4A, and one of the more recent Galaxy phones. The volume output is surprisingly robust for the size. We can hear all around the work site and music is clean from the speaker. We play a mix of mostly country, 80s music and some Tejano - nothing really with high bass. And the occasional audiobook or podcast sounds clear as well.

I'm using this sound bar with a 55" tv in a normal size bedroom. The TV's speakers are actually pretty good, but for some reason the volume had begun to fluctuate unexpectedly.

This sound bar corrected that issue - I've used the ARC connection via an HDMI cable and no more sudden loud spurts while watch a movie. The overall sound quality from the bar is decent. I mean, this not a famous brand or high end unit, but it is suitable for movies and tv shows in the bedroom.

The unit connected quickly and has a separate remote. My Samsung TV remote recognized this bar so I don't need to use the separate remote control at all.

These are surprisingly comfortable and that's directly related the selection of different sized ear pieces. The physical buttons are easier to use than a phone only or touch sensitive only controls.

Using these earbuds for audiobooks or music while outside doing chores is nice. The sound is crisp and clear even when my phone is 20 feet away. The noise cancelling feature works reasonably well when I'm out in the wind too.

I wanted a light, inexpensive set of earbuds for traveling. Something that lets me do a Zoom meeting on my phone or just listen to music or an audio book on the go.

These are reasonably comfortable and paired easily with both my Pixel and Note 20 phones. The sound quality id perfectly fine for my needs and if I lose this set, it's not a big deal. The battery life 2as still above 50% after a little over an hour.

Our puppy ate the original white solar powered remote for my 6 month old 55" Frame television. I have a different brand and style replacement that works, but doesn't have the pre-programmed channel buttons for Netflix, Prime and Samsung TV. I really like those instant buttons.

This remote uses 2 batteries and the back slides off to change them. Except....it's such a tight fit it was nearly impossible to remove. That's the only negative I've found over two weeks of use.

The remote did need to pair with the TV within seconds and everything worked immediately. The voice search is fine and Alexa still responds properly. The volume and channel toggles operate smoothly. It's a good replacement.

Our much loved puppy ate the expensive remote that came with my fancy Frame tv. Lesson learned for me while she's still learning her manners.

Amazingly, this generic remote control actually paired with the TV via Bluetooth on the very first try. And it works! The volume, channel, pause/play, power, and settings buttons all do exactly what the original remote did. This one requires regular batteries rather than using a solar charge. However, the rechargeable batteries are doing well so far.
I'm just using these for a television and sound bar. They are working correctly and the sound bar functions now. I think these are pricey for my simple needs.

We have a high end Sony 55" in the living room and a sub three hundred buck off brand tv in the guest room and the difference between the two is instantly noticeable - image quality and sound are in two different lanes entirely. This Samsung Frame is in the master bedroom and I am in love.

The matte screen means almost no reflective glare at night with lights on in the bedroom. That's something I did not realize bothered me about our other two tvs until there was no more glare. No matter where I look at the screen, it's clear and I don't see the reflection of my bedside lamp.

This tv does weigh more than the other two we own in the same size. I would definitely not try to move this or wall mount it alone. The box has a complete wall mount ready to install, but I don't want this that high since it's a bedroom television, so we installed the feet and set it on a table. This also comes with an old school box for connections rather than just plugging everything in directly to the television. That's a little old school, but it makes sense because they intended for the tv to be used on the wall as an art display as well and you don't want visible cables hanging off that.

As far as the art viewing goes, that's really nice if you are willing to pay for the subscription. I am not, but viewing the samples is pretty cool. This is a Google and Alexa friendly voice control set up and I do like that. The free Samsung TV app is very nice - it's sort of like Pluto TV, but proprietary to this television brand. Lots of free channels and a ton of choices at no cost. We use Netflix, Prime, HBOMax, and Paramount Plus as our paid streaming options - no cable or satellite here, just streaming. Everything works seamlessly and smoothly. My favorite thing here though, is so simple and small and I can't understand why every tv doesn't have this - the remote control is SOLAR powered!! No more buying batteries and it works well.

These are comfortable enough for my uses and the overall sound quality for music is fine. I am using these out hiking or while working around the barn on chores. The addition of a memory card is certainly useful when you don't want your phone nearby for a bluetooth music link - like when you're cleaning water troughs. Calls are fuzzy though and that was with both a Pixel 5 and a Note 20 phone, so it's the headset rather than the phones or connections. That's not really a deal breaker for me though.

These are inexpensive earbuds that actually work well for basic stuff. The buds do fit in my ears without pressure or pain after an hour.

I primarily listen to audiobooks and 80s Rock or Country music, so I don't know or care about a lot of bass. For my needs, these are working well.

I've only connected them to a Pixel phone and the range is about 20 feet line of sight before I notice any degradation of the connection.

I listen to audiobooks through the day whenever possible. I have a pair of wireless earbuds and wired versions. But my wireless get staticky once they reach a 50% charge level and that drives me nuts.

These are comfortable to wear and the sound quality is fine for books and basic music. Mostly though, the sound does not deteriorate as the battery discharges.

After almost 3 weeks with this television, I am amazed and very, very happy with it. There's a lot to like here and a couple of things that I wasn't expecting from any television.

First is the ease of set up. Our previous smart tv was a ROKU and reasonably simple to set up as well. The Google connection here means just signing in with your existing Google info and the tv uploads your existing apps. Just like moving to your new Android phone or tablet. All of our streaming apps populated and we were able to sign in without drama - HBOMAX, Prime, Paramount Plus, HULU and Netflix. We only stream and haven't used cable or satellite in 5 years, so easy app access with a new tv is important.

The 4K picture is outstanding. There's no distortion in picture quality or digital noise even from old 1940s movies. The colors are rich and full and the tv settings let you adjust to your preference as well. We've watched a lot, A LOT of tv recently and every show on all platforms has been gorgeous. Frankly, we probably watch way too much tv as a rule and that's not going to change. I've been amazed at the picture quality difference between our year old HD tv and this one.

We've connected Alexa to this tv and the voice controls work...most of the time. Using the voice control via the remote control renders better responses for sure. The tv has recognized a Fire stick, Roku Express stick, and a portable DVD player for us without any drama. We don't have a gaming system, though.... I'm considering buying one for this giant screen.

But my final show stopper moment with this television has been the sound quality. We've never had a tv that didn't require a sound bar. Until now. Despite the tv being quite thin and lightweight, the speakers still produce a deep sound quality without any tinny undertones. The settings have a calibration option for the speakers that you definitely need to do for the best sound - it works. I truly believe this is the best television we've ever owned.

I'm working on a long term volunteer project in deep West Texas in 2 different state parks. I find myself spending long periods of time working alone, away from the public and my Audible books are a joy on those days. I have wireless bluetooth ear buds of course, but the recharging is an issue if I'm out in the back country. So I always carry a pair of corded buds as backup.....and I inevitably lose them. Often.

This 8 pack is exactly what I needed. I can keep a set in my car, in the State truck, in my backpack and my purse and still have 4 replacements home. The sound quality is solid. I'm just listening to Audible audio books and some music, not trying to ferret out a french horn amidst a symphony with these. The sound is balanced and clear without static or distortion. The buds are fairly comfortable when worn for 60 to 90 minutes straight.

I wanted a small second television in our travel trailer on my side of the bed. A regular tv turned out to be too big for the space available, so I had to think outside of the norm a bit.

I settled on an under cabinet mounting with a tablet rather than a traditional, old fashioned television. That required a mount that not only folded up, out of the way, but one that rotates almost completely around. This worked perfectly!

It was super easy to install with the included screws - I think we had it up in less than 10 minutes including time to empty the cabinet first. It's holding a 10" Fire HD tablet that weighs almost nothing. I just used two adhesive hooks on the back of the tablet to attach to the mount. I'm able to stream Prime, HULU, HBOMAX, Netflix and Paramount Plus with a touch of the screen and a tilt of this mount. The best thing is the total setup for the refurbished tablet and the mount was under a hundred bucks.

I'm using this with a Samsung Galaxy View 2 tablet and a regularly television.  I wanted to share photos from my cloud on the large tv screen without a smart tv. It works just fine for my needs. The connection was smooth and clean and the photos were displayed with good clarity.

I wanted Alexa Auto in my 2006 Sequoia, but it is not equipped with bluetooth or the new tech. Fortunately, Alexa Auto comes with an AUX cable connection. This cable let me connect her to the car radio and my phone via Bluetooth to the Alexa app. Problem solved in one step.

My husband finally upgraded his 4 year old tablet to a Tab 5SE - that 10" screen is a huge improvement over his old 8 inch tablet. But of course,  a new gadget requires a new case. This one is really working well for us. It fits exactly and all the buttons are accessible. The charging port is equally easy to use. I love that this case has built in rails to prop up the tablet so you can watch Netflix etc.

It seems like there are never enough power strips in the house. Between the TV's, phone chargers, tablet and laptop chargers, sound bars, air purifiers, fans, lamps etc etc, we're always short on outlets.

This power strip fits nicely the bedroom and the cord is a nice length for reaching the beside table. It handles two phone chargers, a table lamp and the tablet charger without any problems.

I decided against installing this radio myself for reasons. We hired a local shop to do it. It seems to be done correctly and everything is working as it should.  The 6.8" screen is big enough to see and make the choices I want driving. It's working with my LG phone via bluetooth and that was the primary reason I wanted a new stereo in the older Sequoia. We'll see how it fares as time goes by.

This is the second bluetooth adapter I've tried and it's the best one. It stays plugged in despite bumpy roads and that's definitely a plus. I paired it with my LG V40 phone and for 3 months it hasn't forgotten my phone and connects automatically every time I get in the car.

The sound quality is fine for music and audio books on the go. The volume can be adjusted three ways- on my phone, on the car's radio control or on this unit directly. It also fast charges my phone and an LG Stylo 4 which is always welcome. My only complaint is the sound quality of hands free calls. On my end, they are fine. But on the other end, there is a noticeable buzz or tunnel type sound. Not a deal breaker though since I only use it for music and audio books 95% of the time.

As a rule, I prefer over the ear headphone style for comfort. But there are circumstances when ear buds are safer and more practical - like riding horses. These buds are better than expected and suit my needs pretty well.

The case is the actual charger and you can charge the buds without the case being plugged in as long as it has residual power. You do need to put the buds into the case at the precise angle or they don't charge. These do come with small, medium and large ear pieces so you can get the correct fit for your ears. I do wish the right and left markers were more obvious and easier to see.

I listen mostly to audio books and country, 80s or classical music. I don't use or care about heavy bass in earbuds at all, so I cannot speak to that performance quality. The do fine with the 80s pop and hard rock and behave nicely with classical music as well. There is an option for noise cancellation - called Through Sound. It actually works and there is a very noticeable difference when it's on. I'm pretty impressed by that. I do not like having to put yet another app on my phone to set these up and get full functionality out of the ear buds.

I love my wireless earbuds in specific circumstances, but there are times when I don't want to worry about batteries or bluetooth etc. I'm using these corded earbuds for basic stuff like listening to audio books and some music while walking dogs mostly. I've been using them with my LG V40 phone and an older Samsung tablet with no problems.

The sound is clean and clear and I have not noticed any buzzy feedback. The buds come with additional ear piece covers do you can the fit you need. I'm not expecting fine musical depth or clarity....seriously, these are just no name cheap ear buds. They are fine for that. The claims of noise cancellation are weak at best. They do not actively cancel outside noise, just soften it a bit as you listen to your book.

My old power strip finally quit and I replaced it with this one for a TV, sound bar, streaming box and a small dehumidifier. I like the cable on this one. It's very well made and doesn't look like it will fray from bending. Using it with the TV, sound bar and streaming box for a few hours consecutively  is fine - nothing gets hot and everything works fine.

We have two dumb TVs and like it that way. The Rokus work perfectly with them and all's well.  However, I wanted to do a slide show of photos on the big screen from my tablet and that required a work around. This adapter fixed the problem. The USB type C works with both our Samsung tablets and the HDMI end fit properly on the TV. I was able to do my photos on the big screen and everyone could see them comfortably.

I keep a sensor at the point where the driveway opens to the barn area so I know if someone is arriving while I am doing horse stuff. Our old one lasted several years, so I hope this one lives up to that standard.

This one just went on the same fence post hook as the old one. The sensor is about 38 feet away just inside the barn door overhang - so it's a very short distance. (I can't speak the 500 foot claims)This system allows you to choose from several different alert sounds and that's nice... Our old one had a single shrill shriek that got old fast. So far this is working correctly and doing the job without problems.

I love my Primetime tablet and have used it daily for two years. My old screen protector cracked after a dog knocked it off the sofa. So this one is the replacement. It was easy to install and fits exactly as it should. There's no clarity or touch sensitivity loss with the protector on the screen. I only see on bubble and it's hidden by the edge of the case, so I'm happy.

We cut the cord in 2016 and haven't looked back once. We stream Prime, Hulu, and DirecTV Now for a quarter of the old cable bill. My only issue is the inability to get our four local channels - ABC, FOX, CBS, and NBC. I tried a very expensive antenna and it brought in only Telemundo...we have zero interest in that.

This one is very thin and doesn't require an electric connection. Just connect it to the tv and scan for channels. After trying four different locations and rescanning each time, this antenna is better than the other one. We now get the Telemundo AND CBS and Fox. Still no NBC or ABC, but an improvement. The signal is clear even on a rainy day.

As a rule, I don't particularly care for in ear earbuds, I usually choose the traditional headphones instead. These come with different size ear pieces so I was able to get the most comfortable fit I could. They aren't bad and I've been able to wear them for an hour at a time with no real discomfort.

I had no trouble connecting these to my phone and using them working around the barn and horses. The sound quality is good for my needs. I mostly listen to audio books and a mix of country and classical music. Bass isn't a thing really for me. The clarity of sound is decent for Beethoven and current composers like Hans Zimmer.

I've gotten a couple of hours at a time without needing to recharge, but I haven't tried to run them down fully. The charging storage box is very handy. The earbuds can be stored and kept clean and charge at the same time - clever. box

We have a awesome Bose 500 soundbar for our living room TV that connects via digital optical cable only. And we have a low end projector that only has the RCA cable connections which means it can't talk to our soundbar. So we rarely use the projector because it's tiny speaker is essentially useless.

I managed to get this converter set up and working between the soundbar and the projector. It's not perfect or as clear as the tv to soundbar connection, but it works. We can watch a summer movie outside on the closed garage door and hear it now....that is a win. The nieces were here and we watched The Black Stallion outside to their utter delight.

We installed the Ubiquiti Rocket M9 Wireless Access Point to create a separate WiFi network in a second building on the property. I don't know all the technical details on how that whole system gets created etc - it is complicated and required a legit pro to set up. However, the Rocket M9 didn't come with external antennas and I didn't care to spend a bunch of additional money for their brand. Instead, we got this antenna. It works perfectly and fit immediately for about a third of the cost. The signal in the building is strong and unwavering and I'm able to stream Netflix etc on the tv when I'm working in there.

We've never had a projector before and this is a reasonable beginner/introductory projector. It helped us realize that we're not really projector people for a couple of reasons. It works best in a completely dark room or outside with no residual daylight or street lights. We found the best picture came from using the the included screen out on the patio around 9pm. The picture wasn't bad, but it certainly wasn't really 1080p using the Roku stick. Going outside in the summer here for a movie is a cute idea, but this is Texas and it's just too humid and miserable for that.

The projector has speakers built in, but they are small and the sound is tinny. You can connect a sound bar if yours uses the RCA type cables - niether of my bars do. They only use HDMI or Digital optical line and the projector only has one HDMI port and no optical audio line. So we're just stuck with the built in speakers. I'm not unhappy with this unit, but I don't see us using it often at all.

This is a neat gadget. It breaks apart so you can use it in multiple ways. I just need the original tower for the living room TV set up with the streaming sticks, tv, sound bar and router equipment. So far it is working just fine.

I have a pair of the Masters & Dynamic Leica edition and I absolutely love them even after almost a year. Lately though, my husband has been skulking about wearing them so trying these out was a no brainer. I've used these MW50s for three weeks now and I actually like them better.

First, the rich saddle color leather is really beautiful and there's no mistaking these headphones for some random pair. Second, they connected via Bluetooth to my LG V40 phone, my old Sony Xperia phone and two different Samsung tablets easily and quickly. Third is the excellent battery life on these. I've literally listened to music and my Audible audiobooks for three hours at a time for four days in row before recharging them. That includes getting a couple of calls. The fit is the main reason I prefer the MW50 phones over the Leica edition. These can go on or over the ears and since I have small ears, the on ear option is very comfortable for me for hours. No cauliflower ear and the heat build up is slower.

The sound quality is excellent and clear without distortion or fuzziness. I listen to a little of everything - country, classical, old rock etc. I can clearly discern the French horns in classical music as well as the background banjo in some old country music. I don't know about the quality of heavy bass with these simply because I don't listen to heavy bass music. Audiobooks with full production recordings, are clear and crisp - I can detect background sound effects comfortably without any fuzziness or distortion. Bottom line is these are worth that eye opening price if you use them every day and appreciate style as well as function.

I have the 25 foot length so we could connect a tv directly to the router. The tv was losing WiFi signal since it's several rooms away from the router - we only stream and don't have cable, so a clean, clear internet connection is a must.  This cable was easy to use and run through a hallway wall with little drama. It's flat and that makes a difference. I haven't noticed any distortion of signal or buffering and it fixed the lost signal problem.

I have a very good pair of Bluetooth Sony earphones with pretty good noise cancellation, but I wanted a second set that could be used with a regular 3mm plug with my phone. Traveling brings enough aggravation without worrying about battery life on one more gadget.

These are very comfortable on the ears for an hour or two while listening to an audio book and my ears don't get hot. These are light enough not to cause cauliflower ear either. I tested the noise cancellation feature both at home with the tv and in a semi truck idling. Those trucks are pretty quiet inside compared to standing next to one outside, but the noise is still there and it impedes sleep if you're not used to it. I'm pretty pleased with how well these block external noise - it's an absolute difference and a little better than my Sonys.

Music is a pleasure with these also. There are adjustments to increase bass etc if you're so inclined. My primary use though is audio books. The full production Audible Originals with a full cast and sound effects are especially nice with these headphones - you can hear the background noises and details clearly and not the dog barking next door. I find myself reaching for these almost every day lately.

These Chromebooks are a weird hybrid of tablet and real laptop. They don't do everything can full laptop does, but they do more than a simple tablet. Oddly enough, there is a place for these. This is the second one we've had in the last few years.

This one is very light and easy to grab and use in the armchair or while on the road in the passenger seat. The screen is vibrant and the colors are true when watching a movie or looking at your photos. The beauty of a Chromebook is having super easy access to everything stored in your existing Google cloud account - photos, books, passwords, contacts, email, etc. This syncs exactly like your phone and tablets do so you can switch between machines and still keep current.

I've been pleased with the battery life on the Acer. It can go with light use and sleep mode a couple of days before needing to be charged. It has no trouble connecting to and staying connected to our WiFi even outside on the patio. I've connected my Bluetooth headphones and watched a movie with it and it works fine. I like this and find I'm grabbing it more often than I thought I would.

Sometimes, I like to listen to my audio book in bed while my husband watches TV. In order to avoid disturbing him, I use a fancy pair of noise cancellation earphones that vost several pretty pennies. They work well, but can feel heavy after an hour or two.

This set is a decent substitute that I won't feel bad about breaking/dropping etc. They are extremely light and don't have noise cancellation, but that's fine. The fit is decent and the ear covers are soft and don't feel hot. The sound quality is better than expected - audiobooks are clear and clean. I listened to a bit of country and classical music with these and the music sounds right, but not quite as pure as with my Bose headphones - of course, that's not a fair comparison. Still, these are a good option for basic stuff.

There's a lot to love here with the Bose 500. We have a Denon Soundbase w/ Bluetooth Streaming Audio in our master bedroom and a Bose Solo 15 Series II TV Sound System in the living room - both are from 2015. I'm replacing the Denon unit with this Bose 500 for several reasons, but primarily for significantly better sound quality and Alexa integration.

This is connected to a 2014 Samsung smart TV via the HDMI port. I had no issues connecting the sound bar to the Bose Music app (be sure you get the correct app from Google Play). Next you find the sound bar with the Alexa app and link your Alexa account to this machine. All I had to do for tv sound was turn off the TV speakers through the tv settings and press the tv image button on the Bose remote. Be sure to have 2 AAA batteries on hand because they don't include them for the remote.

You plug in the included headband and use the app to fully calibrate the best sound in your room by sitting in five different locations and letting the headband and sound bar talk. This takes about 6 minutes and it's definitely a step worth doing. The sound from this Bose is amazing - playing Beethoven or Hand Zimmer's soundtrack from Hannibal is immersive and gorgeous. The television is equally good - you can use the app to set the tv sound to dialogue centric for a talk show or regular for movies. You can also adjust the settings for the sound to increase/decrease bass and treble and to move more to the center or sides of the projection speakers. Once you get it set up exactly to your preferences, it can feel like a movie theater without the volume blasting you away. I'm especially loving rewatching Firefly with the Bose 500. The app also let's you do 6 preset favorite music streaming stations from Tune In, Amazon, Spotify and another service.

As to the Alexa functionality... This is actually pretty good with two glaring faults. The sound bar is always listening for the wake word like the Echos do and there's a privacy button as well. I have noticed a tiny lag on a few requests, but it's not constant. I've been getting a weird message telling me that this unit is not compatible with my Alexa routines, then it performs the routine perfectly. (For example, I say good morning and Alexa turns on our bathroom lights, the bedside lamps and gives me the weather) It's a bizarre glitch, but as long as the routines are completed, I don't care.

The first real problem is this unit cannot link to your other Echo units in a music everywhere group - I'm not sure if that's a Bose issue or an Amazon proprietary issue because our Harmon Kardon Alexa speaker cannot be linked either. This is a shame, but not a deal breaker for me, but it's still an issue. The thing that does aggravate me is that this unit is unable to connect to and read my Audible audio books. I get a message that says it is not compatible with Audible at this time. The work around is simply to use Bluetooth and stream my book via my phone or tablet. That's ridiculous with Alexa integrated into the sound bar. This may not bother anyone else, but I listen to audiobooks more than I read now and having that full body, room filling crisp audio is a great thing.

Bottom line for us is that we love this sound bar for television viewing and music. It's sleek and modern and just does it's job. In some ways, the Alexa integration isn't complete, but the basics are there for most functions. It's definitely an improvement over the old Denon box we used to have and it's even better than the Bose Solo 15 in our living room.

I normally avoid in ear earbuds and use wireless headphones or do without. My ears are small and most earbuds hurt within minutes, but I have one really inexpensive set that works ok, but if I'm outside working in the horse barn, they can get sweaty and slippery. These are far better than I expected.

They come with three different size ear bud attachments so you can get the right fit - the smallest set fits me well and they don't pinch or hurt even after an hour of wearing them. The over ear hook isn't hard and it's thin enough to fit over each ear love when with my glasses on. I work with horses and the associated barn chores so that means sweat and lots of movement which can be a problem with earbuds. These have impressed me. After daily use for a week, they haven't fallen off, slipped out of place or lost the connection to my phone despite sweating, shoveling, riding and high heat.

The sound quality is fine for my needs. I listen to mostly audiobooks and some classical music while out with the horses. I can clearly hear the violins vs a harp or French horn without distortion. The only real complaint is when I get a call. I can hear the caller clearly, but they say I sound like I'm in a tin can.

I have the Jabra 35 headset also and this one is noticably different with regard to the quality of phone calls, but that's really the only material difference I can find in my day to day use. The other unit does offer some noise cancellation effects that this one doesn't have and people you call can definitely tell the difference. My husband said that he could hear background noise much more clearly when I called him from this 15 than with the 35.

As far as battery life, this thing is really solid. I've used for three hours on two different days without recharging between days. I primarily use it to listen to audiobooks while I'm doing my barn chores and checking fence lines. I have noticed that I'm pretty limited with the distance I can stray from my physical phone before this headset begins to stutter to lose signal - it seems to be about 20 feet with my Sony Xperia phone.

I like the idea of a single ear microphone and little speaker for when I'm out at the horse barn or riding. This unit is significantly better than a really old one I had several years ago. It paired with my Sony Xperia phone in moments without any trouble.

I mostly use this for listening to audiobooks while I do barn chores and the occasional phone call. The sound is decent with calls, I haven't had trouble hearing anyone clearly. The audio books are clear and the volume is fine for my needs - if I were trying to use this in a moving car, it might be a bit too low. My husband says that he can hear me fine on the other end, but he does get more background noise compared to when I just call directly through my phone.

I do think my big Bluetooth headphones have better range than this unit away from my physical phone. I can set my phone on the gate post and ride in the big arena and never lose the signal with the headphones, but this one stutters a bit after I get 20 feet away. I'm not a huge fan of the ear hook - I have small ears and getting any sort of earbuds to fit comfortably can be tricky. This fits, but it takes some finagling to get it just right. In the end, I think my husband will take possession of this for his daily use on the road - it definitely fits his physical ear better.

I'm not an audiophile by any means, but I do appreciate excellent quality recreation of certain types of music and full cast production audiobooks. I don't like earbuds for more than a few minutes at a time for a number of reasons so I try to always have a good set of wireless headphones around. My older Sonys are very good, but beginning to show their age after three years of regular, reasonably hard use. I think these will serve nicely as replacements.

The form factor here is just as nice as the actual function and that's not always the case with high dollar electronics. The materials are very nice and put together flawlessly - the entire unit is really gorgeous. These are actually quite heavy in the hand, yet balanced so perfectly that I don't notice the weight at all wearing them. The ear pieces are attached with magnets to the arch piece of you can remove them for cleaning or swaps in the future. The lambskin is very soft and doesn't cause excess heat build up for my ears.

Pairings with my Sony Xperia phone, my Samsung tablet and a Fire tablet were all easy and painless. I've used these headphones for streaming music via Amazon, Pandora and my own stuff from my cloud files plus Audible books for a couple of weeks now. I'm currently using them on vacation right now with the included travel case - they fold up a bit and the charging cable & 3mm direct connect cable fit in the case as well. Sound quality is excellent as well here for my types of music - primarily classical, country, and 80s pop. I can clearly hear the French horns, flute, or soft cellos in Hans Zimmer compositions or a Beethoven concerto. Aretha Franklin sounds great with these BTW. (I can't speak to thumping bass reproduction because I detest that style and don't listen to it.)

My husband travels constantly with his Samsung tablet and he's dropped it once in a different case with zero damage. However, I've met him and seen the havoc he can wreak on electronics, so the Ottorbox cases are a requirement here.

This one fits correctly and the buttons work. The case adds significant bulk to an otherwise thin tablet, but it's worth it for real protection. The corners are well buffered and bumping it on the car door or a piece of heavy equipment shouldn't damage your tablet at all. He's noticed a little loss of touch screen responsiveness with it on, but not enough to stop using the case.

Sometimes you just need a super basic pair of ear buds that aren't fancy or expensive. I have a pair of high-end, very pricey Bluetooth over the ear headphones for use in the house. But I don't like wearing them working out at the farm or riding horses.

These are very light and work fine with my LG V10 phone for music and audio books. The buds have three different size ear pieces - my ears are a bit small and the small ones fit comfortably. Using these while shoveling horse stalls was nice and the thin cord just tucked away in my jacket pocket. I much prefer doing chores while listening to a book and these allow me not to worry if I drop them or they get damaged.

I have the Wi-Fi enabled leak detector not one of the outlet plugs. It's a pretty simple set up. Put in the batteries, download the app, sync to your WiFi and set it where you need it. I'm using an LG V-10 Android phone with this and have had no problems.

I have it behind a toilet which shares a wall with the big hot water heater - if we're going to have a leak, that seems like the most likely location. I tested the sensors with a small amount of water on a level countertop and it worked correctly. The sensors emit a very loud squeaker and my phone beeped an alert as well. I don't think you could hear the alarm if it's out in the garage though. So far I haven't had any problems with it.

As an avid fan of Alexa, I am delighted to have this Harman Kardon Alexa speaker. I've had my original Echo since the first week they released the initial invitation to buy and have since added a Dot and Alexa controlled thermostats, dining room lights, Fire TV sticks and plugs through out the house. This unit was meant to enhance the music sound quality from Alexa and expand our Alexa listening group and work with the living room television.

The speaker itself is considerably larger than my original Echo - wider and heavier. The lights on this are brighter as well - when playing music at night or listening to a book, you can leave the light on and it works as a night light. You can also turn the light off if you prefer. Setting this up takes a bit longer than my Echo or Dot - it's slower making the initial WiFi connection, but once you link to Amazon via the Alexa App, you're good to go. It connects via Bluetooth to both my LG V10 phone and my Samsung tablets without drama.

This unit is significantly louder at every volume setting than the original Echo and makes the Dot sound like she's whispering. I have this in our formal living room where we have 30 feet tall ceilings, grass cloth covered walls and an enormous open space - the room was designed for correct accoustics with my Grandmother's grand piano and music simply sounds beautiful in here. The Harman Kardon Alexa sits on a table where the piano used to be and the sound at volume 4 simply envelopes you no matter where you are in the room. Set the volume to 6 and I can hear my book or music two rooms away almost as if it's floating through the halls. The sound quality is excellent and playing Beethoven or opera or country music renders each instrument precisely from tiny flutes to cellos and twangy fiddles. I'm immensely pleased at the improvement from the Echo to this for just music.

The reason for the one star deduction is because I thought/expected the Harman Kardon to by fully, 100% integrated with Alexa. It is not. This unit cannot be linked to the Fire TV sticks, meaning that I cannot use it to verbally control the living room television. It cannot be linked to my Echo and Dot units. That means we can't include the Harman Kardon speaker in our multi room group so the same song/book can be heard throughout the house. We cannot do the Drop In skill where Alexa acts as an intercom system for multiple rooms. There are a couple of other skills this speaker isn't able to perform simply because it doesn't speak to the Amazon Alexa products. If they can correct this glaring deficiency, then this would be a five star product and one i would consider buying for the guest suite and master bedroom. As a stand alone Alexa unit, this is a top notch choice, but if you want to link to your existing Echo, you can't do so.

I have the grey TrackR Pixel and I am using it on our spare garage door opener. It's the opener we give to houseguests to use while they are here and on more than one occasion, it's gotten misplaced. Hopefully, this TrackR will cut down on aggravation of hunting down the opener n the future.

Once you load the TrackR app on your phone, it gives you pairing instructions via Bluetooth and you're ready to go. You have to allow the location permission in the app for this to work. There's a large button to press for location of the TrackR and you can make some small customization of the alert sound.

Actual use is a bit limited. My TrackR can't be found or alerted once I get more than roughly, twenty feet away from it. If you know your misplaced item is in a specific area this might not be a problem. However, if you have it on a key and dropped it without realizing it, you may be in trouble. The crowd source search option might work well in a large city, but in our small town, there aren't going to be many folks using these gadgets....much less within twenty feet of a dropped garage door opener out in the wild. For my needs this will work fine though.

I have had my main Echo since the first days after the initial invitation to buy was sent out. I absolutely love Alexa and use her for tons of things daily. - she lives in the hallway between the living room and kitchen where we spend the most time. I added the Dot a month ago to bring the Alexa functions into our master bedroom.

The Dot is as easy to use as the big Echo and now that the two can be connected, we have music throughout the house at the same time. I also like the intercom skill so we can talk to each other across the house quickly. My one dislike is the tinny sounding small speaker n the Dot. I've grown so accustomed to the balanced, clean sound from the big Echo that the Dot sound quality was a let down with music. However, reading me the news, ordering Starbucks, reading my audio books, working as an alarm clock or intercom is smooth and works just fine. I especially like being able to control our tv with Alexa voice commands - we cut the cable cord and stream via Prime, Netflix and Hulu Live and Alexa has made searching for a specific show much more simple.

After three price increases in two years from Suddenlink, we said Enough and cut the cord to streaming only. We had two Fire Sticks already, but needed something for the living room television. I picked up the Roku Express plus at a local store and in less than five minutes had it connected and working. So very easy.

I'm amazed at how much we've been missing by being tethered to cable! There's just a plethora of free tv and movies out there. The Roku essentially just gathers a ton of the options and puts them in one spot for you. You do have to activate most the big time channels through a paid service like DirectTV Now - TBS, NBC, Bravo, AMC, A&E etc. All require an activation and verification to watch vua the apps.

The remote is small, but feels sturdy and is simple to use. No getting lost in a jillion random buttons. My only complaint is the need for a second remote control for volume. We use sound bars for the 55 and 65" TV's and the Roku remote isn't set up for volume. Not a deal breaker by any means, just make sure you have another way to control volume. We're using the DirectTV Now cheapest option and the HULU LIVE beta for the first two months and then we'll keep the one that has been used most and drop the other. One thing I noticed immediately is with Roku (and the Fire Sticks) the 1080p picture on our big Samsung is much cleaner and prettier than when we had the cable service - we've used only the HDMI connection for years. I'm extremely pleased that we finally made the leap to streaming.

I rarely use ear bud type earphones because they always hurt my ears. I prefer traditional over the ear, cushioned earphones as a rule. However, there are times when the extra bulk is a problem - like on horseback.

These have a couple of different size ear pieces and I have been able to get the fit adjusted enough to wear them comfortably for a couple of hours straight. The sound is good with classical music and country. I don't do the whole extra bass type of thing, so I cannot comment on that aspect. I can clearly hear the French horns, clarinets and background piano in several different pieces of music.

My issue here is that these don't connect by Bluetooth easily to every device. It took multiple tries to connect to my LG V10 phone, they never connected with my husband's Sony Xperia phone or my Android tablet, but they did connect to my Samsung tablet after two tries. These devices are all current and have updated software.

I ha a pair of Bluetooth headphones that I love for audio books around the house, but now and then the battery will die just at a climatic point in my book. I have to stop and recharge them and switch to the Echo which means anyone else has to hear my book as well or... be tethered to the short cord and plug the in.

The ten foot length here makes being tethered a little more bearable. I can listen and fold laundry or paint my nails etc That's just not as easy with the typical 4 or 6 foot cords. This cable works very well at charging my Sony headphones, a regular phone and a tablet. Definitely handy to have an extra Micro USB cable in a super long length hanging around.

I finally had to replace my last glass screen protector after a year of hard use. This one fits perfectly with no gaps or uncovered spots - the front camera lens and speaker cut outs are precise. I am really pleased with how easy this installed, I got this on my phone with zero air bubbles on the first try. The glass doesn't effect my touchscreen or the clarity of the screen at all.

I purchased my Fire 10" almost a year ago after having used my Fire 8" for 18 months previously. This tablet is surprisingly light considering the large size and it is thinner than my Fire Fire tablet.

I am really happy with the larger screen. Watching a movie or even just shopping and surfing websites is a nice experience. Better than lugging my laptop from room to room. My only real complaint is that the screen definition on my old Fire Hd was significantly better than this one.

I can use my tablet outside on the back deck because the WiFi reception on this tablet is stronger than my older Fire. I have also been really pleased with the battery life. I use this tablet daily throughout the day for email, surfing, games, record keeping for various projects, review writing, and of course, videos from time to time. I charge it over night and it rarely drops below 30%. I do have a memory card and back up my photos from both tablet and cell phone to the cloud with no problems. Bottom line is this is a nice tablet for basic use and it also travels well.

I bought my Bose Solo 15 at another online retailer during a one day sale for a price that made it irresistible and after a month, I am happy that I did it. We have two 55" televisions and the one in our master bedroom has the Denon sound base under it and that unit has simply been outstanding. I was actually looking to just buy a second Denon for the living room tv and chose this Bose unit due to the one time sale and the Bose reputation.

This unit sits directly under our 55" Vizio smart tv and connects with the digital audio optical cable - just like the Denon base. I turned off the tv's physical speakers and let the Bose take over. The sound is full and significantly improved over the thin tv speakers. The unit shines when watching movies that have lots of rich soundtrack music and when you use the Dialogue button to soften background sounds and highlight conversation type dialogue.

The Bluetooth connected with my LG V10 phone and my fourth generation Fiire tablet immediately, allowing me to play music and my audio book through the Bose. Very nice extra functionality - the Denon does this as well. The Bose includes a universal remote control that requires some effort to set up correctly and completely. However! Once the cursing and hair pulling was over, I got it done. The Bose remote now operates our television, the Bose base, and our TiVo/cable box exactly as the cable remote does.

My one star deduction is because the only way to use the Bose Solo is with their included remote control. There are no physical buttons on the machine and that strikes me as a real design flaw. If you break or lose this proprietary remote you cannot even turn the Bose on or off, much less actually use it for sound. At least the Denon sound base can be operated manually or trained to respond to other remote controls with three steps. For me this Bose Solo is worth the price I paid (under three hundred bucks) and it is equal to the Denon in sound quality. But for overall value and ease of use, the Denon is the five star product.

Honestly, I have wanted a pair of good Sennheiser headphones for years, but I couldn't justify it to myself - I mean we have a Denon sound base that connects via Bluetooth and Alexa for music, so a personal pair of headphones seems like a selfish indulgence. OMG. Do it. Be selfish. I have been wearing these things for days now every chance that I get and falling in love with music all over again.

First thing, I must correct a misstatement in an earlier review - the HD 579 are NOT noise cancellation headphones. They do not have that technology and are not intended to, not marketed as such and I double checked with Sennheiser directly to be sure. It might be easy to mistake the beautiful sound quality and encapsulation of the sound for noise cancellation at first - simply because the headphones fit very well and at an upper volume, external noise doesn't readily intrude.

The fit is far more comfortable than I remember headphones being. The band is nicely padded and adjustable and the ear cups are very soft, thick and they fully cover your ear without any pinching. I have worn these for thirty minutes and up to three hours consecutively in vary increments, every day for five days now and never had cauliflower ear. Nor do my ears get hot. I'm using these with my Fire Tablet, my LG V10 phone and Sceptre 55" television playing music through our cable provider's music stations. The connection plug is tight and the cord has proven to be long enough for use in bed at night while reading, on the sofa reading & it rolls up to put in my pocket while wandering around cleaning house and doing barn chores.

As to the quality of the music.... simply outstanding. Far better than I really expected. One of my favorite soundtracks is from the movie Hannibal by Hans Zimmer. It has a mix of pure classical and opera. The HD 579 phones let me hear the French horns and the soft build of the clarinets as crisp and clearly as the big cellos and trumpets in other, louder movements. Simple acoustic vocal pieces from James Taylor, Tracy Chapman and Paul Simon are beautifully rendered and you can appreciate the realism of a live performance. These headphones are very nice and I wish I had bought something like them long ago, but now that I have these, I won't be far from them and I definitely will be grabbing them every time I want music, which is daily.

You can never have enough good coaxial cable around the house. Between multiple televisions, cable boxes, DVD players, streaming boxes, surround sound set ups etc something always needs to be connected.

I was trying to rearrange the guest room and pulled too hard on the cable from the wall causing a short or something where it connects to to cable box. The replacement offered locally was only 12 foot long....not helpful. This one is 25' long and I was able to get a friend to help me swap the bad one out in the wall with the new one without a call to the cable company. I'm very pleased with the quality of the Amazon Basics line - it works perfectly with no degradation of signal and was easy to twist into the box.

I bought this television (I double checked the exact model number to be positive that t I am reviewing the correct one) used at an estate sale in January and it's been used daily in our master bedroom every since. The color and clarity of the picture is simply wonderful. In comparison to our brand new Sceptre 55" 1080p tv in the living room and the 3 year old Samsung in the guest room, this Vizio has the prettiest picture and best refresh rate. The Samsung has the best native sound though without a sound bar enhancement.

This Vizio is our only Smart Television and I have a Firestick on the living room tv. As of today, June 16, 2016, the Amazon app and others are all working just fine through the television's remote control with the direct access buttons. Connecting this tv to our wifi network did take several attempts and I had to update the firmware twice before it would connect and hold the connection for more than 48 hours. (To be honest, I have no idea if the former owner every actually used the internet connection so it may not have been updated before I got it) Since January, I have had no trouble with the connection or streaming. We do have a super fast internet service and a dual band router with this tv as the only thing typically streaming on one band.

My one star deduction is the tiny receiver area for the remote control. If you are using the actual remote rather than a universal one for the cable box, you have to aim directly at the very tiny eye in the far left bottom corner and it can take a couple of tries to hit it just right from across a big room. This drives me nuts when I'm streaming from Amazon Prime and need to pause the show quickly or try to flick through the selections. However, I would totally buy another Vizio tv again in the future if the new ones are as good as this two year old used one has been - I've definitely gotten my hundred fifty dollars worth out of this one.

In comparison to my Toshiba Satellite 15" with similar specs, this ASUS is about equal - there are definitely some things I like better about the ASUS for everyday use and a couple of small quibbles that bother me. First off the computer itself is about the same weight as my Toshiba so carrying it around is exactly the same and it fits in my existing laptop sleeves and bags. It does have a DVD tray so you can play movies & music and burn discs as needed (as does my Toshiba), but a lot of laptops don't offer this anymore, so this is a definite plus.

I do really like that the ASUS comes a lot cleaner out of the box than my Toshiba - almost no bloatware pre-installed. The basic Windows 10 and you can don't have to spend 30 minutes messing around with a bunch of garbage you don't want and won't use anyway. Additionally, the ASUS boots up about 20 seconds faster from off than my Toshiba and again from the sign in screen, the ASUS is still faster. The screen is very pretty and clear with a variety of images and video - keep in mind that it's NOT a touchscreen. I've been averaging about 6 hours of use with the battery before it hits the 30% mark - that is net surfing, watching some random videos, and mostly word processing. Leaving it on in sleep mode with no use - it went almost 4 full days before needing a charge. The wifi connects immediately and I've had zero issues with it dropping out either inside or out on the back deck.

I really like the keyboard and the overall shape of the frame on this particular laptop. My Toshiba has the keyboard just open and exposed and what happens is that the heels of my hands tend to slip upwards as I type or bump the space bar. Or my thumbs slide into the mousepad area and now my cursor has bounced someplace new & I'm typing in the wrong spot. The ASUS keyboard is slightly lowered and has a border around it - for me anyway, this design is MUCH easier to type with. (See the photo.) The shape of the overall frame is better on the ASUS than the Toshiba as well. The rounded corners and edges on the ASUS don't poke into your wrists after an hour of writing or research.

My quibbles seem small on the surface, but after almost three weeks of use, they are aggravating me. First - the ASUS doesn't keep time as well as the Toshiba. It's off by 2 full minutes. (See the photos) I've checked both a couple of times and set them manually at the same moment and within 24 hours, the ASUS has lost 2 minutes - it never loses more than that though. Second - The charger is smaller than every other one I have for the other two laptops and the Chromebook in this house. The other three are standard size, but the one on the ASUS is a tiny bit smaller and thus you can't use another charger for this laptop in an emergency. Third - the speakers on the ASUS don't sound quite as full as the ones on my Toshiba. Of course... no built in speakers on a laptop are really meant for full music enjoyment.

My bottom line is that at this price point, this is a nice machine and will do almost anything you can want with regard to basic internet surfing, movie watching, office work and the like. This is not a gamer's computer and it's not meant to be. But as a regular, go to every day laptop, it's a pretty good one. I want to give it 4 1/2 stars.

I bought this television new from wally world on one day sale for under three hundred bucks and it has turned into an excellent purchase that I would have been happy with had I paid full price for it. We have the 50" unit and it was extremely easy to unpack, attach the included swivel stand, and place it on our entertainment center by myself. The entire tv weighs around 20lbs maybe - it's light enough for me to pick it up without strain. There are three HDMI outlets, a single USB outlet, the usual RCA plug-ins, the cable connection, and a digital audio connection for use with a sound bar.

The picture is clear and sharp and easy to adjust for our personal tastes with regard to color temperature, contrast, and brightest etc. There is no stuttering or shadowing watching sports or other fast moving live action. We have it connected to our cable box and a DVD player through the HDMI cables and the Amazon Fire Stick on the USB - all work correctly and are easy to swap between.

My one complaint is the native speakers are tinny and thin sounding, but that seems to simply be a fact of life with large flat screen televisions. I bought the Denon DHT-T110 TV Speaker Base with Bluetooth aptX Streaming and Dolby Digital Decoding to enhance the sound. The digital audio connection was a snap to connect and the box comes on as soon as the tv powers on. The two pieces operate as one and our living room has become the center of our evenings again....movies are a pleasure to watch and listen to. 45 days with this Sceptre tv and I am very pleased so far - it's every bit as good as our smaller Samsung for far less money.

I bought a Vizio smart tv at an estate auction last weekend for next to nothing and it works perfectly, but didn't come with the original remote control. The codes provided by the cable company allow the cable box remote to power on/off and control the volume, but nothing else. The only way to make use of the smart functionality or adjust the picture quality is with an actual Vizio remote. I ordered this one and it works perfectly (our tv model is the E500i.A0) The remote takes two AAA batteries and the quick buttons for Amazon, Netflix etc all work as long as your TV is connected to the internet.

I bought this at another website thanks to a Christmas gift card, but I researched the different types of sound bars and enhancement systems on Amazon & various places first. I wanted a very simple to use, unobtrusive setup, a digital connection and something that could work with our very open and large room without requiring setting up ugly components everywhere and still sound clean. This Denon base ticks every box for me.

I literally had this unit out of the box, installed under our 50" television, connected and working in less than 20 minutes - that includes reading the directions and unpacking. The box looked huge at first just sitting there alone, but once the tv was on top of it, it sort of vanished.
