Another 5 minutes and I had the Denon machine trained to respond to the volume buttons on my cable remote control. Mine came with a remote control, the digital optical cable and the red & white style connection. It connected to my phone and tablet via Bluetooth on the first try and played music through both using the Amazon Prime streaming and music saved to my devices - the sound is excellent by the way.

The included remote is handy for switching between daytime and night modes - the overall sound is lower in night mode. And you can choose between the surround sound mode or regular with the remote as well. One thing I have noticed, is that it can take three to five seconds for those changes to register and to hear them. The box turns on automatically when it senses a signal - no need to fiddle with it. Just turn the tv on & go about your business like always. The most impressive thing here is the improvement in the quality of the sound - every single bit is better! The guy reporting the news, music channels, background sound effects in movies, conversations in dramas... it's all crisp and clear and full. I am really pleased.

These are more narrow in person than I realized from the description - that's ok. The four inch length is excellent for small indoor projects and the narrow width has actually turned out to be useful as well. I have several of these reinforcing a couple of decorative pieces on an enormous outdoor holiday wreath. You can't even see the zip ties. I also used a couple to repair the broken Velcro strap on a horse show championship neck drape so it can be displayed. No sewing required. Again - these ties are small enough to be nearly invisible.

I listen to music when I'm riding in the arena and I do some freestyle dressage to music which means my horses need to hear the music as well. I'm always hunting for a Bluetooth speaker that can be used inside and outside without breaking because of a little dust or sprinkle of water and that I can hear from 60 meters away. The actual quality of the music has sort of been pushed to the bottom of my wish list. This speaker has been a pleasure.

It has a carbiner snap and a loop on top so you can hang it up or hook it on a wall, but it's balanced perfectly and sits on a flat surface normally as well. For my purposes, suspended from a hook in the air is perfect. The speaker swings just a bit and the sound is projected outward rather than just up. Leaving my phone near it on a preset play list works very well when I ride - the speaker doesn't skip or stutter. When an email or text message comes in to my phone, the speaker just makes a pleasant boop noise and continues the song. No loud beep like some others.

The volume is sufficient for my outdoor needs while on horseback - I've used it with classical music, some country, some folk music and some 80s pop. I can't speak to the bass or thumping noise for hip hop or even heavy metal because that's not my listening preference. But the crispness of a violin, the breathiness of a fast flute and the deep resonance of a solo cello are well rendered and have no fuzziness or distortion. I have used this four times for an hour each time without recharging between uses, but I don't mess with it - I don't pause, skip etc. In all, this the best outdoor Bluetooth speaker I've used and indoors,it's pretty good too.

I've been using a 2009 17.9" Gateway Windows 7 laptop happily all these years until just recently when it began to cough and sputter and generally show signs of wanting to die. I nursed it for several months while shopping for a replacement and suddenly this Toshiba L55T-C/5388 appeared from Vine. Serendipity. I am writing my review from the Toshiba actually rather than my tablet which what I've had to resort to for the past few months - that's a nice change actually. My initial impressions after a week of daily use are pretty good overall with some niggling design complaints for the physical hardware.First - for the record ... I'm not a gamer - just a regular person using my laptop to write articles for the local newspaper now and then, do a lot of email, a lot of online shopping, some social media stuff, watch some videos now and then, sort and store serious quantities of photos and average net surfing. If I want to listen to music, I tend to use Alexa (the Echo) for that rather than my computer and we watch movies on the big television around here - though sometimes I'll use my laptop instead of my tablet for tv shows etc when I'm traveling.

This Toshiba has a very nice high definition screen and I haven't noticed any fuzziness or blurred screen edges etc. The HD video I downloaded from Amazon as a test sample looked as crisp and bright on the laptop as it did on our Samsung 1080p television. The sound clarity is very good for dialogue and background music - the full speaker running across the length of the front of the machine is really good and the volume is quite loud.
Additionally, the touchscreen is responsive, but not so sensitive that just brushing it will mess your page up or close an open tab. I did run into a couple of sessions where the screen would go to black as I was scrolling rapidly by touch - this seems to be a Windows 10 issue when using the new Edge browser and not a laptop physical issue. I haven't had a repeat of this in the Chrome Browser in a week. (It could also have been a fluke)

The battery life on this computer is freaking amazing! I've been using it for almost 3 hours now for a variety of things and it's currently sitting at 74% with an estimated 6 hours and 35 minutes run time left. By three hours of use, my Gateway would have already been at 10% and that's before it started having problems. Thus far, I have used this laptop for a five hour straight run - writing, with email refreshing in the background and music playing as a test at the same time and the battery barely hit 52% when I was finished working.

Uploading and transferring files from both the cloud and my old computer hasn't been as big a hassle as I expected. The USB 2.0 thumb drive I had handy worked just fine and everything came over intact. The cloud transfer was a bit stickier just because Windows 10 now wants to make unzipping files more complicated than before. (Thanks Microsoft) Additionally, the DVD RW drive works fine and I have had no problems at all uploading the software for my 3D printer and downloading files from the net for it. For those that are interested, unlike other reviewers, I had zero problems uploading and am now using Google Chrome as my browser etc. I've included a photo of my basic screen - the Chrome icon is right there. You just have download Chrome and then unzip it manually.

My one star deduction is for physical comfort. This is a light computer compared to my previous one and I appreciate that. However, the edges are not rounded off. They are sharp, square and pointy. This means that as you are typing - doesn't matter if it's on your lap or a desk - after awhile, these pointy bits will dig into your wrists or arms and this HURTS. My five hour marathon the other day left a little indention on my right wrist. That is just ridiculous. The second design flaw is the touch pad. It is very large and sits perfectly flush with the base of the laptop. This is pretty, but you tend to brush over it as you are actually typing and that can make the cursor jump - now you're typing in an entirely new location. These two issues are obnoxious enough that I am now looking for a way to create a little rubber bumper for the front edge of the computer and a wireless mouse.

In general, this is a nice replacement for my old workhorse Gateway - I've grown used to the smaller screen because Toshiba has made it very easy to enlarge the font and any image on this screen. The 8 gig of ram makes multi tasking and switching from things prompt and thus far, I haven't experienced any lagginess. There is some bloatware pre-installed (like with any computer), but it is easy to get rid of. WIndows 10 requires a learning curve of course, but that's not the laptop's fault. Four solid stars after almost ten days and if that changes, I'll update.

*********SIX MONTH UPDATE April 29, 2016 ********

After a little over six full months of regular, almost daily use, I have had no problems at all with this laptop. It just does its job with no drama. It streams movies, music and uploads photos and files to the cloud. It handles my word processing needs and email and all the regular stuff anyone does on a computer. It also handles my software for my 3-D printer with grace. I am still very pleased with the battery life and it has had no trouble connecting via blue tooth to my external speakers when needed. I still don't like the slightly sharp edges on the corners, but it's not the end of the world. All in all, this is a nice machine and I'm still using it and pleased with it in general.

I waited almost a month to write my review because I wanted to see if the claims really were true. I received two screen protectors in the package and put one on both my husband's and mine 4th gen Fire HDX 8.9 tablets. The sheets fit exactly and the manufacturer claims of fewer fingerprints and less oil build-up on the screen surface seem to be true. The protector is clear and does offer more clarity when viewing photos & video than other brands I've used in the past.  My primary complaint is the sheer obnoxious difficulty of installing this screen protector compared to other brands out there...multiple steps and it took at least two tries to get it just right on both tablets. Oh our package came with a photo of the iPad on the front,not the the Fire, but the screen protectors inside were correct.

Wow! I got the Fire 8.9" tablet for my husband as an early Christmas present while he's recovering from major surgery. (I used a gift card for another store, so thanks Mom!) This is his first ever tablet - dragging the man into this century is like pulling an ox out of quicksand with a rubber band. I needed a tablet that would be: easy to use, back itself up, was big enough for his giant hands, light weight to use while in recovery, have access to all our photos in the cloud while he was in and out of the hospital and bed rest, and easy access to movies and the books already on his ancient Kindle Keyboard. As expected, the first hour with his new Fire HDX was full of complaining and cursing and shoutiness. (This also happened with our new car, the Kuerig coffee maker, yogurt, blue underwear, and every new toothbrush in the past 18 years. )

Two days on....The man is carrying his new Fire everywhere he goes. He's doing email on it, SKYPEing with a buddy, Twitter, reading the news, watching movies, shooting video and pictures of the dogs and throwing them to the TV via the mirroring with the Fire TV stick. (That is a neat trick). In short, my beloved Neanderthal has finally arrived in 2014 and I am delighted! To be honest, I love my 7" Fire HDX, but after seeing and using his new 8.9" in person, I am jealous and sort of want the bigger version myself now.

I am not super "techie" like some of the other folks reviewing this router, just your average housewife who likes gadgets and tries not to drown in the constant wave of weekly tech improvements. As such, I wanted a new router to replace our two year old dual band Belkin with similar speed output, but only a single antenna. The Belkin had a number of dead spots despite using one of those extender things and I had had enough. Enter this TP-Link router.

I was wary of the installation after seeing some other reviews and the difficulties folks have been reporting. However, after reading the box and the instructions fully FIRST and then following the directions exactly, I had no problems. One thing I did notice immediately, is this router is meant to be used with a cable modem and that modem must be powered off before you connect it to this router. I used the website installation method and was up and going in a total of 20 minutes - that is from opening the box to having all our wireless stuff connected to the internet again. The website management page is very detailed and allows for a lot of customization of your network, honestly, more than I need or understand. But changing the router's password and setting our network name was simple and worked on the first try.

After three days of use I like it. The speed is decent and the dual antenna set up has improved the coverage problem we were having with the old Belkin router. I haven't experienced any slowdown or degradation of connectivity with multiple devices going at once thus far. A Fire Phone surfing the net, Fire tablet streaming music, laptop doing email, and a smart tv streaming video all at once in different rooms. So...a good router for every day family use in a pretty typical home.

*********** UPDATE FEBRUARY 2015 ***********
After 90 days this router is trouble free and really working like a champ. Our cable company upgraded our modem and increased our internet speeds recently, requiring a full shutdown and reconnect of my entire network. It was a snap and the router has had no problem with faster connection and the new modem. I relocated everything to the center of our house when everything was being swapped out and the router is now sending a five bar signal out to the back deck, which means I can sit out there with the dogs in nice weather to do email etc.

*****************UPDATE APRIL 2016 *************

I'm still using this router every single day for literally every single WiFi device in our house and it just does its job with zero drama every day. We now have two tablets, two smartphones, three DVR boxes on WiFi, two laptops, a printer, a Fire Stick for streaming movies, a smart tv connected the web now and then, and the Echo that's connected all the time. (yeah, I know...we watch a LOT of television in this house!)

Right this minute I am streaming music on the Echo, recording tv shows on two different DVR boxes, using my laptop to update this review, and uploading 42 photos from my phone to the cloud and pushing email to my tablet. Oh - and I am sitting outside on the patio enjoying the lovely spring day. This router is powerful and I have no dead spots inside or out in the backyard.

So comfortable! I hate earbuds and finding actual earphones in Bluetooth that sound good has been a chore. These fit over your entire ear and have a full cushion, allowing for extended use in relative comfort. This has come in handy overnight at the hospital lately, trying to rest on the guest sofa next to a family member's bed. I found the battery life to be excellent for music and movies and games....several hours use at a time, turned off and then used again before recharging. I love being able to use the cable when the battery is dead or if you have a device without Bluetooth.

I have paired these via Bluetooth with my Fire HDX tablet, Fire Phone, and two new (2014) Galaxy phones - all worked perfectly. The NFC pairing was trickier, but did work on the Fire Phone and the Galaxy Note 4, after I figured it out. The sound is pretty good - way better than any of the other, less expensive, lower end headsets I've had in the past. The bass boost is definitely noticeable...I tried it on pop, rock, and even Beethoven. These are great if you listen to classical music, btw

Very slim and sleek! The leather is soft and feels great in your hand which is big plus for a tablet case. There is an elastic strap that pops over the front of the case to keep it closed when not in use, but it's not really sturdy enough to double as a hand hold if you're using your Fire to read a book. The inside is nicely lined with a soft fabric that will keep your screen and the back of your tablet from being scratched up. The cutouts are correct - but one odd thing, the package does not specify which version Fire tablet this case is for, it just says "Fire". While my 7" HDX does fit in this case, the cut outs for the power & volume buttons don't line up, this case is meant for the other Fire tablet.

The reason for the single star deduction is because of the way the case holds your tablet. It slides in under a flip type tab on the top and the bottom two corners are held in place with elastic straps. This is fine if you only use your Fire sitting in bed or on the sofa and never really carry it around with you. I drag my Fires around everywhere - in the car, out to the horse barn, the doctor's office, the kitchen, airplanes, the garden, etc etc. (My current go to case has a hard plastic pop in style shell that is really difficult to remove.)I wouldn't trust this MarBlue slim tech case to hold the Fire super securely for my daily use and lifestyle. One snag of the bottom corner strap on a nail at the farm and disaster!

Very light weight, sort of disappears in your hand. To be honest, I wasn't impressed when I pulled this case out of the box. It felt flimsy and I worried it might pull apart after a couple of days with my lifestyle. I am hard on my phone cases...in and out of my hand bags and pockets constantly, in the pocket on my saddle pads when I ride almost daily, and the covers get opened and closed hundreds of times a day. I even drop my phone now and then -GASP! The horror!

This one has a hard plastic shell that your Fire pops into and a face cover to shield the screen from scratches etc. The cutout on the back for the camera is excellent - a little oversized which I actually like, no chance of the edge of the case appearing in my pictures. The plastic shell carries over to cover the volume and Firefly buttons with a flexible push through so they are protected, but still fully functional. Again, I like this...no accidental photos in your pocket. Additionally, the face cover is cut back a bit so the folding hinge piece isn't coming into contact with your volume or Firefly buttons open or closed. The outside material feels like a cross between linen and leather...soft without being slippery and it doesn't catch dust or fingerprints on the front. The metal look on the back is eye catching and helps the phone stand out from the crowd a bit. Overall...a very good case and one I will pick up in another color.

I tried the Anti Glare screen protector rather than the clear so I could use my Fire out at the barn and dressage arena in the sunlight more easily. It was super easy to install and took less than two minutes. I cleaned my screen with a lens wipe first to ensure it was free of lint, finger prints and oils. Followed the included instructions exactly and lined up the screen protector with the Fire's camera etc and laid it down. The package had a stiff cardboard piece that works better than a credit card to smooth the protector sheet as you go - I have no air bubbles at all on the first try. Once it's in place, you need to remove the blue top layer to reveal the actual clear screen cover you will be looking at and touching when you use your tablet. There should NOT be a blue tint of any kind on your screen.

The use of any screen cover is going to diminish the clarity of your high definition video, that's just a fact of life. This one is no exception. But...it does cut the glare in direct sunlight and it really helps prevent scratches to Fire's screen which means I can use my Fire in more places than before and in turn makes it more valuable to me. So this screen protector does what it says and does it well.

I use these primarily to watch movies and for game play on my tablet rather than to listen to music on a regular basis. They work nicely with both my Kindle Fire HDX and my Kindle Fire phone and a laptop computer. The beauty of the 3mm plug in is that there isn't a blue tooth connection or battery issue to worry about, it just works as long as you have the headphones plugged in. The ear pieces are pretty well padded and do a decent job blocking out extraneous noises - the television for example can still be heard, but sort in the distance. I much prefer traditional over the ear headphones to ear buds, you can wear them longer with less pain and these Philips live up to that. They didn't pinch or bind even after watching a 90 minute movie. The sound is decent, full and complete and both sides seem correct, neither ear was missing out on dialog or background music. My one issue is there is a distinct static feedback when you connect them - I have to jiggle the cord or pull it out and try again more than once before it's clear with almost every device I connect them too. Not sure what that's about, but it's a relatively minor complaint.

I was very surprised at how powerful this little pod speaker actually is - it really does have a significant amount of volume and can be used in your car if you don't have a blue-tooth enabled system (for example my Mother's 10 year old Suburban out at the ranch) or at the barn when working horses in the round pen or dressage arena. It works via a standard blue-tooth connection or using the NFC option if your smart phone is equipped. There is also a microphone built in and the speaker does in fact, work very well with phone calls - we placed and received two calls using this as a speaker phone and the calls were a tad "tinny", but if you need to speak to someone hands free while cooking a meal or grooming a horse and you don't want a traditional headset, this is an excellent option.

I tested this speaker both inside and outside and it kept the signal from my Amazon Fire Phone almost 60 foot away outside in a direct line of sight with no degradation playing music. Inside the house, it managed to retain a strong signal through a closed door for about 30 feet before it lost the connection and that was far better performance than a no name blue tooth speaker we bought at Hastings in December. Sound quality is pretty good with both classical and country music. Pop can be a bit hollow at upper volume levels and hard rock has reasonable bass sound, but the vocals tend to become somewhat shrill to my ears. This is not a big deal in the least - just turn down the volume and know that at this price range you're buying the idea of portability rather than some super hi tech music snob gizmo.

Connecting this TechMatte Sound Pod to my Amazon Fire phone was super easy & took literally 10 seconds via NFC. It also connected just as easily to a Samsung Galaxy S2 and a Samsung Galaxy Note 1st Generation. My one complaint is that the on/off switch is directly over the charging outlet, so you have to disconnect the charging cable to turn it on or off and then reconnect the cord if you need it to charge or want to power it via the outlet while in use. A minor irritant that is at most worth a half star deduction. Overall, this is a very nice portable speaker that does exactly what it claims to do and fits in the palm of your hand. I did receive a sample speaker to test and review.

I got the gold case....think Gold Lame Barbie from 1985 to be more precise. Not ugly, but you definitely won't mistake this case for someone else's generic black folio Kindle HDX case. The case is actually a two piece set. The first part is a simple hard plastic pop out cover that goes over the back of the Fire and offers protection from scratches and bumps etc. It adds no bulk or weight at all. All the cut outs for the power & volume buttons and speakers are precisely placed and don't interfere with operations at all.

The second part is the zip around folio case. You snap the Fire with the first cover into the attachment on the folio. This is surprisingly secure and sturdy. Once it was snapped in, I jiggled and flapped the entire contraption every which way, trying to shake my Fire loose. It never budged or slipped. The folio case opens like a book would and can be folded back sort of like a paperback. There are pushable rubber buttons that reach inside the folio to actually touch your Fire's power & volume buttons, allowing the exterior of the case to remain solid with no holes except the speaker openings. This is a good thing since it's meant to be a travel case. The zipper is a bit stiff ~ something I don't mind, might keep it from coming open in a carry on bag dashing through the airport security etc. It does slide in and out of both my handbag and a carry on size suit case easily and packs well. There are pockets in the front cover for business cards and a loop to put a stylus as well. One thing I do like is the little handle/strap on the outside.

My reason for the one star deduction.... This case does add a bit of bulk to the normally svelte Fire HDX 7" and it doesn't allow for standing up to view videos and it can be hard to pop the Fire out of the folio part if you want to switch cases. Overall, it's not a bad choice and certainly a viable option when traveling ~ I'm writing this review on my Fire HDX sitting in this case at the end of a 4 day trip having used it.

For five dollars, this was almost too good to be true. I love this case. It fits my new 7" Fire HDX perfectly - the tablet just pops into the four corner slots and stays put. The cutouts for the speakers, power & volume buttons and the charging slot are all easily accessed and functional. When the case is open & folded back, the hand strap is tight and sturdy, allowing you to securely hold the Fire while reading or playing a game - sort of reminds me of the feel of an old school paperback with the front cover folded back. The case adds no weight or real girth to the Fire, still fits into my handbag and the center console of the car easily. This case does put the Fire to sleep and wakes it up when completely closed, which is nice for battery savings if you use your Fire like I do - it's feeding music and audio books to my car's stereo system via the Bluetooth streaming, but there's no reason for the screen to be running or the XRay lyrics info etc while I'm driving. I can set the Fire to stream my audio content, shut the case and go on with my business. I don't understand why anyone would spend $40 or $50 on another case - this Poetic product is awesome & at these prices I can have more than one in different colors to match my handbags.

I've been using these for a few days now and I'm pretty impressed. I use them mainly for listening to audio books & podcasts and some music while working out in the barn or cleaning house, that sort of thing. My normal usage pattern requires comfort when wearing for a couple of hours at a time in some serious heat & humidity outdoors. These Kinivo bluetooth headphones have just enough padding to be comfortable, but not enough to make it hard to hear oustide noises. The distance is pretty decent too - I know for a fact they are recieving & playing a clear signal at least 100 feet from my cell phone out at the barn. Now, that is in a relatively unobstructed line in any direction - just one or two half walls & gates. At home, they work throughout the entire house and only start to break up or lose the signal when I go outside to the yard and leave the phone inside. To my thinking, that's pretty darn good overall reception!

I have been VERY impressed with the battery life. Yesterday I was doing a hard clean in the barn and listened to 4 hours of an audio book non stop while I worked. Then got home and used them for another 2 hours straight while cleaning house and the battery was STILL strong. When I do charge these, I use the USB to wall plug adapter thing that came with my Kindle and it works just fine - you can also charge them via the USB on your laptop. I have only used these headphones with my Samsung Galaxy Note cell phone so I can't speak about how well they work with a laptop or other brands of phones. I have taken a couple of calls with the headphones and the sound is clear on both ends, so the microphone works fine. Overall....an excellent purchase!

I had decided I did not "need" a Kindle, having tons of other gadgets for all sorts of things. Then I began to lose the vision in one eye and realized over a period of weeks that I could not read normally (or at all some days). Magazines, books, the newspaper.... heck even email was difficult to impossible some days. All my friends have Kindles, so I borrowed one for a day and fell in love. We immediately ordered the Special Offers Wi-Fi Keyboard version. I've had it about 45 days now and my quality of life has seriously improved! I can enlarge the font and change the style of the font depending on my needs at that moment and on really bad days, when my eyes are tired or refusing to focus, the voice function is amazing. The very idea that it reads aloud to me is tremendous and once you adjust to the sometimes robotic pronounciation of some words, it works like a charm. So far, all the books I've purchased have allowed the voice option.

I signed up for Audible.com about two weeks after getting the Kindle and the quality of the audio books on my Kindle is excellent. No robotic voice here - you get the narration exactly as read by the real person - it's an MP3 file I think. Additionally, getting the local newspaper every morning on my Kindle has returned to me my morning tradition of the local editorials & coffee. I do love the number of free books available as well - some are garbage, but most are pretty decent and some have been excellent books. (Loads of Sc-Fi for free too, what's not to love?) I have used the sample option for a ton of books and it's helped me decide to spend the money purchasing a novel, or not. In case you are worried about the Special Offers... they are the screensavers while the Kindle is in sleep mode and NEVER show up in your actual books. I've used a couple of them already now that I think about it.

One last thing - the Kindle in a case, fits into almost all of my handbags and has saved my sanity sitting in doctor's office waiting rooms and at the car repair shop, and I can now sit out under a tree on a pretty day with my horses again while I read a great book. This version of the Kindle will also play my own music while I'm reading. Bottom line is that the Kindle has helped me get a valuable part of my life back and this in turn has allowed me to be more rational while facing possible permanent loss of vision in one eye. Very worthwhile purchase!

Ok I will be clear - I am NOT a super techie like some of the other folks who are reviewing this router, so I can't explain some of it's fancy gizmos and tricks. What I can do is tell my impressions of this unit from the point of view of your average person who knows a little bit about the techie things and can set up my own wireless network at home. The things that make this router different from the lower priced options out there seem pretty straight forward to me - it's fast and it's secure and you can use it for multiple wi-fi connections in your house. What more can your average family ask for? Well I'll tell you... SIMPLICITY of set up would be on the wish list. Here's what happened the day the new Netgear N750 router arrived.

Out of the box we noticed there was no instruction book. Just a single sheet with basic instructions. Ok, so it's a simple process, simple enough not to need a big book of directions. At first this was true, then things got complicated. It did hook up easily enough and had no drama talking to our cable provider's internet service and the Windows 7 desktop computer saw the router and they communicated very easily.

The Good.....As a test of the range, we used a Blackberry and walked throughout the house and the front & back porches searching for the wi-fi signal. This is a 4000sqft house with two stories on a normal size lot, so when the Blackberry saw the Netgear network and was able to connect to the internet even out in the yard we were delighted! Upstairs, downstairs, in the kitchen, at the opposite end of the house and in the garage we had a solid, strong signal from the router. We then tested the connection with a Roku box, a Wii game system, a netbook computer, a different smartphone scattered all over the house. Every piece of equipment found the network and connected to the internet like they were supposed to. And using the Wii, netbook and Blackberry all at once to load a photo heavy website was amazing - twice as fast as the old, cheap Cisco router and smooth as silk.

The Obnoxious...The next step of course, was to the name the network and do the security block so strangers can't piggyback on it. Especially since it was broadcasting out into the yard and off the porches. And that's where it got complicated and obnoxious. It took two hours to sort out the security settings. The first time we did everything as directed by the software. The end result was a loss of signal from the router everywhere except the room it was physically located in. Multiple subsequent adjustments rendered it useful in three rooms, but no longer were we able to pick it up or access the internet upstairs or on the back porch or even in the far bedroom where the Wii console is located. Not good. The end result was to wipe all the information, reboot the entire computer and router and start over using the lowest security settings. (Can you say frustration?) Once this was done we had a signal and were able to maintain the connection with the Roku, netbook, and smartphones throughout 80% of the house and a weak signal on the porch. The Wii however, cannot hold the signal at the far end of the house which means the router will have to be moved to a more central area of the house.

End result.... The weakened signal issue might not be a big deal or even worth taking a star away from my rating, but I keep coming back to this one thought. The el cheapo, 2 year old, VERY basic "off the shelf at a big box store" router we had been using put out a stronger signal for a third of the price of this Netgear N750. However, the Netgear router IS faster than the old one and there isn't a noticable reduction of speed even when multiple things are connected at the same time. If that's more important to you than overall range, then this is a darn good router for the average home.

Nice headphones for a bargain price. Good fit with no cabbage ear after a couple of hours - sound is clear and crisp. Bought these to keep my husband from driving me crazy with the sports at full volume on the television. Worked like a charm!

Works okay. There does seem to be an issue where occasionally the volume down button on the steering wheel doesn’t work. Didn’t seem to have any problems before installing. Not a show stopper. Price is good for such a low demand product

I thought these sounded a little silly, until I actually used them. They work really well!

These adhere via hook and loop, not adhesives. I have found them so useful for keeping small cords contained. You can easily write on the tab portion with a sharpie type pen. I've even used them to keep track of certain pens in my nightstand.

Super useful for cord containment and identification.

In this day and age, everyone needs to stay aware and be safe. This little guy can hang off your keychain.

The alarm is not as loud as I expected. But it is enough to at least make someone look your way, which is part of the goal. It sounds kind of like a car alarm.

Overall, it is just an additional part of a personal safety routine. Staying aware of your surroundings is still #1.

These are cute little keychain-sized personal alarms.

We tried one out, not sure what to expect. It was loud, kind of like a car alarm. It was not nearly as loud as I had expected. But it would at least attract a few glances.

The alarm button is on the back, which doesn't make sense to me. It would be very easy to bump it if you have several keys. I would have put it at the top, but that's just me.

Not sure it would make a difference, and hope I never need it. But always better to have it and not need it, than wish you had one.

Well, these are certainly interesting!
I often lose my little Roku remote, with it sliding off the bed, then being hard to find under the bed, under cat stuff, etc.

These are silicone covers. If you or your child has ever bought a game controller cover, these are like this.

These are not super easy to get on to the remotes. There are so many button cutouts, it gets caught every step of the way. As a chubby woman, it brought back flashbacks of trying to put on pantyhose too soon after a shower, or on a humid summer day...good luck! 😄

But, I persisted and slowly got it on correctly. It has a textured back to help keep your grip. It does kind of cause the volume button to feel recessed a bit, but that is not a deal breaker. It also includes a wrist strap, but there is no designated punchout for it, so it seems useless to me. The strap is also too small to go over your wrist, so just a pointless addition.

I love the colors though, and it will definitely help me find it on the floor, or amid blankets. The silicone might even help stop my cat from ceremoniously shoving it off his spot by my pillow, but we'll see about thay one.

Overall, I'm pretty happy with these. The only negative side is having to peel it off again if a battery change is needed, but that isn't oftem enough to be a concern.

Okay, I realize that everyone's definition of "easy to set up" comes from a different place. For me, I've worked around computers for over 25 years now, so pretty comfortable, BUT - I am more comfortable with software than hardware. So although this should not have been intimidating, it was a little bit. I formerly was using a Linksys router on our home network. It did a fine job, and was very easy to maintain. However, it didn't give much of a boost to the downstairs connections. The computer was always slow, and would drop the connection from time to time, and require a reboot to get the connection back.

This router is truly great looking. It is white, sleek and has nice blue lights. It sits vertically, rather than horizontally like my old one. I wasn't sure I'd like it, but I do. It comes with three screw-on antennas that can be pointed in any direction to boost your signal in that direction. The metal frame is very sturdy and would take a LOT of pressure to bend. I currently have mine on a separate little shelf because my current desk is too small.

There is only a quick set-up sheet included with this item. Ironically, if you need help, it tells you to go to the company's WEBSITE! Ha! So, if you can't get it to work, go ahead and get online. Yeah, No. But, if you are willing to disconnect and reset up a single-user home network using your old router, it could work! The sheet does give you very plain graphic instructions that tells you which item to plug in where, which many will find very helpful It came with a very short ethernet cord, so you either need to keep the router close to you or buy a longer cord. (The one I had was just purchased last year and was six feet long, so I was in good shape.)

Now, I couldn't get it to connect right away. The short troubleshooter on the insert says to reboot your modem, then to reboot the router. I did. Several times. The computer refused to acknowledge the new router! I was ready to just reconnect my Linksys when I decided to go against all logic and swap the ethernet and modem cords. For many years, computers and peripherals have been fairly color-coded to make it easier for non-tekkies to hook things up. In this case for the TP Link, the ethernet ports (there are four) are yellow and the modem port is blue. I even had previously bought color-coded wires so I didn't accidentally pull the wrong one. After 45 minutes of not being able to connect, I take another look at the back. Everything is in the right spot. But, since I wasn't connecting anyway, I decided to swap out the modem cord and ethernet cord, plugging yellow into the blue slot and the blue cord into the yellow slot. Totally backwards. As you might guess, it took off immediately! So apparently, our unit was either labeled backwards or connected backwards on the inside. Seriously strange. But as long as it works, I don't much care.

The default setting of this router is PUBLIC, so be sure to change your settings to PRIVATE NETWORK, if you don't want everyone in the neighborhood to try and tap into your network. Yes, they would need your password, but there are a lot of smart hackers out there, so you just never know. Better safe than sorry. There are default settings for the account name, network name (your SSID) and passwords, so you will need to change those as soon as you can. (If you forget to write them down, there is a reset button on the back to rol it back to the default passwords.) I also had to change the other settings to WPA2 for our area for the home network. No big deal, just different from before.

The TP Link C9 runs two parallel bands - 2.4Ghz, which is what most home routers use for regular internet access and browsing, and a 5.0 Ghz band, which is for streaming videos and movies. The nice thing about this router, is that if you name BOTH the 2.4 and the 5.0 the same name, it will AUTOMATICALLY switches to the strongest network for your use. I love that! The on/off switch is on the back of the router, so it won't easily get bumped. While my photos show the antennas straight up (we haven't had to move any of them to get a better reception), they rotate and bend towards whatever area you might need a little boost.

Has our reception improved? Yes! The downstairs computer now cruises like it was directly connected to a wired access point. The kids can watch movies and I can browse the net without anyone slowing down. The reception range is fabulous - we live in a multi-unit building, and could probably provide internet connection to all four units. It offers connection speeds of 1.3Gbps over the clearer 5GHz bandwidth and 600Mbps on the 2.4GHz bandwidth. We have not yet found a dead spot in our place - even outside picks up the signal.

In addition to the fabulous signal and great connection speeds, this router can also handle your USB 2.0 and 3.0 devices. There are ports on the side of the router, so you can easily transfer files, photos or data from an external drive to your own computer, or even hook up your printer to print wirelessly. (I haven't tried that yet, but the possibilities are there.)

It also offers a "tether" function for your smartphones. I have not used that, and won't be using that, but it would be great for parents who want to monitor network access/usage from work for their older kids. It is nice to know that option is there.

I am so very pleased with this router! I probably would not have looked at this brand, since I tend to stick with the equipment companies I've had previous success with, but I cannot state enough that this would be an asset to anyone's home network setup.

This radio looks really good wherever you place it. Ours looked exactly as advertised.
The design is not obtrusive, doesn't require a huge footprint, and the buttons are easy to use.

The only DOWNSIDE I found is a major one - the battery consumption is apparently off the charts.
I didn't put cheapie batteries in it either - I got the blue lithium Energizer batteries.
That is the only one we use in our digital cameras due to their ability to last. I take an average of
500 photos a month between my home business and our family and pets, and get at least a month of camera
usage from a set. (I date them all with a Sharpie so I know how long they last.) Even when they are spent
for camera purposes, they still have enough power in them to get our haircutters going, so they are great batteries.

Anyway, I put in a brand new set of the blue lithiums 24 DAYS ago. I had the radio turned on to program it,
but other than that, turned it off until/unless severe storms were in the area. We hadn't had any, so it wasn't
sitting in the "on" position, listening to the regular radio, etc etc.

We had reason to use it this past Saturday, April 24th, when severe storms hit our area. (Part of that huge
system of tornados that hit so many states.) I hadn't thought about it much, even though there were bad
thunderstorms in the area, but there was no warning light on the radio. (It has three small lights on the
left side that light up if there is a watch or warning in your area, and you can turn it on to hear the NWS warning.)
However, suddenly, our town's tornado warning went off! We'd never heard it go off in the 3 yrs we've lived here,
so it was a big deal. We headed downstairs for safety, and I grabbed the radio to take along.
Guess what - dead as a doornail. THREE WEEKS without even being turned on, and the brand new
lithium batteries were DRAINED!!! O-M-G. There ended up being a tornado only a few miles from us that did quite a
bit of damage. I would hate to think what could have happened if I relied on this radio for our only information!!

Once the worst had passed us, I sent my son back upstairs for more batteries. We popped them in and
immediately had the weather warning lights and broadcasts. While that was good, it could have EASILY
been too little too late. I cannot even believe how this thing ate the batteries already that power my digital
camera for a month at a time with constant usage!

There is NO low battery warning light at all, nothing to tell me that it was not working. No beeps, no lights,
nothing but dead air when we needed it the most. If it had been nighttime and we were asleep, who knows what could
have happened! Note to Midland - you NEED a low battery light! Make it blue, so it does not get confused with
any weather warning lights! This is a potentially life-saving product - go the "extra mile" here and provide
a notice of some kind when the power is gone. I never expected the batteries to be drained after about 3 wks without
even using the radio.

If you get this radio, I highly advise keeping it plugged in somewhere. I do not know if the batteries will
continue to drain while it is also plugged in (without being turned on), so I'll revise my review when I
know. I am now on a hunt for the adapter that was supposed to come with it. I do not remember seeing
one in the package. I just got the original box back out this morning to get the adapter, and there's nothing in
there. So, it is possible that the box I got didn't get one put in there. I hadn't planned on plugging it in,
but now see that might be my only real way to get dependable notices. I'll check the radio to see what voltage
the adapter should be, and see if we have an extra one from some other electronic item.

This is the really bad weather season for us (Midwest), and it is very important this radio do its job!
Do NOT rely on the batteries, and keep a spare set of batteries on each floor of your home (if you have an upstairs
or basement, make sure you have some available for flashlights and radios on EACH FLOOR - I had not even thought
about that, but we keep our batteries upstairs, and did not want to go back up during the actual tornado warning!).
I have flashlights tucked every conceivable place in the home (including the bathroom, under the kitchen sink, etc etc), but never really gave a second thought to having extra batteries available per floor until last Saturday when we needed them.
Lesson learned!

S.A.M.E. technology is a must - don't consider any weather radio that doesn't have it, or you'll hear a
lot of stuff that doesn't even pertain to your location. This radio has it. Note though that on this model, you
have to choose the ALERT ON option to ON or you won't get the warning lights. (Odd that it is not a default to on, but it isn't.) You have the choice of a LOT of various types of warnings that will pertain to your area, which is great. You choose which warnings to turn on, except for tornado warnings. This is defaulted to the "on" position, although the manual does not tell you that. I wrote to Midland to ask about it. It took them two weeks to answer me, but they confirmed it was a default setting, which is why it was not included in the storm warning options lists.

In summary - great radio, great look, beyond-poor battery usage.
I've taken off one star for the poor battery life - I've never seen any electronic use them faster.
The lack of a low battery light or beep is a huge mistake for this type of product.
It takes four AA batteries, so be sure to keep a pack of them available on each floor of your home.
Husband uses this in his office and he is super happy. It's easy to use and nice and loud.

I would first like to state that i own a Sony and Toshiba LED backlit LCD televisions.
I have never seen the samsung LED DLP screens or the laservue DLP.
I will be making this comparison solely compared to my other LED LCD televisions.
I do not yet own any 3D movies or equipment.

Pros:
PICTURE:number one is the size of this screen, i love it! it is great for HDTV and HD movies. Image is very clear and crisp.it has 120hz witch is much better against motion blur. it has advanced video calibration options. i just went to [...] and used the settings there.
INTERNET TV:I also enjoy the wireless Internet. it has movies and it has news. my favorite feature is the ticker option. you can have a ticker at the bottom of your TV with facebook on it as well as other apps.

MY $25 mike really didn't put out enough volume even though I had the setting at 100%.  So, for far less money, I bought this.  Problem solved!!
I liked the camera.  The microphone is set at a low volume that I can't seem to change.

It has four ports and does not use AC power. The idea of using AC power had always seemed appealing but the ports were always dead. I have an external CD/DVD burner which requires two ports. It runs flawlessly. Since I use this for other purposes I unplug that. It's ports are in use for a printer, an external HD for backups and a fan since the Ivy Bridge CPU is really an overclocked low quality CPU (as is the Haswell). It burned out two parts, I send it back to Toshiba and they replaced the parts and, as I had requested, did away with the overclocking. It's still extremely fast.

BUY THIS
It takes the guesswork out of the equation.

Even at top volume the noise cancellation on this set of headphones isn’t great. With a name like Microsoft I expected more from the product. Since this is about the best set I’ve found for the money I will be keeping them, but it hasn’t been my best purchase this year.

Very satisfied from battery life to product quality. The dual drivers are incredible, and allow for lower phone volume with loud music still. They come with extra earbuds in different sizes. Those are an odd material, a little different from standard earbuds. More firm I’d say but nothing wrong with them still. More over, the actually earpiece isn’t bulky and fits very nicely without sticking out of your ear very far. Overall very pleased, worth the extra few bucks I’d normally spend on some earbuds.
Perfect! Runs pretty quiet unless under a lot of stress.

OK, so I waited awhile before purchasing my first pair of earbuds. I finally decided I needed the so that I could watch videos/etc. while sitting in public spaces (coffee shops, libraries, etc.) without disturbing anyone.

Bear in mind that I'm 71 yrs old and although I spent my career in IT, I was a SOFTWARE person, not hardware. So anything hardware related is always a bit intimidating for me.

These were relatively easy to set up. Pairing with my iPad and iPhone was a breeze. They seem to hold a charge quite nicely. The noise canceling feature is wonderful! Very happy with that.

I'm a classical musician, so I'm kind of picky when it comes to speaker sound, and I experimented these earbuds using a variety of my favorite classical hits. The sound I'm getting is excellent -- a bit surprising as I wasn't expecting it to be as good as it is.

No problems so far -- highly recommended!

I own several pairs of earbuds. I just seem to accumulate them like I do my reading glasses -- several pairs in each room where I tend to use them. Most of mine are in the price range $20-30, so those are the ones I'm using for comparison. Based on that, these new Pioneer earbuds seem to be the best of that group.

I listen mostly to classical music with a smattering of other genres (folk, 1960s-70s rock, Broadway). These provided acceptable performance for all genres, but do seem to lack some low-end bass response. One of my test recordings is the Erich Kunzel/Cincinnati Symphony recording of Tchaikovsky's "1812 Overture" with cannons, and the low-end loss was noticeable. Still, the rest of the sound is excellent, and these will work just fine for my day-to-day listening -- music that I have going on in the background while working on something else. For serious listening, I'll use my over-the-ear headphones.

Good performance for the price. I like these.

Holy cow! I was NOT expecting the sound from this little speaker to be as good as it is. I own 3 other Bluetooth speakers, one lower price point, one "moderate"/medium, and another that is comparable in price to this unit. None comes close to the sound quality.

It's really unobtrusive looking, almost drab, slightly "retro" in a gunmetal gray with a darker gray screen. A single button surrounded by a ring on top of the unit controls everything that needs controlling (on/off, volume and skip). A thick rubber base keeps it from sliding around on polished tables (like a nightstand, where I'll be keeping this).

It took just over 3 hrs to fully charge using the included wall charger and cable. I paired it with my iPhone -- nothing tricky there -- and proceeded to play music. I'm a conductor/composer and write mostly music for choirs, so that's what I tend to listen to most of the time. First up: the [[ASIN:B0018NQ066 Britten: War Requiem (2 CDs)]] I'm intimately familiar with this work, having performed it three times and conducted rehearsals for it on one occasion. It's one of my "desert island" recordings. It has a huge variety of "sound" from soft/slim orchestration to full out full orchestra and chorus. The LG performed beautifully. NO distortion, every slight nuance was audible. The recording is a quality recording but I've listened to it on all my other wireless speakers as well as my Bose surround wired speaker set up, and the performance of this small LG speaker is impressive. Seriously exceptional performance.

OK, next up, something completely different: Fleetwood Mac [[ASIN:B00B1MHXY2 Rumours]] -- again, virtually flawless performance. All the "bits" of percussion come through crystal clear. It has a decent bass sound, too -- again something I wasn't expecting from a unit in this price point or of this size.

I've been playing this almost non-stop for over 5 hours and it's showing no signs of low battery. The description here says it runs 9 hrs on a single charge; I'm beginning to believe it. Also, it shuts off after 20 minutes if these is no input (Bluetooth mode). You can also turn it off from your smartphone using the app downloaded from the iOS app store (there's an Android version, too).

This has no built-in microphone, so you can't take phone calls on it. It's just a speaker but a VERY good one.

I really can't find anything wrong with this so far. It's really that good.

I got this to store the back-up of my external hard drive, and it does that job very well. I have a key chain on which I store a number of flash drives for various purposes that I leave hanging on a hook in my office, so it doesn't get a lot of abuse. So far, I've noticed no problems with quality -- it's VERY small, and fits VERY snugly into the USB port on my laptop, but once I get it right-side up, it's easy to insert and retrieve.

Speed is adequate for my needs. Very happy with this so far. If that changes, I'll edit this review.

OK, let's get this straight at the beginning: I'm not an audio expert. I don't work in the industry, I haven't studied this stuff, etc. But I DO know what sounds good especially when it comes to classical music recordings. I've been involved in classical music my whole life, I've played and sung with orchestras, so I know how things should sound.

Bottom line: this unit produces very good quality sound over the range of dynamics and timbres that come with a variety of classical music. I have a few recordings that I use as "tests": Carmina Burana (the opening "O Fortuna" section); Bach "Magnificat"; Stravinsky "Firebird"; Mozart piano sonatas; Beethoven String Quartets; and various choral works (Eric Whitacre, Brahms, etc.). I got none of the tinny sound that sometimes happens with piano works; the softer sections of the Eric Whitacre choral works were clear and precise; the range of dynamics in the opening O Fortuna of "Carmina Burana" was crystal clear with no distortion. Really, this outperformed my expectations.

The unit is smaller than I expected, which is a good thing, since I intend to take it along when I travel. It's attractive (I got the orange color), and has a nice "feel" to it. The controls are easy to manipulate on the top of the unit, and I really like the ability to take phone calls via the unit (it has a built-in microphone).

Overall, I'm very pleased with this purchase. I paid less than forty dollars for mine, and at that price, I consider it a super deal. I've had it only for a couple of weeks, so if there are issues with durability, I'll update this review. For now, it's definitely worth 5 stars.

I've used this with both my iPhone and my iPad2, with generally good results. As others have mentioned, the dock accommodates only "portrait" orientation for an iPad, so if you want to watch movies in "wide screen" landscape orientation, you're out of luck.

Still, the sound is really good -- I have several other JBL speaker products in my home, and this one seems to match in terms of quality of audio. It's not overly large, either.

Definitely would recommend. I've had mine for awhile now, and it's still going strong, with no issues at all.

I am amazed at how good these speakers are for the size. I've been using them with my iPod nano as well as my laptop, and they're really quite good. Others have mentioned the lack of bass, and I agree -- it could use a little more "oomph" on the low end. But it's not that bad, really -- and the overall sound is really excellent.

This little unit is truly portable, with its own little drawstring bag. I've been able to fit everything -- the power cord, the unit, and the device cord -- into the bag. It's a tight fit, but it works.

I'm very please with the On Tour speakers -- definitely recommend them if you need something portable to provide more/better sound than your internal laptop speakers or something to connect to an MP3 player. Look for them on sale (I got mine via a Goldbox special).

If you can get only one add-on for your digital camera, let it be this one.
I took my Kodak digital camera decked out with this 128MB CompactFlash card on a 6-week road trip. I used the "middle" quality setting for the pictures, and managed to take over 130 photos (the equivalent of 5-6 24-shot rolls of film), filling not anywhere close to half the card (at that setting, the card will store over 300 photos)!
I'm not a digital photography technoid by any stretch of the imagination -- I just like capturing memories of the places I go and the things I see. Having the extra memory afforded by this little card meant that I could relax and not worry about running out of space for all my photos.
Transferring the photos to my laptop was a piece of cake, and took very little time -- partially a function of the card.
I highly recommend this as the *first* accessory/upgrade you purchase for your camera!

Got the first one from a black Friday special and set up in the living room. Great for playing music, jokes, games, and found so much available for this! My family loves it (my son always yelling something out to her!) During the holidays, it's perfect for fireplace sounds or music. Love so much I got a 2nd for my craft room.
Very discreet device! Love the features with Alexa. I hid this behind a decoration for the holidays and so nice for the music and sounds. Probably will be getting another one!

Love this mouse. The scrolling function is phenomenal. Just what I needed. If you use a lot of Web sites that require a lot of scrolling, this will be the perfect style for you. Love the design and color. Fits my hand perfectly. Couldn't be more pleased.

If you want 4K in a 32-inch TV, this is the one to buy. Even if you don't want 4K capability in your 32-inch TV, this is still the one to buy. It's the best 32-inch I've ever had or seen, and it's also superior to Sony's other 32-inch TV, which is only offering 720p max.

I had to deduct a star because of the included remote control. This TV has Google TV with Google Voice Assistant, where you press the microphone button on a remote control and then Google will control the TV for you, including turning it off, and also answer all of your other Google inquiries. However, and astonishingly, Sony doesn't include the remote control that has the microphone built in. Without this, the Google Assistant is inaccessible and thus useless. So, if you want that convenience, and you do want it, you have to buy a separate Sony remote control for $65.

The picture quality is excellent once you remove the factory default picture settings. I highly recommend anyone wanting good brightness for this TV to turn off the light sensor. With the light sensor on, the TV won't get as bright as a lot of people like.

The Vivid setting is nice, and it doesn't oversaturate the picture the way some other TV's Vivid setting does.

The operating system in the TV is fast. Sound is okay, but of course, not as great as some of Sony's larger TVs that push the sound out from all over the screen, as opposed to small speakers at the bottom like this TV has. Of course, you can easily add an external speaker, if desired.

Viewing angles are not nearly as good as Sony's larger 4K 2022 models, but it doesn't bother me since I am almost always just watching the TV straight on.

The price is higher than a lot of inferior 32-inch TVs, but again, the Sony technology offered, along with it capable of 4K, justifies the higher price, in my opinion.

This is a good alarm that's easy to use. The alarm feature is loud. The remote control seems to work at a nice distance. The infrared sensor kicks in immediately. Seems good quality. I am not using the door feature.

You have the option of using alkaline batteries in the main unit and infrared sensor, or to plug them into mini-usb situation for power. The USB cables and USB charger are not included.
The clicks are very quiet, which is great. Range and accuracy and battery life are great. The middle scroll wheel is not quiet.

There is a lot to like about this monitor. It's easily height adjustable, it can pivot, the angle can be tilted up and down, it has built-in speakers (I am using a Bose Solo 5 soundbar instead of the built-in speakers), the side and top bezels are not too wide, and the picture quality is very good, with a lot of picture configuration options. (I plugged a 3.5mm stereo patch cable from the back of the monitor into the soundbar.)

I watch TV broadcast and cable channels, movies, and TV shows via my computer, so I wanted a larger high quality-picture monitor with a higher DPI capability. I did not want to spend so much and buy one of the many monitors above $500, but I did not want one of the cheaper 32-inchers that had less DPI capability.

This LG has so far satisfied what I want. I have settled on the "HDR Effect" Picture Setting for most use, and it is quite nice. There is also a "Custom" picture setting that allows for a lot of configuration. (I could never have just settled for LG's factory default picture settings.)

The monitor is very heavy...much heavier in weight than I expected. Attaching the stand is really easy. Detaching the stand is also very easy. Build quality of this monitor seems good. Assuming this just-released monitor stays working perfectly for a long time, LG did an excellent job and I am glad I bought it.
DisplayPort on my computer to the HDMI input of my TV ... picture and sound are as expected. The cable is working as it should.

There is a lot to like with this computer: The small size is great. There are 2 USB-C ports instead of just 1 like with a lot of others. There is no bloatware. You can hook up your monitor to either the DisplayPort or USB-C connection. They include a USB-C to HDMI adapter. There are 4 USB 3.0 ports. Good speed for regular computer use with the I7 processor and SSD.

The biggest thing to dislike is the volume of the fan. You wouldn't think a computer this small would have such a loud fan, but it does. It's annoyingly loud. If you're going to be working on the computer a lot while in a silent room, I would recommend to not buy this computer because of the fan noise.

I deducted 1 star because there is only 1 HDMI port on this TV, when there really should be 2, and because the audio output is of extremely poor quality. I think the use of an external speaker is a requirement when using this TV. I was really surprised at how bad the audio sounds on the TV. A prior reviewer called the audio sound "garbage." I would have to agree.

The TV is lightweight. The picture is pretty good for a $135 TV. I like that it has both RCA audio out jacks and a standard 3.5mm stereo out jack. If you want a small size TV, this is certainly one to consider.

It works. The annoying hum is gone. I can't believe that it works since other hum eliminators I bought failed.

I have a 2017 model High Def TV that has RCA audio output jacks. (The built-in speakers on the TV leave a lot to be desired, of course.)

I am going direct from the TV RCA jacks into the RCA input of an expensive speaker. The hum was bad.

I tried all the suggested tricks, including using shielded RCA cables, plugging the TV and external speaker electrical cords into the same outlet, or a different outlet, plugging the electrical cords into a line conditioner, and buying cheaper-than-this-product hum eliminators. Nothing worked.

I then spent $100 for this Sescom IL-STEREO-19...and I found success. The hum is gone. (The only reason I deducted a star is because it's expensive at $100. It's a passive box.)

This does the job...and better than some similar units that can only do PCM audio.

Only negative: The box feels plastic-cheap for a $35 adapter. I just hope it can last a long time.

I am glad I bought this, so far.

It works as advertised.

For my use specifically: Optical audio sound goes in one end. Analog sound comes out the other end (I use the 3.5mm stereo jack).

If you keep this in context regarding the fact it costs just $11, you get your money's worth for sure.

But if you want a very loud alarm built in, you'll have to spend more money than this and find an alternative.

In my opinion, the volume of the built-in alarm is not loud enough. I was disappointed with the alarm volume immediately, as I was expecting it to be louder. The volume is not scare-inducing at all.

The tiny screw they chose to use for the battery compartment is ridiculous. How many people have a tiny screw driver handy that small? Yes, of course there are some people who will have one. But I didn't.

The item feels cheap, and thus does not inspire confidence the alarm part will last a long time. Maybe it will. Maybe it won't. All I know is that it doesn't inspire confidence. (I read a review at Amazon that said the alarm part broke after 3 uses, and that it is only being used as a silent door stop now.)

But the above notwithstanding, since I love the fact this will stop the door from opening (or closing), combined with the fact it is so inexpensive and that it does have an alarm, I feel the product deserves 5 stars. (Plus, the company is very responsive and stands behind their product.)

Luckily, both cables are working as advertised. I am hoping for longevity, as we all know many 3.5mm patch cables can fail after a while.

The cables seem well constructed for their reasonable price.

I have one going from my TV's headphone jack into an expensive external speaker. The other cable is going from my iMac's headphone jack into another nice speaker. Sound quality is as expected and desired.

I put my money into getting two Spot cameras via Indiegogo back in November, 2015, and I am very happy I did. Once I received the cameras I knew right away I made the right choice. I love the Spot cameras. They work exactly as described and are of great quality.

Set up was very easy. I have the app (which is easy to use and works well) installed on my iPhone and iPad. Picture and sound quality is very good.

With the cameras being so small and light, they are easy to move to a different location, if desired.

The Spot camera is perfect for my needs. I was so happy to get a product that really works as advertised. I have had my Spots turned on 24/7 for approx. 5 months now, and have not had any negative issues.

I recommend the Spot camera. It is a good camera from a good company.

For specific circumstances, this Asus VivoMini UN62-M037M is perfect and wonderful. My specific circumstance: I wanted a computer to put next to my High-Def TV so I can play movies and TV shows, etc. My TV becomes the gorgeous computer monitor via the HDMI input. I have Ethernet right there, so I did not have to buy the additional WiFi adapter for the computer. I use a wireless keyboard and mouse.

This Asus has 4 USB 3.0 ports. I recommend this Asus model with the 4 ports instead of their model with only 2 ports.

I bought one 8-Gig RAM stick for $44 (Crucial CT102464BF160B via Amazon). I bought a 256GB mSATA drive for $103 (Crucial MX200 via Amazon). (I already had a wireless mouse [Logitech M525] and a wireless keyboard [Anker A7723].)

So, I spent about $435 total. (Luckily I already had a copy of Windows 8.1 I could use, plus a USB DVD drive. Of course, you can also install Windows via a USB Flash Drive.)

Opening up the bottom by removing the 4 screws is fast and easy. Installing the RAM and mSATA hard drive is also fast and easy.

I hooked up my HDMI cable direct from the computer to my TV and the rest went easy.

The Windows drivers are easily downloaded from Asus Website.

The computer is very quiet and small and nice. The i5 processor runs as expected. Boot times are fast. The Intel Video chip they provide is great at doing what I need it to: Provide a crystal clear picture to my TV, and allow me to stream high-def movies and TV shows from the computer.

For what I do and at the total price I paid, this Asus VivoMini is perfect. (With it seeming solidly built, I am hoping for longevity.)
If you need a 15-foot 3.5mm male to 3.5mm male patch cable, this one is a great choice. It appears very well constructed. I like that the cable is thin. The ends seem solid. Sound is clear.

The Hosa YRA-104 RCA Male to Dual RCA Female Cable works exactly as advertised and as expected. Seems well built. Sound is fine. Good price. Good value. I can only report that the cable does indeed work and is doing its job.

This Hosa CMP103 1/8 inch TRS to 1/4inch TS Cable 3 feet long works as expected. Seems well built. Sound is fine. Good price. Good value. I can only report that the cable does indeed work and is doing its job.

I have 2 of these Monster CableLinks Y-Adapter XLR Male (2) to XLR Female (1) splitter/joiner. They work very well and seem good quality. Well built. I use them to combine the left and right audio source from the XLR outputs from a mixer into a single XLR input of a powered speaker. Sound is perfect.
I am just using this as an audio switch box. And it seems well built. It works perfectly. I recommend this product if you need either an audio or video switch box.

First, let me say I own the 47" LG 47LE8500 for my living room with its stunning high def picture and extremely poor speakers. I was looking for a slightly smaller (and less expensive) TV for my bedroom and chose this 42" Vizio. Vizio has a similar 47" model under this newly released line. (So far, I am mostly happy with my purchase.)

Both the LG and Vizio have LED LCD with Local Dimming. I have to say that the high def picture on the Vizio is not as stunning as on the LG 47LE8500, but it is close, and still satisfying.

The black levels are better on the LG, but pretty close on the Vizio.

The Vizio arrived with one of the round rubber "feet" missing under the base. (Better quality control and inspection please?)

The WiFi on the Vizio is fabulous. The remote having a qwerty keyboard is fabulous.

First thing I had to do (for personal preference) is turn off the room light sensor. The picture was way too dark for me when the light sensor was on.

Also, the default screen brightness setting with the light sensor off is too bright, in my opinion. The brightness level is at 50 by default on the standard pic setting, and it looks brighter than the 50 setting on other sets. (But it is very easy to adjust, of course.)

The speakers on the Vizio are much better than on the LG.

I dislike that the Vizio does not have a swivel base.

Standard def is quite acceptable (and better than on the LG).

So, bottom line: If you want to save some money, this new Vizio line is a very good choice (and recommended). Once you customize the pic settings, I think you will be happy with the high def picture. If you have extra money to burn, the LG will give you a more stunning high def picture with better black levels, but you probably will dislike the LG's speakers, especially if you listen to a lot of music with the volume raised.

Adding to my review, August 28:

When the TV is off, the Vizio logo at the front is lit up in orange. I have found no way to turn this off. I hope that if enough people complain, perhaps Vizio will release a software update that will allow the turn off of this orange Vizio light.

I have encountered bad lip sync issues. But luckily, Vizio has included in the Audio settings a Lip Sync adjustment setting. I had to enable this setting, as the lip sync mismatch problem was really bad. The adjustment has helped.

Good computer, my only complaint is caused by living far enough from town that getting it updated has been a nightmare. Approximately 1300 MB in required updates with an equal number of recomended ones. My internet signal is good for 1MB per minute on a good day. Updating them before shipping would have been a good idea.
good price, and it worked.  ,  had to say more to get the 18 words required to get this to work.

Plugged Bar and sub-woofer into power. Connected to Visio TV with HDMI and that's it. No other setup needed. It comes on with the TV and TV remote controls the volume. Use its remote to enhance voices or bass. Super easy!

better than the "I home" that stopped working. This has wonderful sound and many well designed features compared to the I Hime speaker the same shape which costs more. Good buy so far. The I Home worked fine for several years but the sound wasn't as good.

I love the Kindle.

I have noticed different comments that I would like to address. In the Amazon store, you can turn off the one click option. I never use one click as it is easy to make a mistake.. When you first enter your acct, it tells you one click is on and gives you the option of turning it off. I'm not a buyer of high-end ear buds. At my age my hearing isn't acute enough to hear much of the nuance of music through headphones, but I do like the sound to be much better than if I were holding a can and string up to my ears. That being said, these are the best earphones I've ever owned. When I first put them on, the bass response actually startled me and the middles and highs were present and clear --without any adjustment to my player. The "stays in your ears" feature actually works; you give them a twist in your ear and they stay put, as well as keeping out sweat. You can hear ambient noise just fine, but unless there's a high wind or other competing sound, you continue to hear the audio just fine.

I don't agree with other reviewers who report that the plastic earbuds fall off easily. I think those reviewers must be actually pulling the buds off to clean them and I don't believe that's the manufacturers' intentions. I clean mine with a mini-fiber cloth well moistened (but not soggy) with rubbing alcohol without removing them from the actual earpieces.

The reason I didn't give these earphone five stars is that there is no inline control --no mute off, or volume control. I like them VERY much, and would buy them again if I needed to replace.
