It was easy to set up and program, mostly with the remote that works quite well at about a 40-degree angle to either side. I loaded a USB thumb drive with around 390 music files, all of which are playing flawlessly (mp3 and/or WMA), with a way to shuffle or random play from one artist or from all files.

The different EQ settings could be more varied in tone and effect; however, I'm 67 years old with some mid-range hearing loss, so that might be my fault. The bass response is fine even without the bass boost feature, and vocals, especially high male and women's voices, can seem a little harsh. Volume is fine without distortion, even at enough cranking for me --not sure how it would satisfy a head banger!

My only "like to haves" for this unit include a way to mute the radio or CD playbacks; however, the volume control is very responsive so that's not really a problem for the radio, and one can pause the CD and USB file playback. And of course, I can't imagine what Sony was thinking not including a regular headphone jack.

It's not the most elegant-looking set I've ever owned, but I'm quite satisfied, especially for the cost to value ratio I got on this unit. Very pleased!

After a career in advertising, during which I've been around video cameras of all sizes, weights and shapes, this is my first camcorder for personal use. After one day of monkeying around with it, I'm delighted --with a couple of reservations. It appears to be of very good quality, feels lightweight and yet sturdy (with the exception of the rather stringy hand-strap/lanyard) and the user interfacing seems straightforward and intuitive, once you figure out where things are. I'll be back in a few weeks or months to describe my experiences with the software, data downloading and manipulation, etc.

The main criticism I have --more of an observation, really-- is that, for my somewhat arthritic hands, operating the controls are challenging because of their placement on the camera and because the thing is so darned small. (As in the length of a soft drink can --at only 2/3 of the diameter!) This may be simply because I'm unaccustomed to using camcorders, or indeed holding any camera as one does with the JVC GZ-HM550. Many reviewers have complained that this 2010 model still has scrolling and MENU, OK, and INFO buttons rather than Mac-style rolling touch screens. This doesn't bother me, although it takes a very delicate touch to get to the right menu selection on this camera, because they zip by so rapidly under a man's stubby fingers.

Low light results seem more than adequate, especially for daytime indoor shooting, and the shake reduction seems to me to be working very well. The zoom function is smooth and quiet, but --for me-- will be difficult getting used to because the toggle from wide to close-up is at the top rear, where it's difficult for me to reach with my admittedly somewhat inflexible fingers. As I said, I'm new to these mini-cameras, so they may be designed for two-handed use...??

All in all, I think it will be a very good mid-range camcorder with the advisory that people with large hands might find a somewhat physically larger brand/model easier to handle. GET A WARRANTY. (Square Trade offers a good policy against damage, etc.) This JVC model is small enough, the finish glossy enough, that I feel it would be fairly easy to drop it.

This review is for the Uniden BCD436HP I see reviews here for other radios, so not to be confused.
I used Amazon Prime Now to get the radio to me, in less than 1 hour (about 45 minutes) the delivery person was knocking on my door with my new receiver, wow, I was highly impressed and I will always check to see if Prime Now is available for all my deliveries from now on.....
So, the radio....
This receiver has a 4 gig SD card preloaded with every known frequency with text for the entire US and Canada. They have software called Sentinel you install on your PC and this is your gateway to all updates and firmware and it can control your radios SD card any way you like. Sentinel has an extensive database of all frequencies and let me say this again, all frequencies have text description included which is the most highly advanced scanner database system I have ever seen and I have owned scanner receivers most of my adult life, (long time)..
This is a digital receiver using the latest technology available. It can monitor any analog or digital TX (with some exceptions, like encrypted signals) and gives you extensive control over what you're listening to. There are FCC laws regarding what is legal and not legal to monitor and Uniden has got us right up to the maximum legally allowed to be monitored by civilians. If you are law enforcement persons you will have much more powerful receivers available to you capable of Cell phone conversation monitoring etc., things no civilian should even be interested in.
There is another version of this Uniden radio, the BCD536 which is a tabletop version. If you have large powerful outdoor weatherproof antennas the BCD536 is a good option and it is completely transferable to vehicle dash mount and back from your work desk to your vehicle.
I like this handheld BCD436 best personally for my purposes.
This is basically a plug and play receiver. It comes with 3 2300 milliamp rechargeable batteries, load those, charge them or just leave radio plugged in, enter your zip and you're in. Well theoretically that's how it works, in the real world? No.
When you first receive the radio I would suggest positioning yourself in front of your PC. Have the paper manual, the radio, you and your PC right there in front of you. Get ready to read and learn your radios keyboard layout and what these great, well thought out keys can do for you. You will learn, trust me, you will quickly come to love this radio.
Some cons:
No wall charger adopter included. You can charge from your PC's USB ports but you will need a wall charger with USB port. Most of us have several of these around the house from old cell phones etc. They work fine.
This unit should come with a nice wall charger adopter. That's really the only con, not to bad really.
Antennas:
Your ability to scan and receive signals on any scanner is proportionate to your antennas. The more robust and correct (correct meaning size, materials used etc).. You will need some nice antennas for this nice radio to increase your scanning powers. Amazon has some nice antennas, scannermaster.com has some also. Your local radio shop retailer will have some also. The included rubber ducky antenna is garbage, toss it from across the room to your garbage can, see if you can make a rim shot. Like I said, I have been playing with scanners for many years so I have many antennas to pick from.
Verdict:
This is without a doubt, the most powerful handheld scanning receiver available from any manufacturer. It is the luxury sedan of the scanning receiver world. It is easy and robust. It is backed up by Uniden's Sentinel software which will future proof your radio for many years to come.
I give Uniden 5 stars for this winner.
I give Amazon 5 stars for Prime Now 1 hour shipping, also a winner.

I've had this processor running in my new build for about a month now. I was being annoyed by the stock cooler fan buzzing at very high rpm whenever the heat rose to moderate levels like 52C. The fan was really buzzing like a little aircraft prop at full throttle for takeoff. It would crank up to 6600 rpm at the slightest provocation like CPU temp hitting 50C.
I decided to take everything apart down to the motherboard coming out and all components attached to it.
When I pulled the cooler off the CPU and looked at the thermal paste situation, OMG what a mess. The stock thermal paste was not covering the whole area, it was reduced to a gummy, sticky glue. I had to pull very hard to get the cooler off the CPU.
I cleaned the cooler base and the CPU thoroughly and applied a pea sized spot of Arctic Silver 5 then reassembled everything.
Instant cure. Instant quieter fan. Instant low CPU temps andQUIET!AMD needs to stop using whatever they're putting on the coolers and just include a syringe of a high quality thermal paste for customers to apply themselves because whatever they're using is junk.
The stock cooler and fan they include with the fx 8320 are very high quality but the pre applied thermal paste is garbage.
Just apply new first quality thermal paste, you don't need to spend big dollars on third party hardware and I suspect those of you who have installed new coolers and seen great results is because of the new thermal paste used during installation.
The fx 8320 is a very powerful processor don't smoke it because of 10 cents worth of cheap thermal paste, use the best for your investment and this hot CPU will give many years of great performance.

Another good one. Been restocking my radios, making sure I have a couple in the house, one in each car, and even one on my person. I keep them everywhere because you never know when the need for info from the outside world will be needed, and right now that seems more relevant than ever *vaguely waves arm around*.

I have to say, other than price and a few details, the functions and overall performance are the same. This is a (refreshing) bargain at $9.99. For that, I recommend this.

I have found that radios of this style pretty much all work the same, sound the same. Just look for details that are of interest to you. When it comes to this Prunus radio, I like the small size. LOVE these over the ear air conduction earphones. I have a pair of bone conduction earphones that I fell in love with, and I wanted another pair of different style to for use when working out (my others stay at bedside for evening podcast listening, music, meditation). These looked like they hook over the ear securely, and they do! If new to this style, be prepared to play around with them a bit, and take advantage of the ear plugs as they help deepen the sound. I personally find the sound to be good and clear. I have some auditory sensitivities, and these just feel right- no irritations, aggravations, or off sounds.

The reason why I dont use IN ear ear buds is because they always bother me- usually pain or some headache or nausea ensues. I can wear them for short periods of time as needed, but I do not enjoy them for longer duration- ie listening to music while working out. I can never find just regular headphones that hook over the ears without going in. So that is basically how I got to know bone conduction. Now that style is my go to. I also like that I can still sense/hear what is around me with these, again perfect for working out. Being waterproof puts me at ease when I sweat profusely.

Pair with a bluetooth MP3 player, or add to memory card for direct play through the headset.

Good price, good quality, so far really good experience. I recommend!

I'm pleased with these bone conduction headphones. I almost never use ear buds because they can give me a headache (I have a one piece bud for use while hiking), and over the ears are really hard to find. They are always ear buds. The headphones that have the strap over the head are ok, but they can be bulky, and over a period of time a give me a headache too. I basically have been searching for an over the ear outside sitting headphone where the strap also goes behind the head. Last time I was able to find one was like 10 years ago.

So another search brought me to bone conduction. They are pretty much what I am looking for. I noticed that the sound is way better with use of the ear plugs, and the sound can vary depending on how the headset is placed. When everything is lined up perfectly, the sound is really impressive. When the line up isnt perfect, the sound it doable but not perfect. I find that these are great for use when I am lounging and just want to listen to music or a book or podcast.

I have not tried them in water, doubt I ever will (unless I am walking in rain).

I have a big head (23.75" around) so that might contribute to the placement, and how well it sounds. Very easy to pair with my phone, easy to adjust volume, and easy to move up or back a track.

4stars for the variability in sound depending on placement (and definitely best is used with ear plugs)
5 stars for comfort, and never ever produces a headache. That was my primary concern, and so I am extra pleased with that.

Perfect. I have an MP3 player that I use while driving. While it has Bluetooth capability, my car does not, and while my husbands car does, I dont want the hassle of making it connect. I am perfectly fine with using an auxiliary cord for easy plug and play.

I had a black wire style cord, but it eventually frayed at the head. Figured it was time to replace it. Hence my needing to buy another. Works very well, sounds are good, absolutely no problems so far. I pout one in each car, so I am never without my music.

This came up as an option, and I decided to take my chance on it (initially thought it pricey for a mini DVD player--but if it worked, then it would have been a good purchase).

It meets all my needs. I wanted it to have a display, and a remote. It has both. Picture quality and response is spot on. No issues with sounds. No issues at all!

Everything works. I tried everything on it. I tried it on two tvs and a monitor (it is that easy to use). I kept a DVD going for a few hours (season 1 the office) and no issues.

I have tried both a store bought DVD and a rewritable. Both worked fine.

I noticed a slight pause when I was messing around with the cords (working on cord management when putting in the main spot I plan to keep it). So I am not sure how it would be for "active" use. I dont plan to move around with it.

So far, I am quite pleased with this unit. Meets all my needs. If I learn anything else, or experience anything else worth sharing, I will be back to do so.

My primary use is simply to have a set of headphones for listening to music or watching videos. It has a built in microphone but I haven't used it for phone calls or giving commands. Not sure if I will.

The set up is easy. 1st, my pair came fully charged, and it has yet to need a charge, so I do not know how long it takes to charge from dead. It has a USB charging cord and it came with some other audio plugs. It paired easily with my phone. Just had to press and hold the center button for it to turn on the bluetooth function. The box did not come with instructions, but there is a link to their PDF manual on this product page under "product information" and then to the far right is, "Technical Specification". The link is under that.

The headphones can be used as a regular set- you will hear your music, as well as other environmental sounds, OR you can turn the Noise Cancelling feature to ON, and then you will notice a drastic reduction in other sounds. It says that it will reduce most sounds but human voices may still be heard. I had them on in our bedroom. My husband likes to watch tv, and I find it distracting, and loud. We also have the AC on, which adds to the noisy atmosphere. When I put these on, the sounds were mildly muffled. When I turned on the Noise Cancelling feature, the sound of the AC pretty much disappeared. So weird. The sounds from the tv were greatly reduced, though I could actually hear the person talking a little more clearly since the AC sound pretty much disappeared.

So yeh, it all functions as it should.

The controls on the side take some getting used to--figuring out which button does what without having to take the headphones off. I recommend practicing- long press to advance or back up a song, short press to turn up/down volume, etc.

The headphones are comfortable and accommodate my big head. They are adjustable. I like that they can be folded.

My only dislike, which can be a big one is that they hurt my ears after awhile. Not sure what it is, but my head feels like it is dragged down and my ears along with it. I really dont know what causes that, and if it as feature of these or something with my structure. Has a low level pain/discomfort associated with it. I can maybe use them for 45 minutes or so, then I need them off or simply take a break. You may not experience this.

To turn Bluetooth off (and save charge), you must remember to press that center button again. Turning the noise cancellation feature on/off does not do anything in that regard.

I bought this simply to play music, primarily mp3. I don't use any of the other functions, but it has several such as e-reader, FM radio, pictures, video, alarm, pedometer. Lots of extras if you like that sort of thing.

I just load it up with music from my computer, then either listen to music through a set of wired headphones, or I connect to a bluetooth speaker, or my main reason.. listening through speakers in my truck. It's an old truck with no current technology. I use one of those cassette adapters to play this music. Or when I borrow my husbands newer car, I use the bluetooth or more often, use an auxillary cord to connect. I never intentionally listed to it through the built in speaker. I like that there is that option despite not making use of it.

Since I use it primarily while driving, I needed to be able to get to the music without having to look at the screen or buttons. The only MP3 player I ever really loved was the old ipod classic circa 2005- so easy to navigate. I have yet to find anything quite like that, but at least this RUIZU Mp3 player is easy enough to navigate, so that makes me happy. It takes a little getting used to though.

So when it came time to buy another MP3 player, I looked at so many-- then circled back around to Ruizu since I was already familiar with it. The price makes it worth trying. I am using this strictly to boost the sound on our smart tv- a secondary but often used tv. I had purchased a similarly looking sound bar for my smart tv several months ago that works well. When this item came up as an option for review I figured it would an interesting item to try out since it has the addition of a subwoofer. Maybe it would be louder? Maybe it would sound more dynamic? We would see.. er, hear. So I tasked my husband with replacing our other sound bar with this set. It took him very little time to get it set up (less than 10 minutes, and it only took that long because our cat was helping. "helping").

The sound is definitely better and clearer than just using the speakers the tv comes with (which is usually the case). The sound is on par with the sound bar we had been using, except with the added dimension that the subwoofer provides. Without the subwoofer, it sounds just louder. With the subwoofer, it adds some depth and a nicer overall sound. We really just needed our tv to be louder. Cable is typically loud, but some programs on the various streaming services we have all have different levels of audio, with many being much too quiet. So better speakers have helped a lot.

The subwoofer connects to the soundbar via bluetooth. Both plug in, so plan to have 2 open spots in your power bar or wall receptacle. We have this system set up so the volume can be adjusted using the smart tv remote, rather than having to use the remote it came with. No issues there at all. Easy!

While I have the soundbar directly under the tv, I have the subwoofer set up in a corner a few feet away

The soundbar has spots in the rear in case you want to mount it to a wall. Subwoofer, does not.

Both are basic and minimalist looking. Subwoofer is black on black, soundbar is black with dark gray. No obnoxious branding or colors.

The instruction booklet is thorough, including information about the remote, battery info, placement and mounting, general operation, bluetooth operation, AUX in operation, Line-in operation, Optical-in operation (which is what I am using for use with my tv).

Overall sound is decent. Not home theater experience, but it definitely provides a sound and volume boost to internal tv speakers. I haven't yet tried it as a speaker for music. I really only purchased my original soundbar for use with tv (and replaced it with this for same purpose). I may give it a try anyway sometime soon. If I do, I will report back on how it does.

I like the added dimension that the subwoofer provides. I like the overall aesthetic. And because the combination of the two allows me to hear shows better than just using the tv speakers (on low audio streaming, as cable is always loud), I am pleased to use this.

I don't know hat this product costs, so I can't compare it. But, in short, it is about the same as just about any other low to mid priced soundbar. This is better sounding with addition of subwoofer. Not amazing, but definitely adds to my listening experience. 4 stars so far.

I'll keep it simple.: decent, lightweight holder; multi pack offering is best value

PROS: These are super light weight stands that will prop up pretty much any phone or tablet. They are adequate for their purpose. The stand can be adjusted to any position, and the spot that the device rests on is generous. Small, light and easy to carry around these have convenience in portability. Also, as I have the multi pack, you can place them all over or share. Or lose some, haha. Best value is multi pack. Single price is too much for quality of this product.

CONS: They claim anti-skid, but it fails in that feature. So lightweight that if you intend to tap at your device often, depending on what surface you have this placed on, it will scoot around some. I recommend modifying it with a couple beads (or line) of hot glue to give it a rubbery bottom. Or use a scrap of rug pad (that non slip material), or simply use it on a less smooth/hard surface. If just needing to prop up phone or tablet, then it will stay put. The kickstand is solid.

I am most comfortable using it on a smaller device if only because these have barely any weight to them. I have a much heavier stand that I prefer to use, but the price for one is significant. These are basic, light weight and super budget friendly (for multi pack).

Would make for a good stocking stuffer!

In my pics, I am demonstrating this product with pixel phone and LGtablet

Not to shabby of a gadget. It's just a wee little thing- fits in the palm of my hand- a little smaller than a deck of cards. Is powered through whatever device you are using. Does not need to be separately powered or charged.

What's in the (generic) box:
--Amplifier unit (roughly measured at 3.5" x 2.5" x .75")
--Type C to Type C Cable
--Type C to USB Cable
--3.5mm to 2rca Cable
--User Manual (a piece of paper with info)

I also received some other cable assembly in the box that I do not know what it is for. Appears to be used in Optical port. Bonus in terms of what is listed in product description, I guess.

What is on the Amplifier unit:
--One end of unit has: Headphone input, On/Off Switch for Bass, Volume knob
--Other end of unit has USB C port (in), Optical port (out), Gain (H/L) Switch, Line Out port.

Connection Diagram shows use between SPEAKERS OR HEADPHONES, and Mobile phone, Laptop, computer, or PS4. States that it does not work with tv. I haven't tried it yet, but I may attempt a work around- I'll let you know if I am successful.

In mean time, I have tried it between my smartphone (Pixel4XL) using AmazonMusic and two different types of speakers.

The first set of speakers is a nice plug in variety. They are circa 2004 CambridgeSoundWorks- where one cord is plugged into wall receptacle , and the other plug goes into a headphone port. They sound nice with use with my phone, so I didn't expect much difference when adding this amplifier. True enough, they have similar quality. My speakers without the amplifier are loud and I can hear some range. The addition of the amplifier allowed me to manipulate the bass, which can be nice depending on what I am listening to. I switched between High and Low on the gain switch. High boosts the overall sound, and low brings out a more mellow tone. Either are good.

Next, I tried it with a pair of novelty speakers circa 2002. Little SONYspeakers that are really just a headphone style output. So for purpose of review, using these is to mimic a set of basic headphones. They just happen to be in the shape of a speaker sitting on a desk rather than on the head. Cute little things, and when plugged into anything they really produce no further sound advantage over a basic set of headphones other than they aren't on the head. Thought these would be perfect to see how much this amplifier can help a bare bones basic sup par listening item. The sound went from a very low, just make out the music sound to truly being amplified. I could boost the volume and the sound opened up- not just got louder. So, while I will likely never use it with these, I thought hearing the difference on a terrible set of "speakers" (again, really just non head headphones) was absolutely worth mentioning. Tells me that this product IS working as intended.

Now, my Pixel4XL has fair sound already- not nuance, but not sounding like a tin can either. Using this with my nicer plug in speakers is great. Using my phone, with my nicer speakers AND this amplifier is a little nicer, but not hugely so. Perhaps in a larger room, or in other conditions where I may need a more dynamic sound to carry. This isn't a knock on the product, I think it is a nod toward the quality of my old speakers. I definitely can hear the improvement with ability to boost bass. High to high sounds similar. My speakers can't display a low end gain. So good for this product to offer that.

I do happen to have a speaker hooked up to my TV, and I am going to try to make that work if it doesn't complicate my wire management.

As for cord length.. if you are using it with your headphones, this is fine. You would otherwise be plugging it into the headphone port on your device, so really, with addition of the amplifier and the other cord to connect to device, you gain several extra inches of length. Beyond that, your mileage may vary in terms of what will work for you.

So far so good.

PS, I had low expectations of this unit, so I am impressed with my experience so far. As I continue to try it out with various devices in various environments, if I learn anything new-- good, bad, helpful, enlightening, I will surely be back to share.

I think it is worth trying out. I can't comment on price as I am not sure what these are really worth, and if there are true differences among the options out there. So my rating is based purely on effectiveness of product and accuracy of product description. If I had one wish on the options provided on this product, that would be to allow some additional range in the High/Low gain switch. I'd give this 4.5 stars, but since it is whole numbers only- 5 it is (unless I need to change it over time through learning something new about it).

Update!!: my review below was originally written 07/2019. I wanted to add an update THREE years later, 07/2022. This little laptop is still kicking. I use it every single day from comfort of my couch to write reviews, do basic doomscrolling (lol), write emails, etc. Camera still works. Speakers still good. No major issues. I never did do any adjustments to it. Just sort of kept using it as is. I;m maxed out for memory, so it isnt something I would rely on for loading pictures onto, but as mentioned.. if you just need something to get online with and do some shopping or searching, then this is fine. Has been worth it. I happen to be sniffing around for another laptop so I can go more photo work with it, but I havent been in a rush. I came back to this review so I could refresh my mind on the specs. It was then that I realized 3 whole years has gone by! OK.. back to orginal review:

It's a basic laptop. The price is right. You aren't paying a lot for a little. You are getting quite a bit of what you need for a couple hundred dollars. Cheaper than most tablets. If you just want something to get you online, to browse the internet, watch some videos, listen to some music, write some messages, play some basic games, do some video chatting, then this might be for you.I think most people want that. It doesn't have a lot of memory or speed, or a slew of storage- but it will get you far if you don't expect a lot from it.

I'm a gamer, so I won't be playing any MMOs on this (nor on most prefabs that are out there). But I will use it to play a variety of offline and online games such as those found on FB or POGO (ie; puzzles, word games, board games, hidden object, casino style, etc).

I use youtube to listen to music, watch videos, listen to podcasts etc.. the speakers are fine. I can hear what I need to, clearly and loudly, if I wish. Some of the sounds that come through are more dynamic than I expected, so that is a plus.

I do a little bit of office stuff, so I will continue to make use of Google docs but there is an option to activate a free 1 year trial of Office 365 which includes 1TB of storage (One Drive); after that there is a fee. The Microsoft website breaks down the pricing options, which include pay for the year, or by the month, if that is of interest to you.

This Windows 10 is in S mode, which is a special mode that essentially limits Windows 10 in a variety of ways to make it run faster, provide longer battery life, and be more secure and easier to manage. YOU DO NOT HAVE TO KEEP IT THIS WAY! The idea is that there is less security with non proprietary items (apps, browsers, internet security), and greater chance of phishing, slower processes, decreased PC health, etc. So "S Mode" isn't a different version, it is simply a different mode, with the usual Windows 10 home, underneath. From what I understand, you can take it out of S Mode, and you will have Windows 10 Home (and then you can use browsers of choice, apps of choice, security software of choice, etc) BUT you CAN NOT switch back to S Mode. It is a once and done deal. S Mode default browser is Microsoft Edge, the default search engine is Bing.

I'm used to using a different browser, and having more freedom of choice, but I am curious how this S Mode will do, as I have noticed in my time of using it that it never bogs down. It is likened to Chrome on Chromebook- it seeks to streamline all the while being as secure as possible. If at any point I just don't like it, at least I know I have the option of just using Windows 10 Home. But again, it is a ONE WAY DECISION.

The laptop itself is super light weight. It comes in at just 3.24 lbs according to description. Full keyboard, touch pad, USB 2.0, USB 3.1, headphone/microphone port, media card reader, web cam, 3 prong charge plug with long cord. Attractive black textured design. I've got some fingerprints on the lid/cover, but doesn't look bad.

No dvd/cd player. I bought a cheap external for those times I want to use it for storage, watching a video, or listening to a CD. Hey, I like options.

Set up is quick and easy. When Cortana (Microsoft virtual assistant) came on, I let her guide me through the start up process. I could answer a lot of her questions with speech. It did well with recognizing my words.

I still have quite a bit of learning to do about this laptop. One thing that I find interesting is that it has an option to use a phone app- where it will link your laptop and phone to each other, so you can (according to Microsoft website)
-Link your phone and PC to unlock a variety of cross-device experiences for Android and iPhone.
-See recent photos from your phone on your PC for Android only.
-View and send text messages from your PC for Android only.

Again, the price is right. This does come into play for me in terms of rating. For a couple hundred dollars, I am able to scroll through FB endlessly, add some comments without tapping them out on my phone or tablet, can access full webpages, can take pics, or video call with web cam, can play some lightweight games, etc..

At this point in time, I give it a full rating. I mean, I wouldn't go below a 4 for this anyway, and a 5 might be pushing it, but it is a nifty little machine, and I am happy so far. Once I realized that I am not stuck with S Mode, that boosted my opinion of it (not all PCs or laptops are given this S Mode option).

If I learn anything more that I think you will find useful, I will come back to update. I hope what I have provided thus far has been helpful to you. Take care :)

HOW TO GET RID OF THE SOAP OPERA EFFECT:

Ultimately, I found out turning off PICTURE CLARITY doesn't work, so you need to set it to CUSTOM, then turn off everything one by one, especially the BLUR and JUDDER reduction.

1. From your Home, go to MENU on the left side bar.
2. Then go to Settings, then ALL SETTINGS.
3. Go to PICTURE.
4. Choose your picture mode, I like DYNAMIC.
5. Then go to EXPERT SETTINGS.
6. Scroll down to PICTURE CLARITY SETTINGS.
7. Change it from Auto to CUSTOM.
8. Then reduce the Blur Reduction to 0.
9. Then reduce the Judder Reduction to 0.
10. You can also set the "Noise Reduction" to OFF, instead of AUTO. I can't tell the difference with noise reduction off. It's not like all of a sudden, your tv looks grainy. The difference is imperceptible, so I leave it off. Because a little noise makes the movies look more like theatre quality.

As mentioned above, I'm with Frontier and they use 192.168.254.xxx, so depending on how I hook up the NVR to my network, the DHCP will generate a proper working address, or it may not. Here are some noteworthy things I discovered. This pertains to my personal network/situation, but if you find yourself in the same boat, maybe this info could be useful:

Then, connect an ethernet cable from the Network port of the NVR to any of the POE ports on the POE Switch. Once I hooked it this way, the NVR's DHCP created an IP address that is in line with my Frontier network 192.168.254.xxx. Now I can view the cams on my ethernet PC, as well as my wi-fi app.

I've been trying to get good coverage in my garage so the security cams and smart devices don't get dropped connections, or long wait times when I try to connect from my app. This is finally the one! Frontier uses and all in one gateway, Arris NVG468MQ. In order to use the Netgear as the main router, I would need Frontier's help to put the Arris in bridge mode. I'm not sure if they can even do this, and since I purchased my own Arris to save rental fees, I wasn't sure how much they'd be willing to help either. So I didn't bother to try, instead, I set up the Netgear router in AP mode. To do this...

1. Go to Frontier's admin to turn off all wi-fi modes. Turn off both 2.4 and 5.0 modes.
2. Connect ethernet cable from the WAN port of the Netgear Router, to any available lan port of your Frontier gateway. Turn it on.
3. Using your smartphone or PC, connect to the Netgear wifi using the credentials labeled on the Netgear Router.
4. That's it. You should be online with the new wi-fi, but you'll want to change some things such as the orbi's admin password, your SSID's, etc. When you launch a browser under this new wi-fi, Netgear's admin should pop up allowing you to login to change your credentials, if it doesn't, then use routerlogin.net or orbilogin.net.
5. Since you've disabled Frontier's wifi, all your connected devices at home no longer works. But if you change your orbi's SSID to the same SSID that you were using, all your devices will work again. Keep in the mind, the Orbi system allows 4 different SSIDs. So you can still create other networks with different security levels.
6. Place the Orbi Satellite where you need better coverage. Power it on. Go back to Orbi Router and hit the sync button, within 30 seconds, you need to go back to the satellite and hit the sync button as well. Once they sync, which is indicated by solid blue for a few minutes, all lights will then be turned off. So keep that in mind, when it's up and running, there are no lights on the orbi router, or orbi satellite. I'm used to seeing some sort of lights on router equipment, so when there wasn't any lights, I was wondering if it was working properly. As it turns out, all lights are turned off when everything is up and running properly.

Even if you're not Frontier, the process I laid out above, to connect the Orbi in AP mode, should be similar. Hope this has been helpful! This is 5-Stars all the way!

All right, so a quirk that some of you may encounter is that when you connect the splitter, your TV may turn on Action Smoothing automatically. I have a TCL and that's the term they use. Other TVs may go by a different term. But essentially, it is the "soap opera" effect. It is great for sports, but weird for movies. But when I turned it back to off, the "soap opera" effect was still there. So I thought the splitter overrides the TCL settings, which would make it unusable for me. But on a hunch, I decided to unplug the TCL tv, and when I replugged, the "soap opera" effect was gone. So if you're experiencing this, try unplugging your TV and replugging it. I was able to reproduce this quirk with a different HDMI splitter, so this is not an issue with the HDMI splitter, it is an issue with the TV being stuck on Action Smoothing... In my case, it's a TCL.

Original Review
------------------
I needed to disable HDCP for a PC-less capture card. This splitter is more advanced than any splitter I have ever used. I'm used to the splitters that just splits and has no settings. This splitter makes you use your brain, and sometimes I don't want to use my brain. After a lot of tinkering with the various combinations of the switches, I ended up leaving the EDID at COPY1 and the Scaler switches to OFF... which was actually the default settings they ship to you. LOL!

Also understand that for every setting you play around with, if you don't get a picture, it might not mean it doesn't work. Along with your settings, you need to try switching your tv inputs back and forth, turning off/on your sources, turning off/on your capture card, etc., to truly see if it works. This will be the most confusing and frustrating part of setting this up. Not to mention, do you have the proper HDMI cables? Manual says use HDMI 2.0 cables. A lot of my cables are 1.3 or 1.4, but it still worked. So maybe if I had some HDMI 2.0 cables, it would have saved me some headache?

Ultimately, I stumbled upon the fact that if I leave it at COPY1 and Scalers off, turn off my capture card, then turn it back on, as well as switch tv input, then switch it back. It works! And it's not something you always need to do every time you turn on your tv. It's a one time thing. Once the splitter and your devices are in sync, you're good to go. There is one more step you can take if this doesn't work. There is a pinhole on the splitter labeled "UPDATE." Right on the splitter itself, there are printed notes on what this pinhole is for. Basically after resetting switches, changing inputs, etc., and you still have video or audio issues such as garbled noises, you need to use a tiny pin key, like the ones supplied by your smartphones to remove your sim trays. Poke it inside and feel for a button. Press it until it flashes 3 times. I guess this does some sort of "update" telling the splitter.. "Hey, these are the new settings, get with the program!" It worked for me in fixing garbled audio.

I will acknowledge that user experience and expertise level in AV tech plays a role in how much "tinkering" is necessary. The less you know, the more you're going to tinker. Still, I think the manual could be better and more in depth, maybe provide a pin key for the pinhole? Regarding this pinhole, the instructions says to push the "button." There is no button, and I had to look around for my sim key. For most consumers, this won't be "plug and play" as the listing suggest. But it works, and I will go 4 stars for this.

I was using the Harmony companion for the longest time, and before that, the Harmony 900. This Caavo is by far the best universal remote because it's so much more than that. Harmony is just a remote, it does not give you one unified user interface. If you've played around with a Smart TV's user interface, then you'll get the idea what this Caavo is all about. Except with Smart TV's, you still have to reach for your other devices' remotes, and if any device has voice search, it's only good for that specific device. The Caavo controls and searches all your devices! If I have a movie that's in my Tivo, that's in my plex, that is also available on Netflix.. all the choices are presented to me, so I can launch it from whichever device I choose. I have PLEX as my search priority, and it works beautifully. I was also a little nervous when hooking everything up because my TV is a Samsung from 2009, my Audio system is Sony from 2010. The Caavo has ZERO issues controlling everything.

My set-up.

Input 1: Tivo
Input 2. Fire TV
Input 3: Chromecast
Input 4: Currently Nothing
Optical OUT to my SONY AV system

My TIVO is set as the default. So when I push the power button on the remote. The Sony AV system comes on, tv comes on, and Tivo is what I'm watching! I was pleasantly surprised that it has all my Tivo controls because each button does double duty by short or long press. Let's say I want to watch a movie, I use the voice search to say BACK TO THE FUTURE, and since Plex is my priority, CAAVO gives me a list of choices with Plex highlighted. If it's in my tivo, netflix, prime, etc. it will give me all the options, but Plex will be highlighted since I set it as my priority. If I hit play, the Caavo switches input to my fire tv, launches Plex and auto-starts Back to the Future. And it happens fairly quickly. It's buttery smooth. If your preferred device to play Plex is on something else, say a Roku, you can set Roku as the default to launch Plex. If I fling something from my phone to the Chromecast, Caavo switches to my Chromecast input automatically. The voice search is perfect for youtube too because If you search something that doesn't sound like a movie, for example, How to Shop For a Miter Saw, the search results will show that there is no such movie, but included in the search results are youtube WEB searches, so you can easily play a youtube video on how to shop for a miter saw. LOL! Youtube is something I mainly do on my phone or pc because of the typing involved. But because of Caavo's voice search, we're watching it more on the big screen.

BTW, the voice recognition is terrific. It's pretty much on par with anything else out there. I've seen videos where some guy is complaining that he says Open Plex and it keeps giving him search results for DUPLEX. I don't know if Caavo has improved since his reviews, or if it just didn't like his voice, but I've never had an issue with Caavo not understanding what I said. Alexa, Google Assistant, etc. can also be integrated, but I don't see them as an efficient way to use Caavo, unless you lost the Caavo remote, then you can ask Alexa to turn on your tv I guess.

There is a slight learning curve, but it will be time well spent. And it will be easy to teach to your household members because it simply works. Lets face it, non-techies in the home will never touch your Harmony, right? I've used Harmony for 10 yrs, and nobody in my family touches it. They know how to use this Caavo!! This is a game changer!

July 17, 2019 UPDATE:
--------------------------
If you have Plex as your search default, I have a tip for you. The voice search will not understand funky spelling. For example the documentary "Comix: Beyond the Pages." The voice search will spell Comix correctly as COMICS, and so you will get zero results. But if you simply say "Beyond the Pages," the search engine will be able to find "Comix: Beyond the Pages" for you. Another quirk I ran into was "Mr. and Mrs. Smith." Even though the search engine spelled it exactly as my Plex has it, for some reason it didn't find this title. But if I just say, "Smith," it then pulls up the movie for me. So basically when you hit a snag, just use fewer words instead of saying the whole title. That's it! I really love this feature of the Caavo.
