Some cool features about this dash cam I didn't realize existed before it was installed and I was driving with it:
+ Has lane departure warning visually and with a beep noise
+ I think it's also alerting me whenever I'm being radar gunned or there's a speed camera nearby because there's a wifi symbol with a beeping warning that sometimes appears.
+ You can replace the included SD card with a larger one so it will hold on to more recordings before overwriting the older files

There is room for my 13" laptop, my 12.9" ipad pro, all my camera lenses and the body for my sony A7ii, snacks, water bottle, and you can attach a tripod to it.

The failure of this camera backpack (along with all others I've tried is that it looks really bulky on my short petite frame ( 5'4" woman). I think it makes me look fatter because of how wide the bag is, I tried it on my guy friend (also a photographer) who I was hanging out with and it looks much better! He really appreciated the hip and chest straps that go across the front for when he's on his motorcycle.

I would definitely use this for travel. Your expensive camera gear can only be retrieved by taking off the backpack since the zipper is next to your back which makes me feel safer. Would be great for carrying everything through the airport and sending your photography equipment through the security scanners.

The hip and shoulder straps really help to distribute the weight of the bag so it's also great for long hikes to get that perfect landscape shot in the mountains. I'm looking forward to trying it out more this summer in the rockies.

TLDR:
Pros:
- color/texture of the bag is really attractive
- has plenty of room for your favorite lenses and mirrorless camera (I don't have a DSLR so couldn't test that)
- can also fit laptop + tablet, charging cables, snacks
- comfortable shoulder straps
- comes with a waterproof bag that fits around the backpack in case you're stuck in bad weather
- camera section is modular which allows you to fit a variety of lenses, I was also able to fit my flash in here.
- GREAT bag for the price. You can't beat $44 for this.
- there are thoughtful interior flaps by your lenses that prevent water from touching them in case if rain gets in by the zipper.

Cons:
- Bulky looking
- could have more pockets instead of two laptop sections.
- If you open bag when its sitting up instead of laying down your camera will fall out
- the interior finishings arent as nice as the outside fabric
- mine was missing the black strap you see in the product photography that holds the camera in vs. having it just sit at the top of the bag.

Overall it's a great bag if you're starting out in photography for traveling and just to store all your gear in one place safely. I think you can't beat the price for this bag and the fabric on the exterior is very attractive. It does get heavy with all your gear in it so I really appreciate the hip straps to distribute the weight.

We bought a pair at Costco for the same sale price here (59.xx) fit my(his) fat head perfectly, with room to move about freely, instead of like most headsets where you feel them moving around etc etc, cancelled noise very well, (I imagine they'd be great on my motorcycle) but after about a week, someone stole them while I was charging them at work :/ my fault, I know, but I really wanna get 2 more sets for our cruising!

excellent quality, sturdy as a tank, has options to change response time among other things, the ASUS of equal specs that I bought is cheap compared to these monitors, could not recommend more highly, like the other reviewer here says "never heard of viewsonic so I was skeptical" well, take it from him and me, it is an excellent monitor, have purchased two, the ASUS we recently got was cheaper, but.. it's also cheaper quality, would recommend this monitor any day of the week over the ASUS!

also, this comes with all cords you could need vs asus only coming with a DVI...

So far so good with this product. I was a bit uncertain when I first got it, because the hinge seemed really tight and I was afraid I was going to break it, but after a few uses, it loosened up enough that it no longer worries me. This case is useful for a number of different reasons. The keyboard is easy to type on and very quiet, so if you are trying to take notes in class or work without disturbing someone, it is very appropriate for that.

The keyboard lighting is awesome, giving you ten different colour options and three different settings for each colour, as well as letting you go without backlighting at all, if you choose to do so. Some of the colours are unique, like pink and aquamarine.

The different ways you can spin the ipad whilst using this make it convenient for a lot of different situations, although mostly I use it in laptop or tablet mode. The case feels relatively well built and the set up is so easy that you don't need any technical know how to do it. The instructions that came with it were simple and easy to follow and I have had no issues with is so far.

The battery life is easy to check, since there is a button just for that, and the colour of the case itself is an exact match for the rose gold of the ipad I bought.

My only real complaint, is that it is somewhat difficult to get the ipad out of the case once you have put it in, without feeling like you are either going to damage the device or the case itself. perhaps there is an easier method to do it and I just haven't discovered it yet. Otherwise, this is a great product and if it endures m abuse for a year or so, I will consider it to have been well worth the money spect on it. It certainly beats having to drag around and extra keyboard and separate stand everywhere I go when I want to work on the fly.

I'va had good luck with this brand previously, and this particular device seems to be no exception to the quality I have come to expect. It works right out of the packaging, is quick and requires no great knowledge to set up. Great for when you need additional backup but don't want to bring a larger storage device with you.

We haven't had this for a long time, but so far we are very pleased with it. The setup was easy, it connects to all the devices we need it to, the sound and picture are both good and it has a lot of entertainment options built into it. You can get over 3000 streaming services with this television and the remote makes it easy to get to both Amazon video and Netflix right away without having to scroll through a lot of options.

I like that everything is built in and you don't have to stress over trying to connect other devices to get to your various streaming accounts. I was also impressed with how easy it is to connect to wifi and how well it works, without stopping to buffer. The receiver is strong and works better with Netflix than our other devices have in the past.

Overall, this was well worth the inexpensive price.

This TV has excellent color and a beautiful display. I like that the features are simple to understand and yet it has a lot of features to choose from. The sound is excellent and with the addition of a home surround system it sounds just like being in a movie theater. The remote can be programmed to do multiple functions and the set up was pretty straight forward. The response time is great and Shark Week was terrifying on this TV (yes that was important.) Pretty much everything in the menu is interactive and fully adjustable for the viewer's preference. I love that it has the theater wide settings for optimal viewing as well.

The only real problem I have with this TV is that there is a screen glare issue. My living room has a giant picture window and no matter where I put the TV there is still a glare. Otherwise I think this is a great TV for the price and would highly recommend it for the movie buff.

I'm very satisfied with this product. The auto-connect feature is my favorite part. I can leave my phone in my pocket, never having taken it out and still listen to my music on my iPhone (where it left off) and take/make phone calls as well. Very easy to pair my phone with the device. When my car turns off, the device is disengaged and disconnects from my phone. When I turn my car on, it takes about 3 seconds and then I hear a small beep noise, and now I can click the button on the puck which resumes my music/media.

Like my title says, this is exactly what I wanted. I wanted complete hands-free in my car, but didn't want to use any annoying bluetooth earpieces. The sound quality is good as well. I did get some loop noise in my 2008 Mazda 3 so I did have to buy a female-to-female 3.5 mm part from RadioShack for $5 which resolved the noise problem. I already had a cable with a noise loop shield so all I needed was this part. You can also buy little filter clamps at RadioShack which you would just place right on the cable and should reduce noise. The part was only $3, I just chose to use my existing part instead which I also bought on Amazon

Overall, 5 stars! Great product! The price is right. I'm a happy customer. It was shipped and received sooner than I expected. I am overjoyed about this product.

I wish the instructions on this were a little more clear. This thing is so loud and disruptive, that if you don’t know how to turn it off, you’re really going to turn some heads. I had this installed in less than 20 minutes. Very easy. It does come with a template but I didn’t have to use it. There are 2 adjustable brackets and all hardware is included. I adjusted the width to snuggly hold my soundbar and it’s solidly in there! No issues. I recommend!

Surprisingly good solar security camera. The solar panel eliminates the need to have to dismount unit and recharge battery. This picks up almost 180° field of view and night vision is decent. Everything you need to mount is included. You need a micro sd card for this!!! But no membership required because of that.
Excellent speaker. Easily connects to Bluetooth and the sound that comes out of this is awesome! The tube shape makes it easy to take along. It also has a carrying strap and little rubber feet.

[[VIDEOID:818a872c08a61d024a46458a38ec538d]] For such a tiny speaker this thing really packs a punch! I ended up ordering six to give out is party favors for a girls weekend and we had the best time using them. The colors are really bright and individual. There is a strap connected to each speaker that fits around your wrist. The top is where the speaker unit is, the bottom is where the on/off button is located, as well as the Bluetooth connect button. Connecting them is actually easy, but not after a few beers. Lol. You have to make sure your phone is not connected to anything, and the speakers are turned on prior to connecting to your phone, it takes a little bit of practice. Each one comes with a c cable to usb cable wire, But no charging block. Each one comes with a zippered carrying case that is actually pretty well-made. It doesn’t smash in your backpack or tossed into your purse. I highly recommend these for the price you really can’t beat the sound they make.

After years and years of running with Vizio, I finally switched to this Samsung. This new model is the thinnest, flattest screen I have ever used. It is heavier than the Vizio brand.  Still it fits a standard wall mount. The picture is incredible. It’s ultra clear, the picture almost looks fake. The remote is extremely responsive, and so intuitive everything you need is easy to access. You can also use Alexa to turn off/on and locate stuff. Most of the apps are built in. Awesome sounding speaker too!! I am not tech-savvy. I do enjoy streaming a few times a week and we have family movie night weekly. So, lots of colorful, loud marvel verse pictures. 🥇

My husband is over the moon with his new speaker. It BOOMS! He hooked it up in about 10 minutes via a HDMI cable connection into our Vizio tv. It’s low profile and easily fits on our console table, tucked in the back. You can walk mount it too. I can cast onto the tv thru my phone and quickly change a song on video. [[VIDEOID:35b82c05743ed9063e3118beba856973]] What a fun record player! I got this as a gift for my 15 yo daughter and she’s surprised me with how often she’s used it. It’s compact and has a pretty decent sound for a one piece system. You can hear a chime when you lift up the sound arm so you know it’s on and working.

For the price, these are fantastic. I got them for my 3rd grader to use at school. She can toss them in her backpack and thrash them up pretty bad and they still haven’t broken. They fit comfortably over her ears, they can be worn for quite awhile without aching, and she said the sound quality is decent. I am so done with spending too much $ on headphones. Kids are so rough on them. So, I’m happy to have found these at such a good price.

For the price, you can’t really beat these! They plug into a c port and come with a little zippered carrying case. Any ear bud I wear eventually makes my ears hurt. These do too, but no worse than any other one. They have a comfortable rubber tip on them that’s easy to adjust. They sound very decent.
I like these alot. They fit in my ear nicely and comfortably. They cancel out the noise fairly well and they dont leak sound. I have never gotten the tangled but we will continue to see about that...

I...LOVE this gadget!❤️ It is so easy to use and very very helpful. After initial charge, I easily connected to Bluetooth. Then, it can be unplugged and it holds a charge for weeks. My iPhone fits snug in the holder and the speaker is loud enough to easily hear podcasts and audiobooks clearly. It takes phone calls too and obviously can be used as a speaker to play music on. I’m super happy with it. I want one in my bathroom to listen to books while getting ready, and one in my kitchen to prop my phone up while looking up recipes and listening to music.

For the price, these are a great option for replacement earbuds. Which I am always losing or breaking. They are comfortable and I can wear for a long time without irritation. They fit perfectly in my iPhone. The sound is remarkable decent! Obvs, not perfect, but for price, I’m not disappointed.

These are my 12 yo boy’s favorite head phones. He uses them for school work and for gaming. He said they are comfortable and the sound is awesome. He prefers having 1 ear uncovered. It’s easier for me too because it’s easier to get his attention when he’s “immersed” in a game. I feel like this is a pretty sturdy set too. We’ve used it for a full month on a daily basis and have had no problems. They connect to Bluetooth smoothly and hold a charge for a long time.

[[VIDEOID:25eadd9d5b2ee9acadb4b980a82344ea]] This is our first ukulele. It was simple to tune and holds its tune for longer than we expected. It’s light and comfortable to hold and play. This comes with an extra set of strings, tuner and strap. Seems like a good solid instrument. Comes with a really nice little padded case. The case has backpack straps as well as a carrying handle. Also has a front, zipper closure pouch.

SUCH A GOOD PRODUCT! I read the reviews on past models and it seems like this company really listens to their customers. (Some annoyances included only 1 charging cable and wistful dreams of these being solar so they didn’t have to be continually recharged, as well as a clock that offered both a 12 hour format and 24 hour format) This new model took those things into consideration and they produced an even better product. Now these DO come with 2 chargers and a plug so you can charge both sensors at once. This also means you can keep main unit plugged in all the time now, even if you need to charge a sensor or doorbell. It took more than 2 hours to initially charge sensors. They come 20% charged. Their light changes from red to green when ready. After charging, I had to adjust the sensitivity levels. You’ll need to unscrew the back plate (a screwdriver is included!!) and simply move the switch from low to high or in between, whatever your needs are. After putting back plate on again they are ready to mount. The initial set is already “paired” to main unit so you can change the chime thru the main unit easily. I chose 3 different sounds so I know what zone the movement’s in. Mounting screws are included. Though 3M outdoor strips would be heavy duty enough to hold these too if you didn’t want to drill holes. My sensors are about 300+ feet from my house. There’s no problems with reception. I used the “doorbell” as more of a panic/assist button. We live on acreage and sometimes yelling for help when you’re far past the home is impossible. So I mounted the doorbell on the barn and programmed a panic-inducing chime for it. I’m sure my kids will really like that. :/
Overall, this took about 20 minutes to install. The directions are very well laid out and the product comes with a two yr warranty. This combined with what appears to be excellent customer service means these sensors are totally worth it!
I gave 4 stars because ear cover is teeeny. Sound is good, hook up is good. Plastic but hopefully they will stay intact.

I'm using these for Rosetta Stone lessons. Working brillantly so far. Quite comfortable, the volume is easy to adjust and the sound is clear. USB plug in. I plug into my desktop tower and cord is long enough to reach my office chair.
These are very simple and straightforward headphones. They are comfy and have clear sound. They adjust to head size and use a jack, not a usb port. We've had no technical problems with these at all.

I have been using this Dell All In One for about 6 weeks. It's definitely the nicest computer I've ever owned. Right out of the box it's basically ready to go; you need to register it though. The touch screen is extremely sensitive and fun to use; it's also large enough to use for movies, tv etc. The camera pops up when you want to use it and has high resolution and pops back down when not in use. The sound is boomin'. Both the mouse and keyboard are wireless and require batteries. I've had no problems with either. Right after I initially set this up, I tripped over the cord and broke it. It costs $80 to replace and I had to order on Dell sight.  (Only imitations on Amazon) I bring this up because replacement parts are expensive. It is loaded with Microsoft, so, Cortana is voice assistant. And Microsoft edge is search engine. No probs using chrome however and I've downloaded several chrome extensions. There is no disc drive. There is an HDMI port on the back so you can connect to a DVD player etc if you want. On the bottom, next to power button, there is an HDMI button that allows you to switch to hdmi mode to use a DVD player or external drive. It's light enough that I can pick it up and move it anywhere. It tilts on it's base too so when I stream my exercise workouts and I'm doing floor work, I can see so much better than my old computer. It doesn't come off base so it can't be mounted to wall or anything. I'm super happy with it and it is a joy to use everyday.

I set this up at my property entrance just over 1/4 mile from my house. I totally get the signal 100% of the time. It was easy enough to install, might work to have 2 ppl install so 1 person can align the 2nd sensor easier. The chimes are really old school chimes. Like, original cell phone chime and 7-11 store chime. They are either SUPER LOUD or quiet. The receiver is this UFO plastic piece that is really bulky and hard to place discreetly in your house. Mines in my laundry room so it's not too big an issue for me.

I've been using these almost everyday since they arrived and AM LOVING THEM!! These are the 2nd pair of Santana bluetooth I've ordered (the 1st being from the "oye" line) These are head and shoulders better than those. They are super easy to connect to bluetooth tooth. I've used both my phone and my computer as devices with ZERO problems or drops. The sound is freaking AMAZING! I started off with Soundgarden's 'Slaves and Bulldozers' and from the 1st second of that baseline it felt like I was enveloped in sound. I then listened to Lana Del Ray to hear a airy, female voice and the sound was pure and ethereal. You can hear each distinct part of the music. The bass is balanced and not overblown. I use these on my morning walks everyday so now they just play all random stuff. They are comfortable and even if I sweat in them, they wipe clean to a like-new product. The charge lasts for a solid 24 hours. The controls are ergonomically in the correct place. These headphones prove that music is indeed the best invention in the world!

Fantastic quality! These are comfortable to wear for extended periods of time. They do a pretty decent job of cancelling out outside noise. The sound quality is solid, with bass, treble, low pitched and high pitches coming in clear. They've held up perfectly to daily wearing by my 2 boys.

Totally decent radio. Small. Easy to dial in a station. For the price, the sound is fine. Antenna pulls out to capture longer range. I just feel like it's smart to have one of these on hand in case of emergencies.

This motion detector is installed at the entrance to my property about 1/4 mile from my front door. There are tons of trees between the sensor and the chime. It works FLAWLESSLY! We don't get many suprise guests, as we live behind a closed gate on a country road. But with this, I can tell when the kids or our dogs leave the property. Or when my husband comes home at night. You can't see our front gate from our house, so it's definitely added an additional layer of peace of mind for me. It does go off at night occasionally due to deer or raccoons passing the sensor. I have it set to the lowest volume and the shortest chime so it doesn't bother me. I gave this 4 stars because you cannot plug anything else into the socket when this is plugged in. It's pretty big. Also, the chime choices are all really irritating. Most chime choices sound like the 7-11 store door chime or the old, old wireless phone chimes from 25 years ago. It gives it feel a slightly tacky effect. I have this in my laundry room though so I don't see it and the chime stays quieter.

Vegan leather is just pleather, y'all. I looked it up. I did not want to like this bag. But, I got it and had to review it. So that meant, I had to use it. And use it I did. It is a joy to use!! Suprise! There is so much room inside. And all my stuff fit and was so organized. The pockets are all roomy, the middle zippered pocket is big enough for my massive day timer and various documents. My phone, kept in the phone pouch, stays up toward the top so I can reach it along with my wallet. The bag is sturdy and doesn't slump all over. The inside vinyl part makes a scratchy, plastic noise when anything touches it. That bugs me. And to describe a vinyl purse as vegan leather is disgraceful!! But it looks classy and pretty authentic. I won't tell my husband though. He'll make fun of me. #savethecows
I like these. They look a bit retro and are comfortable to wear. The volume works fine. I use them with my chromebook to watch movies. Have used for a month. No problems.

My 6 year old daughter loves these! The sparkles don't flake off and they have soft, leather-like padding for the ear cover. She says they are comfortable and they sound decent too. They fold down a little so they don't take up too much room.

We have had no problems with our new system. Set up was pretty straightforward. I think the unit looks clean and modern. Comes with a free trial period of cloud access. Must purchase membership afterwards if you want to store your surveillance!

These earbuds are pretty good. They tilt at an angle. Much different than previous earbuds,which stick straight out. These,  are pretty comfortable, they have a rubber ear piece and gently angle out. They sound fine. Honestly,  earbuds have to be replaced so often,  it's hard to get stoked about them.

These are in my opinion the best wireless headphones I've worn. They are so light, flexible and comfortable. I've worn them dozens of times now for hours at a time. I've had no issues with connectivity and the sound had been clear and vibrant.

It doesn't get much easier than this to enjoy music with no cords or wires. So nice to not have a cord to contend with!! Set up was easy and sound quality is great. Paired easily via bluetooth with iphone 7plus. So far, these have been very comfortable to wear and stay in my ears while I'm working. I ordered specifically because of the diamond coating. I work in an environment that has dust and particles flying around all the time and wanted something slightly more durable. Can take them out and put in pocket too without worries that they'll get tangled and thrashed. Well done, Anker.

So far, I have only good things to say about this sound bar. I waited 2 weeks after setting up to write review. It is pretty heavy in weight. If you're planning on mounting to wall, make sure you use metal wall anchors or try to find studs. I'm using this with a 55" Vizio. My greatroom is 25" x 25". Half of that area has 15" ceilings. This soundbar fills the space up nicely without being echo-y. Good bass, rich sound. As always, your HDMI cables make a big difference in the quality of your experience. Installation was not that hard. The directions are clearly labeled. Also included is a mounting template which I thought was a nice touch. I didn't use it. Mine is just on a media table. The included remote is lightweight and easy to use. I'm sure you can spend tons more $ on a super high end sound bar. But this one doesn't suck and I love being able to have a surround sound experience.

This is the 1st set of wireless headphones I've ever owned and they sound like FREEDOM! They arrived in a pretty classy box with 2 extra silicone earbud inserts and a charging cable. The earphones came in a small and suprisingly solid, snap-close carrying case that IS THE CHARGER! Meaning, you place the earbuds into the case and then plug your charging cable into the case. Very cool. I had to download the jaybird app to set up the earbuds. I had no problems and followed the prompts successfully. The sound from these little guys is freakin' amazing! You can very clearly hear distinct instruments during songs. There is no fuzziness, just very crystal clear sound. They are pretty comfortable to wear. The charge is supposed to last 6 or so hours. After wearing them a few times exercising,  I just out them back on charger. I hope they last. Very very happy with this order.

For the price, these are great. I am totally over spending a small fortune in headphones for my kids. They get excited or absentminded and chew or pull on cord which renders headphones useless. The sound quality on these is totally fine. They are very very light. Easy fit on their heads too.
So far, these have worked great. They fit and stay put. The sound is above average. We go thru these so fast, so this price point is decent too.

The monitor looks great & is very portable. I don't game so I'm not an expert on lag but I don't notice any in day to day use. I do travel for work & work from multiple locations & this has been wonderful for setting up a 2nd screen. It works best when plugged into the A/C power adapter but it can be powered from my laptop from a single USB-C cable that also provides the video source.

It is very thin with the stand/cover so it easily fits in my laptop backpack. The packaging it shipped in is nice & sturdy & has a lot of foam which made me question whether I should be unceremoniously chucking it in my backpack but it hasn't been damaged. The screen & case stand do weigh a little over 3lbs so the addition to my backpack is noticeable.

The case/stand was a little confusing to put on but it works great. The surface is grippy enough to tilt the monitor all the way to the edge. The speakers are about like laptop speakers in volume but lack low end.

These look different but they are comfortable & stay put, I guess earbud design is not a settled issue yet. I have been using these primarily for voice calls & listening to music on my computer in a very noisy warehouse where noise cancellation is paramount.
I have pretty much made these my 'computer' earbuds because the microphone is so good & the volume can be loud. The music sounds good but isn't especially dynamic. There is no volume control at the earbud but they will start/pause & answer calls with touch. They will also answer a call by double-touching the button.
I like the voice confirmation when turning on & off the noise cancellation. Instead of just different tones a voice says "active noise cancellation on/off" or "talk through mode" (it gets loud in the warehouse & I couldn't always be sure if the cancellation was on with my other earbuds). These default to no noise cancellation when they are turned off by putting them in the charge case which I do not like.
Pairing was easy & the two earbuds have never failed to connect to each other which is something I can't say about any other Bluetooth set I have used.

[[VIDEOID:c19caf51ed5645772d7b1a0a5834b6d6]] The Soundbeast video capture device couldn't be easier to use. I have been wanting to make files from some old tapes & DVD's I recorded over the years but I dreaded using the computer. This device is so much easier to use & also doesn't tie up my computer. It simply plugs into a DVD player, VCR or even a camcorder with RCA type plugs & records to MP4 in real time. The device even has a tiny little screen & a tinny speaker so I don't even have to use a monitor to see & hear what is recording. It does have an HDMI output (not an input) to run a monitor directly from the device but I have just been hooking a TV to the DVD player while it plays.
The capture device records MP4s directly to either a USB drive or a micro SD card. I have only been using it with the USB stick. The little speaker sounds bad but the little screen has surprisingly good resolution. I have used it connected to the DVD player & a camcorder. It also converts purchased DVDs in my experience.

I ordered this mouse for my wife to use with her new Chromebook & she loves it. She likes the large, domed style with the thumb relief & hasn't been happy since her old Microsoft mouse died. It has more buttons than I know how to use (forward & back on the thumb side). I'm not sure if she even uses the thumbwheel but it is large, grippy & rolls smooth with light detents. We have been using it on a finished wood table & it moves smoothly & doesn't have any issues with the laser reading. The mouse requires the included USB, receiver dongle which stores in the bottom of the mouse & is easy to swap between computers.
I had to look up what the CPI adjustment button is but it is pretty handy in that the speed of the mouse can be adjusted from just the button on top. The mouse takes a single 'AA' battery. I prefer my rechargeable mouse but this is better for her.

[[VIDEOID:9b88dadfbf58bb503f1928922845b685]] I ordered this dash camera after stumbling across a dash-cam video on the internet & realized I could potentially save myself a lot of hassle either in an accident or even a police encounter. I had one a few years ago when I had a long commute but these days I do most of my driving in rental cars & in unfamiliar areas I wanted something small, portable & quick to install. This camera just takes a second to stick to the windshield with the suction mount & it takes a mini USB plug for power. It comes with a 12V port adapter with a very long cord but I mostly power it with a short USB cord & my own adapter.
I'm very pleased with the video quality & sound. I have tested it with 1080p30 1020x1080 & 720P60 1280x720. Given the long record time with the included 32gb memory I will probably keep it at 1080p. The microphone picks up the sound of the turn signal switch which is good & also my singing to the radio which is bad.
I don't know how well the video resolution will come across in the attached video but I'm impressed with the image I get on my computer, especially files made at night. In reviewing the videos taken at 1080p (& with my filthy windshields), I have to be right behind car to make out its license plate. I have since maxed out the resolution to 1440P because of this but I'm not sure it made that much difference. The wide angle also tends to make things look further away than they are, the car in the last clip was much closer to my car than it looks in the video.
The included 32gb memory card holds over 4 hours of video at 1080p30 1020x1080 resolution & that's day & night. The camera will over-write files that aren't saved & it has a "save" button that stores files where they won't be over-written. The software also has an adjustable feature that automatically saves files where an impact is detected. In the 2 cars I have used it, a big pothole or bump in the road will trigger an incident on the medium setting (see my video). The camera will also take still a still picture when the impact detection is triggered or the file is selected for saving.
The camera doesn't have it's own battery but so far it has managed to save the last file if the car shuts off the 12v port or usb when the key goes off. I have mine to record short, 5 minute clips as a precaution against this, The clip length is adjustable up to 10 minutes. Without the battery, won't record any activity when the car is parked even if the car is bumped if the cord is not plugged into an active port.

I just got finished mounting a 65" Sony television to my brick chimney with this kit. I love how much adjustment there is with this mount once it is up. It is easy to pull the set away from the wall & also turn it to the sides. The tilt angle is also adjustable but requires hand-loosening & then tightening a couple of fasteners. There are 2 height positions for the TV that are pretty easy to change &, at least with my Sony, more room for adjustments based on how the brackets attach to the TV.
The instructions for this mount are pretty good but there is a lot of measuring, math & test fitting involved in setting up the height which isn't addressed in the instructions. The kit comes with a variety of hardware options & even comes with a small, magnetic level to help position the mount, an HDMI cable & some cable organizers.
The only issue I had was concerning mounting to the brick chimney. There are a variety of holes laterally for different stud spacing but only two sets vertically. The vertical spacing was not to my liking because it pushed the mounting holes too close to the edge of the bricks. I was also a bit weary of the plastic inserts to mount to brick or concrete walls instead of the metal expanders but the screws bit hard and gave a good, tight feel when they were snugged.
Now I just need to sort out those wires.

I have been working out of detached workshop behind my house & set this in front of my house to capture the circular drive. It's not excessively far but it's out of range for a bluetooth device reach. It rings if anything goes through the circle (where the Camaro is) or down the drive past the house. I have tested it by walking at the very edge of the drive & it hasn't failed to alert. I may adjust the settings down before I move the receiver inside because it picks up a lot of cat activity. I didn't realize how many neighborhood cats stroll through my drive early in the morning.
I wanted to check this out before I committed to a mounting place so I set it under that oak tree. I thought it might be too shady to maintain the solar power requirements but it's been there a week with no issues. It's so discrete I'll probably just keep it on the rocks & move it closer to the tree. The mounting hardware is pretty nice, though, with a ball-jointed mount that sets up easy since it comes apart & has a lot of adjustment.
The receiver has three or 4 chimes & none of them are subtle. It also has another 30 or so songs. Some are holiday themed which could be fun if you were expecting guests for a party. It has some public domain tunes from the Baroque & Renaissance period as well as some contemporary tunes like "Music Box Dancer". I currently have it on what sounds like a mariachi band playing "March of the Toreadors" from Carmen which is kind of hilarious but I can't imagine what maniac would want to be alerted by that in their house ever. Most of the rest of the songs are like that.

These wireless headphones sound good but I wouldn't say great. They certainly have a lot of features for the price point. The charge case has a battery inside so they can charge while in a pocket & not plugged in. Both headphones have a button that can pause or answer calls but unfortunately there is no volume control on the headphones. These worked very good for phone calls, I am especially impressed with the microphone since it is at ear level & doesn't pick up ambient noise too much.

I mistook the "wireless charging case" for a case that could be set on a wireless charging pad & I was astounded that the headphones still had plenty of charge after 10+ hours of use without plugging in. Because of that I have only used them for about 4 hours a day without putting them in the case (where they got recharged without me realizing) so I haven't been able to test the 6 hour battery life yet. The case easily fits in a pocket or bag. The battery is only down about 20% after 3 days of re-charging the phones after 3-4 hours of use per day.

My set came in a fancy box with magnet enclosure. I may have gotten a pre-production version though because the contents don't exactly match the description & the instructions have some mistakes. These did come with several sets of memory phone & rubberized ear cushions. I tried a couple of different combinations & found that the foam cushions that were pre-installed were the best fit for me.

The headphones came installed with the "ear hooks" that go around the ears. The box also contains "ear fins" or "Freebit clips" which hook inside the ear. I tried both & prefer the inside ear option. They fit in the charger much more easily, don't interfere with my glasses & they stayed in place during my most rigorous activities. Both types of ear pieces slip over the headphones 360° & can be put on backwards or from the wrong side. It can take a lot of tinkering to get the fit just right.

Pairing was quick & straightforward. There are specific instructions for re-connecting the right earphone if it drops. I did have to do that once & it is several steps. I took a picture of the instructions so I could do it again but the set can also be "forgotten" & paired again to correct it.

These are pretty bulky. They don't feel all that big when wearing them so I was surprised when I saw myself in the mirror.

These earbuds sound good & don't have an exaggerated bass. The USB-C connection is flawless but it does stick out unlike a 3.5mm headphone with a right angle. The earbuds fit well but are bulky & the wires are heavy.

I love the volume and pause/play button section. It is large & easy to tell the controls by feel. The earbuds are also easy to tell the left from the right by feel because the left is convex & the right is concave. The microphone is better than any other set of earbuds I have had to date & I go through a lot.

When these earbuds are plugged into my LG phone calls & texts sound through the speaker when the earbuds are not being used.

The 1st thing I noticed about these headphones when I received them (other than the amazing box they came in) are that they are noticeably heavier than my other headphones. I take that as an indication of higher quality speakers.

They do sound amazing. I listened to an album I have heard dozens of times before in the car & on earbuds & could hear elements I have never picked up on before. I actually thought I was listening to a different version of the song. I expected an exaggerated bass like I get with some earbuds but the sound is straightforward.

The noise cancelling seems about the same as my much cheaper headphone set but both are very good & make a world of difference on a plane or other noisy situations. Pairing is practically automatic on Apple devices but it is also easy for my Android phone. I think we have 3 or 4 devices currently paired to this set.

The headphones turn on as soon as they are unfolded. This is a cool feature but it means they are always on if they are worn around the neck. The battery lasts a long, long time. One charge played movies & noise cancelling for 7 hours of flying, probably another hour of music plus at least 4 more hours of just noise cancelling because someone forgot to close them until they were down to 2%

The volume & play /pause are easily controlled by tapping the right ear cuff. The charge port is the robust Apple lighting cable type which was a surprise to me until my daughter told me that Apple owns the Beats brand.

The carry case is much bigger than the folded headset. At first glance it doesn't look thick enough to provide good protection but pinching the material reveals that it has a thin, soft layer of foam or something inside. The zipper is the waterproof type which is a nice. The case comes with a hang tag & carabiner.

The headphones were too tight for my XL head. My ears were sore after long days on airplanes. I extended the cuffs all the way to reduce the tension which helped a little but made them harder to wear. The ear cuffs are a little smaller than another pair I have & I like the larger cuff because I can move them around a little on the ear for comfort while still getting a good 'seal' on my ear.

I ended up giving these to my daughter & she absolutely loves them. She is very is proud to have the Beats brand which isn't so important to me.

I am using this HDMI to RCA adapter so that I am able to use my Fire stick on an older tube-style television in my workshop that has RCA connections. Installation is easy. It comes with a wall USB power adapter and a power cord & attached RCA plugs. The HDMI cable just plugs into the sides. It has an on/off button on the side of the box & a small indicator light.

The picture from the adapter is very clear. I have another of these adapters and there are almost always feint lines across the screen. This one doesn't have any artifacts on the screen.

The RCA connection wires are hard-wired into the unit with plugs on the end making it a little harder to hook into the TV & reduces options of where I can put the adapter. I'm not sure if I can leave this on all the time or whether I should turn it off when not in use. Turning it off & on requires access to the box which means I can't just stuff it behind the TV. The instructions say not to use the box in hot & humid locations. This is in my detached workshop & I live in the South so it will definitely see some of those conditions for the next couple of months. I'll update if there are any troubles.

I replaced all of the speakers in my wife's old 2001 Camaro this year and put these 6.5" subs in the sail panels. We are middle aged and it has been decades since I last messed with stereo stuff and had a 600 watt system in my ElCamino with 8 separates and 15" subs. I was a little worried that these subs would be too big to fit in the hole from which the paper speakers came but they slipped right in. After the install I stuck in an old copy of Bach Busters and I thought the whole thing sounded great. I was very impressed with the bass from these little subs as I ran through all the big bass tracks on the disk.

After my wife took the car to work I asked her about the speakers. She told me that there were some issues... She said that "Funky Town" came on the radio (did I mention that we are older?) and the subs were rattling the car and it embarrassed her. She isn't enjoying the music as much because she is self conscious about someone hearing the speaker rattling her car. I am going to replace these with some mid range speakers in her car and put these in my Jeep. One word of caution, these speakers absolutely need a box to be heard. When I was testing the wiring I thought I would be disappointed because I could barely hear them until I placed them in the enclosure. They might not work on say a trunk package shelf with too much air space.

I bought this as a gift for my 20 year old nephew who usually gets a gift card from me.  He absolutely loved it.  He immediately set it up and began streaming music while we were opening presents.  I wish I had gotten a few more as gifts and I'll probably get one for myself.  It is very loud, very easy to set up and it even came charged enough to play for a couple of hours.  We only used it on Bluetooth from a phone so I can't speak to the other functionalities.

I purchased this DAC/amp a few months ago for myself and liked it so much I bought another as a Christmas present for my son. It provides excellent audio quality with my Focal and Sennheiser headphones.

This small device packs a lot of technology in for barely over $20. Easy to pair via Bluetooth and transmit via the fm radio. Call reception is very good. I plugged in a USB thumb drive with flac files and the music playing on the radio sounds great. I also hooked up my Astell & Kern AK Jr via the aux input and again got very nice audio quality with the radio. Also charged my iPhone quickly. Highly recommend and lots less expensive than replacing the stereo in the car.
Very handy little case to store my digital audio player.
I did notice a slight improvement in sound quality over the Apple connector. Seems sturdy and well built. Good value at less than $20.

I liked the original version of this iPhone headphone adapter so much,I purchased a second UGREEN iPhone lightning headphone adapter. I have several sets of quality headphones (Sennheiser HD598, HD599, Martin Logan Mikros 90) and want the best possible audio signal. Using these via the UGREEN adapter, I can stream HD quality music from Spotify and Amazon Music HD. If you have an iPhone and want the best audio signal for your headphones, I would highly recommend this item.

I purchased these JBL speakers to replace the original speakers in my 2001 Dodge Dakota pickup. They provide better sound quality, especially at higher volume levels. These are a very good value also. Are there better speakers out there? sure, but I would have had to spend several times the price of these to do much better.

It is so nice to be able to use wired headphones with my iPhone XR. A wired connection with my Sennheiser HD598 headphones provides better sound quality that using bluethooth headphones. For me sound quality is far more important than bluethooth convenience. This seems more sturdy than the Apple version and enables a high resolution audio signal when using Amazon Music HD or Spotify. I liked it so much, I also purchased the updated version.

I was very pleasantly surprised what a difference these ear pads made to my Mikros 90 headphones. These are more comfortable and improve the sound quality of the headphones versus the original ear pads. They are a bit tedious to put on but are well worth the effort. If you own a set of Martin Logan Mikros 90 headphones, I would encourage you replace the ear pads with these Geekria pads even if the originals are not worn out. You will appreciate the improvement. Highly recommended.
I have purchased several of these to store music for playback in my car. They work well and store lots of music with much better sound quality than most radio stations.

I purchased 2 of these for separate stereos in my house and both work perfectly. Setup was very easy using the included RCA to 3.5 stereo plug. You can also use a separate RCA to RCA patch cord (not included). Pairing a Bluethooth device was also easy. I chose this Logitech unit since it had both RCA plugs and 3.5 Stereo plug for extra flexibility. Audio quality is good when streaming music from Spotify or Pandora. I would buy this device again.

I already own a pair of Sennheiser HD 598 open back headphones, which are excellent!! I ordered the HD 598 Cs to use for travel and times when a closed back headphone would be needed. The 598 Cs was a very good choice.  They are easy to drive with portable audio devices, so no need for a separate headphone amp.  You also get an iPhone compatible mic that works well for phone calls.The sound quality is very nice, although a bit different from the open back 598. Closed back headphones are not as open and spacious in their sound presentation as open back headphones. The 598 Cs has a bit more bass emphasis, but not excessive like other brands of headphones. Vocals, acoustic guitar, strings and percussion are well presented on the 598 Cs. Comfort is excellent also. I can wear these for extended periods without fatigue. If you are looking for a comfortable set of headphones with very good audio quality, you will really enjoy the HD 598 Cs.

I purchased this case for my Sennheiser HD598 headphones, but unfortunately, it is too small to accommodate them comfortably. In order to zip the case closed, it is necessary to rotate the ear piece 30-45 degrees, which I'm not comfortable with since the HD598 ear piece is fixed and not intended to rotate. For a smaller mid-sized set of headphones, the db case would work great since the case is well built. If you own a set of full size audiophile headphones, you should consider other options for a case.

Very good quality replacement cable for my Sennheiser HD558 headphones. It was a very easy plug into the the headphones. Audio quality is as good as the original cable and the 1.5m length is perfect for use with portable devices. Highly recommended.

I order this CD player to replace an old Denon CD player that I have been using for over a decade. The Denon has always been erratic about reading my CDs and skipping during playback. Amazon had a great sale price on the Onkyo, so I order one. The player has a nice weight to it, so I assume the components are good quality. The Onkyo reads my CDs quickly and plays everything I have tried on it, so all is good. I also noticed an improvement in sound quality with a tighter, more focused sound. Not major, but definitely a noticeable improvement. It is connected to Sony's entry level stereo receiver and out through an older pair of Boston Acoustics A70 speakers. It is perfect for my bedroom.
2/16/18 update. The CD player drawer has developed a problem in the past year. When I press the open button, the CD tray opens and immediately closes repeatedly. After multiple presses, it may work, but often not. Very frustrating. I now use my Oppo BluRay player as my primary CD player.

I purchased a set of these cables along with a new Onkyo C-7030 CD player for my bedroom stereo and noticed a nice improvement in the sound quality of my system. The system is pretty basic. Entry level Sony stereo receiver and older Boston Acoustics speakers.  I'm not sure if it was the cables or CD player, but I could hear a tighter, more articulate sound of my CDs. I would certainly recommend these for an upgrade in sound quality. While my bedroom system is not high end, it still sounds very nice with these improvements.

I purchased a pair of these cables to connect my Pro-Ject Carbon Debut Turntable to my 20 year old Denon AV Receiver running out to Boston Acoustics M25 speakers and immediately noticed a significant improvement on overall sound quality of my LP records. Most noticeable was a significant increase is bass response with a tighter, more focused sound. Overall clarity of recordings improved as well. I'm going to order another set to connect my Oppo Blue Ray Player. I'm really enjoying the overall improvement in sound quality of my LPs now!!

I purchased a pair of these cables to connect from my CD player into my receiver and and noticed a nice improvement in the tone quality. So, I ordered a couple more sets for my DVD player and my turntable. Not as much difference with these 2 pieces of equipment. As other reviewers have stated, there is some variance on the size of the input jack. They did not fit snugly into my turntable or DVD player. The build quality is good otherwise. The cables are nice and thick and the plugs ends appear to be well made. If you are looking for a good quality, and very affordable audio cable, these will work nicely for you.

The AKG K450 (& K451) are very nice headphones. They are the same in sound quality, but the K451 has an iphone compatible, in line mic with volume controls. These are very light wight and comfortable to wear. I could wear them comfortably for hours. The tone is clear and smooth. The bass response is nice, with warm mids and smooth highs. If you are looking for a heavy bass however, such as rap or hip hop, you should look elsewhere. For a very comfortable, nice sounding set of headphones, you can't go wrong with either the K450 or K451.

For $95, I could not pass up this deal. The sound on the Mikros 90 headphones is well worth the price. They deliver a very precise sound with tight, well controlled bass and excellent high end response. The are very well suited for jazz and vocals, and they can rock. Van Morrison's "Moondance" and Tony Bennett's duets CD "Playing With My Friends" sounds great. Tony's duet with Cheryl Crow sounds awesome. For some rock, I listened to Thin Lizzy's "Dedication" and guitar solos were clear and strong. These headphones deliver a very clear and accurate sound, so if you listen to a poorly recorded record, you will notice the marginal audio quality of the recording. As others have stated, they are quite snug on your head. The major issue I had with them initially was that they rotated too far forward, allowing the forward edge of the headphone under the ear pads to press into the side of my face just in front of the ears. This got to be uncomfortable after 15-20 minutes. I noticed that they did not rotate in the opposite direction, so I decided to listen with the ear pads on the opposite ear (left channel over the right ear and right channel on the left ear). In this position, the ear pads stay perfectly flat on my ears for a much more comfortable fit. I really enjoy the refined sound that these headphones produce.

Looks like I have the privilege of being the first person to review the BA M25 speakers. I picked up a pair of these on Christmas Eve and have been playing them constantly over the past 2 weeks. My focus has been on 2 channel stereo recordings instead of movies. My set up is through an older Denon AVR 610 receiver that I have had for almost 20 years. I was initially impressed with the smooth, balanced feel of these speakers. Good mid range, nice high end, but not too bright, and a very strong bass response. The M25s defy their size in producing bass tones. Give them some break in time before making a final assessment. These speakers excel at producing music performed on real instruments. The do a great job on jazz, blues and acoustic folk styles of music. Vocals come across nicely as well.
Boz Scaggs "But Beautiful" CD of standards sounds great. Upright bass, piano and vocals make you feel like you are in a small jazz club. Diana Krall "Live in Paris" also plays very well. Nice piano, guitar & vocal reproduction. Jorma Kaukonen's "Blue Country Heart" CD showcases some great finger style acoustic guitar. Very natural acoustic guitar tones. Linda Ronstadt's "Winter Light" CD has some of the most powerful vocals you will ever hear and the M25s reproduce Linda's voice and backing instrumentation extremely well. The sound is never strained or harsh. Initially, I was a bit more apprehensive on some CDs with lots of bass. They sounded like they were trying to overcompensate on bass, but this has evened out over the past week. Eric Clapton's "Pilgrim" CD has come serious bottom end and the M25s produce very deep, tight bass response. Peter Gabriel "So" is a similar story. Deep, tight bass response that does not bottom out. Paul Rogers "Muddy Waters Blues" is a treat on the M25s. The opening track features some acoustic delta blues guitar, followed by a chorus of female backup singers and later some nice Strat blues guitar tones. It all sounds great on these speakers.
The look and finish on the speakers is impressive also. They are finished in a polished black exterior with a leatherette finish on the top, back & bottom. They look like a piece of fine furniture that would fit into a modern style of home décor. These speakers are very expensive though. I got a demo pair at less than half of the $399 per speaker list price. I don't think I would have bought them at full price. I have been listening to Boston Acoustics speakers for over 20 years. I still own a pair of A60s and a pair of A120s that have served me well over the years. The M25s have replaced the A120s as my primary speakers in my living room due to their sonic capabilities and their stylistic good looks.

Update 6/24/14 - After listening to these speakers for 6 months, I continue to be even more impressed by the Boston M25s. I bought these thinking they will do until I can find better. While there are better speakers out there, I have concluded, after many demo sessions, that I would need to spend at least $1500-$1800 or more to get some form of improvement over the M25s. Short of stepping up to KEF R300 @ $1800, B&W CM5 @ $1500 or Aperion Verus Towers, the M25s deliver the goods with very balanced & neutral sound, great detail in the upper register and sold bass. Highly recommended.

My granddaughter loves to watch her videos on her tablet. It was getting irritating trying to hear my show over hers. These were the perfect solution. Now we can cuddle and there's no noise interference. The sound quality is pretty good, she has no  complaints, the fit on her head is perfect. The only trouble is her little brother wants to hear, too. Guess I'll have to get another pair.

Great cover for my tablet. It fits perfectly. It was a bit difficult to insert the tablet into the cover, but I was glad because it made for a tight, secure fit. It is not a "cushy" cover but very sturdy, so I know it will protect my tablet. I was a bit afraid that the cover would dampen the sound, but not. I am very satisfied with it. The colors and vibrancy are exactly like the pictures here on Amazon, and a little girly, which I like. I'm very satisfied! It feels just like leather. There's no manufactured smell to it. Just a high quality case.

Hopefully I will never need to use this nor my nieces whom I also gave one to.  But it emits a VERY loud sound.  Works well and helps to give me peace of mind.  The pattern on it also makes it nice for my young nieces as they don't mind clipping it to their backpacks.

I've never had anything but Windows in the past thirty years but I can honestly say I will never go back after buying this HP Chromebook! It's wonderful in so many ways it would take a book to list it all! No more expensive virus protection programs, no cluttering up the computer with software since it's all on the cloud now! If you are looking for an inexpensive laptop for home or school use I highly recommend this one! You won't be sorry....I'm not!!
I bought these for my hubby and he can't stop telling me how great the sound is so I guess it was a great purchase!

I actually like this a lot better than the last backpack I tried from Amazon. I need something to bring my laptop and some gear along when setting up portable live stream studios, and the last backpack I tried offered a lot of storage space but not any padding- I felt like all my equipment could be felt through the fabric, and putting it down was going to scuff up the laptop.
Not with this one! This backpack feels like my stuff is safe inside. There's still plenty of space, but the padding and handles feel pretty rugged, I'm impressed. Really well made, solid handles, good material. Definitely would recommend this!

The biggest pro of these speakers to me, is how uncluttered they are. One cable goes into a USB port, and that's it! They look GREAT on a tabletop, almost like desk ornaments, and they glow when in use, lighting up the wall behind it. I have an ancient pair of Altec-Lansing speakers that actually sound amazing, but take up WAY too much clutter on my desk. Traditional computer speakers have a cable going into the computer's 3.5mm output, a cable going to a comically oversized wall-wart AC adapter plug, and then another cable going to the other speaker. I try to keep my desktop neat and cable-managed, and honestly I usually go with headphones for that reason.

But these solve that problem by being a USB sound card, self powered and everything all wrapped into one connection, no more space on your power strip being used or still powered on after your computer has shut down. In fact, I can unplug them and put them away when I don't need them, if a client comes to sit and work with me, it is literally one plug to get external sound again.
There are cons, however:
The Right speaker has a shorter run than the Left one does. They clearly expect your desktop to be on the right side of your monitor. In my case, my L-shaped desk has my desktop housed on the right, with the monitors to the left of it. I'm trying to see if there's an easy way to have Windows flip the L+R sound so I can swap back when using headphones. The other thing, which is arguably more important, is that the sound quality is ok at low and mid volumes, but once you start to crank it up, it begins to peak. If you want loud high quality sound, this isn't the best option. If you just want aesthetic gaming speakers that won't clutter up your desktop, or just want occasional speakers like I do, they are perfect! They sound good enough for my uses and look pretty awesome- I'm a fan.

EDIT:
They apologized for the units that were DOA, and sent a new set. Very happy with the customer support, if something is wrong they stand behind their product. Bumping up the rating to reflect this.

Original review: Some of these appear to be damaged as soon as we removed it from the packaging. Thankfully there are plenty more in the set in case some of them don't work, but keep that in mind when ordering- get more than you need in case you end up with some duds.
The ones that work seem fine. These do NOT have an inline mic so if using with a laptop for zoom, etc, you will need to rely on the built in microphone or whatever options you have available off this. These are great for things that are expecting just plain L+R+Ground (TRS tip) plugs, such as older headphone jacks, cameras, or seat backs on airplanes. They also don't have sound isolation ear cuffs, which can be a good thing if you don't want to block external sounds while listening. They sound pretty good as long as you get one that isn't broken.

Wireless headphones are great, but I have a love/hate relationship with using Bluetooth on a PC. When using the mic with headset profile for calls, the audio gets routed totally differently than regular stereo sound (A2DP), which gets confusing if multitasking and playing sound while also using the mic. And then there's the delay/lag etc that usually comes along with Bluetooth from a Windows desktop. But that's why I love the USB dongle here!
Plug the little USB bit in, and it detects the headphones like an alternate sound card, full blown crystal clear stereo audio, even if using the mic! And the mic can be extended or retracted, something I love since I lost the removable mic on my old headphones.
But, if I want to use it with my phone or tablet, I can revert to standard Bluetooth and connect that way on my Android devices. The price is a little bit steep, but the quality is there, this is a well designed and well made product that works as intended so far. I'm impressed.

This is a VERY interesting Mini PC! I have to admit I'm not 100% sure what market this is trying to target, but I do find it a unique offering among the many Mini PCs I've had the pleasure to own and try over the years.
The biggest things to stand out?
-3x HDMI ports (that's right, TRIPLE display built right into the box!)
-2x Lan ports (dual LAN!)
-Small square sized footprint

So, having 3x displays is a cool touch, this could be great for digital signage or a job that requires a lot of data visible at once (day trading, etc). The dual lan is also cool for IT guys who want to monitor or bridge multiple networks, these are unique features to find on any PC, let alone one this tiny.
The N5095 isn't quite as fast as the N5101 chips I have in other Mini PCs, but it is still faster than most of the chips found in MiniPCs at this price. Impressive for the asking amount.
But the part that irks me so very much is the lack of USB-C.

Yes, you get 3x USB3 ports which is great, but not even a single USB-C, let alone thunderbolt?
Once again, the price must be considered here. You're getting something super capable and really unique with the hardware offered at the asking price. If they made a more expensive version with a higher end CPU and USB-C/Thunderbolt port, I'd recommend that in a heartbeat. This is a solid value if you have a need for the hardware, though. Very cool and different.

I'll admit, I'm a fan of Sony. I've owned all sorts of things from the brand, from the aftermarket stereo in my car to my professional camera equipment I use at work. They just make reliably good products. However I've mostly owned Samsung television sets just because it's what I had access to on a more regular basis.
I was therefore excited to try out this TV and see how it compared. To be honest, I really REALLY like Sony's color science. It's part of why I prefer their camera equipment, and it shows on this display. The contrast ratio and dynamic range are everything I wanted it to be and more. The skin tones as well, however the average consumer probably wouldn't notice or care about these things. Where the big differences lie in major TV brands these days is going to be features. The latest crop of Smart TVs have so many bells and whistles, you practically don't need anything other than an internet connection anymore. Unlike Samsung's UI which has embraces Amazon's Fire Stick style UI, Sony has gone the Google TV route. There are pros and cons to both approaches, although I think perhaps arguably there isn't as much free included content as Samsung (Samsung actually includes free live TV channels via "Samsung TV", which Sony does not have). But for all the content I actually WANT to see, Netflix, Prime, Disney+ etc, it works perfectly!

So why only 4 stars? This isn't the fault of Sony's TV, but I really wish they'd make it easier to spot and turn off... I really REALLY hate the default motion smoothing (aka "soap opera effect") that all the big brands use these days. As a content creator, I shoot videos in a particular frame rate on purpose. The motion blur or lack thereof helps tell the story in some kinds of scenes. But most TVs want to show off their high refresh rate and therefore use realtime smoothing algorithms to create fake overly-dramatic effects to pump out extra in between frames. The motion looks too smooth to the point it seems CGI (because it sort of is). It just looks off once you notice it, and Sony is no exception. You have to dig around and figure out what they call it on every TV just to make it look normal again, on this set it is called Motionflow and it can be confusing to turn it off. I wish manufacturers would make it a simple and easy to understand toggle switch... maybe even present it as an option to the viewer upon setting it up so they can understand what they are enabling and decide if they want it or not (I strongly recommend not!).
But again, that's true of all modern Television sets, on its own right this is a solid TV and I would recommend it.

I've used wireless HD systems for productions before- whether to monitor a camera op from a distance, or send a wireless cameraman on stage as part of a live multi-camera gig. Usually we would rent Teradek equipment from someone like B&H since the gear can cost thousands. There are cheaper options I've seen before, but they usually have a noticeable lag of nearly 2 seconds, or require too much setup to be portable (designed to plugged into a source of power, etc).
This product blew me away. I'm not kidding. It is clearly designed for mountable use, with tripod style 1/4" - 20 threading as well as standard Sony NP-F battery mounts, you can easily mount this to a camera rig and go live. The delay is almost non-existent, and I'd say close enough to get away with on a live broadcast mixed with wired cameras. It gets a little bit warm when using, but not any worse than an Atmos Ninja recorder. For the price, this is almost too good to be true! I wasn't expecting to be as impressed as I am, it's really very VERY good at almost 1/10th the price of a Teradek!

Yes, the UI and apps are very clearly Android. No, it isn't a mini tablet.
Players like this are an interesting market that is hard to pin the audience down for. There are music players that are cheap on the market for those that would rather have a dedicated player (ie, not their phone). However the user interface tends to be wonky and slow, and newer generation features like bluetooth 5+ and streaming are often a mixed bag, if even available.
The idea behind players like this one, is that it is based on a supported operating system (Android, in this case) so it can play almost any format you throw at it, has plenty of support for popular streaming apps and features, as well as a familiar user interface that is already so polished, it seems silly to reinvent the wheel like the super cheap older media players.
Is it a mini tablet or phone without service? Not exactly. This is not a Google certified device, it does not have the play store or any Google apps on it. Unlike some other Android based players, I couldn't even get sideloaded apk files to install (it kept throwing errors at me). It seems like this device was purposely locked down to keep it an mp3 player. That's good in some ways, my kids aren't allowed unlimited screen time and their schools don't want them bringing smartphones around, so this is a strictly music-player oriented device (especially once you remove things like the browser for them, which it allows you to do). But I also know there are more capable players out there, some of which have quad DAC audio chips. Also, what happens when an app gets updated and goes out-of-date? Sometimes streaming services make changes and updated clients are required for it to work, however you are largely stuck with the version that this came with unless they issue a firmware update or something.
This is still cheaper than the higher end mp3 players that support high end DAC and app updates, but not by much. It seems to be a sort of in-between product. If you have a use for something like this, it could be a pretty good option. But if you're expecting a handheld tablet or alternative concept to an ipod touch, it is not exactly that.

This is useful for so many things. If you want a big easy to use knob for your gaming setup or live audio production rig, this is a really great way to avoid having to hunt for buttons or click volume controls with your mouse. I like that the LED glows under the knob, but I sort of wish it stayed on all the time so I could find it quickly in the dark (it lights up during use, but then seems to turn off the light after a few seconds of non use).
Personally, I wanted to use this to add a volume knob to my aftermarket car radio. For some reason, new head units all rely on buttons and touch screens, but I want a good old fashioned volume knob. Thankfully this is compatible pretty universally as a USB input device (no drivers, so even Android can recognize it!) so I can pop off the knob and drill a hole in my double din adapter to mount the knob behind my dash. Plug it in, and it changes the volume as needed. Awesome! It isn't designed to work this way, you're supposed to just connect it to a desktop I think, but the fact that it worked the way I wanted means this makes it also a great modder/hacker/tinkerer's tool.

OnePlus already has standard buds which are more expensive than these. I've tried those and was fairly impressed with them for the price compared to other leading brands (*cough* airpods). I'll be honest, I wasn't sure what to expect here with these "Nord" brand ones. Nord is supposed to be OnePlus' value brand, and the price reflects that. I've tried out headphones that cost more than this which I didn't care for, so I was a little anxious.
However, I have to admit I'm fairly impressed. They sound better to me than other wireless earbuds at this price range. While they aren't as well made as the standard Oneplus buds, they aren't bad at all, especially for the money. Much like the Nord phones themselves, Oneplus seems to know how to make a value product that punches way above its price tag.
I know the brand has taken a hit lately with their Android 12 offerings (still holding out for OOS13 to fix this colorOS mess they are in), but I can say with confidence that their earbuds are pretty great and worth considering whether or not you are a fan of the brand.

As a photographer, I recognize Lexar as a trusted storage media brand, up there with Sandisk and other industry brand names. This product does not disappoint- in benchmarks, it appears to perform as advertised. And for the money, you get a very healthy amount of usable storage at U3 rated speeds! This is great in my DJI Mavic as well as GoPros and other recording equipment. Definitely recommended.

The speaker is small and portable enough to fit into a large pocket yet can produce some very respectable volume with its 14W power. My daughter found this is a great way to turn a fanny pack into a hip-mounted sound system (she's a counselor in a summer camp and using this speaker a lot). The sound is surprisingly immersive and the fact that it is waterproof enough to use around the pool or in the rain is a huge bonus. Great speaker!

[[VIDEOID:b24da4d426cb291b56dc311a2d09dc8e]] If you've got a USB-C port and no 3.5mm input, THIS is the mic adapter you need! The phone receiver is so clean looking, it plugs directly into the port and is self powered by your phone, so no additional batteries or charging needed. It just sits there, like a chin bump. The transmitter needs 2 AAA batteries (4 if you want to use both transmitters).
Note: On some devices like the OnePlus phones, the built in camera app doesn't recognize external microphones, so you'll need to download something like Open Camera (excellent free app I recommend anyway for more camera control). Pixel and Samsung phones I tried this with did not require that.
ALSO- when this is plugged in, it registers itself as a "headset" to the phone, so it will not play back audio until you unplug it. I was able to monitor the audio via the headphone jack going in, but then I could not hear it recorded until I unplugged the receiver. This is simply how it works on Android and not the fault of the unit, however it would be nice if a future version could route outgoing sound over the included headphone jack (I was a bit disappointed it did not do this, however the product was so good I still want to give it 5 stars).

[[VIDEOID:33b9e8cfecdf6f700ec0f6e6b36a3153]] I'll cut to the chase: Is this the best performing gaming tablet on the market? No.
But is it one of the best in the price range? Absolutely YES.

And when you consider that flagship Snapdragon 8 class options such as the Galaxy Tab S8 can cost 4-5x as much as this one, you have to consider that they aren't actually 4-5x BETTER for the money. The rest of the specs (storage, ram, sim slot, etc) are all pretty similar to this one, but for a price that makes this a no brainer to me.
I bought a Lenovo M10+ FHD last year for work related apps that require a lot of document reading, and it was almost the same price as this but with very VERY weak specs in comparison. I wish I had known about this back then instead!

It does what it claims- it's bone conduction so the sound doesn't need to cover your ears to be audible. That's great if you want/need open ears so that you can hear those around you. However there are brand name versions of this that are much clearer. This is good, and it works, but the sound quality is going to be lacking some fidelity if you're looking for rich musical notes compared to earbuds in this price range. Everything has a sort of heavy treble tone to it.
The microphone is pretty good, as long as you don't mind it always sticking out. Even if you twist it away, it's always there, just pointing behind you. You can't really remove it. Callers can hear me, and much better than other headsets that have a mic up by your ears. I wish it could be removed to look a little less in-your-face when you don't need it. Also, I wish the unit had USB-C like all other new devices. This has the older micro-USB plug. I still have plenty of those in my wire bin, but most of my newer tech uses C and I prefer to have one set of cables for most things (my laptop, phone, over-hear phones, etc, all use USBC now). Just feels like they could have made this a little bit better. But it works.

[[VIDEOID:75569821202ef0194cf65687a61f63d]] This is a fully featured 11th Generation Intel laptop in a tablet form factor. I love Windows on a Tablet, I've been a fan ever since the original Lenovo Yoga convertibles and Microsoft Surface tablets went mainstream.
The only problem I've had with those Windows tablet concepts is that sometimes you encounter applications that were designed for a mouse and keyboard rather than a touch screen. And that's what makes Windows 11 so great: You can finally run Android Apps thanks to built in virtual machine support. This is the first time I'm trying a Windows 11 Tablet, and I have to admit there's some initial setting up to do to get Android app support working (you can't just download an APK like I was expecting to). But once you do, it's pretty awesome and works the way I imagined and expected!
I'm not familiar with the brand Alldocube, but I have to admit the iWorkGT is actually pretty solid, has good build quality and an excellent display for the money. Since you are running an actual X86 Intel CPU, you're going to get a powerful experience compared to an anemic ARM processor like a traditional tablet would have, but the trade off is it will need to cool itself off like a laptop sometimes. That means vents and fans, which you will feel in your hands.
And this leads me to the cons:
There is NO CASE included with this product in the box. And since it is not a major brand like the Microsoft Surface, finding third party cases are going to be difficult if not impossible. Alldocube does sell 2 keyboard style cases which are interesting, however they are sold separately and not cheap! Sure, this is a lot less than a Surface, but at least a surface has plenty of after market cases and holders for every style and budget. I can't help feeling like it should have come with at least some sort of basic protection case. Even the Surface at least gives you the kickstand to stand it up, with this you have a portable computer that can get warm in your hands and nothing to really hold it in or stand it up with. You NEED to purchase one of their cases here.
The other con is that I did notice some strange behavior at times- the tablet wouldn't charge the first time I used it until I turned it off and rebooted. Another time the sound didn't work, and also wouldn't come back until I rebooted.
