I had to pry open the battery compartment on both the mouse and the keyboard with a knife. Then it took me a little bit to figure out how to turn the keyboard on. In order to extend its battery life, the mouse turns itself off when not in use. So it needs to be double clicked to turn it back on again. Not a big deal but it does take a bit to get used to. Finally, the nice thing about wired keyboards and mice is that one doesn't need to worry about batteries for them. Though the clutter of cords and wires can get messy, as I can attest from personal experience. Only you can decide if you would rather have the clutter or the gear that needs batteries. Should you decide to go wireless, this product is a nice, basic, no frills set up.

As an old, retired guy, I find technology still significantly impacting my daily life in two ways. The first is that I spend a lot of time every day online - either gaming in my favorite MMO or binge watching the various streaming services. The second way is that I keep in touch with my far-flung network of family and friends via social media. Now, my desktop pc handles the first of those two very nicely. The problem is that I can get immersed for hours in gaming or in a good streaming show. Social media notifications break that immersion, causing me to move away from whatever I was doing to see what the latest notice was about. If I don't, it could be quite a while before I get around to checking my social media and responding to the messages there.

This is where a tablet comes in. I figured it would be nice to have a tablet that quietly beeped new notifications and allowed me to just glance over at the latest notice to see if it needed a quick response or not. Little did I know how hard it would be to find a low end tablet capable of that simple task. This is the fourth tablet I've tried and the first one which could do that one simple thing for me. The other low end tablets quickly crashed and burned for a variety of reasons. This is the first that actually continued to work after the first few days, giving me the notifications I wanted and that I could check out at a glance.

There are some issues with this tablet that folks should be aware of. The sound is tinny enough that I wouldn't listen to music or audiobooks on this thing. The visual quality is sufficient for modern movies and tv shows but vintage ones do look a bit fuzzy. The charge doesn't last quite as long as I'd like it to. The tablet needs to be charged twice a day, even when it's just sitting there beeping when a text message or email comes in. Charging once a day would be nicer but it is what it is. Still, this is the first low end tablet of four I've tried that actually does the simple task I want it to do. So for that, I have to give it a solid 4 star rating.

As an old, retired guy, tech factors into my daily life in two important ways. The first way is that I spend hours every day online, playing my favorite MMO. The second is that my extended family, spread across the United States, stays in touch via social media. The very specific niche I got this tablet to fill was for a way to get social media notifications that wouldn't disrupt my gaming. I first tried an Amazon 7" Fire Tablet. The audio notification on that tablet died after the first day or two. There was also no way I could find to turn off the sleep function. The tablet kept shutting down so I couldn't just look over to visually see if there any notifications.

This Android tablet works perfectly to fill that niche. It sits quietly next to my main computer screen and gives a soft audio notification when I get an email or a text message. A glance shows me the first lines of the text or email, letting me know if a quick response is needed or not. The notifications were easy to set up and the sleep function is set to Never. So this tablet does exactly what I want it too.

There are some issues with it that you should be aware of though. For one thing, it charges slowly but drains quickly. For another, turning it back on sometimes takes a bit of extra button pushing. It looks like it is coming on but then shuts off again. At times I've had to hit the power button 4-5 times before it turns all the way on. Videos are just on the edge of being grainy while the audio is distinctly tinny, without any depth. I sometimes listen to audiobooks while gaming but the sound is just too tinny and irritating to listen to them on this tablet.

Since this product does exactly what I want it to, I have to give it a 4 star rating. Other than my specific niche use though, this is a basic, entry level product, which is why I can't give it 5 stars. It just doesn't have the high end quality of far more expensive tablets.

First, let me say that I am not an audiophile and have no need for fancy, high-priced speakers and such. For an ordinary listener like me, these speakers had a nice, clear, stereo sound. Both music and special effects in movies or tv shows came through very well. Dialogue in movies sounded a bit flat to me but I wasn't sure if that was the speakers or my ears. When I had the family fifteen year old listen to them though, he thought the dialogue came through just fine. So the issue was my old guy ears, not anything to do with the speakers. All and all, they really do have a nice sound for the price.

To talk about the quality of the speakers' construction, let me make a distinction between cheap and inexpensive. Cheap implies something flimsy that will easily break and fall apart. That's not an issue with these speakers. The materials they are made of are not high-end fancy, but they are not flimsy either. So let's call their construction inexpensive but not cheap.

There were two practical issues though, one trivial, one possibly a bit more problematic. The trivial issue is that the cord which connects the usb plug and speaker jack to your device has a very short connecting wire between the plug and the jack. For a phone or a laptop that is probably a non-issue. With my desktop though, I had to rearrange the usb plugs to open up one close enough to the speaker jack.

The issue which may be more of a hassle is that the volume controls are on the back of the sub-woofer. People usually tuck a sub-woofer away from easy reaching distance. So adjusting the volume may be a nuisance. Personally, I don't know why the volume controls aren't on the speakers which are usually more accessible. This may not be a big deal though if you can control the volume from your device. Just be aware of the possible hassle. In any event, our fifteen year old uses this speaker set to listen to music and movies on his laptop and he is happy with it.

When these became available I asked our 15 year old nerd if he wanted them and his response a shrug and a "whatever". Mom wanted to try them though. She uses earbuds when she's walking the dog and wanted to see if these had better sound. Well her response was a big yes, their sound is really good. So is the Bluetooth range. She can leave her phone in the front room and hear just fine all around the house, even in the upstairs bedroom. They paired easily with her iPhone 7 Plus and are lightweight enough to be good for extended use.

When our nerd saw the headphones, his "whatever" immediately switched to "I have to try those!" He loved them too, saying the sound was great. With his iPhone 6 though, he has to connect them to his phone with a cord. The more recent Bluetooth of the headphones won't pair up with his older phone. Nice as she is, mom agreed to share the headphones with him so our family happily gives the product a 5 star rating. :)

P.S. I'm thinking of buying our nerd his own set of these headphones for Christmas. Don't tell him I said that though. :)

While I've never bothered with a webcam before, having one now, in the middle of the pandemic, seems like it will be useful. As an old guy with a number of health issues, I am staying at home all the time and haven't been venturing out at all. Rather than actually going to the doctor's office these days, the webcam will allow me to teleconference routine medical checkups. It's also good for keeping in touch with family and friends I can't see face to face. Just this evening I spent time in a Google video chat room talking with a dear friend who lives in another part of the country. Then I checked in on Facebook video chat with one of my sisters. Talking with someone in a video chat is much nicer than chatting by text or visiting over a landline phone. So if you don't already have the capacity for video chatting, you might want to think about getting a webcam.

On my Windows 10 desktop, this really is a plug and play piece of equipment. No software or other downloads needed. One of the minor issues has to do with setting this webcam up for the first time. The instructions are minimal and of no practical use. At first, I kept getting error messages when trying to use the webcam to make a video chat call, with no clear indication of what the error was. Some trial and error efforts showed it to be a simple problem. I needed to give the device both camera and mic access before it would work. Once I figured that out, I was easily able to make calls without any further error messages.

Another minor issue was that when I first tried to put the webcam on my desk, it kept flipping over on its side. So I had to make my first video call holding it in my hands. Later, after the tight coiling of it's cord eased up, it sat just fine with no tipping.

Then, if I held the device too close to the computer screen, sitting just over the speakers, the webcam would pick up enough of the other person's voice to set up a feedback echo. Moving the device away from the computer speakers easily solved that.

Finally, the video on my end was okay but not great. I looked green but that may have something to do with the lighting in my room. Still, I loved chatting with my friend and my sister. Both enjoyed the fact that I looked so green and neither seemed to have any problem hearing me. This is the first webcam I've used and I'm pleased enough with it to give the device a 4 star rating.

I live in a family compound which is an old house divided up into several apartments. What makes these walkie talkies useful on a daily basis is the water situation in the compound. All the apartments are connected to the cold water line and a couple of the apartments share a hot water line. That means if you are taking a shower and anyone anywhere in the house turns on a cold water tap, not only will your shower lose water pressure but the cold water flow will abruptly decrease, leaving the hot water hotter than ever. For the apartments that share a hot water line, the same kind of thing happens. Suddenly you are taking a cold shower in a a trickle of water. These walkie talkies have solved that problem. With the group call button you can let the whole house know you are going to take a shower so no one will use any water till you call in that you are done.

Nor is that their only use. Several times a year our town will get a tornado alert. Should a tornado actually appear in our area, the whole family will head down to the storm shelter behind the basement apartment. With the walkie talkies we can make sure everyone got the emergency alert and knows that they need to be ready to move fast if the sirens go off.

One our family members has been sick the last couple of days and these units were in an easy way to check in on her throughout the day to see if there was anything she needed. By assigning each apartment its own channel and having everyone on the same group channel, it is easy to call one apartment or to reach them all, whichever is appropriate for a given message.

The units are easy to use and even our least techie family member quickly got the hang of it. The sound is clear even when calling from apartment to apartment. There is a flashlight function that is fairly bright, one that will come in handy in case of emergency. All in all, our whole family is well satisfied with this product and it deserves a 5 star rating.

My desktop tower pc has 4 usb ports in front, all of which are in use. So I thought it would be nice to use this adapter to give me some extra usb connections. Sadly, that won't work too well on my computer. The usb ports are high enough that the adapter dangles in the air because its cord is so short. Our fourteen year old nerd has a laptop which would work much better with that short cord and so the adapter was passed on to him.

One odd thing of note - I have a headphone set up that uses a usb charger. When I plugged that set up into this adapter, the sound through the headphones was noticeably higher and shriller than it was without the adapter. That was strange enough that I listened to the same song with and without being plugged into the adapter and the difference was very real and very noticeable. Why that is, I have no idea. I also don't know if that would affect sound quality when used with a streaming tv stick or other audio devices. Keep an eye on the other reviews as they come in here to see if this is a general issue or not.

Other than the cord being too short and the odd effect on the headphones I use, this does seem like a good product. It really is plug and play and it does provide extra usb ports at a time when we are attaching more and more stuff to our various devices. If I could use this with my desktop pc I would but our fourteen year old should be able to put it to good use with his laptop.

Somewhere there is an ancient marketing survey that identifies teen-age boys as a prime segment of the gaming market and that says they really like bright, flashing lights. So manufacturers who want to sell to the gaming market still think they have to add flashy lighting to all their products. Well, the gaming universe is much larger than teen boys these days and bright, flashing lights have nothing to do with playing a game. With that pet peeve off my chest let me add a couple of things to give this review some context. First, I do spend a lot of time online playing an MMO but I'm very much a casual player, not a hardcore competitive one. Second, I am not an audiophile. High end stereo gear is wasted on me as the music coming from most any clock radio is good enough for me.

To my non-audiophile ears, the sound from this speaker is fine. It provides a nice range without being too heavy on the bass end or too shrill on the high end. Whether gaming, streaming videos, or listening to music and audiobooks, this speaker holds its own nicely. Though, like the flashy lighting, the sound quality really doesn't make any significant difference while I'm playing in my MMO world. The ambient noise, NPC chatter, battle music and such, all come through nicely but that's a perk, not something that particularly improves my game play.

The under the monitor design of this speaker really doesn't save me any desk space. The mini speakers I was using before were much smaller and were out of the way on the side of the monitor. This space bar basically sits in front of my monitor and takes up more room than other speakers. One strong plus to me for this speaker is the fact that it really is plug and play. I had it up and running in just a few minutes. Other "gaming" gear I've tried with flashy lighting systems require software to control the lighting and sometimes getting that software to install and run properly can be a major, frustrating effort. So I really, really like that this product lives up to its "plug and play" claim.

There is one last negative point to mention. a minor one. The volume and other controls are flat buttons on the side of the soundbar. So to adjust the volume, change the lighting, etc, you need to move the soundbar to look at the side of it so you can see what you are doing. I call that a minor issue because my keyboard has mute and volume control buttons on it and I can just use those to adjust the sound as needed.

The bottom line of all this for me is that I wouldn't buy this speaker as a "gaming speaker" but simply as a nice mid-range speaker who's sound quality I like, one that is easy to set up and use. Oh, and lest I sound too much like a Grinch, the lights really are pretty, the way Christmas lights are. It's just that they have nothing to do with gaming. :)

First, let me put this review in context. As an old retired guy I'm playing around on the computer for hours a day - gaming, streaming videos, reading the news, and keeping in touch with folks via social media. Let me also add that I am too old and slow to be a hard core, competitive gamer. So even though I can spend long hours in an online MMORPG, I'm actually a casual gamer. And here's a bit more context - over the last few months I've tried a variety of keyboards from high end gaming gear with high end prices to low end cheap stuff so flimsy it feels like it could fall apart even as you take it out of the box. In that keyboard spectrum, this one is not too hot, not too cold, it's just right.

The most expensive gaming keyboard came with all kinds of bells and whistles, from programmable flashing lights to programmable keys for running macros. Unfortunately the software needed to run that keyboard locked up so badly after three days of use, that I couldn't get it unfrozen, making all those expensive extras totally useless. The cheapest low end keyboard stuttered with a noticeable lag bad enough to get any gamer killed in a boss fight. This keyboard is just right for my use. It has a solid, durable feel that does not at all feel cheap or flimsy. There is a muted sound when hitting the keys, enough to let you know that you really are typing but not enough to be distracting. It also stays in place while typing with no slipping or sliding. The cord is long enough that the keyboard doesn't feel tethered on a short leash. It really is plug and play, with no extra software needed to run the thing. And there is no stuttering or discernible lag at all.

The Amazon Basics brand seems to be developing a solid line of products, from clothing to computer gear, that is well made, durable, and affordably priced. This keyboard fits well in the Amazon Basics family and I very much give it 5 stars.

Pay attention to the measurements of this thing. I didn't, and I was shocked by how long it is. Most of us think of a surge protector as a compact set of outlets that can easily fit behind a computer or home entertainment center. Not this one. It's more than four feet long with the outlets in a single line running down that entire length. It's what you might see in a store's electronics department where they have a line of television sets all turned on at the same time so you can readily compare their pictures.

The instructions specify that it is for home not commercial use though. I have trouble visualizing a home set up that would require a row of outlets set in a four foot straight line. Perhaps a home workshop with power equipment? Or a more elaborate computer set up, one with components on a rack of shelves? The surge protector can be wall mounted so it could work well with a rack of components.

Despite my own bafflement I am still giving this surge protector a 5 star rating for a reason. If you have a place where you can use something along these lines, this could be an excellent product for you. It is solidly built with a durable heft to it. The rating for 600 Joules of protection is significant. A quick google search about Joules turned up a site saying that most surge protectors bought for home usage are rated at 200-300 Joules and as such are essentially worthless. The minimum suggested was 400 Joules and this surge protector is comfortably above that. That won't help in case of a lightning strike but should be good for more normal occurrences. I'm looking forward to reading the other reviews of this item to see how people would use it in a home.

P.S. I dunno if they would actually have something like this in a Walmart as I've never shopped there, or anywhere else, for a four foot surge protector. :)

Bottom Line - The speaker itself is excellent but Bluetooth can be an irritating technology.

The speaker is lightweight and even has an attached carrying strap. Unlike a lot of lightweight products though, it doesn't feel flimsy or fragile at all. Instead it has a nice, solid, durable feel to it. While I am not an audiophile, the speaker has a deep, rich sound that I really like. It does well with audiobooks, music, and videos.

The problems seem to be with Bluetooth. One major issue is that the sound stutters while using Bluetooth. It's very noticeable when playing music and very irritating when listening to audiobooks. That's happened with every Bluetooth speaker I've ever tried. A google search indicates that it's a common problem related to the amount of information the computer is trying to pump out to the speaker. There's a checklist of possible issues to go through to try to fix the problem but the stuttering seems all too common with this technology.

Another issue involves changing modes on a Bluetooth speaker. To sidestep the stuttering I plugged this speaker into my computer with a standard jack. It worked fine and the sound was good. When I unplugged it to bring the speaker into another room with me, I had to redo my audio settings. When I plugged it back in with the jack, an audiobook played just fine but there was no sound while playing videos. Again, I had to go into the audio settings and fiddle with them to be able to watch a movie. I've had similar issues with other Bluetooth speakers.

If you are a techie you may be able to resolve such things quickly and easily. The less tech adept you are, the more hassle they will be though. Myself, I'm just going to leave the speaker connected to my pc via a good old fashioned jack because I like its sound. Bluetooth? Bah, I haven't got time to bother with it.

What I wanted was something I could use to listen to tv/movies/music/audiobooks/NPR while doing other work on my desktop computer. The Fire Tablet fits the bill perfectly. The video is crisp and clear. The screen size works nicely for an old guy who's had cataract surgery and wears bifocals. Even the closed captioning I need these days is easily readable on this screen. The speakers are not master quality but are more than adequate for this non-audiophile. This is my first time using Alexa and I love how easy she makes it to get the news and weather before shifting back to Netflix. The whole thing integrates nicely with my Prime account. So far I've just begun to scratch the surface of the options available through Amazon. I wouldn't try to use this tablet to do any heavy computing. That's why I have a high-powered desktop. For the entertainment niche I wanted to fill though, this tablet fits perfectly.

There are some glitches. At times Alexa will freeze up for no discernible reason. Netflix can stutter at times too. This on a new tablet with only minimal apps, used one or two at a time so I shouldn't be overloading it's capabilities. For someone new to Fire Tablets and Alexa, there is a bit of a learning curve. It's not too onerous though. In a short time I expect to be using this tablet familiarly. Every computer I've ever used has had occasional glitches and there is always a learning curve on a new device. So far I haven't come across any deal-breakers and I can whole-heartedly say I love my new tablet.

For streaming Amazon and Netflix videos, playing Steam games, and general web browsing, the screen is beautiful and the computer has been working flawlessly since I got it four month ago. I have no complaints on those fronts. However, there are some other things to talk about.

One of the minor flaws is that the mouse turns off after several minutes of inactivity. You have to click it to turn it back on again before you can use it. That may sound like a trivial thing but it can become an ongoing irritant, especially if you work on several different computers and have to remember to click this particular mouse before usage.

Another minor flaw, one that became a major irritant for me, was that the screen would turn off after 5 minutes without any keyboard or mouse usage. It would even turn off while I was watching movies. In the Windows 10 Power & Sleep settings I would change the screen turn off time from 15 minutes to Never. That would fix the problem temporarily. However, every time I rebooted the computer, the screen turn off time would reset itself to 15 minutes. So I would have to go back into the settings to change it again.

Fiddling with the Windows power plan and scouring the net for solutions turned up nothing. Yes, the power plan was set the way I wanted it. No, the problem had nothing to do with a screensaver. No, there was nothing in the Bios that would trigger the reset. After four months of constant irritation, I finally stumbled across the solution by accident. It seems that ASUS has it's own power plan that overrides the Windows one. The default setting on the ASUS power plan was to turn the screen off after 15 minutes. Changing the ASUS setting to Never finally solved the problem. Why ASUS felt the need to put it's own power plan on their machine when Windows 10 already had a perfectly good one, I have no idea. I especially don't know why ASUS set their plan to override Window's.

That problem touches on the potentially major flaw with ASUS. In trying to find a solution to a minor problem on another ASUS machine, I found that their customer service sucks. When, after much effort, I finally got to talk with a live person, their accent was so thick that I literally could not understand what they were saying. When I asked for someone who spoke clearer English, the service rep got all huffy and I never did get to talk with anyone else and my questions never got answered.

This happened after I had already bought the ASUS Zen Z240-C1, otherwise I wouldn't have gotten a second ASUS machine. Now I've got my fingers crossed that nothing major happens to this one lest I get tangled up in their customer service mess again. So, this machine itself deserves a 4 star review for good performance with only minor flaws. However, ASUS customer service would get no stars from me at all and that will keep me from buying anything else from them.

If your desktop didnt come with speakers, well let me tell you this is the product for you! The sound quality is great! It doesn't take up too much room to setup and it isn't complicated to setup. Once plugged in just make sure the computer knows those are the speakers and its done!!!!

Love the size. The best part is that the player corrects some of the freezing/stopping issues with some DVD's. I had purchased a retail DVD that kept freezing and then starting again a few minutes later (on other players). It got to a point in the movie that it froze and would not unfreeze on it's own - I had to skip quite a bit of the movie to free it (the FF wouldn't work on the big freeze). When playing on this machine, the DVD froze, but the player corrected it almost immediately and continued on without losing part of the film. When it got to the big freeze, it corrected it and continued playing it, again, not losing part of the film. I have had many DVD players throughout the decades, but never one that corrected flaws in the DVD itself. I am very, very happy with this, as sometimes you cannot get another copy of the DVD because the movie or TV show is no longer being manufactured. Also, the DVD doesn't make noise when it's being played. I have a very expensive player from a few years back and it has developed a noise from the rotation of the DVD being played and it drives me crazy. No noise on this one.

Once I got everything set up, these buds give awesome sound. Retention while in use hasn't been a problem. With noise cancelling on, I generally get about 5 hours use before I have to recharge them. The charging case is good for about 3 recharges from 10% to fully charged, and it accepts fast USB C or wireless charging. I can control the buds by touch, or through either my S22 Ultra or my Watch 5 Pro. Yes, I decided to go all Samsung this time out, and, so far, I'm satisfied with the choice.

I bought this card to expand the capacity of my tablet. As such it is there to store movies, books, music and pictures that would overwhelm the internal storage. It's plenty big enough (at least for now), and plenty fast enough for my requirements. The only glitch had nothing to do with the card but with the delivery. It was a day late, despite being at the Amazon delivery facility on time. Fortunately, this proved to be only a minor inconvenience, This time.

Excellent headset. With phone makers ditching the headphone jack, Bluetooth headsets are the best way to go for private sound. These are not noise cancelling, which, for me, is a good thing in this case. I have an over ear noise cancelling headset for when that is appropriate. These let just enough outside information pass through so that I'm not oblivious to my surroundings while still delivering that fine Bose sound.
Nice and compact. Excellent range, battery life and sound quality. If you need something like this, I highly recommend it.

Huge Bass, Low Price, great living room speakers, have them hooked up to Amazon echo dot. Sound very warm, great for house/edm also.

Lacking HDMI input would be my only complaint.
Omg love these!  Was worried with neg. reviews so bought 4 yr warranty.  But for $100 per speaker?!  Crazy sound and power for small size!  Getting 150's next.

Finally, have coverage in the house with these APs. Our router and cable entry point in the house is all the way at one end and we wanted to full coverage up and downstairs on the same network and into the garage. I have two UniFi APs and they do the trick. Initial AP setup was very very easy. The second AP needed to be setup to uplink to the first and that required a firmware upgrade. That could be done from the management console, but it took me a couple of tries to figure that out.

The upgrade notification was clear in the UI, it just wasn't clear that the APs needed to be on the same version in order to uplink. Nevertheless, for the coverage and the cost, these beat anything else out there in my opinion. Very happy.

My wife got this for me for my 40th birthday. Clearly, a subtle signal that I needed to workout more and was already over the hill and needed a heart monitor. She also got it because I'm a bit "techy" and the other reviews stated that you could track an immense amount of information with the GPS and monitor.

I absolutely love my Garmin. I use it all the time when I run and bike and religiously upload the information. It is outstanding for heart zone workouts and maintaining pace and can really give you a sense of how you're tracking on your regular routes. The upload and sync is easy. Over the 18 months I've had this, I have transitioned from PC to Mac and both syncs work well. PC actually works better and the application has better rendering. This is actually the only knock I have. I would have expected the Mac version to be more polished. That said, all the data is there and can be easily reviewed.

The GPS tracks well. The initial satellite sync can take a while, but I've found that if I bypass it by hitting the mode button, it will still pick up satellites and track pace and location relatively quickly. The display can be easily customized to show the information that you care about and there's a lot of workouts that you can program to augment your training.

The heart monitor works well. I've run into two issues when cycling where if I have a layer, like a wick shirt for running or biking, on, it can cause a strange heartbeat spike. This is actually due to some initial static that gets generated with some of the workout shirts, but can be resolved by sweating, or (what I do) licking your hand and wiping a bit of spit on the underside of the sensor before working out. I'm like accurate stats and seeing a 197 heart rate is disconcerting to me. I have not had to replace any battery on the monitor yet and it's comfortable and sturdy.

I absolutely love this thing and to this day, my wife and I agree, that it is one of the best gifts ever.

I've gone through multiple earplugs in recent years, and these are by far, the tops for solid, rich sound at this price. The noise canceling is outstanding and I've even just used them as earplugs on flights for when I want to sleep. I recently forgot them on a trip and purchased a cheaper pair at the airport. The difference is enormous.

That said, I think there are two draw-backs in my opinion: (a) even though the fit is snug, when I run do other mobile activities, the earplugs fall out occasionally (b) this isn't the worst thing given that the noise canceling probably doesn't make them the safest to wear when running or biking.

I only gave it 4 stars because it doesn't connect with my TV like it claims it should. I thought it would turn on and off my TV with the voice. My remote to my TV has a voice button.
I do like using it as an alarm clock though. Auto dims and is a photo slide show, it sounds decent also, but I have better Bluetooth speakers. My kids like asking it to play a certain songs and ask it to tell them a joke.
I use these for about 3 hours a week at the gym. Was looking for an inexpensive pair and these do the job. Not a lot of bass but which is fine with me.
Works...decent picture...speakers are horrible and if you use the 3.5 out its sound is still messed up

I bought this for my Dell XPS M170 after I was having issues that seemed to be related to heat.  When I play my game, my laptop gets extremely hot.  I also usually have my laptop on all day long.  I ordered this in November of 2006 and it still works great.  I like that it has an extra USB port.  The fans are very quiet that I forget they're even there.  The black matches my XPS perfectly and the width is perfect for my 17 inch.  Only thing was...as the other reviews said...it's too short in the back.  Mine is short almost 3 inches.  I have to be very careful when I move the screen because I have my laptop set on a small laptop cart and if it tips over, it's going to hit the floor.  This is the only reason I took away a star.  If it was just a little bit longer in the back, this product would be perfect in my opinion.  And it definitely keeps my laptop a lot cooler.  There is a noticeable difference in temperature.  I would recommend this product to others.

I just wanted a basic microphone to use with Ventrillo to be able to talk to my in-game buddies.  This is the first mic I have ever bought.  I didn't want to get anything too expensive since its primary use is for chatting.  Very easy to install.  Just plug it into the USB port and you are ready to go.  My friends say my voice is crystal clear.  I also like that I don't have to be  really near the mic to be heard.  My only complaint is that sometimes I echo to my friends.  I'm sure that is because I'm not using headphones and it is picking up my speaker sounds.  It is not bothersome enough for me to switch to a headset which I didn't want to do.  I spend long hours on the game and cringe at the thought of wearing headphones for that long.  Great little starter mic to use with chat especially for the price.  I even bought a second one for my husband's desktop.  I've had it for a little over a year now and it is still going strong.  I've never had a problem with it.  Great buy.

This was my first webcam purchase so I did a bit of research before I actually purchased it.  So far, I really love it and the camera is very cute (a lot smaller than what I had imagined).  Installing was very easy and very quick.  I was concerned about the clip when I read the other reviews, but it fits my Dell XPS M170 laptop very well.  I purchased this camera to use with Skype and the quality of the picture is great.  Although it seems the picture is better on the receiving end.  When I see the image on my screen, it seems grainy to me.  I had planned on just using my Logitech mic that I use for gaming but when I called relatives, they said that the mic sounded good and didn't echo.  The USB cord is the perfect length since I already have a jumble of wires behind my laptop so that was a plus.  Only thing I really would like is auto focus but once you focus it the first time, you don't really need to adjust it anymore.  Overall I am very pleased with this purchase.

I highly recommend this product. I truly do not have a negative thing to say so far.

The application for the product is simple and secure, it doesn't feel invasive or computer exhausting compared to typical launchers. Setting up the password protection was easy and I feel confident in it's programming that my data would be secure should the device fall into the wrong hands.

The device itself is far lighter and smaller than I expected. I kick myself for not switching to a SSD sooner after lugging around bulky, slow HDD devices. Sure the price can be a bit of a hit, but it's worth it if you rely on external devices and mobility frequently.

I move footage around constantly as a freelance creator and this was exactly what I needed. I highly suggest this to anyone looking for external storage of any sort. Having always used HDD for external storage, switching to SSD and specifically this product, was the best thing I've done for my business in a long time.

I've owned a green screen before and researched a lot, but after reading reviews I decided to go with what seemed like the best. I was correct in my decision.

This screen is amazing. It's a bit heavy, and a little bit bigger than I expected, but honestly it's perfect. The screen is so easy to adjust, I truly don't know how to explain the simplicity behind the design. You can move it up and down from any position without having to lock it in place. All you have to do is move it to the desired height.

Not only is adjusting the screen smooth, but the ability to store the entire piece of equipment with ease is a real plus. All you need to do is collapse the screen, lock the easy to use braces, and turn in the feet under the case.

I am really happy with this purchase. I think you'll be happy too!

The product itself is an absolute tank. You can tell the product is build with some quality material. The instructions are rather unclear though, in fact I'm still not 100% sure I correctly assembled it considering there were screws already in place in spots I was instructed to install them in.

The heavy duty nature of the mount does lead to the only big issue I have with the product. It requires a lot of desk space to mount to. As in in the edge reaches pretty far in to spin to lock on. The device used to screw the lock onto the desk is also massive and difficult to manipulate. If it wasn't for the desk mount itself, I'd give it a 5/5.

Overall though, I'd suggest it to buy. For the price I paid I was not expecting such a durable product.

Cheers.

When my wife saw this, she said "order it" She wanted to be able to play cassette tapes. So far we have only listened to the radio part and the sound is only fair.

I collect flashlights and can always use more batteries. This 6 pack will come in very handy. I often gift my flashlights to friends and clients. Anyway, I like this set. The plastic battery box that came with mine holds 4 batteries and the other two are just loose. No big deal.

I was having a lot of neck strain from working on my laptop all day at home. I got a stand for my laptop, but needed a wireless keyboard and mouse. Since my work laptop is not a Mac, this set was my best option. I've owned this for over a month and I have to say this is nearly perfect.

Keyboard:
Overall, it's a quiet keyboard. I tend to slam on my keys, but it's a lot quieter than my Dell keyboard. I like that this is fairly compact for a full size keyboard and is very light. The appeal for me was the full sized keyboard because the other available keyboard for Windows at the time was Logitech and the round keyboard was too small and was missing quite a few keys I needed for my job. I work a lot with numbers, so the keypad was a huge plus for me.

The battery slot wasn't very intuitive, but once I figured it out it was smooth sailing. My only cons are that it doesn't have legs to prompt the keyboard up at an ergonomic angle for me. Also, I don't use most of the preset function keys, but I'm sure there's a way to change it.

Mouse:
I used to use a Microsoft Wireless 4000. It was ergonomically perfect for my long fingers, but I could not stand that it would run through a whole AA battery in 3 weeks (maybe I just work too much). This is a bit small and flat for my hands, but it works well. I just have to get used to it by either sliding my hands back more or using my entire finger instead of the finger tips to operate the mouse.

I was concerned from another review that it will burn through the battery quickly, but it has an auto-shut off feature where it'll wake up when you click the mouse key. The clicker is very quiet and the scroll makes some quiet clicks when I scroll through, but I like the control. Wish it was more ergonomic for me, but it works well.

I bought this for my work laptop that tends to overheat. This keeps my computer fairly cool and is whisper quiet where it doesn't disturb my conference calls. However, one con I have is that the grip pads left a weird yellow stain on my surfaces. At first I thought it was because the heat from my laptop was melting adhesive, but it still stained another surface of mine after using it for 10 mins (even though it was cooled and cleaned before using).

My husband works out and I recently (accidentally) washed his workout shorts with his earbuds in the pockets. This Huasori case for my Fire HD (10th generation) is gorgeous. The colors are orange, cranberry, white and yellow. The design is cool – flowers, swirls and the sun. Very abstract.  My Kindle Fire snapped into the case easily. The cut-outs or holes for the camera, power cord and volume, are correct. This case closes with a magnetic snap which stays closed securely. There are two things that I wish this case had that my current one does. On my other one, there is a little area that you can fold the cover and prop my device open. This particular feature lets you prop the device open easily and view videos. Secondly, you have to slide and Velcro my Kindle in, which seems more secure. While it has never happened, I wonder if my Kindle if dropped will pop out? It just seems like the Velcro secures the device better, but I will see.  However, even with these two criticisms, I would recommend this case and definitely plan to alternate between the two that I have.

The Jabra Evolve 65t EarBuds are pretty sweet. They come with a convenient zip case (with handle), charging case (USB cable included), Bluetooth adapter (dongle) and three sets of ear pads (so you can size them to fit comfortably in your ear). The directions for connecting to a device are pretty simple. For the computer, plug in the Bluetooth adapter and download the Jabra Direct app, and for your telephone just hold down the button until your earbuds turn blue and connect.  No matter the device, once you follow the directions, your device is operable within a few minutes. Placing the Jabra Earbud into the ear is simple, just insert into your ear (once you pick the appropriate set of pads) and rotate into place. In my opinion, the sound quality is fantastic, with both music and phone calls. You can work the controls (i.e., pause, play, hold and mute) with a tap on the device. A charge on the earbuds are believed to last up to 5 hours, and you are able to get two full battery charges from the rechargeable case.  While these are a little expensive, they are in my top five earbuds that I have owned. Overall, when I consider the sound quality, functionality and appearance, I give these five out of five stars, hands down.

The Acer Aspire 5 is a nice little laptop. I think it is perfect for the average student (high school or college) or for the home. Set-up is really easy. It is lightweight and fits into the average laptop bag. This makes it convenient and easy to carry or travel with. The screen size (15.6) is nice and the resolution clear (1060 HD). There are several ports: USB, Type C and HDMI. There is no CD reader, which is fine because most laptops don’t come with that anymore anyway. Most people just use a USB. There is 8GB of memory. Once charged, the battery life is decent. The sound quality from the built-in speakers is decent, so listening to videos or music is great. There is also one feature of this computer that I really like. It has fingerprint technology which adds an extra layer of security. Now, the two things that I would change about this computer: additional memory and make it a touch screen.  First, why not have more memory out of the box versus having to add some later. AND don’t most screens today come with touch technology? I think that would be an awesome feature.  However, for the cost, this computer has a decent amount of bang for the buck. It is affordable, lightweight and can do a lot, especially for students. And since my son will be entering his freshman year this fall, I will probably let him take this laptop.

My youngest son graduated from high school this past weekend. I wanted him to be able to capture memories. Kids today use their cameras, but never go on to print out the photos. Of course, I am from a generation where we use to print out photos and scrapbook or place them in a photobook. Instead kids today Instagram or Snapchat, simply posting a memory that will be gone if those platforms crash. So, I instead am trying to get my son to capture some moments on film. The Polaroid Original One Step 2 provided gives him that option. Simply point and shoot. Instant fun, instant prints, instant memories captured.  I remember begging for a Polaroid when I was younger.  My parents said that they were expensive, and it seemed to take some time before “Santa” gave me one. But once I did, I enjoyed snapping photos and waiting those few minutes until the photo came to life before my eyes. So really, this is more nostalgic than practical. I wanted my son to know the wonder of a Polaroid. So of course, this review is from that prospective. The One Step 2 is easy to load. There is a built-in flash and other great features. Unlike the old Polaroids, this one has a built-in rechargeable battery. That’s a very nice feature. The only thing is that this camera DOES NOT come with film, but that was pretty easy to rectify. I simply ordered mine on Amazon. While some would say that the film is kind of expensive, 8 pics for about $18.00 which equals a little over $2 a photo, it is FUN and the exciting thing is now you can get black & white film. How much fun is that? Start capturing your memories. 4 stars.

I have owned a few surround sound systems in the past, but this one is one of the more advanced systems by far. Not only does it look great but sounds great too! While the Yamaha RX-A880 seems bulky and large, it will fit in most cabinets. It is sleek looking with a digital display. It is very simple to set up AND has the ability to give you a full surround sound experience. It is capable of running up to a total of seven speakers along with a subwoofer. It comes with seven HDMI inputs which can accommodate multiple devices. The Bluetooth wireless connection gives you the ability to connect the device to a smartphone, tablet or computer. All you have to do is download the free Yamaha Musiccast app from Google Pay Store or iTunes.  You can play music through most of the popular sound apps (i.e., Spodify, Pandora, Apple Music, etc). The Sound quality is great and gives you the ability to choose different surround sound options (i.e., sports, action games, music video, standard, adventure, drama, mono, etc). The system also has the multi-room capability and the ability to make adjustments on your television screen. Power is not a problem and gives you 100 watts of power per channel. Overall this is a great receiver (for the amateur music enthusiast) and gets 4 stars.

They are made to last, so I expect several years of quality listening and enjoyment. I’d definitely recommend these.

The detachable cable allows the user to control the volume, pause, forward and play songs. The cable also allows the user to stop and answer phone calls. The clarity is very clear. I have an android phone, but I am sure that they are compatable with the Iphone as well.

Sound Quality: These headsets have a frequency response of 18000- 22000 hz which allows the listener to hear those deep bass lows and high notes that are popular today in a large genre of music. Again, the sound quality is very good and great clarity.
Overall, these headphones are 5 out of 5.

This Acer computer (Aspire V17 Nitro-Black Edition) is extremely attractive (ok, that shouldn’t be the most important thing but it helps). The aesthetics of this computer are great. It came in a sleek black box that if you are giving it as a gift, would make quite the statement.

The computer itself is black (almost a matte finish) and when on, the keyboard lights up neon red. The keyboard feels comfortable and is surrounded by a rubbery type material. The monitor/screen is 17.3 inches. It is clear, shows videos and photos in HD. I haven’t noticed any bleeding or distortion. The keyboard is comfortable, but I am a girl with fingernails that aren’t too long. My husband and teenage sons did not complain about the shape and size of the keys, but that is an attribute that may depend on your personal preference.

The computer was pretty easy to set up. It came preloaded with Windows 10 and Cortana (Microsoft’s version of Siri). You can cut that feature on and off. It has a camera and the other basic features of a laptop. The sound quality is sharp and clear. The charge seems to be appropriate for the use.

When you read this review, you must first understand I’m not a techy, so for me this laptop is perfect. I can surf, watch movies and do the basics. I haven’t noticed any issues but will update this review if I do. Overall, I give it 4.5 stars.

Lenovo has made a great gaming headset. You can connect to a computer or gaming console with a USB, and for those who would prefer to use their telephone (android or Apple) there is a 3.5mm connector. When connected to your computer you can go to the Lenovo's website - http://www.lenovo.com/gamingheadset, download the software and make adjustments to the headset. For example, one feature is a delay in the mic. It allows a two or six second delay, or will stay on continuously. There is also an equalizer, that you can manually adjust that allows you to enjoy different genres of music (ie., jazz, dance, rap, classical, etc). There is a Movie/Surround sound setting/adjustment that allows for music and gaming. The Audio Brilliant sound adjustment and Dynamic Bass Selection gives you deeper bass sound through different levels. There is Smart Volume setting which allows for high dynamic sound with music and Low Dynamic sound for voice. There is also a Voice Clarity setting where the decibel level can be changed for clarity over the mic and surround max. The other settings (Voice Control and Magic Voice) are for the microphone and changes the sound of your voice.

This headset is attractive and comfortable. It is black with red accents. There is adequate cushioning around the ears and the headband is adjustable. Lenovo folds up neatly for storage. The only negative (while I didn't deduct for) is that it doesn't come with a carrying case, and it would be nice even if it was a drawstring bag. The external mic is removable and attaches about six inches off of the right side of the headset. A feature that I like is that the mic can be moved forward and backwards, which is different from previous headsets that I have owned which only move up and down.

Overall, I would give these headset five stars when I consider all of the options provided, sound quality and comfort.

Reviewed by my husband, a photography enthusiast.

Over the last 20 years, my husband has purchased several LowePro camera bags/backpacks (i.e., Mini Trekker & Micro-Trekker 100). He has found that they have been some of the best he has ever owned. He prefers backpacks because they are easy to carry and keep up with, especially if you are on the go. Backpacks also allow for easy storage and are super convenient. They give you freedom of movement and your hands are free to capture those special moments that you may not otherwise get if you were holding a bag in your hand. The Viewpoint (LowePro) BP 250 is the perfect addition to his bag collection especially since it is specially designed for small video equipment.

Here’s what he liked:

• This bag is attractive. The design is smart, functional and full of surprises. The Viewpoint BP250 is well-made with plenty of room for your Go Pro and accompanying equipment. There is a ton of storage (inside and out). There are several compartments where you can store your accessories, cords, lenses and other equipment. On the outside of the main bag, there is a zipper pocket (which allows for small items like a memory stick/card or thumbdrive). There is a pocket on the other side of the bag which will fit a small tripod or other item (like an umbrella). The entire bag can be zippered so you won’t lose any of your accessories.

• It is ideal for those who use (small) video and other digital equipment. There is a space dedicated to a small computer. While this backpack will not allow you to carry one of the larger sized laptops (our 17” didn’t fit), it has adequate space for the smaller ones (about 15”), a SurfacePro, iPad or other small notebook or tablet. He finds that the option of carrying a computer is great because it will allow you to quickly upload and edit your videos wherever you are. There is no reason to wait….just review, edit (if needed), and upload!

• The straps are unlike the traditional ones that come straight down the shoulders. The BP250 LowePro’s straps are curved which he found to be less stress on his shoulders. After some adjustments (he’s 6’1, average sized with average shoulders), it was a good fit. The straps are slightly padded and comfortable. There are small snaps that lock the straps in place to ensure that they don’t fall down when walking or hiking.

• There is a small (lunch box sized bag) that can be removed and can hold your GoPro camera and equipment. Once closed, it fits directly into your main LowePro Bag. It is padded and once inside, will protect your camera and smaller lenses. Or if you want, this smaller bag can be used instead of taking the large one.

• This bag comes with a rain cover. Not sure how much you will use this feature, but if you are ever caught in a drizzle or rain storm, there is a plastic cover that can be removed (unzipped) from the bottom and cover your bag. This is perfect for keeping your bag and equipment dry.

• The price. While this bag may seem a little pricey (about $130) it’s worth it. The craftsmanship and functionality will prove invaluable for the amateur or professional photographer. It’s a small investment with some heavy returns. You’ve got protection and functionality.

Overall, my husband gives this bag 5 stars. He finds that it is not only good to use for a GoPro, but other small video and photography equipment. Backpacks are useful for photographers because they allow your hands to be free to capture those moments or events as they unfold. In the past he has purchased Lowepro equipment and found them to be sturdy and durable, and the Viewpoint BP250 is not different. It looks good and he won’t leave home without it.

For some purchasing this pair of BOSE SoundTrue headphones would be quite the investment. The question then becomes "are these headphones worth the money?" Over the last two years or so, I have purchased several headphones as gifts. My sons (both teens) had been begging for headphones, specifically the Beats by Dre, for some time. So began my research on headphones on the market. I wanted a quality product for a reasonable price. So when Amazon offered a special on the V-Moda headsets, during the holidays two years ago, I couldn't pass up the deal. I purchased two pair and was pleased. Both of my sons loved them, especially when they compared them to their friends "Beats". The V-Modas were sturdy and not as bass heavy as the Beats. The bass of the V-Moda wasn't amplified and overwhelming. They didn't feel that they were sacrificing sound quality or style. During this same time period, my husband purchased two sets of Sennheiser (PX 100 and 250 series), one for himself and another as a Christmas gift. One set was around the ear and the other, over the ear. So, over a two year time span, I have had the opportunity to listen to music with all of these headphones and can offer an opinion. And while I am not an expert, I am an average wife and mother who intends to use these headphones for recreational purposes (i.e., when cleaning the house, walking in the neighborhood, etc) only.

These headphones are:

1. Extremely light weight. Light enough to put in a purse, book-bag or briefcase, etc. without weighing you down.
2. Comfortable. The ear-covers and headband are padded and extremely comfortable when worn. They block out most if not all of the outside noise. Your ears are completely covered and the sound is crystal clear. **While the ears of the set remain secure or in place, I did notice that the headphone would fall down occasionally. To correct this, I would suggest that you adjust the headphones tighter than you normally would, especially if you have thick hair and this seems to correct the problem.
3. Functional. There is a long cord that attaches from your device to the headset. The long cord gives you some flexibility and mobility. But caution, you may want to secure some of the cord if you are using an armband type holder for your device. Otherwise the cord might get stuck on stuff while you are using it. You can operate various functions (volume, etc) from the back of the microphone. It is located on the cord near your mouth. However, I do wish that the microphone with the function button was lower on the cord, or could be adjusted because while it is comfortable when using the microphone, it isn't when you adjust the sound. If it was further down, you could adjust the sound easier and see the buttons clearly.
4. Can be used with multiple devices. I use mine with my IPOD, IPAD, computer and Android phone (Nexus 4, Google Phone).
5. Enclosed in a convenient carrying case. It fits well in most bags or luggage. They are easy to pack up and travel with.
6. Sound quality. While not bass heavy at all, I think these are perfect for all kinds of music. My playlist includes music from artists like Mree, Daley, Jhene Aiko, The Weekend, Diana Krall, Young Summer and Cary Brothers...and the sound is great. These headphones have a nice, kind of surround sound quality. These definitely complement all music types. But if you want deep bass, I wouldn't recommend these. But if you want clear sound, these are the headphones for you.
7. Kind of Expensive. These headphones cost about $180. And while that price is comparable to others (i.e., The V-Modas are around $200 and the Beats can range from $200 to $300.) on the market, are you getting the same features for the price? Probably. However, if you are a DJ or money is no object, you may not blink at the price, hence viewing it as an investment. But for the average consumer, you have to consider the features and decide if they are worth the money. So if you aren't looking for bass heavy or exaggerated sound, and you like the fact that these completely cover the entire ear, these are the perfect headphones for you. I give them 4 stars.

I found myself in the market to replace my Belkin IPOD armband (the Velcro began separating from armband). I knew that it would probably be cheaper to just buy another one, than to try and repair it. The pack is slightly padded and appears to offer just the right amount of protection. With the exception of having to flip the device upside down so that you can access the cords, for the price and for what I intend to do with this product, it is absolutely perfect.

I was looking for stocking stuffers for my two teenaged boys. Both had expressed an interest in the Beats by Dre. I don't know about you, but I was looking for a reasonable pair of headphones to accompany other high priced gifts (new Xbox, Laptop etc) they were getting for Christmas. BUT paying almost $200 for the Beats seemed unreasonable. So when these (V-Moda, Crossfade LP) were highlighted on Amazon on Black Friday, I seized the opportunity and purchased two pair (which was still cheaper than one pair of Beats), and hoped that I could rely on the reviews that I read. (Please note that I did read reviews for Beats, and found that the V-Moda pair received more positive reviews.) So with both sets of reviews under my belt, I begin to compare the features and was even more convinced that I had made a wise purchase. (Also note that later my sons were able to compare them with the Solo Beats by Dre and they still liked the Crossfades better.)

Features that my sons say make these a standout amongst most headsets:
* The overall sound quality is great and not too bass heavy.
*The over the ear covers (ear piece) have memory cushions. They are very comfortable and you can't hear outside noise (Of course I found this to be true when they could not hear me calling them. Of course, they may be ignoring me). I also can't hear the music that they are listening to.
* The volume or pause feature can be used from a control button on the cord. They even say that besides skipping songs, the rarely have to touch their devices when using these headphones.
* These earphones are versatile and can be used with multiple devices (i.e., the computer, Ipod, cell phones, etc). They are able to even use them in the car by connecting with the stereo.
* These headphones are stylish and attractive. I ordered one pair in Phantom Chrome and the other in Phantom Black.

And finally, what Mom likes about the headphones...well, the price. These headphones were reasonably priced and offered the same features as the Beats. And later when I compared them with the Beats, they appear to be better quality in terms of sound quality and workmanship (the Beats are plastic looking and don't seem to be as well constructed as the Crossfade, which seems sturdy).
Finally, overall for the money I think I got a top notch product. I highly recommend these to anyone on the market for some headphones and give this product five (5) stars.

When I ordered the Cyber Acoustics CA-3908 3 piece set, I thought it would be perfect for our home office. I thought it would enhance the music that I played from my computer, as well as hook up easily to other devices. What I received was better than I could have imagined. Instead of being something that I could only use in the home office, I found that this system is a great little item for just about anywhere in the house. My sons have used it to attach to a variety of other devices...the IPOD touch, the Xbox, cell phones (I have a G2), and our personal PC. The sound quality is great and carries well throughout the house.  No matter what kind of music you are listening to (bass heavy or not), the sound comes across with no vibration or distortion.  This speaker system is easy to setup with only two wires connecting the subwoofer. The system is compact and doesn't take up too much space. Come to think of it, this system would even be perfect for a dorm room or apartment.  The volume control, on/off switch, headphone jack are located on a circular dial.  Overall, I am extremely pleased with this item and believe that it is a small investment for a quality system. I give it 5 stars.

When I selected the Philips AS140/Fidelio Docking System for the Android, I really did not have any expectations only the hope that it would be easy to set up and do what I wanted it to do....play music and maybe wake me up. I definitely did not want something too complicated or difficult to operate. And to be honest, the Philips has just the right amount of technology and features for me because there are times when I am technically challenged. Simply stated, the directions for electronics need to be easy to read and understand. And who could ask for more than easy to follow directions will illustrations (even in Spanish if you need them)? And while I probably have not untapped all of its possibilities, I think I have a decent understanding of its basic features.

Setting up the Philips was easy enough. You simply go to the Android Market and install Songbird on your phone and PC (this allows you to download music and access it). In general, I consider the Philips Docking Station to be a super tuner (I am sure that there is a better word for it...but again, I am a girl), which allows you to access local and internet radio stations as well as podcast). You even have an option for an alarm clock and timer. When you attach your android phone (I have the LG G2x and it fits perfectly with or without the case), you can use the blue tooth feature as sort of a remote control. The phone doesn't even have to be attached to the docking station for you to surf radio stations or podcast. I was even able to access "Pandora" (a station that I access on my telephone) and listen to my favorite music selections. And remember, you aren't limited to just the radio, or other programs, but you can download music (from Songbird) to your PC and access it from your phone.

The positive things about the product:
(1) Easy set up. Download program, and you are in business!
(2) Decent sound quality. The sound is clear. It seems a little heavy at times on the bass, but maybe that is simply because I need to play with the features a little more and learn how to address it.
(3) The time automatically syncs between your cell phone and the station so you don't have to really worry about it.
(4) Your phone charges while docked.
(5) The blue tooth technology allows you to use your phone as a remote...changing the stations easily.
(6) There is a timer and alarm feature/option.
(7) Downloading music is simple.
(8) It's cute and doesn't take up a whole lot of space on your nightstand or dresser. And if you don't want to necessarily use it as an alarm clock, you could even use it in your kitchen. It's probably better than one of those under the cabinet radios.

Overall, I like the Philips AS140/37, it has some pretty neat features that a girl who isn't necessarily technologically savvy can enjoy. It's easy to set up and use. I give this system a solid 4.

The Logitech Pad N120 is light weight, quiet and cute.....just as advertised! The "cooling" pad is extremely light weight, and can easily be held between two fingers. It is really slim (not bulky at all) and therefore doesn't take up much space when stored. It is the perfect size (at least for a DELL) and comfortable to use anywhere. There is a USB cord that once connected to your laptop, turns on the fan which keeps cool air circulating underneath. And when the USB is not being used, the cord can be hidden underneath the cooling pad, its cord slipping smoothly into the area where it is designed to go. The fan of the Logitech Pad is extremely quiet. I can barely hear it when it is on. And finally, this cooling pad seems to be well worth the money. While it might be more expensive than some I have seen, it seems worth the money, and definitely has those features that I think most people desire.

Quality and Style- 5

For Christmas I received the Kindle and this cover. Trust me when I tell you that selecting just the right cover is as important as selecting the Kindle itself. Warning: My husband said that when he ordered this case, it took longer than expected to arrive. It was apparently from Britain and had to go thru customs before it arrived. Durability - 5
