I hope this review has helped, as reading reviews for products is something I do all the time.

I have purchased quite a few wireless head sets.  I have a regular full cushion headset that works great as far as distance, but must say, this is by far the best sounding, comfortable head set I own to date.  Plus the fact I paid more for my next best wireless head phone.  I bought my son-in-law one, and he loves it for working out at the gym, and for running!  GREAT PRODUCT!
Beautiful DVD. The sound and picture quality is awesome

I have a pair of Apple AirPods Pro, which I like well enough.  I bought these after reading a review somewhere.  I love them.  The sound quality and noise cancellation seem to work as well as the Air Pods, and they actually seem to stay in place better.  I’d definitely buy them again.
This turntable’s movement is so easy, quiet, and smooth.  Very impressed with the quality.  Great service from vendor, too.
I love this! Has a lot of ports for every cord some plug ins they positioned to go the other way so all cords can fit equally on there without bumping into another one.

I purchased a new desktop computer and I had Bose speakers (basically these) that were over 14 years old and so I decided to pass them on figuring that the PC speaker would work fine with music based on the fact it is 2022.  No such luck - the sound was okay - but for someone who likes to hear all the nuances I decided to purchase a new pair.  Not so easy - I did not want bluetooth, as they do need to be recharged and honestly I just wanted to turn the suckers on and go - - - I decided on these, the price was double what I paid 14 years ago, however I also expected a better product and it is!  Easy to set up (yes the left side cord could be longer, but the sound is awesome!  I was worried they would vibrate on my table as the old ones did (I used a potholder underneath to prevent the noise) but these are a tad larger and much heavier and there is no vibration no matter how loud Imake the speaker.  I don't consider these breaking the bank and back in my high school - college days sound and receivers nearly took an entire wall in a room and were quite costly getting into the higher quality stuff - these smaller speakers can pack an awesome punch - using my Amazon Music set on Ultra High Definition I can't get over the lovely sound.  So for me these are a 10 plus and for someone that wants a nice sound, but not such a hefty price they are worth every penny.

We traded in our high end new car purchase (a thing now for dealers with no cars to sell), and purchased an older vehicle (20 years old, but a super high end model at the time) deciding to wait a few years while things shake out in the economy and e-vehicles become easier to purchase and use.  It is a wonderful vehicle, and aside from the laughing about a cassette player in the dash, of course there is no navigation screen.  I kept looking at the dash to see the navigation screen.  LOL  So I decided that we do have areas where we like to know where we are, and we like to know if there is traffic issues ahead so I went exploring on Amazon and came up choosing this.  I love it.  The reviews were daunting - to difficult to set up - no way to store information - no battery life, etc.  I found no issues - clearly going through the set up and checking out all the bells and whistles - this navigation has an app in it for truck drivers who need to keep hours and such, more than one driver can be tracked.  Well I don't need that for sure but who cares, I have everything else I need.  Day and night colors, sounds for certain driving functions, voice choices, car icon choices, a device so you can place it on the dashboard and an adapter to keep it running.  It clearly states in the instructions that the battery life is for emergency use only and has a limited use time.  You must keep it plugged into a power source.  I had to do the same thing for my TomTom, which was purchased in 2004 and can no longer be updated which is why I looked for a new one, and a less expensive one.  I have set the home function, and have entered quieries for road trips, which the device has set up and moved forward with NO issues.  I placed the dash clamp just where the 9" screen sits just over the dashboard, where a navigation system would normally sit on the console.  My husband who claims to have eagle eye vision along with being able to hear a cat walking 100 feet away absolutely LOVES this screen because he can "easily see it" and "clearly hear it" as well.  We shall see the next time I tell him to take an exit!  LOL  You cannot beat the price and I am a very happy purchaser!

These are awesome.

They came in very nice packaging that seemed above the price of the headphones. They came with extra ear pieces and a carrying case.

I love the volume changing feature - always helpful.

The only weird thing about these headphones is how big they seem compared to my previous pair; this is mainly due to the thickness of the cord since it's tangle-reducing.

I really like these!
I am very happy with the sound and overall fit.  However,  the headphones start to hurt on long calls when wearing glasses.  Overall it is s great product.

I was very impressed with this wireless keyboard/mouse combo. I am partial to mechanical keyboards so it is hard to transition to a normal keyboard and still type with precision, but the keys on this keyboard have great rebound and I have had no trouble typing with it. The keys are also surprisingly quiet, which makes it useful in any setting. Even the box that it came in is great for storage. I also like that their are a number of hot key/function keys. Even better there is a function lock button that allows you to use the function keys continuously without needing to press the function key. The mouse clicks are also extremely quiet, and I had no issues with the plug and play as soon as I put the usb receiver in it everything was ready to go. Even though this is a full size keyboard with a full number pad, the thin structure makes it useful as a travel keyboard as well. I recently used it on a trip with my iPad and it came in very handy. I like the mouse but I think the keyboard is definitely the star of this combo, and highly recommend as it is a great value for the price.
I use it in my patio and the sound is clear and great!

I am returning the first one that I got because I think perhaps there may be a flaw in it because for no reason at all it just shut itself off or wouldn't show me any information on the watch and it did that to me twice so when it happened again today the second time I decided I'm returning it and requesting a replacement if it happens with the replacement then I'm getting my refund. I don't like sleeping with it on it's uncomfortable not used to sleeping with any kind of jewelry I did use it a few days and checked my sleep and it seemed to give me the same answer every time so I don't know if that's very accurate either? I realize these gadgets are not accurate however I'm just trying to find a way to motivate myself to move around more and I refuse to pay over $100 for one of these smart watches so I got this one on a lightning deal.
I like this a lot, I wish the sound was better on it for the price but it does make me wake up feeling more ready to wake up!

I can't justify not giving it 5 stars because it seems to just be the best case available, but there are issues.

The power, volume up/down buttons are labeled on the backside, which is great in case you need a reference, but the thick case makes it difficult to find and especially PRESS the buttons. Everyone knows the volume up is above and volume down is below, so instead of + and - labels, just make them textured so you can actually feel the correct location and boundaries of the buttons, to press them spot on.

It would be better if the material above the buttons was thinner so it was actually easier to push the buttons in without having to simultaneously brace the front of the tablet forcefully with my thumb while applying pressure to the button from the button on the slight-rear of the side of the tablet. It's frustrating enough that I'm trying to remember to just use the pull down software menu from the display.

Positives:
Well constructed and sturdy feel you'd expect if you've had a similar style case from Spigen. All cut-outs line up properly. The design looks hilariously sturdy for an iPad Mini; even the stand is sturdy. I don't have kids, but there are seemingly two separate sets of hand holds on the back, presumably designed for a set of very small hands in mind. The case seems tough enough for kids as long as they're not literally throwing it around. It should withstand many drops.

Confirmed to work with the Nintendo Switch using a USB male C to female A adapter. Just plug in and pair with the little button.

Tech note on aptx: In order for the sound reception to be low latency, the headphones or headset you're using has to support aptx as well. The APTX website has a product listing page for compatible headsets.

Quality is better than expected, and the light looks fantastic. I wish this was wireless like the mac-only one.
Cons: The Griffin application has to be running at all times in order for this to work. Why not just have the default driver for this act like a keyboard volume control natively with software optional for custom dynamic mapping? The volume knob in my keyboard does not require special drivers or software and worked right out of the box but I am changing keyboards. This product overcomplicates and should have a default option for users wanting to use this as just a volume knob.

Ordinarily I just buy AVR Receivers for about twice this price that seemingly have similar specs, but this one stood out because of its really high SNR (going from low 90s to 110 is apparently a /huge/ difference). I can't believe how quiet it is when its on and how crisp the sound is compared to much more expensive AVRs I've had. The only sound distortion I ever hear is from the cables themselves as I have them running through a crowded cable area. Its also quick to fully power up and even indicates when its still warming up with the light fading in and out for about 2 seconds until its on, so that you don't blast out your speakers trying to get sound to come out only to find out that the amplifier wasn't ready (some units really don't indicate well when they are actually ready, or they take so long that you're not sure).

The Sound is also very loud. I can only turn the volume (gain) knob in the back of the unit to about halfway with my [[ASIN:B0071MSYEE Polk Monitor 40]] (20-125W, 89db) speakers. The manual indicated that ordinarily, you would want the power amplifier to have its gain knob at full, but that just makes my PC's volume settings way too sensitive.

The downside is that the unit only has a volume knob in the back and its very small and only meant to be set once really. The volume is intended to be changed from the source (preamp), or in my case, a volume knob on my keyboard that turns up and down the volume in windows on my PC.

If you're on the edge, trust me this is great for the price. This whole experience just made me wish that I had bought discrete amplifiers for all my other setups instead of AVRs.

Whether this product works is going to depend on your vehicle much more than this product. I tested this in two different cars. In one car, a 2010 F150, it worked so well that it didn't even matter what radio station frequency that I set the unit to, it would power over even the most powerful local stations and sound fantastic. In the other car a 2004 Ford Explorer, it was still able to get fantastic quality that sounded just as good as if it came over a cable (and i'm often picky about such things), but only if set to a mostly empty frequency and it was much more difficult to find one.

I should also note that this was the top choice for an FM-transmitter in a review from the wirecutter, a popular consumer electronics website with articles comparing different products.

This essentially works exactly the same as the other, nearly identical cube shaped real tone alarm clock radio. If you're debating between the two, get this one. The buttons are more intuitive and it has a real antenna. Sounds virtually the same to me. Same functions.

What I didn't like, the radio tuning knob is above the volume knob. When reaching for it in the morning (or anytime) I always instinctively assume the top knob is volume. The color in person seems a tad more saturated but it's no big deal.

I don't know why there are so many negative reviews for this. This is my second one (a gift) and it works fine and the price is great.

My old enclosure stopped working. It showed it was getting power, and the drive would show up, but I'd get errors trying to access it. Figured it was my enclosure or my drive....and the enclosure is much cheaper to replace (not to mention the lost data if it's the drive). I browsed amazon real fast and this one seemed solid, and the price was good, so I bit.

In fact, I like it much better than my old Rosewill enclosure. No tools required at all. Very simple. I didn't even need to look at any directions. It was put together and plugged into my computer in under a minute. Worked straight out of the box with Windows 10 - I needed nothing else. I plugged it in and the drive appeared. I can't speak to longevity because I've only had it a month, but the enclosure itself feels very solid and like it could take a beating (not that you'd want to, like, toss it out your 3rd floor window or anything). I feel like my drive is safe in it.

It works perfectly, feels very sturdy, couldn't be easier to assemble, works plug-n-play with no additional software in Windows 10 at least, and the price was very reasonable. I can't really think of anything negative to say about it. I am pleased with my purchase and would buy it again.

If you're looking for a cheap pair of headphones that you don't have to be super upset if you lose, or a spare pare to keep somewhere just in case...these are it! For the price, they sound quite good and they seem to be very durable. Sure, you're not going to get the same audio quality as a $60 pair of earbuds, but these sound very good, not overly tinn-y and with a good bass. If I lose this pair, I will buy another just like it. I'm quite pleased with it.
Also love that it comes with multiple sizes of earbud attachments, as I have small ears.
I love that even though it is digital, the manual features are great. The audio quality is very clear.
I love my sound bar! My tv be on zero and it still be booming!

Love the color but extremely flimsy. It does not even line up with the iPad mini very well to shut it off. I was very disappointed.

these worked out better than my sony wireless. This cooler pad is pretty light. It's all plastic so it feels a bit flimsier than I had imagined it would be. It does produce a decent amount of air from it's fan. Pretty quiet too. Definitely quieter than an overheating laptop haha I wish there was an option to just set a single color rather than rainbow, but all the lights can be switched off too if you don't want any lights.

These are seriously great for the price. They come with different sizes of ear pieces to accommodate different ears. I've only charged it once since I've received them, and I use them frequently. I hope this review is helpful!:)

This flashlight is great! I was initially just looking for a small portable radio to use when we go to the drive in move theaters so I don't have to leave my car on.

This works great for that and so much more! The sound is pretty crisp with the antenna, and the dials are smooth and easy to use.

It's compact, but sturdy and has a nice rubberized finish to it that gives it a nice grip. Recently used it in some caves while hiking and the flashlight was awesome, it has 3 settings depending on how much light you'd like to shed. Also has a very bright work type light (the "reading light") that's also motion sensor.

It's really nice to know I can have this available and ready in an emergency since it's both solar and crank operated. I just keep it in my trunk for whenever I may need it. Will be awesome to take camping too!!

For the price I think these are pretty decent quality bluetooth headphones.

They stick out on the sides a little more than I'd like as well.

If you like your music LOUD, these will be for you. In comparison to some beats headphones I have, these are about 2x as loud. Quality is decent but can definitely become distorted at the higher volumes.

I found these comfortable at the top of my head but the ear pieces did begin to make my ears sore after a while.

They come with a wire to make them regular headsets which I think is awesome for places or times you can't charge these.

Overall for the price, I think these headphones are pretty good, just don't expect a luxury item. Would probably work great as travel pair.

The battery life is nice, I use it regularly and have had to charge it only a very few amount of times so far.

The lights it comes with are super fun too, I think it really helps set up a party atmosphere, even if that party is just me cleaning at home by myself! Haha
The silver on these headphones is plastic and looks quite cheap in person. For the price and sound quality, I think there are a lot of other options for a lower price.
solid unit, runs a bit loud but not really a concern.  Everything i look for in a car unit and more

Bought these as a backup headset for work from home and they’re a great value for the money. The sound is acceptable, controls what you would expect for headsets in this price range, and Logitech makes durable products in my experience.
I would recommend these for anyone looking for a quality headset for videoconferencing or work from home.

Slow down and read the screens as you're installing the Blink camera - I also was clicking through the screens and encountered a problem. So I started over and actually read the App screens as I scanned the QR codes on the Sync Module 2 and the Camera the 2nd time and that's where the problem occurred on the first attempt!! Not reading the screens.
After actually paying attention, the camera was successfully connected to my WiFi and Sync Module 2 showing live video of my front porch. This is Day 2 and so far, so good. I'm not interested in paying for cloud storage so have attached a USB drive to the Sync Module 2 and can access my stored events.
The only reason I didn't give the system 5 stars - yet - is the video capture does lag as other reviewers have clearly stated by a few seconds. I'll need to see if this is possible to adjust. Night vision quality is decent for perhaps 15 feet away and then darkness. That's okay because it's how close someone would be to your door when you could see them on a home grade camera like this. All said and done, for $69 on a deal I'm pleased with what's provided except the lag in capturing video. Will update when I have researched more.

Cloud drive this, that, and the other - BLAH BLAH BLAH. I've worked in IT and InfoSec long enough to tell you sometimes you just need to make a local backup with your computer disconnected from the network in the event you fear corruption from a virus, malware, or ransomware. I keep a rotating set of thumbdrives offline with a 2 month history and one of my 128GB drives acted a bit sketch so this is an excellent replacement. Tested and read and write speeds excellent. Would recommend.

I've had issues with every pair of ear buds I've ever tried that I could afford except for these. The sound is clear and crisp, perhaps lacking a bit in bass but frankly I need these for phone calls not intended for listening to music.
Anker makes good, if not great, products and gives you tremendous value for the money. The only reason for the 4 in sound is lack of pulsing base, the battery life is absolutely amazing. Another solid Anker product.

I LOVE these headphones!! My wife HAS to have the TV on at night to go to sleep and I dislike TV playing when it's bedtime. Suffice it to say this product has reduced a lot of tension and I've used them as well to hear clear crisp audio.
I picked an extra one of these up so I could have one at my office and the other on my nightstand. Quality audio and a convenient way to charge your tablet

Very pleased with the audio quality from a relatively inexpensive pair of earbud headphones, even more so given their price.

UPDATE: I've purchased additional pairs of these earbuds for myself and my family. They really have quality audio, come with a very nice zipper case, and are one of the best values I've found in headphones/earbuds. Very pleased and will likely buy again when they're on a deal of the day.

I am on conference calls for at least 6 hours a day as a telecommuting IT manager so comfort and sound quality are of equal importance to me. This product is so comfortable that having it on my head all day does not give me a second thought and the audio quality of those on the call and of my voice is excellent. I am seriously considering buying a couple spares of this product for whenever the product is no longer available - that is how pleased I am with the headset.

I got this to replace a Toshiba fire TV that was showing it’s age. I didn’t like the fact that the Toshiba lacked some normal features that you would see on a normal TV like being able to adjust the aspect ratio. Crazy. It also came with extremely limited app storage and you couldn’t delete half the apps that were taking up the limited storage. So far the Google TV operating system seems faster and easier to use. The picture is gorgeous. I don’t have cable, so I rely on digital OTA channels or streaming channels. I had to tweak the color slightly for my taste, they had the oranges and reds boosted a little too much. But it’s really fantastic. The sound is really good too, although, I am not an audiophile, and I don’t rely on my TV as my primary music source like some people seem to do. It has a cool feature where the sound is customized to the acoustics of your room and your position in it. You run this calibration holding the remote at chest high and the TV plays some sounds that sounds like space invaders and the remote records them and adjusts the sound accordingly. Oh, yes, the remote has a microphone built-in do it so you can use voice search and other voice activated features. The TV was easy to set up, although the whole linking of the Google accounts and all the other things they want you to sign up for was a bit of a chore. I opted out of some and kept others. Your mileage may vary. The table top stand is the easiest to install that I’ve ever seen, you just plug it into the bottom and there it is. No dealing with screws or anything like that. There are a decent number of HDMI inputs and two USB ports, so that’s a plus. Finally, while it says you need to people, I didn’t have two people and it was not that difficult to handle the TV. You do need to be really careful not to press on the LCD, which is a given for any TV. But the TV only weighs less than 30 pounds so it was easy to carry. All in all, it’s a really nice TV. I think it’s a little pricey, but you’re paying for the Sony name. And it does appear to be excellent quality.

I was a little aggravated when I first got this as it arrived with a starburst crack in the top of the case. However, after some pretty heavy rains none has gotten into the case through the crack. The base was getting too wet, but that was because I had it sitting on the table. Once I mounted it on a mount it works better. The Infrared lights reflecting off the inside of the case at night. However, if you have a motion sensing light mounted nearby and it illuminates, the camera works really well.  One thing that surprised me is that the sound still works pretty well. I haven’t tried using the speaker function, so I can’t comment on that. I’m leaving one star off for poor quality control that the cracked item got through.
You do need to do your research and make sure your system will accept audio input, not all do. It's a simple mic and the power splitter cable worked fine with my zosi bullet cams. Nice addition.

No one is going to confuse these with Bose, but at this price point I think they are nice headphones. I do agree with other reviewers that it would be nice if the earcups swiveled but I didn’t find them uncomfortable. One pet peeve I’ve had with some other headphones is that I can’t turn them up loud enough. Yeah, I know everyone is worried about ear damage, but if I can’t hear what I’m trying to listen to in a noisy environment like on the train the headphones are no good to me. They paired easily, sound good and the buttons work as expected so what’s not to like.

These earbuds are really cool. I *love* not having wires and being able to just wear one without having the other one dangling annoyingly. The sound is good. Not great, but good. I definitely felt like my Jaybird earbuds have better sound, but losing the wire more than makes up for it.
Now what I don't like. Number one, the lack of compatibility with ipads and ipods and any other tablet is really annoying. I get that the primary purpose is supposed to be exercise but for the price of these earbuds I want to be able to use them with everything I do. And my ipad is my primary music device as it has waaaay better battery life & storage capacity than my phone so I use it on the treadmill, on the boat, sitting out on the deck, even on the bike, etc. In fact, the only time I use the phone for music is walking/hiking. It does not seem like it would be that difficult to make it work with all devices so I hope they do. The earbuds will pair with the ipad and play music, but the only earbud function that works is play/pause. You have to change volume, skip forward and back, etc on the ipad. Not always possible and never very convenient.

I love this laptop. It's replacing an HP Envy that isn't even a year old yet. The ergonomic on this laptop are way better.I haven't accidentally bumped the touchpad while typing, and the keys are large with a nice feel. Performance.....well, I'm not gamer. It's doing ok on Photoshop, Lightroom and Chrome, and that's pretty much my big three. The backlit keyboard is something you'll never be able to live without once you've had it. The screen is gorgeous. It could, perhaps, be a touch brighter.  The sound from the speakers is ok. No one will confuse it with a surround sound system but it's good for a laptop.  The hard drive is quiet. The spinning of the one in the hP drove me mad. The USB ports are towards the back of the machine. I have not been a fan of the recent trend to move them up front as I'm forever bumping them. Great to see. Despite being larger than the HP, the power drain is MUCH lower. I live in a solar powered vehicle so this is important. Right now, with music playing and the screen at max, in high performance battery mode, I'm showing it using 17w. When I first plugged it and it wasn't fully charged yet, I saw a max draw of 29w. The HP drew almost 50w charging and 90 or better while running. I could not be happier with the Toshiba. The tablet mode thing......well, it's nice to be able to adjust the screen to any angle. Using it in tablet mode......I haven't found a lot of reasons to do that yet. It's pretty heavy and unwieldy to carry it around like an ipad at 5 pounds. But I guess it's nice to have the option. That brings me to another small quibble....it's kind of heavy for how thin it is. I was a little taken aback. I guess you can't have everything. Well, you can, but you'll pay two grand and up for it. For the $$ this is a great all around machine. I'm definitely not buying another Envy. Windows 10......boy, I was prepared to hate it. I don't. So far anyway. A lot of headaches can be avoided by setting your wifi connection to metered, then all those background updates don't happen as far as I can tell.  PS The stupid stickers they put all over these things came off with little effort and no residue. I hate those things. The Intel one put up a little fight but came off relatively easily.

I love this thing. It's gigantic, it's heavy, and it's awkward to move in close quarters. But it kind of brings me back to my youth where big stereos were the norm. It brings joy to my heart. It's like my 80's boombox, with Bluetooth. The sound is great. Bluetooth pairing was effortless, inside of 30 seconds after unboxing it I was streaming Spotify. And it sounded great. Mom loves purple so in her honor I changed the light to purple. (I still think she's less than thrilled, however.) My stepfather got an electric guitar for Christmas so the fact that you can use it for an amp is a bonus. There are handles on the top so it's not too bad to lift.

I wish it was easier to roll, you have to tilt it kind of far back before the wheels touch. I guess they're afraid some drunken partygoer might nudge it and mow down the crowd. I also wish there was an option to run it on 12v or batteries. I know I can use an inverter but it seems like something like this would benefit from the option. The cord is a little short too. But all in all, if you love music, you'll enjoy this.

Very cool little speaker with big sound. This is replacing a Canz speaker for use in my rv and while biking. I really like that this has buttons, unlike my Canz, which required me to go to the phone to do anything. I just started riding bikes again after many years and it's nice not to have to go digging in my pocket for the phone when I want to skip a song or something. The mounts could be a bit more robust, but I'm riding a beach cruiser on bike paths, not mountain biking the back 40.

I upgraded to the D810 from a D800e. My reaction to the first shot was, "Wow, it's quiet!!" The noise level of the shutter/mirror action is in my opinion less than the Quiet mode on the D800, and doesn't sound odd to my ears. And the Quiet mode is even quieter. What a great upgrade that I wasn't really expecting.

I bought the D810 primarily for the new s-Raw option. I loved having the huge resolution of the D800e, but didn't love the way I was burning through memory cards and portable hard drives with the giant file size of the raw images. I did a month and a half long trip to Alaska last summer and ended up having a new portable hard drive & a few memory cards Fedexed to me in Kodiak as I ran out of space too quickly. My choices were huge raw files or shooting jpgs with the compromises involved there. Or shooting in DX crop format and trying to remember to compose correctly. It was a headache, and when I got back I bought a D600. Unfortunately that camera is not really comparable, and I ended up selling it. When I saw the new D810 had the s-Raw option I jumped on it. It's great for the less critical shooting situations where I don't need the full resolution raw file, but I don't want to go.jpg. The s-Raw resolution is 3680x2456 12-bit uncompressed. I anticipate that my travel laptop will have an easier time handling these files in Lightroom as well, which will be nice.

The high ISO settings have considerably less noise, which is another welcome improvement. The AF seems more accurate as well. All in all, I'm very pleased I upgraded. Very, very happy with the improvements.

I got this as a Christmas gift and I was a bit stymied as I'd never seen or heard of such a thing.  Rounded up some batteries and an empty box and was amazed at the volume of sound.  I just took it for a weeklong camping trip and it was nice.  You don't (or at least I don't) want very loud music when camping....it's rude to the other campers and scares of the wildlife and masks the sounds of the outdoors.  And why are you there if not to enjoy the outdoors?  So at the subdued volume I like it was fine.  Here's the deal, if you think this thing is gonna sound like Bose, you're dreaming.  If you think 2 AA batteries and a Starbucks cup is gonna provide you with a rock-the-house experience, you're dreaming.  If you're looking for a little conversation piece you can toss in a bag and forget it's there that will provide you with a little background music, your dreams may have just come true.  Really fun item.  On a side note, the current price is too much, the $10 or $15 folks got them on Groupon for is more reasonable.

Nice case.  I wanted it primarily to protect my Kindle Fire HDX in my backpack, and it fulfills that function admirably, especially since it has an elastic band on the inside front cover that you can slip over the back of the Kindle when it's close to ensure it doesn't open up in your bag.  Nice touch.  I agree with the other reviewer who stated it's less comfortable to hold vertically.  However, I got used to it quickly, and now kinda pinch it against the Kindle with my left hand, and the lower left corner rests in my palm.  I tend to hold it horizontally most of the time anyway.  The horizontal stand function is great.  There are 3 grooves @ 1/4" apart that hold a tab on the edge of the case, so it's a bit more secure than those that rely on friction alone.  It doesn't pop out of the case at the slightest pressure, it takes a little work, but it's not like my iPhone hard case which requires 10 minutes of cursing and praying every time I remove it.  I like it, and may look for a Belkin case for my iPad as well.

I currently use an Induro BH2 which is just a bit too large and heavy for my casual usage.  I was hoping this would be a better fit for my carbon fiber travel tripod, and it is.  The movement is smooth as silk, and it holds my Nikon D800 with 28-300 lens with no issues.  It also accepts every Arca-style plate I have though it's a close call with the RRS L-bracket.  I have to open it to its absolute widest to get that in there, but it does fit, unlike my old Giottos ballhead.  The other plate I use all the time is my Cotton Carrier tripod adapter and that works fine also. Another review mentioned how every plate used required an adjustment...well that's an issue with every ballhead as every manufacturer makes their plates in slightly different sizes.  Vanguard helpfully provides you with a detailed picture showing the size of the included plate so you can tell if it will work for your application.  So far, I have no complaints with this ballhead..

I was excited to get this product as I travel, go camping and also frequently spend time on my boat.I like it very much, the sound is much better than the cheap folding speakers I had been using. I was quite surprised by how loud the volume got before there was distortion.

I used this with an iPhone 3Gs and it worked perfectly. No pop up about having to put the phone in airplane mode or any interference.

I have an Incipio Silicrylic case on my phone and was able to get it into the dock without too much trouble, which was nice. I hate accessories that require you to remove the case.

The speaker looks good, and comes with a neoprene case to protect it. The case isn't very pretty though. There is an odd, somewhat floppy, attached pouch for the a/c adapter that looks like a bit of an afterthought, but at least it's there.

The only reason I give this 4 stars is the stand. It is thin plastic and swivels out when you press on it. The attachment does not feel terribly robust, and I worry about its durability. Also, the battery cover is behind it and didn't close securely the first time I installed the batteries.

UPDATE: Six months later I am still using this and it's held up fine. I love it. I still wish the flip-out stand was a bit bigger/more robust, it's pretty easy to knock over. But I am very happy with it overall.

Update after a month:(6-2-06) XM setup on this unit was a real pain. I have 2 other XM radios so tried to add this one to my account online. No go, you have to call to activate this. Which means they charge you a $14.99 activation fee. It is $5 less online and sometimes they don't even charge it. Calling XM is an exercise in frustrating voice response menus, which won't let you activate the traffic service anyway. So just cut to the chase and say "Operator" loudly several times at the outset and save yourself some time and aggravation. It took 2 days and 3 calls to get the radio activated and working.

Secondly, do yourself a favor and toss the card about the 3 "free" audible.com ebook downloads. First of all you have to give them your cc info. Then you don't get 3 ebooks. You only get one real ebook. You get one credit and many books are more than one credit! They also "give" you a 30 minute speech by some guy, whoopie doo. So you get 2 downloads. They also don't tell you you have to download their player even to download anything. I figured that out finally after 5 tries. The player has crashed twice, I've heard 5 minutes of audio. If you actually want to transfer the ebooks to the 2730, you need to hook the unit up to the PC, and make sure the pc's connected to the internet. It's all too spywareish for my tastes. I cancelled it immediately but I regret ever signing up for the service.

I am very pleased with the gps. The routing is good and screen is bright and has nice graphics. I did not think I'd like the 3d view but I do, very much. You can add your own points of interest which I have had to do a lot....this area is growing so rapidly that many things are missing from the database. The traffic function of the XM radio is fantastic, unfortunately the coverage is very limited. Only 2 roads in my county have any coverage and it is only a few miles of each.

I love the MP3 player, and the remote is extremely handy. The XM radio is not nearly as full-featured as my old unit. I am used to being able to punch in the channel number, you can't do that on this unit. The other thing I *really* miss is the "favorite song" feature on my old XM radio (where it alerts you if a favorite song is playing on another channel) and that is not available on this unit. The FM transmitter is a lot weaker than my old XM one also, I often have static problems. I do live in the DC area but I had no trouble with the old radio. I really wanted the MP3, traffic and weather features, I just didn't expect the XM radio to be so disappointing.

This item was easy to assemble. Assembly just requires screwing the small poles into the slots on the stand. All you need to do is figure out how much space you need for each device and make sure you make enough slots for all your devices. The only thing I dont like is that there is no way to make sure the poles on each side are even; you just kind of have to eye it. The stand is very sturdy and made of good quality. I currently have my samsung chromebook and my samsung tablet on this stand, and that's really all I need it for. Instructions for this item were really clear and it was easy to setup. All I had to do was remove the plastic strips from the under the ear buds then they pair with the case. Then I turned my bluetooth on and found the item and they paired to my phone without any problem (I have a Samsung Galaxy S10+). I would have given 5 stars but the tap functions dont work so well. You are supposed to tap twice to pause or play music. This usually worked about 3 out of 5 when I tested on both ear buds. I tapped faster and slower to see if that would change the results, but it didnt. When it came to the three taps for previous/next song, the ear buds seemed confused and began pausing and playing the music at times. Again, I couldn't tell if I was tapping too fast or slow. This functions worked about 1-2 times out of 5 tries. The range is great though. I was able to leave my phone on my bed and walk out my front door (about 20 ft away) then outside to my front door and there was no static or insidication that the connection was fading. I just plugged it in and connected my fire stick and it worked. The only problem (and I noticed this with any projector I've used) is that the sound on netflix does not come through--I havent found a resolution for this issue either. The sound quality is good, doesn't sound totally localized like some other devices I've used. The control works well with the item too. I would recommend this item.

Easy to connect. The sound is clear when using to talk on the phone. Range is good as well, can walk about 20-30 feet away and is still connected. These ear buds fit comfortably in my ear; it feels like I dont have anything in. The color is this pretty bubblegum pink, maybe a little darker, but has a metallic tone to it. It was easy to pair with my phone (I hsve a Samsung galaxy s10 plus). They fit perfectly into their case. They come on once you pull them out of the case and turn on when you put them back in. I've been using them for a few weeks now and haven't had to charge them yet. The sound quality is good with both ear buds in, but with one, it's hard to focus on whatever you're listening to.

The top and the ear piece are padded and very comfortable. The ear pieces rotate about 90 degrees, and they can be folded in. There is an audio jack, a mini usb port, a volume increase and decrease button, pause button, noise cancelling activation button, and power button. When you turn it on, it makes a noise and tells you the status of the battery. The headphones are pretty loud; I was able to hear what was playing clearly while holding the headphones in my hand. I've sought a pair of wireless earbuds for a couple years now, both for general use, and for when running/working out. I originally purchased a pair of Blueant Pump earbuds a few years ago. They are completely waterproof, and have over-the-ear hooks designed to keep them firmly attached during vigorous activity. Those buds are very solid overall, but have a couple critical flaws that prompted me to keep searching. My ideal earbuds would have the following characteristics:

* truly wireless
* strong battery life
* in-ear "wings"/arc support, as opposed to employing over the ear hooks (I sometimes wear glasses and also hats which I didn't want competing for space with the ear buds)
* excellent audio (music and phone calls)
* hear through/ambient listening capable

The Blueant pumps lacked the ambient option, and also had a cable connecting the two buds, which prevented me from effectively performing weight lifting exercises while laying down, since the stiff cable would bump against the bench when I laid back, and knock loose the earbuds, breaking the seal in my ear canal.

After exhaustively researching my options, I decided to give the Powerbeats Pro a shot (in spite of the over the ear hooks), as well as these earbuds under review, the Sony WF-SP800N model. I decided against trying out the very popular Jabra Elite Active 75t, due to the shorter battery life relative to the Powerbeats and Sony options.

The Powerbeats Pro are indeed comfortable, and do a great job staying in place. What I learned is that they do not offer listen-through audio, (which I need for situational awareness when running/biking), and the audio when taking phone calls was incredibly scratchy. This was not a Bluetooth connectivity issue, because the phone played streaming Spotify audio just fine, and the cell phone was in my pocket the entire time, so distance was a non-factor. I found that I could manage to wear glasses at the same time as the Powerbeats buds, but it was slightly awkward. Additionally, I noticed some worrisome discussion on Reddit about the long term battery life of the Powerbeats Pro model, and so for those factors (and considering the high cost of this item), I decided against the Powerbeats Pro earbuds.

The Sony earbuds have performed fantastically. Initially I was disappointed because there was an unbelievable amount of wind noise on my first run using them. The fit felt sloppy and I was concerned about them dropping out of my ear. When I got home, I switched the earbud tips for the largest size. That made all the different in the world. The wind was largely sealed out (there is still some), and the music jumped to life. The fit was true, and I had no problem with the earbuds falling out, even when I went out of my way to shake them loose.

Battery life promises to eclipse even the mighty Powerbeats Pro, and the Sony model offers ambient listening. The water resistance looks to be at least the equal of the Powerbeats, and phone call clarity was excellent. All this at a price more than $100 less than the Powerbeats.

I will update this review if my opinion changes significantly as I get more time in with these Sony earbuds. Based on my initial experiences, I strongly recommend them, for both athletic and casual use. They are excellent.

This case cost just under $6 when purchased a few days back. As is my practice when purchasing or accessorizing an expensive item (in this case, the Sony HX20V camera), I did fairly exhaustive research prior to making the purchase. (Other cases on my shortlist were the LowePro Apex 20 and the Lowepro Rezo 30). My main interests were portability and protection. I wanted to be able to store one extra battery along with the camera, inside an efficient case that would allow for belt-carry and had a dual-zipper design to allow for the wrist strap to be used while the camera is inside the case. This case meets all those requirements. The fit is snug but not tight around the camera, and the zippers have protective flaps along the inside edge to protect against scratches on the camera. The front pouch, which has a velcro flap is pretty small, but will accommodate the extra battery. The dual zippers can be closed at the middle of the case with the wrist strap coming out between the heads of the zippers. This facilitates carrying the camera by the wrist strap if desired, while still benefiting from the case's protection in the event of bumps or falls. The padding sewn into the case is firm and seems like an adequate buffer against minor knocks. One feature I really like is how the belt loop works. The belt loop extends from the upper back edge of the case, and snaps in place at the bottom back edge. Instead of being a single piece of material that extends from the top to the bottom of the case, it is an actual loop. The upshot is that you can run your belt through this loop, and leave the bottom connection unsnapped, so the case essentially hangs about two inches below your belt line. I find this to be much more comfortable carrying method than having it flush against my belt, where it would be crumpled against a jacket waistline, or creating a bulge at the belt line. Originally I had planned to order a carabiner in order to achieve this same result, now that will not be necessary. If you are looking to travel light, you will be well served by this case. It is an outstanding value. Note, the approximate dimensions of the camera I have are 4.2 x 2.4 x 1.4 inches.

UPDATE, 2/20/2013: The case has proven its worth already. A couple days ago my wife sitting in the car and carrying the camera on her lap, in its case. When we arrived at our destination, she got up to exit the vehicle, forgetting that the camera was on her lap. The case tumbled to the ground just outside the car. After dropping from a height of about two and a half feet or so onto concrete, there were no ill effects noted.
We have been using these for a few months without any issues. Love them!  Use a netgear wifi on the ocean so not the best connection but still show immediate motion detect and great video and sound.

This has been perfect for letting my wife sleep through the night without disturbances interrupting. They pair easily with multiple devices, sound quality is excellent and noise canceling properties are impressive.

These are excellent for increasing both the range and volume of wireless (and wired) devices. Give your phone stereo sound with real separation and no complex control interface. I have nothing to say about the sound and the easy to use features. My only qualms about this are that I found the earpiece uncomfortable.  It would have been better if they were a little bigger.

I not going to go on and on about it, because I have to say that I was super pleasantly surprised by this headset.  At first it was seriously not what I was expecting I thought it was going to be bigger and bulkier. But I totally love the fact that it’s not. So what I love about it is that it’s not bulky, so it’s easy to not take too much space on my already crowded computer table.  I wish the battery life was a little better, but I’m not going to complain much. The sound is super good for a 32 bucks headset. And the leather on the ear is soft and not irritating at all.  So for the I’m satisfied with this product for the price that I paid.

Well I don't have any complaint. The only reason this mouse is not getting a 5 star with me is the little fact that I found it seriously noisy. I haven't owned a computer/monitor since high school. For the price I am so happy with this purchase. It is super simple and everything I need to get school work done. Easy to use and so loud with clarity! I'm so excited to use this recorder for class.

I was so happy to find these on Amazon. Its always disappointing when companies discontinue your favorite products and such is the case for these headphones. These are honestly some of the best headphones on the market in my opinion. I do not care for the earbuds that you stick in your ears as I do not find them comfortable. Great earphones. I use them like every day. As long as you take care of them and clean them out and stuff, they'll last you a good while. The sound quality is good and I love all the functions it has. Plus, the app that goes with it that you automatically have in a Samsung phone makes it even better. I am a normal person-not a computer geek. This fan was easy to install on my own. Others I bought would connect to my TV set and at times, x object to my neighbors. This one, for the price, has features we all would use. Battery life is great. But, too much bass
Simple. Love all the features. The ability to calibrate sounds is of great benefit.

These are good headphones. I prefer to use headphones to earbuds when I’m at home—just more comfortable but not all headphones are comfortable. These are. Sound is good, hookup is easy and battery life is good. Overall a great investment for me.

Other than USB cables it seems everything needs a battery. This was my first attempt at rechargeable batteries and the only problem I have is that I have so many devices that require batteries that this isn’t enough. They work, recharge quickly. I’m off to get more.

So the sound quality is good, battery life is good but for me the most important point is they are comfortable. I've been through a LOT of ear buds in search of something that I can wear for several hours without my ears starting to hurt and these are them! Charging case doesn't feel very substantial, but since I don't need to charge them every couple of hours I can live with it.

I had a bit of trouble getting this sync’d to my smartphone but once I did, it’s great. Great picture and sound and it’s nice to have a big screen effect from my little phone. After the first setup I didn’t have any more trouble so it may have been me. Great buy.

This is a battery pack for my Dot which makes it totally (within wireless range) portable. It doesn't take up a lot of room but it does eliminate having to find a spot and plug it in when I want to use it. Now I just take it to another area of the house and I can listen to an audiobook or music or just ask important questions that only Alexa can answer. Battery life is decent but the portability is priceless.

With so many electronics and pretty much everything requires some type of power, there are never enough plugs. I like that there is surge suppression so I don’t overload it but there are also usb connections which is very helpful. 2 to 6 is a good expansion and really fits my needs. So far it’s working great and has really been useful.

These took a while for me to feel comfortable and secure with them but once I did, I was sold. Sound is good and they are very easy to wear and feel like they'll stay in place, now that I'm used to them. I really appreciate how good the sound is. A little annoying to try and store but worth the effort.
Sound is good but most importantly, they are comfortable and stay in for a long time without irritating my ears. Easy to wear. Easy to charge and battery life is good. And they do sound good.

I'm not sure what happened to my original Roku remote but it could have been kids playing with it. I was getting frustrated when this showed up and solved all my problems. It works just like the original Roku remove (I have a roku tv) and seamlessly took the place of the broken on. I haven't had any trouble. It does require batteries but that was easy. Removing the aggravation factor -- that was important.

I didn’t even know I needed this but it makes my echo dots portable which is fabulous! Just plug it in and take it with you. Battery life is decent and it works perfectly although the limitation of the dot continue — sound is good but not great but for a portable dot, that isn’t a deal breaker. Self contained and easy to set up and use. Sound is good, the whole thing can be packed up, moved around and carried to another location with easy setup. Footprint is small. Sound is pretty good for what it is but when it’s hooked up to speakers, it’s way better. Great for the price.

I have a number of webcams and this one finally does the job. It has a cover so I feel better when it’s off and the ring light really makes a difference in helping with shadows. Camera quality is decent and it works without any hookup problems. Sound is just okay but I can live with that for now - I’ll probably end up supplementing with an additional microphone but this does the job and it’s all in one so I’m not trying to organize a bunch of different things. It works when I first plugged it in and hasn’t stopped.

I just plug this into my laptop when I need more connections and it works fine. I do use it more than I expected to and I love that it’s lightweight and small but mighty. I never seem to have enough ports for everything when I travel so this little gadget has come in handy. I haven’t use all the ports, there are couple that I just don’t need, but the ones I do, I use frequently and they all work just fine.

It’s taken me a while to get this to where they are comfortable for long term use. I’m not sure I love noise cancelling because I feel like I’m cut off from the world. However, these did pair quickly and easily and the sound is good. Once I got them adjusted to my ears, they stay in and are fairly comfortable. I know I’m not maximizing the benefits by using just one most of the time but it balances my need to be aware of what’s going on around me (and I still get to listen to my tunes or an audiobook - my newest addiction).

At first I knew it would be hard but then I found that I was depending and focusing on the prompter and reading rather than ‘talking’ to the camera. For me it works better if I bullet point my materials rather than trying to read the whole talk (again I found I was reading rather than talking) but with the bullet points I can talk about my material, not miss any points and can do it directly into the camera. Now that it’s working for me, I’m not sure how I managed anything else. It’s easy to set up and now it’s easy to use.

This is a nice starter kit or is suitable for someone who is an active but not professional user. It’s not always easy to setup but it’s not that hard once you figure out what’s happening. It comes complete with everything you need and it’s all in one compact package. Great deal for what you get. Does a good job with video, audio is just okay but workable. Just having everything in one is a step in the right direction.

So far these haven’t taken a dip in the pool but we are using them poolside and waterproof was a safety feature. The sound is good, pairing is painless and the battery life is good. Does what we need/want and I’m happy. Now I can have tunes when we are sitting around the pool.

Never enough hookups for charging. This really helps when we are on a trip - now there are two more plugs. This works well and I’ll probably get another for the other outlet in the car. I remember (fondly) the days when no one NEEDED to charge something. Now everything requires a port and this helps. Cables seem to work fine and color coding is good - saves arguing.

So, I never thought of anything like this but boy has it come in handy. I didn’t have anything like this but did have all my electronics stuff in one place. This cleans up my act, allows me to actually find something when I’m looking for it and gives me a nice grab and go bag for all things that require plugs, etc.

I've got an "extra" computer that is a bit older but still gets some work done. This has helps with the marginal sound quality I was getting. This does a great job of picking up sound but it's a bit awkward in size and shape and isn't the "perfect" solution I was looking for. I'm still using it and will keep on doing so when I'm in a meeting but doing presentation is going to require some rethinking.

All my earbuds require a micro USB and all the cables that come with them are short. This is long enough to be useful and does the job. Pretty durable - I’ll be getting a few more because everything is coming with micro usb now and those annoying short little cables that aren’t easy to work with.

If anyone else has a million kitchen appliances (they wouldn’t make it if I didn’t need it, right?) this is the answer. It replaces the measly two outlets they give you so I can keep everything plugged in (no I don’t use everything at once but it’s nice to have everything already plugged in). The USB ports were an added plus since I’ve recently seen several kitchen items (a candle lighter, my stand for my iPhone and other things) that actually require a usb hookup. I’m getting these for all my outlets!

This was easily enough to install and use. I've had infrequent lags but it may not be the device, it may be my service at the end. The quality of the camera is good unless you are trying to record. Then I tried to record a meeting and the quality of the recording left a lot to be desired. If you are just visiting or even working without trying to record anything this camera is fine. The video camera I had on my computer suddenly stopped working in the middle of a zoom call. I grabbed this, plugged it in and it worked perfectly without any adjustments and picked up right where it left off. I was very pleased, audio and video quality seem good and I like the privacy cover which just flips up and down.

I’ve gotten tired over the years of trying to move cables around and these have solved my problem. I’ve tried many other types of labeling but the size of these is great and I can put one at each end of the cable which speeds up moving things around when necessary. I use them on my computers and on my audio/video equipment. Very nice! Obviously a pain in the rear to set up the first time but they’ll pay for themselves many times over in lack of aggravation.

My laptop (new) just doesn't have decent speakers. This works just fine, doesn't take up a lot of room and gives my external speaker full range. Does what it's supposed to.

I'm in a cramped space and can't easily move around or add extra "stuff" to my computer area. I wish there was a camera cover for my own peace of mind but it's easy enough to turn to the wall. I've been told I sound just fine and I can see a truer picture of myself than I did with my old cam so it's easier to set up and align. Works great. Was easy to set up and easy to use.

With the advent of Covid, everything has gone on-line so I added the webcam to one of my desktop computers. I still prefer to do most things on my laptop or iPad but with everything on-line it’s a must. This works fine, it was plug and play and the quality is adequate for my needs.

I’ve got these scattered all over my life. They are easy to use and extremely handy to have. Since I travel a lot, I’ve got a set just for “on the road” and they really clean up my carry on bag that requires every kind of cable I might need for the rest of my life. I like these better than the ones that come with the cords — they are easier to handle and way easier to spot.

These are pretty noise cancelling which I'm not sure I'm totally in love with. This has been used to replace the cable company's Internet Cable. Good tight connectors and feels like it's going to last forever. In any event is way more sturdy than the cheap cable they gave us when they did the install.

Plugged it in to the usb port. Snapped it on to the top of the monitor and we have video. The technical part of getting the video working (software and users) was harder than getting this working. Delivers a nice picture and sound and was an easy add-on to an older computer now that everyone is zooming.

As my laptops get smaller I find that they have less "stuff" on them. I attached this to my window laptop and it worked just fine. I've also used it on my desktop computer for an additional drive and it too worked fine. If this is what you need, this is a good sturdy piece of equipment that works very easily. Just plug and play (no additional workarounds needed).

We didn't use this for a baby, we had a very ill person staying with us for a couple of weeks and we used it to keep track of him. He was supposed to stay in bed but didn't want to so we set this up so we didn't have to go running every time we heard a sound (now we only ran when he was trying to get up). It made some long nights way more bearable. We hooked it up and set it up without the instructions and at first every little movement was pinging us.  Not quite when he was breathing but we got every twitch. We finally adjusted the setting so that normal movements were okay but "big" movements we were pinged. Once we got  that figured out it worked perfectly. Better than a standard baby monitor because we could hear but we could also see what was happening. Great night vision (it was dark but we could still see) and we had no trouble hooking it up to our wifi. The app went right onto our phones and we were notified when there were changes. If you are using this for a baby, you'll find that it works well and is very easy to use. Highly recommended.

Decent sound and fairly comfortable but I found them to be just a bit heavy and it didn’t feel like the earbuds would stay in with a lot of activity. That said, they are very comfortable, don’t wiggle around and don’t just fall out.  I thought the case was a bit oversized and the whole package was bigger than I like for wireless but as long as I’m not moving around a lot, they stay in, are very wearable and the sound is decent. I’ve got another pair that I wear frequently and compared to those these feel a bit “top heavy” so it may not be a problem for someone else.  I do want to comment that they come encased in a foam holder and it was VERY difficult to get the earbuds out of the foam.

You’ll need to plug these into your phone with the audio jack. This is NOT a lightning connector  and it is NOT wireless but if you can still use earbuds that plug in these fit fine and the sound is decent. I don’t think they are stable enough for a lot of moving around but if you are more or less stable, these will do the trick. Earbuds have enough options and I found them to be very comfortable.

Good product but at highway speeds it is difficult to hear. Possible issue with install but every now and then I can hear static. Overall great unit and very user friendly. Great battery life. Just needs to be a little louder.

Assembly requires lining up threaded holes in the interior pipe with unthreaded holes in larger outer pipe and using the hex wrench to screw the pipes together. Typical but a bit fiddly for me 'ol hands. Also black-on-black hard to see. Better would be a slot in the outer pipe and ready-set bolts sticking out from the inner which slide into the slot and are tightened with a strong wingnut. No fiddly tool needed. Same for the upper connection which is slightly but not fatally out of align likely due to the crimping of the inner pipe which inevitable shortens it by a 1/16th inch or so. As the threaded holes were likely set in prior to crimping, this moves them down a tad versus the outer pipe holes which were punched with a certain alignment that is not there after crimping. Net: slight misalignment not fatal but do not expect the holes to be properly centered. Just push real hard on the top pipe to encourage alignment as best you can. Back speaker support bracket adjusts horizontally and vertically. High enough for my Polks and design permits wires from wire posts to pass through unobstructed. This is a very clever, unique, successful design. So we now have 2 very strong and satisfactory speaker posts. Well worth the money. Might spray white Rustoleum on them to blend with the wall and replace speaker fabric with white available right here on AMZN. Then we would have something truly superb. Net: these posts are very good. Buy them, say we.

Been buying Polk for decades. Never disappointed. Stay with what you know. Why go elsewhere? At this price point anyhow. Sounded good when I was younger and had better high-range hearing. Still sounds great 20 years on. Its the clarity, donch'a know. Running off my old legacy spare Sony STR-695 plus Sony legacy 5-CD carousel changer set up in the bedroom as an auxiliary music source.  Tried others. tried Bluetooth connection. Rejected. Just use wires and figure out a wire route. Under the rug at these low voltages is not gonna kill you. Or get a wire run. Or get an electrician to pull thought the walls. These Polks deserve a proper input. BTW: Classical (meaning Beethoven and the like - NOT movie music) is what I typically play and the Polks do well with this material. Might add a subwoffer if I go crazy but not really needed for classical - I think. We shall see...

with a Sony 5 CD carousel - so I can listen to my huge CD collection. (Yes, later, will burn to disk but for now...), Just plugged it into the headphone out, with an extension to get to where the USB power hub was  (needs power, thought I) and this little gem paired to Bluetooth Headphones and now I have wireless headphones that the then SONY did not have. Next step is to buy shelf speakers because if the cans sound, so will the boxes. We are very pleased. Simple, cheap, effective - what more is there to say, I ask you?

So last thing to check if no sound but VU meters moving and headphones sound OK. Yes, the factory installed speaker wires were pushed too far into the connectors so the insulation prevented metal-to-metal contact. Solution: back out the speaker wires an reinstall. Just trying to be helpful. 2 days later: noted clipping and crackle in the FM radio at peak signal. As pointed out elsewhere, this is a bad FM radio. Occasional click/pop on the CD.

1) No little feet on the back bottom. The keyboard cannot be tilted. Thus when flat, the key lights can be seen underneath the keys, creating a bright, distracting pattern of lines. These disappear if the keyboard is tilted so you can look at it straight, or nearly, on. But given my desk height versus chair height and consequent angle of vision, I am looking at the keyboard from approx a 45 degree sideways angle. Keyboard needs to be tilted to achieve an approx 35 degree angle of vision which would require about 1in feet on the back bottom of the keyboard. I'll have to use a book or something. And even when properly angled, the numeric keypad leaks light along the left edge of the keys. 2) When the F6 and F7 dim/bright keys are set to "Standard Function Keys" per the set up, then the dim/bright function is lost. I need standard F's. Possible solution: Provide dim/bright slider on the back next to the on/off switch. Doubtless the keyboard can be re-mapped as a fix but: How? More later... And now: 3) Waving hands over the keys and light will not turn on! So hit space bar or something and have to wait 1 Mississippi 2 Mississippi then the light grudgingly comes up to 100% bright. Which is not all that bright! All this when powered through USB port. Sigh. And it turns off on a whim. 4) But wait! I'm using this specialty item wrong: not for the desktop but for the lap - literally. When sitting well away from the PC and big monitor, sit back, relax and watch tube video but control with this wireless, lit keyboard which you look directly down upon - as it is in your lap. Problems solved. But not a serious desktop keyboard. I'll keep it for this one use - entertainment.

So the camera position lock fails and the camera flops around like a dead turkey neck. Please, ye assemblers, tighten down the set screw and use a dab of Locktite. Sloppy assembly is like a tire falling off your SUV: Clearly, someone forgot to torque it down. And now the set-screw is lost. And as we urgently needed the camera arm for a Zoom session, this equipment fail was most disappointing. Send me another set-screw in the mail and we shall be friends again (not likely). Or simply send me the specs on the set-screw and I will try to find a replacement - again, not likely.
2021-02-05 Edit: But thanks to the good people at ACE (yes, it is the place) a new set screw was obtained and with my new 2.5mm Wiha 96325 Precision Hex Metric Screwdriver, 2.5 x 60mm $7.45 on Amazon, it was, well, set. Securing the ball (of ball-and-socket) against the thumb screw which together lock the camera mount at the desired angle. So all is good. That I had to put in a bit of time and money for the fix is in the nature of life: What can go wrong will go wrong. So: No hard feelings.

Arrived in sturdy, protective packaging undamaged. Batteries are NOT included and be aware that two different battery sizes are required:  The mouse takes one AA; The keyboard requires two AAA. I had a hard time viewing the battery schematic showing which side went which direction, but that’s partially my older eyes! It IS kinda hard to see because of location, small size, and color! (I got mint green hoping that the mouse will be easier to find when I lose it—-a very frequent occurrence for me!) Enough about that! Honestly it’s only two batteries so how many possible combinations can there be?!? You’ll be able to turn it on then and it will work pretty much like expected—feels solid, crisp key action, stays in position. I’m not someone who spends hardly any time using a keyboard in a professional capacity; I bought the set primarily for the mint green mouse! If you’re a person whose fingers fly over a keyboard like a virtuoso pianist, you probably already have some idea what kind of keyboard you want anyway! For the rest of us, it’ll get the job done and did I mention it’s mint green?

Let me be frank....I was honestly expecting to have a hard time with this. We all have "Screen Protector Installation Gone Wrong" stories by now, and I was totally resigned to another. With two films included in the pack, I figured that improved my odds of getting one on there half decent. I even had an adult beverage to steel my nerves for the ordeal, which is something I generally only do once a year on the Fourth of July. Yeah, I definitely had a few misgivings.

I started by pre-cleaning my screen with an alcohol square to remove any grease. I then watched the video from the link provided on the instructions twice. Then I simply followed their instructions. The installation was flawless--so flawless that I initially thought I had peeled off the entire film protector with the second tab and was back to bare screen. When I examined it with a magnifying glass, I was able to discern the cutouts around the "Home" button and camera. That's how perfect it went.

No sterile containment suit or CDC reverse vacuum seal room necessary. No special powers or ninja skills required. Just follow the instructions PERIOD. Believe me. If I can do this on my bed with a 110 pound pit bull and a cat beside me and get PERFECT results, anyone can! Thank you, amFilm.

I recently came across some tapes that I had kicking around which I really wanted to hear. They were books on tape which they no longer have available in digital format. TAPE

MICROPHONE
The microphone is not bad for a small cheap mic. It works fine for basic recording.

SOUND
This machine is AWESOME! Seriously. I can not believe how loud it is even on halfway volume. There was no buzzing, distortion, or problems at all that I have had in the past with other machines. This one played the tapes beautifully and I had no issues hearing at all.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This machine exceeded my expectations greatly. It not only is easy to use, but the sound quality is fantastic. I am very happy with this tape recorder and will finally be able to use some of the tapes that no longer are available in digital format.

I am always on the lookout for radios to use in an emergency. Having lived through an extended outage during severe weather emergency for several weeks, not having any way to find out what was going on was difficult.

SIZE
This radio is a nice small size. Picture two juice boxes standing next to each other side by side. It fits just about anywhere. If you want to take it on a trip or camping, it has a very small footprint for packing.

CHARGING
Charging this is either micro USB, crank, or solar. I would say solar is more of a way to keep the radio trickle charged. I would not use that as my primary source as it takes a long time.

SOUND
The sound is really really nice. I am shocked at how nice this little unit sounds. It has great bass and midtones without sounding tinny or far away.

FLASHLIGHT
In an emergency having this as a flashlight is handy, although I would not use it unless no other options were there.

CHARGING PHONES?
I have not used it for charging phones. I keep power banks for that.

ALARM CLOCK/CLOCK
This is a great feature if you are camping or if you have to be up at a certain time during a power outage due to expected weather, checking on sump pumps, etc. It works well if you follow the instructions.

SD CARD
This plays music from an SD card and I have to say the sound is great.

CHARGING TIME
This took a few hours to charge up for us. Between 3 and 4.

PERFORMANCE
When running the radio, we got several days. We did not have it full volume, and we only played it a few hours at a time, not continually.

LOW BATTERY LIGHT
This has a low battery light which is a great feature. It helps you not let it run dry in power.

RECEPTION
The reception is excellent for FM, Very good for AM (some stations don't come in as well), and WB is also hit and miss, but still way nicer than most radios of this type that I have had.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is a fantastic little radio. The sound is way nicer than expected and performance is great. Lots of great features make this handy to have.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. This is one of my favorite radios so far. It is really nice to work with and all of the power sources work well.
