If you want a good solid set of headphones to use with phone and music that work well, are in balance, and great for listening. The controls are not as convenient as they could be, which can be frustrating at times.

MY RATING
Four stars. If the control area was set up just a little more conveniently so that you can not accidentally press the wrong buttons all of the time, they would probably be five stars.

When it comes to hands free devices, I am pretty particular about what I need to have handy. I like to have ear pieces like this handy when I am shopping or out doing errands should I need to receive important business calls. I also have to be available due to health issues of family members. Let's see how this one measures up.

WHAT IS THIS EARPIECE LIKE?
This hands-free earpiece is black. That does make it harder to find in a pocket of a purse or carry case. The outside of the entire unit is black.

LIGHTS
There is a green battery light on the outside and a blue bluetooth light on the outside when you turn it on. When you turn it off, the battery light turns to red so you know that is what you are doing with it. I LOVE this feature.

EAR BUD
The ear bud is only one size. There are three ear covers in this set. Two of them have an ear circle in them which allows you to wear it with or without the ear loop that hooks over the entire ear. One of them has no ear circle (the kind that fits into your hear cartilage).

EAR HOOK
There is one ear hook connected to this ear piece and then there is an extra in case you break that one. This fits around the outside of the ear hooking it into place for added security.

Mini USB
The charging plug on the outside is pretty uniform.

CORD
It comes with a 12 inch cord that goes from USB to mini USB for charging. You will need to have a receptacle to plug that into.

INSTRUCTION BOOKLET
Instruction book is minimal. This is a basic set which I LOVE. It is pretty straight forward. You turn on the phone, turn on the ear piece and they pair. Then to turn up volume, you press one side of the bar, down is the other side and muting is both at once. To hang up press outiside of earpiece.

BATTERY TIME
This thing stays charged a LONG time. I rarely have to recharge it, although I do not use it daily. It also holds a charge when not used for a long time as long as it it not left on endlessly.

RECEPTION/MICROPHONE
Here is where my review gets difficult. The first few times I used this, the caller at the other end complained because the sound was so bad. I was even told that the old handsfree speaker in my car was better and that was like a tin echo chamber.

I was all set to write my review, after all, it was pretty cut and dried. Then for some reason I could not write my review, and I had to use the earpiece to call someone again. WOW, the comments:

"I am so glad you are not using your ear piece, that thing was awful. Your voice has never sounded so clear."

"WOW, your phone is so CLEAR. I can not hear anything around you. Where ARE you?"

That second comment, I was shopping in a loud area. Now I had a dilemma. It was like I had two different earpieces! People were commenting on how wonderful it was now, but previously, these SAME PEOPLE could not stand it before. Nothing had changed. Same phone, same earpiece, same people.

So, I tested this quite a bit and the more positive feedback outweighed the negative, so I will say that this is a fantastic OMG marvelous earpiece sometimes and other times it is not as good.

STREAMING MUSIC
This is a decent earpiece for streaming music or programming on the phone, but I tend to use it more for temporary phone answering when I am not in my car.

COMFORT
This is not as comfortable as other earpieces I have had. I still prefer my older plantronics ear piece as it is so comfortable I don't notice it is in my ear after a while. This one is a bit too large. I actually prefer to wear it without the rubber cushion on it if I have to use it for any length of time. The ear hook helps it stay on pretty well. Once in a while I will use the rubber cushion and it is not too bad.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is a solid performer as a hands free earpiece. It has potential to deliver fantastic phone calls much of the time, and once in a while not as nice, but it still works. For comfort, I have had better, but this is not too bad. It has extra pieces which I love, and the colored lights on it are fantastic.

MY RATING
FOUR STARS. This is a nice solid hands free ear piece. Despite a period of time when I was not so sure, longer term testing brought out its good points and solid performance. I would get this again.

My husband has a lot of use for communication on jobs he has to do in the contracting world. We have had some jobs here at the house which required walkie talkie communication. Let's see how these performed.

WHAT ARE THESE LIKE?
HOW ARE THEY BUILT?
These walkie talkies are tough. They come with the batteries outside of the units, so you have to put them in.

HOW TO PUT BATTERIES IN
You will need a very pointed screwdriver or a small Phillips head screw driver to get the battery cover off. When you screw it back in, it is pretty sturdy.

HOW TO TURN IT ON
The on button on the top is large and easy to cold, dirty, or gloved hands to turn on and off. You can also adjust volume.

CASE?
The case snaps on and off of the units. They stay hooked to the clothes pretty well as long as you are not moving around a lot. In that case, we found them most useful to hold the walkies in the pockets with the clip.

CLARITY OF SOUND?
The clarity of sound was superb. We were doing roof work on the top of a third story and they worked great. We also had to do work about 100 ft away from the point of origin of a wiring job, so we needed that for communication to test the connections. Again, they worked great. Very clear and worked very well.

TOUGH?
These have been dropped a few times and worked very well.

RECHARGING?
The recharging unit has a place for both walkies to be charged. The plug is separate from the base that you charge in. Each receptacle has a red light on it to let you know that the walkie is charging. The plug is small so you can use it on a power strip or in the wall outlet without blocking other outlets. Recharging is fast- within the hour- and they seem to last quite a while before needing to be recharged.

CLIPS
The clips have to be removed prior to charging.

CHANNELS
The different channels we used all worked well. We did not have to use them in a very busy area with multiple walkies, however, so we did not get to test it with a lot of walkie talkie traffic happening on a huge job site.

THE BOTTOM LINE
For a very sturdy set of walkie talkies which charge up quickly and last a long time, these are fantastic for contract work and any jobs that we have had to do. My husband plans to take them to his jobs as well when needed. They have a decent range to them and are easy to operate even with gloves on.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. We really love these walkie-talkies. They have been fantastic so far for all of the jobs we have had to use them for. I will update if we have anything valuable to add in the future as we continue to use them over time.

I have had the chance to try out and use a wide variety of headphones over the years. My family has a thing for headphones, ear buds, bluetooth speakers. Someone is ALWAYS trying out a new type or brand so I have a pretty good idea what I enjoy and like. I have had the opportunity to use several high end headphones such as Turtle Beach (and others) as well as lower end gamer head phones, or computer headphones with mics on them. I have been able to test out wireless and wired as well. Let's see how these measured up.

WHAT ARE THESE LIKE?
These head phones come in a REALLY nice presentation box. There is a set of headphones of course, nestled in a nice flocked mold. There are two ribbon loops on each side so you can lift that out. Underneath are three very nicely folded black paper boxes, reminiscent of origami. Inside there are cords for recharging, plugging into jacks where there is not USB for corded listening, adapter with double plug in it, and instruction manual.

COMFORTABLE?
These headphones are one of the few headphones that I can wear for quite a while and not get a headache. They fit really nicely on the ears, the top is not too much pressure on the top of my head, and they do stay in place reasonably anyway.

HOW DO THESE HEADPHONES PERFORM?
The instruction book does give the basics for these headphones. I have to be honest with you, they are not user friendly. If I don't use them for a bit, I tend to forget which switch is which for what and have to read the booklet quickly again to remember. They are not well marked for those who are not used to the high end head phones it might be a bit of a learning curve. For those who are used to headphones of this type, it probably won't be that difficult to remember.

LISTENING
WOW- I have to say these are definitely NOISE canceling. They work beautifully. As for the sound- it is impeccable for me. I have tried these with direct jack and wireless and both are really beautiful soundwise. Let me put it this way- my family takes these and runs with them and I have to fight to get them back. We have a LOT of headphones to choose from and these are most popular. The sound is beautifully balanced and 3D. I can still hear what I need to hear around me if I have to. I choose to listen on noise canceling settings most of the time as I love it.

PAUSE
The pause feature is wonderful except if I have to adjust the headphones- it will pause at times when I don't take them off and only adjust them. Not a deal breaker. I love that if someone wants my attention, I can put the headphones down, pick them up and continue to listen. This carries over to YouTube on my tablet- not just general listening. I also love that if I really like a song and want to share it with my husband, I can put the headphones down, he pick them up and they continue to play at that point.

APP
I did not like the app. I had a lot of problems with it and just stopped using it. I prefer just to use them as they are.

INSTRUCTIONS
The quick start menu is all pictoral. It might be a bit difficult for some people to understand, but if you take your time and really study the illustrations, it should make sense to you. I found that only one of us had a difficult time understanding what the pictures meant (not me, btw).

CHARGING
I usually get about four or five hours out of these, but that includes putting them down here and there and then putting them back on again, so continuous listening with no break could be shorter.

RECHARGING TIME
I had a full charging time of anywhere from an hour to an hour and a half. I can not explain why- although I have tried to observe any differences- I just don't know.

PROBLEM
I could not get these to pair at all with my Roku or Television (samsung series 6 UHD Smart TV) no matter how hard I tried. Not sure why, but I have other headphones and devices pair with no problem with either of these.

THE BOTTOM LINE
The absolutely best headphones I have to date. I love to use them with my tablet, MP3 player (jack), and computer. I don't keep a lot of music on my phones so I tend to go to my tablet for that. I also listen to YouTube with these on and the pause feature works well on any of these devices. I wish I could get it to connect to my TV or Roku, but it is not that big of a deal. My whole family fights over these.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS for these headphones. They are comfortable, do not sweat or give headaches, and the sound is just the way I love it.

UPDATES
If I have forgotten to mention anything that you want to know, or I find out anything additional to add, I will update this review.

One thing we have a lot of use for in this household is Bluetooth headphones. Whether it is for work, keeping privacy in the house, using with phones, exercising, running, walking, or other uses, everyone in the house goes through headphones. I was very interesting in these especially for exercising as it is hard to find a good pair that stay in.

WHAT ARE THESE LIKE?
These earphones are meant to be used for activities that are rather intense- hence exercising, moving around, etc. These earphones come with a short USB cord for recharging and a few sizes of gel type fittings for different sizes of ear canals.

HOW ARE THESE TO USE?
They hold a charge for six to eight hours depending on how intense the listening time is and if it is consecutive or not. The controls are easy to use on the right ear wire. It does not tell you who is calling, but it does ring in the ear. Answering was easy and the call went through well with decent volume. They do stay in the ears quite well for more intense activity. Once in a while I might knock one out if I am intensely exercising, but most of the time they have been good.

SOUND?
The sound is good, but tends a little toward the flat side compared to other earbuds I have used. We have found that breaking them in by using a lot has helped them to sound better than they did at first, so they are really not bad.

COMFORT?
That is where the stars come off. Yes, they stay in the ears, but after wearing about an hour or so, they really begin to hurt. It is not the size of the cushions, but the hard plastic under them that presses against the ears. Two of us have tried them out and it does it for both of us.

WHAT ARE THESE BEST FOR?
These seem to be the best for exercising, running, walking, or an activity that is limited to an hour or so. They are good as far as sweat and water resistance goes. Recharging time is pretty good it can take from one to two hours to fully charge, depending on the day.

THE BOTTOM LINE
For really cool looking earbuds that stay in the ears during more intense activity, these are a good choice. Any time over an hour, however can be uncomfortable. Music playback is good, but not overly dimensional if that is something you are concerned with. We like them for exercising, walking, or running.

MY RATING
Four stars for these, due to lack of dimension in sound and discomfort after wearing a while.

WARNING- This is an in depth review for those who are seriously shopping around for a GOOD projector. IF you prefer a short summary, see section titled THE BOTTOM LINE
---------------------------------
We have an appreciation for electronic gadgets and aids in my family. When I had the opportunity to get a new projector, the reaction was nothing short of ecstatic, and for good reason. Our kids are heavily involved with using projectors at a local church that shows movies every month. It is quite a nice event and our son in particular is very particular when it comes to running projectors or other devices. He will go on for quite some time about how it works, features, and what he thinks of it, even when the listeners have long checked their ears out of commission.

This projector has created a rise out of our kids that I have never heard to this degree. This projector, in short is AWESOME!

WHAT IS THIS PROJECTOR LIKE?

IN THE BOX
Projector
Remote control
2 AA batteries
Power cord (3 prong plug, cord about 5 ft long)
USB cable with USB male end and USB A end
CRT cable (for PC monitor, about 5 ft long give or take a few inches)
Wireless LAN module (to make the projector wireless capable)
Quick Set Up Guide
CD for links to projector manual and software (you can register from this CD too)
Case (has shoulder strap with pocket with secure strap for projector and separate pocket for accessories and cords)

PLUGS IN BACK OF PROJECTOR
This projector comes with the following plug ins at the back of the projector:
USB A port (for the WiFi module)
USB port (for computer)
CRT port (for monitor)
RCA plug-ins (for yellow, white, and red plugs)

2 volume buttons (one goes up and one goes down, doubles and left and right navigation buttons for menu)

THE SET UP THIS WAS USED WITH
Playstation 3 through HDMI, full 1080p, projecting on a 5' x 9' screen in a church sanctuary with very high vaulted ceilings.
Watched Bluray movie (Machine Gun Preacher was the last movie they watched) , tested with couple of games. Sound was accessed through a stereo and not this unit using fiber optical cable.

Also tried with desktop using Windows 7

HOW DID IT RUN
Ran very smooth. Picture was absolutely gorgeous, way better than the theater. Initially the picture looks decent. After tweaking in comparison with a Samsung Touch of Color LCD deep color, we were able to make it look even much better than the TV which has a fantastic picture with very dark blacks and fantastic color.

The effect on the picture was amazing. The picture not only was brighter, but it looked way more 3D if that makes sense. The depth of color, definition and contrast gave a depth to the projection that surpassed the TV on the exact same picture/video. The following adjustments were used to achieve this:

DIFFERENT OPTIONS TO ADJUST PICTURE QUALITY

COLOR MODE
There are five different presets. PRESENTATION, DYNAMIC, CINEMA, sRGB, BLACK BOARD (automatically adjusts for chalkboards that are green)

BRIGHTNESS

CONTRAST
Big range for contrast which gives a lot of options for adjustment

COLOR SATURATION
This you can really control how much saturation of color you want to a very fine detail- something that is extremely important to our son who is very color sensitive.

TINT
This one was a struggle- there did not seem to be much different from one end of the spectrum to the other. Very little difference. Not sure what it was supposed to control at this point, but will update if we figure it out.

SHARPNESS
COLOR TEMP

RESOLUTION
The native resolution of this is 1920 by 1200.

COLOR BRIGHTNESS AND WHITE BRIGHTNESS
3400 lumens
(Very bright even in a bright room. Excellent visibility)

WHAT PROCESS DOES THIS WORK ON?
3LCD 3 chip technology. This gives a brighter picture and very detailed deeply color picture. Excellent black depth as well.

COMMENTS
Previous to this projector, we had been using the EX5200 series from Epson. It had 2800 lumens with the 3LCD technology. Compared to this projector, it was nothing near the high quality of this one. This one is hands down PHENOMENAL and so impressive that it has been the talk of the movie time ever since first viewing it. Both projectors could handle 1080p, but not only is this one brighter, the color depth and fine details of the picture are more clear and crisp. With this projector the fine tune ability is far better than the other which was very limited in what you could do to change the quality or picture.

AUTO PICTURE SELF ADJUSTMENT
This also has an auto picture self adjustment which means that even if the unit is a little crooked, it will adjust the picture to make it level and look straight- one of the more impressive features of this unit.

THE BOTTOM LINE
For a great picture that beats out any of the theaters that we have been to, this projector is fantastic. With a lot of options for sourcing, and for using with different devices, the capability for adjustments and alterations makes this one of the most impressive projectors we have seen at this point. The color saturation and depth is unbelievable. The extra features and ability to do a lot of adjustments make this one of the best in its class at this point.

MY RATING
Five stars would be ten if possible. We have not had the opportunity to try it out with a lot of different devices but will update with any further experiences with other devices in the future.

It is harder and harder to find any radio that has an AM radio band on it, let alone a really good one. It is also rather difficult to find a decent radio that is not digitally tuned and controlled. This radio is a good solid radio with both of the above features on it.

WHAT IS THIS RADIO LIKE?
This radio is a good solid radio. It has a slide switch under the tuning bar which has three settings - OFF, AM, and FM. On the right side are two dials. There is one with volume that goes from Minimum to Maximum. The other dial is the tuning dial. That makes the tuning bar slide up and down for both AM and FM. There is a handle on top that flips up or goes down. There is a pull out telescopic antenna on the top for better reception. There is a place in the left side where you plug in the electric cord, but you can remove it if you prefer to operate solely by batteries. The cord is a little over 5 feet long. The plug is a two pronged plug and is polarized. There is a door on the back which slides off and allows you to put in 3 AA batteries. The door has attached hinges so you don't have to worry about losing the battery door off of the unit unless it breaks.

HOW DOES THIS RADIO PERFORM?
For AM I would say that it has okay reception It is not WOW but it is not terrible either. Since AM is not really dominating the airwaves anymore, I imagine that some people would not find this to be a problem. If you want really strong AM reception, this is okay, but you might be able to find better.

For FM reception, the radio is great. It pulls in quite a few stations and also plays them very clearly. The speaker is best showcased by FM. It is a full sound and impressive considering the size of the speaker and the basic nature of the radio. I found that it is a nice sound and enjoyable.

HANDLE
The handle has a bit of a recoil to help it snap back into place, but it does seem just a little bit flimsy to me. I wish it was just a bit sturdier. It is not enough to take off a star.

WHAT WOULD THIS RADIO COME IN HANDY FOR?
For those of you who are from the era where radios of this nature were commonplace, I am not writing this comment section for you. You already know what this would be good for. For those of you who think that In Tune, or other internet radio stations would suffice for any AM or FM radio stations, I would like to mention that during weather crises, that AM/FM and shortwave radio tend to be the only reception you can get if any. That includes disasters. At that point, internet is not an option, so it is important to have a back up communication capability to keep up on what is going on and any emergency information that might come up, or even information about upcoming help.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This radio is handy. It is a decent size, sturdy, and a solid basic radio. It gets decent reception and has a nice speaker which is especially nice for FM. During emergencies and times of crises, this is a good backup to have should internet not be an option. Running on both electricity and AA batteries, this would be a great addition to your basic emergency kit.

MY RATING
Despite the handle being a bit flimsier than I would like, it is still decent and a solid radio. I do not think that it is worth taking off a star.

(WARNING- This is an in depth review of this laptop. My goal is to help those who are truly interested in making informed buying decisions. This is done from an experiential point of view of most consumers and not highly technical. If you prefer a shorter summary, see paragraph titled, THE BOTTOM LINE)

WHAT IS THIS LAPTOP LIKE?
I have had a lot of different tablets, laptops, desktops, and have built my own systems over the years. One thing I have not had is a hybrid laptop which changes from tablet to laptop and back again. I was not too fond of a 15 inch size as I tend to like smaller laptops, but I was willing to try. I am SO glad I did.

COVERING/CASE OF LAPTOP
This laptop is a thin profile, but feels very substantial. The bottom does not have tiny little rubber feet like some HP professional laptops I have had, but it has solid large rubberized pads that are 1 inch by a half inch. There are a decent amount of vents in the bottom as well. The top is a slightly textured metallic top (etched look) and not shiny. The hinges are very strong and hold the screen in a variety of directions solidly. They do not budge until I move them again.

SIZE
I am amazed that this is the first 15 inch laptop that I actually enjoy using! The size and way that it works makes it fantastic for me. I can tilt the screen in any direction and use my hands on the screen or keyboard in laptop mode which is a pleasure.

KEYBOARD
The keyboard is soft touch and rubberized key-wise. As soon as I touch the keys, a back light comes up so that I can see what I am doing. The back light goes out in 15 seconds or so when the keys are not being pressed. There is a full numerical keyboard and plenty of room between keys for my medium sized fingertips. It is also spaced well for those who have longer nails.

SCREEN
The screen is shiny. It doubles as a screen as well as touchscreen. The view on the screen is fabulous as it has a full HD 1080 resolution. The colors are not as intense as the Saumsung Galaxy Tab S2, which is one of the most amazing color screens I have worked with. Since I am a person who likes color, I like color intensity in my screens. However, this screen is fine and is by no means pale, it is just not quite as intense as I am used to.

TOUCHSCREEN
When you flip the keyboard back, the touchscreen clicks into place. You are given the option to choose the touchscreen if you want so there are no mistakes. As a tablet, I have found that it is very accurate and works quite well. I have put it through a lot and so far, I have only had a few instances where I was frustrated for a second, but it was easy to correct.

OPERATION
This turns on so fast it is almost jolting. My laptops, though usually professional level, often take quite a bit to boot up. This one, however is so quick it always surprises everyone here.

As for operations, I have found this to be a very fast and easy to use system. Load up is quick and the only problems I have from time to time are due to wireless and not really the fault of the laptop.

Turning it off sometimes makes me laugh out loud. Press button. BAM! It’s off.

WINDOWS 10
I am not a fan of Windows 10. But unfortunately that is pretty much the choice for any laptop at this point. This laptop seems to handle it very well.

GAMES
Because Windows 10 is not as game friendly as previous operating systems, I have not had the time to mess around with games with this. I have avoided Windows 10 until now, so I have not figured out what if any games will work with this. I will update when I do.

RUN TIME
Charging seems to take only a few hours for a full charge. The run time varies between 3 and 5 hours depending on what I am doing. I will say this- I rarely run it into the ground in one sitting, which makes it very helpful for me.

VIDEO
Runs very smooth on here. Using a DVD player means I have to use the USB port to run my independent unit and be in a stable position to do so. Works well. Beautiful to watch.

USB PORTS AND SD READER
I have found the USB ports to work very well. No problems to this point. Load up is fast. Using the SD reader is also a pleasure. The photos load up fast and due to the high resolution screen viewing them is really detailed and helpful. I have not installed professional graphics software yet to test this system for photo editing.

TOUCH PAD (AND FRUSTRATION)
The touch pad on this laptop is a bit challenging to use. There is a finger reader which I do not use, but the buttons are hidden in the pad itself and not two different buttons. The pad is pretty accurate as far as tracking. The only problem I have is location. When I rest my left hand on the rest area, sometimes it interferes with the touch pad and causes things to go a bit crazy at times. I am not pressing ON the touch pad, just in the area next to it.

SOUND
The sound is not tinny or awful. I find that it is sufficient for most of the applications I want to use it for. If I prefer to have a better sound, I use my Soundbot speaker and that gives me even better sound for movies and videos.

COMMENTS
I have to say that although the touch pad situation does frustrate me now and then, I do love this laptop. I have always wanted a hybrid because since I started using tablets, I would always catch myself touching the screen when I was using one of the household laptops and it was frustrating.

This unit is really nice. It is so fast and easy to use, it surprises me, honestly. It is so easy to switch between tablet and laptop modes and I find it a pleasure to work with for photos and movies.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This hybrid is VERY fast, easy to use, and boots up and shuts down so fast it is startling. The screen is a pleasure to look at, although not as color saturated as Samsung can be. So far, USB and SD works great. Sound is good enough for most applications. This is easy to use and not at all cumbersome. I love that I can touch the screen even in laptop mode if I am frustrated with the touch pad. I am very happy with this laptop/tablet hybrid.

RATING
FIVE STARS! I will update if I have anything else to add in the future, but at this point, I am very happy with this.

I have been building computer systems and troubleshooting for a long time. I really enjoy taking parts in and out and programming systems to do what I want. I remember looking at a commercial for the new tablets and saying to my family- "What the heck would anyone want one of THOSE things for?" The Acer was a fantastic little first tablet. It performed as well or better than a few Samsungs and older Apples that we had the chance to put it up against, and for the price, it was a great little tablet. I found some use for it and found myself reaching for the tablet when I didn't want to do work at the computer. It was more portable than a laptop and easier to do quick surfing and simple tasks on, and GAMING.

I thought that all was well until I began to have a few issues with the Acer. It was at that point that I saw a great price on the new Samsung Galaxy Tab S2. I was hooked.

WHAT IS THIS TABLET LIKE?
I plan to write this review to people who are not as interested in the detailed specs of this unit, but instead I will write this for an average user who might not be as technically astute. There are quite a few well done reviews that have lots of specs and details that will satisfy those who really need that information to make decisions.

SCREEN
One of the things that I did not like about the older Samsungs was the size. I preferred the more squared screen of the Acer than the Samsungs I had worked on. My daughter has one and although it seems nice, I just was not keen on the screen. This model has exactly what I wanted to have. The shape makes it easier to work on the web , use as an E reader, and play games. I find it easier to read than more elongated screens.

One of the things that I found to be frustrating is the slick surface of the screen. For web surfing or book reading it is fine, but games can really get frustrating as I find the screen to be very sensitive and it is easy to mess up.

As for the brightness, it is very bright. I have it turned down by about 75% and it is plenty bright enough most of the time. Also, the color contrast is breathtaking. The screen is very sharp and the blacks are BLACK and the colors are very saturated. This thing is eye candy squared! It is hard to look at other screens when I am done using this.

COLOR
This is not really gold in color. I would say it is gold tinged platinum in color. Do not expect a bold gold.

SMOOTHNESS AND UNEVEN EDGES
There are a few things which bug me about this tablet, but not that much. Getting a good case from Fintie took care of it. The button on the bottom of the vertical positioned screen stands out from the unit. That means if you are going to get a keyboard in the case, it could press on the button and cause problems. The Fintie case is raised enough to protect the button.

There is also the camera lens on the back that sticks out quite a bit. Again, the case takes care of that problem. The back itself might be plastic, but it feels like metal and looks like metal so it is not cheap looking.

SPEED AND FUNCTION
WOW is this thing FAST! I have to say that it really has blown me out of the water with the speed and smooth operation of everything I have tried to do. It works smoothly, load up is fast. I know part of that might be due to the inclusion of Lollipop but also the hardware and set up. I have not found it to lag at all. Great performance. I also know that this model is scheduled for the Marshmallow upgrade sometime this year which could change performance to be even better.

I have 32G microSD card in this right now but it is expandable to 128.

BATTERY LIFE
I was very concerned about all of the complaints about battery life. I was so concerned I almost didn't get this tablet. I am SO glad I did, however. I keep location turned off and bluetooth as well unless I am using it. The battery stuns me with how long it has lasted. I loaded that baby up to 100% last night and this morning about 11 AM I began to work intensely on the tablet, trying to back up files from my Acer and transfer them over to the Samsung via bluetooth. That means that the bluetooth was on all day, I was downloading and installing all day long. I have to say that I am shocked. It is about 12 hours later and there is still over 50% battery left. I had to recharge my Acer once during all of this time.

So, compared to what I am used to (which is about 2-4 hours of work on a tablet before recharging, including no location turned on) this tablet is dreamy for me. The battery is way beyond what I am used to with the Acer, so I am very happy.

THE BOTTOM LINE
I will update as I find things to tell you about, but I wanted to start off with the basics as that is what I was looking for when I was trying to decide if I should get this tablet or not. I still do not find tablets to be useful for all of my work, but they are great for smaller web surfing, quick look ups, apps for certain things and of course games and skype. As for the keyboard and typing, it is not really practical at least for me to use this for heavier loads of work- desktop or laptop are best suited for that.

Is it worth the price? At $300 it is a very powerful device with a screen that blows anything else I have seen out of the water. The colors are a feast for the eyes, the clarity is crisp, and the smooth operation is delightful. If you really enjoy having a tablet you can depend on, I would say that this fits the bill.

Could you do with something less expensive? Yes. But you might have more frustration with that lower price tag. The set up of this tablet is easy to work with, great operation and having two windows open at the same time is delightful. I am very happy with this and despite my misgivings after reading so many reviews with disappointment in them I can say at this point, I am very very glad that I went ahead and got it. It is a really great tablet.

Please check in with this review as I plan to expand it greatly as we continue to explore the uses of this fabulous action cam Live View remote kit. We have been working with this kit as much as we can, but the weather has been horrible so we have been limited on the action filming we can do with it. I plan to update this review very often in the next month or two as we experiment with the different uses of this camera set with more detail of our experiences.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
The set comes with the camera which looks very small- smaller than a pack of cigarettes. There is a waterproof case as well as mounts, a wrist screen to monitor and control what you are filming because you won't be able to look through the camera window on the camera itself. This is designed to use the wrist screen for use. It is not like a traditional video cam that you look through the screen on the camera as you film. I am using a microSD card that is 64GB with this camera.

DOCUMENTATION AND LEARNING CURVE
The documentation was a bit challenging for me to wade through. It was printed on what looked like recycled paper that is very cheap and not sturdy. It came in a bunch of different pamphlet forms and other languages too. I found that this camera was a bit challenging to learn at first. If you are a hands on type of person who tends to jump right into things without reading directions well, you might find a bit of a learning curve with this set. It is not like a traditional video camera. It has a few different ways of doing things that I found challenging at first to learn how to operate. My kids (the techie fanatics of the house) also had a bit of a challenge to operate it at first, so it was not just me.

WATERPROOF CASE
The waterproof case is easy to get on and off of the camera. It makes it so that you can film in the rain or the presence of water without any worries. The enter and hold button is rigged so it operates through the camera case as well as it does on the actual camera. The previous and next buttons also work well from the waterproof case as they do on the actual camera.

LIVE VIEW REMOTE (WRIST BAND)
The live view remote as a great picture on it. It is pretty easy to see despite it being very small, it is sharp and decent enough so you can direct the filming to where you want it to happen. The camera is controlled from the live remote so that you don't have to be near the camera to make it work. That means you can use it on your car, helmet, or bike, etc. The wrist band works well but has to be recharged via mini-usb connection that you can get with the cord that came with the unit.

CAMERA
The camera was a bit of a challenge to work at first. The screen has to be rotated through various settings quite a bit at first to get the idea of how it works. It is black and white and quite basic in nature. You can use the camera without the wrist band, but it seems to work best together. You need to have the camera recharged via the USB to mini usb connector cord that comes with the set. I have not had the camera run down yet so I can not comment on the recharge time.

FILM QUALITY
This is where I was truly amazed. I was not expecting this camera to be too great, but I was so WRONG. The quality of the video we got is fabulous. VERY high quality HD video and sound for the size camera it is AND used in the waterproof case that we have had to use constantly due to rain we have had ever since we got this set! We did notice that the sound on the recordings is exceptional too. It picked up birds singing, all kinds of sounds around but at times footsteps were magnified heavily too.

MOUNTING
The mount can be transferred from one place to another in various applications. There are clips, bands, and all sorts of mounts you can use which will allow you to use on helmets with air holes, helmets that are solid, and in a variety of ways. It is very versatile. We also have some car mounts that weather permitting we can test out as well and I will update with results.

WHAT WE HAVE USED THIS FOR SO FAR
So far we have had our daughter strap it on her bike helmet and take it for a ride in the rain, but she could not go far due to the rain being too strong. We have tested it on a helmet walking around the yard and running. We have used it to film fish outside a tank, and a variety of settings outside, but have not been able to test it in a very fast moving nature yet.

EDITING SOFTWARE
So far it has been pretty easy to use and view the videos from the software. I went online

WHAT WE LIKE
-filming through waterproof case is fantastically clear
-clarity of camera is excellent
-mic is very good- almost too good. Picks up tons of sound(including footsteps which sound rather loud)
-extra gear is fantastic so you can slip the mount in and out easily so you can transfer from one place to another easily
-wristband is comfortable with great picture and is easy to use when you can not reach the camera
-can still use the camera without the wristband although not quite as nicely as with the camera only
-editing software is intuitive and easy to use with a small learning curve

WHAT WE DON'T LIKE
-learning curve at first is a bit bigger than expected
-wristband can get hot
-instructions can be confusing if you are not a highly technical person
-mic can pick up footsteps or other background noises loudly
-enter button on the camera is sensitive so if I drop it in a bag, it will turn on even inside the case
-putting camera on the side of helmet can get a bit heavy which might bother some
-paperwork is cheap and in too many pieces. I prefer a good solid manual that you don't have to go online to get

THE BOTTOM LINE
Due to weather, we have not been able to film in as much variety of high action as we plan to do. As it is right now, we have used it in mildly active circumstances and in a lot of rain. The film quality is AMAZING and the sound is also very good. The online videos and instructions do help some to understand how to use it and what to do with it. This camera can switch between video, loops, and photos- all of which can be controlled through the live remote wristband. If you are a video fanatic, you have a lot of possibilities with this camera set. If you are a dabbler who wants to have some fun, I still think you can have a lot of use for this set. This camera has a lot of possibilities and we plan to continue to explore them as our horrible weather lightens up and we can get back out and do some fun videos. Hopefully I can upload something to show you the amazing quality of this camera.

I highly recommend this action cam and Live View Remote kit. The quality is excellent and it has a lot of fabulous possibilities to journal trips, capture action accomplishments on film and find new ways to document action and interesting video. The size and mounts make it possible to do MANY different things and I can see years of fun with this set.

As I said in the beginning, I will be updating and streamlining this review as I continue to learn and use this camera set. My entire family is really excited about this and we are all enjoying having it. There has even been talk of strapping it to the kitty to see where he goes all day.

This review is going to be a bit difficult to write in that there is SO much to say about this system that different people might be interested in knowing about. I will attempt to be as brief, yet well rounded in my review as I can due to space constraints.

WHAT IS THE ALIEN ALPHA CONSOLE (7980)?
In essence, what this unit is, is a complete Windows 8.1 PC unit with the ability to boot directly into Valve's Big Picture console interface of the Steam accounts immediately, or boot directly into Windows. No matter what, you have to be online to be able to the Steam Console because of the fact that in order to access your account, you have to be able to log in.

In order to log in, you have to be online. Big Picture mode can also be accessed through Windows. By pressing the icon for Steam on the desktop (which will take you directly into your Steam account) you can also access the Big Picture console interface by pressing the controller symbol in the top right corner of the window.

This console comes with Windows 8.1 which is a challenge in itself as the operating system has a lot of quirks and frustrations that come along with it no matter WHAT hardware it operates on. There is a bit of a learning curve with Windows 8.1 but it is worth taking the time to work with it, if you have never used it before.

The machine itself is very small- smaller than a PS3 unit. It has a cool alien head on the front of the machine that changes colors during different operations. You hook it up into your sound system through HDMI or Digital Optical Link, or into TV directly using HDMI.

The power cord is in two parts- it is 68 inches from the console to the AC adapter and 32 inches from the adapter to the plug. It also comes with a 6ft HDMI cable.

There is an HDMI IN so you can input HDMI sources to pass through this unit into your TV.

WHAT CAN YOU DO WITH THE ALIEN ALPHA CONSOLE?
This machine is set up with the gamer in mind. It is very powerful and does play some of the highest demanding games on the market right now without any trouble. It is also set up with the console gamer in mind, specifically the Xbox crowd as it comes with a wireless Xbox 360 controller (which is already set up to work in Windows).

Many Playstation gamers as well as others are not fond of this controller. We did manage to set up a Playstation 3 controller using the Motion Joy and Pinnacle Profiler method that we downloaded from online. Motion joy is free, but Pinnacle Profiler is a one-time fee to download it (after a 20 day trial period).

CAN YOU PLAY OLDER PC GAMES ON THIS SYSTEM?
One of the concerns I had, which I am sure others out there might have is- "Can I play all of my older PC games on this unit as well as Steam games?" The answer is YES! All of our games (purchased through Gog.com previously) work beautifully on this system. That means you do not have to be connected to the internet to play them.

WHAT SHOULD YOU PLAN TO PURCHASE?
--Keyboard (I use Logtiech K400 wireless w/ touchpad on board I use for basic Windows stuff)
--Mouse (I use Marathon Mouse for games)
--DVD-ROM/CD-ROM USB drive (if you want to install anything using those)
--Wireless headphones if you want to use them for gaming

BLUETOOTH
I have a pair of Turtle Beach i30 wireless headphones that operate by bluetooth. I found conflicting information on their site as to whether this would work with Windows 8.1 or not, so I tried installing it.

Windows 8.1 has some idiosyncrasies with bluetooth and is notorious for causing problems in this area. When attempting to install my headphones with this system, the process somehow completely messed up the bluetooth operations in the system. It took me a couple of days to figure it all out, but with a lot of perseverance and some Free Ccleaner added for registry and system cleaning, I managed to get the bluetooth headphones to work beautifully.

This is not a console problem but a Windows 8.1 problem.

ARMA III
We ran this game with maxed out settings, this system ran 30fps smoothly and perfectly. (At the time of this review Arma III is a military simulator that has a very high graphics demand. It is one of the top most demanding games on the market at this time.)

Graphically it looks way better than anything from Modern Warfare.

IS THIS WORTH IT?
PROS
-completely functional PC in all aspects of Windows 8.1
-small physical footprint
-plays all levels of PC games very well
-comes with Xbox controller
-works with PS3 controller
-can get decent keyboard and mouse for very little extra money
-allows family gaming
-more convenient for limited space in living area
-will shut off with front switch like console
-everyone can have their own account
-can play old PC games on this (if updated as in GOG.com purchases)
-can upgrade memory and hard drive

CONS
-expensive(but very powerful for this price range)
-need to purchase keyboard and mouse for Windows operations
-Windows 8.1 can be a bit frustrating at times (Win 8.1 is not unique to this console, however)

THE BOTTOM LINE
When I first read about this console/PC unit, I thought it was way overpriced, but after using it, I REALLY like it so far. We have put this thing through constant use and pushing it since we got it. I have to say it is up to the task. My son who is an avid gamer and builds super computers is even impressed with it, which is saying a lot. In his opinion, it is a very powerful system for the price.

This is a PC designed for console gamers who might not really have discovered the world of PC gaming yet. It seems to be a solid machine that performs well. Working with Windows is not always an easy task, but in set up and basic gaming operations this system is really impressive to me.

WHO WOULD NOT WANT TO GET THIS SYSTEM
This is a high functioning computer that will run games on it and has a console experience attached with it. If you are just interested in using this for Steam, I would say that it is not worth the money. If you want to have a highly functioning Windows 8.1 system (capable of some great gaming) that allows you to have a console experience with Steam as an added bonus all on your TV, then this system is great.

UPDATE 6-2015
We are still crazy about this system. The more that we use it, the more fun it is to explore. The Alien Respawn takes a bit of messing with to get it to work right, but after the update, I finally got the system backed up.

The Steam console has been fun to use, although again, it is quirky when trying to use the Xbox 360 controller that we got with it. There is a glitch that causes some problems occasionally and has to be re-installed from time to time. I am not sure if it is a Windows 8.1 problem or a Steam problem. We are hoping to get the Steam controller when it comes out if it looks like a solid option.

We all have gotten and use Steam accounts and found it to work well so far. We are playing on Wi-Fi (not solid line in) and it still performs quite well.

All in all, this system is FANTASTIC and I can not recommend it highly enough. If I could give it TEN stars, I would.

And as silly as it seems, having the ability to change the colors on the alien head and the triangle shape thrills me to no end. Simple but fun.

Will update if we get the Steam controller to let you know how that works.

I have ready many reviews on tablets, and have found most of them to be why a certain tablet is better than another to the nth degree with all kinds of technical jargon which really just pits one expert against another. As a person who tutors people who are not technologically savvy, I am going to review this tablet from the point of view of someone who has not had one before and whether or not this is a good choice if you want to get one.

I have been told by several business people and those who claim to be very tech savvy that they have gotten rid of their laptops except for occasional spreadsheet work in their offices or at home. Can you get rid of your laptop by getting a tablet like this? Let's take a look.

WHAT IS THIS TABLET LIKE?
SIDE SWITCHES
This tablet is around the size of an ipad mini or a Kindle. The on off switch is on the upper right hand side (with screen facing you) and below it is a rocker switch just below the power switch. There is a space between the two buttons which will allow for elastic bands should you want to get a case for it that has them. That will make it so that the tablet will not be turned on and off by accident. The power button has to be pushed and held for a moment before the unit turns on.

SCREEN
The tablet screen is shiny which can be annoying, but that is the nature of the beast.
The touch sensitivity is excellent- I did not find any problems with response time or lag.
The orientation changing when you turn the screen around is also well set. It works nicely and is not overly sensitive.

INPUT
To input into the tablet, you have a choice to either type or speak what you want the tablet to do. I have to say that this tablet responds very well to either set of input. After working with several i-pads, my daughter constantly raves about how this Acer tablet is superior in the way it responds to input with the microphone than the i-pads are. I have not had any problem with typing into this tablet beyond what I normally do on any unit. The microphone occasionally mistypes a word, but it is not nearly as bad as I expected it to.

Response time of the tablet is excellent. I am quite impressed with how quickly it responds to input without lag or difficulty.

APPS
I have put a few apps on this unit which tend to be popular with tablet users. Sketchbook Pro is one of those apps. I really like it. The response time is good, and the app seems to work well on this tablet. I also love the radio app which allows you to listen to radio stations in the area or around the country. With a case that folds into a stand, it is a great panel to use in a room where you want to listen to the radio.

Quite a few apps that come in the tablet already are handy and easy to use. The screen is quite intuitive and easy to use.

INTERNET USAGE
This tablet is wi-fi accessible to the internet which means that you can not go out in no-man's land to use it like you can an android phone, but you have to be near a wi-fi station to use it.

The wi-fi response time is excellent- although it does occasionally lag when the signals get weak- something that all wi-fi units will do.

Android is a Google engine so everything you do will be monitored by Google or you will be using something they have designed to get where you want to go. You can find other ways to purchase apps if you don't like the Google store, however, such as Amazon.

This tablet comes with McAfee virus scan which is not a huge deal, but I am not sure how to replace that yet, should I desire to do so.

CAMERA
I am not a big advocate of phone and tablet cameras. This one has a decent camera to use on the back, and an adequate camera on the front of the camera to use for Skype which is pretty much all you need. If you want a really nice camera, buy one. For quick pictures to capture something you want to show someone, then this will be fine.

PROS
Easy to hold
Screen responsive
Speech recognition works well
Good fast performance
Boots up quickly
Clear screen makes reading books nice
Good colors for photos on the screen (better than laptops)
Power button hard to accidentally turn on or off
Learning is pretty intuitive for first time users

CONS
Wi-fi only
Not as easy to use as laptop for extensive typing
Can be a bit clumsy to use at times (the nature of tablets)
Start up literature is a bit underwhelming for first time users

THE BOTTOM LINE

CAN YOU GET RID OF YOUR LAPTOP?
Can you get rid of your laptop to substitute this tablet? My answer would be no.

Even if all you did was go on the internet to wander through web sites, using a tablet is a bit cumbersome if you want to do any kind of extensive writing. If you use the microphone, it will probably be pretty accurate, but you will still have to use the keyboard to correct what is used.

For occasional internet usage, watching videos, movies, and reading books, this tablet is fabulous. I think it works beautifully. I would say that it is just as nice as other more expensive tablets and you will invest a lot less money in it.

If you want a tablet and do not want to pay a fortune for it, this is the way to go. The Acer Iconia A1-830 is an excellent value and I use mine a lot. I just could not substitute it completely for my laptop. I prefer to have a choice in my browser, features, and fine tuning or replacement of parts should I desire to do so.

I do find that having the tablet helps a lot when I want to quickly do something on the internet and don't want to boot up my laptop. This tablet is pretty quick and I like it. If you are a tech fanatic and have to have the biggest and best, you might find fault with this tablet, however. It is worth a test run in any case.

UPDATE 3/4/2015 SAMSUNG GALAXY 4 (8 inch) vs ACER ICONIA A1-830
I have had quite a chance to get to know this tablet over time and also to use a Samsung Galaxy 4 8 inch tablet in comparison both on its own and with a keyboard. After working with both tablets, I have to say that I still prefer the Acer over the Samsung and here is why:

-Acer has slightly smaller screen area, but is easier to work on
-Acer has the return and menu buttons incorporated into the screen instead of on the side so it rotates with screen
-Acer surface is less shiny and has less glare
-Performance of Acer is the same as the Samsung in terms of speed
-Wifi of Acer is as good as the Samsung
-keyboard of Acer is much easier to use than Samsung (the one in the screen)
-set up of the Acer is much easier and user friendly
-voice commands on Acer works MUCH better than on the Samsung
-Samsung speaker is a bit nicer than Acer, but I use a bluetooth speaker for best sound anyway.
-Samsung battery does last a bit longer than the Acer, but the frustrations of the Samsung still make me prefer the Acer.

All in all, I have to say that I have tried to honestly look at both tablets and give them a fair comparison and I still like the Acer better. The price is better and the ease of use is better too. The microphone on the Acer seems much more responsive than the Samsung. The screen of the Samsung is a bit more dense in terms of pixels and color perhaps, but the glare is more annoying. I also get very irritated at the side buttons on the Samsung. They are static (stay put) and when the tablet is on its side, it is way too easy to hit a button that screws up what I am trying to do on the Samsung. This is especially true when I am trying to type something and is VERY frustrating.

There is one thing about the Samsung that I really wish the Acer had and that is longer battery time. The Samsung does run a little longer than the Acer without having to recharge. The speaker on the Samsung is a bit nicer, but with my portable bluetooth speaker as my main source of listening, I don't find that to be a problem for me.

So, after time and the chance to use the Acer and the Samsung so I could compare them, I still really like the Acer tablet better. Because I do a lot of graphics work and computer work, I still would not get rid of my laptop or desktop, but I do save a lot of time using this tablet when I want to look up quick information and cruise the internet.

As time has gone on I have enjoyed using the Acer Iconia A1-830 very much. It is a nice tablet for an affordable price.

When I first got this Turtle Shell, my electronically addicted children turned up their noses at it. They thought it was stupid and did not really do much for them. The dynamic range of sound is really good and it has fantastic mids with the perfect touch of lows so that the sound is balanced. The design is very easy to use, carry, set up, and use whether staying put, or carrying with you. The design of the Turtle Shell sends the sound in multiple directions that covers a wide range of area. You can either aim it on its side or have it sitting up to cover about 120 degree of sound direction.

The cover of the jack and recharge spots is a bit difficult to get into place sometimes, but it is doable. A small frustration with an otherwise fabulous speaker. If you don't use the blue tooth, it will shut the blinking light off so that it won't use battery power. It is light and is very solidly built. The volume buttons are a bit difficult to press and that is a bit frustrating. They seem a bit stiff and not easy to control. Maybe over time they will loosen up, I am not sure.
