The sound is clear, not a lot of bass as I would prefer but at least they have a good crisp sound. The buds are also very comfortable to wear for awhile.  They did not irritate my ears at l. I have to get used to the sensitivity of the touch button on the bud, though. They are very sensitive to touch and if you're trying to adjust the fit, you'll be pausing or forwarding a song in the process, but that's just my issue. Happy with these and looking forward to using them often. They paired quickly to my android devices and the directions included were simple to follow.

I am only regretting I haven't bought it year ago...I spent so much money on a variety of $20-40 equipment which was not comfortable to use or cheaply made. I highly recommend you this! It's very steady, super easy to use, but moat importantly great quality and you can bend it so many ways. And yes with a tablet added it makes so much easier to film my cooking videos!! Lesson learned!!

Noise canceling, high quality sound, at its loudest— person besides me can’t even hear a thing. Long lasting charge. Best part is they fit my ears and I’ve never had a pair that fit properly- they always fall out- I have small, odd shaped ears but these fit! It comes with an entire case of different sizes and shapes!
These work great and are easy to use. Sound is perfect. I gave 4 stars because after an hour on your head,  your ears start to hurt from them squeezing too tight and there is no adjustment for this.

Fit is so important with noise cancelling earbuds & for me, these are the best fitting of all the Apple earbuds for my ears. I only wish they had the same audio characteristics as the apple airpod pros so I could use them as a hearing device

I’ve tried audio mask headsets before & they never fit my head. The speakers were in the wrong place & the masks didn’t fit properly & were uncomfortable. With a little sewing to alter the nose area & shorten the Velcro plus move the earpieces around to be near my ears, this mask could be made to work, not perfectly & certainly not noise cancelling but acceptable

I’ve tried iPods, Bose SoundSport Free & many other wireless headset - these are the FIRST TO FIT PROPERLY & stay in my ears. I wanted a headset that would work with the iphones new widget  “Live Listening”, which only works with AirPods or the Powerbeat Pro
8 hrs battery time, lightweight & fits a small ear very well. I listen to audio books on my iPhone while walking the dog.
These earphones are great with wonderful sound. Appears that the material used are very good quality. Really don't know about the durability yet but so far so good.

The color is beautiful. They seem to be made well. I purchased these to replace my Apple iphone earbuds, which I did not like. I had to keep adjusting them all the time. These are really good and stay in place with nice sound. So far so good!

So far so good! Just received today and they work well! So that's great! Hope i'm not jinxing myself by saying that!lol! They are very comfortable and secure. The sound is very good also. The fabric itself is very light and it is lined with mesh. These headphones are (in my opinion) WAY over priced. Let's just hope they last for a while.

I owned the previous generation of Oontz Angle, and while I loved that one, this iteration is a lot better sounding! The bass really sounds great in this device! I'm still getting used to the buttons and the rubberized edges, but I really like it. The bluetooth is easy to connect to and stays connected throughout its use. I like the new rubber pads on the base, it doesn't slip around and feels very sturdy. The color is identical to the previous generation's which I also appreciate.

Pros: THAT BASS! The Volume range

Cons: the controls take a little figuring out

This is my 4th kindle device, I still use them all for different purposes. I love the small, thin lightweight size of this one and after using it for several weeks now, it's become a favorite because it takes up so little space in my bag. The only aspect I'm not in love with yet is the pale gray background which requires an external light source to read the darker gray text. The font style and size is adjustable, it holds a charge well and reaches full capacity quickly. This is affordable, compact and holds a huge library. Just be prepared that if you are outside reading and the sky becomes dark, you will likely need to move inside where there is a lamp.

I have gone through many Bluetooth speakers and had yet to listen to one that had such depth of sound as this Bose SoundLink Revolve.  I know it's not the first Bose SoundLink Bluetooth speaker, but it's my first and it blows away all the others that gather dust around here.  Visually similar to my Amazon Echo, I had to let Alexa know that she has a competitor in my home but reassured her that she is still loved.  I can't talk to this Bose, but each time I turn it on, a generated female voice alerts me to the battery life remaining and what device it's pairing with.  Setup took only a minute, the manual is only a few words and diagrams, and after a full battery charge, it's still going after daily use for what seems like dozens of hours.  I'm serious, I have not plugged it back in yet because I want to see what happens when the battery nears death.  I did not want to wait to write this review because I'm so impressed with the audio that is generated from this little speaker that can also withstand being carried outside without harm.  Of course, I'm not willing to test it in the rain, but have to say that my neighbors could not believe the music was coming from this little black speaker.

Unlike the Sennheiser HD 598 headphones I often use, the HD 559 does not include a 3.5mm adapter plug, so if you need one, have it or you will be unhappy should you want to use these for a laptop or other small device.  To test these, I kept my adapter in the laptop and switched between the two headphones, listening to an assortment of various tracks so I could really compare the audio elements and physical feel of the headphones.  I prefer the HD 598 headphones over this newer model and see that they are both comparable prices now because a newer model is available of the 598's.  You may prefer the HD 559's if you prefer a tinner, bass accentuated audio, but I would rather hear the differentiation between the elements of audio which I hear more clearly with the HD 598's.  The separation is simply more refined and I guess I'm spoiled. The newer 559 is cheaper than the upgraded higher end model, and i find them to be a tighter fit which becomes uncomfortable and irritating when worn for hours at a time, something that I never experienced with the others.  I think this band is stiffer, too. These produce a much less elegant sound which some may prefer, but the more I listen to these, the more I wonder if there is something wrong with them due to the pounding sound which is replicated each time I switch to them.  To avoid prejudice, I had an assistant do the switching for me as I kept my eyes closed through several songs and an audio narration.  I worked in the film and video industry and always used Sennheiser earphones, so my experience with the brand spans decades. These just don't match up, and that may just be the cause of my disappointment. They are not bad headphones, they are not great for my desires in experiencing audio in either recording or playback modes.  Of note is that the detachable long cable is nowhere near as easy to remove or insert as my other headphones which is of concern.  This set was made in China and it comes in a no frills 2 part box with a simple document written in numerous languages.

Being a Mac user for decades, it has been some time since I've had the opportunity to use a Windows based computer, so I was eager to try the Windows 10 operating system on this convertible notebook computer, also a first for me. The Acer Aspire R 14 R5-471T-79YN has far exceeded my expectations in form and function, despite the learning curve I'm experiencing. I won't get into the Windows 10 system, but will say that I can definitely see the influence of the Mac operating systems on its development and I am impressed. Perhaps I like it more than many users might simply because I can't even remember the last Windows system I used being that even my remote work situations tend to not use these computers now.

The Acer is not as lightweight as a tablet, of course, but it's also not the weightiest notebook of this size, and the brushed metal texture of the case is appealing. It looks sleek and feels good when the computer is used. I find the keyboard to be very comfortable, the touchpad is positioned well and the silver edging surrounding it is a nice contrast. I do not like the position of the power button which is directly beneath the power plug, as I find that if plugged in, I have to fiddle with it to turn on the computer. The USB ports, HDMI port, SD card reader and volume control are all easily accessible and have functioned well so far in every case I've used them this week. The speakers are a little odd, but that makes sense since the convertible form of this means that when used as a tablet ,the rear speakers will face the area between the folded computer. To my surprise, I find that the sound improves in tablet form, better than when used in laptop or tented configurations. I have mine set to ask if I want to switch to tablet layout because I found that it did not always respond appropriately when set to automatic conversion. The true HD makes this a very nice system on which to watch videos and with external headphones or speaker, either cabled or Bluetooth, it becomes a great system. I would actually consider this one to be best suited for entertainment, and would imagine that it is excellent for games although I have not used it for that purpose at all. The touch screen is very responsive, but it does take some time to get accustomed to the responsiveness. The computer is very fast, very quiet, very cool (temperature), and it starts quickly. I rather like the lack of an optical drive because that keeps it quieter and lighter, yet allows me to add a peripheral drive if I want or when it is needed. I rather enjoyed streaming a movie from my Amazon Prime directly to a non-smart TV. I've used this in the kitchen in both the tablet and tent configurations using the Kindle app and much appreciated having a larger screen than when using my Kindle Fire for recipe following.

For the price, I think this is a great convertible computer which comes with a single year warranty. I intend to give this Aspire a workout and hope that I never need to discover how the Acer warranty service performs.

Not a fan of big and bright walkie talkies, I was attracted to the Motorola T260 because of its simple grayish color and no frills appearance.  It is powered by either 3 AA batteries in each which the consumer provides or the single rechargeable NiMH battery for each which is included.  The batteries do take a very long time to charge, so have AA's on hand if you need to use this immediately.  The operating manual is well written and when followed, seems to be accurate.  Some steps to prep the devices seem to take longer than they should, but since they do work, I won't complain.  The two-way radios can be married by any one of many channels, we had no difficulty getting one pretty quickly, and the volume is audible.  This model offers weather channels which come in loud and clear, and it also allows the user to activate the iVOX feature which allows hands free operation without accessories or with additional things you can purchase separately.  The only thing I didn't care for with this pair is the "Roger" tone which was very annoying to both of us, but fortunately, I finally discovered that it can be turned off.  It helps to read the manual even if you don't think you need details.

The wallet may be marketed as a phone holder, but it is a wallet first and foremost. It is attractive and the zipper functions well, with very shiny gold colored hardware and a nice wrist strap. Aside from some stitching that I am concerned might become loose because the stitch gauge is too long, it is very well made and very utilitarian. It holds quite a bit, including a phone, making it a good accessory to carry when I don't want to take a purse or backpack with me. Since it is closed by a single surrounding zipper, I don't hear the phone if it rings unless the volume is turned to the highest and the zipper is left with an open gap. All in all, I have grown to like this wallet more and more each day.  The leather is holding up beautifully and I can't tell you how often I am asked about where to get one.  It is a really good value, too.  Sample  was provided for review.

First of all, the marketers of this [[ASIN:B00JVUO0RO DE Chrome Robot Dual Headphone Splitter]] have a good sense of humor as is evidenced by the instructions on the package. Very cute.

I don't carry much on my keychain because I don't want additional weight in the car's ignition weighing it down. This robot is lightweight despite its size, therefore, I put it on a separate lanyard so I don't misplace it. When hung in a special place, I know where to find it quickly. The robot separates, revealing a mini plug with splitter eyes for using two electronic devices. I've had no problems so far and find the plugs fit smoothly, but it's really a novelty item and not my number one choice as a splitter. It's a handy little device to take on long trips with kids, so the driver can enjoy a quiet time with the kids enjoying a movie while wearing headphones, and if you keep it in the car, you're always ready. The quality is not great, it's just a cute novelty for a robot loving person.

I received the product for review.

According to the synthetic leather Clarino website, CLARINO is three times stronger than real leather, requiring only a third of real leather's weight to achieve equal tear strength.  So, if you like the look and feel of leather but do not want an animal skin, you could consider the human-made [[ASIN:B00JP46IC6 BUFFALO Case for All New Kindle Fire HDX 8.9", BLACK (will only fit All New Kindle Fire HDX 8.9")]] instead of genuine leather.  It is indeed lightweight, fitting, and folds back to hold the Kindle Fire HDX 8.9" in landscape position.  This is good for using an external keyboard or watching a video.  I personally like the look of the Amazon Origami case, but this one works fine to hold the device.  I would not expect this to protect it, just to give it a home.  The device can be positioned in a single position.

I have a love/hate relationship with Belkin products. Some are a major disappointment, but then there are those that are so well constructed and attractive that I forget about those others. The [[ASIN:B00D2CNXK2 Belkin 11-Inch Laptop /Chromebook Sleeve, Blue (B2B081-C01)]] is a beauty that I am very happy to have requested. Unfortunately, the dimensions are just as described and if your device is a hair over, there is no leeway because the outside gusset is not stretchy or flexible at all. You can't really tell from the images, but the opening of this sleeve is on one single end, that is the shorter side of the rectangle. Because the corners are all rounded, the zipper extends about an inch or two down the length, so you can wiggle your device in and out of the sleeve, provided it is not wider than 8 inches. Seriously. As I said, the black gusset is made of a woven heavy duty fabric, measuring about an inch in width, and there is piping sewn into both seams, front and back, for a finished appearance. A full sized pocket is sewn into the front of the sleeve and it contains a zipper as well. There is a small handle made of the same gusset fabric which is beautifully concealed when not being used. The neoprene is a lovely blue which is darker than the image online and I love it.

Because none of my devices can be squeezed into this sleeve, I am using it for other purposes. The price of this is perfect for a terrific sleeve.

The Belkin Miracast Video Adapter works well if the correct equipment is available, but doesn't work at all if you are using a noncompliant smartphone or television.  I first thought my two year old Vizio television would not work because it has no USB port, but after ordering a new set, realized that the USB could be utilized from an outside source.  After trying several times to ate my Razr to the Belkin, I realized that the connection was unobtainable because the phone is not operating on the correct system.  I then enlisted a friend with a compatible phone and we were able to make the connection very quickly, then watched gleefully on the Vizio.  For a smartphone with Miracast capability, this works well and should be considered.  Since technology changes rapidly, as do our phones, I would not hesitate to use this if it fits into your budget.  When I replace my smartphone in the next few months, I will certainly verify on the Belkin website that the new purchase is compatible because it is an outstanding option for viewing images and listening to audio on a big screen.  I have been satisfied with my other Belkin products and find them to be a reliable company.  If your set has an HDMI port which isn't easy to access, this device also includes an extender which has worked well for my set.  Otherwise, I would not have been able to plug in the USB cable because of its position.

I purchased a MacBook Pro a few months ago and love the laptop computer. I've been an Apple customer since the inception of Macintosh, owning only one PC in my lifetime. I have never purchased an iPad. The [[ASIN:B00HRO3IBA Toshiba Chromebook CB35-A3120 PLM01U-002005 13.3-Inch Cloud Computer]] is Toshiba's first entry into the Chromebook market, my first Chromebook and it did not disappoint this consumer.

It is about the same dimensions as my MacBook Pro, but thinner and substantially lighter in weight. With a solid state, no hard drive or DVD in this one, it is the one I'll take when traveling. Out of the box, I plugged in the Chromebook, then opened the lid. Immediately, the registration process began and since I'm already a Google customer, it was quick and simple. Setup was faster than fast and within a couple of minutes I was on the web, with access to all my Google contents, even those from my Android. Another few minutes and I was set up to print from my Epson printer which is in another room. Whereas I need to use an Epson app to print from the Android, this prints from the Google Cloud. The Google store offers a lot of apps, many of which are free, and a few which I found desirable and downloaded. With two USB ports, I'm able to carry a USB with me instead of relying on the cloud for everything. With the HDMI, I can hook up to a larger screen if I want. Chromebooks are designed for streaming and internet based operations, and there is no software to install. It's all out there for you to use without taking up space or requiring moving parts in your computer. Microsoft Office doesn't work, but documents can be put into Google Docs, then be converted to an Office document.

The appearance of this Chromebook is very sleek, with an attractive texture to the cover that feels good in the hand. For me, it's an easier, less slippery grip than others I've held onto. Start up is nearly instantaneous with the Chromebook as soon as the lid is lifted up -- I turn it off each time I'm done with it. The battery time is longer than I'd expected, fortunately because although the charge time is fast, the power supply I have gets uncomfortably hot. Because of this, I do not keep it plugged in while charging. My second criticism of this unit is that it makes a disturbing noise on the left side closest to me periodically while operating. At first, I thought the sound was coming from the power supply, but determined it is from the Chromebook after disconnecting the power supply. It's not constant, just annoying when it occurs because it takes over my focus. The keypad is very comfortable for me and I've not stumbled moving between my MacBook Pro and Toshiba Chromebook. The trackpad is a little jumpy, but not as bad as it could be, even after making adjustments through the Settings. The screen presents a terrific image and the speakers also are better than I'd expected at this price. All in all, I can't believe they are selling this Chromebook for 279. I can see why Chromebooks are all that in schools now. It's nice to have an option to lock your Chromebook if you're taking it to a place where it might "walk away" and requiring a sign-in to access the operating system is another plus. I like it and could love the Toshiba Chromebook in time.

UPDATE a few days later: Amazonian Consumer, another customer, provided comments on my review which I think are important. He/she noted things that are posted on the Toshiba website, so I'll address the components. I have used the Bluetooth with no problem at all. The RAM is limited to what's installed and the battery is not user-replaceable. There is a Skype limitation because Chrome OS uses Hangouts instead, and the camera does work fine. The SD card reader works, too, without a problem. I also didn't mention that I like the Velcro cable wrap attached to the power cord, so I don't have to add one. Mine power supply still gets hot, but when the charge is complete, it cools down. Ironically, my Chromebook has stopped making the noises it was initially making. Another observation I've made is that the trackpad seems to occasionally have a mind of its own and it sends things before I'm ready. It's more than being overly sensitive and I'm going to need to work on correcting this.

UPDATE 2/6/14: The audio now continuously goes in and out and the machine sound which I mentioned in my initial review is occurring again, usually when the audio goes out. I have a call in to Toshiba but they aren't trained yet to deal with the Chromebook, so someone will be calling me back "in a day or two." I'm also still experiencing the cursor arbitrarily moving up on the page when I have stopped typing, so I have to be especially careful to assure that what I'm typing is being entered where intended.

UPDATE 2/18/14: The audio problem is even worse and Toshiba never called me or net an email other than a survey on their customer service. It took several of my initiated attempts in phone calls and I'm finally awaiting a box and label which will take another two days to arrive for this Chromebook to be returned to Toshiba for repair. They offered me no option of simply sending a label and letting me return it in the original boxes. Dealing with them has been terrible and one rep had the gall to ask if I'd rate him a 10 on a scale of 1-10 for assistance in a survey.

I'm tempted to reduce my rating of four stars but will hold off until I receive my repaired lemon of a Chromebook which I still love despite its clicking sound, faulty speakers, sticky trackpad and terrible Toshiba telephone customer service.

UPDATE 3/11/14: Received my repaired Chromebook last night (FedEx signature required delivery was only option) and the speakers had been replaced. What a difference! No clicking sound, humming, anything other than the sound of lovely audio through the speakers. The trackpad still isn't the smoothest, but more importantly, it still selects things that I have no intention of selecting. For example, when selecting an email, one above or below opens instead of the one I select. I've also had pages close or disappear for no apparent reason.

I'm impressed. First of all, the [[ASIN:B00DRA4CW2 Mefoto A0320Q00B DayTrip Tripod Kit (Blue)]] lightweight aluminum mini tripod is lovely. It is housed in a nice black cardboard box that makes a good first impression. The tripod inside is protected by a black carrying case with orange piping trim. There's an attached lightweight adjustable carrying strap that functions without any padding. Inside of the case is a side zippered pocket that contains a hex tool and the owner's manual which is very well written in two languages. The English is easy to understand and without many grammatical or spelling errors. The two pages of diagrams are also well done and the publication is very basic. I'm happy that too much money didn't go into this part of the package and there weren't additional packing materials either!

The tripod I received is an appealing blue which reminds me of the Caribbean waters. It's definitely a color I would have selected in a B&M store. The entire tripod weighs less than 2 pounds and stands a maximum of about 24 inches tall. You can safely mount a camera of a maximum of 8.8 pounds. Each part of the tripod seems well constructed and very well designed. My favorite little treat is the bubble level which is recessed in the mounting platform, underneath the easily removable mounting plate. The ballhead allows for a relatively smooth head movement, better than I'd expected. I appreciate the retractable weight hook for situations where a bit of extra stability is required. Another feature is the reversible center column which I use quite often for shooting table top close ups. Having the tripod legs fold up greatly reduces the packing and carrying size of this tripod, and it can be folded and stored in the bag very quickly if necessary while on the go.

I must say that when I first read "Mefoto", I saw it as "Manfroto". They are not the same company or products, but for the cost of this great little tripod, I don't care what it's named. It's a bargain that securely allows you to better use a camera in situations where a full sized tripod is either inconvenient, overkill or simply too cumbersome. I'll likely purchase a couple as holiday gifts this year and will also check out their other products! This was a fine introduction for me.

We've been using the [[ASIN:B00DR8LAE2 SanDisk Connect 64G Wireless Media Drive Streaming On the Go (SDWS1-064G-A57)]]successfully and have encountered no problems since first transferring pictures and sound files.  Its size is compact, about the same size as a Royal Castle hamburger and bun I used to order as a kid,  The battery lasts longer than any other portable media storage device I've used, making it a perfect traveling companion.  I think this would be a good little device for a gift and am considering one for a niece who has no television.

I intended to give the [[ASIN:B00AQRUW4Q Seagate Wireless Plus 1 TB Mobile Device Storage with Built-In Wi-Fi Streaming (STCK1000100)]] a rating of four stars, but have decided that it really is a five star product. The near deduction was because of the frustration I experienced in my attempting to get the device up and running with the limited information provided in the package and on the website. Once I successfully downloaded the software to my Droid, Kindle Fire and MacBook, I still encountered more trial and error than usual until I was able to figure out how the darn thing works. Fast forward to days and weeks of loving the device!

The Wireless Plus can be used as an extra drive for storage if you're not interested in using it for streaming, but if that's your true need, I'd likely recommend purchasing something else. With it's own Wi-Fi streaming, you don't need to use your home or hot network. Using it's Wi-Fi has been quick and has been glitch free for us thus far. We have used three devices at once and found it to be problem-free, with no freezes, crashes or difficulties. We had it up and running for four hours and still had battery power, then recharged. Although it can be charged via the USB on your computer, it is much faster by plugging it into an electrical outlet if one's available. Since we haven't drained the battery yet, I can't say how long it really lasts.

Music, movies, pictures, documents, audiobook, you can use whichever you want on any networked device as long as the device has the appropriate application installed. I watched the Seagate tutorials several times and found them to be difficult to follow, however once I spent some dedicated time just feeling my way through, I discovered that I do like the applications, too. Even if I'm not accessing the Wireless Plus on my Droid, I have been using the Seagate app.

This arrives with little documentation, but it is USB 3 capable if you need it. The housing is lightly rubberized and it has a matte metal plate in a charcoal gray color on the face side. The plug appears to be proprietary, the second reason I almost deducted a star from this review. It looks like a hybrid mini plug that's attached via a thin wire, not a cable, to a USB for either a device or the two prong electrical plug. No case is included, but I have a couple that work great. The size isn't so big that it feels cumbersome, but it is heavier than it appears to be upon first glance. I don't mind the weight because this little device holds 1 TB, much more than I have loaded on it as of today. I highly recommend this device and look forward to Seagate upgrading it as time passes. It's unique and not expensive for what it offers.

I've been using the [[ASIN:B00BFNYD90 Jabra VOX Corded Stereo Wired Headsets - Retail Packaging - Black]] for a couple weeks now and like them but don't love them, largely because they don't do all they can do on my Droid. I downloaded the Jabra app and was all set to improve their capabilities, but all I got was a really good app that allows me to import, organize and equalize my collection. I ended up listening to radio stations because I don't usually download music to my phone anyway. I tried the phones on my MacBook and iPod as well, and found them to produce satisfactory sound, albeit a little tinnier than my other headsets, either canned or budded.

The headset is attractive and lightweight. It appears to be well constructed and the sets of gels fit well onto the pair of appendages. They originally attached gels fit my ears without a problem but the left one tends to make a squishy sound when inserted. It's the actual earbud because it happens when I place it in either ear. I like the knobbed design of the buds because that angle lets me know in which ear to place the bud. I simply can't read the LEFT/RIGHT on the headset. These are comfortable for a very long time (hours) and I get only a little extraneous sound seeping through most of the time. On phone calls, this is outstanding for myself and the people to whom I've spoken. Five stars here. The standard microphone is another asset, and my voice commands on the Droid are smoothly recognized, too. It's not omnidirectional, but I don't really need that in this headset. The 3.5mm jack isn't as snug as others I've used and I have to be really careful about inserting it at the correct angle so that it's not jiggled while I move. Listening to Phillip Glass was at first awful, until I realized I'd moved the plug. Once it was inserted properly, the sound was beautiful and larger than what comes through many other earbud headsets. I appreciate the magnets on each wire because they allow me to wrap the cables uniformly and put into the little lightweight storage case. The pouch case has a nice opening that's comfortable to open and close with one hand and it stays closed well. I also am using the hard plastic shell in which this was packaged, but you could recycle it if you have no use for the "package."

I'd recommend that if you have no device which allows you to use the in wire control, you save some money and get something else. For my use, it just gets in the way and is frustrating. I was disappointed that I couldn't even answer a phone call as I was under the impression this would work on my smartphone. I can't blame my misinterpretation on the product, though, so no stars off here. It's tempting to use these earbuds while I drive, but I try to remove one so that I can hear what's going on outside of my own space. While walking the dog, these are great, again upping the star rating. The volume control only works on Apple devices and the pause/play music, answer/end call, reject call, redial last umber, or skip track forward/backward are phone dependent on the in wire control. None of these work on the Motorola Droid. If you're looking for realistic hifi sound from your device, try out this headset that weighs in at just over 1/2 of an ounce, but I'd suggest thinking about if you need or can use the mic and music control which adds to the price of this product. This is a five star design and it seems like the headset will surpass it's 2 year warranty. This was made in China.

The [[ASIN:B009FHFFIG Sennheiser Momentum Over-Ear Headphone]] are circumaural  which means they cover the whole ear and they have a closed-back.  They are lightweight, gorgeous with soft brown leather cushioned earpieces, have two easily switchable cables, one for general use and the second for specified mac devices.  A MacBook is not one of the specified devices, but my iPod is.  With its swivel plug and embedded on the cable remote, I'm sure iPhone and iPad users will be as thrilled as I was when I tried it on a friend's devices.  Crisp, clear, complete, these need no amplifier, but they do need ears which are not larger than average or the whole ear coverage is lacking and therefore, so is the desired effect of a circumaural earpiece.  I've listened to music on a MacBook, an android phone, a Kindle Fire, and tested these on the aforementioned iPad and iPhone.  In each and every case, the sound was outstanding and my ears did not tire, nor did they feel uncomfortable or overheated.  Most sounds surrounding me were not heard and those nearby did not hear what I was listening to at any time.  Watching movies is enhanced every time and I'm finding that even when impulsively finding a video on the Web in my usual activities, I tend to grab these headphones to listen instead of simply hearing through the computer.  My favorite music in these earphones thus far today has been John Coltrane's [[ASIN:B000V698WE A Love Supreme]].  I tend to switch genres throughout a day, but thought this was worth mentioning.  Nothing like really hearing the instrumentals as they were intended to be heard!  Outstanding headphones.

The [[ASIN:B008S2DC1Q Tribeca Genuine Leather Portfolio Case for Kindle Fire, Berry Metallic]] is very pretty and shiny, smells creepy because it's only been out of the box since last night, is comfortable to hold, fits the Kindle Fire snugly with four elastic corners, has a tab closure that can be folded back into a slot when the Kindle is being used in landscape mode on a flat surface with the case folded back, and is better than average, but not fabulous. It's lighter in weight than my previous cover and feels better, but I'm not 100% sold on it for several reasons. Any time an accessory arrives with a nasty smell, I'm not happy and I found it necessary to remove the Kindle for now and let the case air out. The packaging states, "Folio design converts into a stand with multiple viewing angles." I was able to view in a single angle with the stand folded properly. The tab closure is secure, but it's an extra step to slip it through the holder and the tab is a bit long. I imagine this will improve as time goes by when it's used frequently. The genuine leather exterior is a thin leather that's irregularly finished with the metallic look, but I don't think the "cushioned" lining will protect the device well if it's accidentally dropped. Tribeca claims, "You aren't boring, so why should your accessories be?" That's a catchy phrase and the accessory has a bit of cuteness to it. It is easy to locate because this one is bright, and it does make a statement of color. I think it's a nice product.

EDIT 3/27/13: I like this case, but the odd smell remains on its interior after three months. Otherwise, it's condition is great.

The compact [[ASIN:B006C248BC Motorola H19txt Universal Bluetooth Headset - Retail Packaging]] arrived in an attractive hard plastic box which I'm using for storage of some little bits which made me happier than having another package to recycle.  The headset is compact and different than my other bluetooth headsets because the boom is foldable.  The most difficult part of getting this up and running was removing the little plastic from the headset, so I'd give it tom marks for accessibility and function.  Easy to charge, this headset hasn't burned the charge any faster than my other headsets, another plus.  Pairing with a Motorola Razr was simple and required nothing other than turning on both units, yay for ease!  I'll admit that I was startled because a voice spoke to me as soon as I opened the box, but I wasn't too surprised since the light was already on in the headset.  I've had no problems with the fit in my ear or the reception, but I dpn't usually travel too far from my phone, so it hasn't been tested to the max.  The design reminds me of a Volvo, boxy, if you know what I mean.  I'm very impressed with this Motorola headset, but must admit that I prefer my Plantronic bluetooth headset which is in this price range.  I am not complaining about this one, I just really prefer the other because I like it's design better.

The Vanguard Auctus Plus 323CT Professional Tripod for Cameras and Camcorders is even better than I was anticipating and now I must purchase a new tripod head to get the most out of this high quality photographic instrument. To maintain a stable and secure foundation for a camera, this is outstanding -- attractive, easy to assemble, sturdy, and versatile. It arrives in a very nice cardboard box with a handle, so if you're inclined to store it in the box, you have that option. Also included is a black and orange carrying case with a shoulder strap and there is a little zippered compartment near the top of the bag for the hook, included hex key, car key, flash drive, roll of film or whatever you'd like to store. A hand crank raises and lowers the center column and it moves very smoothly, not too easy and not too hard. The tripod can simply be converted for macro shots with low camera placement. For low angle photography using very wide legs, the bottom half of the center column can very easily be removed by simply unscrewing the hook and turning the bottom ring. Very smart and pretty fast, too. Having the option to attach anti slip spiked rubber feet is a great advantage in snow or sand and adds to the stability of the tripod. When the tripod arrives, the large rubber feet are snugly attached and I doubt that they will be lost when removed to use the spikes or standard rubber feet. The three sectioned legs are extremely easy to extend with a slight turn of the amply sized twist locks and each leg has clearly marked segments for perfect measuring. They can be locked at the top, another stability and security advantage, at three angles (25, 50 and 80 degrees). If desired, a camera bag or weight can be hung from the hook on the center column. The rubber foam casing at the top of each leg makes for a very comfortable feel and aid in moving the legs and carrying tripod. Although there's a little bubble level, mine was dry, so customer service is sending me a replacement level. It's small and may be obstructed when a head and large plate or camera are attached, but it's a nice little bonus nevertheless. Changing the camera screw from 1/4" to 3/8" is another simple process that takes seconds. I'm not sure if the orange anti-shock ring really does much, but it can't hurt. This carbon tripod can hold 39 pounds and it weighs around 8 pounds. It has an ample extension and I'm very satisfied with it in all regards for use in the studio as well as in the field.

UPDATE: Vanguard CS is out of this world. When they promised to send a replacement bubble level, I was politely told it would be 2-3 months before they were expected from the manufacturer. Several weeks ago, I received a padded envelope containing a brand new perfect bubble level. It's rare that follow-up isn't necessary in a situation like this, but Vanguard clearly maintained the information to fulfill this promise. If I could award another star in my review, I would!

The TOMTOM GO2535 TM WTE is quite attractive with a large screen and smooth appearance but because of its size, this is a heavier GPS than many others. A magnetic plug attaches the power supplies either to a computer with its USB plug or to a car with its accessory power plug. As with most GPS devices, no "home" DC power supply is included. I have found the car mount to be great, easy to attach and remove from the windshield with a simple turn. My only complaint with the mount is that it takes some work to direct the device to a visible position and I fear that it will not last as long as the GPS. The magnetic plug slips into a cutout in the mount, allowing it to remain in position so the GPS can quickly be inserted or removed for safekeeping.
As for the functionality of the GPS, it has some problems, thereby preventing me from giving this a 5 star review. I'll simply list the Pros and Cons.
Pros:
Start up time is quick and option to start from last destination can save time if the satellite connection is delayed.
Menu options are easily learned even if at first they seem to include extra steps.
Responds quickly to need for alternate route when a turn is missed.
Ease in moving through functions on screen.
POIs are expansive and easy to discover
Map identifies a location I frequent which is not identified by any other GPS I've used.
Identifies traffic light cameras adequately. Have yet to receive speed camera warning.
Voice commands are intuitive and a little printed card is included if you're in need of prompting.
Connectivity to my Mac is easy and the option to automatically check for updates can save time.

Cons:
Speed is not always accurate. Often has my car going at 10 mph less than actual speed.
When setting a new destination, I've been unable to change the state unless I do it using the voice command. This may be possible, but I haven't had the time to investigate. Since I'm in a metropolitan area and may venture through 2 states and the District of Columbia in less than an hour, it's important for me to access the individual states.
When using phone through the GPS, although I can hear the conversation with no problem, the person on the other end of my call can't hear me clearly. Every time I've used it with a phone, the call has been dropped. I've never had a call dropped otherwise with my phone or other Bluetooth capable device.
Does not recognize voice commands at times.
Voice prompts are very frequent and I'd love to be able to reduce them but not turn it off.
Seldom comes up with the routes I usually take, even with a second try after selecting the Change Route option.

All in all, this is a good GPS navigation device and the lifetime updates are a definite advantage. I haven't traveled the wold with it, but will update my review as necessary with observations internationally. I do know the maps are on the device because I saw them when I performed the update last week and couldn't figure out how to get back to the USA on the device. For some reason, TOMTOM put me in the UK even though I'm registered in the USA and confirmed that selection.

What's interesting is that I still prefer my 3-year-old Navigon for its ease of use, accuracy and lovely displays, with two exceptions. I do not care for their customer service or necessity to download map updates to the device's SD card instead of doing a direct update on a Mac. This TOMTOM excels there and it comes in a very definite second for any GPS I've used. When the time comes for my beloved Navigon to bite the dust, I feel confident that I'll still be happy with this TOMTOM.

Although I've used a Plantronics Bluetooth earpiece, I must admit that I've never been crazy about the idea of an earpiece.  The Jabra CRUISER2 Bluetooth In-Car Speakerphone is so much more comfortable for me to use while driving!  After I realized that it would take a couple hours to charge the unit, I plugged it into the car and it was ready for pairing by the time I arrived home from my day of errands.  The pairing was intuitive, the voice basically guided me through the process, and I was making my first hands free, earpiece free call in a minute!  The clarity is excellent and the battery is outstanding.  Because it's so cold outside now, I've charged it again, but the battery was still alive.  I love the option to charge the unit either in the car or via the usb option.  This is a lightweight unit, small in size and the clip is lightweight but sturdy.  It doesn't contain extraneous buttons or lights, just what it needs.  Listening to music through the FM worked, but I doubt that I'll use the function often.  All in all, I really like this speakerphone and see why my favorite warehouse club store offered it through their coupon booklet recently.

The Case Logic DCB-307 SLR Shoulder Bag is structurally sound, pleasing to the eye and compact enough to not weigh you down with heavy construction or materials.  It's streamlined shape stands on its own without toppling over, yet when carried with the optional detachable shoulder strap, it doesn't bounce around on my hip like many other "boxy" camera cases.  Although I tend to prefer bluish reds, the orangish red is a lovely contrasting interior and it's extremely well put together.  Having a lighter weight fabric for the interior reduces the weight and increases the flexibility of the adjustable padded sections, also giving a smoother touch when against my delicate camera gear.  In some cases, I wrap lenses even with their caps attached for added protection, but with this one, I don't think that's necessary.  I would not worry about any surfaces as long as they are separated from adjacent components with the not too thick or wide included removable pads.  The zipper pulls are smooth and strong and the attention to detail with a little fabric cover under which the pull is stored is much appreciated.  If I were to only use a case with a shoulder strap, I would be bothered by the upright handle, but since I personally use the handle to carry the case on many occasions, it doesn't bother me.  Using the case for an SLR film camera, I would have liked a single pocket to be a bit deeper for film canisters, but I can compensate by putting a roll or two inside the case or attach them to the shoulder strap.  I also find the shoulder strap to be comfortable and not bulky, easy to carry the goods.  I tend to not carry too much extraneous stuff with me, so this size is perfect!  Since I dedicate camera and equipment only to the case, I don't need more space or other compartments, hooks, baubles, fobs and the like.  The top loading zippered case meets my needs better than most and I'm grateful to be using this Case Logic DCB product.  I will definitely investigate the smaller cases for other uses, too!

If this was Mac compatible, I'd buy many as gifts.  It's easy to set up and operate and the quality is great for the price.  The Logitech HD Webcam C510 with 720p Video and Swivel Design gives you the capability of live video and audio communication at a cost that's likely less than your cell phone.  The size is compact and fits nicely in a laptop USB as well as a desktop computer.  It would be great to have a family bundled pack!

My first GPS was a hand me down Magellan that I could never get to work. My second was a Navigon 2100 max 4.3-Inch Portable GPS Navigator with Text-to-Speech which I absolutely love. Next was the Nextar SNAP5 Super Slim 5-Inch Portable GPS Navigator which I seldom use. This TomTom XL 340M LIVE (Lifetime Maps Edition) 4.3-Inch Portable GPS Navigator is better than all, but I still love the Navigon for it's quick re-routing and ease of operation. That being said, I'll describe my experiences over the past few weeks of owning this GPS.

Out of the box, it's necessary to hook the GPS up to your computer to check on the maps and register the product. I did remove the extra voices to create some space as was recommended by other reviewers, saving them to my computer before removing them from the device. I wasted time trying to find Tom Tom Home and like another reviewer, was able to get it through an internet search. The website listed on the box (as I recall) was not accurate and it's not intuitive. Once I had the software downloaded and installed, I began confirming that I had the most recent map installed. This can be done only once. I reviewed the online manual because there was none included and that was no big deal for me. No papers to lose. Although I did not register for the Live option or provide any information (payment), I've used the live services to do a Google search for a POI and the gas prices has already been used 3 times with success. I'm not crazy about having the computerized female voice as the only option for "speaking" street names, and the names are not always pronounced correctly or even completely, but it does work. The Navigon is far superior in this regard. The Tom Tom accesses satellites very quickly for me and I don't find myself waiting ever for the device to start navigating. The POIs are far superior and easier to access on the Tom Tom. Rerouting options were not intuitive for me and a friend showed me the way to select specific options. The mount is lousy in my opinion and the GPS has popped out on too many occasions for me to be comfortable. It's the weakest link for me in the entire package. I did have the audio set to automatically change with the speed of the vehicle but that drove me crazy with a computerized female voice yelling at me as I was driving the Beltway, so that's been changed and she's set at about 70% consistently. I wish I'd had this GPS a week earlier because I received a $150 speeding ticket in the mail from DC through a Radar unit. Once I recover from the shock and guilt, I'll travel the route again within the speed limit and see if the GPS warns me of the radar unit. It does alert me of the red light camera installed (but not operational) which is permanently installed on my street corner. The first few times I heard the alert, I had no idea what was going on, until I read the online manual again. I now also set the speed alert to let me know when I'm exceeding a speed limit, but the limits have not always been current. One day, I will notify Tom Tom of several routing major screw ups I've discovered but that's going to have to wait until I have some time on my hands. The Navigon is superior in this regard of more direct routing and fewer errors. All in all, I like this and would recommend the product. Perhaps when my Navigon Fresh Maps subscription expires I'll remove the second GPS from my car, but for now I just can't give up Sarah (the Navigon text to speech voice).

The Lorex LNE1001 Easy Connect Network IP Remote Surveillance Camera (White) was not too difficult for me to connect after reading the materials and checking the Lorexcctv website.  A lengthy brochure describes the step-by-step sequence for setup which must be followed in order, but to install on a Mac, I had to go to the website for instructions.  The camera is small in size and a short white ethernet cable was included.  Unfortunately, for our needs, we'll be getting a wireless surveillance camera, but this was an inexpensive way to get started.  We'll also be looking for a camera that enables us to record on a Mac which is not an option with this camera and the reason I've deducted a star from the review.

I'm one of the folks who had a hard drive crash without having backed up for several months.  That was all it took for me to realize the importance of backing up my hard drive regularly and not simply putting current files on a flash drive.  I'd been using a Western Digital drive for the past three or four years, then was told that hard drives have a limited life span.  That made sense, so I decided to replace the external drive which is used to backup my MacBook.  I almost purchased the Seagate FreeAgent GoFlex 500 GB USB 2.0 Ultra-Portable External Hard Drive STAA500100, then decided that I don't take the external drive with me and didn't need it to be portable.  Enter the Seagate FreeAgent GoFlex Desk 2 TB Desktop External Hard Drive STAC2000100, a shiny black drive that looks much sleeker and way more shiny than the dull Western Digital.  2 TB seemed like more than I need, but I went for it anyway.  Before the package arrived, I watched the videos available on the Seagate website, so I was prepared for this drive and felt comfortable using it as my new backup drive.  My only question was whether or not to format it for use with Mac and PC or just the Mac.  Decided on the Mac only and didn't install the other options onto my MacBook.  Since I use Time Machine, I immediately proceeded to backup the hard drive.  Not having purchased the optional Firewire, eSATA or USB 3.0, the transfer is not faster than on the other external drives I've used, but this one sure is quiet and it's much nicer to look at.  It also doesn't weigh as much as other desktop external drives.  Looks like the attractive Seagate sleek shape, just bigger.  There is no button to push, just plug in and connect, then go to Time Machine.  I cannot review the included Memeo backup because I've not installed it.  Can't imagine that it would be better than Time Machine.  This meets my needs and exceeds my expectations.  It also looks nicer when locked up in my fire retardant portable safe than any other drive.

When the huge box arrived, I thought I'd made a mistake by ordering the Altec Lansing VS4621 Octane 7, 2.1 Computer Speaker. Fortunately, the shipping box was much larger than the item, so my blood pressure was quickly reduced. The speakers do have a small footprint and the taller contemporary shape is quite attractive. The subwoofer size is compact enough and unobtrusive in it's solid black boxy shape. I now have it placed on the bare wood floor, so my downstairs neighbors are likely not too happy with me right now. I will be placing a small carpet beneath it this afternoon.

Installation was intuitive and quite simple -- the most time consuming aspect was removing all the plastic. I didn't even notice the visual directions for set up are imprinted on the inside top flaps of the box. Because there is no bottom covering on the speakers by design, I'm especially careful when moving the speakers from one position to another. You'll get a different sound depending upon what surface you place the speakers. In the past hour, I've listened to Bob Dylan, The Grateful Dead, Johnny Cash, Radiohead, Sigur Ros, M.I.A., my Dad's dictation of his life story, Charles Mingus Lama Karta, The Black Lips, David Sedaris and Luka Bloom. The least pleasing on these speakers was a classical piece by Schubert which demonstrated the "muddy" nature of this sort of speaker system. Now this is a wide variety of music and sounds and my impression is that this is a really nice system which for the most part I would recommend. There's also an AUX input on the front of the speaker with controls so it can be hooked up to another electronic device of choice. Being able to adjust the volume, treble and bass gives me simple control options but by using the iTunes Equalizer, I can adjust to my preference with each cut. Throughout the years, I've purchased and used various speakers for my stereo, iPod, computer and entertainment systems, and I'm very impressed with these! Can't now wait to watch a movie and hear how these speakers reproduce the sound!

I first bought this GPS several months ago when Costco had it on sale but ended up returning it because I was not pleased with the time it took to recognize my location. More specifically, I would be on the Capital Beltway surrounding DC and the stern female voice would repeatedly tell me to make a U-turn. Impossible. I then used a friend's hand-me-down Magellan which would not hold a charge, not recognize the location and simply needed to be retired. Enter Amazon and their great price for the Navigon 2100 max. Since I'd read that the device was improved with the Fresh Maps update, I purchased Fresh Maps and I highly recommend you do the same if you're contemplating this beautifully sleek GPS.

If you have a PC, you are able to upgrade by connecting the GPS directly to your computer. If you have a Mac, then it's a little more complicated but so worth the effort. You need to remove the SD card from the GPS and transfer the downloaded software to the SD card with a card reader/writer and then reinsert the card into the GPS. I kept a backup of the original software on my hard drive just in case, but have had no need since the upgrade immediately worked. Now on to what I really like about this system.

The 4.3 inch screen is easier to view than the 3.5, particularly if you have many of the POI's selected for display. I first chose them all, then realized they obstructed my map because I'm in the DC metro area. Mine connects with a satellite in only a few seconds each time and reroutes immediately if I change my route. Previously, it would announce that it was rerouting, but it no longer does that, just does the work. Three choices for trip planning are fine enough for me, I tend to choose the Optimal Route. I love being able to select different destinations, too, if I'm going to different places. The address book is easy to access and locations are easier to save. Traffic support is a great asset and now comes free with this device -- I've been saved from many a jam and not have to be tuned into the radio for traffic reports on the 8's. I have the screen set to automatically change from day to night and have had no problem viewing the screen at any time. With the new software, you are able to turn off the GPS from the touchscreen in addition to the usual power button at the upper right hand edge. I love the 2D/3D view, especially when I'm approaching a multi-lane area and I'm unsure as to which lane I need to take. Two voice selections are fine for my needs, Dagmar is more pleasant, but the higher pitched Sarah gives the text to speech option (TTS), so that's the one I've selected. She's not very pushy, either, as some voices I've heard on GPS systems. In the pre-update version, her voice sounded more Germanic, I assume from its origin of Germany, but it's not as odd now. For me, this GPS is intuitive to use and I can make any adjustments from the touchscreen very quickly. I've yet to have a freeze of the system and it has always known where I was with one exception when I was off road on a gravel trail.

My only real criticism of this unit is the rigid cord which extends straight out of the bottom of the device, being so inflexible that I sometimes dislodge it when attaching the mount to the windshield. I'm not crazy about the mount either, but am trying to decide how to approach a new mounting system. I do not want the display obstructing my field of vision but am not ready yet to get a sandbag type dashboard mount. I'm thinking of constructing something myself using the little plastic disc which was included with this GPS system. Also included is the USB cord, but no AC power supply.

At the suggested retail price, I would never have made this purchase, but because it was a reasonable Gold Box offer, I leapt toward my first bluetooth earpiece.  The pink was not a selling point, but I preferred that to a more common black contraption, and I'm not at all disappointed.  It's more of a mauve than pink which was more pleasing to me.  It synched up immediately with my cell phone and I suspect it will do the same when this phone is replaced in 2009.  The manual was easy to read and understand and I had no difficulty placing the earpiece into the lovely leather carrying case/charger or removing it to use.  Although some have complained about short battery time, I have not experienced that and have not have the battery die at any time.  It is easy to check the battery level by depressing the two buttons on the device and observing the number of red flashes for remaining power.  The small size might be easy to lose for some, but I'm aware of that possibility and exercise caution when I put it in my bag or pocket.  Because of that small size, it takes only a second to plug the earpiece into the ear and I do not wear it unless I am on a call.  Realizing that it's lightweight, I am also cautious in more windy situations.  I had only one experience with a less than perfect call and was a bit disturbed until I realized the static was generated from the other end of the call.  In general, I like the fit, clarity, ease of use, and don't feel like I have a growth erupting from my ear.  I'd buy this again.

Listening to my favorite playlist via Amazon Music on our new 4th generation Echo. Wow, the sound is dramatically improved. I'm hearing instruments clearly that I never noticed with our older Echo. Awaiting the battery base (and nicer Florida weather) so we can have Alexa with us to play music on the patio.

I wear it all day while working in my home office. It's comfortable and has true noise cancelling. There are times the lawn is being mowed or the leaf blower is going outside, and it does not disturb the people I'm speaking with on the phone. It charges quickly and lasts for 6+ hours of talking.

This recent purchase is a backup keyboard and I'm not using it yet because the coffee I spilled did not affect the performance of the old keyboard. The keyboard in the picture has been in use since January of 2017. The fact that I purchased a 2nd one in case the original stops working tells you how much I like using it.

Pros: the ergonomic layout is better than most split keyboards; it is super quiet--I interview people on the telephone and type while they are speaking--with my former keyboard, people would ask what all the noise was and could I hear them okay--this keyboard eliminates that distraction completely; battery life is long.

Cons: several letters have disappeared (E, R, T, S, D, F, C and most of the G and N) so it is a good thing that I'm a "touch typist" and don't need to look at the keyboard much; I don't have small hands but it is a bit tough to reach the & key while pressing the shift key; the wrist rest shows a lot of wear after a short time.

Overall, I recommend the keyboard if you are looking for a quiet and ergonomic keyboard.

I've been using this keyboard and mouse since it arrived on 12/27/16 and it fits my use perfectly. I work from a home office and got a treadmill desk for Christmas and needed a wireless keyboard so I can move it back and forth between the treadmill side and the keyboard tray on the other half of the desk for when I'm seated. I got so used to a split ergonomic keyboard and had difficulty finding this style in a wireless keyboard.

This is low profile enough to fit under the desk when I slide the keyboard tray out of the way. You can use it with or without the very easily magnetic attachable riser to raise the wrist rest; I use it without the riser when on the treadmill and with it when I'm seated so this is a great feature for me. I suppose it is somewhat equivalent to using the legs on traditional keyboards.

A large part of my day is spent on the phone with executives and I often type while talking with people (conducting telephone interviews). This keyboard is so much quieter than my old one! Now people don't even know that I'm typing while speaking with them. It did take me a day or two to get used to the keyboard layout since it is a bit different from my old wired ergonomic keyboard.

The mouse seemed too big initially but now I really like it.

I use the number keypad a lot and having it separate from the keyboard is sometimes not the most convenient. However, if it was attached to the keyboard, the set up would be too big for my keyboard tray and mouse so it is more of a positive than a negative with the new treadmill desk set up.

Overall, I am very happy with it and recommend it wholeheartedly. You will especially like it if you are used to using an ergonomic keyboard.

Good bass, nothing too powerful, but waay better than a phone. Fits into your car cupholder, in large pants pockets, backpacks, etc. Never hand any problems with hooking it up bluetooth to my devices, though the other features admittedly confuse me a little... there's basically one button to switch modes? It's just me, but I don't use the other modes cuz I honestly don't understand how to get 'em going.

I love the ring doorbell. It looks nice at my front door, especially with the option of different colored faceplates, and it works well. The video and sound quality is good. The app is easy to use, and I like the ability to get notifications on my phone when there's motion at my front door. I dont live in a high crime area but it's always nice to have that extra set of eyes on my home. Plus it comes in handy for me because while I'm at work I'm able to see my son leaving and coming home from school every day.

The battery lasts a long time before needing to be charged. I've had it for over a month already and I'm still on my original charge. I ordered a spare battery so that when I need to charge it I can just switch them out and not have to worry about interruption in service. The battery charges with a regular phone charger so it's easy and convenient.

My only complaint with the ring doorbell is that in my situation the motion detection is almost too good. I live in a townhouse that is only about 15-20 ft from the street so anytime a car drives by or someone walks down the sidewalk, it triggers my camera. In the settings there is the ability to adjust the field of view slightly but it hasn't been enough to avoid the false alarms. I dont really fault the product for this. It's doing what it's meant to do. Just keep that in mind if you intend on using it in a high traffic area like I do. Other than that, I've been very happy with it and I'm glad I got it.
I bought this to plug my son's Wii into our smart TV that doesn't have AV jacks. Works great. My only complaint is that it requires being plugged into a power source.

Excellent beginner or backup set. Pretty decent quality equipment for the price. I'm by no means a professional photographer but it's a hobby/passion of mine. I wanted to try my hand at portrait photography and thought I could practice on my kids with this low-cost set up. Definitely worth the money. I'm glad I bought this.

Got for Black Friday deal. Great little piece made my tv feel new. It does not do volume control or on off. I brought the 4K one as well which is much better just due to volume and power but ruin which you get used to.
Like the product. Can be slow at times however for the Black Friday price my old tv has brand new life. However I can not get the volume controls to work maybe due to how old my tv is.
Awesome flex but only ok sound

My new computer monitor has very poor, nearly nonexistent sound capability.  I don't have enough room for two large speakers, nor did I want to have to move everything to plug a speaker into the back of the processor.  This speaker works beautifully.  I simply plugged it into the USB drive on the front of the processor and immediately was able to hear what was playing on the monitor.  In fact, my husband could hear it in the next room.  I especially like that I don't need to keep the speaker plugged in all the time as I only listen to videos occasionally.  One speaker, easy setup, great price - win-win!

I bought this because my new car doesn't have a CD player.  I wanted one compatible with Bluetooth, which this is, but unfortunately it doesn't sync to the car.  A separate Bluetooth transmitter also didn't work with my car (although it did work with the CD player), and I wound up with wires everywhere. I had to go out and buy a separate portable phone speaker in order to use the CD player in the car, but once I did that everything was fine, and the sound is decent event though it doesn't play through the car speakers.  I just put the CD player and attached portable mini-speaker on the passenger seat or the center console rather than try to wire everything into the USB ports.  Actually, much less complicated that way and so much easier to move around.

The hard drive on my computer was more than half full, and I wanted a place to store all my computer videogames.  Being technologically incompetent, I hesitated to buy an external hard drive. Since I am a fan of audio equipment, I usually replace my receiver every 2-3 years. I purchased the Onkyo TX-NR626 on WOOT a little over a year ago. This unit replaced a Yamaha RX-V671.  I will try to leave things out of this review that other reviews have already talked about.

Wi-Fi and Bluetooth
To my surprise, I have never had any issues with Wi-Fi or Bluetooth. My Wi-Fi network uses WPA2, and I use a variety of Android devices to Bluetooth to the receiver. This means that from a back room of the house, I can turn the receiver on via the Android App, and Bluetooth whatever I want to whoever is in the living room.  One time out of the blue I made thunder play loudly to an unsuspecting room full of people and animals. The pandemonium that was created as a result of that, was both memorable and delightful.

Remote
The remote on my RX-V671 never saw much use, due to how cumbersome it was to use  The remote on this Onkyo is so easy to use, that I now use it instead of my Logitech Harmony.  I use the Onkyo remote to control my receiver (of course), the TV set, the xBox, and the LG Blu-ray player.

Sound / Setup
It sounds as good as the RX-V671, but is easier to use.  I felt that the Yamaha had too many unnecessary settings, which actually made me want to play with it less.  What I don’t like about the Onkyo though, is that the labels for the buttons on the front of the receiver are hard to see.

The famous HDMI sound issue
This happened to me twice over the last year.  Each time I needed to unplug it, and plug it back in to resolve the issue.  I don’t think this is related to heat, at least in my case, as I have plenty of room on top for ventilation which is open on either end to enable a cross draft.

You can plug your favorite headphones right into the remote on these! There is no need to mess with a quirky Bluetooth set, that doesn't sound as good as your corded Sennheiser, Audio-Technica, or alike.

I think the Roku is much easier in general to use for streaming than any other device I have tried including: Chromecast, Xbox, LG Smart Apps, Onkyo Smart Apps, Yamaha Smart Apps, Wii, or a regular media PC.

Why I chose the 439 over the rest

Clamping force and comfort
I have a large head, and have read comments from other large headed reviewers stating that some of the other big brands are not comfortable for long periods of time. I can tell you that these are comfortable for both my large head, and others with smaller heads that have tried them. Not sure how they would be for large ears though. I have regular sized ears, and they fit perfectly.

Replaceable Cord
These are the only headphones in the lower-mid-range closed back Sennheiser line that has a replaceable cord. You would think that the 449 does (since it is a higher number) but it does not. Yeah I am pretty good with a soldering iron, but that doesn't mean that I actually want to use it.

Why I exchanged the 518 for these

Sound isolation
The open back design of the 518 was more prohibitive to my lifestyle than I had originally anticipated, as they leak more sound than I thought. You could actually hear the sound leakage in the next room if the doors were open, and the house was fairly quiet.

I watch a lot of cartoons and strange independent dramas. I also listen to ancient heavy metal, along with a smattering of other unlikely musical genres. Few people want to hear that combination of things spewing from my headphones. Now I can enjoy watching things like the Rectify (Especially the Drip Drip episode) without having to explain later to others in the next room.

Roku and Smart Phone use.
The 518 has a 1/4 plug, and the 439 has 1/8. I like to use the headphones with my Roku 3 remote a lot, and having a 1/4 to 1/8 adapter in my pocket with the Roku remote adds a lot of bulk. On the other hand, whenever I want to use the 439 on my old school stereo, I just use the included 1/8 to 1/4 adapter, which isn't really a hassle at all.

This item is one version of the OSSC, and turns out it is not case-compatible with the official one, having several different components populated on the board, so it will not fit in the normal OSSC cases.

It is not at all confidence-inspiring that the manufacturer here deviated from the official board layout and component selection. The PSU is extremely cheap, and some things are just incorrect.

Some of the components I noticed were different are:

- the screen: The height of the screen is quite a bit lower than what's shown in pictures of the official OSSC, and on closer examination, it appears the screen was soldered to the wrong side of the board because of layout issues.
- the buttons: the buttons here have yellow nubs on top, but the official one has low profile tactile buttons. This is another point where 3D printed cases made for this (such as those sold by Laser Bear) will interfere with this OSSC, preventing the case from closing.
- The audio select switch: the switch is mounted to the bottom of the PCB instead of the top. There appear to be traces for the switch on the top of the PCB, but it's not clear why they were mounted to the bottom of the board. Again, this is an issue because cases will have allowance for this switch, and expect the switch to be located on the top of the PCB.

Given that these components were swapped or moved, I can't be certain about the rest of the component choices, and given how cheap the power supply is, I'm not confident at all that the manufacturers here prioritized quality over price in any way whatsoever.
