The sound on the speaker is not very loud but loud enough if used in a small room but you can hook it to a louder spreadsheet via Bluetooth. I keep one on the bathroom with a nightlight attached to it. I play my music when doing my business and it's loud enough considering my bathroom is not that big. You can manually turn off the mic if needed. It plugs right into my socket without any wires dangling. The nightlight comes on when darkness is detected and goes off when it's bright. Great for a midnight bathroom run. If you choose not to use any accessories, the USB port on the bottom can be used as a phone charger. Alexa works like a charm on this. Overall, I really like this product.

I CHOSE this model over another because of the supposed built-in Alexa compatibility. You can indeed connect the soundbar to an Echo device *as a regular bluetooth connection*, but the instructions to enable Auto VA (auto virtual assistant mode) via Bluetooth so the soundbar maintains a BT connection with Echo while using other inputs DOESN'T WORK. The instructions say to first connect the soundbar to Echo via BT (✅), and then to press the Bluetooth button for 10 seconds to enable Auto VA (❌). HOWEVER; after five seconds, the soundbar enters Bluetooth pairing mode. I've tried dozens of times, connecting and disconnecting the BT connection with Echo and restarting and resetting the soundbar: NO DICE.

It's frustrating because this feature is in the title of the product and is clearly described in the User Manual — and yet it doesn't work at all.

I imagine Auto VA via AUX input works okay, but that means I have to move my Echo or get a wicked-long audio cable, neither of which I want to do.

However, otherwise the soundbar sounds fine. Not quite as good as the Bose Companion computer speakers I used previously, but whole worlds better than the built in TV speakers. It's just a shame that I have disconnect and reconnect to Alexa so often.

Works great for using my laptop with the media stations in the classrooms I teach in. This is clearly a solidly manufactured cable and feels very sturdy. The video always works, but sometimes the sound doesn't come in. I'm confident it's something to do with my laptop since putting it to sleep and waking it up seems to fix it.

I can't get over how good this sounds for the size. For real. My last radio was just a tad bigger and it sounded like it had paper cups for speakers. This sounds great. I keep it in my office at work so I can listen to NPR while I work.

Why are they not available now? It’s a great device!!! I’m not a ‘tech’ person at all! I’m a single female that’s 65 years old and have problems with almost all of these things EXCEPT for this one! This is a small, handy ‘plug’ with a mini speaker - great for a relatively unused room. I have mine in my 3rd spare bedroom that I use for my ironing board, drying rack, etc. I’m home alone just about every day and I have music playing from the time I get up in the morning till I fall asleep at night and with this I can now hear it while I’m doing my laundry chores. The sound quality isn’t great but acceptable for its purpose and Alexa responds quickly and very well with my voice commands, whether it’s music related or something else! I like that it’s both a small plug and has some of the capabilities of an Echo Dot, Show, and the other larger Smart devices. I can also use the USB port and normal, non ‘smart’ outlet. The cost was minimal and I’m really bummed that I can’t buy this anymore! I only started using ‘smart’ things several months ago and now I’m slowly adding more and more. Amazon, PLEASE make this again or an ‘identical’ item! Note: I gave this 3 stars because of the combination of the item (5*’s) and the fact that it’s no longer available (0*’s).

I am a single 60+ year old female so I can’t really go into much detail about all the features of this TV. What I can say is that the picture quality is great and I have no complaints about the sound being very low as one reviewer mentioned. This problem is likely due to the program channels and not the TV itself, at least it’s what I’ve noticed. This is my 5th TV and the largest one that I’ve ever had. I have one that is also a Samsung and a Sony, LG, and Insignia - each one a different size. This size (as are all TVs) is based on the diagonal measurement and not the width - so it should be able to fit into a space that’s not larger than the given length and height. The best part is the price and the ability to have it delivered to me at home. This spares having to go to a Best Buy or other store and being overwhelmed with the variety of brands, sizes and salespeople hovering over you and trying to make you buy the most expensive one. The delivery was mixed up and it took a few extra days to get it back to my town and it was delivered without any damage.

Awesome!

I have the QC25's and I have been very happy with them, when the QC 35's came out i was like Meh I dont need them boy was I wrong.
The sound quality and build are terrific and they feel light on your head which is a huge plus for me. I have been wearing mine everyday and I do not miss have a cord one bit! I would say I have used them around 15 hours so far and it still says 40% charged!
Well worth the extra $49.00 over the QC 25's

Works excellent!
All functions work and the sound is good. No issues with era pads fit well and did not have to replace them. This is a great buy and fast shipping!
Bought these for my wife and she loves them! came packed very well and shipped fast. sound quality is better than my sons beats thats for sure!

I have an older iPod about which I'm sentimental because a loved one gave it to me with all the money they had at the time. Unfortunately its storage capacity was small and I had to listen to the same things repeatedly if I was out walking or doing chores that didn't give me time to re-load from my computer. Enter this wonderful little extra memory card ... not only is it adorable (it bends!) but it holds enough music and audio books to keep me happy and hearing new material for several days. This company is a lovely one with which to deal, as well ... I am beyond 5-stars happy with both my bendy memory disk and this wonderful company. We'll be doing business again soon. Many thanks from a happy customer!

As the title says, they are the BOSE sound quality you are used to.  The charging case is sleek, modern and designed well.  They are waterproof and also come with different sized buds to create the perfect fit.  The phone conversations were clear and crisp, as well as all my favorite music.  Would definitely recommend.

The Echo dot was a great value. Overall a great way to ask Alexa anything, no connectivity issues, volume adjustments are easy to spot and the shape of it is fun looking.  There is a light ring on the bottom for different indications, which I've only remembered green is "you have notifications".  Still learning but the set up was quick and easy.  My only gripe would be the sound quality when playing music.  I know this isn't a Bose speaker but I expected a little better than it is.  All in all I would get another one, if only for the convenience of being hands free.

I was pleasantly surprised when I received the screen savers.  There were 2 in the pack, a microfiber cleaning cloth, lint remover tapes, and cleaning solution wipes.  The pack also contained a plastic guide to help with alignment for the tempered glass protector for easy installation.  Once I removed the air bubbles, the protector was an exact fit and the clarity of my iPad screen was amazing.  Such an awesome product for a pretty decent price.  It arrived ahead of schedule and very well package.  I would definitely recommend.

Item as described, shipped super fast!  Once I figured out how to pair it with my Nikon D3400, it worked great!  I was laughing out loud to be able to click away without holding the camera.  I have a tripod on order, so excited to be able to take still shots and not have to hold the camera waiting for lightening, fireworks etc.  If your camera is listed, get one.  You will have a lot of fun with it!

It's a little on the cloudy looking side which I can see would be unappealing to some people but in all honesty no one sees my laptop but me so I don't care much. I did dock one star for that reason though because it could be better aesthetically. Other than that it's great. Doesn't slow down my typing and doesn't move around as I've had some skins do in the past.
Love it. Clear crisp loud! Good price and good battery life.

I'm surprised at the build quality, overall functionality and sound of this unit (including bluetooth which I'm listening to as I write this).

The only caveat would be I wish they had tuned the speaker for a little more bass. The volume is definitely centered in the middange/treble zone; when a trumpet came on I had to turn it down. The bass is there somewhat just subdued. The volume knob goes to loud too fast. It'd be hard to adjust very low. I think the price is too high.

However it's instantly likable and as I got it exclusively to stream CBS Radio Mystery Theater next to my bed I'm unconcerned how it would reproduce modern music. Listening to my 20s/30s/40s playlist the bluetooth connection is solid, no hums or crackling, and volume is more than loud enough. Sounds great! Love the light, knobs, feel. Happy purchase!

I updated to 5 stars! This has a very clear, loud and upfront sound; not at all like ClearClick wooden radios which are crackly, introduce artifacts, skips, are muffled, and have a very low bluetooth volume and poor connection.
After using it a year it's still my go-to favorite radio. Reception, durability, quality. And sounds great with or without high quality headphones.

I returned $50 Edifiers because these have much better bass and more trilling guitar highs and are just more... LOUDER! Plus I need the earloops for them to stay in my left ear.  Only caveats they seem just slightly right of center and the case isn't charging. I listen to mostly stadium rock and these fit the bill like my Sony and Mpow headphones.  For $15 they're a definite keep.

This is the one that I'm keeping. I bought a lot of radios including vintage GE and watched many videos, and I liked the Eton Elite Executive a lot and the included folding protector/case, it's great size for travel; but this radio by modern standards is HUGE (Executive is dimension of Field speaker grill), bigger than the GE, sounds FANTASTIC. Really heavy, more than substantial, and comes with the vinyl brown case that does not have speaker or control holes.

I honestly didn't think they built radios like this anymore. Size, weight, construction of quality vintage, but reception, functionality and features of new. I absolutely love this radio. And it's cheaper than all the more expensive smaller ones that can't begin to sound like this.

Padded handle that doesn't quite leave enough room for fingers (I'll find out if it adjusts), and carrying strap with the satchel. I didn't pay more for the satchel so good deal. Reception superb. I saw lower reviews on this particular model so I'm really glad I took the chance and got it with the others, which are going back, because while they're great this is greater. Also some newer brands don't have better reception or circuitry despite some reviews.

Did I mention I really LOVE this radio?

Update: Still loving this radio, no regrets. Great for AM/MW (DSP) DX. Oklahoma, California, Texas. Something on EVERY frequency; I didn't have patience to wait and hear each call sign. So don't know about bad reviews on shortwave, but on AM this outperformed all the others esp. smaller expensive ones by a mile. You need DSP to filter digital interference these days. AM DXing is what I bought it for so very satisfied. Also Bluetooth works/ sounds great.

A Little Later: Okay, I got to try it more and used a clip-on antenna and headphones. Yeah, as others have noted this is totally deaf on shortwave. I got best SW results with a $16 Supersonic. Really. After trying quite a few. But for Shortwave this isn't it you'll have to look elsewhere. I still prefer this radio for its excellent AM DXing reception (and FM!), speaker sound, and build quality. And BT.

Incidentally to turn the annoying beep off turn radio off, press and hold ALARM and display will say beeping off. Done.

[[VIDEOID:8b366adad91b69c42b315be4becc6f62]] Yes, it's plastic. Yes, it's expensive. But i couldn't afford things like this as a teenager and was a poor kid in a rich school. Amazon is about changing all that. The sound is decent. i love the lights. no one else seemed to want the pink, er rose-gold one. my biggest fear is the lights will go out. the equalizer display is fantastic and works! (all 4 speakers are blue). there's a treble, bass, and balance knob instead of mid level. i won't use the cd player. 3.5mm aux in and headphone jack on top. turning light show off turns off *all* lights except tiny power and fm stereo red dots on top and red lettered cd track number display in front and blue bluetooth dot on top.
if the light display remains working I'll remain thrilled!

As a tip the coin battery goes in fancy side (also marked +) in first, behind the little black tab which is behind the trap door in the back. This is because the connections touch the center and edge separated by the dark ring on one side. The compartment could be to store the included antenna except the radio isn't portable so doesn't make a lot of sense. None of this was mentioned in the instructions which is a one-page get started sheet. If there's a larger instruction manual it was missing on mine. You have to wait 30 seconds for a station to be established before tuning up to the sub- channels (HD2, HD3) like all the modern HD portables. There is no AM, however I noticed some of the major talk AM stations (ClearChannel) are broadcast on the FM sub-channels. The sub-channels include news talk, sports, and music (often oldies). Push the Mode on top for settings, then the Volume selects from the menu and pushes in to enter selection, then you adjust selection parameter with Tuning, then push Volume again for previous menu or Mode to leave settings or just wait and it'll return to normal after a few seconds on its own. It's more simple than the instructions once you get the hang of it and the controls, being the Volume and Tuning knobs are consistent throughout the menus.

For an HD receiving and FM table radio, after turning the bass up all the way (to level 12), it sounds good and performs adequately. It does not receive all my local stations unless they're powerful.

Bluetooth is where it totally fails me. The sound is unacceptable even with volume up to 20 (radio is loud and clear at 6). It might be good enough for narration but not music. The volume difference, and quality, between radio and bluetooth is extreme. Again on FM and HD radio the sound is good and clear on volume 6 with the bass turned up. Odd the sound on bluetooth was so poor.

I started the return process just to see what would happen since it's shipped from a 3rd party and received the shipping label within a few hours without giving a reason. I decided to keep it because of the good radio sound and HD and quality build and space-saving form-factor. It's white in the front and wood around sides. Black plastic in back. You can choose the display text to be orange, blue, or white. It displays the time and date when off. It is AC powered only and does not run on battery.

If you merely want to listen to strong local FM stations and HD sub-channels I would say it's worth the price.

[[VIDEOID:c68bfe5e1896c7feea704ebab5fd4d8f]] Finally! After all the stuff I've had to send back, the portable/table radio I've been looking for! Surprisingly heavy (I thought batteries were in it) and well-built for modern plastics, by today's standards this is built like a tank. Stands up well no problem, sturdy. Again for today's standards. Handle good. Sturdy a/c plug. Plugged it right in and sounds loud and surprisingly full if you're not a basshead, not a Tivoli, but really good compared to everything else (larger radios that were positively screechy).

And tuning to my classical station that some radios can't get easy, no interference without pulling out the antenna, which is also think and well made. This is the familiar experience you remember despite modern plastics. Wish the dialface was stark white? So happy I bought this, mostly by accident following video link to another product, never heard of this brand, but I'm an instant fan! Replacing a wooden table radio I purchased that starting popping off and I was afraid it was a fire hazard so I returned that. Good thing for Amazon's extended Holiday return policy! So happy I bought this!

Also I personally like the volume/off wheels. I bought Allmax 'D' cells just for this!

I was surprised at the sound quality from these phones right out of the box. I'm a fan of the Sony sound and normally use MDR-7506 with my home equipment. These have balanced highs and lows, and a good stereo field. The only caveat they don't go really loud. They're adequate, probably as loud as my old ears should listen anyway. But i turn my phone up all the way which is unnecessary with my earbuds. For $11, definite buy.

Update: I got my 3.5mm to 1/4" adapters today and was able to try these with my home theater stereo in place of my 7506's. Looks like I already mentioned how good they sound. They weren't very loud on my Amazon tablet. They were better with a handheld radio. Softer on my phone. With my home stereo (Sony) they were amply loud and surprisingly good. I don't like "on-ear" phones. But the reproduction of this pair was excellent and lives up to the Sony standard, for the most part. Obviously you have to have a device that pushes enough watts to power them adequately. I had different volumes with different devices, from full volume to way too soft. The stereo field width and separation isn't quite the 7506's, so don't expect something 10x the price. But for $11 they're more than fine. If you're device can power them.

I'm going to be the odd one out and give this handled portable my approval. I've tried nearly every handled radio on Amazon and sent them all back for various reasons, chiefly they would wobble or couldn't stand up by themselves. Some had controls making it impossible to tune.

Yes, this is feather-lightweight plastic, etc. However this radio is just slightly thicker than the others and stands by itself even as you adjust the all- frontal knobs if you're careful; it tunes well and sounds loud and well, more treble than bass. The handle is flimsy and flops back down by itself but I don't in danger carrying the light radio by it. Easy to take to beach, etc. and loud enough for outdoors. When I live within 1,000 miles of a beach I'll take it there.

I unboxed it and tried the knobs and to my surprise it came on lol. Then I opened the battery compartment hearing rattling and the empty 'C' or 'D' cell (?) compartment was empty but contained the power/charging usb cord as the radio was playing. The 'AAA' battery designation in description is wrong. The most important part is it has a good wide base and sits securely for its weight (one bird feather) without wobble. I also like that not only are the controls on the front and simple,
but the top and both sides are free of controls and the radio is large enough. Keeper.

Update: After trying an old radio with batteries that nearly blew up, I'm appreciating this even more. The lithium charging system works better than the old. Still playing out of the box with me not installing batteries, plugging it in, or anything. Great!

A year later now and happy with it still after several new and vintage radios couldn't get my local stations. This rocks. Sorry it's double price what I paid for it; I liked the silver better. It's got a brand stamped on it now.

I've bought a lot of radios on Amazon; I've had to return most of them for very poor quality including impossible tuning.  This is one of the ones I kept.  All the features work and I'm currently listening to it while charging it with my phone micro usb cord.  I especially love the 2 color lights to function.  It sounds really good,  better than cheaper bigger radios I've tried,  and it's built more solidly than they were.  The tuning is feather light touch and much easier than the others with less static and a harder to get classical station I like comes in clearer.  You're not going to listen to it from your pocket because just handling it the tuning knob will change frequencies; you have to treat it like a table radio.  But it performs as one,  admirably.  Bluetooth connects easily,  sounds great and the whole radio is a joy.  I believe this brand also makes a larger size portable/ table radio with a handle I'll have to try as I've not found a good one yet.  But this is at the top of my keepers.

I got the "acceptable" unit for total $17 (sorry), one foot pad is missing, I'll innovate. Firstly, I had wanted the chrome front but couldn't afford it and didn't want to wait a week; when I saw this used for the price I just pushed the button.

From the pictures you would think the front is all matte black, it is not. It's actually a very dark brown and the controls are a dark bronze, in shiny metal; closer to chrome aesthetic and looks far better with more tones than the photos would suggest. I'm actually happy I bought the darker color now seeing it. I tried to capture this on my pic, but it's too dark and still doesn't capture the wonderful appearance.

Plugging it in and turning it on was instantly satisfying, easy to use controls, no stiffness, good quality, lights work, radio is a deep amber or orange. Nice wood, looks and operates easily and great.

Tuning to a somewhat hard to get classical station locally was surprisingly easy and the signal came in loud and clear, unlike the other radios I've tried from Amazon. It felt like an old stereo where you didn't have to give it thought and was instinctive in the first 30 seconds without the difficulty and poor reception and static and crackling of tuning and volume controls or pops of turning it on nearly all cheap modern radios have now.

Bluetooth connected and performed seamlessly, perhaps a little softer than the radio but not horribly so. And the sound... On both radio and bluetooth the sound quality is superb; *just* enough bass without being muddy and the treble is good and clear. Bass in the voices and high pitches in the music, and very loud without screech or static at still low volume on the knob, with room-filling sound on FM and bluetooth.

This is the most pleasing product I've purchased from Amazon in a long time, especially in the radio category.

Update: After trying several others, I bought a second one! Like New $21. The only thing I notice is neither sits perfectly evenly, there's a slight wobble, even with all four feet pads. No biggie. Love the radio, excellent big sound, bass, but not muddy. Best radio on Amazon, and a true "table radio".

Just get it. This is my new go-to radio. Blows the 910ET away at half the price. Superior sensitivity, selectivity, stereo signal reception, and sound quality which is both bassier and LOUDER; stereo FM way louder and better sound (more bass) over quality earphones with a much stronger and stable stereo signal and spatial field. AM and SW sensitivity also superior to the DSP digital tuning 310ET.

If you're older and grew up instinctively "DXing" on your clock radio in the 1970's, this is the experience you're looking for. So much more fun than letting an ATS or ETM circuit do it for you, and again it gets more stations on both FM and SW and that's without an added antenna. This one comes with a free clip-on antenna to boot. But natively with telescopic I'm getting more SW than 910ET with SW antenna plugged in. As mentioned this doesn't cut sound during tuning inbetween frequencies. Seriously, heed this tip and turn the analogue volume on the left all the way down to bottom before turning the unit on the first time; nearly broke my eardrums.
This is my favorite radio by far, and closer to being truly portable.
One was lose, tightened it, one had a bag one didnt, plugged right in and noticeably superior sound quality especially in stage (field?) separation on streamed television like Hulu.

Amazon removed the account link to write/view past reviews and replaced it with purchase recommendations, uh-huh. I have only been able to stand two headphones in my life:  Sony studio/5xxx, and Phillips earbuds for their excellent reproduction.  I'm new to Bluetooth and knew I'd be taking a quality hit. However these are loud and bassy and the treble isn't boxed in too much like many sets and i enjoy listening to them in my chair. So i recommend them.

I find the skill set/setup dubious and the Alexa app was slow and very glitchy. This review is strictly about the device as a streaming Wi/Fi/Bluetooth speaker and sound quality.

I am an Amazon Prime customer and all my music is on Amazon streaming. Both ease of use (on Amazon Music/Pandora, etc. only) and sound in one word, Superb! I'm completely surprised because I own the $200+ UEBoom (which has been sitting unused on a shelf, I had to go look for it) and assumed the sound on that would be much superior as reviews and it's reputation suggest. Not so! I just listened back to back.

Without intending to compare them, I got my UEBoom to play while I setup the marvelous SOAIY Aurora projector (upgraded version), and in the back of my mind notice the music, not played very loudly because it's nighttime, was rather muddy; I think it wows people for its volume and base. On a whim I switched to my new Amazon Tap received today (I hadn't much time to experiment with it) and... Wow! Fantastic sound quality! Much more enjoyable than the popular UEBoom.

Better flat frequency response like a pair of reference headphones (like the Sony Studio MV6 I prefer), more clear definition and detail, not muddy, better treble response (I don't mean tinny or lack of bass), and bass rivaling that of UEBoom. Oh, the main thing I noticed also, which confused me at first, is the wide stereo dispersion (?), um, I mean wide field effect and stereo separation. I literally looked at the cylinder puzzled as to what I was hearing and mentally verifying only this device was on and was the source of the sound I was hearing.

The UEBoom always sounded merely monaural from one sourcepoint; this sounded like surround sound effect applied to a two-speaker (not 5.1+) tv. I was amazed at what my senses were reporting to me. Okay, I'm going to say it, to my ears, and I have a class D amplifier and 5 pairs of quality headphones of different brands, the sound of this Amazon Tap is superior, right out of the box. I was amazed. And of course streaming directly sans device is certainly more convenient. It "just works". (After connecting to your Wi-Fi network.)

I learned to say "playlist rock", since I have a playlist named rock, or it will play all my Amazon music in the genre "rock". I did ask for the weather after entering my zip code through the Alexa app, which I dislike, and it responded with detailed information. Luckily music playback works directly without a need for app use. I will now mention this superior sound quality is half the price of it's aforementioned similar-sized competitor. I'm now really glad I bought it :)
***
Update: I returned it. It couldn't find a track in my music library, I checked title of track and found it instantly on my Fire, but the Tap still couldn't find it; everything I've tried to do with it either completely fails, or I resort to a different device because it's quicker and more convenient. It's mistaken "no" for "yes" and when asking for Julie Andrews started playing the soundtrack to Fifty Shades of Gray. It's been sitting on the kitchen counter unused. I could spend the money elsewhere better (I purchased two Fire HD 6" tablets which are excellent, speedy devices and fit into my front pocket). To each their own.

I've owned a pair of these along with my Philips GoSpark player for years, and they've been the absolute best combination for sound quality of any mobile equipment I've tried ever. Be sure to set the player to "Full Sound" (wide spectrum with enhanced bass), and these buds handle it superbly; rings around any other phone/player I've tried including Sony. Also the over earloop keeps them on perfectly as you walk around. You don't need to press them into your ear to hear well, but it will increase your bass. Doesn't give ear aches some do. Mine, after years of use, still work fine (the player control is going) and I'm only getting a second pair if these because I was looking at phones on Amazon in passing and decided to do a search. I've had iPhones, etc. etc. This has provided a far superior sound experience. Don't pay more.

Solidly built, quality-crafted, and excellent 5-star functionality. The problem is, especially for a player and brand as good as this, the sound quality is disappointing enough (without being awful) to be distracting. The cheap player that comes with an ebook subscription has superior sound, for example. I wanted to get rid of the wires, but for this reason I'll go back to the cheap player. For the price, pass. I got it on sale in a box store for $35. I'll keep it, but I'm not using it. Don't pay this price for boxy, centered bass, and non wide-spectrum stereo without a high-top. $10 around-the-ear earbud set from competing brand offers superior sound. This player does not have sound presets or tone adjustments, which is sorely needed since the default fails.

This little camera exceeded our expectations for underwater photography.  We have only experienced the Fujitsu disposable underwater cameras in the past.  These produced very poor quality images and required being taken to Walmart or some other disappearing non-digital photo lab.  This little camera also does rather amazing underwater videos.  The only "negative" that can be said is that the lens (and who would expect a top notch lens for $29?) creates a fisheye effect so objects appear farther away than they actually are.  The photo was a still captured from a video.

I thought it was alright when I first got it. Sound was def better than the TV's sound.
My family doesn't want all these speaker wires running around in the living room so it was this or a normal/cheaper soundbar. I can tell you its worth it.
After seeing DUNKIRK with it's constant tense soundtrack throughout the movie, it was an experience. Much better than my friends Vizio 5.1 sound system and the Bose Solo doesn't even have any extra satellites speakers hah! (although after hearing this thing, it makes me wish I could add 2 speakers in the future in a modular way [which i heard you can't unfortunately]... The bass is pretty decent for such a small speaker. Think that was my main concern that it wouldn't have enough 'umfff' but has enough.

Product as advertised. Works great and no setup required. Just plug in and start using.

This is my second pair of KPH30s. (My cat chewed the first pair) The first month of wear they felt a touch tight, but they became more comfortable with use.
They are easy to adjust for sizing. Sound quality is good for general music listening and meetings.
One downside is that because the microphone is not directional, it picks up background noise. So if you are in a meeting, I recommend keeping yourself muted, especially if you are in an open space or if you are multi-tasking, as other participants will hear you typing.

I work from home. I needed a better camera than the one on my work laptop and this one is great.
It's easy to use. There is a bracket for it to sit on top of a monitor, but I found it to be a bit loose, so I put some bluetack beneath the camera to hold it in place and it's just fine.
I very much love that the camera came with a lens cover. The cover functions well.
Image quality & sound are very good for video calls.

The audio from these earbuds are way better than my other head set.
They are not noise cancelling which I need the most and my ears are small so these dont fit that well. Overall theyre great for the price. If you're looking for great audio these are it.

Tried these earbuds tonight. I listened to my oldies for over an hour and the clarity is fabulous!
I have had issues with other brands with them falling out of my ear. These fit perfect and did not fall out once. I'm happy with my purchase.

I bought this for my smart tv. Im having issues installing and tried everything and wasted hours. There is no video showing how to. Is there an app involved here? So frustrating!
As far as sound goes it is powerful. You can tell just by turning it on. Im sure itll work fine with a computer but thats not what I bought it for. I guess I'll have to take one day just to work on it as I have a list of other things I have to do. I will update after I figure this out.

UPDATE.
I have a Samsung smart tv and just purchased an upgraded Firestick.
I finally got the Soundbar connected! Had to go to settings and then to bluetooth. Sigh.

Purchased two of these Eufy 2K cams to test out and determine if they're good enough to replace the Wyze cams. These Eufy cams definitely capture higher resolution, more detailed videos compared to the Wyze cam v2. The pan and tilt feature is great when I want to remotely check different parts of an area and the pan/tilt action is very silent. You can set the cam to automatically track/follow motion when it's detected. The amount of time it takes to go to live view on a cam is within a couple of seconds and the alerts for motion is definitely faster than the Wyze cam v2. The time from me waving my hand in front of the cam and getting an alert on my phone is about 3 seconds or less.

I did experience issues with one Eufy cam where it would randomly start panning by itself and would do a 360 degree pan. The Eufy app works overall, but I did notice several times I had connection issues when trying to live view, but this issue also happens on Wyze cams, too.

You can set the Eufy cam to record only when motion or sound is detected or set the cam to continuous recording. If you choose continuous recording the video resolution will be reduced to 1080p resolution. For motion recording you can set up activity zones (specific areas you want to detect motion), adjust motion detection sensitivity, detect people, detect pets, and detect all other motion. Eufy's app is still missing the ability to view multiple live views of cams at the same time, which is a shame and hopefully they have a software update for that.

Overall, the Eufy 2k cam has great video quality, the pan/tilt motion is useful and silent, has a lot of features, and the price is competitive. They go on sale from time to time, so if you're not in a hurry then I'd wait for a sale.

Then, the files will play in the correct order on the device. This command will skip/ignore existing files if they already exist for whatever reason.

I bought my Fitbit One after a considerable amount of research among the various "life activity trackers" on the market. As I read, my focus shifted from the features of the products themselves to the personal goals I intended to accomplish once I started moving around. Ultimately, this helped me make my final purchase.

As you may have found, I discovered that despite the choices available to the consumer, I did not find a particular fitness tracker that measured all daily activities equally well. Design philosophies and marketing strategies seem to conspire to confuse the subject further and make it difficult to match a particular product to your needs. However, many excellent reviews have been published by Amazon-reviewers as well as by online product-review writers which were very helpful.

In any event, I was looking for a decent pedometer and sleep monitor. I can't run anymore due to arthritis, but I do enjoy walking and was pretty sure that I am not moving around enough. I also suspected that sleep apnea was starting creep up on me and hoped that the sleep tracking function could share some insight into my sleep patterns. I do some biking and other exercises, but I wasn't all that concerned about accurately tracking those activities through the Fitbit. Other electronic gizmos cover those areas.

The Fitbit appealed to me because it is tiny and can be carried discretely. Pedometers tend to work fine, but can be bulky and clunky-looking. The Bluetooth syncing was also a big selling point allowing data entry to be very simple, although for some the data analysis may be too simple. As of this writing, the Moto Droid just became Bluetooth 4.0 compatible with Fitbit products. According to the website more smartphones and tablets are being added on the Android platform. The package came with a small pocket clip, an armband for sleep tracking, and a charger.

Since I picked this product up, from RadioShack incidentally, I have been very happy with it. The pedometer function is very accurate and works equally well at measuring flights of stairs, which is a very nice feature. The small size is great for pocket carry, particularly in the change pocket of a pair of jeans, and can be clipped to pants or shirts depending on your preference. I compared the Fitbit's ability to monitor sleep patterns with a sleep monitoring app on my Droid. Gross measures of restlessness were comparable for each and it seems that I sleep better than I thought.

I've worn this unit during other activities, but the accuracy of movement that it measures is questionable. The Fitbit One, at least, is probably best suited for walking. Nonetheless, with consistent wearing, overall activity can probably be deduced, but will have to be inferred from data recorded as "steps".

In sum, the Fitbit One seems to be the closest match to an activity-meter that meets my personal needs. That means measuring natural everyday movement, such as steps, stairs, and sleep, in a tiny sleek wireless package. It helps raise my awareness of non-structured daily activity and is an important tool for overall health.

The cord is three feet long, perfect for me since I get tired of getting the cord tangled as I pace around during calls, but it might be a bit on the short side for some. For use with the computer the USB adds two feet between the USB port and the controlling buttons. The cord is round, and so far, has been resistant to kinks.

The volume and mute buttons are on the cord instead of the headset, I like this because I don't have to memorize the placement during a call and the indicator light for mute keeps me from forgetting that I have muted a call and no one can hear me because I muted to sneeze, cough or shush my cat.

The only drawback is that unlike with a bluetooth headset there are no volume or mute controls as part of the headset or cord when it is plugged into a smart phone.

I am using this for the bluetooth headset with my Windows 10 Computer.

It gave me better reception than what I had with my old dongle. It works exactly as I thought it would, the driver was built into windows 10.

I was able to walk to another room in my house (same floor) and still had clear sound. I am using this for a work IP phone and so far it has been perfect.

I got out of range when I went outside to check the mail. Then I had to turn the headset off then on again to get it to re-pair.

I would buy this again and would recommend it for anyone.

First off, because it wasn't entirely clear in the product description, this is for a car audio system, not a computer office system. So if you were hoping to hook this up in your home, you are out of luck.

Second, I don't know a lot about car audio systems. Half the time I'm in the car, I don't listen to anything at all. My usual commute is through several construction zones and I like to have all my attention on the traffic. I'm a nervous driver.

But I do like a nice sound system to listen to audiobooks on. I don't know if there is a comparable brand. But I am super impressed with this product

This is the nicest camcorder I've ever used. It's pretty lightweight considering all of the great features and it creates a great picture.

The zoom is so crisp I might finally get a video of the racoons fishing in my backyard that is watchable.

My son has been setting up a several lego stop video animations and so far, with this camera the movie is turning out crisper and better than we expected.

the new and upgraded anti shake feature is great for when you are trying to set up a longer shot. I haven't even touched on the more technical specs. For true artists this camcorder has manual control of the balance and white shift. You can manually adjust the zoom and shutter speed, something true professional find absolutely necessary. For us amateurs it offers a rare chance to experiment with home videos.

The sound on this was great and the auto wind correction was perfect because we were outside videoing and the wind didn't seem loud but I knew that another camera would have been overwhelmed by wind noises.

All in all a great camcorder.

This radio is a lot smaller than I thought it would be. I guess I've watched too many movies, because I was expecting something much larger, more military, like in a movie where a group of soldiers doubletimes it to a an evac point and then uses their radio to call in a chopper.

This radio is tiny by comparison, it's smaller than the freebie Clinique bag I got from Nordstroms. The radio itself is very lightweight too, which I would have already known if I'd taken the time to read the product description.

Also, it's a bit quiet. My husband and I had to strain to hear it, but since it is so lightweight, it wouldn't be much of a problem to carry it close to your ear.

The screen is tiny, but easy to read and once you've turned the radio on, it doesn't crackle and shoosh roaming through stations to find a live one. You have to manually turn it to the station you wish to listen to. The reception was pretty good, we live in a flat area and get a lot of radio stations, but I'd imagine that if you took this hiking, you might have trouble receiving anything, the antenna is a bit short.

The crank seems a little flimsy, I imagine that repeated cranking would cause a stress fracture that would eventually break, rendering the radio mostly useless. We haven't tried charging this with solar power yet, it's been super overcast here, but as soon as we have a sunny, rain free day, I'll give it a go.

Pretty good radio, I don't have any other emergency radios to compare this to, so I don't know if its flimsier than it's competitors.

Something to know about this is that this has a one way radio. I was a bit surprised that it had a radio at all. Our old camera didn't.

This also has a motion detection feature and because of the radio, it has a sound detection capability. This last bit turns out to be sorta annoying since we live off a busy road and every car or truck, every group of chatting people sets off the camera.

The picture is a lot clearer than we had before and I feel sure that if I set this up in a mouse traffic area (We had a terrifying mouse infestation last year) I'm sure this video is clear enough that we would be able to see the nasty rodents scurrying around on their horrible tiny little feet. Blergh!

All in all, this is a pretty nifty product.

Washing dishes is fun because I listened to the Battle of Hogwarts
I rode my bike up Grant that little bit faster because I was listening to the Hives while riding.
I didn't mind cleaning the toilet because I was just about to find out who was killing everyone in Gretchen McNeil's Ten.
Vacuuming the house went by faster because I created a Clean the House playlist with all my favorite kpop hits.
My root canal was still horrible, but at least I couldn't hear the high horrible drilling noise because I was busy listening to Jesse Eisenberg narrating White Cat.

Loading books is easy and there is enough memory for me to store several audiobooks that I downloaded to it.

Which means as long as I remember to bring it with me, and charge it overnight every once in a while, I will never be bored enough to read a pamphlet on gingivitis at the Dentist's office or waste time trying to remember the name of all of the dwarves in the Hobbit.

Update - the kindly people at Snugg sent me a new case, frankly, I wasn't real enthused about it, I figured it would probably still have the design flaws that made it a worthless $20 investment, but I was wrong, wrong, wrong. That will show me to stop being such a pessimist. I couldn't be happier with this now, it is everything I was hoping for, it clips on to the strap of my apron when I'm getting my cooking on, it hooks onto my backpack when I'm out riding. All in all, it is wonderful.

The headphone/earbud thingies I use, pretty standard ones called Coby also the ones that came with my ipod are able to make contact with the bottom portal which is now clear of the protective rubber. The carabiner clip seems slightly more substantial, I'd have to weigh it or take it apart somehow to verify this part.

So here's my old review, use this for info, in case you end up with a flawed Snugg, I guess you should just return it then, or maybe the bugs have been worked out now and all new Snuggs are good. Anyways, here's the old review with a listing of the pertinent problems.

!OLD REVIEW!

The problems Other people have mentioned, mainly the difficulty inserting the nano into the clip case, wasn't really a problem for me. Once it was in my iPod did appear to be very secure. The carabina clip is a bit of an exaggeration, it isn't nearly as sturdy as a carabiner, the like of which is used by climbers, this is more of a jewelry version and feels very lightweight, I'm not pleased with that.

The second fail for this case is that the rubber casing covers part of the headphone port.

I couldn't hear anything at all. It was so disappointing. For a moment I thought that my new iPod was defective. Nope.

It turns out that there wasn't enough room for the headphone jack to make a complete connection unless you peeled back the case wall and held it in place while listening.

These headphones are even better than I'd hoped. I tried them out for music, which is really the deciding factor when it comes to headphones, I allow a lot of leeway when it comes to sound for movies, audiobooks and tv shows.

But these were super nice. They are comfortable too. The cord is thick and is the right length to go from head to pocket with extra wiggle room and the sound adjuster is on the cord, tres convenient.

It was hard to see in the picture, but they are not totally white. there is a thin line of lime green that is on the out part, the color is bright enough that it almost seems to glow, like a LED light from the sides of the headphones, it looks pretty cool actually.

Like many. my laptop had the wireless module as part of the motherboard so when wireless went out I had no WiFi without an adapt0r. The first adaptor I got did not have enough range to reach the far side of the house where the wireless router was installed. This one gave me a good strong signal. It did not require any special drivers and they have a 24 hour technical support line, which would be good to have if you have any problems, I didn't, but it's a nice little feature.

The casing feels solid and sturdy but is nicely lightweight and portable, but it lost a star because it is bigger than I thought it would be and blocks the other USB port on the side of my laptop, that is until I found the included extension cord, this way the other USB port is free to use and the device can be mounted on the side of the screen with double sided tape so that it is like a TV antenna (a lame Mcguyver'ish solution to keep it out of the way of all the other stuff on my desk).

This is basically the same device as the IPEVO adapter. The difference is that this one doesn't have the audio out nor does it have its own power supply. Also the design is flawless, the IPEVO had a crooked HDMI IN.

The adapter is pretty basic and it delivers what it promises, a male HDMI to female VGA adapter compatible for use with Macs. Because of the adapter I've been able to avoid buying a new laptop or monitor for my son.

The positives about these headphones outnumber the negatives.

In no particular order;

1. Easy set up. Like all bluetooth devices, these headphones were a quick set up by simply turning them on and my mac responded with 'Do You Want To Use This Device?' The total set up time, approximately sixty seconds!

2.Excellent for VOIP gmail phone.

3. You can charge the headset, while you are using it. So on marathon conference call days, I can plug them in, while using them for about twenty minutes and then they are charged enough to last through a long, boring, three hour conference call (more's the pity!).

4. They charge off the USB port and they come with a cable for doing this.

5. They are lightweight and comfortable to wear, so no headaches!

6. Adjustable volume which is perfect for the hard of hearing.

We tore the couch apart, lifted the area rug, moved the television, I even checked the refrigerator! But no luck, the tiny white wafer that controls what we watch, when we watch itand if we watch anything at all was gone.

I called my hubby to find out if there was any way I could watch my favorite shows without it, nothing but dreadful silence from his end of the phone. So we ordered replacements, an heir and a spare. Yahoo, television!

This is the fifth headphone splitter I've bought. The others all suffered from the same, unusable defect, they were crapola and broke. Worse the sound quality was crackly and very 1985 (remember listening to tapes with a walkman, yeah, that's the sound quality I'm talking about).

I love this, I can listen to a book on tape while my hubby watches a movie and my kiddo listens to music, all of us lost to the world for a little while.

When this one wears out I'd order another lickity split!

Likes.

1. Simple to use.
2. My IPhone recognized the radio immediately, establishing a bluetooth connection. It never cut out.
3. The sound quality for both music and voice is very good. OTA radio less so, but that’s understood.

Dislikes.

I wish it was smaller. It’s much larger than I expected. Make sure you have enough room.

Overall.

The radio works flawlessly, both with four C batteries and by plugging it into an outlet. I tested the sound quality by playing some songs that I had downloaded from You Tube Premium, to my iPhone. The sound was very good. I then tested voice quality by playing an Audible book through it. It was Neil Gaiman’s voice, and the sound quality was very good. The volume was fine.

The bluetooth connection.
I set the radio to bluetooth, then went to bluetooth settings on my IPhone. The IPhone immediately recognized the radio, and paired. I played both songs and the Audible books, using this connection. I ordered the radio in order to listen to hours of Audible books at night. I usually fall asleep while listening, and it played throughout the night. That way, I wouldn’t be exhausting my IPhone battery constantly, as it uses a lot less battery life, when it doesn’t need to pump out volume. I have 2 Sonos systems and a bluetooth Bang and Olufsen sound bar. However, I wanted an easy to use radio right next to me in bed.

Likes.
Good build quality.
The sound quality of the music is fine.
Quickly connected to my Iphones and Ipads.
Comfortable enough.

Dislikes.
No plug provided.

I am an audiophile of sorts. I have a Bang and Olufsen soundbar, a Sonos Playbar, and a Sonos Beam. Obviously, these headphones do not compare. The music quality is very acceptable for my purpose.

My wife has the main TV on 12 hours a day at a mid volume. I like to sit in the same room because the comfortable chairs are in that room. The TV dialogue was very annoying to me. These headphones do a great job of allowing me to enjoy my music, as they block out the TV sound very well.

The quiet mode works well. It is not a true noise cancellation headphone. That’s okay. There is no annoying air pressure, just 3 modes of what is best described as programmed white noise, such as rainfall. Excellent for blocking sound.

The phone quality is excellent. You do have to hit a button on the earphones, if a call come in, or to call out. The “active,” feature shown in the instructions controls a lot of the features.

Although it was a snap pairing it with my iPhones and IPads I wasn’t able to pair it with my Samsung or LG OLED TV. I also wasn’t able to pair it with my Apple TV. I’ll keep trying.

I was considering buying the Airpod Max for my over the ear headphone. It’s been available for about $ 450. I figured I would upgrade every year. However, I checked the big yellow store and the trade in value was only $ 80, for the current model. WOW. Pay $ 450 today, get $ 80 tomorrow. No thanks.

My dislike was that a plug was not provided. It seems minor. However, I received a $ 90 pole lamp from Amazon and the plug was missing. I used a plug from another pole lamp and it blew out my new lamp. The wattage was too high. Who knew? The instructions say to use a 5W plug. Reading the microscopic lettering on the plugs has you guessing what the wattage is. I used a basic Amazon tablet plug and it worked.

Overall. The build quality is excellent and I believe it’s a very good value overall.

My Air-tag fit into the holder perfectly and works well.  I am submitting photos of this air tag holder, next to the Apple branded Air-tag holder.  I bought the 4 pack of air tags, and two Apple branded holders, which cost me about $ 35 each. The brown one is the Apple holder.  It is open on both sides as the photos show.  This holder is closed on one side. I was concerned that having one side closed would affect the transmission, but it instantly pinged very loudly.  This holder is a much better value.

This is a review of the new Beo Soundstage soundbar.

The instrumentals are amazing. Listening to the London Symphony, or Boston Pops, I can differentiate different string instruments.
Vocals are excellent.
I listened to podcasts and didn't find much difference in the speaking voices.
However, this replaced my Sonos Playbar which has fine audio.

This is an outstanding speaker with a poor app and virtually nonexistent instructions.
This would not be a problem if professional installation is used.
Because I have not used HDMI ARC previously, and I expect that most buyers will either use professional installation, or have experience with B&O or similar high end products, I did not deduct a star. My rating is based on the audio quality.

My current audio equipment includes a SONOS Playbar, a SONOS Beam, a SONOS one, and the Sony HT-X9000F.

I found this Beo Soundstage soundbar the most frustrating to set up.

Setup.

I did not get anywhere trying to get the unit set up using the app.
I have all Apple equipment, plus the Google mini, and the Google Home App.
I have a paid subscription to Google Play and You Tube Music.
Apparently, Beo and LG have a relationship, and the instructions for setting up the TV gave the setup instructions for the LG OLED TV. I have a Samsung TV.
The Beo app stated I could use the Google Home to set up the speaker. I have a Samsung TV. I followed the instructions in the app. That didn't help at all either. Not for WiFI, not for bluetooth.

I finally got bluetooth connected with no help from the app. My IPhone eventually connected to the Beo, via blue tooth. I never connected via WiFi. After connecting via blue tooth, and while listening to music via bluetooth, I again tried using the app to get WIFI. I received the message, error cannot connect to bluetooth. Sure, I was already using bluetooth.

I then moved the Beo to the room with the ethernet cable. I had never used an HDMI ARC connection. I made the connections.

I then turned my Samsung TV on, and the soundbar worked perfectly. My Direct TV remote worked perfectly without any pairing.
I then changed the source to my Apple TV. Everything worked perfectly. I used the Direct TV remote for that also. So, yes, your TV remote will control the sound.
I use bluetooth to play music from my IPhone.

Beo says the speaker can be wall mounted, or used on a tabletop.
My wife doesn't want it wall mounted.
My TV is wall mounted, and I wanted to place the Beo, vertical side up, on our entertainment center, directly under the TV. However, if used in the vertical or tall position without wall mounting, it will fall over. It is not balanced. I was very disappointed.
If used in the horizontal, or flat position, resting on a shelf, one of two soft pullout tabs must be removed. The power cord and HDMI cables can then go through the bottom of the speaker, to the back.

Beo needs to provide or sell, a small stand for table mounting. They do sell a large entertainment type piece of furniture, apparently adapted and with screws to hold the speaker in the vertical position. I'm not interested in another piece of furniture. A separate company sells three different accessories for the mounting. The one for tabletop mounting consists of a few pieces of soft feet. It sells for 100 pounds plus 20 pounds shipping from England. Probably weighs 5 ounces at most. I'll pass. Beo could have included that with the Soundstage. Probably costs under $ 1 to produce.

The speaker looks much more impressive in the vertical position, than it does laying flat on a table. For those that prefer a non intrusive look, the horizontal position would be fine. I tested it in both positions. In the vertical position, speakers aimed directly at my seating position sounded much better than in the horizontal position. However, when in another part of the room, as you may be when entertaining, the sound was better in the horizontal position. In the horizontal position, the speakers face my 12 foot ceilings

I did contact B&0 and asked if horizontal placement degraded performance. A simple question.
They e-mailed back. Contact a dealer and have an installation technician help me. More $$$$.

The speaker is just under 44 inches long, and weighs about 20 pounds.
There is no remote.
The wall mount is part of the speaker, and it just drops onto two small round holders put in the wall with screws. Screws are not provided.

The small box provided was missing the fabric puller, which would allow the speaker direction to be changed for tabletop placement.

Update.

I finally connected through the B&O app.
There are a number of optiuons.
One of features allows me to tell the speaker whether it is in a horizontal or vertical position.
On my failure to get a Wi Fi connection, I didn’t notice that the speaker has icons that can be pressed for pairing.
The icon, and others such as sound and the on/off icon are deliberately made hard to see in order to present a more streamlined appearance. In my initial setup, I set it up in the vertical position, propped up to keep it from falling over. I just didn’t see the icons.

There are 2 ways to hook up the TV to the speaker.
1. Plug the HDMI cable from the satellite or other type of receiver directly to the TV. Works great. An initial 20 second delay in sound when the TV is turned on.
2. Plug the HDMI cable from the receiver directly into the soundbar. This reduces your cable use by one. In both cases, the ARC connection remains the same. The sound was instant.

With option 2, on my Samsung TV, the "Anytime NET, " appears to cause compatibility problems.
The soundbar went on immediately, but after about 30 seconds, the video disappeared, and the message appeared, "check your connection." My Apple TV was not affected, neither was the OTA connection. The soundbar was working fine for both of those.

Troubleshooting.
On my Samsung TV, I went into menu. Nothing notable there.
I went into tools.
It showed the Anytime Net setting.
I clicked refresh, for the Samsung Genie, the Apple TV, and the B&O.
Each time I clicked refresh on the B&O, the video shut off, along with the sound.
I tried everything a number of times.
I went into every setting.,
I disconnected the Anytime Net. Nothing helped.
I have read that some older satellite receivers can cause problems with HDMI ARC.

I finally decided to go with my original connection, the receiver to the TV, and then the ARC connection for the robust sound. That did give me one extra cable, but is problem free.

Dec19th update.
Things coming together. I finally connected my google nest mini to my Soundbar. Went through the google home icon.
I selected my premium YouTube Music as my default service.
Now every time I want to listen to music on the Soundbar. I just say, Hey Google, Play Dean Martin in the family room. Works great.
I also noticed that when I request music, the Soundbar automatically turns my TV off.

I’m very pleased with the features. Just wish B&O had a 30 minute You Tube video walking buyers through the features.
Would have avoided a lot of frustration. I really love the features and the sound quality.

I am using this watch daily, and am continually providing reviews, as I learn things.

I previously commented that the watch disconnects occasionally. This was caused by my swiping/ clearing open apps. The wear os app must be left open.

I like this watch enough to wear it daily, and my Apple series 2 has been relagated to a stay at home nighttime watch,
Killer looks make this my watch of choice for outside use.

As I said earlier, no speakers mean no phone calls, and texts sent through the Apple IMessage system don’t come through.
Does everything else important to me.
Overall, a keeper.

Caution. There are many versions of this watch, so make sure the watch you order has the features you want.
This watch has no speakers, but has the heart rate, GPS and Google Pay functions.

In reading this review, please keep in mind that I am an I Phone user. I am very familiar with Apple smartwatches.
I believe an Android user, would not have the same problems I reported. Especially a user familiar with an Android smartwatch.

Correction to initial review.
I stated the watch does not receive texts. It does.
It does not receive texts sent through the Apple System IMessage.
All texts sent by banks, pharmacy, everything else is received.

Pros:
Connects to I Phone.
Very attractive black stainless watch.
Nice leather band.
Many customizable faces.
Functions most important to me, such as weather, heart rate, fitness and step measurement work well.
Google Pay.
Easy setup.
Gmails come right through.
Apple News, a news feature I like, also works fine.
The watch also has an always on function I use. When on, the screen turns a darker shade, but is easily readable.
A flip of the wrist brings it back up to my customized blue screen.

Cons.
No speakers.
Cannot talk on it.
I do get a vibration when a phone call comes in, and the screen shows the phone number calling.
This is helpful if I’m relaxing and I don’t want to answer that call.
Watch didn’t recognize my Apple AirPods

I have had I Phones since the early 3GS model. Have had Apple smartwatches from Gen 0 to my wife's series 4.
They work well but the aluminum models look cheap, and the upgrade to stainless is an extra $ 300. Was $ 200.
Apple is now forcing everyone to pay an extra $ 100 for the cellular capability, in order to get a stainless steel smartwatch. I resent that marketing ploy and am looking at smartwatches by other makers. That is why I selected this watch. It is a great looking watch.

There are a number of very nice customizable faces, appropriate for office wear, as well as several sport faces.

Setup.

Had an initial problem where my I Phone couldn't find the watch. Just hit factory reset on the watch. Problem solved.
Went smoothly after that.
The Google OS watch App., downloadable on the Apple App store, walked me through everything.
Current and resting heart rate, and the fitness app are the apps I use most on the Apple smartwatch, and these are comparable. Weather App is very good.

Downloaded Google Play Music, which I subscribe to, but I could not listen to it since I couldn't connect my Airpods.
The problem with the connection may be in the way the watch shows available devices. It identified my Apple TV, and my Samsung TV. Five other devices were identified only by meaningless codes. The first one I tried, turned out to be my Sony Soundbar. Worked fine on it. Trying another code turned out to be a time consuming process. Gave up after over an hour.

Overall. Works well enough for I Phone users, wanting a more attractive smartwatch than the Apple watch.
Probably would be 5 stars for an Android user.

I have three Sonos devices. I purchased both the Playbar and Sonos One, and received this Amazon Vine item. Sonos software is incredible, and is worth buying for entry into the Sonos world. My Playbar is connected to our main TV, and my Beam is connected to our bedroom TV.
I actually think the dialogue clarity is better on the Beam. Maybe it’s the smaller room.

I am using optical on the Beam. Several reasons. I had trouble getting the HDMI to work on my Samsung. My bedroom TV, a 50 inch Samsung, only has two HDMI ports. I need one for my satellite and one for my Roku. Sonos provides a connector that makes the optical connection seamless. I had an HDMI connection on my Sony 9000. It has an HDMI in and an out port. My satellite went through that to the TV. That left my Roku going straight to the TV and I lost the benefit of the speaker with Roku. To me optical is the most trouble free connection. The sound from any device goes through the speaker. Very happy with optical on both my Playbar and Beam.

For those not having a Sonos, and being apprehensive about not getting a remote, be thankful. Your phone, or your tablet is the best remote possible. It shows every music service available, and makes searching for any song, or radio station, or genre so easy, and so complete.

Sonos as a Wi FI device. Wi Fi is so much better for your soundbar than Bluetooth, including Airplay 2. I like music when I fall asleep. I select a radio station or loop songs, and shut my phone down. The music plays all night without diminishing my battery. Cannot do this with Bluetooth or Airplay. Songs don’t get interrupted. It does not make a difference on your TV.

Airplay 2 is Bluetooth equivalent. The Sonos website gives very simple directions. I started my google play song, swiped up on my IPhone, hit the same type of icon, right above the song, that shows on You Tube. For those that don’t know, there is an icon on top of the You Tube screen that allows to watch You Tube on your TV. I also used Airplay 2 to connect You Tube music to my TV. Works easily.

The Beam is compact, has big sound, great clarity, and you control volume, or pause, by just saying Alexa.
I do not have a Sonos sub or surround with either system.

I can’t imagine any competing systems in this price range, being comparable in value.
I think this leaves Bose as an afterthought.

After a week's worth of usage, I am modifying my original review. I am also providing a comparison of this Sony Sound-bar, to the Sonos Playbar. I'm doing this as I think the price range of each is similar enough to interest potential buyers in each system.

I am rating the Sony Sound-bar as excellent.

1. My Direct TV remote, and my Samsung remote control the volume on the Sound-bar. They also turn it off. No pairing was needed.
2. Both of the above remotes also turn it on, but since you need the Sony remote for the HDMI link, you must use the Sony remote when turning the TV on. There are also easily accessible buttons on the Sound-bar, in case you lose the remote. Once the TV is on, you don't need the Sony remote unless you want to change the optional features such as voice for news, dialog, or music.
3. Bluetooth is a snap. You use the remote to activate the Bluetooth function.

Sonos Playbar vs Sony Sound-bar.

For TV only usage.

The Sonos cost $ 700, with no subwoofer. The subwoofer doubles the price.
The Sony has a wireless subwoofer. As a result, the Sony is better as a TV soundbar.
I purchased my Sonos as a standalone item, 6 months ago. If you plan on only buying the Sonos Player, it is not a good value. The value of the Sonos its for those that intend to have a multi-room Sonos system. Last month I added the Sonos One in a different room. The Sonos software is outstanding. I fully agree with a comment I read a year ago, that the Sonos Playbar is worth $ 350, and the Sonos software is worth $ 350. The software is a pleasure to use.

Both give clear dialog.

Winner for TV usage. Sony Sound-bar by a wide margin.

For music usage.

No clear winner as each is very different.

The Sonos Playbar is connected through your internet.
It does not have bluetooth. That is a big negative. However, it is always on, and not dependent on any other device. You use your phone, IPad, or other device, as your Sonos remote. Very simple, with their great app. You can shut off all your other devices and the Sonos will play all day and all night. You will only need your phone remote to select a new station.
It is very easy to change music services on the Sonos. Once music is on, I just tell Alexa to increase or decrease volume, or shut the music off. Alexa is incorporated in my Sonos One, and I have the Echo Dot next to my Sonos Playbar in another room. It is a wireless connection. You just tell either Alexa which room to play the music in.

The Sony Sound-bar has bluetooth. That is very convenient. It also has the subwoofer.
Excellent music quality.

The Sonos Playbar is not competitive with the Sony soundbar, as it doesn't come with a subwoofer. A full fledged Sonos system would cost over $ 2000, and would be awesome. That is beyond my budget.

Although I really like both my Sonos devices, on a value basis, I would buy the Sony Sound-bar. The included subwoofer makes the difference. The bluetooth is also more convenient, for playing a few songs.

A final note.

We prefer the styling of the Sony. Consider it a miniature Sonos Playbar.
It is longer than the Sonos Playbar, but definitely a miniature look.
The actual length is 37 inches. A template is provided for mounting on the wall, but no hardware is available.

Important comment.

Using the HDMI connection from the cable box, through the Soundbar to the TV and return. My streaming devices are only providing audio through the TV speaker. I guess I need to connect an optical cable to get audio through the soundbar on streaming devices. That should work.

Also. I’m thinking of going from Direct TV to Direct TV now when my promo ends. The latest Apple and Roku devices have HDMI so I would think after removing my cable box, I can connect the HDMI directly through the Soundbar. The streaming device simply replaces the cable box. That will leave OTA stations only providing audio through the TV speakers. Need the optical connected for that. Am I missing something?

5 Stars based on prior Square Trade purchases. One large claim. Immediate service. Washing machine. Called Square Trade. Diagnosed over the phone. Part sent directly to my home. Repairman came next day. Fixed four days after initial failure. Very impressed.

On this item, Square Trade cancelled this warranty due to a mistake.

I purchased a Sonos Soundbar at the military exchange. I then purchased this warranty on Amazon as it is listed separate from the main item. I provided the receipts to Square Trade and they told me I was covered. A week later they contacted me. It turns out even though it is listed as a separately available purchase for my device, you must purchase the covered item from Amazon. They said they sell it at a very low price based on volume sales on Amazon. The Square Trade Direct price is much more expensive. It is a great bargain when purchased on a Amazon. Not only price, but a longer warranty.

My first Sonos.

Tried to buy this through Amazon but the Thanksgiving day price went up substantially between the short time I placed it in my cart, and the time I checked out.

Would buy again. I use my IPhone and my Direct TV remote. Very easy setup. My first Sonos. Ethernet connection. Recommend you have a spare Ethernet cable and a long optical cable.

My Apple express has only one Ethernet port. Fortunately the Sonos has two. Removed the Ethernet cable from the express router, connected it to the Sonos. Then connected a second cable from the Sonos back to the express router. Very smooth.

Incredible improvement in clarity of TV dialogue. Stream music directly from Sirius XM, with the TV off. WI FI connection, not Bluetooth.

Alexa link.

Easy connection using the Alexa app.

I had one problem. Wording.

I asked Alexa to play the Carpenters on Sonos. Nope.
Finally, asked Alexa to play the Carpenters in Family Room. Worked beautifully.
Since I named my location Family Room, in Sonos setup, that’t what Alexa knows.

Wish I bought it sooner.

Upgrade from 3 stars to 5.

I originally graded this 3 stars because of Bluetooth issues.
I'm upgrading to 5 stars.

This evening I paired the headphones to my Amazon Fire TV. Paired immediately. Now I get the full sound of Game of Thrones, without waking my early to bed wife. Very important to me.

These paired easily.
Amazon Fire TV.
iPads. Both Pro and Mini 2.

Not paired.
5 year old IMac.

I have the Apple Music subscription, and used the full spectrum of music to test these speakers.

Fantastic quality of music. Quality feel and appearance.

No Bluetooth through IMac

Perfect Bluetooth connection on IPad Pro.
Perfect Bluetooth connection on IPad mini 2.
