Realistically, while I consider Bluetooth critical for light walking/exercising headphones, as well as stand alone speakers, it is less critical for these studio type headphones that are best for home use. I'm content using the cord to connect my iPhone, while I relax on the sofa. I'm thoroughly enjoying them as I type this review on my IPad Pro using Bluetooth. I can't go over 3 stars because of the Bluetooth issues.

This is identical to the remote that came with the pricey 60 inch Samsung 3D TV I purchased 6 years ago. SN is not the exact same, but the remote is.

A few years back, I purchased this replacement remote for a less expensive 50 inch Samsung TV. Paired instantly. Works perfectly. Gave me functions the cheaper OEM didn’t,

I just purchased a new 2020 Samsung TV Q model. I am not a fan of the Samsung One remote that comes with the newer Samsungs. This remote actually gives me easier to use adjustment functions than the Samsung One remote. Performed perfectly. Paired automatically. A steal at this price. When using this remote, on new Samsung TVs, the labeling doesn't match the functions, so a bit of trial and trial. It’s much more user friendly than the new Samsung One remote, in getting to adjustment functions, going fast forward/reverse, and volume controls. Wish Samsung stayed with this great remote.

Thank you seller for selling these very reasonably priced remotes.

USB connection to computer.  Very clear sound.  You can hear someone in your vicinity call you, which is what I want.  I use it at home, and it's very good for that purpose.  If you want total silence, you don't want this headset.  Long cord is a big plus.  I have been a Logitech fan ever since I had a warranty claim on a large purchase.  It was handled promptly and correctly.  The replacement was ordered while I was still on the phone.

I purchased these primarily for Google Voice. GV recommended by Clark Howard.

Very clear phone set. People on the other end have no idea that I'm not on a regular phone.
Now I can call anywhere domestically totally free. Cost of this handset was the only phone cost.

Two issues though.

Intended to use these with my MacBook Pro. However, the USB adapter appears oversized, and will not fit unless I remove the other USB cable. Inconvenient to remove my other USBs each time. So I connected this to my old Dell, which is my backup computer. Worked fine on the Dell. For the Apple Mac Book Pro, I use a two lead logitech, and only plug in the headphone jack. Works fine.

Other issues. My wife says it's too heavy for her to feel comfortable. She uses the $19 logitech instead., The mute button is not labeled. My wife made a call and the other party couldn't hear her. I got out the instructions, and they showed an unmarked mute button. It turns out when my wife picked up the headphones, she touched that button and disabled the mic. A red light indicates the mic is in mute. Tap the earphone, and sound comes back.

Summary. Not for MacBook Pro. Great for PC.

This is my 4th HDTV, and my 3rd Vizio (one returned), so I think I can write a worthwhile review.

This replaces my 4 year old 37 inch Magnavox HDTV. Was very pleased with it. No problems. Still sharp picture. However, the color was no longer vibrant. Moved it to a spare room for Wii play. I think LCD TVs are good for 4 years max - due to color fading. To be clear, color fading is tolerable in the kitchen TV, and bedrooms, but not in my main TV.

I am satisfied with my one year old 32 inch Vizio kitchen LCD HD, and went with Vizio again.

Since I was going from 37 to 42 inches, and have a glass stand, I wanted a light TV. This weighs under 40 pounds, with stand.
Easy to handle. The base had a single screw (directions said 4, not true), which you hand tighten. Easy installation. The Magnavox base was difficult to install. Had to call their tech support for help.

These come with a good instruction manual, and are very easy to setup. Sound is good. Picture, very good in HD, good in standard. Soon, all programs will be in HD. Blu Ray discs look great, as do sports events and movies.

Purchased at my local warehouse club, as their extended contract pricing is very low. I have had surge damage, on several occasions, and buy these warranties to protect against that. Great price for a TV less than 2 inches thin.

I purchased this cable to hook up my Apple laptop to my HDTV. I wanted to keep my laptop on the computer desk, rather than move it back and forth near the TV.

Watched Secret Life of a Teenager. PQ was perfect HD. This HDMI cable has to be good.
This is a good show to test PQ quality on. It really was equal to my HD satellite transmission. I have 8000 kbps download speed.

It did go out once for a few seconds. I may not have had the cable fastened securely.

I'm still amazed that with the computer on the desk, I can point my logitech remote mouse at the HDTV screen, and it works perfectly, as if it were the monitor. These long cables really are useful.

Did not work initially, so I ordered two more cables I didn't need. With Amazon Prime, you can't cancel.

My problem. Hooked up the mini display to the Macbook Pro. Hooked the HDMI side to a 3 ft. HDMI cable. Hooked the audio cable in.

Only an inch of the page was showing, on the HDTV. Bright purple colors on the rest. Tried resetting everything on the TV and computer. Nothing. Then ordered another type adapter. Then went to comments on other sites.

My problem. The default setting on my laptop was set to scan. To fix. Go to the Apple logo, then system preference, then display, click display, click arrangement, click set mirror image. Worked instantly. I'm surprised no one else had this problem, or mentioned it. Glad someone on another site detailed the fix. Watched cable show, ABC family channel in near perfect 720P HD.

The other cables I ordered were the mini display to DVI, and the Dvi to HDMI. My Vizio actually recommends this set up. I'll try it, but there is little room for improvement.

A word on my setup. I placed the Apple under my Kitchen TV, a 32 inch 720P Vizio. This meant a wireless transmission. Hooked the short HDMI and audio cables in place. I used the Apple wireless keyboard and Logitech V220 wireless mouse, on my kitchen table, to do everything without bending. No cables across floor. Despite wireless transmission on G router, approx 40 ft, just a few seconds of buffering.

I originally purchased a 26 Vizio VA 10T. I had some initial problems and read the warranty. On TVs less than 32 inches, Vizio requires that you ship the TV to California at your expense. I don't think so. I returned it to Walmart, and then purchased this TV at Sams. In home service on this one.

This TV has much higher quality and workmanship than the 26 inch model. Excellent PQ, VG sound, VG viewing angle, no glare. . The cable hookups go in horizontally, while the 26 inch model had vertical hookups. The vertical hookups would be fine with a wall mount, but were difficult to use on my stand.

Cons. Remote is pretty basic, and the menu is somewhat confusing. Since this is used with Direct TV, I only use the Vizio remote to change some preferences.

Addressing comments on Walmart purchases. Consider this. I initially purchased the 26 inch model. I paid a pre BF price of $ 248, reg. $ 327-348. At $ 248, my 3 year extended warranty was $ 19.99. I wasn't happy withe TV, returned it, and did not have to pay a restocking charge (hello-Best Buy). I had to open the Box, and remove the TV, to get to and read the warranty. Only then did I find out I needed to ship the TV to California, at my expense, for warranty work. Even under the Wally 3 year extended warranty, the mfg terms still applied. So for any warranty work, I needed to ship it at my expense. I think it stinks that companies don't disclose the significant terms of their warranty more prominently, prior to purchase. Their behavior sticks you with restocking fees. Love this 32 inch Vizio. Go for it.

I usually replace my computer every 4 years.  This time I'm going to upgrade my 4 year old Dell.  This keyboard is my first step.  Contrary to one review, the lighting can be brightened or lowered easily.  Sound adjustment is nice.  Nothing to be dissapointed about here.  It is a corded model.  My first Logitech product. Glad I made the purchase.

When I talk to my friends for hours on end the last thing I want to do is hold my iPhone in my hand up to my ear or even be on speaker phone. My husband does not like hearing the speaker phone when he's trying to concentrate on his iPhone. It takes too much effort to talk on a speaker phone for hours. So as soon as I answer the phone I switch over to these headphones and talk through the microphone in the headphones. Perfect!

My friend who calls me once a week sounds like a radio DJ, in fact he used to be one but the headphones make him sound that way just naturally. It is really cute. He's always had a nice voice but this makes him come through like rich stereo sound. At first I thought I was talking to a stranger, but got used to his new voice sound.

You just have to hold the button down for a few seconds and an AI voice tells you what the headphones are doing. So if you are finished with the headset you just press the middle button and it tells you the headset is off. So that saves on battery power and makes it easy to know when the power is on or off. I find that I can make these the best volume easily and have it now where I don't need to change it at all.

My friend who calls me every week told me about these headphones and I bought them on his recommendation. I had these years before I got an iPhone because I prepare ahead of time!!!! Now that I have a new iPhone 14 I'm happy as can be with my headset. Since the microphone is built in this is perfect for phone calls but it also works like a regular headphone if you want to listen to audio on your phone. I haven't started listening to music on it yet but will report back when I do. The sound is just superior to any headphones besides my AKG K553s.

~The Rebecca Review

Here is the conundrum. I got a new pair of AKG K553s and they apparently have shortened the cord to four feet. That's it! Who does that? I need a much longer cord to reach from my stereo boombox to my bed so I can listen to CDs and the radio in comfort and warmth. This extension cord works great to extend the AKG cord. 25 feet is pretty long and so I can walk around the bedroom too without risking damaging my AKGs. Everything sounds perfect. No reduction in sound quality at all. The cord looks very durable and I'm happy.

~The Rebecca Review

If you have ever owned AKGs before you know they need to be well taken care of. My K553 headphones fell apart in my hands the other day and I was so upset. So I decided to go back to buying the K240s as they seem to last longer. These are the most comfortable AKGs I've owned so far. You can wear them over an hour and they don't hurt your ears.

The bass is a little heavier however. I enjoy using these for classical, electronica and other music that does not have a heavy beat. I find the K553s are better at suppressing the heavier beats so am getting another pair of those too. I think you need both for the full range of music choices.

These are an affordable luxury and music sounds great on them. The headphone case is perfect too if you want your headphones to be protected and last a long time!

~The Rebecca Review

When looking for an extension cable for a small speaker I wanted to plug into my computer, this looked like the right one. Yes it works perfectly and now I can listen to music flooding my office with sound. The cable came in a nice box so was very protected in shipping. I was impressed it didn't just arrive in a plastic bag. It seems like a good quality cable and was easy to hook up to my computer and speaker. Happy Me! :)

~The Rebecca Review

On this new little speaker music sounds like a magical secret world. The high notes are very crisp and the melody drifts across the mind like a dream. I'm glad I took a chance with this speaker. Only thing is the speaker does not have regular volume control (just has high and low) and needs to be charged with a USB cable. The speaker was however already charged so just plugged it in to my computer and it was good to go.

The color is a little darker than pictured. Online it looks hot pink whereas it is actually a lavender purple. I think for the price and if you listen to music at a medium volume, this is great. I have it plugged into my computer and it works for what I bought it for.

I do recommend you use the extension cord or even get a longer one – I got a six foot extension cord to use it with my computer. I also got a splitter so I can have my headphones and the speaker plugged in at the same time. I can just turn the speaker off when I want to use my Sennheiser headphones.

I have a feeling this little speaker is going to be used a lot. I'm enjoying using it and romantic electronica and classical music like Rachmaninov sounds wonderful on it. It takes up very little space and looks really cute on my desk.

~The Rebecca Review

P.S. The green light may still be on this speaker when it needs to be charged. I thought it was broken after a few uses, but it really just needed to be charged I guess. A few hours later it is working again. Will continue using it to see what happens next...the battery charge may not last as long as my other mini speaker.

For about a month I was dealing with a problem with my computer. I figured I had some annoying virus on it and every single time I clicked on anything it would open windows twice or not show me a pull down menu properly. Finally I decided to buy this keyboard and mouse and wow, it fixed the problem. Apparently the old mouse had become defective. I'd had it for six years or more so it definitely needed to be replaced. And the keyboard works perfectly and it way quieter than my old one. I also feel like I can do everything faster now. The mouse scrolls super fast compared to the HP one I had. So very happy with this purchase and wish I'd taken action sooner.

~The Rebecca Review

This is the best little alarm clock I've ever owned. It is cute and functional and has a radio and adjustable volume controls. Two alarms can be set at the same time.

The FM radio comes in great and I have it set on a favorite station. You can program in stations and then you can wake with the radio or listen for a specific time before going to sleep. There is a nap, sleep button which is very useful. I press the radio button, then the sleep button and the radio turns off automatically after a preset time ( 15/30/60/90 minutes).

This also has a nice big snooze button on the top so it is easy to turn off the alarm when you want to sleep a little longer.

What I like is that you can adjust the brightness of the display so it doesn't light up your whole room at night. However if you want it to act as a night light, you can set it on the brightest setting.

Also, I find this useful when charging my little speaker I use with my CD player. This alarm clock has two USB charging ports which is very convenient. I can charge my kindle and the speaker at the same time! If you have a cell phone or iPad you keep by the bed, this is also a good feature as there is also a line-in jack so you can play music from your phone on the alarm clock speaker.

The only negative I'd say is the AM radio which does not seem to work very well.

The instruction book is however great and makes setting this clock up easy. It seems the company who makes this alarm clock really did think of everything. My favorite thing to do is climb into my warm bed, put on the radio with one touch of a button and read to my heart's content.

I think you will love this alarm clock and it doesn't take up a lot of room on your nightstand.

~The Rebecca Review

I was very conflicted before buying these headphones as I read the negatives and questioned whether these were as good as the last Sennheiser headphones that just broke. I will say that these perform differently when not charged fully. It is best not to use them before you've left them overnight on the charger. Then you will have less problems with static. You may hear static when you first put them on but as soon as the music or youtube video has started the sound is crystalline. I'm currently listening to some of my favorite music and it could not sound better. So I'm glad I took the chance even when I expected there to be issues. Sennheiser is really as good as AKGs once tuned in. You can also walk around the house with these on and take your music with you. Just charge them before using for the best results.

~The Rebecca Review

If you are looking for a portable DVD player that has intuitive controls, a remote control and a case to hold the DVD player so you can view the screen while seated in the back of a vehicle, this is a good choice. The screen swivels around so you can fold this in half "backwards" so only the screen is showing. This is helpful when using the case for use in a vehicle.

Compared to my regular TV this is an enhanced viewing experience. I found this to be a better visual experience. All the colors were vivid and almost velvety. Whether I am watching a favorite movie or a nature DVD, the colors are fantastic. Greens and yellows are super crisp and water looks totally glossy. I can't emphasize enough how beautiful the colors are on the screen.

I found many uses for this DVD player. It literally became my entertainment companion for two days while I tried out every feature. What I loved best was playing my virtual fireplace DVD with a beach fire and ocean waves. The stereo sound on this is excellent, I felt I was really at the beach which made me happy.

The remote control works very well and allows you to do things like turn the subtitles on or off. The audio controls let you choose between various options. You can stop or pause the movie you are watching either from the controls on the DVD player or by using the remote control.

This DVD player also has a screen saver that comes up when you put it on pause or don't turn the screen off. There is a button that says TFT ON/OFF that turns the screen off when you only want to listen to the sound. I found this played CDs too so that made me very happy. You can listen with the stereo speakers or use headphones.

If you are looking to view widescreen movies, this works for that too.

This is perfect to take with you when traveling. The only caution is not to use it for yourself if you are driving. It does have a cigarette charger that will work in cars and RVs.

The only thing I do when taking out a CD or DVD is to turn the DVD player off completely.

Some other uses I found for this DVD player was to play relaxing DVDs before bed to calm the mind. I also watched an underwater DVD with fish swimming by. This DVD player allows you to have entertainment wherever you are. The battery lasts about 4-5 hours, but if it starts to run out you can just plug the unit in and continue watching.

The only thing I noticed that was different than a regular DVD player was when you are halfway through a movie, put it on pause instead of taking out the DVD. This does not seem to have any memory of where you left off so when you put the DVD back in it just starts from the beginning again. This is not a big issue if you just hit the pause button.

I'm very happy with this DVD player and it is fun to go into your own little movie world. This is handy to have when someone else is using the computer or main TV. You can watch movies anywhere you want. I use this mostly when sitting in bed.

~The Rebecca Review

I received one free DVD player for review purposes.

These headphones were a recent gift for my birthday and I must say they are very impressive. At first I didn't realize that the jack had two options so I didn't get to use these the first day. My friend who gave them to me explained that you just twisted off the larger jack to get the smaller jack which then fit into my CD player and computer.

The band that goes across your head also can be a bit uncomfortable but I fixed that problem with a wool headband I wear during the winter. I put it between the metal and my scalp. That was more comfortable and the metal seems to soften a bit with wear. You can also buy a wool cover to make it more comfortable, which my friend is also sending me. The extra effort it takes to make these comfortable is worth it. See photos.

As far as the sound goes, these reveal a pristine clarity in everything you listen to. I especially love how John Lennon's Woman sounds and also I listened to Ulrich Schnauss' Goodbye and Evening Ocean's The Kiss. Wow. Everything sounds new again. I hear additional things in songs I never heard before. I'd say listening to music on these headphones is as close to an out of body experience you will ever have. You will feel like you are floating in an ethereal domain of sounds. Vocals all become more interesting as the sound is softened and each note is crystal clear. The sound does seem to hypnotize you a bit. I feel that these headphones reveal the complexity of music in all its beauty. What you get is an ecstatic experience.

You will fall in love with AKG all over again when you get these headphones. I had the AKG K240 headphones for years and really loved them. In comparison these are sonic bliss. Even my Sennheiser cordless headphones don't sound this good. I have a feeling I'm going to be listening to a lot more music than normal. Once you put these headphones on it is hard to stop listening. I spent probably four or more hours the first day I put these on. I just had to listen to all my favorites one after the other to see how they would sound. I was not disappointed. As I told my friend the fact that I'm thrilled about these headphones is a major understatement. They are worth the investment for the high level of pleasure they produce.

~The Rebecca Review

P.S. It's 2021 and my first AKG K553s fell apart in my hands the other day after six years. So it was time for a new pair. They don't last forever especially if you use them all the time. Get a hard shell case for them and don't wrap the cord around the headphones.

Cool on the Go is a cooling fan that is highly portable. I'm using it at my desk. You can plug it into your computer and it works instantly or you can charge it (put rechargeable batteries in first) or use 4 AA batteries. The air output can be controlled and it is pretty powerful on the high setting. It is fairly quiet but you can definitely hear the fan. This comes with an armband, a lanyard (to wear it around your neck) and a USB power adaptor. This does not however come with an A/C adaptor or a USB car adaptor. I think this works best as a table top fan which you can keep pretty close to you for maximum cooling. It is also interesting to wear it. So order some batteries to use with this otherwise you'll only be able to use it with the USB cord. I'm also now using this when I walk on my treadmill. It is so cold it is like air conditioned air blowing on you while you walk. I'm upping my review to five stars because I'm starting to really love this.

~The Rebecca Review

I received one free product for review purposes. This review is my honest opinion.

If you don't like the sound of your keyboard to reach the rest of the house (like if people are sleeping and you are up surfing around or talking at forums) then you might like this keyboard a lot. It is quieter than my old HP keyboard. If you type slowly it is quieter than if you type fast. The only thing I was disappointed by was the length of the cord. I've ordered a USB extension cord since to use this keyboard I have to have my computer up on the desk. That is the only way the cord will reach. It really is far too short. But I have a big desk so that is probably the problem.

~The Rebecca Review

P.S. The letters on the keys are wearing off really fast. Maybe I just type too much!!!

Do you fear that your alarm clock will not work if the power goes off sometimes at night? This Dream Machine has a battery back up so you never have to worry about the alarm not going off at the right time. Well you may have to replace the battery at some point but otherwise it seems very reliable. The instructions for setting up this clock radio are simple and easy to understand. There are two alarms and of course a nice snooze button. I feel it is nicer to wake up with the radio playing than a buzzer but this alarm clock has that option too. The speaker is not very high quality so don't expect stereo sound. For the price I feel that I got lots of good features. I'm happy with my purchase.

~The Rebecca Review

I'm a fan of the GR07s but these GR01s impressed me with their pristine clarity. There are also 15 eartips so I was able to get a perfect fit. Although these go a little deeper into the ear canal. If you don't get the right fit they tend to fall out of your ears so you might have to try a few eartips to get the right ones. Then they stay in place quite nicely. What I noticed about these earbuds is that vocals shimmer and the bass is smooth and silky instead of jarring. Dancy pop is bright and sparkly. I especially like listening to Owl City with these earphones. Electronica really sounds incredible. I hear more details than when wearing Sennheiser or AKG headphones and that is really saying something. So is spending a little more for the GR01s worth it? Yes definitely. Go for it and you will be happy you did.

~The Rebecca Review

You can actually enjoy watching TV, use your VCR/DVD player or listen to your stereo without disturbing a single soul.

The headphones rest on a transmitter that recharges the headphones after you plug them back in. They are always ready for use and the batteries must last forever because so far, I've not had to worry about the batteries wearing out.

This tool set is almost perfect! I’ll start with a little background... I am tech savvy for the most part, and I refurbish my own electronics, as well as stuff for friends and family from time to time. My MacBook Pro was bogged down by a “feature” known as thermal throttling. When older thermal paste dries up, it fails to conduct heat as well, so performance takes a nose dive in favor of preservation.

I’m not entirely sure if Apple actually does this servicing upon request, or not, but I honestly wouldn’t think that they do. So, after figuring out what was going on with my laptop, I rolled up my sleeves, brought out the few electronics tools I had around, and proceeded to gut my MacBook. Bad idea. You ever hear that saying about not bringing a knife to a gunfight? It went about that well.

Long story short, I busted a clip off of the motherboard that would have held the keyboard ribbon cable in place, and you can’t really just replace the clip on a motherboard, you have to replace the entire board. If I had this tool set in time for that repair, I could have saved the cost of replacing the board.

That said, these arrived in time for me to do the motherboard swap, and before I did (managed to upgrade to the i7 processor from the i5, a mild boost in performance I’m sure.) I made sure to once again, remove the heat sync, and remove the old thermal paste, replacing it with fresh TG-7. My geekbench scores now come in above what is average for the i7 version of my MacBook Pro. Above average is virtually unheard of. It’s like a brand new machine.

But these tools, if you attempt to do a repair without them, you could end up costing yourself a few hundred extra dollars. Learn from my mistake!

My only negatives here are for the durability and sturdiness, because I feel like the plastic spudger thing is definitely going to break eventually at the sharp pointy side. I don’t trust the plastic much. Other than that, the kit is well worth it, and every Mac enthusiast who plans to repair their own machine should really have it.

After retiring my well used and beat up Welt tripod after 35 years of field use and began looking for a new tripod I was shocked when I saw the prices of medium to light weight tripods for 35 mm camera use. $200-$300 -- are you kidding me? I like quality and long term durability (as was my Welt, but...no longer made) and am usually willing to pay for it. However, I decided to give this relatively inexpensive Benro a try and couldn't be happier. I've had it in the field 8 times already, setting it up in water, on muddy slopes, in freezing temperatures and it performs very well for me. The legs extend easily. It is firm. It is light, and with the attachment of a shoulder strap is comfortably carried. I also purchased the Benro BR268 Ball Head for it and it too is of high quality and excellent functionality. This is a great value.

----
Update March 2012. This may be moot, as Benro no longer makes this model. It has been updated to the A0580F as far as I can tell. Anyway, this inexpensive aluminum tripod has performed great in the field. I've done my best to beat it up everywhere from a hike to the bottom of the Grand Canyon to sloughing through the Everglades. It works fine. The Benro Ballhead BR268 is another story. The quick attachment/release spring loaded button/pin now longer works and the entire mechanism has too much play in it. I only paid $38 for it. So I upgraded to a Manfrotto 496RC2 which works wonderfully, smooth and tight. As I was researching ballheads I checked out tripods. Nothing comes close to the value, portability, and toughness of this cheap Benro. There isn't anything out there with the stability and light weight of this Benro. At 2.4 lbs it is lighter than all Carbon Fiber tripods of the same relative size costing $250 and up.

Note to reviewer who complained that Amazon.com should have better details on the size and weight. He is right, but I think most people do the research and find that information elsewhere, then come back to Amazon.com to buy. Benrousa.com is easy to find and has all the data you could want.

This is a fantastic external drive that exceeds expectations! This is a massive amount of storage, in a quiet professional looking designed enclosure that with USB 3.0 connections makes for an incredible value to expand the capacities of an existing PC while adding backup capabilities for recovery purposes.
CrystalDiskMark test shows the drive's sequential read at 213 MB/s, sequential writes at 198 MB/s which is really fast for a platter based hard drive (even faster than some if my WD Black internal SATA drives). The random reads are also very quick at 27MB/s for 4Kib and random writes of 2.3 MB/s are beyond my expectations as these speeds are faster than some of my USB thumb drives. The drive can be placed flat, or on its side and the heat is passively vented from the rear of the unit. The blue LED blinks when data transfers are taking place and when PC is off the light is also off to not add additional lights to a room. The drive comes with backup software Backup Now EZ which is fairly intuitive allowing for scheduled backups of specific files and even an entire PC. I've not had to do a restore yet from this software's backup so it may be more useful to do a windows image to the drive and then restore from that. I would highly recommend this drive for anyone in the market for an external USB 3.0 drive with large capacity looking for fast drive speeds. Very satisfied with this product and I will be looking to Toshiba for future storage needs.

I feel like Buffalo has created a quality product with the TeraStation, but some of it's features get in the way of it being a really intuitive product. From a hardware perspective, the processor is quite capable and is really responsive. While small it is larger than comparable 2 drive NAS devices, but I can say that it is quiet and fairly unnoticeable in that regard. The drives included are WD Red 1 TB drives in RAID 0 for redundancy providing approximately 900GB of network storage (which would seem small by today's standards depending on the data / number of pc's backing up to the drives).

Accessing the configuration of the device is easy to do either from the desktop software itself or by accessing the NAS from a browser and typing in the IP address which is displayed on the LCD screen (a feature I really like). The login has given me some trouble in that after typing in the admin password or user password I am often met with user authentication failed, but if I refresh my browser I am able to access the settings and it indicates the correct user.

That being said, the user interface is pretty standard and is broken up into appropriate categories from File sharing to drive management, web services and backup. I've been able to add users and folders pretty easily, and have been able to set up time machine backups to the system as well.

Transfer speeds to the NAS were approximately 75 - 80 Mbps using gigabit network connections, copying over 5gb of files across the network.

There is the capability to run a web server off the device as well as a mysql server, which I have not had enough time to test out but seems fairly robust. There are built in DLNA capabilities to allow for sharing of media files across devices that support it, as well as the capability to create an iTunes server as well as a print server.

Overall with my limited experience with the Terastation I have been pleased but there have been hiccups. I would recommend this device for use in a small business / office setting, but for personal use something more like a Synology NAS or a WD Mycloud might be more appropriate. Additionally the 1 TB drives will have limited long term capabilities as storage requirements continue to rise, and would almost necessitate the need to purchase at minimum the 2 - 2 TB drive version of the device.

The Lexar 32gb 3.0 USB Thumb Drive is likely the first usb 3.0 drive that I have had that has exceeded my expectations. The JBL Cinema 500 5.1 surround sound speaker system is a quality upgrade from a box setup home theatre system.  There is a significant improvement in sound clarity and the overall theatre experience.  Starting with the center channel speaker, voices are clearer when watching movies, providing a solid balance between music and ambient sound.  Often with surround speakers, they excel at volume for music and effects, but voices get washed out.  This is not the case with these speakers.  It is amazing how well one can hear even the slightest breath from a character on screen regardless of background sound.  The front surround speakers have excellent mid-range reproduction with no audible distortion at high volume levels.  There is an excellent sense of space with effects and soundtrack reproduction.  No sense of emptiness with the sound, the content comes through as the producers intended it to be heard.  The surround speakers, the satellites of this system are larger than some, about a foot from top to bottom, but have a very nice modern appearance.  They do have a keyhole type mounting for anchor mounting on a wall, perhaps different from some other speaker mounts.  The sub woofer has a large base on the floor, but the pyramid shape minimizes the shape near the top.  It completes the sound range and can have its output controlled from rear controls to increase volume as well as crossover to prevent higher frequencies.  The built in 500 watt amplifier does boost its volume significantly.  It has plenty of capacity for a large space, as we did not feel the need to crank it up in a smaller space.  When the bass hits in music, it has a very clean tone and compliments the surrounds nicely.  Testing a wide variety of music on these JBL speakers, it is easy to just get lost in the music.  Everything sounds amazing on these from pop and rock to classical.  Whatever the taste in music, it will sound superb.  This system is a great value and a terrific replacement to any standard home theatre in a box.  We are thrilled to have received this product to review, and do recommend it.

You can connect to the amp via several methods, and that is a major plus for me. We normally use the amp with an Echo, which we connect via Bluetooth, and it works flawlessly. It seems to be well built, sturdy and has a decent weight.

The amp is fairly small, and can be mounted virtually anywhere, or simply sat on top of any place of your choosing. It is mostly black with black dials, the "Pyle" logo in blue, numbers and lines around the three dials (volume, treble and bass) and in other places are white, and there are a few more small words/sentences on it in white. There are USB and SD slots on the front of the amp, above the LCD screen. It isn't an eyesore, and can sit in any room without being noticed or taking away from the decor. It blends very well with my living room and doesn't look out of place. The LCD screen isn't excessively bright. It is bright enough to clearly see what is on the screen, but not excessively bright to the point of being distracting at night or in the dark.

The sound is awesome. While I'm not extremely well versed in this kind of technology, I have enough knowledge to say that this is a very decent 2-channel amp. Our speakers aren't "top of the line," so alone, they don't put out the best sound in the world; but with the amp, though, one would never be able to tell that the speakers are on the fairly low-end of the price and quality spectrum. Are the speakers awful on their own? Absolutely not, but this amp does a lot for them. The sound is crisp, clear and loud.

The amp comes with a remote, which you can use to power the amp on/off, change the mode (input), decrease/increase/mute volume, pause, fast/skip forward, rewind/skip backwards, pause/play, scan (there are other things included on this button), randomize/repeat songs/tracks (at least I think that button does one of these things), access the equalizer and enter numbers. I honestly use the remote to control the amp a lot more than I use the controls on the amp itself.

As I use the amp with more devices/speakers, I will update my review as/if necessary.

Just a note: It doesn't come with cables, so you'll need your own or purchase them separately.

Let me start off by saying that I have used many, many different earbuds and headphones over the years, and these are by FAR the best bang for my buck in terms of quality, durability, and comfort. I've always managed to land jobs where I'm able to listen to audio content throughout my workday, and have consequently spent most of my working hours with at least one earbud tucked into my ears.

I thread these down to my pocket where they are plugged into my iPod full time. No matter how much running, walking, lifting, jumping or moving around I do (and I work as a package delivery guy, which means hundreds of movements and ten miles of walking a day), these things take ages to wear out. Under normal use, I'm sure they'd never need replacing unless you managed to blow out the speaker somehow, or cause blatant damage to them. They don't cut in and out from wear on the jack end or on the headphone ends like some other earbuds, which will give way after being cranked around a bit.

Next, I have to address the comfort of the ergonomically shaped buds themselves. They are formed to fit into ear, with the speaker being offset from the center of the housing. On others, such as the classic white Apple earbuds, the round shape causes me some discomfort and soreness after hours of wear. But these are just fantastic. I wear them for up to 11 hours at a time with no discomfort whatsoever.

Finally, the sound quality. While an audiophile purist will say that they probably don't meet the highest standards in the land, they do a pretty good job. They stand up to much more expensive earbuds, and if you use the proper sized adapter for your ear (three sizes included), the speaker isolates sound very well, so you don't even need any noise-canceling feature. I wear them while driving a diesel truck with the doors open driving down the freeway, and I can hear every word of the audiobook I'm listening to. The treble is good. For less than ten bucks, there is no better ear bud out there. I've owned three pairs over the last two years, and I would only have needed one if I didn't abuse them so much with daily use and extreme wear. Installation activities.

Make sure and use a drill bit big enough for the protector to pass though if it will be placed inside a wall, or overhang etc. You are not just drilling a hole for the cable. Look at the camera and you'll see the size you need to make it. I also ended up needing a longer HDMI cable, the one that came with this was about 6' I needed a 10' due to my particular situation. [[VIDEOID:6f0dc76b357c6acd70c1666d3f7b0b85]] I was in the market for a USB-C hub for my iPad Pro that I just recently got second hand. I have the Logitech Combo Touch keyboard case so I can turn it into a laptop, but I felt like I was missing extra functionality that could make me further use my iPad Pro in a professional way for school or anything else that I need to do. I did some research and I came across this $20 hub and I knew that it fit the criteria that I wanted out of a hub, but unsure how compatible it would be with my iPad since there isn't many in-depth reviews with them. I was mainly an audio jack since using AirPods all the time can get quite annoying with charging. I was thinking about ethernet, but honestly it's not really necessary since this is an iPad so it's not that serious.

All I can say is that the hub really worked well in all aspects. It has a metal casing that is cold to the touch like a macbook, a braided cable and all the ports work as intended, but with some caveats.

1. You can't change the audio level when the hub is plugged in. This is whether or not you are connected to a monitor/tv/projector with speakers or even playing off the tablet. You must unplug the hub, change the volume, then plug it back in. Not a lot of work, but it could be annoying. (I show it in the video)

2. You can't use the SD card reader and the microsd card reader at the same time, only once. But you can use a hard drive plugged into one of the USB slots and an SD/Microsd card at the same time. And if you want to do more, you can probably have a USB SD card reader to plug into one of the ports and read them all at once if you wanted to. Haven't tried it, but honestly might work.

3. You can plug in a mouse & keyboard and have everything else functioning at the same time. Charging, audio, hdmi, sd card, the iPad Pro can handle it all for the most part.

4. You can't change the source of audio if you have the HDMI plugged in and headphones in the audio jack plugged in. The iPad will only play sound out of whatever the HDMI is connected to. So you are better off with using AirPods/Bluetooth headphones if you want to use a monitor and listen to something independently.

I currently have no complaints and if something goes wrong then I'll update my review, but I'm satisfied with my purchase. So if you're looking for a relatively inexpensive USB-C hub for your iPad Air (3rd gen+)/iPad Pro (2018+) with an audio jack and everything else you might need besides an ethernet port, I'd recommend this hub.

TLDR: Used or not, the newest base kindle is a great buy for anyone looking for a good e-book reader. The features of the higher end models are nice to have, but by no means need to have. The money you save on the device can be put toward more books to actually read, which, at the end of the day, is what we are all here for.

This is my second time buying a used kindle device (the last one was an Oasis). I have to say, it is my preferred way to buy Kindles. The Kindle I purchased this time was in Used-Acceptable condition (I believe that is the lowest condition amazon warehouse sells used products- the rest go to woot or get recycled).

When I unboxed it, I found that it had very minor scratches on the bezel and back- visible from only certain angles - all just superficial surface scratches, nothing gouged into the plastic. Even if it cost more (I paid less than $40 for it) I wouldn't be annoyed in the least to find the very faint, surface scratches on this device. I have zero regrets and would do it again. Not only that, but I was pleasantly surprised to see that special offers was turned off on the device despite the fact that it was sold as 'ad supported' (it is likely the previous owner had turned them off and amazon just never turned them back on before selling the device - I wouldn't expect all used device to have it turned off, but it was a nice bonus to see that I got lucky and saved the $20 removal price).

Device works just like new and I am very happy with it. This is my second Kindle (and 7th e-ink device). My last Kindle was the second version of the Oasis. I traded that in to get the discount on the new paperwhite, but I am still waiting on it to ship (looks like I will get it in Late November)- hence the purchase of a cheap device to have on hand. This version of the Kindle has most of the features of the second version of the Oasis minus:
-Dark mode - I liked this mostly because I found the automatic light settings to be too bright most of the time and I liked to read in bed.
-Auto-light settings - Often too bright and I would manually adjust it anyway (or my hand would cover the light sensor and the device would suddenly get bright).
-Page buttons - Nice to have, but definitely not a need to have. The way I hold my reading devices is usually from the bottom anyway, so the touch turn is the most ergonomic.
-Waterproof - I tried reading in the bath once. It wasn't for me. I don't really sit and read in places I am going to get wet.
-Resolution - 167ppi may sound low, but when compared to mass market paperbacks, printed on recycled paper, I would say the text looks about the same - perfectly legible. Plus, you can change the font type and size to suit your taste, so it is superior to most printed text.
-Option for cellular data - Looks like Amazon may be phasing this out since it isn't available on the newest paperwhite. I rarely used it, but it was nice to know that I would be able to buy a book on the go without having to connect to public wifi if I really wanted to.

The current Oasis and Paperwhite also have warm lights in addition to the normal lights (which is the main appeal of the paperwhite for me). Again, not a deal breaker for a device, but it is nice to have.

I know this reader has been out of production for a long time, but I felt like I needed to send it a little love as I have been using it again and just realized it is over 10 years old.

Lets start off with what this device is missing:
-Comfort light
-Wifi
-Bluetooth
-Expandable memory
-Audio output for audio books

With all the features that you expect to see in a modern e-reader, you may be asking yourself why I would rate this device so highly. While this device only carries 512MB of internal, non-expandable memory, I find that I can easily carry a library of over 300 books. The contrast of the e-ink screen is great for books; though it should be noted that it only has 8 levels of gray. This device is definitely a text only device - no comic books, graphic novels, PDFs, or manga here. With all these draw backs I keep bringing up, who do I love this thing so much? It is reliable. I know it is always there when I need it. If I want to dump a book onto it, I just fire up Calibre (since the old sony software is obsolete and they recommend adobe editions - no thanks). I rarely find a book I can't put onto this device with Calibre.

I don't use this device as much as I use to, but there are times like when I want to trade in a kindle to upgrade to the newest model and I am waiting for the trade in and release of the newest model and I will be without my kindle for a month. It is times like that where I dust off the old PRS-300 and load it up with books for the time without a kindle and I am reminded of why I love this device. It is simple, straight forward, rugged, and pleasant to stare at for an extended amount of time. I don't even mind that I don't have the comfort lighting - I even kind of prefer not having a light on my device because it just looks more like paper. It isn't any kind of hardship to turn on a light to read by.

Bottom line, this device is a delight despite all the modern features this is missing.

First and foremost- What every prospective tablet user needs to consider: What am I planning on doing with my tablet?
For most users, tablets are for entertainment and are considered a luxury item. They aren't good for working on school work, or anything that requires a lot of typing, so for most people, these devices are for consuming media (news, videos, social networks...).

Why pick the Wifi only:
When I was looking at Xooms at the local electronics establishment, I was confronted with the decision of getting the $599 Xoom Wifi or the $799 Xoom 3G/Wifi (upgradeable to 4G at a later date at no cost). For me, while 3G was tempting for convenience, it was still a pretty easy decision to buy the Wifi only device. With the 3G, you are tied into a service contract. If you go with Verizon's service (which is advertized with the device), you only pay $599 for the device, but you have to pay $20 a month for 24 months. On top of that, you can only use 1GB of data. For a device that is going to be used for the consumption of data (especially videos), I don't want to be limited to only 1GB. Another decision point was the fact that I knew my Xoom would be used mostly at home, where I have a Wifi network, or at local eatting establishments that provide free Wifi. The real nail in the coffin on this decision was that my 4G phone is capable of wireless teathering and my data plan is unlimited- taking that into consideration- there really is no need to pay for an additional data plan.

The Device- an out of the box look:
Out of the box, you find the approximately 1.5 lbs device, power cable, and a couple booklets. I would have been nice to have a sleeve for the Xoom, but Motorola doesn't provide any type of protection for the tablet. I made sure to pick up a [[ASIN:B004S748UY ZAGG invisibleSHIELD for Motorola Xoom (Screen) (MOTXOOMS)]] to make sure my screen stayed pristine. The device is a solid little tablet. The back id 4/5 aluminum and the top part of the back case is rubberized plastic.

The hardware feels solid. Additionally, the layout of the device generally makes sense. The power button was a little confusing, but once I found it on the back, the idea really grew on me. It will be a little wierd when it comes to accessories, but I have no complaint about the device itself. Next to the power button, there is the HD camera lense with LED flash. Having an HD camera is nice, even if shooting pictures on a tablet isn't really practicle. The back of the device also includes stero speakers that are surprisingly loud for a device of this size.

All of the connectors (power, usb, dock...) are all located on the bottom of the device, except the headphone jack. Not sure I am a fan of this oddity, but I have yet to use headphones, so it is not really an issue to date. Also, the volme buttons are located on the left side of the device and are sufficiently easy to reach and use.

On the face of the device, there is a forward facing camera- this is great for video chatting. While GTalk works, Skype currently does not support video chat on this device (app issue, not hardware). There is also a light senseor- I hate the light sensor- I sometimes find that the brightness of the screen changes abruptly by a huge amount because I accidently put my thumb over the sensor. The best fix for this is to just turn off the auto adjustment.

Orientation:
Deviating from the norm, the Xoom is built to be oriented in landscape mode rather than portrait mode. With the 10 inch screen, landscape works great. I find that I am able to thumb type on the on-screen keyboard without straining much to reach the keys in the middle. The size is really what makes landscape work well with this tablet. In portrait, I (like many others) find that the device is a little bit hard to balance- feeling a little top heavy. It isn't so bad that the device is difficult to use- it just takes a little getting used to.

Android:
The android 3.0, Honeycomb load on this device is great. Many who don't use android or are iPad users will probably find that the device will take a little bit of learning to get used to. I am an android user (though my phone has an older version of android), and found that I was able to fully use and understand the device in 30 minutes of playing with it. The learning period may take up to a day, but once you fiure it out, you will notice that the controls really make sense and are easy to find when you need them.

Overall, I love this little device. There are some minor little design dislikes, but nothing that impacts my 5 star rating of this device!

Overall, this little lens is perfectly sufficient for gaining view angle for your pictures.

The only thing I didn't like with this lens had nothing to do with the actual lens- the thing I don't particularly like is the little metal ring that you stick to your device so you can attack the lens magnetically. The little metal ring has a sharp corner on it that is annoying when you are handling your device. This may not be a big deal for devices you only use once in a while, but if you decide to stick one of the three rings that you get to your cell phone, you will notice it and your hands will drag over it frequently.

Other than that I like the lens and think it is a great non-permanent accessory for your camera!

When my iPod buds finally died on me, I decided I wanted in-ear 'phones. However, I was short on cash, so I decided against the Shures, Etymotics, and the like. I saw the Smokin' Buds in a store for $[...], and gave them a shot.

First off, the sound wasn't terrible. It was at least on par with the Apple buds. I had problems with the fact that the sleeves wouldn't stay put in my ears for any reason, slipping out almost as soon as I'd inserted them. In addition, the cord was rather thin, and anytime it rubbed against my clothing, or heaven forfend, my jacket's zipper, it would create enough noise to drown out my music. The nail in the coffin was the small chrome ring on the left bud. I had foolishly thought it was structural, but when it popped loose it turned out to be merely ornamental.

I took them back for a refund, and sent off a letter to the company expressing my dissatisfaction with their product. Much to my surprise, I was invited to try another pair, with the promise that improvements had been made and I was sure to find them more to my liking.

The buds that arrived in the mail were the Full Metal Jackets. The difference in construction is night and day. Where the bulk of the Smokin' Buds is plastic, these are aluminum. The sleeves never slip from my ears. The cord is far more durable, and thicker as well.

The sound was quite boomy when I first tried them, but I let them run at high volume for 24 hours on static to loosen them up. This helped quite a bit, and the sound continues to improve. It's still bottom-heavy, but turning off the EQ function on my nano helped balance it out. I really like that I can run my nano at half volume and still hear everything clearly. In fact, I would caution against running them at full volume while they're in, as I'm certain one would suffer hearing damage. My battery life has improved tremendously. I'm very happy with the sound and the comfort of these buds. I can't think of a better set of earphones for the price... and the warranty is first-rate.

9 February 2008: I sent my FMJ's back for a warranty repair, which turned out to be a warranty replacement. The jack on my 9mm FMJ's had developed a short, and was causing the left 'bud to cut in and out.

I received an RMA number within moments of contacting them at their website, [...], and while I paid for shipping the 'buds back, they replaced them immediately, free of charge. Not only did they replace them with a new set, they sent the 11mm FMJ's. The jack is a bit longer, in order to provide better strain relief, I suppose. Otherwise, the build quality is identical. More importantly, the sound is far better balanced top to bottom, and while the bass is still great, it no longer dominates the sound spectrum as it did on my 9mm's.

In short, the 9's are really good, and you can't get anything better (in my opinion) at the price, but the 11's are worth the extra money. All the things that made my experience such a positive one with the 9's is improved with the 11's. Definitely a 5-star rating.

These speaker pins were exactly what was needed to connect our stranded wire to the spring clip connectors on our speakers. Constructed like a Banana Plug, the pin head guarantees a good connection. The color coded males come 2 to a box, enough to hook up a pair of speakers. Being a staight pin reduces the chance of crossing the leads. The price is very low and includes fast shipping. Sring clip connectors have some shortcomings.  Unless the wire is cleanly stripped and cut to exacting lengths, strands of wire can be loose and short the hot to ground leads.  Also, they can be inconvenient as the wires must be disconnected when moving the speakers or cleaning and dusting near them.  The more often the leads are reconnected, the less the tension holding the wire becomes.  These shortcomings can create noise, stastic, even cause an amplifier to turn off or cause component repair problems.  These inexpensiive connectors reduce the chances of such problems while making a professional looking connection.

I was researching televisions for MONTHS and could not figure out which one to buy. He found this TV and after sorting out what could be "insider reviews" from genuine ones, we decided that it sounded like a great deal for the money, and though the name is not exactly a household one yet, it was worth a shot, as another buyer said the same thing happened with Vizio a couple of years back.

So, we bought it for each other as a joint Christmas gift, figuring what the hey. If it wasn't as advertised, we'd send it back. And it had a lot to live up to, considering this was essentially our only gift to each other this year. It has been over a month now, and we LOVE this television.

Pros:

- No side glare - you can see the picture well, even if you are sitting on the side of the television.
- It is lightweight and super thin, so it is easy to transport.
- Very clear picture.
- Decent enough sound - you don't really need a sound bar if you don't have one, especially since there are options to change the sound (i.e. "music", "film", "surround sound", etc.)
-Provided you are not signed in to a game system (which you can change the video input from your remote), there is a setting where the TV will automatically shut itself off after 10 minutes of lack of use. This is very helpful if you have a roommate who tends to fall asleep in front of the television.
- There are plenty of settings to customize the picture and sound, as well as "label" your game systems with the pre-loaded options so you know which video input to select for your X-Box or PS3 (for example, I have the PS3 set to "Blue Ray", whereas the X-Box is set to "Game").

Cons:

-It is not a "smart TV", if you are in the market for one of those. It's a simple design, which was perfect for us.
-There are no buttons on the TV itself, so if the remote ever breaks, I have no idea how we are going to turn it on and off, aside from buying a new remote.
-There are a shortage of plugs in the back for cables. For example, I can hook up the cable box, X-Box and PS3, but there is no room now for the sound bar. Not a huge deal, but I could see where some people might find that to be annoying.

This television lived up to all of the positive reviews it received here on Amazon, and I am so thoroughly satisfied that we decided to go with this one that I kept reminding myself to write this review so I could help others who were as in the dark as we were about which TV to buy. I didn't get the dreaded "green screen" upon turning it on, as some people have experienced, and the packaging didn't overly give it away that it was a TV, (though we got the 48" one, so I'm sure people could figure it out).

Bottom line: If you are in as much doubt as we were about which TV to buy, trust us on this one - TCL rocks!

For the simple fact that this camera can do EVERYTHING I want it to do in my pocket, it get 5+ stars. I could go on for days about this camera, but I will try to hold this review to my personal game-changers.

HFR: Shooting video at 1080p, 120fps (100MB) and slowing down the footage in post produces better slow-mo videos compared to the HFR feature that can do 1080p 240fps at the best quality. The ultra HFR feature was a big sell for me, but I feel like 480fps and 960fps have garbage quality and it's really really difficult to get the timing right when you are taking the shot in that feature mode because you only have a 2 second timeframe. I must have spent 2 hours trying to get a slow-mo shot of a bee in my garden when I first bought it, but could never get the timing right on pressing record when the stupid bee would start flying. Shooting in normal video mode at 120fps and slowing down in post at 24fps is seriously amazing, and I will likely never use the HFR again.

Time-Lapse: Pay the $9.99 extra to download this app, because holy cow, it is freaking awesome. There is full manual control over intervals, # shots, etc, and it blows me away that it can produce day-night time-lapse with little to no flicker and amazing color with accurate white balance throughout. If you don't want the hassle of editing the stills in post, then you can just have the camera produce a 1080p 24fps video file in-camera, although post allows you more creativity and ability to produce 4k time lapse.
Slog2: I've been shooting all my videos in Slog2 (4k & 1080p) since I bought the camera several months ago, and up until just now I did not have a computer beefy enough to process the footage in post (which is the reason I have waited on posting my review). For the last week, I've been color grading my Slog2 footage with the Color Finale plugin in Final Cut Pro X. The footage is stunning and the dynamic range blows me away. I'm still trying to figure out the over exposure sweet spot of shooting in Slog2, but for the most part it looks really nice when shot at +1 - +2 stops over exposed and re-adjusted in post. There's not as much noise in the shadows as I expected, and I'm about to get the Neat Video Noise Reduction plugin that I expect to help with the little noise that I'm seeing. I went out to Joshua Tree for the meteor shower and shot 4k 24fps video of the stars, which is insane for a little camera like this.

Lens: Having the faster lens fully zoomed in (f2.8) compared to the RX100 M1's f4.9 is changed the way I take photos of my baby. It really was difficult to get a decent bokeh shooting at typical portrait focal lengths with the M1, but very easy now with the M4. Fast, clean and crisp, this lens is great.

Compact Size: I wanted a camera that I can put in my pocket. As long as you don't wear skinny jeans, then you're good to go. I don't wear skinny jeans, but I'm just saying. Cargos are the best, but then I realize that I've become the dad that wears cargos, and then I see the guy in Honduras swapping heavy lenses with a dslr around his neck and don't feel so bad. Although, I often worry when it's in my pocket that the lens ring control might bend and not be as smooth as it is, but that hasn't happened.

Focus Modes: Changing between focus modes is my one gripe about this camera. In a run and gun environment, I have not been able to figure out how to easily toggle between the various auto focus modes. It's easy to go between MF and AF, but trying to toggle between the AF modes when trying to get the right video clip of my active baby is extremely difficult. However, note that using the lens ring in AF mode for rack focusing is possible, which I wasn't able to do on the RX100 M1.

Overall, I wanted a camera that could do EVERYTHING, do everything WELL, and that EVERYTHING it does WELL could fit in my pocket….

My house is 2400 sq. ft. and the router is upstairs. We pay for high speeds from our ISP but the signal downstairs where we have our big screen TV was weak... so weak that streaming videos was becoming a huge problem. I used a Netgear Nighthawk router with an expensive extender downstairs for the past 4 yrs. It did the trick until recently. The extender just wouldn't do the job downstairs no matter what I did. Additionally, the signal was extremely weak in the front of the house regardless of the extender.

Anyway, I decided to do some research. Thought I'd get a new extender but soon realized that would be like putting a bandaid on an existing problem. So, I asked around and was told to try a mesh system. Reviews for the Orbi are the best PLUS I'm used to Netgear and have had success with the brand in the past. I replaced the Netgear Nighthawk router with the Orbi router rather than using the new Orbi as an access remote. Set up the Orbi extender downstairs. It gave me a few issues in setup initially because I forgot to set up the desktop pc upstairs as "wireless" rather than with the ethernet cable. It finally dawned on me and then everything was okay. I had to reset EVERYTHING with the new wifi connection (cell phones, smart devices, Alexa, Smart TV, Firesticks, etc., etc.). You don't realize how many connections you have until you have to reset everything! LOL! One of the other things that I didn't realize until after I set up the Orbi is that it doesn't differentiate between bands. It just decides automatically which is the best one for your setup. One of the nice surprises is that the Orbi setup works with the Netgear Genie that I had on our upstairs desktop pc... it's a great tool to control the router, change channels, determine traffic, etc. I didn't have to do a thing because it just synched perfectly on its own!

The end result is that we have had ZERO issues with connectivity or signal since installing the Orbi. We now get speeds in excess of 200mbps throughout the house rather than as low as 20mbps downstairs. Of course, the speed is determined by your ISP plan but the signal throughout your property is determined by your equipment of choice. We are so happy with the Orbi and highly recommend it!

I really wanted to love this receiver, but the quality control and attention to product usability detail are not what I have come to expect (I'm spoiled by Apple attention to usability, no doubt)..

Let's start with the iControlAV2 iPad app, since that is a major reason why people want this receiver. The functions to setup the audio (eq etc) are nice, but you basically use them once. After that, your main use of the app will be changing volume and input, for zone 1 and zone 2 (if you enable zone two like I have).

Here are the major problems with this app control:

1 The receiver's wired ethernet port will power off with the receiver, and when it powers back on, it doesn't request to renew the same IP address it had before (even if 'before' was 5 seconds ago). This typically results in the receiver getting a different IP address, and the iControl app then giving you an error when you try to control your receiver on next launch. You have to then go back into the iControl settings and 'select your product'. Very annoying, and completely breaks the 'wife+kids friendly' possibilities of using app, completely. UPDATE: You can configure the receiver to make the receiver stay in 'standby' mode so you can turn it back on from the remote. I'll admit I simply missed this option in my earlier setup.

2 The iControl App lets you turn off both zones of the receiver, but if you do, you end up powering off the receiver and guess what? You can't turn it on again unless you physically push the power button on the front of the receiver.. which then gives you problem #1 again. UPDATE: This is rectified by enabling Standby mode in the network settings.

3 While 99% of customers are likely going to use this as an AirPlay device, confusingly AirPlay isn't mentioned anywhere in the user interface or on the Ipad application. You have to select 'H.M.G.' (Home Media Gateway), which then enables airplay. Works fine, but the other 90% of the HMG functionality is useless to me, and simply confuses the user interface. You can control song play / pause / next / last from the iControl App (effectively remote controlling iTunes), but this control is nowhere near the control you get with Apple's Remote app, which you will almost certainly want to use instead of the iControl app.

4 No iPhone / iPod touch version of the app. Pretty dumb, again considering the main use case of the app after the novelty of everything other than input control and volume wear off. UPDATE: There is now!

Problems with the receiver UI:
1) The receiver itself has a decent UI, but to configure many things you will need to have a TV display connected. The menus for this on-screen display look like bad shareware from 1992, but are functional enough. It seems crazy to me however, that a product with built in ethernet / IP networking wouldn't have a simple built in web server to allow configuration of inputs etc (everything the O.S.D. does) from your computer, or better yet your iPad. Navigating the On Screen Display to configure inputs and such is tedious and slow; this should have been completely configurable from my computer / iPad.

2) Zone 2 and 7.1 surround are mutually exclusive. While I knew this when I bought it, there is no reason why Pioneer couldn't have made a simple toggle to turn on zone two and automatically disable two of the surround speakers (which almost certainly wouldn't be used during zone 2 'music' listening anyway'. Perhaps nit-picking here, but an intelligent usability feature went completely overlooked here by a product team that clearly sought no customer input on this capability. UPDATE: OK, I figured out why there is no toggle! You have to wire the speakers completely differently if you want to enable zone two. So if you wire up 7.1 speakers, and want to have another pair of speakers off in another location (I have a pair over my desk), then your only option is to wire the remote speaker pair to what ends up being the 'Speaker B' outputs. These speakers get the same output as the main front R+L speakers, and you can toggle between A+B, A, B, or Both Off (which is pointless, in my opinion). Annoyingly, you cannot toggle the Speaker A/B/A+B/Off setting from the iControl AV2 iPhone/iPad application, which is a shame since this is simply a soft button control on the front of the receiver. This effectively makes the Speaker B -> Remote speakers option useless for me, since I would have to physically walk to where the receiver is from my office (different room). It still seems like Pioneer could have engineered this thing to allow 'soft switching' between 7.1 and 5.1 + Zone 2 settings from the iControlAV2 remote application, this would have provided maximum flexibility. As it is, if you plan on connecting 7.1 speaker setup, the Zone 2 features are completely unusable to you.

Miscellaneous minor complains:
1 No S-Video inputs or coax digital inputs.
2 No native zone-2 via my Harmony 890 (presumably not Pioneer's fault, but if I were the PM for this product I would make an effort to get prolific up to date support for all features in popular 3rd party products).
3) Only 1 subwoofer out (would be nice for a 2nd output for zone 2).
4) No AirPlay Video support. This means I have to add an AppleTV2 to one of the HDMI inputs on the Pioneer.. which means that the built-in AirPlay audio support in the Pioneer now serves no (unique) purpose and would be redundant.

Lastly, I had to return (to Amazon) the first VSX-1021 I was sent; after operating for a few hours, the HMG / network control functions would stop working, and would require a power cycle to rectify. A (lengthy) call to Pioneer tech support led to further frustration, as they wouldn't simply cross ship me a replacement, despite the unit being less than a month old. Their answer is to 'bring it to a Pioneer service center'. Oh yeah? And that service center is going to have a wireless network, ethernet switch, Apple iPad etc etc to duplicate my problem? Seemed fantastically unlikely. Fortunately Amazon picked up Pioneer's poor technical support slack and sent me an New In Box advanced replacement (I had already discarded my shipping box.. thanks Amazon!)

To be fair, i'm only picking on the things I don't like. The sound quality is quite good, and certainly that's incredibly important. All in all though, my main reason for buying this was multi-zone and AirPlay support. In hind-sight, I might just have bought something else and added a $100 AppleTV2 via Toslink digital out and saved myself the trouble (and had AirPlay video support).

3 Stars for now (UPDATE: making it 4) many of my complains could be addressed by a firmware update of the unit and updated iPad (and hopefully iPhone / iPod Touch apps).

After 3 months of use, I do like the Pioneer unit. However since I did expect to be able to use the Zone 2 features, i'm now in a quandary.. do I buy another VSX-1021 (or VSX-1121) to power the speakers above and behind my desk? I want Airplay for those too).

I got the newest 4K streaming stick with alexa voice control remote. As of yet i haven't purchased a 4K T.V. but the firestick works on any high def T.V. with a hdmi port. There are lots of free movie and T.V. apps so you can cut the cord and save lots of $$ doing away with cable. You will just have to simply connect a OTA antenna to the back of your TV to receive your local channels. The remote is ok but not great. It does sync easily with your T.V.s CEC control and lets you use the remote for T.V. power on and off. Volume control and alexa voice command. But personally i found it just as quick and easy to manually navigate the apps you want to watch rather than using the button on the remote to ask for a certain app. More times than not the voice control will get what your asking it wrong. But the volume control and power control on the remote is a very good plus over the basic remote. The battery compartment for remote is a little tricky to get opened at first but if you just apply a slight pressure at the same time as sliding the compartment down jt will slide right open. And getting to the streaming quality it will depend on which app you are using. Surprising to me is that the Amazon Prime Video app uses a lot more wifi data than most of the other apps making the shows and movies buffer quite a bit sometimes. I am curious why Amazon Prime uses so much more data vs Netflix or Hulu for example but it surely does. And if you have a Roku device and are used to the Rokus functions it will take a bit of getting used to how the Firestick apps are downloaded and stored compared to the Roku. But they both have equally good and bad comparisons when it comes to their individual functions. Both have excellent picture and sound. What i would really like is for Amazon's firestick to have a remote control app for your android or ios phone. Roku does have the free remote app to download and works great navigating and also has alexa voice control and tou can plug earphones into your phone for private listening. And also remember when buying a firestick to check the gift box if it is going to be used by someone else in their home. If you check the connect to my account box instead all of your information on your other firesticks will be on the new one and also the Amazon buying app with your personal information. So be vigilante and at least have a PIN set up on your Amazon account so no non approved purchases can be made.

Most of the time, I use mine with a Fiio E12A Mont Blanc Special Edition headphone amp, and Shure SE215 In-Ear monitors. I will also sometimes connect it using the line-out port to my car AUX input or my home stereo. It sounds great in all cases.

I tried 2 other antennas at this location and was less than thrilled by the results. One was an amplified unit that I purchased years ago that had two vertical antennas that could be independently positioned forward or backward up to a ~45 degree angle from a straight, vertical position with a rotating base. I don't recall it's brand, but it worked fairly well most of the time, but I found myself going back to the old method of adding aluminum foil to get the best reception. The second antenna I tried was an RCA amplified bar antenna. It picked up most channels, but I had to change its direction back and forth depending on whether I wanted the CBS or the NBC affiliate; I could receive most all other channels with either direction. I returned that unit to WalMart.

According to AntennaWeb.org, I should receive 27 channels from 13 stations; the government site stated that I should receive 8 stations with a strong signal, 1 station with a weak signal, and that I would not be able to receive 1 station in the area. With this antenna, my TV found 49 channels this morning when I re-ran the scan, including all the channels listed on both sites that I mentioned previously. The first night that I ran the scan, I was able to pick up over 50 channels, including Channel 5 from Nashville! It was very cloudy that night, and I assume that reception was due to a propagation anomaly since I have not been able to receive that channel since then.

I highly recommend this antenna. For the record, I ran this test 11 floors up in a high-rise apartment building in downtown Louisville. As others have noted, very slight changes in the orientation of the antenna significantly affects reception of some stations. My antenna is currently attach to a window on one side and bends around the frame and attaches to the wall on the other side of the antenna. (I recommend getting some of the 3M replacement strips to attach the antenna so that you can re-arrange it as needed.)
