This is an excellent machine for just about all uses except gaming which requires more power - but since I do not use it for gaming, I can highly recommend it.

These are by far the best blue tooth headphones I have used.  They arrived mostly charged (enough to last about 3 hours right out of the box).  They paired easily with more than one device, the sound quality is excellent and they are very comfortable to wear.  They also come with various size replacement ear buds and ear hooks.  A great product and a great deal for the price.

I have now purchased 2 of the Fire HD 8 inch tablets and am extremely pleased with both.  These are sturdy and still thin and lightweight.  As far as the mechanics, this is as good as an competitive tablet including the ipad mini.  I have the 16 gb and find that it is adequate for my use.  Some of the other reviews suggested that you will need an SD card for extra memory, but in my experience, that is only if you are storing a very high volume of photos and/or video.  Otherwise, it can manage several hundred books and audio books with no problems.  This is truly a fabulous tablet!

I already own more than one Kindle device as well as a Samsung tablet, but I love this reader.  It is small enough to take anywhere and is perfect for reading outdoors in sunlight.  The only drawback is that it does not have an audio function, so if I am both reading and listening to a book, I need a separate device.

This is a great portable CD player. The quality of the sound is excellent with no skipping. The headset is also good quality with nice comfortable ear buds.

There are much cheaper versions available, but this Sony version is well worth the price.

Hauppauge does it well. You do need an original Win-TV 7 or 8 install CD, (The win 8 version has more features) A $10.00 download from Hauppauge. If you don't have a Win-TV7 driver disk, The drivers are required. If you have a Win-TV7 disk, Win-TV 8 is free.

I've been using it for more than a month & 1/2 and I am impressed with the speed of this drive. Very snappy and it would be hard to tell the difference between this SSHD and a quality SSD without software statistics. I have an ADATA SSD as my primary. This drive is my #2 drive and for games and software. I have a 3.5", 1TB Barracuda for backups. I figure if this drive last's a year, I'll upgrade it to 5 star's. I do have a 60mm CPU cooling fan blowing on it so if heat is a concern, I can't test that. This is a laptop hard drive but works great in a desktop due to less space requirements. All PC's I build new from here on will have 2.5" drives of whatever type. By the way.

The PWM fan on this cooler is so quiet I can't even hear is. I was running 130 degree F with the stock AMD CPU cooler on a 6300 running at 3800 MHz. After installing the Enermax my CPU temp dropped to 95 degrees while recording two movies at the same time and surfing the internet. I am very pleased with a 35 degree drop in temp and the fan hasn't gone over 1222 RPM.
Good fans, very quiet and look cool in my AMD  red case
You cant love a fan but this is a very good one. It ramps up and down, moves a lot of air and is very quiet.
A very good and stable PSU. For the price with a 3 year warranty, it would be hard to beat. Mine is very quiet, I can't even hear it run.

It is a very good power supply. Very quiet, the cooling fan ramps up and down as needed, I would say (very solid). It can easily run three drives and a video card. Don't expect it to replace and fit in the same space as the Rosewill PSU in the R-379 HTPC case. What a hunk of junk that that psu is. The Solid Gear is longer and blocks off the case blower out fan by 1/3. I kept it because it works great, I bought a motherboard extender cable and now my psu sit's outside the case. Not a problem because it's all in a cabinet anyway.

This cooler is better than I expected. When installing you can rotate 90 degrees from center and totally clear your memory. The heat sink and fan are awesome. This cooler will cool your motherboard chipset, and the entire board. I will purchase again. The fan is silent, I have this installed on a new build ASUS mobo with an AMD A10-5800k APU and the noise level is zero. I have my new HTPC sitting next to my older one, I built a few years ago, with a Zalman cooler and I can hear the Zalman but cannot hear the Gelid Shero. Very well designed and manufactured. The heat sink radiator fins are wide enough apart not to allow dust buildup and I see no reason this cooler should be limited to an HTPC case. The thing I like the most is the fan spins at lower RPMs due to it's size and blade design. You don't have to tweek the RPMs electronically because the Shero cools regardless and shuts off when not required. Very unlike my Zalman that has to run constantly to maintain a 40 c temp under no load on the APU and MOBO.

This is a good combo drive if you don't plan on writing Blue Ray discs and all your writing/burning requirements are CD/DVD. This is a very good drive, very quiet and I didn't need any special drivers or software to make it work. I loaded Windows 7-64 with this drive on a new system build with zero issues. The only reason I didn't give five stars is the face looks just like the picture. Jet black with no detail other than the green activity LED.
I bought this set for my nephew. They sound good for the price, are comfortable and I like the way they fold up.
I use mine as a jumper/extender, frequently.

I still haven't decided who makes the best drives, Seagate or Western Digital. But I do know this, it's a dead heat race.
I am currently using 3 Seagate and 3 WD drives. The Seagate drives are very quiet and fast, and I haven't had one fail on me in 10 years (since I stopped buying computers and building my own) but you have to temper that knowledge with the fact that these drives are spinning at 7200 RPM so I always have a cooling fan on my drives. I learned the hard way some years ago and lost tons of critical data. I'll buy more of their drives in the future because they are proven to me as fast, quiet and reliable.

They are very comfortable, you can do whatever and they won't fall out, and they sound fantastic, certainly for the price.
A very good product I'll recommend to anyone.

This board has lots of features, can hold more ram than you'll ever need and is a good board for an HTPC case. The 7.1 surround sound is also pretty impressive. My setup has the AMD Liano 3870 APU turbo clocked at 3.3mhz, Zalman cpu cooler, Radeon 6570 GPU for dual graphics, Samsung combo dvd/blue-ray, a 1 TB HDD, 16 megs of ram, and a combo usb flash drive/mem chip reader, in a slim HTPC case. The machine does exactly what I wanted. Record and play movies, videos and music very smoothly. The boards graphical interface software is very cool and easy to use in Windows or on boot up, to change the bios settings. I'm only using a 300 watt power supply and this setup runs smooth as silk. No hiccups or blue screens. I do have a couple of extras installed, HD TV tuner card, side mount case fan, hard drive cooling fan, and a dual SATAIII rear bracket. A nice board, I like it! Also I should mention. I'm running 3 TV tuner recorder cards, one internal, two external and this set up will record three shows at once or two while playing one, with Windows 7.1 Media Center.

A very good fast drive, very quiet but then again all WD drive are quiet now, compared to the 1980's, there is no comparison.
I make certain all my drives are adequately cooled by on board case fans or I install a fan on each drive.

This is a good solid APU. It does run a little warm when turbo clocked but I'd say, get a good cooler like a Gelid Super Hero for an HTPC and also a high performance case exhaust fan. and problem solved.
I'm running this chip on an ASUS F1A75-M motherboard combined with a relatively inexpensive Low profile Radeon 6570 GPU for dual graphics and it does everything I wanted my HTPC to do. Record and play movies, audio files and blast some sound. With my Asus FM1 MATX board, plus 16 megs of ram, It runs smooth as silk for movie recording and playback.

Update on 8/6/16: still running solid like a champ. Granted it's usefulness is tech outdated but running very solid.

I haven't had a single problem with these hard drive cooling fans since I started using them two years ago. The fan is so quiet you can't hear it run when it and the hard drive are installed in the case. As a matter of fact, even a good hard drive makes more noise.
Other than the fact that my drives remain very cool to the touch, I don't have any scientific data through testing supporting their use, other than, it makes perfect sense to me. The fan comes with the screws needed to install it to the drive however, you will need to plan your fan and drive mounting into your case. The four pin Molex connections are very simple and the fan will go on/off with your drive.

All in all, this little case is a good buy with the 300 watt PSU. The PSU is also very quiet.

things I did to help in cooling was to install a hard drive cooling fan. I also upgraded my CPU fan and heat sink.
My other complaint is the removable drive cage could be designed a little better for the 3.5" drive bay to facilitate
various internal hardware such as a 3.5" card reader/extra USB ports, 3.5" bay housing
with 2.5" HDD's, etc...
Other than that, this is a good case and it looks good lying horizontal or standing vertical.
If you plan on standing the case vertically, make certain your CD/DVD/BD can do the same.
I installed an ASUS blue ray burner that does both.

The packaging alone speaks quality and the individual cases are very well made.
So far I've burned two music videos flawlessly and this review may be a little premature
however I have every expectation that the 3 remaining DVD's will burn equally as well.
I also noticed an increase in burning speed while using Windows Media Center.

I purchased two of these cables as a replacement for the springy , stretch, cables for use with my two set's of head phones. Getting the length right is important and these were perfect for me. The mini ends are very well made and the cable it self is stout.

So let's get into it!

I assembled version 1 and to my distraught face, the stand was incredibly wobbly. The pole piece mostly didn't fit the screw cuttings in the metal and overall the product was incredibly dissatisfying and took forever to essentially assemble wrong (since correct assembly was impossible).

Meanwhile, my friend raves about how great it is (he got version 2). So seeing some folks had similar issues, I contacted support. About a week later I received a very nice message back. The thing I appreciate most is this wasn't a simple PR cut and paste. This sounded like it was directly from someone who really cared.

He took my address and promised to ship out a replacement with Version 2 immediately. Not only that, he actually explained in detail the issues I had experienced and how they had fixed them with Version 2. He even went as far as to confirming version 2 was shipped to my friend.

Thanks again for everything.

I find the bass response lacking when compared to a Lapai amp driving Micca Club speakers. Don't get me wrong, they don't sound terrible, but just not the sound I was expecting. I realize that everyone has different tastes, so this is only one mans opinion....
UPDATE: I have changed my original 2 star rating to 4 stars. Reason being I was originally not happy when connected to my computer. But I purchased an Amazon Dot and now I am pleased with the bass response of these units. However, I must admit that still prefer the Bose Companion 2 speakers to these which are priced the same. Again, this is only my humble opinion.....

Already owned an Echo, but really did not like the lackluster sound when playing music.  So I bought a Dot (at Bed, Bath and Beyond) because the black units where on backorder at Amazon.com.  Hooked the unit up to a pair of Bose Companion 2 powered speakers via the 3.5 mm output jack on the Dot.  Really sounds so much better than the echo.  My only problem is that the output jack on the Dot is a little touchy, but once locked in everything is fine.  Not worth a trip to exchange.  I still use the echo in my bedroom.  I live in a small house, and only the unit closest to my location responds.  Very impressive.....

I was lucky enough to get two of these computers a couple of months ago at a great price.  Both machines have worked flawlessly.  They are fast and quiet.  I wanted windows 7 because I am old and did not want to have to learn a new operating system.  7 will not be supported after Jan. 2020,  So I have lots of time left on these before I have to upgrade or buy new computers.  Anyway, I am very pleased with these PCs.

Call me old school, but I think wired networks are the way to go, for speed, security and reliability.  I have been using a Dynex 4 port wired router which was working fine, but I now need more ports.  I have two computers, and 3 Roku wired set top boxes and plan to add the Ooma Telo VOIP in the near future.  Finding this unit at such a low price surprised me.  But after reading mostly good reviews, I thought it was worth a try.  Glad that I did.  It was simply plug and play.  Up in running in just a few minutes.  The good news it that when running only my main computer my speed increased from 54 mbps to 61 mbps.  While streaming one Roku box speed on the computer dropped to 47 mbps.  I will never be running more that two devices at a time on my network, so I am very happy with this router.  A couple of small things, I wish the unit was not white and black.  I would have preferred all black.  Like most new electronics the LED lights are too bright.  I found a good way to solve that a few years back.  I use a layer or two of static smoked tint window film you can buy at Home Depot or Lowes.  Perfect fix.

Have been using the companion 2 series 2 speakers for several years and was very happy with them.  When I saw the series 3 at a local store I decided to see if they were any better than the series 2.  They are exactly the same size.  They are now black, rather than gray. I like the black more than the gray.  The input jacks are now mini jacks rather than the RCA jacks on the series 2, which is an improvement.  The series 3 can be turned off with the volume control, the series 2 had no on/off control.  It was on all the time.  The series 3 draws so little power I leave them on all the time anyway.  NOW THE BIG QUESTION:  DO THEY SOUND BETTER THAN THE SERIES 2?  In my opinion, they sound exactly the same as the series 2 they replaced. So unless you want any of the features new to the series 3, I would recommend saving your money.  The series 2 was a great product, and so is the series 3.  Bose makes outstanding products.

This is a pretty nice looking and functioning keyboard/mouse wireless combo. It is plug and play easy set up. Works very well. No problems detected while typing or using the mouse. I do think that the mouse is too flat. It needs to be more rounded at the top, however, I am getting used to it. The box also contained a CD with software that shows caps lock, scroll lock, numbers lock, on screen as there are no lights on the keyboard for that. The software also displays battery state on both the keyboard and the mouse. After installing the software these items are displayed in a box on the right lower portion of the screen. The box containing this information is rather large and in my opinion is not worth the trouble to display it. I also had my computer lock up several times after installing the software, but once I removed the software everything was fine. So I would suggest not using the software, it is not required for normal operation. I was using a Microsoft 800 combo before this unit, and I like the size, looks, and action of this keyboard much more. I recommend this item....

3/5/13 - A problem has developed since I wrote this review. Sometimes the mouse or keyboard will not wake my desktop computer from "sleep". When this happens I am still able to wake the computer from sleep using the computer start button. This problem is happening about 10% of the time. I have used several other wireless keyboards and mice and have never had this problem. Not a deal breaker, but annoying......

Not a whold lot to say.  This is a very good looking keyboard.  As the others have said the cord is too short.  I had to add an extension USB cable to reach my computer.  The key action is as good as keyboards costing much more.  I like the volume controls on board.  I do wish that it had adjustable feet for height adjustment.  But I do like the feet, becuase they have a rubber coating that really keeps the keyboard from sliding around.  For such a low price I really have no major complaints, and consider this an excellent buy from Amazon.

Using this little amp as an headphone amplifier.  Well built small unit.  Lots of inputs, little heat generation (no fan required).  Treble and Bass controls work very well.  This is a very nice amp at a very low price.  Most happy with this purchase!

Bought these for my hard of hearing 96 year old father.  Most headphones produce so much bass that it makes it impossible for the hearing impaired to hear the dialog in movies and other TV broadcasts that have music in the background.  I had tried all types of headphones for him, but none worked until now.  These headphones do not produce an overwhelming amount of bass as all the others do.  It does have base, but not too much.  The headphones are comfortable,the in line volume control is a must have feature.  I cannot say enough good things about these.  I also purchase a small Pyle 40 watt amp to boost the output from the TV and to give him control of the bass and treble.  The combination of these headphones and the Amp (from Amazon) have made watching TV so much more enjoyable for him.

Bought this unit a few weeks ago at Target when it was cheaper than Amazon. Now the prices are virually the same at the two stores.  I read the good reviews and decided to give this a try.  It looks better than the pictures.  It is small enough to fit in front of the TV without blocking controls or remote sensor.  The sub is small and easy to place out of the way.  I have a 5.1 system from Pioneer and love it.  But I must admit the sound from the Philips is just about as good, just no surround.  I know of no other sound bar at any price that gives you so many input choices and they all cost way more than this little wonder.  I think you will be happy with your purchase.

Still can't believe how small this thing is.  As the other reviews stated it is very, very quiet.  It did have some bloatware that took a little time to remove.  Updates to windows and other programs took about an hour.  Not too long.  Documentation is pretty much non existant, however, the unit is basically plug and play.  THE ONLY ISSUE:  as others have stated, this unit WILL NOT PLAY NETFLIX HD!  I hope this problem gets resolved in an update from somewhere.  I would have given this computer 5 stars except for this one issue.  It is a little slower than my small form eMachines desktop.  But is does better than I expected.  Recommended for anyone looking for a nice little HTPC.

When I had a power outage right in the middle of a Windows Update I deceided I had to get a UPS. I spend a lot of time researching my options. This unit seemed like the best deal providing an LCD readout and the ability to easily turn of all alarms.

Unit is well built. Documentation is adequate. Easy to set up. I did not install the provided computer software, as the LCD screen on the unit gives me plenty of information.

When connections were complete and everything powered on (HP slimline desktop Computer, Modem, Router and 23" LED Monitor to the batttery outlets) the readout indicated I was only using 40% of the UPS output and that I could expect a battery back-up of 22 minutes. More than I had expected. I unpluged the unit and everything worked perfectly. All conected units stayed on, as if the power was still plugged in. Pluged the UPS back in and the unit went back to the household current. PERFECT...

I highly recommend this unit. For the price, it cannot be beat!
UPDATE 8/22/14: Unit continues to perform well. I have installed the software, and find it very good. I don't know how long the battery will last before it will need to be replaced, but this was money well spent. I hope they produce this product for many more years.

UPDATE 7/9/16: The unit finally needed a battery replacement. So I got 5 and a half years life out of the battery. Not bad.....

Sound quality great & easy to use:)

I liked how you can change the color easy and the 3.0 charger. I disliked the background static. I used it for my car.
Works sounds better than previous versions

If you're looking for an inexpensive but very good radio \Bluetooth speaker, this is it. The sound quality isn't perfect but it's very good. If you're looking for speakers for dubstep or heavy bass, you'll need to spend more but it does have good bass for everything else. Additionally, the bass level is adjustable with the tone knob. It's loud, not house rocking loud, but loud enough to hear well outdoors from my living room.
I was surprised to see that this is not rechargeable but connects to the wall, so, not portable. This, however, was exactly what I wanted because every BT speaker I've had breaks down at the charger port. I bought and returned the SEVIZ "40 watt" (actually 4 ten watt speakers) in less than a month for exactly that reason.
I'm not surprised by all the complaints about the radio adjustment given that we live in a time that people have gotten used to everything being automatic, but if you're old enough to know how to use a radio like one from the 80s on back, it's not a problem. It is, after all, a "vintage", non digital, speaker. If you want more precise radio adjustment, buy one with digital tuning.
I get so many stations it's ridiculous and I live at 6000 feet, rural, at least a half hour away from all but two stations, so, if you're not getting stations you must really be in the boonies. I get stations from Mexico and I'm 45 minutes away. The stations also come in very clearly with no interference at all.
I have had a slight issue with the BT competing for a connection with my other speaker and then having a connection with no media or no phone and having to manually reset the connection, but this only happens if both speakers are on.
It's also very solidly built, although, it is manufactured in China. It's MDF, not wood, but it looks great. It's also not one of those vintage speakers you get and end up surprised at how dinky it is and how much it looks like a kid's toy. It's big for a BT speaker.
For the price, this is a great speaker. For the price, you're not getting a Kenwood, an automatic tuner, or tons of bells and whistles. If you want a good speaker for YouTube, TV, or other generalized use, this is it. I definitely recommend it. I'll update if anything untoward happens down the road.

I've waited 4 months to write a review for this and I must say I'm more than happy with it. Perfect smart TV with everything you need. Took one star off due to measurements on given for outside dimensions, who really cares about that when you are placing a product inside to fit! Deduct a half inch overall due to thickness of product. Overall the product is very good and well made for the price.

I spent a LOT of time looking for an LED/LCD tv to go in my bedroom. I had planned to go smaller than 46'' but in the end I chose this TV because of the stellar reviews and the incredible feature list.

Wow. I really like this modem. This is a barebones rock solid dead simple workhorse.

It's got a plug for the cable and one ethernet (RJ-45) port out and I think an on/off switch.
That's it. It makes a connection. And hasn't failed since I got it a month or so ago.

All I had to do was call my ISP and give them the MAC address (on the sticker on the device)
and they updated their tables and that was it. Turn it on. It goes through the startup cycle. Takes a few minutes to connect like they all do and that's it. Set it and forget it.

What prompted me to get it, is I don't like having to rent the modem from the ISP @ $10.00/mo forever. This literally pays for itself in 16 months, and most people will have their Internet connection for many times that long, and time flies. So it's a good investment.

It doesn't have phone connection like the ISP's modem did. So I called the company/provider that owns copper phone lines in the area and ordered landline service. I'm a nerd/techie and don't care what people say about landlines being for old fogeys, it's like having a backup generator ... I know I can use that landline if the power goes out or if the cell tower gets overwhelmed (too many calls or cell traffic at once), or there's radio interference in the area. Technically cable phone is a 'land line' (hardwired cable connection to provider) and the battery backup in the modem (which the ISP charges more for), could give you emergency phone service in an outage, but a cable phone connection can (and does) fail for more reasons than copper wire phone service does. (Those copper wire connections are called POTS - which stands for Plain Old Telephone Service), and copper wire phones are the most reliable.

Having a separate modem from a router is optima for a few of reasons... Generally hybrid units of anything do everything okay, but nothing optimally (for example combination modem-router units like my ISP rents out). Better to keep the modem separate from the router. Then you can swap either out independently to upgrade as needed, disrupting less of your own network configuration doing so, and also help avoid a single point of failure. Plus, you might be able to score a router in a pinch on shorter notice than a cable modem if the router is the component that fails. Then you can choose the router you actually like, for whatever reason, and don't have to settle for whatever bundling du jour your ISP decides is right for you (even if it isn't).

That gets me to the other point. What DID the ISP decide was right for me (but wasn't)?

For awhile my ISP modem connection was dropping briefly in the middle of the morning. My computer came back up connected to the ISP's 'general public' wi-fi connection to their router which did not work for me and I'd have to keep manually switching back to my own internal Wi-Fi LAN (network). That was not only inconvenient but it forced me to investigate was was going on there.

I learned my ISP gives lets passersby connect to their rental-modem's Wi-Fi signal, without giving me any way to disable that service! That really pissed me off to learn. The idea is that people driving around who have accounts with the provider can get internet access around the neighborhoods. If I was a passerby, that could really help me, so at first glance maybe 'why not, be a good samaritan'.

But wait! There may be more too it than that.

Besides the fact that I don't like it (for good reason), they give me no control over that 'feature'!
And I see some downsides. What's good for the ISP isn't necessarily optimal for me.

What I don't like about that 'service' is that one or more people could sit outside and suck down bandwidth (e.g. slow my connection down), unbeknownst to me. It also might cause the unit to use more energy and put out a stronger wi-fi signal than it needs to. Which health conscious people are well advised to be aware of. Wi-Fi is radiation. Not strong and may not ruin your life, but it is a stressor at a cellular level, this is known. And strong signals, persistent signals and people who are more sensitive or have immunity issues can be more vulnerable (headaches, sleep disruption, or worse). But I like Wi-Fi so I settle for whatever unknown health consequences I may not be aware of.

Also it makes me wonder if a hacker might be able to use it as an additional point of access to my home network.

I also wonder if it's 100% clear to law enforcement at first glance who might be visiting sites or doing something nefarious from the connection point. Might it look like the owner is doing something that a passerby did (and even if they can sort it out later, what if it takes awhile to figure out and they make a bad assumption?)

Anyway, I don't have that problem with this modem and I'm just much happier with it all the way around.

Plus it's blazingly fast.

In 2 words: it works. I can plug in the adapter into my car's USB port and after about 20 seconds it connects to my phone, a Samsung Galaxy Note 20 Ultra 5G.

However, getting everything working was not without some initial installation woes. Here are my observations.

1. Download the app from the Google Play Store.
2. Plug the unit into your car's USB port that connects to the car stereo
3. Start the app, go through the prompts, then pair the adapter with your phone via Bluetooth. This is where I had some difficulties. Pairing took a bit of time.
4. The app will search for a firmware update. If one is available, download & install the update. Note: the AAWireless adapter forces a Wi-Fi connection to your phone and will download the firmware update using your cellular connection. Poor connection = slow download & update. This was the 2nd source of frustration.
5. Adapter will restart and attempt to reconnect with your phone. This was the 3rd source of frustration. The phone & adapter weren't pairing/connecting. I had to view the FAQ's in the app, then perform a few configuration changes in my phone. This could be a bit much for some users.
6. I ended up doing a reset of the adapter & deleting the app before reinstalling it.
7. After repeating the above steps, the unit paired via Bluetooth & established the Wi-Fi connection necessary for Android Auto. Everything worked perfectly.

Having the wireless Android Auto functionality is a huge benefit. The unit works great & sounds great. I don't notice any delays or interruptions when playing music or audio books, nor any hiccups using Google Maps.

However, word of advice. Make sure the Hub is connected to a reliable 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi access point and assign the Hub a static IP address. This will ensure a stable connection within your network to control Wi-Fi devices, specifically the Roku Streaming Stick. Also, the Elite remote does not provide control of RF devices: I wasn't able to setup my Luminoodle bias lighting because of this fact.

I wanted to be able to incorporate the Harmony Hub Extender with Harmony Elite remote into my existing Z-wave network, to control lighting. It was easy enough to pair it with the Hub and download new firmware to it.

However, there was quite of bit of trial & error to get it paired with my Qolysys Z-wave panel. Many times it would not pair properly. And the Extender & Hub kept going offline, making it hard to do anything.

So I read some advice online and did the following: (1) do a reset to factory defaults for both the Harmony Hub & Extender, (2) swap the power adapter for a fast charger, giving the unit a more robust power supply, (3) made sure Hub was connected on the 2.4 GHz side of my Asus Wi-Fi Lyra mesh system, (4) assigned a static IP address to the Hub, (5) added & removed the Extender several times from the panel and (6) not try to make the Extender a secondary controller of the Z-wave network.

Eventually using the mobile Harmony app, the Extender started recognizing all of my devices. I can now reliably control lighting & the thermostat from the remote. It complements the control I have from the panel & the Alarm.com app.

Was it worth the effort? Probably not. But got the Harmony Elite, Hub & Extender as refurbished units for half the price of new, so that dampens the frustration some.

To enter the BIOS, press the DEL key repeatedly during startup. If that doesn't work at first, try "restart" from Windows. Try using a PS2 keyboard (purple circular connector).

The machine uses UEFI. UEFI is is common on new machines, but was uncommon a few years ago and is likely a reason why installing a different operating system is not as straightforward as one would expect. Note that along with UEFI comes a different hard disk partition scheme: GPT (instead of the older MBR). I had trouble installing Ubuntu, but was eventually successful. Should be easier now since I helped isolate a bug in the boot-repair package.

Reinstall tips:

* From the BIOS, try disabling SecureBoot and/or FastBoot.
* If installing Ubuntu, start with the Ubuntu UEFI community documentation (not the older UEFIBooting page)
* If nothing else works, try enabling CSM (Compatibility Support Module), which should allow you to boot without UEFI. Note that you'll need to revert your disk to using MBR---I had mixed success with CSM.

I wanted to find a cheaper alternative to my wife's wireless Bose headset, something with decent noise cancelling for flights and work. So far I've used Bose, the MPOW H5, Treblab, and Woltix with ANC.

Nothing will compare to Bose noise cancellation - but these Woltix are actually really nice for the money. The MPOW H5 don't have as good audio clarity as the Treblab, but at the end of the day I got noise cancelling headphones for the noise canceling. I ended up returning the Treblab and the MPOW H5 and I kept the Woltix because they are more comfortable than the MPOW and had the best low-price ANC. The MPOW also had some sound interference issues randomly when the ANC was on, and the Treblab had a slight hiss to them when ANC was on.

I ended up keeping the Woltix brand. They just work, they're very light, and they are not too tight on the ears. The Active Noise Cancellation isn't as good as Bose, but they actually work pretty well for a $65 set of wireless ANC headphones. For the price, I'm very happy.

The ONLY thing I don't like about these is that there is no battery meter display on my iPhone when these are connected via bluetooth. With the other brands there is a small battery meter. I have no idea when these are low, so I just charge them like once a week.

So, quick breakdown of my experience with these wireless ANC headsets:

Bose: Best noise cancellation, good audio, comfortable, but definitely expensive!
Treblab: Best audio, worst noise cancellation (you can hear a slight hiss when turned on), comfortable, but large and they don't fold down too small.
MPOW: Good audio, good noise cancellation, but was getting some weird sound interference with the ANC on sometimes. Tight on ears.
Woltix: Good audio, good noise cancellation, most comfortable (way lighter and less tight on the ears than the MPOW), and fold down the smallest. No battery meter displayed on phone.

This past weekend I got to use both the SN600N and the Yongnuo YN568EX with the YN622 triggers. Basically both function completely with the YN622 triggers in both manual and iTTL modes. The only thing that I noticed with the SN600N was that manual power 1/1, 1/2, 1/4 all seem to be about the same output using the YN622 triggers - you have to lower it to 1/8 or less to start seeing lower outputs. Not a huge deal, but I'd like more output options. More on this below:

Here are a few details that a pretty important about these two alternatives to the Nikon SB series:

a) The 568 light is much higher quality - and I really mean the LIGHT quality. It is even, consistent, and clear. On the other hand, the SN600N is very scattered - what I mean by this is there are lines of brightness and darkness from the flash burst. This must be an internal flash "lens" issue - whatever the light is bouncing around and through within the flash is creating texture and light inconsistencies. This is not the case with the 568.

b) Yes, the SN600N is a more powerful flash, but in my opinion, it needs to have more levels of output on the lower end (1/256) because it's TOO bright for some situations. I use grids and modifiers during wedding receptions, and I like balancing the natural light with the flash output. 1/128 with the SN600N is equal to about 1/64 on the 568. I use the 568 at 1/128 quite a bit for details - so this was kinda a bummer to me.

c) The AF beam on the SN600N is better and more centered than the 568 - but they both need to improve designs. The ONLY reason I'm holding onto my Nikon SB900 at this point is the AF beam - which makes accurate AF possible in pitch black - no joke. The AF beam on the Yongnuo is a joke - they need to fix it on the 622 triggers too - it's basically worthless and too bright/annoying to the subject.

d) In my experience using the 568EX, the batteries get warm and stay warm, whether you're using the flash or not. If the flash is on, the batteries will get warm. It also EATS through batteries. I used to be able to photograph 2 weddings without recharging my Nikon SB setup (using SB600 previously) - now I have to recharge between weddings. I've upgraded to 2800mah EBL AA rechargeable (previously using Amazon 2000mah) and it has helped quite a bit.

So this is my current setup: SB900 on camera, 2x 568EX off camera group A+B for reception lighting, and then SN600N as group C for periodic fill. Rather than commit to a single brand, I'm using them all as tools for different situations, because they all work differently. I also am really enjoying the SN600N as on-camera if I don't need the AF beam - the quality of light is bright, crisp and rich - and the SN600N "brain" (basically how it works using iTTL mode) just works really well with Nikon - it's a very consistent flash, sometimes even better than my SB900. I like that it can zoom all the way to 200mm, too. If the SN600N had a better AF beam and better quality of light, I would ditch my SB900 and use it all the time. But I switch between the SB900 and the SN600N for different effects. I actually like the previously mentioned internal lens flash inconsistencies at times - it creates a grittiness that I like.

Point of clarification: If you're NOT using optical wireless, and you ARE using radio triggers (such as the YN622), then you do NOT need the SN. The N will give you all the same options at $50 less.

I own both this drive and the Western Digital WD10JPVT - nearly identical drives, but there are a few differences.

At the end of the day, I'd end up purchasing the Samsung M8 for a few reasons.

I'm usually a WD fan, but the Samsung M8 is faster in most practical user situations. Most reviews will state the WD drive as being faster, but that is only with very large file copy sequences - writing/reading files in this way is not what most people want a drive for.

The Samsung M8 is zippier with practical file operation - such as flowing through large batches of music or photography. If you edit photographs, the Samsung will be faster. If you are moving large batches of HUGE files (such as ISO's, disc images, etc), the WD will be faster, but only by 3-4 MB/s. For how much faster the Samsung is in most areas (nearly double the speed, 40mb/s vs. 20mb/s), getting the Samsung is more practical.

The Samsung is almost double the speed of the WD with most file operation, such as editing photography or flowing through music.

This is unquestionably the best docking station for any MacBook that supports Thunderbolt 3. I have tried several other similar devices and they all had serious problems, while this provides 87W of power, dual display support (DisplayPort 1.2), both an analogue and digital audio (TOSLINK) device, SD card reader, and extra 5 Gbps Thunderbolt 3/USB-C and USB 3.0 ports.

Regarding the 1 star reviews, with the exception of the person with the defective unit, I am almost positive the problems people have been having are because of their cables. Most people don't realize that the white USB-B cable that comes with their MacBook (which they probably just use for power) is Thunderbolt 2 and will NOT support Thunderbolt 3 devices! To connect your computer to the dock, use the cable they provide. If you need a longer cable, be sure to buy an actual Thunderbolt 3 cable that is less than 2 meters long. As for your display cables, it is critical the cable is DisplayPort 1.2. I also connected the second monitor to the Thunderbolt 3 port that converted to DisplayPort 1.2 (I just got the Amazon Basics brand and it works as it should. I have used this on both my 2017 and 2019 MacBooks and they both work flawlessly. Its so nice to just have one cable to plug and unplug for all devices!

2nd Update: Virtiv support confirmed that the display wake-up issue described below with the MacBook Pros is a known issue with this switch's firmware. I am told they will swap out your switch with one that is updated. Unfortunately, it would seem that Amazon's stock of this item as well the 2 display version have this issue. Since this is literally the only DisplayPort KVM that even remotely works with a MacBook Pro I would suggest this is worth the trouble if you fall in that category. (I haven't gotten mine back yet but I will update this when I do to confirm it's working properly.)

I also purchased the two display version and there is a problem where it creates a "stutter" in mouse movement that makes it painful to use. Even the MacBook Pro's built-in trackpad is affected by this problem! Vertiv again said that this is a firmware issue that is known about and has been fixed in later versions so a replacement is necessary.

UPDATE: I finally ran into a case where the display wouldn't show a signal even though my MacBook behaved like the monitor was attached. The case is when the MacBook wakes up from sleep. Otherwise, it works flawlessly. Also, I discovered that a "premium UHD" DisplayPort I bought on Amazon actually created problems where there wasn't one before. (If it aint broke...). When I swapped out my no-name DP cable for the fancy new one all I accomplished was creating the same problem I just described (the problem that afflicts all display switching with cheaper KVMs) where my original no-name 4K cable worked fine (except for the sleep issue.) Therefore, if you see this problem with your MacBook and your dock or KVM, try swapping out the DP cable! It would appear that Apple's DP support over USB-C is really bad.
Original Review:
For whatever reason, the new MacBook Pro support of DisplayPort from the USB-C port is very flakey. With other high-end KVMs I found that when switching back to my MBP, nearly all KVMs - even the renowned, industry-standard Black Box KVM had problems Getting sync emulation to work reliably switched to another computer and I had to replug my display cable to get the monitor to work even though the graphics card still thought the display was connected. Even with this switch, using some DisplayPort cables had the same problem with this switch but using standard 4K cables (not the flashy woven kind) worked great. Just be careful what cables you use with your MBP and you’ll be fine. The audio and USB lock feature is also super useful.

Also, you should get a good dock if for your MBP that provides full power to the USB-C port as this makes everything work better. I have found the USB-C to DisplayCables are not very good and require resets a lot. Again, I think it’s because Apple’s doing a bad job with DisplayPort. The dock has its own conversion so DisplayPort is native at that point. The CalDigit dock is worth every penny,

ASUS makes excellent routers overall with the added bonus of being compatible with a variety of free-ware router software like DD-WRT, Tomato, and Merlin-WRT (recommended). It includes all of the features you need for a proper home LAN, far better than the junky wireless routers offered by your internet provider, especially Comcast XFinity. (Don't believe the hype- their equipment is terrible.)

Some great features include
- Great 802.11ac support (5 GHz wireless support)
- Legacy 802.11b support (2.4 Ghz wireless support used in most cheap IOT devices)
- DHCP support which includes local DNS and MAC ID binding to make NAT and Firewall rules effective with having to manually configure your devices with easy to use client management
- Easy to use QOS with instrumentation features
- VPN support
- Many storage solution variants to allow for of personal cloud and LAN network storage (NAS-like functionality)
- Gaming networking enhancements galore
- Excellent security features
- Excellent compatibility with other devices
- Excellent and easy to use web-base administration software
- Excellent community support on countless on-line forums
- Best router for the money; Similarly featured Netgear routers are significantly more expensive without a real edge

Some downsides:
- Terrible vendor support (not really necessary unless you need a warranty replacement, but they are okay here)
- Some software limitations make many features will only work when you use local subnets within the 192.168.0.0/16 class B network
- Network storage throughput somewhat slow

It is devices like this that have had me a loyal ASUS customer for routers for nearly a decade. The fact that you can use Merlin-WRT as your software which IMHO more stable than the factory firmware makes it a slam-dunk.

These are pretty much as basic an RCA cable you can find that will extend the length of your existing RCA cables without the need for another male-to-male adapter. While for components that have RCA hookups that allow you to use any RCA cable that your can find, I would recommend buying a single longer cable as every connection point is a place for potential signal loss. However, for components that have their RCA cables integrated with the device, you have little choice but to buy an extender such as this. Turntables, especially the older variety, are the most notable components that have this configuration, and since most people like to be able to play records from a location that is easy to reach and has plenty of headroom, this is often far away from your receiver and the built-in cables on the turntable are usually far too short for this. This is why these cables are a perfect way to add an extra 3' while only introducing one additional connection in your linkage, where using a standard RCA cable with a male-to-male adapter introduces two.

Also, since the cables which are connected to turntables are almost always of bare-bones quality with the minimum gauge of copper necessary to carry a signal (that's assuming the wire is made from copper at all, and not from some other cheaper alloy), these are probably going to be the same gauge. Your connection is only as good as the weakest link, so buying some thick gauge cable that is made out of magnetically polarized copper probably would only serve to drive the price up with no actual benefit to you except for being able to brag about them. Therefore, this RCA cable extenders is all that you really need and will spare you the embarrassment of spending money on something that you actually do not need at all. Some "high end" users might complain about them being of a small gauge because they have convinced themselves that they have to use overpriced Monster cables to connect their gear to be able to fully enjoy it., but I don't necessarily buy into this. True, good cable makes a difference, especially when you are sending a signal over a longer distance (10' or more) chances are the mid-grade cable of 16 gauge copper wire with gold plated contacts is all you're going to need. This cable solves your short cable problem while telling the world "I am care about how my music sounds, but I am neither a sucker nor a fool!"

I'm typing this review on this Chromebook right now! I'm a graduate student, and I got tired of my Windows computer installing updates every time I opened my laptop. It was frustrating. I just wanted to open my laptop and get right to writing my homework. Now I can! It's also very lightweight, so I can easily bring it and all my books with me to class. It holds a charge for at least 2-3 days of active homework use and general internet fun for me. It starts up almost instantly when I open it! The screen size is fine, and I often have two windows open at the same time, side by side. I've been trying to read more articles online without printing them, and using online textbooks via my Kindle app. After a bit of a learning curve, this has worked out awesome, because if I have my Chromebook, I have ALL my textbooks with me, plus my course information, and my notebook to write things down. I love it. Plus, it doesn't get hot or make a whirring sound when you use it for a long time. I like that because I often use mine while I"m sitting on the couch.

Getting used to using the Chromebook had some hiccups. First, I recommend using Google Docs for writing because it has an offline mode. The Windows OneDrive and cloud version of Word works ok, but if your internet has any interruption, you can't keep typing. That's annoying. So use Google Docs, and don't worry about it! (But if you're working on a project with someone, and they use Word on a Windows laptop, you can collaborate with them no problem using the cloud version of Word.) Second, organizing my files confused me, until I realized that "Save As" is now "Move to folder.' Also, you can download a few files to your Chromebook, so if you need to upload an attachment to Blackboard, you can pretty easily. You'll use your Google Drive for much of your file storage. I did connect my OneDrive to my Chromebook, but it's through a third party app thing, and the connection always has to be redone, so I don't really rely on that, and I plan to move my OneDrive stuff to my Google drive soon.

The only thing that was really hard was setting up my Chromebook to print to my WiFi printer. Google cloud print is in beta, and in theory, it's awesome. When you're done setting it up, you could print to your home printer from anywhere, using your mobile device. However, Google your printer and how to set up cloud print, and give yourself some time to set it up. If you're in a rush, you should just plug your printer into your Chromebook.

Lastly, since many public schools are going Chromebook, I thought it was a good idea to get one myself. I'm working on getting my Master of Arts in Teaching to be an elementary/middle school teacher. Using one for my own schoolwork helps me be able to help students use their Chromebooks. Additionally, the price is so nice, I don't worry about having to ever replace my Chromebook, because if it was damaged by schoolchildren, I'd only be out about $160 (instead of $2000 for a Mac). I'm even thinking of getting one for my mom, since most of what she does online could be done on a Chromebook, too.

Oh, and one very last thing, the keyboard is really enjoyable to type on. The keys are spaced comfortably, and the individual keys make a nice clicky sound, are springy, and are nice and thin, for fast typing. I know that might sound weird, but I'm picky about my keyboards.

We took a pretty good hit somewhere near our house which knocked out power for a pretty large area, and caused some damage to the grid. Unfortunately, the little power strip that I have all my home network gear plugged into didn't stop the surge and it blew out the internal fax modem of my all-in-one printer. (I'm rather disappointed that the house circuit breakers didn't provide enough protection. This is a new home.) Now, we don't fax every day. But, when you need it, you need it and don't want to go to UPS store to fax a simple one page document. We did this for a while. But, finally, I broke down and got a new printer. So, this time, it's going to be well protected. As is everything else in my home network equipment. This APC unit protects ALL of the connections, phone, ethernet, coax AND electrical. It even comes with jumpers for all three data connections. $25 is a small price to pay, to protect over $2,000 worth of equipment. Oh, and just remember that most surge protectors have to be replaced like every three years. This one comes with a LIFETIME warranty with $1000 equipment replacement guarantee. So, good purchase. Five stars.

I'm using it right now. I have a new tablet computer that was not the most common of dimensions. It's built more like a reader than the typical tablet. So, I wasn't sure that this keyboard folio by Cooper would work. But, it does, very well. And, the keyboard is just awesome. The key stroke response is great. The battery life is great. The cover is VERY well assembled with quality materials. The stitching is perfect. The PLU leather is beautiful. After doing everything in black for years and years, I opted for the red one. Very happy with that decision. The one thing that I wish that they had done was to include an elastic loop inside the spine to hold a stylus. I have large fingers and find most touch screens rather annoying. I MUST use a stylus to navigate through a maze of touch screens. So, having a stylus handy is required. The detachable keyboard is very handy when I go to Instagram, which always stays in portrait mode. I just detach the keyboard and tilt the tablet. So, all in all, I have to give this keyboard folio a five star rating.

I have tried a lot of tablets, for distribution at a local school. For the money, this is one by TOKECY of the best ones I've tried. It works as well as some costing much more. The octa-core processor can handle multiple tasks simultaneously, plays video flawlessly and responds quickly to input commands. The display is crisp and clear. The sound is nice and clean. It comes pre-loaded with Android and Google. Funny thing, I didn't have to go through a whole lot of set up steps like I have with others. 6 gigs of RAM gives you plenty of operating power and the 64 gigs of ROM means plenty of storage capacity for movies, videos, pictures and apps. That ROM is also expandable with up to 128 additional gigs by onboarding a micro-SD card. (Be sure to use at least a U2 card for speed. U3 is the fastest and is better for running UHD video.) The battery life is great. I charged mine about 4 days ago. I've been playing for a few hours with the tablet every day, without ever shutting it completely down and I still have about 25% battery left. It comes with a USB-C charging cord and AC adapter, and a USB-USB.C adapter. One point where I have a small issue is the instruction manual. it's very small and very poorly written and printed. If this is your first Android tablet, it may take you a bit to sort it all out. But, thankfully, Android OS is very user friendly and quickly learned for most. I'm one that likes to keep a screen protector on my tablet and keep it in a folio cover, sometimes with a Bluetooth keyboard and stylus. I haven't looked for any of those accessories for this tablet yet. But, I can tell you that I have five other tablets and none of the accessories I have for them will fit this one. I'll start that search today, and report back what I have been able to find. But, aside from that, I cannot find a single fault in this tablet and can say that it really is a good deal, worth every penny. Five stars.

Update: Cooper makes a very good keyboard folio cover that works very well with this tablet. The only downside is that it doesn't have a holder for your stylus. I have to figure that one out for myself. Here's the link to the folio:
https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B00NA1Q80M/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_asin_title_o03_s00?ie=UTF8&psc=1

[[VIDEOID:564842fa221c9d26bfda6afccb1830a8]] Musibaby has a line of speakers, from this little personal compact M88 up to a big guy powerful enough for a major party. I like the M88 for a couple of reasons, the sound quality and battery life. One thing that I wish that they had done was to put another passive cone in the other end of the speaker and set it up to lay on it's side. But, just as it is, it still provides great quality sound. The bass is great for such a compact size and the treble is nice and crisp, even at high volume. The battery life is great. On a single charge, I have been able to listen to my favorite music for several hours for two days and still have battery left. It comes with a lanyard, usb charging cord and a 3.5mm auxiliary cable. The short video will not do it justice, because you're hearing through your laptop speakers. But, trust me, the sound quality is there. Good purchase. Five stars.

This xdobo speaker IS amazing! It was almost fully charged when I got it. So, I didn't have to wait long to try it out. Maybe about 20 minutes. it paired with my phone perfectly, instantly. Now, I'm sitting here, listening to it while I write the review on it. I am truly impressed and surprised by the quality of the sound coming from this speaker. Usually, when I get a Bluetooth speaker, I have to use an app on my phone to richen the bass and clear up the treble. I was already planning on opening up the app to test this speaker. I was blown away, when I started playing my favorite Pandora station and was actually FEELING the bass thumping through the table. You don't have to turn the volume up very much. The richness of the sound is even better than my JBL Charge 3. (No. Really. It is.) I don't miss a thing. It's all perfectly reproduced, from the highest trebles to the deepest bass and everything in between. I can't speak on the waterproof qualities. I'm not going to test it. I'm sure you can splash it by the pool and it will be fine. It's rated to withstand a good drenching. The twin cones are great. Much better at producing stereo than a single. The true wireless stereo means I can connect it to any other speaker that has that capability. That's gonna come in handy at the pending Christmas party. Fantastic purchase. Five extremely happy stars.

I have to attend virtual meetings three times a day. I have a very good speaking voice. I was actually a DJ in a past life. But, with the microphone built into our laptops, I noticed that recordings of the meetings had pretty poor quality. So, I bought this USB mic from VIMVIP. As luck would have it, I made a great selection. The quality of the recordings is now very lifelike, almost like real time in person. It's super easy to set up. The pop screen is a big help. The background noise cancellation helps a lot too, eliminating background conversations and office racket. I am very pleased with this purchase. Five stars.

The Duterid USB condenser microphone is a modest, compact, simple microphone designed to get you the best quality sound with the least amount of hassle. Plug it into a USB port, go to your settings on your laptop and select this mic as your audio input device and you're good to go. I am very impressed with the quality of the audio recording I got with it. It eliminates most background noise as the pick up is omni-directional (toward the user). And, the sound is reproduced faithfully in the playback. I know that part of this is determined by the quality of the playback equipment. But, you also need to have a good recording to start with. I like the Duterid microphone and am very pleased to give it five stars.

I really like GVM photography studio lighting products. In fact, for nearly all my indoor photo and video projects (and sometimes outdoors too) I use GVM lighting. This was my most recent acquisition, a 'softbox'. If there's only one lighting tool in your 'tool kit' this should probably be it. The soft box is used more often than any other light, because it's the most versatile. For it's size, it has brighter light than many panels, and can be adjusted for sharpness as well as intensity. In your studio, you will probably want to leave this one assembled and standing in the corner or somewhere out of the way. The 'dish' or the umbrella looking part is NOT easy to assemble and it takes a little time. Each rib must be fed through the fabric and stopped in the pocket. At first, the ribs might keep falling out of the hub (very loose fit). But, at the end, you will be straining to get them in place. The fabric is very taught and those fiberglass ribs are very stiff. The light is really bright at the high end. There are two diffuser panels. The large one that covers the entire reflective dish. And, a smaller one that just covers the lamp and still allows SOME brighter lighting from the dish. Then, using both of them together would soften the light much more. The electronics could get very warm. But, the lamp has it's own excellent, super quiet, built in cooling fan that prevents overheating. (Very nice!) The set comes with a carrying bag that is big enough for the cords, power pack, fabrics and ribs. And, the boxes are good enough to use for storage and even carrying to a remote location. I think that a carrying bag or case big enough to carry the whole kit would have been nice. The boxes WERE NOT DESIGNED for constant use like a bag or case would be.  But, over all, I'd say that GVM has yet another great product to their line up, and my studio. I'm very pleased. Five stars.

I really like this Fositan light box. I don't have enough room to keep a light box this size open all the time. But, when I'm in need of some close up photography of something related to my hobbies (I share a lot), I want to take the best pictures possible. The Fositan light box is simple to stand up or take down. It stores easily, has a carrying strap and looks like a poster folio when folded. The LED lights are great, with a clean white light that is dimmable. There's a diffuser panel that goes inside and softens the light, eliminating reflections. It has three ports that are closed with velcro. One on top and two in the front. Each port cover can be completely removed or adjusted to your liking. The backdrop panels are nice, heavy matte sheets of plastic. With a good enough range of colors to suit just about any requirements. They are held in place by straps, one at the very front of the bottom and one at the very top of the back. And, of course, if you want, you can always make your own 'custom' backdrops out of nearly any sheet material that you can trim to fit. With some objects, like the 4WD RC car I have in the pics, I am planning on getting some kind of poster that either has an outdoor theme or maybe a race track. Because most posters are glossy, you will need to go to the art store and get some clear matte spray to reduce the glare and reflections.  In those pics of the RC, you can see how well the Fositan box works. No bright glare. No shadows. Just a very cool looking RC. I am very happy with my Fositan light box. I know I will be using it for a LONG time, and getting a LOT of great pics with it. Five stars.

I am really hooked on bluetooth speakers and am always looking for the next big thing or the next real bargain. I also really like to give this kind of thing as a gift to family and friends. So, I was very pleasantly surprised to find this gem by Daykit. I have had similar appearing speakers and given them to co-workers as gifts. But, appearance is all they had in common with this one. I was actually stunned when I heard how deep and rich the bass was, coming from this compact speaker. I mean, it rivals speakers twice it's size. I did some testing with my favorite rock group from the 80's, the Electric Light Orchestra. Because they are a rock group that employs the full range of orchestral arrangements, their sound is really hard to reproduce with less quality products. I can tell you, with all sincerity, this speaker got it all and the sound is magnificent. There is one area that I think that could use some improvement. The speaker has no obvious front, back, top or bottom. Only the location of the 'control panel' gives you any indication of how to position it. It turns out that the control panel is on the bottom side, not the back. So, charging it requires that you have the top facing you, which isn't all bad. That's where the midrange and treble are coming from. The best bass is being resonated from the ends, where the passive diaphragms are. So, standing this thing on one end or the other is going to negatively impact your listening experience. In my opinion, they need to put some bumps, stubs, nubs or something in that silicone strip that covers the control panel to indicate that it is also the proper bottom of the device. This would give you the best listening experience and also prevent the thing from rolling over (annoying). I have been able to use the attached cord to prop it in the best position. But, feet would still be better. Anyway, it still gets five thumping stars for both the sound quality and the battery life. You can listen to your tunes for many hours on this speaker without going back for a recharge.  Good purchase. Five stars.

[[VIDEOID:acdf4e3eeba5db6935b5794352d29f3b]] These walkie-talkies are PERFECT for just about any activity where you need to talk to someone while you're out on some adventure. (We even use them when we go shopping. I get half the shopping list and she gets the other half. We go opposite directions in the giant stores and keep in touch with these wonderful little guys.) There are more features to these walkie-talkies than I can list here, that make them perfect for nearly any environment, including professional work in the field, including squelch, CTCSS and 'roger tones'. You can even keep things quiet by plugging in an earphone. They have a small flashlight built in. But, I would not depend on it to light my way on a dark night, just for digging around in your tent or backpack.  In my video, I was down at a friends house, three blocks away, and talking to my wife, who was still at home. The price for this four unit set was crazy cheap, for the quality and function built into it. Great purchase. Five stars.

I like bluetooth speakers. I have a few. I'm always carrying one in my backpack, with my laptop, or tablet computer. I looked at the specs on this one. Then, after careful consideration and comparison, I decided to get this one. I'm glad I did. First, it came with nearly a full charge, so I didn't have to wait to start using it. [[VIDEOID:f860621c3051d81a898f0e15eb53a17f]] Whether your doing blogs, vlogs, voice overs, or any other kind of recording, you need a good mic. This is the one. I now have security cameras all the way around my house. This Yeskamo security camera was a super simple answer to a really complicated issue. If you think about it, we have made ourselves slaves to the phone companies and internet providers. We have to stream or download everything. It has to be live. Well, sometimes, it's just not possible. And, after you start using a device like this MyMahdi MP3 player, you will find that your anxiety levels get a LOT lower. [[VIDEOID:571a38012f4389ea2c6a60c0d56833ce]] The best thing about Motorola is their reliability. I'm an ex-cop. And, I'm still involved with first response teams with my current occupation. I have seen Motorola products used by professionals for as long as I can remember. Motorola has been around for a looooong time. These headphones cannot be beat by any other in this price range. The sound quality is comparatively equal to any other in this range. The treble is slightly muted and the bass is slightly flat. But, the midrange is crisp and clear. The quality of the sound is unaffected by the volume. It's just as clear at full volume as it is at 10%. The earcovers are very comfortable, and do a decent job at the 'passive' noise cancelling. Bluetooth connection couldn't be easier, turn them on, select them on your phone and select okay. [[VIDEOID:31c0baac202ec9459a67e0db40c729c]] First, I have to say that this projector reminds me of the character 'Eva' from the movie Wall-e'. Next, It's simple enough for kids to set up and use. First, the quality of the buds themselves is great. I really noticed how good the sound quality is, the rich bass and crisp treble. Then, how simple the touch controls are. Nice! And all functions, music, calls, pause, play, etc. work perfectly. Good purchase. Five stars.

This RCA extension cable is the answer to those installations where the turntable (or other component) is too far from the receiver, in your home entertainment center to connect with it's built in cable. You would think that this cable would be easier to find than it is. I'm glad that Vrllinking has this one. It's reasonably priced and well made with quality materials. Good purchase. Five stars.

I really like this new set of B350 noise cancelling earbuds from Tranya. They are as close to perfect as I have found in this type of earbud. I got this digital microscope for the school where my sister-in-law works. It's a school for troubled boys. The school is not well funded and I donate a lot to them. Long story short I lost my airpod pros. Saw these on major discount ($90 for Black Friday), and couldn't resist. So here's my take in four parts. Sound Quality. Noise Cancelling. Ambient pass through. Features.

Sound quality -- versus the airpod pros, these are almost identical in sound. The only difference is the beats buds are a touch bass heavy. It's good, punchy bass, but noticeably more than the pros which were more balanced with its lows. So if you're a bass head, or hip-hop enthusiast, the beats win hands down.

Noise cancelling -- now this could have to do with the shape of my ear, but I found the beats to actually be a step ABOVE in noise cancelling. My gf still has her airpods and I compared. The seal the beat creates, paired with its noise cancelling makes it seem like the world doesn't exist. Beats win for me in NC.

Ambient pass-through -- this is where the beats lose out. Their noise cancelling is too good. So even when you have transparency turned on the world sound a little muddied out, while with the airpods, if I had transparency on it was almost like I wasn't wearing them. I miss that alot. So if you are in an environment where you need to hear what people are saying without removing your buds then airpods might be your pick. It's not to say that beats mak you deaf or anything but things are just noticeably quieter in transparance vs airpods with its full clarity.

Features -- another loss for the beats. They don't work with the beats app so no equalizer function... why beats???? WHY?? So you'll have to go third party if you want to equalize. The beats also won't stop the music or video you're watching if one falls out. No biggy for me as I like that but some people might not. Other than that it has similar functionality to airpods. One click to pause, two to skip, etc. It doesn't auto switch between devices but does actually switch pretty similarly. Takes maybe two clicks to switch it to my mac. The pairing is a breeze with iphones. Just open the case next to your iphone and voila. It's paired.

I should state that the drive was recognized by my computer internally when it was connected to a Sata port, but once it was put into the Sabrent, it's drive information was changed and made unusable until I performed the procedure above.
