Love this case. Love it! It's super compact. You still have easy access to all of the Rasperry Pi4 output pins. Was easy to assemble, has rubber fit so it doesn't slide around on your desk. Lots of airflow vents and the included fan is super quiet. Recommended.
Loud enough for this old fart to hear

Headphones are as stated.  They are comfortable to wear and come with several sizes of earbud covers.  The sound quality is excellent.  The noise cancellation is pretty good.  They charge quickly.  Very happy with these headphones.  Would definitely buy again!

I would have preferred it to be a little larger - but the price difference was too large to warrant spending it on the larger version when I already have an Ipad.  It is okay to navigate but not as easy as my previous kindle with the built in keypad.  One or two of the games I liked on my previous Kindle did not transfer - still trying to figure that out but I think I won't be able to play them.  Am still trying to figure out a better way to navigate through all of my books - seems like there should be an easier way.  I am happy (even though it sounds as though I am not!)  It is what it said it was and does what it needs to do!!
My husband is enjoying this present very much -- he had it out the box and set up in under an hour! Sounds great, easy to work. Can also use as a blue tooth speaker for music.

Use these with my computer at work. Arrived very quickly and packages well. I have been using them for a while and would buy them again. They are god for the price you pay.

Positives:
El Cheapo!
Somewhat comfy
Good Battery Life
Button navigation is easy to use
It is wireless
Make and take calls using the Mic
Can be folded to a smaller size

Negatives:
They feel a little cheap so good thing the price is rather low.
The audio cuts out for a split second periodically around once every 20 minutes. Hasn't bothered me that much yet, but do take note.
Base is average at best. My Apple OEM ear buds (plugin) have a better base sound than these
At times they seem a little tight on my head...maybe I just have a big head.

I just got the TOZO T6 waterproof headphones tonight. One of the main reasons I picked them is because they were same day delivery for me. Since my skullcandy wireless earbuds had ticked me off for the last time I was ready to find something new. I am so happy to say that so far I am not disappointed.

First of all, the packaging was immaculate. The unboxing experience felt like I was unboxing a new phone. Everything was packaged so neatly and purposefully.

Fit - There is a wider availability of earbud sizes than any other headphones I have ever gotten. Not just in girth, but also depth, so there is an option for people who may have a more shallow ear canal. Very thoughtful. As soon as I paired the earbuds and picked the appropriate sized silicone earbud tip I put them in. They were lighter and fit more ergonomically than my skullcandy did. They are smaller and fit my ear more comfortably.

Pairing - the process as simple as pulling the earbuds out of the box, taking the plastic tabs off, putting them in the charging case, taking them out of the charging case and waiting for the colored lights to begin flashing blue and red (took about 6 seconds). Then I scanned for TOZO 6 under "bluetooth settings" on my phone. It was literally the simplest pairing experience I've ever had. Especially considering I nearly returned my skullcandy earbuds after over an hour and them not showing up on my phone when I scanned. This was pleasantly simple and the directions given actually worked as they were supposed to.

The sound - I didn't do any adjustments to the sound on my phone, other than volume and the sound was crisp, it was full bodied, clearly hearing bass, and even the highest notes in clarity. I had the volume of the song I was listening to at a bit less than 50% and full sound that didn't allow normal room noises to infiltrate. I even knocked quite hard on my wooden nightstand to test this and I could not hear the knocking.

There is the option to alternate which earbud is first or secondary. Just turn off the one you want to be secondary and the other will remain primary when you turn the other back on again. I appreciate that either earbud can be primary or secondary or that can be used one at a time as well.

Phone call clarity. I was able to hear crisp clear sound while on the phone and the person I talked to said I sounded crisp and clear as well.

Charge - the earbud case is able to charge on a charging platform or with a micro-USB charging cable (included.) This was the only disappointment I encountered as I would have liked the T6 case to a accept the same USB C cable that my Galaxy Note phone uses. That is a minor thing that would not make me not want to use these earbuds.

There were several colors to choose from, black, white, light blue, mint green, purple and pink. I chose the light blue since it matches my current phone case. However, if ever after your purchase you tire of the color of your case, there are silicone charger cases available on Amazon for purchase specifically for the TOZO T6 charger case. This can allow your earbud case to be conveniently hooked to a bag or belt loop.

I cannot vouch for battery life yet, since I have only had them a couple of hours. I've had them in my ears for about 1.5 hours and they are still reading at 100%. So I am giving it 5⭐ for now.

Over all well worth the $39.99 I paid for these. I'm so happy with my purchase.

So I finally upgraded from my old Roku.  Take into account that I am technically challenged, I was able to set it up in just a few minutes!  I am so happy!  For one, I have an older tv, but the picture is so clear, my tv remote doesn't work so I could use my 4 yr old Roku remote but it doesn't have the volume control on it so I would have to get up and manually change the volume on the tv.  Now it's on my new Roku remote, yay!  I have also noticed that my programs don't buffer like they used to all the time with my older Roku, bonus!

These are decent sturdy stands for the price.  They do the job for smaller, rear surround sound  speakers.  My only complaint is that the key hole mounts were too large for my Samsung speakers.  I had to drill out the keyholes on the back of my speakers a bit to make them fit.  So, either Samsung’s keyholes are not standardized, or the pegs on these stands aren’t.  Overall though I like the stands.  They are stylish and work well.  Check the height for your intended use.  I originally wanted to place them behind my sectional, but the stands were too short so they were lower than the sectional back.

These speakers are ok when connected to my Samsung soundbar/subwoofer.  They are not completely wireless, as you must connect speaker wire to the hub which then connects wirelessly to the soundbar.  Speaker wire should be longer, especially for those using this in a larger area.  As to sound quality, this is not for someone looking for a deep, rich, powerful surround sound experience.  I like to watch music concerts and videos and this set up is a bit lacking for my personal preference.  You must set rear speaker level to six, the highest setting, to really produce much sound.  The instructions that come with them are very, very lacking.  I had to research how to utilize the settings, such as equalizer and rear volume control on the internet.  It is pretty good for basic television watching and ok for movies, but not a system in which you’re going to feel immersed in sound.  Overall. considering the price and style I’m pleased with the speakers.  The set up was easy and they have worked consistently since I got them.  I would recommend if you’re not concerned about high end audio but are just looking for a basic system to enhance the sound of your tv viewing.  Very basic and average for listening to music via Bluetooth from a tablet or phone.  Audiophiles will be disappointed.

I bought this device primarily to use as a fancy alarm clock.  It is a nice looking device and looks really sharp and modern on the night stand.  I also bought the premium swivel and tilt stand which I like a lot and makes adjusting the device to exactly the position you like very easy.  Sound quality is similar to the 3rd gen echo dot.  I would not recommend if you are considering this to listen to music, although it does ok for low level casual listening.  Voice recognition is good and the display is clean and clear, albeit small.  This is not a device I’d want to watch movies on, but the size is ok for short term viewing (think about size of a cellphone screen).  Several different options for clock face, or you can customize with your own personal photos.  Like many other reviewers, I do not like the “try this” suggestions which constantly come up on the screen.  It’s like an Amazon propaganda machine.  Yes, you can switch off the continuous rotation in settings, but you cannot turn if off completely.  Every time you interact with this Echo, you have to endure a brief period of “try this” suggestions.  Cannot understand why Amazon does not do something to get rid of this as so many users have raised it as a issue.  I like the device and will most likely keep it, but I do wish the display was more customizable and that I could completely shut off the “try this” suggestions.

The 3rd generation dot is a decent upgrade from previous version. Looks nice. The sound quality for music is still lacking, but ok just for casual background music. If sound quality for music is important for you this is not your answer, although I don’t believe it was designed to function primarily as a speaker. It functions well as a
smart device to control paired outlets, lights, etc. and other functions and skills offered via the Alexa app. Although some skills still need some serious work, for example the a DirectTv app is spotty and works inconsistently for me. This is not related to the device itself however. I also do not like the new power cord on this one. Previous version had a standard usb/charging style cord that could be plugged into a charging cube, or a port on a computer, alarm clock, tv, etc. This generation device does not, but rather just has a standard type 120 cord. Not a deal breaker for me, but not as convenient as my old dot which I just plugged into the back of my alarm clock and didn’t have to take up another electrical outlet. Al in all, a decent device that performs as advertised. If you want something for better sound quality for music, I would recommend considering an upgrade to the larger Echo device.

Nice looking device.  Sound quality is better, with more bass than the 1st generation echo.  Good for casual listening/background music but not quite there yet for premium sound.  I do like this device at this price point.  It is responsive, picks up voice commands well, looks good, and has decent sound.  Would recommend.
Audio problems...need speakers????

Simple and straightforward. Good picture, surprisingly crisp. The remote is very lightweight, which doesn't feel great. The type in the display is really ugly, some kind of serif font that's painful to look at. Given the price and the picture, it's a decent value. Not overly complex with features I'd never use. I usually buy Sony AV equipment but this is more than satisfactory.

Why would I need this device, then? It works great, sets up easily, good picture, quick response -- but I need a cable subscription to watch ESPN? What's the point, then? If I had cable service, I'd just watch that, correct? This is a neat gadget but the content is lacking. The photo upload service requires a later revision of the Mac OS which I am not interested in. I'm just not comprehending what this thing is actually good for beyond watching NFL Thursday night games, and I can do that via my Prime subscription on my laptop.

Interesting but frustrating.

Eliminate all vibrational "creep" with this rubber gasket.
Keeps things nice and quiet, too.
Very useful speed controller for the AC Infinity series fans.  You don't want the fan running full blast all the time. Dial in just the right volume of air you need.

Very nicely packaged, no waste but everything is well packaged and protected. NOT PARTICULARLY STRONG, so don't think of building a drone aircraft with this as an engine or anything. Generous cord length. Quiet as a whisper. Works well. Very pleased with this item.

Another outstanding AmazonBasics product. The cable itself is supple and not at all stiff. The plugs are large enough to easily grasp. The ferrule surrounding the male jacks are well designed and well made. The yoke where the RCA L and R jacks branch off is reinforced, not a simple join. Overall, the quality is excellent. What I admire is that EVERY AmazonBasics product I've had occasion to try has been equally as well designed and produced. It's brilliant to address lower-end everyday items and to produce a superior product to what's available in the marketplace. Rather than buying a cheap and cheaply made 3.5 to RCA L/R cable, buy this one, which is clearly built to last.

An interesting and unique kind of "skeleton key" for HDMI audio. Please see photos of inputs and outputs. ** I received one of these units for review purposes at low/no cost **

This comes beautifully packaged and once you pry it out of its soft foam sleeve the product itself is very attractive, that kind of shiny hard plastic Darth Vader(tm) black material. It's not too big, either, smaller than an AppleTV. The vertical edges are nicely curved. It's far from ugly. Both a good package design and a good product design inspire confidence.

There's a panel with the power switch and lights indicating 2.1, 5.1, 7.1 and ARC (Audio Return Channel) operation, on another panel is a 3.5mm headphone jack, a Toslink socket and HDMI input and output. A third panel is for the included 5V power adapter.

Now, what I've been struggling with along with some other users of Windows 10 is the fact that, apparently, if your motherboard manufacturer didn't pay a fee to Dolby Labs, no matter what you do you cannot get a 5.1 stereo surround sound option. I've ordered a Toslink cable and I think that this little box might be the answer to this conundrum. I've got an older 5.1 receiver and I want to get 5.1 sound out of my Windows 10 PC. MSFT support forums do not hold out any real hope. So this really caught my eye. Ear. You know what I mean.

The intended uses are delivering HDMI sound from an Xbox of PS3 or Blu-Ray player to a "Smart TV" or 4D HD set which can play the audio output of an HDMI signal, meaning that you don't have to worry about separate audio cables. It's an interesting little device that provides several options to solve various audio problems and issues. I've never seen anything like this CSRET device before. I'm impressed.

The only thing I can find to complain about is the small size of the type in the three-fold instruction brochure. I'm old. I want BIG TYPE. Make it easy to read.
Looks great, works great. I use this to connect my PC to my stereo. I just wish that Windows 10 supported 5.1 audio! Little details like this product really make a PC your own. STYLISH.

An astonishing example of technology like nothing I've ever seen before.

It's been forty years (!) since I first saw a video camera in high school, a big b/w camera with a backpack that contained the batteries and internals. It was impressive! Then we used a kind of mini-VHS video recorder to share kid videos with our parents maybe 15-20 years ago. Then I got an iPhone which had kind-of video capabilities. So I guess I was ripe to be blown away by this Sony FRAX53/B.

It's small and compact, like a small football. The swing-out screen is breathtakingly crisp and the internal operating system and menus are not only in color, but accompanied by clear, bright sound! I charged the battery and took a video of one of my cats. I could not believe the clarity of the image when I viewed it on the screen! The video is of such high quality that it's easy to overlook the still camera, which is remarkable. High-resolution, bright images. The "Photo" button is kind of oddly placed, it's not easy to operate it while you're holding the device with its right-side hand strap. You can also use a "Manual" mode and twist the lens to achieve custom focus. There's a 20X optical magnification which ought to satisfy anyone.

The Sony software is thorough and functional. The camcorder will transfer photos and video wirelessly if you have a fairly modern computer. I had to use a PC laptop rather than my elderly Mac. That meant using Windows 10, which led to some baffling moments trying to figure out if anything was working.

Between the Sony software and the camcorder and our WiFi setup and Windows 10 I found that the best thing to do sometimes was just WAIT. Windows would give me bad information and I would misinterpret that as an error. Ignore what Windows is telling you and be patient while the FDRAX53/B does its work.

The printed manual is basic and you'll want to spend time reviewing the online documentation. I'm still trying to figure out how to use the Sony FDRAX53/B and a "U-Stream" service to get a live stream going. There is a LOT of technology packed into this camcorder! Expect to spend some time reviewing it all. As I mentioned, Sony packed a TON of features in this device, and there's a learning curve to really understand and appreciate them all.

If you're planning a vacation or expecting a newborn child, BUY THIS CAMCORDER! You cannot take enough videos and photos of your kids when they're young, and the same goes for vacations -- this camcorder is small enough to tote with you (it does not like fog or water, though!) and the QUALITY of the images are incredible! It's not so heavy that it's going to be a burden.

The sound is very good, and there's a "gun" style microphone if you want to A) avoid wind noise B) capture audio of what you're shooting (like at a kid's soccer game) rather than local chitchat.

One thing that occurred to me while I was fiddling with the camcorder in my right hand, that being that if you were holding one of your kids in your left hand and the camcorder in your right hand and they both began to slip... which would you grab? This camcorder is THAT nice. Between the quality of the camcorder and its fantastic lens and the Sony software for image management and manipulation, this could be a major hobby in and of itself. You can easily edit, trim and combine videos with sound and add captions and text. For a consumer level product, the video and image editing suite is quite impressive. You will want a fairly modern computer, as I mentioned.

Something I come back to again and again as I figure the FDRAX53/B out is the absolute wonder of it. The small size, the quality of images, the ease of operation -- I just can't get over it. Beyond sensational and well into the realm of magical. I've never seen anything like the FDRAX53/B before.

Truly gorgeous earbuds, almost more like jewelry than audio hardware. These come packaged in a STUNNING plain cardboard box (please see photos!) -- sophisticated and impressive, demonstrating the use of materials in an artful manner. Inside the box you'll find the earbuds and related materials presented in a beautiful, magical way. As if you'd bought these at a museum gift shop or Japanese garden. Everything is beautifully presented. There's a small notebook and pen (!) as well as a few different sized rubber collars for you to choose from. The wood on the earbuds is gorgeous. They fit well.

Now, the bad news. The sound is a bit muddy, even listening via iTunes on my Mac with the equalizer. The high end is somewhat lacking. They're more than adequate, but the fact of the matter is that the sound is a little bit on the muddy side of things. The sound is beautifully rendered, but I'd love a little more brightness at the high end of things.

Overall these are easily the most beautiful earbuds I've ever seen. These would make a stunning gift! Truly gorgeous. Quite unique.

I received this at a discount in exchange for my honest and unbiased opinion.

1. Gorgeous -- best looking cans I've ever seen
2. Comfortable, they fit great
3. Great packaging and presentation, would make a killer gift. Came in a nicely designed big white box, not a blister pack.
4. Easy to understand controls and documentation and all that.
5. Super lightweight

It kills me to say so, but the sound is a little bit muddy from my iPhone 5. The bass is covered and then some, nicely defined. The midrange is all there, but there's a certainly brightness missing from the sound, even with the volume up a ways, which helps. The stereo separation is outstanding, the "sound landscape" as I heard it described. The sound overall is VERY good, but I find myself wishing that there was a bit more of a sparkle at the high end, you know? Like a car that's perfect aside from needing a decent coat of wax to shine nicely. Connected via Bluetooth to my MacBook where I can tweak the EQ, I can get the sound I want. Something to consider. Set your songs with the EQ you want them played back with. This is worth the extra effort and will deliver the sound you want.

That said, these are just about the best Bluetooth cans or speakers I've ever heard. These would be fantastic paired with a Pono type of Hi Fi music player. There's an aux cable included in the box along with the charging cable (internal battery charges via USB). I'd heard (ha) that Bluetooth isn't a particularly robust solution for sound playback, but these headphones leave very little to ask for. The absence of a wire to get tangled up in is worth the compromises of the Bluetooth connection. The connection is not always 100% reliable. Which is frustrating. That's the tradeoff here. Nearly perfect connection, but not 100%.

Powerful dual-band router. Easy to set up, even though I managed to take a few wrong turns on the way. Get your phone and take a photo of the password on the bottom of the router after you have it connected and before you sit down to get everything functioning. I'd purchased a cheap router last year and this product tells me that buying the cheapest kind isn't always a bright idea -- this router is much more powerful and a lot faster than the El Cheapo I had. My kids ought to be thrilled, they both play online games. When I want to scare them, I tell them stories about 14.4K modems from 25 years ago... This router was easy to set up, comes with very clear instructions (so simple a guy can follow them). Now that I have it set up, the things I stumbled over seem inconsequential. I'm on a Mac, so things are fairly clear anyway, compared to Windows. This router is a major upgrade from the hardware I had been using. Now -- should I tell my kids the 5GHz password or let them use the 2.4GHz speeds?!?

Unique solution to the problem of splitting RCA L/R audio. I wanted to use a TV's speakers which I have facing the kitchen along with a surround sound box that I devoted the "B" speakers of also facing the kitchen, But I had only one set of RCA output jacks on the back of the DVD player! This is ideal, the second cable actually connects in the rear of these cables, splitting the signal with zero loss of quality (we are talking about RCA connectors, here, so don't expect miracles). This makes a huge difference for me when watching movies like "Theater of Blood" which was recorded in MONO(!!!!) and which sounded terrible when played on the tiny TV stereo speakers. This cable allows me to maintain the sound from the TV along with the processed/amplified sound via the surround box, which GREATLY IMPROVES the audio! Delighted!

Small and sexy like some kind of classic 1960s Japanese sports car. James Bond would use a laptop like this one.

Weighs next to nothing (2.6 lbs). Dark, smooth metal finish. Pry it open, there's a surprisingly large trackpad (4.5 x 2.5 inches) and a responsive keyboard. I wish the keyboard were backlit. Surprisingly comfortable keyboard. You click the bottom of the trackpad, which took me a minute to figure out. I have big hands and didn't have any trouble using the keyboard.

This thing is so small and sleek that it reminds me of jewelry. Especially the very tiny power and HDD indicators, set in the front edge. Clearly visible, but out of the way and ultra-sophisticated in appearance. The whole laptop is groomed and polished, nothing clunky about it.

On the left side there's the power plug socket, volume control, on/off, a Micro-SD card slot, Micro-HDMI port, a USB 3.0 socket and a USB 3.1 Type-C socket. On the right side there's the 3.5mm audio jack and a USB 2.0 socket.

Packaging and initial setup is as smooth as silk, totally professional and seamless, no bumps in the road, no weird stuff. Cohesive and enjoyable.

Windows 10 is quite nice! I am happily surprised! There's a new browser called "Edge" which is impressive in that you can annotate, draw, and type on web pages, make notes on a web page as if it was paper. Very clever. I was not happy with Windows 8 and it looks like Windows 10 has addressed complaints people had with that OS iteration. I'm usually disparaging of Windows at best (user since Win 2) and this is actually not bad at all. Kind of a nice surprise.

I very cautiously opened the laptop past 180 degrees… very slowly. This did not feel natural or advisable. But it works great! You can use laptop mode, "tent" mode, "stand" mode and "tablet" mode with a virtual keyboard that appears. The "stand" or "easel" mode, where you'd have the keyboard rotated to make a stand would be useful for presentations. Folding the keyboard all the way around behind the screen would give you a tablet. I'm actually kind of interested in using this in tablet mode streaming a movie from Amazon while on the treadmill. Have to use a bungie cord to secure the device, I guess.

The touchscreen feature has a fairly extensive set of motions which I will need to use the included cheat sheet to learn. This is terra incognita for me. The whole touchscreen concept is kind of baffling at this point in time.

Connectivity is good, completely transparent. You may not want to run Photoshop on this device, but for general use, it's more than adequate, more than fast enough. It comes with a 64GB flash drive which is mighty snappy.

I am VERY interested in finding software and a style that might work with the touchscreen to draw on. Electronic paper?! Sign me up. I'm not sure this is possible or if it would work that way, but I want to find out. I think this is just a daydream.

Setup with painless from start to finish. Battery charged up in no time.

The big-as-they-could-make-it display (1366 x 768) is saturated with color, very impressive. The sound is surprisingly good for the size of the laptop. I can't imagine how they achieved that. Now I'm reading that there's custom software onboard called "Asus AudioWizard EQ software" which delivers the sound via one of five preset modes. Nice touch.

Overall surprisingly fast and powerful for its size. I'd read a complaint about the screen resolution not being up to 2015 standards but I certainly have zero complaints. It looks great and this is as powerful as any other modern computer I own and the form factor will make your jaw drop. I was expecting a kind of glorified tablet, but this is a full-on computer, no compromises or apologies. And the thing is you're not going to be lugging around a battleship-sized laptop. That's heavy baggage. This will fit easily in a backpack. Which means you'll take it with you when you're out of the house. Perfect size. Looks professional. You would not be embarrassed taking this with you to a business meeting. Charge lasts a surprising long time.

Gorgeous little laptop, sexy as can be. Small and powerful. Can you imagine such a device back around, oh, 1995? Laptops weighed 15 pounds back then and could barely load a spreadsheet. It pains me to say that this little gem is as well put together and functional as a MacBook. I never thought I'd say that about any PC.

For the price and for their size, these S120 speakers are remarkable. I'd bought a pair for a PC build and was fooling around with them today -- I've got a space music Internet radio station on, and the sound is outstanding, really gorgeous, full music. I bought them to get booms and ka-pows playing video games on that PC. These things are cheap, robust, and cost next to nothing!

Fantastic sound for their size! I use these with the Pono Player along with a "Topping TP20-MK2 MKII TA2020 Class T" amp -- the sound is incredible! Nuanced -- I hear things I've never heard before. Could not be more pleased. These are not going to fill a big living room with sound, but as desktop/bookshelf speakers they're an almost unbelievable value!!!

Bought this and a pair of Micca speakers to use with my Pono Player. The amp sounds incredible. I hadn't had a "real' stereo for 10 years or so, so between the Pono, this amp and the speakers, I am thoroughly impressed and satisfied.

It's a beautiful laptop, 17"x11" shut, the screen is huge, 17" measured diagonally. This is NOT a small laptop. It looks tough, almost tactical, with battleship-like lines and a somewhat menacing dark grey color.

The presentation or unboxing is sensational: it comes in a kind of large dark grey cardboard suitcase complete with handle. You open the box and there is the laptop along with two small rectangular insets in the top part of the box. No clutter, no plastic bags, even the power cable (which is also huge) is nestled, hidden, in a compartment near the hinge of the box.

Setup is magnificent and smooth as can be, a real delight. Nothing clunky about it, a genuine pleasure. The keyboard is enormous and includes a full numeric keypad to the right. The trackpad is (oddly) centered below the keyboard, not centered on the body and features two mouse-click areas below it.

The sound is as good as a laptop is going to have, which is somewhat tinny with no bass. You will want a set of external speakers. I had a Windows 7 home built computer which I stole a $10 set of Logitech speakers from which provided more than adequate sound.

The keyboard, function keys, Alienware logo and top and front lights are all PROGRAMMABLE, meaning you can set not only customized keystroke functions for the function keys, but set detailed COLORS for all of the elements to dream up customizable schemes, which sounds goofy but looks *awesome*. This is a gorgeous laptop from top to bottom, stem to stern. Easily the nicest laptop I've ever seen.

Would you use this for business? As in tote it to a business meeting? Probably not, you know, it looks great, but it's not business-drab styled. It's meant for gaming, and it truly rocks at that.

The screen has nearly unbelievable saturation and brightness, the colors almost drip off the screen, they're so rich. The tactical sensation of the keyboard is outstanding, it's not a mechanical "click" keyboard but rather the standard sensation with buttery-smooth Rolls-Royce operation. There is no optical drive, but that doesn't really matter these days. I was able to download a copy of Painter Essentials which would not run on my Mac, which ran great on the Alienware laptop.

I downloaded a trial copy of Illustrator and put it through its paces, the laptop had no trouble with anything I could throw at it. Plenty of RAM, no heating problems, a battery which lasts quite a long time uncoupled from shore power.

In short, the laptop is outstanding -- fantastic. Second to none. Beautifully designed, faster than any other laptop I've ever seen with a display better than any desktop computer I've ever used. The sound is weak, but it's impossible to squeeze decent speakers into that form factor -- external speakers or headphones are required. Software on board will support any sound system you want to add. It's all ready to roll and buffed like a body builder. Incredible!

And now, gentle reader, I need to address the sole problem I had with the Alienware laptop, and it's a big one: it ships with Windows 8.1.

The killer part of this is that having a gorgeous laptop like this with Win 8.1 is like having a yacht when you live in the desert. One doesn't really function without the other. I found Windows 8.1 impossible to use, it simply made no sense to me. Windows would pop up I never asked for, navigation was absurdly difficult -- it made no sense to me on a fundamental level. I was not a fan of Windows before, but Windows 7 on my homebrew game box functioned and was comprehensible to me, things MADE SENSE.

But Windows 8? I ran across a video critique (http://dottech.org/94027/this-hilarious-video-explains-why-windows-8-sucks-video/) of the interface and the fundamental flaws built into it -- one has to be curious what Microsoft was thinking. The interface choices simply make no sense. Why would they release such a horrible dog of an operating system?! I'm not a n00b when it comes to computers. And I could not make heads or tails out of Windows 8.1, which soured my experience with the Alienware laptop. Here we have a laptop which is outrageously powerful with a gorgeous display and an OS which I don't have anything good to say about. It's awful, truly, honestly awful.

My point being that if you want to get anything DONE with this laptop, beware Windows 8. If you're happy with getting your favorite games set up and playing those, then you'll be satisfied. For example, you're expected to enter or create a new e-mail account in order to proceed -- well, that I did, and in the month I've been trying to use this laptop, I've NEVER gotten the Microsoft e-mail account to function properly! Internet Explorer is included, and it's kind of buggy and suffers from the computer either changing programs or bringing up windows I never asked for ALL THE TIME. It's maddening. I'm not exaggerating or joking -- this thing is a train wreck, a real crazymaker.

Why not ship this laptop with some flavor of Linux? Or cobble together a Dell version of an OS? Windows 8 really is that bad. You can imagine the frustration of an OS that is the equivalent of an insane person on your laptop. Your beautiful, perfect laptop. It would have been great if there was a simple downgrade path to Windows 7. Or XP, or Win95 -- seriously, it's THAT BAD.

OK, enough of that. The OS is not Alienware's fault, but it does greatly interfere with the use of the laptop. Perhaps you'll have a better experience. For me, it was a major stumbling block EVERY TIME I TURNED THE LAPTOP ON. Absolute endless frustration. I just cannot figure out what Microsoft was thinking.

So, to sum up: this is the best laptop I've ever seen, absolutely ideal for gaming, and the other "serious" programs I got to run on it all performed beautifully. You will want to add external speakers and possibly an external CD/DVD drive if you need one. There are plenty of USB ports and the other sockets you expect. Support for sound is outstanding.

But the Windows 8 OS is like a rock in your shoe which makes every single step you take painful. With a different OS, this may well be the PERFECT laptop for personal gaming use. Absolutely gorgeous!

---

You should DEFINITELY UPGRADE TO WINDOWS 10!!! The difference is remarkable! A massive improvement in user experience compared to Win 8.1!!!
Quite substantial, a big, black USB cable. Twice the width of my other USB cables. The heads are equally chunky. Really robustly-made.

Beyond the way it looks, it's relatively easy to pair via Bluetooth, you can charge your phone via USB or NFC, the wireless near-field connection scheme. I'd have given a tooth for an external speaker like this back in the 80s, when battery-powered speakers for the Sony Walkman existed. It's more than adequate for a dorm room or office space, it's lightweight, it seems to be pretty durable, each of the EIGHT speakers have a metal screen protecting the cones. CX -- No, I was wrong, there are NOT eight speakers, there are FOUR speakers, plus four extra cones which amplify the sound. I counted the grilles and assumed they were all speakers. My error!

This comes in a beautiful package, it would make a fantastic gift. It promises up to 8-10 hours of play, which is more than decent. There's a Mic In jack, which I'm somewhat baffled by, and an Aux jack, which is very handy if you own an older non-Bluetooth iPod. There's a Talk button for use with your phone. I'm unclear how that would function. This can be mounted on a wall, AND THEY INCLUDED THE WALL ANCHORS AND SCREWS. Very thoughtful.

The main thing, the sound quality, is better than I've heard with other Bluetooth speaker solutions, which, honestly, is not saying that much. I'm looking for a software EQ on my iPhone and I don't find one. I don't want to ask for the Moon, but an EQ on the speaker would be worth more to me than the NFC charging scheme.

A very good Bluetooth speaker solution. It looks gorgeous, it's easily paired, the sound is relatively bright and clear. Room-filling sound. It won't replace home stereos, but that's not what it's meant to do. Anyone young enough to NOT remember how good vinyl LPs sound will be positively thrilled with this device!

---

This device actually sounds better filling a room with sound than it does just sitting on your desk. For whatever that's worth. It sounds better if it's not right under your nose.

---

This device does match up with my iPhone very well, and without a lot of fuss or headaches like other Bluetooth solutions I've tried. If I can't get each device to sniff one another's butt, I lose interest pretty quickly. This device matches up on its own and easily, so that's a major plus.

I bought a pair of these for Kid #2's birthday. Kid #1 was QUITE envious (he has a cheap headset for his PC). Unfortunately, there are TWO 3.5mm jacks, so on a Mac, which have not had a "Sound in" jack for years, you'll need a solution like Griffin's iMic: [[ASIN:B000BVV2IC Griffin Technology iMic USB Audio Device]] -- fortunately I had one on hand, but I have yet to be granted permission from Kid #2 to get it working -- but I'm reasonably certain that is what is missing, and why she couldn't get these working at first. Apple discontinued the "Sound in" or MIC input quite a long time ago. So that could stop you cold. Overall, however, these look really good, and judging from Kid #1's being impressed, they have a good reputation. I'll report back once I get the Griffin iMic working and hopefully get all the features on the headset functioning.
...

Now I see this kind of external USB sound card [[ASIN:B0058P0I2C Logitech USB To 3.5mm Jack Audio Adapter]] which would obviously be the cheaper way to go compared to buying a device like the iMic! I'd never seen a USB-3.5mm device before and it looks like this is what is missing on the Mac end to use this headset!

The novelty of a Bluetooth speaker weighs in its favor. Setup is fairly easy, just know that you need to pull open the accordian-like back end of the speaker to get it to turn on and power up! A little bass heavy, but it's such an improvement over listening to music via the dime-sized speakers in laptops that the improvement is dramatic!

---

I had purchased this as a Christmas gift for my teenage daughter. Who did not find it cool, or interesting. So as we used to say on the aircooled VW list, "Your Mileage May Vary". I thought it was a really neat solution. Maybe you want to think about a gift card for your teenagers instead. I was disappointed that my kid didn't find this speaker useful.

The magnifier is SMALL, which is the thing I liked about it. The optics are decent and the two LEDs provide more than enough light. It's not perfect, but it was extremely inexpensive -- it's the IDEAL size to fit in a toolbox and not take up valuable space or add weight. I have a 30x magnifier that must be four times the size of this little thing. It's probably not 45x magnification, but the image is decent. It comes with an equally tiny cloth bag with a velcro closure. You're getting really good value for your money with this thing. I can see buying another and keeping it with the knife sharpener to inspect the edges of blades.

I would like to get a more powerful magnifier, but this is impressive for the price.

I find myself listening to my MP3 collection all over again to hear what I've been missing by listening with my iPod earbuds or my iPod boombox from Apple (anyone remember those?) or through my dime-sized laptop speakers. NO MORE. Even thinking back to the big speakers I had when I was in college, these headphones reproduce each and every note beautifully. The over-the-ear design takes a little getting used to compared to wearing earbuds, but the fact that there's no wire to tangle is a major plus. The sound was a little on the boom-y side of things until I used the iTunes EQ. Very impressive headphones, they look great and, most importantly, they sound fantastic. I had zero setup issues, in fact the device had connected to the tiny transmitter before I could put them on. And my kids won't march up to my iPod boombox and turn the sound down on me while I'm listening through these. Keeps my music to myself. These would be great to wear while working (but don't wear them during staff meetings).

Before opening the box: I notice and am concerned about the three logos I see (Buffalo, Cloudstor and Pogoplug), all of which look amateurish and unprofessional. The box design is another cause for concern. It's unsophisticated, like a rough draft. These are, in my experience, not good signs. It's not as if you can't throw a rock and hit a graphic designer.

---

Well, it was a breeze to set up and appeared eager and willing to store everything I have on hand and make it accessible from anywhere you can establish a web connection. There's a $35/month subscription which I understand makes it possible to stream your music or movies. I can see where this would be a neat device for someone who was on the go a lot and might want their personal or especially their business data at their fingertips.

Since I use a Mac the non-standard interface freaked me out. My kids have Windows computers and anything that remotely resembles that kind of interface makes my blood pressure rise, anticipating problems. Since the User Agreement said that the device was for 18+ users only that was kind of an issue -- could I use this for their data? I didn't think so.

If you have an iPhone or Android or a phone or device like that I can see where this would be a great device to have, unfortunately I don't own any kind of smart phone.

Overall, sorry to say, the non-standard interface, the companies I'd never heard of, the first-draft feeling of the graphics didn't inspire me to trust the device. If I were a Windows user this thing might seem like the greatest idea since sliced bread. Slick, fast, seems to do everything it promises to do -- I think I might be too much of a couch potato non-mobile user to get much out of this device, really. I have a couple external drives for backups or photo storage and seldom stray from home. This isn't a bad product, but I get the feeling that I'm not in the target market group for this kind of device.

---

Six months later: I didn't grasp what this device was for initially. Now that the light bulb has come on over my head I realize that it's remarkably cool, useful and PAINLESS to operate. Somehow initially it struck me as a kind of convoluted hard drive setup, now it seems intuitive and rather suave. I'm not clear on why it took me so long to figure it out, or for the fog to lift.

The first hard drive I ever bought was a Seagate. It was a 20MB internal. Once I'd gotten it installed I thought "I'll never fill up all this space." That was more than twenty years ago (and it turns out I did fill up all that space).

Here is the latest and possibly the last of the Seagate Barracuda drives, and it's a beauty. I just cannot get over how BIG the drive is. Two terabytes is TWO TRILLION BYTES. And it flies! Until SATA3 becomes the de facto standard, this drive will satisfy the needs of any hard-core gamer or video editing pro.

I'd read about earlier large Seagate HDs having issues in multi-disk arrays on Mac or Linux systems, but I found that this drive works and plays well with everything I've got plugged in to my system. Installation was easy. The drive is remarkably quiet. The capacity reminds me of those stretch limousines you see on the freeway, amazingly large but moving right along.

100% recommended. This is a terrific hard drive. And it's HUGE.

---

Months later: I've been trying to choke this thing somehow or other and it laughs off my every attempt. Really a nice bulletproof drive.

Quite impressive overall. It's SMALL yet I wish it was just a little bit smaller. I have yet to read the manual cover to cover but have enjoyed snapping pictures in the automatic and manual modes so far.

The size of the S410 was one of its two biggest selling points. I want a camera I will have with me, not one that's at home taking up space. The other thing I wanted was decent to good image quality, and what I've seen so far makes me think that this camera is a good choice.

I ordered a second battery and used an inverter I already owned to charge it in the car. Much cheaper than the Canon car charger. The manuals are (somewhat comically) also very small little books. A useful road-map poster of features is included along with a quick-start guide, which is always square one as far as I'm concerned.

Color reproduction seems very good. Clarity is decent at this point. I obviously need to read the manual to understand everything that's going on, and it's clear that there's a LOT of technology stuffed into this little gem. The controls are well-placed and the menus seem concise, operation overall is quite snappy. I'm pleased. The LCD screen is extraordinarily bright and crisp. Time between shots is acceptable, pretty quick, really, and time-to-first-shot is very good.

I don't think you'd need a case for the camera. Wrap it in a handkerchief if you're worried it will get scratched. I like the lens being covered by two little doors that close on power-off. Keeps the lens safe and you don't have a loose lens cap to worry about. The camera is smooth, no protrusions to catch on anything. It's a great looking little thing. It's a little bit heavier than you'd think it would be. I wish it was a little bit lighter and a little bit smaller. Which seems greedy given how light and small it is now!

One thing I like in particular is the B&W setting. Shooting in black and white is something a lot of folks who didn't spend time taking Intro to Professional Photo back in college may not have experienced, and it's worth checking out, particularly for portraits. Black and white can tell a better story than color.

I'm probably being unfair giving this camera only four stars -- there are certainly no glaring faults, far from it, but this was a realistic choice for me, a camera that I can take everywhere with me, and, no, for this price it's not going to perform like a Canon D20 which is ten times the price, but it is MUCH smaller and twice the resolution of my beloved old Nikon 950 (circa 1999). Maybe I'm expecting D20 performance at a S410 price..?

For its size and the price, this camera is quite a good value and is everything I expected, very well put-together and quick. A good choice. Not film-quality images, but very good for what it is. A good balance of resolution, size and weight. A handy, good quality camera to snap photos of the kids with, small enough to have with you everywhere you go. Not that I'd mind the "inconvenience" of having a Canon D20 over my shoulder 24/7... but that's simply not in the budget!

No regrets at all having chosen the S410!

Five years later: I had dropped my S410 and I couldn't use most of the functions, so I shipped it off to Canon to be repaired (for $100, ouch)... and it stopped working after about a month. I was sharply disappointed. I didn't want to send it off AGAIN (another $100), and I was unhappy having no camera. Canon offered a "loyalty program discount" or whatever they called it, I could buy a refurbished next-step-up camera from them for about $150, but after the $100 wasted on a not-very-robust repair I was reluctant to do that. I ended up buying a used S410 off a popular auction site. I expect things to last basically forever, so I was disappointed that I was clumsy enough to drop my camera and disappointed again that Canon's repair was extremely short-lived.
We use this for our kids as a noise maker at nighttime we love it

I love the volume button in the side of the headphone.  I didn’t have to have my device to raise or lower the volume.  Very easy to install and get started.  Ear pieces are very comfortable.  I was a little disappointed in the range of the headphone.  Your device has to be close.  I couldn’t not go into another room and have the stay connected.

The battery life on these are great. I am typically on 4+ hours of calls a day and listen to a about 20 minutes of podcasts a day. The battery life is as advertised. I found the bluetooth connection to be pretty solid as well.

The rubber earbuds that fit into your ear do a good job of blocking out ambient noise. They sit comfortably on your ears. I have yet to work out with them though, but for daily work calls and use... they get the job done easily.

This is a great, little device!  First of all, I think it's beautiful and sleek, and easy to use.  Just slide it open, plug in the cable that links to your iPod, and if you are using batteries, that's it, good to go.  Just plug in the AC cord if you aren't using batteries.  Uses 4 AAA batteries, so the batteries are small, don't add any noticeable weight to the unit.  Your iPod stays in it's own protective case, no fitting it onto a dock slot.  I've had one Altec Lansing speaker set and one Sonic Impact speaker set that the slot became damaged, so I'm glad I don't deal with that anymore.  This thing is light, small, about the size of a very, VERY large eyeglasses case so it packs very nicely in a purse, carry-on or suitcase, even better if you can get along without the bulky AC cord and just use batteries.  But it's about the sound, isn't it?  If you are looking for sound in your hotel room, or bathroom, mobile home, bedroom, kitchen, garage, den, etc., you are going to LOVE this little guy, and it will be more than loud enough, it can crank!  The sound is really great!  It looks great, performs great, and I just bought another one for a friend going to Mexico in a week.  Now, if you want a loud, space-filling but still portable speaker, get the In-Motion IM9 unit, as I did also.  I have both.  The IM9 is too big for the suitcase, and it's REALLY heavy, but it's screaming loud, great for the backyard or tailgating or any party setting, and very compact and portable while protecting the iPod within it's great loading system.  But this JBL is your OTHER speaker system for light weight travel or just to fill a room at home.  If you don't love it as I do, I don't know what planet you live on!

I haven't written a review before, but in case there were others like me who were thinking about buying their first HDTV, don't be fooled by the low price.  This is a great TV!  The colors are magnificent, bright and bold, but best of all, true, and true throughout the screen.  The contrast amazes me.  The blacks are really black while somehow delivering really bold, bright colors.  In automatic mode, the TV always subtly changes the picture size for watching standard broadcast or HD programs.  You never have to adjust anything yourself.  Pictures also look great using my regular DVD player, but my best movie experience is always watching HBOHD.  The sound is great too, but I've connected my home theater sound system, and now TV watching is a breath-taking experience!  Watching sports is the best experience.  The wide format allows you to see more of the game, and the sharp detail allows you to see things you missed before.  Hockey has always been hard to enjoy on regular TV, so if you love hockey, you have to get HD. Finally you can follow the puck, and the cameras don't have to move so much because of the wide screen.  You will love watching sports on this TV!  I used to do other things while watching TV, but now it commands my attention.  This is a great set for watching within 10 feet, so if you have a cozy area for gathering around the set, or say in the bedroom, it's more than enough size.  It only weighs about 40 lbs, so it's really light, easy for one person to get a grip on it and move it around.  If you're worried about such a low price for an HDTV, don't, not with this set.  It's highly rated by the editors at [...], and highly rated by me, too!  I'm really loving this TV!

The picture quality and brightness is great. It's probably the best value in picture quality for the price of this TV, but the main problem is that won't connect to Wifi in my living room that is using a WiFi range extender. I have an iPhone and other wifi devices that have no problems connecting to the same extender, but this TV doesn't. I tried moving the TV closer to my main wifi router and it connected and was able to complete the setup process. Otherwise this TV is excellent with the number of HDMI ports, screen brightness and clarity. The room it's in doesn't get a lot of direct sunlight, so I can't speak to it's display quality in bright lighting, but generally happy with it except for the wifi problems.

What's to rate on this? If you're looking at this listing, you're pretty much sure this thing does exactly what it's supposed to - split a 3.5mm head phone jack into two separate RCA channels for connecting to things like amplifiers and recorders. Cable is braided and pretty flexible, there's no static in the line and seems to be well shielded to not pick up any interference from a power supply the cable runs next to.

These are amazing for the price, since it's in-ear ear buds, it does a great job of isolating and blocking out outside noise. Initially, I wasn't expecting much from these due to the low price of 15 dollars, I bought them to replace my set of Plantronics Backbeat GO's whose battery no longer holds a charge. But after powering these new ones on(battery came dead from the factory), it blew my mind on how good the sound quality was - base is deep and clear - these do seem to lean base heavy, so make sure that's your thing.  I'm not able to get 10 hours of play time, but at least closer to 8, but that's not a problem considering Apple's AirPods gets a measly 4 hours at best. The back of these have a little magnet inside of them so they stick together. The build quality is pretty good, but I doubt these are water resistant or sweat proof, considering they use a hard plastic flap to cover the micro USB charging port instead of silicon or rubber. Pairing it with your phone does take a few tries, definitely read the manual

If you're looking at this, it's pretty easy to figure out what this does. If you're looking for something to do what this thing looks like it does, then this 3.5mm audio splitter does that perfectly! The leads are a good length, there's no static or interference, the contacts make a clean clear connection! I used this to split the audio out so one line goes to speakers and another to a subwoofer. Works well!

It's hard to find a 4k monitor in the 27-32 inch size and out of all 4k monitors in this size range, this monitor is a great value - the colors are bright, supports VESA mounts and has both HDMI and Display Port inputs. The bezel isn't the thinnest, but at only half an inch, it's still good form to function. There is only 1 multi function joystick type button for all display settings and power. Has 3.5mm speaker out for DisplayPort and HDMI audio. One huge bonus is that it uses a standard computer cord and doesn't require an external power brick unlike a majority of the 4k displays. Has multiple display modes for gaming/reading/movies/etc, but I wish I had a dark room/reduced blues/night setting.

I got this for a around 60 during the prime day special - the cam was easy to setup and although the iPhone app is a bit basic, it does the job done. The good thing about the amazon cloud cam is that it's backed by Amazon so there's less concern about the company going out of business and losing support for the camera. Got the basic plan, which offers 24 hours or video recording. The motion detection seems to work ok, 👍 and the night vision is very usable. I would buy it again, since it works exactly as expected

Monitor came well packaged and works well on both the HDMI and display port connection! I managed to use it with an IBM laptop and a MacBook Pro over the display port! There's also an ambient light sensor to automatically adjust the brightness depending on the indoor lighting conditions! Monitor is almost too big, but it's not too heavy. Colors are bright and there are no dead pixels. No built in speakers even though the HDMI says there's an audio connection. Works as expected so 5 stars!

Seems a bit flimsy - it feels like it's made from lightweight plastic and definitely not water/dust resistant. Battery only holds a charge for about a week before needing to be recharged. Otherwise, it works as expected. Allows you to find the locator using your phone, or if you click the button on the finder, it makes your phone ring. Good if you frequent lose your phone or keys, but as someone who doesn't, then its restricted to being a novelty item.

Pelican cases are the standard for hard shelled cases to protect valuables from shock, dust, water and humidity. The stuff in this case won't survive a trip to the bottom of the ocean(though the case itself might), but it'll definitely protect any equipment you have if your basement gets flooded for instance. Comes with a block of foam on the inside with cutouts you can tear off to make a form fit for the stuff you want to protect. Latches shut with a reassuring snap

I bought this with the intention of hacking it and putting Linux on it, but surprisingly, it works straight out of the box with all the features I need. The only drawback is that the firmware is buggy in the diagnostic side. It often shows devices connected over WiFi as connected over an ethernet/LAN port. The speed is way faster than what my cable provider provides. Also, for wireless MAC control, the built in firmware does not display the netbios name for the machine - requiring you to enter in mac addresses manually.

There's nothing wrong with this cable. It's 6 feet, and I used it to connect electronic audio doodads together. Because it works as expected, it gets 5 stars. If looking for a cable like this, you ought to know what you need it for.

This is super tiny, and usb powered, so theres not any messy power adapter cables to tug around. Its whisper quiet and runs cool. USB 3.0 worked fine with my older USB 2.0 slot. Had to reformat when using it on my mac.

This is a perfect no thrills alarm clock radio. You can select the alarm time and either the beeper or radio as your wake up sound. It's not digital tuning, so if you're constantly changing radio stations, this might not be for. But the radio reception is great, and the power cord is the antenna so there are now weird wires dangling around. The face of the alarm is smooth and glossy and the led display is a soothing amber color that is not too bring for small rooms but perfectly readable. The important buttons to set the alarm time and to turn on the radio is easily accessible and memorizable on top of the radio, while the buttons to set the time are well hidden in the back. Got this from target to save on shipping so that the radio will keep my dog company while I'm away. Does a good job of waking me up too

This isn't a Bose, but then I'm not paying 200+ for it either. It's a great subwoofer to replace commonly blown out one in the jeep wranglers. Sounds a lot better than the stock subwoofer. Installation will take about an hour to remove the old subwoofer from the enclosure and was a great fit.

I have only tested two of them. Both of them work.

I use them for conversation only so I can't rate them for music. (Sound quality or noise cancellation.)

I am tough on ear buds so these are great for me. I can simply toss them and the wire goes bad.

My guess is that these will last as long as the ten dollar ones do.

One important thing is that if you have small ear holes these will fit much better than most other ear buds.

I had hopes that it could help with VHF signals. (Two of my best channels use VHF frequencies.)

However, that was a gamble on my part.

This one is very good for what it was designed for. (Receiving UHF Signals.)

The Tile Mate is thicker than I would like, but that's because it has a replaceable battery.
The alert sound is not loud enough if the "lost" item is under a pillow.

Plastic seems to be too easily cracked when batteries will have to be replaced. Base for the signal generator is too light - too easy to knock over. It would help if the base were constructed so it could be attached with tape. Individual sounding unit could be attached to their devices using the small, circular double-sided tapes, but that would probably interfere with replacing the battery in the future.

These batteries are an economical replacement for the Canon batteries. If you buy a battery pack / grip to double your photo session, you will need to buy more batteries.
The only con for these is that they must be recharged annually, not just left in a camera bag or desk drawer until needed. They can lose their charge and then become unusable or require much more frequent charging. The same happens with Canon batteries.

Does what it is designed to do - store data.
For me, the SSD is connected to my USB dock with a short cable - no housing / case required. I can clone my current hard drive and then replace it with the newer SSD. Not too difficult.
The SSD was to be delivered by USPS but when the envelope arrived, someone had torn a hole in the envelope end and removed the SSD, then they used packing tape to tape it back together. Contacted Amazon about the theft and received the replacement a couple days later. Then I received an email asking / reminding me to return the damaged SSD. Haha!

UPDATE (12/25/2021):

I have removed this skin (bought on January 27, 2020) for 3 reasons.
1. The keys were not so visible below the skin because it has become more translucent instead of remaining transparent.
2. The shift key on the left side was ripped from being used and from my fingernail, I would think. IOW, it's not so tough.
3. A sticky liquid has formed between my keyboard and the skin. I removed it with more than just wiping. No solvent has been used at any time. Perhaps the silicone reacted with the plastic keys. Nothing has ever been spilled on the keyboard. Still, I have a skin on the keyboard as protection against any liquid OR dust OR hair getting into my keyboard that I have been using since 2008 when it was new.

My replacement (Allinside) is now in place and I can once again see the keys.
The skin fits the keys such that it does NOT have to wrap around the edges of the keyboard.

UPDATE (7/14/2018): After one year I have to replace this keyboard skin because it is wearing out in several places, mainly the left side command key where there is a ¼ inch slit. When I have to type a long document / letter, I remove the skin so I can type faster on the aluminum keyboard because the keys require only a light touch. I have not switched to a BT keyboard because this one is so good, and the fact that it is wired is not a problem with a little tape to keep the cable out of the way when I slide the keyboard shelf in and out. The skin I received is transparent with nothing printed on any of the keys.

For those who have the wired Apple aluminum extended keyboard (with keypad), this product fits correctly to protect the keyboard from dust and spills. It is in use on my Mac Pro (early 2008). The description says for iMac, but it fits any of these keyboards of this style, not just the iMac keyboard.

It arrives folded, but that does not matter if it comes from a seller in the US who delivers it in a timely manner.

The keyboard cover does make it necessary to slow down the typing speed. That's not a real problem unless one is a touch typist or writer who spends a lot of time on the keyboard.

Very adequate case for the WD Passport Ultra 2 TB hard drives as well as the 1 TB HDDs.

The case has 2 sides, one for the HDD and the other for the cable to connect the HDD to the computer. I have other flash drives in the mesh pocket and the cable is left connected to my USB hub.

UPDATE:
Stayed on the phone for over an hour to speak with a couple different customer service persons on January 2. After finding out that my "registered" Echo Dot had stopped, all they could come up with was that it had been reported as "lost" or "stolen" to explain why it would not register later. And then, after getting it straight with the customer service folks, I EDITED MY ORIGINAL REVIEW. For some reason, Amazon did not include it in my reviews; so here I am again.

Now Alexa responds when I say "Alexa" - or if an ad on the TV says "Alexa."

Alexa may be used more in the future as the abilities are expanded. Right now Alexa does not always understand what I am asking, especially when the TV is producing noise.

Alexa app keeps a record of whatever I have requested - on my phone (Android) as well as the iPad. On my desktop computer, I also can check my devices that are registered through Amazon. Now the Echo Dot shows up as one of my devices.

ORIGINAL REVIEW:
Alexa cannot answer simple questions such as "Who won the Gator Bowl?"
The music Alexa played is NOT my Prime Music, although Alexa did play Adele songs - shuffled. And another person was correct - no iTunes music.

Then, several hours later, it / she told me the Dot had to be connected to the internet … again, after having set up the Dot.

Alexa tells me I am not registered even though I had set up the Dot using my iPad and had been asking Alexa questions and getting various replies for several hours. Alexa is good at telling me the temperature in a nearby place - 10 miles away, although Google Maps has my location accurate.
So I attempt to reconnect using the app on my iPad and continue getting an error message that login failed as it nears the last ⅓ of the progress bar.
The Help is not available from the app because it stays on the error message.
So I use the app on my phone to see if I can access Help. I am told to reset the Dot. How often is this going to occur?
Of course I have other Wi-Fi devices. That should NOT be a problem.

This is NOT ready for prime time … no pun intended.

I do NOT intend to have to set up this device every couple hours.

Heat and noise

I was concerned that the end result might be louder, but it ended up working rather well. I settled on a slightly higher idle temperature of 45-50c for the CPU to keep the fans from revving up and down. In the end the issues I had with my build were not with the CPU but rather with the south bridge of the x570 instead.

Clearance

I had no issue with clearance with the board and ram.

Sturdiness

There was no damage to the heat sink. I shipped with fedex in a double box in a fractal define C case.

This is a nice heavy case that I settled for when I was looking for a windowless case. My criteria was that it had to be quiet, and not have a window yet fit an ATX board. But not being cheap. I wanted a CD-Rom slot as well, but you can't have everything and I settled on an external.

Cable routing

The cable routing was perfect in my configuration. This was paired with an MSI Edge x570 board (I do not recommend this one, go for a more expensive board or stick with x470) and the fan headers being on the bottom were a perfect fit. Of course, I used cable extenders to achieve this.

Noise and heat

It took some time to figure out the fan speed profile for the case. There was no rattle but I had to use an anemometer to figure this out. I only used one fan for the exhaust and three for the intake - with additional filter material. I had to settle for a slightly higher idle temperature as a compromise to get rid of the sound of rev up/down of fans. The only issue is the hot south bridge, but that is a limitation of the x570 rather than the case.

Space

I configured the case with an NVME and two 3.5 hard drives. The bottom half of the bottom fan provides cooling for these hard drives (after you remove the plate in the way). I installed four fans.

Compering to my other Platinum PSU, there are no faults that I can find with this unit. I have this installed in a Fractal Design Define C case on the bottom. I do not hear any noticeable noise from this unit.

I only buy Platinum PSU for two reasons. First reason is due to better power efficiency that comes from better components and system power swings. The other reason, and maybe even the main reason, is my expectation that Platinum rated PSU units built with better components will live longer and reduce the risk of catastrophic PSU failure.

Installed this on a raid card as a makeshift cooler. I can't hear it below 3500rpm in my case. Expensive, but nothing else is on the market in this segment which comes close which pushes good amounts of air for little noise.

I use this as a computer monitor for my photo workstation. I use it to preview images in a catalog. At the distance used there is light fall off in the corners, so if you have the funds a curved monitor might work better for the same purpose. For my needs it is not perfect but good enough for a professional adobe display. According to my calibrator this does Adobe 87%. The IPS display it replaced was slightly higher % wise but had an annoying red color cast that I could not calibrate out.

Out of the box I got 4:2:0, I needed to get an NVIDIA 10 series card to do full 4:4:4. This did nothing for color space but did remove annoying purple "frigging" around text. You NEED a card that can do HDMI 1.4 out in order to use this as a computer monitor at 4K. In which case a NVIDIA 10 Series or AMD equivalent.

As a TV it is perfect. The low end reach of the speakers was surprising, I was going to get pc speakers but the one built in are good enough. The included apps work fine.

My only issue is the standby nag screen. If you have the TV on and turn the computer off, the TV might go in to "No signal" screen which does not seem to go away. I had the input set to PC, it should know to turn itself off. You need the remote to change the sound and turn the monitor on and off.

This does not come with a power supply. I bought this, thought not from Amazon, specifically because I had a number of power supplies already and was looking for a cheap USB 3.0 adapter for checking hard drives. My unit is labeled stw-25u018, on Windows 7 no drivers are required. I tested this against another USB 3.0 enclosure I had with the same hard drives and the benchmarks are more or less the same.

When transferring a large amounts of files I had this unit drop down to 7mb/s after 30 minutes. I was using a program with verification functions and I'm not sure what to make of this since it's possible this could be normal.

The downside of this unit is the really short cable that limits your options of where you can place this unit. An adapter that has a detachable USB 3.0 cable would be a better choice. If the listing does not explicitly say that a power supply is included, assume it's not included.
