Have mine for several years now, still works perfectly. The fans do not make much noise and still going strong. Right now it seems about 5% faster than the GTX 960 and about 30% slower than the GTX 970. Though I feel no urge to upgrade since most of the stuff I'm running now is still getting good FPS.

I have the glossy black version. This is a very attractive minimalistic case. It comes with stand-offs for SSDs. While I didn't realize it at first there are slot for regular hard drives as well on the bottom. it's harder to get to them, but I like how they are out of the way. The case has been designed with minimizing visual clutter so most cabling is hidden away. Of course there is no slot for a DVD drive, but was not an issue for me with using flash disk. The fan on top is 120mm but can support 140mm, but I have not replaced it since it seems adequate. There is filtration built in the fan shrouds on mine.

I'm actually not a fan of window case designs do to the mess that is usually contained inside, but this design is done very well.

I prefer this battery organizer box type over the rubber ones because these are available in transparent containers, which allowed you to see what you actually have. I have many boxes of these type, and I also have some that I ordered from China. This is sturdy and I have not had one break.

The good thing about Prime and Amazon is that I can order these and have them when I need them, like in the middle of a vacation when I realized that airline security requires that your batteries either be in their original packages or have their terminals protected. Not wanting to leave my rechargeables behind, I ordered these quick.

This simple card works for my HTPC use. The radio reception seems to be one bar lower than what I would expect (in contrast to another desktop in the house that came with a built in wireless card) but the reported throughput seems were it should be. I wonder how much the metal case of the computer itself interferes with the signal. There is a trick to antenna orientation, since the higher the db rating the more directional the antenna becomes. Since my router is below the computer, I oriented the antenna parallel with the floor. I didn't have any issue with disconnects or dropped connections after prolonged operation unlike my [[ASIN:B002SZEOLG TP-LINK TL-WN722N Wireless N150 High Gain USB Adapter, 150Mbps, 4dBi External Antenna, WPS Button, Support Windows XP/Vista/7/8]] adapter that I have on another computer which requires me to periodically disconnect or disable/enable to restore the connection.

This works even better than I anticipated for HTPC use. I would say a lot of thought went in to the design of this. The connection is easy, just plug in the usb receiver and off you go. No pairing needed. I had no interference issues with wireless that I could notice.

The F1 through F12 are accessed though the FN key like that of a laptop. Otherwise those buttons are HTPC specific playback buttons, and I found them very useful. They even out a left click button on the left side of the keyboard (yellow button) for when you need to hold down the left mouse button and scroll.

The only area of improvement I would wish for is that the F1-F12 keys were separate (in an addition to the HTPC buttons) and didn't require the FN key to activate. If the keyboard was backlit that would also help since when I'm watching TV I usually have the light off.

This was the tallest heatsink I could fit in to my HTPC case. This is running on top of an i5-2500. The noise levels are good. Naturally when the CPU is under load it does pick up some but not in a noticeable way. Installation didn't give me issues with clearance.

If size was not a concern, I would have gotten the Cooler Master Hyper 212 EVO instead. I didn't want to spend more than $35-40 or so and this was a good pick. I took off the sticker from the top of the fan plastic shroud, which improved appearance a little but left a sticky residue. I wish the fan was a standard fit rather than propriety, but hopefully since I got a ball bearing fan it will last long enough.

These were used with a Toshiba Satellite S70 to make the sound a little louder for watching some quite youtube videos. To start the toshiba speakers have pretty good volume (for a laptop) to begin with. But even they were not loud enough for some quite youtube videos. These were ordered as an inexpensive way to boost the sound volume.

My mother is not computer literate, but she figured out how to connect them to the computer by herself. These are attractive to look at and have good stereo separation. Though they are larger in person than one would think. But they were not louder than the Toshiba Satellite S70 speakers. On the other hand that problem was solved by positioning them closer. She actually prefers these for the stereo separation effect that they provide. I guess if your laptop already has good speakers you'd want a more expensive model, but for all other laptops these are a good, attractive and inexpensive upgrade.

Personally I do not like these speakers. The main issue is that lack of tweeter option which makes human speaks sound muddled. This is something that only I noticed, so it might not be a problem for you.

This was bought to replace a tape unit to record class lectures for about $50. It is was a major upgrade. It's compact. When you can make recordings they come with a date and time in the file info which makes sorting them much easier. You can also record in to different folders, though you can only edit the folder names on a computer. I have also used this with an external microphone, with which it also worked well.

I use this recorder with NIMH batteries, but it doesn't seem to like them given how it stops recording when the charge of the batteries drops to 40% (tested separately afterwards). I guess this is really meant to be used with alkaline batteries. When the unit quit in class, which I could tell because it beeps when it turns off, I reached for my cell phone. Listening to the cell phone recording afterwards and comparing it to this device I can tell that the cell phone records with background noise and at low sensitivity. While I like that I can use my cell phone as a backup, it would not be my first choice for recording lectures. The recordings from this device, in contrast, have little noise and sound clear.

What I like about this fan is that it gets similar performance to the much more expensive low noise fans. The lowest speed of the fan don't make those typical annoying clicking noises that usually happen when slowing a fan down. It's not the quietest fan exactly, but it's pretty versatile in that it can be used as either low noise fan or as a mid-level cfm fan.

Previously to this fan I spent a lot of money on a couple of Scythe PWM fans only to discover that the motherboard didn't support fan speed control. This is a much better value.

I bought my example of this fisheye lens from ebay for the EOS mount. I use this on a 1.6x crop and I have also used it on a full frame camera as well. It's not good below f11, but it is good at f16. Ken Rockwell mentions this in his review of this lens. With this lens its best to increase ISO even at the expense of image noise rather than open up the aperture beyond f8. I have tried to use this lens at f2.8 in low light on a 1.6x crop camera and it just does not look good. Not only is there a large loss of sharpness but for some reason the image becomes more orange on my example. I should mention that with my ebay example the coating on the front element wasn't even, so it's possible that it might be from that.

The lens cap on mine doesn't stay on do to a broken tab, which can be annoying since it's specific to the lens.

I think this lens is a good deal, if it can be had for cheap. I'm not sure I would buy another one if I lost mine at the current prices that this lens goes for though. The primary reason would be because a fisheye lens has limited use do to barrel distortion, I'd rather put that money towards a rectilinear wide angle.

Immediately after installing I noticed the idle speed just sitting in BIOS to be 50C. That's quite a bit! More than any processor I've come across.
At first I thought I seated it wrong so I undid the heat sink, used really good thermal paste and tried once more.
Same result. Idle temp at 50C.
And under load it's getting up to into the low 60s and termal throttling like crazy. However it seems to perform well even under that heavy load, which is nice if that's all you care about.
But I'm doing a build for my dad and I don't think he'd be content with having to hear a jet engine under his desk day in and day out. So I'm going to have to look elsewhere.
That's on me though. I probably should have known better from my experience with another FX processor. Ah well.
Still considering if I'm returning this or not.

UPDATE:
Ok, I did some more digging and it sounds like my motherboard is not equipped to handle this processor.
WARNING: If you have a MSI 970A-G46 Motherboard DO NOT BUY THIS PROCESSOR.
Go research "MSI 970A-G46 FX 8350"
You'll find numerous testimonials of people who have had terminal issues trying to use a FX 8350 with this board.
Since the MB is at fault for this and I can not accurately benchmark this product, I'll give AMD the benefit of the doubt and make this 5 stars.

So I bought one of these omnidirectional microphones because I really dislike internal computer microphones because they have low sound quality. Of course are more expensive microphones out there for professional recording but this is an excellent microphone for talking with people over the computer, speaking programs etc. it also has some decent weight to it so it does not fall off anything easily. It is not cheaply made in any way.

Wouldn't recognize on the eSATA port. It would detect the HDD, but would not format nor store data. I thought it would be plug and play. I submitted a return request (which the seller approved), but after extensive Googling, discovered how to make it work on my machine.

1) For Windows 7 (I think Windows 10 may not have this issue), make sure you have the registry entry to allow AHCI.

I'm not sure if its just the case design or the GPU fan but this is louder than any system I've had in a while. This case does have enough room inside for a 120 radiator if you want to add watercooling, thats not enough to cool both the CPU and GPU but it would definitely be an improvement for not much money.

Overly loud fans while gaming
Appearance/shape of case is not my favorite
Case design wastes space that could be used to improve cooling

The main annoyance with this mic is that when using it in windows 10 the driver does not have native mic gain control option. In many recording programs you can boost the mic gain via other means but if using this mic for gaming or other purposes through the native drivers then you will have to be very close to the mic to produce adequate volume (ie you pretty much need a boom arm) or otherwise you will need to boost gain via external passthrough program such as APO equalizer. I have also tried this mic in linux and the drivers there do have native gain control.

Overall I do think the sound quality and construction of the mic is good for the price and I would recommend it .. just note that if using windows 10 you will probably either need a boom arm or need to use external software to boost the mic gain. A boom arm is strongly recommended anyways to prevent extraneous noises like keyboard clacking, etc..

This is a large screen laptop with a classic design, it is somewhat bulky but incorporates some features that are often missing on many modern laptops with sleek case designs.. like a built in DVD drive, a keyboard with decent key travel, and a wide array of ports. It has the latest 10th gen Intel processor which offers a lot of performance with minimal power consumption, so this thing operates cool and quietly under normal usage, and even when you stress it by playing games or something the fan noise is pretty mild.

The only downside of this particular build is the lack of SSD. Boot up time and performance under many workloads can be greatly improved by swapping the magnetic hard disk out for a solid state drive. Another benefit of the old-school case design is that it is very easy to take this laptop apart and upgrade the drive yourself (many newer laptops with sleek case designs are very difficult to upgrade).

Overall I think this is a great laptop for the price, perfect for watching DVDs or streaming video with the large screen and plenty of power for most web/office/productivity tasks. The only thing its not ideal for is gaming since it only has the onborad intel GPU which isn't sufficient for most modern games.

The drive runs really quiet and the aluminum enclosure does a good job of working as a heatsink to dissipate the generated heat without the need for fans or vents. As a software developer and tech geek who also dabbles in graphic design and photography, good color calibration is an important thing to me. I find it extremely bothersome when looking at a multi-monitor setup where the colors don't match well. I originally bought a spyder 3 some years ago when I started using a 3 monitor setup with two different types of monitors (a 144hz gaming monitor in the center and two 60hz displays on the sides). While the spyder 3 worked well, it was very slow at calibrating which was frustrating when doing a multi-display setup. I think it took around 5-6 hours to do all 3 displays with the spyder 3 (Note that I was using ArgyllCMS/DisplayCal, but the Spyder software was equally as slow)

Last year I replaced all my monitors with new ones which are all the same type and I actually never calibrated them because they looked pretty good from the factory and I never felt like spending the time to use the spyder 3.. but when I saw Datacolor had released a new lens-based Spyder with claims of it being much faster and more accurate I knew I had to try it.

I am reviewing the SpyderX Pro, which has the same hardware as the SpyderX Elite but has software limitations locking some features (the most important being the limited calibration options for gamma/white point/brightness). Because those settings are important to me and I have previous experience with DisplayCal, I am using ArgyllCMS/DisplayCal software with the SpyderX hardware instead of the default Spyder software. (SpyderX support was just added to ArgyllCMS in the latest version 2.1.0 on 4/10/19)

I haven't done a side-by-side comparison with the older baffle based spyder 3 to say whether the lens-based spyderX is more accurate out of the box.. but I will say that the calibration looked good to me and I can vouch for the manufacturers claims that the SpyderX is much faster than the previous generations.. The SpyderX took around 15-20 minutes per display compared to 90-100 minutes per display with the Spyder3.

Overall I am pleased with the SpyderX and think it is a worthy upgrade over its predecessor.. but I would recommend using it with DisplayCal if you really want the best results Note that both ArgyllCMS and DisplayCal are both Free, Open Source Software so you don't have to pay anything extra if you want to use them... the only downside is that they are more complicated than the Datacolor software which is designed to be very user-friendly.

I've had the M40 monitors since they first came out in the early 90's and they were really starting to fall apart so I decided to look for a replacement. I was somewhat surprised by all of the praise for these Denon cans considering that last time I paid attention to the headphone scene Denon wasn't even making headphones. However, after looking at the response curves and reading all the glowing reviews from knowledgeable users on these and the D5000 series I decided to give these a shot as my new studio monitors.

Overall, I would say they live up to the hype. These are definitely the best sealed cans I have heard, the highs are very accurate with an airy presence which feels like you are listening to an open headphone. They do not sound quite as neutral as the M40 to me, primarily due to the punchy low frequency response which can be a bit excessive with certain sources but that may soften up once they are properly broken in. Like any good headphone these will greatly benefit from quality amplification, but I must say they sound quite good unamped compared to some of my other high end cans like the Beyer DT990 which I consider useless without proper amplification.

These are also very comfortable although they could have made them a bit smaller, my head is somewhat small and they just barely fit me on the smallest setting.. all of my other headphones are too tight on the smallest setting so I am not sure what denon was thinking when they came up with the sizing for these.

It does what it's sold to do very well. I've tested several types of ebooks (PDFs, epub, doc, txt), mp3 files of various quality, pics, and vids (avi, x264, and x265) - it read and ran everything well and smoothly.
Basically it's a low-end phone running an old distro of Android. It's super locked down and there's no internet access, so there's no updating and no adding of apps - this includes bluetooth tethering. That being said, a few of the apps are ones I've used for ages and (obv) I like them: specifically moon reader, the ebook reader - it really works well on this device. And I believe the video player is MX Player, also an old fav. Moving files via TF card was a bit of a pain, as the older version of android only supports up to 4GB at a time, but otherwise it moved everything without error. I tested the reader with several cards, from a generic 32gb to a samsung 512gb u3, and they all read well, so you can easily have a large library of media at hand. There's no cam or wifi; and there aren't any sensors, so it can't tell tilt, ambient light, etc. The screen is tiny but looks surprisingly good. The speaker is decently loud, but it def sounds like a phone speaker, still though, it's better than expected.
If you just want a simple media device with some neat features (FM works really well btw), this is great. Heads up though, they can swap out the TF card if they have a media collection you don't know about, and Moon Reader supports requiring passwords for opening the app.
If you want something you can do more with, I'd suggest foregoing the 50% off coupon and getting a burner phone at this device's list price. A burner probably won't work as smoothly (because it will have more hardware/software), but it'll have wifi and an app store and updates.
I plan to use this as an extra/backup media device. I've run the following services on it, some are a bit slow but they will work - YouTube, Netflix, Disney+, Paramount+, ESPN, curiosity stream, frndly, and a handful of free streamers. The battery life is phenomenal - it's a large battery and I haven't seen the tab use more than 1,000mA at any given time. It charges on standard 5v - it doesn't support QC or PD. The USB-c port supports basic otg card readers, but I couldn't get it to work with a USB hub.
The screen is adequate. Resolution is a bit low but color and brightness are good. The bezel is huge. I wasn't expecting top-tier glass, but the plastic they used scratches super easy. I ordered some screen protectors, that will need to be custom cut.
I had prepared an SD card on my main phone, and despite it being readable on the phone, I was forced to format it on the tablet and re-add the content; it does work well now though.
TL;DR - it's a nice, functional tablet that is well worth the price tag. Just keep in mind that low price when using it.

For buds that sit outside of the ear canal, these sound really good. Frequency range seems superb, bass response is decent for earbuds.
I haven't had anything with a cable braided quite in this manner, but they don't tangle at all. The drivers disconnect from the wires and the plug is swappable. The swappable plugs are really cool for international use, but I don't understand why the drivers aren't permanently attached.

I tested all of the features*, and it works as expected. LAN connected easily and HDMI, USB, and audio were automatic. The card readers performed better than expected as it will read both slots simultaneously (all hubs I've had previously would only read one or the other). Having USB-c data on board is very nice.
*The only exception is VGA, as I don't have anything with that port.

This matches my turn-table almost perfectly and looks great with it.
The sound quality is good, but there was a noticeable drop in quality when I connected it to my TV by BT - the OEM Vizio built-in speakers shouldn't be better than a speaker this size.
BT connected easily to my Google TV and FM reception is phenomenal.
The remote is a pain as the only display is the analogue dial (which isn't even backlit), so there's no visual confirmation of changes made or indication as to what you've selected via the remote.

My elderly mother lives with me due to her infirmities. Using these little guys is so much easier than shouting across the house to each other. Quality is good on low power across a medium house. Despite the EM soup we live in, there's very little distortion or quality loss.
All of the features seem to work well while I was testing them. Unfortunately vox picks up loud background noises too (TV, dog barking, etc), but PTT works just fine. Battery life seems pretty good, but we keep them on charge when not carrying them around.
The size is perfect, I left the clips off as it's just easier to through it in a pocket it's so slim.

Sound quality is better than any of my other radios listening to my FM transmitter. It also has reasonable to good reception of local stations. Speaking of, the preset option is nice, though interesting that it came pre-programed - it makes me curious if it's set for stations in a particular city. It's not super loud, but the sound quality is pretty good on moderate volume.
Battery life is reasonable, though you'll want to use a battery pack with it if you plan on all-day/night use.
Bluetooth works well and paired easily.
The TF card and recording function work well with a 32Gbc10 card.

I got these for my mom and just now had a chance to try them out.
And WOW, I'm really impressed! Frequency response is really good and clarity is great. Maxed out volume (spotify on tab, no booster) maintained most of the clarity and was def loud.
Noise cancellation is effective, I had my TV on while testing these and can't hear it over moderate volume.

Sound quality is better than any of my other radios listening to my FM transmitter. It also has reasonable to good reception of local stations. Speaking of, the preset option is nice, though interesting that it came pre-programed - it makes me curious if it's set for stations in a particular city. It's not super loud, but the sound quality is pretty good on moderate volume.
Battery life is reasonable, though you'll want to use a battery pack with it if you plan on all-day/night use.
Bluetooth works well and paired easily.
The TF card and recording function are a bit iffy and I'd deduct half a star if I could. If I put audio files on the card, they'll play fine, though it puts everything into a flat list. If I use a freshly formated card, the recording functions work great. The problem is when I try to record onto a card with data already on it - it completely crashes/reboots the device. Forced to choose, I'll likely keep a blank card in it, but it would be really nice to have the audio files handy, too. Oh, on the note of the card - I tested several 32GBc10s, a 64GBu1, and a 128GBu3 and they all played media and supported recording, just not on the same card at the same time.

The unit feels solidly built and everything works well.
For an emergency radio this has the largest battery capacity I've yet seen (10Ah) - I had it playing TV audio for 90hrs continuously before it dropped to 50% charge. Analogue tuning is a bit tricky to get a solid lock on even nearby stations, though it was able to pickup my FM transmitter with minimal static. Speaker is decent quality for the size and it gets fairly loud.
The spotlight is bright and narrow. The flood lights on the front are bright and give a good, even lighting. The reading light would probably be good for reading a map on someone's hood, but it's way to bright (and not dimmable) to use as a reading light before turning in for the night.

The one thing this needs to do well, it does - it moves the heat away from my laptop's woefully inadequate vent. The design allows it to be off if the computer is just "idling", and the fan is pretty quiet on low. If you're overclocking and pushing your machine, it may start to sound like it's going to lift off on max, but it moves a lot of air doing it.
The lights are pretty, though a BT companion app would be really cool to customize them.
It's not thin by any means, but it will raise the computer a few inches off a surface.

In testing, this little guy performed surprisngly well.
I had to turn gain down from what I assume was default for phone mics, I didn't test the low-end of the volume spectrum (I don't have a quiet enough environment) but I'm guessing this will pick up some soft and quite sounds. With dB gain down, it did an excellent job recording environmental noices, voice, and a sound system. Recordings were *mostly* clear - there was a bit of background noise and I'll be picking up wind guards ASAP. With the sound cleaned up, recordings were crisp and clear, stereo is noticeable.
It works just as well on a usb-c extension cord and a y-plug.
*Although the notes/documentation say that samsung phones require a special app, I was able to record from the usb-c microphone in all the apps I've tried. I tested it with a Fold 3 and a tab S8+ and it worked as well on both.

The station was easy enough to set and the Bluetooth to connect. I found the ideal station at radio-locator and it transmits beautifully. The remote is a nicer feature than I thought it would be. It's handy, but it needs volume controls. It would also be nice if the buttons needed more force to click as it's really easy to press one while spinning the steering wheel. The main unit really needs a mini battery to just last a few seconds for when you bump the device and it disconnects.

Works well for sending BT as FM. It allows me to broadcast on any frequency. FM output needs to be stronger - my local airwaves are quite crowded and I'm constantly getting static or bleed-through. About the design - idk what it is, but I CAN'T get it to work in my car's socket without it resetting every few seconds. I got a USB to 12v adapter and it works just fine now. So to make it work I have it plugged into a 12v adapter that's plugged into a USB adapter that is plugged into the 12v socket.
I decided against using it in the car and it's working pretty well in the house.

It's the multifunctionality that really wins me over, and in such a small package. I've replaced my EDC bt speakers with these. Bluetooth volume and clarity are on par with Altec Lansing's mini-H2O speakers. Battery life is awesome, I can go 8-10 hours on mid-volume Bluetooth. It also runs & charges at the same time. Radios have good reception & favs is a good feature. I really appreciate the scan feature, especially with shortwave. Button lock is handy. Having a wheel in addition to seek buttons is a nice feature, as is analogue volume. The tf software has a lot to be desired, considering the lcd panel, they really should've offered a menu for sd contents.

I'd like to request, in the future, offer audio-out - either a headphone jack or ability to send radio over BT to a device... Basically, I want to be able to record, or at least use my galaxy buds to listen to shortwave, using my phone as the host. If you release an upgraded model with the aforementioned features and more radio bands (TV audio, CB, USB (upper side band), LSB, air, and marine) I'll be first in line for one.

AM(MW) and FM work great. I'm still new to shortwave, but I was able to find a few stations within about 10mins. As I learn more about SW, I'll update this review if this radio is significantly better or worse than average.
Having a TF card slot is handy, but it doesn't display folder hierarchy or playlist, it just puts everything into a simple flat list. I believe it's based on alphabetical order, but I've yet to put enough effort into it to know for sure. I just loaded up a bunch of single-file audiobooks on a card and kept the file list on my phone for reference. It seems to jump from one book to the next easily and has no trouble playing them. You can also punch in the number for the audio file. I can't find any other use for the keypad.
Speaker is clear and loud, but I didn't push it to max.
The light is reasonably bright, and you can put the radio on it's side and put a water bottle over the light to get a lantern.
I love that it has an 18650 battery bay. I use this size for a variety of electronics, so I've always got a few handy. You can also find this cell size in a lot of devices with internal batteries - a great feature for emergencies.
My only complaint is that it uses a MINI USB plug - everything you see in life is either micro, USB-C, or apple. If you lose the charging cable you'll likely not find one IRL and will need to await delivery.

Most of the PCs I work on predate usb3, but this is faster than my other USB 2 or 3 readers on usb2 ports. I really like that the card inserts from the "outside". I use it for portable apps and it gets a lot of low-volume, high-frequency data transfer. I've only had it disconnect if I've bumped it while removing something else. Worth great will splitters, hubs, and otg. Small size/low profile was a primary reason for buying it and I've been happy with it's size.

Although it works great, it only outputs at a max of 1600x900 to a standard 1080 tv. It's not my computer or tv as I had a different style adapter previously that outputted 1080 with no problems. That being said it does give a clear and clean picture with no lag. Not sure on audio as I don't use audio on this computer.

I got this for my home set-up. I love that I can leave everything plugged in (incl power) and it's always good to go when I plug in my computer. (Other brand hubs I've bought tend to need to be power cycled at least a few times a week, if not daily.)
When my batt isn't full, it pulls as much as 40W on usb-c pd and the hub handles the throughput just fine with no overheating.
VGA is stable and as clear as it can be. USBs are both highspeed and work fine with a second usb3 hub (with or without power to it). Usb-c port is secure and cable stays plugged in despite occasional tugs. I haven't tested the LAN, HDMI, or audio jack, so I can't comment on them.
I use 2 of the 3 to put my bluetooth receiver in just the right position. There doesn't seem to be any sound degradation and they stay securely connected.

I use this daily in my car and it works great, sound quality is on-par with the basic, factory sound system. Had to add a little dot of velcro to easily feel which button is which. Also needed to add some 3.5mm right angle adapters to put it where I want, I don't like it sticking straight out from the dash and wasn't crazy about having it on a wire. Biggest problem is there is nothing to filter out noise from the charger. If you're planning to use it for more than a couple hours (or forget to charge it when not using it) plan to have a battery to charge it with or you'll get static from a 12v usb adapter (I've tried expensive ones and cheap ones, they all do it).

Got this for the compact size and multiple speeds for work. It's excellent - low fan speed is equivalent to one of the DG usb fans and mostly all I use. I charged it up last night and have been using it off and on all day and it's still blowing well on low. Almost no noise and sits perfectly still. Not crazy about the pivot points, having them at "3 o'clock" and "9 o'clock" would be better. Going to buy another for the bedside table.

I've been using the LG Tone Ultras for about a year now, and decided to switch to these because of the external speakers.
Sound quality is about the same, both very good. I don't listen to anything with heavy bass, so these cover my music's full frequency range very effectively.
The external speakers are like having a cell phone speaker on each shoulder - not very loud or great range, but it's nice to be able to listen to music while still hearing my surroundings; I also like to leave the external speakers on when not listening to anything for the read-out alerts.
Step counter is a cool idea but compared to my fitbit and smartwatch, it's WAAAAY off - 1200 steps vs 3700 on fitbit and 3000 on the watch, and I only take the headphones off at night.
Battery life is excellent, I can listen to music more/less all day and they're still not dead when I plug them in at night.
I've been using necklace style headphones for about 2 years, so I'm very used to them, but I find these especially comfortable. They also resist rotating better than the Ultras.
The ends aren't as long as the Ultras so relearning muscle memory (button location) took a bit, but now that I'm used to them I prefer the smaller size, they're less in-the-way.
Only thing that disappoints me is the mic - when on a call the other party can barely understand me and usually complains of muffled-sound. Just a note to LG or any other manufacturers out there: combine this with a high-end headset for calls and I'd happily pay 200-300 for it, as is I wear these and carry a headset for calls in my pocket.

This is my second Kindle Fire.  This time I bought one with a larger screen and memory.  Only thing that surprised me is that it is not as loud as the Kindle I have from 5 years ago.  Sound quality is fine, but not as loud.

First of all, The Speaker is EASY to hook up. Opening the box took longer. Sound isn't bad. If you want your eardrums to bleed, that won't happen but using Pandora, a class lecture CD, Hulu and an online Radio Station, I found the speaker to be very sufficient to fill a room that is over 20 feet long by about 15 feet and could be heard well beyond that too. The including USB transmitter and speakers receiver work well even through the wall. I wish they cost less but that's the nature of wireless. At least these include everything you need, including the Rechargeable battery and the power cable. I know that sounds funny but some of the others I read about don't always have these things.

Volume control is on the back of the speaker but that is no big deal since you can control the volume just fine using your computers volume settings or those found in programs such as Pandora.

I had purchased some cheap dongles before and I think they damaged my laptop because they were always disconnecting at the slightest bump. My headphones were also difficult to connect with them.

I can't even describe what a difference these high quality dongles make. They never disconnect and the sound is much better in my headphones.
I didn't know anything about this kind of cable when I bought it but I have used it almost everyday for months and it works great.  The picture on my TV is sharp and clear and the sound is perfect.

I have had three generations of Ion speakers (and one brief and a horrible stint with a Monster Bluetooth speaker), this is the best one to date. Well designed, awesome sound and the LED lights look amazing. The pairing was difficult at first because you have to pair two items to have the IOS app work. Once I figured that off it was off to the races. I am a youth sports coach and this speaker is perfect. I also use it at work. the wheels on this speaker seem to float. Well done ION... Well done!

My Live View doesn't work as advertised. Seen it work once or twice so I know that it can but not consistent or when you want it too AND NO RESPONSE FROM CUSTOMER SERVICE REQUEST so that drops rating to 1 star. Quality is more than adequate and you will be happy with that feature. Worst part is No Doorbell inside on the module ONLY your phone pops up an alert that someone is at doorbell. Such a shame not to include the doorbell on the included sync module like a 20.00 doorbell from Wish. Can't stand that company tho and their products are overseas junk with no support either.
EDIT: after customer service checked over the settings, he figured it out and his instructions help me delete doorbell and add it to the module properly so Live View is now working.

Nice little unit. Loud for such a small unit. Does get distorted at max volume (being honest). Instructions suck (being honest) but you will figure it out. I do not see 2 speakers as described in the ad. Took few tries but eventually was able to get the FM radio to work and the micro SD card recognized.  For the price I am not complaining.
Beautiful display.  Nice sound.  Only drawback is figuring out how to get Playstore /Chrome installed.  But now it's all good.  Can't beat it for the price.  I'm satisfied.

Good device. Provides excellent quality on TV.  Snappy performance.  Still learning what I can or can't do with this thing. Having some problems sideloading any other apps. Amazon is not sure if this will be updsted to the newest software and that's going to upset Alot of customers.  Several of the apps require a subscription to your cable provider. Guess what?  Xfinity customers are one of the few not compatible.  That is a major letdown.  Shame on Xfinity but what else is new.

All good, however a major thing is not being able to view playback unless i take the sd card out and view on my computer or i had to sign up for cloud services. It was difficult to get working and may prove to be difficult to many. Last thing i didn't and like, might not be an issue to others, is was the red lights for night time view were very light, so i couldn't tell if the cam was facing at night. Major no playback so i have to return them.

I have been through a few different brands of shower speakers and I thought they were good but this speaker proved me wrong. It has a nice rich sound quality and the design looks just as nice, the LED lights are a nice addition would be even cooler if they were synced with the music but it’s still very cool. It’s louder than any other shower speaker I’ve owned before and I enjoy my music on blast. Ive been using it for over a week now I believe and still haven’t needed to charge it so the battery life seems to be great and to charge it it’s very simple and easy because it’s a micro usb one of the most common usb out there so if you lose the one provided you won’t have to look far in your house to recharge it. The suction cup on the back works very well with my tile shower wall i could easily stick it to any side of my shower as i please. I couldn’t tell you how well the FM radio works since I’m not 80 years old I just use the Bluetooth feature and that connects with a breeze. All and all I truly love it its a great bang for your buck only problem is I now take longer showers lol

If you plan on being very active you should definitely think about investing in plastic clip ons for your airpods to make sure they’re firmly attached to your ears I have had them fall out plenty of times and sometimes you don’t even notice! You can find it with the app but you have to be in range and the peeping isn’t that loud espiecally if it’s being muffled you’ll have a hard time finding it. The noise cancellation could be a lot better but I also like the fact that I could be aware of my surroundings as well. It does feel kind of magical I can’t lie lol I would love to give it 5 stars but there’s definitely areas in need of improvement
Its very ugly lookin but it doesnt need battery and it was only $5 and it actually sounds pretty damn good so i'll give it 5 starts for the sound quality and the price
The twisted ends really make a difference they lock on tight and the sound quality is great compared to any other wires i used. this is HIGHLY recommended
Thick cables, came with everything i needed and than some. This right here is quality stuff guys now my system is bumping louder than ever
I’ve lost my last pair so I got these. They sound good and they stay in my ear. They paired easily with my phone and the case fits in my purse or pocket.
This is just the right amount of light and sound for my room.  I like that I can use my own music and I don't have to use my cell as my alarm clock any longer.

[[VIDEOID:73a70a32d1ed59e36e4551ac21034428]] If you run hot this is the fan for you. It’s small and doesn’t make that loud fan sound. USB powered so you can take it into your next all day meeting. It definitely came in handy the past few days. I like that it has a touch sensor so your not turning a dial interrupting those around you. Plus that’s pretty cool.
Lotta sound for a small price. Love it.  Connected to my TV & can take outside as it's a portable bluetooth!  Love it!!
I love that Alexa plays radio stations with no static. I can ask about the weather, ocean, have her play music I like. There is nothing I don’t like about her.

I have two pair for battery continuity.  They're that good.  I know people complain about Bose, but these are simply the best headphones I have ever owned.  Bass response is amazing.  High notes are amazing.  I love the easy to use control on the cord.  This is my go to.  I have other earbuds and what not, but don't like them.  This is what I use and you should to.  You won't be disappointed.

This is a fantastic upgrade for my travel trailer.  The old am/fm/cd had no inputs, no frills, and  was quite boring.  I decided to upgrade and install this unit.  I have two TVs in the trailer and no longer need an HDMI splitter.  This feeds both simultaneously and provides the flexibility of having  the audio come through the trailers built-in speakers or the TV itself.  The bluetooth feature works great while camping for music and the extra inputs provide the flexibility for movies from blu-ray, computer, etc.  I highly recommend this, it has been a huge success in my trailer.

There are some good reviews which I won't try to duplicate.  My take is this...  overall, very impressed.  I LOVE that you can fully customize all background and text colors on the screen.  If you are partially colorblind, this is a blessing.  Next, I love the size.  This is extremely compact and I was pleased to see it had a fan.  Some of the cheaper chinese radios don't.  This makes me more comfortable using it for longer periods.  You can directly input frequencies from the keypad on the mic, but you have to go through the typical baofeng menu structure to change repeater mode, offset, tones, etc.  Once you recall the menu numbers, it isn't bad, but more difficult than some of the name brand counterparts.  I'm not a huge fan of the PTT button on the mic, it's big and sticks out quite a bit.  I'm also not a big fan of the fact it requires yet another programming cable.  I have HT cables, RJ45 cables, serial cables, etc.  This one is a USB to 1/8" stereo cable.  You need that if you want to program it.  It's possible to program without a computer/data cable, but you need to have a free day and a lot of patience.  If you are impatient and try to program manually, you'll probably put it through a window before you complete the task.  Audio quality is good, power draw is good, easy of use is good (once programmed and even for a single VFO).  Overall, I am quite impressed and would call it a good purchase.  I'd like to have another one!

I was really surprised by the Show. My first impression was that it's a little bigger than I expected. It's also fairly heavy. Now having used it a few months, I'm glad for the weight. As you are pecking the touch screen with your finger, the extra weight keeps it very stable.

I was anxious to get it started up and see how it's sound compared to my original Echo. I was surprised. I think it sounds better. It has a deeper bass response and the sound is a little more directional with the speakers being in the front.

Other features I really enjoy is that you can load a custom home image, and it constantly scrolls "trending" topics across the home page when not in use. If you see something you want to know more about, you can ask it and it will play the audio or video clip. If you miss something, you can ask it what's trending and it will list everything.

I love that most things you ask it will give the normal Alexa audio response, but also a visual. The weather is a good example. It reads the weather just as an Echo would do, but also shows you the visual on the screen and allows you to scroll through the days ahead with a touch of the finger.

I use it for video calling with a friend who also owns one and it works well. The audio quality is good and we're able to communicate face to face.

I search for and watch youtube videos quite often. If there is something specific you are looking for, it can be painful. The search doesn't always understand slang or complex words, making the search results a little unreliable.

Overall, I really like it. It doesn't "hear" better than the original Echo and does frequently respond when you aren't talking to it, just like the original. It just has a little better sound and a nice touch display screen!

I actually love this thing.  It was a bit of a pain to get started.  The material blocks the charging port and it took a few minutes and some careful dissection with a pair of scissors.  However, once cleared I was able to plug it in easily and get it charging.  It has pretty decent sound.  I wasn't expecting the volume to be great or the quality to be as good as it was, but it was a big surprise.  It easily gets loud enough to hear, even over power equipment and the sound is pretty good.  It keeps my ears warm and works very well.  The battery life also surprised me.  I get a day out of it without trouble.

This is a good quality cable and works perfectly to split the output of sound from my laptop.  I bought this so a friend could share my screen with headphones on a long flight.  It worked perfectly.  Of course the one downside is that it's only a splitter so if you are using headphones, you both have to listen at the same volume level.

I am actually quite impressed by this speaker.  I've had a few cheap Bluetooth speakers, but none have sounded as good as this one does.  I fully expected it to have a small, tinny sound.  It surprised me when it didn't.  Mind you, it doesn't have a big bassy sound either, but it is as good as a normal radio and much better than the speakers in most portable devices.  I would recommend this.

Good headphones.  The highs are clear, but the lows aren't as good as they are with some other headphones.  Overall, the sound quality is very good.  I would buy these again.  For the price, they're about as good as any!

I'd looked at many scanners before deciding on this one. Overall, the feature set is very rich and I'm happy with it. I'll start with what I like and then tell you what I don't.

I love the fact that it can scan multiple trunk systems and conventional simultaneously. I like the ability to import new locations and save multiple configurations as "v-scanners" without having to erase your original configuration. I like that it keeps a separate volume setting when you have headphones plugged in vs using the speaker. I like that you can completely program it via the computer (in fact, you just about have to). I like the fact that it monitors radio IDs so you can see or learn them to know who's transmitting. I also really appreciate that you can select discriminator output in the menu and it changes the headphone jack to discriminator out. The search features are also great. It has so many options, search by frequency, band, service... you can tell it to scan CB and it will. It will show you what channel they're on and everything. Same with FRS/GRMS, only it also tells you what tone is being used. There's so much more to this, these are just a few of the things I really like.

I don't like the built-in battery charger. It isn't smart and will continue to charge your batteries, potentially cooking them. A separate battery charger is a must. The antenna isn't that great, either. It's easy to change though. I also am not overly impressed with the audio output of the built-in speaker. At full volume it's not loud. In a quiet environment it's fine. In a car, it isn't. Very ridiculous is that it doesn't work with Windows 8 out of the box. You have to implement a workaround which you can find on the Whistler website in the FAQ section. The driver does not load and you have to do a workaround. Fortunately, it isn't too difficult. I would just expect this new of a product to work with a version of Windows that has been out as long as Windows 8 has. Also, you CAN program it from the keys on the unit, but you won't want to. Unless you're only importing from the database and not customizing at all, you will want to do this via the computer. I've also noticed that if you program too much into it, it scans a little slower than I'd hoped and you can miss the first part of a transmission. Keep your scan list a little shorter and it works great!

This display is awesome. I would buy it again without hesitation. Just know that it isn't 100% perfect, but none of them are. I believe this to be the best available right now.

This is a great charger.  I have charged a variety of brands and sizes of batteries and it works perfectly every time.  I would buy this again without hesitation.  One rare feature that I really love is that you can charge a single battery.  Other charges require you insert pairs.  I have a couple of things that I use which only take 1 battery.  Being able to charge 1 means I have a spare charged and ready all the time.  Great charger!

This is an awesome power supply.  It came with every connector I could possibly need and has been working great for over 6 months now.  It's quiet and easy to work with.  I am very happy with it!  Recommended for sure!
Great fans.  Exact fit, quiet..  Have been in operation now for a few months without any problems.  I recommend this fan.

I like the case.  It has many features and you can cram just about anything into this box.  It keeps everything cool and running quietly.  The only disappointment is the large opening on top did NOT precisely fit the matching Thermaltake fan.  You must bolt it through holes not intended for bolts. Received as a Christmas gift. As I am not a licensed ham yet I have not transmitted on the radio, so I can't speak about any transmission issues that others may have experienced. To date I have only used it to monitor ham radio bands to understand how hams communicate.

The radio comes with a decent book (when ordered from BAOFENG TECH). There are also quite a few resources and videos online to assist in usage.

I found programming of stations to be fairly simple although a bit time consuming. There isn't really that much to it. If you are going to program in multiple channels or set offsets for repeater use then a programming cable would be a good investment. The programming cable also allows you to name individual channels.

There are some potential issues that can occur with use of this radio.

1. This radio covers VHF and UHF ham bands but also conflicts with police bands, city maintenance, and private corporation radio frequencies. There is the potential to accidentally transmit on an unauthorized band.

2. While this radio will scan UHF/VHF police, fire and EMT bands most have shifted to a new system. Some agencies are on the older systems and some simulcast on UHF/VHF but in general if you are planning on using this as a police scanner you probably aren't going to hear much.

3. There is no way to lock out the transmit key, so it is easy to press it while handling the radio if not paying attention.

As a monitoring radio the battery seems to last forever. If you are planning on transmitting a lot then an extra battery or 12VDC adapter may be warranted.

So far I really don't have anything negative to say. Good introductory radio.

These are definitely good value for the money. Bass response is decent as long as you have realistic expectations. The build quality as well as the fit and finish of this amplifier board is better than most of the cheap TPA3116 bluetooth boards on eBay and AliExpress. When connected to decent speakers and a 24V switching power supply with sufficient current drive capability, the performance of this amplifier is quite impressive for its size.

Four potentiometers in the front, from left to right are: bass level, treble level, treble volume (volume for the two stereo channels) and overall volume. These pots, as well as the speaker outputs in the back are clearly labeled on the PCB. Tone and volume control circuit appears to use a couple of 072 opamps and an SGM358 opamp. These are not high-grade audio components, simply a low cost solution for a product in this price range. Except for the electrolytic capacitors, most components are SMD.

I tested this amp by connecting it to a pair of Sound Appeal 6.5" 2-way bookshelf speakers for the stereo channels. I did not have access to a passive subwoofer at the time, so I connected the subwoofer output to a 15" bass guitar amplifier speaker cabinet. I used a 24V 5A switching power supply. A 24V 5A power supply may not be sufficient if you are driving 4-ohm speakers and a 4-ohm or lower impedance subwoofer, but all three of the speakers I used were 8 ohms, so 120W of power input was sufficient. With the right speaker setup, the volume output of this set-up can get quite high, even in a big room. Partly due to the efficiency of the 15" bass speaker I was using, it was possible to achieve a quite impressive "thump". Distortion levels are not low at high volume levels, but having the subwoofer output on a separate TPA3116 chip makes it possible to keep somewhat reasonable distortion on stereo channels even when playing bass-heavy music.

Connecting to the bluetooth interface was easy and straight-forward. The amp remembers the previous bluetooth pairing after being powered down.

A few observations about the shortcomings of this amplifier:
- The heat sinks are quite small, and they don't have any mechanical support. Even when driving 8-ohm loads, the heat sinks get really warm at high volume levels. If you are driving 4-ohm speakers at high volume levels, thermal shut-down is possible. If you are using a 18V or lower power supply, you probably won't have any thermal issues.
- There is only a 1000uF 25V filter capacitor at the power input. 25V max rating is a bit too close for my comfort, I would have preferred a 35V capacitor. You really need a well regulated DC power supply to drive this board.
- Bluetooth has a built in antenna on the PCB, but no external antenna interface, making it impossible to mount this board inside a metal case without doing some surgery to the board.
- There are no line level inputs. Bluetooth is the only input option unless you are willing to do modifications on the PCB

Overall, for the current price of $26.99, this is a very nice bluetooth 2.1 amplifier. If you have a couple of decent bookshelf speakers and an old subwoofer lying around, the volume and quality of the sound you can achieve with this amp will be better than any integrated bluetooth system that sells for less than $100.

Update: I recently tested this amp with [[ASIN:B00NOA58RS Dayton Audio B652-AIR 6-1/2" Bookshelf Speaker Pair with AMT Tweeter]]. These speakers are 6-ohms, so it's possible to get a little power out of the amplifier, and especially the high frequencies sound noticeably better.

This is a decent amp. It is a dual-channel BTL configuration, so it can feed a lot of power into 8-ohm speakers unlike many other integrated amps that can achieve the advertised power rating only with 4-ohm speakers.

First, there is slightly incorrect advertising going on in the description. This amp is based on the TDA7498 chip, which can deliver 100W+100W into 6-ohm speakers, but this requires a 36V supply. This board's maximum operating voltage is 32V (probably due to the 35V 2200uF capacitor that is used as the main power filter.) According to the TDA7498 data sheet, the maximum power you can get at 32V is 93W per channel. Given that there are many amps out there that claim 4x (or even 10x) more power than what they can actually deliver, a less than 10% overstatement of power is probably not a big deal.

Secondly, the maximum power is delivered at 10% THD. That kind of distortion may be OK for a PA system for announcements, etc., but you probably don't want to listen to music at 10% THD. This amp can still deliver about 70W per channel into 6-ohm speakers at around 0.2% THD (at 1KHz), and by 80W per channel, THD is approaching 1%, which is probably maximum distortion one can tolerate for music. Also, like many other Class-D amps, THD levels are higher for higher frequencies, but I couldn't find specific data for this device at high power output. At 1W output, when THD at 1KHz is around 0.05%, THD at 8KHz is nearly six times more at 0.3%.

In the likely case you are using this amp with 8-ohm speakers, the maximum power is around 74W per channel with a 32V supply, again with THD around 10%. At a more reasonable THD level of 0.3%, the amp can deliver about 60W per channel, which is typically where you would use this amp for maximum volume for music. (For comparison, many 2x50W amps based on other integrated chips like TDA3116 can only deliver about 2x10W at low distortion into 8-ohm speakers.)

As always, power delivered by the amplifier is just one aspect of how volume you can achieve. The efficiency of speakers is also very important. There could be easily be 10dB sound level difference between a low efficiency speakers vs high efficiency speakers at the same input level, which means that you might hear twice the volume with the same power input.

As many other reviewers noticed, the frequency response of this amp is not very flat. For low frequencies, there is a minor dip starting around 60Hz, and for high frequencies, there is a rise starting at 2KHz and reaching about +1.5dB at about 15KHz. If your source device does not have some kind of tone control or equalization capability, you may want to purchase an active tone control board (sub $10 item) to compensate.

Finally, to get the best results from this amp, you need a decent power supply. The efficiency of this amp is 90% (which is very good), but if you want to be able drive 2x80W without clipping, you need at least 160W / 0.9 = 178W of power input. A reasonable target power supply specification would be 32V @6A. If you are using a 24V supply, the best you can do is 2x60W into 6-ohm speakers, which requires 120W / 0.9 = 133W, so a 24V @6A power supply is recommended. If you are driving only 8-ohm speakers, even a 24V @ 4A supply may be sufficient, since you are not likely to get more than 2x40W power output at low distortion levels.

Overall, this is a nice compact integrated amplifier that is capable of driving 8-ohm speakers to reasonable power levels with low distortion. You need to correct for the frequency response by using some form of input equalization, other wise, the output is somewhat bass-poor and treble-heavy.

This is a very decent Class-D audio amplifier. Unlike many other products on Amazon and other websites that have unreasonable claims about maximum output power, the information on the Amazon listing for the Nobsound amplifier is correct - confirmed by checking the TPA3116D2 data sheet on TI's website.

The enclosure is aluminum and roughly 4.25" x 3.5" x 1.5" excluding protrusions like the volume knob and speaker connectors. The fit and finish appear to be very high quality, no rough or sharp edges. The speaker connectors are post type. The unit has decent weight for its size, and even comes with four little plastic feet attached on the bottom. The power indicator is an unintrusive and very small red LED, which I strongly prefer to bright blue power LEDs that many manufacturers seem to use.

I tested this amp with a 12V 6A supply and 18V 5A supply. I didn't test it with a 24V supply, as my application doesn't require very high volume. (If I test it at 24V in the future, I will update this review.) If you really want loud volume, according to the TI data sheet, this amp can output 2x50W into 4 ohm load with only a 21V supply, which is very impressive. After running the amp at a "reasonable" volume for a couple of hours, the enclosure doesn't even get warm.

I have listened to quite a few Class-D amplifiers in the past and I have not been happy with the sound quality of many of them, especially high frequencies. After listening to a number of recordings from my music collection, the Nobsound amplifier appears to have significantly higher audio quality and lower distortion than other mini/micro amps I have tried in the past, especially when coupled with good quality speakers. The data sheet on TI's website indicates that TPA3166D2 is capable of providing up to 2x40W into 4 ohm speakers with less than 0.3% THD when using 24V power supply. Note that when using a 12V input supply, THD starts rapidly increasing after about 10W (with 4 ohm speakers) or 6W (with 8 ohm speakers), so if you really want drive a lot of power with this amp, especially into 8 ohm speakers, make sure you invest in a 18-24V power supply that can provide at least 5 amps of current.

Update 10/13/2016: I tested this amp with a 24V 5A switching power supply and the result is even more impressive. Coupled with a pair of efficient speakers, it can get really loud when using a 24V supply - and with minimal distortion until clipping sets in. Just for fun, I also tested it with [[ASIN:B01E0184FC Dual SBX6502 2-Way Full Range Speaker Box with Two 6.5-Inch Woofers and Two 3-Inch Horn Tweeters]]. Nobosound amp sounds decent even with these bargain basement speakers. This combo is probably the best amplification setup one can put together under 70 bucks.

Update 11/16/2016: I recently tested this amp with [[ASIN:B00NOA58RS Dayton Audio B652-AIR 6-1/2" Bookshelf Speaker Pair with AMT Tweeter]]. These are 6-ohm speakers and appear to be a very good match for this amplifier. High frequency response and clarity was better as expected due to the AMT tweeter, but even the low frequencies sounded much better. With Class-D amplifiers, optimal sound requires a good match between the output filter of the amp and impedance of the speaker configuration, and B652-AIR speakers and the TPA3116 board used in this amp appear to be a very good match.

This is the best record cleaning I tried so far. I is very effective in removing dust (and associated static noise) from records that are in reasonably good shape. Of course, it cannot repair records which have been damaged due to being played while dirty. If you acquire a used record in dirty condition, it is probably a good idea to wash it with distilled water first before using the discwasher on it.

I noticed that there are several one-star reviews complaining about the direction of fibers on the cleaning pad that comes with this system. Yes, the cords of the corduroy-like microfiber material does run along the edge of the brush, but this is actually how it should be to provide even coverage across all the grooves. The cords of any fabric is much too thick to fit into the actual grooves on the record. If the cords were to run along the direction of the the grooves, some grooves would be cleaned and some wouldn't. Having the cords being perpendicular to the grooves on the record ensures that all grooves get cleaned evenly. After all, it is the microfibers, not the cords of the fabric, doing the cleaning.

Another advantage of cords running perpendicular to the grooves of the record is that, as you slowly rotate the brush on its axis (as shown in the provided directions), dust that has been collected gets trapped between the cords that are being lifted off the record as the next (clean) cord of the fabric starts making contact with the record surface.

I am delighted with my new speakers. The sound quality is very good. I was also glad that I did not have to do anything but plug these end and they worked. I am not real computer savvy so I like things to be easy for me to use.

I used these headphones all summer for daily swims. I found French contemporary music online which fit perfectly the pace for learning free style. The sound quality was good and cancelled out the joyful noise of children playing and diving. I found that I could swim a lot longer without getting bored or tired.

I have had 2 Tom Tom-Go GPS units and have been reasonably happy with this brand. My first Tom Tom Go lasted less than a year at which point it lost its "mind" in the LL Bean parking lot, uttering, "Turn, turn, turn." The 2nd Tom Tom lasted 2 years when it suffered screen damage. When both units worked, they were reliable and paid for themselves many times over in gas savings.
I decided to invest in the 1350 Nuvi refurbished Garmin to try out a new brand, to be reassured of having up-dated maps and to receive a 1-year warranty on this refurbished product whereas Tom Tom provides only a 6-month warranty on its refurbished GPS. I also liked the prospect of using the GPS for walking tours of NYC, Philadelphia, Boston, etc.
My Garmin 1350 arrived quickly and in perfect condition. It could be used right out of the box.I was impressed by the sturdiness of the case and by how well the suction gripped the windshield. The unit seemed to turn on a bit more slowly than my Tom Toms but the route planning may be somewhat faster. I liked having the points of interest scroll down the screen. There appear to be many more POI choices on the Garmin than the Tom Tom. The categories are intuitive and it is helpful to quickly see both map location and contact information. Since my cell phone is paired with my car, I did not use to Blue Tooth feature to call up the store via the GPS unit, but this would be very helpful.
I don't think that the default setting gives as much screen detail; e.g., providing names for all the streets. I have found the greater visual detail of the Tom Tom helpful when driving at night, but it is probably a needless distraction most of the time. It is very helpful to have the streets spoken at turns. The volume was perhaps even better than that of the Tom Tom. This surprised me, having read numerous complaints about Garmin being inaudible. I even had to turn down the volume to 80%. The pronunciations were reliably clear with only a few oddities; e.g., the town of St. Davids was spoken as "Street Davids."
Route corrections were made more quickly than I experienced with Tom Tom and it is helpful to know which side of the street the destination is on.
In making comparisons with the Tom Tom Go, there is a feature which I miss: the IQ routing. My Tom Toms had an uncanny knowledge of different routes and respective drive times at various times of the day. Quite fequently, the return route would differ from the original Also-- and more importantly-- the drive time was extremely accurate.
In contrast Garmin seems clumsy and mechanical. Perhaps, this is because I am stil getting used to the Garmin? So far, I am extremely frustrated by Garmin's under-estimation of drive times. Even when I go 4 miles above the posted speed limits, I am seldom able to catch up with the predicted drive time.There seems to be no allowance for stopping at lights. The greater the distance, the more this discrepancy.This is surprising given the Garmin's close attention to changing speed limits.
Also, I do not think that Garmin provides a warning about toll roads and the option to avoid them. I found this a very helpful Tom Tom feature.
The option of adding a memory card to the Garmin provides increased flexibility. I am yet to download additional points of interest to the card from the various on-line web-sites which provide such information free. I also look forward to trying out pedestrian information for NYC, including (I hope) public transportation details. Had I known that Garmins with MP3 players are needed for auditory tours, I might have chosen such a model.
A convenient feature is that the Garmin turns off automatically less than a minute after the car engine is stopped.The unit comes off the windshield readily for toting.
While a manual is available at the Garmin web-site, the curious user will find various hints and tips on-line.
I e-mailed 2 questions to Customer Service and received a helpful response within a couple of days-- even on a weekend!
I am still exploring so have not firmed up my opinion as to which brand is the better choice. I am tilting toward Tom Tom because of the IQ routing, but then I would not want to give up the more detailed points of interest given on the Garmin.
So quiet, no clicking. No downloading, just plug and play.
Finally a reader that is fast for my music, audiobooks and ebooks.  I got sooo tired of waiting and waiting and waiting for the others to download.  This one is exceptionally faster.

This is the third Netvue Camera I purchased. At the time of this review, this Netvue Orb Cam is the same list price as the Netvue Home Cam I previously purchased. Taking into consideration that Netvue Home Cam doesn't have the Pan & Tilt feature that this Cam does, getting added features for the same price is always nice.

Linking this camera to my account was straightforward and easy to do. Also, setup was easier to do than most wifi plugs and wall switches.

My son added my Netvue cameras to my Alexa account and setup Routines so the motion detection turns on lights connected to smart plugs as I walk through the house.

Performance of this Camera matches the quality of my other Netvue Cams and my Ring Doorbell 2 cam.

Pan & Tilt feature is sluggish and does not allow for small adjustment. For me that's not a problem because I won't be changing its angle or position regularly.

As seen in the attached photo, my son installed it at the edge of a window so that the anchor screws went into a stud and the camera wire could be hidden behind a curtain. He moved the surge protector that my cell phone charger and clock plugs into and mounted it on the wall so the camera could be plugged in as it was not long enough to reach the electrical outlet. We had to move furniture around to hide the surge protector.

NOTES:
TO PET OWNERS, if this camera not mounted and is set on a bookcase, the Pan & Tilt feature will not angle down below the level of the item it is sitting on, which means you may not see your pet walking around. I have a German Shepard as a service dog (mobility dog) and I mounted my camera on the wall so I could always see him.

Standard house door is roughly 80" (6' 8") and most home ceiling heights are 8 ft (96") but sometimes 10ft or 12ft. The power cords on all 3 Netvue cameras I own are 6ft (same as a standard household item such as a fan or clock). Every camera has required an extension cord and moving furniture.

I have have read numerous reviews about Smart Home devices complaining they are only 2.4g. 5.0g Wifi has faster transfer speeds but lower reception distances. 2.4g, like this device has, is more reliable with less connection interruptions.

My son uses this mounted on the dash of his Silverado 4x4 with a Huawei Ascend Mate 2 and i use it in my Chevy Malibu with a Huawei Ascend Mate 2 (my son and I both have a Huawei). He uses it both on highways and on pasture land while our feeding cattle. I have spent the same amount and more on other products that would not stay mounted with our heavy phablets even when driving on flat smooth pavement. This mounts securely, stays in place and holds well. As mentioned in other reviews, my phone has to be positioned carefully as not to press my side volume controls but it is the only mount that has worked for me.

Works a little too well; listening to movies, streaming, YouTube. The louder you set the volume, the more static and tinny the sound. Keeping the volume low helps with sound quality. Does not always work well with some phone calls however. Caller sometimes hears lots if static. Overall, works in a pinch.

Great headphones for my little boy! Only complaint is with iOS and the volume limiter. Volume limiting only seems to control the output on the actual headphone jack, not a bluetooth connection. Kinda a bummer, but my boy knows to keep the volume in the middle of the slider scale.

Overall great construction and I wish I could get a pair for my head at this price point.

I use this cable as an extension between a computer dock and my headset.  I ordered the calbe in late March. I've been using it for several hours 5 days a week since then, taking conference calls with multiple headsets.  The right-angle plug is useful to help gather and bundle cables coming out of the dock.  Audio quality is good.  The cable looks good and blends in well.  The braided sheathing is a nice touch.  I would buy this again.
Really good speakers for the price.  Primary use inside an office setting  Sound is clear at lower volumes.  Have not tested at high volume.  Would buy again and happily recommend.
Sound awesome. Husband won't take these.
Awesome sounding. Blocks out surrounding sound.
For a reasonably priced item, this is great. I find it comfortable and, despite some deafness, I hear clearly with the volume at max. Would buy again.

Well maybe not thousands but I've had plenty.

The software that runs this voice activated GPS is the best EVER. Many annoying features of other programs- not in evidence! So helpful and clear in the least obtrusive and informative way. In cities, it even tells the COLOR of buildings in driving instructions. (i.e. "Take the next left, after the white building")

Voice activated from a phrase that you program. Mine is "Hey, GPS" and it responds "Say a command" Not perfect, but very good voice recognition rarely confounded by ambient noise. Learn the commands and you have a steady co-pilot!

Excellent performance - recording my voice and voice in telephone as long as it is next to telephone speaker. Make sure you are not around a loud motor, fan, or other noise maker. It will record it better at times that anything else around.

This is the only case that I will buy for my Pi 4's from now on. The temperature controlled fan works perfectly and quietly, even at 100%. The power button makes it very easy to restart or power off. Putting all the connections in one place makes it easy keep things more organized.
I bought these to replace the hot end fan on my Tevo Tornado. They fit and work perfectly. Much quieter than the stock fan, while providing much more airflow.

This review is for the grip and four batteries. This grip works EXACTLY like the Nikon grip, but compared to buying the Nikon grip you will have $160.00 left over for gas to go out and take pictures! Fit is perfectly tight and secure, no wiggling or rattling. All the buttons and dials work as expected. My D7200 instantly recognizes this as the Nikon MB-D15 grip and enables all the menu options.

As for the batteries, the are recognized as official batteries by my D7200, their battery life is at least equal to the Nikon battery that came with my D7200, if not a bit longer. They are basically FREE. Nikon charges about $50 per battery, you get four with this grip. If you add the $200 the batteries would cost, to the $160 you saved on the grip, you have actually saved your $360.00 by buying this combo.
Very quiet, very efficient. I use this to cool the filament after it leaves the extruder on my 3D printer.
My son loves the camcorder. Tripod is pretty weak, but used at low levels is more than adequate. Case is small but adequate if you leave the charger out.
The product is fine but I hate that you require a specified number of words for feedback. this is stupid

This is a good-looking keyboard.  The keys are perfectly snappy and my typing speed has improved for this reason alone.  The sound is duller than most keyboards I've used, which is a plus.  It's hard to beat this for the price.

Okay....I wasn't sure if I should get these, but I would have been at a major lost!!! Sound is crisp and clear, set up took seconds literally and just a matter of picking them up..they connected to one another. Located my bluetoot connection and with one or two selections I was good to go.  I tried my music selection of choice and was in awe.  Amazing!! I will try out the other amazing qualities after a few songs because they are pleasing to my ears.  You must get these...I promise you won't be pleased!  I love the touch sensors on each bud...it pauses/plays, returns to previous song, accepts/rejects calls.

First thing I notice when I opened this package is that there is no charging case like you get with other true-wireless earbuds. You just get the earbud and a micro-USB charging cable. No charging case means you cannot easily recharge it on the go if the battery runs out; you need to plug it in to a USB charger. There is also no hard case to protect the earbud and keep it clean when not in use.

Two ear tips are included in the package. One is small size and the other is medium/large. They work OK, but are not as secure or comfortable as the memory foam ear tips that come with better quality earbuds.

The earbud paired easily with my Android phone. Sound quality is not good enough for music (to my ears), but fine for voice playback (like podcasts, news/sports, or phone calls). Volume is not really great, but sound quality is not noisy so you can max out your phone volume without hurting your ears.

The Amazon product description says you should get 12 hours of playback time, but the instruction sheet in the package says 5-6 hours of playback time. I listened to voice podcasts at close to maximum volume for 10 hours and still had 50% battery left. If you listen to music, battery life will probably be worse.

This earbud does not have any water resistance rating like you get with most better quality earbuds.

I often use a single earbud when I am running so I can hear car traffic with my other ear. This earbud is good enough for my purposes so far, but it is probably the worst quality wireless earbud that I own. 3.5 stars.

I have a Google Pixel 6 phone that has a USB-C port and no stereo audio port. I ordered the USB-C version of this microphone. When I plug the microphone into my USB-C port, I see that the phone automatically identifies it as an external microphone. I configured my recorder app to use the external microphone and it works fine. When I am close to the phone, I cannot say that the external microphone gives me any better sound quality than the phone's built-in microphone. When I am farther away, especially when I am aiming the phone to take a video, the hinge on the microphone allows me to angle it towards my subject (or towards the narrator) which does noticeably improve sound quality in some situations.

This adapter works OK with my Google Pixel 6 phone. I use it in my car so I can charge my phone and listen to stereo music or podcasts through the AUX jack on my car stereo. I get a strong clear audio signal through the stereo cable. Charging my phone is as fast as charger that it is plugged in to.
