The manual doesn't say how big is the internal battery for this speaker, but it must be huge since they claim 24 hours of music playing. You can forget those days when bluetooth speakers had only 1 or 2 hours of battery life. There is even a USB-out port on this speaker so you can use the speaker battery to recharge your smartphone if you really need to.

Unfortunately, there is no carrying case included with this speaker. The speaker does have a scratch-resistant rubberized exterior and they claim IPX5 water resistance, so it work great for outdoor parties, even when the weather is iffy.

I have a few different topics to cover in this review, so bear with me (if you want). If you already have experience with MICROSOFT Windows 10 laptops, maybe you can skip the middle (setup) section.

FORM FACTOR
The first thing I noticed when I opened the box is that this computer is huge and heavy. They advertise it as a 13 inch laptop and the screen does measure 13 inches (diagonal), but the machine does not even fit into a 14 inch laptop sleeve that I owned. I had to get a case for a 15 inch laptop to protect this. Total size of the laptop is 13 x 10.6 x 1.0 inches, which is about the width of a 14 inch laptop and the depth of a 15 inch laptop, with only a 13 inch screen. Amazon does give you the option to buy a form fitting case with this laptop and that is certainly something to consider (if the price is reasonable). According to my scale the laptop weighs 88 ounces (5.5 pounds), which is twice as much as some 13 inch laptops and more than most 15 inch laptops. The power brick is 28 ounces, which is also quite a big heavier (and more powerful) than typical laptop chargers. I'm not saying that these sizes and weights are unreasonable, just that you probably want to know what you are buying.

In case you are wondering (like I was), the power brick is hidden in a secret compartment in the back of the box (see photo).

SETUP
I have been using Microsoft computers for many years and have been very comfortable and happy with them in the past. I have used Windows 10 on a desktop computer, but this is my first experience with Windows 10 on a laptop. I HATE YOU, MICROSOFT! The system defaults seem to be set up for a cell phone, not a computer. When I first turned on the computer, you have to go through several MICROSOFT screens that try to download your personal information for their advertisers. What's up with that! I can understand Facebook doing this since they are a free service, but this laptop costs almost $2000 and I don't need this nonsense on top of that. So I very carefully went through each screen to turn off all their data grabbers (as best I could tell). Then I tried to download the MICROSOFT security patches (always a good idea for new computers). Then the MICROSOFT lockscreen kept popping up every 30 seconds, effectively killing my security download every time. Come on MICROSOFT, this isn't a cell phone. I had the computer plugged into the charger the whole time and I had the MICROSOFT security update program running, that should be a hint that I want the screen to stay on, right??? I had to spend a good couple of hours searching the internet for a solution to this problem, since the printed information that comes with the computer has no useful information about MICROSOFT. Fixing the lock screen problem is harder than it should be because MICROSOFT brilliantly put the lock screen controls in a different settings page from the power saver controls. Most of the online help pages say to change your power saver controls, but THEY ARE WRONG! Finally, 2 days after I received this machine, I have it working. I HATE YOU, MICROSOFT! Did I say that already?

PERFORMANCE
Once I have the machine setup, it performs beautifully. I disabled MICROSOFT Cortana and MICROSOFT Maps and MICROSOFT advertising services, MICROSOFT location services, etc and replaced the MICROSOFT audio and video players with VLC because after my experience setting up this machine, I really do not trust any of that stuff. I don't have an Oculus Rift or HTC Vive yet, so I didn't test the VR features of this laptop yet.

Quad-core CPU, NVIDIA graphics, SSD hard disc, and 16GB of RAM is blazing fast. Probably the fastest PC I have ever used. Each one of those components boosts performance in different ways and I've never had them all together in one machine before. This is like PC heaven.

HARDWARE
If you are using this laptop for VR, beware that there are only 2 full sized USB ports plus 2 USB-C ports. The keyboard is fantastic. The keys are backlit, full sized, and move beautifully when you type. Love the trackpad, too - large, nicely backlit, very responsive, and it has 2 physical mouse buttons. Sound from the built-in speakers is not real loud, but very clear. I did use the Alienware equalizer to boost the bass. The speakers don't noticeably distort until I get over 75% volume. The screen is very sharp and vibrant. I'm not able to compare this IPS screen to the Alienware OLED screen. No touchscreen on the IPS, which may be useful for some apps. Battery life has been mediocre at best; 2-4 hours at a time in the first few days of use. On the other hand, this machine is heavy enough that I'm not planning on using it on the move very often. When I take it somewhere, I'll bring the power brick with me. The back of the machine does get warm during use, but I suppose that is to be expected with all the power it is packing.

CONCLUSION
There's no getting around the fact that MICROSOFT Windows 10 is a pain in the you know where, especially to initially setup. If you have the technical ability, experience, patience, etc to work around MICROSOFT, then this is a fantastic laptop. Alienware makes several different 13 inch laptops. This is one of the mid-priced models. The higher end models have OLED touchscreen displays, which may be a little more exciting for you high-end gaming people. Lower-end Alienware laptops are best used for plugging into external monitors.

This is easily the best sounding Bluetooth speaker that I own, though I admit it is also the most expensive Bluetooth speaker that I own. Clarity and bass are both really great. The sound quality is especially impressive for a relatively small and lightweight speaker. Unlike cheap portable Bluetooth speakers, this one can fill a small sized room with music without significant distortion.

At 10 inches long and only 1.3 inch thick, you can easily drop this in your briefcase to take on business trips and really wow your clients with your presentation. I do wish that some kind of carrying case came in the box for this price, even a simple neoprene case to keep the speaker clean and avoid scratching.

Syncing the speaker with my Android phone was no problem. Just press the Bluetooth button on the speaker for 2 seconds, then look for it in the devices available for pairing list on your phone.

The B&O app is a surprisingly large 75MB on my Android phone. The app has an equalizer feature, that I assume adjusts the sound processing in the speaker, not just in your phone. It also lets you sync multiple B&O speakers (if you have them) and shows you a battery level indicator. Personally, I only have 1 speaker and don't think the other features are useful enough for the amount of memory the app uses on my phone, so I deleted it.

When I first opened the box, I was surprised to see just the speaker with no documentation or cables. I eventually discovered them hidden under the foam in the bottom of the box. The charger is a USB-C cable, which is becoming an international standard for smartphones and laptops, but yours may not use yet. You need to click the cable securely into the speaker to start charging (light on the speaker turns on). Plug the other end of the cable into your USB phone charger. Unfortunately, the slim documentation doesn't say what power levels you can use or how long the speaker will take to recharge (and I don't have the patience to measure it).

Fit-and-finish and build quality are excellent. The appearance is not especially attractive (plastic exterior over a sturdy metal frame), but build quality is solid. All the buttons and lights and ports are also solid. 5 stars for top-of-the-line functionality, but at this price you need to make your own value judgement.

There are a lot of the LG Tone refurbs on Amazon. That's not a good sign for quality of this product. After a dozen uses, mine are working great. Build quality seems good and the Bluetooth pairs flawlessly with my phone. I paid $20 for these and the sound quality is better than any other $20 Bluetooth headset that I have used (much better than most). Bass level is good and clarity is excellent for this price level. This is my first experience with this collar-style of Bluetooth headset. I have to say that I like it much better than Bluetooth headsets with the electronics in the earbuds, since that makes the earbuds bulky, heavy, and uncomfortable. With this headset, all the weight is around your neck and the earpieces are very lightweight and comfortable. I'm not a fast runner, but I don't have any problems with the collar when jogging for a couple of miles and the lightweight earpieces don't fall out like the heavier ones do.

The headphones come in a simple plastic bag with a few extra ear tips and a USB cable, but no case, no wall charger, no other accessories. My cell phone charger works fine to charge these and they charge very quickly. There are plenty of LG Tone cases on Amazon that are moderately priced and work well. Because of the bulky design, I recommend that you do use a case with this headset, especially if you're carrying it in a backpack or messenger bag.

"Certified Refurbished" seems to be a program managed by Amazon that and not associated with the product manufacturer. Amazon is kind of vague about how these refurbishing companies get certified. You do get a 90 day money-back warranty, so I do plan on testing this product thoroughly for 90 days.

LG Tone 750s retail for $40 and I paid half price for these refurbs that seem to work fine, so I'll rate this a 4-star deal for now.

I really like this compact, lightweight Bluetooth speaker. Pairing with my Android phone is quick and easy. Sound is not super loud, but very good for a speaker of this size. Don't expect it to fill a room with rich sound, but it is more than adequate if you're a few feet away. Most small speakers will painfully distort the sound at higher volumes or the maximum volume is really tame, but this one is still tolerable at a good volume volume. Battery life is great. A charging cable is included, but it uses the same cable as my phone (and most non-Apple phones). This is easily the best ultralight (under 1 pound) Bluetooth speaker that I have used.

This is a reasonably priced flash drive that works very well. Mounts easily to both my PC and my Android phone (using an OTG cable). Speed is more than adequate for my usage. The USB port cover is a little clunky, but works if you pull hard enough and is nice to have.

This is a smallish lightweight mouse for use on-the-go. It does require a USB RF dongle, which conveniently is stored inside the mouse body (next to the battery) so you don't lose it when traveling. An RF wireless mouse is usually more reliable and responsive than a Bluetooth mouse, but the dongle can be a hassle. The product description says the mouse is compatible with Microsoft Windows, Linux, Chromebooks, and Android. Of course, Android devices usually do not have full-sized USB ports for the dongle, so Bluetooth is much more convenient with those devices. I tested this mouse with my Windows laptop and desktop computers and it installed quickly and worked flawlessly. The smaller size is not as comfortable to use as a bigger mouse, though smaller is more portable. The lightweight plastic shell does feel kind of cheap, but that is because this product is cheap. For the price I really cannot complain.

This is a decent speaker for the price. Sound is clear and there is some bass. However, volume is very limited (less than I was expecting, even for this size speaker). It is fine for desktop use when you're sitting a couple of feet away. More distance than that and the sound is not satisfying.

These headphones sound much better than most other $10 headphones that I have used. Since I loose them often, I get to try a lot of headphones, and I also value the low price of this set. I'm only giving these 4 stars however, because of the disappointing set of accessories that you get. All other MEElectronics headphones that I have bought come with a nice carrying case and twice as many different ear tips to guarantee a comfortable fit. This set comes in a plastic bag with a minimal set of extra tips.

I'm not an audiophile, but I do like my music and I've heard a lot of awful headphones over the years (including awful and expensive). These are great all-around headphones. They are not real heavy or real bulky, but they still fit over my ears, which is much more comfortable than on-ear headphones, especially if you wear glasses. Sound quality is very clear and neutral at all frequencies. The bass is not overwhelming like you get with some designer headphones. The microphone works with my Android phone, though only the middle button works (to answer calls or pause music). The up and down buttons are unfortunately only for iphone. I like that these headphones fold up for easy portability, though not including a protective carrying case is disappointing (you just get a cloth bag).

I bought this head when the price was $16. Now that the price is $22, I'm deducting 1 star. If you search on Amazon, you will find similar products for around $16.

Comparable name-brand tripod heads cost $50 and up. The name brand heads do operate more smoothly, which helps you work more quickly. For many people who only use a tripod infrequently, this cheap head may be all you need.

Better quality tripod heads are also more secure; unlikely to wiggle and ruin your photo after you lock them down. If you're using a lighter-weight camera (like an ILC mirrorless camera with the kit lens), this head is probably sturdy enough.

The mount at the bottom of the tripod head (where it fits to your tripod legs) is 3/8", which is the international standard for better quality tripods. More expensive tripod heads often come with an adapter so you can use them with low-end tripod legs or monopods with 1/4" mounts, but this head does not. You can buy an adapter at your local camera store for a couple of dollars or Amazon is selling packs of 10 adapters for around $5. Note that some tripods have reversible mounts that fit both 1/4" and 3/8" heads, so check yours before going out to buy an adapter.

Unlike most earbuds, these do not have soft rubber tips that fit in your ear and seal off outside sound. If you find the rubber tip style to be uncomfortable, you may want to give this design a try. These earbuds have once-size-fits-most hard plastic tips that are fairly comfortable in my ears. I've used a lot of headphones and these are about average in sound quality for this price. Sound is balanced, unlike some popular brands that over-emphasize the bass and only sound good with rap or rock music. Midrange clarity is pretty good. Volume is OK; these do not get as loud as some other earbuds, but probably get loud enough for most people. Build quality is pretty good, with midweight cords that resist tangling, but are not so heavy that they bounce around uncomfortably when running. No carrying case is included, unfortunately.

These are not the best earbuds that I own, but the sound pretty quality is good, making this a really great value at $8. Vocals are clear and the bass is rich. Build quality is very good for this price. Microphone works with Android, not just iphone. I bought 5 more before the price goes up.

Most $10 headphones sound tinny. These actually sound decent. Not as accurate as $50 earbuds, but decent bass and good clarity in the midrange. These also come with much better accesories than other earbuds in this price range. The case is very useful and you get 5 pairs of ear tips to guarantee a comfortable and clear sounding fit. The wires are not thick and heavy like you get in a lot of better headphones, but heavy cables are a negative if you use the headphones for running since they uncomfortably bounce around. These cables are thick enough to reduce tangling problems, but not heavy enough to cause problems when exercising. I really can't complain about anything for the $10 price and you regularly can find these for $10 from various vendors, including Amazon at times.

After reading the comments here, I decided to not bother with the Sony software. I installed "Nexus Media Importer" from the Google Android app store and it automatically detects and mounts the Sony device. I can read and write files with no problem, including playing audio and video files without copying them to the phone memory. On my PC, the Sony device mounts like any other flash drive. I would give this 5 stars if it was $30 (and if it came with better instructions), but the $45 price seems high for what is essentially a flash drive with a micro-USB port. You can get the same functionality (in a larger form factor) by using a regular flash drive and an OTG cable (sold here on Amazon for less than $2).

EDIT: I'm still happy with this device, but since writing this review, I've noticed that several other companies (SanDisk and others) have come out with similar products (flash drives with both micro and regular USB connectors) and some of them have much faster USB3.0 speeds. Sony has reduced their price to be competitive. Shop around; I expect functionality is similar.

This is a nice portable desktop speaker for personal music playing or for use as a cell phone speakerphone. Bluetooth connects very easily to my Android devices. Controls are easy to use (but read the instructions because the volume and music controls use the same buttons). Sound clarity is excellent for such a small speaker. Don't expect booming volume, though. It is fine if you are sitting a few feet away, but even at full volume, it will sound weak from across a room.

This is a nice portable desktop speaker for personal music playing or for use as a cell phone speakerphone. Bluetooth connects very easily to my Android devices. Controls are easy to use (but read the instructions because the volume and music controls use the same buttons). Sound clarity is very good for such a small speaker. Don't expect booming volume, though. It is fine if you are sitting a few feet away, but even at full volume, it will sound weak from across the room.

I use these with my Android cell phone. The controls mostly work. I can make calls with the microphone and answer calls with the middle button. When playing music, the middle button also pauses/resumes the playback. The volume control buttons appear to have no functionality with Android.

Very happy with the sound from these headphone. There is very good bass as well as good detail in the higher frequencies. If you're using the stock headphones that came with your phone or MP3 player, these will give you a significant improvement in sound quality.

The drivers on these headphones are very large compared to many other products, with a large chunk sitting outside your ear. Seems comfortable enough, but the headphones will be very noticeable to people who see you on the street.

The thick cords are both good and bad. The good is that they are very tangle-resistant. The bad is that they are heavier than wire cords and bounce around uncomfortably when running. I'm going to use different headphones for running. I haven't had any problems with durability yet, but I haven't had them very long.

Now that the price has dropped to $24, I ordered 3 more. I have used a lot of headphones over the years and these are clearly the best that I have ever bought for less than $30. I don't give out 5 stars ratings very often, but will do so here because of the unbeatable value at the $24 price, despite the volume buttons not working with my phone.

There are a lot of Bluetooth rechargeable speakers on the market these days. Most are smaller and lighter weight than this Philips model. The Philips P8 weighs almost 3 pounds and uses its bigger size and weight to produce better bass than most of the competition. I thought the treble was adequately crisp, but that depends on the type of music you play as well as the quality of your Bluetooth connection. This speaker does tend to emphasize bass, so that may drown out your treble at full volume.

The Philips P8 looks nice with an all-black aluminum case. While the speaker is big on the front, it is relatively thin and easy to carry in a briefcase or backpack. They even include a carrying bag, since portability is obviously a big feature of a rechargeable speaker.

Pairing with my Android smartphone was quick and easy. Just click on the "Philips P8" entry in the phone's discovered Bluetooth device list.

My only real complaint is that it uses a non-standard charger (not micro-USB), so you will have to pack the special charger with you when traveling (and don't ever lose it). The Philips charger probably charges the battery faster than say an ipad charger, but at least having the option to use a USB charger in a pinch would be a nice touch.

I have a couple of these Marley earbuds, as well as more expensive Klipsch S3 and S4 earbuds. These Marleys have a noticeably stronger bass sound than the Klipsch products, but it is smooth, not harshly amplified like in cheaper products. If you like bass or like music that sounds good with heavier bass, then give these a try. You're not going to find much better for $20. The Klipsch models are a little more accurate in the mid and higher frequencies, which is great for classical music or opera.

The Marley earbuds do have a cloth-wrapped cord which looks kind of cool, as well as adding strength and reducing tangles. The microphone and push button work great with my Android smartphone. The rubber ear tips are comfortable for me even during hours of continuous listening, though they don't seal quite as well as the oval Klipsch ear tips. No quality issues after months of use.

The D5100 was a big improvement over the D5000. The D5200 is only a minor enhancement over the D5100, but at a much higher price. More AF points is an interesting change for some types of photos. More MP is rarely useful at this level. Stero mic on the camera isn't really important; use an external microphone if you care about sound quality. If you're thinking about a D5200, do yourself a favor and look at the Nikon D5100 also. You might find one for half the price (especially Nikon factory refurbished) and not notice any performance difference.

I use this card for copying JPEG photos from my camera to my Android smartphone. This allows me to email photos immediately in the field via my phone's data connection, without having to plug the card in to my laptop and search for a WiFi hotspot. This is great for journalists, travelers, or just heavy Facebook or Instagram users. Yes, you could use your phone's camera, but a dedicated camera takes way better photos, especially in low light conditions or zooming in or macro closeups. Copying a photo from my camera to my phone takes about 3 seconds.

Setting up the connection between the Eye-Fi card and your phone does require some semi-complicated configuration work involving both your PC and your phone, so make sure you figure it out well ahead of time. The process is not documented with the instruction manual or in the PC app, but you can find it on the Eye-Fi web site. You only need to do this setup once.

Aside from the one-time setup issues, another issue is that this card needs lots of power. I figure I need 3 times as much camera battery power when using this card compared to a regular memory card. My camera can normally take about 300 photos on one battery charge. With this card copying all my photos to my phone via WiFi, I only get about 100 photos per battery charge, so bring lots of spare batteries.

This card also burns your cell phone battery. I use my smartphone for lots of things, so hard to measure the impact of the EyeFi, but I can easily burn through almost 2 smartphone batteries while using this card (for 200 photos), while I can usually last a full day on just one battery when I'm not using this card. Think twice about using this card if you do not have spare batteries for your phone.

I only copy JPEG photos to my phone with this card. I set my camera to shoot JPEG+RAW, but this Eye-Fi only transfers the JPEGs. That's fine with me since the RAW files are huge and would take forever to copy and my phone's RAW-to-JPEG conversion probably is not as good as the camera's. RAW files have more detail for printing, but I can always copy the RAW files to my PC using the old card reader.

I would give this card 5 stars if not for the battery issue, and also the price is kind of expensive if you're not using it all the time in the field.

If you're looking for a smaller self-contained Android speaker dock, give this one a try. If you don't have much space on your table or desk, this one is nice because it is one piece with a small footprint. Sound is pretty good for a small unit, though of course it doesn't compare with higher powered separate stereo speakers. Bluetooth is easy to setup and doesn't seem to degrade audio quality. The micro-USB power port works well and is more stable than it looks.

Philips does have a couple of Android apps that are designed to work with this dock. Reviews for the apps are poor and features seem limited, so I didn't bother installing it. Numerous high quality audio apps are already available for Android and they work fine with this dock. Android's standard Bluetooth features also work fine with this dock. I run the Bluetooth for several hours at a time at my desk with no problems. Since the dock charges your phone at the same time it powers the speakers, you don't have to worry about your phone's battery running down even if you keep the screen on all the time.

I haven't tried the battery power mode yet, but that could be useful if you're using this dock outdoors or in the garage away from a power outlet.

My only issue with this product is the astronomical price, but huge discounts are sometimes available.

I am reviewing this device when paired with a Verizon Samsung Galaxy Nexus Android phone. I assume it fully works with recent Motorola Android phones. No idea how well it works with other phones.

Motorola is selling a bunch of Android accessory devices that enhance the functionality of their Android smartphones, especially for business users. The Android bluetooth keyboard has special Android-specific function buttons (like the ones you see on your phone). The Android multi-media docks power your phone and have HDMI outputs to connect to a big screen TV. The laptop docks convert your phone into a laptop computer. This "smart controller" is another device in this product line.

The smart controller is a bluetooth touchpad and with a few smartphone-specific features. On the side, there is a volume control that works just like the volume control on your phone. On the back, there are the 4 standard Android buttons (menu, home, back, search) that work just like the buttons on your phone. Also on the back is a 2 inch square touch-pad that remotely controls your phone's touch screen, except a little differently. One finger drag gestures move a cursor around your screen to you can select specific objects in the Android GUI. Two finger multi-touch gestures move the screen around; scrolling the screen up-and-down or left-and-right. On the front is a telephone handset so you can make or receive voice calls. There is a single phone button to make or end calls.

This device paired easily with the Bluetooth on my Galaxy Nexus. All of the advertised features work fine. One finger gestures on the touch pad work easily, though the cursor is blue and can be hard to see if your background is also blue. Two finger gestures take some getting used to, at least if you have fat fingers like me. Phone call quality is pretty good. You can make calls using the touch pad to access your phone's contact list or touch dialer. Or press on the phone button to redial the last number you called (or to pickup an incoming call or end the current call).

Do you really need this device? If you have your phone hooked up to a HDTV to watch videos or slideshows or business presentations on a big screen, then this controller is very handy, though of course not everyone is going to do that. If you only do this kind of thing occasionally, the $100 price tag for this device is very expensive. If you already have a bluetooth mouse and bluetooth headset, those will probably give you most of the same functionality.

The smart controller has a rechargeable battery that runs for more hours than my phone, so no complaints there.

4 stars because this smart controller mostly achieves what it is designed for. Knocking off one star for the price and also because the two-finger gestures are a little tricky on the small touch pad.

Picked up a couple of these when Amazon had them on sale for half price. Had to return one because it was out of focus; Amazon processed the return quickly and the replacement works great.

Very pleased with the image quality of these cameras in the 1080p mode (which I always use). The video quality is sharp and colorful. Make sure you use the camera software to set the image quality to the highest level for best results.

Sound quality is a mixed bag. This camera uses noise reduction to reduce wind noise (which is a big problem with older Contour cameras at even moderate bicycling speeds), but the noise reduction also severely muffles your voice if you are trying to narrate a video while filming.

The camera controls are very easy to use, which is an improvement over earlier Contour cameras. The instant-on feature works great if you're filming only pieces of your event. I get about 3 hours of video from one battery charge. That also seems to be the amount of video that fits on a 32GB microSD card. If your event is longer than 3 hours, use the instant-on/instant-off feature to switch the camera on for just the important parts. The instant-on feature is a nice improvement over earlier Contour cameras that are difficult to turn on when you are moving.

Contour cameras seem to go on sale more often than GoPro. If you can catch it at a good sale price, I think Contour is a much better value than GoPro.

I don't know what this thing really does, but it is magic. Without it, plugging my NookColor into my decent quality portable speakers created awful static noise. The noise was so bad that I almost returned the NookColor as defective (my ipod and cell phone work fine with the same speakers). A friend recommended this PAC device, which he bought for $20 at a local car stereo store, but I bought for $13 here at Amazon. It is magic. Music played from my NookColor now sounds wonderfully clear.

The PAC device uses no batteries; just plug it in like a headphone cable. My friend says it matches the impedence from a music player and incompatible speaker systems. I don't know what that means, the Amazon description is not helpful, and the device comes with no useful documentation, but it really does work.

This light is designed for a specific problem:  lighting close-up macro photos.  When your subject is a few inches or a few feet from your camera, traditional flashes usually have trouble lighting your scene evenly.  This macro light solves the problem by lighting from all around your lens.  No, it is not super-sturdy.  Nor does it does have a lot of different settings or controls.  More useful products are available for much higher prices.  For its moderate price, I think this product does an adequate job for beginners or cheapskates.

I've been using this for about a year now. The automatic configuration did not work with my Covad DSL. I had to call Covad to get the DSL configuration parameters. After I entered those into the DSL modem (along with my account information), the DSL connection has been rock solid. I have it on all the time. Once every couple of months, it loses the signal for a couple of hours. That is more likely due to a Covad problem than a modem problem.

The Wireless-G router works great, too. I have laptop computers, internet radios, and my Tivo hooked up to it and they all work fine. The wireless-G speed is more than adequate for my needs. If you do a lot of big data transfers between computers, then the wireless-N speed may be better for you.

No problems with the wireless encryption. All my devices are able to login OK. No problems using the internet router firewall either. I trust that a lot more than the software firewall in my PC.

I've had my Slacker player for about a month now and use it almost every day. It's a great device if you like listening to music and don't want to buy (or steal) thousands of dollars worth of MP3's. Even if you do own a huge MP3 library, Slacker is still interesting if you don't want to have to constantly manage the content of your iPod and your playlists.

Slacker sound quality is way better than XM/Sirius or FM radio. I use the free Slacker service and commercials are minimal; maybe once every couple of hours I get a 5 second "this is Slacker radio" announcement.

The pre-programmed Slacker music channels are very good, but the real nice feature is being able to design your own music stream by selecting musicians that you like and asking the player to play only those or (your choice) to discover similar bands. Slacker does not have access to every song ever recorded, but neither does any iPod owner's personal MP3 collection.

Setting up your player does take a bit of work, but it is not rocket science. If you use the wi-fi connection, you do need to know how to set up a wi-fi connection (usually by looking up and entering your MAC address and wi-fi password). You can also download by USB cable, which may be faster. The documentation included in the box is a little sparse, but you can download a more detailed user manual at the [...] web site.

Programming a music stream is as easy or as hard as you want it to be. Easiest is selecting one of the many pre-programmed stream. Second easiest is to select one band by name and asking Slacker to create a stream of similar music. I entered 40 bands and asked Slacker to expand on that by discovering similar music. Then you just connect the Slacker player to your wi-fi and let it download your music. The first download will take a while since it has to download all 8GB. After that, it only downloads enough new music to replace the songs that you have listened to. Do a refresh as often as you want (but 8GB of music should last you for at least several days).

I only have 2 complaints. First the device is kind of big (mostly wide). It does come with a free case, but the case does not have a belt loop. At least the big screen does make it easy to see the album art and read the artist bios and album descriptions. The Slacker G2 devices are smaller, but also much more expensive. Second, the off switch is kind of finicky. Sometimes I have to press it a few times or even try it from different modes to get it to switch off. Other than that, I think the 8GB Slacker for [...] is a great value.

If you're still unsure about Slacker, go to the Slacker web site and try the free on-line music player. Create your free own station, and listen to it for a few hours. If you like what you hear and want to listen to it while you are away from the Internet, then this device is for you. When you get the device, you can download the music stream you created on the web site to your Slacker player.

The SoundBot SB520 3D HD Bluetooth 4.0 Wireless Speaker is perfect for my use.  It's easy to connect to your device and once connected does not have to be connected again.  The sound is excellent.  It's as loud as I need it t be and it's clear!  I think the buttons should be on the back instead of on the top.  It's a nice size and can easily be "to go" wherever.  I would recommend this speaker for its sound quality and its simplicity of use.

This is my 2nd review of this speaker because it's the 2nd one I've gotten! I'm happy to say the dual pairing ability, at this price, was a no brainer. Great battery life on my first one from a few weeks back. I hope this 2nd unit does just as well. The sound is great and having them paired makes them so much better. I recommend.

Good product for the price. I'm considering getting a 2nd unit to see how they pair with each other.

I ordered these and did not expect much. These are amazing. They are almost a dupe for my original iPhone earbuds. The sound quality is excellent. I had them in and my doorbell rang, I barely heard it ringing! I have only had them for a couple of days, but so far, so good. I have wanted wireless earbuds, but I have been having trouble with connecting them or I have lost them, so I guess I will stick with my trusty "wired" earbuds.

Loud sound, good reception, works on 120 V AC or off batteries.

I don't listen to radio much but bought it in case of emergencies as it doesn't require an Internet connection and will work in a blackout.

Note that you don't need to extend the antenna for AM reception.

It's Panasonic and feels like it, not your cheap no-name Chinese radio...

This module is perfect! It comes all soldered and has the screw-in terminals.
Like almost all relays of this type it can't handle more than 10 A. In the rest of the world that would be no problem since 230 V breakers trip at 10 A. But in North America, with 15 A and 20 A circuits, this is not going to work. That limits you to devices 1200 W or less.

My first project with it is a system to water plants. The pump only requires 4-12 V and probably a few hundred milliamps.
By the way, if you want to power bulbs or for many other applications, I recommended using DC voltage. The bulbs will light up just the same, but it will be much less dangerous than dealing with AC.

ONE PROBLEM: It lacks labeling of the relay terminals. NO Normally Open, C Common, NC Normally Closed are not printed.

ONE GIANT ADVANTAGE: This module compared to others is great because you supply 5V to it through a separate pin, so you don't have to provide the required current on the input pin. The module does that for you. Many boards out there will have only an input pin, which you can't use directly, you'll have to build the missing circuitry so you can control the relay with your Arduino or whatnot. Plus some boards are missing the very important diodes!

It also has one status LED per relay so you know what's going on at all times. Note that it is active low.

Black Friday sales have brought the Echo Dot to under $30, and that is how I am now buying my second one.

So yes, often times you do need to formulate your requests in a certain way (for instance, try asking Alexa how much time it will take to go to work... I gave up on this...) and enunciate them more clearly if you missed, but in general, this technology is just amazing.
Sometimes I even ask Alexa for information I don't need, just for fun.

I like that they named it Alexa. That's so much better than "Okay Google." It feels like a real person. Who in hell at Google thought it's a good idea to force users to use their company name, and thus remind them that their huge creepy analytics private data gathering network is behind it?

Possible improvements:
* Bring back the matte finish from 1st gen. I shouldn't have to pay more to not have it shiny...
* Listen to the word "stop" when the alarm is ringing. Currently you need to wait until it's not ringing and then say "Alexa, stop."
* Add confirmation and modification prompts to "Add a new event to the calendar." Currently if she misunderstood one word, you have to start all over again.
* Alexa bluntly tells you that she cannot tell you about the events in your calendar on a specific date... C'mon guys...
* Implement the word "Repeat": sometimes you didn't hear or didn't catch the information you were looking for, and currently you have to formulate your request again
* Only gives info about the last Amazon order. She can retrieve more order but you have to be very specific about what they contain.
* I wish Alexa could Google more stuff.
* Choose your own wake up word

I never use Siri on my iPhone, but for some reason it feels very natural to use Alexa, maybe because the device is more "fixed" whereas my phone could be in a backpack, in the other room...

The Killer App is MUSIC. We have an Echo Dot in the bedroom, and my wife just loves to ask Alexa for tunes. We have it linked to Spotify.

Also, I am a software engineer, and I have added some custom features through my own skills. I wish somebody came up with something simple to add your own skills, because this is really useful. For instance, the bus comes in front of my house at the most random times, so I developed a skill that tells me in how many minutes the next buses will come. So much faster than having to check a website on my phone!

I use two of these to store my GoPro footage. I set them up as a RAID 1, so they have the exact same content at all time. Can't tell you about the performance because of this, as RAID 1 increases the throughput. Very happy with them.

They don't make any noticeable noise, even with both of them powered on. Not the case of an older WD elements I have, which is about the sound level of a quiet laptop fan or the level of sound a distant water pipe makes when your neighbor takes a shower.
The Seagate though, no noise...

When I give it 5 stars, it's obviously not on an absolute scale. I have audiophile equipment, but for the price these are really excellent. Love the fact that it's USB powered. Sure you don't get a headphone jack but if you need that a Y splitter is dirt cheap. They can deliver rather well at a good volume. They are the perfect size next to my 13" MBP laptop. One tiny complaint is that there's no label Left / Right (the one with the knob is the right for me).

If I could put 6 stars I would.
There are several things I can't live without: food, water, toilet paper, and the Mighty Mouse.
My only hope is that it stays like it is forever and they make it until the end of times.

I configured it so that the wheel scrolls the content of the page (in both directions) while holding the small left button. It's a shame only Linux lets me customize it this way. On Windows, I once had a donationware that allowed me to do the same but forgot the name.

Pros:
- ergonomics! better than thumb-operated
- your health
- practical for small to gigantic resolutions, no need to ridiculously lift the mouse (but you'll need to lift your finger)
- no noise while scrolling
- scrolls in all directions (horizontal + vertical)
- works without installing any driver, plug and play
- easy to clean
- This thing is RELIABLE. I can't remember when I bought mine
- A real bargain! I can't believe it only costs $22 now. I bought it for twice as much back then.
- Cool factor!

Cons:
- Needs 30 sec cleaning once a month.
- There is a learning curve, but to be honest that's the case for any mouse, you just forgot or didn't realize it as a child. You'll be a pro after 1-2 weeks. The way it works is by "launching" the wheel at high speed to reach the other corner of the screen, then use your finger to position the pointer precisely.
- You'll need another mouse if you share the computer.
- Not suited for gaming or image editing (you should really be using a graphics tablet anyway).

There is so much talk about the declining sales of iPad. I think the key to making a decision to buy the iPad Pro lies in a wallpaper Apple provided with the very first version of iPad. It was a licensed photograph of Pyramid Lake by Robert Misrach. The exposure, made at night, appears to be in daylight. The clue that it was a night time photograph are the star trails that resulted from the long exposure. The lake surface appears as smooth as a mirror. The mirror surface of the lake in this photograph enables the viewer to immerse himself or herself in the device, making it a perfect fulfillment of whatever there desires might be "for iPad". The iPad is a perfect "evocative object", evoking whatever feelings and intentions the iPad user brings to it. That is why the iPad is so undefinable and uncategorizable. It is is whatever ever we want it to be.....and with iPad Pro Apple reaches again for that elusive quality.

After 7 days with the new Apple iPad Pro I am happy that I followed my hunch that the iPad Pro would be better for me than a laptop for a mobile multi-purpose device. I am very pleased how the slide over multitasking works. Bigger is better whether using multi-tasking features live slide over and picture-in-picture. The user does not get poorly sized Windows for both applications. For example if your browser is open in one window, and photos is open in a second, but applications are scaled to size in each window.

I purchased the 32MB version because I tend to use iCloud to store photos, music, documents. I only need local storage for IOS apps and the few documents I need.

I purchased a black rear cover, and a contrasting white front cover. The only accessory I use so far is the Apple Pencil for drawing in Paper by 53 and Apple Notes ( to take notes in my University classes ). I use the iPad Pro almost exclusively landscape or horizontal, the only iPad that can be used in portrait is the Mini. At the time I purchased the iPad Pro the wait times for shipment of the Apple Pencil was 4-5 weeks. However, I was able to find one locally at my University Bookstore. I am concentrating on using the Apple Pencil at the moment, using just the on-screen keyboard. I have an open mind about buying the iPad Pro keyboard in the future. However, the iPad is all about creating art through use of touch and the pencil right now. I don't want it to be a laptop. I want it to be a "blank sheet of paper".

The audio produced by the 4 speakers produce a very pleasing music listening experience without headphones.

One final note: it appears the iPad Pro includes technology that can be used in the future today's blog post in Daring Fireball notes that the Lightning connector includes support for USB 3.0, a much faster transfer speeds. It will be interesting to see what applications take advantage of that speed next year.

GENERAL INFORMATION ON USB CHARGING

In order to test this device for my Vine review, I spent over two hours (!!!) trying to find comprehensible information on what the term “smart” means in the context of a USB port on a power strip like this one. Unfortunately, I was left with more questions than answers, for which hassle I’m dropping a star off this review. I’ve included some of what I learned below, for what it might be worth to any fellow Amazon customer who might be thinking of purchasing this product.

A smart USB charger port supposedly can, in and of itself, figure out what the optimal charging speed of a specific device is when it is plugged into that port, in order to neither overload it with too much current or under-deliver to it the optimal current. The question on everyone’s mind these days (it certainly has been on mine), is whether it is possible to destroy the battery in a particular device by slamming too much current into it. Apparently, the answer to this all-important question is: No. If, for example, you take a phone which comes with a 900mA wall charger, and you plug it into a 2,100mA charger that comes with a different device you own, it will not damage the phone. It will only speed up the length of time it takes for the phone’s battery to charge. However, if you have a USB device older than 2007, it may not charge on any USB ports newer than the (now ancient), 500mA USB 1.0 and 2.0 PC ports. Which means such older devices may not charge even on the “smart” USB ports on this device.

USB charging current is measured in mA (milliampere, 1/1000 of an ampere, the basic unit for measuring electrical current). There are three kinds of USB ports which are defined by their current specs: a standard downstream port, a charging downstream port, and a dedicated charging port. The first two are found on a desktop computer. The third kind is a “dumb” wall charger.

USB 1.0 and 2.0 standard downstream ports on a computer can deliver up to 500mA (0.5A).

USB 3.0 standard downstream ports on a computer can deliver up to 900mA (0.9A).

USB 3.1 and USB 3.2 ports can deliver between 1,500mA (1.5A) and 3,000mA (3A).

Charging downstream USB ports on a computer can deliver up to 1,500mA (1.5A).

Dedicated USB charging ports on a computer can deliver up to 3,000mA (3A).

I have had very good luck with AmazonBasics products, and this one is no exception. It is excellent value for the price.

This power supply for a PC is priced at the lower end of the Corsair line of power supplies, but it so far seems to live up to Corsair's excellent reputation. It runs quietly and functions well, offering reliable power. It offered no installation problems, and it is compatible my CPU platform. All in all, I am satisfied with this product.

These earbuds work as well as the Panasonic ones my husband and I have purchased for years. The sound quality is excellent, and the price is about half as much. I've already ordered a second pair. It comes in a pleasing variety of colors for all tastes. I got the pink and my husband got the blue.

I got this fan in the pink-and-white color. I personally don't have any complaints about this fan, but there are a lot of features I really like, including:

--This is a very cute, attractive fan. It is a nice, bright pink in the center with white trim.
--This fan is small enough to carry around in a day pack or large purse, which makes it handy to use when going on a hike, walking around an amusement park in the summer, or lifting it to bring it closer to your face just sitting at your desk. It measures about 5 inches in diameter, and weighs only a few ounces.
--It is rechargeable using a white USB cable that comes with the fan. I have recharged it using both my computer or an adapter attached to a wall outlet. It charges quickly either way, and it seems to hold a charge well. The other big plus of it being rechargeable is that I can plug it into a USB hub on my desk and run the fan all day long without worrying about it losing its charge.
--It has a foldaway piece that acts as a stand, similar to what you find on some picture frames. This allows it to stand erect quite sturdily, on a desk or tabletop. This makes it really convenient to use at my desk where the heat from my computer often makes even the combined air flow from air conditioning, a ceiling fan and a small floor fan not enough to keep me cooled off.
--This would make a great emergency fan for a power outage in the summer.
--It has three options for air-flow speed, low, medium and high, which are accessed through the pink, round, toggle switch at the top of the fan. This same switch is the on/off button. This is an extremely convenient feature in such an inexpensive fan.
--This fan is not silent, but I personally consider it very quiet for a portable fan in general. In particular, it is much quieter than either of the small, 9-inch, portable fans I own. One of them, in fact, is so loud, I realized recently that if I sit such that it is within four feet of my head, it actually gives me tinnitus in the ear nearest that fan. Not so with this fan, thank goodness. I currently have it on high speed just 18 inches from my ear, sitting on my desk, and I can barely hear it.

I have owned these headphones since August, 2014. They are easy to use, and the sound quality is excellent. Prior to owning them, I tried out some $20 wireless headphones from a local drugstore which did not work at all, and I also did a jury-rigged setup with a very long, trip-hazard cable linking some headphones I owned to my TiVo. Never again. Both were a disaster.

This system is absolutely wonderful for two reasons:

First, I have weird hearing issues in that when I am trying to sleep, every little sound bugs me and I seem to hear even a conversation in the next room far more clearly than I have any desire to do, but when listening to TV, I can't understand 75% of what the actors are saying without captions. Go figure. With these headphones, no more problem. All dialog is clear as a bell.

Second, I no longer have to drive my husband crazy blaring the TV in order to adequately hear the actors speaking. By the same token, if my husband is watching a program on TV that I'm not at all interested in, I don't have to be subjected to listening to that either.

It's win-win.

I will say that I was not myself techie enough to install these headphones. My husband is an IT guy and he had to do it for me. So that's one downside for the customer who struggles with techie installations. Other than that, all is great.

This is a very high quality, "braided" type cable versus a smooth plastic one. I've had both types, and I much prefer this type. It is more durable. I tested this cable on my iPhone 5c. I used this cable to charge my phone via a wall outlet using an adapter. It works very well for that. I also tested this cable hooked to my desktop PC, and it does an equally excellent job transferring data and charging my phone in that manner.

I would definitely recommend this USB cable to friends and family.

This is the third SanDisk MP3 player I've owned over the past five years. The first was 1GB, the second 4GB, and now this 8GB player.

At first I struggled a bit with the changes in interface, but ultimately I decided they were useful upgrades.

The sound quality is as good or better than the previous models. The color is very attractive, and the device charges quite rapidly.

All in all, I remain a big fan of the SanDisk MP3, and I will continue to buy them, even though they only last about two years before they burn out.

This charger and docking port with speakers is specifically intended for an iPod or iPhone. You can use this Bose SoundDock to listen to music on high quality Bose speakers while recharging those devices. This Bose system is attractively streamlined and modern in design, and it would look well with almost any decor. Volume control is achieved by touch rather than a dial, which is a nice feature.

This product can also be used for an MP3 player or attached to a Kindle.

If you respect the Bose name and can afford an expensive "Cadillac" product among an array of many different, small, external speakers on the market, you might enjoy this product.

This is a high-quality, four-port USB 3.0 hub. It works at the same speed as if I were plugging a device directly into my laptop or desktop computer. It has a 12-inch cable, which is quite handy. It has an extremely attractive, sleek design, and when it is on, a blue strip lights up.

In my opinion, this product works better than any USB hub I've ever owned, and I highly recommend is as a terrific gift idea for friends, family or coworkers.

Disclosure: Due to my being an Amazon Top Reviewer, I was approached by the manufacturer with a request to try out this product in order to, at my discretion, write a review.

I bought this monitor to use for a standing desk, and the key feature I was looking for that this monitor has--which most apparently do not--is the ability of this monitor's screen to tilt backwards. For me, this is essential to avoid neck strain as well as the picture distortion I experienced when I was using a vertical monitor placement.

The quality of the picture and overall screen resolution for this monitor is excellent. There is slightly more glare than I prefer, but not enough to be truly uncomfortable to my eyes.

The design of the monitor is extremely attractive. It has a very sleek, modern look, and the frame around the monitor looks like a good-quality picture frame. I had no trouble assembling this monitor, even though I am not particularly handy, because all I needed to do was snap on the base of the stand.

The monitor comes with a power cable and a VGA cable. They are of standard specifications and would fit most any monitor. Conversely, most standard cables will fit on this monitor, as well. In fact, I didn't bother removing the cables that I had used for my old monitor when hooking up this new monitor to my computer, since they worked just fine. I stored the the new cables in the event they old cables break at some point.

All in all, I am very satisfied with my purchase.

Update 12/10/13: I just spent 30 minutes on the phone with ASUS support regarding some issues with the monitor which, interestingly, I ultimately figured out myself. The monitor's resolution had suddenly gone wildly out of whack, and there were dancing pixels all over the screen. The support technician was very friendly, and extremely helpful, but he went through a whole bunch of settings suggestions without ever thinking of asking about the cables. It turns out the VGA cable had come loose. (This kind of reminds me of long ago, in the early days of television, when you could call a TV repairman to your house. The first thing he would invariably do was to check and see if the TV was plugged in.)

I purchased this tiny mic to use with my [[ASIN:B00966PFHW Philips DVT1000 Digital Recorder]]. Since they are both made by Philips, I assumed that they would be compatible, and my assumption proved correct. Using the two together, I am able to do convenient, hands-free recording, which was my goal. The sound quality with this tiny mic is terrific, just as good as using the digital recorder's own built-in mic.

I purchased both of these devices to use with my [[ASIN:B008NP76H4 Dragon NaturallySpeaking Premium 12]] software. I knew the DVT1000 was compatible because the makers of Dragon put it at the top of their list of compatible devices on their website, but I was a little nervous about this mic. Fortunately, but all my concerns were laid to rest the first time I used it to make a recording and transcribed it with Dragon. The accuracy was identical to that of the DVT1000 using its internal mic.

I am 100% delighted with this purchase.

I primarily got these CD's for data backup, but they work very well for recording music, as well. You just have to create a data CD instead of an audio CD by changing the default format.

These CD's have a lot of storage room. The CD's are also clearly distinguishable as to which is the front and which is the back, and there is plenty of space to label the CD on the front.

An extra bonus is a slim-line jewel case to hold the CD's that is of good quality.

I got this recorder for one purpose only, because it is at the top of the list of compatible recorders for Dragon NaturallySpeaking. It works extremely well for that purpose.

Besides that, I like these features in general:

--It is small and light, using two AAA batteries.
--The unit comes with a USB cable and batteries, which are (rationally enough) not pre-installed in the device (to avoid potential damage from battery-acid leakage).
--When I listen to recordings I have made, rather than simply using them for Dragon voice-recognition transcription, the sound quality of the recording is exceptional.
--The unit has an LED display, which makes reading the very small screen much easier.
--There is an alarm feature, which I don't personally need, but others might.
--Much like a camera, this device has a date and time feature that you set, and it is used to date stamp all recording files.
--There are advanced features that some may want to use, which I do not, including voice-activated recording, timer-based recording, and an indexing feature to "bookmark" particular spots in a given recording.
--This device can be connected via USB cable to a laptop or desktop, and thereby move, copy, delete, or save files. These files can be emailed or transferred to other computers.
--The device itself has, internally, 2GB storage. If you want more than that, it can hold a 32GB microSD card to expand storage. This card has to be purchased separately and formatted to the unit.
--You can program the unit to automatically stop recording at either 5 minutes or 15 minutes when nothing is recording.
--You can lock the keypad.
--This recorder is useful for recording meetings or lectures, and there are specific settings for various needs, including: speech-to-text, dictation, lecture and conversation.
--There is a one-year limited warranty.

I have a few small complaints:
--I had to download a manual online on the Philips website.
--There are four preset folders, A, B, C, D, that the device automatically records in, using one folder per session. You cannot create additional folders of your own. I have to make a point to move files off the recorder after I have run them through Dragon and transcribed them so the recorder's folders don't get cluttered.
--The USB cable is very, very short. When I use it, I have to hook it to an adjunct cable to extend the length.

I tried out two of these speakers, one in red and one in black. It has a lot of excellent features and functions:

*The red color is gorgeous, very bright and clear, and the black is deep and rich.
*The speaker can expand or contract, with a nice accordion feature. It needs to be open when you are using it, and you close it to pack it up to carry it around.
*It is rechargeable, so you don't have to worry about changing batteries. It takes only a couple of hours to charge and lasts up to 12 hours of play time.
*If you have more than one, you can hook them together and create a tiny, stereo system.
*It can hook up to your iPhone, PC, laptop, MP3 player and tablets--essentially anything that allows you to plug in earbuds.
*The sound quality is excellent for such a small speaker.
*There is a black, unpadded, cloth, drawstring bag to carry the speaker in.
*There is a audio/charging cable, and you can charge the speaker with a USB AC wall adapter or your PC.
*When the speaker is charging, the LED light on its bottom will glow red. When it is completely charged, it will glow blue.
*There is an on/off switch, an audio/charging input port, an audio-input jack, and a volume-control dial. Note that you have to turn on the volume both on the speaker and on the audio source you have it hooked to.
*This tiny speaker weighs less than 3 ounces.

I've personally used this speaker hooked up to my iPhone to listen to music through [[ASIN:B005V1N71W Pandora]], and to my [[ASIN:B002MAPSC6 MP3 player]] to listen to audiobooks. It works extremely well, and I'm delighted with it. My husband tested out this speaker, too, primarily with his iPhone, and he loves it as well. The sound quality is good, not tinny, but quite resonate, and I am able to turn the volume up high enough that I have to remember to turn it down late at night so as to not disturb my neighbors.

I have only two minor complaints: (1) The instructions provided are in such tiny print, I needed a magnifying glass to read them. (2) When I hook the speaker to my iPhone, its cable is so short, the speaker has to be unhooked before I can use the iPhone for any other purpose than to play an audio app. If the speaker's cable were were even six inches longer, that wouldn't be necessary and I could multitask on my iPhone a lot more efficiently while it is attached to this speaker.

Disclaimer: I was offered a sample of this product so that I could try it out in order to be able to write a review.

I owned a 1GB Sansa Clip for about three years before the clip fell off, but I kept using it anyway, even though a huge convenience was gone, because it is so light to carry around. Recently, though, as it reached six years of age, it started being unreliable when playing it, so I finally gave in and bought a new one. This time around I ordered the 4GB model. I really wanted to get the dark pink color again, but it wasn't offered here on Amazon, so I got the purple color called "indigo." It is much darker than the picture. It looks almost black, and the back side of the device actually is black. However, it is an attractive color.

This updated version has a lot more features than my old Sansa Clip. I probably will never use every feature it offers, but I am extremely happy to have quadrupled my storage space, and the sound quality is much better.

The on/off switch is on the top right, instead of the left side, and where the on/off switch used to be on my old Sansa Clip, on the left side, is where the volume switch is on this model. Until I figured that out, I had accidentally muted the device.

I am hoping to figure out soon how to download WMA audiobook files from my local library onto this device. One of the prime uses I have for an MP3 player like this one is listening to audiobooks when exercising or doing chores around the house.

So far, I am really happy with this new version of a beloved device.

We have several different brands of earbuds around the house, and these are the ones my husband and I like the best. They come in a large variety of colors, the cushioning at the tips is very comfortable in the ears, the sound quality is great, and the price is excellent.

The next time we have to purchase earbuds, we will be buying this brand again.

I've used the Sonet equipment for white noise to sleep at night for about 12 years. My first set lasted 10 years, and I've had my second set for two years now. It only has one type of noise, a kind of static. It does a great job of masking highway noise, the TV in the next room, and even the neighbor's loud lawn mower and leaf blower.

There are many ways one could review this product. I am choosing to give an example of how my family used it. It is a great, functional cable with many other possible uses as well.

After an attempt to use [[ASIN:B005INJ4ZG My Zone Wireless Headphones]] was a bust for me due to its terrible sound quality, my techie husband bought this cable for me as part of a setup that allows me to listen to TV as loud as I want without disturbing him or the neighbors.

I directly hook up this [[ASIN:B000KIPT30 amp]] to a head phone or earbuds when I am sitting close to the TV by using a special [[ASIN:B00009UVPN adapter]]. Head phones and earbuds have a 1/8 inch (3.5 mm) male jack (AKA male connector). Without an adapter, they can't be inserted into this amp, whose plug (AKA socket, female jack, or female connector) measures 1/4 inch (6.35 mm).

Because I like to move around my living room when I am watching TV, my husband also bought me a special [[ASIN:B0010CX798 male-to-female, headphone adapter, extension cable]]. The 1/4-inch, male jack of this cable fits into the 1/4-inch plug of this amp, and it has a 1/8-inch plug on its other end into which the jack of a head phone or ear bud can fit.

In order to use this setup, my husband also hooked into the amp this particular male-to-male extension cable. As you can see, one end is 1/8-inch and the other is 1/4-inch in diameter. The smaller end fits into a plug on the TV. When I want to use this external speaker source, I use the TV remote to access a menu that allows me to do that. Once this system is hooked up, I can no longer adjust the sound volume on the TV itself. I use the volume control on this amp.

Note that there is no On/Off switch on the particular amp we used. If you want to turn it off, so that you are not wasting electricity when it is not in use, you unhook the power cord from the far-left side of the amp.

This setup is a little complicated for the non-techie to figure out on their own, but if you have anyone techie in your family who can do it for you, it works really well.
