SanDisk has come out with an extension to their array of MP3 players, beyond the Clip and the View. Their new mp3 player, the Sansa Fuze, is definitely geared towards casual someone who just wants a basic, functional, and well-put together media device for their pocket.

The Sansa Fuze may look like a tiny device at first, but this thing packs some serious features. It has the ability to playback music, video, photos, FM radio, as well as audiobooks. The features for the Sansa Fuze are very impressive to say the least, as it also features a microSD card slot to add extra storage space, content, etc.

The first feature we will focus on is the one which will likely get the most use, the audio aspect. The music menu is organized with artist, album, song, genre, etc. There is also a recently added section which shows the most recent songs added onto the device, as well as a top rated section.

The album menu allows you to see album icons as you are scrolling through the various albums. There is also the ability to form a playlist directly on the player.

The sound quality is very well-done. If you have a great set of headphones you will not be disappointed in the least bit.

The video aspect is definitely not the highlight of the Sansa Fuze. Part of this is due to the low power of the device, and partly due to the screen itself. The supplied Sansa Media Converter does make it easy to convert movies into a format for the device though. A typical movie will take up a little under, or over 1GB. The video looks respectable, but can get a bit choppy at times. One very cool feature about the video is the ability to add a bookmark while watching it.

The photo viewer is very standard as you can view photos from the internal memory of a microSD card. You can set up a slide show with time intervals, and add music as well. The images looked quite sharp.

The FM radio feature is done extremely well on the Sansa Fuze. You get some great reception and the auto program feature picks out crystal clear radio stations. It also has the ability to record radio in WAV format.

This works with voice recording as well thanks to a microphone located right below the microSD slot.

Podcasts and audiobooks are pretty self-explanatory, but one issue with the audiobooks is the lack of a bookmark feature.

The overall user interface for the Sansa Fuze is put together nicely, set up in such a way that a first-time user could pick up this device and feel right at home with it. You have a scroll wheel as well as a home button and a middle click wheel. The scroll wheel can also be clicked up and down, which can make things a bit confusing at times. Overall though, beyond a few hiccups with organizational aspects of the UI, this is one easy device to use.

Getting media onto the Sansa Fuze is extremely simple as you can use any desktop media player to create playlists and such, easily syncing them to the device. It also supports drag and drop without the need for any software. We used Windows Media Player as well as a few other media players to test this all out, and syncing was as simple as can be.

The quality of the device itself is top-notch, as the screen can put out some great contrast and vibrant colors in spots. The screen is extremely clear and does a nice job with photo presentations. Battery life is equally as impressive, as I have been getting around 20 hours on each battery charge thus far. Video playback came in at around 6 hours on a charge.

The package comes with a proprietary USB cable and a pair of earbuds, pretty basic.

Also shipping with the Sansa Fuze is a great bonus, a microSD card which comes with DRM-free music from more than 50 new and emerging artists. This is a great way to immediately test out the music capabilities of the Sansa Fuze, and also adds value to the entire package. Music videos, images, and more are also included on the microSD card.

Overall SanDisk has done a great job with the Sansa Fuze.

As befits its price tag, the Sony has the look of a budget receiver with its old-school silver chassis. Build quality is decent enough: the fascia has a mixture of polished buttons and knobs including an input selector and volume control. The unit's remote control will be familiar to some - it features styling similar to the remotes that come with Sony's W Series of LCD TVs.

Before we get stuck into how the SRT-DG820 sounds, it's worth noting that Sony went back to the drawing board for its whole 2008 receiver range. And the Japanese giant has introduced various new features that, it claims, help improve performance.

For starters, the chassis of the STR-DG820 has been strengthened and embossed in certain places to help control any nuisance vibrations and minimize their effect on the key video/audio components found at the rear of the receiver.

High-definition audio decoding

Sony has even used custom-made brackets to secure the front panel and chassis and improve rigidity. The key video circuitry has been positioned as close as possible to the receiver's HDMI inputs for a shorter signal path and minimal interference.

The STR-DG820 offers 7.1 channels of surround sound (100w per channel) and can decode all major high-definition audio formats, including Dolby Digital TrueHD and DTS-HD Master Audio.

An inquisitive look around the rear of the receiver reveals a good selection of sockets. These include four HDMI inputs, (including a dedicated Blu-ray input), one HDMI output and three sets of component video inputs. The receiver also includes one coaxial and three optical digital inputs.

However, there is one notable omission: multichannel analogue inputs. So, your player has to be able to stream the HD data through HDMI for everything to work properly. In addition - not that you'd really expect them at this price - there are no pre-outs.

At this point it's also worth pointing out that the STR-DG820 can't upscale (Sony's step-up 'ES' range can upscale to 1080p), nor can it upconvert (again, the 'ES' range can). These features aren't vital, but upconversion would have been a welcome addition.

Sky HD usability issues

It also has to be noted that early versions of this receiver have had compatibility issues with Sky HD, which does not carry surround sound via its HDMI connection.

When you hook the Sky HD box's HDMI feed into the Sony and the Sky HD surround sound in via an optical input, the receiver over-rides the optical so you only hear the stereo feed supplied via HDMI.

Sony is working on a fix that will be applied to all existing and future STR-DG820 models. In the meantime, you can get round the issue by connecting your Sky HD via HDMI directly to your TV or projector, and via optical through the receiver - in this way you'll get both HD pictures and full surround sound.

Silky sound, dynamic dialogue

But back to the receiver in action. Set-up is done through Sony's Digital Cinema Auto Calibration system. It's ridiculously quick, easy to use and accurate - the receiver takes just a few seconds to set up.

And, hooked up to a Blu-ray player such as the Panasonic DMP-BD30, the Sony sounds sensational. Fed the Dolby TrueHD soundtrack from Batman Begins, the STR-DG820 impresses with its solid, controlled sound.

When Batman's Tumbler causes havoc on the streets of Gotham City, the Sony delivers explosions with a fine sense of immediacy and impact. Bass notes don't wallow or linger. In fact, you soon forget you're listening to a `budget' receiver.

The Sony is a dab hand at dialogue, too. Voices sound full-bodied and boast exceptional clarity, even during the most boisterous action scenes. There's no trace of brashness or harshness in the sound that could prove tiresome over prolonged listening.

Sure, more expensive receivers can give you a greater spread of sound and greater scale but, for this sort of money, the STR-DG820 is an absolute star.

It's equally adept at music

Dare we say it, the Sony also sounds adept when it comes to CD playback. Press the Analog Direct button to turn off all unnecessary internal processing and the receiver's clear, composed sound once again comes to the fore.

It exhibits a fine sense of rhythm for an AV receiver and dishes out decent bass weight during Eminem's Without Me.

This thing is great for what it is. Has a bright screen, decent sound for hilu or Netflix and good battery life. Cheap enough to not worry about theft or the kids destroying it. It is not a business laptop but great for email,  web browsing or watching movies in the hotel room. The pic shows the chromebook on the left compared to my windows computer in my "home office".

We bought this topper for our 7.5 foot tree and have 9 foot ceilings. The projection is quiet and we love the moving snowflakes. The light is bright and doesn’t get hot. It’s not too heavy but also not too light that it would fall over. The base is very sturdy and will easily sit wherever you place it. The chord had plenty of length to be plugged in and has some extra length for a larger tree.

I adore this little mouse! I never knew how irritating the sound of a mouse click was until I bought this noiseless one. It's fantastic! The soft silicone feel keeps your hands comfortable for long use, and the slot to store the USB plug when the mouse is not in use is very convenient and is behind a cover to prevent it from falling out. This was the cheapest wireless mouse I found (broke college kid struggles) and I was very impressed by the overall feel and performance of it. I use it with my MacBook pro. I have to use an adapter for the USB port, but most people woth macs have an adapter already, so it's no hassle!!!

Wow! Worked so well with our 9 year old car that came with no bluetooth capabilities. Once we found an FM frequency that was not in use on the radio, the sound quality got sooo amazing.
Our 12 day roadtrip now will have a background score that we like!

My wife bought it for me 2 weeks ago. I have been using it regularly. The seller must know what it is....it is not a high-power adapter.... just for medium power like laptop, mobile, etc... It is very compact but has enough ports (1 power socket, old three usb hub, and one usb C) for your laptop, cell phones, tablets, power backup.  This charger is particularly useful for me when I travel back home. It is small, light and easy to carry around.... and thus does its purpose. The sliding button that pops out the socket plug is a great design serving the compactness issue, and also smartly labelled. It would have been the best product if would support high powered equipment like heater but for the given price its a reasonable product.

I've had these for about a month now and they work great. They connect to Bluetooth and device fast. The battery life is great. People have trouble hearing me if there is noise is the background which is a bummer but I don't plan to use this much for the microphone

Works great, fits in my Amazonbasics charger and lasts so much longer than the disposable AAA batteries at got at the dollar store. I have a smart door knob that requires AAA batteries and I kept having to change the batteries every month. These have been in for a week and it is still almost fully charged. Also happy that these are more environmentally friendly. Overall, highly recommended.

These buds were very easy to set up, connected easily, has simple controls, and has a great battery life and sound quality. The only flaw I can say it has it that it charges with a micro usb charger that is included. For a 2020 product, I would expect it to charge with a C charger by now, meaning you will have an extra charger to carry with you if you plan on traveling with these. comes with different sized bud pieces to fit your ears. They aren't completely sound isolating. It is enough sound going through for you to keep aware of your surroundings. Overall, a great starter bud set for teenagers or college students that enjoy listening to music or need then to listen to lectures while doing schooling from home. Overall, highly recommended.

The sounds quality of this is very good. Charges with a USB-C cable. Comfortable to wear for long periods of time case charges the earbuds every time you put them in. Controls are easy to use with simply pressing the sides of the buds. Noise cancelling but you can adjust how much sound passes through for you to stay aware. Overall, highly recommended.

These earbuds connect very easily to bluetooth and are very comfortable with the design. Not too heavy, and weighted enough so you know they are in your ears. The controls are very easy as well. The only problem I found with these earbuds is that it uses a micro use charger instead of a usb-c charger. It is inconvenient to have to pack another extra cable with you when traveling. Overall, the sounds quality is great and they did a great job with the design. Overall, I'd recommend them if you do not mind carrying an extra cord with you when traveling.

I have another set of earbuds but they are a bit heavy and I have trouble with them slipping while working out. I also got a few true wireless buds but I don't trust myself not to lose one while working out. I actually really liked these buds. The wire is adjustable, as well as it being much lighter so it doesn't slip as much, especially if you choose to only have one bud in at times. The volume control is easy to use as well, and it is easy to pause and skip tracks when needed. I have smaller ears and the wings did a good job with staying in place. Charges with a USB and was a breeze to connect with bluetooth. I found myself only having to charge them once a week after using them every day. Overall, great product. Would highly recommend these for anyone needing buds for the gym or runners.

My dad needed a new radio since his old one is crackling very badly after years of use. this one is small, and easy to use. the vocals are very clear and crisp without that annoying buzzing or static noises on most channels. The buttons are easy to press, and the overall design is easy to understand and adjust. Overall, it is a great product. Highly recommended.

First off, I think this headset is pretty good. I'm a female gamer, and I would say this set is kinda heavy compared to my older Razer set I've used for about a year. These are glasses friendly. I would say the tension of the ear cuffs is a good fit. I do wish that the set was a bit shorter. I am on the shortest length currently and it still feels a bit long. The feature I really like is that you can amplify and adjust your voice level. I am able to speak normally and still give loud clear instructions over Discord. Pairs easily, I didn't even need to go into my settings. The only flaw I see is that the mic is kinda short. I wish it was half an inch or an inch longer. You mute and unmute yourself by moving your mic up or down. I honestly wished it was a button instead, but it isn't a deal breaker. The voice is very clear and crisp according to my friends on discord. I use this for my PC and it works great. Overall, highly recommended.

I would have absolutely loved these in college. They are compact and have a long battery life. Also charges easily with my regular C usb cable I use for my phone. Highly recommended! They don't make my ears itch or irritated, even after long periods of wear. It's great for work, especially if you want to block out background noise. Has several modes so you can choose what the noise filter lets through. I personally keep it on the setting that allows you to hear what a person is saying if they are right next to you but blocks out background noise. Overall, highly recommended!

I've gone through tons of ear buds from $10-$400. These are amazing! I've use them for a little over two weeks now, and the battery life is surprisingly super long. The sound quality is amazing. It provides close to total noise cancelation. They are super comfortable, and doesn't make my ears itchy and sweaty after prolonged use. It charges with a "C" charger which makes it super convenient to travel with. The only thing i wished this came with was a passes carrying case, but the pouch is okay too. Comes with several sized buds for customization, inckuding ear hooks. I have very weirdly shaped ears, that has very little groove, but these stayed in my ears with no problem. Highly recommended!

Work requires that you enter alot if sensitive information into the computer, so this is great. You have to stare directly at the screen to view the information. Especially helpful when dealing with massive amounts of guests and having to gather information such as social security numbers, passwords, ect. In a crowded area. It was super easy to install and clings on its own.

When I first opened the box, it was quite dusty, but after using some compressed air, it worked just fine. I love how easy it is to pair to devices. The sounds quality is great, and the backs of the ear pieces are magnetic so you can wear it like a necklace when not in use. This would be great for commuters or students. I would have loved these in college since you don't have to fiddle with your cord all the time. Overall, would make a great gift or even for yourself!

This is great for commuters and college students. It isn't noice canceling in the traditional sense, but allows some background Boise in so you can be aware of your surroundings. For example, you will be able to clearly able to hear people calling you right next to you, cars and trains approaching. In my opinion, these are the best kind since you get the sound quality you want from your music, bust still not compromise on safety, especially for those that may not be very aware of their surroundings. As with any cuffed headsets, your ears will get a bit sweaty on a hot day. This has a microphone for calls, and can be used wired or wireless. The battery life is surprisingly long, and it easily changes with a USB. Only thing I wish it came with was a carrying bag or case.

I got this for Black Friday because my previous speakers blew out. This is just amazing! The sound is crystal clear! When I first set it up, I was actually really startled by how loud it could get! This is perfect for outdoors since the projection is just so well designed. Easy to use and pair with all your devices, and stays clean compared to other devices.

We used this in our pop-up camper for 3 nights without charging it and it was a life saver! The neighbors were loud till all hours but this fan was just enough noise to cancel out their party and keep us cool. I won’t go camping without it now!

I really love our new TV, easy and quick set up...(I did it all by myself when the husband was out of town)...awesome picture and sound...only complaint is the remote control has no lights at all (the buttons do not light up) so it poses a frustrating situation when trying to channel surf or whatnot when the husband is sleeping. Tilting the remote hoping the light from the TV will illuminate the buttons enough for me to see - it doesn't BTW)
Who'd know this was such an irritation? But it is Lol!
Is there another remote you could send? Otherwise very very happy with our purchase

With the restrictions on luggage for both weight and volume a monocular is a much more practical choice than binoculars for use while traveling. This is an excellent monocular, very powerful and easy to use.  The eye piece can easily be adjusted for those who wear glasses.  The viewing field is large, and clear from side to side.  This is an excellent choice for bird watching, or to take on vacation.

Even though I have always had an interest in astronomy I was never able to work a course in this subject in my college schedule or afterwards. When I saw this telescope offered I realized that now I had both the time and the means to explore my interest a bit further. I had very little difficulty setting the scope up, and spent some time familiarizing myself with the various components. I practiced using this by checking out objects in my neighborhood, and managed to get an 'up close and personal' view of some birds in a neighbor's yard and quickly realized that this scope was powerful.

That evening I took the scope to an upstairs window to see what I could see, and despite the pesky street light was able to get a great view of the full moon (btw did you know that it sparkles a bit?). I saw details that I had only seen in photos before which was fascinating. Then I decided to take a look at Mars, which was near the Moon that evening. That is when things got complicated. The finder scope and the main scope need to be synced, and I don't know how to do this (yet). With some fiddling, and aided by Mars' close proximity to the Moon I was able to find Mars, which was exciting but for some reason it was distorted (it had a starburst appearance). My husband and I fiddled with various lenses and combinations to try to eliminate this but were unsuccessful. The experimentation was further complicated by the touchiness of the stand....it was difficult to make small, smooth adjustments and to keep the scope locked in position. Some of this is no doubt due to our in expertise, some I think is due to the equipment.

My enjoyment of this scope would have been much greater if more instructions had been provided. We discovered, more or less by accident how to lock, at least partially, the scope into place. We managed to make some focusing adjustments by trial and error. Even some rudimentary instructions in a small booklet or even a sheet or two describing how to adjust, focus and lock the scope as well as an illustration of the scope with all the components clearly labeled with a brief description of their function would have been greatly appreciated. This is a basic instrument, one that will primarily be used by beginners or novices who will not necessarily be familiar with this equipment. Basic instructions should have been included. As it is my unfamiliarity with the various aspects of the telescope make following many of the instructions I do find on-line difficult to follow.

Despite this problems I am enjoying my new toy. I found the stand to be steady, and the tray located on the stand to be a handy place to put lenses and covers. As I mentioned earlier this is a surprisingly (at least to this beginning user) powerful scope. I'm going to play around with this some more, and will probably upgrade some of the lenses and add some accessories based on my experiences. Besides star gazing I think this will be a great item to watch birds or wild life, and it is certainly portable and forgiving enough to take on a camping trip.

This is a good power strip with a surge protector. It also has the capacity to be synced with Alexa (after down loading an app). It sounds like a great idea but, as others have mentioned, it is an all or nothing situation. Alexa can turn the entire strip on or off but cannot control the individual outlets. Even so it would be convenient to have one or more lights in a room on when coming home after dark or even to be able to power down lights or other items that might have been left on inadvertently.

This power strip would be a useful item, particularly for a dorm room or any other place where things might be unintentionally left on.

This is a very well made sleeve. It has plenty of room for my 13 inch Mac Book, and my Kindle in the outer pocket with room left over for the requisite cords and a power adapter.The zippers are sturdy, the main compartment is lined with soft, felt-like material and is lightly padded. The outside pocket is lined with a slick material, and only padded on the inner side.

This is sturdy enough to stand up to a daily commute either in a brief case or back pack, light enough to easily fit into a suitcase, even the outside pocket of a carryon.
This is a very nice system.  It set up easily and is simple to operate.  The sound is OK for a small area, like a bedroom or dorm but not for a larger space.

This is advertised as a 'sleeve for a 13" laptop' which is such an understatement. Not only will this hold a laptop up to 14 inches, it also has compartments for a cell phone, an IPad or other tablet device (my Kindle fits in there quite nicely) and all the necessary chargers and earphones, making this a one stop transportation and storage device for all personal electronics. There is even a bit of room left over to tuck a newspaper, or a file or two. And, unlike most sleeves, this has handles and an optional shoulder strap.

The compartments are zippered so things should not spill out too easily (although I would open the compartment holding the chargers cautiously). It is a nice, neutral grey color that should not make anyone feel self conscious about carrying it and seems to be reasonably durable. The various compartments seem to be adequately padded against the normal traumas (I don't think I would count on it to protect my computer if it were dropped).

There are a few issues though. First since it is not a typical sleeve it probably would not easily fit into a backpack. Second, fully loaded with a computer, phone, tablet and chargers it will be heavy enough that handling this plus a backpack or briefcase during a commute could be awkward. Third, having everything in one spot could be convenient for travelers except dragging everything out to go through TSA and then repacking it would be time consuming.

Overall this is a great product.

This is my kind of electronic product. It does exactly what it is supposed to do - recharge my iPod and allow me to listen without earphones - without requiring me to spend hours learning how to use it. I had it up and running in minutes. The controls are easy to understand and use. The speakers are of good quality.

In short this is an excellent product.

I was pleasantly surprised at how easy it was to set this up, it was simply a matter of attaching the base, connecting a few wires and plugging it in. The set scanned the cable system while I inserted the batteries into the remote, we finished about the same time and I was ready to start watching TV. The hardest part of the whole thing was getting the heavy monster it replaced out of the way.

The picture is quite clear, the color and sound are both good. The DVD works well (for the most part), the controls on the remote are fairly intuitive. I had been a bit concerned about the size of the set, the one it replaced was just slightly larger but even so I can still see the set quite clearly from across the room (about 20 feet). So far the only problem I have had has been that it hung up on the DVD one time. I could not get the set to return to the regular viewing mode even after removing the DVD, and turning the set off, then back on etc. The problem was solved by unplugging both the set and the cable box and restarting everything. The problem has not recurred so I am hoping for the best.

I am quite happy with this product and am would not hesitate to recommend it.

I had been looking at various GPS units for some time for my wonderful, but directionally challenged husband but was put off by the price and the monthly fees required by some. When I found this unit was offered by a local department store at a deeply discounted price I decided to check it out. I was very pleased because:

1. There is no monthly fee involved.

2. The screen is large enough to read.

3. The unit gives directions as you go along, both written and verbal, including updates 'in one mile turn....in 1/2 mile....in 500 ft etc'

4. When a turn has been missed the route is recalibrated, first prompting the driver to correct the error then ultimately selecting an alternate route.

5. There is a wealth of information, besides route ETA, speed (with the option to set a warning), altitude, local points of interest including restaurants, gas stations, etc.

We took this along on several trips since getting this, one of several hundred miles, others a bit closer, and were quite pleased for the most part. For the most part this was like having Mapquest in the car with you. It had some of the same problems as Mapquest (addresses might be slightly different, recent changes to route not noted etc) but had the advantage of being able to recalculate the route if you for any reason deviated from the plan, like to stop at a restaurant. There were a few minor problems some were caused by our reluctance to really read the manual, preferring to just push buttons and figure it out, others are inherent to this product.

First the on/off switch is in the back and must be operated with a pen/bent paperclip. Once started it did take a long time to locate the satellite and load. Another issue is that, like mapquest, local names are not always used and addresses may not appear exactly like they are used. In addition we discovered that a very small (pop 300) town we were looking for was not available on this unit. Most of these problems were minor inconveniences.

I highly recommend this product particularly for those who have not had a GPS before. It is quite user friendly and forgiving of operator error.

My teenage daughter listens to podcasts and a lot of music on these headphones. She feels that the sound quality is very good. She has petite ears and the buds fit her well and do not fall out. The pink is fun and makes it easy to tell them apart from those of other people. The noise cancellation is pretty good, as she often needs a visual cue to respond to a person's attempt to communicate.
This speaker is quite small but puts out a decent quality sound unless you try to get really loud. At the greatest volume, it gets a bit tinny. Easy to use and very lightweight and portable.
Easy to use, works when wet. This speaker is compact but has a decent sound quality.
These head phones are cute and comfortable. The sound quality is good.

These buttons were very easy to record a brief request on, but getting my dog to use them is something I am still working on. Dogs are color blind, so I don't know if he can ever differentiate one button from another. My tactic is to expose him to just one button at a time, and maybe keep them in different locations. Suggestions for recording:
Can I have a treat?
I need to go out.
My bowl is empty.
Can we go to the dog park?
These headphones took very little time to set up according to the directions included. The sound quality is very good. The headset is lightweight and comfortable.

This bag is lightweight and compact. The padding is not terribly thick, but it is adequate. It fits a laptop or large tablet but not much else. The bee themed print is fun but not too cutesy, it is totally appropriate for an adult.

I like the pink color that makes these earbuds instantly recognizable. Most similar earbuds are white and can easily get mixed up with those belonging to other people. The sound quality is pretty good. One ear occasionally cuts out for some reason, but once jiggled goes right back to working fine. These are a good deal for the cost.
So far, so good. The sound quality is fine and these are comfortable to wear. A nice product for the price.

These earbuds look similar to the crazy expensive ones. They seem to work just as well too! Sound quality is very good and they actually stay in her ears comfortably, which can be an issue for a smallish user.

These earbuds are comfortable, which is not always the case for a smaller teen/adult like my daughter. They stay in and do not fall out constantly. The plain white design does not scream "third party knockoff" either. Sound quality was a pleasant surprise. It is actually pretty good, though not the best we have ever heard. The charge seems to last a long time, which is very convenient.

This computer's graphics card, processor, and SSD harddrive dramatically improved performance for my die-hard gamer. He is extremely happy with this machine. The clarity and detail of images is top-notch. There is no lag time with changing screens. This is an exceptional computer for gaming and visual-oriented work.
I love the robin's egg blue color of these earbuds! They are distinctive and will not easily be mixed up with other people's headphones. The sound quality is very good.

This camera bag is roomy and has TONS od pockets for storing accessories. There is a spot for one or two camera bodies, plus two slots for lenses. There are four tiny flap pockets for memory cards. A quick perusal shows me 19 separate storage places: pockets, zipper compartments, pen holders, etc. Plus, this bag has an attached rain shield like my high-end backpack! That is a nice touch. The bag can be carried in different ways with the handles and straps provided. It can be worn at the waist like a fanny pack, carried in hand like a lunch bag, or slung over the shoulder with nice wide adjustable webbing.
This is a good sized catchall for camera equipment. It is perhaps not enough for a professional photographer, but has ample space for most people.

Targus is a top name in computer bags for technicians. They have not disappointed with this gaming backpack. The bag is generously sized and can accommodate a larger screen laptop for gaming. There is ample padding: both for protection of the equipment and for comfort of the wearer. The exterior has two detachable pouches that are secured with heavy strips of velcro interlaced with seatbelt webbing. The pouches are about 10" x 5" and 10" x 10"; each has an exterior zipper pocket as well as the main compartment. The inside of the bag is loaded with different compartments to keep all your gaming accessories organized. It even unzips on three sides to open like a book.
This bag is for people who don't want to just throw all their stuff into one of those "black hole" design bags where things get tangled and crushed. It even has a pull-over rainshield that will protect your bag from the elements.
Please do not purchase this bag for young children. This is a BIG bag that is nearly 22" long and it has some weight to it. It is specialized for teen or adult gamers who want to protect their devices and peripherals when they travel. Top marks!

I gave these bluetooth earbuds to my young teen and she was able to set them up in about a minute without any help. They are comfortable but tend to fall out- I think many people with smaller ears can relate to this problem. They are made for men and even in pink are bigger than desirable for a girl. The sound quality is very good.

Let me begin by saying I am not a heavy headphone user. I like to wear them on occasion when I am doing a task that is rather mundane and doesn't require a lot of movement. I am not an audio snob and big names do not impress me. I want good quality sound and comfort. These headphones are perfect for me. They are not too heavy and they actually seem to fit and stay on! I am a smallish adult and some sound systems - especially earbuds- just don't fit. I don't want to feel lost in an overly heavy and large set of headphones, either. I am quite happy with these plantronics.

Great graphics! This computer runs fast and is terrific for playing games. The screen is a good size but consequently this laptop is a bit heavy. It tends to heat up, so I recommend that a fan be purchased to accompany it. The sound quality is excellent. Sound effects are very clear and less "tinny" than on our non-gaming laptops. The blue lights on the keyboard are fun too. My family has not had a Dell before, and we are pleased with the performance of this model.

Easy to set up, very good quality sound. This was instantly apparent after changing from a Tap to Sonos. The sound is richer and louder. One drawback is that it is not bluetooth enabled. Voice control works as expected.
This works great and it allows us to move our dot from room to room freely. The one drawback is that it announces in a loud voice when the battery is running low- even if it is 3 am. :)

I LOVE this microscope! It is easy to work with and sets up in about five minutes. My homeschool science group used it recently.  Seven students were all looking at the screen and could see the same image at the same time. The dials for focusing are very sensitive, so should be turned  gradually for best results. This instrument is extremely lightweight! The plastic may not last as long as the heavy older types, but it is also far less expensive and is easier to transport.

Clear, crisp sound, quick set up for bluetooth. These headphones/earbuds are comfortable, but do not fit me as well as I would like. They seem to be made for someone with fairly large ears. They stay in place pretty well while I am stationary, but tend to fall off when I am in motion.

This bluetooth product was easy to set up. The two ear set makes a nice stereo sound, and the general sound quality is excellent. The curly wires make it a little different- sort of floppy, to wear. This works with a nice array of devices. Recommended!

This Sony system was easy to set up in minutes and the quality of the sound is quite good. The design of the bar is inconspicuous and blends in easily with any decor. The boxy sub woofer is a little bigger than I'd like, but I suppose it would add to the price to shrink it. The speaker that it replaced actually was MUCH larger- like 30" tall, so I really should not complain. I  feel Sony is a trustworthy brand. This is an excellent system for home use.

This laptop bag is well padded and of adequate size for any laptop. There is a separate compartment for documents or a tablet. The large zippers are fast opening and closing and don't seem to stick. The basic black design goes with everything. A great buy for the cost.

This is a nice little gadget that allows multiple users to listen to the same music or audiobook. My daughters have enjoyed sharing tunes with their friends. The sound quality is very good and it is very simple for a first time user to enjoy. The bright color makes the device easy to identify and difficult to lose.

The Samsung Galaxy camera is basically a cell phone on steroids. It takes gorgeous pictures, which are easily cropped, edited, and transformed into works of art with the photo wizard program. Sharing to email, facebook, instagram, or other platforms is incredibly easy. I am genuinely thrilled with this product. The screen on the back of the camera is about 2.5" x 4" and allows the user to see images clearly both before and after capturing a shot. The camera appears to have a tremendous amount of memory, as mine now holds hundreds and hundreds of images. One feature which I have not yet played with allows the user to sort photos based on time, location, or people. Aside from the great camera- the Galaxy is also a functional cell phone which allows the user to access social media and download apps. Videos are good quality in both picture and sound, and it took my 13 year old about 10 minutes to figure out how to upload them to YouTube. I would like to balance this review with a few negative comments, but I actually cannot think of any. Highly recommended!

The sound quality is quite good, and these buds seem to be made of slightly more durable stuff than some of the others I have used. I have given up on buying the cheapest earbuds, as they don't last at all, and one pair gave me a nasty shock. I am pleased with the Philips brand and will gladly recommend them.

The Bloggie is very much like the Flip Video Camera my family has had for a few years. I'd say that the video quality is the same or perhaps a bit better, and the sound significantly better. The downside is that compared to the Flip, this camera is harder to edit and download onto the internet. My 11 year old daughter can manage the Flip stuff herself, but needed help with the Bloggie. I don't think this is a major impediment though, as most reasonably technical adults should be able to work with the Bloggie with only a small investment in time.

All in all, the Bloggie is a good quality video camera for a very affordable price.

These speakers are very easy to set up and the cool little round control system allows you to turn them on/off and set the volume with a simple twist or tap. The sound quality is fantastic.  I am very pleased with these speakers and recommend them as a great gift for someone who wants to share audiobooks or music from their mp3 or ipod player.

I love the Jabra WAVE bluetooth headset.It's a bit unorthodox - it starts in your ear, curls back behind your ear, then extends down to the microphone. There were multiple earpieces available, and I was able to find one that fit comfortably. There's a cover for the mike that helps with ambient noise.

I was easily able to connect it to both my HTC Thunderbolt Smartphone and my Notebook. The headset can be linked to two devices simultaneously.

Battery life is excellent, I get around 4 hours of talk time on a full charge.

The call clarity of the headset is excellent, although I did experience some unexplained interference a couple times.

These earbuds come with three different sized soft cushioned bits, so users can find the size that suits them best. I am a small to medium sized woman and I prefer the smallest size, though the medium are also a decent fit.  They are quite comfortable and can be worn for a long time without discomfort.  The sound quality is pretty good, though not as good as some of the real (bulky) headphones I have used. The bright color is nice, too.

No tapes or camera cards needed- The Flip Video Mino has a pop-out USB that plugs right into your computer to download videos. I LOVE the ultra-portability of it, as I haven't taken videos in years due to my reluctance to cart around the cumbersome old cam I had. The mino is easy to use and the picture and sound quality are quite good. I haven't tried to use ti with a tripod yet, but it does have the necessary plumbing to receive one. My kids can use this without trouble, as it is incredibly light and all they have to do is push a button to record. My daughter did accidentally cover the lens with her fingers initially, but other than that, was using the camera well within seconds.

The black model is on sale now for about $130 and for an extra $20, you can choose a yellow smiley or other brightly colored Flip. There are many cases available, but we just use the soft pouch that came with our Flip and after a few months we don't have a single scratch.

This dvd player replaced an older and much more expensive model that finally bit the dust.  I was quite pleased to find that the price had dropped considerably since our last dvd player was purchased.  My kids use this player almost daily, and we have had no problems with operation, sound quality, etc.  The discs go in and they play just as they are supposed to!  We often use this model while people run on a treadmill nearby, and we still have no issues with skipping.  It's a heck of a bargain and very compact too.  I am quite pleased with this product.  I would give it five stars, but as we've only had it for a couple months, I award four stars for now.

But the other day, I decided to give it a try. Two bits of advice: if you can get through this without disconnecting the wifi connector (you can if you are really careful), do so, and (2) if you accidentally disconnect the wifi connector (I did), don't panic. Watch videos of people putting iPhones back together (the older, the better). These connectors are fussy. Do not force them. If they are seated correctly, a light press will connect them. You'll feel the click. But it's almost like threading a needle to get it seated correctly. And if you push too hard, you'll break it. Same with the fan. Just be careful. If you are pushing and it's not connecting right away, it's not lined up right.

Okay, so deciding to do the drive replacement took awhile because the above two steps seemed very daunting. And the project took me several hours, because I had to stop and rest a few times (if your hands work and you keep your screws organized, it should take about 45 minutes). But it was worth every minute.

I'm not paranoid (famous last words). No, really, I welcome my personal assistant overlords. My family is pretty vanilla. He can ignore my texts and refuse to answer the phone, but Alexa lets me yell at him from anywhere in the world. On the downside, Alexa won't give you suggestions if she doesn't know something. She just gives you an Elizabeth Jennings (The Americans) type, "Hmmm," and a disappointed note.

The Echo Plus also seems to "hear" better and have fewer false activations. And the sound is better for music - by a surprising amount. So, if Alexa has a place in your home, the Echo Plus is a good way to get her. Four stars. I'd give five if the wake word were more customizable.

I tested this in a USB 3 adapter on my MacBook Air. Why would I do that? What could possibly be the point?

Well, I couldn't persuade my son to pull his m.2 drive and test this one against it (haven't yet, anyway - next time he wants a favor bad enough to stop playing Dark Souls to as me for it, I will update with results).

Couldn't afford a thunderbolt adapter (what is up with that). So my question became whether USB 3 is fast enough for an m.2 drive to make a difference versus a SATA SSD.

And it is. The Nvme drive clocks in at 400-500 mbps over the SATA drive's 240 top speed. And the price of the drives plus their adapters is about equal per gigabyte.

My son has some fancy gaming headphones, so when I tried these and liked them, I asked for his opinion. He says they are not as comfortable as his, and the mic does not seem durable to him, but they sound decent. When he saw the price point (twenty smackeroos as of this writing), he opined that these are a fantastic bargain.

As the person who purchased the fancy headset (and two previous fancy versions that were eaten by kittens), I agree. If you have kittens, though, I suggest you go ahead and spring for a set with a braided cable.

I have old demo tapes from my husband's 1980s-1990s music projects. I need to bounce them to digital before they disintegrate. This walkman-type converter deck works better than I thought it might. So far, it plays true - no speeding up or slowing down - and hasn't eaten any tapes. I'm getting better results than I got the last time I tried this (I got a boombox I had to send back because it sounded terrible - line out was scratchy, speed was random). This is worth a try.

This did exactly what I needed to connect two different kinds of digital I/Os and dump 50 DAT tapes with musical performances on them onto my old Mac Mini (none of my more recent computers has digital audio input).

So old school that we don't spell it "skool." We still have CDs. We still play CDs. The main reason is that we like the sound quality. If that's the medium the music was mixed and mastered for, that's the medium you should listen to it on (according to my husband, the studio guy). This player does very well for itself in the sound department. Its internal speakers are just okay, but the sound you get from plugging in a decent set of external speakers is much better. It can play from an SD card and has several other convenience functions that make it a good value.

Use your smartphones and streaming platforms to find music you like. If it's older music, try to find it on CD or vinyl. One cool thing: Amazon includes digital access to pretty much any record you buy here. So, a lot of the CDs I've bought on Amazon, I can listen to on my phone or an echo or my computer any time I want.

It's a cable, right? How good can it be? For the very reasonable price? Excellent. The quality is excellent. Nothing flimsy. And it sounds great. I don't give five unless something exceeds my reasonable expectations, and this cable was way better than what I thought it would be.

I had a bad experience with my previous Annke security DVR. I could never get it set up with the online viewer, couldn't back it up, and eventually couldn't do a thing with it when the USB port stopped working (you need a mouse). The way I found out the port was no longer working was when I went to review footage of a creep on my porch. Couldn't do it.

So far, this one is lots better. It seems to have a better build quality, and, while set up was not easy, it was doable.

I'm really tired of stuff not working - especially security equipment that, at best, is just okay, and, at worst, does no good whatsoever. If this keeps working, I'll be thrilled.

I bought this extender at the same time that I bought an Orbi with one satellite. I figured that even if the Orbi did not work out, the EX7500 would be helpful with my then-current setup (four Apple wifi routers that could barely cover my home).

The jury is still out on the Orbi system, as I have had to reset it a couple of times already, and it does not play all that well with all of my smart devices. BUT the EX7500 is a trouper. I have not had to do one thing to this extender beyond plugging it in and setting it up once. Setup itself was easy and took under five minutes. Adding it to the Orbi network increased my speed in the farthest ranges of my house by a good 50-75 Mbps.

I've had other extenders that, for example, gave me duplicate IP address errors and/or constantly snatched my wifi connection. My Apple extenders let excluded MAC addresses onto my network unless I duplicated those settings for each extender. This one runs completely invisibly. It's probably the most troublefree extender I've ever owned. Seriously. It is wicked expensive, but it is the one piece of networking equipment I currently own, including my Apple setup and the Orbi, that I can definitely say that I am keeping.

This is an excellent modest-budget power supply. It's quiet. It comes with enough connectors. It's super reliable and delivers steady power. The ONE issue I've had with it comes from installing it in a full tower that has a lot of wire management: some of the power module cables are barely long enough. Just another inch or two would have made installation much easier.

Still recommend.

The Cloud Core is probably the best performing headset in this price class, at least that I have tested and used. Mic quality is excellent, even when used by a screaming teenaged boy in the throes of fight game frenzy.

The headphones are comfortable and noise isolating, and the cable (and extension) are long and cat-proof. That last one is important. In the 18 months she's been on the planet, The Sylph has eaten several headsets and three MacBook Air adapters. Happy with purchase and would buy again. Hopefully, won't have to.

I got these used at a really good price. They are quite good. I tested them on one of the frequency range videos available on various streaming services, and they register the entire range of human hearing. There's perhaps a bit of mud in a small part of the mid-range, but it is barely noticeable. Music sounds fantastic.

The mic works with no echo. Also, they come in a nice box.

The lifetime warranty on this doorbell is the real deal. This is a very well-supported doorbell.

I was having issues with holiday season package thieves and a non-working wireless doorbell. Ring is the only video doorbell I could find that will work wirelessly. The first one had battery issues. Replaced no problem. The second one had sound issues. Replaced no problem. The third on works FLAWLESSLY. I absolutely love it.

The smart motion sensor works well. I see everyone who comes onto my porch, but not my neighbors' porches (three doors lined up on one big house). Two way sound is mostly good -> if it's really windy, it's hard to hear sometimes. The video is way better than I thought it would be. I can see well enough on my phone, but if I download and watch on my computer, it is very impressive.

I signed up for the cloud recording - it's the least expensive pay service of any of my security cameras, and it has been reliable over the few weeks I have been using it. The doorbell is also conspicuous enough to act as a deterrent. I've had a couple of alerts where people looked like they were going to come up the steps and then changed their minds. Both my postal carrier and my UPS driver said that a lot of their stops have these, and they really like them.

Bottom line: It took a couple of tries, but I am one hundred percent happy with this doorbell. If you have an issue, use the warranty. It's a real thing.

UPDATE: I have a CHIME now, as well, and it also works beautifully. The Ring Company gave it to me for free as a promotion, because I had bought two of their doorbells.

This is a solid, tool-free SATA to USB 3.0 drive caddy.

The speed is excellent, and the build quality was surprisingly good in this price range. It handles 2.5 and 3.5 inch drives equally well, and it made an archiving project I am doing with many years' worth of hard drives from now defunct computers very easy.

If I could wish for one thing, it would be that the caddy would be made from something that disperses heat a little better, but the open construction means that heat build up is not really a problem anyway.

*Review of Free Sample*

Arlo is probably the easiest security camera system out there. You don't need to plug it in or run any wires. There's no complicated internet set up. The free cloud service supports five cameras, which you can add for quite a bit less than what you pay for the first one. Motion sensitivity is excellent and the push notifications are reliable.

There's no sound, no air quality monitoring, or any of the other fancier features of - say - Withings (my other favorite). But there is also no hassle.

This is a decent power conditioner - actually excellent for the price - and suitable for home theater systems like mine: a bargain brand tv, nice sound bar, cable box, somewhat nice receiver, and pretty decent computer. It monitors your wiring and voltage in addition to filtering your power, and it has a power saving feature that puts outlets to sleep when you are not using them. It also has an LED display that tells you pretty much exactly what is up at any given time. I swapped it in to replace an older model I bought years ago back when there were a lot more brick and mortar electronics stores, and while I lost a couple of outlets, this is really pretty nice,

The power conditioner was easy to set up. The instructions are clear and written in plain English, and the display is easy to interpret. It's really really big for having 8 outlets, and it would have been nice to have a bit more room between those eight outlets, considering how much room the power conditioner consumes. However, at the current price, these are minor complaints. I am happy with my purchase, and I am planning to buy another of these for the upstairs.

Arlo is not perfect, but it is wicked close.

What's Great: You can put it anywhere within range of the link/router. The alerts are reliable, if a little slow on the uptake. The picture is good. Set up was simple and worked the first time. A reasonable amount of cloud storage is free, and it's easy to download whatever you want to save. The cameras are easy to move around to wherever you need them, and you don't have to set them up again.

What's Okay: A person who walks fast can get through a room almost faster than Arlo can start recording. Now, it's still much faster than an old Belkin Netcam HD, which sends pictures of where the motion WAS. Before the picture. And the D-Link 930L, which is a fine monitor cam, but has never been able to send a snap or a clip, no matter how many times it has been set up to do that. However, both of those cameras have audio and stream reasonably good images via their apps (the Belkin video resolution is way better than the Dlink). That makes them okay monitors next to smart security sensors - if the sensor alerts, you can look to see what tripped it and listen to see what's going on. Arlo will - most of the time - catch whatever set it off and let you know within seconds. And it's free, not an extra $$$ feature.

What Could Be Better: The link thing is enormous. It could be a little less expensive. And it would be WONDERFUL if it integrated with Z-Wave or Smart Things. The plan here is to station the Arlo cams near other devices that send push notifications - Nest Alarms, Smanos smart sensors, etc.

How It Compares: Beats the Canary I couldn't get to activate. Way better than the other netcams in the house. Love it. Just added another camera.

This is exactly what I wanted. I have set up two different activity-based logitech-type remotes. Neither really did everything I needed them to do, and even though both had lighted buttons, they were of limited use to me with my bedroom set up, because I still needed my glasses to do anything with them.

Why I like this (and who will most likely feel the same way): I have reasonably new components in a reasonably common configuration in a smallish bedroom. When I started this particular set up, my dish joey remote did everything I needed it to do: turn on the tv and joey, turn off same, adjust channel from the cable guide, set dvr, control volume on the tv, *MOST IMPORTANT* fit on my bedside table. As time went on, I acquired a sound bar and a FireTV, neither of which was controlled by the dish remote. The dish remote also would not change the input on my tv, so I had to have that out as well if I wanted to use the FireTV. I have experience and patience with the logitech set up process. My husband and I both have smartphones (and mine is already on my bedside table at night). Set up took a bit of time and patience, but resulted in a universal remote AND smartphone app that control everything I need them to control (and I can use accessibility features on my smartphone so that I don't usually need my glasses to find the buttons). That's a lot of problems for one device to solve, and this one did it.

Also, if you have wanted an activity-based universal remote and haven't wanted to pay hundreds of dollars for a product from this manufacturer, this is an awesome choice.

Who may NOT like this: People with devices that are not 100% controlled with the logitech app/program. People who don't have/don't like smartphones. Senior citizens who are uncomfortable with technology (although I would not be above putting the app on a big bright tablet for a parent or grandparent who is open to the idea, especially since many tablets can be made to play a sound that will let you find where you set them down). People who are fine with having/using a few different remotes or who really don't use more than one or two remotes. I mean, this thing is really cool, and I love it, but if you're not having any problems with what you're doing, you may not want to spend money to solve a problem you don't have.

I bought this tv solely because of the price and because LG seems like a good brand. I was replacing a Vizio that I had been using as a monitor for my Mac Mini. I didn't think stepping down from 1080p to 720p was going to make a difference at 24 inches, but the difference in resolution is noticeable when using this to type and edit text.

Watching movies and tv shows, the picture quality is excellent, and the sound is good enough that I do not need external speakers or a sound bar. I wish the resolution were better, but for the price (less than the smaller Vizio), I am happy. And if this lasts longer than the Vizio (dead within four years), I will be even happier.

These speakers are not going to compete with sound sticks or the higher end multimedia speakers from Bose or even Creative. They are a bit on the tinny side and are in no danger of rocking the house with their volume. There's no low end to speak of.

But if you want to watch movies or video presentations on your laptop, for example, without having to lay your head on the keyboard to hear through your laptop's speakers, these will do the job for a pittance compared to just about anything else. Spoken content is crisp and clear. Music is just okay. Performance is meh. Price is fantastic. Value is solidly above average to excellent.

I have two Seiki tvs. One, I love. The other? Grrrr. Not so much. The main reason for the not so much love is the sound. It was borderline back when I was viewing video from mostly analog sources. When everything switched to hdmi, it became unusable. No matter how I set it up, the sound rendered by the speakers was unintelligible at worst and just kind of muddy at best. Except the background music, which was deafening on any standard definition commercial that came over my high definition satellite box.

It was so bad, I turned on the closed captioning and just left it there.

I should mention that I am not deaf.

Anyway, I saw this sound bar and thought I would give it a try. One thing I hadn't figured on is that the bad tv doesn't have an optical output, but luckily, this has an analog input. And comes with a cable. I plugged it in, turned it on, and all of a sudden, my tv world is alive. Thoroughly clean clear sound - dialogue, music, all good. The presets are good - I didn't have any need to mess with the equalizer - the sound bar to ally solved my problem. Bluetooth pairs easily with my computer and my iPad.

The only thing I don't like is the remote. A bit bigger than a credit card - buttons are hard to push and you can't see a thing in the dark. Good luck setting the sleep timer. Still, the overall experience with this sound bar is good, especially for a reasonably priced brand (NOTE - the Amazon price for this sound bar as of this writing is under $80). I recommend this product.

These speakers are not going to compete with sound sticks or the higher end multimedia speakers from Bose or even Creative. They are a bit on the tinny side and are in no danger of rocking the house with their volume. There's no low end to speak of.

But if you want to watch movies or video presentations on your laptop, for example, without having to lay your head on the keyboard to hear through your laptop's speakers, these will do the job for a pittance compared to just about anything else. Spoken content is crisp and clear. Music is just okay. Performance is meh. Price is fantastic. Value is solidly above average to excellent.

I have some cognitive impairment and mobility challenges from lupus, and I was able to set up Fire TV really easily. The batteries go in the remote; the hdmi cable goes where it goes, and the power plugs in where it plugs in. The interface is simple and intuitive, and you can get everywhere with the home button, the directionals, back, and select. The only painful part for me/my hands was logging into my wireless network via the onscreen qwerty keyboard.

The screens are responsive with virtually no latency, thanks to the quad core processor and 2 gb ram. And video streaming is also very smooth. I have only been using this a day, but I haven't had it pause to buffer yet. I have a Chromecast in my son's room, a recent model Mac Mini in the living room, an older C2D Mac Mini in my room with Boxee on it, and a Raspberry Pi, and they all buffer at some point during just about every movie. I stayed in a vacation home with a Roku 2 last summer, and it was great, but it also had to buffer a lot. We also have three game consoles that have streaming video apps, and they buffer, too. I think the Fire's secret may be its wifi card. I am sure that, at some point, my ISP will find a way to slow it down.

So, yeah, I am giving the Fire TV four stars for doing exactly what I need it to do. I had come to Amazon to get another Chromecast, but I saw this and thought it would probably be better suited to what I need in my bedroom (I need my husband to be able to watch a tv show without my help - he is completely tech-challenged and cannot work the Dish remote - too many buttons).

The reason it doesn't get five stars is that there aren't yet enough content apps. There is a manga channel, a documentary channel, an art house channel, along with Crackle and Flixter and Plex (Plex is a for pay service that lets you stream your home content). There is plenty to watch if you are a Prime member (I am - and I appreciated having that already set up on my Fire TV - Thank you, Amazon!) I am also a Dish subscriber, with HBO and a Hopper. I have apps for those directly on some of my devices. I can get them on the internet on the tbs I have hooked up to computers. I can even blast them over to my Chromecast from my tablets. But they aren't on Fire TV, and none of my tablets will screencast to Fire TV. Soon as they are, this is a five star device for me.

I read in Entertainment Weekly that HBO and Amazon Prime have come to an understanding that will make lots and lots of HBO shows available through prime, which will also make them available through Fire TV. For the ones that are not, HBOGO will have an app for this. Between that news and my son's enjoyment of an eight dollar (as opposed to 40 to 60 dollars) platformed on this thing, I am adding a star.

CAVEAT: this is a stricly consumer-level review. I do not have any expertise with home theater components - I am just the person responsible for buying them and hooking them up.

I finally had more hdmi things than I had hdmi inputs on my tv; that is the main reason I decided to replace my old Denon AV receiver (so old it has composite inputs as the "fancy" ones - no component) that sounded great and worked just fine.

I hate hate hate spaghetti wires. And dust. But the price I got this at was not to be missed (it was cheaper than an hdmi switcher I was looking at), and I couldn't run the Hopper (best DVR ever) through the Denon, so what the heck. Figured it was worth a try.

Set up was easy and ended up getting rid of a lot of the spaghetti I dislike. Sound is totally serviceable. I actually have a completely different stereo for listening to records, so take that for what it is worth. I am currently using this with only two speakers, because the room my home theater is in is so very small, but I tried it with 5, and it sounded great. Really great for the price point.

3D works great - no problems.

Mostly, I love how easy it is to use and the GIANT easy to read display. There was zero learning curve. Love it. I imagine it's even easier with a Bravia TV and other Sony components.

Word to the wise - you look at the back and you think there's going to be more inputs than there actually are. I also am not completely happy with the naming conventions used for the inputs, but oh well. There is no phono preamp, so if you are using this for everything, you'll need one.

Other than those very minor quibbles - I love this AV receiver.

If you can get one of these refurbished for around a hundred bucks or so, this is a great alternative to buying all of your old VHS tapes, etc. again.

The lack of a tuner isn't going to be a deal breaker for most people, but if you need a tuner you should look at the ZV457MG9. Try to get a refurbished on there, too.

For this machine, the pros are that it's easy to set up, they seem to last just about forever - at least the refurbished ones do, and picture quality is very good. You can record from VHS to DVD as long as you're not trying to record copy-protected material, and if you finalize the disk correctly, it should play in any DVD player. I haven't used this function in a really long time, having gone mostly to digital movie rentals and storing my home movies on itty bitty sd cards. Another plus is that everything will output to your tv over one hdmi cable. Finally, you've got a lot of inputs with this, so you can have several different AV sources.

The only cons are that you may need adapters for some older equipment (anything that needs the old antenna/cable input or output) and the thing is actually kind of big and ugly. Other than that, it is awesome. And the remote is HUGE (love it - I have some visual impairment).

First and foremost, in deciding what you are willing to pay for this bargain tv, you should include the costs of buying a decent stand and some speakers or a sound bar. The stand that came with my TV broke within a couple of months (the panel is too heavy for the cheap plastic - we made do by drilling extra holes crossways and adding screws, but that it certainly not a living room friendly solution). The speakers built into the TV are abysmal and won't do in a room that has any other noise.

This is my second Seiki. I also have a 40 inch Seiki [[ASIN:B004NF1KES Seiki LC40G81 40" 1080p 120Hz LCD HDTV] ]and I like that one a lot. I like this one, too, but not as much.

This is a budget television, no doubt about it. The frame is made of plastic that neither looks nor feels expensive. When installing the stand, you want to be very careful to get those screws in all the way (without stripping them), or else the television will not be steady on the stand. The rest of the set up process was very easy. Probably my favorite thing about this television is that it has component and composite inputs, meaning that I can still use my older dvd player and dish network dvr with it. One thing to be aware of, though, is that it has only one analog audio input, so you can use a component video source and a composite video source, but you can only get audio from one of those devices.

The size difference between 40 and 42 inches is more noticeable than what I thought it would be. If bigger is better for you, or if you are replacing a tv that's 42 inches or larger, I think you might like this one - the SE421TT - better. The picture is not quite as good, and there is some fade out at the edges, but the blacks are nice and deep, and the colors are vibrant. The first thing I watched was a PBS HD documentary on elephants, and the picture was quite stunning. The television sits on a high boy dresser in my bedroom, and the viewing angle is still excellent from down low.

Using input from a standard definition dish network dvr, the picture was considerably less stellar, with blurring and occasional lag. My 40 inch tv does a noticeably better job of rendering from the satellite dish. Both televisions are excellent for over the air HD content, and the 42 inch tv, surprisingly, did a better job of connecting with my Mac Mini over a dvi-to-hdmi cable. Unlike the 40 inch, which is a newer model, the 42 inch gives full 1080p with no over-scaling.

The sound is where the 42 inch falls apart. Tinny, weak, and truly awful out of the box. I was able to get an acceptable sound for a bedroom tv (which is what I am using this for) by playing with the equalizer and presets (I set it to jazz and dynamic). I do not think it would work in a busier, louder room. For now, the picture and sound are enough better on the 40 inch that I have decided to keep that one as my living room tv (my living room is tiny), but the 42 inch is great in the bedroom.

I shopped around a long time before I bought the 40 inch tv, because I've got serious budget constraints, and I needed something I could afford AND that I wouldn't regret buying every time I tried to watch it. Now that I have both of these, I have to say that I still think the 40 inch is the better bargain with two "unlesses" - 1. Get the 42 inch if size really matters to you, and 2. Get the 42 inch if your primary video source is going to be 1080p dvi-to-hdmi (i.e. you have cut your cable and are using a computer as your main source of entertainment). If that's the case, you'll probably want to get a decent set of speakers to go along with this.

My first real camera was a Pentax K-1000 with manual everything, and my preference is always to try to get the best looking picture I can have before any image processing happens. Digital point and shoot is a much different animal from old film photography, but I still want an excellent lens, because without one, I feel like I might as well just stick with my iPhone or Bloggie and not have an actual camera at all.

I bought the Lumix for the Leica lens, and I was a little disappointed that it does not render accurately close up. In the automatic setting, there's a noticeable amount of fisheye distortion that is clearly visible in any close up photo involving lines that should be straight or in portraits, which end up looking like funhouse shots. It took some experimenting, but it turns out that the portrait setting completely corrects this (and you can use it for still life shots, too). Once I gave up my notion of how I thought things ought to be and started to work with the camera to get the results I wanted, I sort of fell a little in love with the thing.

It's got a very large LCD. I have lupus and am losing my eyesight. Tiny lcds just don't work for me. Setting navigation is easy and very very intuitive. The buttons aren't too tiny. I did not install the included software or read the instructions, and I am having a very easy time finding my way around and loading up the pictures. Once you figure out what setting you need to depict accurately the person, place, or thing you are trying to photograph, you get sharp, accurate pictures, even in low light or under other difficult shooting conditions.

This led tv is much better than I expected it to be for the price I paid for it. I was not in the market for a new television, but the one I had in my bedroom died. It's a small room, and the dead tv was 26 inches. I started looking for something around that size and stumbled on this one for not too much more than a smaller one. So, I figured I'd give it a try, and if I liked it, I'd put the 32 inch tv from my living room in the bedroom.

Set up was very easy. I put it together using the stand. I had enough screws. They all fit. You have to screw them all the way in straight, or the tv kind of wobbles on the stand, but once I did that, the thing is very stable.

It has one component input, one composite, one antenna, one VGA, and three hdmi, and I'm using all of them. Very very easy. the whole thing, including moving the other tv, took half an hour, with the only slight pain being that my late 2010 Mac Mini won't under scan at 1080p, so I had to go to 720p, on the hdmi connection. I don't even know what any of that means, except that this is what I had to do in order to be able to see my menu bar.

Picture is really nice for the price, even my little intel atom its box over the VGA looks good. What impressed me most is the sound. I only use the tv's speakers for the Wii U, and they are surprisingly clear. I'm still figuring out some of the settings, but up and running in half an hour and enjoying the results is pretty amazing - especially for the price.

My k1000 will be 30 years old this Christmas, and it has been the most reliable camera I have ever owned. My lenses are still nice and sharp. My light meter and flash shoe still work. I have probably changed the battery 3 times. There are no light leaks. Everything works just like the day I got it.

This is a great first camera for any person who wants to learn about photography: exposure, composition, etc. With digital point and shoots, it's really easy to just be a documentarian and rely on photoshop or filters to fix things up a bit later, but there's no real incentive to get things right in the first instance. Film - real film - requires patience and discipline and a critical eye. Which is why I am teaching my 11 year old son to use this.

A tip on loading the film (I was dead broke for a lot of the first decade I owned this and could not afford to waste a bit): Before you try to load the film, bend just the last little bit down, so that it makes a little l-shaped piece that will catch in the slot. Put the tag into the slot and carefully pull out just enough to fit the film snugly into the camera. BY HAND, turn the spool on the left side about half a turn to set the film on the spool and make sure the holes are caught on the teeth. When you turn the left spool, the film should come easily out of the canister. Only do a little bit, and if it seems to be working (i.e. pulling the film out of the canister), close the back of the camera. Cock the camera - WATCH the film counter to make sure the film is advancing. If it's not, don't rewind unless you are sure you can do so without losing your leading edge into the film canister. Just open the back and re-set the edge onto the spool and try again. If it is - and you should be able to feel the resistance in the mechanism - shoot a picture. The first one won't come out. The second one may, and by loading carefully, you should be able to get an extra couple of shots on every roll of film.

When my old internal hard drive began making grinding noises in my late 2006 MBP, I started thinking about replacing the whole computer. I bought it used a couple of years ago for a really good price, and it doesn't owe me any money. OTOH, money's kind of tight these days, and this was a pretty fancy machine back in its time.

I decided to upgrade my hard drive to an ssd and max out my ram, rather than spend a ton of money right off the bat, and see how my old beauty did with it.

I lost quite a bit of disk space going to a solid state internal drive. I can use an external drive to hold all of the stuff I'll probably never want to look at again but just might possibly need someday, but I wanted a solution for my iTunes library and media files that would be faster than USB or firewire. This is a lot faster, and with a class 10 card in it, performance is EXCELLENT. It moves as fast as thought. And the adapter sits flush with the port when installed, so it's not bulky or awkward. I wear these to bed so the wire and plug get a fair amount of abuse with twisting and pulling and so far they have held up and haven't developed any shorts like other brands I have used have.  Also haven't had any problems with the tips popping off either.

Very impressed with these earbuds.  Sound quality is probably the best for any earbuds that I have owned, wireless or otherwise.  Noise cancellation is good, but I haven't had an opportunity to really see how well it works in various settings.  For me at least, they are also remarkably comfortable.  Battery life compared to some other options on the market isn't as good, but for me it hasn't been an option.  I usually have an opportunity throughout the day to throw them in the case and let them charge for a bit.  No reservations about  these and I have recommended them to several of my friends.

I've been thinking about upgrading from my Canon 50d for awhile now. I thought I wanted a full frame camera, but I could never justify spending that kind of money on a hobby. One of the main reasons was that I had sort of got out of the habit of shooting as much as I used. Part of the reason was that it always seemed like such a pain to lug around the camera. There were always times I wish I had a camera, but didn't.

This camera solves a lot of that for me. Take the lens off the body and the thing literally fits in your pocket. Leave it on and it fits nicely in my car's center console. It feels nice in my hands, although I bought the metal thumb grip at the same time as the camera and must admit that does help quite a bit.

Compared to my 50d (which is a little long in the tooth) the image quality is superior. The color reproduction in particular seemed to be good. It also seemed to perform better at higher ISOs than my 50d does. Really, the only area where the 50d still out-performs the XE-2 is how fast the autofocus works. The XE-2 is good, but my 50d is still a touch better. Maybe a firmware update will improve this.

Despite using a Canon products for almost a decade, I found I really like the controls on this camera. I found it really easy and intuitive to change the shutter speed and aperature.
