ISO and most of the other frequently used settings are easily reached by hitting the Q button. The layout could be tweaked a little, but overall it's pretty good.

I've never had a camera with wifi, but it's a feature that's gotten more use than I thought it would. Being able to transmit pictures to Facebook, Twitter, or whatever is really simple once you upload the photo from the camera using Fuji's app. I don't post a lot of pictures online, but that may change a little bit now that it is a lot simpler.

The build quality is really good and the included kit lens is really nice. The screen is sharp and the EVF is clear. Like I mentioned before, the size of the frame is nice and compact and is much easier to take along wherever you go.

Is this a replacement for a full frame DSLR? No. Is it a good alternative for a crop sensor DSLR? In my opinion, absolutely. First, the price and performance makes it very competitive. Second, the size is going to be tough to beat. Finally, for me at least, it is a camera I am more likely to use more and take with me more places. As other's have mentioned about this camera though, if you like putting everything on automatic or different shooting modes (sports, portrait, landscape, etc) then this camera is probably not for you. If you are interested in learning how to shoot without those crutches, this camera would be a great place to start.

I got two sets of these. Snce the impedience is rated as 6 Ohms I wired them in series fo get a 12 Ohm impedience, which, from some rersearch, I think is an easier load for the reciever to drive. I set them at at aboui a 30 degree angle ro each other for wider dispersion. I also think distortioin is lowered as each speaker has to play less loud then if I only had two. IF YOU DONT KNOW THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN WIRING IN SERIES AS OPPOSED TO PARALLEL STICK WITH ONE PAIR!  Bargain speakers for soft music.
I'm loving these wireless earphones.  Sound is adequate for exercising.  Controls on ear pieces make controlling music. .. And answering phone easy.  Great product!

Directs sound into ear canal even creating a noise canceling effect. I have small ear canals which make using earbuds difficult as none usually fit.  These have cured the problem.  Three come in pack making it easy to choose the one with the right fit.

Pretty, and has an apple pencil holder.  There are slots at the bottom of the case to hold the pencil, the charging adapter and the top cap for when you are charging.  The pencil only goes is with the point to the right.  Also the slots for the adapter and top cap require that you get them exactly in alighnment for them to snap into place.  Other than that, it's great!

Work great so far, and it is especially quiet.
Perfect for what I need!
Will update to see how long it can last.

The thing that I like best about this Kbear Wired Earbuds is that the cord does not tangle. Given how annoyed I get waiting for wireless earphones to pair (or when the pair fails), I'm starting to prefer wired again, but the cord tangle is annoying too so this product's cord being non-tangle is a win to me.

The sound quality is okay. I'm good with it. It does come with different sizes of earbuds as per the standard. It has a friendly price point as well.

Overall, I give it a 4-star as a solid performer.

The one and probably only thing that I do not like about this Bluetooth Headset with Microphone, V5.1, Noise Canceling Wireless On Ear Headphones is that it is a bit tight on fit and there isn't much flex there so I can't wear for too long. I didn't realize that my head was so big. Otherwise, this headset works pretty well. The battery life lasts good amount of time. The sound is good as is the microphone. It isn't top-notch, but for the price point, it is more than adequate. The fit is the only thing that keeps me from giving it a 5-star but if one has a smaller head than mine, it may be a perfect, or near perfect, fit.

We just wanted a small fan for the dining table. We have a small condo and the dining table is in an area that doesn't get any benefit of the ceiling fans. We just wanted something small and portable to get air flow. This camping fan looked like it would work and it does. The battery life is fantastic. It makes very little noise. At the lowest setting, it is silent. We also like the light. We don't use it that often, but we've had a few times when we did. We couldn't find the flashlight and remembered that this fan had a light. So convenient.

It comes with everything needed to get it started. The remote is nice as well. Overall, we are very pleased with this item.

My previous headphone was an IFECCO Bluetooth headphone. I loved it and I didn't want to give it up but it was getting to that time that it was time to replace. It had outlasted much more expensive headphones and out-worked them too.

Even when I selected this new IFECCO headphone to try, I was skeptical that it would be as good. As soon as I started using them, my skepticism went away. The ease of installation, the sound quality, and the comfort was all there. It even has a much-appreciated feature that my old headphones did not have - an easy on/off slide switch. Such a simple feature but oh so appreciated.

So my old IFECCO headphones were finally retired with a 'thank you for your service' ceremony and the new headphones have been put to work and they are doing great.

This UPGROW HDMI to VGA Adapter HDMI Male to VGA Female Converter Support Computer is working as expected. It was easy to install and get running. It gives me a little flexibility with some slightly older equipment. I am satisfied that this worked so well.

I selected this item at the request of my son. He needs to start replacing the ethernet cables (he prefers wired to wireless) and wanted to see if the Cat7 is faster and worth further consideration. It came in fairly time which was great. The cable was 5 ft as described. Almost a bit short for what he needed, but it worked out and yes, he confirms that it is faster. It was well worth the try and he'll looking in to getting a few more Cat7 in the future.

Asltoy Laptop Folding Desk Tray is sturdy and stable. I haven't used the small drawer much but it is a nice-to-have should I need to. The main functionality of the tray is solid. It is easy to store. When in use, it feels sturdy and stable. I've used while sitting on the bed. I've used as a 'standing desk' when I need more light for a project that I'm working on. I've used it as a dinner tray. It is versatile and useful. Best of all, no assembly required. That alone is worth a star.

The one concern that I had about the MODFAMILY PRODUCTS THAT SIMPLIFY LIFE Cinema Light Box was that it wouldn't have all the letters, but that was fine. It doesn't have an even amount of letters (ex: There were more E's than X's) but it made sense. I didn't expect an endless amount of letters but it did contain a sufficient amount to start with. It is easy to use. It does require Double-A batteries. Interestingly, it seems to need 6 batteries but as soon as 3 batteries in a row are put in, the light came on. Still, I used the 6 batteries. It has been working well. It is fun to swap out the words. It is clean in design so it has a nice versatility. It is a trendy item so I think the price point reflects that, but it is a fun item to try out.

It was time to swap out to new monitor risers as my current ones were starting to show age (dipping forward). When I saw this monitor riser, I figured it was worth a try.

What I like about this Olive Oak is that it was easy to put together and it has solid form and function. I'm pleased with it. I like the vents on the side because it makes it easier to pass cords through side rather than back and the way my desk is organized, that works well for me. The monitor sits on the platform with ease and it is steady and sturdy. The only reason I'd keep it from a 5-star is that the holes were tight and the allen wrench is a bit bendy so it required extra pressure to turn but at the same time, not too much pressure or the allen wrench would start to feel like it was about to snap, if that was possible. That said, it was still fairly easy to put together. I'm quite pleased at how it looks and works.

It wasn't so much the retro look of this Byron Statics Radio AM FM Portable Radio Retro Classic Table Top Analog Radios that caught my eye, but more that I just wanted a simple radio. I do like the retro look as the curved edges make for a nice pop in the room. Yet, the thing that I like most is that it gets the radio stations that I like and I don't have to fuss too much with it. I can use batteries for portability or I can use the adapter and plug into the wall. It works well in every room and given that we had a recent blackout in our area, the radio was a real nice to have. The sound quality is decent as well. I'm glad that I decided to try this radio out.

For myself (a beginner), I liked the Acepen Ap604 6×4 In4mm Electronic Drawing Tablet Pad. It was easy to install on my PC and fairly easy to use. It wasn't plug and play which was a little surprising since my PC is fairly up-to-date but not a deal breaker. I nearly gave it a 5 star but I had my son try it out and he was a little less enthused. He did note that it requires that if there is another tablet installed, the drivers for that tablet had to be uninstalled. It was too small for him and the pen wasn't quite as sensitive as he was used to. However, he did say that if he were starting out, it would be a good beginner drawing tablet.

Gaming Headset, EasySMX Cool 2000 Over Ear Stereo Gaming Headphone with Mic and Volume Control is a solid performer that is comfortable to wear. The audio was crisp and clear right out of the box. The mic working at optimum did take some tweaking when using with the PC but it was easy enough to figure out. All in all, a good solid headset at what looks to be a reasonable price.

I have a collection of hard drives from PCs that are long gone. I keep them because there are various documents, files and programs that I still like to access but don't necessarily want to keep on my current laptop or upload to the cloud. That's why I wanted to try this Sabrent 4-Bay USB 3.0 SATA 2.5"/3.5" SSD/HDD Docking Station (DS-U3B4).

It is convenient in so many ways: Easy to set up; easy to use; easy to put away when not in use. I have had it for several months now and it is holding up well. I have a few very minor quibbles but otherwise, this is a very convenient item to have.

I have a couple of tablets and this StarTech.com USB C Multiport Adapter has been quite handy. I haven't used it to connect a HDMI screen, but it was great for the USB and connecting a portable CD/DVD player. It picked up quite easily and worked as needed. It is lightweight and easy to store when not in use. Currently, it is a nice-to-have but I can see using it more frequently as I find more options in its use.

I'm wavering a bit on how I should rate the SHANLONYI Radio with AM/FM, Time Projector. On the one hand, I like the face of the clock digits and the projection light is pretty nifty. On the other hand, I still can't figure out how to set the radio functions to save stations. But then again, setting the alarm was easy. Yet on the other hand, I keep having to re-tune the radio although I'm admittedly not used to a radio outside of the car so the issue may be more with me than the product.

Honestly, I think I'm going with the 4-star because the main reason that I wanted to try the clock was for it to be used as a clock, not a radio. I really do like the size of the digits on the clock. It makes it easy to read. It was also easy to set the time and alarm. I also like adjusting the volume of the alarm so it wakes me up but it isn't an obnoxious level of sound.

The USB port is also a nice-to-have. The radio does get decent reception too. It picks up the local college radio station and that can sometimes be problematic. So all in all, I rather like the clock and even the radio since I really just listen to two stations anyway.

The Sony RF400 Wireless Home Theater Headphones (WHRF400) was an interesting but easy set up and the sound is fine. All in all, it is comfortable, wireless and works as we had needed so we are good with it.

Pioneer Hi-Res Audio in-Ear Headphones are comfortable. When it comes to earphones, comfort is important to me. They are standard in-ear headphones so there isn't much fancy about them and I like that. I wish the sound quality was a bit crisper but that may be a good thing for the health of my ears. Overall, I like them because they are steady and consistent in quality.

I like the earbud design of this JAM Live Large Earphones Bluetooth Wireless Earbuds in blue. It says that it has 7 hours of playtime. I haven't timed it exactly but that seems about right. I did have to try several times for my phone to finally pair with the earphones but once it paired, it worked quite well. As noted prior, I like the earbud design. It is bigger than usual but it makes it easier to find and keep track off and it is comfortable to wear. The sound is above average. About the only thing I'm not too keen on is that the cover to the USB port doesn't quite snap close for me but that is a minor thing.

AmazonBasics Wireless Keyboard - Quiet and Compact - US Layout is indeed quiet and it doesn't take up any more space than needed. It connected immediately and I really appreciate that it came with batteries (AAA) to start. Now that I have this keyboard, I'm hoping that there will be a wireless mouse available as well and if there will be keyboard/mouse set available. I'd definitely be interested in the latter.

About the only thing I'm not as keen on is that the keys are a little soft but that goes with the quietness feature so it is a trade-off for me and I'll get used the feel the more that I use it.

I've become more partial to wireless headphones but I have a device that just won't take the wireless headphone that I use with my phone so I figured I'd try this headphone. Cords can annoy but the sound and comfort of the Mi In-Ear Headphones Pro Silver Dual Driver Earbuds with Mic is really nice. I also used it with my phone for the mic and that was worked well too. So while I still have a preference for wireless in general, this item is something that I would consider for future purchase due to the sound and comfort quality of the product.

My first external drive ever was a Western Digital so I have a soft spot for the brand. Since we needed to back up an older laptop that was starting to fail, this WD 4TB My Passport Ultra Portable External Hard Drive with USB appeared at a perfect time. It has two things that we need: ease of use and storage space. It was easy to use for back up of the laptop's data and had so much storage left that we could use it to transfer files from the other PCs. We still have a lot left for storage. We aren't a big cloud using family but I imagine if we were, we'd use it as a back up for the Cloud as well. Overall, it has worked out well for our household.

I was a little skeptical when I selected this item, but once in use, the B&O PLAY by Bang & Olufsen Beoplay H4 Wireless Headphones won me over. I have a wireless headphone already that I like (and still do) but these headphones really are nice and comfortable. The instructions were a bit thin but we still got them up and running quickly enough. The sound is good and the fit is comfortable. One thing that I really like about these type of headphones is that they don't irritate my ears. The bonus is that my son can use them as well. He's a big guy so he often finds that headphones can a little too small and tight but these headphones have flexibility and they are as comfortable for him as they are for me.

When this first arrived, my son started to test them out and he's a little picky about the sound on earphones. Plus they were a little tight for him. For me, the "Francois et Mimi VT006 Active Noise Canceling Over-Ear Headphones" are perfect. They paired perfectly to my PC. The sound is just right and the cans fit comfortably around my ears. All in all, a great product for me.

I received this item on Friday (super fast delivery; I'm impressed!) and was anxious to try them right away because although I prefer the over-the-head headphones, the in-ear headphones are more compact and easy to take on road and I spend a lot of the time on the bus.

I do like the sound. As with the other AmazonBasics headphone that I was able to try out, I feel like I can hear again. No more having to turn the volume up to 100%. Thank goodness. It is a little tinny in sound if you don't have the buds sitting in the ear correctly, but when the bud is set correctly, the sound is nice even at 40% volume. Clear and pleasant.

I still prefer the over-the-ear headphones because buds have a tendency to irritate my ear if I use them too long but on a bus ride to and from work, this will work perfectly.

I probably should bump Polk Audio Buckle Headphones to 4-stars but I just can't do it because the sound and comfort of the headphones is just so good.

Reason to possibly bump it down was that the microphone didn't quite work as expected but really, I didn't select it for the microphone so I don't really care.

To be honest, I haven't had a headphones this good since... well, I don't think I've ever had a headphones with sound this good. I actually had to keep the volume at half because of the quality of the headphones.

I'm not sure yet what the 3 button control is used for. I'm still learning about the headphones. I'm sure I'll figure it out once I can get it back from my son who likes the headphones even more than I do.

Price on the headphones may be eye popping but now that I've used them, I can see why some headphones cost as much as they do. There really is a difference.

I briefly mentioned comfort and yes, they are very, very comfortable.

Installed easily. Connected easily. I had a problem and reached out to the supplier (Person naked this responded), and they were super attentive and sent a replacement. Problem was more then able and not the unit. I’m using these off the rear deck of our cottage and the sound is great. Highly recommend these for the price. I wouldn’t want a smaller size as I’m not sure the bass would come through as well as these. If you want $300-400 bass and sound, go spend that, but I have a lot of speakers of high to mid quality all over various properties, and these work great. I’m connecting it to an Echo Dot through Bluetooth so the family or guests can just ask for music or whatever anytime they want.

Thanks to Chris at Herdio for being so quick to respond! I was pretty impressed where I wasn’t sure what I’d be getting into.

I read a lot of the reviews and of course the bad ones make you apprehensive, despite all the good ones.  I've had this a couple months now.  It rocks.  Nice bass.  Deep and rich.  Rubber feet are what I wanted for when I'm working outdoors.  The eq hardly makes much difference (sadly), but most devices allow you to adjust on the source end, and I never had a problem with how it sounded as is anyhow.  Battery life is not bad but it won't be running all day.  And it does seem to trickle down quickly when not plugged in - so I find myself wanting to keep it plugged in (which may not be good for the battery?) just to be sure it's on the ready when I am (that's where the fifth star went).  But I would recommend this and buy it again knowing all that I do now.  Price / value is great. Use it for working in the garage, in the house, dinner music, deck music, and for the hotel when we travel.

Good headphones for the price. Not the beat I own or anything sound quality wise But I bought these for working out and something I can get sweaty. These are great for a combination of quality Sound and durability. I definitely think that I would purchase again if I needed another pair. Absolutely stays in place with very little slippage of the earpiece once you find the right size for you which several are included
Completely satisfied with this product. Love the way Yamaha has put together all function Sound, internet and ease of use.
My new computer doesn't have an internal drive and I didn't miss it until I needed to access something I'd stashed on a CD-Rom, pre Cloud storage.

My favorite bluetooth buds. They stay in the ear comfortably, have a good range and a fair amount of ambient noise blocking. Just purchased them again after losing my first pair. Can't beat the price, and they now come with a zippered box to hold the charger protect the buds when not in use.

Extremely convenient, catches even pretty narrow cables.  I like the ease of popping cords in and out, like chargers or headphones.  For more permanent stuff I have zip ties.  These are adequately sticky for small-medium cords, and I haven't tried anything large.  I got two six-packs, and I'm satisfied.  If I needed more I would buy again.

I got a new 50 inch 7 series samsung tv that has a curved back, so the screws that came with the stand does not fit. The required screws were M8 x 45mm, but the longest screws were m8 x 35mm. I'm ok with that as this screen is newer and has a different curve on teh back than most flatscreen tvs out there.

After a run to Fastenal to obtain the right length screws, everything installed fine. In order to level horizontal axis properly, I left the screws on the horizontal bar slightly loose. After putting on the screen, adjust for horizontal level, and then tighten the screws on the horizontal bar.

Only issue that i came into after that was the whole tv would lean backwards ever so slightly, like 4-5 degrees. Very noticeable since my tv is next to a door and bookcase. I noticed the problem was in the design of the vertical bars that are installed onto the tv itself.

The upper hook part that clips onto the top part of the horizontal bar is not the same thickness as the bottom hook part that sits on the lower part of the horizontal bar. Thin vertical top, thicker vertical bottom, you get a screen that is angled looking slightly up. Maybe its a design flaw or maybe its designed to accommodate heavier TV's that may cause the screen to lean forward (my tv was kinda light).

A fix for my TV leaning back was shoving a few shims under the back of the base plate to get it to lean more forward (i used a stack of like 8 business cards on both rear corners of the base plate; seems to work fine).

Overall, i'm happy with my product. The ability to swivel was the sole reason i bought this.

i've only recently started soldering and putting kits together. this radio is technically my second kit! sure, there were no step by step instructions, but i felt like i learnt a lot more from just trying to figure it out, staring at digrams, and watching youtube vids about it.

The youtube videos clarified a lot, along with other users here. i didnt follow the instructions suggested steps about building them by system, but rather just went down the list and plugged components in till the board was filled.

once all components were installed, i shoved some batteries in and check the current thru each system, as the instructions indicated. I was within range so i didnt have to tweak the resistors to get the right amps.

overall the kit was fun to build. the speaker is loud and crisp, and the whole thing has a lovable retro disegn.

I'm a concept artist for film and games, so as a profession, sorta need this thing - cost doesnt become an issue when u consider its like a photographer buying their own camera equipment.

The new 21 UX is great to deal with. One of the reasons why i did not pick up the previous model is 1) heat - got warm and sweaty, 2) contrast ratio - everything was grayish, 3) corners were not perfectly aligned to the pen.

So I held off and bought a smaller 12 inch cintiq for use. But man, that small one got me hunched over it, and the real estate is WAY to small for my photoshop needs. I'm an artist, i'm used to drawing on 18x30 newsprint. After 2 years of use, tons of felt nubs, and my aching back from poor posture, the 21 UX came out, and the office got one for me to use. It was a world of difference that i decided to pick one up for home use/freelance work. all problems mentioned above are either reduced greatly or not there in this new model :D

EVERYWHERE is SOLD OUT THOUGH... not even WACOM, whom i mailed, had any in stock and IN fact they replied, letting me know that they won't be shipping directly from their site due to unfilled backorders with other clients (ie best buy CDW etc). Considering a variety of entertainment studios pick them up in bulk, it was hard to get one to a single person in teh suburbs.

I ordered through Amazon because of price, and because i'm on their prime membership - 3 bux for next day woo woo. Amazon said anywhere between 2-3 months to ship - i was ok with that. Surprisingly tho, it shipped within 3 weeks! was not mentally prepared yet for the 2K of money being sucked out of my account... but nonetheless, it was nice getting it sooner than expected :)

thumbs up on amazon for best price and best shipping.

Still learning what Alexa and the Echo Dot can do. The Dot was a gift from my brother and I was going to give it back to him. However, he said he already had four of them, so I said he'd have to teach me how to interact with it or it was going on Craigslist.
I now use it in place of a clock in my bathroom to tell me what time it is and what's coming up on my calendar for the day ahead. My husband made the comment "do you know how stupid you sound talking to that thing" , but he's a Luddite and so I ignore him.
We don't have any smart appliances or plugs (yet). I'd like to get a plug for my bedside light, but one problem I see is that the plug is behind some furniture that will have to be pulled away from the wall by about 3 to 4 inches in order to plug everything in. Wish someone made a plug that goes sideways.

If, like me, you want a shower speaker for listening to audiobooks and podcasts, you probably want to skip this one. It doesn't have a rewind/replay function, only a skip to end function. Returning mine and wishing its functions were listed in the product description. (If they're there, they're far too easy to miss.)

I purchased these after reading a review (CNet, I believe) about the best earbuds. I'd been looking for wired ones because I've bought nice, top-end Bluetooth earbuds before and have never been happy with them. Usually, they don't work consistently, are subject to interference, drop the audiobook/podcast/call, and are too finicky.
These, though? They've exceeded even my highest hopes. The sound quality is excellent. They have a wonderful case that charges them until its battery dies, which then recharges quickly with its included USB-C charger cord (no plug, you need a regular USB port to plug it into).
They're super comfortable, they stay in my ears impressively well, you can wear one at a time if you'd like because they connect independently and each has the pause/play button on it. They have an impressive range, too. I've accidentally walked away from my phone and made it 4 rooms away without losing the sound (it does get a little fuzzy). I've used them frequently since I purchased them 3 months ago and I'm still super impressed. Reliable, excellent, and I'm no longer looking for wired earbuds. I highly recommend them. The one downside for me is that they're noise-canceling. I'd love it if there was an option not to, but to make up for it, I just wear one when I'm out walking or need to listen for something.

I purchased these for my 9-year-old daughter. She's not the most attentive person and often leaves things lying about, which means they often get dropped, stepped on, sat on, etc. These have held up well to over a month of such treatment. She's also very sensitive to things that feel uncomfortable and has no complaints about the padding on her ears; she loves them. (She has thick, curly hair which sometimes gets snagged on the metal upside down u-shape over the headphones, though.) They are very good at noise canceling, which she loves! (I don't always since she can't hear me calling her, ha ha.) Great, great headphones for the price. I recommend them and would buy again.

Excellent earbuds for the price. I use mine many hours a day every day, both outdoors (dog walking) and indoors (folding laundry, cooking, etc.). They put up with a fair amount of wear and tear and have held up well to it. I really appreciate the remote on the cord. There are 3 buttons: volume up, play/pause, volume down. I don't use mine to take calls, though I do believe you can, so I cannot comment on that part.

I highly recommend these if you're looking for a quality pair of earbuds for a very reasonable price. Love them!

I have been looking for a quiet keyboard and this one fits the bill! I love the cover that comes with it since it makes it easy to clean and offers some extra protection. It's a great keyboard and I loved the reasonable price. Very happy!

I love these headphones! I often snag my headphone cords and with the over-the-ear style, they're less likely to pop out on me. They're comfortable and the sound quality is good. Happy with my purchase.

My son is 16 and wanted these, but the reviews and pictures made it seem like they were child sized. I figured I'd return them if they were too small. They seem to be regular sized as far as I can tell and the have decent sound. Not as good as some of his other cans, but he doesn't like to walk around with the more expensive ones, and uses them, instead, for recording class or at home.
Works well overall. Holds the iPad in three positions well. One star off as it is just a bit difficult to access volume and power button. Too soon to know about durability.

These work great and are easy to install. I purchased them mainly for the chime function to alert me to my young children running out without letting me know. 4 stars because even though it works for this purpose perfectly, the chime is LOUD and grating for the person opening up the door. Not at all chime-like. More I-hope-I-didn't-just-damage-my-hearing-like.

Used this to consolidate several A/V components that require both traditional and USB power. Frees up plugs at the wall outlet and provides power right where it's needed so fewer long cords to manage.

Works like a charm. Only problem we had was the video stream from the security camera system would not feed through to the TV, everything else we plugged into it looks and sounds great. Remote feels a little cheap but haven't had any problems with it. May end up buying another one for another room.

Works well, but microphone is very temperamental due to the noise canceling feature. I added a little textured notch so I could be sure just by feeling it that it is positioned correctly which resolves the issue. Other than lacking that tactile indicator, this works very well.

I got these to replace a wired headset for my phone. The mic is in the U shape so it picks up sound rather well. Has a bit of an issue when waring masks, but otherwise very clear.

Sound quality is really good, if not at times a little quiet. the noise cancelation sometimes gets confused and will amplify sounds like running water over voice, but its easy to avoid.

the battery lasts a rather good amount of time, and the headset has a decent range if you put your phone down to charge. It will sometimes have momentary disconnections if you are in a winter coat or near different electronics or machinery, but for the most part you have to walk into a different room before audio quality is truly effected.

I sometimes forget that I have it around my neck. if you have it running for hours at a time, your ears might hurt a little bit form the earbuds or wax might build up in the speakers, but its otherwise very nice to use. I should read the manual as I didn't realize I could answer and end calls, or stat/stop playing with the power button. One charge usually lasts me a few days of heavy use.

Seems to work fine with minimum hiss, but the power adaptor that it came with was either not sufficient to power the unit, or was defective itself. I found a spare adaptor that was able to power it better.

So, I got two of these, one to use as audio splitter and one as a bootleg combiner for mics.
I was expecting it not to work, but it can handle signals in both directions (all be it with a slight DB loss).
Im not saying this is the best solution for that, but its a lot cheaper then an audio mixer or the combiners you can find otherwise. I am also converting this over a USB sound card and using phantom power from two condenser mics, so it will introduce a small amount of background noise but its not very noticeable.

It cant handle two way signals, so you can not hook in the mic and audio jack at once, but it will work one way, either combining 5 or outputting them.
I've had this for about 4 months.  It works well with no popping/crackling/noise distortion.  Converts the cable so that I can use my Turtle Beach "Xbox" headset for usage on my PC.

With the help of the adaptor, I can use AirPods and beats solo 3 when playing switch. Currently I’m using it to play ring fit adventure, and it works smoothly so far. The only problem is that the volume has to be above about 35%, otherwise it will be cut off every now and then.
The color is beautiful and it fits my 12.9” iPads and Apple Pencil perfectly. The volume keys are cleverly designed and work smoothly .
These are the right size for using in close space requirements. When the cables are too long, it is such a mess and these cables solve the problem.

This device enhances clarity on your TV over the earlier versions of Fire TV. You can also get Apple TV on this device - you have to search (next to HOME) for Apple TV because the app is not part of the App Store, but it is available. Easy to setup. If you have access to Showtime, HB, EPIX, etc. through your internet/TV provider, you simply sign on using those credentials. It was a good buy.
I like this speaker and the nice round bass sound it provides. Just what I was looking for. I'm thinking of getting a second one for the stereo experience.

My dog chewed up my Bose soundtrue headphones.  Really.  Luckily the speakers still worked even though the foam covers were completely ruined.  The replacement covers look and feel good.  I used a YouTube video to understand how to put them on. It was as easy as can be, once I saw how.

Purchased for my mom in her 80's enjoying classical and rock music; she couldn't rave enough about yhese earphones with great stereo sound and comfortable ear pads. I highly recommend them and purchased another pair as a gift!

I was gifted this and was skeptical at first but after having it a few months, this speaker is one of my favorite accessories. After an accidental coffee spill on my phone, the speakers no longer sounded the same so this seemed like a good solution.

Pros:
- Bluetooth connects right away, no lags (I’ve got a pair of Beats headphones that don’t always connect)

- Sound is exceptional for a device that costs less than $30

- Rubberized bottom stabilizes the device

- Rubberized ends allow you to use it vertically in a narrow space (I use it this way when my desk is full of paperwork)

Cons:
None so far.

I’ve owned it for a few months. Will update if anything changes.

This product works well and has met my expectation. Cant wait til the summer time gets here again as I had several movie nights in the backyard. Easy to put together and can be done with one person- BUT not "easy". Does require getting use to. I relabeled all my poles so that the stickers would not come off and I know which connections to make. Takes about 10-15  minutes for me to put up. The only flaw I have is that the 2 velco straps on the far left and right are quite difficult to connect and seem like they may not have been made long enough. I can rarely get them to connect but does not affect the functioning. I usually tuck these towards the back and out of the way. Plan to complete manual construction to the straps next year to fix the issue by making them a bit longer. Otherwise would have given the product 5 stars. Overall construction, ease of use and quality - 4 stars easy!

Absolutely love this travel case. It provides a good level of protection for my Soundblaster Roar and love the fact that the charger can be easily stored in the zippered case below the bag. Definitely has exceeded my expectations. It is a must have for your valued soundblaster!

They work great. I use them with the powerbeats pro and it makes them sound so much better. Only weird thing and it might be my ears but if I fully turn the beats into me ear it seems to break the seal. But if you turn the so that the volume buttons are horizontal then it keeps the seal.

Does exactly what I needed it to do. I have a Fractal G case and the audio header was too short and I had accidentally pulled a wire when initially putting it together and had to order a whole new I/O panel to replace it. This extension was just what I needed to help deal with the cases short coming of the audio header being too short. Its a 9 pin connector, something to consider with all the different connectors. It's also well made and just the right length.

So let's start out with that it's a nice step up from your standard car radio. I like the overall design and you can save up to 20 channels and have 5 saved stations that you can tune into to transmit your signal, which I find nice for those areas when you start picking up other radio stations and there is bleed through. I didn't realize this at first, but the radio does have an internal transmitter, though I don't know if having it directly plugged into a transmitter will make any difference. So far mine has done nicely without the help of a third party transmitter. The little screen is nice too. It is not a touch screen, but you can see it well during the daytime and I find that for me the brightness at night is just right, not super blinding bright, but not so dim that you can't see it either. The radio also works similar to DVR and you can rewind to play a song again.

Set up is fairly easy and the instructions are easy to follow as well. I'd say it may take 30 minutes to an hour tops to set it up (that includes tucking away cords and positioning it where you want it) and activating it.

It does not come with a remote, but I think it would improve the experience of going through the channels, especially when driving, so you can still keep your eyes on the road and change the channel if you are wanting something different from your presets. Also, I believe you have to have a Sirius dock/boom box of sorts if you want to bring it inside and play music. You can transfer this radio between cars too, depending on your setup though, you may want to have a secondary dock and antenna set up in the second vehicle so its easier to transition and your not having to drag the dock and accessories around from car to car.

Something to take into consideration if you are thinking of getting this radio or other xm radios is that if you are not familiar with the subscription charges, is that you will have to pay the subscription fee, your state tax and a royalty fee and there is an activation fee. So outside of tax, I didn't realize there were other charges with the subscription fee. Personally I went with the 10.99 subscription and my fees were estimated to be 14.99 (this will probably vary from location to location), so not too much extra on regular fees after the activation fee. Just something to know so your not caught by surprise.

If its really cloudy or if you are under something like a metal awning/covering, the signal will go out.

I think the only thing that I don't like about the radio is the antenna. The reason I don't like the antenna is because the cord is too long for how I use it. I keep the antenna inside my car and the signal works fine, but the cord is ridiculously long. It could be upgraded to a motorcycle antenna, which is about 8 inches long, compared to X amount of feet. For others this won't be a problem, because you may need every bit of that extra cord, so it just depends on how you plan to set it up.

I had an older version and the upgrade is worth it.  Just have the volume and power on one remote is great.  The streaming is faster and less interrupted.  Fast easy.  Even my mom can use it with simple voice commands.

Gets the job done and is well built  The fans are far from quiet but they aren't loud enough to make you stop using it.  I love the dual switch so you can control how many and which fans get turned on.  I was on the market for a while looking at different cooling products.  This was the best of them and I have no regrets with the purchase.

What I like about this:
1. It is USB powered. I have a USB port sitting on my desk and when I need the fan I plug it in and adjust the fan head without any effort.
2. It is little - easy to tuck away in my drawer when not in use
3. It is nearly silent. I work in a crowded work area and this fan is not adding to the noise level at all. In fact noone has ever noticed when I've had it turned on.
4. Cools me not everyone around me. I walk to work and in the summer months I would get to my desk a tad overheated. I needed something that would cool me off quickly. This did the trick without bothering anyone around me

What I don't like about this product:
a) I don't like that there isn't an on/off switch. I would like to leave it plugged in when not in use or turn it off for the purpose of adjusting the fan head. This fan doesn't support either of those two needs.

I would buy this again in a heartbeat - I would highly recommend this product to someone needing a quiet, personal fan.

Received the keyboard/mouse yesterday. It was extremely easy to set up. I used this combo, right out of the box, within minutes of opening the box. I waited until the end of my work day to load the software and set up some of the keyboard shortcuts. I have a true split keyboard which I love in one work location and had a standard keyboard in another which has been replaced with this new one. The wave design will take some getting used to but it is definitely more comfortable to use than the standard. I have found the zoom buttons on the left side to be very useful. The application switcher is something that I am not sure that I will use. I tend to use Alt+Tab when I need to switch applications. I may end up programming that button to do something else. I do like the fact that with the Word Function key I can program that to open a specific folder that I access frequently to hold my in-process documents.

About the only thing I do not like about this keyboard is that it does not sit on all four feet. I've tried using all the angle options and still the keyboard rocks. From what I can tell the keyboard is just formed/molded in such a way that it doesn't sit flat on a surface with all four feet touching. This doesn't affect the use of the keyboard or mouse - it just one of those things that I noticed and that annoys me.

Update 1/29/2013: I noticed today that the keyboard no longer rocks. I am not sure why - the work surface hasn't changed but since it was the only annoyance I had with this product I thought it was important to come back and update my review.

I don't use all the buttons on the mouse (left, right, scroll up/down) so I can't comment on the usabilty or function of the other buttons. The mouse is smooth to work and I like the fact that there is a compartment within the mouse to store the USB receiver.

I could not believe how nice this little speaker sounds for the price I paid.  Really, it worth much more.  Great features, easy to use, good battery life and come with everything you need for various configurations.  It is heavy and seems very well made.  I recommend this device.  It does not have a strap, and there is no way to attach a strap.
A nice-looking mouse that works well, feels very good in the hand, and has a nice, quiet click.  I have used mine for a couple of weeks with no issues.

I purchased this as a gift for an old friend.  Charged it. Copied some 40's music to a micro SD card and fired it up.  Sounds great and is easy to manage.  He is just going to play MP3s.  My friends loves it.  Time will tell if it holds up.

These headphones work well and sound just fine.  I have paired to a Nexus 7, iPad, and computer with no difficulty.  The are comfortable and the battery lasts a long time.  I have had no problem with range up to twenty feet or so.

I purchased this player just for audio books and it works great. When you turn it on it remembers where you were in the book when you last shut if off. Really works nice. Get a good set of headphones for real pleasure.  The case is a little flaky. I used some clear book tape to reinforce the joints and it much better. Many hours of play time on one AAA rechargeable battery. I recommend it.
Stays in very well and I like the sound quality.
My headset needed this since my last one was bent at the metal usb port. Pretty expensive for a small piece but it is required and it's better than buying a new headset altogether.
Bought it for my brother and he likes them. Sound quality is pretty good.

My Kindle is almost like an iPad; it has so many capabilities. It seems that I keep learning new "how-to's" every day. It's really so much fun. I like the fact that it has the CLOUD capability so that I can use it with other products.

The only reason I didn't give the KINDLE FIRE a 5-Star rating is because I believe it would REALLY be the best ever if it had a 3G capability. There are so many times I could have needed that capability; loved having it in my other KINDLE! Also, I'd love it if there was an automated orientation to this product.

Tips are easy to install, come with a protective mesh to keep gunk from getting into the pod mesh, and conform so well to your ear canal that it makes the noise cancellation work better! It also makes the AirPods far more stable in your ear, almost customizing the fit. I bought this version for my kid, and they couldn’t believe the difference.

Wow! These tips are a game changer!!! I only recently decided to break down and invest in AirPod pros, and see if all the hype was legit. The sound was incredible, and the noise cancellation was amazing, but those silicon tips that came with them! What the heck?! The mediums were too big and hurt, the smalls were way too small, and my EarPods would fall right out while I was just sitting at my desk. I noticed that I was rarely using them, because I had to choose between being annoyed and having my ears hurt.

As a desperate measure, I decided to find out if anyone made foam replacement tips, and I came up with Abazar memory foam tips. The clock into place just like the Apple OEM tips, but HOLY COW! The mediums (for me) feel like I have custom ear tips! I tried to see if I could shake them out, jump them out, even Burpees didn’t shake them loose. Also, the noise cancellation is AMAZING with these memory foam tips! Also, I got the black tips, which contrasts well, and makes them a little more visible if I lose track of them at my desk. If they had Red, Blue or Orange, they’d really be easy to find!

I've used this adapter with my iPad and a 60% Ducky mechanical keyboard, and boy is it the way to go if you want to leave your laptop at home, and travel with a few small items instead. What I didn't know, is that my kids would enjoy using it to connect peripherals like their vlogging microphones to their iPhones for their social media stuff etc.

The trick is, when using a peripheral that draws power from what it is connected to, you will have to use the input to plug in your adapter to a charger, then the device into the usb port, and you're off to the races. Just remember that the iPad requires the large block plug, or their won't be enough power to push to the microphone or mech keyboard.

I purchased these after trying a similar set in the same price range. The sound on these is quite good, and the positioning in the ears can further isolate the ambient noice. They have proven to be waterproof, and secure when placed firmly in the ears. The charging case can charge the ear buds at least three times. I had to remove one star because the range is a bit limited, and the battery life on each charge is pretty low, at about 3 hours of playback. However, at this price point, the sound is comparable to ear buds at three times the cost, so the battery and range issues can be somewhat forgiven.

I have owned Bose and Beats, and these Plantronics are in that same league, only they cost up to $100 less. Highs are bright, lows resist distortion even at higher volume, and the noise cancellation performs excellently. I'll buy these again when the time comes, and skip past the costly brands.

I've been replacing old hard drives with this product for years, and have never had any issues with them. This one has run like a champ on my kid's hand-me-down laptop. Easy to install and easy to image, these hard drives have performed well in relatively adverse conditions. Quiet and reliable as well.

These headphones are a Godsend. My kids listen to the most modern (noise) music I've ever heard, and they play the most (irritating) stimulating video games on their tablets. These headphones keep the peace (and my sanity) quite well. They've stood up agains the (abuse) use that two unruly grade school kids can dish out, and have even resisted the puppy's attentions, though I wouldn't recommend keeping them in a puppy's path for too long. I tried them out myself, and the sound is surprisingly good for such a reasonably priced headphone.

Long battery life, comfortable, great range, the only real complaint (and why the loss of a star) is the sound. The base is good, but there seems to be an issue in getting the volume to go to max. I don't mind hearing ambient noise, because it keeps me from getting run over, but when you're at the gym, you can just hear your music over the garbage they play over the speaker system. Oh, and the little charger cover eventually broke off, which is a shame because I used to wear them when I was casually swimming and didn't want to annoy the neighbors with loud music.

*****UPDATE***** After the most recent firmware update, my headphones are suddenly able to to max, and there is very little distortion. It's been a year and the battery life still kicks serious butt, the range is still awesome, and the sound is nearly as good as my Bose. You can still hear the important ambient noise, such as traffic etc.,

The sound quality is good, and it is loud, but these speakers don't want to daisy chain wirelessly as advertised. I was only able to get two speakers worth of sound by connecting it with the attached cords, and then one speaker was perpetually quieter than the other. The problem seems to be that, at the Bluetooth level, the device only wants to recognize one speaker at a time. If anyone has a solution to fix this, I will restore the star, because the only reason I bought these two speakers was for the daisy chain capabilities.

I usually do a lot of research before I buy anything, mainly because I hate to waste money, but also because I'm too lazy to return things, so I end up suffering with the 'crappy' until it finally breaks beyond repair. So after a ton of research, I was pretty sure that this speaker system was going to be worth the cost, but happily, I'm blown away. You get A LOT more sound for the price with these speakers. I am a Bose fan, but the cost can vary from expensive, to 'are you flippin kidding me!'. I initially bought these just to get more sound out of a computer that we sometimes play movies on, but now I'm thinking about buying another one of these for the main entertainment area, they're that good. The base is deep and you can push the volume all the way to the top without vibration or annoying distortion. Highs are crisp and clear. There is a light in the jellyfish looking woofer, which you can't dim, but it sheds about the same amount of light as a nightlight, so it really isn't a bother. I can recommend these, and I will be purchasing them again.

This case is definitely as good as the first iPad defender case, with major improvements in the way that the port coverings work. I found the first iPad port covers to be a bit unreliable, and slightly ill fitting right from the beginning. We've had this case for almost a week, with the charging ports opened and closed frequently, and the port coverings still fit extremely well. We have had one accidental drop already. The device was unaffected, and the case withstood the impact perfectly. It would have been nice if they had a few color choices, as we keep mistakenly taking the other's iPad, but that's really the only complaint I have at this time.

*Updated: After many months of severe torture testing, these cases have stood the test of time and trial. The iPads are injury free, even though the cases have taken quite a few hits. It's bulky, and boring looking, but if you want to really protect your investment, the Otterbox case can't be beat.

*****Edited to Add Update******

It's been quite some time now, and the iPads that have this case on it are still in perfect shape, but the one which didn't have this case on it suffered a fall and glass break (mine). Guess which case I'm using now. The older cases are still 'in the box' new in condition, and that is through a lot of abuse. The stands are all still working too. There have been many spills onto concrete, tile and hardwood floors, and so far the cases did the job without breaking.

This is a good alternative to the more expensive brands, because it performs just as well for a fraction of the price. The battery use (rechargeable Sony NP-FM70 in my case) is minimal, I've experienced great battery life with this light. The color filters are adequate, and the diffusing filter is very useful, but I haven't tried to find out if other filters work with this light.

My only complaint is in the build quality for the dimmer wheel. With repeated use, the screw that kept the wheel in place unwound itself and came loose in the case. Luckily, I'm handy, and was able to disassemble the case (very easy) and replace the screw, which had managed to escape the case entirely before I could rescue it. The wheel works now, but I have to be very mindful to be gentle while using it. A replacement screw for a sunglass arm will fit nicely in it's place if you should face the same problem.

I would have rated the product a five of five if this issue with the build quality hadn't happened. The light is a very good performer otherwise.
I use it to connect to a speaker without having to use bluetooth. I also keep one in my car for aux purposes. Sounds comes through great. And it feels nice and quality.

This is much wider than I would have expected. I may have underestimated the size required to support three 27" monitors. It is easy to install and feels very sturdy. From looking at the images you shouldn't be surprised by any of the features or limitations. The only thing that I think may be unclear is that the side arms are in two parts and meet at the middle bracket. Because of this they are always mounted symmetrically. Something that may be relevant if to you if you mount your monitors asymmetrically.

Sounds pretty good. "Noise cancellation" is true somewhat, earbuds can only do so much in passive noise cancellation. Sounds comes through fairly nice otherwise.
The build quality is where these really shine for me. The cable looks and feels nice. The end pieces appear to be all metal. I've been very happy with these ear buds.
I use it to hold several SD cards and an adapter. I usually keep it in a (Altoid) tin. It required a fair bit of hacking away at the corners to ensure a good fit. Otherwise a decent enough product.
Used for at home access to things requiring smart card certificate. (CAC) I like how portable it is, how easy it is to store.

I haven't ever used this to burn anything, but it reads optical media like a champ. My previous one required two USB-2A plugs to run, this uses a single USB-3A. Transfer rate is very good. I generally use it to rip CD and DVD, I don't know how well it works for watching media.

I use the USB3 version with DisplayLink and two monitors. All of the things I run on those are pretty static so I go pretty light on it. I haven't noticed lag at all. I had trouble deciding which dock to choose, I ended up rather pleased with this one.

I enjoy this keyboard. I chose it over other others due to size and the novelty of the circular keys. It is closer to chicklet style in terms of key travel and feel, but the response is a little softer than a true scissor-chiclet keyboard. I'm not very aggressive with my typing so I don't really notice much difference in comfort between this and my mechanical keyboard. I do however notice the sound, this one is absent the cacophony that comes with the mechanical. The battery life is great and the Bluetooth is reliable. If I somehow managed to kill it, I would most likely buy another or try a newer/similar model from Logitech.

Great radio for the price. While tuned to walkie frequencies it did pick up interference from users that were very far away. After using it for a while I would agree with the assertion that this the perfect starter radio to get you hooked.

Already much better than the more expensive Asus Collection Pen my Transformer Mini came with. It worked straight out of the box--no setup required and isn't disconnecting or reacting to my palm sitting on the screen (which I assumed was a problem with the tablet, not the pen). It's also a little shorter than the Asus pen (this isn't a pro or con, just an observation).

I'll update this if it becomes anything less than a five-star product. My only disclaimer is that I only have the Asus Collection Pen that came with a refurbished computer to compare it to.

UPDATE 1: Day 1 and the eraser button is sticking occasionally. Not a huge problem, but enough to show the pen isn't perfect.

I have purchased a lot earphones. But these are the only ones that are still going strong in both ear buds right and left.

Only slight improvement would be to be able lower volume to lower levels. If in a super quiet environment.

Bought this to keep peace and harmony. Especially when viewing and/listening tastes don't mesh at times when one is trying to unwind. The cord is long enough to lay down and still be connected to a portable device bedside. Great for travel or even at home. Sound quality is amazing.

Have yet to find anything negative. But will definitely update if something goes terribly wrong.

I've had questionable luck with smallish music products, so I didn't expect much from this one, but I was so wrong! Right out of the box I was impressed by the thoroughness of the manual and the fact that it was written in comprehensible English (Most are a couple of small pages with translations that are confusing and often weirdly hilarious.)

The user interface is clean and clear, the controls do exactly what they're supposed to do. (Every time I thought they didn't, it turned out to be my own fault.) and the sound quality is excellent for a radio this size. T he scan for local stations was fast and accurate, and the reception, even with the telescoping antenna unextended is excellent. The sheer number of internet radio stations available -- via really well thought out menus, I should add -- could keep you listening happily for years. Even as a classical music listener, I found so much worth marking as favorites. That doesn't happen all that often!

I originally misread the listed price (or it was on sale when I made the product request, I'm not sure which) and had thought it was about half the listed price I'm seeing today. I was going to jump up and down and wave my arms and shout about how at that price EVERYONE needed to order one because it was just that good. Now the price seems to be about twice what I originally thought it was, and y'know what? I'm still wildly enthusiastic about it, and recommending it to all my friends. This really is a radio to consider, IMO.

I was knocked out by the sound quality and power of this little thing.  I mostly use it as a radio, and it does a great job of picking up local stations.  The only quibble I have is that because of its size, it's much too easy to bump the channel knob while you're turning on the unit or adjusting the sound level.  I could have wished for a channel lock feature so I wouldn't have to futz around retuning it if I've accidentally moved the dial.  Also, it's really cute in a retro way.  I'm very pleased with it.

I was looking for a good, basic clock radio to replace the one I had that had begun to behave as if it was possessed by a demon.  This one... well I wasn't sure but the price was good, and it absolutely fit the space requirement so I requested it, and was pleasantly surprised.  Many clock radios are miserably hard to set and program, but this one is surprisingly easy.  The instructions are clear, and it doesn't take any extraordinary effort to get the time, day and year set, or to add station presets to the mix.  The dimmer is excellent.  At Level 1 it's just bright enough for me to read without disturbing my sleep.  The sound is good, the bluetooth function works well, and is easy to activate.  It charges my phone overnight just the way a direct connection to a power strip would.  In short, it's everything I would ask for.

I have drawers and bins full of old media that I can't find anywhere else, and very little option for conversion, at least very little that doesn't cost me more than I can currently afford. The Geeklin is a good option for me. It's easy to use, and can be run on batteries (I probably wouldn't recommend that if you're converting.) or via a USB plug. For conversions, just plug a flash drive into the unit, press play and record, and it's done. You can set it to play both sides of the cassette, or stop at the end of the side. The sound quality is decent, but nothing special.

I see that it does other things as well, but I've been so wrapped up in converting my old tapes, I haven't even bothered to explore. Once that job is done, I can play, and I will!

This is a strange little speaker, but it does the job. The sound is good, obviously not high-end audio, but now I can listen to my audiobooks while I shower, or when I'm working around the house and don't want to be wearing headphones.

It's compact, with a compartment in the bottom that holds the charging cable (USB to, I think it's mini. I never remember the name.) It also comes with a cable that you can use to connect it to the headphone outlet on your phone rather than use the bluetooth. It's loud enough to be heard over running water, and of course waterproof. I wish the hanging strap was a bit larger, but it'll do.

These little guys take a bit of getting used to. I still can't put the right one in my ear without triggering the woman who lives inside it to play music when all I want to do is listen to my audiobook. But once I got the hang of them, got them paired with my new phone (didn't work great with the old one) I found that I really liked them. The sound is lovely and clear, and I can walk half an apartment away from my phone and still listen without the signal disappearing. The ear buds themselves are surprisingly comfy, and they stay put. Why can't everyone build ear buds that stay in your ears?

I still haven't used them to answer a call, but that's mostly because I almost never answer calls. I get maybe one a week worth answering, and so far that's never happened when I have the ear buds in. It's no big, really, I just want them so I can do housework and listen to books or music without the sound being drowned out by running water, or a vacuum cleaner. And for that, they're great. I'm guessing it would make a commute on public transportation much pleasanter without bothering everyone nearby.

I was a little skeptical when I received these. I do have trouble with a lot of the earbud-style headphones which tend to shuck around in my ear, hurt, or slip out if I'm moving around at all. But these are comfortable and the choice of sizes means that I have the right fit for my ear canal. There are also over-the-ear hooks to ensure they'll stay on, and even these aren't uncomfortable.

The sound is really quite good. I was astounded by it. On the downside, the set-up was a little iffy. I never got the audio instructions and had to suss things out for myself. But that wasn't difficult. I was up and running in a matter of minutes.

The controls are a little persnickety. I'm always hitting the voice dialer when I'm trying to adjust the volume, and answering calls... I'm just not that good at it. It's going to take some practice. Since I rarely am willing to talk to anyone anyway, it's not a big deal for me.

There are some trade-offs, but all things considered these are nice hands-free headphones.

Disclaimer: I was sent this product to evaluate so that I could write an informed review.

Actually this is my second LotFancy cooling pad, and I took it because I do like their products. I haven't had any bad experiences with them except for breaking off one of the little plastic stops that keeps your laptop from sliding off the pad when the rear is elevated, but that was entirely my fault. I left the pad on the floor and someone stepped on it. Can't blame LotFancy for that.

The design of this pad is kind of interesting. It has two controls, one for the large center fan and the other for the four smaller side fans. This, plus the width of the pad itself, allows you to use various sizes of laptop efficiently. If you have a small one, you never need to turn on the side fans. If you have a 17" one, they're in position to help you cool it. I'm curious as to why the green light (signaling that the center fan is on) is set so much lower than the light for the side banks. A strange feature, though not something I have a problem with. It's just odd.

The pad is adjustable to seven different heights (including flat), so you've got a lot of positions to choose from. I write in a variety of places around the house, so this is one of my favorite things about the pad. It allows me to work without having to find all sorts of things to prop my laptop on. The locking mechanism is solid. Since it's USB-powered, there's an extra USB port at the back so that you don't lose that functionality. Most cooling pads have some way of doing this, so it's expected rather than special. It's quiet, but it's far from super silent.

It's a good pad. Yes, some of the construction seems a bit flimsy, but my other LotFancy pad has held together just fine and I see no reason to think this one won't.

I came to this tracker cold. The Housemate has a Fitbit, but I never used it, and really haven't paid a lot of attention to what it did so I had no expectations of what the Pivotal Living tracker might do. However before I tell you what I discovered, let me explain some things about myself. I'm in my sixties, and have a sedentary job. I would like to be more active, I would like to compare my actual sleep habits against what I perceive them to be, I would like to keep an eye on hydration. I have some other goals, but these are the main ones that apply to my use of the tracker.

So how does the Pivotal Living tracker stand up to these goals? First off, because so much of my everyday movement is not easily measurable by the tracker, I'm not really getting an accurate step count. (Moving around the house holding things doesn't always register. Sitting and doing something like folding laundry sometimes does.) This is a bit of a problem because it makes it difficult to estimate how I'm doing on my step goal. So, accuracy in step count? Not so much. Going to stick to a pedometer or pedometer app. C, maybe C+ because I can set my own goals based on my health and how my day is going. (Right now I have a torn meniscus, and all my steps are limping or cane-assisted. Not fun, and not conducive to accurate step counts.)

Hydration? Great, unless you forget to enter an amount until after midnight. Whoops, sorry, can't add anything to your daily total. This is a huge oversight IMO. I sometimes finish my daily amount late in the evening when I'm not thinking about using the mobile app. However, the process of tracking it on your own is a good one. They simply need to fix the access problem. B+

Daily activity. Honestly I have NO clue how this is tracked. I'd have thought it was step-based, but I've never yet had daily activity show up on my dashboard, so there has to be some other way this band tracks activity. However, having an activity alarm that reminds me to stop what I'm doing, get up and walk around for a few minutes... that's immensely valuable to me. Without it, I'd simply forget and keep on writing or editing. I'm going to give it an A because I love the alarm which can be set for 20/40/or 60 minutes.

The rest? Sleep alarm... I've been wakened by this exactly once, when I was very nearly awake anyway. Every other morning it's done zip. I'll wake up an hour later and think, "Wha?" It's back to my clock radio. C, at best. However the sleep tracker seems surprisingly accurate based on what I remember of my nights. It fairly accurately charts how many times I've woken up, and how much good sleep I've gotten. I find this quite reassuring. A, even A+.

Calories burned: Since this is both step and activity based, it's pretty useless for me. Anyway, my goal isn't about calories, it's about activity, so I'm not going to grade this part of the app. Also, weight: Clearly this is another sub-app like hydration, which requires you to input your numbers. It keeps my weight in front of me which is a good thing, but it's not really something I feel I can adequately grade.

Problem: If you take it off it will turn itself off. I tried to put it on my desk when I was typing since it interfered with the position of my wrist. I could hear the activity alert when the band buzzed against the desk, but then it stopped because the tracker had shut down. I thought it was out of juice and couldn't figure out why I was getting less than 24 hours on the battery. When I finally figured it out, I had to start wearing it up high on my arm. Fortunately the band is big enough to allow it to sit several inches above my wrist.

Price: Very, very good. I recognize that the modest cost of the tracker is intended to get you to buy the yearly subscription, but I don't mind that. If the service works, I'm happy to pay $1 a month for it. That's still minor league stuff. However I get frequent errors saying that the goal information can't be updated from the site, and I get odd readings on my dashboard. However, by the end of the day it's usually sorted itself out, so I don't have a lot of quibbles so far.

Overall, and taking price into account I think I'd give this a B, at least for my needs. It reminds me of the things I need to remember to do, and it gives me a place where I can keep track of those goals. The cost to do this is, as I indicated, quite modest. If you're not ready to drop a lot of money on a more sophisticated tracker, give the Pivotal Living tracker a try.

Note: I'm using this on a Fire phone, which means I had to side-load the app. The instructions on how to install Google Play and everything else you need to side load Google Play apps are available on You Tube, and it's dead easy. Once you've done that, just go to the Play Store and download the Pivotal Living app, and have at it.

This came perilously close to being an angry review of Windows 8 the first week I had the 13, but then I calmed down, learned enough about how to navigate the new OS, and began to enjoy the computer for its own sake. It's a fast, powerful little number with a startlingly quick boot up, something I can't say for any of my other machines. It multi-tasks better than any computer I've ever owned, and I'm not just talking about having Chrome open with a couple of Word documents. I'm talking a couple of graphics-intensive programs plus Spotify, plus a web browser with a lot of open tabs. Basically a bunch of memory hogs couldn't even slow the 13 down, and I am loving that.

Why? Well I'm not a gamer per se, so what's important to me is that I can do the work I do -- I'm a writer, editor, and artist with a lot of social media outlets -- in the way I want to do it, which is often a matter of moving from one program to another, to work in a limited time frame. With music. The 13 can handle everything I throw at it including large graphics files, without a wibble. The games I do play play flawlessly and look terrific.

Specifics: The keyboard is fairly compact, and there's no number pad, which I miss only a little. It has a good feel, which is important for anyone who spends hours typing. The screen is small, obviously, but it's bright and crisp. Graphics look good on this screen, though I have noticed that color is rendered a bit differently than on my other laptops. I haven't tried adjusting it yet. Once I start printing out my art, I'll do any color adjustments I need to do. The sound? I love it. It's clear and warm, nothing tinny or muddy about these speakers.

It comes loaded with some decent software. There's not a lot of bloat here. What you get is useful or genuinely fun, like the Alien FX which tickles me because it allows me to change the lighting theme. Yes, yes, I know that's fru-fru stuff, but I like the shiny. Oh, and a terrabyte HD? I am so there. I have a lot of media files, and that lets me keep them all in one place rather than having to store them on an external hard drive. And speaking of drives, do be aware that there is no optical drive in this unit. If you need one you'll have to get a stand-alone. This isn't a huge hardship, they're not expensive these days. It's just a bit inconvenient.

Look, the bottom line here is that if you can afford a computer just for gaming you can probably afford something bigger and better. But if you also have to use your computer for other things, work, school, a life... this is going to serve you pretty well, in my opinion. If, like me, you want to do graphics work on a laptop (My desktop is ancient and creaky but up to this point was the only machine I had that could support Photoshop effectively.) this is a machine to consider.

My job requires hours of work wearing headphones, and though I've tried a lot of different ones, none have been entirely satisfactory. Usually around hour 4 they start to give me a headache. I've also found that the distortion can be difficult to work through, making my job harder than it really should be.

When I tried the Sony MDR1As I didn't hold out much hope that they'd be significantly better than any of the others I've tried, but I was mistaken. They're much more comfortable over the long term with generous sizing for my big, pumpkin head, and a nice amount of padding, so that they don't actually press too firmly against any single spot on my head. This seems to cut down on the headache factor. The position of the cord is convenient, and the cord itself (They come with two.) is a heavier one than I'm used to, and doesn't kink up as I work

But the real pleasure is the sound. I can hear a much broader range of sound allowing me to do my job faster and more efficiently. I don't just use them for work, though honestly if I did, I'd still think they were worthwhile. But the quality of my music is so much better that I sometimes forget I'm wearing headphones. It's utterly involving to hear music this rich and full. It gets into me in a way I rarely experience except during live performances.

I'm sold on them, which is a good thing, considering the price! I honestly never thought I'd say I thought a pair of headphones were worth this sort of money, but I'm quite prepared to admit I was wrong about that. I think these are, and I'm happy to have them, both for work and play.

This is not a bad clock radio for the price I paid. It's not a great one either, but it fit the profile of what I wanted with one exception, which I'll get to in a bit.

First off, it's smallish, which is a blessing on a crowded nightstand. The display seems fine to me, neither too bright, nor too dim. It's easy to program, thank goodness. I've had a lot of electronics that require three hands, and a stopwatch to be properly programmed. The ICF-C218 has a button or a dial for each function. Just follow the instructions and you'll be fine. It's a bit hard to see the radio dial unless you pick it up, but that's a minor thing for someone like me, who pretty much keeps it on one station. It's not programmable; you have to change the station with a tuning dial. However the reception is excellent, even without an external antenna.

My quibble, and it's a relatively small one, is that the sound is tinny. I don't expect a lot out of a small radio like this, but I have a Sangean which is even smaller, and the sound is much better. It's not a deal-breaker, I got what I wanted in every other respect.

Bottom line: Good price point for a basic clock radio with excellent reception, and so-so sound.

I've been using a Master Cooler pad with my laptops, and have been really satisfied with it, but when I was offered the AVANTEK, I figured I should at least try it. You never know, right? And I'm happy I did because the AVANTEK Chill Mat is an excellent product, and one that I know I'll use all the time.

It's lighter than my old cooling pad, and keeps the laptop even cooler. The trade-offs are minor. The fan is a bit louder than the old pad, though I've already stopped being aware of it. There are only two heights, flat and slightly raised, where the old pad had four or five, making it a bit more flexible. And there is only one USB port on it where the old one had four. This is a pass-through on the USB plug that connects to the laptop, a fairly efficient design. It works perfectly.

The blue light... well that's odd. I don't know what it's for beyond looking cool in both senses of the word. I don't mind it and I don't love it, but it does make the pad stand out. I suppose I'll be the coolest computer geek at my local coffee house.

All things considered, I think the AVANTEK Chill Mat is a very good deal for the price.

I use headphones for my job, and I'd never been entirely happy with the ones that were provided to me. They were huge and heavy, and very uncomfortable to wear for hours at a stretch. I began using a set of Maxell headphones that I'd used with a Walkman -- so you know how old they were -- but the sound was never as good as I'd hoped. When the foam pads finally wore out, I knew I had to pop for a new set, so I chose these JVCs.

I'm very pleased with them They're light and easy to adjust, and the sound is a whole lot better than my old Maxells or even the enormous earmuff headphones that came with the job. The only problem I have with them is that they're kind of hot to wear in the summer. However they manage to muffle the screams of the brats next door, so it's all good.

The ones I got were a beautiful royal blue, nothing like the photo. I expect you get what you get. No biggie, they work the way I want them to, so I'm happy.

I had a bit of trouble with the dongle at first because Windows 7 wouldn't discover it.
