Well, we really had nothing to worry about with this TV.  There is no ghosting while watching action onscreen, like some LED/LCD models we'd looked at.  The difference in definition is really not noticeable - the difference between 720 and 1080 is barely noticeable with the human eye, anyway.  We watched several shows in the first few days with the mock 3D feature (a selection on the remote allows the TV to change a regular 2D show into 3D).  The only issue we had was a bit of eyestrain from wearing the glasses for an hour or two.  I have a heavy vision correction; this could be a factor.  Another issue is that we still need to purchase more glasses for the rest of the family - the kids faces are a bit small for the adult sized glasses.  They're also expensive and easily damaged.  Another factor (if you're looking at cost) is that to use the 3D capability for movies, a 3D bluray player should be purchased, which is a bit more costly than a regular bluray.  There are only a few 3D movies available.  3D shows on our cable company aren't available yet.  We're considering switching to DirectTV, which has some 3D content already. We really like the 3D feature on this TV - the novelty hasn't worn off yet and we've been using it over a month.  It really makes the whole TV watching experience more captivating.  The sound quality is great - which was a bonus for us.  We had a problem with glare on our other TV, since it sits in a room with a wall of windows.  This TV has a bit of glare, but not as much as we'd expected.  The ability to swivel on the stand is a huge help in preventing the glare while watching in some parts of the room.  All in all, this is a really good TV at a great price - and the 3D feature just puts it over the top.

I bought this as a replacement for my Onkyo 7.1 receiver which bit the dust.  I use it with the speakers that were already installed and luckily they were in the correct impedance range.  The sound is very good and the different modes work well.  the only thing I wish this receiver had was a remote that could turn on my TV too.  My old Onkyo remote did that, but this new SONY does not.

I was a former employee of DIRECTV and received free service from them. Now that that's over this is a great replacement, small and simple!  Just plug it into your TV's USB, or your sound system USB and it will connect to your TV and provide outstand sound and video. You will need a sound system that supports HDMI CP,  it also has apps installed for SLING TV Netflix Hulu and more. I highly recommend this product. Like everything Amazon it's great!

I loved that setup was so easy. True it did not come with paper instructions but as soon as you turn it on it guides you through.  Very easy!  IT does games and surfing and all that.  I was most impressed that it does video calling with no glitches.  IT's fairly fast.  It is a budget item but honestly it's better than expected by a long shot.  Best money i've spent in a long time.  Very pleased. Watching movies the screen is a nice size and the picture and sound is good.  Honestly a great value; why buy more expensive tablets this does everything.  This works for me.
Very comfortable and good quality sound. I would buy these again.

I received this the next day. The flash drive connected to my computer and I quickly moved everything to a folder so I can add them to my microSD card in my smartphone. I listen through my music player. These are not remastered so there is static and skips from aging. Some shows appear to be repeats, though. That may be due to when the shows were re-aired. They are authentic and I love them.

I received this the next day. The flash drive connected to my computer and I quickly moved everything to a folder so I can add them to my microSD card in my smartphone. The entire folder takes up about 3.3Gb. I listen through my music player. These are not remastered so there is static and skips from aging. However, they are authentic and I love them.

I received this the next day. The flash drive connected to my computer and I quickly moved everything to a folder so I can add them to my microSD card in my smartphone. I listen through my music player. The entire folder takes up about 14.2Gb. These are not remastered so there is static and skips from aging. However, they are authentic and I love them.

I received this the next day. The flash drive connected to my computer and I quickly moved everything to a folder so I can add them to my microSD card in my smartphone. The entire folder takes up about 3.3Gb. I listen through my music player. These are not remastered so there is static and skips from aging. However, they are authentic and I love them.
It paired easily and the sound is great.

If you have a new cell phone that does not have an microSD card slot, you may not want to take up so much internal space with music you don't listen to that often. It's nice to have the option of playing a CD on a specific player. Mine arrived well packaged and was fully charged. I like the black and antique gold colors. It comes with in-ear phones but I prefer my over ear headphones. It's easy to use as a CD player. It has an equalizer but I have not yet needed to use it because the bass is more than adequate for me. I have not yet paired it with my car and I will update my review when I do. Overall, I really like this especially because it's rechargeable. No more having to carry or fussing with batteries.

This little boom box packs enough sound for a small room. It's perfect for my mother's room. She is bedridden and wants a radio for her favorite channels. The sound is good and the channels are easy to find. My only problem is that the instruction manual does not explain how to set a channel in memory. I keep plenty of batteries around so she is not tethered by the power cord. She won't use the other functions but the capability to use a storage card is nice.

The form and size of this tablet is nice for being portable. I don't have to take my S7+ everywhere. Plus, it has LTE so I could use this as a backup. One little thing is the tinny speakers. Sound is great when I use headphones but not too loud. My other issue is watching video content online. Most of the time it's great but it spends some time buffering, which ruins the flow of the video. Other than those things, I used a 256Gb microSD memory card which the tablet recognized immediately. A nice black cover was included.
I bought these used, so I did not get the audio cord. However, they paired fine with my computer and smartphone and the sound is great, as it should be.

At last, I finally found a pair of over ear buds that are comfortable and sound good. The case magnet is a little difficult to open, but they are easy to pair with my Samsung Note 20 Ultra. I downloaded the beats app and a bass boost app. They work well together.

At first I was confused by some of the reviews that called this small. It is not small when compared to my devices. It is about the size of my tablet. It was very easy to pair. I tested the bass by playing "Hush" by Deep Purple. It has a strong sound but not the table shaking throb some people like. The speakers are located on either side of the box. The LED is nice at night but I usually leave it off to save battery power. I haven't yet tried the TIF card function. The instructions were okay. It is not a Bose, but it is fun.

This is a versatile set with audio and call functions. I have the burnt copper which reflects a nice reddish-brown color in light. The sound is good compared to another set of headphones I own, the ones named after a DJ/rapper(?). On these, however, I can press the :Sound" button to enhance the bass or make voices clearer. I normally use the cord to connect but Blue Tooth pairing was easy. The ear cups are soft and provide deep cushioning. I have owned Panasonic headphones before. They were great but I lost them and I really miss them. Theses are bigger and bulkier, the sound quality is up-to-date.

This cube is not very small because it has adapters for so many nations plus four USB plugs. The nations are EU, US, UK and Australia. There is also a plug to add other plugs if the one you need is not on the device. If you are like me, you will find this device very useful for frequent travelers.

I have always wanted a good fisheye lens and I was finally able to get this for my Canon 80D. I watched the Digital Goja video on YouTube to learn how to use it. I played with it in both manual and AV modes. It will take some time to get used to because there is no communication with the camera body. I am in complete control of each shot. The distortion depends on the shooting angle and each photo can be amazing. Luckily I have lots of learning time before my trip to the Grand Canyon this spring.

This is a great fixed lens for short wider angle shots. I am an intermediate amateur photographer, so I am as picky about my shots as a pro might be. Still, I like good quality shots that do not require editing. This lens worked great on my 60D and with the 430 EX III-RT flash. The filters are exactly what I needed to complete this set. The cleaning kit was also most useful in the carry pouch provided.

I watched a YouTube video by a guy named Flossy Carter who has the black/gold version of this little gem. I got the white/chrome. It's okay but not as elegant. He played his gangster music as his test, I think I went one better. I immediately tried mine with the theme from Peter Gunn, the version made famous by the Blues Brothers film. This little guy packs a loud sound I can hear from my living room to the kitchen. If you like bass, this is it. It vibrates with the heavy sound. I have the option of pairing with Bluetooth or using an 3.5mm auxiliary cord. It comes with a USB/micro USB cord and a carbinier, both are black. Why send black accessories with a white speaker? Oh well,... There is a rubber ring around the speaker with a loop for hanging. The back of the speaker is lined with silicone for laying down. If you stand it up and play a song with heavy bass, it may start "walking." Just something to be aware of. This is not waterproof, so be careful around the pool. This great for kids, teens and adults.

I am writing this review from my new toy. I watched a few YouTube videos to get a good idea of what this product was designed for. If you are an on-screen artist, this may not fill your needs. If you are a basic computer/tablet user and wants a mobile computer for everyday tasks and a few games, then this works well. The screen clarity is marvelous, but the sound is a little tinny. I don't know about the battery life, but it works well on power. I was able to start up, set up my programs, get online and download several programs with no problem. I downloaded both new and old programs to see how they operate. Everything, so far, has been fine. The included keyboard is easy to type on and is back lit. The magnets are powerful and attached themselves to the tablet when I held the keyboard close. One reviewer complained about bloatware but I found only two programs I wanted to remove right away. It comes with MacAfee and I prefer 360 Total Security. One concern I have is with the overheating (?) of the device. This is supposed to have an internal cooling system but I do not feel it at work. Perhaps it will kick in after the device has been in use for a while. This did not come with the stylus included, so I ordered it. I tend to use the touch pad often but I should find the stylus useful. Overall, this is a nice 2-in-1 laptop. The ability to detach the keyboard and use it when needed is a convenient option. The brushed silver finish makes this a handsome device.

Update 11/25/16: I attempted to add an external DVD player to this laptop but, so far, nothing worked.

I received the touchscreen version of this laptop. I am pleased with that! This is a basic laptop with a large wide screen. The DVD bay seems a little flimsy. I hope it will stand up to less than average use. The initial startup took a while but I was able to get up and running fairly quickly. It immediately connected to the Internet and I was able to establish my Outlook and Amazon accounts fast. The hard drive is noisy but it settles down after the laptop has been on for a while. The touchpad is not always responsive and hangs up sometimes. When that happens, I touch the screen to go where I want. I am not a gamer, so I am not interested in how fast it functions for the latest games. I am a YouTube power watcher. The screen clarity is great and the colors are vibrant. The speakers seem good. They are not too loud, but the sound is clear and it has good bass. I installed Microsoft Office from a different account. I got rid of some of the bloatware. Overall, I was offered this laptop just when I needed it. I wanted to upgrade from my AMD run Toshiba. This functions well for my needs.

I watched a few YouTube videos to get more info about these headphones. I received white but the black might have been a better choice for me. Lots of ear plugs and wings in various sizes, plus a clip and a devise to shorten the cord if it is still too long for you. I usually have an issue with the skip while wearing wireless but these did not skip so far. To be able to listen to a full song without that blank interruption is great. Some reviewers do have an issue with the extra weight the external battery adds, in addition to making the headphones feel off balance. I do not exercise wearing these, so I have not experienced that issue. I tried pairing these with two different phones, a Samsung Note 4 Edge and a Sony Xperia XA Ultra. The sound was tinny on my Samsung and there was little bass. I downloaded the Jaybird app from the Google Play Store and installed it on my Sony. The sound was better on my Sony but with the app, it was amazing. Being able to select different setups or customize my listening preferences really helped. I tried listening to both music and audio books.  Both sounded great. The biggest drawback of these headphones is that you can only recharge them through attaching the external battery. If I lose the battery, the headphones become useless. Overall, these seem great so far. We will see how they age with wear. Hopefully, the company with offer additional external batteries for purchase.

I have a 3 year old Vizio 43" that seemed to work well with this device. The device is more than wide enough to fit under the TV's pedestal. Setup was pretty straightforward. I just happened to have the necessary cables from other devices I was not using at the time. The HDMI cable is important but, if you are a tech junkie, the other cables are usually found around the house somewhere. The sound is adequate. My sister has the surround sound speaker set up, but I was not expecting that level of quality. It was certainly better than the TV's built-in speakers. This may probably work better with a newer TV, but I am pleased with this so far.

I love this! I wish it were a little smaller and less bulky, but it does a great job of adding sound and bass to my smartphone music app. It arrived with a charge, so I could use it straight from the box. There are three choices: flat for little or no bass, M for more bass and L for lots of bass. The connector cables are included and they fit my devices. I know I should not listen to very loud music, but I like the option.

I was looking for in-ear phones that would fit my tiny ear canals. These still do not fit but the sound is good. I like more bass in my music and these project more bass than most earphones I've used. I like the metallic red color because it matches my smartphone.

I have a Canon 60D DSLR. I downloaded the app onto my Toshiba laptop. The app started up right away and walked me through the setup. When I inserted the card in my camera, it took a few moments for the app to locate it. Once it did, it identified the camera make and model. I could immediately start taking pictures and transfer them to my laptop. The transfer happened so fast! Unfortunately I could not make use of the cloud. I travel to places where I do not have an Internet connection, so the cloud would not be useful for me. It is much easier to save to my portable hard drive. The USB card reader is a nice extra should I need it. This is a great card for people who take a lot of photos and want to review them right away on their computer where it is much easier to study them.

I am not a pro, so I do not need to spend $$$ on this already expensive hobby. However, I do like good quality equipment that is affordable. I have a Canon 60D and I bought this filter set to use with my Tamron 18-200mm lens. I replaced my standard UV Haze filter with this HD UV filter and I could see the difference immediately. If nothing else, the +10 macro lens is worth the price.

These are just basic in-ear phones so I did not expect much. I tried these headphones in several different devices: a very old music player, Samsung Galaxy Note 2 and my iPad 4. All gave the same level of quality in sound. I have a pair of Bose and these are not as good, but would be a great back-up if my Bose were to fail or get lost. They are easy to store in my purse and backpack. For the price, you can't beat it unless you insist on pricier name brands. Sometimes, simple can be better.

I wanted some wireless headphones for use around the house. It paired easily and quickly with my Samsung Galaxy Note 2. The bass is great when I listen to music but I do not believe these are noise canceling. Still, they free me from a wire and that is great while I do houswork and hobbies. I ordered the wine color which is great. Making a phone call was easy, too, once I got used to the placement of the controls. The initial charging took a few hours, so I did that overnight. I really like these headphones and I would recommend them.

I can never have too much storage for my Samsung Note II. I like to keep certain media types on separate cards so I can better track how much storage they require. I keep short videos on this one and I have had no problems with access or read times. I think it is comparable to Sandisk but a much less expensive option.

I got this through the Amazon warehouse deal page and paid much less for an unboxed slightly used item. Yes, this is bulkier than, say, a battery sleeve, but the sound is amazing. I played a movie and I could hear very well, so much better than the iPad speaker. I have a portable bluetooth speaker but this is easier to take with me when I travel. It comes with a cover that is also a stand. I downloaded the Thunder app which is free. It's like a mini eq with sound choices for only speaking, music, video and gaming. Installing my iPad inside the case was easy once I realized the slide for the connector moves. I probably should deduct one star for the bulky recharger, but the sound makes up for the archaic recharger.

I ordered the brown leather to match my attache case and purse. It seems well built and sturdy. It is easy to remove the Kindle Fire when I need to clean it. I deducted a star because the speakers are covered and there are oddly placed grill holes for the sound. Otherwise, this is a keeper.

Update: I got this home and listened to a movie. The sound did not seem muffled or distorted, so maybe it doesn't make a difference about the grillholes.

I do plan to buy the 128GB iPad but for now I am enjoying this device. My friend got this Kindle but he didn't like not having a back camera. We traded devices. In terms of price, I think he got the better of the deal, but in terms of performance, I think I did better. I have very close bandwidth in my country, but I was able to download a full movie. I was able to download all my Kindle books. I'm debating about downloading my Audible content to this or leave it on my Samsung Galaxy Note II. The sound while watching a movie is great when listening through headphones. Other reviewers have gone into the pros and cons of this device so no need to rehash their comments. Overall I am please with my trade, but it can't totally replace my laptop. It will strictly be for entertainment.

I have outgrown my Kata backpack now that I have so many lenses. This backpack is larger than I expected and is surprisingly lightweight. There is plenty of room for my camera and accessories plus the laptop section is roomy enough for a 17" and books. I do miss the outside loops to hold a tripod or monopod. Still, it is a very useful bag. There are two ways to access the equipment inside and the rain cover is a plus. I will use this mainly to carry my gear when I change duty locations. I don't like the idea of putting my DSLR in the mail. I own a lot of Case Logic products and I am glad I got this one.

I bought this as a smaller alternative to my iPad. I love the red garnet cover and device. It's a refreshing change from the standard black or white. In the US getting online and downloading apps was quick and easy. This version of the android operating system seems smooth and more user friendly. I added a 32GB microSD card for audiobooks and ebooks. I intend to use this as an ereader but it's nice to have the option of checking email and purchasing more books when I can access Wi-Fi. This was a limited edition issue, so anyone interested had better act fast.

04/07: I still love my device and the beautiful red color, but I am back in Africa and the device is having a hard time staying connected to the Internet. I've read other reviews and some people are having the same problem. I've been able to download a few apps but I have trouble downloading my Kindle ebooks. I took it out of its case but that didn't help. This doesn't work as well as my Galaxy Note 2, which works like a charm and stays connected when I'm downloading. Battery life has been pretty good, though. Overall, this fails as a possible replacement to my iPad. That's okay because this was an impulse buy. Still love the red color-so gorgeous!

I read the reviews but I ordered these anyway because I wanted own everything associated with the HP Vivienne Tam Buttery edition. I have the netbook and mouse, but I don't like the neoprene cases. I just received these and I immediately tried them with an iTunes selection on my laptop. The sound seems fine on mine. The bass and treble come through clearly. My earbuds came with maroon butterflies which really look nice against the champagne casing. My box contained the earbuds, one bag of round earbud covers of assorted sizes, one bag of three-tier funnel type bud covers of assorted sizes, a round zipper pouch and a square microfiber pouch. The push-to-talk button sits a little too high but I like the style. I deducted one star for the price. I understand designer brand items tend to price higher but with all the unhappy reviews would have dropped the price. I bought these at $56, which I think was the lowest I had seen so far. Hopefully my earbuds will last a while. If they don't, I'll update my review.

05/18: I am using these headphones with my Samsung Galaxy Note II. Pause and play will work but not the volume control. All functions work with my iPod Touch.

I bought this to carry my Canon EOS 60D with one lens and two batteries. The holster style is just the right size for transporting just a few pieces of equipment for a short outing. The reinforced bottom is nice and a shoulder strap is included. I deducted a star for my only complaint--the front and side pockets are a little tight for storing bulky items like extra batteries and the charger accessories. I think adding an external flash would also be a tight fit inside. Still, it was a good purchase.

Ordering non-OEM parts for any electronic can be a crap shoot. I ordered this for my iPad 1 because the original cord broke. I need the extra brick and cord because I travel frequently for my job. It came promptly in a resalable plastic bag, always useful, and the items do the job.

I was excited when I bought the previous VT Red and Orchid Mini a few years ago. However, the hard drive was only 60 GB and I need more storage space. I'm not really a butterfly fan but this Mini caught my attention. I wanted this for my collection and I'm glad I got it. This is a truly lovely netbook, muted shades of black and red on champagne gold. It comes with a microfiber sleeve which is fine for me. What makes this useful is the larger hard drive, the extra RAM and the full Win 7 OS. My Mini boots up quickly and it is definitely not slow operating. I got an extra 6-cell battery so I will be really mobile. I also have the matching mouse and pad. I would love to get the ear buds, but they have such low reviews. If they come down in price, I will consider their purchase. In the meantime, I will enjoy this!

04/22/13: I bought the last pair of reasonably price earbuds. Mine are great and have great bass sound. My collection is complete.

I got the brown and silver, which I think is a nice color combination. The ear cups really do noise cancel, blocking out all outside sounds. The cord matches the head part but the controls are set too high up for me. I like bass and one reviewer thought there was too much. For me, it was not enough. I listened to music through my iTouch and iPad 2. These are too bulky to be portable but they are nice for listening to the home stereo.

I wanted to listen to old cassette tapes but I have no stereo system available and I didn't want to buy one just for this purpose. This old players are still useful for basic listening and recording. The front speaker is a little tinny but I didn't expect more. The price was right, too.

I go through ear buds like crazy. I am constantly losing them, tearing the wires or losing the ear cups. I've now added these to my collection. These are about the same quality of sound as other ear buds I've owned. The magnetic backs are a nice touch and make storing them easier without too much cord tangle. The brown color is a little dull but would probably make a nice gift along with a music player or ebook reader.

I wanted a smaller device as a backup to my iPad2, so I bought this secondhand. It was easy to navigate around the contents. I added a N2A(Nook to Android) 32GB microSD card so I can also access android apps and have more storage. Amazon has the best price for that and after installing the card, I can get more out of this device. It was a little frustrating at first to navigate around the android OS but it has been worth it. Sometimes my iPad2 is too large to carry around, and the Nook Color easily slips inside my purse. I am using this mainly as an ereader and note taker. Maybe later I might install some free games. Putting on an antiglare screen helped a lot for when I am in bright light settings. The color and clarity of the content is really nice. I gave this only 4 stars because I think the OS could still use some tweaking. Overall I am pleased.

I have to say I really looked forward to receiving this item. It looks cool and I like the option of rotating the device for vertical or horizontal viewing. The single page user's guide is pretty thorough for such a simple device. The speaker dock comes with 2 types of cords: USB to a power cube and USB to mini USB to connect to a laptop or computer. Set up was easy with my iPad 2. I decided to try it out by listening to Santa Esmerelda's Greatest Hits. I am disappointed in the sound of the speaker. It sounds high and tinny, and it took some time to get used to it. I have a Brookstone travel speaker dock, which is similar but without a pedastal. The sound from its speaker is stronger, much deeper and more stereo-like. This would probably be okay in a small space like an office if you work alone and would like to hear or watch your iPad content. This is not a portable device like the Brookstone dock which has the option of external power or battery power. This would a decent gift for a youngster or someone who is not too much of an audiophile. This will be a good back-up in case my Brookstone fails.

I bought this to use with my iTouch 4th gen and Bose bud earphones. The attachmnent works well. This is not a remote for functions in the iPod or iTouch. It controls the sound only and also can hold/resume a track. I wish there was a fast forward/rewind, but it does the job.

I already own an iTouch 16GB 1st gen. It still works well but I needed more storage for my ever growing TV show and movie collection. I bought mine overseas at a military store that could not keep these in stock. My first thought was how thin it was compared to my old iTouch, nearly half the size. But, recent technology has packed so much more into this small case. I didn't read the specs. I already knew most of what it was supposed to do. I did not know about the external speakers, which sound fine if you make some adjustments. I've watched Blackadder's Christmas Carol and the clarity was amazing. I took some pictures and I don't really like the stills because they seem blurred. The video camera, however, is great. I downloaded the Kindle reader app and was able to sync my existing library. It's nice to see my bookcovers in color and reading the written page is clear and easy on the eyes. The iBooks app is also nice for reading PDFs. Getting online was really quick after locating the nearest free Wi-Fi signal. I use my iTouch mainly for listening to Audible audiobooks, of which I have a massive collection. Because of its size, it is truly more mobile and easier to carry than my Sony Touch ereader, and I don't need additional light to read the screen. Only my netbook gives me more entertainment options because it have much more storage and an external keyboard. The virtual keyboard is small and does the job for typing in website addresses. I would rather use the voice recorder to take notes. I do have a capacative stylus to avoid fingerprints but I will get a screen protector soon. Overall, I paid full price in case I needed to return it for problems. So far, it's been a good deal.

My laptop has a 512MB memory permanently installed, so this is an additional 1GB. My system now reads 1536MB of memory so it seems to be accepted by the computer. My graphics intensive games are still running jerkily but the sound is fabulous.

Whether you are a professional photographer or a serious traveler who likes to take along a camera kit, this backpack more than meets the needs of the seasoned road warrior. When I ordered this, I didn't think 19 inches was so much, but this can handle so much inside and out. It is well padded on the back and on the body straps. The lower part of the backpack has straps for support of the lower back and hips. There are two carrying handles--one on top and one on the side. There are bands to hold a tripod or monopod on the front and side. There is a side zipper to access the laptop pouch which can hold up to a 17" laptop. I have a 16 inch and it slips right in. On top, underneath the handle, there is a slot hiding a strap to connect it to other luggage. On the front the zipper reveals room to carry miscellaneous or personal items. On the bottom of the front, there is a velcro opening to access the rain pouch. Inside the main section there is so much room for carrying the camera body, many lenses and flashes, and more pockets for storing memory cards or whatever you decide. This backpack leaves plenty of room for customizing the interior to meet your needs. Right now I only own a camera body, an external flash, and three lenses. The only thing it is missing is wheels. Fortunately I have a lightweight trolley that I can use to carry this if I don't want to carry it as a backpack. It's big enough to be a cabin carry case if I take out the velco spacers. There is so much one can do with this bag that I highly recommend it if you travel and want to take plenty of camera equipment with you and know it will be well protected.

I am stationed overseas so I had to purchase mine through AAFES(military shopping). I owned a 17" Toshiba previously and in the end, the S6030 won. I am a true road warrior, constantly traveling. Moving from a 12" to a 16" was not as difficult as I thought it would be. The weight is about the same. Startup is a breeze compared to my old HP. Windows 7 is a blessing compared to Vista. The sound of the speakers and the quality of the video really sold me on the A6030. I listen to audiobooks and watch movies and videos, so I needed a laptop that had the best quality I could afford. The speakers are so good that I don't need to carry an extra set. I set up my Dolby and surround sound for the speakers and boosted the natural bass. The sound is great in a large hotel room. I tested my DVD drive with one of my favorite films, "Without A Clue" starring Michael Caine and Ben Kingsley. No Bluetooth is not an issue since I rarey use it. If I should change my mind, I can add a small adapter and software later. I loved my HP TX for as long as it lasted but Vista was too frustrating. I wanted to get another touchscreen slate computer, but brands like Fujitsu are so expensive and HP's TM series does not include the DVD drive. I compared the Kindle 2 and this device for many months and also the nook when it came out. What made me decide on this one was: 1) the variety of documents it could read, 2) the touch screen, 3) the capacity to add more memory through both an SD card and a memory stick, and 4) the solid body construction. I originally wanted red and was ready to order from this website, but this is an electronic device. I have to say the sound is awesome! I downloaded books and some MP3 files to test the audio features. The sound is crisp, not tinny and not too much bass. It's almost as good as my iTouch, but the Reader can't replace it. I loaded language learning files instead of music. It's too bad Sony has no relationship with Audible.

What keeps me from giving a higher rating is the quirkiness of the software and the difficulty of reading in low light. I took the advice of some reviewers and installed a program call Calibre. It converts most ebooks but not Kindle content. If I'm in a well lighted room, I have no problem with reading. I need a portable light source if I want to read in less than ideal situations.

My fingerprints and stains are lightly visibile on the black body. I'm using a microfiber cloth to keep it clean. I ordered some decal covers from MyGift which should take care of the problem. I use one called the Bayou on my Acer Aspire One and it looks great. It will also protect the reader from bangs and scratches.

My reader seemed to be already charged when I took it out of the box. The neoprene slipcover will do until the sturdier leatherette cover I ordered arrives.

Overall, this is a nice product. It's not perfect, but it's an electronic toy that will undergo more improvements as more of the public embraces electronic reading.

Perhaps i got "a good one"…..and if that is the case, I'm a lucky  guy, but it really was the best twenty bucks i last year!

I've been using this on a Win7 laptop (P8400 core2 duo, 2.26ghz), along with other "native" plugins. Without the UAD-2 Solo, my cpu would have been at 100% utilization a couple of dozen Fx instances ago. This card "runs" the plugins, freeing your cpu for your DAW software. Using just the laptop's CPU, each instance of a plugin processor or instrument sucks more CPU, at some point causing noisy artifacts (pops/crackles), dropouts, latency issues, etc.. This card is a GREAT BUY, and includes some prominent, highly rated processor plugins with purchase. It makes my laptop a far more powerful DAW than if I used strictly "native" plugins, e.g. Waves (which are mostly excellent, btw). I do have some Waves plugins as well. Before deciding to go with just your CPU, simply Google "UAD-2 SOLO review" and see what the many reviewers have to say about this new DSP Accelerator. Several forums will give an idea of the many users who are already using it, with Win XP and beyond (as well as OS/X).

Installation/Compatibility:
I know of MANY PC users still running XP sp2 that use the UAD-2 Solo card (or even earlier UAD PCIe accelerators who LOVE them!). The SOLO has been out for 2 years now, and been installed on MANY XP/sp2 systems. Pretty sure that some had to upgrade (ExpressCard) drivers, or their laptop BIOS. Even when using a new Audio interface (USB/Firewire), this is often required. Some call it "maintenance", and it's generally a good thing, to update the software that supports hardware as it get's "older" (1.5 - 2 years, let's be honest). Hardware drivers and bios' are upgraded (improved; bugs fixed), and installing these is, sometimes, as important as installing patches to Windows or any OS (esp. for a laptop in which the card slot was perhaps never used). Laptop manufacturers issue updates for the drivers for _fingerprint readers_, for SD Card readers, etc... It is normal. In a case where a SOLO card needs configuration mods, or driver updates in order to work, this would be an issue with the _laptop_, not with the new ExpressCard item you are trying to use. Nowadays, flashing BIOS or upgrading drivers is quite easy, and to be expected if adding hardware or peripherals to your machine. Even PC CHIPSETS (e.g. Intel 45 Express) have upgrades issued sometimes, allowing support for faster, more powerful CPUs, etc.. that didn't exist when the chipset was built. Bottom line: When adding/upgrading hardware, you may have to tweak, modify or upgrade software. This is the nature of the beast. :)

As for UAD software:
UAD plugins are among the most highly rated software plugins you can buy. Many are designed by, or in collaboration with, the designers of the ORIGINAL HARDWARE being emulated; The Neve console/etc plugins are endorsed by Rupert Neve; Empirical Labs' designer Dave Derr endorses the Fatso Jr (and other) UAD-2 plugins. Not that many plugin processor/emulator offerings have such endorsements.

I now own two emergency types of radios, this one, and another. This means I can compare this to something directly. The following are the reasons why I like this radio more than the other:

1). It’s TINY. It can fit in the front pocket of your shirt or jacket.

2). It’s analogue. This old fashioned tuning style happens to be my preference for radios. It is simple, and you have more control in tuning into the exact radio station that you want without hassle.

3). This radio comes equipped with an antenna extension that includes what appears to be a copper coil. So if you can’t get good reception with this radio’s built in antenna, out comes this Tesla-esque looking attachment!

4). It is yellow jacket yellow. It won’t get so easily lost in the clutter, if you choose not to use it unless hazardous weather conditions are reported.

Now: things that I like less about this radio:

1). It isn’t water resistant/ waterproof

2). For the money, I think that an extra feature or two could be added. For the same price, I also have an emergency radio that has solar panels, reading lamp, compass, an SOS alarm, flashlight, a hand crank, and provides a powered docking station for my devices in case of a power outage.

But to each their own. Perhaps those reading this review aren’t interested in owning an emergency radio that is a transformer. Maybe you want to keep things simple, and are not as enamored of gadgets as I. Regardless of which radio you ultimately go with, and this one is great for size and analogue tuning, you should always keep it charged up and use it frequently enough during non emergency times that you will fully understand how it functions and not be taken by surprise by a random power outage.

If there is one thing I love, it is a “transformer” type of gadget. Well, this little emergency radio is all that, and so much more. Please keep in mind that my review only reflects the use of the radio during non emergency situations. I spent just under two years living in the Great Smoky Mountains caring for a sick, elderly person. We were constantly losing our electric power, so this type of radio became a high priority item. The person for whom I was caring already had one, so that is the only one that I can compare this one to. The radio I am to review today came in a cardboard box titled, “Libovgogo Multifunctional Radio” Inside the box was a very tightly packed radio inside a thin plastic casing and cellophane bag. Within the plastic casing, there was the radio in its box, and extras hidden in little nooks in the flimsy plastic tray. Among the components out of the cardboard box were: a USB charging cable, a spring buckle, a special reset needle, and what appeared to be some sort of vice or clamp. There was also the owners manuel, and additional literature explaining what the additional items outside of the box were to be used for. I then read the manuel, and put this radio through it’s paces. The owner’s manuel identifies my new radio:”emergency radio DF-557/DF-580” According to the enclosed literature, this is the only radio offered with WB/NOAA capacity. The radio itself is made with a hard red plastic casing and black speakers. It features a hand crank, a USB cable, and a solar panel as ways to charge the radio. I tried all three methods, and I can tell you: try to charge vis a vis cable or solar if you can! In the literature, it states that charging with the hand crank will take several more HOURS than the other options! You must have the radio turned off to charge. A little red light goes on when it needs more of a charge, and the light turns green when it is done charging. For the most part, everything worked more or less the way the manuel said it would, with one exception being the SOS siren, which is LOUD. Despite what the literature stated, my radio SOS siren was turned off by quickly pressing the SOS button and releasing very quickly as well. To turn on the siren, press and hold the SOS button. I was amazed at how powerful the reading light was; which can be accessed by raising the solar panel. Equally impressive is the sound quality and volume! This dainty little radio can really belt out loud and succinct sound, especially when you raise the antenna. The sound is so good, in my opinion, that I opt to play this radio instead of my smart devices for enjoyment, and can’t help but notice it sounds just as good as my husband and my son’s speakers. Other added features include a built in flashlight, AM/FM radio, Blue tooth and TF capabilities, and cell phone charging capabilities. I received this radio as a gift, and I am very happy and grateful for it. I would strongly advise customers not to wait for an emergency to put these types of radio purchases through all of its capabilities and become familiar with its functions long before they are ever necessary to know.

I've been a FitBit fan since September 2011. My first model was the original, now known as Classic. My next model was the Ultra. Now I have the One. I'm on my second One and it is a vast improvement over the former models. The design is wonderful; it looks like a gem. The two older models were designed in a hairpin shape & served as the clip. The flaw in the design was that the repeated stress on the curve from attaching & detaching it to clothing caused the curved end to crack. The One's design is slim, polished, and elegant. It slips easily into a silicone, non allergenic holder which has a built in clip for attaching to clothing. The sleep band is also improved. The unit slips into a pocket & the band itself is far more comfortable & easier to don.

The prior models required a charging base. The One charges on a simple design USB charger. This let's me charge just about anywhere; my laptop, PC, a USB wall adaptor, even my car stereo. However, the battery life is unbelievable & charging isn't a real issue & when it does need it, it is completed pretty quickly. The Bluetooth sync is wonderful. With former models, the sync took place while on the charging base. The One comes with a small USB dongle so that whenever my One is within range, it syncs automatically to the FitBit Dashboard (free, BTW); no need to remove the unit from my clothing. ALSO, with a BT smartphone (I have the Galaxy S3), I can sync via bluetooth through my phone app.

The feature set has improved. Not only does it track my steps (and distance), it also tracks my sleep (time I went to bed, time it took to fall asleep, how many times I woke up during the night, time I got out of bed, total time in bed, total time actually asleep), flights of stairs, VAM (very active minutes). I can set goals and it will send me messages to encourage me or award me "badges" for my accomplishments & milestones. I can even set vibrating alarms.

Using the dashboard, I can manually log & monitor my weight, BP, water intake, food intake. FitBit has an extensive database. When you track your activity, it will also track your calories burned. The dashboard also allows for custom goals & provides detailed graphs of progress. There is a huge community of FitBit users that one might choose to join for encouragement and challenges. Additionally, the FitBit is compatible with many, many fitness apps. Finally, the FitBit One is sweat, splash & rain proof.

The FitBit ships complete with the unit, the sleeve/clip, the wireless dongle & the USB charging cable. The customer service provided by the manufacturer is nothing less than STELLAR. And this particular price with free shipping is unbeatable.

Just got this today because we are having wifi accessibility issues in our upstairs guest bedroom (and every good host knows that if you don't have decent wifi in your guest room, you can expect your guests to leave you a holy mess, in retaliation).

Couldn't believe how easy this is to set up, though! I'm pretty tech-savvy, anyhow (after 2 years of various tech-related military schools). Not that I needed to be! The included instructions are incredibly clear and easy to follow. On the contrary, the last AP/repeater I bought merely schooled me in when it's acceptable to take a hammer to one of these things. (FYI: it's right after you've tried, unsuccessfully, for an hour to get it to connect to your wifi). So I really appreciated how simple and fast this is to set up.

How fast, exactly? It literally took like 2 minutes to set up...and only THAT long because I had to go all the way into the other room and log into my laptop to complete the instructions.

Just a head's up, for the less-tech savvy:

This is NOT a wifi signal amplifier, as such. You WILL be creating a NEW wireless access point (aka wifi log-on)...even if you install this in "repeater" mode--vs. the wired-to-wireless AP (access point) mode.

So, for example, instead of logging into whatever your network is called, when you need to use the wifi that this repeats for you, you'll be logging into a new connection. They call it, by default, "My Repeater" (I assume that is so you'll never forget who actually owns it), but you can rename it to anything you want (mine is henceforth known as Fluffy Gigglebuns). You'll still use the same password as you use for your main connection, though...and therein lies the genius of it. You can make your guests feel special (or, in my case, humiliated) by personalizing the repeater network name, but the password will be the same as it is for whatever network AP you are having it repeat.

Lastly, this does offer an extra feature I think is worth mentioning:

You can also use this as a wireless adapter to connect a multimedia or other tech device that requires or ONLY allows internet connectivity via an ethernet (aka wired) connection.

So if you have something like an older roku, or game console, etc. that can only connect to the internet via an ethernet cable, you can apparently use THIS device to quickly convert it to use your wifi connection.

So, about three years ago, I stumbled upon the Fantom Greendrive and was, at first, kind of put-off by the apparent size (it's actually not as big as the Seagate, it turns out). I really wanted something small and portable. But, after all those issues with other drives, I really, REALLY wanted something RELIABLE. I first did some research, took a chance and ordered this drive.

DEAR GOD. IT IS MARVELOUS.

That was, as I've said, three years ago. Three years of constant use: heavy data transfer, being knocked around (even dropped on the ground a couple of times), never defragged (I got lazy cos' it's so reliable), never disk-checked, numerous power-loss and disconnection incidents....nothing can kill it! It hums along nicely no matter what you throw its way.

You don't have to ever worry about unmounting it before you turn off the power--you just unplug it and go. It's never failed me and, to be honest, that makes it better than one particular husband, in my book (the second is doing quite nicely, thank you).

The "Green" is for:

---Firstly, it doesn't take a lot of power. Nice.

---Secondly, despite being dropped a few times, it hums nicely and quietly. No loud grinding at all. I always have to check to see if it's on (which is easy because a green light shines through the grate of the front to let you know the power is on).

---Thirdly, if you have it plugged in but haven't accessed it in a while (like fifteen minutes), it will initiate a semi-hibernation, then go into a bit of a deeper hibernation after like a half hour or so (never timed it, but it's cool when it does it). So if you hear a click and a sound like the motor is clicking off, that's what you're hearing. Cooler still, the minute you click to access the drive it's ready to go--little to no wait.

It's also very fast. As drives go, mine is almost full and THREE YEARS OLD and, like I said, never defragged, yet it still runs faster for data transfer than my brand new laptop...which makes me wonder about my laptop. ;/

I actually love this drive so much, I figured with my bad luck, one day it's finally going to give up on me and quit for good. So, about a year ago I purchased the newer 2TB drive[[ASIN:B002XITVCA Micronet Technology Fantom GreenDrive 2 TB USB 2.0/eSATA Desktop External Hard Drive GD2000EUS]]for more space and extra backup. I love having the two of them because, unlike many products, Fantom keeps the peripherals consistent, so the power supplies (though upgraded to a one-piece rather than two-piece on the newer model) are interchangeable, as are the USB cables (though the 2TB, being newer, is obviously a 3.0 rather than a 2.0). Still, transferring data between the two is easy-cheesy and fast.

So, all in all, I have to tell you that, despite being an incurable tech-geek, this drive is honestly the best, most reliable, and durable piece of electronics equipment I've EVER owned.

This worked just fine for powering a few small items. When choosing what you are going to run on this add up the total wattage of all devices, then add at least 50% more to account for peaks or spikes in the power draw. For example if your coffee maker draws 500 watts, your laptop 300 watts, and your toaster 200 watts (total, 1000 watts) you should account for the extra 50% (1000watts + 500 watts (the 50%)=1500watts). In this example, a minimum 1500 watt inverter should be used.

If the item is motor driven, it requires additional start-up (surge) wattage (typically 2-3 times the continuous wattage required) to start the device. For example, a miter saw that runs at 700 watts might require 1400 watts to start up. If your inverter only supplies 1000 watts, you will not be able to start it up. In this case, you would want to select an inverter rated at least 1400 surge watts to handle start-up needs.

I understand how wattage works and for someone who doesn't, any inverter could fail if overloaded with more power than it can handle. An overload feature that automatically shuts the device off would be helpful for anyone who is unsure. This has an overload feature, but if you blow a fuse, you'll have to replace it. Do your research and know how this works, and it'll work fine.

The speakers are placed above the top row of keys so it gives more of a surround type sound. They aren't anything to rave about but I like the placement.

For the size of this, I feel like a number pad could have been added on the right side of the keyboard. Not a big deal but it would be nice to have the option.

Overall, good value for this chromebook!

I have a 70 inch vizio tv and connected this to my tv with an hdmi and optical cable. I really like that the subwoofer is wireless and automatically connects with the sound bar when powered on.

I was unable to connect via WiFi through my router. Something to do with the security settings that wouldn’t allow it so I cannot perform any firmware upgrades if there are any. I may try a pass through connecting through my Blu-ray player.

The remote is small and simple, the volume and subwoofer buttons do not press down, rather, they push upward and downward to adjust settings. On digital in mode, the sound bar powers on when the TV is powered on.

When connected via BT on my iPhone, I experienced some crackle from the sound bar. I haven’t had an issue with tv connection because it is hard wired but wireless connection even within a few inches of the sound bar produced moderate distortion.

The subwoofer will rock your house. It produces a deep, surround sound and sounds great placed behind my recliner with the sub facing the wall. Sound reflects off of wall to create a great listening experience.

Overall I’m happy with this sound bar and will be looking for add on speakers to complete my setup.

I like that the cord can be removed from these headphones so that if the cord goes bad (and my daughter has a bad habit of destroying cords from pulling them out by the actual cord and not the plastic piece at the end), the entire headphone does not have to be replaced. I like that the volume isn't too loud and I don't have to worry about damaging little ears from listening too loud.

When ordering this, I assumed the speaker would be much larger. I was disappointed when I took it out of the box because it was so small. BUT, this speaker is truly amazing. The sound that comes out is incredible.

To connect your phone or other Bluetooth device, the BT button has to be pressed for 2 seconds. The cool thing is that more than one device can be connected at the same time. Maybe I’m behind on technology but this is the only BT device I’ve used that supports this function.

The range of the volume control needs a little tweaking though. The volume is fairly low at the 1/2 way mark, so the first 1/2 of the volume isn’t of much use to me. I usually like mine set around 8/10. I’ve gotten a good 20-25 hours of play time at this volume. According to the manual, charging for just 20 minutes will get you 6 hours of play time. I don’t know if I go as far to say that this is accurate. I got around 4 hours but for that short of a charge time, while I’m in a rush, getting ready to leave and I throw it on the charger for 20 mins, I know I’ll have my tunes to keep me rockin out!

I really like the sound quality of these earbuds. The bass is decent. The foam ear plug type material caps work well at cancelling out outside noise. The only issue I had was trying to put on the sport portion of the earbuds, it doesn’t come attached so you don’t have to use them. I did find that they stay in my ear better with the sport portion attached.

I wasn't hopeful when I bought these. I've had some pretty low quality earbuds. I like my music loud and always have an issue with distortion. These don't have the distortion and the bass sounds great! Packaging is nice and they fit into my ears well. They come with 2 extra pairs of different sized rubber ear pieces. I was surprised at the noise cancellation these offered as well! The cord looks like it's braided but is actually a pliable rubbery type. I bought them for my daughter to use for her iPad but I think I'll keep these ones for myself!

I was one of the FIRST people to own an iPad back when they were introduced. It was a birthday gift. And, I honestly regret giving up a trip to Disneyland for it. Yes, I had a choice between what I thought was going to be a lifelong, productive item for a trip to Disneyland.

I did go to Disneyland in 2015 though, so I was a few years late. Regrets? Should’ve taken the trip and NOT gotten the iPad. It barely works today (can’t upgrade the iOS due to NOT having a camera – a front facing one for some updates). And, I have it in my desk drawer. REALLY PEEVED at Apple for that one.

So, I’ve been REAL hesitant to jump on the eReader or tablet train. They upgrade, change, and modify so fast. Honestly, I use my iPhone for certain things while I use my laptop. The rest? I use my laptop. I don’t really read eBooks to justify an eReader, nor do I like it. [I did try it with this – still a no go – clunky, awkward, no “book smell”, and so easy to lose my place.]

Seeing this? I decided to grab it. After all, I USED to be a Samsung Galaxy (Android) user. I had to replace my GS8 and the iPhone I was had a cheaper plan through my carrier. No regrets there. But, I still remember the Android system. My mom still has her GS8 phone, so I HAVE to know it.

Looking at the price, around $60 (as of this review) – this is a basic, no frills tablet. It is a “no-name” brand, but that doesn’t mean much. I’ve had trouble with numerous brand name items, so name doesn’t matter.

Now, this is VERY SLOW. Even a cheap Acer laptop can be slow. My mom had one and the language … hello? Content warning!!

This is, to me, great for pre-teens and teens. It’s not too expensive that parents will really scream if something happens (like say an iPad or more expensive $100+ tablet). Or, it can work for someone who wants some internet functionality, and wants to read eBooks. The Kindle app works great here, just not my style.

I can check my email accounts – Outlook and Gmail – no real issues. I’ve ordered fast-food. As far as games? The one I tried didn’t work (Hogwarts Mystery)

As far as a user manual – like most devices nowadays (or the ones I’ve bought in the last 5-8 years) – the MANUAL (instructions) are on the device, usually a PDF. This was the same for the last three HP laptops I bought in 2010, 2011, and 2019. And, it was the same for the last two phones (GS8 and iPhone 11). Also, my iPods in 2008 and 2013. So, yes, I do have a LOT of experience with the lack of a physical manual. The manual can be accessed by swiping the homescreen UP. It is a PDF file.

There are some apps that ARE NOT COMPATIBLE with this device, even if you have them on a Galaxy phone. These can range from productivity to fast food. IE: Tropical Smoothie Café’s app is compatible, Taco Bell isn’t. My bank’s app isn’t compatible, but I can access the website through the Chrome browser (which I also have on my iPhone).

However, a GIANT bonus for me – MICROSOFT 365. I was able to add WORD to the tablet, and since I have cloud storage – ALL MY DOCUMENTS are AVAILABLE to view and edit.

Overall – this is, as I stated: a BASIC or STARTER tablet. Better suited for ages 8 to 15. I say this based on the fact that at 8, I would be able to care for this, and use it. By 15, I’d likely save up my allowance for a higher priced tablet or get it as a gift.

I am pretty pleased with it, and will likely use it for several things.

After a BAD experience with my Samsung GS8 - going through cables like crazy - I made sure to stock up on cables when I got my iPhone 11. For the price - which is a little over $11 - it is a great bargain. I wouldn't hesitate to get a few more as extras - or to keep in other areas of my town home.

In 2013, I gave up my paid TV subscription.

Yes, for eight (8) years I’ve had no TV service – satellite, cable, OTA (over-the-air).

Through my cell phone provider, I do have HULU (free) and Amazon Prime Video (included with Amazon Prime). I recently subscribed to CBS All Access (which is change its name March 4th) and Disney+. For less than $45 per month, I have a LOT of TV to view and no contract. No extra bulk equipment.

But, I don’t like watching the services on my phone or laptop.

Enter this little device. I hook it up to my GS8 (which I use solely as a WIFI device and not as a phone) and hook up an HD cable to my HDTV – viola! I can now watch all the shows I want.

Quality and sound are great. This device, the cable, and my phone are easy to transport for traveling. As of the last hotel stay I had in 2015, nearly all good hotels have HDTV, so I can plug this right in. That means I can have everything listed on the go.

For the price, it really is a great value. Durable and easy to install.

I’m old enough to remember the old 8-track players, but growing up my media player was of course a cassette player, and sometimes a “dual” player.

But, in 1995, I opted to transition to CDs. By that time they were a bit more affordable, though the average $17.95 felt like it was anything but.

By around 2005, I was transitioning to an MP3 player. The first one was a literal BRICK (Creative Nomad).

And, by 2008, I had an iPod Nano. By 2011, I had the iPod classic. Even my 2008 Chevy had an aux port to connect my iPod to. So, I really had NO need of a CD player. After all, most of my music was on my computer or iPod. Living in an apartment is NOT ideal for a “stereo”. I wouldn’t want to hear someone else’s music, so I don’t think they’d want to hear mine.

When I saw this, I decided to get it.

It is COMPACT, no frills, no remote control. In fact there is only a “selection” button, not a (back track or forward track).

I haven’t tried the radio function yet. The CD top loader consists of a manual opening (no push-button), and the CD has to be popped in and out manually. The sound is pretty decent for the size of the unit. This is more for desktop or bedside use. Definitely not for a home “sound system”.

I then tested the AUX cable for the iPod and the sound was the same as the CD. That feature was REALLY easy to use.

It is a pretty solid, light-weight unit. I do believe it could be a bit cheaper. I wouldn’t mind getting a second one should the price drop.

These are something I definitely dislike replacing. But, I go through quite a few of them.

This one seems a bit more durable with regard to a braided cord as opposed to silicone or rubber. The sound quality is fantastic given the age of my car radio (12 years old) and my iPod (7 years old). So, that is saying a lot about this cable.

I'm hoping I don't have to replace it down the road - but, I will choose this one!

It took me a little while to rate these. I have an IPOD Touch and walk on my treadmill a few times a week.
I had the earphones that came with my IPOD and I also bought another set. I spent a little more money on the other set and thought they worked perfectly fine...until I got these.

I couldn't even hear myself clopping along on the treadmill.

I charged my headphones one week, and it is still fully charged a week later. Of course I don't listen all the time or for hours on end, but it's great that I don't have to charge them all the time.
One thing I really like about these, besides the comfort and noise blocking, is the fact that they are wireless. I like to be able to get up and move away from my computer and still keep listening.
I'm very glad I got these!

This is adorable, I love it. It sounds like a little bell when I walk because of the metal ball inside. Pretty nice quality considering the price.

This could not have been easier to set up. Well, the directions would have been easier if they separated each language instead of listing one direction in several languages in a row. Anyway, it was fully charged when I got it. I just had to turn it on, turn on the Bluetooth, then turn Bluetooth on for my Kindle fire and search for this device. I then played music from my Pandora app and my Amazon music app. I left my tablet downstairs and took the speaker upstairs and tried it in all of the rooms. The sound is great (it is a small speaker but it is very impressive). I didn't have any connection issues and the music still played even when my tablet was in sleep mode.
I am really very pleased to be able to listen to music from different services and my own music library that I keep in the Amazon cloud.

This comes with a usb cable to either charge through your laptop or a universal charger (charger not included, only the cable).
I noticed when I did charge it, it will show green when it is fully charged but then the light will go out. This confused me at first. You can't tell how much change you have left until it gets to 15 -10% left and shows red, then flashed red. You are supposed to get 24 hours of use when fully charged and that seems accurate based on what I am getting. I will play relaxation music while I sleep and I can use it two or three nights without charging unless I use it during the day.
Another feature that doesn't bother me but may be annoying to others is that there are no buttons on the speaker. It shows the small icons (power, blue tooth) and then you just press into that spot.

This is actually my first flat screen tv, though everyone else has them and they look so great and the price on this was so reasonable. I recently got rid of cable because it is just too expensive and I watch mostly Prime or Netflix. I didn't want to get a smart tv because I've heard some people say they stopped being able to watch Amazon. I have a Roku so setting this up was super quick. The price is great. This has great picture quality and I'm happy with the sound. I like that there are different options for how you want the picture and sound to be. It hardly takes up any room, the stand seems quite sturdy.

I am a big fan of my kindles. I have the kindle keyboard ereaders 1st and 3rd gen , the 2nd gen Fire 8.9" and last year I bought the 6" Fire. I would not have bought this one except that my 6" Fire has gotten glitchy. I have not had problems with any of my kindles before so I chalked it up to just a bad egg.
I was thinking of replacing it when I found this great deal on the lastest 7" Fire. $100 for a tablet is such a deal. $50 is AMAZING!!
There isn't a huge difference other than this one is a little bigger. It was easy to import everything from my old tablet to my new one. My books, photos, songs, even my book marks from Silk. The set up took minutes.
The home page is different, it looks like the ones on iphones with all the apps on the home page. You can group them into smaller collections, you can also upload your own photo to be the wallpaper. I like this better than the carousel. You can also group your books into collections. There is a button so that you can move between applications without them closing out. It will show all the last places you went so you can pick up where you were and just switch screens. This is my favorite new feature, even more than the change with the home screen.
I'm not super fond of Silk but it is less annoying since they did an upgrade.
I have only had one problem: when I was first setting it up, the screen kept freezing. I rebooted it and I haven't had an issue since.
This is just as fast as my 6" tablet. Battery usage seems the same as well. According to the specs this should be a little slower than the 6" with less battery time but I have not noticed a difference. The plastic back feels only a little less durable than my other kindles but I'm not concerned. I feel like I have gotten quite a deal.
The camera isn't really improved since there isn't a flash and the sound quality is the same as well. Movies look great. I'm really happy that I can add a memory card. Movies, music, and audio books use a lot of memory but now I'll have more memory than I need.
You are getting so much for your money. I've never used other brand tablets, I'm not an Apple user. They may or may not be better but are their prices worth it?
I love Prime access for music and videos and that they can be downloaded.
I'm very happy with my new tablet!

Right out of the box I am loving the sleek design. It is harder to find those in this price range and with a touchscreen that have the DVD drive and aren't bulky. The power button is a small button on the right, next to the DVD drive. The power cord goes on the left side which is my preference. This is the first laptop I have seen with out a round connecter for the power slot, but one that is flat. I have no idea if this makes a difference or is just an esthetic choice. Also, it has a smaller ethernet port than my other laptops so I bought a usb adapter for size RJ45 ethernet I have in case I need to use it.

This model starts pretty fast and the programs run fast. I have not been waiting on anything even though I haven't yet removed any of the unnecessary programs that are standard with any laptop. It is fast, sleek, and cool to the touch no matter how long I am using it.

I don't think I can review this without reviewing Windows 8 to some extent. (This model has 8.1, I don't know the difference, I assume it is a fix for glitches with original 8)
I have never used Windows 8 before so it was all new to me. I do see how it is best used with a touchscreen. Set up for the Lenova takes a little time, you will want to customize when you have that option so you don't just automatically sign up for Bing as your search engine or Microsoft features you don't want. I really like that I can alternate between keyboard and touchscreen without clicking on anything first.
You will start out in the Windows 8 app screen. There is a lot of useless stuff on there. Just right click to unpin from start window. You can scroll down to find other apps to add to start. Those are all ones that come pre-loaded. There is a shopping bag icon you will find under "store" where you can find all the apps available, some free, some not. That icon is also on the more familiar Windows page.
The start button is gone,instead you will find an icon with four squares in the bottom left corner. You can click that to toggle between the app screen and normal screen. Right-click on it and you will find all the same commands you are used to with other Windows.

Much of this stuff I learned by trial and error. I think it would be nice if computers using Windows 8 came with some instructions and handy tips. The four square icon is also a button on the keyboard. It took me over an hour to realize it was that simple to move between screens!! Before, I had no idea what I was clicking on that was making anything happen.
When you have an app open, you have to move the pointer to the corner of the right screen and it will give you an X to close.
Right now when I have an app open, I can only toggle between the app and the Windows 8 page, not the normal screen. I'm sure you can, I just don't know how yet and I am trying to learn things without googling them.

I like this keyboard and having a backlit option. (The symbol for this is on the space bar, I won't tell you how long it took to figure that out). The keyboard has a numbers pad which I find handy.

So as for the flex mode that allows you to flip back the screen with the keyboard facing down. It is easier if you just want to use as a touchscreen only but it isn't the same as a notebook but is almost better, like a tablet with a stand that can quickly flip back to being a laptop. I do find this handier for using just touchscreen. I also like this position when I am streaming movies. Which by the way looks great on this screen and the sound is the best I have encountered on a laptop. It does seem odd having the keyboard face down, you want to make sure you are putting it on a surface that wouldn't scratch or that is dusty and will clog the keyboard but I don't see that being an issue. I often flip it when it is in my lap, it's more comfortable to use like this.

All in all, I am very happy with this laptop. I did receive this free in exchange for a review via Amazon Vine program but my review is an honest one.
If you are hesitant about Windows 8.1, rest assured. I figured it out and I am not that computer literate. I am sure there are also many websites with helpful hints. Or ask me.
I have owned 2 HPs and a Gateway laptop. At work, I use a Dell. So far, I like the Lenova best and I will update with any changes.

Updated-11/28/12 I thought charging problems were related to problems with my Kindle e-reader charger. I purchased the power charger and things seem to be better. However, when I plug it in to charge, it does not always start charging and I have to unplug it, wait, etc. And now I noticed that it isn't holding the charge very well. I called Amazon and they are sending me out a replacement right away. If the replacement doesn't have any issues, I will keep the 5 stars and assume i got one with a glitch. It happens. If there are still issues, then it will be an overall problem and my ratings will drop. There was a person on the forum page that also had this problem. Most others are reporting no issues with the battery. So for now, I will gave Amazon the benefit of the doubt.

I have only had this for a day so I have not explored everything. This is my first tablet so I have little to compare it to, but I have a Kindle e-reader which I love. I found this to be pretty user friendly considering I don't even have a smartphone so apps and touchscreens are new to me. I found the user's guide to me helpful as well as the Kindle forum to answer questions I didn't feel like looking for answers to. I had no problem uploading my favorite sites. Some said they couldn't watch movies but I have been able to with both Netflix and Amazon on demand.Also, I guess there were some issues with the sound in the first generation Fire. I didn't have any problems, I didn't even need to use full volume when watching shows.
I downloaded a few free apps to play around with. And of course my books. I like that I can download some to the Fire but if there is one I want to read that I already own, I can download it from kindle Cloud. I can read books without downloading them via the Cloud but that means keeping the wireless on. Same with music.
I'm not to great with touchscreens and I loathe fingerprints so I prefer to use the stylus that I got separately. I didn't get a charger (it comes with USB cord only but charging through the computer won't really work), the one for my Kindle fits but doesn't charge as fast. So I ended up ordering the fast charger as the Fire isn't meant to last as many hours as the Kindle e-reader. But I still think the battery life is pretty good.
I like reading on this, I thought the back-light would bother me, but I can adjust the brightness. I actually prefer reading in the portrait mode as it shows two pages and looks like a book page would.
So far I am very happy with this, my third Kindle device. I like Amazon and find them to be very user friendly when I need help so I have no concerns so far. If there are any issues, I will update my review because I take spending my money very seriously.

This as smaller than I thought it would be but I love it. I had no problem downloading songs and audiobooks and creating folders, it is very user friendly. The sound quality is great. My last mp3 was a Sandisk also and that worked well, it was just time to upgrade.
The only downside is that I bought it hoping I could listen to music at work and not be bothered by co-workers but that isn't happening. But since this wasn't promised to me in the product description, I can't blame Sandisk :)
I highly recommend this, at this price it's a steal.

I don't have much to say, it works just as the description says. It charges the ipod and plays what ever music I set it to when the alarm goes off. The sound is good though not great but nice to wake up to. It is easy to use. It plugs in but also has battery back up which is handy and would make t good for travel. It also has a timer so you can listen to music while falling asleep and it turns off automatically.

I loved the idea of having an electronic board as a family hub. With an Echo in almost every room of our house (except for bathrooms) this one fit the bill. Now that we have it installed we use it once or twice a day but not as frequently as I expected. My husband still asks when I have a day off even though my calendar is right there for everyone to see. I wish I could think of more uses and can’t wait until more is readily available to truly make it a one stop shop for the whole family. We even watched a YouTube video the other day at dinner which was cool, but I couldn’t figure out how to make it full screen. Will keep trying!!

Sometimes I forget that I've been wearing noise cancelling headphones all day and start yelling at my husband when I think I'm speaking at a normal volume. These are great, but the do feel a little snug around my ears (probably to help cancel out the noise). They do not cancel out everything - I can still hear birds outside my window but they definitely do the trick for use on conference calls. They seem to do a great job at cancelling out noises in my room from going over the mic into my calls.

These are great headphones! I have very small ears for an adult so it's difficult for me to find wireless headphones that truly fit and these ones absolutely do. There is also a slight little curve to them, so they have a better chance of not just popping out of my ears (at least that's what I tell myself). The sound is good quality and I like the little charging case too. It's a little difficult to get the earbuds out of the charger if you don't put them in just right, but I've figured out a good angle and can get them out every time with no issues. This is the second wireless headphones I've purchased that were Rowkin, and by far these are my favorite pair.

I've been really happy with this laptop.  I use PCs exclusively in my personal life.  They are my preference, but I am forced to use a Mac at work.  I have found that this PC uses a few of the things I like from my work Mac, but has them on a PC platform.  Namely, I've found the scrolling features to be similar.  This computer runs Windows 10, as is standard.  I have found the memory to be plenty sufficient for my needs ( which are storing some pictures, running a bunch of browser tabs, playing some online casual games, and similar).  The keyboard is comfortable for typing, and the touchpad is adequate.  If you want more control (and especially if you are a serious gamer) you will probably want to add on your own external mouse.  I've been using this computer happily for 2.5 years.  I travel with it regularly- it is not too heavy.  It's not as light as my Mac, but it's not onerous.  I plan to continue happily using this into the future.

This little alarm clock gets the job done at a great price.  This is a no-frills clock that does exactly what I need it to.  It has an easy to program alarm, it wakes me up reliably, and it lets me know the time.  The digital display shows the time in the dark without being too overwhelmingly bright.  I've had clocks whose displays would light up my room.  This one does not.  Setting the time and the alarm is easy and intuitive.  The alarm is loud enough to wake up a sound sleeper- I can say this with assurance, as I am very resistant to waking up.  The best thing about this clock is the price- cheap and cheerful!  I've just ordered my second of these clocks for another room.  When I need an alarm clock, this is my go-to.

These headphones are generally good, but some of their features are better than others. I'll start with the good. For listening to music, these headphones are excellent.
