The sound quality is fantastic. I listen to classical music while I work, and for that these headphones have been fantastic. I can hear all sorts of nuance, and beautiful, clear sound. These headphones are comfortable to wear, and sit steadily on the ear without pinching or slipping.

The noise cancelling feature is another story. When in noise-cancel mode everything sounds odd in these headphones- almost like the sound is dislocated. It's hard to describe, and not particularly pleasant. I was very interested in the noise-cancel feature, and disappointed that it created such odd sound quality.

These headphones are competitors to Bose, and similar. I'd recommend trying them if you've had problems finding a comfortable fit in other higher-end headphones, but not if you want them mostly for noise-cancelling.

Sadly, I thought originally that the bottom cover did not fit. That's not the case, it was user error. It's tricky so please pay careful attention to the instructions to attach the bottom cover. :-) Overall, I like this case, the top cover is very pretty, I got the "Peony" print and it looks great, the colors pop and the case is Matte. The keyboard cover is a little bit unfit, but perhaps it will settle out over time. I will be ordering another keyboard cover for my other laptop and my wireless keyboard in the same print. I think that it's a good value, it's worthwhile to protect a couple thousand dollars worth of equipment.

I know it's a bit expensive for a micro USB cable but honestly the quality is worth it. I have a bunch of electronics and gadgets and I've bought a plethora of cheap USB cables and they all suck. I have 3 Amazon fire cables and they are the only ones which charge the fastest, have not broken at the USB point, and don't look like they have been used as a jump rope or garrote. What I'm saying is they hold up nicely.

So, the first cable is close to four years old and I can't tell it apart from the extra I bought a few weeks ago. I wish they were not so spendy I would buy more so I stop switching electronics and have one for the car only. I recommend keeping your eye on the price. And if you're buying a kindle buy an extra you get a discount and you'll want more. As childish and "first world" as it sounds these are my favorite USB cables.

i got this as a present for a friend who just put in a backyard pool. She loves it. I was over the other day and the sound quality on the speaker is great. It is not too complicated so even non-techy people like her and I are able to make it work. The battery life is right at 5 hours from what we could calculate and that honestly is just perfect. I got the black one, but I do also like the other colors of red and blue and feel like they are fun outdoor/summer kind of colors. I wanted her to be able to bring this in during the winter and still be able to use it.  Her phone fits perfect, (she does not have a thick case) so overall it was the perfect gift for an outdoor pool and would be a great addition to any summer time, or outdoor activity. 5 stars from me.

We sent all of our employees home with laptops to work from home for what we thought was just a quick couple of weeks, well now 4 months later we are still at home and needing to come up with some more solutions for the at home worker. One of them is getting them all laptop stands. I am trying a bunch of different ones to see what works best. This one is nice a light weight but sturdy enough that we don't have to worry about it collapsing. It is well made and came in a nice compact packaging. I didn't like that it is adheres with tape, guess I should have read it closer, but it is nice quality tape, but forget about removing it, or moving the legs ones you have placed them. So that is con number one, con number two is that they don't move at all, no swiveling, or being able to get different positions with these risers.  But the pro's far outweigh any cons, it is worth it to save the company's equipment, I found out many agents were putting their laptops on pillows and they were over heating and shutting down. this has helped save the equipment and our productivity. 5 stars from me.

If you are looking for a high quality waterproof speaker that is reasonably priced, this is the one for you. It is portable and not super heavy. It has a great, sturdy casing around it and it is 100% waterproof.  I hooked it up in the shower and i still have not had so much as a crackle in the sound.  I love the LED feature that you can change with your mood and with your music.  it might seem odd to have music and a light show in your shower, but I love it and it helps me wake up and get my day going in a good mood.  I saw that you can blue tooth two speakers together and I am going to get another one so I can do just that., and be able to keep the music going even when I am out of the shower. My only downside to this is that sometimes I want to skip a song and you are not able to do that on the speaker itself, but that is not a huge deal to me so I did not take away any stars for that.

I got this speaker to use outside at the pool, and was highly impressed with its sound. It is a bigger speaker, not something I would want to carry around often. However, the sounds quality is amazing on it.

I use this USB C to HDMI Adapter with my 2017 Intel MacBook Pro, with Thunderbolt 3 ports. I have hubs and docks, but sometimes all I need is HDMI input and to charge my computer. This adapter is very handy in that regard, and would be great to keep in your bag if you travel. It’s only 8½ inches long from end to end, and does not require any drivers to use. It’s plug and play (and charge).

I use the adapter with an external monitor (60Hz refresh rate) and to charge my computer. It just works!

I like that the HDMI port is on the end of the adapter, most of my HDMI cables are stiff and this works better with my desk setup.

This review is for the MacBook Pro 13 Inch Case.

The case fits my 2017 MacBook Pro, model number A1706. This is just a top and bottom case, no screen protector or keyboard protector.

The case snaps on, it’s easy to put on and take off. And you don’t have to use both halves for it to stay on. I personally just the top, I use two external monitors with my MBP so it sounds like a jet engine most of the time. The bottom of the case does have cutouts to disperse heat, but I prefer to use the top alone.

The glitter is SO sparkly! There’s a mix of tiny and small pieces of glitter, and when the light hits this case, it’s like a little disco ball.

The case is smooth, you can’t feel the glitter at all. The bottom of the case has pre-installed white rubber feet to prevent sliding on a surface. The case is slim, I don’t even notice it’s on while I’m using my laptop.

I’ve tried using cord holders before, the type that sticks to the desk or other surface, and has a few slots. Of course, I always stuck them in the wrong spot, or they didn’t stay stuck for long, and they were made from such lightweight plastic they were basically useless.

All that is to say, I really like the weighted base of the CordBrick. The middle section has a steel core that’s heavy enough to keep the CordBrick wherever I put it. But not so heavy that it would be annoying to take traveling.

I have a few work spots in my house, all with cables that slide off the desk. The CordBrick works perfectly to keep those cords in place on the desk. The silicone accommodates all sizes of cords, I’ve even used it with HDMI cables.

I have two complaints. This color is Glow in the Dark, but it doesn’t glow at all! The description actually says it’s “made of a special silicone that has energy absorbing crystals [...].” Apparently, the “energy absorbing crystals” are supposed to suck up any light and use it to make the CordBrick glow. No dice. Mine doesn’t glow at all. So I’m left with a boring, cloudy, off-white colored CordBrick.

The second complaint is very minor: I wish the steel core was fully covered in silicone. One end is visible.

The BOIFUN Portable Monitor really IS portable. It’s not that much bigger than my 13-inch MacBook Pro, and it weighs less. I could see packing the monitor for a trip, to use for work and play. I have used the monitor with my Mac and my Nintendo Switch, and it works great with both devices.

The monitor has USB-C and Mini HDMI input options. It comes with cables for both options, which I appreciated. That’s one small downside, you’ll need to make sure to take the Mini HDMI cable with you.

I used the USB-C input with my Mac, it worked. I used the Mini HDMI to HDMI input for my Nintendo Switch, it worked. With both devices, the picture on the monitor was clear and bright. The monitor is plug and play, no instructions really needed.

I did some online Splatoon matches with my Switch to see if there would be any noticeable lag or freezing on the monitor, there were no problems. The game looked great, although the built-in speakers are very tinny.

I do have a few complaints about the monitor. The “smart cover” is super basic. The pictures show folding the cover and using it as a stand, propping the monitor against it. Like a tablet smart cover. But that’s seemingly impossible to do. The cover is very floppy, with no support to hold itself in any stand-shape. The box does include a basic plastic stand, but I wish I could use the cover as pictured, since the stand is one more thing to pack if I go somewhere.

Also, the cover is like a file folder. There’s no way to attach it to the monitor. It relies on magnets alone to stay in place. I wish it had some sort of clip or strap inside, to secure the monitor.

Secondly, the input ports are on opposite sides. The USB-C port is on the same side as the power port, but the Mini HDMI port is on the other side. So if you want to use the monitor in landscape position, you’re limited by input type.

The monitor is powered via USB-C, a cable and wall adapter are included. The wall adapter is a basic 5V USB-A wall adapter. I like that it isn’t some proprietary charging cable.

The MoKo Case fits my iPad Air 4, model number A2316. I really like the pencil holder feature, it works to hold the Apple Pencil in place and also allows it to charge. The holder is snug, you have to push the Apple Pencil in and tug it out. I like that too, much less chance of the pencil getting knocked off.

The case itself feels sturdy and solid. The back is a little slippery, it’s a harder, less flexible plastic than the TPU sides. The back is clear frosted, the sides are black. The case has all the necessary cutouts, including the power button/Touch ID. The volume buttons are covered.

The cutout for the charging cable fits the stock Apple cable head.

I like the camera cutout, too. It has a raised edge that fully protects the camera lens. The edge around the back of the case matches the height of the cutout, so the case doesn’t rock when resting on a hard surface.

This is a basic two button mouse with LED lighting to add pizzazz. The mouse connects via wireless dongle or Bluetooth, there’s a switch on the bottom to pick which connection type you want. The wireless dongle stores in the bottom of the mouse and doesn’t impede usage if you’re connected via Bluetooth.

I connected via Bluetooth, all I had to do was set the switch to Bluetooth and wait for my computer to find it.

The LED lighting cannot be turned off, nor can the mode be changed. It’s a slow scrolling rainbow of light.

The buttons are supposed to be silent click, they are pretty quiet. The wheel is a little louder.

The mouse charges via micro USB, a short cable is included.

I’ve been using the Soundcore by Anker Life P3i Earbuds for about a month. For the price, they are a nice set of earbuds with some good features. The sound quality is above average. I’m not an audiophile; if I can clearly hear Billie Eilish songs, I’m happy.

On the downside, the ANC could be improved and the case itself doesn’t support wireless charging. The earbuds can be charged in the case, but the case itself charges via USB-C.

What I like:
🎧 The earbuds are comfortable. Of course, this is somewhat subjective. But I have a few inner ear piercings (rook, daith, and tragus) and some earbuds irritate my piercings. I can wear this pair for a few hours. And if needed, I can use one earbud at a time, you don’t have to use both for playback.

🎧 The controls are tactile, not touch. I personally dislike touch controls on earbuds, they’re way too easy to accidentally activate. To avoid pressing the earbuds deeper into my ears, I hold onto the “stem” part when using the buttons. The Soundcore app allows customization of the controls, you can change the settings for single tap, double tap, and hold.

What I don’t like:
🎧 The app requires an account to use. Just let me customize my settings without signing up.

🎧 The case can’t be charged wirelessly. It only has one LED status light on the outside. The light only turns red to indicate the case needs to be charged when it has 10% or less remaining.

🎧 The ANC is just okay. I can hear the TV about ten feet away from me.

The Wirehard 106 in 1 Precision Screwdriver Set is a compact, nicely designed screwdriver kit. I’ve just gotten into building my own keyboards, this kit has every conceivable tip size or type I could need.

The set is packaged in a hard plastic case, the lid is held on with magnets. I would personally prefer a snap-on lid because if the lid falls off, the pieces are going to fall out and that’ll be a mess. But I did try dropping the case and the lid stayed on, so perhaps I’m just being paranoid.

The case is lined with foam, and everything has its labeled cutout spot. All of the tips and sockets are labeled by size and type; however, the font is black on black foam, so it can be difficult to read the tiny text.

The screwdriver is small but adequate, with a nonslip grip and a swivel cap on top. There is a soft, flexible rod extension so you can get into hard-to-reach spots, and also an extension rod. The bits are magnetic to lessen the chance of dropping screws.

Other than the magnetic lid and the tiny black on black text labels, I’m quite pleased with this screwdriver set. It’s a big upgrade from the basic repair kit I have from a hardware class eons ago.

The WFB Bluetooth Wireless Mouse is an obvious take on the Logitech MX Master 3. The two are very similar in form factor and design. The MX Master 3 happens to be my daily driver. I’ve been using it for the last year and a half, so I can make a good comparison.

This mouse weighs less, the build quality doesn’t quite match the Logitech. The most noticeable difference is the scroll wheel; the Logitech scroll wheel is quite possibly my favorite ever on a mouse. It scrolls at MagSpeed, which really means it scrolls super fast and super smooth, and it’s fun just to flick the scroll wheel to quickly get to the top or bottom of a webpage or document. The WFB mouse’s scroll wheel is average, but I will say, it is quiet.

The clicks are muted too, on the WFB. Right and left click are muted, and to me, they feel like they take more force than the Logitech. When I switch to using the WFB mouse, there’s always an adjustment for me with the difference in clicking.

The WFB mouse has some RGB lighting, a curved strip that goes around the horizontal scroll wheel. I like the lighting at night, makes it really easy to find my mouse when the room is dark, but it can be turned off if you don’t like it.

The WFB mouse has Windows and Mac mode to switch between. I like this a lot! I’m not a fan of Logi Options to customize my Logitech mouse. The Mac mode allows the use of Misson Control when hitting the Windows/Mac button (under the DPI button) and also to Command+Tab when hitting the front side button (next to the back/forward buttons). For me, having those two navigation methods is fantastic, as I use them constantly.

The back/forward buttons work for web browsing. The horizontal scroll wheel seems as useless as Logitech’s.

The mouse charges via USB-C.

I’ve been using the Bloody M90 Earbuds for about a month, and I’m quite impressed with them! I usually prefer over-ear headphones because they are more comfortable for me -- I have quite a few inner ear piercings -- but I’ve barely used any other set of headphones for the past month.

Once you find the right size, these buds are comfortable and stay in your ears. The box includes three sizes of ear tips: small, medium, and large. I did have a short adjustment period, the noise cancelling made me nauseated. This is not a fault of the earbuds, it’s something that can happen, and within a week, I was able to wear the earbuds for hours at a time.

I use the earbuds to listen to music and stream shows. I’m not an audiophile, but I think the sound quality is pretty good. Music sounds clear and punchy, no tin can or thin bass here. The noise cancelling is not as robust as a pair of over-ear headphones, but it dampens enough of the background noise in my home that I can clearly hear what I have playing.

The main advantage of these earbuds is they don’t give me a headache like over-ear ones do after a few hours. There’s no headband sitting on top of my head, or squeezy tight ear cups. As I mentioned, I have a few inner ear piercings (tragus, rook, daith) and I’m still able to wear the earbuds comfortably. They stay in while I walk around the house.

I can use one earbud or both, and they have tap controls. They connect easily, all it takes is opening the case and they’re connected to my computer.

The case is pretty swanky, matte black with a thin strip of metallic red. The case has 4 small LEDs on the front to show battery and charging status, the lights go on when opening the case or when it’s charging. The case works with wireless charging or via USB-C, a short cable is included.

The instructions are easy to understand. The Quick Start guide was all I needed to get up and running.

The Shure AONIC 40 Over Ear Headphones blew me away. I’d never heard of the brand before, so I wasn’t sure what to expect. The quality was a great surprise. From the packaging to the headphones, I was impressed the second I opened the box.

I’ve been using the AONIC 40 headphones for almost a month and they’ve become my new favorite headphones. The ones I put on every time I sit down at my desk. Sometimes I use them just to dull the background noise in my house -- I’ll turn them on and not even play music. The noise cancelling doesn’t entirely block out all sound that way, but dulls the background noise enough when I’m overstimulated. Before the Shures, I was using Razer Opus headphones every day; there’s no comparison.

When I play music or watch a show, then the noise cancelling blocks out nearly everything. I can’t hear the videos my mom is watching in the next room, or when she talks to me. 😈

The sound quality is fantastic. I’m not an audiophile, but even I noticed a difference in how much better music sounded with these. The Shure app can be used to further tweak sound settings.

Battery life is fantastic too. I get at least 4-5 days of using them for 4-5 hours per charge. Checking battery life is easy, just double tap the power button. The headphones have physical buttons for all controls, which I really prefer over touch controls.

My only complaint is that after a few hours, the headphones are too heavy and squeezy on my head, and thus give me a headache. Compared to my Razer Opus headphones, the Shures are noticeably heavier. The earcups are adequately padded and comfortable. But the headband isn’t very padded and the headphones are so tight they feel like a vise after a few hours.

The headphones come in a medium-weight case with a long zipper pull. The top of the case has a mesh pocket holding the instructions and a 3.5mm cable. The bottom of the case has a printed outline showing how to properly fit the headphones in the case, a handy reminder that will always be there. A USB-A to USB-C cable is included for charging; the case has an elastic band to hold the cable.

The Logitech Folio Touch is a JOY to type on. I really love typing on it — I’m writing this review using the case. I’ve typed quite a few long documents on it. I turn to this keyboard when I want distraction-free writing.

The keyboard reminds me of Apple laptop keyboards before the disastrous butterfly keyboards. The keyboard is backlit, and the brightness of the backlighting can be adjusted via the function keys. The row of function keys is another good feature for me. I find it much faster and easier to adjust the iPad’s brightness or volume using the function keys.

I downloaded the Logitech Control app, but it doesn’t seem to give any options for customizing the keyboard. All I see the app do is check for keyboard firmware updates. When I wanted to change the trackpad scrolling direction, I had to hunt through the iPad’s settings — I thought that would be in the Logitech app. (I learned those settings became part of iOS, so the Logitech app seems … unnecessary.)

I don’t really like the trackpad. I’ve used Logitech mice for years. My current daily mouse is the Logitech MX Master 3, so I *know* they can do a good Mac mouse. But I just feel like they dropped the ball with this trackpad. The trackpad works but it could be better. I notice drag at times, and I don’t like the noise or tactile feedback when I click it. I can adjust a few settings (scrolling direction, tracking speed, tap to click, and two finger secondary click) in the iPad’s General Settings, but I want to be able to customize more through Logitech.

The corners of the case are reinforced. The bumper is a bit thick, too thick for some hubs or USB-C cables to fit without using an extension cable. There is a cutout for the power button so Touch ID can be used. There’s a spot for the Apple Pencil, it can rest inside the bumper or fit through a slot on the latch.

The Folio Touch pairs via the Smart Connector, so it’s super easy to set up: just stick your iPad inside and it’s ready to go. The iPad powers the keyboard, so I don’t have to remember to charge it, which I like. I haven’t noticed it being a battery hog.

Overall, I really like the Logitech Folio Touch. I actually use my iPad more now, since I like typing on the keyboard so much. The case has made my iPad more functional for me.

Skullcandy’s description says it all: wireless simplicity with noise canceling. These aren’t headphones for audiophiles who want to control and customize every sound option. These are headphones for people who want affordable Active Noise Cancellation (ANC) and decent sound output.

I’ve noticed the ANC works better when I’m listening to music rather than if I’m watching a tv show or movie to cancel out the background noise in my home. If I am watching a show, I can hear someone else watching a video in the next room; the noise of their video is cut about 75-80%. If I have music on, the noise of their video is cut about 90-100%, depending on the type of music.

Switching ANC on and off is easy. The headphones have a dedicated button for that, one second press to turn on, one second press to turn off. So it’s very quick if I need to hear someone speaking. The button has a raised open circle (◯) on it, so once you get used to the different symbols on the buttons, it’s very easy to feel it. The headphones also provide audio indicators (“Noise cancelling off/on”) when turning the ANC on and off.

The other buttons include + for volume up/track forward, ⚫ for power/play/pause, and -- for volume down/track back. I’ve used Skullcandy headphones for years when working outside, and I really like that they keep using physical buttons. I find physical buttons so much easier to use and know what button I’m pressing.

Sound quality is okay. I’ve noticed that the bass seems punchy, like I can feel it echoing against my ears. I don’t often mess with sound profiles, but this is a case where I would try to reduce the bass for my audio comfort. Otherwise, the sound is average to good.

The headphones stayed in place on my head, from sitting at my desk to walking around the house, folding laundry, and putting it away. I didn’t try with intensive activity, but as I mentioned above, I’ve used the previous versions of Skullcandy Hesh for working outside and they stay put. These look and feel almost identical to my old Hesh headphones, so I’m confident these will perform the same. They are tight; I sometimes get a headache when wearing them.

The headphones charge via USB-C. The box includes a USB cable and an audio cable. I used the headphones for about a week, probably 20 hours, before needing to charge. I like that I can get 3 hours of use with a 10 minute charge, very handy for if I’m going somewhere and forgot to charge ahead of time.

At first glance, the Razer Opus ANC Wireless Headphones don’t look like a Razer product. Where’s the green? Where’s the RGB? Even the branding is subdued.

These headphones are a grown-up Razer product, probably meant to be headphones you can take anywhere and not stick out as a gamer.

The Midnight Blue color is a nice change from black. I have a few pairs of wireless headphones and every single pair is black, so I appreciate having a little variety. Midnight Blue is a very deep blue -- so deep it’s almost black.

I’ve been trying the Opus headphones out for a few weeks and they have become the headphones I use every day. Before, I was using the Sony XB900N.

My favorite thing about the Opus headphones is how comfortable they are. The headband and ear cups have cushy padding. The headphones don’t squeeze my head too tight and don’t weigh a lot. I can wear these for 5+ hours at a time and not get a headache.

Sound quality is decent. I mostly use the Opus for listening to music and TV/movies. Compared to Razer’s gaming headsets, this isn’t one I’d pick for serious gaming. There is a tiny bit of lag and the low, deep sounds aren’t as punchy as with say, a Razer Kraken headset.

Razer’s claim of up to 25 hours of battery life seems pretty accurate. I didn’t keep a log every time I used the headphones, but I was able to use them for 4-5 hours a day for a good week before needing to charge. Unfortunately there is no battery indicator on the headphones to know when the battery is running low.

I don’t love the Razer Opus app needed to tweak a few of the settings. I have an older Android phone running Nougat, the app is incompatible with my phone. So I had to borrow my mom’s iPhone to install the app. By default, the headphones shut off after 5 minutes and I could only change this setting in the app. The app also allows you to switch between a few audio presets (but you can’t create your own) and check battery life.

If I take the headphones off my head, they automatically pause whatever I’m watching or listening to. I like this; my mom often talks to me when I’m wearing headphones, so it’s a lot quicker to just take them off and now I don’t have to manually pause. This is a setting that can be changed in the app.

The Active Noise Cancelling is what I expect for a pair of headphones in this price range. It’s decent. Not great, not horrible, but good enough to mute most background noise. But I don’t like that there’s not a light or indicator on the headphones to tell when I have ANC turned on.

The Opus doesn’t support Bluetooth multipoint.

The headphones charge via USB-C. The included case stores the headphones, charging cable, USB-C to USB A adapter, 3.5 mm audio cable, and airline adapter. The case actually has an outline on the bottom to tell you how to fit the headphones inside.

This is a review for the LeadsaiL RBG Black color option. This mouse pad has an LED stripe around the outer edge. It measures 31.5 inches by 12 inches.

I’m a big fan of anything that lights up, so I like this mouse pad quite a lot! The light is just subtle enough that it doesn’t constantly catch my eye, but it’s still there.

The mouse pad really shines in the dark. It looks so cool, and goes with other light up peripherals, like a LED keyboard. But it looks neat on its own, and also during the day. I’ve included a picture of the blue static color, taken during the afternoon.

I usually leave the mouse pad on one of the static light options. The dynamic ones can be distracting. One mode scrolls through the rainbow, another is a blinking rainbow, and the last is a rainbow fade. The light choice is controlled by a button on the left side of the mouse pad.

The included micro USB cable that powers the LED lights is a braided cord. So it sits flat on the desktop and doesn’t tangle.

I think the sound quality on the bopmen S40 Active Noise Cancelling Bluetooth Headphones is pretty good. I’m not an audiophile, but my ears know what they like. These headphones provide smooth playback; they don’t sound tinny or like I’m listening from far away.

The Active Noise Cancelling is about as good as noise cancelling I have on Sony headphones. I live with my mom and she watches videos that drive me crazy. So the bopmen headphones have saved my sanity for the last month. The ANC mutes enough of the loud background noise of her videos that I can get some work done.

The headphones are made from plastic and feel solid. They fold up for travel; I don’t feel like they’re going to break in my bag. The box includes a pouch for storage/travel.

The ear cups are a bit smaller than I would expect for over ear headphones. The earmuffs are some sort of leatherette material that is soft, with pretty good cushioning. If I wear the headphones for more than 2 to 3 hours at a time, I do start to get a headache from the squeeze and fit.

This is a review for the AmazonBasics Rotating 6-Outlet Surge Protector Power Strip with 2 USB Charging Ports.

This is a useful surge protector/power strip. I especially like the USB ports, as my Mac only has USB-C ports, so if I want to charge something with my laptop, I have to go find an adaptor. Now I can just plug whatever I need to charge directly into the surge protector. The max outlet for the USB ports is 2.4A.

The USB ports don’t support fast charging.

The rotating outlets allows me to plug in power bricks, since I can rotate the outlets to stagger the larger items.

The instructions give a notice that the max equipment for the surge protector/power strip is 15A / 1800W.

I’m not a sound snob, so I can’t speak to the sound quality of these headphones. To me, they sound just fine. I use them almost every night, either paired with my laptop or phone.

The active noise cancelling feature is my favorite. I’ve tried similar features on other headphones and sometimes I get nauseated after having the noise cancelling on for too long. I don’t have that problem with these headphones. The active noise cancelling doesn’t block out all sound, but it does a decent job.

The ear cups are round and nicely padded. The headphones aren’t too tight on my head, either. If you have a larger head, this pair of headphones might not be too comfortable, as the ear cups are on the small side.

I’ve used the BenQ monitor for a few months to give it a good workout. I’ve used it for gaming, watching movies, and writing.

I use it as an external monitor for my MacBook Pro, via USB-C. The first time I hooked it up, I had momentary panic because I couldn’t get anything to show up on the monitor. If this happens to you, make sure you’ve pressed the appropriate button on the monitor for the connection you’re using.

For everything -- the curved aspect of the monitor seems to be a gimmick. I didn’t notice any extra immersion or less eye strain. The opposite, actually; the first few days I used the monitor, I had a headache after.

For gaming, I play World of Warcraft. After years of playing on an 11” Air, I can’t tell you how amazing it was to upgrade to 35”! I was actually considering an iMac before this monitor, but I prefer the versatility of having a large external monitor for when I want to game/watch movies and unplug my laptop when I want to do other things. Colors were crisp, though the resolution was a little fuzzy and required some tinkering in the game settings.

For show watching, I gave Hannibal a spin. Primarily because the show is very dark; when I watched on my Chromebook, I had a hard time making out all the details. On the BenQ monitor, I could see the rich blacks! Kicking back to watch a movie on this monitor is a great experience.

For writing, I like the massive amount of screen real estate. I like to have lots of pictures and files open at once, which I was able to do. This monitor was also amazing when I was working on my taxes and had a bunch of spreadsheets open at once.

It’s not just a gaming/entertainment screen, which is important, because the monitor weighs a lot and takes up a lot of desk space. You’re not moving this thing around every day.

When I shop for headphones, I shop primarily for comfort. I’m not a sound snob -- I just need headphones that are super comfortable.

I’ve had a few pairs of over-ear/around-ear headphones. If I wear them too long, they give me a headache, either because they are too heavy after a while or squeeze too much or both. My last was a pair of Skullcandy’s, Hesh style, and I couldn’t wear them for more than 2-3 hours. These Bose SoundTrue’s feel a little lighter, and the ear cups are oval, not round, which makes them fit me better. They also don’t feel as tight on my head as the Skullcandy’s, but I don’t feel like they’re going to fall off.

Soundwise, I think they’re fine. But as I said, I’m not a sound snob, so as long as music sounds good and not like it’s played through a tin can, I’m happy.

Convenience wise, the ear cups swivel so the headphones fit in the included flat case. They don’t fold up a lot, but the case will be handy for when I want to take the headphones out with me. The cord is detachable, and has a remote for music/phone call control. I received the Apple version to review, so only the play/pause worked on my phone, but the other functions worked on my Macbook Air.

Decent sound and easy to adjust to fit better. Used to watch movies but not have the sound up loud enough to annoy the neighbors. More comfortable than headphones or earbuds. No complaints other than lack of basic controls unless I use my phone.

Both the kid and his tablet (Amazon Fire) love this charging set up. No longer is he scraping up the side trying to plug it in for a charge. Just snaps right on easy peasy. It fits fine even with his tablets thick kid safe cover on it.

Also works equally well on my husbands Samsung tablet. The best part, even though one uses a C port and the other a micro USB, they actually can both use the same cable to charge. Helps cut down on trying to figure out which cord goes to which.

Magnet is strong enough to stay put even when they are using the device and moving it around. However, you do need to take care and not pull too hard or it will pop out. Much like a regular cord would.

Our 2012 Chevy Equinox is too old for Bluetooth, which means it can't pair with an iPhone to play music or answer calls. Popped this in and after pairing was able to use the radio to play music off the phone and receive phone calls through the car speakers. You still need to use the mic on your phone to talk to someone, so it can sound far away depending on the placement of your phone.

I will say that there is a bit of static, but that is pretty common with all of these types of devices that use open FM channels.

My son's laptop gets super hot when he does anything that taxes the vid card. To the point that the keyboard keys start to be warm to the touch. To prolong it's life I purchased a similar cooler a year ago and it did very little, was loud, and the laptop kept sliding off. It finally gave out and I thought maybe I'd try my luck with a different one.

This has been soooo much better. It cools it better, is quieter, and has tabs in the front to keep the laptop from sliding off. He loves the lights (I don't really care about that stuff, but they are neat) and that his keys don't get so warm.

Great value for the price. Lightweight with a flip up to mute mic. I recommend these for kiddos as they aren't the end of the world if they break, plus they adjust down far enough to fit a smaller head. While not technically an open back they aren't super sealed either so they can still hear you if you need their attention. Plus, they do not do that annoying negative pressure thing that noise-cancelling headphones create. Many kids and some adults (me) can't stand that pressure feeling on the ear drum.

Are these super steller sounding and amazing, no. But they aren't bad for entry level. Great for $40.

Not bad for a beginning gamer headset. Love the flip up mic to mute, this should just be how all mics work if you ask me. I did ding a star for the price. These do not have a $60 build quality. They are plastic and cheap feeling, they sound fine but we are on our third pair as they just don't have the durability. The cord isn't even braided. If you can find them for under $40 it would be a better price point.

Sound quality is good but not great. At only 10 feet from the transmitter there was some cutting in and out (I have a different brand and they are just fine at this distance). They are way too big for exercising with, but okay for sitting to watch TV.

Ok so we had a hoot with this. Mostly spying on backyard critters, which so far has only been a couple of rats, the neighbors cat (I knew he was the one pooping under the bougainvillea, so busted), and the three legged opossum I thought had died a couple of years ago.

Not having a camera like this before our expectations were pretty low. It was fun, but the image quality wasn't that great and other than as a novelty I certainly wouldn't rely on this for surveillance or anything requiring detailed pics.

Ok I can be a bit of a headphone snob, but at a near $300 price point I have some pretty high expectations. I ran them through my standard audio tests and these passed every one with flying colors. Bottomline, where most wireless sets fail is with bass, either its lacking or they overcompensate for it at the expense of everything else. (I'm talking to you SkullCandy). These however managed to be astounding on bass without it being overwhelming. Deep rich sounds, but mid and upper still came in crystal clear. It was impressive.

They also manage to have noise canceling without the annoying hiss present in the high end SkullCandy set I recently reviewed. The AKG's are superior and even performed better than my beloved, but admittedly old Sennheisers. How they would match up against a newer pair I can't say though, I will fangirl all day over a high end set of Senn's, but these AKGs give them some serious competition.

The ambient pass-through was a welcome addition, and these paired effortlessly via blue tooth. The ear cups were comfortable, although warm like every other pair of closed noise-canceling headsets I've tried. I will be honest I tend to prefer an open headset, but that is more preference than anything to do with this set. The ear cups were smaller than other pairs I've worn, I'm petite so that wasn't an issue but if you got yourself some good sized ears keep that in mind.

So if you have $300 burning a hole in your pocket and need some very well balanced wireless headphones, I highly recommend.

Hubby had better luck with these than I did. He said they were super comfortable and stayed in place at the gym just fine even on the tread mill. I for the life of me couldn't get a comfortable position but I'm also a bit smaller than him. He liked the noise cancelling and I found it annoying especially since there is no passthrough/talk through feature on these. I ended up yelling at everyone not realizing how loud I was being lol.

Just sitting still and listening to music these have impressive sound quality. They can't match my true over the ear Sennheisers but as far as earbuds go these are some of the best I've heard.

For me they were 3 stars because I didn't like the fit and didn't function well with them, hubby said a solid 5 stars he loves them and has claimed them as his own for the gym. So averaged out to 4 stars between us.

Kiddo LOVED this (he's 7) I however am starting to question my own judgment. It's not like he needed assistance in being loud, and I went and handed him a microphone and speaker... gah.

It has lights, and a radio, makes a ton of noise, it's basically every kids dream. It is not at a professional corporate party level, but would be fun for home use, kids parties, annoying your inlaws with a gift they can hate you for, hehe. I have a few nephews that would love one of these, so their parents better be nice to me or its going to their house at Christmas.

I got these for my 7yr old who kept wanting to use my Sennheiser's. After about the fourth time he dropped them and/or tried to walk off with them still on his head I decided it was time for kiddo to get his own headset. I was skeptical of these, due to the low price, but the reviews were decent.. and he's a menace, so figured I'd see.

Pros:
*Price, they are wonderfully priced for what they provide
*Mic is crystal clear, his voice comes across bit higher pitched but he's 7 its not like it was all that low to begin with.
*Flip up mic to mute. I love this feature, I have it on my Senn's and I'm not sure I could do with out it. If you hate push to talk, then you want a flip to mute mic. Unless you like to entertain discord with your drama.
*They are adjustable to the point that both my kid and my husband fit them comfortably.
*Volume adjust is on the earpiece, I hate trying to find it on the cord, this is much more convenient. Now I just have to convince him that he needs to keep the volume at a safe low level. His headphones for school are for kids and had a volume limiter. I see why now.

Cons:
*The connector cable is old school rubberized plastic (rather than the more durable braided cord).
*Connector is also super short, no way he is using them on a docked Switch
*They feel a bit flimsy and plastic, however this also makes the light which is nice
*Thin on the padding across the headpiece, although the ear cups are comfortable enough
*Ear cups are on the smaller size. They were fine for everyone in our household, but if you have issues with headsets and your ears you will probably have them with this set.

As a neither pro or con, these only block some outside sound. I wouldn't say they are open or close, but somewhere in between. He can still hear me yell at him from the other room which is nice, but I do have to yell. Sound is lacking in substantial bass, but at this price they are all going to be. For a gaming headset under $50, the sound is crisp and clear, as was the mic.

TL;DR If you are on a budget or just don't want to see an expensive pair get destroyed (kids, dogs, etc) I highly recommend these. I did ding a star though for the cord, they say they are for the Switch and I just don't see how a docked switch could use these.

**Updated Review**

Ended up repurchasing (although went for the grip only option as we don't need a travel case). Why repurchase after returning it for not being able to stay docked (see original review below), because EVERY other option we tried was even worse. And after my 6 yr old dropped the switch and the joycons flew off I decided I would rather find a new way to dock it then wait for its inevitable demise at the hands of the destroyer.

This time around I also purchased their version of a screen protector as its thinner than the tempered glass one I had on originally. Which seems to have done the trick. Because either the new grip is thinner or shaving 1mm off the screen protector was all we needed. You do need to use a bit more finesse to dock but it stays docked, no more rising up mid game and disconnecting you. I also got him a separate controller and just told him to leave the joycons and case on so the grip doesn't take unnecessary wear.

Kiddo is ecstatic because the grip feels great in his hands and he was pretty peeved at me when I sent it back the first time around.

I have since revised my review to 5 stars. I would highly recommend going with their screen protector rather than the tempered glass ones if you have issues keeping the thing docked like we did.

------------
**Original Review**
I wanted to love this, it feels great in your hands. However, it is not dockable. Oh sure it can go into the dock but it slowly pushes itself up and disconnects you in the middle of your game, not okay. We have a newer switch (June 2018) so perhaps it fits last years switch's better?

Also, the top corner part by the triggers is a super thin strip and just waiting to break, especially considering this is the part that takes the most abuse when putting the case on and taking it off. Looks like I'm going to be stuck putting one of the crappy clear plastic covers on kiddos switch, lame.

To be fair I have only had this telescope since yesterday. But it was easy to put together. Getting it set up will require you to go watch some YouTube videos to actually USE. The instruction manual came in 5/6 different languages but the photos were very small and didn’t always show exactly how or what direction things are supposed to go. There are however videos you can go watch that will help you along if you’re new to this. It came in several boxes like a Russian nesting doll. But it was definitely safe when it was delivered. It was slightly overcast last night so after getting it set up we were able to see a lot of really wonderful detail on the moon, I cannot wait for a clear sky and a full moon! I’ve wanted a telescope since I was 5, this one has exceeded my expectations so far and I’m looking forward to seeing more things! Btw the software that comes with this is phenomenal!!! Taking it out tonight too :)

One of my AirPods has been difficult to use because whenever I’m on the phone people say I sound like I’m underwater. Well it turns out, it were just dirty. Gross! I ordered this set and it seems to have cleared up the problem. I was worried I was going to have to buy a new AirPods. You could also use this kit to clean some of your other devices as well. Good buy.

I loved the idea of sleep headphones because I kept losing my AirPods in my sheets at night. This one by MMUSS paired easily with my iPhone and the battery time is really good. I like how you can maneuver the headphones inside the cloth to fit your head shape. What I didn’t like is that the band itself was uncomfortably tight. I don’t have a large head either. I think I might be able to stretch it out a bit hopefully as I wear it. Also these didn’t get incredibly loud, which was fine for nighttime music, but listening to ASMR wasn’t quite loud enough. They’re a 3.5 for me.

I needed a quick and inexpensive replacement for my headphones after dropping my old AirPods in a sink full of water. After that incident I was happy to notice that these are water resistant. I’m not going to test it out by submerging them or anything. But from the looks of it they can handle the occasional splash or two—just in case of mishaps. These headphones paired easily with my iPhone X and the sound quality was just as good as my older style of AirPods. I’m very happy with these. Good value!

Not all cables are created equally. This USB C to lightening cable is a step above. It’s high quality with attention to detail and it works great! I love the sort of braided wire that’s so much more durable than the other smooth kinds. Not that it matters, but it looks nice too!

This is probably way more power and performance than I need for my casual and infrequent gaming, but I love the look of the video and when I do play my favorite life simulation game, the graphics are outstanding. I’m not good with computers so I can’t speak much towards the complicated technical components, but one issue I do have is the keyboard. I find it a bit difficult to type on since none of the keys are raised at all. It’s probably something I’ll get used to and I do like the size of the keyboard at least.
Got it for kicks but still cute and an okay volume

They're a little on the small side. This is good for me because they're easier to store and lighter, so more comfortable to wear. For a large man, these might be a little too small.

The sound quality is excellent for meetings, videos, that sort of thing. They aren't virtual surround (and they never said they were) so they aren't ideal for gaming. I use them for foreign language study practice with a remote tutor and they're perfect there, especially that it's easy to mute in a class setting.

I charge them every few days, and the battery lasts a good long time. They charge via USB-C. They charge quickly and there is an indicator light on the side to show when they are charged. Pairing is simple. Just hold down the power button until they go into pairing mode.

For my purposes, these are nice.

What I don’t like

The lack of a numeric keypad is a little disappointing, especially since that could be done on the letter keys with a simple num lock.

What I like

This machine is blazing fast. I’m used to telling a machine to do something that should be a long-running process and then going on to do something else. I don’t have a chance. By the time I switch windows, it pops up a “Done” message.

I wanted to use this for gaming, and so far every game I’ve tried has said this machine meets or exceeds the required specs. For a basis of comparison, Jedi Fallen Order, a game notorious for being demanding on its system requirements, lists this as “Should run well on this machine”. I have seen no problems playing any games so far.

They gave me a fingerprint reader with this, which is nice, if a little difficult to set up because it sits on the side of the machine connected via USB, but which is likely not needed as the camera on this can handle Windows Hello. Please note, at least on my machine, the camera came disabled on the function keys. The camera button on the top right was lit with a slash through the camera icon and the machine said no camera was detected. I hit the button and it was fine. I’m used to a “camera is disabled” not “camera doesn’t exist” message here, but no worries other than if that happens to you, check that before panicking like I did. I should add that the camera and microphone are excellent for Zoom meetings.

Another reviewer said it’s hard to see the writing on the keys. Personally, I have no issue with that. I do like the backlighting in dark situations and don’t think that makes seeing the keys any more difficult. The product photos look to me to be accurate on this point, so they will be a good guide to whether or not this will be an issue for you. I will point out the backlight shuts off after a brief period of inactivity. Touching a key, the screen, or the touchpad brings it back.

The pen is magnetic, but seems only able to catch on the sides of the machine, not the back. That makes it easy to store and keep track of. It has two function buttons, comes with two spare tips, charges via USB C and has a small cover when not charging. Just pull the top up to expose the USB port and push it down when done. I went from no charge to full in less than fifteen minutes. I ordered a pressure sensitive pen to use this as a drawing tablet, but don’t plan to just retire the stock pen. It’s a nice one and I can see it being the go-to when it’s time to bring this to the office or something. I should point out mine came with a black pen, not the silver shown in the product photo. I've used that silver pen before and it isn't as good.

The screen is beautiful for gaming and for video. The speakers are on both sides of the keyboard, making this exceptionally good for the new virtual surround feature Netflix released.

The switch to tablet mode is smooth and easy. I didn't feel resistance or anything I would find concerning.

It’s light given its size. It’s not as light as an iPad, but that’s the tradeoff for the larger screen. I find it comfortable to relax on the couch watching a video or reading comics on the huge screen, but I do rest it on my knee or a book pillow. I have a Comixology backlog to catch up and the app works beautifully on this.

This is great for gaming, art, business/school, and making your friends jealous.

The good:

It’s loud, so it’s easy to find.
With the subscription, you are notified if you leave something behind, more or less. If the phone goes into power save, this doesn’t seem to work, or at least me it doesn’t, and there is a decent lag.
With the subscription (it really is useful) you can get a history of where something was last seen.
It works in reverse and can find your phone which is helpful.

The bad:
They don’t seem to last. I had two break so far. With the subscription you get a replacement, but without it’s a pain.
There is no way to disconnect one from the app, only replace it.
The good features need a subscription.

This is a beautiful device.

I’m not in love with the case. It connects via magnets and that isn’t very secure. I plan to upgrade that in the near future.

The pen is excellent. You do get the writing on paper not a screen feel from it, which is perfect. The button as highlighter is a nice feature, especially given highlighting is a common thing for books. The eraser feels a little harsh, no rubber and you do need to press down enough to depress it, but it’s not a stopping point. It’s an excellent pen. The Staedtler digital pen works, including the eraser, so if you lose the one that comes with it, there are options.

I am disappointed that waterproofing and cellular, both included in the Oasis, are missing in this.

I see a lot of comparison with the competition, with some disagreement as to who the competition is. Contenders are dedicated e-Ink writing tablets such as the Remarkable 2 or SuperNote and the Kobo Elipsa. I’ve used all of those, so let me try to break down how I see this stacking up.

For the Remarkable 2/SuperNote family, it depends entirely on what your goals are. Those are dedicated note taking devices that threw in some ebook capabilities. The Scribe is a reading device that enhancing the note taking and threw in some notebooks. The difference in the focus drives the difference in user experience. The e-note devices have multiple virtual pen options, from pencil to fountain pen, to brush pen controlled by the pressure of the stylus on the screen, where this has a very limited selection. You can add templates (with Remarkable 2 that’s a bit of a pain and you need to redo it with every software update, but you can do it; with Supernote it’s simple). E-note devices offer OCR and the ability to synchronize with multiple services, such as Evernote, OneNote and DropBox (Remarkable with a subscription). Kindle Scribe has no OCR I could find and sends notes only via email to the account of record. I see no way yet to add templates, but I bet, as with Remarkable 2, someone will design a workaround.

Where e-note devices are better at creating and sending documents, Kindle Scribe is better at receiving and reading them, especially with the updated send to Kindle website. Remarkable, best of breed for that, can send with a Chrome extension that sometimes flakes out and an app that requires almost constant logging back in. Kindle can go through a Chrome extension, a web page, an app, email, or, for Kindle books and library books, right from the Kindle store.

In addition, the Kindle Scibe has a superior reading experience. The screen has a higher resolution, which makes for a more comfortable reading experience. Where, with the exception of the Boox Lumi Max which is in a totally different price category, those devices have no front light at all (they’re for working, where the environment is presumably well lit) this has 35 leds (I find that excessive, but I’d rather too many than none at all). These lights adjust depending on the ambient light and can become warmer either manually or automatically as the time of day changes. This is ideal for reading in bed or reading before sleep.

Technically, I think the e-note devices are faster in response, by an order of a fraction of a millisecond. In practice, this makes no difference.

If you want to take notes primarily, go with an e-note. If you want to read primarily, go with an e-reader. If it’s an even split, I think the Scribe is the best experience. You have the option for the most memory with this. You’ll need to do workarounds one way or the other, and this is the least burdensome.

Now to compare e-readers. The Kobo is 0.1” larger, so little I can’t count that as a major win. The Scribe offers adjustable light temperatures. While some Kobo do, the Elipsa does not. I’m singling out the Elipsa for its note taking abilities as it’s the closest match to the Scribe. Neither are waterproof, which is odd for both as both have sibling products that are.

The Elipsa allows you to search your local library system and download a book right from the device. The Kindle lets you borrow a book, then send from the Amazon page for that book. There are wins on both sides here. For the Kobo, this is far more convenient as long as you only use one library system. You can put a book on hold and check your place in the queue right on the device. However, you can only use one library system. I have a library card for the Brooklyn Public Library and the NYPL. I borrow from both -- a thing Kindle can do, and Kobo can’t.

Elipsa doesn’t have Bluetooth, so no headphones and no support for audiobooks (Audible would have been locked into the Amazon family in any case). Scribe works perfectly for Audible, but I have to wonder, given the size of the device, if that’s the best way to listen to audiobooks. I’m not going to score that as a major win. Kobo lets you use DropBox to wirelessly put books on the device, but honestly, Amazon has been winning that game since the start and they continue to win here. There are just too many convenient options.

Kobo often has more sales on books, as they are Canadian and not constrained by the agency model, and you can save points for free books, but it looks like Amazon is heading in that direction as well, so that has no clear winner either.

For my purposes, I prefer the Scribe for the multiple libraries, for ease of transfer of books, and for how comfortable the device feels.

If you’re considering this, and reading this review, you’re probably considering your first foray into Kindle reading. Good choice. A few things to note about this.

The ads are not pop ups. I know some dead tree fans would have you believe, right in the middle of a tense scene, an ad will interrupt the page. That’s not how this works. What happens is, when you put the device in sleep mode, rather than say the cover or the portrait of a famous author, you see an ad. If you use the physical cover to turn on and off the device, you won’t see much if any of the ads. And yes, you can dog ear a page.

I have no idea why memes keep popping up to say you can’t. Actually, the things you can do with a print book that you can’t with a Kindle book are: Donate them to the library if the library starts taking books again, give used copies to a friend, sell used copies, have a bookmark accidentally fall out, and use them for, well, kindling. Kindle can do everything else. Things you can do on a Kindle and not a print book are: read in the dark, search for text, carry dozens of books in your pocket, create notes of virtually unlimited size (you run out of room in the margin of a print book), pick up a new book nearly anywhere, anytime, and instantly convert your entire library to large print.

Most library systems can send any borrowed e-book directly to your Kindle. And your place and notes are stored in case you borrow the book again or buy a copy. You don’t get that with print.

Amazon recently improved their send to Kindle features with a drag and drop web page that makes moving your own documents to the device extremely simple.

This comes with a USB-C cable, but not a charger (aka wall wort) so if you don’t have one lying around (I think the expectation is most of us do) you will need to pick one up.

16 gig might not sound like a lot, but most books fall under 2K. I’ve seen public libraries (I’m looking at you, Florida) with fewer books than this can hold. Audible eats the memory a bit more, but I find this to be more than enough.

You don’t get cellular connectivity with this, but that’s only with the premium Oasis line now. Scribe even missed out on that. I find it convenient, but I understand wifi is ubiquitous enough these days it’s not a big deal for most users. I have an annoying habit of finishing a book on the crosstown bus, then needing the next in the series. Yes, the cell phone tether works. No, that’s not as convenient as built-in cellular.
It has fewer LEDs than most, but that’s not a big deal. Four lets you read in the dark. The scribe has 35. Guys, it’s an e-reader, not a disco, no one needs that many separate lights on that small a device. The absence of a warm light and auto adjusting lights are a bigger issue here. The warm light makes a big difference when you’re reading before bed.

It doesn’t have the waterproofing, which I thought was a bigger deal when that first came out, but in all the time since I’ve yet to (knock wood) get a Kindle wet. It’s a nice to have, not a have to have.

The size can throw people at first. The screen approximates two things – an index card turned portrait and a mass market paperback page. The occasional “ghosting” mirrors the see-through element of the cheaper mass market paperbacks, except on the device it refreshes quickly, and the ghosting goes away.

There were some studies done that suggest memory is improved from reading from print rather than e-book. I want to point out a few issues and cite my own experience. First, all the studies I could find cite pop ups and other distractions as the primary issue. That is, the test is on a general-purpose tablet, not a single purpose e-reader. When they either do a study on an actual e-reader or compare with pop ups on the tablet vs someone coming over just as often and tossing brochures on their print book I’ll believe it. Unless all factors are equal, the study is inherently flawed. To my experience, my ability to absorb and either use the information (if it’s non-fiction) or retain it over time (if it’s fiction) is nearly identical in both, with the slight advantage of the e-book being able to search back in the text for prior information. It drives me nuts when a quote resurfaces in a print book, and I can’t find the prior mention again. Or when I need to find a code snippet in a shelf full of computer books rather than just search on device and have it in seconds.

So, if you’re comfortable with the mass market paperback format, the size, the quality, then this is a huge step up. If you want to lay your hands on information quickly, then this is a huge step up.
If you want portability, then this is a huge step up. I just had to help an elderly woman move into assisted living and the loss of space cost her nearly all of her much-loved library. I find it comforting that nearly all of mine fits in my purse. No more culling the library for space, then finding you need to buy a new copy. If you delete an e-book from your Kindle, you can download it again for free. I remember, in the dark days before the Kindle was invented, being stuck on a flight from Arizona to New York with nothing to read but the most misogynistic, worst written mystery novel I’d ever encountered. If I had a Kindle, I’d have had at least a dozen better choices at hand, not to mention rereads.

The downside here is twofold. First, Dune and The Great Gatsby look the same size on the reader, so it’s hard to eyeball that one is a super-fast read and the other a meaty novel. It’s also a little too easy to build up a massive TBR pile, given it takes no physical space, the device memory is ample, and Amazon keeps offering free books to Prime members every month, sometimes more than one, and a crazy number of deeply discounted books Prime or not.

If you are concerned about the environment, then this is a matter of economics of scale. On the last study I checked, the magic number was 20. At 20 books the manufacture and transport impact of the e-reader ties the impact of manufacturing and transporting print books. At 21 and beyond, the e-reader has almost no further impact as compared to the printing and transporting of physical books. E-readers have boasted substantial improvements in reducing their carbon footprint since that study, but I can find no more recent information. Even at 20, the worst number, it’s clear that e-readers are a pure win for the environment.

It’s a great device. If you want to go with this one as the entry level, you won’t be disappointed.

I’ve had a few Fire TV sticks over the years, and generally I love them. For this model, the first one I got was a dud. It died in 2 days. Amazon took me through some reasonable troubleshooting steps, then replaced it quickly and easily. The second one is a lot better.

In general, I find the remote has a weird tendency to, I guess “rot” is the word. The case starts to feel like it’s covered in a sticky mess. I don’t know why. I guess that’s why the remote covers are so popular. Not a stopping point – they still work – just a point of note. The optional game controllers do not have this issue.

There are ample streaming options. I’ve yet to look for something, even less common things like Wonderium and Funimation, and not find it. The UI is easy to navigate. The device is responsive. I put it through a 7.1 sound system and it can handle that no problem.

A few things to note, not exactly faults of the product, but faults you will encounter while using the product.

For the Disney+ login, the trick of using the phone just errors out and asks to re-authenticate over and over. If you use a strong password, that can be a pain. Once it works, it’s fine, just a pain to set up.

For the Ubisoft+ integration, for many of the games it starts to load then fails. I don’t see the same issue on the same games on PC, so it’s probably related to the app. This was the primary purpose for which I bought the device, so it is a bit of a disappointment. Also note, you need the Luna service for this, which is totally worth it on its own, by the way. Also, at least for me, while the video streaming was fine over WiFi, the gaming required the Ethernet adapter.

It’s not perfect, but it’s outstanding for such a low price. I often use it rather than power up my PS5 to watch Netflix because it is so much more convenient, and of identical quality.

What I like

It’s a strong unit. I wanted something I could put a long-ish lens on. I didn’t intend it for one of those giant lenses some people use to photograph birds from like a mile off, but maybe a 300 mm tops. This can totally handle that and probably can handle those giants too. It’s strong.

It has a good swivel arm to it. It gives a nice amount of resistance and stability to a motion shot. I like that for panoramic photography. I think it will be fine for that.

It has a good, round, bubble level built right in. It’s easy to use and has a target dot to line the bubble up over.

The height is nicely adjustable with four extending leg segments and a crank neck.

It’s portable. It’s lightweight. There is a collapsed handle you can pull out to carry it around if you’re moving through the day and don’t want to put it in a bag.

It has a nice sturdy hook on the bottom to hang your gear bag from, they say for stability, but I say to keep the bag off the ground. The unit is plenty stable on its own. I can hook a bag with a flash and about four lenses in it no issue.

The accessories are nice. You know the part that’s supposed to screw onto the camera? I’m not sure the name. You get two of them. I’m probably weird because I like to leave mine attached to the camera all the time, rather than taking it off and putting it on, and they are standard, so they fit any camera and any tripod. But if that’s how you like to use them, they give you a spare. I’m not arguing. Now I have one for a video camera.

You also get a phone holder that clips in the same way, and is large enough for the iPhone XS Max, which is a pretty big phone.

You also get a quality travel bag, big enough to hold those extra accessories so they don’t get lost. The strap on it is comfortable to sling over a shoulder or carry handheld.

What I don’t like

The color. I’m not a fan of metallic orange. That’s the worst I can say. It’s a great unit.

What I don’t understand

It comes some assembly required, but once it’s assembled it all fits into the travel bag and the box it came in, so why send it in pieces? You need to screw the little rubber feet onto the bottom. You need to screw in the turning handle. I mean, it’s five minutes of work tops, so it’s no big deal, I just don’t understand it.

This headset lasted until the foam over the earpieces rotted off, and I wish I could have replaced those because this is by far my favorite headset. They are super comfortable, especailly for long gaming sessions or long meetings, and I used them for both.  They're lightwight. The sound quality is increadible. The mike is fantasic. They're perfect.

For the price it’s decent. It’s not a gaming machine or a dev box, but it surfs the web, runs office software, and isn’t bad for video or audio editing for podcasts. Students aside from those in computer science will find this more than adequate.

I use them for the PS4 and I may have set them up wrong, but they don't vibrate. The sound quality is great It's easy to pinpoint enemies or whatever you're looking for. I had one game where I was looking for cats. For voice over game they're great. I used them playing Destiny 2 with a friend with no problems. They're good for a long gaming session.

I'm coming at this from the point of view of a beginner so I can't speak to any advanced features or rather features that require advanced techniques. For a beginner, I found it easy to set up and easy to use. It gave me no trouble when I worked with it in following the assigments of the class I'm taking. It is an absolute pleasure to use. I think one of the troubles in learning something new is struggling with difficult tools, and you won't encounter that here. This is wonderful.

I like the sound quality for calls, for music, and for audiobooks. They're small. They're comfortable. They stay in well enough to take on a run. The mike is a little above average for ear buds.

The only concern I have is about fit. Yes, they fit well, but I'm using the smallest caps on these and I usually take the medium. The small is about medium on others and the large is the largest I've seen, so if you usually use the smallest you may have a problem and if you're a big guy and the large can go too small for you, these are definitely worth looking at.

I'm not sure what the point of the USB cable is. You can't plug in your backpack. You can't use it to charge your phone. It's more like you use your own power bank, and rather than use the cable that came with it, and thus have the freedom to charge your phone everywhere, you use the port in the bag instead. Like I said, I don't get the point.

It's not perfectly waterproof. I got caught in a downpour and some of my papers got wrecked. But it was a downpour and I had no umbrella. It was better than most bags I have, so I can't complain too much there.

It's sturdy enough to stand up to the attack of the cat without issue. I give it high marks there.

That it has an RFID shield is perfect these days. That's almost a modern backpack requirement.

Once you can get them on, they stay on no problem. I found them a bit big and I can't wear them for long. The biggest problem I have is getting them in my ears properly. I find the wire keeps twisting and they keep popping out. That makes them a bit hard to use.

I use them to go running, and I have not had an issue. They last a long time on one charge. They have been fairly soaked in sweat and don't seem to care. They fold up nicely to be stuffed in a running belt.

The sound quality is excellent, both for music and for spoken word.

This have excellent pickup on the mike. They're great for online gaming. I have to admit, I use them as much with the PS4 as with the Nintendo Switch and they work just fine for both. They'll work on anything that has a standard audio port.

They can size a little smaller than most headphones I see, which makes them great for kids. They can size up for adults as well, but few go small enough to be kid friendly.

The sound quality is on point, exactly as you would expect from Turtle Beach. They are one of the most, if not the most, respect name in gaming headsets. The wire is long enough even for an adult to use comfortably.

I love them.

I'm in love with these for the gym.

I don't find earbuds comfortable in general, but these are somewhat better than average, so for people who don't have issues usually, they'll be great.

I do audio classes from Aaptiv. Some involve a lot of jumping and bouncing. Some, like yoga, involve putting the headphones in an unusual position (think downward dog and the headphones sort of danging). They stay. No matte what, they stay. I run. They stay in. I do cat-cows. They stay in. I love not having to keep adjusting them.

The sound quality is excellent.

This took a bit of getting used to, adjusting the ear cups and all. If there is a volume adjuster on the earphones, I've yet to find it, but I have it paired with an iPhone, and the Apple watch can set the volume just fine.

The sound quality is about what you'd expect in this price range. I use it for audiobooks and podcasts, and I think it's perfect for that.

The battery life is extraordinary. I accidentally left it playing an audiobook all weekend. I had started on leaving the office on Friday. I thought I stopped it when I got home, but come Monday morning it was still playing. The battery was half-drained. So if you need longevity, these are the headphones you want.

They don't fold and they are a bit of a pain to carry around. That's about the worst I can say for them.

They were a little tricky to pair with an ipad. I don't see the app as particularly helpful for these.

The best feature is one of the swap on ear pads. It looks a little more matte than the others with a visible tiny circle in it. Those crush up like earplugs, and then exactly like earplugs expand to keep the earbud in place. Those are also the most noise reducing. I can't say noise cancelling. These aren't that. But it does help keep of the ambient noise down. My main concern was one falling out, but with that pad, that hasn't been a problem and I doubt it will be.

I had no problem with ear buds disconnecting from each other. Once they got started, they were rock solid. I got about two hours worth of use out of one charge, and then ran out of time to listen. I think for me they will last long enough, and the case holds a charge for powering up on the go. It uses a standard USB cable. I like things that follow an industry standard.

These are seriously noise cancelling. The "I'm worried about walking down the street using these" kind of seriously noise cancelling. Fortunately, the app handles that. Your phone determines if you are sitting, commuting, walking, or running, and adapts the sound as appropriate. At the lowest noise level, total noise cancelling, these things are amazing. I sit in front of the machine room, and nothing. Every time I have a coworker put them on, they get an amazed look on their face. At the other extreme, and this has 20 levels, most of the noise is present, but muted. If I select Focus on Voice then I can barely hear the machine room, but I can hear my coworkers. In fact, when the machine room is loud, it's actually easier to hear my coworkers while wearing these set to focus on voice.

You have a lot of control of your music through the headphones without taking out your phone. The right ear piece is the touch-sensitive one. You can double tap it to answer or end calls, or to pause or play music. You can swipe up or down to raise or lower the volume. You can swipe backward or forward to fast forward or rewind. I found that feature a bit tricky to get the hang of and kept skipping tracks while trying to go back a little in my Japanese lesson. It's a little fiddly. Hold your finger on the touch pad to voice dial or to activate Siri (I'm not sure if this works with Hey Google or Cortana). Hey Siri won't work through the headphones, even if you have Hey Siri turned on. You can cover it completely (not partially, not cup it) to hear people through the microphone if you want to talk without taking these off.

There is a special app on the phone for these to enhance their performace and their ability to adjust to the environment. Get the app and run through the setup and configuration for maximum performance. There is even a button on the headphones you can push to have it optimize the noise cancelling. It optimizes for the area and for how you wear it, such as with your hair up or with glasses on. It is definitely worth it to take out the five or ten seconds it takes to let it do that. You get a much better experience that way. Keep in mind, however, that this runs in the background and eats the battery, at least a little.

It comes with an excellent case, again fiddly to get the headphones to fit in right, but excellent. They fold to lay flat against you if you take them off to wear around your neck. They do not grab your hair, even if you have long, wavy hair.

It's fiddly on setup as well. I paired it with an iPhone and it would show paired, but would not play music through the headphones. The issue is this. If you have it paired with two devices, it will only play audio for the first one it connects to. So if you want to go back and forth, you have to disconnect one before you connect the other. For a while I had to keep going into Bluetooth to connect it again, then go into the app to connect it again, rather than have it connect automatically once paired, or at least work in one step. It eventually straightened itself out there.

This morning I turned them on and they lauched the music app on their own. That is not a desirable feature, and I have yet to figure out how to turn that off. When it comes to what gets played, it's human's choice. It only happened the once, so I'm hoping that was a fluke and not an implementation of Auto Play.

A couple of things to be aware of:
1- The manual advises using the included cable (just a standard audio cable), not wireless, on an aircraft.
2- The unit cannot be used in any way while charging. It doesn't noise cancel. It drops the bluetooth connection. When it's charging, that's all it's doing. It does charge very quickly and with a standard micro USB cable, which comes included. Kudos for sticking to industry standards. I hate custom chargers.
3- The unit can be used for normal calls (you can even answer a call by tapping on the right earpiece) but it can't be used for apps like Skype.
4- Because this is doing a lot of sound processing, it's going to be slighly off for videos or games, much like a home surround sound is. Because it doesn't have control of the video, the way a home receiver would, it can't correct for that. I didn't notice it much.
