Unfortunately, I misunderstood and this is a very expensive selfie stick. It extends to 3 feet, is incredibly lightweight, is well-made and has a fabulous ball tip so that you can tighten your camera in any direction needed. It would be great at a wedding or event where you may not be able to see everything but want to capture some footage. It would also be great for taking selfies with a normal camera or recording with a small video camera. Basically, if you want to selfie stick to use with actual camera equipment rather than your cell phone, this is a very high-end choice with a padded handle, a lightweight telescoping aluminum arm, and easy to use lever to tighten the ball head, and a universal screw at the tip. Can't do much better than this. I also love the stylish bluegray finish.

Comparing the TR-985-C to a similar speedlight I own, I find the controls on this one to be much easier to navigate. It's nice not having to go find the manual whenever you want to change a setting. The built in deflector and diffuser are very convenient, as are the automatic options that check range and lighting conditions..

I've been using this TR-985-C flash with a Canon 7D Mark II. I take a lot of portraits and macros, and don't often use a flash. That said, it's nice to have a versatile set of camera equipment around for those times when you really want to take (or make) a shot in unusual conditions, and I'm not about to spend hundreds of dollars for the Canon version of something unless it's central to what I do.

I hate the effect of a built in flash. You get this terrible reflection, and the offset between flash and lens leaves a thin hard shadow around one side of everything. The thing I've appreciated most about this flash is that I can set it up somewhere beside or behind my subject and have it trigger when the camera shoots, which can really set up a nice effect in what would otherwise have been insufficient lighting conditions.

This flash has a lot of features for the dollar and feels well made. Thus far I'm happy with it.

I'll admit it right up front: I am an organizer junkie. I love having all of my things laid out perfectly and well organized in all of the different areas of my house. While I try to minimize as much as possible, if I do need to have a variety of items, and let's face it, electronics accessories and cords seem to multiply like rabbits, I want to keep them in an organized, attractive way so that I can always find what I'm looking for and so that they look nice on my shelves.

This two-piece set is meant to be a travel organizer kit for your electronics, but I'm using it in my office to keep all of the excess cords, cards, plugs, etc. for all of my various peripherals. It's fabulous, because I have one that I keep near my computer and one that I keep in my closet, depending on the frequency of use. If I need to get a cord out, it's right there, yet the cases are subtle enough that I don't feel like I'm looking at something overly functional all the time. It just looks neat, clean, and well-planned.

The quality on these is amazing. They are just stiff enough to hold their shape, yet flexible enough that if something's a little bit taller I can close the zipper over it and it's no big deal. The dividers attached by Velcro and so you can move them around so that it works perfectly around whatever it is you want to store and there. I've changed my mind a few times, and it takes two seconds to move the Velcro to hold everything perfectly in place so that it doesn't shift when you move the case around. I don't travel much, but if I did, I would definitely consider getting a second set for on the go. They are lightly padded and so would be a great way of keeping chargers, batteries, and other essential accessories safe. Honestly, I'm such a geek I would probably even use these for toiletries if traveling, because most toiletry cases seem like a messy jumble to me and I like how organized these are.

Overall, if you are on the fence about these, I would hesitate no longer. They are fabulous. I'm only bummed they don't make them big enough to house all the rest of the loose items around my office!

I've been using this TT660II flash with a Canon 7D Mark II. I'm not a professional photographer doing studio work. I take a lot of portraits and macros, and don't often want to use a flash. That said, it's nice to have a versatile set of camera equipment around for those times when you really want to take (or make) a shot in unusual conditions, and I'm not about to spend hundreds of dollars for the Canon version of something unless it's central to what I do.

I hate the effect of a built in flashes. You get this terrible reflection, and the offset between flash and lens leaves a thin hard shadow around one side of everything. The thing I've appreciated most about this flash is that I can set it up somewhere beside or behind my subject and have it trigger when the camera shoots, which can really set up a nice effect in what would otherwise have been insufficient lighting conditions.

The manual that comes with the TT660II is noticeably translated, but a bit of back and forth fiddling with the flash was adequate to learn the controls. The built in deflector and diffuser are very convenient.

This flash has a lot of features for the dollar and feels well made. Thus far I'm happy with it.

The 3600e is a bit bigger than it looks in the picture, so check your dimensions. I was impressed with how easy the setup was. I plugged in a couple cables and turned it on, and it was up and running. Changing the size and focus of the display are very easy, though you can only scale it by 50% or so with the lens.

During my initial setup, I had the projector at an angle to the wall I was projecting to, so I got a chance to see how much it would adjust to placement that wasn't optimal. I couldn't get all sides to end up square, but I got it close enough that it didn't look too bad. Overall, the adjustments should be plenty good for giving you a bit of flexibility in your placement, but you will want it reasonably square with where it is projecting.

Moving the projector to an optically optimal location took it away from my input devices, so I braced myself for a complicated setup of the wireless transmitter. I plugged in my HDMI cable to the transmitter, hit the wireless button on the remote control, and the source was projected on the wall! I've never seen a wireless transmitter setup so easy.

I also noticed the air input vent on the projector pops off and has an air filter like a small version of what you would find on a car, which sure beats trying to blow the dust out of the circuit board.

The 3D is an impressive feature. Not only does it use depth of field cues to convert regular video into a pretty convincing 3D, it can also convert side by side 3D to full screen that works with the glasses (2 pair are included). I found a lot of things in this format on places like Youtube. The 3D feature is a bit of a workout for the eyeballs, so I don't suggest having a 3D movie marathon until you are used to it.

In the middle of the day, the projected image is quite watchable, but feels a little faded. In a darkened room, it looks spectacular and seems more vivid than a conventional screen. I notice some fan noise when I turn it on, but have never noticed it while watching. It runs surprisingly cool.

Overall, I'm more than impressed with this projector. I love it right now for dance marathons and playing Just Dance with my toddler, and with the new technology coming out for the Kinect that is meant to work with projectors (not on the market yet but I think they are working on it) I wouldn't be surprised if this gets even cooler in the years to come.

This is a great out of the box projector for families, teachers, and those that want a simple, workable solution that isn't hard to install or understand. I'm really impressed with it. It's light years away from the giant projector I bought ten years ago!

I have been using this headset for about three weeks exclusively with Dragon Naturally Speaking voice recognition software. I spent about 30 hours per week narrating emails, reviews, and articles with voice recognition software, and I have found that the microphone sitting at my desk is a little bit too low for me, so I have to prop it up with a book and sometimes find myself hunching over if I forget to do that. Having a headset is really nice because I can sit back in my chair or sit with excellent posture, and the microphone comes with me. Most microphones have a pretty heavy base, so this is a huge plus. I have tried using a wired microphone in the past, and just found the wire annoying as it constantly got stuck in my armrest.

Things I love about this headset:

No wires, great range. I was able to walk down the hall and look out the window to see whether a friend had arrived at my door while finishing narrating a paragraph. I certainly don’t need to go far, as my house is not very big and it’s rare for me to want to narrate when I’m not looking at the screen. But it’s great to have the option.

The cradle is super awesome. The cradle is a small rectangular device that you can set the headset on when you’re not using, and it charges. The base to the cradle is very sturdy and won’t tip over, and it’s great to have all of the wires coming off the cradle rather than the headset. I find it easy to seat the headset on the cradle properly so it charges. I like that the whole unit can sit out of the way of my desk when I’m not using it. With my wired model, I just had to set it down on a flat surface, which always felt untidy to me.

The microphone seems to be at the perfect distance for using voice recognition software. The software recognized what I was saying without a lot of fuss and adjustment.

The earphones are very soft and comfortable, and did not hurt my ears even after using them for a few hours straight. I like that they muffle outside noises since both of the earphones are over my ears.

Things that aren’t so great:

The sound quality is fine if you are listening to a podcast or other spoken word presentation, but you should know that these headphones are certainly not meant for music. For my purposes, the sound quality hardly matters at all since it is so rare for me to listen to anything while narrating.

The earphones do slip off or need adjustment if I take a particularly vigorous sip of water or turn my head quickly to the side.

There is a tiny bit of white noise or static coming from the earphones all the time, and I have not been able to get rid of that sound. I’ve adjusted my computer settings in every location I can think of, and I just think that this is something I have to live with with any headset with included earphones. My wired model did that as well.

Honestly, I kind of wish there was a wireless headset that didn’t include any audio at all. All I need is the microphone, but all of these headsets seem to come with audio, and that tiny bit of white noise is just annoying enough to keep me from wanting to use it as my primary microphone. To be 100% clear, it’s not this product’s fault. All headsets seem to make that white noise that annoys me so much.

Overall, if you need a wireless headset, this one has good range, is comfortable on the ears even for a person who has sensitive ears like myself, and feels like a huge step up from the lower end Logitech wired models which I have been accustomed to. As long as you are using it as a communication device and not for any type of music, I think you will be happy with this purchase.

I was actually really shocked at how great this little portable speaker is. My cell phone found it in seconds, and in less than a minute I was listening to music from my cell phone, only out of this little speaker, it actually sounded great. In fact, the bass was so effective out of this thing that some of my favorite songs made it dance around the table.

I love that it is so much louder than the music I get out of my cell phone, and I also love that I can listen to hip-hop and rap and enjoy actual bass, which usually doesn't come through for my cell phone speaker at all.

You can actually control the music from your cell phone from the speaker itself. It has a pause/play button, forward and back, and volume controls. It also has a speakerphone control, in case you wanted to have a quick conversation from the speaker itself. I would not personally want to use the speaker as a speakerphone, but it is nice to have the option in a pinch.

The one thing I didn't care for is that when you tap the volume button and it hits its maximum, it beeps at you to let you know that it won't go any louder. It's a pretty annoying sound, and in my view they could just have left that feature out. I'm sure I would figure it out soon enough that it wouldn't go any louder.

Overall, I was really surprised at the quality, ease of setup, and range of sound from this cute little speaker. I'm delighted to own it, and anticipate it getting a lot of use over the coming months and years.

When I purchased my Dolica AX620B100 tripod, it was advertised as having a ball head. However, the ball head on that tripod only moves side to side, it doesn't fully rotate. Since most of my photography is outdoors in the landscape, it took a little doing to make sure my photographs were level even on bumpy ground.

This Vanguard ball head attachment fixes all of that. I have three tripods and one monopod in the house, and it attached easily to all of them. The ball head is easy to adjust and has an intuitive friction control lever which allows you to move the ball head just a little or a lot. I feel like I've got great control. However, it never gets fully floppy to where you could accidentally damage your camera, as with a ball head I tried in the store.

I also really liked the turning action of the quick release knob, it feels a lot more secure than the usual lever that I'm used to.

Overall, this is a great addition to my humble set of landscape photography and video equipment. It's easy to use, took me about two minutes to figure out and attach, and gives me much better functionality than I had previously.

I've been a fan of Seagate for many years, since their drives are generally long-lasting and reliable, yet inexpensive compared to comparable items on the market. Over the years, I've never had a Seagate hard drive that I felt died too quickly or had any kind of unexpected problem.

So when I was given the opportunity to test this huge Seagate drive, I was thrilled. Obviously, it's a bare hard drive, so you'll need to know how to open up your computer and connect the drive. Once I did that, the drive was immediately recognized by Windows and the drivers installed automatically. In order to make the drive show up and start working in Windows 7, I had to right-click on computer, click manage, double-click storage, double-click disk management, partition it, give it a drive letter, and format it.

This drive is built to handle 24 hour a day use as storage device attached to a network. Because I am a home user, I am not using the full capability of this drive, but for my purposes, having a huge hard drive to store my collection of horticultural images in raw format, this drive is faster than my other (non-solid-state) drive and I'm not noticing any noise when the data is being accessed.

Overall, this is a huge amount of storage space for the price and would make a great drive for home user or small business user. I've wanted to try one of these liquid CPU coolers for ages, but it always been a little too cheap to spend the extra money on one, and I confess I've been mildly concerned about using a liquid anything inside my computer. I'm glad I tried this out.

This particular model has a radiator style grate which the fan sits on (there is some conductive paste included), then has tubes leading to the cooler unit. The water is totally enclosed in the system, and I can see no danger of leakage. The fan is quiet and unobtrusive.

It has a four pin connector, so if your computer has a four pin connector as well, your computer can control the speed of the fan. However, the four pin connector can also connect to a three pin connector and it works fine, you just lose that extra bit of control.

The one small improvement I'd like to see is that the water/cooling area only goes to one side of the radiator type grate, not around all of the edges, so one side of it will always be hotter than the other. It still disperses heat well, just seems like a less efficient system then it could be.

Lastly, I love the thumbscrews included for installing. I hate dealing with normal screws, and the thumbscrews are such a thoughtful touch that it made me think well of the company for including them.

Overall, if you've been on the fence about testing out one of these new liquid CPU coolers, I don't see any reason not to try out this one. The price is reasonable for what it is, and it looks like a highly effective setup, certainly better than just using a fan.

When Amazon offered me the opportunity to review this product, I jumped at the chance. I was intending to purchase a new computer soon anyway, and the opportunity to try out a thunderbolt device and experience the faster transfer speeds I have read about was too good to pass up.

I was also excited to see that when purchasing from Amazon, the cord is included in the box. When purchasing from Western Digital, the cord is sold separately. This may sound like a small benefit, but given that thunderbolt cords can run $50-60, it's actually quite a nice perk.

Unfortunately, the Amazon product page does not, at the time of writing, say anything about whether this device is meant for PCs or Macs. I went to the Western Digital webpage to see what they had to say, and they say that the device is formatted for Macs. I am a PC user, and do not wish to switch to Mac because I use a number of industry software programs that are only available for PC.

However, I've seen a number of reviews lately of new PC motherboards and laptops that do have the thunderbolt connection, so I wondered if, despite Western Digital's initial formatting for Mac, the product might work just fine on a PC.
In order to figure that out, I called up Western Digital's support line (1 (800) 275-4932) to ask. They say that because the hardware for PCs is so new, they have not yet been able to fully test whether or not their devices work for a PC. In theory, they say, their device should work just fine with anything that has a thunderbolt port, because the manufacturers of thunderbolt friendly devices would have created the port to use with devices just like this one. But they certainly can't guarantee it because the hardware simply hasn't been out long enough for them to have tested their devices with these new configurations.

In order to use the drive with a PC, you'll need to start by formatting it because it comes formatted for Mac. Western Digital has instructions for formatting your drive on their website, and that should be pretty simple.

One disadvantage to using this product with a PC right now is that the drive utility software which allows you to switch from RAID-0 (fast) to RAID-1 (duplicating data for a dual backup) or JBOD (just a bunch of discs) is only available for Macs. However, the main appeal to me was using the RAID-0 setting, which Western Digital says is the default. (And for any computer newbies who are paranoid like I am, you should know that formatting your new drive will not change the default, as that is a hardware setting.)

Support staff did say that they are working on creating drive utility software for their drives that will work for the PC. Unfortunately, since PCs with the thunderbolt connection have been slow to come out, they are unsure of when exactly the drive utility software for PCs will be available. It partly depends on how fast the market embraces this technology.

As far as the benefits of this new technology, the faster transfer speeds speak for themselves. Support staff let me know that you can see some of the testing information for these devices in writeups from the recent CES tradeshow. It would be particularly helpful to have this kind of speed when doing things like video editing, 3-D design, or any other activity that requires fast storage or moving a lot of data constantly. It can be used as a scratch disk to load video or audio clips faster, to crunch numbers or to create a final file from a build file even faster. While a faster storage device will not make up for a lack of RAM on your computer, if you have a high-end device and use it for activities like these, you should see a major bump in productivity from the addition of a device like this.

Some other notes:

You can daisychain up to six devices.

You get 30 days of free phone support to help get you set up, and I was only on hold for about two minutes prior to speaking with a human being. There is also pretty good online support available.

Support staff are excited to talk with PC users and help walk us through any issues we may encounter. If you find that level I support does not know how to answer your questions, ask to speak with a level II support staff person since they will be eager to take notes and share the experience with the people working to develop the products.

I personally do not yet have a PC that will work with this device. Now that I've been able to speak with Western Digital and ascertain that it will probably be worth my while (and the extra cash) to invest in a PC with a thunderbolt port, I am eagerly researching the best models of motherboard and building my computer. I will absolutely report back as soon as I get my computer and am able to test this device with a PC.

And as is the case with headphones, for a bit more, you can do MUCH better, and for a bit less, you will get roughly similar results. (In other words, headphones under $75-$100 are, more or less very similar, and then suddenly, your options get drastically better.)

Here's my analysis on the general sound quality and other features:

MISC:
Phone calls: 5 stars: Easy to use, works great for calls on both ends, and blocks outside sound quite well!
Ease of use/pairing: 5 stars: It passed the test of not having to read instructions, meaning it is incredibly simple to pair and use
Appearance: 5 stars: Neat! It's colorful and fun, as well as practical and functional!
External noise: 4 stars: Because it has a pretty tight seal, it is like an earplug, blocking outside sound quite effectively
Comfort: 3 stars: comparable to others of this design. Totally fine at first, and annoying after long use.

SOUND:
Treble: 2 stars: quite tinny
Bass: 2 stars: ok depth, not great, not very powerful
Overall: 2 stars: not much detail in the sound, but it can get pretty loud without distorting, and it is definitely good enough for basic listening and phone calls. There also appears to be a *very slight* hiss in quiet/silent moments when the volume is louder.

OVERALL:
The average is 28 out of 40 possible points, or 70% (a "C" grade, if it were going to school ;-), but because the above analysis does not take price point into account, comparing this to brands like Bose, as well as dollar store headphones, this means that for the current list price of roughly $29.99, this is a reasonable expectation.

The average number of stars based on my rubric is 3.5 stars: decent for this price point, and certainly good enough to enjoy music and spoken word, and to have successful phone calls.

Between the perfect fit of the earbuds and the detailed full-range sound, these headphones create an immersive sound experience.
The bass is deep and powerful, and the treble is crisp and clear—not tinny like many headphones. The sound is detailed and clear enough to allow the listener to hear ambient sounds in the recording like breath or clothing (depending on the particular track, of course), so one can pick up fairly subtle elements and enjoy music with both very quiet and quite loud parts. Likewise, it’s great for radio and podcasts because voices and words sound defined.

And the setup?
Well, it passed my “can I make this happen without a manual or instructions” test. I didn’t open the booklet, and that was fine! Turn on Bluetooth, press the button between the volume buttons for a bit, it shows up, and bam. You’re ready to go. So far, I haven’t needed to read anything—it works and is straightforward.

Phone calls?
Fine! Just like the wired headphones but wireless—no issues!

Pairing and installing this handy little gadget took about a minute after installing the free app. Allowing you to name each TrackR, you can easily ping whatever thing you’re looking for and probably hear it as much as a ringer on high. There’s one small bug in the app, which is that it keeps saying Bluetooth is off, even when it’s not, but you just click on it, and it sort of realizes it’s there, so it’s not a problem.
Easy use and installation, replaceable battery, nice loud volume!

Bose has been and remains the best headphone maker. I’ve tried at least a dozen different products on amazon, with perhaps a dozen more in my life, and in all those experiences, the Bose name always stood far ahead of the crowd.

First, their noise cancelling technology remains the best. Eerily effective, especially on airplanes and in cars, trains, or buses, you put them on, and the world becomes quieter, making you realize how terrible the ambient noise was! These have the added benefit of adjustable noise cancellation, unlike previous models.

In comfort, these are built for long-term use, remaining wearable for hours. Most other headphones I’ve tried tend to make your ears sore, but not these! They feel soft and lovely everywhere they land on your head.

With or without Bluetooth, these offer exceptional clarity of sound, powerful bass, and clear crisp treble, none of which turn to distorted noise, even at high volumes. Yes, these are very powerful! And they offer the option for wireless battery-operated use or plug-in use. They sound equally good in either setting. As for battery life, these won’t let you down. They last hours and hours without needing a charge.

My partner has the QuietComfort 30, I believe, and I always loved borrowing those, so it’s great having a pair of my own (in an even better version, no less!)

Fantastic! No product compares to Bose.

There’s a lot that’s great about these headsets, and only one kind of annoying thing.

The annoying thing is the app.
You need Spotify for the app to do anything. Once you have it, it seems to only work by leaving the Jaybird website, where it re-routes you to the internet, which then tells you to go to the Spotify app. I tried it a few times after setting up a Spotify account, and at no point did the pretty and cool-looking Jaybird interface work. Instead, I went through the ridiculous Jaybird to safari internet to Spotify loop. Annoying fail.
It also lets you make minor adjustments to the sound levels, with both pre-set stuff and manual stuff. I didn’t see a huge difference.

Aside from that nonsense, the sound is fine. Not great, but very good. The earbuds last about 4 hours, and with only 5 minutes in the little box (if fully charged), you get an additional hour-long charge worth of usage! That’s pretty cool! In total, the fully charged box can provide an additional 8 hours, giving you a total of 12 hours. Very nice.

They have a certain amount of inadvertent noise canceling, which is great if you want that, but not so much if you’re driving or doing something else that requires partial attention.

Good product with many nice qualities—not the best version of this, but still excellent!

Bear in mind that as gaming headphones, the sound quality is not as suited for other applications like listening to music. Having said that, here's how the experience went:

Appearance: maybe this is some macho thing, but they are enormous and intense-looking in an almost exaggerated way. So if you're one of those people that likes huge flashy stuff or ostentatiously masculine-looking things, this is perfect? They're huge.

Comfort: Very comfy! The cup part is large and fits great, and the headband adjusts nicely to most average head sizes. The microphone is fully adjustable, making it work for anyone.

Sound blocking: pretty good! While it does not use noise-cancelling technology, the sheer size and generous build of the headphones allows for Very effective sound cancellation. I had my partner listen to something with her back to me so she could not see me, and with the volume turned up, I had to full on Scream for her to hear me.

Sound quality: Better for spoken word and voices, honestly. The sound is crisp and detailed, but it's also a little canned-sounding, with somewhat sharp, tinny trebles and less-than-intense bass. This does best in mid-range and capturing voices and sounds, and less so for actual music. Having said that, it is certainly better than cheap headphones for music, so it does have some versatility if you're not too picky.

Overall: These are pretty great! They even have an adapter that can be used by other devices that unites the audio input and output, which comes split for certain applications like computers or other gaming. (Meaning, theres a separate cable for the microphone and audio input, and they come with an adapter to have a single "female" connection that can work on phones or other single-plug devices using audio in/out.)

Cool!

There are some pretty neat features with these headphones that make them uniquely better for some people. For example, if you are slightly hard of hearing (but do not use/need a hearing aid), these can actually turn the world around you up, making it a bit louder to better hear conversations. Likewise, you can turn the world down and make things more quiet!

The charging and holding case is also pretty awesome! They live and charge in this neat little box that indicates when it is charging or ready to pair, a process that was relatively easy, but sometimes buggy when putting on and taking off.

For music, you get a nice amount of detail in the sound. I always test it with orchestral music to see if you can pick up on the gentle rustle of clothing. Yes, you can hear that! At the same time, however, the sound can be a *little* tinny and lack richness among the treble notes. Overall, the quality for music is good. Not amazing, not mediocre or bad. Just a solid good.

For audio, it is excellent--crisp, clearly-defined sound!

And yes, you can make phone calls with these!

They take a little troubleshooting to figure out, but they're well worth the effort for their many interesting features. Cool technology!

I tested these out with my parents, who have some hearing issues when we watch tv, and this has made a HUGE difference!

First off, setup wasn't bad at all, and once the power and audio stuff is connected, it is SUPER easy to use. No crappy pairing process, as is usually the case with bluetooth. These are paired to the base already, so to turn them on, you basically just wear them. When you take them off, sound stops coming out. To charge them, you just put them back on the base. No re-pairing, loss of signal, etc.

Also, the range is great! We have a big house, but you can walk pretty much anywhere and keep the signal going. It's nice because if you have a show on and need to do something by the kitchen or in the garden, you can keep listening as if you were in the same room--no problem!

The sound quality is perfect for TV. I know some people aren't thrilled about it for music, and while that's totally valid, these are more for tv/movies anyway. For that, the clarity of sound is great, and you can go to pretty high volume. Also, you can adjust the volume differently for EACH EAR. So if you have hearing loss on one side but not the other, you don't have to harm your good ear and only hear quietly from the other--it has easy adjustments for this!

Comfort: Great news: these hook into your ears and hang down comfortably, and they do NOT have to go over your head. Why does this matter? Because you can wear them with glasses without interfering or squishing the glasses into the side of your head. The pressure is strong-ish (so they don't slip off) so if you are sensitive or prone to headaches from pressure, you might not want to wear them all the time, but for most people, it should be fine for a few hours at a time.

Difference between the 2000 and the 5000 model? 50 feet range difference, and 3 hours less time on a full charge for the 2000. Sound quality seems the same, and functionality is pretty much the same.

Awesome solution for those with so-so hearing, or people sharing space and not wanting to bother neighbors or other residents.

The main issue I have with headphones is usually the fit, then secondly, the tendency for the sound to be tinny. But this is Bose.

Known for innovative and exemplary sound quality, Boss speakers and headphones are consistently top-of-the-line, and these are no exception to that expectation. The high and low ends remain clear, crisp, and defined, free of distortion of echo, maintaining detail in whatever you are listening to, whether orchestral or spoken word, hip hop or show tunes. Everything sounds great!

As for fit, that is also great! They stay in perfectly and block out noise quite well, and I can dance with them without problems for the most part. That's a first!

These are excellent. But if you've heard of Bose, this won't be a surprise.

This would have easily gotten 5 stars if it worked better with Apple products. It is really not wanting to work with my iPhone at all. We are on the same wireless network, and I have the remote control app. I follow all the simple steps in the instructions, and...nothing. I've spent a good amount of time and really don't want to invest more, so as of now, the only way this thing works is by directly connecting it to my laptop. Not so much with the wireless options, which is what I liked about this to start with.

Having said that (and it's a big problem if you're a Mac user, to the point that if I had to pay for this, I would be incredibly angry and probably want my money back), the image is clear and has excellent definition, with plenty of settings to adjust angles and distances. It doesn't have to be pitch black to look good, either: the projector has impressive throw for the size. It is fairly quiet and doesn't have a huge heat output, and for the size, the speakers are decent (though you can use others, of course).

I hope they do something to make it more Mac compatible. I hate how few things work with my devices.

The last few speakers and speaker systems have had a common theme: bigger isn't better, and pretty doesn't mean good. This is another such case, where of course, these speakers are an amazing add on compared to standard factory speakers, but are not exactly "amazing" or anything. They look fantastic and are big, so if you like flashy, this has got it! And their sound is solidly good. It is not great. Expect distortion at high volumes with music heavy on bass, but also expect a big improvement on your sound if you use this at a reasonable volume.

Setup for my mac took about 30 seconds--I clicked the Mac setup button, and it installed something very quickly. The rest was drag and drop, which was equally fast. I was able to drag and drop 4-5 minute movie clips in a second or two, where back in the day, you'd have to wait a bit. It's really that easy and that fast! great product!

This is the second or third Seagate brand portable external device I've owned and used for my Mac without any problems. It works quickly and plays fine with "Time Machine". It works quickly (faster than older generation externals I've used) and is quiet and small. These things get better and better every time! I love it!

Not only does it update writing in almost real-time, as well as make appointments, but it uses the phone audio to record while taking notes, in case something got left behind. The notebooks cost a bit, but for a neat luxury item like this, it probably doesn't matter for users. The pen looks elegant and isn't too bulky, There aren't many changes from the previous mode, according to the distributer, so it's mostly what it was before, but happily, older papers and newer ones will work with this, and supposedly, the battery lasts a tiny bit more.

For people not upgrading, but rather trying this for the first time, here are some of the features with this product:
-can turn legible writing to text on apps
-can save artwork and immediately make it digital (REALLY useful for artists, designers, engineers, etc)
-jot down text with audio context available by clicking on text

It's not an office essential, but for some jobs, it's pretty great.

Not only is the video clear (no more of that low-res fuzzy junk of the past), but it also has a wide view corrected by software that prevents it from looking distorted. The technology is great, offering more security, motion and sound sensing, and selective recording. To top it off, there's a very quick and easy installation video so you don't have to read instructions--this is a big deal for people with little time and patience (me). Great results for a reasonable price--my small business needs were met with this!

I'm not great with technology, and this is the first time I try to install one of these things with no help at all. It didn't go very smoothly, so if you're like me, just consider that. I put all the plugs in the right places and....nothing. I got my computer out to set it up and followed the instructions. It didn't work. I had to call support, and thankfully, that got me up and running, so yay for that! The house is pretty big (2 stories and over 3,000 square feet), so before this, we had to have one of those Apple things (I'm so embarrassed at the fact I don't know what this is called--sorry, people) in the upstairs to boost the signal and also to keep the network for a wireless printer close by and closed-off to other house traffic...anyhow, we kept that because of the last reason, but we are happy to say the router IS a bit more powerful than the other option we had, and those nifty antennas appear to be more than "for show"! haha

So yeah...good tech support, stronger signal to my otherwise substandard AT&T garbage internet (side note: don't use AT&T internet), and it was user-friendly enough for me to eventually work it out. Eventually.

Some stuff isn't great with Mac. That sucks, since 4 out of 5 of our computers are Mac, and we have iPhones, so no app for us, and no CD installation (not required, but still...).

4.5 stars!

This case is pretty amazing! It is slim, VERY lightweight, and almost completely waterproof. I even did the submerging test, and much to my surprise, it had no leakage whatsoever. Very cool. Below are some details:

Protection: 4.5 stars
I can't help it. I love protecting the screen, and this doesn't do that. I had to take half a star off. Other than that, the body is VERY safe in this device, not just from drops, but from liquids and most day-to-day nonsense. But in a bag, where the face might get scratched? meh... not so much! It was also a little unclear if you could apply a screen protector and still keep all the benefits like it being water-proof.

On that note--the waterproofing is impressive. The clever design uses a tight rubber seal around the areas where water might penetrate, allowing your ipad to still be exposed where it is safe (the screen). It even has a special extension that allows you to use the headphone jack. VERY cool.

Functionality: 4.5 stars
You can use the charging port and heaphone jack fine, but the speakers don't sound so great with this. (Completely understandable, and it's just a trade-off you have to make if you plan on making a mess on your pretty toy ;-) This is why we can't have nice things, am I right?)

Design: 5 stars
The concept and execution are brilliant, combining functionality with durability, practicality with aesthetics. While putting it on and taking it off is an ordeal, the flip side of that is the fact it won't fail you. This case is dependable. Best of all, unlike some similar super-strong cases, this one is low-profile and lightweight--not the clunky thing you would expect at all.

EXCELLENT

This is a great tool for small businesses using tablets for payment processing and record-keeping, which is a growing trend in point of sales. As a small business owner, I look forward to using this over what I was doing before, which was just using my iPad and handing it to customers when completing transactions. This way, it can live on the desk instead of in the drawer and swivel around when wrapping up a sale. A nice bonus is that it slightly deters theft by requiring a key to unlock this whole heavy stand from the iPad.
Adjusts well, is sturdy, and looks clean.

Great portability! This door alarm is perfect for dorm rooms, hotels, and travel. Following the simplest of instructions, you will get a loud alert that someone is entering the room, which will wake you up (or get your attention), startle the person trying to enter, and slow them down a bit with the door stopper. It's nice peace of mind for some situations.

These had FAR better sound quality than I would have expected. Usually, kids' headphones (from what I've experienced) don't bother with making sure the music has detail, decent treble and bass, etc. While these have a volume limiter, which is great for protecting their ears, the headphones still pick up everything a pretty good quality set would.

Likewise, we put them to the test and sat on them, bent them, dropped them--they survived! These guys are TOUGH. The added padding that is removable is a nice touch--they can grow with your little one by letting them adjust the fit for the size of their head.

Great product--best I've seen so far!

My only disappointment was the wire that came with it. It didn't correspond to anything on my Macbook Pro, but looked like it would connect to a computer I had 10 years ago--definitely not a Mac. It SHOULD have come with a USB-->HDMI cable.
The picture clarity was excellent, and it did remarkably well in a lit room, but as might be expected, looked incredible in full darkness. It is portable, very user-friendly as far as basic usability goes (plug and play), high resolution as long as the original image is, too (obviously, low-res images and video like some youtube stuff will look even worse when projected from far away, as the pixels look bigger and more noticeable, but that is not the projector's fault).
EXCELLENT PROJECTOR!

Some downsides common to all projectors:
-some noise from the fan
-heat produced from the exhaust

Some downsides to this projector:
-does not come with wire options for a Mac, so make sure you buy/have a cable for this. Takes USB-->HDMI, which worked great for me
-not widescreen

I wanted to give this 5 stars. The pairing process was So easy, the product is excellent, and if I had a skin to protect the back of the iPad, I would actually use it. Here's the problem: the skin comes after a lengthy bunch of nonsense, and because that is part of the product, it must be part of the review. I was unable to get mine in time for the review, but it is on its way.

GETTING THE SKIN:
You have to go to their website, some parts of which contain dead links, like the registration info that came with the product. Likewise, it kept going to the mobile site, which, ironically, did not get me to where I needed to go for getting the iPad skin. (Yes, I couldn't manage to get the iPad stuff through my iPad.) I used my computer and filled in a detailed registration with more info than I like to give for these things. The info card said I would get an email with a promo code in exchange for all this info, and that promo code would let me get the free skin. No promo code. I went back to the ridiculous site and tried to contact customer support via email, but apparently setting up an account was not enough, because when I logged in with the info I gave them to set up the account, it said it was invalid (and that same info DID work to pull up my customer info, so I do, apparently, have an account with these people now...not that I wanted to). I decided to not make a second account but then call instead. They're closed on Saturdays (which is when I am writing this), and I am honestly too fed up to spend another hour on this. Not fun, not easy, and lots of catches. I even had to take a screenshot of my order info to prove I purchased it.

The code came after a bit over half an hour of nonsense. It doesn't sound like much time, but for a busy person that doesn't care to fool around on the internet giving companies lots of info, it isn't great. I was sent to the website where you can customize skins for an iPad.

The customizing site was pretty cool. It offers many pre-made designs, as well as allowing you to make your own. I opted for the latter as a small business owner. It looked great on the screen, so we will see how it looks in person.

Updates soon! (hopefully)

UPDATE:
A few weeks later, the skin arrived, and it actually looks great! The application was easy, and it is completely customized the way I intended. This product came with some hassles, but it was worth the wait and trouble. I am going from 4 stars to 5!

For the price, this is a good product. The sound quality is 4 stars (clear, good volume, some sound cancelling, though probably more because of proximity to face and structural design of mic), the fit is 3 stars (decent comfort for a short call, but irritates the tops of ears after a while; also doesn't look great for Skype/Face Time calls), and value is 5 stars. This is a great inexpensive option if you want to avoid the echoes and background sound interference of using the speakers in your computer. Nice!

I was a big baby about opening this one up. I didn't want to deal with the instruction manual or learning how to program it or have to figure out how to use different features. Much to my surprise, this was so easy to set up, I didn't once have to read anything--everything was self-explanatory, and unlike smaller clocks, this one had enough buttons so you didn't have to press and hold things for ages and hope you didn't overshoot and have to start over.

Setup:
*Plug it in, wait a few seconds, and the correct time shows up!
*For alarms, press and hold "alarm 1" or "alarm 2" until it flashes. Enter the time with the number pad and select AM/PM. To activate the alarm, you set to the "radio", "buzzer", or "off" This takes less than a minute
*Radio works like any other

Features:
*The alarm doesn't start with the usual abrasive, loud sound that can be startling; it starts inaudibly and gets louder (maybe not quite as loud as I would like, but ok)
*Snooze button allows for radio playing or soothing sounds
*Soothing sounds include ocean, babbling brook, meditation music--sound quality on these isn't great, but it's a nice touch for snooze
*Time can be projected onto a wall--the projector can be turned on and off, and rotates 180 degrees. Excellent feature!

I hate clocks and always use my phone, but this is great! I might switch so I don't get tempted to play games at night, not to mention the ability to get weather info if the lights go out. BEST alarm clock I've owned! Very nice!

Contrary to some other reviews, I found these to be excellent earhook headphones! My favorite part was the fact they actually fit!! Other earhooks won't stay on my ears for more than two seconds, but these have two features that make them perfect for workouts and movement:
-rubberized earbuds that go into the ear canal (with three size options)
-a special rubber adjustment on the earhook itself. You slide the red bump on the side of the earbuds down to change the shape of the hook and lower the arc. For women, this is essential, as I am pretty sure other earhooks don't take us into account

As for the sound quality, there are better ones out there, but they cost much more. For the price, these are good--better than others I have gotten, that's for sure! As it says on the description, it is optimized for workout music, so it does best with pop, hip hop, and house music, but it's fine with other stuff, too.

Other features: it has a very nice hard plastic carrying case and a little clip on the wire to secure it to clothing and avoid movement

Great product!

For the non-professional photographer looking to get high-quality images in a variety of settings, this camera works great. I did a little experiment to see how it performed by taking it with me to Europe along with a much more expensive semi-professional Nikon (D3100). Here are the results:

Advantages:
-With our limited time, my camera was able to take a variety of shots (panoramic, zoom, close-up) quickly and easily while the Nikon could only take limited kinds because of the need to bring several lenses and because of the complexity (sometimes) of setting up a given shot
-Because it was small, I didn't have to lug around a big camera bag, which also had the potential of getting a little too much unwanted attention
-One feature I really enjoyed was the two simultaneous flash/no flash shot which gives you the same picture with and without flash, letting you choose later which you prefer
-Didn't need more than one lens
-With city shots of architecture, my camera fared better with its versatility

Disadvantages:
-In the mountains, the Nikon did better, capturing color and clarity/detail. In my shots, the trees looked less defined from high up. Also, his zoom lens was able to capture much more detail than my camera.
-Nature shots and portraits have slightly duller colors, missing something the other camera was able to capture
-There was slightly more blur in shots with movement with this camera

Conclusion:
For the price, this camera performed much better than I expected and was not as much of a hassle as our semi-professional camera, so for most people, this is not only going to be a better value, but less frustrating and cumbersome. For the professional, this is obviously not the best choice, but this isn't being marketed as a professional camera. This is a great family and vacation camera that everyone can use, and that still yields quality images with plenty of artistic integrity.
Great little camera, and fun to use!

I thought I had an ok sound system with my old iPod/iPhone dock, but once I heard this gorgeous machine play music, I had to toss the other one immediately. The sound was crisp and detailed, handling bass beautifully. I listen to a wide range of genres, and they all sounded marvelous--from classical and orchestral to hip-hop, world, and acoustic. The latter was particularly moving when I played a slow middle eastern violin piece--you could hear the clothing of the violinist move with the strokes, and occasionally hear him inhale a breath; it added such depth to the experience of the music, I was captivated. This sound system is of high quality and, as intended, works well with iPhones and iPods (the iPhone does not have to go into airplane mode, by the way, so you can still receive calls; also, it charges the device).
The docking station also has a lovely aesthetic--sleek black, unobtrusive size, small easy-to-use remote. GREAT product!!

I do not have a great point of reference because this is my first set of headphones of this type, but I am a big fan!  The set up was super easy.  The headphones themselves are really comfortable for me which is important because I have small ears.  The sound quality is great and the microphone works well.  I am not a tech person by any stretch and it was easy for me to integrate with my computer and phone.  Great product - I am a convert!

This is a really nice soundbar.  I have an integrated surround sound system with my main TV, so I am spoiled and this did not disappoint.  It was super easy to set up, though we did need to get a cord since our TV is older.  It is a little disappointing that it does not have WiFi, but that is not a deal breaker at this price point. The sound is great and it is relatively sleek looking. Very happy addition!

This is a great speaker. My preschool age daughter has been begging for a bluetooth speaker for her room for months and this one completely fits the bill. The sound quality is great and the bass is surprisingly good. It would also work well for small outdoor gatherings. Definitely the quality I expect from Sony.

These are decent kid sized headphones.  They came in super handy for use with my preschool daughter's kindle fire (the pinks match perfectly!) for a long haul flight. The only complaint I have is that they do not come with any type of carrying bag.  Also, just beware that they have a regular audio jack.  Depending on what you intend to use them with, that might be a nonstarter.  They are not compatible with new ipads/iphones without an adapter and they are not Bluetooth compatible.

My title pretty much sums it up - I love the Kindle Paperwhite! I am a big reader, but I resisted the e-reader obsession until December 2010 when I gave into a Nook. Back then I decided on a Nook because the Kindle did not allow you to borrow books from the library, which was a deal breaker for me.

Fast-forward two and a half years... My Nook was getting older and the discrepancy between prices and availability of e-books between Amazon and Barnes & Noble was becoming increasingly clearer. Also, I love Amazon as a general rule, and order from them pretty heavily for a variety of items, so it made sense to switch over. After brief research, I stumbled upon the Kindle Paperwhite. It met all of my requirements - a dedicated e-reader (no tablet for me, thanks), with a built in light. Yippee! My hubby and puppy (okay, just the hubby) purchased the Kindle Paperwhite for my birthday at the end of August and it was love at first sight. It is unreasonable to compare the Kindle Paperwhite to my old Nook, so I won't. I can freely admit that most of my love comes from the new technology and association with Amazon. I love the light. It is awesome to not have to use a clip on light at night. They are usually terrible and not evenly spaced. The light makes reading at night a breeze. Plus, it is a perfect light, so it really is like reading a book and not like reading on a backlit screen (a la the iPhone or iPad). I love the ease of purchasing books from Amazon, and I love their prices and special deals. But, most of all, I love checking out library books! The very thing that turned me away from the Kindle initially is now the best. There is no need to connect my Kindle to a laptop to download a book. Yay! I can just wirelessly send a book to my Kindle, the same as purchasing one. You must be a wireless network (not 3G), but that my dear friends is a tiny issue. Overall, I love my Kindle Paperwhite and I cannot think of one single thing to make it better! Love it.

Helpful tips - 3G or not? I love the 3G, but it's not a necessity if you have wide access to wireless. I would definitely say to go for the ads, however. They are entirely inoffensive and unobtrusive. They only come up when your Kindle is asleep. Save the $20 and buy yourself a few books!

These are fantastic! I needed some fans for a new build and wanted something that wasn't too 'flashy' and just worked well for airflow.

These low noise FDM fans are perfect for whatever application you need in your case build. They've held up well for a few weeks even at high RPMs for testing.

This is a great AP and I’ll tell you why.

Not only is it instant on, and requires only a few seconds to come up and sync, but it has the flexibility of 3 ports for expanding your network through it even further without running new home runs.

The Aruba management software leaves some to be desired, however.

After a few minutes of tinkering I was able to integrate this with my existing network, but you should be aware that in order to do so requires access to the web portal. The web portal requires a WAN IP to be connected, so if you are ever without connectivity you’re out of luck.

I've been using Zyxel equipment for several years now for things around the house, so I was excited to pick up this device and try it out to do more.

My favorite feature is actually the ease of setup for VLAN configuration. I operate a vlan heavy environment and it is difficult at times to get everything working right.

Thankfully the Zyxel makes it easy with it's straightforward and tidy interface.

The content filtering is a 'miss' out of the box, as other reviewers said it only inspects http traffic, however with some installation of certificates on your devices you CAN inspect https traffic.

I found this to be a very capable, very cost effective firewall that handles all the traffic I throw at it. I'll update my review over time as I have more time to break it in.

I recently picked up some Ubiquiti wireless equipment that is instant on and 802.3af powered.

I was a little bit worried at first that this would not cut it, but I was wrong. It took me only a few minutes to get this up and running and after that I was good to go.

I also tested it with Shoretel IP230 phones and aruba wireless equipment and did not have any trouble with the flexible power delivery across any of the devices. It's a great budget Gigabit POE+ adapter.

These batteries work well! There are a few requirements that I have for batteries. I want them to charge quickly and stay charged until I use them. I also want them to perform well once charged.

These batteries do all of these things and I very much appreciate them lasting all the way through the night!

I had not heard of the Yealink brand before, but I needed to demo some of these for work.

I utilize microsoft Teams most of the day and was interested in a teams certified device.

These Yealink devices are really just fantastic. I have dogs and kids in my house, and live on a busy street.

When I am using these headphones no one can hear anything going on in the background but they all say I sound like a RADIO DJ because the voice quality is so clear and in their ear. Excellent.

If you do any kind of Teams usage all day, these are your best bet. The teams button automatically launches meetings, and the USB controls let you mute and pickup/hang up callers.

This is a fantastic 4K camera for the price point. I have been revamping my surveillance equipment to include PTZ cameras so that I can adjust them after install.

This camera has it all.. local storage, H.256+, onvif support for third party camera software.. it's a full featured camera for certain!

My favorite part about it is the weatherproofing that was done to ensure proper functionality even in the worst of storms. The IP rating is wonderful and I have had zero problems since installing it underneath the eaves of my house.

The POE powered cables are wonderful, and they even come with waterproof connectors to ensure no long term damage occurs from moisture penetration.

We recently got our children a bunch of the film for those instant cameras and we have subsequently had a million little pictures everywhere.

Enter the photo album! Classic!

I had no idea that something like this existed, but it was an easy way to organize it for my kids.

Best of all, it's a bit customizable for you to make it "yours" and really make it a fun keepsake.

I grabbed this Azores AX1800 Wifi6 router to extend my existing Wifi6 system that I have with Azores.

The main issue I have with these is the lack of administrative options and detection.

I have used Netgear and Linksys equipment for a long time and always ran third party firmwares, but with this it does not appear to be an option.

Because of this, I generally operate these behind my network rather than as the primary router. So it is an SSID that sits on top of my network, rather than being a WAN device that connects directly to my modem.

The good thing is, this works fine in this mode and has no issues relaying internet through my house.

Don't let the packaging fool you - this mount is sized for 3 different stud distances and is sturdy for the price!

It comes with a giant hex wrench that you need to be wary of, I found that when mounting it on my wall I had mounted it so high that then I couldn't use it to adjust the mount any longer because it was so long.

The level-after-install feature is great, as it lets you adjust the TV level after installing since it is a more static installation than other types of armature mounts.

A friend of mine gave me an old TV but had no remote..

Universal remote to the rescue!

I purchased a model that said it was appropriate for Panasonic TVs, which ended up being a good choice.

What I was not expecting is that this remote ALSO works with my roku! Wow!

After putting fresh batteries in and I initially read the instructions which stated to let the remote auto config for the device.

This didn’t work for me, but thankfully I read onward because it actually states he preferred method is to hardcode your TV set to the device.

After looking up the Panasonic code, it took a little bit of tweaking (hint: press the buttons the number of times for the code needed. Example.. 1,1,1,1, is equal to 4 in the first digit of 4235. Then 2,2, 3,3,3, 4,4,4,4,4. Hope that makes sense!

So far working great and it comes programmed out of the box with streaming appliance support.

It's your typical extension cable. The bonus about this one is that it supports microphone as well as audio feeds.

I used this to extend my apple headphones to my PC and make it easier to talk on ZOOM and other types of conferences without constantly fighting with my headphone cable length.

The wrapped cable is durable and attractive, if that's important to you.

Mine came missing a black ring on the third divider, but it hasn't impacted performance.

The plugable USB C dock is one of a kind. I've been using iterations of plugable docks for years, and one of the best things about them is the way they combine USB expandability with additional monitors in a way that does not impact the performance of the underlying device.

What this plugable dock affords is a brand new way to think about computing, combining charging, connectivity to video monitors, usb, and network, AND audio, all through one cable. It's the "dream team" of the dock world.

I unboxed the plugable and found the smell to be invigorating, it's the perfect "new car" smell of PC devices.

After plugging the device into my PC, plug and play drivers (one of the claims of fame to plugable is plug and play compatibility) detected the device and windows update grabbed the latest driver.

Within minutes, I had my laptop plugged in to my three HDMI monitors and all of my peripherals ready to go.

The plugable dock is truly a great fit during this home-work environment.

I recently bought a bluetooth transmitter/receiver for my stereo system. It support SPDIF connectivity but I had exhausted those ports already, so I was stuck with phono connectivity which is 1/8in connectors. This adapter goes into my receiver, and then the phono cable goes into the adapter.

Audio quality is fantastic and have had no issues with popping.

I purchased this for my daughter to wake up for school with. It works great! When you set the alarm time, it goes off with a tone as well as a 'time' to wake up with the light.

The light begins going off in a countdown (say, 15 minutes) to the tone. So if your alarm is supposed to go off at 8am it will start lighting up at 7:45 to brighten your day.

It comes with 15 volume levels and 10 different tones, the 10th being the 'radio'.

Setup is straightforward and overall works great!

This audio cable works perfectly for what I grabbed it for. I'm up stepping it to a 1/4 inch adapter to attach my bluetooth transceiver to my stereo.

For this purpose, it's well suited and I did not get any 'cracks' 'pops' or 'sparks' when attaching it to my equipment.

That said, I would prefer more of a 'smooth' surface rather than the slightly grabby 'tacky' surface that this has.

Stereo equipment tends to collect dust and this style tends to attract more than the usual amount. Time will tell!

That is neither here nor there though, as sound wise it sounds great and delivers the analog signal as good as one could expect.

I'm a big headphone enthusiast and I was excited to review these. In the last month I've reviewed a pair of Jabra open air headphones and they blew me away. So I Was excited to do a base comparison of both sets.

First up.. comfort. Right out of the box these exude comfort. There is a THICK 1" pad that cups over my ears and sits snugly on my head. The headband is made of covered metal that ensures a nice reliable tight fit without being intrusive.

Second.. sound quality. There is a rich and well mixed sound stage for these headphones. Trebles and Bass both are well represented and the mids don't get lost in the mix.

Bass boost.. The bass boost feature is substantial and when it is on it feels like a subwoofer is on your head. Pick any 'bass heavy' track and you can actually feel your ear lobes vibrating from the bass response. excellent.

Charging time.. I have noticed that the claimed charging time is a little off. I leave these to charge overnight and after a day of listening the voice prompt tells me they are "medium" in charge. Well.. that's not 50 hours. I haven't done a full test to see just how many hours I Get out of it, so it may just be a quirk of the voice prompt detection.

Pairing is easy and it pairs well to multiple devices.. so far I have had no issues or interference under those circumstances and an 'all day wear' is easy with the comfortable pads.

All in all these are great!

It is my SINCERE pleasure to be reviewing these headphones, the Jabra 45H.

I have been an audiophile for as long as I can remember and I am always excited to break in a new pair Of headphones For the first time.

I recently received a pair of Monster brand headphones that I was supremely impressed with, but I have to say that these headphones blow away any expectations I had.

First - audio quality. The in-app equalizer that is presented after doing the custom audio tuning for your specific hearing is wonderful. I can quickly change my tuning based on application at the touch of a button and the volume level and mixing delivers!

Pairing wise, to couldn’t be easier. A dedicated pairing function in which you hold the button into the pairing zone makes so much sense. So many headphones combine the power in function of pairing with powering on that It can become difficult to get the device paired with multiple sources. Brilliant.

Smart buttons — this is my only gripe. The option button is a mute if you’re in a phone call, but the rest of the time it’s a “intelligent command” button. In my experience things like “play music” yielded “call Tito Hyuan” Instead. I’m going to contact Jabra and try to understand better.

Charging... this is a shine. 10 minutes gets you 15 hours. Enough to go make a pot of coffee and work for the day. Perfect.

Outside of that, the Jabra app shines. My favorite feature is the soundscapes to tune out ambient noise. They sound way better than you would expect and truly are an amazing help.

I’m excited and thrilled that this is what headphones are becoming. Bravo Jabra.

I've had my Sony S350 Blu-Ray player for over a year now and here are my thoughts. The picture is completely amazing, even makes regular dvd's look better. I love that there's no more cords for picture and more cords for sound, just one HDMI cable and poof - high quality picture and surround sound.

A couple things to consider before buying your Blu-Ray player and subsequent Blu-Ray discs:
1. Blu-Ray will play your regular dvd's but if you have a regular dvd player (such as in your car) you cannot play Blu-Ray discs in it.

2. Patience is needed with this unit. After putting in a movie, especially if it is somewhat new, it could take 3-5 minutes to load. I am personally never in that much of a hurry to start the movie. While the movie is loading (a progress/status bar is provided on-screen) I can make popcorn, get the dogs situated, etc.

3. In conjunction with #2, the owner of this player must also be diligent about updating the firmware inside the player. I updated my player once last year (in November) and have noticed slower loads with current movies, so I plan to update it again next month (March). My guess is that it's good to update it 1-2 times per year.
What's involved in updating the firmware? I log onto a blu-ray firmware site, choose my model of player, then burn the update to a dvd disc. Place the disc in the player, it will read and update your firmware (took mine about 5-10 minutes as I remember). Afterward, your player will load movies more quickly.
Note: Loading never occurs during the movie, the only load-time that is experienced comes immediately after inserting the disc. Here's an example of the patience it takes to operate this blu-ray player:
Turn the player on - wait about 30 seconds for the unit to be able to receive or eject a disc (if you're trying to quickly eject a disc and run it back to the movie store, this can seem long!)
Insert disc and close - wait 3-5 minutes for movie menu to load

After that, you're set to go. For me, it's worth the wait and the trouble to keep it updated. I am quite sure that future models will require less patience and diligence, but for now this is the way it is. If you want extremely good quality with your movies, it's a wonderful addition to your home theater.
