This is a terrific little device. In fact, this may cause me more problems as in the past I was always reluctant to talk on the phone while driving. Not anymore.

I have always loved the Keyboard version (and still do), but unfortunately without the benefit of backlighting and the poor selection of cases with adequate lighting (I've ordered and returned several), I started to use it less and less - and used my Iphone App almost exclusively. But I really wanted to use a Kindle which was designed primarily for reading books as opposed to the small screen of a Smart phone. And I'm not about to go lugging around an Ipad day after day.

Last year I purchased a Kindle Touch but was extremely unhappy with the instability of the touch screen and other issues with that model. So I bought the aforementioned Keyboard and made do with it. I should add that I have owned five Kindles since their launch in 2007. When the Paperwhite was announced, I immediately got one for my husband while I waited for a 3g model for myself.

I have to admit that I had contacted Amazon about sending it back within a couple of days of receiving it, but for some reason (maybe maturity?), I decided to keep it for another few days just to play with it a bit more.

If my husband hadn't had his own Paperwhite for a month and shown me all of the basics, I can assure you that this model would be back in the hands of Amazon employees right now. They don't need to include some overwhelming instruction manual. Just one piece of paper with some simple "how to" notes would be perfect - I'd even be willing to draft something up for them!

Now that I've settled down with my Paperwhite, and have begun to take advantage of the outstanding benefits that it offers (i.e. instant dictionary, reading in the dark, lightweight and gorgeous, etc.) I would not part with it for anything. And my Keyboard is about to become a special gift to a friend who has always wanted a Kindle.

So I have never written a review before & my fiance was laughing after the first day of the camera's use when I loudly stated "I am going to write my 1st product review". Being someone who relies on reviews before any large item purchase, I think it was my duty to write a great review on a FANTASTIC product!

Knowing that I would be going on a trip to Mexico, I knew water activities would be included so naturally I thought it was important to purchase a camera for those times. I had 5 days until trip take-off, so it was hard taking the time to find the "right one". With about 2 hours of searching I stumbled upon a few that I thought would suit me well. I paid for the 2 day shipping and got it right on time, ran out to the store to get the SD card while the battery charged. The first few pics were amazing so I knew this camera wouldn't fail me. Scared for the let down (per several other reviews), I did not test it in water first, in fact my fiance threw it in the swimming pool about an hour after arriving to our resort!!!! Screaming I went in after the camera... everything was just fine with it! The seals are solid, in fact at times hard to open the compartments, but would take that considering it's protectint it from water. I did also by the yellow CHUMS wrist float, which also held up incredibly well, in the ocean & pool the camera did not sink to the bottom thanks to that floatation device. The thing I wish I would have known is that for water proof cameras there is a solution to help keep the water from fogging up the lens & screen. It allows the water to bead up and roll off the screens. A friend told us in that pinch that spitting, YES, SPITTING on the lens and screen, rub the salive around then re-submerge in whatever water you are in would help. Sure enough, it did! Of course you have to do it a few times during your trip if you are in water a lot but it worked!!!

The camera was submerged the majority of the 8 days there, in swimming pools, hot tubs and the ocean, amazingly there were no issues, it held up great throughout the whole thing. One downfall was the battery (granted a day and a half of constant video taking and photographing is not bad) but I was devastated that it died while we were out whale watching, and it was about 15 minutes after we found the whales!

We laughed all the time about people screaming that their cameras or cells phone were getting wet in the various activities, since that was the last thing we had to worry about. I had two cameras with me and after the second day I quit switching back and forth between dry and wet activities cause the CANON far superceeded my expectations, even when taking noraml dry land photos. I forgot this this was a 12megapix camera so of course the photos were clear, bright and outstanding!

It is no SLR but who would want to spend that kind of money for a camera that can't get wet on the spot, we still have our nice camera for professional looking photos, but it's not something we want to risk breaking, losing or damaging while on vacation, not to mention it's sheer size! This canon is portable, compact and goes anywhere and everywhere with you esp on those fun family trips! In hind sight I would have paid $500-600 on this thing for the quality and durability. We did drop it about 10 feet, on accident, but it never skipped a beat. This little thing is a gem!

At first I was in agreement with others who said that it does lag between picture taking, but for those times when you want it to go faster you can change it to take more, even continuously by just pressing and holding the shutter button! Highly satisfactory!

If you are still concerned, I wouldn't be. Even if something happens to the camera (drops and doesn't work or water damage) there is a factory warrenty and from prior experience with Canon they honor their warrenties, and fast.

Hope this helps others of you!! Great purchase.

Under 'speakers' I can also set the ipod display to always be on, always be off, or only come on when I press a key on the dock or on the remote.  Speaking of the remote, the range is strangely bad as you need to point it almost directly at the unit.  To make the NAS bluetooth capable then you'll need to buy the adaptor separately.  I don't know if it's only the Pioneer adaptor that will work but if that's the case, it's a pricey option at about $70. If this were an issue for me I would have rated the Pioneer three stars.  The sound quality here just doesn't earn it a five-star rating but I'll be keeping the unit.  If I had it to do it over again I would go with another Bose.
These are wonderful if you cannot afford big price security. Very loud.

Arrived on time. Safe and Sound.
Good product.

Great price and fun to play with. If you're interested in smart home technology this is a great place to start since it's easy to use and connect to other devices down the road. I bought several as Christmas gifts and when people figured out how to use it they loved it. The built in speaker is ok, I knew it wasn't as good as the more expensive Echo so I wasn't disappointed. If you already have a Bluetooth speaker or sound quality isn't a huge factor for you out of the box then you can't beat the price. I don't have any issues hearing Alexa's responses with the built in speaker, but when I want to listen to music I just connect my Bluetooth speaker (very easy to do) and can move it around the house with no problems. We have a dot on each floor of our house (2 stories) that are located in the most used areas. I keep a Bluetooth speaker in our bedroom and use the Alexa remote to interact with the Dot in our tv room since she can't hear me as well. This allows you to still connect to, and hear Alexa, without having to yell and strain to hear her.

The shopping list and to do list feature I really like since I'm horrible at writing down what we need around the house before I go shopping. I just tell her what to add to my list as I notice it, and it instantly shows up in the Alexa app which I can open when I get to the store and add/delete items. I also love these features to capture random things I want to research later like book titles, tv shows, serial numbers for parts etc that I might forget if I don't have it written down somewhere.

The only reason I didn't give the dot 5 stars is because most of the skills that are available right now leave a lot to be desired. I'm sure down the road this will improve but there isn't a lot to choose from right now that has a lot of practical use. Like a lot of people I would prefer Alexa be able to answer questions based on a Google search rather than having to enable skills for different things. If I want to know what flu symptons are she doesn't understand what I'm asking. But when you factor in everything she can do, and what she can connect with, then the dot is definitely still worth purchasing based on the price.

This is a great tv for the price. I love that I can get Netflix on it and how inexpensive it was. I needed a tv for my bedroom but didn’t want a huge one in there. It’s mostly for sound while I fall asleep- on a 2 hour timer. Love it. Good picture, good quality, excellent price.

I love the new Echo Dot.  The sound is impressive, as is the round shape.

The question is are you buying a radio or an MP3 player?  Sound quality is great, radio is very sensitive, and it is very easy to load up a micro card with your music and plug it in.  It has a nice bright screen. Why not program it to identify what you are playing on the card, and allow you to scroll down and select tracks? I noticed this was a problem on other players, but did not think it would be a big deal here. But after using it a few time, it is annoying. I certainly will keep it because the radio is so good and the little speakers are excellent.

I have had this for almost 2 years now and backed up my main computer several times.  It is really quite easy - plug it in to a USB port (for my PC, the back USB ports work for this, however the front ones do not), and windows explorer recognizes the drive.  Then just copy and paste or drag and drop files and folders to the drive.  Not the fastest process, but safe and secure.  Just got a new laptop with a big hard drive (I am not a cloud guy), and copied and pasted in about 100 gigs of photos, art, music and docs to the new drive.  Maybe it is easier to upload to the cloud and back up that way, but I prefer this way, and for under $20, it is really good.

Bought this for my wife, who likes to listen to the news when she is in the kitchen.  This is replacing a GE under the counter radio, which died after a long and happy life.  Similar replacements are very expensive.  Using it with the batteries, it is a little heavy, but plenty of power and easy to move around.  I listen to music, and found the sound to be clean and clear, really very good for this type of radio.  Dials are easy to read, tuning is accurate, FM sensitivity is good with the antenna up.  Good value for the price, don't see how you can do much better with as name brand.

My nice and expensive CD player crapped out, and who pays big bucks for a CD player anymore?  OK, you do, but the need for a stand alone CD player is not really a big ticket item anymore,. and I was looking for an inexpensive way to play my large collection of CDs on an occasional basis.  This machine is small, but not too small, and packs a big sound.  No, they are not Bose quality speakers, but they are better than satisfactory, especially at this price, and the power line is built in, so easy to use.  Would have liked a battery alternative, but not really necessary (get a longer extension cord).  So far, easy to use, and I can plug in an MP3 player as a bonus.  So nice item for the price.

I know MP3 players are not cool and everyone uses their phone these days.  But I use my phone just to make calls.  I load my music on my tablet and laptop, but these are not always convenient to carry around.  This is why the MP3 player still exists.  This one is small, but not too small so you cant see the screen, holds a ton of music, is easy to use, synchs for bluetooth easily, and sounds good to me.  It can power a small external speaker if you need it.  FM radio works.  Don't need it for much else.  Have it about a month now and still working well.  I switched the headphones because i do not like the hard earbuds, and works very well with a good set.  Really good value for the price.

I have been looking for the perfect backpack for travel and work and this appears to be as close as I will get - I need to carry a netbook, tablet, and here is the kicker, 2 cameras and camera equipment. Very happy so far, will check back after an extended trip.

I have been a user of these headphones for over a year. Love the stereo sound, great fit, and easy to charge. Also, call sound/mic works really well and another reason why i still use these.
Daughter loves them. Nice sound quality.
Just what I needed to hook up my surround sound
The case needs charged every day or so. Wish that was better. But like the sound and ease of use.

I built a backup server and the drives were getting hot, so I thought I would add more fans. Installation was not easy, but that is because of the case I was using and the locations I needed the fans to be in. I ended up only being able to use 2 screws on each because of the front case wiring, however, they seem very stable. I think these would work even better on a top fan location and installation would be much easier there. They work fine once I turned on the computer. I don't hear much sound, so they seem fairly quiet.

You also need a PATA cable for them. They do come with a male/female option on the cable, which was great, since my PATA cable was female.

I liked these earbuds.  They were easy to use and pair with my phone.  They were comfortable to wear and stay in well.  Sound quality is good.  I haven't really been able to test the noise cancelling abilities because I haven't used them anywhere that needed noise cancelling yet.

I find these to be comfortable to use. They connected easily. The sound quality is good. I found they last pretty well. I don't tend to get to use them for more than an hour or two at a time without interruptions. But rarely have to charge the case. The earbuds automatically charge every time you place them back in the case, which I do whenever I take them off. It is easier to find a case than a couple small earbuds. I like the mirror and the way the LED tells me the percentage charged the earbuds are.

They are supposed to have noise cancelling abilities. I never really have been able to check that so far because generally, where I work, it is not that noisy and I have to be able to hear the phone ring. I do have to say, wireless earbuds are so much easier than carrying wired headphones or even earbuds around.

This is great if you need to carry a number of cords and cables, such as for phones or hard drives. It is also good for USB drives and plugs. You are limited to what fits in it as it isn't huge, but it is a good size otherwise.

I basically got it for my mobile music production rig. So, USB cables yes, audio cables probably not. The small 1/8" headphone cables fit but the bigger 1/4" patch cables won't fit. It will also hold some of my dongles, which is great. The hard sides seem pretty sturdy. I haven't put anything really heavy on it and I don't really plan to see how much weight it can take before cracking.

This wasn't too hard to put together. I also like that there is a case for the frame, though not for the background and "sandbags" (fabric pouches that you can fill with sand or dirt to weigh the frame down if used outside) It is pretty wide. I thought I requested the green background, because it looks like it would be the perfect color for putting in images, but I ended up with the blue. The color is pretty bright and I have another background I can use that is more toned down.

It also comes with clips to hold the fabric on. I like that you can adjust the height fairly tall. Overall, I would recommend the frame. Not sure about the blue color. The fabric is pretty light and folds up fairly well. It just doesn't fit in the carry bag.

Okay, I was going to try to find my 45's and 78's before writing this review, but really, they are somewhere in my storage area. So I used it on my 33-1/3's. At first, I thought it had horrible sound, but it turns out, you do have to remove the guard from over the needle. The sound was actually really good for a small unit without a good speaker system.

I don't have a bluetooth speaker to try it with, so I didn't really test out all the options. And I have better setups to listen to my digital music. I just wanted a record player that works. And it does. When I have a bit more time, I will try testing the USB to see if I can record to my computer. More for curiosity's sake, as I have mostly replaced my records with CD's, though not all.

I use a lot of these enclosures. They don't make external drives with 7200 RPM HDDs, so I use an internal drive and an enclosure. This is maybe the 4th Orico one I've bought. They work well and are easy to use. The hard drive slides right in and the cover slides on and off easily. Though not easily that if falls off. The USB 3 makes them fairly fast and with the 7200 RPM, they work well for streaming audio when you can't afford an SSD in a similar size

My only complaint is that they don't put the amp in for the plug coming in or label the plug. It is 2 Amps. I tend to misplace the plugs in the box of plugs, so there is a concern about blowing out the enclosure, since I have a mix of 1.5 to 3 amp plugs. I've recently started labeling them with the information.
I use external CD's with my music hobby, as the virtual instrument libraries take a lot of room.  This works great so far.  It was easy to install the drive.

I really like that there is no cords (other than the charging cable) and they fit in your ears. They are a lot cheaper than air pods, and they sit in my ears comfortably. The sound is good, though so far, I mostly use them to listen to audio books. They don't shut out outside sound, but I don't notice them as much.

Easy to charge by placing them into the case and plugging the case and using a USB C charging cable. It comes with a very short one - good if you plug into your computer, but maybe not so much if you need to plug into the wall. I have a multi USB charging port that I use for all my various electronics - this doesn't come with the plugs.

I do music production as a hobby and have very large virtual instrument files. Loading almost 500 GB of libraries on to this drive was fast. It would usually take a couple hours or more on an HDD or an hour + on an SSD. This was something like 20 minutes for all the files.

I am computer literate and have built a PC. I am saying this because though I found it easy to install this drive, others may not. The tricky part is to get the end into the connector slot. This varies from machine to machine. Sometimes it is hard to see where it fits in. And then you have to gently screw it down. Mine was attached to a PCIe card, then into the computer, which made it a little easier. There are a lot of YouTube videos out there to help with how to install. It is much easier than installing a CPU, but not as easy as installing RAM.

I hate track pads. As laptops start having less and less ports to plug in, having to waste one on a mouse is very frustrating. I'm really loving that this is Bluetooth and doesn't require a plug unless you need to charge it. And? you can charge it using your phone charger with a micro USB connector (I have a multiple port hub to charge my personal phone, work phone, iPad and whatever, so it can be charged there) It actually lasts pretty long on a charge due to its annoying habit of turning off when you aren't using it. But longer battery life vs flipping the on-off switch is a reasonable trade for me at least.

I have medium sized hands and the mouse fits well. It seems pretty ergonomic for me. No complaints.

Oh, and just a note - the "purple" is a pretty good match to my rose-gold iPad and accessories. It has a slight purplish hue, but is really more rosy than what I would call purple.

This is the first backpack that fits my 17" HP Envy laptop. It is not a thin laptop and there is still room. So it gets 5 stars for just that. I was hoping it would fit my music equipment. and it does fit most of it. I can get my extra drive and Scarlet 2i2 in it without a problem, as well as all the cords and cables needed. but my Launchkey mini (25 mini key keyboard) doesn't quite fit if I have everything else in it. I think if you have a thinner or smaller laptop, more things will fit.

There's a funky side pocket that pulls out a net pocket that i think is supposed to hold a water bottle? I think a 1 liter would fit without a problem. Anything bigger, I don't think I would put in it.

I always seem to misplace these things. Most of the newer headphones come with the smaller jacks because all the newer equipment - laptops, phones, etc... - use them.  But I do audio work as well and my audio interface needs the 1/4" adapter.  These work well.  No extra hiss or noise was noted.  They seem well made.  I can't say how long they will last as I tend to misplace them way before they quit working.  However, if I they happen to die before I lose them, I will update my review.

These are a nice set of headphones, look-wise. They don't look cheap, fold up well and are fairly comfortable once you get them fitted right. I was getting some ear pain at first, but extended the top a bit and they now fit comfortably.

The bluetooth connected easily and easily allows me to go into the next room and still listen to my iPad that is more centrally located to pick up the wifi. Great for when I'm cleaning and want to listen to podcasts or YouTube. It charged fairly quickly and has lasted about a week of non-continual use. When the charge ran out, I was still able to hear by plugging in the phones into the audio until I had time to recharge.

Now the noise cancelling. It works. Our A/C unit sits outside the family room and is very noisy when running. I put on the NC and it was gone. Only problem was a static sound that popped up periodically. It wasn't continuous but loud enough to be annoying when it did. It may not be an issue for someone else, but it caused me to ding it a star. I haven't yet tried these on an airplane, which is where I normally use noise cancelling. But base on how it worked with the A/C, I expect these will do a great job. Just don't expect it to wipe out outside noise. I could still hear the TV going and my husband talking. Just no A/C loud rumbling noise. Now if only I could sleep in these to kill the sound of my husband's fan.

I did get these free in exchange for my honest opinion. What is funny is a just bought a new pair of noise cancelling headphones because my old ones just died and I like these better so far....

So far so good. However they make a lot of clacking noises which worries me a bit.  The tests say the drive is good, but my experience is drives that make that much noise are getting ready to fail.  I've been traveling for work so I think I missed the return date to just return.  Hopefully if they do go it will be under warranty.  I will update if they die soon.

So it is a tower case, not sure there is much more to say about that. Everything fit.

Pros:
The hard drive bays are easy to work with. If your motherboard supports it, there are places for about 8 drives (2.5 and 3.5). The drives snap in and can be screwed if needed.
Came with sufficient screws - I had leftovers.
Looks like it will fit most MB configurations.
Easy to pop out the front screens to put in a DVD drive
Seems to have a lot of ventilation

Cons:
Only one USB 3 and one USB 2 port in the front.
Once you remove the back openings for PCIe cards, they are gone. You can't reinstall if you decide to change the configuration. So then you need to get the covers.
The case fan can be a little noisy - part of this is solvable by moving the cords out of the way so they don't vibrate. The cords come out of the top of the fan instead of the bottom, so gravity causes them to lay against it which makes noise.

This may be a plus or minus, depending on what you like:
The Lights. The lights will light up a dark room. This is made worse/better by the clear side (that shows all your messy cords if you don't make them look all nice.) where the blue and red lights glow out of. Mine is currently still in the open room, as I am waiting for more RAM and loading programs. When it is all set up it will be under a desk and maybe not so noticeable when on. Though I guess if it is in your room it would be like a night light. :)

I wish I had found this before I changed out my hard drive. I had to take apart one of my drives in an enclosure just to move the files over after using an image actually worked.

So this is for when you want to use a internal drive externally but not on a regular basis, such as cloning the drive and then exchanging the drive into another or the same computer. I am a heavy user of my computer and hard drives only last so long. This is a very useful tool and very easy to use. I used it to move some additional files that got missed during the initial transfer and it worked well. It was immediately recognized by the computer. The transfer rates are consistent with USB 3.0. I have used Sabrent enclosures for years and found them to be consistent, so I expect this will too. It may require more gentle handling than an actual enclosure, but it isn't made for constant use - i.e. your drive will have no protection while using it, so it is not a long term solution. But I could see a computer repair person using it on a constant basis on multiple drives. I think if you are careful in the plugging in and unplugging, it should last for years.

I hope you find this review helpful!

First off, I will start by saying anything I can attach to my computer that runs on Bluetooth is always a bonus for me so my hopes were quite high when I ordered this and pleasantly, I was not disappointed at all. So we liked the first pair we tried so much that we ordered another pair so the price is what I am going to discuss first, only because I was not expecting much at this price but then when testing them out and using them that is the first thing I considered was, "how good are these for that reasonable of a price". This headset does not disappoint at all. I am pleasantly pleased with how well these perform. The noise cancelling is spot on, the sound is great and the battery life is fantastic. This projector screen is obviously a lot of real estate, as the 120" designation would imply. The screen itself is quite adequate, but the frame is a bit lacking. The construction of the frame makes it inherently weak and subject to possibly getting bent of coming apart. By the very design, it's nearly impossible to get the screen tight enough to eliminate the waves and wrinkles, which does impact the viewing pleasure. For indoor use, it's passable. For outdoor use, please be aware that, even with the water bag weights this will not stand up to much more than a very light breeze. This is simple physics and you are pretty much just making a sail. For outdoor use, we find that it works much better when placed up against a wall and protected from any wind as much as possible, but you really can't get it really "against" a wall due to the design of the leg bases. It's a trade-off, but a necessary evil.

The screen itself does a good job of displaying the image and is of good quality. No complaints from me on that point, but it will take a good amount of time to get the wrinkles to flatten out, so be prepared.

Overall, it's a decent screen with a massive area. It's fun to watch movies on the "Big Screen" and the price is certainly reasonable.

This is a decent entry level projector for every day use and a very good unit for specialized purposes like outdoor viewing on a large screen.

Its picture quality is better than most I have seen in this range and is brighter as well. The native 1080p image is sufficient for what you are buying, but one would never compare it to a higher end model. Of course, most of those start by adding another zero to the price, just for starters. I have had a couple of projectors in this price range and none of them really have a "great" picture, and that's honestly to be expected.

With this projector, you get a watchable image in daylight hours, but really improves if you black-out the room with darkening curtains or are watching after dark. The image will clearly show on a light color wall, but will improve drastically if you use an actual screen.

The fan noise is a little more intrusive than I would like, so it does interfere a bit if you are just using the included speakers. My suggestion is to connect it to a stand-alone external speaker setup. This is especially recommended if you are setting up an outdoor viewing screen.

It does tout 4D±50° Keystone correction, but it's not really as good as all that, in my opinion. I could never get the picture shape quite right at these angles. Connectivity is adequate, with several input options, so that's really a plus. I had it hooked up to an external hard drive as well as my Amazon Fire Stick and it handled each of them nicely. The WiFi connection is adequate and I had no issues connecting to my network. 5G connection is definitely a plus here as long as you are relatively close to your router.

Overall, I would say that this projector is a good value for the money spent. Try it out to see if Projection Television is for you. It's a whole new world, that's for sure. I don't miss going to the cinema as much anymore. Watching movies on the "Big Screen" at home is so convenient... and the popcorn is much cheaper.

Boy, I wish I had that option as a kid!

The lenses are quite clear and obvously of good quality, as are the eyepieces. The adjustments on this scope are very solid and precise and the included tripod will serve you well. It's quite sturdy, which is absolutely critical for stargazing. Trust me, a weak tripod will drive you crazy and everything you are looking at will be shaking. Not so much with this unit.

The included protective case is a great addition so that you can keep your telescope and accessories in great shape when not in use. It's very well organized and is nicely crafted. Very much appreciated.

Once you learn how to set the scope up, the sky is literally the limit. I remember well the first time I looked through a telescope as a kid (oh, so many years ago) and the memorable experiance the first time I actually saw the rings and moons of Saturn... the colors of Jupiter. Suddenly, the Solar System seemed not only real... but "closer" that I could have imagined. They were not longer points of light in the sky. They were really planets. I was in the market for a case for a thin mini itx system I was building and this one was the cheapest I came across that didn't make me fear for my components. I read all the reviews I could find and even watched a few YouTube videos and ultimately decided that this was the case for me. The build went fairly smoothly (no late night trips to find parts I found out I needed at the last minute or incompatibility issues), but I did encounter a few problems which other reviewers had also mentioned and I chose to ignore.

First Problem: Cannot use hdd mount with stock Intel heat sink installed
The product description claims this case can accommodate a stock heatsink, which is absolutely true, but if you do use one, a hard drive, even a thin ssd like I used, can't be mounted using the bracket they provided. I thought I was stuck at this point, and even tried mounting the ssd to the top of the case, but then I noticed some screw holes on the back of the case just above the I/O shield that seemed to be spaced just right for the holes on the side of the ssd. A few minutes and a little creative drill work later, and I had a place to mount my ssd, no bracket required.

Second Problem: The front panel connectors are way too short
My major problem with this case is the front panel connectors. For a case this small, it seems like it would be easy to include cables long enough to reach from the corner where they connect to the case to the opposite corner, just to be sure there was enough wire no matter what the motherboard setup was. Minibox did not take this approach, leaving me to splice the wires for the power button with and led with doorbell wire and plug the front two usb connector into a single auxiliary usb header, which only allows one port to work. It's mainly for this reason that I knocked off a star.

In conclusion, this is a really nice, well-made case if you're willing to deal with the few problems that it has. View the attached pictures for a better idea of how I ended up mounting the ssd and a general view of what this case looks like with a system in it.

System Components:
ECS H81H3-TI2 Thin Mini ITX Motherboard (includes wifi/bluetooth mini PCIe card)
Intel Core i3-4160 CPU with stock cooler
Kingston 120 GB SSD
Universal 90 W PSU

I first heard about Cobo Vault on twitter from a few of the various people I follow on there. The thought of a new hardware wallet that was open source (something I really like about Trezor) but also air gapped (no Internet connectivity or USB, bluetooth, etc.) was also super appealing to my ultra paranoid side. I figure as Bitcoin and perhaps other cryptos go up in value, security will become even more paramount so the ultra-paranoia is justified.

Anyway, I started with the Essentials version of the product and I was first impressed with the way the product was packaged nicely; nothing loose in the box, everything protected well. Upon removing it from the packaging, the build quality of the device itself was impressive, setup was straightforward as well.

I really like the fact that the Cobo Vault hardware has a sync to the mobile app. Setting this up is part of the initial setup wizard. Doing this allows you to view the balance in BTC, ETH, etc. or fiat equivalent on the mobile app without actually having the hardware wallet. You can also receive via the mobile app through a QR code. It's likely better to use the QR code off the hardware wallet display itself if you're ultra paranoid but, again, it's an option to use the mobile app only. Keep in mind, you can't view the fiat balance on the hardware wallet since it's air gapped.

For sending, you initiate it through the mobile app but you will need the hardware wallet to complete the actual transaction. This is accomplished through a back and forth process of scanning of QR codes between the hardware wallet and your smartphone.

Because I liked the Essential one so much, I bought another Cobo Vault but this time the Pro version. The reason I bought the Pro version is because it has a fingerprint scanner and I found it to be easier to unlock and perform other operations using that method. Without that feature, you have to either type alphanumeric passwords on the tiny keyboard on the touch screen display or draw a pattern on a display (similar to smart phones). Both seem to be difficult for me as it is a little difficult to type the password correctly on the small touch screen display or draw the pattern correctly without going slowly; especially if you have bigger fingers.

To address this, perhaps having an random ordered numeric dial pad for a password might also be a good alternative.

Battery life: Another reason why the Pro version is superior to the Essentials version is that it includes a rechargeable battery as well as the AAA option. The AAA option seems to have inconsistent battery life and seems to drain really fast for me. I brought this up to the Cobo team and they were really responsive to me and explained why the AAA battery life was hard to calculate and inconsistent at times. Still, it'd be nice if there was some way to bring consistency to AAA battery percentage displayed. That being said, the rechargeable battery is the way to go for consistent use but the AAA battery option is great for long term assurance of the device should it outlive the rechargeable battery.
Suggestion would be to allow the device to be powered and/or charged while in use. Right now the rechargeable battery requires the battery to be detached from the device itself in order to be charged.

firmware updates: I'm really impressed with the frequency of the firmware updates as well as the new features being introduced. A+ on that. Performing the updates has been a mixed bag for me. I've found that for some updates, using the rechargeable battery (charging it to full) and then performing the update works best. Other times, most noticeably the update to 1.40 multicoin, I had to use the AAA battery pack with fresh batteries to update both my Pro and Essential; a fully charged rechargeable pack did not work. I'm confident they will work through this as the product continues to mature.

Which brings me to my last point, the thing that impresses me the most about this product is the response from the Cobo team. They are open to feedback and suggestions and both acknowledge it, respond with great detailed answers and work hastily to incorporate new features. I'm really impressed with the support.

I use a mix of different hardware wallets to store my crypto offline and Cobo Vault is probably my favorite to use right now. I'm super excited to see and be a part of this product line as it matures.

I upgraded from a previous Vantrue X3 dash camera which I really liked. The nightvision on the X3 was already really good but the improvement of the nightvision on this N2 pro is significant.

The build quality on the N2 pro feels really sturdy and is top notch.
The dual (internal facing) camera really needs to be positioned in the center of the dash window to get a good field of view internally. This could be a restriction for some car mounts as people may not want it right in the middle of their windshield. Recording can be set to record both external (street view) and internal (passenger view) at the same time, it can also be set for external view only and multiple resolutions at that for those that want privacy. GPS is an option but requires a separate product addon.

The SD card slot is hidden behind a plastic cover on the side of the camera. This wasn't super intuitive for me to figure out (I admittedly didn't read the manual...) but it is a nice improvement as it adds an extra layer of protection from incidents in which the SD card falls out accidentally.

I live in a hot and humid climate and the X3 mount would occasionally fall off my dash window every few months. Time will tell how this N2 mount will hold up. That being said, the suction cup mount, in general, is a huge improvement over other vendors' camera's sticky tape type mounts which never hold up for more than a week in my climate.

I really like this dash camera and would buy it again if I were in the market for a quality one.

(software developer, experienced technology device user).

First concern I noticed is there is lack of grip on this unit. The back is stainless and the front smooth faced, so its hard to hold. There is a Next button perfectly placed for your right thumb, but in the same place on the left is a... Next button! English readers are wired to believe left is back and right is forward. Instead, the Prev button is higher up on the left and requires a conscious effort. Next buttons on both thumbs: why?!

Kindle needs a master Enter button, beyond just pressing the control knob. Like most laptop touch-pad users would, I keep finding myself pressing the adjacent "Menu" button as an expected Enter button and going back to where I came from. Frustrating.

The main buttons clunk a bit too much; patrons at the library will know every time you turn a page, which is often. Kindle needs to sit in a Honda for a few minutes and learn how a button should respond to your pressing it. The screen already undertakes an annoying and unnecessary slide-machine-style blackout between screens, so no need to have audible clues to your navigation.

In Text2Speech mode, I turned the Kindle off... the display shut down but the speech went on. That's a QC bug. Had to turn back on, quit the story, then turn off... a major bummer because the Kindle is designed to pick up where you left off, but in this case, now you will have to both reselect the story and re-turn-on speech mode every time. Ouch!

Finally, I mistakenly selected Dutch for Wikipedia, and cannot get back to English Wikipedia. Its cookied in. I know well enough to go to the en. prefix version eventually, but most users won't...

Small gripes include a front white face destined to get very dirty, a lack of face coverplate and low rent AmazonKindle logo quite unworthy of a $360 device.

I'm an early adopter of lots of "smart everything" internet connected products (Nest stuff, Smart Grill, SmartVents, internet connected cars, etc.). I have found the Ring doorbell to be one of the most useful and reliable of these types of products. Remote functions that are really valuable to me:
* Remotely "greet" and reschedule the delivery guy who was 2 hours late, while you are out doing other other errands. Warning - it does really freak out most delivery guys to hear your voice emanating from the doorbell button !
* Receive confirmation that your tween/teen has made it home from school, even when they don't see fit to call or text. Plus do a body count to see if any "extras" are visiting. Plus also have a concrete, time-stamped log of any late night returns, so you don't have to stay up late to intercept returning teens.
* Capture video evidence of stolen packages, unwanted solicitations, and prowlers.
The cloud recording cost of 30$/yr is a far better value than other services like Next or Flir. Ring is the clear choice for door monitoring as well as a really cool doorbell.

My only caveats for buyers:
* Take care with the physical installation on very rough surfaces like rough stucco. Holes need to exactly align (no slotted mounting holes) plus the mount plate is sensitive to bending. If the most bends too much to conform to the wall, the actual button/bell unit will not attach.
* Make sure your WiFi signal is strong enough in the location where you are planning install the ring. Plaster and stucco (with embedded screening) attenuate WiFi signals. WiFi basestation with beam-forming really do help (one of my neighbors needed to swap an Apple Airport Express for an Airport Extreme Basestation to achieve reliable and no-laggy video, but now the Ring works like a charm)
* Make sure your transformer is putting out an in-spec voltage, for a wired installation. Mine worked fine, but the another neighbor who recommended the Ring to me wen through two units (replaced by Ring), before they determined the doorbell voltage from the transformer was too high. Things worked flawlessly with the third unit when my neighbor moved to unwired operation.

I got my echo in January '15. Used the remote infrequently; probably 20 times, at most. Yesterday it died. Totally dead. Overall, this is a nice little backpack for someone in need of carrying a laptop, ipad, and other cables and charges needed to get some work done. Essentially, it would replace a briefcase for the businessman or provide a tech-friendly student adequate means of safely transporting expensive electronics.

SIZE

For the most part, this is a smaller sized backpack after it has the intended items in it, an ipad and/or backpack. However, I tested up to a 17 inch laptop and it fit perfectly with an ipad and other cables. It has the same sizing as your average school backpack or day pack, but is much thinner. But then again, this is a specific type of backpack designed for carrying a laptop.

COMFORT

The backpack is pretty comfortable. The back panel has a mesh-type material that promotes coolness and airflow to prevent sweating on hotter days. The shoulder straps are also lined with this material. In addition, there is also a sternum strap that will help carry a heavier load and take stress of the back and shoulders by transferring weight comfortably to the chest area. This is a really nice feature if it is needed.

ORGANIZATION

This pack truly shines in this aspect. There are many small pockets for different items and some, including the ipad pouch, are marked on the outside to let you know what is in each pocket. The laptop compartment, and much of this pack, are also heavily padded. This bag will protect all your electronics without a doubt. The computer slot has a Velcro strap to minimize movement in transport and has about an inch of dense foam padding at the bottom. Also, the ipad pouch does not go all the way to the bottom of the bag, keeping it from hitting the ground and easily accessible. On the exterior,

CONSTRUCTION

This is where I would deduct a star. At first glance, it is really uncertain as to how long this back will last. It seems like most of the exterior materials are pretty stout. However, there is only singe stitching throughout the interior. In addition, the nylon type material in the interior is really thin and seems like it would rip easily. Only time will tell.

Overall, I would recommend this bag for someone looking to protect their laptop while also not carrying too many other items. If you need a lot of books or papers carried around, try to go with a larger bag. But if a simple protection bag, this will definitely do the trick.

This past Christmas (2011), my husband and I decided that a new camera would be our gift to each other to replace our old Kodak EasyShare system. Since I am the main photographer in the family, I thoroughly researched available options. When I say "photographer," I am using the term lightly--while I love taking photographs, always document major events, do some minor photo editing, and do spend some time making albums/scrapbooks as well, I am by no means an expert or even an "amateur" photographer. Therefore, I was looking for a quality camera that would take excellent photos, but one that would do most of the work for me rather than require me to fool with a lot of settings myself. The one feature that was particularly important to me was a superior zoom lens, which is part of what attracted me to this model.

Overall, I have been very satisfied with the Nikon S8200. I am probably most pleased with the zoom lens, which captures shots of amazing quality, particularly in comparison to my previous camera. Another feature that I unexpectedly love is the "Selective Color" option, which allows you to take a photo highlighting a single color (for example, the red of a rose against black & white). You can also change photos to black and white or sepia right on the camera, and there are plenty of other great shooting options such as continuous burst and best shot selector. Finally, if you are someone who DOES like to fiddle with settings, you definitely can--EVERY single setting on this camera allows for individual adjustments to the user's specifications.

Several other reviewers have mentioned that the placement of the flash on the camera is a problem, especially since it pops up. Yes, the placement is a bit awkward, but because it pops up when you are focusing, you DO have time to move your hand out of the way before actually taking the photo, so I haven't found this to be a problem. What I DON'T like, however, is that the only way to reset the flash to the "down" position is to turn the camera off.

There are a few other things that I don't like about this camera as well. For me, these issues are quite minor, but I am mentioning them in case they might be important to others.

-->If I take a vertical (portrait) photo, the camera displays the photo in the same orientation, whereas my previous, older camera re-adjusted the orientation manually (e.g., so that all photos faced the same direction when the camera was held upright).
-->The camera has two different SCENE settings. For one, the user chooses the scenes manually (choices include "Food," Party/indoor," "Sports," "Snow," and 10 others), but for the other SCENE selection, the camera choose the appropriate scene. However, this is just confusing to me--which is better? Do I choose? Do I let the camera choose?
-->At first, I was finding that the camera was having a second or two of lag time in transferring photos to the memory card (especially in low light), but that was when I was using my old 1 GB memory card. So, I purchased a new [[ASIN:B003JTHN2W Lexar Professional 16GB SDHC 133x Class 10 Flash Memory Card]], and since then, I have not experienced any further speed issues.

Again, none of these things have been major concerns for me; at most, they might bring down my rating of the camera to about 4 1/2 stars. Still, I would highly recommend this Nikon, especially for casual photographers like myself. If you do purchase this camera, I would also recommend the [[ASIN:B004N91BK2 Must Have Accessories Bundle Kit For Nikon Coolpix]]. This is worth it just for the extra battery and charger (neither of which come with the camera), but you also get several other nice bonus items, include a very good case and a USB converter.

I have been very pleased with this flash drive, which I purchased for less than half of the price listed here in a Target store.  It requires no setup, making it very easy to use, and so far has provided flawless performance.  It is small and very lightweight, and I like that the stick retracts, meaning that there is no cap to lose.  The only thing that might be a slight downside to some is that the drive does not come with any kind of hook or carrying strap, although there is a very small opening on the one end where you could add your own (thin) lariat if desired.  Overall, I would definitely recommend this product.

I'm a little perplexed why other reviewers had such a problem with this product. The software was relatively straight forward. Once you skip past the wizard and go straight to the advanced settings, you'll find that it's a lot easier to customize the remote to your liking. My setup includes a Panasonic TV, Harman/Kardon Receiver, JVC DVD player, General Instruments Cable Box, and Panasonic VCR. It had no problems learning any of my remotes, and controls everything flawlessly. All together, it took about 1.5 hours to program the remote exactly the way I wanted it.

The one thing I didn't realize when ordering this remote is how HUGE it is. They aren't joking when they call it a 'remote commander.' However, it's a lot smaller than having 6 remotes on the coffee table!

All in all, a great remote control! With a little patience and learning, anyone could probably get it working perfectly.
Seems well made. Easy to set the alarm.  I like the tone and volume of the alarm.
We like the sound this puts out.  Good quality for such a small item.

They work pretty we.. Have been using them when I am shoveling snow and they are very nice. Sound quality is on par with my corded skullcandy. Have plenty of bass. Battery life seems to be good as well. Also have worn them for several hours and they do not become uncomfortable after longer periods like some of the other headphones I have owned. The over the ear piece is a floppy piece of silicone, but it seems to be enough resistance to keep them in place. I will be buying them again if I need replacements.

Works very nice. Added it to my CAPSMAN setup in my home. I like having the added 5ghz capability. I am a network professional and I have been using these for some time. This is not a typical home router and requires knowledge of networks and how they work. I would not suggest this as a home solution for your average user, but if you know what JUNOS and IOS are and are comfortable with them, then give this a shot. I switched from Cisco to Mikrotik and my wallet is much happier.

Had this running a few weeks. Software could use some more work, however I have had no issues with the board itself. Settings work great. Did the BIOS update right away. Fan controls are great. Keeps the system cool and quiet even under load.

I have had this for a month. It is the third different desk unit I have bought to replace my old Bose wave II. And it seems like the best solution. The sound quality is excellent--possibly better than the Bose wave. The price very good. It looks good. If there is one small complaint it is this: it takes a while to turn on, read disc, eject disc and load disc. If I am starting from off, it takes a good minute to where I am playing a CD. We'll see on reliability and duration. But at this price, if I get a few years, I will be very content. I am very happy with the TV. It was easy to set up and picture and sound are great!
Only down may be having only two HDMI slots.
The case is a very well put together item. However, when the cover is closed, the speakers are both blocked and dampen the sound.

The XClear Wireless Earbuds arrived in a nice Apple-like packaging. Included are the black rectangular charging case, left and right black earbuds, a short USB-C cable, and 3 various sized earcaps. For the price I did not expect much in terms of quality; however the plastic material has a nice matte feel to it. The angular exterior of the earbud pieces makes it stand apart from the Airpod.

Charging didn't take too long. My first impression wearing these was that they were very comfortable. I generally do not like earbuds but these are small enough that they don't cause pain after wearing them for a long time. Initially I thought the sound was a little tinny, however with a little adjustment I was able to get a better rich sound once the buds were properly seated in the canal. There's a definite lack of bass if you are into that.

Overall for the price I was very pleasantly surprised by the material and construction of the Xclear earbuds. Only time will tell if these will hold up but after testing for a few hours I can heartily give these two thumbs up!

These are amazing, but I do have a tip to save you some $$$.  I recommend buying the refurbished model for only $4999.99.  It is ALMOST as good as brand new, I compared the used version with my two friends who bought the new one and unless you are a genuine audiophile there is very little difference between the two.  The only bummer is that you have to pay for shipping, which almost killed the deal for me but I'm so glad I took the plunge and raided my sister's piggy bank.

I purchased these because I purchased the Sennheiser Momentum True Wireless 3's to replace my 2's & they did something to the silicon tips that make them thinner & they lose shape while taking them out of your ear, their much more "flimsy"!! Plus I like the foam tips using them on my Moondrop Variations so I decided to try these out

First, they fit great on the Sennhesiers, easy to put on & provided better overall noise cancelation. The PRIMARY issue I have with these are that once you fit them on then the buds NO LONGER fit properly within the recharging CASE!!!

Keep this in mind before you buy. I literally have to "shove" them into the case & several times 1 bud or the other did NOT get a charge because the foam tips prevent the buds from connecting securely to the metal charging nibs within the case.

I had the MTW 2.0's for almost 3yrs. The right bud just stopped working, wouldn't connect & wouldn't even power up. But this is after 3yrs of daily use, working out, getting them used thoroughly!! So I opted to stick with them since I like Senn's sound signature & have or have had several Sennheiser products in the past. These are slightly louder but definitely noticeable but keep the rich & detailed sound stage. The bass is perfect not overwhelming but definitely textured like on the 2.0's. I'm glad I ended up trading up but really had no choice since the 2.0's were done!

I jumped on the mechanical keyboard trend without doing much research I just knew that the shallow butterfly thin keyboards weren't working for me (while typing now on a MacBook Pro! LOL! ) But for some reason laptops are okay with these shallow keys but for a desktop I wanted a regular old fashioned mechanical.

The issue is the first 2 I bought were LOUD! While on a Teams meeting people were pinging me to mute my mic because the "clitter clatter" was too loud. So I did a little research this time & found the "Silent Red Switches" were what I needed but I wasn't finding any that had a good "style" to them until I found this Mistel. I love it, very satisfied.
I love the "plug & play" aspect. I didn't have to download some weird driver that most of these docking stations require. Took no more than 5 minutes to get up & running

I'm not a gamer but I wanted a mechanical keyboard because the thinner low travel keystroke keyboards out now (Like my MacBook Pro) just causes me to make typing errors.

This version is just way too loud for "office work" typing

I've had my fair share of IE monitors & over the ear headphones & as far as sound quality, imaging, sound stage, separation these are amazing. Bass was very present but not overwhelming. The highs were not sharp or sibilant at all. But when it came to the fit I couldn't get past 1/2 hour & I tried ALL of the tips, which FIIo does a great job of giving you plenty to chose from. But unfortunately for me these just killed my listening enjoyment.

These headphones really debunks the theory that more expensive is "more better". AKG did a fabulous job with these headphones. Now, I am not a headphone techy, I don't know the fancy terminology to describe what these can's sound like BUT I do like music & listen to all types from Alternative, to R&B & Rock thru Hip Hop & Jazz!

Recently I've kind of become a headphone junkie. Within the last year I've purchased & then "re-sold" many headphones including, Sennheiser Momentums, Sennheiser HD650, Beyerdynamic DT880 32ohm & Ultrasone Pro900. What I ended up really wanting was a good pair of headphones that had the iPhone remote cord that did NOT need an external amp.

So with that in mind obviously the HD650, DT880's & the Pro900 went back. However in all honesty if I purchases like a FiiO Mont Blanc I would probably go back to the Sennheiser HD650. I loved the Momentums but my ears stick out a bit & the "Mo's" are just too uncomfortable for me for long term listening however they were the easiest to push without an amp & were the loudest out the box just using my iPhone or iPad.

Now, I was set to purchase the NAD Viso HP50's but after some youtube videos switched my purchase to the K545's because I heard the HP50's did not have the bass presence the K545's had. And I'm so glad I did, because this set of headphones brought a lot of the good qualities of the HP50's & Momentums together in one package! It gave me the midrange detail I wanted from the NAD's & the bass presence I wanted from the Momentums. Now don't be mistaken when I say "bass presence" these are NOT Beats by Dre or bass forward headphones but the bass is there, its extremely tight & accurate but are NOT in anyway boomy.
If you're style of music is majority drum & bass Trap or Dubstep then these aren't for you!

But maybe you have a good collection of older hip hop tunes from the 80's thru early 2000's, same era for Rock, R&B, Alternative these would be great! I think they're also very good for a lot of dance/trance but once again if you're looking for bass forward then these aren't for you but if you want bass with a lot of midrange detail then you should try them out especially for the price.

I'm finding a lot of detail in music that I missed out on the Momentums & the K545's are once again convenient with the remote.

I bought this keyboard for my old iMac I use as a backup computer. This was one of very few inexpensive ones that actually has Apple keyboard layout and is wireless.
The nice thing about this keyboard is that there's really no setup required: plug in the USB knob, insert batteries - finished! It worth pointing out that Mac will treat it as a USB keyboard and mouse. Both worked well. Most basic Apple keyboard shortcuts worked. You don't need Bluetooth function on the Mac to be turned on. It thus seems that "Keyboard Setup Assistant" will not recognize the keyboard. However, you can still use System Settings to done few tuneups.
Strangely the keyboard requires 2 AAA batteries and mouse requires 1AA battery. I wish both would need same batteries. There's no power button on a keyboard but instruction manual (full of typographical and grammatical errors!) states that it turns off after 2 minutes of non-use.

Out of the box, these earphones look surprisingly appealing and well-constructed. There's nothing "cheap" about themThey are very easy to connect to Bluetooth.
I use these earphones for running. They are a bit tight when placed over ears, but at the same time they stay on very well. I found ear cushions quite soft and comfortable. I did find it difficult to locate "backwards/softer" button by feel while earphones are worn, but eventually got used to it.
Overall I think its a very nice "bang for the buck" product. Time will tell whether or not sweat will cause problems; so far it has not.

The player appears to be well constructed. It is also quite small and light. Transferring songs is pretty easy, but, as every other non iPod MP3 player, it doesn't support Apple Purchased AAC files, so those will need to be converted to MP3 format. I didn't use the enclosed headphones, so I can't comment on those, but, listening to songs while swimming, I found the sound to be very good. I clipped the player to my goggles and it felt nice and secure. I did try to use Blue Tooth pairing with iPhone while swimming, but, as was mentioned by some reviews, once the player is as inch or so underwater this function stops working. I will try to "tinker" with this a bit to see if I can get it to work, but so far no luck.
Now for cons. For one thing, there's no way to create playlists. The choice is straight play through all songs or shuffle. I had 5 playlists on my iPod, but now I'm forced to combine all of them or sync each one separately every time I use the player. That is the main reason I give this product 4 stars instead of 5. The other irritating thing is if you press "Stop" button while in Bluetooth mode the player automatically reverts to "memory play", so you have to re-connect to Bluetooth again. Volume and skip songs are adjusted by same buttons, so if you are not careful you will skip songs instead of adjusting the volume.
I hope that this player will be improved to allow playlists to be created; then it will become significantly better.

This is my second pair of Swimbuds. I've always struggled finding headphones that would not leak while swimming.  It must be some anatomical issue with my ear canal, because I've tried at least a dozen headphones - and all of them leaked or fell out at some point.  These swim buds are so light that they actually stay in my ear.  Short cord doesn't get tangled up.  And I guess the Christmas-tree tips are a bit different because so far these headphones are the only one that have not leaked, but I do have to insert them deep into ear canal.  I use just a touch of petroleum jelly on tips to help the insertion and to moisturise ears, because these headphones (like most other waterproof headphones) can cause irritation of the external ear canal.  There are a lot of tips to choose from.  I use them in my Endless Pool, so I don't know how they will perform in regular pool during turns and flips, but my guess is because of their lightness they will work fine.  I don't care much for clarity of music during swimming, but I found sound to be quite acceptable with these headphones.

I've tried about 10 different headphones for swimming; all of them either leaked or were falling out. I guess my ear canals refused to follow the evolution theory of Darwin and remained primitive. But finally I found something that even worked for me. I've been swimming with these amor about 2 years. These headphones have a very nice snuggle and comfortable fit, they don't leak or fall out after 45 mins swim in endless pool (I haven't tried them in a lap pool). The only peculiar thing is I found that if I wear them in proper orientation (that is left channel to left ear) I couldn't hear anything out of the left bud! However, when I reverse them and wear them "upside down" with right ear channel in the left ear, the sound is perfect and the buds still don't fall out. Short cord doesn't interfere with strokes or get tangled up.
These come with a myriad of different shapes and size buds, extension cord and very nicely packaged.
Overall I'm extremely satisfied with these - I think the money is well spent.

Bluetooth: Despite using an older version of Bluetooth (2.1), The unit paired easily with my earbuds, and stayed paired. No flukey disconnects like I've experienced with budget no name players.
Performance: Reliable. Set it the way you want, turn it on and use it, shut it off when you're done, no nonsense.
Some people have complained about low volume. My experience was that you are given options in the setup menu which allow you to overcome that. I have the player volume at near maximum, and use the volume control on my earbuds to do the rest. There are 8 songs loaded on the player when you get it, but you can easily delete them when you hook it up to your computer. There is a 40 page instruction manual available as a pdf on Sandisk's website. The good: solid documentation of all features. The downside: a ponderous amount of info to absorb, but like me, I think most people will set it and forget it.

The other day, I absentmindedly walked away from the Timkoo by about 20 feet, and realized I was still getting my music loud and clear.  I can walk around with the player in my pocket and listen, where I have to hold my other player in front of me or it cuts in and out.  Some reviewers have criticized the lack of features on this player, but for me, it's not a big deal, as I generally put the player on shuffle play, and just listen to whatever comes on.  I wish there was an EQ.  Overall, I think it's a pretty good package for the price, especially considering the highest rated MP3 players easily run north of $200.

UPDATE 6/1/2016: Sound is MUCH improved with the 2.1.0.5317 version of the Polk Omni app I downloaded today. The popping/crackling/hissing I was hearing esp on solo piano music is gone, and I'm updating my rating to 5 stars. This unit is really a tremendous value at $199, and a great value at the current price of $287.

ORIGINAL REVIEW:

Got this on sale for $199 at Crutchfield and I see it is now on sale at that price here on Amazon. Great value at that price, but there are some issues.

1. The control software is flaky. It was initially horrendous with my media server constantly becoming invisible requiring reboot of everything, but the Sept 2015 update seems to have fixed the worst problems. (I was going to return it before that update).

2. The Polk Android app wants access to seemingly EVERYTHING on your phone including your phone number, caller id, etc. Sonos doesn't ask for that stuff. Polk is overreaching here. Why?

3. The volume control buttons on unit are too coarse; can't fine tune at low volume levels. But note you can tune more finely with control app.

4. This is a minor thing, but the control app's user-interface design seems somewhat clunky and odd.

5. Polk doesn't seem to be selling many of these, so I worry about their commitment to the software and platform. I'm basing this on fact that the Google Play store has only hit the 5,000 download benchmark for the Polk Omni app for Android. Denon's Heos has hit 10,000 there, and Sonos has hit 1 million.

Those issues aside, on the plus side I think the unit sounds great and it is based on wifi rather than bluetooth, which is a plus for me.

I also considered the NAD D 3020 which has a nice analog volume knob, but it is bluetooth-based and about twice the price (when on sale for $399 as now).

I was a big Squeezebox Touch fan, which you can still get for around $300-350 on eBay. This Polk Omni gives you that same sort of streaming functionality, and will even work with your existing Squeezebox media server; it recognizes it as a media server automatically. The difference is it also gives you a nice amplifier and is only $200. You sacrifice the visible display, but everyone has a phone or tablet so what does it matter?

UPDATE 10/17/15: BIG PROBLEM: I've changed the rating from 4 to 2 stars based on further listening to the unit. I bought the unit to stream music from my computer, and I've determined that when the Omni streams music at moderate to high volume, it adds a popping/crackling/static sound to higher volume moments of the piece. Not very high volume: could be just a solo piano playing certain notes somewhat louder. I've determined the problem is with Polk's streaming, because when I play the same piece through the Omni's auxiliary input, even at much higher volume, there is zero popping/crackling. The popping/crackling is noticeable when the Omni streams both .FLAC and .MP3 formats, from both the Logitech Media Server and from MediaMonkey's UPnP/DLNA server. Again confirming the problem is Omni's streaming, I streamed the same music from Logitech Media Server through a Squeezebox into Omni's auxiliary input, and again, zero popping/crackling. Since the Omni amplifier hardware is capable of playing the same music with no popping, this seems to be a problem with Polk's wireless streaming. The crackling/static sound that hits when the music get a little louder makes you feel something is wrong with the speakers or connection, but it's not. It's distracting enough that I will either return the unit, or only listen to music through its auxiliary port.

This is a fine quality little radio that comes with "all fixings".  (It was smaller than I imagined, which made it all the cuter.)  It's loud enough to hear while showering, and reception is clear.  A great gift item--if you can part with it.
