Sound quality is fine--no hiss, no static, no stuttering. Build quality certainly appears quite good,  though of course only time will tell. Good company, good product

worked fine--plug in and no issues whatsoever.  No problems with fit, not static, no volume issues, no hiss.  All good. Cord is a good length--long enough so not too tightly tethered (or to reach to the back) but not so long as be annoying. Seems well made/constructed. Very happy--does just what it's supposed to

This is a decent little camera/mic. Set it up on my mother-in-law's Dell with Windows 10. Was true plug and play save for one exception (more on that later). Video was immediately available and was nice and clear and vivid. It's in a well-lit area and the picture quality was certainly bright--no noticeable loss of light. The camera is a very basic tilt/pivot/attach, but for as basic as it is it does its job satisfactorily--was able to adjust for different users' preference. The mic was instantly picked up by Windows and we were able to use text-to-speech with no issues of clarity or volume. Worked in other programs requiring a mic and/or video as well.

The one exception (so far) is Zoom, where the video works fine but not the mic. We're still trying to figure it out (I'm a Mac guy so Windows settings are mostly a random seek for me). I'm assuming we will, as it's as noted the only program that the mic isn't working in, so I'm sure it's a preferences/settings problem. I'll leave this here as an assumed solved issue. If we could not get it to work I"ll come back in and note that it remained unresolved. Otherwise, decent inexpensive camera.

Based on its price, it's pretty easy to tell these aren't meant to be top-notch earbuds. And they're not. They aren't as rich sounding or richly featured as my AirPods/Airpod Pros. And my Powerbeat 3s also sound more full (though not as good as the AirPods).

If you know that going in (and you should, since you're paying sub-100) and your expectations are set, then you should be fully satisfied. They do sound good, just not great. I'd say they're rough akin to my several-years old Jabra Elites, though these are more bass-heavy, so I actually slightly prefer the Jabra.

they're comfortable given that have a neck wire (obviously if that bugs you don't get these) and there lighter than my Powerbeats.

all the basic controls are here in-line and work smoothly. Pairing was, as always between Apple products, fast and effortless. Immediately paired with all our phones/iPads fine.

call quality was good, microphone worked great.

they click together magnetically, but the wiring isn't super flexible, so I don't feel comfortable storing them in a small space. They come with 4 eartips for sizing.

As always with Apple, packaging was nicely minimal

I got these either for myself to have a pair of cheap earbuds to take places I don't want to have to worry about losing or to send to my son at college so he doesn't have to worry about losing them. They're budget earbuds but still fine sound, just not as good as the high-end ones, as should be expected. That don't come with a charger (just a cable), which I'm fine with as by now I've chargers up the wazoo, but something to be aware of.

excellent product for its niche

So long as you don't think you're getting a high-quality projector screen, you should be quite satisfied with this. We look at it as two steps above projecting on the wall and one step above projecting on a huge sheet, which is usually what we do. The sheet has worked fine, especially outdoors, but this is definitely better and is more than serviceable for our needs.  There's no creases, it doesn't wrinkle like the sheet can (or require ironing like the sheet), its heavier so it holds its flatness, and while not really heavy, it does do better when a light breeze kicks up.  It has grommets and comes with adhesive.  We use carabiners attached to our gutters if we're showing it outside against our garage and powerful magnets to attach it to a ceiling beam if we're showing inside.  Both work perfectly fine and are easy to set up and take down.  For the price we are very pleased and like how it's an improvement that is noticeable but not too expensive

Unfortunately , I can't say much about sound quality etc. with this mic because each time I tried to use it (and I tried multiple times), I kept picking up radio chatter. Now, we do live within about a mile or two of some powerful transmitters, but this is the first time I've ever had any electronic pick up radio noise (I'm assuming it came from the towers, don't know for a fact).  I held off on reviewing this because I didn't know if this would always happen. But I've recently gotten another mic and have since used that multiple times and had no issue whatsoever with background noise. So clearly this one isn't shielded enough, at least for my situation. It's possible someone else wouldn't have a problem but if you live in an urban or urban/suburban edge zone (that's our house), you're probably best trying something a bit more expensive and more shielded

sometimes things are as simple as--does it work without screwing things up? And this is that sort of product.  It needs to connect your jack-less phone to your corded earbuds.  It fits perfectly with both, no degradation of sound quality, no lag time. Your music just plays and you don't notice.  And it's small enough that you really almost don't notice it.  Saves the old buds from being obsolete (especially if you plunked down some money for them), saves you when you forgot to charge the wireless ones. Excellent product

I'm not an audiophile, nor do I have fancy audio equipment to measure, compare, etc. I'm just a guy who likes music. So that that as you want. That said, not that I've finally managed to get these hookedup, I can say I"m super pleased.

The look is sleek and compact. The black will fit into any modernist style, not so much if you're more rustic/wood-based decor.

The sound is rich and clear, especially if one doesn't push volume super high. There isn't a deep low bass, but that's to be expected with bookshelf speakers so I don't consider that a flaw. You can perhaps deepen the bass a bit by moving them close to the walls/floor, but I found that muddies the sound for me. Not horribly so, but noticeably. If you're looking for chest-pulsing bass therefore, you'll want to add a sub-woofer. If you don't need that, the bass coverage is fine. Mid-range and high are good as well, without sounding tinny or hard or thin, including at high volume. Vocals are clear and what I"d call natural-sounding or smooth (I recognize those are vague). Vocals stayed true through several genres (rock, singer-songwriter, prog rock, etc). Instruments also were clear. You can pick out individual instruments on ensemble pieces for instance, classical piano comes out warm and clear and stands out within orchestral concertos. Full orchestras sound fine, maybe not as full.

For their price, these are an excellent set, better than certainly most bookshelf speakers I've owned, and I don't think worse than any I've owned. I'd call them significantly better than cheap speakers, and yeah, not as good as 3000 dollar speakers I've heard, but most of us don't have that kind of money for speakers. These are a sweet spot for sound and cost. Highly recommended

This is a one-trick accessory that does exactly what it says it does. Easy to use--simply connect and go.  It's a relatively small footprint. It's "brick" part is slightly bigger and heavier than my Anker adapter, but the StarTech cable is shorter. If you don't need the length, then it's nice that it takes up less room (and probably less likely to suffer damage from bending etc.).  The two perform equally well and the size is really not much different. I keep one in my biking commute bag and one in my driving commute bag so don't have to worry about remembering to move and adapter from one to the other depending on how I get to work.  Nice little useful accessory, especially if you don't need more connections (in which case a hub is probably better)

This is a pricey Bluetooth speaker, but a high quality one so you do get what you pay for here. It’s one of my two favorite ones (the other is the Jam Heavy Metal) and outside of the Jam is far better sound quality than the several others I own. If you’re looking for something that gives you “adequate” music and can handle a splash or two, this is overkill. But if you want rich sound and insurance against big rain (or worse, a dunk in a pool), it’s probably worth moving up to this one.

Pros:
IP67, highly water-resistant. I confess, I didn’t test this by submerging it as it says you can; I’m gonna just trust ‘em on this one

Rich, distortion-free sound. Despite its size, this can get quite loud (in a nice touch for those wishing to pump it up, the volume controls on the speaker, unlike most I own, work independently of your source device (i.e. you can max out your iphone volume and then in addition max out the speaker). Even at high volume the sound doesn’t distort. And the bass is powerful and thick (not sub-woofer but then, if you want that, get a sub-woofer. For a portable speaker, it’s perhaps the best bass I’ve heard). It’s also quite clear. In comparison to the Jam, I’d say the bass on this is better but the Jam just edges out in terms of clarity with treble/voice. The sound quality is also quite good as a speaker phone.

Connecting. Pairing via Bluetooth was pretty instantaneous with my iPhone and iPad. There’s also an audio-jack to plug in

Stereo potential. You can link it with another, though I don’t have a second so can’t speak to how it sounds

Size: it’s small enough to toss easily into a backpack if not a pocket. Has a heft to it in terms of a quality, durable build-feel, but not so as to strain you carrying it around at all.

Cons are all pretty minor
Buttons are a bit stiff (maybe this will change)

No charging cable with mine

Neutral: no connectivity with voice activation like Alexa
Charges in a few hours and last anywhere from 8-12 depending on volume, not the best but far from the worst

Personally, I hate tinny, thin-sounding speakers. If I’m going to listen to music, I don’t need it to be pristine, but I do want it to sound like my music, so I think this is a good value. The sound quality alone is worth it—it blows away cheaper Bluetooth portables— and combined with the high-level water resistance, it’s makes it an even easier recommendation

I had an old Tile without the replaceable battery, which always bothered me as much from the environmental issue as for the annoying have-to-replace-the-whole-thing issue. Glad to see they've fixed that problem with the newest Mate, giving it an easy to find replaceable battery. Otherwise, it's still the same old reliable tool

set-up: couldn't be easier or quicker. Took under 5 minutes to have it on my keychain, connected and found, and then able to test it. Set up was flawless, fast, intuitive with easy-to-follow instructions. Exactly as these things should be

size: It's a bit slimmer than my old one and so less obtrusive. I use it on my keys and it doesn't weigh them down or get in the way. If you want to use it on something else, the size is nice for pretty much anything save maybe your pet beetle.

Sound: You can hear it from a pretty good distance. Indoors, I could hear it with no problem from upstairs on a different side of the house with doors both open and shut. Two flights up from our attic I could still hear it if I kept the doors open, but just barely (straining to catch it) with the doors shut. That's an 1800-square foot house. You may want the louder Pro if your house is much bigger (or you could just wander your house until you get close enough to hear it)

GPS worked fine as well

These things are a little pricey, but they're nice to have and with the replaceable battery I consider them a good value. You can upgrade to premium services for a regular fee for things like 30-day history etc. but that's too much cost for too little value for me (plus the creep factor). But for the basic usage, I'm a fan. Make great gifts too I think.

I readily admit one’s preference for sound is incredibly subjective, so mileage of course may vary, but from my viewpoint The Jabra Elite is, I’d say, a pretty focused product and if that’s your focus, it’s quite good. That focus would be on voice quality rather than music quality.

In terms of music, I’d call them “fine.” They aren’t at all bad (I’ve listened with bad earbuds and these don’ qualify). But they’re a bit thin for my liking, a bit muddy at times., and I prefer, to a noticeable degree, both my PowerBeats3 and my JayBirds for listening to music.

Audiobooks or podcasts are a different story. I’d choose the Jabra over those because the voice seems just a little bit sharper and clearer, more precise. And that’s also where they shine with regard to phone calls, which are pretty crystal clear.

Outside of the sound, the other aspects are all positive. No problem pairing with an iphone. They say the wire is “memory” and I don’t know how big a difference that makes, but it is comfortable. Like most such products, they come with a spectrum of sizing for your ears, and it was easy to make these fit snugly and comfortably. They charge up in about two hours and the 8-hour battery life claim seems pretty safe to trust. I’ve gone 5+ of continuous use and they weren’t dead.

There’s a Jabra App that lets you set some preference and includes an Equalizer and a battery indicator.

The Siri input worked flawlessly. The configuration of the wire pretty much keeps the mic next to my mouth, and the buttons are easy to learn that pattern after not much use. By the third time I wasn’t fumbling around. Click to get Siri and speak and it’s all good to go. My only issue is that Siri is quite loud—much louder than my music—a small complaint. The voice activation—accepting a call, pausing a call, rejecting one—all also worked without a hitch and conversation, as noted above was super clear.

When I’m going to listen to an audiobook or podcast, I reach for these. When I’m listening to music I usually go with the PowerBeats. If I’m listening to music while running, the Jaybirds. I don’t do a lot with calls, but if I did, these would be my preference and I’d tolerate the so-so music quality.

this is a nicely constructed drive in both its build quality and its details. The soft silicone shell is protective without adding weight or bulk and the cable is set into a recess for easy and convenient transport. The size is a decent size (once upon a time it would have unimaginably huge) for today's world--will back up all your documents with ease, and for many people their pictures and vids as well, though some of us need larger. It's footprint on the desk is relatively small, and its compact size and light weight makes it portable. I have thinner, smaller drives the same 1 TB size, so there's no doubt this one is comparatively larger, but one sacrifices a bit of convenience for a better sense of durability thanks to build, the shock-protecting exterior, and a plastic case. It's not the case if portability is your priority, but if you don't mind the extra size for peace of mind, it's not that large or ungainly at all. It's also speedy, transferring docs/pics/vids quickly and works very quietly.

all in all a great combination of traits.

These headphones fall between ones I currently own and are, I'd say, a fair price to pay.

In terms of listening to music, they easily out perform standard come-with or cheap earbuds, no doubt about that. So if you're looking to upgrade from that sort and you don't mind the money, it's a no-brainer. They were a bit better than my next step up earphones--more full, more rich, with better base. They fell a little short of my Jaybirds. Again, these have a nice rich sound, but the Jaybirds were crisper, the Audio-Technica ones a bit more muddy.

The fit is excellent. These are very comfortable, the over-the-ear both stable and comfortable--you don't notice it once you're wearing them and they stayed in place nicely while running. They come with a medium size fit, but also come with two smaller sizes.

The microphone worked quite well, people had no trouble hearing or understanding me. I would have liked the control to be adjustable, or a little lower down, but I get why it isn't. Just a personal preference.

So in the end, these seem well priced. They're more expensive than some, but in comparison to those I own that are cheaper than these, the Audio-Technica out-performs them. They don't sound as good as my Jaybirds, but then, they also cost a good amount less, so I wouldn't expect anything different.

In the end, it's you get what you pay for and so it's all up to whether you like to pay for better sound, fit, and comfort. I'm obviously a yes, so I'd say these are worth picking up to replace you're cheaper set.

So far, the hard drive is working as one would expect. As always with these things, the questions mostly arise in longevity/reliability issues, so I'll be updating this once I've had a longer time to determine how it does in those categories. First impressions at this point, though:

1) the drive has a relatively small footprint, which is nice

2) Feels quite sturdy and hefty (it's surprisingly heavy) with good build quality

3) This isn't powered by your USB, so you'll need an outlet for its enclosed power cord

4) When you start up, it takes a little while (a few seconds) for the display light to come on. At first, I thought it hadn't started up at all, but just wait a small bit and it will light up

5) the display light is located on top but at the rear of the device, which while minor, is a slight inconvenience. I have it under my desk set back a little ways, so to see the light isn't as immediate as one might like

6) the drive is quite quiet. Not silent--you can hear it--but definitely quieter than many I've had

7) the drive is pretty fast, with the uptick from USB 2 to 3 very noticeable as I move from one computer (USB 2) to the other (USB 3)--it varies depending on what I'm copying, but sometimes the difference is half the speed

8) despite the small footprint, with its necessity for power and it's weight, I wouldn't consider this at all a portable drive, though I suppose you could use it as such. But really, it's big and heavy for that.

9) I use this on several Macs--no problem at all reformatting it for those computers--just a few mouse clicks and a few seconds is all

So far, this is a good big backup drive (I have the 5 TB version). And since we all know, or should, that drives will fail, you can't have too many of them. If any issues arise over time, I'll update accordingly

Pros: dual alarm
good reception
so far reliable
feels like it's of good build quality
large display is easy to read in the dark
very easy to set alarms: moves very fast, can go backwards and forwards, I like how it won't even let you set it if the alarm
hasn't been turned on--it flashes "off" at you--a good reminder

Cons: display is less easy to read in light
some might find the alarm sound a little low. Works fine for me (I'm not a particularly light sleeper),but it's softer than most I've
had in the past

Pro and Con: the off-button isn't so easy to hit (snooze is very easy) for the alarm. My wife is annoyed by this because she has to hunt a bit for it. I actually like it because if I need to get up when it goes off, having to hunt for the button a bit (not a huge amount) makes me actually get up--clear the fog from my brain. If I don't have to get up, the snooze is very easy to hit.

So far pleased

The drive is tiny when the shield is in place--just a little bit longer than a small paperclip and about as thick as a pencil.

The shield, besides protecting the drive, has a small hole through which you can run a lanyard or use some other means to attach it to something so as not to lose it (easy to do with its small size)

The build is a little worrisome to me--it feels less solid than any of my other thumb drives and I wonder a bit how it will hold up over time and getting jostled around by other items in my pack

The fit is snug, so much so actia;;u that I thought at first I'd somehow had it upside down and pulled it back off to double-check the first time

As far as speed, it's not the fastest. It took 1 1/2 minutes to copy over an audiobook and 5 1/2 minutes to copy over a 1.5 GB folder of photos, which is roughly the same time as my Sandisk Cruzer--a little slower than some but not a huge difference. USB 3.0, if you can use it, might be worth it if you plan to regularly transfer large files.

it comes with encryption/vault software, though I tend to discard it and free up the extra space on my drives that do so.

Decent speed and small size are both pluses, I'll update if my concerns (small concerns, granted) about durability end up warranted

The drive does just what you want for a portable.

1) It's compact, a little bit smaller in thickness and dimension than my Iomega Ego and a little larger and thicker than my Iomega Prestige and Verbatim. But like the others, it will fit quite easily in a laptop bag pocket and take up little room next to your laptop

2) it comes with a very short USB 3.0 cable, which is just what I want with a portable drive--I don't want to pack a longer-than-I need cable or have one tangled up near my laptop

3) it's very quiet

4) it's backward USB 2.0 compatible

5) The USB 3 is noticeably faster--consistently about 2.5 times as fast as the 2.0

6) it's a bit heavier than my other portables save my Prestige, but not hugely so and it feels more sturdy than several of them

7) It doesn't say so, but it's quickly and easily formatted to work on Macs--took me under a minute with Disk Utility (erase/MacOs journaled--though you have other options) and I was copying over files with no problem

will update if any issues, but right now it's a winner

I'm not going to bother with a detailed listing of times as many other reviewers have done a nice job with that. I'll just say that I did time out this device in comparison to a pair of my 2.0 flashdrives and another 3.0 on a pair of Macs, one with 2.0 USB and one with 3.0 USB. There's no doubt it's speedier in all cases than my 2.0s, whether I was transferring over a folder with a lot of docs or a folder with mixed media (docs, photos, video). Roughly 2-3 times as fast than 2.0 consistently (that's with both of them in the 2.0 ports), though the gap narrowed with really large, mixed folders. When it goes into the 3.0, it was consistently 3-4 times faster, with again a narrower gap with really large, mixed files. In comparison to a Triton, it was definitely significantly and noticeably slower, a little bit better than half as fast.

The device feels very light and the casing not quite as sturdy as my other drives, though I never feel like it's in danger of breaking. Just doesn't have the same sense of heft and durability.

On the other hand, the slide clicks in nicely and solid, with a satisfying sound and doesn't retract easily unless you are wanting it to

If you have a 2.0 drive, it'll be noticeably faster and if you're looking for a drive, makes sense to get one that can go with you to your next upgrade. If you've upgraded to 3.0 and want a new drive just for that, there's no doubt you'll notice the difference, and especially with large files and movies etc. I'd ay it's definitely worth it. As for going beyond to the Triton, personally my need for speed isn't that great--this one would suit me fine. Some people though have less patience than I do. Plus, I'm cheap. So slower than the other 3.0, but I'd say still a fine value.

It took me longer to unpack these than to get music via my iPod Touch streaming through them--the set-up, connecting, streaming process took under about two minutes. Worked fine as well with my laptop.

The sound quality is fine, especially for small speakers. I don't expect them to rattle my windows are pump the base. The lack of a strong bass is noticeable (as mentioned, not a surprise) but I wouldn't call them tinny at all. The sound was quite pleasing and handled high volume with no distortion.

They're small enough to pack or easily move around or outside. They do connect to each other, with detracts from their convenience a bit, and I personally wouldn't have minded a longer connecting cable so as to spread the sound a bit farther apart, but since they're really not made for room-filling sound--aimed more at desktop or otherwise small spaces, it's hard to call that a major complaint or oversight. A longer cable might have pleased me but had others complaining.

I prefer the Creative ZiiSound D3X to these--it's bit more convenient in that it's a single speaker set up and I thought its sound quality a little better, plus it has the ability to add in the subwoofer and other speakers (I have the subwoofer), but really, the difference isn't huge and the intent is somewhat different for most, so these speakers more than suit the bill for their size and purpose.

There really isn't a lot to say about this adapter, which is a good thing--it just does what it says it does and does so seamlessly and easily.

"installation" couldn't be easier
1) plug it in to the wall
2) cable it to your stereo with the attached cable/wire
3) pair it with your bluetooth device
4) play your music

My review is limited to connecting via my Apple devices: a Touch and a laptop. Both worked without any issues whatsoever. I noticed that some reviewers have said they need to repair each time; I haven't experienced that problem. I bring my Touch back into the house, turn on the stereo, hit play on the Touch, and out it comes.

I am not an audiophile by any stretch of the imagination so keep that in mind, but personally I don't notice any drop off in quality when it plays through. Nor does it ever drop the signal.

It's small, discrete, easy to hide or blend in with your stereo. It sits there unobtrusively and lets me play my music collection or Pandora without any hassle of set-up or maintenance. It just works. Highly recommended!

This is only an advance review as I don't yet have a computer with USB 3.0 so I'll have to revisit once that happens. So on the general and USB 2.0 side:
speed: The disc performs at a decent speed but slower than my equivalent Verbatim, especially with large files. The difference was relatively small with documents but minutes longer when I transferred over my iPhoto library: 61 GB took 33 min.

It's got a raised rubber partial casing which makes it easy to hold but more importantly for my purposes I like it because I have a glass top desk (a large one) and with the casing I don't need to worry about scratching

It feels nicely solid and durable--we'll revisit that as well as time marches on

it comes with an Iomega cable (not a basic one) so you'll want to hang onto that. The cable has two plug-ins in case you need extra power. I plugged it into my Mac keyboard slot with no problem and my Macbook as well.

It's small, though not as sleek as either the Verbatim or the Iomega Prestige (part of that is the rubber casing)

It runs extremely quiet and doesn't heat up at all.

As the title says-- so far so good. No complaints at all

There's a lot to like about the Playsport. For one, it's very easy to use as a point and shoot should be. The picture quality is certainly fine for just about anybody's use, save for those who really like blowing their pictures up large. It's very fast to move between photos and movie--a few thumb moves is all it takes. The same for toggling between the movie quality. Which means if you suddenly want to grab a still photo while videoing or are worried about recording room and want to drop down a notch or two in quality, you can do so without missing a lot of action. The zoom is a 3X, which is serviceable. I'd prefer longer and I'm sure the next version will offer a longer zoom, but as I use this for quick shots of the family and not for event shooting, the 3X is rarely an issue in terms of not being adequate.

Transfer of files is easy and fast (I use a Mac) and all the cables come bundled with it. Yes, you read that right--it ships with all the needed cables.

Because it is so small and slim, and held in that vertical position, it can get a bit shaky and you'll need to pay attention to keeping it steady, more so than larger cameras or ones you hold with two hands horizontally. The sound pickup is fine save that wind noise can be a problem on windy days--it'll wash out a good deal of the speaking sound.

It feels rugged out of the box and the number of times I've dropped it, including just recently while chasing my boy and his friend around the corner of the house and getting my foot caught in the extension cord of the Halloween decorations. I watched the camera skid across several feet of concrete sidewalk but it was none the worse for wear.

It's slimness makes it a great pocket camera--one of those where it's defined as such not because you can cram it into your pocket and walk around like you have a grapefruit in there but where it slips right in and you barely notice it. That's one of the reasons it's become the camera I take most often when I know I won't need a larger zoom or a flash.

I haven't tried the underwater aspect in actual underwater conditions (snorkeling, say), but a few practice photos in the pool shows it takes pretty sharp photos in that environment. But I'll leave the gauging of that aspect to those more well-versed in such a need.

In the end, it's a great little camera and as mentioned, it's quickly become the one I carry along most often when we're just heading out for some family fun. For post-dusk indoor, I take a Canon elph and for events or hiking a Canon IS with a 12x zoom and a tele-converter. But for playing games in the yard, birthday parties, classroom events, etc.--the Kodak has become the go-to camera.

highly recommended

Really wonderful product, we mainly use it for watching YouTube in the kitchen. High-quality audio and video calls (Messenger, WhatsApp). Spotify music. Nice screensaver displaying photos from our albums.

A+ comfort
A+ sound. (Disclosure - not an audio expert) Everything sounds good but the biggest difference between this and my cheap wired headphones is the bass. I didn't fully appreciate how obnoxious the bass is on pop songs until I got these.

Negatives:

The sound will drop out for a fraction of a second occasionally. I expect this is because I live in an apartment building with tons of wireless signals everywhere.

The charging system is kind of awkward. You want the base to be hidden out of the way somewhere but you need it someplace handy for easy charging. But I can't think of much of a better way they could have done it.

I am not an audiophile but I can tell you these headphones are comfortable and sound good to me.  I bought these headphones so I could listen to music or videos late at night and be sure not to disturb my neighbors and for car rides.  For these purposes these work great.

This is an attractive stand that noticeably improved the sounds quality of my speaker system by raising some book case speakers I had.  I deduct one star because the base is a little unsteady and will wobble if you nudge it. It's more of a psychological issue because if you aren't touching it, it is steady enough.
Easy to use. Bass notes are surprisingly strong
Quiet, yet has enough power to keep me comfortable (AGE 65) during bible study.
Easy install and sounds great!!
The AC14 is the brightest of the bunch, the AC14 SE is warmest with an open soundstage, and the AC14 XL is the most neutral and clear with good imaging.

I bought both, and the NF-A4x20 definitely seems to move more air than the NF-A4x10, while both being able to run at 100% with essentially no noise. For comparison, I bought a cheaper 7000rpm 40mm and it is unbelievably loud.
Seems to move a decent amount of air at higher voltages, with little noise.

Some consider it BS, but if you have a resolving system and a decent ear, you will absolutely hear the difference between power cables. I started out as a cable nonbeliever, but I simply can't deny what I hear. I bought some of the 10 awg Chinese ones, and definitely prefer these to those. With those, everything is very in your face - detailed, but almost harsh sounding.

These on the other hand seem to open things up, and sound a lot more smooth. I would take a blind test if possible, because it's very obvious. I also confirmed with Pangea that if you're using a headphone amp, you likely will not need the increased gauge of the AC-9. Regardless, I really want the AC-14SE's after using these.
Contrary to some people's beliefs, optical cables can have an impact on sound if you have good enough equipment. I have a $150 cable, a couple glass ones, etc. and this somehow sounds the best. FYI
Balanced sound that gives a faithful reproduction. Also slightly elevated highs which is great for monitoring recordings. Great all-rounder, it's no wonder they're still being made and praised.
Yes, cables do matter. Yes, it's digital data, but if you have good enough equipment you'll notice a difference in sound by swapping out any component in the audio signal path.
Not "veiled" at all if you have it properly amped. Highly detailed neutral sound that is also very musical and enjoyable to listen to.

Yes.

Edit: My neighbor in another house complained about the bass - this other nonsense reviews claiming it's weak are total BS.

If you're like me, you've done some research (extensively in my case) on comparing these two speakers, and have probably come out with a vague case for each of them. Some prefer the Miccas, some prefer the Pioneers. I decided to order both and find out what the deal is for myself. And although I haven't ordered many speakers, I've been a headphone enthusiast for many years.

FYI, I'm using these with a sub (Dayton 1200), so I can't comment on their performance by themselves.

The Miccas sound pretty good, with clear highs - solid performers for movies. But they never made me very impressed by their sound. They seem serviceable, good for the price but not particularly great. They are by no means a bad speaker, but they are a bit thin sounding, kind of one-note.

With the Miccas, if felt like I was listening to music, but with the Pioneers, I felt like I was feeling it. They have a lush tone that is very musical, and I noticed I was bobbing my head to some songs I wasn't before. Better dynamics, soundstage - they really allow you to get lost in the music. Even though the driver size is the same, everything sounds bigger, with more depth.

And even though they have less treble energy than the MB42X, they seem to retrieve a bit more detail. Certainly not "veiled", just darker in tone. I'd prefer there to be slightly less treble than too much - just make sure to remove the grill, as it can make them slightly too dark.

For $20 extra bucks currently I think it's a no-brainer to get the Pioneers, unless you can't particularly stand speakers on the warmer side. I have the center channel coming in today - I've heard mixed reports on it, but if it's anything like the bookshelves I'm sure I'll be satisfied.
Love these, quiet and do the job. Didn't notice any temperature difference between using them and the F12 Arctic which was ridiculously loud. Finally, my computer is quiet.

Excellent. Bass is great and balanced, mids aren't recessed, highs are crystal clear. Sound stage is amazing. Comfort is amazing. Amp isn't required. Looks slick. What the hell else could you want?

Only "downside" is if you want to use it in public / not a closed headphone obviously. I own a 7509HD and a SR125i, the HD 598 is better than both. For $150, even $200 - this is an incredible headphone. I did a tremendous amount of research, and my search ended here. Highly recommended

Ordered these along with 2 Mediabridge HDMI cables to set up new entertainment system, and like the HDMI's this Toslink cable didn't disappoint.  Well-packaged, looks and feels high quality & awesome audio performance!

As with most purchases I over-researched this one, and I'm so glad I did. My priorities were (in same order): awesome picture, enjoyable Smart TV experience, quality, good-looking design & cinema quality 3D experience. After poring over Consumer Reports article and CNET & PC World & PC Mag reviews I was really confused and torn between this Sony & 2 similar models, 1 from LG & 1 from Samsung. Finally, the Sony edged out the other 2 & I ordered it. It arrived yesterday and I installed it. And now I know I made the right decision. Sony's on-screen set-up was very easy to use. As soon as I completed it and the picture feed from Dish Network came up we were blown away!  The picture quality is indescribably good. First, it is so crisp and realistic. And the colors are so true-to-life. But the part that's hardest to describe is how the picture looks 3D even in 2D mode. The characters seem to jump off the screen into the room. The only thing I can compare it to is when I first got corrective eyewear for distance, and everything looked 3-dimensional for the first time in years when I put my new glasses on. Regarding other things I was looking for, within 10 minutes of plugging it in I had the TV set up with our wireless internet and was streaming a TV show on Netflix - couldn't have been easier & picture quality was equal to live broadcast & none of the buffering delays we had with our Wii. Just pulling the TV out of the box and assembling it with the heavy metal stand (unlike heavy use of plastic with so many others) was a testament to the quality. Already knew from seeing it in a retail store that the monolithic styling with the gorilla glass was a show-stopper but wasn't prepared for how stunning it looks in the hole over our fireplace. I've read some reviews on glare off the glass or the viewing angle being narrow, but I don't see what they're talking about. Finally, I charged the 3D glasses I'd purchased separately (bought both Harry Potter & Chronicles of Narnia bundles for total of $270, which was cheaper than buying 4 pairs of glasses alone) for just 30 minutes as light indicated they were fully charged and tested out the 3D.  All I can say is WOW!! Great 3D experience - don't know what negative reviews were referring to. Anyway, I LOVE my new Sony KDL46HX820 - it was worth every penny. Maybe someone else will benefit from all my research.

This little box is amazing. Easy to connect and nice to be able to adjust a few things. I have a Fluance RT83 going into a Yamaha receiver. Sounds great.

Like others, I added a switch to the cord. Really should come with a switch - only reason I did 4 stars.
Worked great. Took it to Peru where I did not need the adapters but appreciated the converter. The fan makes a very subtle white noise.
Sound quality lousy
Good value. Sound is very good, good bass.  Overall very nice
Easy to plug and play. Nice sound.
I like the new style and the sound is richer and deeper.
This is a fun speaker.  Lots of blinky lights, and the sound is really good.  Really enjoying it a lot!
Bought these for my boyfriend and he really likes them. The audio when he is on the phone is a little muffled but for the price I think they are great.
Looks great and was easy to install.  Amazingly quiet, too.
I bought this adapter to add blue tooth sound to my old desktop. It setup easily and has been working well. I use it nearly everyday and have never had a problem
They're nice headphones for a good price. I've enjoyed them and don't have any complaints. They're really good at noise cancellation.

Excellent picture quality for the price.  Everything about this cam is great except the cloud services.  The false positives cause me to turn it off when it's raining or storming.  And the delay after an event (3-5+ minutes) means I cannot use this for any kind of alarm.  But it's still nice to have.

I was already happy with my AirPods Pro v1. They were the best earbuds I've ever owned. The Black Friday sale prompted my to try the AirPods Pro v2: Wow! They actually do sound better.

Everything looked great until I noticed the case discharging by itself at an alarming rate, as much as 5-10% per day. It looks like the built in "Find Me" feature is to blame, and it cannot be turned off. This is an issue for me because I don't use the AirPods all the time, especially in the winter. Finding dead Airpods when I do decide to use them would really upset me. So one star off.

I love my Airpods Pro 1 that I purchased in early 2020. They were worlds better than anything else I had tried and I have used them weekly ever since. The new version 2 looked interesting, but the old ones worked so well there wasn't any push to fix what wasn't broke. Until the Black Friday sale caught my eye and I decided to try them. In short: Wow. I'm in love again. I rather prefer the increased base, and the sound overall is brighter. The other features like the Location should be great to have.

Overall, I don't regret this at all. I've fallen in love again.

I've been using a Sony X55 for 7 years and it finally gave up the ghost. I tried the XB33 to replace it, however the sound quality was below par.

The X55 had a wonderfully balanced sound with the woofer and two tweeters giving tight bass and crisp mids and highs. The xb33 with just two woofers had almost no mids and the highs were muddy at best. The xb33 DOES play much LOUDER then the x55, so for parties it would be the better choice. However, my needs are for low to mid volume while camping, so I returned the xb33 and tried the xb43.

The xb43, with two woofers and two tweeters has the balanced sound I wanted. As a plus, it’s in Stereo! The size, however, sucks: The xb43 looks and feels much larger and is MUCH HEAVIER. (nothing is free)

The included case is nice and keeps the speaker clean and cords organized. I also purchased the silicon condom that fits the xb43, and everything fits in the case.

Overall, very happy with the speaker and would recommend.

Buying a used UPS for more $$$ than a new consumer grade unit might be risky. However, in this case it worked out. This is a solid Network Grade performer with large batteries, and worth it.

My biggest concern was in shipping as most of my 'Zon purchases are packaged poorly. I was delighted that this was packed almost as well as a new unit. Cosmetically the UPS looks almost new as well; no scratches and the display is perfect. The batteries are after-market, (not official APC) but look good. The manufacture date on the batteries is July 2021 (may be new) and the self test passed. I would think this easily passes the "80%" mark.

The biggest problem was finding the 64 bit software for Windows. PowerChute version 10.0.5 is available on the APC website, but requires searching. The software is a bit confusing and clearly aimed at the business networking crowd.

Overall, this is an excellent purchase and I highly recommend it.

I purchased the WD 5TB drive to replace a 3yo 2TB Lacie USB-C drive that I've outgrown. I nearly returned this after I replaced the Lacie with the WD drive and saw the speed drop from 57Mbps to 25Mbps! On a lark I used the cable the WD came with and saw the speed jump to 115Mbps!

Lesson: Not all USB-C cables are equal.

So I see double the size and double the speed with the WD drive and I'm very happy. Recommended!

I needed an upgrade; my 9 year old Vizio was not cutting it any more. Reading the reviews I decided on the TCL 55r615. The voice remote on the r617 wasn’t worth the extra fifty bucks, and the voice function is duplicated on the Roku phone app anyway.

I am VERY happy with the TV; Colors and picture are bright and contrast seems excellent. I’ve watched a couple of 4k documentaries and was blown away with the picture. The Roku menu for the streaming channels really is excellent to use: Far “Snappier” and easier to navigate than any other that I’ve used. (Including my Sony Blu-ray player) The Roku set up allows setting up the apps on your PC and updating the TV afterwards making initial set up a breeze. The Roku app allows listening with headphones to whatever is on the TV, but I haven’t used that yet. (I read where people have purchased older Roku remotes that have the headphone jack, but don’t need that function myself)

Since I read that many people had problems with Banding, I downloaded some test JPG’s to a thumb drive and tested the set: It passed! No banding was seen and colors were even with the exception of very slight darkening in the four corners. Even knowing it’s there, I can’t see it on live TV so I’m happy.

The bad parts: the screen is more reflective than my old set. Since I was going to wall mount the set anyways, I’ll point the screen downwards to minimize the glare. I’m certain the high end TVs costing 4 times as much have this covered, but I’m good with my TCL. Setting up my Directv remote to the set was a HUGE PITA. This was more a problem with the remote than the TCL set, but was an hour of my life I want back.

I haven’t tried using a sound bar with the ARC/CEC function, but I don’t anticipate any issues. Overall, I’m pleased to have found such high quality at this price-point and would recommend this set.

The only thing I don't like about the Roku Express is that you can never turn it off once it's plugged in - the only way you can shut it off is to turn off the TV together, so it basically becomes an umbilical cord to the TV. Otherwise it's great though I'm aware that Roku is packed with advertising - the buttons are marked "Paramount Plus," "Netflix," etc. - so if you don't have these streaming services it's a not subtle attempt to persuade you to sign up for these services. The Roku Channel is fun, there are stuff there that I didn't see on other channels. But note that there is a lot of repetitive stuff on all the "free" streaming channels - it seems like there's a limited amount of content that just keeps getting recycled - one minute Pluto has it, next month Crackle has it, next month Tubi has it, etc.

Overall it's fun and easy to use.

This retro boom box can be used with 4 D batteries or you can plug it in with the AC adapter. The battery option is good for using this radio at the beach but I noticed that it uses up the battery power fairly quickly. The plug in option is better though I wish it used USB as I have plenty of chargers for that. The sound quality is pretty good, not tinny, and the digital read out is cool. The reception is also good. There's nothing extraordinary about the sound quality (it's nowhere near Bose quality) but it's a nifty looking throwback to the old style radios. I think a hipster who wasn't around during the 70s would love this.

These are fairly decent for this price point (you can't expect perfection for something less than $100) but when you turn up the volume, the bass is not great and actually sounds a little muffled the higher you go. However, if you like to listen to classical music and soft rock, it's fine. It works using Bluetooth and syncs up easily. The battery power is fine and the controls are easy to use. My only other quibble is the crudeness of labeling the R and L sides of the headphone in can't-miss big print, as if they're made for older people or those with vision problems. I found this detail gave the headphones a slightly tacky feeling.

I also like the fact that they fold up neatly inside the included travel case and it doesn't take up that much room in my luggage. It's something I would take on a plane or a train - good enough for a trip but I would use Bose or another high quality headphone when I'm at home listening to music.

Though not advertised as such, these headphones are clearly inspired by Pikachu, with the black and yellow design. The sound  quality is average, but then these are meant for kids and best suited for gaming. The headphones are tight fitting but not noise cancelling. The best thing is you can plug the cord on either the left or right, so you can avoid tangling up the cord. You can also lengthen it by pulling on it, so it is adjustable. Overall these are great fun headphones for the Pikachu fan.

This is an unusual Bluetooth speaker - its main novelty lies in the design. It is compact and seems made for small apartments or any area where space is at a premium. The speaker is round, like a mannequin's head, and allows you to hang your heaphones there when not in use. It's a clever design and makes it easy to put away all your listening equipment when not in use. It also charges the wireless phones while docked, which is pretty cool.

The major downside is that the sound quality is not as good as Bose and seems just average for this price point. If you're particularly finicky about sound quality (as most audiophiles are) I would look elsewhere. If you prefer a space-saving device that provides decent sound (enough for a party for example), however, you do worse than this Motorla product.

I thought MP3 players were no longer fashionable since I can listen to songs on my cell phone. Since you can't submerge your phone in the water, however, Finis has created this pricey but well-made device that allows me to listen to my favorite songs while swimming in deep water and even underwater (I don't know if it's possible to scuba dive with it, but we'll see). What's unusual is that there are no traditional earbuds (logical, since you'd be wearing protective anti-water earplugs) and the music is transmitted to your inner ear via "bone conduction audio transmission," a clever new technology that bypasses the ear directly in favor of the bones near the ears.

I was impressed with how good the sound is considering the slosh of water and waves around you. However, it's essential that you wear goggles because the device clips onto the strap itself. I swam a few laps with it and it never slipped off. Design-wise, it's compact and easy to take with you on trips. As with many "sports" devices, it offers only the most basic controls, which is fine given that it's meant to be used while in motion.

In terms of sizing, it looks like a big key chain or a miniature computer mouse. It's small and the gray color made think of a shark or some other sea creature, but its minty-green accents make it easier to see in the water, especially as there's no light function.

Transferring my music files from my tablet to the player was easy. The rechargeable lithium-ion battery lasted me for about 6 hours, which is more than enough since nobody spends that much time in the water, unless they're training for the Olympics.

Overall, this is a very cool product for those who miss listening to music while swimming. Why should runners have all the fun?

These earbuds have an interesting design - instead of the usual black, the wires look exposed because of their copper color - but this is an illusion because they're actually covered with a protective translucent rubber that feels a little slippery to the touch. The earbuds themselves remind me of pencil erasers, because they're slightly gray with copper interiors. The pair come in a zippered black and red case that has a nice mesh pocket on the inside, with an extra set of earbuds that you use to customize the fit.

The sound quality is sharp, crisp and clean. I listened to classical music as well as pop and rock, and the delicate notes came through as well as the thumping bass. To my relief, it didn't have the muffled quality of cheaper earphones and the sound is comparable to the $200 Sony earbuds I bought awhile ago. However, the included earbuds didn't fit perfectly within my ear, so after I customized them with the included set, the noise cancellation feature worked great. It effectively blocked any sounds around me that might interfere with the music.

Overall I'm very pleased with this pair of earbuds. My only question is longevity - my Sony ones lasted almost three years, so if these hold up even half as long, I would consider it a great purchase considering the price point and the sound quality you're getting.

These are very pretty earrings with an eye-catching array of delicate stone in different shades of blue. I bought these at a party thrown by a friend of mine a year ago, when she was still a Lia Sophia consultant (as you know, they went out of business as of Dec 2014).  Although I read some negative reviews about their jewelry (stones will fall out and tarnish), so far I've been very lucky with these earrings - I still wear them frequently and they've never lost their tarnish and all the stones are still there!  My only regret is that they're selling so cheaply now and I paid so much more for them (as is the case if you buy from a hostess).

These In-Ear headphones by Monster are great for listening to music while exercising. Unlike the Sony earbuds that I currently own, the Monster earbuds don't make that annoying "thwomp, thwomp" sucking sound that comes from the earbud moving around and jostling inside your ear.
This is due to the "sport clips" that come with the earbuds; the rubber tip is designed to fit in the curve of your ear and keep the earbuds from falling out. It also ensures that all sounds are blocked out while you enjoy your music. Before this pair, I had never used a "sport clip" type of earbud before - however, there are good and not-so-good things about this type of design, which I mention below.

The package comes with three sets of sport clips (Small, Medium & Large) and a corresponding number of earbuds. In addition, it comes with a little mesh bag to keep all your extra buds and clips in, as well as body clip that you can use to keep the earphone cord in place, so that it doesn't sag or get tangled up (NOTE: for a little set of headphones, I thought the packaging was ridiculously big - a little wasteful, but since they cost over $100, I assume the packaging was made bigger to impress upon you the value of the item)

When you open the package, it's already fitted with the "Medium" size, but I found it was too big, and had to replace it. It was a little confusing at first - you have to pull off the small earbud and then, with a gentle twist, pull off the sport clip. But once I got the hang of it, it was easy.

I really like the Sony earbuds I currently own, but I have to say I was impressed by the deeper, richer bass notes from the Monster pair. It felt fuller, perhaps because the earbud is so tightly secured that you don't lose any sound whatsoever. On the other hand, if you like to pull on and pull off earbuds quickly (I tend to do that when rushing to the bus or subway), you might find it a little bit more awkward and time-consuming to remove the earbud and then put it back in your ears, given you have to align the sport clip with the curve of your ear until it feels right. But I'm sure that it's just a matter of getting used to it.

While I'll continue to enjoy my Sony earbuds, I plan to use this pair exclusively for times when I go running. The instructions even claim they are washable (considering the fact that I sweat quite a bit, this is good news). Still, because of the delicacy of the earbuds, I assume you should only wipe it with a cleansing cloth, as opposed to using a lot of water and soap.

For years I've passed by expensive services offering to convert your old VHS tapes and 8 tracks to DVD. Thanks to this handy little device, there's no need for outside help - you can do it entirely on your own and save yourself lots of money.

Not only is this device easy to set up (if you've ever dubbed VHS tapes, it's roughly the same set-up) but it's compact (the device itself is the same size as a deck of cards). Unlike other gadgets these days, it will work with older Windows operating systems instead of demanding that you download the latest bloatware or update. As if this wasn't enough, you can also convert the music from your audio cassettes and old LPs to a digital format (this is a bonus feature as far as I'm concerned since the product is marketed as primarily a video product). I also liked the fact that you can export the saved file to iTunes and, once ready, can view an old video you made years ago on your iPhone or iPad!

My only quibble is that the editing features aren't as extensive as those programs specifically made for enhancing your old videos, but overall the program provides everything you need to make a smooth transition from copying an old VHS to DVD. Overall I am very happy with this product.

This is a decent, serviceable headset but rather expensive for the price. I have another Logitech headset for home use but this one was definitely better in quality.

Appearance: the plastic casing feels a little cheap, which raises questions about its durability. I once owned a Sharper Image headphone that had a similar feel, and it broke after a year or so.

Function: the headphone is lightweight and quite comfortable to wear, thanks to the padding on the top and the ear muffs. However, the muffs are thinner than I expected. For the price, I would have liked them to be thicker and offer better noise cancellation capabilities. The microphone, however, feels professional grade, being bendable and sensitive. In addition, the long cord is very work-friendly - it's thicker than conventional cords (preventing easy tangling) and long enough for me to reach over my desk without concern that it'll tug or pop out. Also convenient are the location of the controls for volume, phone and speaker - they're on a rectangular box located on the cord itself. Cool.

However, setting up the headphone took some work. With my other Logitech headphone, all I had to do was plug it into the USB drive, let the computer recognize the device, and off I went. Here, I had to be patient and follow the specific setting instructions for Windows 8. Listening to videos and audio files worked fine, but the microphone function didn't work when my phone rang and I tried ti answer using the mike. I pressed the button but nothing happened. As it turns out, the phone function appears to work only when you're hooked up to Linc, an application that nobody in my office uses. The instructions didn't make this clear.

The sound quality is decent for business purposes but for hi-fidelity sound, it's average. I had assumed it was a noise cancelling headphone because of the padding, but I was wrong - I had no trouble hearing some of my coworkers bickering a few feet away while I was listening to a webinar. I had to up the volume to block them out.

The headphones come with a smooth zippered vinyl pouch for storage or for traveling. This was a very nice touch.

Overall this is a decent enough headphone for work but I would have given it five stars had the price been lower.

According to my husband, a former Boy Scout, camping aficionado and Nature lover, Bushnell makes excellent products. These binoculars live up to that reputation - they are well made, powerful in range (10x), and provide crystal clear views. Additionally, it's compact and thus easier to pack than our current pair from Barska. It has twist up eye cups, an adjustable bridge (so that they can rest comfortably on the nose and reduce eye strain) and a rubber casing that makes it easy to hold and grip. Best of all, these are waterproof (the instructions say you can immerse them in water and no damage to the insides will occur) and fog proof. We have not yet tested the waterproof claim but will update this review when we do. Clearly, the product is geared toward the serious nature enthusiast/hunter/explorer type. It comes with a strap, lens cap, and stylish carrying bag.

However, there is one problem - if you have a narrow face (as my husband does), you have to press the tubes very close together in order for it to sit comfortably on the bridge of your nose. Unfortunately, you can't do this without distorting your field of vision. As a result you're forced to spread it wider just to correct the distortion, at the cost of not having it feel 100% comfortable on your face.

Except for this issue, this is an excellent product that I can recommend with no reservation.

I often eat at my desk, which is not the greatest thing. Croissant flakes, bits of cheese and even rice grains often find their way into the crevices of my standard keyboard at work. It gets really disgusting. A few times crumbs got stuck inside the keys and stopped them from working properly. I've used compressed air cans and mini vaccuums but they don't do that great a job. I often end up having to flip the thing over and give it a shake. In addition, I remove all the keys and use a Q-tip to wipe up dust and dirt that get encrusted in these tiny spaces, which is time-consuming.

So you can tell I was relieved to get this washable keyboard. This thing is made for the Oscar Madisons of the world (like me). While you can't use it underwater while scuba diving (the instructions say you shouldn't submerge it in more than 11" of water, and no more than 5 minutes at that), being able to do a wash and rinse (as if it were a dinner plate) is more than enough to get most dirt and crumbs out.

I also like the fact that there is no additional software to install - just plug into the standard USB port, wait a few minutes until your computer recognizes the hardware, and then you're off. The keyboard is about the same size as other computer keyboards, except that the keys feel more like ones you'd find on a laptop. They are round and smooth and make me feel I'm pushing buttons. Because they lay flatter on the surface of the keyboard, you get a softer sound when you type as opposed to the hardier tapping of regular keyboards.

It took me awhile to get used to the feel. The buttons lack the slightly concave ridges that keep your fingers nestled so my fingers felt slippery on them, but not enough to have a problem.

Despite these reservations, however, I think this is a well-made product that is very practical, especially for people like me, who'd rather write than clean. Now all I need is a washable mouse!

Here are my thoughts about Roku. Generally I like the product, but in setting it up I had some concerns.

PROS:
**Easy to set up
**Compact - it's so small it fits in one hand.
**Picture quality is pretty sharp depending upon the source. It is not HD quality but more like a decent DVD (though not Blu-Ray).
**A number of free channels available through Roku. You can add a lot of content. Since I'm an old movie buff, I added Pub a Hub (public domain movies) and Crackle (pretty bad recent movies but some good classics, like Easy Rider).
**Picture is big. I have a friend who has a projector that's five times as big as the Roku, and yet the projected image is the same size. That's impressive.

CONS:
**How much radiation does this device emit? In the fine print, the instruction booklet reads: "This equipment complies with FCC radiation exposure limits set forth for an uncontrolled environment. This equipment should be installed and operated with minimum distance 20CM between the RADIATOR AND YOUR BODY."
Hmm. I don't know about you, but it's hard not to sit pretty close to the projector. I used it in the bedroom and watched a movie on the ceiling. Of course I had to be close to it in order to put it at the right angle. How much radiation is the device emitting?

**Roku asks for your credit card information before you can use the device. When you set up an account, even if you don't want anything other than the free channels, they force you to put your credit card on file. The other privacy issue I object to is the way Roku allows you to connect to Facebook. In order for Roku to work, you were pretty much forced to allow Roku to access your information on Facebook at any time (even when you're logged out!) Not happy about this.

**In order to add some channels to the Roku network, you have to establish separate accounts. That means establishing one for Netflix, one for Amazon, etc, if you don't already have one. This means I'm sharing my account information with a number of companies I may or may not want to do business with. No doubt all this information will be shared among the video providers. That means a lot of spam will be coming my way in my email.

**Roku is geared toward convincing you to subscribe to as many streaming (pay on demand) services as possible. I'm not sure I would pay $300 for it, as it is very much a device aimed to getting you to subscribe to streaming channels. You can use it other ways, but Roku feels like a product sponsored by many vendors, as opposed to a stand-alone projector.

My conclusion? I recommend it with some reservations as noted above.
