I began researching these based on reviewing another popular brand. I am a stickler for detail and after hours of research and asking questions I decided to give these a try because of the cost and positive reviews. I bought these for my elderly parent (90 years old) who has hearing loss but does not wear a hearing aid.
After a couple weeks of use I can honestly say these things are great! Very easy to install, easy to use for an elderly person not technically savvy, works from a long distance (we tried the next room), and the volume of these units can go very loud which is good for all types of hearing. There is also a balance control in case a person hears differently in both ears, and a switch to change from normal to higher or lower frequencies to help those with that type of hearing loss.
We can now watch TV when visiting my parent without the TV being so loud. But it is hard to verbally communicate with each other when they wear the headphones, but that’s not a big deal.
You can turn down the TV as low as needed, even muted, but the headphones can be as loud as needed. We used the RCA output from their TV (a 4 year old flat screen) and that works great. We tried it on a new flat screen and worked well also (digital output). All cables are provided along with extra ear inserts.
I like the fact this uses 2.4GHz instead of Bluetooth or infrared which often can lose connection with interference or movement away from the base station. I went out of the room into the next room and heard this one just fine.
The weight was a concern for me but my parent only watches TV for no more than 2 hours at the time and they said it was fine. There are ear loops provided to help with holding the unit if needed.
The only issue I found was that the input on the base station to charge the headphones was oriented backwards to how a person takes off the headset (have to turn the headset around to charge). And when putting on from the base station you have to turn the headphones around else you’ll put it on backwards which is not a big deal, but the volume button and balance will be reversed meaning my parent the first time turned the balance thinking it was volume and thought something was wrong. That’s one more thing for an elderly person to remember, plus you don’t need a lot of pressure to bend/break the charging prongs in the base unit if installed the wrong way.
We used the “speaker” option one time and it worked pretty well to allow a person to hear conversations in the room.

I’ll update this review should something change, but for now I highly recommend.

Excellent product and has been great, highly recommend. You can see my full review below.

REVIEW:
After researching several products including much cheaper alternatives, I ultimately decided on this particular brand/model. We use this specifically to alert us of cars coming into our driveway. If you are looking to use this for security reasons, be aware the sensor blinks red when motion is detected which can be seen at night.
Based on two week’s usage, I highly recommend this unit thus far and here is my pros, cons, & discoveries after a few weeks of usage:
Pros/Discoveries:
• Easy to setup and install. Read the manual first!
• Transmitter easily mounts to anything. We used a 4”x4” treated post mounted about 3’6” above the ground. Post is overkill but does look nice.
• Does not seem to have many false alarms but will pick up anything within the range of the sensor which has enough movement to trigger the sensor (as it should). Had one alarm over two weeks that we never saw the reason for the alarm. Perhaps something blew across the sensor. We also have a sprinkler system which sprays water across the sensor and it never alerts, which is good.
• Install the sensor at least 3-4’ above the ground which will avoid most dogs/cats/squirrels, etc., and do not place it on metal. I also would not place it near/within range of bushes/tree limbs or similar items which might move with the wind.
• Adjust the sensitivity distance on the sensor (you must remove the four screws on the sensor to do this). Our driveway is for one car so I decreased the sensitivity level to 23’ (set 39’ from the factory). Options are 13’, 23’, 26’ and 39’.
• You can easily adjust the angle of the sensor once installed.
• Has a sensor low battery indicator which flashes inside on the receiver.
• Easy to add other sensors if needed up to 16 (4 on each zone).
• Uses common batteries. Sensor takes four AA batteries (should last a year); receiver uses four AAA batteries and/or wall outlet power. Receiver can be plugged in with batteries installed acting as a battery backup if power is lost.
• Receiver has plenty of sound melodies to select (~30), and can be very loud if volume is adjusted all the way up.
• No problem with range as our sensor is only about 150’ from the receiver but does go through a couple walls.
• Our sensor is installed in the weather without any other coverings. Based on the instructions it can be mounted anywhere outside and I don’t see the need to put the sensor inside a protective covering.
• I like the removable top of the sensor to keep out weather and sunlight on the sensor.
• The 12 volt relay is a nice option for linking to alarms, gates, or whatever else you might want to do.
• Receiver is easily turned off and on. If leaving home really early on weekends for example, I’ll turn it off to avoid waking my family when I drive out.
• Came with a small screwdriver which fits perfectly to remove tiny screws in the sensor for battery installation and sensitivity setting.

CONS:
• I thought the sensor would have been enclosed in stronger PVC (aka thicker plastic). But it does have a lifetime warranty as long as the company is in business.
• Would have liked more color options for the sensor. For example, black, white and camo.
• Worried about losing the small screws when adjusting sensitivity and/or replacing the batteries in the sensor once installed. Our sensor is installed over a plant bed with pine straw, so I had to put down a white towel under the unit when opening the enclosure to make final sensitivity adjustments. Would have been nice if the sensor came with the type screws that don’t fall out when unscrewed.
• Receiver is not the nicest to look at but we managed to place it where it was centrally located in the house and not so obvious.
• There are over 30 melodies available but we were hoping for more chimes/bells similar to doorbell type options. Many are song type melodies which we didn't like.

Overall very pleased and highly recommend.
I would like to see a wifi enabled version for alerts on a smartphone if desired.
Will update this review should something change.

It has a 1 year warranty, so if it continues I will ask for a replacement. Considering how much some of the ear buds are, the Skull Candy ones are great for the price.

Ok, the basics:
- They arrived promptly.
- They were packaged well enough to protect the item well; yet not require me to be a wrestler or an origami grand master to get at them. Also, I didn't feel like I was killing every tree on the planet, nor creating so much plastic trash with packing materials to become an environmental nightmare (that's always a nice detail).
- The product looked great. Just like the photos, sleek black with grey buttons and connector covers that were simple to spot and use.

The details:
I purchased these when they were on sale, and didn't open the box and use the ear-buds for several weeks. When I finally did, the setup was simple and very easy to manage. Unfortunately, they began to malfunction. I contacted tech support at Jaybird, which was ALSO easy. I didn't have to manage an endless maze of voice menus constantly telling you "did you know you can find help on our website?".

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

On that note, I have to digress for a moment. Dealing with a call management system that's set up as a means of insulating the client from the vendor is a pet peeve for a few reasons:

1) It's completely obvious that the translation for "Did you know we have a website?" is, "We'd really rather brush off this call, and not waste our support technicians' time doing, um, support. Please hang up, and go play with your browser." It makes the customer service department seem like they're either cowardly, understaffed, or just lazy.

2) It is nearly always a waste of time to do so. I think most of us are bright enough to search through an FAQ page to look up an issue which was common enough to solve ourselves. I don't want to wait on hold before just seeing if my device is plugged in, or assembled as the instructions describe.

3) Lastly, even if the previous two reasons didn't exist, I'm the client. I gave you my money and purchased your product. If I want to speak to a human being versus arguing with a voice recognition system or dredging through your online documentation… I should be able to do so. Expecting you to stand behind your product is not unreasonable.

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

Now, all of that said - I had NONE of those concerns with Jaybird. I reached a pleasant, professional human voice almost immediately. They said, "Hello, my name is Mikey. What can I do to help you today?". Even better, it was a person here in the United States. I didn't have to wrangle with any language issues, cultural confusion, or regretting doing business with a company who sends jobs overseas!

Mikey was on top of the problem as soon as I explained my symptoms. He asked me to provide my proof of purchase (easy enough with Amazon). Then he arranged an RMA, emailed me all the details I needed to send the defective product back, and sent me an email documenting everything we discussed in case I needed to look it up. Further, since my buds were now discontinued, they replaced them with the next model UP at their expense (they didn't even grumble).

My first item may have been defective, but they stood behind it 100%. They replaced it very promptly, and with a newer, better product to boot. I could not be happier. Sometimes it takes something going wrong to show you whether or not you chose the right product and vendor to spend your money on. I would certainly do so with Jaybird again without reservation, and would recommend them wholeheartedly. Oh, and if you read this, thanks again Mikey!!

I originally bought a 12" cord from another seller for my Meta Quest 2 so that I could connect headphones, but the problem was the Quest 2 audio jack is on the left side and my headphones (Bluetooth that can turn into corded cans) have their jack on the right side. That meant that my only option was to put the headphones on backwards, but then the audio channels are reversed. This is a problem in VR as directional audio is a big thing. If something is sneaking up behind me on the left side but I hear it on the right side, that's no good.

Enter this product. The length is perfect for me to wear my headphones correctly AND having a second one to use with my PC is pretty awesome as I don't run into problems like leaving one plugged into my PC and not having one in my Quest 2 carrying case when I need it.

Arrived two days after I placed my order. It actually beat a letter sent to me from someone across town.

Since there's not too much to a 3.5mm-to-RCA cable, I'm going to go over the very few aspects one at a time.

First Up: Shipping/Packaging - This one isn't going to be the same for everyone, obviously. It arrived super-fast, and due to the nature of the metal tips on the RCA end connecting to the cable itself by threaded connectors, this cable could very easily become damaged in shipping if they come unscrewed. However, thanks to the nice and secure packaging, this was not an issue. The cable got here safe and sound, all in one piece, and tightly screwed together.

Second: Construction of cable - it says the connectors are 'molded'.. boy are they! Perfectly molded design with metal screw-on connectors not only look sleek and fantastic, but they *feel* solid too. It's hard for someone to make a cable "High Quality", but I can tell you this much.. RND did it. They used molded plastic and metal to give it a really sturdy and solid feel.

Third: Length - 6 FEET! (About 1.83 metres for metric folks) Great if you want to sit near the TV and play games on your phone, or if you want to feed it through an entertainment centre to make your phone part of your home theatre system.

and Finally: Picture Quality/Clarity - Sure, it's not HD (PAL and NTSC ONLY.. Though there will soon be a USB->HDMI Cable), but the picture quality is still great. I use it to watch movies quite frequently at 800x400.

Overall, if you're looking for a TV-OUT cable for your Captivate, don't bother with any of the other ones. I've tried a cheaper one, and it didn't work at all. I tried a more expensive one, and after this one arrived... I returned the more expensive one because the RND cable is pure perfection.

I wasn't as shocked as some of the reviewers since I kind of already knew what to expect. I previously bought IsoAcoustics Aperta 200 stands for my desktop LS50's and was completely blown away so I expected similar results from the GAIA III feet. With the GAIA III's I got even more impressive results but that might be partly due to the fact that they went into a higher end system than my desktop setup.

I have never gotten such a huge improvement in sound with this "cheap" of an investment. I put "cheap" in quotations because upgrading my speakers cables to an $1800 pair made a tremendous improvement in clarity and soundstage but don't hold a candle to the improvements that the GAIA III's brought.

Apologies for the buzzwords but after adding the GAIA's I got crazy holographic sound imaging. The improvement in soundstage is unbelievable and undeniable. A second veil was lifted from my speakers. I experienced this "veil" lifting when I upgraded my speaker cables but the improvement with the GAIA's was even more drastic and at less than 1/4 the cost. There is a new level of clarity to the sound and upon listening to Beck's "Sea Change" album I was hearing parts of the song (instrument separation) that I previously had not noticed. It was the same "WOW" feeling I got when I upgraded my headphones from Beyerdynamic DT770's to Sennheiser HD800's.

They removed a bloated bass problem that I thought was just poor room acoustics. Overall, the low end became really tight and focused sounding and there was a boominess that I used to get when sitting in the back of the room that is no longer there.

Another benefit that I didn't expect was how much larger they made the "sweet spot". To get the best sound I used to have to sit dead center between my speakers about 6 feet from the rear wall. Moving forward, backwards, or to the sides as little as 1 foot really killed the soundstage. Now I can sit around 5 feet off center from the sweet spot in every direction but forward and it sounds almost as good as being dead center. This has made listening way more convenient since I have more freedom with where I sit without really compromising the sound.

They also caused a significant improvement when watching movies. Before you definitely knew you were watching movies on a 2-channel system. The dialogue would get lost in the mix sometimes so I would always watch movies with subtitles. Now it sounds almost as if I've got a center channel installed when watching movies. Dialogue is so clear now that I can finally lose the subtitles.

TLDR: Just try them! As long as the seller is "fulfilled by Amazon" you're protected by Amazon's gracious 30-day return policy. This allows you a no-risk demo of them and if you aren't blown away like every other reviewer you can always send them back with free return shipping and get a full refund. There's really no excuse not to try them with that 30-day return policy on the table. With so much snake oil in the audio world it's easy to be skeptical of products that promise big results but this is one product that I can say with 100% certainty is completely snake oil free. I've gotten big improvements from speaker cables but at great cost. I've spent hundreds on interconnects too with negligible results. The GAIA's and the Aperta 200's though... just WOW!

Only ticking off a star because I ran into some quality control issues.

The motor on the first RP6 that was shipped to me wasn't fully mounted and was hanging off the bottom with a 1/4" gap between the motor casing and the plinth. This probably could've been easily fixed by tightening up some screws but with a turntable at this price I decided that it was worth returning for a replacement. Longest two weeks of my life.

The replacement arrived and this time there was an issue with the wiring. I went to attach my cartridge and noticed that the tonearm leads/wires were extremely thin. Like the thickness of 3-4 strands of hair. So thin that I was afraid they would break when trying to mount my cartridge. I didn't remember the leads on the first RP6 being so thin so I looked at photos online and these were definitely not stock tonearm wires.

By this points I was getting extremely frustrated and almost said screw it and changing my purchase to a Clearaudio Concept turntable. The distributor put me directly in contact with Rega who seemed a bit embarrassed and assured me quality control issues are rare and twice in a row was unheard of. I sent them photos of the tonearm leads and it was agreed that it was not the correct wiring.

Another return and another waiting period for the 3rd replacement to arrive. My patience was wearing thin at this point. Thankfully 3rd and final replacement showed up in perfect condition and WOW. It sounded great.

When I purchased the RP6 I didn't have the budget for the RP6 / Exact 2 cartridge combo so I was using it with an Ortofon 2M Red. It sounded good to my ears at the time but after I finally upgraded to the Exact 2 cartridge I about lost it. It sounded like my entire stereo system got an upgrade. The RP6 / Exact 2 combo is a match made in heaven and I wouldn't waste time trying to find a better paired cartridge for the RP6. Rega really took the guesswork of pairing out of the equation with this combo.

In the end, was it worth the hassle? Yes. I can see myself having this turntable for the rest of my life so the month or so of waiting on a working replacement was worth it in my opinion. And the chances you will run into a situation like mine are slim to none. The whole experience was a testament to Rega's exceptional customer care.

TX-NR801 replacement based on component HDMI changeover, Onkyo history and best features/$$ under $1K.

Environ: 5.1 B&W+Sunfire sub, plus Vizio+Roku+DirecTV+custom-built linux media server. All component connections are direct so internal A/V switcher+upsampling is fully utilized.

Extras: Audyssey audio setup does not require post-calibration tweaks and the on-screen setups have built in helps.

Learned:
o Firmware via USB flash, walk through setup and Audyssey calibrate after each upgrade.
o Read the entire manual, esp setup and audio mode sections, even if experienced.
o Same-name audio processor modes sound slightly different that previous Onkyo.
o Run Audyssey in full calibration mode, 3x in a single central location.
o Turn off HDMI/RIHD and Network Control else 'standby' power is +40W!
o Internet radio functions are better than Roku or PC, Onkyo display is usable enough for NET navigation that TV can be turned off, and there's an http interface for favorites management.
o DLNA is excellent for media server mp3 library (minidlna for linux), has repeat folder and random modes that actually work.
o Ethernet via Netgear Powerline AV500 to switch/router, media server on same switch (no wireless bandwidth/routing complications).

Delivered in July, never used original firmware. First upgrade had infrequent 3s internet radio gaps (buffer stall) and DLNA title transition hangs, September upgrade fixed these. Onkyo takes firmware upgrades seriously, apparently.

The case made for an easy build. There are enough reviews out there espousing its benefits, so I will just comment on how to make it even better. The case is marketed as a "silent" case and it has certain features that help in that regard. A foam lined front cover and heavy aluminum side panels dampen the noise. "Antec 2" fans are used for cooling, they have a low and high setting that can be adjusted from the back of the case to suit your sound/performace desires. However, I think they could do better. If you are simply looking for a roomy case and don't care about sound, there are cheaper alternatives out there than this. if you are building a case for silence then this needs some extra work. First, the fans have to go. Even on low you can still hear them in a quiet office environment. Speedfan wont help as there is no PWM on these, they are controlled via the low/high switch. Put in something like the Nexus 120mm PWM silent fans and pair them with a fan controller. There are a total of 7 120mm fan mounting locations inside this case (1 rear, 2 top, 2 front, 2 fron behind hard drive cage). You could always go the water cooling route as well, but this was a little simpler and I have more peace of mind not thinking of possible failures of the system. In addition to the fans, purchasing some closed cell foam about a 1/4" to 3/8" thick will do wonders as well. Not only odes it make the side panels heavier but it also deadens the sound. I attached some on the sides and cut up foam and fit it on the top and bottom as well.

Not completely silent but enough where it is not noticeable unless I put the system through a graphics intensive process, and even then ALOT better than what was there before. So in conclusion, good case that can be made great with some modifications.

Asus

Fujitsu Siemens
Gateway

Of course, you can still crank up the volume to the point where it's hard to hear anything else, but at that point you might as well wear regular headphones. The purpose of these is to hear low background music while still hearing other things.

Just use regular headphones for that. These actually came with ear plugs, in case you want to emulate the audio isolation of regular headphones. But that's a little silly. I'd rather use regular headphones than mess with wearing these and ear plugs at the same time.

One interesting side note, I noticed that when I open my mouth really wide, the sound changes. I think that's because my jaw and cheek bones move into a different position, or something like that. These are a good way for me to extend my wifi to areas in my house that needed a signal boost.
Setup required a bit more effort due to vagueness or incomplete instructions. I had to reset these several times and start setup once I figured out what the units were doing. One key is to decide if you want to use these as a WIFI extender or a wired router system and setup the units with this understanding.

Once setup on the main router was complete adding the satellite units was as simple as pushing two buttons, and now you have a new MESH wifi network where your devices automatically transfer connectivity to the unit with the most powerful signal.

For speed the primary unit is pretty good. if my main router wifi speed is around 450mbs, the primary wifi is around 300mbs which is pretty good. Now the satellite units speeds drop down to around 45mbs which is good for an extender setup, and is somewhat dependent on how far from the primary unit they are, but the speed is never above 50 mbs. That gets us to range. if this was a wide open building with no interior walls I could see where two units would cover 2000 sq feet, but in reality 2 units are good for a around 1400 sq ft. This still isn't bad considering the install footprint.

What I do like these for is the network is always up no matter the main WIFI router condition. In other words if my main cable modem WIFI goes down, but I have my PC and Printer on this mesh system I can still print while the primary cable modem is down. Also devices connected to the mesh WIFI stay connected to the mesh WIFI, so those WIFI cameras outside are still able to record to my NAS drive even though my cable modem is offline.

These provide good clarity and range, and the ability to be constantly on for continued communications. There is an option for an earpiece and mic that would make this basically hands free constant on communications.

The range of these are good in the area where I used them. it is the wide open desert mountains but we had about 6 miles between us, and line of sight basically, but these worked pretty good. I would expect range to decrease if the area is heavily wooded or not line of sight.

Best of all these have a weather alert system, it will alert you to impending weather so you can take cover, this is handy when the next storm may just be out of sight. I would recommend these for any outdoor activities.

Yamaha sound bar is a tremendous improvement over the typically crappy TV speakers found on most TV's today. Setup was easy and efficient using the included fiber cable. Once connected, I selected the sound profile and connection for the TV was complete. It took me about 15 minutes to connect the sound bar and get it configured and running. Using the connection with the TV links the sound volume on the TV to the sound bar so volume control can stay with your normal remote device.

The remote is used for all set up actions for the sound bar. Selections for the sound bar are indicated by a series of led displays on the top of the sound bar for quick reference.

Now for the big question - How is the sound quality? Sound quality is very good, the adjustable sub woofer level lets you customize your sound profile to your personal preference. This items is a nice addition to improve your TV sound quickly and easily.

First off the sound quality on these is amazing for a wireless headphone. Everything is crisp and clear - the power to drive the sound is here. These headphones have good base boost, and volume levels to make these great for those who fly. With the added assist of noise cancelling, these are headphones I like to keep in my travel bag. i am not sure if I would get 17 hours out of a charge, but these can go a full day of travel without requiring a recharge.

These are comfortable for long lengths of time both in weight and the over the ear fit. I will continue using these as my go to when traveling.

This digital camcorder has features not found on many camcorders.
First the things I like about this Camcorder:
This camcorder records in high definition (1020 at 30 fps), and two low resolution (720P at both 30 and 60 fps) select-able from the screen.
There is a option for setting the camera up for motion control triggered recording.
The system has a IR based night vision system to record in total blackout conditions.
The remote can be used to control most modes of the camcorder and start/stop recording.
This system comes with a external mic to help in recording the audio component of your filming, you have the option to use this mic or not depending on your circumstances.
You can use the camcorder as a photo camera with resolutions ranging from 5mp to 24mp along with settings for white balance, color, and shutter speeds.
You can turn off the beep sound for camera functions, something you may use if recording wildlife.
This Camcorder comes with a wide view lens, great when recording in a shallow area such as a room to get everyone and everything into one shot.
Extra battery, handy for extended use or areas where you cannot recharge the camera.

Things I would like to see improved:
The zoom is digital only, not an optical zoom. This limits the camcorder to recording only items in a shallow depth, not great for outdoor use unless you are up close to your subject.

All in all, a decent camcorder for use where you are close (physically) to your subject, or as long as you understand its limitations.

Jabra Talk 45 Bluetooth Earpiece has many features that will satisfy users needs as listed below:

Battery life: for me was around 10 hours of life, recharge time was also quick at around 90 minutes to fully recharge. Not bad for a Bluetooth earpiece.

Sound quality: Sound quality was surprisingly high for such a small unit, clear and without any distortion or hiss some other units I have used had. Volume adjustment also provided a good range for most circumstances.

Comfort: This is where most Bluetooth earpieces fail me, because they are just too uncomfortable to wear for any period of time. The Jabra Talk 45 is lightweight and comfortable for extended wear. The two earpiece rings are sized for different people, not just a single sized loop. Put the correct size loop on and you should be good to go. My only ding on this is the earpiece loops are a little flimsy for daily extended use.

Connectivity: The Jabra Talk 45 connected to my phone right away, no issue there. I did have an issue connecting it to my laptop for a Skype call. It would just never be recognized by my laptop to make the Skype call, this is my only real complaint with the Jabra Talk 45.

The Ihome iB832BC headphones synced right up to my android phone and have worked consistently since being synced. I got these for when I was walking my dog and general activities where a mobile earbud set would be of great convenience. The sound volume is quite sufficient for everyone to use in most activities. Sound quality is not terrific but that is to be expected with bluetooth/digital music combos (even my husband's Bose headset has average sound quality (he says it is due to the digital music limitations).
Using this as a phone headset is average, it works but has its limitations. I always feel the limitations there is the microphones in these units are not the best quality and are the weak link in these systems.
Battery life is good, I average around 6 hours between charges which is good for most uses, but not the highest I have seen on these type of headphones.

My husband put this on one of the farm Polaris CUV's since installation is beyond what I would able to do. He was able to install it on a ranger using the roof system as the mounting position for the speakers. It installed easily enough - basically clamp the speaker to the roof support bars, make sure to use the included rubber strips to get these to clamp securely or you will be remounting these with the rubber strips again once they slide down. Wiring was simple as it all goes to one plug that attaches to the amp. This does mean you will be mounting all 4 speakers. And since the wiring is together in a harness, some thought is required as to where you put the speakers and a good route to where you want the amp installed. The amp install is simple as it basically needs power (12vdc) and not a lot else. It does come with a handy audio input jack so you can use something like an old iPod for audio input. It also has BNC inputs if you have say a radio that you would want to connect to it so there is some flexibility there. The Bluetooth hook up was simple and works well, but again do not hide the amp behind a lot of metal or this may not work to well.

As far as fit and finish, the only thing I can knock this on is the quality of the clamping hardware finish, but being on a rough duty vehicle this is actually okay.

The bottom line is: Overall installation is simple, and the unit is easy to use.

My husband installed this in a Toyota we have, along with the Boss touchscreen radio system. Installation was quick and simple as the unit and the amp have matching output/inputs needed for a complete system. Run some 8ga power wire (with a fuse), connect the low level inputs and it was done. He installed this in the trunk against the rear seats so there was plenty of room available for the unit. Installation took him about an hour total, and it was pain free.
Sound is overall very good, has good range to go along with the power of 1300watts. You can adjust the sound range somewhat using the inputs to get a more custom output. Now when my daughter takes the car we can hear her coming home from about a block away.

When I got the monitor the first thing I noticed was the detail in the packaging, nothing is going to be broken here.The monitor comes with power cable, stand, SVGA Cable, and audio cable. Connecting it was straightforward. You can either use the HDMI connection (cable not included) or the standard SVGA connection with the included cable. The monitor has internal speakers that are serviceable. The color and clarity were very good, and the monitor has several menus that allow the user to customize the screen to virtually any desired configuration.
ViewSonic has always made good quality monitors that are at the top of the category. This monitor continues ViewSonic's trend in high quality monitors.

Setup of the AC750 was pretty straightforward and I had it up and running in a short time. It is a dual band so it is rather quick and has good data throughput, using the ability to connect on different frequencies to different devices, which is nice in a unit like this. While I consider that the range of the unit is limited, most people will find the range sufficient for in-home use. I like to use my PC on a outside patio 70 ft from the house and the signal here was a little weak - usable but sometimes it disconnected.  I thought the video streaming worked well, but I do not stream to the levels some do and usually only with one device streaming at one time.

This portable hard drive is great for backing up files and for extra storage. It has 1 TB of storage available, so there is plenty of room to store photos and videos. Surprisingly, the device itself is compact, which is great since it therefore doesn't take up much room.

The hard drive was truly plug and play with no software required to use it. It connects right to the PC with which you want to use it via a USB cord, which is included.

The product information is a little misleading. It leads you to believe this hard drive works only with Dell computers. However, it works fine with my HP laptop. I'm very pleased with this product.

The Netgear NAS system is having your own cloud storage, anywhere, anytime but it resides at my house and not on some remote server that can have someone accessing the information I want secured. This was easy to set up and manage, the management software was relatively straightforward for someone with a basic understanding of networks/servers/security. Being able to manage and share from my own cloud work and personal data with this unit makes data management simple, and no more reaching storage limits with cloud vendors that I have encountered in the past. The redundancy of the system provides peace of mind that my data will not disappear never to be seen again, again an issue I had in the past with a cloud storage provider. I have not yet had to expand the storage, but it also appears relatively straightforward.

About the only complaint I have is the Android app is not really refined and can be difficult to get to work. All in all a really nice data storage unit that I can directly manage without the problem of having cloud vendor issues I have had in the past.

I am very happy with the iLuv earbuds. I've used them with a Android smartphone and they work wonderfully. The sound is well-balanced for listening to music, but I've used them mostly for phone calls. I can hear the calls better with less interference from outside sounds and the mic works well when talking.

Added features which make these earbuds so great are the pouch for storage and for carrying, the no-tangle cord, and the different sizes of ear pieces for a good fit. They've made handling phone calls while on the go so much easier.

Item description does a great job of listing all of the features of the product. Of all the special features of the earbuds, these are my favorite:

* 3 sizes for a better, more comfortable fit
* Magnets on the split portion of the cord to keep them from getting tangled up
* Controls to allow easy handling of music and calls
* Small storage bag to hold the earbuds when not being used

In addition to these features, I am impressed at how well the earbuds are made. The cord is really sturdy and seems it will hold up to regular use. It has so far! The sound quality is good. It is worlds away from the standard earbuds that come with a product, but somewhat disappointing. The bass is weak, which was a let down considering the price range of the product. So while I love all the extra features of these earbuds, I couldn't quite give them 5 stars based on the quality of sound, which is the whole point of upgrading to a premium earbud.

This bag is well-made and nice and sturdy, yet easy to carry for traveling. It's the perfect size for carry-on. It is designed as a camera and equipment bag, and does well for that purpose. However, it can also be used for other electronics items. There are padded sections that are made to protect camera lenses, but part or all of these section dividers can be removed. This allows more flexibility in using the bag. It also includes a handy padded laptop envelope. I am very pleased with this excellent bag.

I like the GoGear Muse - it's a nice basic MP3 player with a few extras that make it stand out from a comparable model of an iPod. Below are a summary of the top features:

* Small and compact, which makes it very portable.
* Comes with a lightweight case that protects the front of the player and has openings for the various ports, which makes it convenient to charge.
* Headphones have an attachment that clip behind your ear. They have avearge sound quality.
* MP3 player also has an FM radio that works well
* Comes with an arm band to use for exercise, walking, etc. The size is large enough for an average-sized man to wear comfortably
* Can be used with Philips Songbird, but is also compatable with iTunes. (For best results, set up a separate playlist just for the GoGear)

Overall, it's a nice MP3 player to use when exercising, sitting by the pool, or walking. I appreciated the extras like the case and the armband that were included with MP3 player.

The Logitech Ultimate Ears 200vi headset has a lot of unique features. I love having controls on the cord to adjust the volume, pause the songs, and change songs. While I used the earbuds only with an iPod, the manual states they are also compatible with an iPhone and allow you to take calls using the microphone as well as listen to music. There is also some functionality with Blackberries and MacBooks, but since I don't have these items I am not able to speak to these functions.

The sound quality of this headset was better than the standard earbuds that come with an iPod. While I was not overwhelmed with how they sounded, I think these earbuds are a good value. They are noise-isolating, not noice-cancelling, so not all background noise is eliminated, but sounds are muffled. The extra features, such as the controls on the cord, add to the value. Another added feature is the small plastic carrying case that is included. While it's not fancy, I've not received a case with other brands at a comparable price, so this was a nice bonus.

A great feature to these earbuds is the five sizes of silicone ear cushions which are included. I don't get a good fit from the standard iPod earbuds or others I have purchased. I liked the fit I got with these earbuds when I used one of the smaller-sized ear cushions. Overall, a good value and good quality product. It might be a good option for teens that want a better sound quality than the standard iPod earbuds provide, but need a smaller size to fit in their ears properly.
I can now use my old JBL sound system with a 30 pin with my newer iPhone via Bluetooth.

I bought these for my grandmother. She can not hear her tv and doesn’t want to disturb her neighbors in her apartment complex.

She LOVES the headphones. She said they are comfortable and easy to use. The sound is amazing and she can still control the volume with the remote.

*Make sure the tv is Bluetooth compatible. If you don’t know, Google the model number.*

The biggest draw for me about these speakers is the space-saving. They are super cute and take up very little space. My desk is very small and my console takes up the majority of the space since I lay it on its side in order to have my monitor, which is rather large, also fit within the desk space by placing it on top of the prone tower. The height of the speakers does not hide anything vital showing on the monitor as they also sit on top of the tower. They can easily go elsewhere even though they are not wireless, because the cords are a good length. I just like having them within arms' reach for the volume control, which is easy to adjust with a knob turn. I am not a serious gamer, just casual, non-multiplayer, stuff, but I do like my movies, streaming TV shows, and watching YouTube. The sound that I receive with these speakers, to me, is great. I love my action shows and the experience just wouldn't be the same with speakers that do not perform. Very happy with my purchase!

I have been thoroughly enjoying my Fire. My laptop and Ereader rest in semi-neglect. I have a lot of downtime, so the entertainment value and portability of the Fire is fabulous for someone like me. So far, I have downloaded and played the freebie games of Goat Simulator, Mahjong, and FreeCell. My Kindle library has also blossomed since acquiring Fire, and I have watched a movie, read my emails, gone shopping, checked the weather, used the calendar and alarm clock. Syncing is great. I have yet to use any of the other apps, but have been thrilled with the performance of what I have used. I do have to charge more than once a day, then again it is frequently in use.

Best EarPods! Sound is amazing and I don't have to worry about where I've left my lightning adapter. My ears reject earpods of all shapes and sizes so there's no way I'm investing in wireless EarPods.  If these fall out, which they rarely do, they are still conveniently connected to me and my phone. My mom has anti-earpod ears, too, so I ordered a set for her and she loves them.  Such a great buy.
Inexpensive, cute unit, not load but it is good in quiet room.
Cool, Small, Sounds great for size. Great Quality!

I bought this radio as a quick and hopefully adequate sound source for a model circus diorama.  I duplicated circus sounds multiple times on a microSDHC.  The sound was fantastic and the battery lasted all day.  Lots of good comments on the sound from visitors.  The radio also works really well and is now my primary emergency radio for power outages.  With all its features and sound, this device may be an acceptable alternative to much more expensive ways to play music.

I had intended to use my tripod with the 8 foot crane but the crane is way too heavy, so I ordered the stand.  The stand is very sturdy and well matched to the crane.  I use a light camera (Canon XA10) qith 15 lbs of counterweight and the stand is very stable, at least so far indoors.  The crane and stand fit together very easily with the fasteners provided (my tripod was going to require extensive hardware store purchases to even try to work).
Not much to it. It's an antistatic wrist strap and it works. Glad I didn't short any of my components when I was building my PC.

A lot of car stereos are very expensive, especially to get them installed. This stereo is affordable and works just as well as many others. The screen quality is great, touch screen works as well as you’d want it to and it almost automatically makes your speakers sound better.
So far, so good. Just installed the tv and sound bar last weekend and just got cable yesterday, but so far it’s a fantastic TV.

My desktop computer is on the floor during my covid "work from home year" and this extension works great. It allows my iPhone headphones (the original style) to do audio and mic for zoom meetings and works with my recording mic for narrating videos. The length is nice and long so I don't have to worry about disconnecting my mics. Excellent value for the money.

Came immediately. Looks exactly as portrayed. Easy enough to set up that I didn't need to look at the instructions. Comes with extra adhesives and mounting clips. Opened and used immediately with no issues. Sound of music comes through clearly on my radio. Phone calls worked great too. People I spoke with said that I sounded very clear, better than just the phone on speaker even, and that was in traffic on the freeway. Game changing product. If anything I regret not getting this years ago! Also the bluetooth light is very kind to my sensitive eyes, it doesn't distract.

Read some other reviews that it split the audio from left to right but that was not my experience. It worked perfect for my trip so that my friend and I could listen to the same MP3 or Ipod. We used both and it worked great on both. Noise level was great. Highly recommend.
I use this to make calls and listen to audio book while driving. I can hear them and they can hear me, so it was a great find at a great price for me.
My super secret weapon for the Echo in my loud classroom!
Awesome sound! And the battery life if very long. I use these at work all day(830-5) then at the gym after for about 2 hours and the battery is still 1/4 charged.

Years ago I had a Fire and gave it away because I found it not clear and I couldn't read an e-book. I love my Kindle White.
This Fire 8 was on sale and I thought I would give it a try because I wanted to download lots of movies to watch when I travel in my RV. It also has a slot for a micro SD card, but you need to format the card or else you get a "defective card" message.
Words are crisp and clear and it comes with some game apps. The downside of the CW Classic Words app is that there are so many advertisements to buy games and sometimes you can't return to the CW game. I will delete this app.
Set up of the Fire 8 was very easy. To turn on, press & hold the on/off button for a few seconds. Once on, swipe up on the screen to type in your password. I am pleased with this Fire 8 and it fits in my pocket book. I ordered a case for it but all the cases I looked at have the on/off & volume buttons on the bottom which I find inconvenient.

I have wired Apple earbuds with a rectangular piece for controlling volume, phone calls, etc. The earbud stems fit perfectly and I was able to easily wind up the cord including the rectangular piece. I don't understand why another person wrote a negative review because of the rectangular piece.

I have Sony headphones and wasn't sure if these would fit. It took me about 5 minutes to get them on but once on, they stay on. I like to walk and listen to music or stories and these headphones do not distort the sound and are very comfortable. The bonus is that they are not esxpensive!

This is so small and very quiet. It copies quickly and since there are no moving parts, it should last a long time I am using it to back up my photos. A 250 gigabytes would have been more that enough because I have all my photos on it and have only used 50 gigabytes. I agree with other reviewers that the case does heat up and it hot to the touch when connected for a long time. It won’t burn you but it is hot.

I am so happy that
music sounds great on this Echo. My husband has the little disc shaped Echo and I was disappointed listening to music. I changed the name from Alexa to Amazon because it was easier to remember. You need to use certain phrases when asking for something. The Amazon help staff answered my questions. I love listening to SiriusXM and Pandora.

Really don't know why I waited so long to get a streaming device. I used to watch stuff on my tiny laptop screen with crappy low volume, but I highly recommend getting one of these and watching Netflix on a bigger TV. It's awesome such an upgrade.

Not all charging cables are equal!! These definitely are rapid charging cables. 2 hours, fully charged phones. Done. Had others that literally took 6-8 hours, NOT EXAGGERATING! They're STILL for sale, bought them only about 6 months ago!

I took a chance and tried this model, WIN WIN! I have one of these in my electric recliner sofa, and in my car. Now I can charge ANY of my electronics with ONE cable! Excellent invention! Thank you!

Works like a charm! I've a broken radio in my 97 Diesel Ram, BUT... with custom wood grain interior.. it made it hard to replace the in-dash stereo. So I had a small Bluetooth speaker for my cell phone, but didn't cut it in a loudish turbo diesel. So, I got this to put in my back seat to pair with my music; Amazon, iheart, whatever. Pairs right up and stays paired without any extra fuss. VERY loud, good base- (could be better) but bein' that it's portable and al,l just adds to its positive qualities. I didn't try the mic or the radio yet. For $99, it's cheaper than a new stereo for my truck and it's PLENTY loud. I also paired this with my Dish music from my TV and put this speaker outside; same music indoors as well as outdoors, nice!

The best multi task, projection clock, MUCH easier to set, reset, etc than the LaCross brand. Also a MUCH better projection. The LaCross one had to be turned backward, and the projection was blurry when enlarged. This one is sharp, faces me, has dimming ability, right down to black- no light in your face at night. Projection is right above head in between my hubby and I. Small button on side by projection dial is pushed to turn it on. Has built in USB charging capabilities which is very much appreciated and convenient. The ambient white sounds are decent, I prefer the waves. Once again, it is easy to tune, set up etc without reference to instructions. Pleased!

I love how easy it is to use. At just a request it will show my front door ring camera , continue playing my audible book (with nice clarity, tell me the weather, look up a recipe and I even have it reminding me to take my medicine. Best purchase I made.
This is very flexible wire for being 8 AWG. It’s OFC as listed. Clear color difference. Tinned to prevent rust. Absolutely great price for length. My sound quality was awesome. I’d highly recommend!
I put this out in our pool shed and the sound quality out on the deck is fantastic. I’m hooked on this product and between this and the echo dot I’ll be putting them in more of our rooms.

!WOW!

Fascinated with this purchase!

Picked a few up for family on the recent Hawaii trip and all I can say is I am SUPER impressed with the video AND image quality!

EIS works VERY well also!

Audio outside of the waterproof enclosure is pretty good and still works well inside the enclosure also!

I would upload a video, although the 4k videos are LARGE!

Be sure to get a V30 U3 SD card, this cam needs it!

Thanks Wolfang, A+ CAM!

A+ power supply!

HUGE monster of a PSU and is probably the largest PSU I have seen in my 25+ years building PCs.

Silent mode is quiet!

Plenty of power outputs!

Great product.

Great woofer for my home theater setup.

Had a Pyle 15 in the box for about a year, but now I swapped in the Skar to get the most out of my plate amp at 4 ohms.

Sounds great and shakes the walls!

A+ Thanks

Works great for our PS5 connection to our 6 series Samsung 70". Had to bypass our older Onkyo receiver being it is 8+ years old and cant process HDMI 2.1. Used optical out from the TV back to the receiver and this new cable to get HDMI 2.1 going with our new PS5 and Onkyo for sound. Thanks, works great

Works fine for my double din replacement. Keep in mind this does not process AM radio frequencies. I removed 1 star due to the housing quality and the bracket screws. None of them are tapped for the screw threads, you pretty much are tapping the threads when you drive the screws in and is rather tough. Pushing that hard on the enclosure caused me to slightly bend the side but was thin enough to reshape. The radio can adjust all Fader/Balance/Treble/Bass so other review answers stating it can not is incorrect. I have not tried the video, USB or BT option as I simply wanted a radio replacement. I also could not find a "parking brake" lead/wire so I am not sure how this thing will allow playing of video, but I am assuming it will simply play them. Great little radio for $40. Hope this helps someone in the future.
The volume button suddenly quit on my original remote, so I found this and it was delivered the very next day. Pop the batteries in it has been working fine for the last week.
Used them before. Top notch quality and adjustability. I highly recommend these for ceiling mounted surround sound speakers.
I bought for my son for his boarding school, it was a requirement that he have a laptop.
Other magnetic Bluetooth speakers cost a great deal more than this speaker and do not deliver any better sound quality. This is an excellent speaker for the money.
Terrible audio quality. These sound no better than a $5 pair from Walmart. There are definitely better options. Probably will still use them for my Switch, but not really anything else.

1st one received was a tad out of focus.  They sent out another unit right away, before even getting the 1st one back.  Very impressed already at this point.  Now the 2nd camera works as advertised with a beautiful picture and even the sound has more gain and sounds better and louder.  Way to go guys...!!!  Woo Hoo !!!

Still playing around with it, but it is totally adjustable for sound and picture. So Real to Life Looking Picture, Almost too good. The sound that comes out of this set without any sound bars or subs is Phenomenal. Alexa and Google Built in makes things nice. So many extras, I'm still finding them all.
Closest to an OLED, without chance of burn in. As CAN happen with OLED.

I finally broke down and bought a newer Firestick.  It's so much faster than the first generation model that I've had for several years.  I don't use the Voice, Alexa, or Volume Control features, so I can't comment on those, but this Firestick is blazing fast compared to my previous model.

Fantastic speakers. Bigger than I thought they were going to be, but still small enough to fit under my computer monitor and not take up too much desk space. Sound quality is awesome, easy to plug and play. Great little speakers, happy with them!

Our 5-year old 55" Visio TV's speakers stopped working after crackling for 2 days...but picture and all else still sharp and working fine.  We were SO bummed to possibly have to spend $300-$600 for a new TV.  But ALAS!  Thank goodness for external audio systems!  We didn't need bells and whistles, just something to actually *hear* our TV again....and this little gem absolutely delivers.  We're not audiophiles or into surround sound, movie quality TV experiences, etc...so this Polk Solo might not be the "best" audio option out there if you're into multiple levels of sound.  But for us, it's a definite improvement!  And it was waaaaay better than purchasing an entire new TV for one little issue!  Thanks Polk!
The sound was muffled

I was looking for a portable CD player to use in my van which didn't come with one. I also wanted one that was simple to use and didn't have a lot of fancy features. I ordered a different player and wasn't happy with it and ended up returning it. Although this player had some negative reviews I thought I'd take my chances to see if I like this one. It isn't as portable as the smaller one I returned, but I'm extremely happy with it. It now sits on my kitchen counter and I listen to the local radio station every day and I wasn't even looking for a CD player with a radio feature. I haven't tried the bluetooth feature yet and not sure if I will. The radio and sound are great and you can really crank it up loud which I couldn't do with the first player I tried. I like the carry handle which makes it so easy to transport from room to room and the fact that it can be used with batteries. The only negatives I see with this CD player: (1) the size is a bit larger than I wanted but this enables it to have larger speakers and better sound quality doesn't it? (2) I would like it to be USB rechargeable instead of having to be plugged in and (3) the color claims to be red but it is more pink than red (when everything else I own is real red, this is a bit irritating). Overall, I am happy with this Jensen CD Player and will not be sending it back.

What I like about this CD Player: the size and design. What I don't like: sound isn't great and the track and feature display is IMPOSSIBLE to see. What's the point of having a display if it's not readable? Something strange happened when I placed the order. I received an email from the seller telling me that there was a problem with my order but without other explanation. This was the second time this happened because I had ordered a different model from the same seller a couple of weeks before I ordered this one. I also received the exact email after placing the first order saying there was a problem with the order but with no other details. I wasn't sure what this email meant. Was I going to receive the item late or not at all? Since the first order was late and did not arrive at the expected time, I finally cancelled the order to get the payment refunded and ordered this CD Player. Then I received an email saying from Amazon saying that order had been about to be delivered but that I refused the delivery. By this time I was totally confused as to what was going on. I did receive the current CD Player on time but why send me an email telling me about the problem with my order. I just received this item but may return it and look for a player with a larger and more readable display. When I press the MODE button I can't tell what the current mode is since the text is smaller than the size of a gnat.

I can't believe how many features this radio has...from the flashlight and reading lamp to the several ways of charging. I wanted a radio that used batteries because I've had crank radios in the past and never got much power out of them. Solar charging is definitely a bonus. The sound so far is great and it picks up lots of stations on both FM and AM bands plus I received very clear reception on my local NOAA broadcast (although I didn't like what they were telling me since it was more snow - ugh). The size of the 2 dials is great and beneficial when you have arthritic hands like I do. I love the red color and the portability. I plan to use this radio when camping in my minivan or when just hanging out on my patio.

This is a well made, very streamlined and sturdy little hub that I'm using to plug into my iPad and, occasionally, my Mac Mini. You should know, if it's not clear from the description, that all of the ports require one of the older Type A USB cables. That's fine as far as it goes, but I do wish there was at least one Type C port for all those cables I now have so I don't have to hassle with using an adapter with this hub. I will mainly use this for transferring data between machines, so I can live with that, but if I were to be keeping it plugged into my computer or iPad all the time, it would have far less utility for me. I give it five stars for how well the cables fit into the ports. So many of the hubs and charging accessories these days are built so poorly that the cables will not plug securely into the ports. Not an issue with this hub, and it matches the silver tones of the Mac quite well.

The original cable that came with my iPad had gotten damaged and wasn't charging well, so I got this two-pack as a replacement. I like the 10-ft. length because I have my office in my bedroom, and sometimes I like to have the iPad at my desk along with my Mac Mini, and sometimes I like to have it in bed with me at night. The same is true with my Samsung phone, which I'm also charging with these cables.

The fast-charge feature works very well. I've got these hooked into a 100W charging station set equidistant between my desk and my bed. It's working out very well.

I have done production work for a small press since 2007, publishing anywhere from six to 24 books a year, all involving cover design, data files, and templates. It takes a lot of room on my computer and in my cloud storage. I'm going to be archiving fifteen years' worth of work soon to make room on my system for other adventures. This SSD drive is plenty big to save every single thing I have to keep, and I plan to get one other one so I can have two archival copies stored in a plastic SSD holder. I know 120 gigabytes is not a lot in this day and age, but for my purposes, it's going to hold fully fifteen years of very hard work with plenty of room to spare. Not too big, not too small: just right.

I've been wanting to figure out how to take advantage of solar power, but I've got a lot to learn. I've been picking up pieces of this and that to try to understand what connects with what. The first thing I learned is that I want to pick up DC versions of things like fans and water pumps because these can be connected straight into my 60w and 100w foldable camping solar panels. I've got a solar-connectible camping generator that also has both AC and DC outlets; if I've got my only DC in/outs in use, I can plug this adapter into an AC outlet on the generator and run additional DC devices. I can also run those devices in the house using this adapter plugged into a wall outlet.

I'm a mildly dyslexic, hands-on learner; reading books or trying to visualize how things work doesn't cut it for me. I am still bewildered by volts and watts and amps, as well as the different types of plug types, but the more things like this I can get my hands on, and the more I can actually physically plug them into this or that, the more I can learn about how to put together a modest system that takes some advantage of solar. If something I'm using requires more juice than I have power for, it's helpful to me to actually see an error message when I try to run it underpowered. I'm hoping that by slow trial and error, one day I'll understand enough to be able to do something more sophisticated. My next purchase will be a strip of LED lights that takes the add-on adapter type this power supply comes with.

This laptop computer is pretty much as advertised, and I am glad to have it. The screen is sharp and readable in 2240 x 1400 pixels mode. This model does NOT have a touch screen, so if that's important to you, you need to look at other laptops that sport that feature. The system so far is quick to respond to requests and has sufficient RAM and storage space.

One nice feature missing from all the other laptops I’ve owned or used is an automatic power up whenever the computer case is opened. There is also a power button in case you need it.

Beside Windows 11 Pro, this machine comes with significant value added: a year subscription to Microsoft Office 365 (normally $69.99/year) and also a two-year subscription to McAfee LiveSafe security suite (normally $129.99/year).

Most people who use laptops probably don’t mind that this machine, like most laptops now, does not have an ethernet port. However, WiFi seems to be performing well in its absence. I may not be the typical user, but I prefer the option to connect by ethernet.

I work almost exclusively at a desk with the power supply connected, so I have not tested the battery life of this Dell. My only real complaint is that, owing to the 14” display size, the keyboard is correspondingly smaller than I like. If I were to do much typing, I’d probably plug in an external keyboard. If your hands are smaller than mine are, this won't be much of an issue for you.

As has been mentioned in other reviews, this is not a gamer’s dream machine. It’s for normal office and business use. Its compact size makes it good for the road.

When I saw this 55" TV on Prime Day sale for $299, hands-free with Alexa, and with no-interest payments over 24 months, I just jumped on it. I've spent almost that much over time replacing lost remotes! I didn't realize how big this TV is, so I almost cancelled the order...but I'm glad I didn't. I've got it sitting on one of those sturdier metal and plastic folding tables (like a card table but rectangular), and I've plugged my Mac Mini into one of the HDMI ports so I can also use it as a computer monitor. What a difference! I can have all kinds of things I need at any given time open and placed around on the screen (see photo), and because I work in my recliner that's a good distance from the TV, I can read everything very well and get to all my open windows super-fast. Then, at night, when I'm ready to watch TV, I can sit back on the daybed that's on the opposite wall and watch it all on the big screen.

My 2014 LG soundbar works with it, but it's only got the optical port cable and cannot be controlled with Alexa. One of the Fire TV tech guys very patiently told me what I need to get if I want to upgrade my sound setup, and I went on and ordered one of the Echo Dots on sale for 19.99 because I couldn't find the one I bought before. I'll probably get a new soundbar at some point but, for now, I can certainly watch TV and listen to music using the one I have. But right now, I have to have the remote to control things that Alexa cannot control, and I keep it in a remote wrangler tied to my daybed (where I also sleep). I thought at first that the TV was just turning itself on by itself in the middle of the night, but then I realized that either I or one of my dogs was flopping over onto the remote, turning it on. That's a temporary issue because once I have an Alexa-compatible sound system set up for it, I can hang the remote on the wall and forget about it.

I've read a number of reviews of the Fire Omni TV series, and they are shown to be on the lower end, picture-wise. If I had wanted a super-duper knock-your-socks-off viewing experience for MSNBC, which is what I watch more than anything else on the TV, I would have to have spent five times as much, and why would anyone do that? Well, if you're really into the primo video experience and have the bucks, I guess you might...but this TV is perfect for me. The #1 selling point for me, other than the rock-bottom sale price, is the fact that I can control pretty much everything with my voice.

I did knock off a star for one reason and one reason only: In the Inputs setup, you can specify what type of product you have on a particular HDMI port. Soundbar, gaming console, etc., but there is no selection for "Computer." I want to be able to say "Alexa, open my computer." Now I have to say "Alexa, open H D M I 1." Cumbersome. I hope Amazon will add the Computer input with a future software update.

Okay, so this cover/hub for my iPad was pricey, but its quality and value really do show. With the exception of the Loya Ark logo on the hub, it could have been made by Apple as an iPad accessory. The pencil charges. The iPad charges through the charging port. I can charge up the iPad overnight, then use one short magnetic cable to switch between my keyboard, mouse, and phone during the day if they need a little topping up. I typically keep the cable plugged into my mechanical keyboard.

I'd written a much longer review that somehow got blitzed, so I'll try to remember what I said. The cover is like those accordion-style covers on a lot of lower-end cases in terms of how it functions, but it is vastly superior in terms of the materials and stability. When put into the triangular stand, the magnetic attachment to the rest of the case is very strong. No floppiness here! I love how you can just remove the "flap" of the cover if you want to, leaving only the metal tank-like case that holds your iPad secure via two locking mechanisms. (Watch the product video; you'll be impressed.)

I have an elevated magnetic stand that my iPad adheres to, but it will not work with this case; the stand's magnet is not strong and/or has its fields in the wrong direction to work with this Loya Ark case. When I've got the case sitting flat on my lapdesk, propped on its own stand, it sits a little lower than my keyboard so it's harder to swipe up to access my apps unless the keyboard is positioned far enough away from the case. I've got another stand coming that I hope this Loya Ark case will fit into nicely, because I'd rather use the case than not.

The ports on the hub work well. I've only found one cheaper cable that doesn't fit snuggly into the hub, and that's a problem with the cable, not the hub. There is only one USB 3.0 port, which I'm using for my red charging cable, but my USB-C to USB 3.0 adapters fit well and allow for extra ports should I need them for transferring data from thumbdrives, my primary use. There has been room for everything I've plugged into this hub so far.

Being an Apple user is costly, but Apple products feel so much more solid to me than anything else I've ever worked on. It's wonderful to have a hub that's equally solid, that fits in seamlessly into the ecosystem, and just works.

I’ve got an Apple Magic Keyboard for the 2021 M1 iPad Pro, and I managed to spill coffee on it so it doesn’t work quite as well as it once did. So I got this little bluetooth keyboard/iPad case for use at night in bed. Setup was easy: Press and hold Fn+B until you see “Wireless Keyboard” and then connect. I had no difficulties whatsoever. The iPad holder is an edged pocket with cutouts for the important stuff, just like a phone case. All the cutouts were fine except for the speaker cutouts, which were a little off and covered up some of the speaker holes; for me, this does not appreciably affect the sound. The keyboard magnetically adheres to the case and is removable/repositionable so you can fold the case to create a stand of sorts for the iPad at three different angles. This stand is a little floppy, though, so you need to have it on a hard surface like a laptop tray to keep it stable enough not to collapse; your lap alone won’t do it.

The pencil slot below the iPad enclosure is strictly for stowing the Apple pencil or other stylus when you are carrying the closed case. The pencil does stick to the top of the iPad like it normally does, but I don’t get any message that it’s charging off the iPad. The edge of the iPad enclosure is between the iPad and the pencil, so I’m not sure the charging feature from the iPad can “connect.” I don’t use my pencil very frequently, so I did not try to drain it and recharge it off this case. Maybe it works. I just can’t say.

I would have given this five stars for its value (under $25!) if the keyboard weren’t a little hard to type on for touch typists. Even banging on the keys hard, some characters still wind up being skipped if you type too fast. It may be the keys will loosen up a little over time, but out of the box they are pretty stiff. The keyboard is also a little bit smaller than the full-sized keyboard I’m used to. It’s close to the Apple Magic Keyboard, however. Another thing Magic Keyboard users might have trouble getting used to is that the keyboard does have to be charged; the magic keyboard does not because it takes its juice directly from the iPad, as the pencil does. Because this case does not magnetically stick to the back of the iPad, it’s not capable of directly charging the separate keyboard. This would be true of any separate keyboard, even one from Apple.

I like this heavy-duty tower charger and surge protector because it can sit up on the table behind my monitor riser and I can get to all the switches to turn power on and off. We’re trying to cut down on power use, and we like to shut down as much as we can at night. But it’s a hassle with some things because, for example, I leave my computer on during the night (with the monitor off) to do middle-of-the-night tasks and don’t want to have to shut it down. But things like my monitor, lamps, plug-in charging blocks that essentially charge up things during the day but can be turned off at night, sound bar, coffee cup warmer, etc., can all be shut down with the flick of a switch on this power tower.

The five USB fast-charging outlets (four 5V/3A USB A and one USB C PD 18W) are on one side-edge of the tower, and the switch to the right of that face controls them as well as the three grounded power outlets beneath the switch. The other three sides each have their own dedicated on/off switch and three grounded outlets. It just takes planning which three-outlet group(s) you want to stay on all the time, and then the rest can be flicked off quickly. Clearly, one would not want to just switch off anything that has a power-down routine, like a computer, but there is no reason why a monitor or the little charging bricks can’t be shut down this way. Certainly the coffee cup warmer and the soundbar don’t need special handling.

If you want to have the onboard USB charging outlets on all the time (and they ALL must be on or off), then the sensible place to plug in the computer is in the three-outlet bank to the right of the USB ports that is controlled by the same switch. If you want to turn off the USB charging outlets at night, then the computer should be plugged into another bank that can be left on. The tower does not rotate, but it’s not difficult to feel for the on/off switch on any side of the tower. I dedicated the back bank, closest to the wall, to the devices I want to stay on all the time, and the rest I will switch off when I quit for the day.

This 10 pack of thumb drives is a great value for backing up discrete data chunks for portability and archive purposes. I use them to back up completed-job folders with large graphics files that I may have to access in the future but don’t want left cluttering up my system or the cloud. The included labels help me keep them organized.

I know the woven cables are supposedly supposed to be more durable than the plain ones, but that has not been my experience in the past. These cables look a lot like the ones I’ve had before that tore up. So that does make me wonder what the replacement possibilities are should the cables themselves become damaged. It remains to be seen how well they hold up.

With that caveat out of the way, I really like how these cables work! I’m sitting here in my recliner/lap desk with a bunch of little peripherals that have to be charged up fairly frequently: wireless keyboard, wireless mouse, wireless over-ear headphones, my TV remotes, my phone. Before getting this magnetic cable set, when I’d get out of my chair and darken the room to watch TV in bed at night, I’d sit my lap desk with iPad/keyboard/mouse on top of half of my dual-monitor-sized riser (on a table near my recliner desk) and have to decide what to charge with the limited number of cables I had and all the different port types.

Now I have plenty of cables, but I really only need one or two. This kit comes with magnetic port plugs in USB-C, Micro USB, and Lightning formats. Once you plug the proper plug into the port of a device, it stays there and you never have to think about it again. With all the peripherals I’ve used them with, the plugs fit into the ports tightly and just fine; I’m not worried about them coming unplugged like I do with regular cables plugs.

I can tell you up front that you aren’t going to be able to charge an iPad with these cables. I keep my original Apple charger and cable plugged in to charge my iPad at night. You also have to plan to plug these magnetic cables directly into a charging port. I discovered that I can slowly charge my phone using my Mac Mini hub, but the rest of the peripherals aren’t really happy with that so I’ve got a few cables plugged into a wall charger and fed under my monitor riser, where they are out of the way.

I can’t say right now how long these will hold up, but I can say they’ve already paid for themselves over a few days of the convenience of not having to deal with a crazy jumble of greedy little peripherals.

I want to point out up front, for those who are afraid these will be too big for a small head, that they fit me fine. I have a small head. I am a short woman, I have little ears, a little head. When these headphones are adjusted to be fully contracted, even without doing any bending of the top part, they fit great. They are lightweight but substantial, very comfortable, and I can see myself listening to them for hours without discomfort. I can lean back in my recliner without anything touching the headphones.

I didn’t know about the whole thing about burning in headphones. I’ve spent the last few hours down that rabbit hole, with all the opinions pro and con, etc., and I’m glad I’m doing it because I can already tell the headphones are responding to the burn-in process. I went to Spotify and looked for burn-in playlists, and I’m playing through one of them now.

I will not use these for noise cancelling, so I cannot comment on that. I want headphones that don’t bother my ears during hours of listening, that give me a clean, clear experience of the dynamics of the music, and that seem to become a part of me. So far, these are doing that. When I first started listening, I could tell these headphones were a little stiff and muddy, but they are loosening up now and becoming quite wonderful. I’m very pleased. And I’m only a few hours into the burning in.

Update: I just tried the ANC button. I’m sitting here, still in burn-in, watching the news on TV and periodically checking in to be sure the burn-in playlist is still playing. I could hear the TV when I was listening to Alice in Chains, and then I turned on the noise cancelling/ANC switch. Hey, this noise cancelling works pretty good! Of course, you get more pressure in your ears with ANC turned on, so it’s not a mode I would listen in for very long, but it definitely cancels the noise. Can’t hear a thing from the TV now. Flip the ANC switch, and I hear the TV. Flip it again, and there’s no voices coming through from the TV.

I switched to an iPad Pro this year instead of a 2013 Macbook Pro, which I’d planned to use (as I did the Mac) on a lap desk seated in my recliner because of a bad back. The iPad with magic keyboard did not work out for me as a desktop replacement, so I had to get a Mac Mini, but I still hoped to use the iPad as my main input device. I needed something stable to hold the iPad that would leave room to tuck a switchable bluetooth keyboard underneath it and to allow for charging cables at times that I won’t get all tangled up in.

This stand has turned out to be just the thing. At first I thought the magnet wasn’t going to hold my iPad, but when I realized you have to snap it onto the stand at the bottom first, that problem was solved. I put a wee bit of Suguru on the back feet of my keyboard to bring it up to a height where I can work on it while it’s tucked up under the iPad but clears the stand; these feet work far better to keep my keyboard stock-still than the feet that it came with. The hole in the back can be used to run the charging cable through from my Mac Mini, or I can use it to hang little bone induction headphones from. Lovely.

With my desk riser, the TV I’m using as the main monitor for the Mac Mini sits above my line of sight over the iPad, and the stand allows me to rotate and tilt the iPad as needed for work with the Apple pencil. So, all in all, a great solution to what was a major problem for me. And it’s a good thing the magic keyboard doesn’t require juice to work. I threw it on my bedside table for those few times I might take my iPad to bed with me and need to type.
