This tablet has entirely streamlined my educational, professional, and personal productivity. I will preface this by saying I chose this tablet (as my very first tablet of any kind) after 5 WEEKS of research and hours and hours of reading the manual, watching video of reviews, unboxing, customization, how-to's, tips and tricks, and specific software guides. I had the nexus 10 in my amazon shopping cart when I first came across this tablet. I will nowhere in this review compare this to an apple device- I have never and will never own one- personal preference, I wholeheartedly believe iOS is sufficient or ideal for a lot of people's use, just not ever going to be for mine. As background, I am in an international DVM program whose laptop just crashed and all 600+gigs of my life were backed up but now only floating in cyberspace so my requirements were a little heady for a tablet-

a) deal with extensive editing and review of PDFs, PPTs, DOCs, XLXS, etc 14-17hrs a day (terms range from 21-24 credits, 4-5hrs of lecture straight, 3-4 hrs of lab with no access to outlet in many labs). Also when I say edit I don't just mean take notes on I also mean incorporate text, figures, etc from textbooks, websites, and other documents.

b) Be a textbook reader and rarely a e-book reader (novels for fun!) Need to access my extensive kindle library, plus some google books and a few Elsevier/pageburst textbooks. Also this needs to be something I am comfortable and accepting of to literally study off of, enough to give up my previous preferring to only study off of paper/actual printed out notes

c) Allow for flawless email, web chat, skype video and text, some web browsing, and file transfer... all on an absolutely horrible school wireless and LAN setup, unpredictable power availability, etc.

d) Streaming and downloading of podcasts, video, MRI, CT, radiographs, and ECG's

e) Be portable to the clinic and the farms for patient-side transcription, recording, etc

f) Get me through the 5-6hr flight and all the airport time!

g) Occasionally watch videos/listen to things for fun

h) Most importantly, due to a dominant hand injury, multiple surgeries, and continued required hand therapy/rehab, I am currently able to write again but not to type with that hand. I therefore wanted a tablet that was stylus intensive- not just for notes, but for navigation, etc. THIS is what made me give up that wonderful squeaky clean android OS of the nexus 10! (I still thing that is probably the best thing for people that want an android tablet but don't NEED a stylus)
So my tablet arrived flawless and flawlessly. The display is beautiful, if anything the screen is too bright- I'm aware my eyes are light sensitive so this won't match with the majority of people but if I do turn my brightness on at all I don't believe I've ever gone above 15%, though I'm sure there will be some case videos poorly and darkly shot that I may need to in the future.

i) at least temporarily, replace my laptop and download and have as much of my backed up laptop files as possible

The tablet was quickly populated with the apps from my HTC phone and google account. The account set up for everything was quick and easy. The initial 2 updates were completed with no adverse signs. Navigation was great, no lag, and I quickly cleared out the stock widgets, set up my panes, and then went into settings.... I activated Developer options and did some customization and disabling there, but most of the disabling I did in app manager, device, and controls. There are very helpful guides out there if you're not sure which apps are safe to disable as well as a "Guide: Longer Battery Life- How You're Being Robbed on XDA that takes you step by step in maximizing your tablet. It was not created at the time when I cleaned up mine but it would've helped greatly!

Here is the gist. The tablet comes crammed full of software and capabilities that I don't need or want. The My Magazine app, a lot of the touchwiz stuff, the eye movement sensors(smart screen), the hand gesture stuff, reading mode, voice control, motions/palm motions, all of that is just a constant battery drain and I will never use them. They were disabled and the vibration feedback for everything was also turned off.

Battery Report: This tablet was shipped within the US twice, and was brought internationally on a plan 4 days later. It was accidently left on the ENTIRE time for about 8 days with six apps up on standby. It arrived with 18% battery left. I use it for 15-17hours a day and end up having to charge it 2-3hrs per about ever 24hr period to get it back to 100. I can use it while it is charging and it will still positively charge during use.

USE FOR A STUDENT: It has replaced textbooks, laptop, printer, scanner, and painstakenly editing and customizing notes and making documents for me. Disclaimer: as someone who used to be able to type 130+ words per minute, I'll make perfectly clear, if you prefer to type and plan on typing a LOT tablet touchscreen keyboards SUCK. This is a fact of life. You can get used to them, you can get proficient at them, but you'll still probably hate it and you're going to need a physical keyboard case/add on if you do a lot of typing of documents or emails. Now, this tablet is made for a stylus. This is not just a peculiarly edged simple piece of plastic that you can buy for just about any touchscreen device and kind of use as a writing device. This is the s-pen, a WACOM and this device and stylus is designed to maximize the experience so you are writing or drawing digitally with an experience just like on paper. Examples- the harder you press the more solid and thicker your pencil/pen/brush/highlighter/calligraphy/etc line. The button on the stylus brings up air command which can be super helpful and it also allows quick screen shots. The stylus allows for fine website navigation that allows you to open drop down windows etc as mouse would. It also offers things a real pen/pencil cant- selective erasing, and selection for drag/drop/copy/paste of ANYTHING to ANYWHERE. You're typing notes and see a great figure and text on a website, you can freehand or rectangular circle what you want and put it into your document. Then you can resize/edit. It's great. I've been using the Snote app for everything thus far, I have made short futile attempts with Lecture Notes and Evernote but I couldn't really get anywhere. I'm not going to give up on then, I just need to research them more to see if I can eventually get them to do what I want and then I can compare them to Snote.

USE FOR A PROFESSIONAL: So far, this has been wonderful. I can seamlessly take notes, look up references, voice record my exam findings, and awkwardly as only a tablet is, take video and pictures of patient's during an exam for later review. (Extremely helpful during lameness and neuro exams for the file). Collaborative documents through Polaris office and google drive is exceptional- as fast as a laptop and more portable, and better screen size than a smartphone. It runs better than the school computers for running presentations off of onto projectors. I can also have students I tutor digitally sign- literally our weekly sheets and submit them via email with one step- completely negating the awesome printer and scanner I brought down here.

USE FOR A CONSUMER: I find this tablet beautiful for watching movies and videos and the sound is great. In a classroom of 50 people chatting between classes I have no problem hearing the speakers among the hub but there are completely valid reports that even cranked the sound might get lost a little if you're in a very loud close crowd. Sound improves with earbuds but the initial audio set up app (basically a hearing test and then a customized audio scheme for you) was startling when it compared the stock/base line settings to what it came up with for ME.

USE FOR AN ARTIST: I'm still learning and adapting, I'll never turn to this instead of actual physical art supplies and paper but it is fun and I can really see myself doing more digital than before. It has been especially nice for graphic design, photoshopping, etc.

USE AS A LEFTY: no issues except see below for one thing that affects both right and left handers...

ISSUES: 1) One day after about a week of ownership, my battery was in the upper 80's, I was taking some notes and about 2hrs later I looked at the status bar and it was 29%. I went into Battery in Settings, and the s-pen interface was responsible for 80% of the battery use. I shut down and then restarted and it's never happened again. Similarly the Android OS did the same thing at a later instance but again it was a one time thing and in both cases the battery recharged speedily after and stayed charged.
2) Snote- I have had weird episodes where an import fails, or it force closes itself repeatedly when I try to rename or change the cover of one particular document. After this erratic behavior occurred twice in three days and completely clearing and restarting Snote from scratch (everything backed up and replaced on my Samsung account) to no avail, I did a factory reset. The last ¾ of my ownership have seen no such problems any more. I will warn you that if you wipe out S note and you start from scratch in it and re-transfer all your SNote files back in, if you have a lot of really big files, it can take a really long time to re-populate.
3) The menu/return and physical home button- occasionally based on the desk I'm at, if my arm isn't supported and my wrist is resting fully on the edge of the tablet, these buttons will get pressed while I'm writing. Its purely an annoyance and doesn't affect the writing or do anything but I definitely have to reposition if I find I'm getting lazy on holding my wrist up at these desks.

Wrap up: I only use in landscape, it's just like writing on a portrait piece of paper except you can also zoom. I got used to writing on the tablet and the tiny stylus very quickly but there are compatible Samsung styli of various widths and sizes out there as well. I thought about waiting for the new 12.2 whose screen is literally a full piece of paper landscape, but I realized this is perfect for me and more portable than the 12.2 will be (this thing can just squeeze into one of the pockets on one of my lab coats. I was planning on having to use the Nova launcher to avoid any lag but truly, this tablet was a speed demon already and I eventually got Nova solely for the customization ability and cleaner interface. It allows me to avoid more things I don't use and I didn't lose ANY of the software I do.

Bottom line, RESEARCH! PREPARE! And there will STILL BE A LEARNING CURVE! But it will be based on discovering unexpected cool features instead of on frustration). If you won't heavily use the stylus, don't spend the money on this tablet. If you're just curious if you could "get into a stylus" try one out first but prepare first so you can use it to the full advantage while you're there. Also, I came from NO tablet and no Samsung/Note experience and there are changes between the previous model and this. You don't actually lose much but things are moved around and different. Don't be scared to optimize it, I'm not talking rooting, though adventurous forays into that terrain have finally arrived as well. In conclusion I love it, it has made things so much more efficient for me, I get a lot DONE with it and it's basically all I have to carry around. I purchased the 32gig tablet plus a 64gig Sandisk XC which installed and worked like a charm. There are annoyances that come up but any issue I have had I have been able to fix. I have everything safely backed up on Carbonite and there's a million ways to sync all of your accounts if you chose (note some of this may be unnecessary or frequency can be dialed back too)

It performs and looks beautiful and I am still learning.

If you read pinterest or other web sites about how to deal with unnatural lighting from popup flash, they might tell you to put a tissue over the flash and it will "diffuse" the light. This is my second purchase of a Sony Walkman. My first one was for my husband for our anniversary. I bought him an 8g player (NWZ-E438) and once I got that up and running, I realized that 8g really isn't that much when I realized that he has a whole bunch of cd's and videos and pictures. But the reason why I bought the 8g of that model was because it had an equalizer. Now, let's talk about this beautiful S545 model - WOW! It's 16g and what a beauty. the sound quality is A-Mazing, and the picture/video screen is clear and crisp. AND it has an equalizer - 5 settings, plus 2 custom settings = 7 equalizer settings. I bought mine at Walmart, and it was $119. I also got it in red - the red color is a nice color, not faded or pastelie. The sound quality from the exterior speakers will surprise you. Keep in mind that you will not be able to host a large dance party with it, but it is just perfect for a personal experience, let's say in your room or something like that. The sound from the speakers is quite nice, and I would compare it to the speaker from my Motorola RAZR2. My phone can get a lot louder than the Sony Walkman, but the quality of sound is just as good. I was not in any way disappointed with the quality. The only thing I would change on this player is the placement of the speakers - they are on the back, not the front. The picture of this player might fool you to think the speakers are in the front, but they are not. I also learned that this player will not be able to download podcasts. The higher-end Sony Walkmans do.

Another thing is that the software for the player comes loaded in the player, instead of including a cd in the box. It worked really great, it was simple and just way too easy to use. It was much easier to set up on the computer and get going than the one I bought for my husband. With the software, "Content Transfer" all you have to do is drag a song, or a picture or a video right to the Content Transfer window, and POW - it's there, and it knows right where to put it (music, pictures, video). So you don't even have to fuss around and click into the different files. I already have 1,926 songs in WMA format in 48Kbps, 38 videos, and 223 photos, and I have 10g left. Right out of the box, because of the software itself, there is 2g being used for the player, and you get 14g to play with.

This player will also record voice recordings and FM radio recordings (song, advertisement, talk show or whatever). It looks like they give you 99 hours and 59 minutes of recording time.

The FM player will only work if you have either your headset plugged in or your speakers plugged in. The FM won't work with the external speakers - it needs to use the wire as an antenna. And I didn't think the FM was bad - worked and sounded just fine to me.

So, if you are looking for a player, you just might want to consider this one.

This is from my experience others may have not experiences the trails and frustration I dealt with. I was seriously debating on returning it to the UPS store.
I couldn't get the picture to work. I worked on it for about 30 minutes and started surfing the web. I came across a video and watched this guy plug it in on the left side and it worked. So it will help to read and look at the pictures in the booklet first.

To save you the hours of frustration I experienced with this product, I will give you the information you need for this to work minutes out of the box. If you want to read this instead of the book.

1. Plug the USB-C port into the left side of the monitor. (I did all the other ports except that one.)

2. Plug into your USB-C port and the picture will work. No stand by or black-outs unless you use all the other ports besides the one on the left.

3. Issue: How do you have more than one thing on the screen?
System preferences>display>arrangement (important!)
The white box in the arrangement tab above the box, that is your Macbook. The second box is your monitor. If you want the monitor on the right side, move the box without the white bar over to the right. The same goes for the left. Now drag that picture over to the side your monitor is on and Bam!!! Beauty!

4. Problem: You don't want to use the volume on the monitor you'd rather listen on your Macbook.
System preferences>sound>output>slide that over to MacBook Pro speakers and take it off that Z1 crap. (That took me a while too.)
Overall, after the stress and migraine, I endured trying to figure this product out. I will have to say it works perfectly for my needs for now.
You better bet your bottom dollar if I have one issue with this product I will be returning it ASAP! Spending more than a hundred dollars on any product during COVID 19 is too much.

Overall I am glad I made this purchase and I'm glad I didn't take it to the UPS store to return it.

That factor is not anywhere near being a deal-breaker, though.)

I bought this stylus because I have a screen protector on my iPad, and the rubber tip of the stylus I had would drag when I tried to use it. I would try to highlight things with my finger, but that proved to be a frustrating experience most of the time, even though I have long, thin fingers. This stylus definitely makes it easier to underline and highlight with greater precision. I haven't used it to write or draw yet. The disc on the point is slightly annoying, but only slightly. (I used the foil tip posted in one of the reviews, even though I hadn't had any problems with skipping with the stylus as yet--an ounce of prevention and all that.) Yes, the stylus does make a tapping sound when it hits the screen, so I don't know if it would be ideal for use in a setting where you want to be quiet. So far, I like the stylus itself just fine, but the color is nowhere near the dark lavender color in one picture or the grape purple shown on the Web site when I made my purchase. It's more of a magenta color, like the picture that was apparently posted after I first wrote this review (I'm updating it today, on May 3, 2013). I personally was annoyed when I received the stylus and saw the color difference between the pictures originally posted and the actual color.

I'm a typical music listener--not a professional musician or anything--but I like these headphones better than the other in-ear headphones I have tried (Sony MDR-EX38iP, Munito Billets 9MM earphones). The sound is great, the ear buds are comfortable (I use the small ones), and I love that control with which I can pause, skip, and control volume, as well as answer and end phone calls. One song: listening on the 50/50 headphones, the sound is great. Same song: listening on the Sony headphones, I had to turn the volume way up on my iPhone to hear it at the same level. Munito Billets: besides being ugly, they are uncomfortable. The sound is almost as good as the 50/50 headphones, but the control with the microphone only controls volume--no pausing, no skipping, no answering or ending phone calls. I will never try another brand again (unless it's a gift, of course). When I buy headphones, I will buy Skullcandy 50/50 Ear Buds.

I certainly prefer this screen protector to Power Support's HD Anti-Glare version. (I think my problem with the anti-glare one began during installation. I had a hard time with it, and by the time I was done, the protector actually attracted lint and didn't reduce glare as much as it reduced screen clarity, at least in my experience.) I can barely tell this screen protector is on. I can only tell when I get greasy smudges on it, and it certainly resists smudges better than the bare screen. The texture is good, too, except that it makes using styluses a little difficult, since the protector grips the stylus tip more than the bare screen. I was using styluses mostly to avoid fingerprint smudges, though, and this screen protector cuts down on that problem enough that I don't worry about using my fingers anymore. One good wipe with a lint-free cloth and it's good as new. Installation was pretty easy on this one (maybe because I got practice on the first Power Support protector. That was expensive practice, though, so if one hasn't installed a screen protector on an iPad yet, I'd recommend a practice round with a cheap one--maybe something that came with the case he/she bought).

The bathroom steam thing did not--I repeat, DID NOT--work for me. It was a complete waste of my time and energy. The Scotch tape tip, though, was right on the money.

Also, I read a review here that said you should buy direct from the company just to be sure you are getting the right screen protector that fits the third gen iPad, but I have the iPad 3 and it works like a dream. Too, if you look at the Power Support web site, this screen protector is listed as being for both the iPad 2 and 3 there as well. Do yourself a favor and save on shipping by buying from Amazon. I wish I had.

Not being a gopro brand made me hesitant but I was pleasantly surprised at how heavy duty this clamp tripod is. We do fishing videos and though rough riding through big waves may cause it to drop its beyond any clamps expectations to stay totally still. We prop it with a towel around posts and all fine.
Highly recommend. I can't say that to most 3rd party gopro equipment.

The ear buds you get on airplanes, for example, is like trying to put a potato in my ear - they won't stay in, causing me to have hold them in my ears with my fingers, which is extraordinarily inconvenient. Same for the many other pairs of ear buds I have tried over the years. I have tiny ear holes and have struggled for years to find ear buds small enough. The smallest size of tips included with these works fine in my small ears, staying in even when I move around. And on top of that, the sound quality is very good.

I initially purchased a Surface Book over competitors because of the great screen definition, as I am an amateur photographer, and screen definition was important to me. I also use it daily for work as a software trainer, which requires a Windows computer (I was and still am an Apple fan).. At 4 years the screen began to have a yellow mark at the sides, and after research I learned about a problem with these computers, which is an expanding battery. Now the screen is bulging and it is unsafe, Microsoft will replace it up to 3 years, but will do nothing for me, other than a $600 “repair” which I may do, to have it as a backup. When stores were open, rumor has it that managers were doing this for free, but they are permanently closed now. I use this laptop for work, and if It is out of commission, I am out of work.
With a failing computer,, why did I buy another? I still love the screen, size factor is good (I travel with it regularly), and the keyboard is comfortable, but the white backlit key color blends into the keys, so they are hard to see, one of my few complaints. I have been through multiple chargers, the Microsoft OEM chargers have died after a short period, developing a short at the connection to the computer. The new model seems to have a thicker wire, so I am hoping that it lasts longer, but the third party chargers I finally learned to buy work great anyway, and I have backups if I need them. I found this at a fairly good price, so there you go. This was an upgrade to an I7 chip, my first is an I5, for the use I give it I haven’t seen much difference.

One tip, I just went from a 3.5mm connector headset to a USB headset. With the former, I had to use an amplifier, and ultimately the computer stopped recognizing the microphone. With the new headset, the sound is much louder, amplifier is not required, and it worked immediately upon plugging it in.

With significant hearing loss (and hearing aides), and a job training in web meetings, I need an amplifier to boost the audio from my Microsoft Surface Book using Sennheiser headphones sufficiently to do my job. It is so critical to me, and I travel so much, that I have used the tiny FiiO E06 and have a backup at all times, as well as backup cables, because they tend to give out as well. I decided to bite the bullet and pick up a more substantial amplifier, thus purchased this one. Out of the box, build quality looks good. Plugged it into my computer charger USB port and gave it a try. Major static but sufficient amplification. Plugged it into the computer USB port, and the static improved. Amplification was plenty good on Low Gain, but boosted further on High Gain, more than I need. If the battery is really as good as they claim, won't need to plug it in all the time, as I did the FiiO. Still will travel with the tiny one, but this is great for daily work. Can't comment on music quality, as I haven't tried that yet. Will update if anything changes, hope this amp lasts.

I didn’t expect to like this keyboard as much as I do, the feel of the keys is not as “brisk” as my old Logitech Ultrathin keyboard cover (which is not available), but it is lightweight and turns the iPad off when closed, and doesn’t require charging separately. I find I don’t use the keyboard as much as I might, because it means unfolding it, but generally satisfied. The listing said English format, I was expecting a different configuration, but looks like a US format to me.

Update 4/14/2019: still like this cover, although I tend not to open it as a keyboard as often as I did with the other type. The “fabric” backing is not soiling from holding it folded behind the iPad as I feared, and as a bonus, it holds on to the iPad better than other magnetic keyboards, so I don’t fear carrying it without putting it into a slip case. I did add a protector for the back, which adds a little bulk, but not enough to concern me. I still recommend this keyboard especially because of the smart connector, which eliminates the need for charging that Bluetooth keyboards require. Responsive keys, and it activates the moment it is opened,

Received this case yesterday, so I am commenting on the installation and appearance. Won't know how protective it is unless I drop the phone, which I hope not to do. The case fits well, was easy to install, the screen protector went on extremely well, easier than others I have installed. The screen looks clear with the protector, the case is slightly large, but nothing like the Defender, which was too big for my taste. The front wraps around the front edges of the screen and projects slightly, which seems to be enough to protect the screen in a fall, unless something struck the screen directly.  All cases are a balance of protection, bulk, weight, and appearance, and for someone who has been known to drop a phone frequently, I knew I needed some decent protection for this expensive phone. Taking a chance that this will do the trick. Doesn't look bad, shows the Apple logo on the back. None of the color really matched the gold toned phone, but for me the glacier white is not objectionable on a white phone. Can't speak to how well it will slip in a pocket, but with a large phone like the iPhone 6 I won't be putting it in my pocket often.

Took this on a trip with a lot of hiking and walking, and worked very well to hold the camera and provide support on uneven terrain. Had I used a separate walking stick, would have had to jockey the stick and camera, this worked perfectly. Climbing Macchu Picchu, people were envious of my set up, and many commented on it. Easy to set up, folds up small, relatively lightweight, solid. Used with a small camera, without a head, but adequate to hold a DSLR and would use a head on another camera. Put it in the water bottle holder on my backpack, also clipping it to the bacpack with the attached carabiner. The first one I purchased was defective, returned it with no problem (thanks Amazon). Very happy with this monopod.

Purchased for a seasonal home to be able to play music from my computer. Amazed at how much volume these put out. Volume control must be via sending device, like your computer, but appear to work with any device with a headphone/audio out jack. No technical issues thus far. Works with computer, iPad, smartphone, etc. Adjusted with equalizer on my computer to improve the bass, as it sounded a little high as it came out of the computer.

Have several Samsung flat screen TVs and have been extremely happy with them all. This is a basic model without a lot of bells and whistles, but has a great picture on an over the air antenna. Sound seems better than older models, in which it was a problem. Great price, no complaints. Went with another brand for my last TV and the reflective screen is a problem. The matt screen on this one is great. easy to put together, great Amazon shipping.

Have not watched very much, since this is in a second home. Picture compared favorably to the others we compared it with, only negatives are higher reflectivity in the screen than others (our other TVs are Samsung) and sound is average. Have been happy with Samsung, but Consumer Reports rated this TV highly, so we went with it. Price at Amazon was significantly lower than at electronics store, and with free shipping, quite a deal.

Finally....I wanted to post this review 2 minutes after I received these on my doorstep....I took them out of the box, and immediately went to the computer and put my music on.  I put on the song that for me is the test of good or bad headphones and.....wow, Wow, WOW!!!!!  I there are not enough good words in the dictionary to describe how I feel.  The clarity was awesome, I could hear every nuance of the music I was listening to, and believe me, I have waited a long time, and tried many, many, many headphones and earbuds (the earbuds hurt my ears...small canals).  I have tried expensive ones and cheap ones...I started buying really cheap ones because I had to replace them so often, and I have not enjoyed my music half as much as I used to.  I am NOT being paid for this review, and I am thinking about buying another pair, just in case, because of the reviews on how easy the plastic breaks...It would be worth buying more to have on hand for the sound alone.  Thank you for such a Great product and the price is unbeatable...Usually you get what you pay for...in this case you get Much more than expected.  Love it!

I've been searching and searching for a keyboard that is reasonably priced and quiet. I don't like the typical clicking and hollow feel of most keyboards. This one has a very nice solid feel to the keys and little to no noise. I haven't had it long enough to speak to the battery life.

It plugged in just fine & seems to be working, BUT:
1) I don't know how/what to do with it. Too much noise for somebody who is not already conversant with this world.
2) Could not get Kodi 18 to install - no idea why, just won't proceed at the end - so I am left with a service that it useless to me.
3) No useful way to search without Kodi, but everything seems to involve an additional fee, which is exceedingly combersome with any controls enabled.
After 5-6 weeks, I have never used it, and actually don't anticipate using it in the future unless I can get Kodi to install.
Excellent bag for the storing the Meade Instruments Infinity 70mm AZ Refractor Telescope.

Works well to help pick up the remote sound and reduce the nearby noise.  Good for spectator events like gymnastics, soccer, etc.  Pretty sensitive to wind, however.  Not sure how best to handle that.

This is a great little power supply that has really been "universal" for me.  I have not yet found a device that it cannot support.  I have no good way to measure how "clean" the supply is, but the variety of fittings, voltages, and polarities, has been more than adequate.  I recommend it.

Keeps cords with straight line plugs from falling onto the prong and warping it and ruining earphones. Electronics friend helped me pick this out and it's a good thing he did. Some earphones make the sound mono and split it between the two sides. This is true stereo sound, and plug has a third channel for microphone. It is very sturdy. I tried it with a variety of sound [music, lecture, old tv shows] and it all sounds fine.

I bought two packages for a total of six adapters and kept only two. Friends were eager to have them do I think I'm not the only one with a prong problem. I think they'd make good stocking stuffers.

Scared cat and me equally.  Woke us right up.  Only complaints are it's a little hard to find the 'off' button in the dark and that light features could signal a plane to land.  Put it in nightstand drawer and all is well.  Nice little clock for the money.
The volume on this product isn’t loud enough for my liking.

I needed a new mouse, because my old cheap mouse started going out, one feature at a time. When the left button quit, I needed a replacement quickly. If you need an inexpensive mouse quickly, this Amazon Basics 3-Button USB Wired Quiet Mouse, may not be the right choice. I ended up waiting almost a week for it.
The mouse itself is not the best quality, but all the features work, and it was plug and play on my old Dell that has upgraded to Windows 10. The left and right buttons are very quiet, but the scroll button is not a silent click. Scrolling the wheel is not smooth, on the mouse nor the screen. It seems to have a bit of a stitch as the wheel turns, like a grocery cart that has a tack stuck in a wheel. The cord is long, but it is a lot thinner and stiffer than any other mouse I've had. It tends to tangle annoyingly easy.
This mouse does what it was made to do. It is likely one that I will replace with one of better quality and keep as a backup. If you just need an inexpensive mouse to use and are not concerned with little quirks, I would definitely recommend it.

I don't know much about specs or any of the tech jargon, all I can tell you about is my experience using this projector. First of all, it came much larger than I expected it to be. It's also very nice looking and seems to be well made. We have a small one that's made of plastic, but the fabric accent on this one looks nice. The only thing I know how to do is hook my firestick up to it, and that was extremely easy to do. The picture looks great and the sound is much better quality than the smaller one that I have. The smaller one requires an extra speaker just to hear anything, whereas with this one we can easily hear it in our living room and in much of the house. It came with a bag to store it in, but I just repack it exactly the way it came and put it away in the box when we won't be using it.
It may not look and sound as great as going to the movie theater, but it's a fun alternative, as you can eat what you want, wear what you want, and be right in the comfort of your own home while enjoying a great movie with your family or friends.
This FANGOR 701 Video Projector provides a great entertaining experience for me and my family and friends, especially for me and my grandkids. Really, that's all I need it to do. I'm not sure what the price point is, so I can't comment on that. But, I would definitely recommend it!

My computer speakers kept going out on me every now and then, so I wanted this speaker to take their place. It will also be good for using with my projector, as its sound is not very loud. I tried listening to music on it from my phone first, and it sounds pretty good, though it could use more bass, especially for music.
Maybe, it's because I grew up in the 80s era, when there was real music and it had lots of bass, and I still want a lot of it. This speaker just doesn't have quite enough for me, but I still really like it. It is a bit taller and skinnier than a couple of older echo dots, and it doesn't have the same exact quality of sound, but sounds pretty darn good.
The color-changing light effect is pretty cool, but I wish there was a way to turn it off sometimes. Because I'm using it as a computer speaker most of the day, and it's a bit bothersome.
This little speaker packs a pretty good punch, aside from needing a bit more bass, and not being able to turn the light off. It will work great for times when you need a pretty loud sound source and have little room for a big speaker. It's small, has a slot for an SD card for playing your own playlist, it's rechargeable, and lasts for a good while before needing to be recharged. I would definitely recommend it!

I got this speaker to go with a small projector that doesn't have much sound to it. It sounds pretty good, but the EQ on my remote does not work, so I cannot change the sound effect at all. The sound is pretty good unless you turn it up really really high, then it gets a little distorted. It could use a little more bass.
It's nice that it's rechargeable, so that we can put it in the middle of the room for the best sound for everyone. It would be great if there was a way to turn the blue lights off, so that we can have it in a dark room to watch a movie without it being bothersome.
I'm not sure what the price is yet, but I would think it would be within the $30 to $40 range. The sound is better than I thought it would be, and it will work great for the purpose I intended it for. It's a nice sounding speaker for those on a budget.

I'm not a techie person so all I can tell you is my experience when using and watching a movie or TV show with this projector. It took me a bit to figure out the menu settings. I still don't understand some of them, though I've learned how to adjust the ones I need to be able to watch something on it.
This is my first projector and I think the picture quality is fantastic! I don't have a screen yet, so we're just playing it on a white wall and it looks great. We hooked our firestick up to it, and it was up and running with no problems at all. We've tried it at several different distances, and even at the maximum distance, and the picture is still nice and clear.
The sound was quite low at first, but after setting it on the surround sound setting, it was a little bit better. It's loud enough if you're watching something alone and don't mind the sound being low, but you'll definitely want a sound bar or other Bluetooth speaker to get that real theater effect.
A problem I had was trying to connect it to my Echo speaker. It connects, and shows that it's connected, but it will not play through the Echo. I'm not sure why that is, but it would really be nice to have it play through that speaker, as that's the only Bluetooth speaker I have at the moment.
Overall, I'm really happy with this projector and can't wait to get a proper screen and a sound bar to go with it. It seems to be made very well, it's quite small and easily portable, it projects a great picture, and it's easy to use. I would definitely recommend it.

I don't subscribe to cable TV, nor do I have an antenna to get my local channels. I'm also in a hole when it comes to cell service. When the power goes out, I lose all forms of communication, and it's usually due to a storm of some sort. I'm in an area where tornadoes are quite prevalent, so having access to some kind of weather information is very helpful.
I am so happy to have this weather radio! For me, it could potentially be a lifesaver when my power is out and there are tornado warnings. It is so well made, and the sound is so crisp and clear. Music sounds as though it's coming from much larger speakers than just a little small one. If the power outage is caused by lightning or something else, where there's no need to listen to the weather, it's nice to listen to the radio. The sound is just that good.
The flashlight comes in handy also. I keep this radio on the table beside me so that I know where it's at at all times. I'm disabled and slow to get around, so having a flashlight nearby without having the fumble with my phone, is so much easier for me. It shines nice and bright.
There are several ways that you can keep this radio powered. You can hand crank it, put batteries in it, charge it by USB, or by sunlight. I have a portable generator that I will charge it by in case of long power outages, but just use a micro USB cord to top it off now and then.
I'm very pleased with this weather radio, although it's a lot more than just that. It's extremely well-made and rugged, all the ports are covered with rubber coverings, the stations that I've found on the radio come in and sound crystal clear, and there are so many different ways that you can charge it. It will warn me of any impending weather conditions when the power is out and keep me entertained with music when dangerous conditions are not a problem. This device gives me a sense of security, and for that, I have to give it a full 5 stars ✨

This is the the second child of my Echo Show 2nd Gen. and my first Echo 2nd Gen. Speaker. A 2nd Gen Dot, Dottin, is their first child. There is also the Aunt of first 2nd Echo 2nd Gen., an Uncle Fire Stick-who brought his two Fire Stick children, and a distant cousin, the Echo Auto. Needless to say, Alexa runs the house!! This 3rd Gen Dot is so great.... Please don't tell Dottin, but she is in danger of being adopted out or, (gasp) traded in, for another 3rd gen Dot. She had just not been pulling her weight in the family lately.
This little 3rg Gen Dot, or Dottie, wish we could call her that... was the perfect fit for our second bathroom. I mean, who can go to the bathroom and take a shower or do your business, without a little music, listening to a book or playing a game? And, suppose you have a smart thermostat and you can't make a run for it when your in the buff and/or soaking wet? You can just tell Alexa to take care of it. So many needs for a Dot in a bathroom, especially a 3rd Gen!!
The sound is a big upgrade from the 2 gen Dot, and I have had no need for a second speaker to enjoy it during a shower. It is super responsive, and hears you, even from a good distance through the house. I've actually had to name it "Echo", because it sometimes would answer when I would be a room away with the door closed.
The upgrade is really nice and I'm glad I got this little gem. She's a welcomed addition to our happy and continuously growing Alexa family.

I love my echo Auto! I'm disabled, have an old car, without Bluetooth or an auxiliary port. So, I use a Bluetooth transmitter to hook up my echo Auto, and month after month it has gotten better and better. Yes, there were plenty of glitches in the beginning, but every time I left feedback, the problems I had seemed to be fixed the next time I drove- which is only about once a week.
I live away from the city, I have a Samsung Note 8 and sometimes my signal that's not very great, so in a spot or two, the signal gets lost, then picks right back up very quickly. Navigation works great, with my phone suctioned to the side window showing Google Maps as I drive.
But, the greatest thing for me, is being able to listen to music from my playlists. I love all different kinds of music, and there's no radio station that can accommodate that. But, having Pandora and Amazon music playlists at the ready, I'm singing along with every song! Another Plus, it has made my stereo sound so much better!! The music is loud and clear, and I like the bass turned up just a tad... 😉🎶🎵🎶
Being a new product, I expected, and still expect a few glitches here and there. But I can say, I'm really glad I have this little device in my car along for the ride. It's great for someone who is disabled, and I can only imagine that it will keep getting better.

👸My house is, and will probably forever be, owned by Alexa!👸
First, let me say, that I bought the Echo 2nd Generation, and the Google Hub at the very same time, just to try them both out. And boy, I could not send that Google Hub back to where it came from fast enough! It may be great for smart home only users, but it is no fun or really that useful, other than that, at all! You cannot even get answers or videos that come even close to what Google gives you on your cell phone!! And, it is not for the sight impaired- meaning me. If I needed to know the time after 6pm, I asked Alexa. I don't get it...
And, oh yeah baby! I love lyric mode on this thing! This bad boy can rock your booty off, for sure! The bass vibrates everything on my kitchen counter! I love it!!
I call mine Alexxx sometimes... it answers, most of the time, no matter which name- Alexa or Alexxx. I do wish it had a man's voice, sometimes.... really could use hearing one once in a while! It's kinda funny, sometimes, I just get ignored- similar to a man lol. Like, when I asked her to repeat the same song for the tenth time. Or, she will just decide that I need to listen to a certain playlist, instead of said song. It's annoying, but sometimes the first song is so good, it gets me to listen. Still... If I say play this song, and she says, I'll play "this" instead, it's rude!
Another thing I absolutely love, is watching YouTube. I've saved my Channel to the homepage in the Silk Browser, so all I have to do is just tell it to open YouTube. It goes straight to my homepage. I can go to or watch my subscription feed and playlists, go to my watched history, watch recommended videos, and easily search for anything I would like to watch. It is so quick and easy to navigate! My most favorite thing to watch, is Criminal trials, and they last for weeks. So, while I'm working in the kitchen doing other things, or just sitting around the table, I can pick up where I left off on my Fire Stick, and watch them right there on my echo.
I can search the internet for anything! I can type it in, or make it even faster by using my voice and just hitting the enter key on the onscreen keyboard.
I've heard a lot of people complain that there are too many steps to do things on the Echo. But, I can get to anywhere on mine almost as quickly as I can on my regular computer.
I hate to say that I haven't ventured out into the many, many things this thing can do, other than these few things, but they're the ones that I enjoy. One day, I'll try venturing out into unchartered territory for myself on this lovely device.
I know I can tell you one thing is for certain. I will definitely be buying more of these wonderful, booty shaking, singing to the top of my lungs, mind blowing gadgets very soon! I just have to have them in several rooms! I highly, highly, highly recommend the Echo 2nd Generation to everyone! REALLY, EVERYONE!!

From this Fire TV Stick, to the other two Fire TV Sticks, to the Echo Dot 2nd Generation, to the 2 Echo Speaker 2nd Generations, to the Echo Show 2nd Generation and to the Echo Auto's we own.... Well, I'd say we love all things Alexa!!
The best thing about this Fire TV Stick is the remote having the volume buttons on it!! Now, I'm gonna have to replace my other ones with these!! I got this one for the grand kids room, so I just steel the remote when they aren't here.
I guess, as long as they keep making and selling these gadgets, I'll keep buying, using and recommending them!!

When I first got these, I had a problem with the left earpiece not having sound, and the sound that came from the right ear was very tinny. Customer service was absolutely wonderful to resolve this for me very quickly. Since then, the sound is great! I have really small ears and I do find them a bit too big, even with the smallest cover, which keeps me from wearing them as long as I'd like. I haven't actually tried them in wet conditions, so I can't speak to this, but they are very well made and seem like they will last a long time.
--Pros
*Even though I was worried about the earpieces not being switchable, because I am left eared, this has worked alright when I am driving. I just hang the left earpiece on my shirt and use it with my right hand to work the controls.
*Charging is very fast.
*A charge last quite a long time, especially if you only use them for calls. Even listening to music it last a long time.
*The sound is nice and loud with lots of bass for listening to music.
*Call sound quality is great, for me, and for the listening party.
*The are easy to keep up with, using the nice case that they came with. It slips right into my purse or other bag.
*Well made. Durable and made with quality materials.
---Cons
*The earpieces are too large for my ears, even with the smallest cover, and my ears start to hurt after a short time.
*The pieces that go around your ears is shaped in a way that the bottom pushes into the back of my ear, causing it to get very sore.
*They are a bit larger and heavier than I'd like them to be.
*It would be nice to have a small clip for when you are driving, so that you can clip it to your shirt, to be hands free.

Overall, these are great headphones. They need a little tweaking, especially on the earpieces to make them more comfortable on the ears, but I would still highly recommend them.

I had the old flat tv wall mount for my 40 inch tv and always had a problem with the sun's glare coming through the window if the curtains were open. I'm disabled and am home much of the time and watch or listen to the tv quite a bit, so being able to look outside was something I was really missing. I was constantly opening and closing the curtains if I actually wanted to see the tv.
This year I bought a larger tv and wanted to have a mount that could tilt to a degree that I would be able to open my curtains and watch tv without glare. This one works great. It doesn't tilt and turn a whole lot, but it is perfect for my small living room area, so that everyone can see the tv without any distortions. And, I can enjoy both tv and watching the outside world. I love it!!
My son had the old one down and the new one up in a matter of less than half an hour. And, the tv went on just as it was suppose to. The holes lined up perfect and there was no need for any rigging or adjusting to force it to work. The holes are the exact measurements as listed.
Also, I bought it out of the Amazon Warehouse, and it came in perfect working condition, with all the parts that it was supposed to have. This was huge plus for my budget and I feel a great deal for such a nice mount.
I recommend this mount! I love being able to finally have my curtains open during the day while I watch tv.

I've had the TCL Roku 40" TV for several years, and still do. But, my eyesight is getting worse, so I wanted a bigger screen for my living room. I have Spectrum, and this is one of the few brands that offer their app, but I have actually loved my other one so much, that that wasn't a deciding factor.

Have both the 10x42 and their 12x42 binoteck brand binos. This review is for the 10x42. For the price point, these are very good binos for reqular use between me any my kids. TBH, when compared to their 12x42, they seems identical. The 10x42 is slightly less than 10 power, but extremely close, compared to my other name brand binos.

Kids are hard on binos (dropping, touchy, etc.) and they have held up well in the past week we have used them. The texture on the binos have a solid grip and it would be hard to have them slip out of your hands, even with gloves on. Compared to more expensive binos, I am very impressed by this product.

I find that prism binos are much easier on my eyes and these fit the bill. For well lighted conditions, the images are crisp and clear. These are ok for lower light conditions but if that is important to you, then you are easily going to be paying LOTS more for a named-brand binos to get the extra clarity/crispness needed in those conditions. This was a balancing act and it worked for my purposes. I can keep a pair in the truck and not worry about them being stolen.
For the price you cannot beat it.  The quality is good and the mic does cut back on the background noise a good bit.

I use these binos when hunting or at the range or just whenever I need to get a closer look at something. At 200 yards I can easily tell where I hit the target with 30+ caliber and barely with the 25/243 caliber..but not 22 or 17 calibers at that range (100yards no problem though in well lighted conditions). Seeing 125lb game up to 1000 yards isn't a problem at all but I make it a rule not to shoot past 400 yards so these binos defanitely fit the bill. I do often use this in combination with my Simmons 20-60x60 spotting scope when at the range/prairie.

Per dimensions/weight: they are relatively light although I do recommend the shoulder straps for added comfort when wearing them all day long. They fit perfectly in my hands and not too bulky considering them being 10x42 binos and not 10x50.

I currently have Tasco 10x40 and had a Nikon Monarch ATB (lost them somehow) and all I can say is that the clarity in these binos are excellent, even in lower light conditions, worlds better than my Tasco and about the same as the Nikon.

Try a pair...Keep in mind they are Redfield is now owned by Leoupold and the quality you get for under $150 (I paid $139.99 on amazon) is a real bargain.

First let me get the positive out of the way. Very easy to assemble, sturdy, and I like the fact that I can secure the TV on the wall by the top as well as pop it free by unlocking the unit by pulling the two chains s on the bottom. It was very easy to assemble, and I like the fact that they gave you a leveler to make sure its straight. The images I posted is a 75-inch TV, the maximum it can hold is apparently an 80. However, the bigger you go, the harder it gets to reach behind the back to tilt it. There is still 2 1/2 space to run wires and reach around to turn the knob to tilt it forward or backwards.

Now the CON.

I was not planning on tilting this unit forward or backwards because it's a big tv. For those looking for a decent mount and plan on doing the exact same thing having it flat, with a little space behind it so that you can reach around and run the wires the two inches and a half for me of space was perfect. I secured the tilting mechanism to keep it facing forward. which are the two metal knobs as you see in my second uploaded image as well as Amazon's version in the photos. I figured that since it had two turning knobs it was the same as the previous one I owned that had a spinning knob that went forward unlock, and backwards lock. I installed some LED lights on the back of the TV and hung it on the mount 1 month later. However I decided to remove the LED lights on the unit without taking the whole TV off the wall because I can easily take those off by just pulling the lights off.

This is where the problem started and noticed the manufacturing or designer error, hopefully they can correct it in the future. When I pulled the LED off, it tilted the TV slightly upwards, no idea why when it was apparently secured facing forward when I tried reaching around to the side to turn the nob I noticed the little ball fell out of the turning metal nob. The ball that goes into the metal unit was super glued on and it's not a turning ball where you can put it in there, screw in to permanently secure it in place to metal rod.

This created a problem when I wanted to tilt the TV forward, I had to move the metal rod because now the ball fell off it and it could not be attached again because it was held in place by super glue when you turn the knob, the whole unit would slide through falling off. Also if you notice in the picture, it's three separate parts. Not only was the metal rod with the ball superglued on but the unit that you used to turn in place unscrews off because there's no resistance or warning mechanism when you're turning the knob you don't know which way to turn to tilt it.

Since I was trying to figure out which way to make it go forward and backwards I realized that the whole unit was unscrewing because I could keep turning it in a direction until the whole metal rod as well as the screw / nob came completely off. This means that I now had to reattach it back to the unit screw it back in as well as dealing with the ball that had fallen off the stick. I ended up just removing both of them and physically moving the TV by hand forward and upwards luckily it didn't require a lot of force and it must have been slightly loose.

Regardless of all that I would still recommend the unit. It is sturdy it's nice and I like the adequate space behind it or I can reach around the problem is that if you have a big TV and you plan on constantly tilting it forward and backwards before attaching it on the wall. it's probably better for you to tilt the TV and then attach it to the wall because reaching around the 75 inch TV it's a little bit more difficult easier to run a wire because you have more than enough space but harder if you want to reach the handle to tilt it forward and backwards.

Also in the setup video instructions, it's simply rotates the nob without saying counterclockwise lock, counterclockwise relock etc etc. There's also no resistance mechanism that would tell you it can't go forward. So what ends up happening is that you can unscrew the whole nob bar off by mistake leaving the screw on the mount and nob in your hand. Hopefully in a future revision. They use a ball screw to the nob vs super glue it and possibly secure the metal bar to the unit to where it can't be unscrewed off. But I think the best thing to do is it just properly aligned with television to your seating position and set it up like normal straight to avoid having to use the tilting mechanism.

I purchased this mid range one (TXNR797), instead of the higher end one was due to my set up. My old Onkyo was an introductory model that was 75 watts x 5.2.2 bought at the end of 2016 (5 speakers, 2 Dolby upwards firing speaker for Atmos and 2 sub-woofer outputs the .2) Upgraded to this receiver which is a 9.2 receiver that is 100x the channel, with THX mode for gaming, movie etc but also has more power and more room layout variation giving me room to add on and alter or audio in other rooms.

My home layout is 5.1.2 but I plan on adding 2 extra Dolby upward firing speakers behind making it a 5.1.4.

NOW THE REVIEW:

100 x the channel (each speaker), more than enough. My previous Onkyo I bought was a basic model that had Atmos and sounded great, but after I year I decided to go at least 100 per channel. With this one, due having more power at higher volumes, it sounds extremely clean and distortion free. I primarily use this for gaming on PS4 and movies (disk) in 4k/Atmos sound etc I do stream Hulu/Amazon etc but sound quality in those tend to be compressed and even they sounded decent.

For gamers, they do have a dedicated equalizer for action, RPG, stadium etc and various movie tweeks like THX gaming, THX film and THX music. I wanted to address something first. Auto calibration systems in receivers can be off (most are not perfect and sounds does reflects throwing the auto-calibrating system off) its recommended for you to adjust based on how everything sounds in the room to your own preference. What I do is auto calibrate first for distance, if distance comes out correct than adjust the "gains" in the receiver settings (the volume each speakers) Some systems put the volume lower, which makes it harder for sound to reach the ear. Most room set-ups use a microphone and the mic might be overly sensitive and set the gains (volume) lower.

If you hear the effect or the extra layer of sound, you're done.

You may want to increase it higher in case the receiver sets the volume lower. Just take into account Atmos is an extra layer of sound, its meant to be atmospheric, with the occasional raining down effect of a film combined with back and front speakers creating a sound bubble. The extra layer of sound can be hear by simply switching 5.1 and back to 5.1.2 in the receiver in a film that supports it. Sometimes things are recorded as objects. Its not all a rain down effect.

Most, if not all 4k films are remixed in Atmos or DTS X, with some blue-rays non 4k films having it included (Most the times its the standard audio set up for 7 speakers) but receivers that support Atmos and DTS X have an up-converter, which simulates the effect and can be heard, just remember that films encoded for it obviously sound better.

5.1 sound an higher will still be up converted in the receiver, even if the sound playing lacks the Atmos or DTS X encoding. All my games and older films have an extra layer of sound, filling the room that even my own father noticed it was crystal clear (from the smallest bullet, to the effects or basic front sounds).

What I would recommend, play the test tone in the receiver after the auto-calibration. Some default to higher sounds pitch, others, you can increase the volume to what you normally set it to, as the test tone plays adjust + or - of the individual speaker. Increase or lower based off your own personal preference, but allow it to match the other speakers test tone pitch. Don't over drive it. Some prefer a slightly higher pitch for Atmos speakers. In my set up, its increased to +3 vs +1. Even in audio forums some suggested to set it higher 2-3 from the default set up. Remember, if the default sounds fine, than you're done. But never hurts to tinker with it.

Take into consideration that the Atmos speakers are not always 100% on, it's based off how the film was recorded. When I use the basic up-converter on the receiver from non Atmos/DTS X encoding it tends to be more active because its creating a simulation from a non encoded sound file. Try NOT to be far away from the main speakers, or have a massive vaulted ceilings. If you have vaulted ceilings, its better to hang them on the wall aimed down, and turning the receiver into 'height channel' vs Dolby speakers. Its a speaker set up that directs the speaker into the seating area vs up and down. The receiver will than auto adjust itself.

OUT OF THE BOX:

First thing I did was connect the TV to the internet and download any software update before calibrating.The people having issues connecting to the internet, just restart the modem. I had similar issues, but after restarting the cable mode (if using cable) fixed my connection problem. It's the same as when you add a new wireless router, you always have to restart the modem and router. The TV would not connect to the internet even when I used a wired connection. UNTIL I restarted the cable modem -Then instantly connected.

At boot up, the picture settings were basic running on factory default options and having light sensor which fluctuated the colors and brightness since it adjusted based off room lighting.My main room is dark in bright days, but the left side of the room has a door with a mini window that lets light in. (Incase I have all blinds closed) I opened all my blinds letting light in from every angle (right and left walls have a wide window the size of the walls) So its massive amount of outdoor light and the TV performed well. Calibration:

After switching picture modes. I disabled the light sensor that adjust the TVs brightness automatically and any power save modes that affect picture. (This is where some of the Amazon reviews are saying it's dark or cloudy out of the box.) You are trying to calibrate something that keeps shifting based on the light in the room. Shut them off before calibrating. Honestly, some of these modes are not needed since the TV is not going anywhere and you have control of how much light comes in. It has a tendency to make the image darker and faded the less light there is.. Lets be honest here, you're buying a 70 inch screen, you want the image clear, bright, sharp and detailed. AUTO MODE: (Adjust itself based on light in the room), STANDARD: (ENERGY STAR) , USER: Create your own picture preference. DYNAMIC FIXED: Not user adjustable.

PERSONAL TIP:

if your not familiar with Onkyo receivers they use a setting called "Intellivolume" which many think is a power booster. Its really designed to bring all speakers to similar sound levels incase its recorded lower say like a music track, CD, DVD etc you can also adjust these individually threw the speaker settings. I used this at the beginning before an adjustments, but the sound was way to powerful until I found out its not a power booster. People online also were under that impression. Its meant to bring up lower volume settings on all speakers. This creates more sound, and you increase the physical volume less , but if you set your speakers to your own preference, using this on top of your settings might create distortion, or increase sound louder making things unbalanced or to loud.

One of the reason I don't use it anymore is because your subwoofer also increases. Setting the sub volume say at, +3 will sound like +6. I'm cautious since I have neighbors, and I have had cops being called. I own my home by the way (that much of a boost even with windows closed). The maximum I use Intellivolume is +3 since I set my subwoofer to +3 when using Intellivolume I drop it to -3 on the subwoofer volume control and +3 on the receivers Intellivolume to get the same subwoofer volume without it doubling in power. the speakers will get the Intellivolume boost of +3 but the sub will balance out. Its a personal preference. If you have "bright sensitive speakers" like my Refrence series Klipsch, Intellivolume can make the front speakers have a stronger presence than back speakers. Which is why I use mine lower or at 0 (reference level) and just increase the speakers by hand using + or - on the receiver or edit the on board equalizer. At first I was under the impression having Intellivolume on louder say +12 , I would benefit from having to increase the volume control less. +40 sounded perfect, but its the same as not having Intellivolume at 0 and just increase the sound threw the remote to level +60. Except it had less clipping and sounded more balanced with less bass from an already powerful subwoofer.

TIP: for many of those using receivers that do auto calibration. Its better to do yours subwoofer settings by hand and personal hearing preference. Many auto-calibration systems like Audyssey have a tendency to ask you to lower the subs volume on the unit and mutes the bass sound. This is normally done to adjust the speakers hertz frequency and measure the room but system like Audyssey do not take bass into account. So your speakers will probably get shifted to see itself as "large speakers" even if you have towers. This reduces overall bass tracks your subwoofer plays because it thinks the other speakers can reproduce low bass. To fix any lack of bass, change the hertz settings of each speaker at a starting point of 80hrz. This will feed the subwoofer bass tracks that the others speakers can not reproduce. Satellites speakers crank it up to 120hrz or more.

-LFE (low frequency effects) in your receiver settings to 120hrz. Sub crossover or LFE settings are in the receiver itself.
-all speaker herz settings to 80 or test by going higher. Some have a setting for small and large Set them small even if you have towers unless they have powered subs built into them.(this is normally in the settings of the speakers in the receiver) Not the sub itself.

This allows your receiver to control where bass gets redirected. If you set the receiver to control every speaker, you would disable similar settings on the subwoofer itself, That way you don't get the sub and receiver having a double filter effect. The only thing you raise up and down would be the subs volume control and equalizer settings IN THE SUB. I avoid lowering and increase sub volume from the receiver , instead ,do it by hand on the unit.

I have been using this with my computer, laser printer, router, broad band internet connection and TV, and it seems to be working fine. The gadget is equipped with a right-angle plug that helps keep the cord close to the wall. The Product Dimensions is 15 x 7 x 2 inches and it weighs about 2.2 pounds. I am satisfied with this purchase and it is recommended.

I love this case that holds my Acer Chromebook perfectly. The case has two main pockets; the main pocket holds the Chromebook and the smaller side pocket is great for storing power cable and wireless mouse.

This case features a protective padding on the inside and reinforced stiffening that is ideal for absorbing impact. The bag is lightweight, very well made, and great for travelling. It also comes with a cute retractable carrying handle and an optional shoulder strap.

The air-protect feature of the bag allows you to work directly with the Chromebook sitting in the bag; this makes it is easier when you are working in a minimal space such as a classroom. The bag is also equipped with a non-slip EVA molded base that help elevates the Chromebook and the tilt-back design that allows for all screen positioning angles. I am very satisfied with this product and I have rated this bag five stars for design, durability and overall satisfaction.

These are great looking speakers that simply plug into the USB ports on my laptop. The design is great and the quality of the sound is good (RMS Power is 3W; 1.5 per speaker). They don't need any other installation discs and it is powered by USB connection. The volume control is fine with On/Standby options; it is very portable and very sturdy. I have rated four stars for this product for its design and quality.

I have too many gadgets which I use simultaneously; laptop, Kindle, Chrome book, TV, lamps, etc., hence I needed to purchase this equipment. It connects up to six power sensitive devices at one time. This is a simple and economical solution. It is sturdy, good quality and reasonably priced. In fact I bought three units; one for my office, two for my living room and bedroom. It is working pretty well for the last six weeks, it plugs and don't jam in slots and the LED light is a nice feature, which tells you that outlet is on. The devise also protects up to 900 joules of power surge. Highly recommended!

This is a good quality USB 3.0 cable which I use for connecting my desktop to USB 3.0 enabled printer and it works effortlessly. The cable is pretty long, almost 10 feet, and transfers data at fast speed of 4.8 Gigabytes per second, almost 10 times the speed of USB 2.0 connectors. This USB 3.0 is also compatible with USB 2.0 (this cable may be used with devises that has USB 2.0 connector). It works fine except the speed of data transfer is relatively slow.

The USB 3.0 cable has two paths; one to receive data and the other to transmit, while USB 2.0 handles only one direction of data at any time. USB 3.0 also provides more power to devices that require higher amounts of power to operate. Highly recommend this to anyone who likes a long USB cable.

I have been using this for the past one week and it works great. This power unit charges three to four times as fast as via USB connection to your computer/laptop. It doesn't have a polarized plug and therefore can be plugged-in with the USB port. If you are not a regular user of Amazon Kindle, then you don't need this PowerFast charger, trickle charging using your computer would be just fine. Regarding the price, when you order with Kindle it is $9.99. If you order separately it is $19.99. This is something you may need to consider. Some reviewers have complained that this is a bad design, and it is difficult to connect to USB. I did not have any problems using this and it is just fine.
