These are astonishingly good. They’re a big investment, but they are worth it and and once you wear them a few times they feel comfortable.
I also loved the way Apple has a fit guide you can access through the settings on your iPhone or iPad.
It’s quick, easy and made all the difference in how well these work for me.

As much as I adore these and I’m happy to have bought them, I am dismayed by the fact that they only last 4 1/2 hours. As someone who has a very loud air conditioner, 4 1/2 hours is not enough time for me to sleep without the noise.

I really like these and the price is fantastic. The design is excellent, comfortable, and attractive. Even the case is pleasing.
They paired up with my iPhone instantaneously without any glitches.
Frankly, I would give them five stars for all of that, but I really only give them one or two stars for noise canceling. They did not block out the sound of the birds in the background and I was disappointed by that.
Nor did they even block out the low hum of my air conditioner.

These are great.
They aren’t billed as noise cancelling, so I didn’t expect that to be a feature.
Incredibly priced for good quality sound, ease of use, and very sensitive touch control.
I listened to music and spoken word. Both sounded very clear and good.

For comparison’s sake, I also have Apple AirPods. They fit me perfectly, but they can also fall out.
I think these will stay in, but when I first tried them they felt less secure than the AirPods.

If anything changes I will update this review.
In the meantime, I think they’re a great, inexpensive alternative to super pricey options.

I took one star away as they wouldn't pair with my iPad (a newer version), only my iPhone 7.

This is a very attractive iPad case, however, I wish it weighed a few ounces less. I immediately noticed it was heavier than my previous iPad 4 case made by ProCase.
Sadly, while I liked the lighter weight of that one, it was a dirt and lint magnet.
This fit my iPad Air 4 just fine and the volume buttons work perfectly.
It feels durable and the cost is reasonable.
If my experience changes I will update my review.

It’s very helpful to have this small, well made adaptor.
I will use it with my new iPhone and old wired noise cancelling earbuds.
Also helpful for connecting aux from older model Bose radio to new iPhone or iPad Air.

These attractive black earbuds and charging case are nicely presented with a small pouch, charging cord and 5 sets of rubber ear tips in a variety of sizes. The instructions provided were clear, and it was easy to sync to my iPhone. I received good, clear audio immediately. However, the pods are very sensitive and respond to the slightest movement, which resulted in disconnecting a call. This does not seem to be a problem with other audio. Accordingly, it appears that I still need to get better acquainted with the product, but I am satisfied.

I could not get these to charge. Asked the question of the Amazon community and the actual company but received no help.
Also, they wouldn't pair with my iPhone.
Very disappointed.

Update:
The directions are written in a type face that only a mouse could read.
I kept trying a lot of different intuitive ways of pairing these to my iPhone and finally got them to work.
When I see a little red lights on earbuds I assume they’re not charged. Silly me.
They’re red in the case and when you take them out they randomly flash white.
When I paired them with my iPhone Bluetooth they seemed not to be pairing, until I clicked on the BASEUS name.

If I compare them to my Apple AirPods, they don’t have the same sound quality for speech, nor volume capacity; however, they’re perfectly fine once you figure out how to get them going.

After all that, I really do like that design and the case.

Perhaps you’re all far more tech savvy than I am and this would be intuitive to you. Sadly, it was not to me and the directions did not help.

Great little adapter for using my wired headphones with newer devices, like iPhone 7 and beyond.
The sound was clear and strong.
I have some wired noise cancelling ear buds and I wanted to enjoy their benefits, as Air Pods don't afford the same level of noise cancelling. This nifty little adapter was all I needed.

I love this hand crank radio. I have had other ones made by Eton, a very reputable company. What I like about this is it’s extremely compact, the variety of lighting options is incredible, and it hardly requires any cranking to charge it up.

There are four little blue lights that show you how to charged the battery is, 25% 50% 75% or over 75%. I got it to four blue lights, the maximum, with two minutes of cranking, very little effort.

It has two types of connectors for your phone or iPad. One is for older models and one looks to be a lightning connector.

The unit itself is lightweight, compact and attractive.

You can charge it with solar, through the cable, with the hand crank, or using a lithium battery.

Though I might have liked a carrying case, it would have added to the cost and I would prefer to save the money. So, I think they made a good decision not including it.

It charged my phone quite quickly.

All in all, a wonderfully useful item to have in your car and home.

I bought one of these years and years ago and it still works perfectly. The only suggestion I would have is that they increase the amplification ability of the speaker as the volume is not always as high as I would like it to be. I do not put this under my pillow but next to the pillow or on top of the pillow next to my ear. Both seem to work quite well. If I put it under the pillow the volume is too low to be effective.

This soundbar is excellent! It's lightweight, low-profile, and easy to set up. I am not very tech-savvy when it comes to hardware, but the directions to connect it to my new Roku Smart TV were clear and easy to follow, and now my soundbar turns on and off with my TV, so I only need to use one remote.

I love the bluetooth feature so I can play music on the soundbar using the Spotify app on my phone or computer. I can't tell a huge difference between modes, like cinema and music, but everything sounds good to my untrained ears. I recommend it!

Yes, this is a great product in terms of quality and design; however, it didn't fit my iPad Air 2 so the volume buttons were in the right space. Also, I would not call it lightweight, more like medium weight.

Bose SoundTouch 10 is an excellent system that enables you to have music, podcasts, and audiobooks available at the press of a button in any room with wifi.

The sleek black design is compatible with almost all decors, and is small enough to hide in a corner.

You can access your content via preset buttons on the top of the device or by using the remote.

Set up was easy at first and then got complicated because my PC was connected to the internet both through wifi and cable. Clearly, the cable was unnecessary, but I didn't know that. You only need one connection. I initially set up the system through my ipad air which was intuitive and only took about 10-15 minutes. The reason I had to contact customer support was I wanted to sync my iTunes library to the Bose SoundTouch. The person I spoke with was patient, knowledgeable, and solved the problem. (And, waiting for tech support only took about a minute.)

I tried the sound qulaity with both classical music and PBS news. The music sounded resonant and rich and had plenty of volume. The speech was clear and easy to understand.

NOTE: Day two. Apparently, my iTunes library is so vast (17,000 items) that it was hard to keep it synched with the Bose system. I could have synched it through Bluetooth, but that meant having to remember to Bluetooth on and off via my desktop, and I use the sound on that all the time; so, it wasn't a viable option. Another idea would be to spend $80 for a NAS drive but that didn't appeal to me, either. I will buy the 3.5mm male to male cable so I can attach my ipod directly to the speaker. It will do the trick, but is not the seamless experience I was hoping for.

I can still listen to radio stations from around the world, i Heart Radio, Pandora, and anything that's downloaded through iTunes on my ipad.

This is a great product if you use it with Bluetooth, or don't have an extensive iTunes library to sync.

I hope to have it as long as I have had my Bose radio, which is more years than I can remember.

These are an incredible deal at under $30.
I have tried a wide variety of noise-cancelling ear buds over the years, including some pricey ones. This inexpensive set works at least as well, if not better, than some of them.
They cancel out background noise and deliver a high quality, appealing sound. Whether I am listening to spoken word or music, everything sounds clear and rich.
I recently was on four planes and in four loud airports. These ear buds beautifully cancelled out the background noise, making the whole experience far more pleasant.
The volume has a wide range. So, you can adjust from a whisper to a very loud decibel. This may seem like no big deal, but many other noise-cancelling ear buds do not deliver this range of volume. It may not matter at home, but on a loud plane you want the ability to really amp up the sound.
The come with six sets of attachments for any ear configuration and preference. For me, the ones that were already attached were perfect.
I bought the black, which is really a dark brownish-black wood grain. Very attractive and lightweight.
I especially appreciate the flexible woven cord, rather than a heavy plastic/rubber on other brands. This lightness and flexibility makes them less intrusive on your body.

I like these. The bass is excellent, there is a really wide volume range, and they are lightweight.
In addition, the headphones sit comfortably on your head.

I tried them with a wide variety of music, from classical, to kirtan, to rock, to folk---all sounded very good.
I also sampled my current audiobook (Nora Webster) and it came through beautifully.

Bought this for the Yamaha R-S500BL Natural Sound Stereo Receiver and could not be more pleased.
My last Yamaha receiver lasted over 30 years.

I have owned this product for about 2 years, and I think it delivers excellent quality sound. It's especially good for music, and my ipod sounds just as good on it as it does on the Bose speakers. Mostly, I use it for TV where it enhanced the experience ten fold.

The look is sleek and contemporary, and it was easy to set up.

Even more than those accolades, I want anyone who purchases a ZVOX product to know that their customer service is beyond compare. My remote stopped working the other day and they immediately sent me a replacement at no charge.

This new solar powered speaker system has been carefully designed by the innovative people at Eton. (I have happily owned one of their hand crank radios with phone charger for years.)

The shape is aesthetically pleasing, the solar panel moves seamlessly on its hinge, the handle has been incorporated into the design, there's a space with a wide elastic band to hold your phone or smaller ipod in place, and it is lightweight.

As for the sound, I played all sorts of music: jazz, classical, rock, country, new age, Latin, and everything sounded great, provided I pressed the bass button. I even tried spoken word podcasts and they were clear as a bell. Vocals were extraordinarily good and life-like.

The volume went all the way up to loud when on full capacity, but not to an excruciatingly high decibel level.

If you are using an iPod you will need a male to male cable. Remember to press the "aux" button or you won't get any sound.

One more thing, don't press the bass button for audio books as they sounded clearer without it.
I liked the 75 watts of power, the bass control, and the bass sound.  While I bought a ZVOX sound bar for my TV, I would recommend this for smaller applications, or smaller rooms.

I am a fan of these; however, I prefer a slightly warmer sound, hence the four star rating and not five. Their sound is truly crystal clear which, if you are using them with a phone, is desirable.
My other great earbuds from Sennheiser came with a very easy to use pouch for storage. The case included with this set is awkwardly designed and not user-friendly.

I like having the controls on the wire, as opposed to having to access your device for loudness, track shuffling, etc. These have a chic little controller in a very convenient place, at about neck level.

You may want to also check out TDK EB900 High Fidelity In Ear Headphones.

These are not inexpensive, but they deliver a great, warm, rich sound with wonderful bass.
It's interesting to me how much each different set of ear buds produces quite varying levels of sound. These have a lot of volume power, which makes them a wonderful choice for any noisy area, like airports or planes.
I found them a little large in size, but comfortable.
The cord is thicker than other ear bud cords I have used, but still lightweight.
I would have liked an online volume control, but t's minor complaint.
They successfully cancelled out most ambient noise.
When I compared them to TDK, Sennheiser, and Ultimate Ears, they produced the most appealing sound.

OK, I still love my old Bose CD player, and with an aux cable I can use it for my ipod; but, I didn't want to shell out that much money for another one so I bought this JBL.  It works very well and the remote is a great little feature.  I had an Altec Lansing that I loved, but it developed crackling sound issues after a couple of years.  This has been good for the few  months I've owned it.

If you want a cassette recorder for making voice notes or creative ideas this is it. The sound quality is fantastic. There is no static or hissing on the tapes when I play my voice back. A plus is the size and portability of the device.

Like other people I tried to use a digital voice recorder, but was thrown off by the different buttons and multiple features for each button. And if I didn't use it for a few days I'd have to relearn how to operate it. There had to be an easier way. So here I am with a Walkman cassette recorder in 2023.

The radio comes in clearly and recorded songs sound good. I couldn't be happier.
The sound quality is excellent. The volume is louder than expected. The look is retro.
The sound is clear with bass and the volume is better than most pocket radios. I'd buy it again.

This dsl filter made a huge difference with the sound quality of my Western Bell 500 Rotary phones. I use Xfinity for my home phone. My modern phone sounded fine, but my classic phones had static. I plugged the pulse to tone converter directly into the modem (you have to purchase that separately if you can't dial out using your digital phone service). Then I plugged the dsl filter into the pulse to tone converter. Next I plugged the phone cord into the dsl filter. I'm able to both dial out and make clear calls. My phones are 54 and 65 years old and they work better than most brand new phones thanks to this product.  Don't give up on your rotary phone. Try this product first.

I've had two other brands of video cameras in the past couple years, and each had something about them that had me keeping my eye out for another to try. I can happily say this is better than either of those (bigger name brand) cameras and this is the one I've been using and will continue to use. Initially I was having issues getting the micro SD card to work as it would say it formatted but wouldn't let me access it. After trying for quite some time (it was working with my other camera) I tried a different kind of micro SD card and it has been working fine since. I primarily use for continuous loop recording so if needed I can go back and review and/or save if necessary. This works great for that, and the bigger the memory card, the longer the "loop" you can record. This is also nice because I don't have to subscribe to cloud storage to be able to use this. Video quality is good, night vision works well, and the detection features make using this easier as well (I use the human detector primarily as it makes it easier to go back when reviewing as it marks/timestamps the video playback when it recognizes a person). The tilt/pan is great if using a one-camera setup, though I honestly don't trust it when using in conjunction with the tracking feature as the time I left it going it had locked itself onto filming the wall and I didn't notice until later. If it works better than that normally it could certainly be a nice feature. Glad I got this one and so far is working well and has everything I need for a camera!

As fewer phones have a 3.5mm jack these days, these are almost a necessity (for me anyhow). Braided cord has some stiffness so should protect the wire inside somewhat. Sounds good, I get no static and it is a tight fit on both the 3.5mm and USB C ends. Does exactly what I had hoped, and is something that I might end up getting a couple of, as I always have a need on one device or another. Perfect!

These really are great. The silicone tips that the Buds Pro ships with seem to fall out regardless of the size, and just don't feel as secure. These (while a bit tricky putting on the first time) when in place on the buds, don't fall out whatsoever. For that reason they are much better if sweaty or if moving around. The ANC really shines with these on as with the silicone tips a ton of noise still gets through. With these, while audio is playing I can't hear much which is awesome! This also means you can keep the volume lower which is much better for your hearing. Highly recommended, and I hope they hold up. If not (assuming it's longer than a month) I'll definitely get some more!

So glad I bought these as they are much better than the ones that come with the earbuds. Extremely comfortable and don't fall out like the originals did (regardless of the size I used). Cancels noise so much better as well! Very happy with them!
Exactly what I needed.  Charges EVERYTHING that requires a charger for me.
They don't have noise cancelling capability but work extremely well.  Sound quality is excellent.

This projector was easy to setup right out of the box.  All the connections and remote are included.  The WiFi connection took a few minutes.  The picture clarity was more than I expected; very clear and bright.  It made the perfect Christmas gift.

Nice wireless keyboard. Easy instant plug and play and good signal connection. Keys press easily but provide nice resistance. Some clicking but isn't overly loud.
Mouse is small and comfortable.
It's a bit annoying that the mouse and keyboard run on a different size of battery (AA and AAA). No off switch either that I found so you have to remove the battery to preserve if you don't use it often.

This is my third Vimtag camera, and I am just as happy with it as I am with the rest. Very easy to set up (once I figured out how to split my wi-fi channel so I could access the 2.4gHz). Great quality picture and sound. I have it in my office, mostly to spy on my cats, but also because it is an easy place for those with nefarious purposes to possibly breach my perimeter. This camera gives me peace of mind with on-demand video. Storage subscription options are available for extra $.
My biggest complaint is the lack of instructions for use of the app. There are a lot of features but I've had to find them and figure them out mostly through trial and error, and several weren't what I thought they were. So additional usage info would have been extremely helpful.
But strictly speaking for the camera itself, I'm very pleased with it.

I ordered this in hopes of installing it into my older car.  I was hesitant as I didn't know much about cars.  Upon opening and reading the directions, I was pleasantly surprised with how easy it sounded to install.  First problem was that I didn't have a mini SD card. I see other reviews rated it favorably and I possibly would have too, had I been able to install it.  I have no experience with this type of thing, but it was suggested that expertise was not required.  It does state in the manual that professional installation is strongly suggested- I think I will follow that advice and see if I can get it professionally installed.  I will update my review when that happens.

This is literally plug in and go. Incredibly easy to set up. Was uploading photos from my phone in less than 5 minutes.
Beautiful frame. Very classy looking and the photo quality is great. I love that it auto rotates its orientation if you move it.
Companion app is easy to follow and easy to pair. I love that it notifies you if new photos are added from the app. And notifications and sounds are optional.
Will be giving this to my dad for a present...full of picture of my new pup. Its gonna be a hit for sure!

This is an interesting speaker. The flame is more like a disco light- bright and flashy-rather than a flame.
But it is fun and adds some great atmosphere to the room. After charging, it was easy to pair with my phone. The "Welcome" voice was a bit garbled, but the connected sound (music, books, etc) is thankfully clear. It has the options to manage the speaker on your phone, or has buttons on the speaker itself for volume.

It only seems appropriate that I am writing this review on the laptop. I really love this thing. I purchased myself a very expensive laptop just a few years ago. It is big, and it was supposed to have the 360 hinge, but when it arrived it did not. I almost returned it then but didn't want to go through the hassle. It's a great laptop, but it is big and heavy (comparatively), which is perfect when I have to buckle down and focus on work. But when I need something on the go or just want to do something while chilling, it is too much.
So when I saw this I was super excited. It loads up super fast, actually recognizes my fingerprint (most things won't) and has a good battery life. Touch screen is nice and sensitive. I will mostly be using it for basic internet, streaming movies, and maybe a little gaming. The graphic quality is great as is the sound for the size. I haven't tried any video editing on it yet, but I will be soon and am hopeful it will be up to the task. I think the only thing I'd really like would be one more USB port, but I'll just have to dig out my hub when I get to that point.
Bonus, it came with a bunch of stickers you can decorate it with. Not my thing personally, but a super cute idea.

First off, these came adorably packaged in their own little leather case. Made me reminiscent of my old CD cases but on a super small scale. Inside was a small "thank you" paper, the ear buds and extra silicone covers. They are surprisingly comfortable. I had no issues wearing them for hours. The controls on the cord worked fine. No issues there.
Plugged them right in and they have a hiss to them. Is that the noise cancellation? I don't know. I don't think so. It only made everything seem louder.
Ok, no problem, maybe that is just the static white noise energy of not having anything else. I've had a few other headphone sets like that-hissy until the music starts. Turned on an audio book. Nope, still hissy. It wasn't as noticeable while the audio book was playing, but it was there and I am now hyper fixated on the constant "hisssssssssssssss" of static in the background.
Sound quality was ok. Not as nice as some pairs I've had in the past, but not terrible. I can live with the quality.
But can I live with the hiss? The jury is still out on that.

I was hopeful I'd like these. Unfortunately I just don't.
They came partially charged so I was able to use them right away. They paired easily with my phone. They turn on and off easily with just a touch. They also charge quickly, and per the guide you can charge them about three times on one charge of the case.
But I find them incredibly uncomfortable. After just a few minutes the insides of my ears hurt. I also don't find that they are noise cancelling-maybe because they just don't fit my ears well?

Anyways, overall I found these disappointing. I'll be shopping for something else to try.
They are very good quality earbuds. I bought them for my wife as a Christmas gift. She really enjoys the sound quality. For the price, these earbuds are very good!
It responds with clarity and volume. I bought it to replace my first generation Echo device and I'm glad I bought it when I did.
So far no issues with this little gem. I do enjoy the bass boost. It has a speaker. The charger port is protected which you don't always find.

Installation was easy - fit and sound is definitely better than the OEM silicone tips. Time will tell how long they last, and how sweat resistant they are. If I have to replace these more than once a year, it will be disappointing. So far so good. Minus one star because it seems like they are just thrown in the box, which makes a variety pack a little confusing.

I have a 1100.00 top of the line Samsung sound bar for my main TV, and while this can’t compare, it sure gives it a run for the money.

I can’t believe the clarity of the center speaker and all the features you get for 220.00. The sub woofer is the only downside I see so far as it is a bit muddy when you increase the base or raise the sub levels much past 50%. Other than that, this thing fills up a small bedroom with sound you would expect from a much more expensive system.

It’s still early, but as of right now, I am a believer.

This is just an average monitor at a rock bottom price. If you are looking for a great monitor, this isn’t it. But for everyday work and simple gaming it fit my needs perfectly.

One caveat, the speakers are very tinny sounding and don’t have much volume. I would not use this monitor as your main source of sound. But for simple PC sound and the occasional YouTube videos it should be ok.

I went from 4GB to 8GB on a new install of Win 10 and there was a notable difference when working. I ran some tests with CPU-Z and found the memory performing optimally in dual channel mode, so this is the real deal.

The HP laptop these went into required removing the mother board! So I was real happy the thing booted up with no comparability issues. I would have hated to dissemble again. This was a good value for the money compared to other leading brands.

I have had way to may head sets and microphones. I also have a very expensive Yetti that I use for serious recording. But as far as headsets go, these are the est i have used so far. I have had way too many sets of headphones. Mostly because my dog eats them if they are within reach. While I still have not found the perfect headset with these, they come pretty close.

Durability and battery Life - Way too early to tell. I'll update this after a few months.

Noise Canceling- Let’s get something straight - if you put your fingers in your ears, they will cancel noise. That's called passive noise canceling, or simply, blocking outside noise. True active noise canceling head phones are over the ear, and usually very expensive. These head phones do a pretty good job passively blocking outside noise by fitting very well to the ear and being angled correctly.

Sound - Everyone has different tastes when it comes to what they like to hear. Some headphones have good or bad ranges from high to low. But it is the quality of the range that matters. I pre-ordered this product 6 months before it was released. Three different release dates came and went until finally it arrived at my door without notice. When I opened the Amazon box, I saw the first problem. Although I ordered it in black, I received a white one. I was replacing a white one so I figured, what the heck, let’s go with it. I opened it up, looked at the very sparse instructions, plugged it in and within a few minutes it was up and running. However I wanted to use this as an access point and not any of the other three options offered on the setup wizard. More on that later.

Prior to this arriving I would comb through the dozens of questions people posted on the pre order page. One of my favorites was repeated by several people, “Do I still need internet service if I get this”? OF COURSE YOU DO! That’s like asking if you still need food if you get a new refrigerator. If you are asking this question, I highly recommend you enlist a qualified professional to help you assess your needs and get you set up. With that out of the way, let’s get into what this little guy can do.

As Wireless Range Extender (Repeater):

Think of this as a relay race where one runner reaches a mark, hands off the baton to the next runner, who then takes it to the next mark. This assumes you already have the first runner and of course the baton. So to use this as a wireless repeater you need an existing internet connection and wireless router. You will put the Almond 3 somewhere in your house where you get a good wireless signal using any other device such as a smart phone, laptop or tablet. Check to see you have most of your bars on your device, find a wall plug and fire up the almond 3 and follow the on screen directions to set up a “Range Extender”. (The device is just for checking the signal, not for setting up the Almond 3) If you put the Almond 3 too far from your existing wireless router, you will have the same crappy wireless speed you do now. Only you will be confused because you will see you have all the bars on the device which will be coming from the Almond 3. Remember, the Almond is only handing off the same signal it gets. If the signal is bad, that’s what you will get. So keep the Almond 3 as close to the existing wireless router to the point where you just start losing bars on your devices. However don't put it too close to the existing wireless router, or the signals may compete with each other.

As A Wireless Router:

This assumes a few things. First, that you have an existing internet connection. Second, that you are comfortable replacing the main router in your house. This means you will be taking the internet connection from your provider, disconnecting and turning off the the main router and plugging this in its place. In the case of cable internet, you will have to at least have a cable modem from your provider. (NOTE: Only qualified network engineers would ever have two routers in one home). If you set up the Almond as a router and you already have a router, you will start experiencing all kinds of network issues up to and including completely crashing your network and internet connection. Once you have put this in place of your existing router, simply fire it up and follow the on screen wizard.

As A Mesh Network:

If you don’t know what a mesh network is, then do not attempt to try this. Just use one of the above choices. If you know what a mesh network it, simply fire up the Almond 3 and follow the on screen prompts.

As An Access Point:

Again, unless you know the difference between a router and an access point, you are better off choosing one of the first two configurations. To start with, an access point assumes you have an actual Ethernet cable coming from an existing router somewhere in the house. This could be next to the router, or anywhere in the house using a switch or a switched port on the main router. If you are already lost, stop here and choose one of the first two options. If you know what you are doing, then follow these steps. Connect the Almond as a router with your network cable in the WAN port. Configure the setup wizard as a router (its ok to do that for now). When you complete the setup, go to the home screen, select the MORE icon followed by the Access Point icon. Once that’s done you can set up the SSIDs the way you want. It’s unfortunate that Access Point is not an option at startup. It seems an obvious deficiency.

Once You Are Set UP:

Once you get through the first setup screens you get the option to configure the Almond trough an App on your phone. I would download the Almond App before you get started on any of the above options. That will make the final steps of the wizard go much easier. Follow all the prompts to configure the App. (NOTE: this does not connect your phone to your new wireless connection; it only connects the App for future use). Once you get your phone connected to the new wireless connection and get the App set up, you can configure some of the more frequently used options right from your phone. Also don’t forget to update the firmware by going into the setup icon from the device. Finally, make sure you password protect the Almond 3 display so no one can change you configuration.

The App:

The app is a great tool for many reasons. With the optional smart home dongle you can connect all sorts of devices to automate your home. But right out of the box, you can track your family coming and going using their smart phones as sensors. You can be alerted every time someone connects to your network. You can turn on a “guest” network when you have company. The guest network is segregated from your home network so you don’t have to worry about prying eyes on your other network devices. . I am not sure how much I trust this, but a quick test did in fact block traffic from the guest network to the rest of the house. Just make sure you remember to turn it off or your neighbors will be stealing your internet. Finally you can rename your wireless connection from the App for both the 2.4 and 5.7 MHz connections. I suggest using the same wireless name (SSID) and password for both. (NOTE: never name your wireless connection your real name).

The Range & Conclusion:

The range is outstanding! I have a full 5 bars everywhere in my house. My wireless speeds in my bedroom went from 10 to 15 Mbps to 65 – 70 Mbps. My wife is very happy about that. Happy wife, happy life. There is no perfect electronic device and this is no exception. I am using Samsung’s Smartthings for my smart home, so I may not ever get around to playing with that feature on the Almond 3, but one never knows. For the price, the features and performance of this device is far superior to anything I have seen on the market to date. It rivals some of the $800.00 Cisco Meraki enterprise wireless devices we use at work. The free App & cloud service is just icing on the cake.

Whether you are a network engineer or complete novice, most people should be able to get this to work if they select the right options at startup. I am very happy with this purchase and so far it was well worth the wait.

I am an IT person who has several high end machines both desktop and laptop with Haswell i7's and 16GB and 8GB of RAM respectively. The problem is my laptops are very big and weigh a ton. I wanted a laptop that was very small, lightweight, and portable and had a touchscreen. When I looked at the specks on this I wasn't expecting too much.

Upgrades:

First let me start by saying I am an IT professional and have been a audiophile and video hobbyist for many years. Naturally I have had a lot of different audio / video equipment over the years. I had a computer hooked up to my TV long before it was in fashion. And finally, I am always looking for the next great gadget on the market. Enter the Harmony 900.

Here is my current setup in my living room:
Samsung TV HL-T5687
Sony PS3 Move
Nyko IR Adaptor for PS3 - Media Hub Slim
Roku2 XS
Onkyo TX-NR808
Sharp DVDR-VCR DV-RW340
Cable Box Motorola DVR DCH-3416
Shuttle PC with Media Center
X10 Home Automation - Various Devices

I basically use my TV as a monitor, the only cable plugged into it is the HDMI from the receiver. Hence, the Onkyo receiver does all the sound and switching between inputs.

The Harmony 900 Experience:

I did a lot of research before buying this $250.00 remote. Considering this thing is 50.00 more that my Kindle Fire and does a whole lot less, it wasn't easy pulling the trigger.

Ergonomics:
I read the good and bad reviews and decided that this one would best fit my needs. From many of the negative reviews I concluded the biggest concern was going to be dropping it and breaking the screen. It becomes very obvious why this is the minute you put it in your hand. It is very sleek and conforms well to your hand, but is as a slippery as a fresh water eel in your hand. Also due to the few contact points with any surface other than the charger, it is very easy to slide off a couch arm or get bumped off a coffee table.

That being said, the remote is very well balanced and fits nicely in the hand. The buttons are raised and easy to push. However some of the buttons are simply in the wrong spot. The volume and channel buttons should be reversed and the "Menu" button should be located down further on the remote. The fast forward and skip buttons are perfectly positioned and the skip buttons have a notable bump on them to differentiate between the two.

The screen is actually better than I thought it would be. I can make out the display with or without my (fulltime) glasses. On the down side, it is very easy to tap on the wrong display icon when moving left and right through the screens. When this happens, depending on what you accidentally pressed, it takes a while to recover and get back to what you were watching. Some things may have turned on or off and if you weren't pointing in the right direction during the errant tap, good luck getting everything synced again.

Device Support:

The Harmony 900 claims thousands of supported devices. But good luck finding some of them. Instead of having a simple model number look up, you first have to choose the type of type of device, then the manufacturer followed by the model number. The problem is some devices are not listed in the device type or seem to be randomly added to device types you would not expect them in. There is an example in the set section below.

One thing clearly missing is a simple list of all the devices. In some cases like the X-10 IR interface module listed in many of these reviews, it is no longer available. It would be great to just enter X-10 and see every device that was compatible so you could buy the right one as an interface with the Harmony. There is no way to do this. This is a glaring omission that seems very simple to correct. Heck, a downloadable PDF would be better than nothing.

But all that said, I found every device in my house in their database and I had some fairly obscure AV stuff. And as long as the device is IR, you can custom map from any remote to the Harmony, so there really isn't any IR that cant work.

Setup:

Now I wasn't bragging when I said I was an IT professional. I simply mentioned this fact so those who are technically challenged have a baseline to consider when evaluating their ability to use and set up this device. I have built servers, computers, configured high end routers and switches and oversee hundreds of devices in several locations. And it always amazes me when I get a new piece of equipment like this, how frustrated I can get in the first few minutes of using it.

As others have mentioned, you have to install the software and set up an account to use the device. All settings are done interactively and in real time through the internet. If you don't have an internet connection, don't bother with this remote. I did not use the CD but instead downloaded the latest version from the Logitech web site. I also pre downloaded the owners manual several days before the remote arrived and read it cover to cover. So by the time I had it in my hand I was fairly comfortable with how the setup process should work. The software and driver installation was very easy and there were no USB connection problems to the remote. So far painless!

After letting the remote charge for a couple of hours I started through the setup process. I had used my own version of their worksheet and had all the devices written down. The first thing to note, again as other have mentioned is the Sony PS3 requires an add-on device to translate the IR to the Sony's native RF. Although Logitech sells such a device for almost 100.00, I already had a Nyko Media Hub for the PS3. It doesn't have all the functions of the Logitech, but it was only $17.00 and does all I need. And best of all, the Harmony 900 has the Nyko in it's database. The Roku2 XS is mysteriously placed in the DVD section and if I hadn't read some of these reviews I would not have known that. All the other devices mentioned above were in the database and all were added without an issue.

Once all the devices were added the software prompts you to add activities. Activities are the heart of the 900's functionality. However you must understand the concept of "Activities" and how they work to really get the most out of this remote. In a nutshell, an Activity is started by pressing a single button or in this case an icon like "Watch TV" . When you press Watch TV, the TV turns on and switches to the proper input, the Cable box turns on, the receiver turns on and switches to the proper input and output, and finally the 900 becomes a remote for all of those devices at the same time. More on this later.

To get a feel for this device I decided I would first set up all my devices without any activities. Essentially I wanted to just have a remote and be ability to go to one device after the other and see if they worked correctly. At first the software stumped me and didn't appear to let me get past setting up activities. I gave up trying and set some of them up thinking I could always wipe the remote clean and start again. I am not sure where I went wrong but the first activity I set up, "Watch TV" didn't work out so well. The TV didn't turn on, the Cable box turned off, etc. I ran back and forth from my PC to the living room about a dozen times and finally gave up for the night after about 2 hours of head banging. That night I re-read the manual, had the whole next day to ponder and went at it again .

The next morning I deleted all the activities and created them on my own, not using the wizard. I created an Activity, added the devices and then one by one told the software what I wanted each device to do. This was very helpful. I realized this not only got me the expected result, but it made me see how this software and remote really worked. After playing around for about 30 minutes I was able to create several of my most frequent activates. Going back to the equipment I pressed Watch TV. Again the TV did not turn on. If I used the Harmony for that device directly it worked. Back to the PC and set the activity to turn on the TV first. Still no luck. Next I tried the activity and used the on screen help. It asked if the TV turned on, I answered no and presto the TV turned on. After selects "this fixed my problem" on the remote, it worked every time. But; after each change on the PC I had to go through this help processes. I still do not know what the Harmony is doing to correct this.

Once I got all the basic Activities working I found a few other glitches. When I wanted to watch my combo DVF/VCR and use the VCR portion, none of the commands worked. It turns out this device has separate and distinct commands for FF-VCR and FF-DVD. The Harmony set all the DVD commands to that Activity by Default. I simply created two activities, One Watch VHS and one watch DVD even though it's the same source. In fact I found creating different activities for the same source is the answer to everyone complaining about missing the macro feature. It really does the same thing.

Now that I was on a roll my last bit of programming was renaming the activities. If you want the rest of your family to know how to use this thing without a PowerPoint presentation and tutor, I suggest you name the activities in such a way that its very obvious. Examples are Watch TV, Watch Netflix, Use PC, Listen to iPod, Listen to Pandora, etc. Since my receiver has an iPod dock, the Listen to iPod activity changed the source from whatever it is on to the receivers iPod port and then shows all the different music listening modes on the soft buttons. Watch Netflix switches to my Roku, etc.

Now for the best part of the Harmony setup! Its the ability to have the remote on the "Watch TV" activity and being able to program the hard and soft buttons to any other device's remote function. No more switching to the specific device's remote to change an often used setting on that device. If you take your time, you will eventually never have to use the "Devices" soft button as all the things you do will be setup in the Activity you are in. Now this takes some time and trial and error, but it's a huge time saver. Here is an example: You are Watching TV, controlling the sound options and volume with the Receiver, changing channels with the DVR and changing the aspect ration with the TV all on the same keypad. But beware! You can set what buttons do what on the device settings, but that won't change what they do in an Activity. The remote buttons MUST be set up in the Activity to work properly.

I spent several more days fine tuning the remote and now have not touched it in a while. I have a few more tweaks I am thinking of doing. And I would love to find the glitch that makes the TV turn on after I make any updates to the remote. Maybe a call is in order before my 90 days runs out.

USE:

As mentioned above, the ability to have the most common functions for several devices on one remote mode at the same time is huge! Now that I have used it for a couple of weeks, I have gotten accustomed to the button layout and can operate it without looking at it for most basic functions.

When everything is off and you select Watch TV, everything turns on and goes to the right inputs etc. However starting an activity can take quite a while. The remote can not be used while the Activity is being implemented. In my case I am already watching TV with sound on and the remote is still spinning the hour glass for a while. If you have the TV on too loud, you have to wait until the Harmony is done thinking or walk over and turn it down manually. However once that first activity is complete, any subsequent activity is changed fairly quick.

The battery life seems a bit short. I used to change the batteries in my remote once a year. This thing needs to be charged almost every day. If you let it go dead, its time to break out the old remotes during a recharge.

Once set up properly the Harmony 900 is very easy to use and the rest of the family had no problems with it, well almost.

Wife Problems:If your wife, child, etc. has a habit of turning the TV and other equipment on and off manually, you are in for some headaches. Since the Harmony remembers the last state of your devices (if you use it exclusively), it may turn things on instead of off, or off instead of on if someone else manually did that. My wife figured out the remote very quickly they way I have it set up. But she still does a mixture of using the remote and manual power buttons which frustrates both of us. Of course she blames the remote for not working properly when this happens. However anything that takes some blame from me is more than welcome.

RF Setup:

One of my misconceptions about this remote was the boasting of RF (Radio Frequency) capability. IT does indeed have IR capability. However, it does not have a database of RF codes like it does for IR codes. This device will not replace "ANY" RF remote, period. I was hoping there was a RF option for my X-10 home control devices, but that is not the case. For setups like this you need to get a IR to RF converted for the devices you already have. Figuring out which one you need can be a daunting task (See Device Support above).

The only RF device the Harmony will control directly is the IR blaster that comes with the device. An additional IR blaster can also be added. By default the IR blaster emits all the signals the remote puts out through IR to any and all blasters you have set up. You can control which blaster gets which signal. But this can only be done at the remote, not in the software. I am not sure why this is, but it is one of several deficiencies in the software.

Overall:

I went from wanting to return the Harmony 900 within hours of taking it out of the box, to protecting it like it is one of my children. I really love the Harmony 900 and would recommend it to most people. Those with little patients or difficulty working the microwave should avoid it unless someone else can set it up for you. It's overkill on a simply setup, like DVR and TV. But it is a pure joy if you have a medium to complex setup like I do. At $250.00 it is very pricy and hard to justify for a remote. But it seems to solve all my remote issues and to me it's worth it. I give it 4 stars.

Original review

First let me say these only have about 20hrs of time on them so I would not call them fully broken in yet but they should be over that new out of the box sound.

Like a lot of people I'm looking for all the sound I can get in cheap headphones. And technically these are very good and the internet is filled with great reviews. The highs are good and just walk the line of sibilance. If sibilance is there you can hear it, but it's not going to make you want to scratch your ears out. Mids are nice but not particularly impressive. Mid bass is not as controlled as I'd like but it's not smeared either. Drums are handled adequately. I'd like to hear a little bit better separation between kik drum and bass guitar, but it's not bad either. There is a very subtle bloom/extension on the bass. You don't really notice it but you would notice if it was missing. The bass is quirky. If you like a big emphasised bass it's not here. If you like super controlled bass (like hearing the beater on the kik drum and the pluck of fingers/pick on bass guitar strings) it's not here either. But for many people, I think they would find the bass handled well overall. The level of detail on bass I'm talking about just doesn't come on sub $50 headphones.

They do a very good job with acoustic guitar. Where I think they do best is on details like cymbals, and other things with 'ring'. Don't get me wrong these are very nice phones, i'm just being super picky for people who are trying to pick based on the sound signature.

I'm not a soundstage guy, but I would say that soundstage on these is barely adequate. There is no sense of space around the instruments and all the instruments sound like they are in a straight line. There is little sense of the room the instruments are being played or and/or you can't hear much of reverb on the instruments. I'm not saying that these things aren't there at all, but they don't stand out.

What I'm saying is they do a very nice job, and do a nice job for the price, but I'm not hearing the $100+ headphone beaters some make these out to be. But I can see where some people would really like these, and many people do if you read reviews They just are not super impressive in ways I look for. While I could make a case that these are technically better I liked my Vsonic GR02 Bass Edition more. And I liked my old NUFORCE 700M's (about $90 at the time) much better.

At times they are a touch forward and a bit unforgiving of poorly recorded music. Not bad, just a bit unforgiving. A case can be made that is a good thing in 'phones because that is accuracy. And I agree but sometimes it is enough to take me out of the music. If something is bit blaring, like a trump, you are going to notice it is blaring. If you hate Bob Dylan's voice you will really hate it with these. LIke right now I'm listening to Miles Davis and the horn just doesn't sound right. Yeah it should be raw and in your face and it is, but it lacks a certain depth of the horn that would/should balance that out.

They can be a tiny bit dry, a bit sterile? By that I mean they lack a bit of musicality that makes me want to listen to more music. When I was first auditioning with my music I found myself skipping to another song instead of getting lost in the song and forgetting that I was auditioning headphones.

I suspect that these might benefit from a headphone amp, but I"m not going to buy a $50 amp for $50 headphones. I'd rather put that money towards a bigger budget for the phones themselves.

I wanted to try these to see what I think of these and if your budget is less than $50 they are probably hard to go wrong with for a balanced sound. Not flat, not V-shaped, and not too fatiguing. If you told me I had to keep these I would not cry myself to sleep but I plan to up my budget a bit and find something that suits me a bit more. At touch more musicality, a bit more air around the instruments, and more impressive mid-range.

Note: in spite of my criticisms I'm giving these 5 stars because they really are very good and I could see where people would really like these.

Comfort isn't bad and for my ears, the ear cup size is just about right size. I wish the earpieces swiveled a bit more but for my head, they swivel just enough. . They have a left and right and the cups swivel so little that if you have them on the wrong way you will notice.

Bluetooth... These are a pain in the backside on Win 7. When I want to use them I have to go and delete the previous pairing, pair them again and then go to the control panel and set these to be used for output. For movies on the computer, they get out of sync. I even set my movie player (Pot Player which I highly recommend) to use the Bluetooth headphones and they still get out of sync with the audio. I don't know if it's the player, the USB Bluetooth adapter, Windows 7 or some combination of them together.

I like that they can be used with a wire as well as with bluetooth. The controls are a little small, as mentioned by others but I don't have trouble working them.

I also tried the JBL EB45T Bluetooth headphones, which cost almost twice as much, at Target and these sound better overall. The JBL might have had better highs, a little punchier bass but these are more cohesive across the frequency range with nothing tweaked to make them sound 'better'.

The rear panel (for all the ports) sits flush on the back of the computer and the computer back is flat. It makes it much easier to see the ports when you bend over the top of the case.
