Not a big issue anyway because the ear cups fit my ears well and do a great job silencing the outside world on their own.

If you're looking for decent headphones at a budget price, you have found some right here.

Bone conduction is a unique experience. I won't waste your time explaining it here.

These headphones provide clear sound, and fit my head nicely.
I personally would recommend them more for spoken word, audiobooks, podcasts, and the like.
Not saying music is bad through these, but if you are an audiophile, these may leave you wanting more.

I really enjoy these because the bulk of my media consumption is spoken word. And these are great.

I ordered these for my son who says normal in ear earbuds make his ears itch. These earbuds sit just outside of your ears and allow the sounds of your surroundings to be heard. They fit around the back of your head snugly but are still quite comfortable. No sweaty ear canals here!

They have 8GB of internal storage for you to store music and listen to without an external source. I have not tested this function because I primarily stream my music and content from my phone.

I agree with several other reviewers who have stated that this type of device is much better for spoken word (podcasts and audiobooks), than actual music.

While I don’t consider the sound of the music coming through these bad, there is something that is lost with these that you would get with standard earbuds and headphones.

For the price, you could do much worse. Overall, I would recommend these to anyone who has trouble with earbuds being in their ears for extended periods, or for anyone who would want to be able to monitor their surroundings while still trying to listen to their favorite content.
Very nice set. Surround sound for your yard, Bluetooth style.
Easy setup, and this little speaker cooks! It will dance itself off the table, so keep an eye on it at high volume or hang it up on the convenient cord.

The sound quality takes a slight hit due to the size of the wire and the fact that it's a connection instead of a straight line. But it works great, you can charge your phone while still keeping it plugged in to aux.
Sound quality is great through this cord. Perfect for a phone with no 3.5 jack to car with one.
Has a nice fit for those of us with sensitive ears. Sound is decent, battery life is decent. The case holds it's charge well, too.

Cute little speaker to boost your listening. Easily connects to iPhone. The sound quality isn't mind-blowing, but just as good as the phone itself and gets louder than the phone can alone. I especially like the dial for level control so I can turn down the device without a lot of poking or rearranging things to get to the volume button.

Set up was easy though I will say the instructions don't have English instructions, just the guide to what each button does and you an use deductive reasoning from that. The sound quality is good. Not like the most amazing ever but clear and smooth with no extra noise. Comfortable to wear. Great since I have a large number of piercings on my ears beyond just the lobes. I can wear them with a Bluetooth headset piece and glasses and everything stays where is should be. Can hear the things happening around me but also my media.

I have been using a personal gaming headset for work for comfort. When an update rendered it non-compatible I had to surrender to a generic Logitec headset that was too small for my head or ears.

I do have to talk on the phone a lot for work but I also do a bunch of data entry to having podcasts or music going is really nice. It was hard to get a set up where the music was not in my headset when I was talking to people but also I could hear it with the headset on.

This little guy has been a great solution. Airpod in one ear and this little thing in the other I can listen to my media and be readily available. The sound quality I would give a 6.5/10, ease of use 8/10, and comfort 7/10 (but I have small ear canals that always is a struggle). I would get this style again if it ever came to it.

I got this because I like to play some heavier casual games like the Sims 4, terria, stardew valley, on my not-technically gaming laptop that is entirely metal casing. Typically it gets pretty hot and the internal fans run pretty hard. Some games, like the cult of the lamb, actually got the keyboard hot enough to almost hurt to touch the keyboard. And the fan would run pretty hard and loudly.

The addition of this has allowed my machine to run well, more quietly even with the fan going, and not be so hot I can't touch it. The fan is quiet, quieter than the laptop fan itself, so running it doesn't cause any additional noise pollution. The way it expands is nice. There are small hooks on the base end that can be pressed to securely hold the device. The options for different angle lifts is nice.

My biggest draw back would be is my laptop is a pretty standard 15-inch and it does not expand far enough to hold the whole base so its kinda wobbly when not being angled. I would prefer that I could expand it to be as deep as my laptop too.

Spent a lot of time deciding what keyboard I wanted for my WFH set up. Love the keys, since I tend to have long finger nails and extensions, I am able to type without hitting extra keys. Sound is a soft clack, nice but not too much. Mouse occasionally wigs out  a little but working on getting a mouse pad to see if that alleviates anything.
This cable has many uses and is just the cable I needed to plug my phone into my surround sound for music! Easy to use and good quality! Just plug in and its ready to use.

Have always wanted to have a frame like this! Its easy to set up. You do need a wifi connection and  download an app on your phone to be able to add albums to your frame. It does seem like a lot of work to be honest. The frame will allow you to transfer 50 images and if you want more you can add a USB drive or memory chip. It is touch screen and you can change the views on the frame from a clock, to the image gallery cycling the 50 images randomly or in sequence, the weather, or the original home screen. The downside of this frame is it needs to be connected to electricity it is not one you can recharge.

These are perfect for emergencies and everyday use. Dont let the price mislead you, these actually hold a better charge than other brands I have used before. You're not getting the same quality sound as more higher end headphones but these are still a good quality for the price Im impressed. Easy to connect to your devices too!

The cable is thicker than expected which adds to its durability. I was looking for a longer cable than what I originally had and this is perfect! Overall it works great, the sound quality with the optic cable sure does the trick for my soundbar than a regular audio cable.

This little portable speaker packs a punch of sound! It really does have a lot of volume. Its a little taller than a 12 oz can of soda and is portable to take anywhere. You can turn off the light or leave it on to change with the music and comes with 2 cables- an aux plug in and a USB to charge it. It says its waterproof on the box but I wouldn't risk it as you cant submerge it in water for more than 30 minutes or so as noted on the packaging. Also, the speaker mesh/fabric can easily get dirty on the lighter speakers It would be better if it were more sturdy. It doesn't look like it would snag though. Unlike other speakers that have metal netting this one is like a very heavy and thick weave of yarn looking material its quality looks pretty good. Overall I was impressed by how loud it can get.
Purchased this for my bedroom tv and I get superior sound I feel like I am in a theater!  I love this and inking of getting another

Then when you have two of these, you can hang these from the lilac in your backyard, and you can play quiet music with ambient lighting for a soiree on your back deck.

I chose a weak lilac branch and it fell about 3 feet and hit a kayak, it wasn't affected.

There is also a brass threaded insert on the bottom if you want to place it on a tripod. Or it you have a thing you stick in the ground, it looks like a tiki light.

Okay so I was very impressed with the speakers when I first got them, however... They have nothing like 14 hours of battery. I listen to them for a few hours and have to recharge them and now I'm having to recharge them twice a day. I'm also very disturbed to see that the price has doubled. My entire review was that these were good speakers for the price. But my JBL rarely has to be recharged and it's just as loud and bassy it's just not separate speakers.

But until I get around to that, know that these Paxcess Twins speakers are blowing my mind. It cost half of what I paid for the JBL Flip 2 years ago and it's louder and separate, sweet! And they're called the twins, what could be better? I have named mine Tiffany and Sabrina.

They have a big stereo speaker sound, and this TWS technology is awesome. Each speaker has a power switch, you turn them both on. Each speaker has volume buttons which act for both speakers whichever one you use.

If you had these in your cubicle or whatever office at work, you'd have to turn them down to a whisper.

Before I forget and this is important, when they're turned up loud they will creep on their rubberized feet, unless they're on something like marble or steel. So on some surfaces you may want some sort of rubber coaster so it doesn't fall off the edge.

The sound quality is as good as if it were built in to your car stereo, it connects easily pairs easily, and the battery life is better than the Walmart one. I have both. I'll submit pictures tomorrow.

Again, comparing this unit to the one from Walmart, the iWorld, you can tell by holding it that it's definitely a higher quality little piece of electronics, another plus is that it charges through a USBC port, micro USB will be a thing of the past very soon so you don't want to have to keep another cable.

Mostly just operates from a single multifunction button which answers calls with a short press, I think it also has a volume rocker switch. It also comes with both a double-ended mail audio plug, and a short double-ended audio cable. I prefer the cable to the small hard metal jack plugged directly into the dash because I have found that holding down the power switch the three or four seconds it takes is hard to do when the car is bouncing around.

This might sound trivial, but it's not. You wear that jack on your car stereo out by wiggling it around and it will fail soon. I have had the port that jack plugs into, wear out on several smartphones in the past.

Most importantly I like the bass I'm hearing from these small speakers. They're about the size of a Oreo double stuffed cookie. And you can feel the bass! The instructions are very clear, the operation is very simple, there are only two buttons one on each speaker. Also, they have a magnetically attaching charge cable similar to a Fitbit. I will add to this review once I know more about the battery life.

I luv listening to music and sometimes I want to play my cds. This portable boombox fits the need. for my bedroom .
Price was right however I wish the sound was clearer and louder , it did skip some of my older cds
Overall I give it 3.5

Great to use for Mindfulness!!. Nice sound and
Durability
Like the color (orange) and the sound is great . Battery life not great!
So far so good . Nice sound

I had never been able to listen to podcasts in the shower, prior to trying this bluetooth speaker. I would listen to podcasts in the bath on my phone speaker, but it wasn't loud enough to play while I was showering. This awesome little speaker gives me the ability to listen to podcasts or music even while I'm showering. I love that it's waterproof and functions perfectly in places where you couldn't bring a traditional speaker. I have been envisioning inner-tubing with these. :) Meanwhile, this is one of those products that I didn't know that I needed, but now that I have it, I can't envision not having it.

I ordered a couple of pairs of earbuds, this one having the higher pricetag, and wondered exactly how they might differ. I ended up liking both pairs, but this one is definitely far superior, and worth the higher price tag. I am not an audiophile, and can't tell you about the mids, highs and lows of the sound. But there are a couple of ways in which I could perceive clear differences in regards to sound. The first is just in how the earbuds fit. There was more noise cancellation in this pair, and the sound conductivity is greater, I think, because of how the earbuds are shaped, with a longer part going into the ear. The second is just about sound quality. I can't clearly describe how they differ, but I could tell quite clearly that one sounded much better than the other. (The other set was $39.99 and highly reviewed/rated for quality and sound, and use in athletics.) For me personally, I train capoeira, which is an Afro-Brazilian martial art, with a lot of inversions, cartwheels, jumps and spinning kicks. The other set would fly out of my ears with inversions and spinning kicks. This set stayed in much better. For me, this is extremely important, since I like to train with earbuds.

Overall, this is an excellent set of earbuds, definitely the best I've ever used. Although I've never ordered any earbuds over $75, so that's an important point. To my ears, though, these have the best sound I've experienced with earbuds, and the fit feels the best, as well. I am thoroughly impressed.

This is one of those items that I really had no idea that I needed until I ordered it. I listen to podcasts in the bath, but my phone speakers aren’t loud enough to listen to when I’m showering. With this speaker, I’m able to listen to podcasts while I’m showering, as well as when I’m using skincare or brushing my teeth. I love that it’s waterproof and can go with me anywhere that I need a Bluetooth speaker where it might get wet. I use this when I’m using my IPL hair removal device (it can get really boring zapping small pieces of skin). But with this speaker, it’s easy to listen to podcasts or music, and the sound is impressive for a soda can-sized speaker. I really do love this hugely and am so glad that I found it.

I really wanted to love this. I bought it primarily because I have a lot of issues with sleep disturbance, and I thought that it would be helpful to try out an item that would block out both light and sound. Although it didn't completely block out light because of the placement of the "on" button, I didn't mind this too much. It blocks light out mostly, and that works for me. And my initial concern was that the speakers might be uncomfortable when I sleep on my sides. However, although I could feel the speakers, they weren't hugely problematic. I could sleep on my side without feeling irritated by the sensation of them between my ear and the pillow.

My issue with this product stems from the slippery nature of the fabric. The headband is fairly loose on me, and I don't see any way to adjust it. But my hair is also straight and slippery, and between the headband and my hair, I couldn't get the band to stay in place. I would go to sleep with it on, and then wake up with it somewhere in my bed. The other issue with the slipping is that the speakers are set on certain spots on the headband. It's a little bit awkward as it doesn't align perfectly with the size of my head, but it's ok. It does mostly work. However, once I start moving, the slipping will move the speakers off of my ears. While I'm awake, this happens anytime I turn my head on the pillow. I have to adjust them every time I move my head. Once I'm asleep, I have no idea when the headband slips off exactly, I just know that each time I wake up, I will have to dig around in the bed a bit to find it. (I wake up quite often in the night.)

This is a great concept for people who struggle with sleep disturbance. I'm able to listen to white noise or meditation tracks, which can be really helpful. If there was a way to keep the band from slipping around, I think it would be a much better product. I'm giving it 3 stars, because this is definitely more comfortable than using headphones while sleeping, and I do get use of it in my meditation tracks with binaural sounds (which I can't get the benefit of if I'm using my phone or another external speaker). But this is pretty far from a 5 star purchase for me, simply because of the slipping of the band.

Edit: I am changing this to 4 stars, because I have discovered that if I wear this as a headband, with the band under my hair at the back of my neck, it doesn’t slip as much. It does still slip off of my eyes sometimes, and I do still have a bit of trouble getting the speakers to stay strictly aligned with my ears, but it no longer slips into the bed, off of my head. I was initially wearing it like a sleep mask, where I put it on over my hair, and that did not work for me at all, as the band is too loose/slippery for me, to work as strictly a sleep mask.

I do want to add that I’ve been having some weird issues where music on my iPhone (where the band is connected to) will start playing on its own in the middle of the night. I’m not sure why that is happening, and it is a bit disturbing as it will wake me up. (This doesn’t happen when I’m using my phone without the headband, so it seems like it’s associated with the head band use.) But it doesn’t happen every night, and I do find myself enjoying the experience of listening to my meditation tracks before I go to bed, and when I wake up in the middle of the night and am trying to go back to sleep.

Overall, I am enjoying using this product, which is why I am changing the rating to 4 stars, even with the issues I’m having.

This flexible mount comes in very handy for the purpose I've gotten it: to mount my Blink XT2 near my front door without the screwing into walls the Blink's mount requires.  It works well and the padding on the inside of the clamp is appreciated in preventing unnecessary scratches.  The only two slight negatives with this product is how much force is required to open the clamp and to manipulate the flexible arm.  The latter is more of a problem as it can be difficult to move the camera around without dislodging the clamp (in my case, the clamp gets to grip less than an inch of a metal window flange).  If the arm were more easily bendable, I'd give this product 5 stars.

I'm a software developer who works in a cubicle world with the heating system droning on above the ceiling (we're on the top floor of an office building - the HVAC is on the roof). These headphones provide an oasis of silence! The noise cancellation *seems* to be a cut above the others I've tried (Beats Studio at Target and a Sony set at Costco) although it's not really fair to compare as I didn't try the Bose under the same condition as the others (i.e. in a noisy store).

How good is it? The droning AC noise is completely gone. Voices I can still hear - until I play music. Even at low/moderate playback volume, voices are barely audible. People have to pat me on the back if they want my attention.

Comfort is excellent. I wear them on-and-off all day without problems. I imagine people with big ears might be less comfortable.

Power: the headphones use a single AAA battery. Keeping in mind that I maybe play music for 2-3 hours every day, the battery seems to last 2-3 weeks. As others have noted, these headphones will not work (i.e. play music) without power.

My one nitpick (and the reason I can't give it 5 stars) is the god-awful chord. It's some cheap plasticky material that I continually have to unravel by dangling the headphones by the plug end and letting the headphones rotate. It's really quite pathetic to put such cheap cr$p on $300 headphones - shame on Bose for not correcting this. Is it really going to affect your profitability so much you can't do something like the $20 Apple headphones that come with every iPhone (they're more rubberized and don't seem to get raveled).

Update for iPhone/iPad/iPod users: with iOS 7, Apple introduced a new way to invoke Siri (Apple's voice assistant) - instead of holding down the home button (or center button on the headphones) until you hear the Siri confirmation sound and then asking Siri your question and then waiting for Siri to accept your input, with iOS 7, you can keep the button pressed until you're finished talking - and avoid the delay Siri normally waits to know you're done with talking. It's a very useful feature.....and, it doesn't work with the Bose inline chord button :-( Not really Bose's fault, I guess, but I thought it worth mentioning.

I've had the ER-6 (the predecessor to the ER-6i) for four years or so and have always loved the sound they produce. I'm not totally happy about the comfort of the silicone tips, but have heard from others that the foam ones (which I have lost without ever trying them on) provide a much more comfortable fit.

But my review is mainly about my very positive experience with Etymotic Research's customer support. When, after four years of use, I had trouble with the volume of sound produced in the right ear, I turned to their customer support for advice. They immediately suggested that the filter in the right ear might be clogged/dirty and suggested that I replace it. When I told them that I had neither filters nor the tool to replace them, the offered to send me a few plus the tool. No charge - even though I was out of warranty for a long time. Now, I know this seems like a little thing, but to me it shows that this company stands behind its products. They're proud of their ear phones and want their customers to have a positive experience no matter what.

Bravo, Etymotic Research! There are no longer many companies that value their customers to this level.

I was surprised that this turns solid (like ice) in the refrigerator so the freezer isn’t required. In just a few minutes, it’s solid and cold and ready to put around my neck where it does a very good job of providing some cooling relief on hot days. I’ve used it both inside and outside and found it stays cool for about an hour. That’s impressive considering it’s small and I expected the coolness to disappear much more quickly.
It’s pretty comfortable to wear provided you can handle some pressure around your neck. My daughter who can’t tolerate anything around her neck could not handle this because it does touch and, depending on your neck size, could feel sort of tight.
I have to note that when I received the package, it was dirty and looked like it had been taped back together, perhaps after a return. Still, the product itself was intact, so I washed it and felt okay using it.

Since the Macbook Air computers don’t have a USB port, I was looking for a mouse that would connect without having to bother with an adapter so I could attach a USB connection to my computer. I found this one, and I’m happy to report that it connected and it works well with my Macbook Air. The mouse is easy to use with right and left buttons as well as a scrolling wheel, and is very quiet. It’s a flat mouse, so if you’re used to a more ergonomically shaped mouse it may take some getting used to, but it doesn’t take long. For $20, you can’t go wrong if you’re looking for a wireless mouse without the need for a USB port on your computer.

This worked great! (until I lost it last week).  It's a bit difficult to 'open' at first since the fit of the cable and slots are quite snug.  Don't pull on it forcefully, I think this is why people are saying it broke easily, but that can happen with any cable.  The trick is to get as much of the cord to one end, 'unplug' it, then pull the cord to the other end, and voila, it's open.  Same for putting it back away after use.  Sounds elaborate, but it really isn't.  Tiny and flat that it fits in my coin pocket without any bulge.  This is great for those of us who don't carry purses.  My only con for this is I had to carry the portable charger with my phone since it's so short.  I ordered another one for my son's android phone, which he keeps on his keychain.  I will probably order another one to replace the one I lost.

Main thing going for this set is its nice matte black finish and the understated color bands, and the price point.  Though higher than some of the USB 2.0 /32GB that can be bought in bulk (around 2.5 or cheaper in sets of 10), this one seems to be better built and definitely looks nicer.  Dont expect blazing speeds, but for my primary uses (car audio mp3,  pic backups during travel, school work for kids), this is reasonable choice for USB2.  Longevity is tough to predict for new brands, so, it is a somewhat of a gamble; prefer to use name-brand and online options for critical docs.

For a 2k camera with autofocus and reasonable sound quality ,this is a good value.  Colors are fine, auto-focus is not annoying and stable and is truly plug-and-play.  The stiff ball mount makes it hard to adjust for your perfect position, but with a little bit of muscle, one can get the perfect position.  (good thing that it is not too loose that it needs constant adjustment).  Overall, a good value in the 35$ range.  But next time, I will spend more and get a 4k camera.

Sound quality and battery life are the two most important factors for me for ear buds;  this set scores well on both - able to hear crisp sounds without having to pump up my device volume setting.  Was able to find the right pair of buds to ensure proper fit while jogging.  It is a bit bulkier than my previous ear buds - both the bud and the charging case.  Battery life seem to live up to the claims, especially the quick charging.  The hand controls need a bit of a learning curve;  I have mostly given up on trying to memorize different long touch/tap sequences as each manufacturer has their own;  For around 40, which was the price at time of review, this is a good deal.

Though slightly bulkier than I'd liked, this is surprisingly good value.  The noise block/isolation effectiveness is excellent for this pricepoint.  Though unfair to compare it with active noise canceling headphones, the sound quality for this headset is decent.  Worked great with phones and laptop;  easy to pair and battery life seems to last as claimed. For short durations (1-2 hrs or so), the headset is comfortable on the ear - haven't tried it for extended period like a coast-to-coast flight.  Overall, good value for a passive noise reduction headset.

very simple plug-and-play; Zoom and other video programs instantly recognized this as a "USB Camera" available as an option in the video settings. The dimmable, inbuilt ring light is great and is adequate. While the wide view works fine, wish there was a zoom/focus feature (though doubtful for this price point)

Two tiny issues - and may be because of my set up. The cable is a bit too long (and stiff) and clutters my workspace. Second, when used on a laptop, the mechanism to hold it in place seems a bit too flimsy. It will work great on thicker panel monitors, but as long as you don't expect to use the touchscreen when you are on camera, it wouldnt be an issue. Wish there was a snugger way to connect to laptop screens.

...this may be a case of overpacking features to impress, and then so-so execution creates more frustration than delight.  With a Samsung Note, the BT connectivity is fine.  DIdnt have any issues with calls dropping etc.  The sound quality is OK, responds to Alexa etc fine - but the app is not the best - Not stable, not intuitive, and the reliance on the app tmakes this far more cumbersome to justify the 150 or so price tag.  Battery life is as advertised  (6-7 hours or with mixed use of ANC),  volume and sound quality is decent.  Fits in the ear well but appears "unsleek"  Better off with Galaxy buds+ or AirPod Pro for similar features without the hassle.

This is a good choice for a mid range (50-70$) earbuds that comes with a few excellent features and some drawbacks that will make you love your airpods or buds even more.

The main positives - the BT connectivity is excellent and zero loss of signal while jogging/yard work etc. Never had to repair the earbuds to my phone (Note). Battery life is as advertised and very pleasing. Fit is comfortable and no heaviness or blocked feeling.

The could-be-better - getting used to the stem controls is not that easy and has been finicky at times. Volume/bass is mediocre at best. Though some noise reduction is perceivable, it is uneven. It is IPX5 rated, means it should be able to "resist a sustained, low-pressure water jet spray".

At the advertised price, you are paying really for the battery life, BT chip, above-average noise suppression and average sound. Overall, a decent pair for using in situations where you are OK sacrificing performance (travel, yard work, jogging etc - where one could lose or step on it ).

At just over $100, this is an excellent value. Key reasons for the enthusiastic endorsement
- easy set up
- clean, crisp display and low bluelight option
- slim profile, thin bezels provide a very sleek, modern look
- included hdmi and audio cables (obviously the power supply)
- the speakers work fine for its intended purpose for me (just streaming music while working); confused about reviews that say it has no speakers. I am able to change the audio setting from my default to "HP 24mh" and get the audio streamed to the monitor just with the hdmi cable.

The only con is the packaging, I am sure HP can find a way to ship these without having to rely on thermocol.

Overall, a fantastic value for a well known brand. Longevity is of course always an issue of "time will tell"

The main user (a 10 yr old forced to Zoom-school like every other child) finds this to be very easy to hold and operate.  At first the lack of loud clicking was confusing the tactile response, but he got over it fairly quickly and now loves how silent it is.  Zero set-up though the battery cage was a bit tricky to open ( USB receiver is inside this cage)Vibrant red color is another plus.  Overall, an ergonomically designed, quiet mouse.  (update to be added after monitoring battery life - others have stated it lasts 2-3 weeks).

A ton of excellent features packed into this smart watch (worked very well in the past few months with Samsung Note 9).  The two main issues faced with the watch are (i) incredibly difficult to adjust the length of the strap (metal) - bought a replacement leather strap that was easy to adjust  and (ii) the instructions for the set-up are just not intuitive or systematic.  A lot of trial-and-error to get familiar with the menu settings and customization.  Once paired and set-up, the watch worked as advertised.  Particularly relying on it for a few fitness apps (with GPS enabled) and to stream some stock quotes.  Battery life is good and has been consistent in the past 10 weeks of use.  Sound quality is OK,  but not much into talking like a Star Trek person into a watch...  Scores slightly higher points in style than Samsung's own watch, but the price points may make this a tougher value proposition if you are comfortable with Samsung products anyway.

At this pricepoint, this music player packs a lot of good features - expandable memory, FM radio, voice recording.  The headsets are average and tend to create some static - this may be due to the design of the recess that results in creating additional movement.  Apart from that, the only other issue was that not all FM stations in this region (Boston area) was reachable (beyond 105 freq).  Stations that can be reached by the device - the sound quality is excellent.  DIdnt notice any playback issues on mp3 - from the drive nor from the extended memory.  It does seem a bit bulky, but for a low cost device with FM and mp3, this is an excellent choice.  Primarily used by the kids in the house with a different headset than the one included..

This is my first experience with an Alexa-enabled laptop. The key positives are the bright, wide display, good value for a i5 processor, and of course, Alexa. For the pricepoint, the 256GB SSD and 8 GB memory is good - and the performance was comparable to pricier laptops. It provides great connectivity with the USB ports, SSD reader and HDMI; streaming and webcam audio/video was excellent, no issues noted in any of the video conferencing apps either. excellent video.audio clarity.

As a big fan of the Surface lines, this one has a few design drawbacks. First of all, the set up is not trivial - Cortana is the default voice assistant which guides you through the process; it is annoying to have to link to the microsoft/skype account right away, but you have an option to bypass it and create an offline account. Cortana seems to be underperforming Alexa in almost all categories. A minor irritant
includes the default setting for the screen auto-rotate - one has to manually go in and change the settings if this is important for a user in the tablet mode. The sensitivity of the device for switching between tablet/laptop mode is not consistent - often had to reboot. The speakers are in the keyboard and not on the screen, so, when you are on the tablet mode - the speakers are a bit muffled and seems like heating up the keyboard base. if you can tolerate these sub-par design executions, the idea of Alexa integration is well executed and makes it somewhat of a unique laptop. Overall 3.5 stars

update 10/3: the fan is becoming louder even when doing routine tasks like browsing; it quietens after 4-5 mins of use.

For a headphone at this pricepoint, the sound quality is decent but not great (compared to a noise-cancelling headphone set I use regularly - not a direct comparison, I know).  The packaging is very high-end and maybe a bit too much. Excellent graphics of the design elements on the packaging and the sturdy box makes this a ready-to-gift item.  For me, the main use is for travel - so, noise canceling is a must; this set is a bit bulky for travel, especially if you decide to use the included travel case.  Also remember the quality of the sound is more dependent on the source of the sound (streaming music is not a great way to enjoy this headset - any ordinary will do); for this pricepoint, I did not find it a compelling value.  Compared to other over-ear noise isolation headsets (quite a few in 100-150 range, and even sub-100 on sale) are available - and their performance is almost identical for most sound sources (CD, streaming, travel..).  A good entry-level set for a higher-end, but only at the right price - not at the list price.

While the sound quality is excellent,  the "platform" approach of both Amazon/Alexa and Sonos somewhat limiting each others capabilities (at least for this edition of Sonos One), makes this a tough choice to heartily recommend at this price point.  While access to streaming options seems better supported in Sonos, it will be a matter of time that Alexa Skills will expand - at which point, the devices will have to compete on sound quality and broader ecosystems -  Given that you need fairly expensive additions for the Sonos One to unlock its full potential,  this family is going to cheer on the Echo family until it becomes easier to pair Sonos to other devices (no Bluetooth and no line-in is a major disappointment).

Good quality headphones for the price;  for the main purpose of having an easy-to-use headphones while jogging/walking, this is an excellent  option - fairly quick to charge, sufficient battery life (6-8 hours when used on an average of an hour a time or so), easily pairs with the devices, and OK sound quality for mic and headphones.  Not a major fan of the red-black color scheme for the wires - completely black or white would have been a more palatable option.  With multiple options for earbuds and good performance for the price point, this is an excellent choice.

Among the wireless extenders, I have used, this model from Amped has been the easiest to set up, and it works as good as advertised. Using an iPad, it took less than 5 minutes to set up. Very intuitive and well-thought through interface for setting up with very clear information on each screen (an accurate countdown warns you exactly when to expect next steps, etc.). Overall, this has been the most pleasant experience in setting up any electronics gadget that is device-agnostic.

The performance is excellent; in a far away sunroom, the extender easily resulted in a "full" indicator for WiFi devices, and the ethernet port enabled to connect a gaming device (for very infrequent use, this will work very well; I already have an extended port to connect to the TV). The extender has performed consistently as well, no pauses in video streaming, for example.

There is one minor disadvantage, other than what seems to be a tad pricey - the bulk of the unit. It is difficult to place this in plug points with tight corners or abutting walls. I have had mixed experience in trying to print from a device connected to the extended network to a printer on the original network (need to verify settings and will update the review). Overall, an excellent choice for an extender+port option that is extremely easy to set up and works consistently.

At this pricepoint, this is a great value for this configuration. The laptop was extremely easy to set up (power on and a few simple screens to set up account; Windows of course has to make things slightly annoying, so it requires you to sign in to an account or create a new one; on one occasion it allows you to bypass account integration, but for anything with apps, you will need to create an account). Unlike other reviewers who seemed to have issues, I had zero issues with any bloatware or preloaded programs.

The touch-screen works great; part of the reason for choosing this model was the added touch-screen to a good configuration laptop; 2-in-1 laptop/tablet is far more expensive and if you already own a tablet, this is a reasonable compromise to obtain some tablet-like convenience and retain the "workhorse" capabilities of a laptop. The onscreen keyboard will take time to get used to, especially given that the keyboard will occupy only the central one-third or so of the screen.

Audio/video performance is OK, nothing to get super excited about. The optical drive, 2 USB 2 ports, 1 USB 3 port, 1 HDMI port, Ethernet-enabled configuration and the 750 GB drive is an excellent value. Wifi performance has been good so far. The laptop is much lighter than the lenovos I am used to; the power adapter itself is much lighter. The replaceable battery is light and much thinner than most models.

Overall, impressive start with this laptop; time will tell how robust this machine is. Will update review after 6 months and a year.

Like most products, the price/value really depends on the intended use. this well-equipped, sturdy dashcam is a perfect example of that. For a regular commuter or occasional driver more interested in developing narratives for proudly displaying the traffic in your city, or capture a scenic drive, this dashcam is most certainly not your first choice (maybe something from GoPro is more useful).  For a user exposed to high risk of collisions or monitoring of driving behavior, this should be the first choice.  The functionality of the camera, the intuitive software interface and ease of archiving only what's only relevant, relative ease in installation, excellent video and audio quality, quick capture of GPS signals are great attributes that justify the pricepoint.  It would've been nice if an independent battery source or another power source was included to be able to be less dependent on having access to the vehicle's powersource.

For a middle-of-the-road BT speaker, the Altec unit is a well-designed, aesthetically unique choice.  The sound quality is nothing to rave about, but nothing really to complain.  Syncs without fail to any of the three devices I have paired this speaker - and amazed by its battery life.  Considering it is a single unit, stereo effects wasnt that noticeable - so, for those who have high expectations, this may be a drawback.  For background music, occasional use with conference call settings, this is a good choice.

Most of earlier complaints focused on the clock being difficult to set and the user manual (or lack thereof). This unit hasn't had any issue with setting the time - in fact, it is fully automatic. Never had to set the time and it resets to the right time even after I unplug it during the day.

The controls are not that intuitive but with a little bit of trial-and-error one can easily set the alarms and listen to the cliche'd nature sounds (and tiny lights of various colors with ability to change its brightness). I have never understood how these lights are "mood lighting" - but nevertheless, they are easy to operate AFTER you figure out what the different buttons are for (I cant say if the user manual is useful - there was none included).

The docks work fine - I have used Android phones and tablets via the Auxiliary connections and an iphone (minus the case) - you cant expect Bose-like quality - but it is better than cheap portable speakers. the charger seems to work fine as well.

While the unit comes with many interesting features, the lack of intuitive design and the slightly bulky nature of the unit, the OK sound quality from the speakers, makes this unit questionable value at the list price. But at the right sale price, this may be a good value for a decent alarm clock that has a bunch of other useful features (chargers, docking stations and OK quality speakers). 3.5*

This is an excellent choice for a camera in this category providing a 10X optical zoom and a variety of useful shooting modes (low light performance is very impressive, so are the panorma sweep, soft skin and background de-focus). It touts the ability to take 3D pictures and underwater capabilities (though I've not tested either). Compared to the pricier [[ASIN:B006K552V6 Sony Cyber-shot DSC-TX66 18.2 MP Exmor R CMOS Digital Camera with 5x Optical Zoom and 3.3-inch OLED (White) (2012 Model)]], this one provides more zoom; however the pricier DSC-TX66 provides a touch-screen control (OLED display) and is much thinner and lighter. The picture and video settings are almost identical for both cameras. Just like other cameras in this family, the battery compartment doesn't inspire much confidence with its flimsy looks.

Having used to the touch-screen controls of TX66, the scroll-based menu in the WX150 seems less impressive - however, the controls on both are very intuitive - given the wide range of options, it will take some time to get used to all the command settings. The video quality of both cameras are exceptional - and either will replace a handycam easily. If you are more interested in a lighter camera with a touch screen and willing to compromise on the zoom (5X opposed to 10X in the WX150) and pay up for it (about 100$ more), DSC-TX66 may be a better choice. But if the touchscreen is not a critical requirement for you and zoom is of more importance, WX150 is a very compelling choice at this price-point. The DSLR-like quality with a very respectable zoom, plethora of picture settings options, and fairly intuitive scroll-based menus makes this a good value.

but I end up only liking it. (updated on June 11, 2012)
Pros:
- Tiny size that rivals even the slickest smartphones
- Highly responsive touch screen interface (a first in this segment?)
- Negligible delay in "shooting" or focusing.
- Context-aware help files on the interactive screen (useful given the relatively new touchscreen interface)
- A reasonable alternative to lugging around a HD-video camcorder (it records in 29 min segments, so prepare for some minor editing to splice videos etc. having used this only once, I will update the review after more uses).

Cons:
- A flimsy-looking battery compartment and the need to carry around the charger (not a fun situation if you tend to go on long treks like I do). Overall, it looks so delicate that you will be tense handling it ( fear of dropping it or denting/scratching...)
- Some gimmicky special effects that may appeal to children but can be easily attained in both Android and iphone apps for less than 5$. [An exception is the partial color feature that works exceptionally well when there is a stark contrast in the subject (bright colored flowers and green leaves, for example) - this is a feature that is worthy of some exploration if you are into art photography].
- Despite the 18M resolution (also think larger file sizes), the photo quality is not comparable to those from DSLRs even for the same focal range (this one has an equivalent of 26-130 mm).

Ironically, a child may be better suited to handle the interface/controls but the camera looks so delicate, a child probably shouldn't handle it. Despite the innovative interface and brag-worthy ability to shoot in 3D (more money to spend on 3D TV and glasses?), tons of features packed into a tiny sleek design, the price point makes it difficult for an enthusiastic endorsement. At this price range, you must value the weight/size of the camera far more than the need to take better pictures with a DSLR...or love the touchscreen interface to such extent that you will pay up from other options in this segment.

Update on 6/12/12
After a round of video capture using this camera for dance recitals, this has become my default device for all video recording (and for most pictures). The ease of high res video recording is absolutely breath-taking. The ease of set up, sharpness of the picture, the audio capture, response to zoom in recording mode - all aspects are very well worth the price. The compact size is truly deceiving when it comes to video capture.

After about 22000+ reviews, there is virtually no undiscovered features of Kindle. So, this review focuses only on the special offers. Other than screen savers and a very non-intrusive banner at the Home page, the look, functionality, features is identical to any other Kindle.

In the one week or so, I have had the Kindle, the quality of "offers" itself is quite varied and limited to about 4-5 at any time (which can be accessed via the screen saver, or the banner on homepage or using the menu option to get to "view special offers"). Offers have ranged from mostly traditional ads to discount-like offers ($10 for $20 Amazon GC and a 10$ promotion if one pays via Visa card at least one of the listed books). It is not clear how often the offers are going to change. Moreover, the AdMash feature is not active as of this review date.

I will append review after observing the frequency of new offers and when AdMash goes online.

But if you are still vacillating on whether to buy the version with special offers worried about how intrusive it can be...rest assured, you wont even notice the difference. I wish they had a 3G version with the special offers.

Update 5/26/11 - Now, there is a 3G version currently for 50$ more than the WiFi mode. Having used the WiFi only mode for a few weeks, I doubt I need a 3G version - Whether it is a bookstore or cafe, I typically have WiFi access.

For a listed price of around $80, you may be paying more for the "Born in California, Made in Vietnam" tagline than the additional pockets/slots this messenger bag provides. One may want to weigh the value comparing how much of the space you would need and actually use (a good comparison is Belkin's own 17 inch messenger bag).

Having said that, the messenger bag is really spacious. Innovation in this space is not going to be "hot", but the sheer number of pockets (external and internal)provides this bag an excellent utilitarian design (it has so many pockets, it is taking me a while to get used to my "organization").

The padding is just average; the strap is about 2 inch thick and has more shoulder padding than the one I am using now - however, the hooks attaching them to the bag is made of plastic and unsure how long it is going to hold up with all the stuff one can manage to store in this bag. Only time will tell. Very monochromatic traditional black appearance with a slightly smooth texture (this bag did not have the contrast the picture seems to be implying). I really like the trolley-pass-through design - a must for any frequent air travelers.

Overall, a well-designed product with a classic design - price is the only real concern. For a value-conscious shopper, this should be a good comparator and a fine choice.

Reading through some of the reviews from 3+ years ago, it seems that not much has changed with the product design or its appeal. It still does not come with a pass through USB - if that's important to you, look elsewhere. The fan comes in two settings - in the higher setting of the two, it does get noisy and a bit distracting. At the lower setting, it is not that noisy, but for something with a fan, it is very "quiet".  I frequently travel to Asian regions where temperatures can reach 100-110F.  This cooler has helped me become less paranoid about my laptop.  Since you can power it off your laptop, it eliminates the need for any other power converter, etc - an excellent design feature.  It looks stylish (enough for me, at least) and sturdy enough.  If you mostly use your laptop at your desk - this has the obvious added benefit of raising the laptop - eliminating some wrist pain.  Overall, a great value.

Overall, this is a great product. My frequent overseas travels has made me very nervous about data storage and some required redundancy. Plus, all the travels is also keeping my digital cameras quite busy. eGo not only provides excellent storage, but operates with minimal noise, never has displayed a tendency to "overheat", and the file transfers are quite fast. To me, it is also very critical that my storage device can be taken on my travels without having to worry about power transformers. eGO fits that bill as well - it supports 100-240V input (you may still need a plug adapter, though).

Though the transfer speeds are good, it would have been great if the eGO supported the eSATA interface also. A very minor complaint is that I wish the base 'holder' that comes along with it covered more length than what it does now...perhaps they designed it to be able to hold vertically as well.

A prudent shopper should keep monitoring the prices - it sometimes drops by almost 30%.

This little radio was smaller than I expected, but that's not necessarily a bad thing. It's nice for portability's sake, and there's no particular advantage to having a large emergency radio as long as it works well.

This one works pretty well for me at least; it gets the stations I care about in an emergency. It does charge up pretty quickly with a USB charger, but it charges very slowly with the hand crank and the solar charger. Then again, it's been pretty cloudy when I have tried to charge it with solar so I couldn't say how well it would work on a nice, clear, sunny day, but in emergencies the weather isn't always very cooperative, either. It's good to have options, but you shouldn't depend on them too much. That said, if you keep them charged then you shouldn't have to charge them from a dead start.

I am not going to test the waterproof claim, as I don't think it would survive such a test. I plan to treat it as though it is not waterproof at all, as it doesn't really look or feel like it's built well enough to actually be waterproof. But I can't say for certain without potentially destroying it.

If you don't have an emergency weather radio, this would be a fair enough option to cover your potential emergency needs. It's always better to have one and not need it than to need one and not have it, and at only around $30, this one seems adequate.

I was skeptical that this mount would hold my TV. If yours is on the upper end of the weight and size limits like mine is, you might find that it wobbles when you go to adjust it.

My TV is a 75 inch model, weighing about 117 pounds. The mount holds it just fine, but you will want to make sure you are solidly attached to studs in the wall! Also, you will have to torque down the hand grip to keep the angle where you want it, as it will tend to sag a lot otherwise. In fact I had to torque it down while someone else was holding the TV at a much higher angle than I actually wanted, because once they release the weight, it sags considerably.

The mount doesn't sit flush against the wall, there is about a 3-inch gap. It can be pulled out away from the wall and tilted sideways without too much difficulty, although it will wobble when you move it if your TV is heavy. This makes me a little nervous just because of the weight involved. The amount that it can tilt to the side depends on the size of your TV. Larger units will be more limited than smaller ones. The bracket can tilt quite a bit, but the wall itself creates a physical barrier for larger units.

This mount really requires at least two decently strong individuals to install. I wouldn't recommend trying to do it alone. Make sure you have a good stud finder, and try tapping in test nails before drilling just to make sure. A small level is included with the mount.

I seem to have bad luck when it comes to getting these things to fit right. Either they fit over my eyes, or they fit over my ears, but I can't ever seem to get them to fit over both my eyes and my ears at the same time.

They fit well enough to get them to work okay, though, and they are good for travel when you want to cancel out both noise and light. I just wish I could get them to fit a little better, because then they would be ideal.

With the purchase of my new phone, my wired earphones no longer could connect to my phone. I shopped around, and decided to order this pair. I am so glad I did! These truly last for hours. I am truly shocked by how long they last, especially in the case that powers them even if the case isn't plugged in. Because the case has a battery that charges while plugged in, you can use these earbuds while traveling and have one charging while using the other.

The sound quality is pretty good for such small earbuds, and they come with different sized silicone tips to fit a variety of ear shapes for comfort. The case is a little heavy since it has such a great battery, but the fact you can use them for at least 24 hours if you use one at a time on a full charge makes up for the heavier weight.

I found this mouse to be quite responsive. It is easy to set up and use. I did not notice any lag or any other issues; the mouse works seamlessly with my setup which is to say that I hardly notice the mouse at all because it simply does what it should. That's pretty much all I can really ask of a computer mouse, for it to just do its job quietly without making me notice it.

I really like the shape of this tower. It has a pretty small footprint so it doesn't take up a lot of space, but it's not top-heavy so it isn't going to topple over. It can be placed on the ground, or on a table or desk top.

It has a whopping16 outlets, each with ground, as well as 4 USB A outlets (it seems more and more electronics require this now days) and one USB C outlet. This one station should easily handle all of my computer station power needs. It has a handle on top, and the blue illuminated design lets you know it has power and makes it look high-tech.

I have yet to test the power surge protection-- with luck I'll never need to-- but it otherwise definitely seems to work well. The cord is nice and solid, and feels like it can handle the current.

I tested these binoculars in a variety of conditions. Against a bright backlit sky, they do have some purple/green fringing. A little chromatic aberration is not uncommon, but for the price of these binoculars I would expect less of it.

I took them out bird watching recently about an hour before sundown on an overcast day, and found that they captured the light very well. I had no trouble distinguishing between tree swallows and violet green swallows from across a large pond even on this late, cloudy afternoon.

They are fairly lightweight and they have a small profile, and the rubber coating feels tough, like it is well bonded to the metal. They feel pretty solid, as well.

As is often the case, I found that these don't fit my eyes very well; I have a medium-sized head, but my eyes are a tiny bit closer together than average, and these eyepieces just won't adjust that close together. I can see through them okay, but the image only overlaps for about 2/3 of the view. I feel I should note that the rubber straps that hold the protective end caps will prevent the eyepieces from dialing as close together as they can if you remove them.

These binoculars come with a fabric bag with its own strap, and with a strap is included for the binoculars as well. At this price I would have liked more carrying options.

Overall, I think these are nice binoculars, although I do feel that the price is pretty steep for what you get.

[[VIDEOID:2b8bb26ef242fcb874bd3c461ac0e558]] For the price, this is a decent circular polarizing filter for amateurs who want to get into using a polarizing filter. It includes a UV filter that I consider just an extra.

I personally don't recommend the use of UV filters unless you are shooting film, as they generally don't improve image quality on modern digital cameras and, if anything, can only degrade it. I know that a lot of people consider them a layer of protection for their expensive lenses, but I am of the opinion that having a cheap UV filter on your expensive lens is actually more likely to damage it. Case in point, the threads on this filter are very sharply cut. You can feel and hear them grinding when you screw it into place, and when it is tightened down snug, the sharp threads want to lock it into place. If the lens was knocked hard on the corner with the filter in this position, the UV filter might actually become stuck in place and damage the threads of the lens, requiring expert repairs to remove the filter and repair the lens. In my experience, just keeping the lens hood in place offers far more protection than a UV filter possibly could.

With that out of the way, let's get to the meat of this review, which is the CPL filter. For the price, this will perform perfectly well. It will darken the sky when used properly in the right conditions, and can help reduce glare and reflections. It seems to have no discernible color cast which would be a problem. In fact the only real issue I have with this filter is related to the mechanical function.

First of all, the threads are very sharply cut, as mentioned previously with the UV filter. This isn't the end of the world, but it is coupled by the fact that the rotating ring on the CPL filter is also very, very stiff and resists turning quite a lot. In order to turn it, as is necessary for adjusting it to the present conditions, you will need to tighten the filter down onto your lens more than I would like, and with such sharp threads, this increases the risk of the threads locking firmly onto your lens. It is possible for them to lock so firmly that it could be quite difficult to remove it from your lens. While $30 is a pretty good bargain for what is otherwise a pretty decent filter, it's not such a bargain if it runs the risk of costing you a lot of money in repairs to your expensive gear. If you are using a cheap lens, then this cheap filter should be just fine. If you have shelled out lots of money for an expensive lens, I would not recommend cheaping out on the filters.

In the end I settled on 4 stars because the glass is pretty decent quality, and if you are aware of the limitations you can safely use it so long as you avoid tightening it down too much. It's just a little less convenient. But it otherwise works well.

For the price I wasn't expecting too much from this tripod, but it is a surprisingly good one and I'm very pleased. It has enough heft to give it good stability, but it's not so heavy that I wouldn't want to take it with me photographing wildlife in the bush. Even when extended to its impressive full height, it still feels nice and stable. I don't fear that my heavy telephoto lenses are going to topple it over resulting in their breakage, and there isn't any wobble while handling the camera. There is of course a hook at the bottom if you want to add more weight for further stability in high winds.

I like having the swivel head with handle, which makes it easy to track birds and other subjects. There is a fair bit of resistance to keep its movement nice and smooth. You do need to tighten the head down very tight, or else it will come un-threaded when you pan to the left. The tripod has a nice strap to carry it, which feels strong enough to do the job. The carrying case is also nice and feels sturdy.

The ability to convert it a monopod is one that could come in handy as well, especially if you don't feel like carrying the entire tripod with you, or if you are using your camera where a full tripod might be too intrusive, cumbersome, or unwelcome.

The locks are made from metal. They feel strong, and are easy to quickly use. There is a hex key designed to be held in place on the tripod head which can be used to adjust the stiffness of the leg hinges; I wish that the magnet which holds it in place were a stronger, as the key is easy to accidentally dislodge and when this happens it drops to the ground. It if didn't make a loud clinging noise upon landing (on soft ground or carpet for instance) it would be easy to lose it.

All in all, I recommend this tripod if you're looking for an affordable option that doesn't suffer from the issues you typically encounter in tripods found within this price range.

I am using this TV as my primary PC monitor. Since I don't have my PC stationed at a desk but rather use a wireless keyboard and mouse to remotely sit where I want to, the screen can be on my wall and I can comfortably sit back in my La-Z-Boy recliner several feet away while doing work, surfing the web, gaming, or whatever. This screen is really perfect for this, with a 120 hertz rate and 4k graphics. And of course it still maintains all the regular functionality of a TV as well.

I primarily use my computer to illustrate books for my day job, and this screen really makes my illustrations look great! Set to "Graphics" mode (rather than "Entertain" mode) the colors are true and the shadows retain great detail; the highlights are smooth, and clean. The color profile is easy to adjust. I really appreciate all of this very much. In the "Entertain" mode, the colors are amped up and the graphics are sharpened, etc. This is nice for watching films and gaming, but for doing graphics work it's absolutely necessary to have the colors and details represented accurately. The excellent anti-reflection and anti-glare features are also extremely helpful in this regard.

The native speakers are about what you would expect; they aren't amazing, but they aren't really all that bad for what this TV is intended to be either. It's really all about the screen. I personally don't care too much about the speakers, because 95% of the time that I use the screen I'm wearing headphones anyway so that I don't disturb my family. But if you're a real audiophile and that sort of thing is important to you, I would suggest you get some nice speakers to go with the TV, because the built-in speakers are clearly only meant to be just good enough to pass muster, and aren't anything to be wowed by.

For me, it's really nice that it doubles as a picture frame when I'm not actively using it for anything else. I have loaded an assortment of my own favorite photographs and illustrations for it to cycle through, and they look really great on this screen, but you can also access a fairly good assortment of art through the TV itself. This turns what is typically a bit of an eyesore in my opinion (I don't like the intrusive look of too much electronic technology in my home) into a lovely, active decoration instead.

I have not ordered a decorative frame to customize it; the reviews on those seem to indicate that they are perhaps overpriced and fragile, and I think it would be easy enough to make my own anyway, which I plan to do. I think having a frame on it would just be the cherry on top, so to speak.

And to reassure anyone who is wondering about the review that said this is the 2021 model, I think there must have been some confusion on one end or the other, because I definitely received the 2022 model that I ordered.

It came with the "Slim-Fit Wall Mount" included in the box (it's in the Styrofoam packing; I think another reviewer might have just not seen it, as it's not very large and it weighs much less than you might expect) along with a decent length of "One Invisible Connection" cable to attach it to the "One Connect Box" controller. This cable is just silver braid with a clear coating on it to help it blend in better than a regular black plastic cable. It serves as a power source as well as controlling the TV, so there's no bundle of unsightly cables hanging down from the screen.

The connect box replaces the usual bulk of the TV, which is what allows the screen to hang so flat on the wall like a regular picture frame. To use the TV, you'll need to position the One Connect box where you can use the remote to control it. It can be positioned anywhere so long as it's within reach of the cable. You can buy longer "One Invisible Connection" cables if necessary. The one that was included was long enough for my needs.

I got this to replace my old 1080p webcam. The picture quality is far superior, the wide angle is very nice. It's easy to plug-and-play requiring no software to upload. The optional tripod is nice because it puts the camera closer to eye-level, so I'm not looking up high or down low at the viewer on the other end. I very much like the built-in shutter for privacy security; no need to stick tape over the webcam when not in use!

No negatives to add; this is a great value.

Easy to pair with multiple devices. The sound from this speaker is bigger than it would have you think. I haven't tested how waterproof it is, but it does have a plug for the charging ports. Great for picnics, backyard BBQs, camping, parties, trips to the beach or whatever. The light display has 4 different options as well, and the fact that it can be left off is nice for when you want to remain subtle and prolong battery charge.

This won't allow you to track your keys' location through an app or anything like that, but it is an affordable option to help you find your keys if you have a tendency to misplace them around your house. The 4 fobs correspond to the 4 buttons on the remote, so you can use them to help you track 4 different sets of keys, or attach one to your wallet, one to your phone, one to your cat's collar, or whatever else it is that you tend to lose around the house.

The alarm is fairly loud, but not ear-splittingly so. If your keys are in your purse or under a couch cushion it may be a bit difficult to hear from another room. The remote seems to have a range of about 30-ish feet, so if you have a large house you may need to roam through it while pressing the button.

One thing to consider if you're worried about losing your keys while out and about is that you need to have the remote in order to activate the alarm. If you leave your remote at home and then can't find your keys while you're out, you won't be able to use this device to help you find them.

The remote does include a tiny flashlight, presumably to help you find your keys, but the light it emits is incredibly dim, I'd guess around 5 lumens (and of a weird, purplish-green hue). I wouldn't bother using it unless you need to find your keys in complete darkness for some reason and you have no other light options available. Frankly, the light is a gimmick at best. If I were rating this for the light only, I would give it 1 star. However, I feel like the light is not really the main point of the device.

It does come with all necessary batteries; you will need to install them in order to use it.

All in all I'd say this is a good product, but not a great one; it feels a bit cheaply made, but it does what it's meant to do, and for the low price I'm not sure what more you could ask for.

When it comes to zip ties; they either do what they're supposed to, or they don't. If you are simply expecting these to hold things together reasonably well, then they are perfectly adequate for the task. However, when I tested them by tying them to weights and using them to lift, I found that they broke about 1/2 the time at 30 pounds, never quite reaching 40 pounds.

They are reliably good for 20 pounds without breaking, which is not too bad, really, for something so small. While I feel that the 40 pound claim is somewhat misleading, they are actually comparable to most similar sized ties on the market as far as I can tell, and it's doubtful that most others would perform any better. If you're not using them to lift heavy weights then they'll work just fine, and you'd be hard pressed to find a better price for this quantity of similar ties.

The results speak for themselves; they perform the task they are meant to perform, and they won't cost you an arm and a leg.

Compared to other high performance headphones, their small, lightweight design is also comfortable for extended wear. I'm not a highly qualified audiophile, but the sound is rich and true to my ears. This little guy comes with 7 tools and each is good for its own area of cleaning.

Keycap puller: To be honest I have not used this as none of my devices have raised keys but looks like it would work nicely.

Screen cleaner bottle: it is small and doesn't spray a ton at a time, which sounds like a downside but is not. It sprays the perfect amount of fluid so the screen is not soaking wet. It is also refillable so you can use your own fluid if you prefer.

Big brush: This is good for sweeping off laptop keys and general dust. It worked wonderfully and can also retract into the body when not in use.

Wipe pad: Very useful when used along with fluid together they made stubborn smudges disappear.

Microfiber cloth: Decent microfiber cloth cleaned away the smudges and left the screen pretty darn clear.

Qtip stick (not its real name just what it reminded me of): I didn't really know what this was for until I looked around my area and saw my earbuds case. This got down into where the ear tips sit and pulled up a frankly embarrassing amount of crud.

Detail tool: This gets into the really small opening, it has a silicone tip for larger openings, but it can be removed to get into smaller ones. I used this to clean my mice and it did a wonderful job.

All in all it's a great little tool to give your laptop and other electronics a deep clean.

Great clamp, but for attaching a neck strap I prefer the [[ASIN:B00WOUTNW0 Desmond DAC-38 38mm QR Clamp 1/4" Screw Hole & 3 Strap Bosses]]. Yes, this clamp is lighter and a little smaller but I'm not a fan of the 3/8-16 threaded hole that requires I use the 3/8-16 x 1/4-20 adapter to attach a strap. The 38mm clamp has a 1/4-20 hole so there's no extra piece to fiddle with and risk coming unscrewed. More importantly, between the countersink at the top and the recess on the bottom, the threaded hole is quite short. The hole in the 38mm clamp has about twice the thread length, making it that much more secure. Also, unlike this clamp, the 38mm clamp has a solid flat bottom, which I prefer.
If your main concern is weight and bulk, this is still a fine clamp.

So the best part of the Bluetooth headphones are not only the price, it tells you when it's ON and OFF as well as when it connected. The buds are comfortable, sound is perfect. Battery last longer than others .The packaging is beautiful. It will make a good gift. I recommend it 💯
I really like thos headphones, the sound is excellent, battery life is great. It's an excellent quality. It also cancels out noise.

So this headphone was good while it lasted. Overall the sound is good the mic is also amazing. The way the buds are built are great they just fit into the ears comfortably. But unfortunately for me it didn't last as long as I thought it would. It was a good buy.
[[VIDEOID:5d67c33a5f9e333585dc8fa15620737b]] Volumes on the side are an upgrade from my remote. Affordable and doesn’t need to be programmed. Great buy!
[[VIDEOID:4a6c817db05af0f79b409687469a5d15]] Noise level is pretty loud for the little speaker! It’s cute and has a weight to it. Will update if it doesn’t last!
Loves this item, noise cancel, surround sound without irritating eardrums. Let my 8 year old use them and it wasn’t comfortable for her around the ears. Better suited for adults

My daughter says they’re perfect. Retractable, comfortable, noise canceling, surround sound, and you’re able to change to the next song by clicking a side button. She absolutely loves the style as well! Great quality at a great price!

I recently started working from home and have been using my AirPod pros to make and take calls. Using my AirPods 8-10 hours a day has really irritated my ear drums. Came across this headset and thought to give it a try. I really like the comfort feel of the headset versus sticking my AirPods in my ear. Now don’t get me wrong the AirPods are great for my runs and going to the gym, but having a headset separate for work and not irritating my ear drums is a MUST. My clients can hear me clear and there’s no static. Truly a great item to consider

Great size AND unexpectedly loud! Definitely tried out the waterproof feature in my pool - this is ideal for water fun and just having kids around in general lol! I’m excited to try it on my bike next!!

I can connect my white noise program from my phone to my older surround system and have the white noise and rain sounds I need to cover up the snoring dogs!!!  AMAZING!  No connectivity problems at all, just have to reconnect when the power goes out.
I was required to have one for grad school. This screen makes everyone else's look like garbage. Very high quality!

A friend of mine had me try a pair of bone conduction head piece a couple of years ago. Was so strange how well I was able to hear the music without something being in my ear.
Saw these bone conduction earbuds and I had to try them out. I like that I can clip them onto my ear instead of having something shoved into my ear. Won't even try to figure out how they work but, they work.
I am able to hear my music just fine and my ears are open so I can also hear if someone is talking to me.
Not sure if I'd like them better if they were connected by some type of wire of sorts so that I can pop them out and have them hang on my neck when I don't want to use them.
Sound is nice. Nice being able to use earbuds and not have it in my ear.

This comes with a plug in adapter. Thing is, it can't be plugged into an outlet that's on the wall. The light is too heavy and it just sags down and falls out of the outlet.
The other thing is that it has to hang upside down. Unless I missed a setting to switch that. But, I figured out a solution. I put mine into an outside house light where the bulb is upright. I put this light camera into the socket then turned the entire light fixture around so that it's hanging upside down. Is now protected from the rain.
The picture is perfect. Can zoom in and pan around our entire back yard. Which is exactly what we needed.
Instructions that came with this camera didn't say we can add a SD card to it. Wish we had that option so we can save data if we wanted to instead of paying for cloud service.
The light it has is just a few little lights that turn on while it's running. Nothing that has any real use for using as an outdoor light.
Was so easy to download the app and get the camera connected to our WiFi. Honestly didn't even look at the instructions for getting it up and running. Just looked for info on adding a SD card.
Like this and happy to have this.

I wanted a nice small am/fm radio that I can just listen to music through. Yes, I have access to many different ways of getting music but, nothing compares to simple am/fm sometimes.
The device is light and nice and small. Easily fits into my pocket. I also love that it's rechargeable so there's no batteries.
Even has a cute metal antenna. Something I haven't seen in years.
This cute little radio brings me back to my childhood. Sound is great.
Will be using this all the time when I go walking.

I like the size of this camera. Nice and small so I can easily place it in a smaller space or shelf.
Does come with everything needed. Even hardware so I can place this on a wall if I wanted to.
Setting this up was fairly easy. Download the app then follow instructions for setting it up.
For the price, this is a nice security camera. Does follow movement. The delay time is very short.
One thing is that this does not come with a SD card. Not a big issue for me for where I'll be having this camera set up. But, if you want to look at data later on, which many will want to do, you'll have to purchase one.
Does have audio so I can listen and talk to anyone in the room I have this set up in.
Good enough speaker, again, for the price.
Night vision is nice.
Definitely a good value for this smaller security camera.

Always having trouble thinking what to get an older child, this speaker makes it so much easier.
First, it's super cute. Second, it works great. Doesn't have the deep bass sound but, it's still great for a child.
The base stays plugged in. The sphere is charged up then lasts for at least 4 hours of solid use.
Not sure how long it would last if only turned on for about 15 mins at a time.
Great gift idea.
Younger kids love it.

I have a horrible cell phone. So many problems when I'm on a call with someone. I don't like earbuds so I wanted to try headphones.
Was easy to charge up. The instructions were a little confusing. Says to hit the MFB button and I had no idea what button that was. It also states to hit "/" What in the world is that? There's only 3 buttons on the side of the earpiece and none of them have "/" on it.
Now for phone calls. I tried it out this morning. Was so happy that my sister was able to hear me. I was able to hear her but it did sound a bit muffled. But, was still able to understand her. Just wish it was a bit more clear.
Headphones were easy to wear. Ear pads were comfortable. Did cancel out noise in the room.
Not exactly sure what the Aux cable is suppose to go into. New phones don't have that option anymore. Everything is bluetooth.
So far I'm 95% happy with these headphones. Great price.

My other shower speaker died and wanted to replace it.
First thing I noticed is that it doesn't do this loud squeal when I turn it on or off. Goes on nice and quiet.
The sound quality is nice for a shower speaker.
Spouse loves it because I can have my music playing while I'm showering or in the bathroom and I don't disturb her by having to have it too loud.
So happy that this speaker is much better than the one I used to have.

My wife got me this for my upcoming birthday and I love it.
I listen to music, watch tv/movies and listen to audiobooks often through my smartphone. This device works perfectly for all three purposes.
The Bluetooth synch up worked quickly and easily. Not always the case with other devices.
The sound is impressive for such a compact speaker! Great bass sound!
