The buttons on the front of the speaker are very useful. Allowing forward/reverse/pause/play functions. Phone answer/hang-up functions.

The sound fills my home office. I noticed as I walked away from the speaker down a 30 foot hall could hear the speaker clearly all the way to the end of the hall at about 70% volume.
I haven't tried it outside yet (too cold), but am sure I will use it when sitting on my back patio.
Also haven't tested how long the battery life lasts, but it charges quickly.

Great product!

One thing that impressed me to get this doorbell is that it stated that it didn't have monthly fees. Once I'm reading about it, I am finding out that some of the great things included with this doorbell is only free for 6 months. After that there is a monthly fee. Not for everything. But, for some of the nicer conveniences this doorbell offers.
It does come with everything you need to install it. Including a drill bit so you have the exact size needed.
It also includes a 32GB SD card.
Once installed, I did the hard wire installation, you need to download the app and set it all up.
The video quality is great. The color night vision is nice. Audio also works great.
What I'm not too sure about is what exactly I'll be having to pay for after the 6 month trial.
I know facial recognition, voice messaging, and the anti-theft alarm. Might be fun to have for the 6 month trial but, I'm not sure if I really want to get used to it then have to lose it after 6 months.
I think I'm going to skip the 6 month "fun things to try" trial. But, it's a nice option for people to have if they want it.

I wanted some type of security camera for a certain area that's indoors. A place where I can't get power to until I get someone here to somehow run a USB line and get power to it. So a battery one was my perfect option right now.
The video quality isn't the best. I had to find the perfect spot for it so that I can get a clear view when I need it.
Night vision is fine.
Motion detection is a little slow and I don't think it's a 30 ft reaction zone. But again, I am using this indoors and have it set up where the motion detection works fine.
I don't need the audio so I really don't know how well that will work.
Very easy to set up. And easy to download and get it connected to the app.
I don't trust any type of mounting tape so have it up using a screw.
For what I really needed this camera for, it's fantastic! I'm hoping they're right about battery lasting a few months.

What I like about this camera is that I can use this for any room in my house. For us, I decided to use it in the living room. First, because I can pan it down a bit more than some others so I can see more of the floor where my pets are.
It's very easy to set up. Downloaded the app and registered, plugged it in, set up our WiFi, and it was ready to go.
It did take me a little looking to find where to insert the SD card. (in front bubble part at the bottom)
The only problem I had was when I hit the record button on the app. Worked fine until I closed the app. Then it came up with a "failed" notification that popped up.
When I try to look back at video it says "hmm...there's no video in this time".
So right now I can only use this in real time until I can talk with a tech to figure out what is wrong. Or figure this out myself. I might format the SD card and try setting it all up again.
But, I like the picture quality in daytime and in night vision. Audio is a little delayed but works fine.
The panning and zoom function are great too.

Having puppies in the house means things might get chewed up. Our wires were one they got.
I like having the 6 ft length. Perfect for where I needed to run the wires. And now having them clipped up and out of reach of little teeth, they'll be nice and safe.
I like that these wires are a bit thinner than the rubber coated wires I had before. Plus, they're silver and a little harder to see.
Speakers sound as good as ever with these new wires.

Setup was super easy. Just download the app, register, plug in the camera, set WiFi password, and you're ready to go.
If you click on the gear icon you can set up basic settings for this camera.
The only thing I noticed is that when I do full screen, I can use my finger on my phone, swipe, and move the camera view. I have to go back to smaller screen to move it.
I like the zoom this has. Not too sensitive.
I also like that I can get part of my floor where my dogs are at times. And its very quiet when scanning.
Motion alert works great. Have to keep that turned off unless we're leaving the house.
Audio has a little delay but, works fine.
I like that i can have night vision set at auto. This way it will automatically switch to night vision on its own.
Nice security camera that will make me feel a little better knowing I can see if there's any problem in the house when we're gone.

My first complaint about any earbuds is that they're uncomfortable wearing. I didn't find that with these earbuds.
I wear earbuds many hours during the day and then I like to have them in on the nights I can't sleep. These are very comfortable. No irritation at all.
Love how long they do hold the charge. I can wear them most of the night and they still are almost fully charged when I get up in the morning.
After charging up the case, it only takes about 30 mins to fully recharge the earbuds back to 100%.
They seem very well made. The sounds that come out of these are excellent. Can hear all music very clearly.
Like everything about these earbuds.

My driveway isn't overly long but, long enough and wraps around trees so it makes it hard to see when a car entered the driveway.
So easy to install. After initial charge up, the sun will keep it powered up. So far we've had sun almost daily so there's been no problem there. Did go 2 days without any sun. Held the charge and worked great on the 3rd day.
I have the sensors set up a little up my driveway. Keeps them safer from stealing hands. And I can keep them in a more sunny spot for charging.
It took me a couple of days to get used to the sound it makes when the sensor is triggered. With so many items in our home that makes some noise, I had to learn what this driveway sensor sounded like and learn its tune.
I love knowing when guests are arriving or when a delivery truck/mail truck comes. I don't have to worry about packages sitting on my porch getting wet from rain or have to worry about anyone coming up and stealing the packages.
These would actually work great if you have an entry, into your yard, that you can't see very well. Would know instantly if your gate is opened and someone entered the yard.
Nice easy alarm sensors that have been working great for over a month now.

First thing I noticed, after opening the box, is that there are power cables connected to this camera. For me it isn't a big issue but, for someone ordering a wireless security camera it would be a huge issue.
Installation was more complicated for me since I had to drill a hole into the garage wall to feed the power cord through. After doing that I connected the power cord that comes with this camera, then plugged it into the outlet in the garage.
What I like about this camera is that when the motion detection is activated the lights come on to warn any intruders that they're being video'd. Plus it gives the night vision a little extra light that will capture face features a lot easier. Has a loud enough deterrent alarm plus 2 way audio so I can talk to whoever set it off.
I can save the snapshot or video right to the SD card or to the cloud if I need to. I also like that this supports a SD card up to 128G. And I can view in real time any time I need to.
Picture is real nice and clear. Haven't had any issues with any trespassers so don't know how it'll actually work. But, with the test runs we've done it's working just fine.
The 100 degree viewing area is a big plus. My driveway is a little long so having the 98 ft viewing in night vision really helps if cars are in the street and not the driveway.
So far I'm really happy with this outdoor security camera.

Such a nice and easy setup this was with this camera. Buying a SD card is a must. Wish I could have one bigger than 64GB. But, did purchase what I could use with this.
The first thing I like is that it has motion detection with an alert to my phone. I think nowadays that's so important to have with any security camera. The second thing I like is that it can be rotated so I can view the entire room that this camera is in. I haven't set up any particular detection areas for it to focus on. Since I can view the room, I might not need to use that function.
The night vision works well. I am able to see in the room with no problem at all.
The two way audio helps so we can let guests into the home when we're not there and we can talk with them to let them know that we're just about home.
This claims that it will still work if the WiFi is unstable. Not sure what will happen if we lost power. That I'll have to wait to see what happens during a big summer storm.
This security camera is exactly what I needed in our room we need to monitor.

The only thing I would suggest, to whoever does the advertising, is to use spellcheck. Having so many words misspelled in this advertisement would make buyers a little wary.

Because we wanted this outdoors and didn't want to worry about charging it up all the time, we had someone install this for us. I'm not tech savy on installing things like this so it was easier and better to have someone else do it for me. Because of that, I can't speak on how difficult this is to install.
I needed something set up showing my driveway. This way I would know who is here, what time they came, and what the vehicle looks like using our smartphones.
Many times we're out when guests are suppose to come. I can get an alert on when they are there and I can talk to them to let them know the code to our garage and when we'll be back.
The daytime video is good. The 2 way audio works great. The night vision is a great feature to have. Not sure how well it will do in complete darkness. There are some lights outside so the night vision feature works even better because it has some light already. Plus this camera has a motion spotlight on it so it has even more light to see with the video.
Because of the lights, there are also flying bugs around. I've had to lower the sensitivity a little so I'm not alerted when a moth is nearby.
I've only tested the siren once to see what it sounded like. Was loud enough to get the attention of a neighbor or two and hopefully scare off anyone that shouldn't be in our driveway.
Because I can link it to our Alexa, I can just ask her to show me the driveway and have the video pop up for me to see.
So far I've been very happy with this security camera. Keeping me aware of who's around my house 24/7. And that's exactly what I want.

Needed something attached to my keys where I can find them when I come into the house and lay them somewhere and then forget where I laid them.
Downloading the app and setting up this key finder was very easy. Directions are very simple to follow.
It has a cute little chime sound when I push the call button in the app itself. It's not real loud so you might have to walk around until you can hear it.
The only thing I don't like, and it's only my preference, is that my phone does a chime alarm when I leave the house, with my phone and no keys. Not a big issue and it only does it about 4-5 chimes before it shuts off.
I think I can turn that off by turning off the notification on my phone. But again, it's just a few chimes so no big deal.
I like that this comes in a pack of 4 key finders. I have one on my keys, our other set of keys, and I rigged it so I can have one on our tv remote! The 4th key finder will go on something else that I always misplace.
This will save me a LOT of time not tearing the house up looking for my keys.

This device is something I use around the house when my power goes out. It provides AM/FM, as well as, Weather Band radio.
The emergency power comes from either a hand crank, solar panel, or USB (all to recharge LI-ion batteries).
The flashlight has three modes, all fairly bright, of far beam, dipped beam or combo of both.
The volume is surprising for a little unit. It fills my family room.
Seems to be sturdily made.
The popup book light is activated my motion sensor to save battery. So if no motion is detected after a certain amount of time it cuts off until motion is again detected.

Nice unit for a nice price!

I love the versatility of this emergency multi-use tool!
It is powered by a rechargeable battery that comes with a hand crank, or you can flip the switch and run off of 3 AAA batteries. The rechargeable battery can also be powered up by sunlight as there is a solar panel on the top of the item.
It comes with a flashlight and a pop up reading light. The flashlight is bright enough to light up my hallway that is 30 feet away to the end.
The radio bands provided are FM/AM/WB (weather band).
Radio signals come in clear and loud with the short antennae is fully extended.
The volume is enough to fill my family room that is about 20 x 30.
Another option is the Alarm/SOS switch which triggers a wavering sound and a flashing red LED light.

I also love the power source function of this item. I can plug in my portable devices, phone, tablet etc. thru a USB port to charge them during loss of power.

Very useful item for a reasonable price! It is small and lightweight. I am replacing a portable speaker/radio that i used during power outages that weighed about 25 lbs. so this is much more handy.

First have to say to get a SD card right away! I didn't realize I needed one so had to wait a day to finally sit and try to set this up.
I read the instructions a few times before I began setting this dashcam up. I tried going to the support page they have listed in the booklet but, every time I tried I got this message.."Your connection is not secure
The owner of support.zenfox.com has configured their website improperly. To protect your information from being stolen, Waterfox has not connected to this website. (I did this with Firefox and Chrome also with same results)
After the SD card was formatted and put in the unit, I installed this on my windshield with no problem at all.
I also downloaded the Zenfox app onto my Android phone. But, will go into that in a bit.
Setting this up wasn't too hard. It's SO hard to see the little screen and the little icons on it. Wish they had the icons in a different brighter color so they stand out a bit more. So, until I go back out with a magnifying glass and a flashlight, I'll have to wait to get it completely set up the way I want it.
Did drive with it on last night. The inside camera picture covers up the front view a little so you don't get a clear view of what's in front of you looking at the little screen. Looked really nice and clear!
When the record function is working, the light on it stays red. It's a very light light so it's hard to see if it's light outside. If it isn't working then it'll blink and you'll hear a beeping sound. The microphone is red when working, off when it's not. Again, it's hard to see the light when it's daytime.
One thing I noticed is that the screen goes dark after a certain amount of time. It looks like it's off. I did open the phone app and saw that I could see the pictures so I figured it was still recording. Could be a setting I need to change?
Now with the phone app. What I like about it first. I like that I can open the app and see what the camera is seeing. I can also change any settings using the app. Very nice and convenient. So much easier than doing it with the dashcam itself.
What I don't like about it is that the dashcam has to be turned on, by means of turning the car on, to be able to use the app. Tried it out the first time last night and getting past the WiFi setting was a pain. I don't have WiFi when I'm driving so there's no way to connect to it. After 7 mins of fiddling around with it, I finally got past that part (don't know how) and saw the camera view on my phone.
I was going to try to check out the different settings but couldn't until I turned the camera off. Because I didn't want to turn the dashcam off, change a setting, then turn it back on to see the difference over and over again, I just gave up and let it be. Should be able to change a view setting or any setting with the camera running so we can see what the difference is and see if we want to keep it changed.
Over with the confusing part of setting this up, I'll state what I really love about this dash cam.
If I'm in an accident, it will automatically lock that particular time in the loop program so that it won't be over written with new coverage. I can also hit the OK button to lock a particular time so that it won't be destroyed or overwritten. I love how clear the picture is. May look small on the small screen but, it's even better when you view it through your phone. And I'm sure much better if you view it through your tv or computer screen.
I like the peace it gives me that if I am in an accident, I have proof of it on film. Just a nice peace of mind when I'm driving now.
Now that this is completely installed and running great, I'll have to take the time and look at all the setup options I have in the phone app. I think I saw where I can format the SD card and maybe download updates using the app.
For someone not really tech smart with devices like this, I can't really tell you what is the best in the option settings they have. But like anything, what is good for me might not be the best setting for you.
I'll have to keep testing different settings with this to see what is what and what best fits my needs.
Overall it's a really nice dashcam with a nice clear picture. This is something I'll be using every time I have my vehicle on the road.

Not only is this camera great for watching a child in their room while sleeping, it's also great for keeping an eye on your pets when you're away from the home.
Directions were basic on setting this camera up. Down the app to a list of multiple devices. I chose smartphone app. Plug in the camera and get everything set up the way you want or need it via the app.
I love that I can remotely pan and tilt so I can see around the room. Makes a big difference when you can look around the room instead of just one small area.
No big deal for night time because this also has night vision so you can see even if the lights are off or you have a small night light on. I usually have a small light on in the house and I can see just fine. Picture clarity seems to be great.
The two way audio is also a big plus for me. If I notice my pups doing something they're not suppose to be doing, I can talk to them and hope they stop and listen.
The biggest deal, for me, is the motion/sound detection. Sends a notification straight to my phone so I can look at whats going on at that moment. Will be nice to have this set up in my living room for when we're out on vacation or out visiting friends for the day. I'll always have a set of eyes on my home. If my daughter pops over, I can the two way audio to tell her how soon it'll be before I'm home.
I haven't tried using it with Alexa yet. I also have to read more on the face recognition. Something I need to read up on and see what I need to do to set it all up.
I'll also have to look into the ethernet connection to my router so I'm always up to date with updates or new additions.
Over all I'm so happy with this security camera. Does everything I need it to do to make me feel more safe.

If you have coax connections in your house without terminators on them, try putting these on.  It will reduce the noise in your system and make your cable and internet (if provided by cable) work much better!

We all are going to have fun with this little printer gem. I did a test picture and it came out looking nice.
It does requires that your mobile device be connected to the Canon IVY Mini Photo Printer through Bluetooth. And you need to download the Canon Mini Print App. All the rest is as easy to get started.
There are certain areas, in our home, where kids and grandkids have designated areas for certain things. What I am going to do is take their picture then stick the picture in, or on, their certain areas they've claimed.
The first thing I'm going to do, my fun time with it, is to take pictures of their mom and dad, or a group family shot. Then I'm going to stick the picture either on the inside of their lunch bags, or boxes. This way when they open them up for their lunches, they can see those that love them the most.
I'm going to have to purchase more canon print paper because as soon as the older ones sees this, they're going to want to add photos to everything they own!
I really like how the photo paper is peel and stick. Kind of reminds me of those old cameras that printed out pictures right away. But way more advanced.
I know the older kids are going to want to print a picture of themselves with their girlfriends to stick on their notebooks or anything else.
The photo replacement paper that sells here on Amazon is really reasonably priced.
This printer is only 2x3" so it can be easily lost. I will be adding some type of string or bendable wire to this, somehow, so that I can attach it to something so it's never taken and forgotten.

I like the pivot motion fit design, as I can rotate the ear piece to find the perfect fit.
The sound is great! I notice that at the same volume level on my smartphone, the sounds is much louder than other ear buds I use.

Sweat resistance is nice, that it at least has some moisture protection. I don't exercise often but do get caught out in light rain while walking the yard sometimes.

Cord is just under 4 feet. Long enough for my needs as my smartphone is usually in my pocket or my PC close enough to me for that length to work well.
I am pretty picky about my ear buds. Only like the over the ear hook types Inside the ear must be comfortable as I will wear the for hours while working and listening to music, walking, or even while sleeping. These ear buds fit all of those requirements well.
Recommend them to other over the ear hook ear bud fans.

I really like this portable speaker. I like how small and light it is. And I like how it sounds.
Discovered that this speaker has 3 distinct features. Live Sound: I think this feature is suppose be like a three-dimensional music experience. Does it make me feel like I'm in the middle of a music fest? Haven't been to a festival in years so maybe I just don't remember what it sounded like. It's like the music is coming right at me through the speakers with it spreading the sound more in a vertical and horizontal direction. Can't tell if I'm hearing a bit of an echo when it's in that mode or if it's suppose to sound that way. But, I like it.
Party Booster: It will detect tapping, on the speaker itself, from five different directions because of the built-in accelerometer that it has. So, in a way it's like a drum which generates a sound over the music that's being played. And then it has a light reaction to the beat. I don't think I will bring this feature to attention. Having people drinking the hitting my speaker isn't something I want done. And I'm sure it would get very annoying after awhile.
And then Party Chain: This is a feature I haven't tried. I don't have multiple speakers to connect together to test this function out. But, it's suppose to create a wireless party chain where others can join in with the party booster to create additional sounds. With the price of this speaker on the higher end, I doubt I will ever add anymore speakers to it.
I do like that this is dust and waterproof. With our ever changing weather, I don't have to panic if it starts raining and I don't get the speaker inside right away. Or if we're out by the pool. No worries with splashing or wet hands on it.
The lights illuminate along the front and sides of the speaker and that pulse along with the music. It’s something Sony and other speakers have done before. It’s a fun addition, especially if you’re using the speaker in the dark. Thank goodness I can turn them off when I get tired of them. I only have music playing for a few hours when I'm outside when the rush of the day is finally over. Or on the weekends we will spend a few more hours outside working in the yard or again, just having some coffee and resting. As the summer starts, we'll be doing a lot more outdoor activities.
It's good to know that the battery of this speaker lasts up to 24 hours with the lights disabled. Haven't had the time to sit and run it for hours, with the light display on, to see how long the batteries last that way.
I will probably put this in the car every time we go out to spend time with friends or family. It's so nice and easy to bring with anywhere we go. Every so often we go camping. This speaker will be greatly appreciated by all when we're sitting around the fire pit at the end of the day.
We used to lug our large box speaker outside or over to friends homes. Happy that those days are done and over with.

I needed a wireless set of headphones for when I am outside cutting the grass, working in the yard, working in the house, or for when I just want to sit with a nice hot cup of coffee and chill.
These wireless headphones are perfect for everything I needed them for.
Not sure exactly how long they took to charge up. I set them up and went about my day. Came back a few hours later and they were all set to go.
Pairing them with my phone was as easy as can be. Directions were very easy to follow. Once paired, I just turn the headphones on, and I was good to go.
Music from my phone sounds really nice. One touch of the button and I can advance to the next song or hit the next button and I can go back to the previous song. Volume is great to cancel out the loud rumble of my lawnmower.
Very comfortable on my ears for the couple hours I've worn them. They don't have a lot of cushion like the more expensive headphones (not wireless) that I've had. But, for the price, they do well enough.
These will be used ALL the time between me and my wife. 6 hours of playing time is plenty of time for me to get my work done and then pass them onto my wife so she can enjoy her music while enjoying the sunshine.
Love them!
Haven't tried them with a phone call yet. Will have to come back and update this when I do.

I wanted just a small wireless speaker for when I'm in the kitchen. This speaker is perfect!
It's nice and small and looks cute. I added a strip of velcro to the back so I was able to stick it to the wall. I can easily take it down if I need to and stick it back up in a blink.
My phone is always nearby so no problem with connecting to it. Love how loud it can get. It's really nice for when I am baking something and can easily talk to my friends on the phone and stay hands free.
The one thing I didn't like is how it was packed for shipping. Was just tossed in a larger empty box and sealed up. Nothing to protect it from banging around. Is the company too cheap to secure it in the box or were the people, who packed it, lazy? Luckily no damage to the one I got.
Small details like that shows customers how much a company cares about their products.

Great Smart Watch for the low price.
It looks nice and it's thin enough to be comfortable on my wrist.
It's super easy to initially connect on bluetooth. So far almost all the apps work and function nicely with my iPhone. The texting app isn't working properly. But, since I can't text back, using the watch, it's fine that the text comes through the notification app. Remember to sync your contact list to the watch.
I do like that it counts my steps. I like to do a certain amount of steps per day and having a smart watch that does that is very important to me. The watch alerts me when I've reached my daily goals. It will interface with the app to record historical data and I can compare daily stats.
Having my heart rate and sleeping pattern isn't as important to me because I don't run or do heavy workouts but, it's a great feature for all those that do.
My daughter really likes to keep up on her sleeping patterns with her own smart watch. I only know people like doing this function because of her.
Having this Smart Watch offers a nice variety of great heart healthy apps if you use only one or all three.
I really like that I can play music via the watch. I was a little shocked on how great and loud the sound is.
Not sure how it works with Android phone but, you need to remember that after you connect it to your iPhone, you must then download the Fundo Wear app and connect it in order for the phone to sync its time & date, and for the notifications to work.
I'm reading that this also has many other nice functions. Different clock styles, stopwatch, calculator...etc. I haven't had time to sit and read up then try all the multiple functions this watch offers.
So far I haven't come across any big problems with this smart watch. If I do, I will come back and update. Right now it works great with all the functions that are important to me.

I still have some devices that do not have Bluetooth. For those devices these wired earbuds are very nice.
The sounds is excellent. Good through all the ranges, (base, midrange, treble).
The earbuds themselves are very comfortable to wear. Sometimes I forget I have them in my ears, which has not been my experience with other earbud designs.
It comes with a very nice carrying case to carry in a pocket without the wires getting tangled or the earbuds damaged. Once again something that can happen with other earbuds I have used.
It comes with a multitude of sleeves.
I would recommend these to anyone needing earbuds or earbud replacements.

Love it! Waited all year long to get this for Christmas. I have been owning an iPod (for music and video), a 7 inch Kindle (for books, music and video, and a laptop PC for email and everything else. Because of how much I like Amazon Prime Music and Music Unlimited, I decided to try to reduce the amount of high dollar items I need to replace every 3 to 4 years. So I am attempting to use the 10 inch Kindle to replace both the iPod and PC laptop.

So far so good. Email is easy to use. I have loaded the HP ePrint app to be able to print out bills I pay online, etc for records. Having the music available on any device is wonderful. I also have a 7 inch Kindle HDX my wife uses and access the music on my Android Smartphone as well.

The Kindle HD 10 has a wonderful picture. Nice to be able to use the Xfinity app to watch shows off my DVR, like Atlanta Hawks games while my wife watches something else on the large tv. Much better than watching on my 5 inch smartphone screen.

The audio is good and if I want to play it louder can send it over to one of my bluetooth speakers. I use the bluetooth keyboard and love it. That is what allows me to replace my PC as I can type emails rather than one finger type them.

I got the 16 GB with 128 GB SD memory card. Adding the memory card slot is a big improvement over previous kindles I have.

I read graphic novels like The Walking Dead series and being able to see them easily on the 10 inch screen is also a big improvement.

I highly recommend this!

This is a really nice job site speaker. I have another ION tailgater speaker that I have had for 2 years and really like the sound that you can expect from an ION speaker.

Love the design. It does look cool as others have stated.

The sound is excellent. I have an acre back yard and it easily fills the yard with clear and loud sound.

The handle on top is an improvement from my Tailgater model. The Tailgater was always a little awkward to carry. This solves that problem.

The reason I remove one star is the bluetooth capability. I find that I must have the transmitting device within about 4-5 feet of the speaker or the signal starts breaking up. For this reason, I play a mix and just set my iPod on top of the unit. Often I just connect with a cable.

I like the 2 AC power outlets, when I have it plugged in. Also the USB connection is useful when not plugged in to AC.

AM/FM radio works well and is a nice feature when I tire of my own playlists or just don't want to have to decide what to play.

Seems to be very sturdy. Should be able to survive the rough handling that might occur at a job site.

I'm not into Karoke, but tested the microphone jack and mixing controls. They work well.

Separate controls for overall volume and microphone volume.

Would recommend this for anyone needing a portable, loud, clear speaker!

It's always a good thing to be able to monitor your home and your pets while you're away.
Having this EZVIZ video camera, it can't get any easier.

Have been using a different video device for the past year. So wanted to see how this one compared.
Very easy set up. Using the quick set up guide, can have this up and running within a few minutes including downloading the needed app.
Long power cord with this. Can easily plug it in and have enough cord for it to reach a much higher level. Right now I have mine on a small shelf on the wall. If I choose to run it to the ceiling, (sticky pad included to do this) I will definitely get a nice cord cover to hide the cord that would be hanging down the wall to the outlet.
I like that it has audio so I'm able to talk and listen to whoever is in the room. Has nice night vision and was able to see the room when I only had a small night light on.
Video quality is really nice and clear. And love the wide angle with this. I can actually see the entire room.
Because I have animals, I have decided not to activate the motion detection. I really don't need alerts, to my phone, every time a dog moves around.
It's nice that I can buy a larger SD memory card for this. I will probably just increase it to 64GB. I really don't want to pay for cloud service so opted out of buying that.
No updates yet so not sure how well the "one-click updates" will work. But, if it works, it will be fantastic adding new features and functionality with just one click.
This is my first EZVIZ security camera but will love letting me see all of my EZVIZ cameras in one place if I choose to buy some more.

Great video security camera, for a decent price, that will definitely get used a LOT.
Would love to expand and eventually have my whole house monitored.

I too am learning to trust Boss Systems products. This subwoofer is an excellent product. Rich deep bass. The listed power rating is always peak Watts. RMS (average) power will be about half of that usually

Dual 4 ohm voice coil produces clear sound in the voice (middle) audio range.

I like the look of the LED lights. Nice effect.

I had this installed as I am not handy, so can't comment on the ease of installation.

I would recommend this as a value buy of a good product.

Had the home alarm system set up in about 2 hours. Not super easy but easy enough for someone like me who isn't the handiest.
I like that I can set up 8 different zones. I mainly love it for my out buildings. Being on a larger piece of property, there is no way we can hear if someone opened the door to our garage or shed. Motion sensor for our home.

Living out in a more rural area, there is no way the police could get here to catch someone breaking into our home. And we don't have any neighbors close enough to hear the alarm. We would be able to hear hear it from our out buildings only if we were home.
But, having a device with the loud alarm might make a thief back off not knowing if it was a wired monitoring system or not.
It does require batteries (not included). Two 9 volts, and Four AAA batteries.
There are four operation modes which are: Alarm, Alert, Home and Standby. I use the alert when I'm home, alarm when I leave for the day.

Main control panel has a nice display and it's easy to read. Like the back light on it. Also like that it does have an alarm in case anyone tampers with it. But, if anyone is at that point, they already know it's not a wired system.
It does have 10 other options. So you can add up to 10 other remote units/accessories to this system.

I do wish it would shut off and reset after a certain amount of time. Can't imagine this device screaming all day if we lived close to anyone.
If anyone has dogs or cats, I can't imagine if they tripped the alarm and had to sit in the house with the alarm going for any amount of time.
And having to pay for the security decals? Come on SABRE. We're talking an additional 50 cents for a few stickers?
I had to take off one star because of these two flaws.

All in all this is a nice security system if you can't afford to pay a monthly monitoring company.
Price is right for what you get.

As other reviewers have stated, be aware that this is a hard wired video system. You will need to install cables on the outside of your house and run them back inside to the recording hub. I also agree that the 60 foot cable lengths will require you to carefully design placement of the hub and the cameras so that everything reaches.

Once installed this is a nice system.
The 1 TB version recording hub that I received provides plenty of space for recording. The I was pleased with the picture quality. It allows me to monitor my dogs in the back yard and see any activity in the front yard during the day. At night, we leave lights on front and back, as recommended by security professionals and with these lights on can still monitor my yards at night well.

I also like the design of running power and video signal in one cable.

Installation and turn up of the system, was easy and straight forward.

Still learning the features and will come back and post more as I explore them.

For now, I would say if you feel comfortable running cables through your house this is a good system to provide security monitoring.

Love this camcorder.

What I like about it:
-Lightweight/portable
-Shoots at broadcast quality
-Easy access to important settings thru buttons on the body of the camera rather than going thru onscreen menus
-3 lens control rings, very nice focus ring
-rear SD card slot. Transfers mp4's at 35mbps
-4 channel audio recording. 2 external balanced mic slots. 2 internal mics.
-very convenient rotating handle.
-RJ-45 LAN slot or WiFi for remote viewing or file transfer. Files can be selected individually for transfer.
-Can continue filming while queuing up to 5 mp4 files for transfer.
-Customized quick access menu available
-Flip out screen and viewfinder provides good quality viewing.
-Time-lapse, stop-motion, slow motion and fast motion recording options
-Highly configurable
-13 assignable buttons
-Fast auto focus
-20x Optical Zoom
-Stabilization is excellent with three modes available.
-Even with internal fan on, no noticeable noise finds it way into the recording

What I don't like about it:
-Can only preset one FTP server for transfers. So must reconfigure if transferring to different servers at different times.

Bottom line, very useful professional camera.

Great little thumb drive. Very small profile. My only concern is that it is so small it might be easy to lose in my pants pocket where I like to carry a flash drive so I can capture and transfer files at any time.
I tried transferring several large audio folders and although I didn't measure the speed, they transferred in the blink of an eye. Much faster than my previous 16 GB thumb drive.

I highly recommend this. Great price, if I didn't get it through the Vine program, would gladly buy this product for the price. I'm reviewing the 64 GB ($17.99) model.

I love this camera and the app that is used to manage and view it. Easy to set up. The instruction booklet is a little skimpy and could be more detailed, but once I physically hooked it up to my wireless router and downloaded the app, set up following the onscreen prompts on my Android smartphone was easy enough. The app was easy to locate in the Google play store searching for tplink.

The camera provides a picture clear enough for me to view and monitor my dogs in the house, when we go out. It can be switched over to night vision in low light conditions or do so automatically if set to auto. I like that an extension to the power cord is provided so that instead of the length of the power cord (I think about 5 feet) the camera can be placed much further away if necessary. The camera is very stable and can easily be moved from room to room as needed.

Audio isn't the greatest, but I can hear that my dogs are barking if agitated. Video quality is also not high end, but I don't need high end to see that my dogs are safe from harm. Not looking for high quality video or photos of them.

The camera can be used to take snapshots if quality is not an issue.

For the price, this does the job well. I am very glad we got this and would highly recommend it to anyone who needs to remote monitor a room of their house.

For the price and the size of this wireless speaker, I thought the sound was great. It's not something I would put out for a party at home but, for going hiking or camping, this is perfect. It collapses down for easy packing. Or you can attach the shoe string, that comes with it, and hang it from your bag/suitcase/backpack, whatever.
I was able to pair it with my phone without even reading the directions on how to do it. So it's not that difficult to figure out. When it's time to charge it, I've charged enough phones, Ipods, kindles, etc.. to know that within 6-8 hours I'm sure it's fully charged up.
It doesn't have a volume button. You need your phone, ipod, or kindle to do it. But tell me anyone who doesn't have their cell phone within 6 inches from their hand to raise or lower the volume quickly and easily. And if you need those to change the music, no problems to adjust volume that way also.
Was able to pair it and have it running within 5 mins of having it out of the box so the battery is at least partially charged when you receive it.
Great little wireless portable speaker to give to someone who camps, hikes, or doesn't want to lug out a larger speaker outside for a campfire sitting.
Would also be great for an active teenager.

My wife got me this as a Christmas gift. Love the speaker. It has a rechargeable battery for tailgating, but I'll use it on my back patio mainly. Nice, loud, clear sound. Easy to connect to my iPod touch and Kindle Fire.
Been looking for a blue tooth speaker solution to pipe music out to the backyard in summer and this product is perfect for that!

Love the design of these.  Can hang them off the ear so they don't block all other sounds and hear both music and someone talking to me.  Can't find them locally any longer, so glad Amazon carries them.

This little guy is really small, and super easy to carry around. It comes with some sample music tracks, and the sound quality is ok considering what a tiny little speaker it has. It isn’t really made for music anyway. I really like the size because it’s discreet and easy to carry around. And it’s rechargeable!

This is a nice little gadget for organizing and finding your keys. It comes with an instruction booklet with a QR code you can scan for the instructions on how to take it apart, install your keys, etc. The video made it super quick and easy, and the device worked seamlessly with my iPhone’s “Find My” app, so I had it set up in seconds. Now I can just ask Siri, “where are my keys?” and the device will play a sound to help me find it. I’m so glad I got this.

My 13-year-old daughter has always had trouble with headphones. On-ear headphones and in-ear headphones both hurt her ears (in different ways), so she can’t stand to use them for any length of time. But enter this cool little headband. She loves it! It’s comfortable enough that she can wear it for hours without any problem. When other people are in the same room, they can’t hear what she’s listening to at all. The sound quality is actually pretty good—obviously it doesn’t sound like a pair of AirPods Max, but it’s pretty decent. There isn’t really any noise reduction, so don’t expect that. But if you hate ordinary headphones because of the discomfort, maybe give these a try.

Chinese AirTag imitation. They call it an “iTag” but I don’t think they’re fooling anyone. However, it does work. You can connect it to the Apple Find My app, which is easy and seamless. Then the app will tell you whether the item is nearby, and will have the “iTag” play a sound to help you find it. I have been able to find it within the house just fine, although I wish it would beep a little louder. It comes with a battery, which is nice. I used some mounting tape to stick it onto one of my kids’ devices, which is always getting left in strange places or swallowed up by the couch. I’m very pleased to be able to find it now, and I like using the Find My app rather than having to download a separate app (like some other types of finders). Since I didn’t expect a real AirTag, I’m happy with it.

This is a Chinese product, clearly attempting to imitate the Apple AirTag. They even call it iTag and put it in packaging that looks similar! However, it does work with the Apple Find My app, though with less accuracy than a real AirTag. The app can only tell you whether it’s nearby and play a sound to help you find it.

I got this tag to help me find a small Bluetooth speaker that my kids are always losing around the house. I used some mounting tape to stick it to the device, and that seems to work fine. (It didn’t come with any adhesive or key chain, it only has a small loop on top for a string or keychain.) When I have the Find My app play a sound, it beeps. I kind of wish it beeped a little louder, but it seems sufficient for finding a device within the house, which is what I wanted. If you want all the features of an AirTag, this will disappoint you. But if you just want a finder that works with Find My (rather than having to download some other app), and you don’t want to pay Apple prices, this does the job!

The ear buds and charging case both look nice and high quality. Bluetooth connection was super simple and show up instantly when the case was opened. The range is very good having my PC in my bedroom I can walk out into the kitchen and still get full signal. Sound quality is OK for the price you can't really complain. Battery seems to last a good amount of time used it for an hr it the earbuds still had charge. Charging the case takes about an hr, the earbuds took about 30 mins for the red lights to stop showing.

Cons: The charging port for the case is annoying it has a dust cover that partially blocks the Usb C port. You'll have to bend the dust cover out of the way to get to the port. Controls are slow/laggy You have to push and wait for the vol to change before you can press again if not you'll end up stopping or changing the music

I recommend this for someone looking for a low price wireless earbuds that has long Bluetooth range, Great for people working out loosing one of these wouldn't hurt too bad.

The film and switch pad fit and work well for dampening the sound of the keyboard, Apply them can be a pain since they don't remove cleanly from the paper backing and can tear if your not careful. Over all well worth the money since you get both films and pads along with tweezer to help apply them.

Super easy pairing, clear and clean sound. Charging can be annoying pulling off the silicon cover I can see it easily being lost. Sound is clean no added bass or anything else. Sounds flat when compared to other IEM's. Battery life seems good I've been using it for about 4 hrs. shows 70% For the price its very good.

Overall, this is a decent compact keyboard. I'm using it with a Chromebook, and the size is perfect. It doesn't have a numeric keypad which keeps the size way down compared with a full size keyboard. I especially like that the FN keys can be locked. Since I don't need the Function keys on a Chromebook, it's nice to be able to control the volume, mute, etc. with a single press rather than have to press the FN key first.

The backlighting is not as bright as I would have liked, but it's beneficial nonetheless. My main complaint is the short key travel. It is not nearly as comfortable as a regular keyboard in terms of key press, and I often get duplicate letters when typing.

While I would not want to use this to type a report, for the limited typing needed when using a Chromebook it's fine. Five stars for the size and layout; 3 stars for the key feel. Overall rating of 4 stars.

This is a very basic keyboard, but it gets nearly everything right. The layout adheres to the QUERTY convention, it has illuminated indicators for caps and num lock, it has a numeric keypad, and basic multimedia controls (play/pause and volume). It covers all of the bases for a basic keyboard.

The key feel is nice. It's quiet, and the keys are comfortable to press. The function keys are smaller than the other keys to save on space but work just fine. The attached USB cord is nice and long (about 6 foot). The overall build quality feels decently solid for the price point. It auto installed on Win 10 without a hitch.

Misses are minor. It lacks a sleep button. It has a calculator button instead that, for me, is far less useful than a sleep button. It also lacks non-slip pads on the base. There are two legs that can be used to prop up the keyboard, but the keyboard is so light that it's easy to shift the position of it in use. I solved it with some stick-on non-slip material.

I've always used Microsoft keyboards and have yet to have one fail on me. There are other basic keyboards that are a dollar or two less expensive than this, but considering this is less than $11, I'd rate the overall value as very good. If you're looking for a basic, everyday keyboard and don't need/want anything fancy, this will fit the bill well and do so at a great price. Five stars.

While these headphones won't excite an audiophile, if you want to spend as little as possible on a set of headphones but not make too many concessions with regard to comfort and sound quality, this is the set to get. For $25 you get headphones that sound way better than you would expect for the price point, and are also pretty comfortable to wear for extended periods.

The build quality is OK. Again, these are $25 headphones, but they are pretty decently made. They will not stand up to rough handling, but as long as they are treated with care, they will provide a good service life. The earpads are comfortable and do a good job of blocking out ambient noise. It has an attached cord that has both a 1/4 inch and a 3.5mm jack. You have to screw off the 1/4 inch one to expose the 3.5mm one. While I like the convenient way it provides 2 different jacks, I would have much preferred to have a detachable cord. But again, for the price, it's not a deal killer by any means.

The sound quality for the price is excellent. No, it doesn't sound as good as a $200 set, but it's reasonably clear, decently punchy, and doesn't significantly distort at high volumes.

If you're looking for the best value in a headphone, it's hard to beat this. Five stars.

I'm very pleased with these speakers. I'm using them as the front speakers in a 7.1 setup with a Polk S35 as the center speaker (and older KEF speakers as the surrounds and subwoofer). Could not be more pleased with the performance. They are crisp and clean, but have enough bass that, along with the S35, a sub is not critical (but is valuable to have for best performance). The build quality is excellent, and the size is nice and compact.

I tried the ES15 and ES20 and, while they are technically better, these Tsi100 provide me with 95% of the performance but at a much nicer price and a more compact size. It integrates very well with the ES35 center even though it's a different Polk speaker line. I'm using an Onkyo receiver.

Very pleased with all aspects of these speakers -- a solid 5 stars.

I'm very pleased with all aspects of this center speaker. The sound quality is excellent. This replaces an old KEF center speaker and the difference can be clearly heard. The Polk has a crisp, clean sound that clarifies and enhances dialog but not at the expense of a nice solid bass (although I also have a subwoofer in the setup).

Aesthetically it's a simple, clean design. Normally I don't pay much attention to the look of a speaker but in this case, since it's a center speaker, it's in my line of sight all the time. It's about as unobtrusive you can get with a center speaker without compromising sound quality and performance. Polk did an excellent job with the design.

I looked at the new version of this (the ES35) and, while there are some small incremental improvements, I didn't consider them to be worth the extra $100 it costs. Plus, this was on a price dip for the differential between the two was $150, making this the clear choice.

While I have been partial to KEF in the past for speakers, the performance of this Polk has really wow'd me. At present I'm using this center speaker with KEF left and right front speakers, and KEF for surround. I've been so impressed with the ES35 that I'll be changing to Polk for my L/R soon, and keep the KEF only for surround (5.1.2 setup).

An excellent center speaker that hits the mark on all counts. Five stars.

It was a very simple process to swap out the battery on my Cyberpower UPS. Just remove one screw the holds the battery compartment door in place, unhook the old battery, hook up the new one, and replace the door. Start to finish it's about 2 minutes, if that. The leads are color coded so there's no chance of mixing up the pos and neg. The terminals use a spade fitting that does not require any tools -- just slip it on or off.

The performance has been as good as the original. My original battery provided usable life for nearly five years. Hoping this replacement will provide the same life span. It's a bit more expensive than the generic batteries, but I prefer to go with the Cyberpower brand if only for the better warranty should something fail.

The Cyperpower website has a lookup tool where you can enter in either the model number or the serial number of your UPS, and it will tell you the specific model battery needed. I found that provided more accurate info than the product listing.

Although you can stream most radio stations, there's something about using an actual radio that makes it more enjoyable. This radio has a lot going for it. The sound is excellent -- very impressive for a relatively small single speaker device. Usage is about as easy as can be: one dial for frequency; one dial for volume (and on/off). There's a tone switch that basically enhances the bass (it sounds much better with bass enhancement). The frequency display is digital, and is clear and easy to read.

It can switch between AM, FM and shortwave. FM reception is excellent. I could not, however, get anything other than static on the SW band (probably due to where I am located rather than the radio itself). It can run on batteries (not included) or an AC adapter (which is included).

The build quality is just OK. It doesn't have much of a solid feel to it, and is lightweight. This is not a radio you can toss around and expect it to make it through in good shape.

A great item to have on hand when the power goes out (provided you remember to stock up on batteries) or just to be able to listen to the radio without the Internet. Five stars.

I'm pleased with the performance and features of this UPS. While it does not have the features that my other UPS's have (such as a screen that displays battery status, load, etc.) that's a plus, since I don't often use, or need, the info on the screen. This has just a simple on/off button, a mute button, and basic LED indicators that show if it's on line power or battery power.

It comes with the battery leads detached. Before use you need to remove the battery access panel (very simple -- just two screws) and connect the battery (also a very simple process).

I use it to for my router and cable modem so I can maintain Internet access and wifi during a power outage. I've simulated a power outage and both the modem and router didn't skip a beat. While this has a smaller capacity than the UPS's I use for my PCs, the 1000VA 550W specs are more than adequate to maintain a long run time given the light load.

One quibble -- and I have the same one with most UPS systems -- is that the outlets are too closely spaced, making it difficult to use all of them when plugging in devices that have a wall wart at the end. I would also have liked to see the outlets be color coded so you can more easily tell the difference between the bank of outlets that are surge protected only, and the bank that is surge/battery protected.

Those quibbles aside, it's been a good performer that provides all the features needed at a decent price.

This is a pretty basic mouse in terms of actual features, but that's a positive for me -- I just need basic mouse functionality and this delivers. I'm using it with Bluetooth connectivity and it was a snap to pair and use on a Win 10 PC.

The overall look is very nice -- much nicer than the typical mouse. I have it in red, and the paint is very glossy and attractive. The buttons are quiet but, although there is only a very hushed click sound, there is tactile feedback to provide confirmation that the button has been pressed. The scroll wheel works smoothly and has a non-slip coating for precise movement. It has an internal rechargeable battery.

No complaints at all. It works great, is super simple to install, and looks nice to boot. Highly recommend if you're looking for a basic mouse that has both wireless and Bluetooth connection options.

This is a nicely made cable. The covering is braided which helps with durability should it be plugged/unplugged frequently. That's not an issue for me since it gets plugged into a monitor and PC and won't be moved, but good durability usually means overall cable quality. The ends are very solidly attached, and it comes with a handy velcro wire wrap to lasso it with other cables to keep down the cable tangle.

Works just fine with my PC and monitor. Well made and functional -- zero complaints!

No complaints about this adapter. It's well-made, with a decent amount of heft to it. Tolerances for both the male and female plug/port are good, providing a tight fit but not so tight that it's hard to remove. Functionality is good as well -- no crackles or pops in use.  A simple adapter that works well, and is a good value for the price.

I have the original Fire box, the V2 Fire box and the version of the Fire Stick that came out right before this one. All have performed just fine, but this new stick has some major improvements that I really like.

Setup was as easy as with other Fire devices -- it walks you through the steps on screen. It also does a setup for having the remote control the TV and the receiver (my Fire Stick is plugged into my AV receiver). It works great -- I can power on/off both the TV (Samsung) and receiver (Onkyo) by just pressing the power button on the Fire remote. During power-up it also sets the receiver to the correct port for using the Fire stick. The volume on the remote controls the volume on the receiver. Very handy feature that works every time.

The overall speed and responsiveness is improved over earlier Fire sticks. Menus are more snappy and apps load faster. There are also a number of new settings to control audio and video aspects. I left most on their default, but it's nice to be able to get into the settings and tweak them.

A very nice upgrade to the Fire line. 100% satisfied with the purchase!

Overall, this is a very nice streaming system. The setup is pretty easy, although not nearly as quick and easy as the Fire TV since you have to register an account on Roku and give them a credit card (it is not charged unless you buy something).

I have it connected to an AV receiver and it's working great in terms of both picture and sound. The stick is slim enough to plug into an HDMI port on the back of the receiver without blocking anything. Wireless speed and connectivity is excellent.

What I don't like:
1. The four one-click buttons on the remote for Netflix, etc. can't be re-programmed. While the Netflix button is great since I have that service, the other 3 are useless. It would have been great to be able to reprogram them to work with an app of my choice.

2. The power and volume controls do NOT work with an AV receiver, only a TV. Since I have the stick plugged into my receiver, neither button is functional. Disappointing.

I also have a Fire TV box attached to the system. In comparison, the Roku menus are pretty dated looking as is the overall navigation. The remote is more clunky and doesn't respond as quickly at times. But, the Roku has apps that the Fire TV does not, so having both gives me more choices.

I'm very pleased with this monitor. I needed to replace my second screen and didn't want to spend a lot, but needed a monitor with 1920x1200 resolution. This seemed like a decent bet. It has exceeded my expectations with regard to performance. The clarity is excellent -- it rivals my primary screen which cost three times as much!

The monitor is very lightweight. It comes with both DVI and VGA cables, which was unexpected. I like that there's no power transformer or wall wart. It has just a regular power cord. Set up is simple (just attached the base and no tools are needed).

Of course, at this price point some features are not present. For example, while the screen can be tilted back and forth a bit, it does not have any up/down adjustment, nor can it be swiveled into portrait mode. There's no USB connectors and no speakers. But for me, none of those were deal breakers. I wanted a good quality monitor that was affordable, and this hit the mark 100%. Plus, it does not scrimp on connections. There's DVI, VGA and HDMI. I'm using DVI at present since the PC I'm using it with is a few years old. But, my next PC will probably have a HDMI connection, making this monitor future-proof (well, as future-proof as any tech product can be).

If you're looking for a basic monitor that does not scrimp on image quality, this should definitely be on your short list. Also, check Amazon Warehouse for used ones. I got mine there (it was probably a customer's return). It looks brand new, and only ran me $127.

This is not pure copper but rather is CCA (copper coated aluminum). But, unless your sound system costs more than your car, it will provide excellent performance while saving a good amount of money. I'm using this for relatively short runs to surround speakers and it's working just as well as the full copper wire I'm using with other speakers.

The jacket is thick but retains a decent amount of bendability for a 14g wire. No problems stripping the wire ends for connections. Great value for the price.

This replaces a Denon, and I am 100% happy with the performance. The sound quality (I have a 7.2 setup) is top-notch. Granted, I'm not an audiophile so I can't judge all the nuances, but regardless if I'm listening to music or watching a movie, the sound quality is absolutely wonderful. Plus, there are lots of ways to customize the sound to your liking.

I debated between the Onkyo and a similarly-spec'd Denon. I opted for the Onkyo since I've had Onkyo receivers in the past that never failed on me. In contrast, I have had to replace 2 Denon's due to failure (one completely died; the other had a very temperamental on/off button and would no longer respond to any remote control commands).

Setup is straightforward. The hardest part is connecting all the speakers. One of these days I'm going to get banana plus for them, but until then it's a pain getting all the wires properly set. The installation program walks you through the audio testing/calibration (using the supplied microphone), getting online, and other setup processes. I didn't encounter any problems. The firmware update process also went smoothly (had the receiver download it online).

I'm very impressed with all the features, the performance and the build quality. Excellent value for the price, and I would highly recommend this model.

This is a very nice quality cable. The cable itself is nice and stout, but still bendable so it can be positioned easily. The connection ends are equally well-made. I like that the cable ends come covered with a protective cap to prevent damage when not in use, be it in transit, being carried in a backpack, or even when stored in a cabinet. Nothing worse than a bent pin on a cable.

No problems at all with functionality. Good choice if you're looking for a DVI to VGA cable.

This is a better alternative than the one piece design adapter plugs for my needs. The jack for the 3.5 mm plug holds the plug far more securely -- there's a firm snap as it goes in, and it won't come out unless you pull firmly. I use this to hook earbuds up to my AV receiver while exercising, so the cable gets tugged on a fair amount. This style of adapter holds the cables far more securely than the all-in-one design.

Overall build quality seems pretty nice. No problems at all with sound quality. However, I'm using it with a pretty basic AV receiver and low-end earbuds, so I can't speak to how well this works with audiophile-level gear.

Good value for the price.

This is replacing a Arris Surfboard SB6141 and, so far, I've been very pleased with the performance. Set up is very simple (using Cox Cable). It did require a call to Cox to give them the ID number of the modem for activation, but the process was very quick and easy. Set up of the modem itself simply entailed plugging it in.

The modem looks as nice as a modem can look. It's pretty tip-over resistant. The indicator lights are clear without serving as a beacon when the room is dark as the Surfboard indicator lights did.

I've noticed a small increase in both download and upload speeds compared with my old DOCSYS 3.0 modem. I'm presently on a 50 mb/sec tier but will be moving to the 100 mb/sec tier later this year. That's the reason for the upgrade, since my older modem would not handle the higher speed tier very well.

The only concern I have is the operating temperature. This runs rather hot compared to the Surfboard. It does not appear to be affecting performance nor has the heat been so significant that it activated the overheat protection of the modem (the modem will shut down if it overheats and flash an error code, according to the manual). But, it does give me concern about longevity. I'll update the review down the road should reliability be a concern.

Works fine for me. I'm using it to hook a pair of headphones that have a 3.5mm jack to a receiver that has a full-size jack. The adapter stays in snugly, but not so snug that it can't be removed (I have the one with the plastic housing). No problems at all with the headphones making a good connection and the audio quality seems just fine.

I was a little apprehensive buying these given all the bad reviews, but figured it was worth a gamble since it only cost $1.47. Glad I got it -- works fine and was much less expensive than other models. Plus, this was one of the few adapters that came as a single -- a lot of the other offerings come in packs of 2, 4 or more. I just needed one!

Update, Aug 2016: It's been 5 months since I installed this router and it has the distinction of never needing to be rebooted yet! That's a record for me, since some of my past routers needed a reboot every week or two (or even every day or two). I continue to be impressed with the rock-solid performance of this TP-LINK. It's not fancy and lacks some high-end features, but I'll take solid, dependable performance over flash any day.

Original review:
While this router won’t satisfy the needs of those who have complex networking requirements or those who like to tinker and tweak, it offers solid performance, AC speeds and good coverage at a very reasonable price point. If you’re looking to go to AC speed but don’t want all the bells and whistles, this offers a lot for the money.

The footprint is very small compared with other routers I have, which is a nice change. The overall build quality seems very good, and the two antennae are firmly attached (another problem I’ve had with lower-end routers). It has an off switch which is handy if you need to do a reboot. It runs warm but not hot.

Setup is very straightforward if you want to keep the default settings. Basically just plug it into a PC, access the router menu with your browser, set the network name and password, and you’re done. You can access more advanced features if needed, but for a basic setup the time required is less than 5 minutes.

Performance has been impressive. I also have AC routers from D-Link and Linksys that are far more costly than this, but this little guy holds his own when it comes to coverage and throughput. For example, I get Internet connection speeds of about 62mBps with my D-Link DIR-880L. This router, with the same PC and network card, gives me 50mBps. Wireless coverage is a little more spotty with this router on fringe areas (e.g., for a PC located a floor above and at the opposite end of the house from the router) but it still maintains a connection, albeit at lower speeds.

This does lack some features that could be helpful for some situations. It has a USB port, but only has one, and it’s a 2.0 USB port. It lacks a gigabit port as well. But again, for the price, it offers a lot of performance. So far I’ve had zero problems or glitches.

This router won’t excite a power user or satisfy complex networking requirements/demands, but for the basics, it gets the job done with solid speed and performance. Well worth considering if you’re looking for an inexpensive router.

This is without a doubt the best looking soundbar I’ve come across so far. The shape is more than just aesthetics – if you have a TV on a table stand the low profile of the soundbar doesn’t get in the way of the screen. Granted, I’m sure there’s a TV out there that sits low enough that the soundbar will get in the way, but if it does it will be minimal. Even if you have a wall-mounted screen, the soundbar shape is still something that can be appreciated.

No complaints either with regard to the build quality. This feels as solid as it looks. I had high expectations given the price point, and I was not disappointed. The remote is also well-done with a straightforward design that makes it simple to use.

A few years ago I ran wiring for my main TV for a 7.1 speaker setup. It took many hours, and gave me a new appreciation as to why electricians charge so much for fishing wire through walls. So, the fact that I was able to get this set up and running in about an hour (including the unpacking and calibration time) was a real treat. I would rate the setup ease, and the included instructions, as excellent.

There are a number of great features, the main one for me being the detachable side speakers. It gives more flexibility than the usual sound bar in that you can position them for rear sound if you want that immersive feel, but also use them as standalone speakers for other devices. I had no problems pairing one to a tablet. One potential negative is the internal battery. While the run time is fine – I ran it for a good four hours continuously without a problem – I’ve had enough devices with internal batteries go bad (e.g., the battery will no longer take much of a charge) that I always am wary of internal batteries.

The sound quality was both good and bad, and in an unexpected way. I was expecting that this soundbar would be left in the dust by my wired system at high volume. While it was bested (especially with bass given the slim subwoofer) it was a far closer horse race than I thought it would be. This soundbar can put out a healthy amount of volume and still remain in control of sound quality.

Where it fell short is when it was not pushed hard. Soft passages were weak; dialog was unclear at times. Running this at a soft volume (such as at night when others are sleeping in the house) was not enjoyable – I ended up having to turn on subtitles since I could not make out the dialog clearly. Now, this issue could be exacerbated by my aging ears, but others in the house, who are younger, also found it weak and unimpressive at low volume.

I think most people who get this will be looking to have “big” sound in a simple to set up, simple to use system. On that end, the Philips soundbar delivers. It misses somewhat on the soft end of the spectrum, but the build quality, looks, and flexibility warrant a five-star rating even at this rather lofty price point.

I really hate to use the word “cute” but there’s no way around it – this is a cute cam! It looks pretty much the same as the original Cube, but offers improved video and the addition of WiFi. Of the new features, the WiFi is the most significant, and makes this far more useful as a cam.

I also have the original Cube and the build quality continues to be very good. These are priced higher than the “no name” action cams, but after using (and breaking) a couple of those, it’s nice to be able to count on the Cube to keep on working. It’s water resistant, which makes it less worrisome when using it in bad weather or around water. It supports up to a 128MB SD card

The form factor and overall design is much the same as the original Cube. It has a magnet in the base that is more than strong enough to keep it well-planted. It’s not strong enough for significant activity (e.g., staying on a bike handle while riding) but it offers the benefit of tripod-like stability without the need for a tripod (providing you have something metal to fasten the magnet).

The biggest change is wifi on the Cube+. I found the setup to be straightforward – basically just download the app and follow the setup steps. I love that the app lets you use it as a live view – that’s a big improvement over the original Cube. It’s a very helpful feature for planning a shot, plus allows me to monitor how things are turning out without having to play the video.

Image quality has been impressive – zero complaints there. I was pleased with the resolution of the original Cube, and this is a bit better. Audio quality is OK. It’s not outstanding, but it clearly picks up voices. I understand that earlier versions of the Cube+ had very poor sound quality, but the one I have (got it in Dec 2015) is fine with regard to sound.

All in all, it’s a great cam with a fun form factor and look. Well worth considering if you’re looking for a small profile action cam with solid build quality and performance. While the price has increased over that of the original Cube, the wifi features are very useful and well implemented, making this version well worth the additional cost.

This is a pretty decent Android tablet that packs a lot of features for the price point. The overall build quality is excellent (again, giving the price point). It feels very substantial in hand – much more substantial than other under-$100 tablets I’ve tried. I especially like how all the ports and controls are clearly labeled (white on black) so there’s no guessing as to what’s what when it comes to external controls.

The screen resolution is very good for the price – more than adequate for enjoyable video watching, picture viewing, etc. The colors are rich and saturated. No complaints as to screen quality.

The touch control is also well-done. I didn’t have any problems with mis-clicks or having the screen not properly register a touch.

Setup is the same as any other Android tablet – pretty simple and straightforward. The user guide is sparse but pretty clear. It’s not necessary to refer to it if you’re familiar with Android, but if this is the first experience with that OS the manual provides enough info to get you up started.

Weak spots are audio and the cameras. The audio in particular is not well done. The sound is thin and tinny, and it gets worse at higher volumes. An external speaker is a must for this if you plan on getting enjoyable sound. Interestingly, the volume controls are not external buttons but are software-based. I like that since it cuts down on the button clutter on the edge of the tablet.

The camera is also not as well done as with other tablets at this price point, with less than ideal resolution and clarity, especially in lower light conditions. It’s workable but not at all impressive.

The tablet comes packaged in a pretty upscale fashion, with a nice box with foam cutouts. Add-ons are sparse – just a charger. Other tablets at this price point often include a richer set of accessories such as earbuds, a screen protector, case, etc. This is pretty bare bones – basically just the tablet.

While it’s not the best low-cost Android tablet I’ve tried, it certainly is competitive, especially with regard to the build quality and screen performance. Well worth considering if you’re looking for an inexpensive tablet that still provides a decent feature set.
