I like these Bluetooth headphones a lot.  they are very comfortable and feel good around my neck.  The small ear bud covers fit my ears perfectly.  I mainly like to listen to podcast after podcast, and I wore them for about 4 hours straight and the battery is still going strong.  Everything about them is good except the range.  I can't get very far from the device I'm connected too or else it will break up or disconnect.  I basically have to carry my phone with me, or not go further than a average bedroom's distance away from it.  I have a pair of very expensive Bluetooth headphones that have a very large range and I can go outside and leave my phone inside and still maintain a good connection.  But, for only $16.99 I can't complain about these.  The volume button on these is actually easier to use than on my pricey pair, and they're more comfortable.

The Jabra 45 Bluetooth was super easy to connect to my phone and instantly connects every time I turn the Jabra on. The sound quality is very clear and easy to hear voices, music, podcasts or whatever desired with controllable volume. I'm unsure about how long the battery lasts, but I've only charged it once and that was several days ago, however I turn it off when not using it. My only problems are:

1. I can't seem to find the right size earbud cover to fit my ear. The Jabra 45 is a loose fit for now and prone to falling out.
2. It will hear me when I request it to call nearly everyone, but for some reason it just can't understand me when I clearly say in English, my husband's name. And that's too bad because he's the one I call the most.

Other than those two problems, it works pretty well. I must add though, I have a Jabra 25 and I think it works better. I also have a cheap Plantronics and it never mishears my husband's name.

This wireless mouse fits my hand nicely, and has a thumb shelf so my thumb doesn't drag all over the mouse pad.  It just rides along.  It was beyond easy to install and no reboot required.  It comes with an AA battery so no hunting for one.  The turn wheel is fast but it has a little button on top to adjust the speed. And it has buttons on the side to go back and forth between pages.  My wired mouse pointer drifted all over the screen.  The AmazonBasics mouse pointer stays where you leave the mouse.  This is a really good mouse for the price (as of this review it costs 15.99).

These wireless Bluetooth earbuds are great for what I want to use them for, mainly listening to podcasts or Youtube interviews but not for serious music listening. I tried listening to some classical guitar music and they just can't carry the depth of tones that a good set of head phones can, but otherwise, they are very good. For walking about the neighborhood and use at the gym listening to music these are really good for that. For symphonic music, not so good. The battery last about 8 hours before needing recharging, and you will only hear what the battery level is at turn on and I think only when the battery is low. I can't get it to tell me unless it's already low on charge.

They are very light weight and less bulky than another pair of Bluetooth wireless earbuds that I have. They come with several different sizes of rubber ear cups and USB cord for charging. The direction are really bad - only pictures but they are very easy to figure out how to use without directions. I guess the only thing I don't like is the intermittent flash of a blue light indicating they are on. I like to listen to meditative videos in bed, in the dark, and the blue light irritates hubs so I have placed a piece of black electrical tape over it. The on/off and volume control are easy to feel and get familiar with.

Overall, these are very easy to wear, connected to my laptop quicky and are good for casual listening to music, but an audiophile will probably not like them much. I'm kind of an audiophile but for times when I want to analyze classical guitar music (I teach CG), I use better quality head phones.

This is great to use when you need more USB ports.  It plugged nicely into the C port on my laptop and I was able to connect other devices to it with a port left over.  I haven't had an opportunity to plug it into the Ethernet but will when I can.  It doesn't require any drivers to load and worked instantly.  It is solidly constructed and should last a long time.

I received this Roku Express for review, but honestly, I just now installed it and I can't tell any difference between it and my previous Roku Express I got about a year and a half ago. It streams exactly the same as far as I can tell, but it streams very well. It was a bit of a pain to install since the Roku site refused my password and the instructions afterwards aren't all that easy to follow if you lose your password. But, after plugging in all my passwords for internet connection, Netflix, Amazon, etc...it finally started streaming again. I can't tell that it's any faster. Nonetheless, if you don't have a Roku and want to stream a boatload of free channels with movies and lots of other cool stuff to watch, I suggest getting a Roku. You can add paid channels later. And Roku doesn't require a credit card to use.

It comes with a short HDMI cable and everything you need to get streaming. As far as the actual hardware installation, it's extremely easy. It takes less than 10 seconds to put it on top of the TV and connect the 2 cables (HDMI and power). A sticky tape comes to adhere the Roku to the top of the TV since the Roku is so small it tends to fall off with being stuck. This is my 3rd Roku and we rarely watch regular TV anymore.
This Roku will stream in 1080 and 720 psi. I had ordered about 5 or so generic Roku remotes earlier this year since we tend to lose them and one of our dogs has chewed up the original remotes beyond usage, and they all work fine with this Roku.

Roku is always good, just a little bit of a pain to get past all the passwords, codes and stuff in the beginning, especially if your old password for some reason doesn't work anymore.

Our phones got fried in a nearby lightning strike so I bought this to hopefully prevent the new set from getting fried by another.  We've had several bad storms come through our area since then and the phones are fine, but it's really not possible to tell if this has prevented a power surge or not unless it gets fried too which hasn't happened yet.  I will say that I used to use a different (but similar) type of phone line surge protector years ago on the job and they did a good job of protecting our data lines.  I would often have to replace them because they were fried but the equipment was still o.k.

This doorknob alarm is very simple to use and the enclosed directions are well-written in large print. It works fine on all settings and is very loud. I like the idea and might buy a couple more of these, however, my favorite door alarm device are the wedges you place under your door. When someone tries to open the door they scream like BEEE-JEEZESS and also serve to make it hard to continue opening the door since they're wedges. However, this alarm has it's perks too. It's small and can easily be packed into a suitcase for use in hotels, and it will fit over almost any standard doorknob. I only have standard doorknobs so I don't know it if will work on latches, etc...

Overall - easy to use, but you have to supply the three AAA batteries. Very loud and would most probably deter most unwanted people.

This cable works fine for using to charge my Axon 7 phone which requires a type C cable.  The one that comes with the phone is always getting lost so I ordered 4 of these to keep in various rooms of the house so I'll always have a cable.  It's black like all the other thousands of cables we have lying around the house for charging various electronic devices so I have put a piece of bright blue duct tape on mine so I can instantly recognize them and save myself rising anger when trying to distinguish the C from all the others.  I only wish it were a bit longer than 3.3 feet, but whatever, it charges, and it was cheap and that's what I wanted.

I just needed a cheap droid to take with me to places where I know I'll be sitting for a long time with nothing to do such as my kid's various school activities where they get to do all the stuff while the parents sit and wait.  If there is a wifi signal it will connect quickly.  At first I thought the battery didn't last very long until my oldest kid showed me what the little square at the bottom was for.  Now I get rid of all my trash and not let it build up wasting my battery.  I am surprised by how nice a droid this is and I only paid $39.00 for it.  I've paid much more for similar droids and they crashed and burned within a year or two.  I think this one will last a lot longer.  It comes with charging cord but it's too short to use if you're wanting to use the Kindle while it's charging, but it's nice to have as a spare cord. The screen has good clarity and nice touch response.  The sound quality is so-so but if I want to listen to music or watch a video I'll use earbuds. I really don't have any complaints about this Kindle Fire and I think it was $39.00 very well spent.  I just wish I had bought one a long time ago and saved myself several hundred dollars on the other droids that didn't last for very long or were too incredibly slow to even use.

What I like about this monitor:
1. Easy to set up - I used my previous monitor video cable and power cord and had it up and running in a few minutes.
2. Very clear resolution despite having an old video card.
3. It has an HDMI connection but I am using the regular VGA input and it still very clear.
4. A VGA and sound cord are included.
5. Very sleek, streamline black design which goes nicely with my other computer accessories.

What could be better:
1. The included instructions tell you nothing about how to make video and audio adjustments. I can't use a bright setting and it took a good while to figure out how to use the buttons underneath the screen. They are not intuitive at all.
2. Poor Audio - if you want good audio from this monitor that will not be possible. It is a thin monitor and the audio is very thin and tinny. I was hoping I could disconnect my external sound system to make more room on my desk but found out that I must keep it if I want to hear any decent sound from my computer.
3. While testing the volume on this monitor you must still figure out how to toggle using the various buttons underneath. There is no single volume button or toggle switch. And it will not get very loud.
4. If you don't bump the monitor or use the toggle switches the monitor stays fairly steady on it's stand. Otherwise it will rock and jiggle while using the buttons.
5. No HDMI cable is included.

The scant instructions did say to visit their website to download the latest drivers but as of yet this monitor is not listed in their driver drop down window. I don't think that matter much at this time as the monitor is very clear and sharp.
Overall: Good monitor for the price (as of this review it costs $138.24 Prime) which I feel is a fair price.

Boy! does this camera remind me of my old Polaroid Square Shooter. This camera is NOTHING like your iPhone camera as it's big, and totally analog except for the film counter on the back. I love it when the motor runs and film comes sliding out - a sound I well remember. I think the hardest thing about using this camera was getting the shoulder strap put on, other than that it's very easy to use. Though it is on the big side, it doesn't weigh much and the view finder and shutter button are pretty much intuitive. I'm left handed so holding it like a right-hander took a little getting used too, but it's not a problem for me. This camera is made for right-handers so those who are very much left-handed might not like the way you have to hold it, and the shutter button is on the right side front. It has flash and you can adjust the light/dark and distance to you subject with minimal effort.

Loading the film was easy, aiming at my subject was easy, the shutter button was easy to depress and everything is/was easy. The close-up adapter looks like there's no way it will attach itself to the lens, but somehow it does. I took one close-up of my dog but the picture didn't turn out very good because she moved away right when I hit the shutter button-but that's typical for her. I haven't taken a "selfie" yet but it seems like it will be easy to do.

The color development of the film is pretty good. I took a wide angle picture of my raised garden beds and I was able to get all of them in the picture and the various green colors were vivid. I also took a picture of the front of our house, and though I had to still walk across the street to our neighbor's driveway to get the entire house in the view finder, the picture turned out nice. Again, the colors were bright and vivid. It got the entire house plus some area on both sides. In the past with my other cameras I would have to get further away or be happy with just most of the house in the picture so it's real nice to get the whole thing with room to spare.

The film is kind of pricey. For a pack of 40 pictures it costs around $34.00. I figured it would be kind of expensive and I hope the price of the film goes down some. This is a comfort camera for those of us who grew up with Polaroids. It may be that since we are living in highly uncertain and stressful times, having a camera like this is a cool blast from the past and may make us just feel better having one like this, plus it takes nice pictures.

I like the Pono player a lot, even it's odd pyramid shape is easy to deal with. It might take up a little more room in a pocket or purse, and but it does lay nicely on a flat surface making it easy to view the screen. However, I'm not fond of the $399.00 price tag (as of this review). But it's got some great things going for it such as:

1. Ability to download high-resolution quality audio recordings (mainly from the Pono webstore)
2. Sound Quality of these recordings is astoundingly good
3. Ease of transference of music from computer to Pono-no programs to download and install first
4. No requirement to register device
5. Very powerful - can really get LOUD either through headphones/earbuds/external speakers
6. Touchscreen is fairly intuitive and easy to view
7. It will automatically sort your music into these categories: Artists, Albums,Songs and Playlists
8. Easy to hold and use with one hand
9. Rubber coated
10. Can add more memory via Sandisk
11. Has 64G out of box but only about 57 is available for music storage
12. Comes in a really cool bamboo box which you should NOT discard
13. Instructions that come with it are simple and clear
14. Comes with a few free songs already installed
15. Will take basically all types of formatted music - It can reproduce DSD, FLAC, ALAC, MP3, WAV, AIFF and non-protected AAC files at up to 24-bit/192kHz.

What may not be so great:

1. It is basically a glorified iPod of yore - it does not have WIFI capability so all downloaded music must first be downloaded to a computer and transferred to the Pono.
2. Outer rubber coating gets grimy with fingerprints real fast
3. No Bluetooth capability so all external speakers must be hardwired
4. Currently there is not a large selection of symphonic music available to purchase that is high-resolution. It's mainly rock and hip-hop.
5. The price tag of $399.00

I downloaded some music from the i-Tunes store and also copied several classical guitar CD's and listened to them through my iPod, computer speakers and Braven speaker [[ASIN:B00SU3XOI4 Braven Wireless HD Bluetooth Speaker - Retail Packaging - Black]]. Though I could not detect any significant difference in quality of hip-hop, I could hear more clearly the lusciousness of the classical guitar while listening to it using the Pono, especially through quality headphones. I hardwired the Pono to the Braven speaker and was treated to some great classical guitar music that was super clear and nice and loud! The timbre of the strings resonating through the fine wood and outwards.....the sound of the players fingers and he/she played the strings....all very clear as if the player was in the same room with me. I play and teach classical guitar so I was naturally very interested in how well the instrument would sound through the Pono and am not disappointed at all in the sound quality.

Overall: You really need to be a serious audiophile with a sufficient enough bank account to first buy the Pono, and then to afford to download high-resolution recordings because they aren't exactly cheap. Those recordings will cost approximately twice as much as regular recordings. Maybe the price of the Pono and music will go down some later, but I know I won't be filling it up with high-resolution music because I can't afford too. And I can't really yet determine it's battery life. While it's connected to my PC it automatically starts to charge so I will have to play it constantly at a later date to determine length of battery life.

These are pretty much the perfect laptop for kids (and adults too if they don't want to download or install any personal programs). The Google App store has just about every type of app/program you could want. These don't have a DVD drive and you can't download programs unless they are from the App store. It's a good way of keeping your machine safe from malware attacks. No need to purchase and renew antiviral software. The screen is clear and bright, and the keyboard works really nicely. The sound from these is much better than the sound on my much more expensive laptop. Overall, the size and functionality of the Chromebook is much better than my new Windows 8.1 laptop.

My kids were able to get started immediately with minimal help from me to download some apps they like, get their e-mails set up and started using these Chromebooks immediately. I personally am not nuts about having only Google Chrome as my internet browser, thus I don't own my own Chromebook, but for my kids purposes (mainly games and schoolwork) the Chromebooks work out great. I really like how easy and smoothly they work. They are faster than my laptop and I do find that appealing, but I like being able to use a DVD drive and to be able to download what software I might want from the internet.

Printing is possible from the cloud and set up to do that is not difficult. Everything is easy........almost too easy. You can't store any data on the computer itself, only in the cloud. But, I'm not worried about any personal information being accessed by nefarious types because there's really nothing to access.

We've had these Chromebooks since Christmas and they are still working fine with no problems whatsoever.

UPDATE: 2.28.15 - My daughter brought it to my attention that these chromebooks do not have a "delete" key. Interesting.

For an apartment with only one door and one window that opens this set is great. But most places need a few more. For a dorm room this is fine. I've only seen dorm rooms that had one door and usually the dorm rooms windows are several stories up so it would probably be pretty hard for someone to enter that way. Unless it's on the ground floor.

The door stop alarm is extremely LOUD. And it will not stop SCREAMING until it is physically switched off. This is the first of this type I have ever tried out. A few years ago I bought about 10 door stop alarms of another brand and they were also very loud. However, once the pressure plate was released back up they would stop screaming. I guess it's good that it continues to scream until you stop it. Especially in a dorm type living situation. Someone would eventually come to see what was the matter. It takes one 9 volt battery.

The window alarm is extremely simple to install and the double sided sticky tape that comes with it is very strong. I have several of these window alarms attached to various windows at my home. They aren't the loudest but they should get the job done of scaring off an unwanted intruder. It takes 4 LR44 button batteries.

The personal key chain alarm is o.k. It's got a loud scream that makes my ears ring. It takes a good tug to pull out the pin to activate it. The small LED light is better than no light at all but don't expect a bright beam. It will help you find your keys if you dropped them in the dark. I think along with a sincere scream for help and the personal alarm screaming as well, I would think most aggressors would give up and try for an easier target.......at least I would hope so. It takes 3 LR44 button batteries.

This case has an absolutely LOVELY lavender color.  I just love looking at it!  It's durable enough, though I don't know how long it will last with frequent opening and closing.  It's not made out of leather but from durable polyurethane with a microfiber interior.  It's soft and will not scratch your Fire HD.  I am using this case although it was not made for the original, plain jane Kindle.  My gorilla husband managed to force the kindle into it and so it will stay until the elastic straps bust.  So, know that it is not made to fit an original Kindle. It can be accessed from the outside to connect the charging cord, and it has a nice cut-out for the camera lens.

This is a surprisingly good radio, especially since it is also a shortwave receiver. It is a hefty size and weight so I would not advise taking this in your backpack on a long hike, but it would be great for camping and to have as an emergency radio at all times. I thought about putting this on my shoulder next to my head and walking down my neighborhood reminiscing the 70's, but luckily my husband talked me out of it.

The local stations come in loud and clear and adjustments in sound quality can easily be made with the adjustment knobs. Setting the clock was difficult for me and it took several tries before I finally got it set. You will definitely need the instruction booklet on how to set everything that you want set. The antennae is super long and just keeps extending almost to the ceiling. I had to turn off the beeps that you hear every time a button is pushed, it was really getting on my nerves and it eats up battery power. D-cells are required if you don't choose to use the included power supply. Makes for a little extra weight, but it's a good weight, much like the radios back in the day when they lasted forever.

It's simply loaded with features that will take some time to figure out how to use and set and I will only be using a few of them. I don't particularly need any alarms but if you do they're there. Using the shortwave aspect is not as easy because you will have to spend some time trying out the various SW settings and slowly searching for reasonably clear stations. I still want to hit on a station from China but so far have only found about 3 stations that I can actually understand what they are saying. I'm not disappointed in this because I have 3 other shortwave receivers and I get the same thing from them. It takes time and practice to find what you are looking for.

Overall, I think this is an absolutely excellent radio and highly recommend it to anyone who is looking for a larger, heavier quality shortwave receiver radio. I could easily take this to the pool or use outside while working to listen to my favorite AM or FM stations since it has such a robust sound.

The Belkin 8-Outlet Surge Protector is a good one, but I found it a bit cumbersome with the box like structure and with all the cords I have coming from my "entertainment center" I wasn't able to close the box but left it open instead. We've only been using these for just one day, but they are quite good. Of course the range is no where near 10 miles but they will do up to a mile and a half pretty nicely. They called me many times as they were getting further and further away. The connection did get weaker and with static at the 1.5 mile mark, but up closer they were very clear.

The included instructions are very well written in ENGLISH only!! and very detailed. I was able to do all the modifications I wanted by reading and following the instructions. Also, these are nice and small so my kids hands can easily hold them. They seem to be constructed out of durable plastic and hopefully will not break to easily. The clips that can be attached are very sturdy. I don't have a idea of battery life yet. I will be letting the kids play with them and using them to call them home to dinner. I will be buying another set soon and they all can be set to the same channel.

Really nice for a very inexpensive set of walkie-talkies.

I got this for Christmas and have only been using it for a few days now. I did have a problem with the set-up since there were no step by step instructions and you are left to figure out what goes where. I had omitted attaching the USB/phone jack between my old Windows XP computer and the UPS. I've used UPS's in years past, but they did not require a USB connection to a computer. I found out I had a problem when I was trying to install the software and it stopped loading and gave me a problem message, but no solution. I called the 1-888 number and without any fuss or waiting I got to speak to someone in the tech department who spoke very good English and solved my problem quickly.

I was tempted to deduct one star for the lousy (or total lack of) any instructions on how to connect this to your computer but didn't since the tech help was so good. There was a picture drawing instructing the user to remove the battery and turn it over so the green tape is on top which I managed to do alright. I don't hear any fan noise whatsoever as some others were complaining of. In fact, it's so quiet I can't even tell it's on unless I go and see the 3 LED lights on the top panel.

I tested it out a few minutes ago by turning off the power to the room that my computer is in. I was downstairs in the garage at the fuse box so I don't know if any beep occurred upstairs, but when I got there the computer was running off the UPS. Every 30 seconds I heard 4 beeps from the UPS telling me that it was being used as the power source. I only have my computer, monitor and modem connected to the UPS. I figure I don't need the extra peripheral equipment to stay powered up since it only sucks more energy from my UPS. I didn't wait to see how long the UPS would power my PC but I did sit there for about 3 minutes before I went downstairs and turned the power back on. My computer had a message on the screen saying that it was now being powered by regular current again (or something to that effect).

So far I like this UPS a LOT. There's nothing more frustrating then losing your work if the power goes off for only a couple of seconds. I edit a lot of music and it's not always easy or convenient to save it while I edit it just because of the nature of the program I use. So, I really like the idea of hearing my 4 beeps to let me know I might need to close out and shut down and not lose any work. I don't always have lights on so there may be nothing to tell me there's been a power outage except for the beeps on this UPS. There is a mute mode, but I need to hear the beeps.

As of this time, 6.20.12, I have done some research on the Levitron 32120-1, surge panel. I took it with me to our local Power Board last weekend while attending the annual meeting, and spoke with some electricians there. I was told this product should work well with my home since it also has a 120 volt single phase line. I was also told that this surge panel is like the Cadillac of surge panels. My house is pretty typical, 3 bdrm, 2 bath, etc... and it's not attached to any other buildings. I made an appointment with a licensed, certified electrician to come over this afternoon to install it. I was given an estimated cost of around $125.00, depending on how many circuits in the breaker box need to be moved around to make room for the Leviton surge panel. He also says it will work fine for residential, however the acid test will be when he gets here, sees it, and tries to install it.

_______________________________________________________________________________________________________________

INSTALLATION: The electrician left about 15 minutes ago and it took him approximately 30 minutes to install the Leviton 32120 Surge Protector. It cost me $125.00 to have it installed. He only had good things to say about it, to the extent that he didn't think the one he installed on his own home was quite this good. He continued to say that "Leviton" is about the best in surge protection.

It looks very nice where he attached it to the wall in our garage underneath the circuit breaker box. It is large enough that it won't fit inside the breaker box and must be mounted on the wall beside/underneath it and has it's own circuit breaker dedicated to it. I will try to upload a video of it so you can see what it looks like after it's installed.

He explained to me that this device will take a surge of electrical energy, assuming it is of enough voltage to trigger the capacitors to absorb the electricity and stop the flow from going beyond it into your house. If the surge is not high enough to trigger a stop, it will let it pass on through unobstructed. For instance, when the refrigerator turns off, there is a momentary back flow of electrons (electricity) and this is below the amount required for the Leviton to react. But once it has taken a hit, it can no longer be used again and must be replaced with another surge protector. If it does take a hit, then one or more of the two green LED lights (both on during normal function), will be OFF, the red LED will flash and the audible tone will be activated. If that should occur, I am to flip the breaker switch to the OFF position. So, not only does it give a visible indicator, but also an audible one.

He stressed that this was a very good product and is excellent insurance against an electrical overload, whether it be from a lightning strike or a surge through the lines.

I will update this review as I recall other things he mentioned about it, but I think I got the jist of it and hopefully it will be of use to anyone considering buying one of these. Personally, I feel better knowing that our house and it's electronics are much better protected than they had been. We have always been very good about running through the house and unplugging all the electronics and appliances when a electrical/thunderstorm was passing through. He said if you are out of town, or away from home you won't have to worry nearly so much about the electronics because the Leviton should catch just about anything unless it's beyond it's specs. He added that having additional surge suppressors on your sensitive electronics - computer, TV, stereo, etc... will give an added layer of protection.

I will be glad to be able to watch the weather radar on TV when a heavy storm is passing through to see where it's going and not have to unplug the TV for fear of it getting fried when the bright, white light flashes outside. I know that the Leviton can't stop 100% of all electrical surges, but it does give a layer of comfort that we didn't have before. If you want total protection, then those surge protectors can cost thousands of dollars.

I will be writing this review in segments as I become more acquainted with the Sony HDR-TD20V HD Handycam. I have used it about 8 times recording various activities outside in bright sunlight, on cloudy overcast days, inside in regular and low lighting. Overall, the playback on the handycam itself is quite remarkable in clarity. Even the regular 2D has a 3D quality to it, as if you could reach into the picture.

I still need to record myself or a student playing classical guitar and see how good the sound quality of the recording is. This is very important to me as I hope to use this camera to record myself and my students playing various pieces on the classical guitar and possibly upload to You-Tube.

I tried to connect the camera to my HDTV to see the quality of the previously recorded videos. I carefully followed the instructions given in the included booklet, but kept getting a terrible squealing feedback from my Toshiba HDTV. I searched through the manual to see what was causing the problem but could not find the answer. I may have to call Sony for technical assistance.

I don't have a 3DTV so I am unable to review that aspect of this handycam, except for what I see on the flip-out screen.

After receiving this handycam, I read the user's manual completely and studied all the different switches, buttons, etc...to become familiar with them. This aspect of the camera is easy and very straight forward. The touchscreen is very intuitive and easy to navigate. Setting the date and time was very easy, and going through the menu selections is very easy.

I also like the style of this handycam. We have an older Sony video Hi8 bought back in 2003 which physically looks very much like the Sony HDR-TD20V but larger and obviously not nearly as advanced, but the similarity was nice in that I had an instant feeling of familiarity with the Sony HDR. The battery life appears to last for several days before needing recharging. I purposefully recorded my daughter's soccer game on Sat, then used it several times more during the week, and then took it to my mother's house on Mother's Day and it was still going strong. Recharging the battery is quite simple. I used the "Zoom" function often and was impressed that it kept it's focus so clearly at full zoom. I was able to to record some close-up action of the soccer game while I was on the other side of the field.

This handycam isn't something that I can use a few times and write an accurate review. I will have to spend more time with it and do the above mentioned things before I can totally finish this review. I am going out today to buy a longer HDMI cord so that I can place the handycam on the floor in front of the TV so I can use the remote control that came with the handycam and (hopefully) watch the videos on my HDTV. The HDMI cord that came with it is only about 2 feet long and too short to be any practical use. This feedback issue bothers me and I need to get it resolved right away. Also, I am anxious to see if what I thought was very unfocused recording actually happened or not. I noticed that on one recording session, the instant image became very blurry and as I held the camera very still it remained blurry for a few seconds before focusing.

The look and feel of this camera is beautiful! Easy to carry and use, sleek, black and silver, solid in feel and seems very well made. If you look over the manual that came with it, you will see where everything is and how to use them. I am not very tech savvy, but so far none of the controls have presented any problems. I have turned off the GPS tagging function because I don't feel comfortable having that information available on any videos I might choose to upload to various social sites. I don't see any advantage in having the GPS function. Also, I really need to test the stability function more. I get queasy almost immediately when trying to watch video that jumps around too much. I kind of got a little icky while watching playback of video I already shot.

I WILL update this review, that is a promise. I felt I should at least write about what I have experienced with this handycam so far. My personal "acid test" of this handycam will be it's sound quality. I want to record classical guitar and play it back through my Bose Soundbar to know for sure what it can do as far as sound. If I get great HD video and awesome sound I will probably give this handycam 5 stars.

UPDATE: 7.19.12
I recorded a play (in a darkened theater) that one of my kids was in and I was totally blown away by the visual quality of the playback on our HDTV. The camera self-adjusted very well for the darkened conditions and I could clearly see all of the actors as if I were sitting in the audience again. I bought an excellent HDMI extension cord from Amazon for around 3 bucks (Radio Shack wanted over $30.00 dollars for about the same quality of cord!) and I could easily hold and operate the camera at a comfortable distance from the TV(approx. 10 ft.) The sound quality was quite good (through Bose Soundbar) for being recorded from a distance of at least 50 feet away and trying to pick up the shy voices of small children. This camera keeps getting better and better, but more updates will follow.

Though I am giving a review for this backpack, I can't come from the perspective of having used it for a while. I only received my Targus backpack yesterday, but from the looks of it I am pretty darn sure this backpack will last a long, long time. I've used MANY backpacks in the past carrying books, laptops and supplies during the time it took to earn two separate college degrees, and at my previous job of 17 years. I had to carry tools, manuals, laptops and assorted parts to calibrate monitoring equipment around my state. I was rough on the backpacks and some wore out.

I really wish I had had a backpack like this one. It's very well constructed out of strong materials, has a plethora of pockets and places to organize your stuff, and though I don't have a 17" notebook as of yet, it appears to be deep and wide and should easily fit one. There are even slots for file folders and inside zipper pouches. There are pockets on the inside and pockets on the outside. The bottom inside has a foam rubber "shock pad" that neatly folds down flat on the bottom of the backpack and is about 1/2" thick. Plus the bottom is covered in a waterproof rubbery material that should definitely help keep water from seeping up into the bag. That happened to me several times on my job with my other backpacks and it was really frustrating. It's very easy to set your backpack down on the ground not realizing the area is wet.

The shoulder straps are padded and adjustable, and it has a waist strap for extra stability. Even if you didn't use this backpack to tote your 17" marvel of technology around, it would serve well as a camper/hiker backpack. I can't wait to start using it. If something should go wrong or tear up, I will most definitely update this review telling about it, but for now I can find no fault whatsoever with it.

I bought this particular receiver for my 85 year old mother. Her old "Scott" receiver finally bit the dust. She has a lot of vinyl records and I needed a receiver which I could connect a turn-table too and this one has phono outputs.

I had it shipped to her house and after I arrived I had it set up in about 15 minutes. I didn't even have to read the directions as it was pretty straightforward. I also connected a CD player and the receiver has plenty of outputs. It's kind of heavy but that wasn't a problem. After it was all connected I turned it on and *voila!* music! She's hard of hearing so I had to crank it up and it sounded great! I can't remember the size of the two speakers but they are probably around 25 years old, big (sit on the floor) and this receiver powered them just fine.

Mom can't quite understand how to work the radio....that could have been designed a lot more simply but I set it to her favorite station and she was fine. I did have to consult the directions to figure out how to use and preset radio stations. It was not intuitive at all.

Overall, it's a nice receiver. It's not what a true audiophile would buy, but it was a great replacement for a very old receiver.

Ahhh......now I can easily use my keyboard in any area of my desk. I had to keep it close to the monitor because the cord it came with was too short to adequately reach the back of my CPU which sits on the floor beside my desk. This extension cord was easy to attach at both ends and worked instantly. I'm using it now as I type this review with my keyboard in a much more functional area on my desk.

It seems to be just as durable as the original cable so I don't worry about it breaking. I think it's the perfect extension cord but only if you have a PS/2 connector at both ends. And though my original cable is black, the extension cord does not even show since it's draped behind the desk and CPU.

This keyboard is smaller by an inch all around than my other keyboard so it takes up less room on my desk top, which I like. However, the cord needs to be at least another foot longer. I have had to slide everything on my desk towards the left by about 6 inches in order to use this keyboard.

It has no frills - only the basics are included. It's all black except for the white lettering, the keystrokes have a nice feel to them and are rather quiet. The keyboard can be angled up little bit using the two flip down tabs on the back. Also the small rubber strips help to hold it firmly in place.

For the price I think it's a pretty good deal.

I bought several of these for our home and my mother's home. Super loud, and will stop or at least make it difficult for a door to be opened wide enough for an intruder to enter. I tested one out on my husband by placing it at the door he normally enters through. It stopped him, scared him and did just what I hoped it would do. He kind of got mad at me and hollered a few explicatives but it was worth it! We have one door that is on a raised threshold so I set the door stop alarm on a book and the door hits it squarely when opened just a little bitty bit. It's loud - ear piercing loud and that's good as it should scare the bejeebers out of a bad person. On doors that have windows through which the unwanted guest might peer through and see the doorstop, just by placing a light weight towel or papers over it disguises completely. My mom was thrilled with her doorstops. Anything to help parents stay safe is money well-spent.

For my mom I had to write in big letters with a felt permanent marker ON and OFF so she could easily turn them off when not in use and not waste batteries or scare her by an accidental alarm. We'll be taking some of these with us on vacation. These are really great!

UPDATE: December 1, 2011 - I have bought several more of these because they are so practical and good at what they do. I've learned to pick them up by holding the sides of them lest I accidentally hit the metal plate on top and hear it's ear-breaking scream. I've taken at least one of these on overnight trips to put against the door in our hotel rooms. It makes me feel a lot safer knowing this thing will scream if someone tries to break in.

I think this is a good electronic gadget. Actually, it made me upgrade my phone to one that uses Bluetooth. I was still using a cell phone that only lets you receive and make calls, and play a few games so I guess it was time to move forward technically speaking.

The sound is clear, I had my daughter answer the phone at home while I was driving and it worked marvelously. She could easily understand me and vice-versa. After I got home I put my cell phone on the kitchen table after calling my land-line and I walked outside of the house with the Jabra Stone only. I was surprised that I was still able to talk to my daughter from almost 100 feet away from my cell phone. As I walked down the driveway and into the street it finally lost connection. But, I know that at least within a few feet I don't need to always have my cell phone right with me.

The Jabra Stone worked just like the directions said it would but I still kept messing it up during the learning curve. I wish it was a little more secure around my ear and for those who like to tuck their long hair behind their ears (me) it's difficult to do that with the earpiece on. And I have to remember to untuck my hair before putting it on or it will not go on. But once you get the hair problem solved it's well hidden - I don't think anyone can see it while I wear it. Also, it only works for the right ear, at least as far as I can tell so I don't know if it can be modified some way to hook on the left ear. I tried to fit onto my left ear but couldn't figure out a way to do so. So, if you are deaf in your right ear I would check to make sure it could be changed somehow to fit the left ear.

It's small, convenient and functional. So much easier than trying to drive and hold a phone at the same time, but I rarely drive and yak on the phone anyway since it's so dangerous. I don't want to be distracted from driving. But when out shopping or doing something else on foot and I'm expecting an important call it's great to have my hands free to continue shopping as I yak.

The reason for 4 stars instead of 5 - kind of loose on my ear, and the charger doesn't hold a charge for very long. It's frequently plugged into the wall re-charging. But it's great that you can hook the charger to your shirt pocket (men will like that) so you can continue to receive calls all day long.

This is a high quality camera, but you must take time to read through the owner's manual to understand how to get the best pictures. You can just grab it and point and shoot using it while in the "automode" setting, but the resulting pictures may leave you a little disappointed depending upon the photographic conditions. To get the highest quality photos you must become familiar with how this little beauty works. Unfortunately, you might have to print out and tote the manual with you when you find yourself in situations where your pictures aren't what you'd like, or you can't figure out how to do certain things like know what's behind the flashing icon error message, or how to simulate different types of film, or can you choose between clarity, reduced noise and dynamic range? This is not really a simple "point and shoot" camera and all images will turn out great. You will have to study it, practice with it, and most of all have patience and you will be pleasantly rewarded for your efforts. Though the indicators vary with camera settings, there are 23 different indicators just for shooting mode, and 12 for playback mode, not to mention the date/time stamp, battery level, and indicator. It can get confusing.

Although a basic manual booklet is included with the camera, a much more detailed manual must be uploaded from the enclosed CD and then all 125 pages can be printed out or read from your computer monitor. The manual covers all the material in the booklet almost page for page but includes much more information about features the booklet leaves out and the booklet will refer you to specific pages in the manual for more information. Also, in the manual are about 50 FAQ's that are very useful. I am a manual reader, (having written many technical SOP's) and appreciate having well-written and well thought out manuals that are understandable and succinct. Though I would have preferred a manual that I don't have to upload to my computer, it is well-written and many useful pictures are included.

This camera is loaded with many different options/features but accessing and understanding many of them will require reading the manual. For people who don't want to be bothered with all the bells and whistles this camera may be more than they need. I can see very serious photographers using this camera. Reading through the manual I have compiled a list of some of the various modes, options and features available:

Digital Zoom
Movie Mode
Silent Mode
Variable ISO settings
Image size selection
Aspect Ratio selection
Intelligent Face detection
Scene Position
Shooting Modes
EXR Mode
Film simulation
Dynamic Range
White Balance
Continuous Photography
Photometry - multi, spot, average

Playback Options:
Erase
Slide Show
Red-eye Removal
Image Rotation
Protection from accidental deletion
Crop
Resize
Voice Memo
Print Order
Time Difference
Format

Pages 37, 67-68, 86-87, 97-103, and 104-107 would be good to print out and keep with your camera as they contain tables of various camera functions and a trouble shooting chart.

I have taken many pictures and movies inside and out, light and dark, with this camera set on various settings. And though I have practiced with it now for several weeks, I still need to often refer to the manual when I choose to vary from automode. Some things I have found especially desirable are:

Silent Mode - I attend classical music concerts where flash photography is prohibited. This mode will silence all beeps and flashes.

Large viewing screen on the back of the camera. It is exactly 5.5cm x 4.0 cm.

Digital Zoom - extremely good. I attended a local minor-league baseball game and sat far away on the grass well beyond the playing field. I was able to fully zoom and still get good, clear, close-up shots of the players with no blurring.

Movie Mode - Completely surpasses any other I've experienced so far. Images are clear, colorful and the sound quality is excellent. Camera noise was heard and recorded while using the "zoom" function in Movie Mode though it was not very loud.

Multi-frame play back function is very useful to quickly scan for a particular picture.

Fine Pix Viewer Program was very easy to install on my computer. I use Windows XP.

Very good photography in low-light conditions.

Also some things I did not find particularly desirable but are not major flaws:

I cannot directly burn a CD using the Fine Pix Viewer Program which comes with this camera. I have to use another camera program, import the pictures into it and then burn a CD.

Very easy to accidentally turn it on or off and easy to get misfires.

The zoom lever is too sensitive. I have learned with practice to barely move it very slowly.

The camera does not give helpful suggestions on how to get a better picture as does my HP R717.

Not HD capable.

The higher the ISO the grainier the picture though a higher ISO is desirable when shooting in dim/low light levels. I have set the ISO level to 200 and that seems to produce the best pictures so far.

Almost too many options, modes and functions to choose from. Though you can immediately begin to take pictures using Automode, it will take time to fully understand the many other aspects and features this camera has.

In Summary:

I can find no major complaint concerning this camera. It takes excellent clear and colorful photos even in situations where I least expect it - indoors with no flash. Any poor quality pictures I have taken are not the fault of the camera but due to the photographer's ignorance of how to use/understand properly the many features of the camera. The basic mechanics of such things as battery and memory card installation are very easy. Battery charging is a very simple process and battery life seems long. The manual is detailed and covers more than I would probably care to know. This is almost more camera than I need, though I will continue to use it and will update this review as necessary.

UPDATE 2.9.15 - Been using this camera all these years and now it's beginning to show it's age and giving me some problems. The viewing screen on the back has a vertical big black bar but it doesn't appear on the actual pictures. And the lens cover doesn't always completely open when the camera is turned on. I still use it but it might be time to think about a replacement. It's been good though so I really don't have any complaints.

I thoroughly investigated LCD vs. Plasma and decided that LCD best suited my needs. But the job was only 1/2 over - I had to select the set. I read specs, checked prices, read more specs, went to electronic forums and asked specific questions about various sets, visited stores so I could see and compare images and finally settled on the Sharp Aquos 37". I've had it for over 2 months now waiting to see if anything is going to go wrong, but it's just great. It's been tested hard so far and the picture on HD is amazingly clear - I can only imagine that some news casters would prefer analog since every molecule of every mole on their faces can be clearly seen! (Well, a little exaggerated but the HD picture is truly very, very good). The colors are beautiful. We don't have it wall-mounted - sits in a TV cabinet. No problem with the viewing angle or distance. I wouldn't go any larger if you are closer than 14 feet or else the picture will look pixilated. A big LCD screen with a short viewing distance is not the way to go.

It has plenty of outputs/inputs on the back with easy access. I had to make a call to Sharp Technical Support about an input question and they were very helpful and friendly. He also told me that since the set was considered a large one and would be difficult to carry to a repair shop if a problem occurred which would require repair, that they would send someone over to the house free-of-charge for one year to fix it! I also like the fact that Sharp is reputable company and stands behind it's products. I avoided the disposable sets despite the raves about picture quality for fear I would have to dispose of it within 2 years if it needed repair. I hope to be watching this set 10 years from now.

If an electronic device is going to go bad, it usually does so within a year. I have had the set on for 10 + hours a day. I don't plan on keeping it on that much in the future, but I work from home and I like to hear the background noise. My only complaint is with the sound when
on digital stations and when watching DVD's. It is very weak and still hard to hear even when it is cranked full blast. I will probably get external speakers to remedy that. However, when on analog stations the sound is very loud and easy to hear. I don't know if the weak sound is due to the set or the station's/DVD's digital signal.

What I love also is the fact that if a movie has been filmed in a dark environment - night, cave, or dark interior of a house - it is still easy to see what is going on. On my old analog set I missed much of a movie due to dark scenes which we could not adjust to be seen. Try watching, "Clan of the Cave Bear" and you will know what I mean.

And you don't need a professional calibration to adjust the picture. The menu is straight-forward and easy to understand. It's well worth taking the 15 minutes or so to carefully go through all of the picture options and selecting those which make the picture good for you. It will be glaring when first out of the box so take some time to adjust it.

The only minor complaint I have so far is the wait between channel selections. I'm used to going instantly from channel to channel and there is a lag time of about 1-2 seconds. NO big deal.

I like this TV a lot, and have ordered my 81 year old mother a 20" Sharp Aquos. It hasn't arrived yet but I will certainly critique it at a later date.

UPDATE: September 1, 2008

This set has been heavily used. It is on more hours of the day than it should be. It has worked perfectly. I still love this set. No problems ever. We watched the Summer Olympics games in China and couldn't have asked for a better set with which to view them. The opening ceremony in Beijing was truly awesome and no details were missed.

UPDATE: 2.22.12
This set has been great! Still going strong despite it being used several hours every day. Especially now that we use it to play Wii games on and watch movies on Netflix. I love this T.V.!!!

I use these as a backup to my more expensive pair of headphones and the sound quality is almost as good as the ones that cost three times more! This speaker really surprised us and in a GOOD way! It is true to its description of having some serious bass and it is AWESOME. I like to use this in my exercise room when I am doing high-intensity workouts because the music keeps me going and sounds so incredible coming from this! It is definitely worth it and a great value.

Party of one? This is me at work with my speaker, saved from the less lively built-in speakers on my computer. It is a great speaker for personal use with decent sound; it is also great on bike rides. The sound is pretty decent though not as bass-heavy as I would like. However, depending on the music you listen to that might not be as important as an affordable, quality sound which this definitely offers.
We use this for big gatherings in the basement, it's loud, we love the fun party lights and it works great! Simple to connect and play music on with awesome sound at a great price.
I use different PCs and not all of them have the necessary USB slot required to charge an Apple device. This makes that very simple and the charge is fast and efficient too.

My son loves the design of these headphones the most - they are SO nicely designed that they look much more high end than they actually are. The sound is also very nice too for the price and they're very comfortable. A more popular brand would definitely have another $40 (at least) tacked onto the price just for the name, so you will be pleasantly surprised by these.

Fantastic audio and video. Easy to set up and use. I like the way it tracks the voice and speaker so they come quickly into focus and this is great for those who have returned to the office, as we have a few days a week at times to have conference calls with our satellite offices. A solid investment and looks great too!

My husband has been using this because he wanted something lighter and easier to tote around when he has to go to different sites throughout the day. The storage is great and the computer is fast with great response. The screen display is excellent. Chrome OS is very easy to use but takes some time getting used to coming from Windows so if you're new to a Chromebook and want it to be a companion or replacement to your Windows laptop, it can fill those shoes easily. If you have large files, you can get an external hard drive that is portable and have everything you need either there or in the cloud. A very solid purchase!

And that goes for just about everything from music to photos to books and other documents. If you have large video files, it can store plenty of them as well - 2TB is the perfect amount of space for anyone who has an assortment of files they need to have easy access to in volume. The data transfer speeds are phenomenal and this fits in the palm of your hand which means you can have your life's work on you at all times!

My son is of the serious gamer category and plays a lot of games/streams/has an online community that he engages with also, so this upgrade was perfect for him. For the price, you receive the bells and whistles, can use it with gaming consoles and the sound is impressive too. The charging case is also small and can be put right in your pocket. They charge fast and the charge lasts for a long time. They stay put in your ears and the phone call/audio quality is great! My son likes to use this in multiplayer games and also enjoys using it as a speaker for his music, etc when he is not gaming. This is without a doubt the most phenomenal speaker I've ever had and it can handle any genre of music - and I play them all - and bring the most out of each track and genre, from hip hop to house to jazz to rock to Afrobeat to drum and bass to classical. This headset is definitely one of the best ones I've tried! It is very comfortable and has incredible audio and connectivity. I've had to use this on many, MANY calls and have never had any issues.
